# ## Title Page

-> **This is the gate of the Lord** <-
<note>original: "Zeh HaSha'ar La'Adonai" from Psalm 118:20. This phrase was commonly used on the title pages of early Hebrew books to signify the holiness of the text within.</note>

---

# **The Book of**
# **And These Are the Names**
<note>original: "Ve-eleh Shemot," the Hebrew name for the Book of Exodus.</note>
# **From the Zohar**

By the Divine Tanna <term>Tanna: A sage from the era of the Mishnah, roughly 10–220 CE</term> **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai**, of blessed memory.
Including the <term>Pekudei Oraita: The "Commandments of the Torah," a specific layer of the Zohar that provides mystical explanations for Jewish laws</term> and many hidden secrets, along with an index of the biblical verses printed herein.
Edited and corrected by the wise Sage, our honored teacher and Rabbi,
**Immanuel**, son of our honored teacher and Rabbi **Yekutiel**, of blessed memory,
a man of Benevento. And by the youth,
**Abraham** (may his Rock protect him and grant him life), son of our honored teacher and Rabbi
**Meshullam**, of blessed memory, of Modena.

---

# **Here in Mantua**

Under the rule of his highness, our lord the Duke
Guglielmo Gonzaga (may his glory be exhaulted). In the year
**"Five for our help"** according to the abbreviated era.
<note>original: "Hamisha L'ezratenu." This is a chronogram where the numerical value of the marked letters indicates the year 5318 in the Hebrew calendar, which corresponds to 1558 CE.</note>

--- Page 6 ---
<meta>This page serves as a printer's introduction to an early edition of the Zohar (likely the 1558 Mantua edition). It addresses the editorial challenges of organizing the various layers of the text, specifically the "Tikkunim" (Rectifications) and "Ra’aya Mehemna" (The Faithful Shepherd), and critiques previous corrupted editions.</meta>

## Main Text (Introduction)

-> **They Said** <-

The editors, who are named at the gate <note>the title page</note>, even though these are the depths of the end of the levels of beloved poverty, and from the sound of the cry of the shepherds and the wailing of the valley dwellers, the feet of the weak almost faltered. The delay of our feet was caused by the simplicity of the work, and the clouds darkened with sharpness because of the sea of complexities and the cave that overturned us, until we wished to turn back and cancel our preparation. As you may go and see, may the God who made us kings be blessed; the strength of God is the priest of our eyes, and we had no power to rely on our own strength. Had we the strength now to drip after this precious work, and specifically the writing of the Levites <note>referring to the scribal or printing labor</note> which upon the earth the serpent spits out every coldness upon the precious white holes as at first, and they could not see the swallowing of the holy. And it was when they went to the place where we stood, we found and saw the Book of the Zohar; the mighty ones, masters of kindness, dwell upon it, along with some of the sayings of the Book of the Zohar and the *Tikkunei Ruach* <note>Rectifications of the Spirit</note>. Also, thousands of dreams in the midst of the table in the portion of *Bereshit* <note>Genesis</note> are joined from the Book of the *Tikkunim* <note>The Rectifications/Tikkunei HaZohar</note>. They also placed in their general collections the companions of the *Ra’aya Mehemna* <note>The Faithful Shepherd—a specific layer of the Zohar</note> inside between the portions; a little in writing was printed once in one place and once in another, printing the portions without mentioning the name *Ra’aya Mehemna*. As we have heard, so have we seen in their confusion and haste to place the superior parts, as they copied them from corrupted books and did not labor to direct it to fix that which they distorted by the agreement of five strong wisdoms. And in the place where it said in their copy "lowly" from the portion of *Noach* to *Pharaoh*, they placed *Ra’aya Mehemna*. And in the place where it said to lick from the fool at the beginning of the detail of the few, they placed the praises of our teacher Rabbi Isaac <note>likely referring to Isaac Luria or a contemporary sage</note>. Kindness was found in the portion of *Boker* <note>Morning</note>, and its inclusion did many things. Our wise men know that it lacked the salt of that spirit of the hollows in wisdom, understanding, and knowledge. Specifically, regarding those without wisdom, they will speak with their lips and wag their heads when they see the work—to the wise man from our excellence, lest they live like those who turned the gate, released to them such depth in this wisdom. If only the buyers would turn with their money as they do now, we entered and established for them everything to say, for the researcher publicized our wise man, his voice is diminished except for the lacking voice.

Therefore, among the tribes of Israel, let it be known faithfully that we did not build, nor did we mention, nor did it enter our minds to place between the sayings of the Zohar the sayings of the Zohar and the *Tikkunei Ruach*, because they were already printed in the accompanying book by several from Recanati <note>Rabbi Menachem Recanati, a 13th-14th century Italian Kabbalist</note>, and these are his words in the Commentary on the Torah <note>original: "u-ve-zeh leshono be-ferush ha-Torah"</note>. And there the spirit of the spirit is the seal. And the sayings of the Book of the *Tikkunim* which they added in the portion of *Bereshit* were already printed in *Tikkun* 89 of the Book of the *Tikkunim*, and they were compared to their correctness; our mentioned writing will arise in the portion of *Terumah* <note>Exodus 25:1–27:19</note>, for there we understand. And it teaches a disciple of the wise, like the bitterness of the heart for the lack, etc., which is a saying printed in the margins of the *Tikkunim*, not printed in its proper place. Regarding all the commands of *Ra’aya Mehemna*, even though it was our intention to print them all in order as arranged by the author, the Revealer <note>original: "ha-Megaleh"</note>, as he favored them now, we agreed to place them in the place where they were printed and they shall be mentioned there. And the sayings of *Ra’aya Mehemna* that they placed there in the book of *Bereshit* will be printed in the book... like you, pleasantness. And besides what we toiled to align the copies, even now our wise men are like those with senses, to have our eyes open upon the work to let it live, etc., above in justice and righteousness, the opposite of what they did there. For the best will find in it sayings of the *Tikkunei Pelach* and secrets, and missing and extra letters, as seen in every memory of the three rectifications. And he who is wise in the matter shall find good, and it shall increase in our days, and may God send His help from the sanctuary, and may He magnify the Torah and make it glorious.

***

<summary>This introduction by the printers of the Zohar explains their efforts to correct errors found in previous manuscripts and editions, specifically regarding the placement of the "Ra'aya Mehemna" and "Tikkunim" sections. They cite the authority of Rabbi Menachem Recanati and emphasize their commitment to textual accuracy over the rushed work of predecessors.</summary>

## Main Text (The Radiance)

**The children** of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob, each man and his household came: <note>Exodus 1:1</note> *And those who are wise shall shine as the brightness <note>Hebrew: Zohar</note> of the firmament; and those who turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.* <note>Daniel 12:3</note> "Those who are wise" <note>Aramaic: Maskilim</note> are those who gaze into the secret of wisdom <note>Hokhmah</note>, like those wings and movements of the supernal wisdom. "Brightness" <note>Zohar</note> is the clarity of understanding <note>Binah</note> of the River that flows and goes forth from Eden. And this is the hidden secret called "The Firmament," wherein stand the sun and the moon and all those stars that give light.

**The Radiance** <note>Zohar</note> is the firmament that shines with clarity over the Garden. Its branches cover all those forms, trees, and spices that are within it. All the beasts of the field and all the birds of the sky are suspended beneath it and dwell under those branches. **The Radiance** is of the Tree that gives food to all. Its existence is forever and for all eternity. The "Other Side" <note>Sitra Achra; the realm of evil or impurity</note> does not dwell within it, but only the side of Holiness. Blessed is the portion of those who taste of it; they exist forever and for all eternity. These are called "living" in this world and "living" in the world to come. **The Radiance** strikes this and opens above and below; five parasangs <note>A measure of distance</note> is its path. It is hidden and concealed in its simplicity; within this intellect stands a single light. **The Radiance**—all colors exist within it. Those colors ascend and descend; they do not settle in another place when the moon travels. When they go forth from it below—and this is like a radiance that does not shine—they settle and do not settle, they stand and do not stand, because they do not settle in another place. This is found in the visitation of the twelve tribes who are established within it, and they descended in this radiance that does not shine into the exile of Egypt with several supernal Matrons <note>Divine feminine presences or entourages</note>, a congregation and an assembly: *the names of the children of Israel, etc.* **Rabbi** Shimon opened: "It was a day for all the Lord." Arise, there were two.

--- Page 8 ---
<meta>This page marks the beginning of the commentary on the Book of Exodus (Parashat Shemot). It establishes the mystical theme of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) accompanying the Jewish people into exile, specifically focusing on the transition from the patriarchal age to the Egyptian bondage.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And these are the names**<-

Blessed is the portion of those who labor in the Torah! When the Holy One, Blessed be He, arises to bring close to Him all that He saw on the King’s earth, He brings it as an offering. I have seen His hidden secrets which he beheld. Indeed, Ezekiel <note>original: "Yechukal"</note> is, as it were, the essence of faithfulness; everything he saw, he saw through the lens of faith, and he revealed all the secrets of the Holy One, Blessed be He, that were necessary to be revealed. 

Come and see: all the children who descended to the land of Egypt below were carried according to the "Youth" <note>The "Youth" (Na'ar) is a mystical title for the angel Metatron, who governs the lower worlds and guides Israel in exile.</note>. Woe to those who are not accustomed to the Youth, for at the end of their days they expect delights and pleasures, yet they find a Youth who is not a "perfect youth" until there is cause for weeping. When Israel descended to Egypt, they were accustomed to the Youth, for all the days of that righteous one <note>Jacob</note>, their merit was through the Youth. Because of their folly, the exile unfolded as is fitting for every exile. During that entire time, that Youth was perfected, and the upper and lower beings all wept together over them, as it is written:

> **Behold, their brave ones cry without...** <note>Isaiah 33:7. The Zohar interprets "brave ones" (erellam) as high-ranking angels.</note>

And regarding the lower beings, it is written:

> **By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down and wept...** <note>Psalm 137:1</note>

They all wept over the exile, for the children who had been like the delights of kings, as it is written:

> **The precious sons of Zion...** <note>Lamentations 4:2</note>

We have learned: do not be comforted by what is written on the parchment, but weep and weep again! For these are the high mountains of the worlds, and those high mountains are the "precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold." When they descended into exile, their heads were bowed, their necks burdened, and their hands bound behind them. When they were in the Babylonian exile, they were beloved, yet they felt they had no eternal standing, thinking the Holy One, Blessed be He, had abandoned them and would never look upon them again. 

At that moment, the Holy One, Blessed be He, called to all His heavenly family <note>original: "pamalya"</note>, all His chariots <note>term: Merkavot (Divine Chariots/structures of the celestial realm)</note>, all His hosts, the Matron <note>The Shekhinah, the feminine aspect of the Divine</note>, the Throne, and all the hosts of heaven. He said to them: "What are you doing here? My beloved children are embraced by the Babylonian exile, and you are here? Arise! Descend all of you to Babylon, and I shall be with them!" This is the meaning of: "Thus says the Lord: For your sake I have sent to Babylon" <note>Isaiah 43:14</note>. It does not say "The Holy One sent," but "I have sent"—meaning He sent Himself along with all the chariots and the Supernal Matron.

When they descended to Babylon, the heavens were opened and the Holy Spirit rested upon Ezekiel, and he saw all that he saw. He came to Israel and said: "Even in this destroyed place, among all these filthy things, the Chariots have come to dwell among you!" They did not believe him until he was forced to reveal all that he saw... he revealed even more ->to one elder after another<- as was necessary. Once Israel saw this, they rejoiced. 

Rabbi Yessa said: I heard the voice of Israel in the complete exile, and when they heard the words from the mouth of Ezekiel, they stood as a congregation of the Matron, for she was with them. Each one was pained by the exile, for they knew that the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not withhold His will from a prophet... and just as the Throne was revealed, so too it is revealed in every place where Israel was exiled, the Shekhinah was exiled with them. And here, in the exile of Egypt, what is written?

> **And these are the names of the children of Israel...** <note>Exodus 1:1</note>

Since it is written "the children of Israel," why does it then say **"with Jacob"**? It should have said "who came with him." Rather, "these are the names of the children of Israel" refers to the Chariots and the supernal dwellings that descended with Jacob alongside the Shekhinah into the Egyptian exile.

---

# And These

**Are the names of the children of Israel, etc.** Rabbi Hiyya opened his discourse:

> **Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, with me from Lebanon; look from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of the leopards.** <note>Song of Songs 4:8</note>

This verse was said concerning the Assembly of Israel <note>The mystical community of Jewish souls/Shekhinah</note> at the time Israel went out of Egypt and approached Mount Sinai to receive the Torah. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to her: "Come with me from Lebanon"—from that supernal delight you have come, a perfect bride, coming quickly to be crowned from heaven with all light and gathering...

<summary>This page introduces the Book of Exodus by explaining that the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) and heavenly hosts accompanied Jacob's family into Egypt, just as they later accompanied the exiles to Babylon. It emphasizes that God does not abandon Israel in suffering, using Ezekiel's visions as proof of the Divine Chariot's presence in "unclean" lands.</summary>
<keywords>Exile, Shekhinah, Metatron, Ezekiel, Babylon, Egypt, Divine Chariot, Jacob, Song of Songs, Assembly of Israel</keywords>

--- Page 9 ---
<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the soul's journey and the communal destiny of Israel. It transitions from the poetic imagery of the Song of Songs to the opening of the Book of Exodus (Shemot).</meta>

## And These Are The Names

"Come with me from Lebanon, my bride" <note>Song of Songs 4:8</note>—this refers to the Torah. "Look from the top of Amana"—look upon all this and look upon those who will receive the offering for your children. "From the top of Amana" <note>Amana means 'faith'</note> refers to the beginning, when they entered into the supreme faith and said, "All that the Lord has spoken, we will do and we will obey" <note>Exodus 24:7</note>. At that moment, they were weighed in the same scale as the high angels, for it is written of them: "Bless the Lord, O His angels, mighty in strength, who do His word, obeying the voice of His word" <note>Psalms 103:20</note>. Then the Community of Israel <term>Knesset Yisrael; the mystical personification of the Jewish people</term> received the Torah.

"From the peaks of Senir and Hermon"—this is Mount Sinai, which they approached and stood beneath, as it is written: "And they stood at the foot of the mountain" <note>Exodus 19:17</note>. "From the lions' dens"—these are the children of Seir <note>Edom/Rome</note>, whom the Holy One invited to accept the Torah, but they did not want to receive it. "From the mountains of the leopards"—these are the children of Ishmael. For it is written: "The Lord came from Sinai, and rose up from Seir unto them; He shined forth from Mount Paran, and He came with ten thousands of holy ones" <note>Deuteronomy 33:2</note>.

What is the meaning of "He came with ten thousands of holy ones"? We have learned that when the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to give the Torah to Israel, groups of high angels came and opened by saying: "O Lord, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth, You who have set Your glory above the heavens!" <note>Psalms 8:2</note>. They wanted the Torah to be given to them.

The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them: "Is there death among you? For it is written: 'When a man dies in a tent...' <note>Numbers 19:14</note>. 'And if a man has committed a sin worthy of death, and he be put to death...' <note>Deuteronomy 21:22</note>. Are there legal cases among you? Is there theft or kidnapping among you? For it is written: 'You shall not steal.' Is there falsehood among you? For it is written: 'You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.' Is there coveting among you? For it is written: 'You shall not covet' <note>Exodus 20:13</note>. What use have you for the Torah?"

Immediately they opened and said: "O Lord, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!"—but the phrase "You who have set Your glory above the heavens" is no longer written there. Regarding this, it says "He came with ten thousands of holy ones," and then "from His right hand went a fiery law for them."

Rabbi Yose established this verse as referring to when the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> entered the exile of Egypt. He hinted that this verse was stated regarding the Secret of the Unity of Faith. "Come with me from Lebanon, my bride"—the Voice says to the Speech, "Come," because the Voice comes to the Speech and leads it as one, without any separation at all. For the Voice is the general principle and Speech is called the particular detail. Therefore, the general needs the particular and the particular needs the general. For there is no Voice without Speech, and no Speech without Voice. Therefore, "Come from Lebanon"—this is the language of the "root" <note>original: 'ikra'; a play on Lebanon/Lavan (white/root)</note>, for both of them come from Lebanon.

"Look from the top of Amana"—this is the throat, from which the breath goes out to the whole world, from the secret of the hidden and concealed Lebanon. "From the peaks of Senir and Hermon"—this is the tongue that articulates and shapes the Speech. "From the lions' dens"—these are the righteous. "From the mountains of the leopards"—these are the many nations who inherited the malevolent side.

**And these are the names of the children of Israel...** <note>Exodus 1:1</note>

Rabbi Hiyya opened: "Do not eat the bread of one who has an evil eye, and do not crave his delicacies" <note>Proverbs 23:6</note>. "Do not eat the bread of one who has an evil eye," because the bread of a person who possesses an evil eye is not worthy to be eaten or enjoyed. For when Israel was in Egypt, they did not taste anything from them, so that they would not be found in exile and be oppressed by them.

Rabbi Yitzhak said to him: "But was it not a decree that was decreed?" He replied: "Everything is as it should be. For it was not decreed specifically for Egypt, as it is not written 'your offspring shall be strangers in the land of Egypt,' but rather 'in a land that is not theirs' <note>Genesis 15:13</note>, even in another land."

Rabbi Yitzhak said: "We see that one who is a 'master of soul' <note>a glutton</note> eats more than other people. Furthermore, we see that one who looks after the life-force of the 'Evil One' <term>Sitra Achra; the 'Other Side' or source of impurity</term>, which contains the 'Evil Eye,' should cut his own throat rather than eat before him. For there is nothing as evil in the world as that Evil Eye. What is written? 'Because the Egyptians could not eat bread with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to the Egyptians' <note>Genesis 43:32</note>. Here you have the 'Evil Eye.'"

There are three things that push the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> away from the world and cause the dwelling of the Holy One, Blessed be He, not to be in the world, and then when people cry out, their voice is not heard. And these are: One who...

<summary>This page uses the Song of Songs to explain why the Torah was given to humans rather than angels and begins a mystical commentary on the Book of Exodus, warning against the spiritual dangers of the 'Evil Eye' and the Egyptian exile.</summary>
<keywords>Torah, Sinai, Angels, Shekhinah, Voice and Speech, Lebanon, Evil Eye, Egypt, Exile, Secret of Unity</keywords>

--- Page 10 ---
<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Exodus (Shemot). The previous section likely concluded the introduction to the names of the tribes, transitioning here into the moral and spiritual requirements for the Divine Presence to dwell among Israel, specifically focusing on the sanctity of the Covenant (circumcision) and ritual purity.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And These Are The Names**<-

As it is written, "Thus," <note>original: *koh*</note> implying that there is no impurity as powerful in the world as the impurity of the menstruant <note><term>Niddah</term>: a woman during her menstrual period, requiring ritual immersion before physical contact with her husband</note>. The impurity of the menstruant is more difficult than all the impurities in the world. They become defiled, and all who draw near to them shall be defiled with them. In every place where they are found, the Divine Presence <note><term>Shekhinah</term>: the feminine, indwelling aspect of God</note> flees from before them. And not only that, but he brings evil diseases upon himself and upon that seed which he shall beget. For once a man approaches a menstruant, that impurity leaps upon him and he becomes defiled in all his limbs. The seed he begets at that time <note>variant: at that hour</note> draws upon itself a spirit of impurity, and all his days he shall be in impurity. For behold, his very building and foundation are in an impurity greater and more powerful than all the impurities in the world; for as soon as a man approaches a menstruant, that impurity leaps upon him, as it is written:
> And her impurity shall be upon him. <note>Leviticus 15:24</note>

One who lies with the "daughter of a foreign god" <note>a non-Jewish woman</note> sins against the Holy Covenant <note><term>Brit Milah</term>: the covenant of circumcision</note> and does not stand within the other mystery, as it is written:
> And has married the daughter of a foreign god. <note>Malachi 2:11</note>

And we have learned: there is no zeal before the Holy One, Blessed be He, except for the zeal for the Holy Covenant, which is the sustenance of the Holy Name and the mystery of Faith. What is written? "And he took a spear" <note>Numbers 25:7</note> to merit the covenant of destiny; immediately it says, "Phinehas the son of Eleazar." The leaders of the people who knew and did not protest were punished first, as it is written:
> Take all the chiefs of the people and hang them up before the Lord against the sun. <note>Numbers 25:4</note>

Rabbi Abba said: What is "against the sun"? It means against the Covenant, which is called "Sun." And concerning them it is said:
> For the Lord God is a sun and a shield. <note>Psalms 84:12</note>

"Sun and shield"—this is the Holy Covenant. Just as the sun shines and illuminates the world, so too the Holy Covenant shines and illuminates the body of a man. "Shield"—just as a shield is meant to protect a man, so too the Holy Covenant protects a man. And one who guards it, there is no [harmful] female power in the world that can approach him. And this is "against the sun." The leaders of the people are seized in every generation at a time when they do not know <note>i.e., do not take notice or protest</note>, because this sin is upon them for abandoning the Holy One, Blessed be He, in this Covenant. Of one who brings holiness into a domain that is not his, it is written:
> You shall have no other gods before Me. You shall not bow down to them nor serve them, for I the Lord your God am a jealous God. <note>Exodus 20:3-5</note>

And it is all one jealousy. And because of this, the Divine Presence departs from him. One who is false to the Holy Covenant that is sealed in the flesh of man is as if he were false to the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He. One who is false to the King's seal is false to the King himself; he has no portion in the God of Israel, except through the power of constant <note>variant: great</note> repentance <note><term>Teshuvah</term>: returning to God</note>. Rabbi Yose opened and said:
> And they forsook the Lord and served Baal and the Ashtaroth. <note>Judges 2:13</note>

What is "and they forsook"? They abandoned the Holy Covenant. They would perform the circumcision but not the uncovering <note><term>Priah</term>: the second stage of ritual circumcision</note>, until Deborah came and mentioned this and the restoration, as it is written:
> When the locks are long in Israel <note>or: "When the breaches are breached"</note>, when the people willingly offer themselves, bless the Lord. <note>Judges 5:2</note>

One who kills his children—that is, when his wife is pregnant and he causes the killing of the fetus in her womb—he destroys the building of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His craftsmanship. There is no one who kills a man whose killing is as severe as this; he commits three evils that the whole world cannot endure, and because of this the world gradually dissolves without knowing why. The Holy One, Blessed be He, departs from the world, and sword, famine, and pestilence come upon the world. These are the ones: he kills his children, he destroys the King's building, and he causes the Holy Spirit to wander through the world without finding rest. Because of this, the Holy Spirit weeps.
And a nation that is judged by all these kinds [of punishments]—woe to that man, woe to him! It would be better for him had he never been created in the world. Happy are Israel, for even though they were in the Egyptian exile, they guarded themselves from all these three: from impurity, from the daughter of a foreign god, and from killing the seed <note>abortion/wasting seed</note>, and they were found in "fruiting and multiplying." For even though the Dragon <note>Pharaoh</note> decreed:
> Every son that is born you shall cast into the river. <note>Exodus 1:22</note>

There was not found among Israel one who killed the fetus in the woman's womb. All the more so after they merited to leave the exile. From here Rabbi Hiyya taught what is written...

# These are the Names

As it is written <note>1 Samuel 14:32</note> **"And the people flew upon the spoil,"** and it is like a sin-offering, like the royalty of the altars. Why did they merit this? Because they guarded themselves in the Egyptian exile, and after they were purified, they came adorned and crowned like a king in their ascents, awakening within them <term>fruitfulness and multiplication</term> <note>Hebrew: Piryah ve-Rivyah; the first commandment to procreate, here used mystically</note>. The plague of the firstborn, as it is written <note>Exodus 12:41</note> **"And all the hosts of the Lord went out,"** etc. And it is written <note>Psalms 122:4</note> **"Whither the tribes went up, even the tribes of the Lord, as a testimony unto Israel,"** truly a testimony for Israel. **"And these are the names of the children of Israel."** The tribes of the children of Israel. Mentioning the children of Israel—one might say, is it not written "and with signs they are quickly from my lamps"? This is certainly one branch, and the verse publicizes it as it is written, "and he is the son of Chish from Kariosas," see Shelomith the daughter of Dibri of the tribe of Dan. Fruitfulness and multiplication, as it is written <note>Exodus 1:7</note> **"And the children of Israel were fruitful and increased abundantly,"** etc. And from all this they guarded themselves; Israel, like Israel ascended, etc. Israel sufficed, and then: "And these are the names of the children of Israel," etc.

->**And these** are the names of the children of Israel.<-

Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Yose were walking on the road. While they were walking, Rabbi Eleazar said to Rabbi Yose: "Open your mouth and let your words shine forth." He said to him: "It is pleasing before my master that I have observed one matter that is difficult for me. I heard from the Holy Assembly <note>The circle of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> that he said: **'And these are the names of the children of Israel'**—these are certainly all those hosts and camps that descended to go down with Jacob, as it is written **'with Jacob.'** What is the meaning of what is written: <term>each man and his household came</term>? He said to him: "It is certainly so. But come and see: everyone who receives from below, his 'house' is the vessel for that which he gives, and regarding this, 'each man and his household came.'"

Rabbi Eleazar opened and said: <note>1 Kings 9:1</note> **"And it came to pass, when Solomon had finished building the house of the Lord, and the king’s house,"** etc. Since it says "the house of the Lord," why does it then say "and the king’s house"? Because of Solomon it was said thus. Rather, "the house of the Lord" refers to the <term>Holy Temple</term> <note>Beit Ha-Mikdash</note>. "And the king’s house" refers to the <term>Holy of Holies</term> <note>Kodesh Ha-Kodashim</note>. The "House of the Lord" which is the Temple refers to the courtyards, the chambers, and the outer areas; this is called the House of the Lord. The "King’s House" is the Holy of Holies, which is the innermost of all. "The King," mentioned plainly, refers to the <term>Supernal King</term> <note>Melech Ila'ah; a high level of Divine emanation</note>, for the Supernal King is feminine in relation to the Supernal Point which is hidden from all. And even though it is feminine [in that context], it is masculine in relation to the lower king. And because of this, everything follows this pattern, and regarding the repairs of the spirit, it is written: **"Each man and his household came."**

->**And these** are the names.<-

Rabbi Eleazar opened and said: <note>Song of Songs 4:12</note> **"A garden locked is my sister, my bride; a spring locked, a fountain sealed."** "A garden locked"—this is the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>Knesset Yisrael; the mystical personification of the Jewish people and the Shekhinah</note>, which is a locked garden. For Rabbi Eleazar said: Just as this garden needs guarding and cleaning, so the Assembly of Israel needs guarding and watering and the tending of a garden and the tending of a vineyard. Just as this vineyard needs guarding and watering and digging, so too Israel, as it is written <note>Isaiah 5:7</note> **"For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel."** And it is written <note>Isaiah 5:2</note> **"And he fenced it, and gathered out the stones thereof,"** etc.

->**Addendum (Tosefta)**<-

**Mishnah:** Rabbi Shimon said: These upper gates see the flowing of the <term>Holy Chariot</term> <note>Rechiva Kadisha; the Divine vehicle in Ezekiel's vision</note>. They travel in their journeys and the sound of song reaches the kings; it enters the heart, ascending and descending, moving like dew that saves thousands and tens of thousands of times. They open the song from below to above like the pleasantness of the voice of those who stand. They gather in an assembly for the rain of the right side, looking out and observing thousands of "masters of eyes" <note>Angelic beings</note> who see and yet do not see. They stand in their positions. Two other sides were appointed <margin>(variant: prepared)</margin> because of them. And for the rain of the left side, they see and observe thousands. They wait for the nursing, weeping and wailing; the house of their resting place is moved. They open with a blessing and conclude with purity. They weep because of them, and the blessing sits, and the sapphires are opened. At the time of the hour, the Master of Judgment divides what is before them and sits on the Throne of Judgment, and the song is silenced... the masters of eyes see the right side and the depths...

->**And These Are The Names**<-

Come and see: sixty thousand <note>The number 600,000 is often used in Jewish mysticism to represent the totality of the souls of Israel</note> surrounding, sounding the blast and not ceasing (other versions: not extinguished); they open the gates and announce whoever goes and hastens. Thousands are masters of the alarm-blast; they sound the blasts and do not cease (other versions: do not extinguish). A wick of fire from the side of the dregs sits upon the Throne of the Feminine. At that time, He would mention His holy, supernal Name, the secret of the names that guide life for all. He opened and said: "Sanctuary of the King, royal city, arise and depart from the midst of the upheaval; you have dwelt long enough in the valley of weeping, and He will have compassion upon you with mercy." <note>This is a quote from the liturgical poem *Lecha Dodi*, though here used in a mystical context regarding the Shekhinah's exile</note> When the holy wheels first shine, thousands and tens of thousands and masters of the gates praise and say: "Blessed is the glory of the Lord" <note>original: *Baruch Yekara d'Adonai*</note> from the place of His dwelling below. That river of hidden purity in the word, and seventy worlds surround it; the glory of its radiance goes out from the heavens to its radiance, and the radiance includes and stirs all sides... The Shekhinah opened in that hidden place, the Patron of all, and mentions the Name Y-A-W L-H and Ch-Y and L-H <note>Mystical permutations of Divine Names</note>, and they all open in the furrows of Michael, the Angel of Mercy. Who has seen all these mighty ones? The mercies of the worlds are the strongest of the strong, holy chariots... they praise the Holy Name and sanctify the arrangement. And all of them are for you, like the hour of the righteous to be established in that world...

## Main Text (Zohar)

**Rabbi Shimon said:** When the Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</note> descended to Egypt, a "Living Being" <note>original: *Chayah* - a high-ranking angel</note> named "Israel" descended, in the likeness of that Elder <note>Jacob/Israel</note>. And forty-two <note>The text reads "fifteen and two" or "sixty-two" depending on the variant, but often refers to the 42-letter Name</note> holy sides were with him, and each and every one had a holy seal. And all of them descended with Jacob to Egypt. This is what is written: <note>Exodus 1:1</note> **"And these are the names of the children of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob."**

Rabbi Yitzhak said: The verse implies "the children of Israel" and afterwards "with Jacob," which is not as we have learned. Rabbi Yehuda asked Rabbi Eleazar about this. He said to him: Since you have heard the sound of the hoofbeats of the image... he said to him: "And he called out in a loud voice." He said to him: That word which he spoke, the wise ones were licking it up <note>A metaphor for absorbing deep wisdom</note> above and below... This is what is written: "The Living Being and their life-force."

Rabbi Yitzhak was standing before Rabbi Eleazar. He said to him: The Shekhinah descended to Egypt, as it is written: <note>Genesis 46:4</note> **"I will go down with you [to Egypt]."** He said to him: Come and see, the Shekhinah descended to Egypt, and with her sixty thousand <note>original: *shis ribo*</note> holy chariots <term>Rethikin: celestial vehicles or angelic entourages</term> as companions. And these are what is written... sixty thousand holy chariots descended with Jacob to Egypt, and all of them ascended from there when Israel went out of Egypt. This is what is written: <note>Exodus 12:37</note> **"And the children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand..."** Not just as a number, but as the "six hundred thousand" [chariots]. Just as these [the angels] went out, so these [the Israelites] went out. And come see the secret of the matter: when these holy chariots went out from the holy assembly from among Israel, they knew that their children would be delayed... and this is what is written: <note>Exodus 12:39</note> **"And they could not tarry."** It should have said "they did not *want* to tarry," but it says "they *could not*."

And it is known that all the children of Israel were like the "Israel" of the Firmament <note>The celestial archetype of the nation</note>. And this is what is written: **"The children of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob."** And regarding this: **"And these are the names of the children of Israel who came to Egypt."** It is an argument from minor to major <note>original: *Kal V'Chomer*</note>: If when Jacob went to Laban it is written: <note>Genesis 32:2</note> **"And Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him,"** how much more so when he descended into exile and the Almighty had said: **"I will go down with you to Egypt."**

## And These Are the Names

It was not alone, or in a mundane or empty fashion, that they descended; rather, His supports <note>The divine powers or angels</note> descended with them. This is what is written: "...into Egypt with Jacob." Rabbi Jacob of Kfar Hanan said in the name of Rabbi Abba: Who are these "Children of Israel"? For they are indeed called the literal Children of Israel. Rabbi Abba opened his discourse and said: "Come, behold the works of the Lord, who has made desolations in the earth" <note>Psalm 46:9</note>. Do not read "desolations" (*shammot*) but rather "names" (*shemot*). And regarding this, Rabbi Hiyya said: For the sake of the heavens, the Holy One, blessed be He, acted upon the earth. Just as there are holy names in the heavens, there are holy names on the earth. Rabbi Judah said: On that day when Jacob descended to Egypt, myriads of high angels descended with him. Rabbi Judah opened with the verse: "Behold the bed of Solomon, sixty mighty men are around it..." <note>Song of Songs 3:7</note>. These are the commanders engraved in the firmaments <note>original: *kanditin/kalditin* - celestial spheres or ornaments</note>, stationed in their places, commanders in the celestial order <note>original: *stieusa*</note> engraved as it is presented here. He interprets "sixty mighty men are around it" as the "bed" which refers to the Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence, often symbolized as a feminine receptacle or "bed"</note>. "Of Solomon" refers to the King to whom peace belongs <note>A common Zoharic wordplay: *Shlomo* (Solomon) relates to *Shalom* (Peace)</note>. The "sixty mighty men around it" are the sixty myriads of high angels who reflect the strength of the Shekhinah that descended with Jacob into Egypt. "From the mighty of Israel"—this refers to the Israel Above <note>The spiritual archetype of Jacob/Israel</note>. Here he interprets that the names of the Children of Israel, the members of his household, all came, as we have seen, according to their heavenly ranks.

Rabbi Hiyya was traveling from Haifa to Lod, riding on a donkey, and Rabbi Jose was with him. Rabbi Hiyya leaned his hand upon Rabbi Jose and said: I know the resting place of Jacob at the time when the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, "I will go down with you to Egypt" <note>Genesis 46:4</note>. There were angels of the dust <note>earthly messengers</note> for three parasangs near his grave, for so the great masters of the world from the back of the Academy <note>term for the scholars of the Yeshiva</note> explained it. It is written: "And the angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, moved..." <note>Exodus 14:19</note>. He came, and there came with him the "Back" <note>a mystical level of emanation</note>, and the libations reached him. The heads of the fathers and the "Evening Assembly" <note>Knesset Yisrael/Shekhinah</note> went out with them, and it was arranged that all of Israel went out toward them. Who is the "Camp of Israel" that goes out and does not depart? For Aaron and the princes who go out and do not depart, it is found that the children of the "Staff" <note>the tribe or lineage</note> all went out. And if the children of the Staff are thus, how much more so for the Holy One, blessed be He, when He said, "I will go down with you to Egypt."

While they were walking, they encountered Rabbi Abba. He said to him: Today the Shekhinah is here, for one of the members of the Academy is with you. He said to him: Abba, in their partitions and their paths they call out, as it is written: "I will go down with you to Egypt," etc. The entire descent of Jacob to Egypt is as it is written: "And these are the names of the children of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob," for they all descended with Jacob to Egypt. Rabbi Abba said to him: And it was not only then. He opened and said: "The word of the Lord came expressly unto Ezekiel the son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar..." <note>Ezekiel 1:3</note>. There are three difficulties here: One, that we have learned that the Shekhinah does not dwell outside of the Land of Israel. Second, that he [Ezekiel] was not as faithful as the "Staff" <note>Moses</note>, of whom it is written "In all My house he is faithful," yet he revealed and publicized all the hidden things of the King. And third, that he saw in a vision that which was not according to his own mind. Rather, thus we have established in our Academy: that Ezekiel was a complete prophet, and by the permission of the Holy One, blessed be He, he revealed all that he revealed, and it was all necessary to reveal and publicize. For we have learned: one who is accustomed to bearing a burden, etc. And all was necessary, for the Holy One, blessed be He, never leaves Israel in exile until He comes to dwell with them. Just as it was with Jacob who was in exile, the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah, and the high and low holy ones, and all the Chariots <note>Divine vehicles/angels</note> were with Jacob. Here he interprets "who came to Egypt with Jacob."

Another matter: Rabbi Abba opened and said: "Come, come, your King..." Rabbi Isaac said: Woe to the people who do not know and do not observe the service of their Master! For Rabbi Isaac saw that every single day a Heavenly Voice <note>Bat Kol</note> goes out from Mount Korchakhan: "Woe to the people for neglecting the service of their Master! Woe to the people for the insult to the Torah!"

## Main Text (The Zohar)

Regarding the Torah <note>original: *Oraita*</note>, Rabbi Yehuda said: Anyone who exerts themselves in the study of Torah in this world and gathers good deeds inherits the world of worlds. But anyone who does not exert themselves in the Torah in this world and does not perform good deeds inherits neither this world nor the next. Come and see: there is no dwelling place inherited in the world except according to one's station and what is fitting for them. Rabbi Isaac said: Come and see that there is no one who lacks good deeds entirely. Rabbi Yehuda said: If human beings only knew the love with which the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: *Kudosha Brich Hu*</note>, loves Israel, they would roar like young lions to pursue Him. At the hour when Jacob entered Egypt, the Holy One called to His heavenly retinue and said to them: "All of you, descend to Egypt and behold the life of My children." The Divine Presence <note>original: *Shekhinah*, the feminine indwelling aspect of God</note>, the Matriarch of the world, saw her children without a King. He said to her: "Come with Me, My bride <note>original: *Kallah*</note>, with your children, the doe of Eden, for the King is in all His works." This "bride" is the *Shekhinah*, who is like a bride under a wedding canopy. For it was taught that Rabbi Yehuda said: What is the meaning of that which is written:
> "With me from Lebanon, my bride, with me from Lebanon you shall come; you shall look from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon..." (Song of Songs 4:8)
This refers to the Bride. "With me from Lebanon you shall come"—from Lebanon, which is the Supernal Holy Temple. "You shall look from the top of Amana"—this refers to the heights of the mountains from which the faithful look out, and where were they? With Jacob and his sons. "From the top of Senir and Hermon"—for they were destined to receive My Torah from Mount Hermon and to be protected <note>original: *le-nabacha*, to be shielded or barked over like a guard dog</note> during their exile. "From the dens of lions"—these are the mighty ones who are like lions, who look over them in all their labors. Rabbi Hasa said: "With me from Lebanon, my bride..."—is the King below while Lebanon is above? Hasa said to him: At the time the *Shekhinah* descended to Egypt, the Holy One spared His holiness, as we learned that the ministering angels went first, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, preceded them all, as it says, "And their King shall pass before them, and the Lord at their head" <note>Micah 2:13</note>. Rabbi Isaac said: "With me from Lebanon, my bride"—this is the *Shekhinah*. "With me from Lebanon you shall come"—from the Supernal Holy Temple. "You shall look from the top of Amana"—from Lebanon, which is the Supernal Temple, and it is also said to be the Temple below. And Rabbi Yehuda said: The *Shekhinah* has never moved from the Western Wall of the Holy Temple, as it is written:
> "Behold, he stands behind our wall" (Song of Songs 2:9)
And its power hovers over the whole world. "From the top of Senir and Hermon"—from Lebanon the Torah went out to the world to protect Israel. "From the dens of lions"—these are the mighty ones. Rabbi Yudan says: "From the dens of lions"—these are the Torah scholars <note>term: *Talmidei Chachamim* (Disciples of the Wise)</note> who occupy themselves with the Torah in the study halls and synagogues, who are like lions and masters of the Torah. Little Rabbi Hiyya sat before the Rav and asked: What is the meaning of "lions' dens" in relation to the sons of Jacob? First there were twelve, and later seventy, as it is written:
> "All the souls of the house of Jacob who came to Egypt were seventy" (Genesis 46:27)
Exactly seventy and no more. He said to him: This corresponds to the seventy nations that are in the world, and they [Israel] were the wine and the essence compared to all of them. Furthermore, he said: Come and see, there are spiritual "husks" <note>term: *Kelipot* (shards or shells of impurity)</note> that appear as mighty men, appointed over the seventy nations, and they emerge from twelve engraved boundaries that surround the Matron <note>The *Shekhinah*</note> to establish her toward the four directions of the holy world, to count the children of Israel. And this is what is written:
> "For I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven" (Zechariah 2:10)
This teaches that they stand for the sake of Israel like the four winds; just as the world cannot exist without the four winds, so too the world cannot exist without Israel.

**And there arose** a new king... Rabbi Hezekiah opened his discourse: "I will mention the lovingkindnesses of the Lord, according to all that the Lord has bestowed on us, and the great goodness toward the house of Israel" <note>Isaiah 63:7</note>, as it is written, "And the Lord has chosen you to be a peculiar people unto Himself" <note>Deuteronomy 14:2</note>, and it is written, "For the Lord's portion is His people; Jacob is the lot of His inheritance" <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>. And Israel cleaves to Him, to the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: "But you that did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day" <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>.

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Book of Exodus (Shemot) in the Zohar. It establishes the spiritual mechanics of the Egyptian exile, focusing on the balance between the "Palace of Merit" and the "Other Side."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And these are the names**<-

In this manner, the righteous are fortunate before Him because they know how to sow upon all waters, as it is written: *Happy are you who sow beside all waters* <note>Isaiah 32:20</note>. This refers to those who sow for the sake of charity <note>The Hebrew word for "charity," Tzedakah, is linked here to the act of sowing spiritual seeds</note>. And regarding one who sows for charity, it is written: *For Your kindness is great above the heavens* <note>Psalms 108:5</note>. "Beside all waters" refers to Your kindness, which is the kindness "above the heavens"—this is the World to Come—and he sows upon all waters. In the book of **Rav Yeba the Elder**, he said as follows: It is written, *The matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the request by the word of the holy ones* <note>Daniel 4:14</note>. All merits in this world, and all decrees and all requests, all stand in a single Palace where the Sanhedrin <note>The supreme celestial court of seventy-one sages</note> sit and deliberate on the judgments of the world. And this Palace is called the **Palace of Merit** <term>Heikhala de-Zakhuta: The celestial courtroom where human actions are judged favorably</term>, because when they judge a case, they first turn toward the merit of a person. This is not the case in that level of the **Other Side** <term>Sitra Achra: The realm of evil or "dark" spiritual forces</term>, for there is a place called "Guilt." This is because all the works of that place—of which it is written **the woman of harlotry** <note>referring to the personification of the seductive, destructive force</note>—are dedicated to turning a person’s deeds toward guilt and leading their actions into sin. Those of the Palace of Merit are like sweet waters, clear waters. But those of the Palace of Guilt belong to the darkness; they are called bitter waters, *the bitter waters that bring a curse*. In that Palace of Merit, these three things do not depend on merit: children, life, and sustenance <note>A famous Talmudic dictum: these three depend on "Mazal" (destiny/constellation) rather than personal merit</note>. And for them, in that place of Guilt, it is not written that they are sweet and clear, but rather like bitter, cursing waters. Therefore, it says "you who sow beside all waters"—the holy seed to give birth beside all waters of life, for the repair of the seed of all of them is only found Above.

The matter depends on the holy "Mazal" <note>The celestial flow or "destiny" emanating from the highest levels of the Divine</note> regarding all the waters of life. They are "sending forth the feet of the ox and the donkey" <note>Isaiah 32:20</note>, meaning they have no part in that evil side at all. They darken and direct all evil worship and are purified from that side, for all holiness is upon them. When the **ox and the donkey** are joined together, they are two evil plagues to the world. The ox comes from the side of the holy living creature, the side of holiness. The donkey, when it joins with the "shells" <note>Kelipot: the husks of impurity</term> of the Other Side, these two are evil plagues to the world.

Because of this, Simeon was the strength of harsh judgment, and when they were born together, the world could not endure it. For this reason, it is written: *You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together* <note>Deuteronomy 22:10</note>. Jacob explained this matter to his son, as it is written: *I have acquired an ox and a donkey* <note>Genesis 32:6</note>. And he lived in fear, for Jacob was greatly afraid of the deception involved. 

*Now there arose a new king over Egypt* <note>Exodus 1:8</note>. In the book of **Rav Hamnuna the Elder**, it was said: What is the meaning of "there arose a new king over Egypt"? Come and see: all the nations of the world and all the kings of the world were only strengthened in their rule because of Israel. Egypt did not rule over the whole world until Israel arrived and entered there into exile; then they were strengthened over the other nations of the world. All of them are strengthened over the nations only so that Israel may be in their exile. Edom was not strengthened over all the nations of the world except because of Israel, for at the end of their exile, these nations were insignificant like other nations and were the lowest of all. But because of Israel, they were strengthened. Regarding Egypt, it is written *from the house of slaves* <note>Exodus 20:2</note>—they were called slaves because Egypt was as insignificant as the rest of the nations. Regarding Babylon, it is written: *Behold the land of the Chaldeans; this people was not* <note>Isaiah 23:13</note>. Regarding Edom, it is written: *Behold, I have made you small among the nations; you are greatly despised* <note>Obadiah 1:2</note>. None of them had strength except because of Israel. For when Israel is in their exile, the nations return to being strengthened over all other nations of the world. Why? Because Israel alone stands against all the nations of the world. When Israel went down into the exile of Egypt, immediately there was a "rising" for Egypt, and their dominion was strengthened Above over all other nations, as it is written: *Now there arose a new king over Egypt*. "There arose" means there was a rising for them to be strengthened; that level of the celestial minister of Egypt arose, and strength and dominion were given to him over all other nations, for previously that level Above had no dominion. And afterwards, this was reflected in the people below...

<summary>This page introduces the spiritual dynamics of the Egyptian exile, explaining that the rise of worldly empires like Egypt, Babylon, and Edom is supernaturally tied to the exile of Israel. It also contrasts the "Palace of Merit," which seeks to justify humanity, with the "Other Side," which seeks to find guilt.</summary>

Rabbi Isaac said: When the Holy One, Blessed Be He, brings judgment upon a nation, He first executes judgment upon that Minister <note>the celestial angel/patron</note> who is appointed over them above, as it is written: **"The Lord shall punish the host of the high heaven on high, and the kings of the earth upon the earth"** <note>Isaiah 24:21</note>. The judgment descends to judge that Minister above. They remove his throne, and the crown of memory is moved and goes out, and then his dominion is removed. And immediately it is proclaimed in the firmament: "The dominion of so-and-so has been removed from him!"

## Main Text (Zohar)

Until that voice reaches all those firmaments, until it reaches those authorities appointed over this world; and a voice goes out and proclaims throughout the whole world until it reaches the birds and the sparks and those forms of human beings who do not know.

**And there arose** a new king—Rabbi Hiyya said: He was literally a new king, for previously he had issued decrees that no other king had issued before him. Rabbi Yose said to him: But have we not learned that all that goodness which Joseph performed was as one with his master, as it is written <note>Genesis 47:14</note> *“And Joseph gathered all the money... into Pharaoh’s house”*? And he kept them all in a storehouse <margin>in a storehouse</margin> because he remembered [the debt], yet he made himself as if he did not know him <note>Referring to the new king "not knowing Joseph."</note>. Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Yehuda were sitting and laboring in the Torah before Rabbi Shimon. Rabbi Yehuda said: This which is written, *“And there arose a new king over Egypt,”* we have learned that this one "arose" of his own accord; he who was previously insignificant arose, though he was not fit for kingship, yet he strove and arose. Rabbi Shimon said: All of them are like the pattern of those who sinned, who were not fit for sovereignty but rose up of their own accord, and now they are purified and removed from the world. So too here, this one was not fit for a king but rose of his own accord, and he merited to be removed from the world, as it is written <note>Exodus 1:9-10</note> *“And he said to his people... come, let us deal wisely with them.”* And when a king arose above <note>A spiritual chieftain or angel of Egypt</note>, a king arose below. He opened and said: <note>Isaiah 19:1</note> *“The burden of Egypt: Behold, the Lord rides upon a swift cloud and shall come into Egypt; and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at His presence.”*

Come and see: all the kings of the world and all the nations of the world are considered as nothing before the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written <note>Daniel 4:32</note> *“And all the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing; and He does according to His will in the army of heaven.”* And here in Egypt, even though all those powers and exalted <term>levels (Dargin)</term> <note>Spiritual ranks or emanations</note> were before the Holy One, Blessed be He, regarding Egypt what is written? *“Behold, the Lord rides upon a swift cloud and shall come into Egypt.”* Why did Egypt merit this above all nations of the world—that the Holy One, Blessed be He, should be enslaved, as it were, and be under a canopy below with them? For it is written, *“And I will pass through the land of Egypt.”* This is the Lord Himself! It was only because the King <note>The Holy One</note> comes to the field for the sake of the <term>Matronita (The Queen/Shekhinah)</term> <note>The feminine aspect of the Divine who dwells with Israel in exile</term> who was there. And for the sake of the honor of the Matronita, He came.

And because of this, the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired her honor and came down to her to raise her up and to establish her month, just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to do at the end of the <term>Exile (Galuta)</term> of Edom <note>The current exile, often identified with Rome/Western Christendom</note>. Rabbi Yose said: If so, that it was for the sake of the Matronita that it was thus in the exile [of Egypt], in every exile where the Matronita is present, why is it not so? Rather, we have learned that the <term>Shekhinah (Divine Presence)</term> is in exile within six crowns, and at times the Holy <term>Covenant (Berit Kayama)</term> is like a free man. Because of this, they are seized from here, hidden and below, to be seen to do for them what was not the case in the exile of Egypt; for all of them were holy tribes, the Assembly of Israel above. When Israel goes out into the exile of Edom, the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires to be honored in the world and to come to raise the Matronita and to shake her from her dust. Woe to whoever happens to be there before Him, like the tossing of the sea! <note>Isaiah 52:2</note> *“Shake yourself from the dust; arise, and sit down, O Jerusalem; loose yourself from the bands of your neck.”* From where shall the King and the people arise before Him? *“And the idols of Egypt shall be moved at His presence.”* The "idols of Egypt" does not refer to the wise men and sorcerers, but to all those levels appointed over them and over those lower authorities of theirs.

And in every place where Israel dwells, the Shekhinah seeks them out to receive them from those nations. What is written? <note>Isaiah 52:4</note> *“For thus says the Lord God: My people went down aforetime into Egypt to sojourn there; and the Assyrian oppressed them without cause.”* This is a complaint that the Holy One, Blessed be He, spoke concerning Assyria. He said: See what Assyria did to Me! For as for Egypt, though I performed all those judgments upon them, My people stayed there to dwell among them, and they [the Egyptians] received them of their own accord and gave them the best of the land, the land of Goshen. They did not act to distress them in the exile; they did not act with evil toward them, as it is written <note>Exodus 8:18</note> *“Only in the land of Goshen, where My people are...”* and the best of the land of Egypt it was, as it is written <note>Genesis 47:6</note> *“In the best of the land make your father and brethren to dwell.”* And they did not take anything from them, as it is written, *“And of the cattle of the children of Israel [not one died].”* And afterwards they were scoured with many judgments. But Assyria "oppressed them without cause"—he cast them out...

"If a bird's nest chances to be before you on the road, in any tree or on the ground, with fledglings or eggs, and the mother is sitting upon them... you shall surely let the mother go." <note>Deuteronomy 22:6</note> We have established this verse, and it is one of the hidden commandments of the Torah. They are life for us within the hidden longings of the Torah, concealed and hinted at among the companions; all of them hang upon and are tied to the entirety of the Torah. Rabbi Shimon said to Rabbi Elazar his son: "Elazar, at the time when the King Messiah awakens, how many signs and supports will awaken in the world!" Come and see: in the Garden of Eden below, there is one hidden and secret place that is unknown, and it is embroidered with many colors. Within it are hidden a thousand palaces of longing, and no one enters them except for the Messiah, who stands continually in the Garden of Eden. And the entire Garden is surrounded by the crowns of the righteous, and the Messiah stands over many matters and oversees the righteous in the Garden and their mercies and merits. In that place below, within all those palaces, they dwell. Within all those palaces, there is one place, hidden and secret, which is not known at all and is called "Eden," and no one knows of it. And the Messiah is close <margin>Variant: to be revealed</margin> outside of the Chariot <term>Merkavah; the divine assembly or vehicle</term> of that place, until a place called the "Bird's Nest" is revealed to him. This is the place where the herald calls out concerning that Eagle <note>The "Eagle" here refers to a celestial awakening or a specific angelic force</note> that awakens in the Garden of Eden every day. In that place, the images of all the other nations who gathered against Israel to do them evil are embroidered. He enters that place, lifts his eyes, and sees the Patriarchs who entered the destruction of the House of God <note>The Holy Temple in Jerusalem</note>, until he sees Rachel with her tears upon her cloak. The Holy One, Blessed be He, comforts her, but she refuses to accept comforts. Then the Messiah raises his voice and weeps, and the entire Garden of Eden and all those righteous ones who are there cry out and weep with him. They cry out and weep a second time, and that firmament above the Garden trembles—one million two hundred thousand upper hosts—until it reaches the Supernal Throne. Then the Holy One, Blessed be He, signals to that Eagle, and his nest trembles, and he gathers toward the Messiah and calls what he calls and awakens what he awakens. Until from within the Holy Throne, that Bird's Nest is called three times, and the Messiah ascends on high. The Holy One, Blessed be He, sees him and swears to remove the other kingdom <term>Sitra Achra; the "Other Side" or forces of evil/exile</term> from the world by the hand of the Messiah, and to take the vengeance of Israel, and all those benefits that the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to do for His people. Then that Bird's Nest and the Messiah return to their place. The Messiah returns and is hidden within that place as before.

And at the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, awakens to repair the worlds in perfection, the letters of the Name <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> will all be repaired to be as they should be in one vision. Then a single star will awaken in the middle of the firmament, the color of glowing purple, and it will sparkle in the day before the eyes of the whole world. A flame of fire will rise from the north side within the firmament, and this shall stand opposite that for forty days, and all the inhabitants of the world will be terrified. At the end of forty days, the star and the flame shall do battle before the eyes of all, and that flame shall spread with a burning of fire from the north side within the firmament and think to swallow that star. And many rulers, kings, nations, and peoples will be terrified by this. Then that star will move to the south side and rule over that flame, and the flame will be swallowed little by little in the firmament before that star until it is not seen at all. Then that star will make its paths in the firmament for twelve days. After twelve days, all the inhabitants of the world will tremble, and the sun will be darkened at midday, just as the day was darkened when the Holy Temple was destroyed, until heaven and earth cannot be seen. And a voice will awaken with thunder and lightning, and the earth shall quake from that voice, and many hosts and legions shall die from the force of it. And on that very day, a flame of fire shall awaken in the great city of Rome <note>Symbolizing the seat of the exile</note>, and that voice shall awaken throughout the entire world.

For the Supernal Light was the light and radiance below, but since they sinned and were banished, and the kingdom of Babylon ruled, that light was covered and darkened. That radiance departed, and that Supernal Spring, which was the source of the Spirit, ascended higher and higher to the Infinite. Then those seventy years were not shining like that radiance that was heard, and the exile of seventy years was pushed away. Once the dominion of Babylon was removed and all were banished, they did not return to find or see the treasure of the bundle as before, but only little by little in confusion. And then, when they finished, it was not found, and the woman, the Assembly <note>Knesset Israel/Shekhinah</note>, labored below. Then the Supernal Subjugation descended, not with all the strength to break through as it was before, but little by little in confusion. And they were not shining as is fitting. And because of this, the Supernal Subjugation was not, as it were, a radiance, but rather to return and join little by little from the staff of the Name. And this "He ascended" was illuminated in them, for Israel draws near to the thorns until it strengthens and covers the heat. And they were seen in exile in all those twelve tribes, and they burdened them. <meta>This page begins the Book of Exodus (Shemot). It follows the conclusion of Genesis, transitioning from the patriarchal narratives to the themes of exile and the spiritual mechanics of divine justice. The text focuses on the concept of "Vanity" (Hevel) and why the righteous suffer while the wicked prosper.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **And these are the names** <-
<note>original: "Ve-eleh Shemot" — the opening words of the Book of Exodus.</note>

Come and see why this section is different: for the darkness of the night was separated from the light of the day until they were walking in the light, and then the time of exile arrived. Rabbi Eleazar saw that the matters of exile had departed, and they contemplated them; afterward, they rose and went on their way. Rabbi Eleazar opened his discourse and said:
> "There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there be righteous men, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there be wicked men, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also is vanity." (Ecclesiastes 8:14)

This verse has been established and sealed. However, regarding this "vanity," King Solomon addressed them all, and we have established that the world stands upon seven "vanities" <note>The Hebrew word 'Hevel' means vanity, but also breath or vapor. The Zohar treats these as the spiritual foundations of the universe.</note>, and these are the seven pillars that support the world, corresponding to the seven firmaments. And these [firmaments] are: *Vilon, Rakia, Shechakim, Zevul, Ma'on, Machon, and Aravot.* And in the tradition of all "vanity" mentioned in Ecclesiastes, it says that all vanities are a "vanity of vanities," just as there are seven firmaments, there are others that are finer than them, which spread out and emerge from them. So too, there are other "vanities" that spread out and emerge from these, and Solomon spoke of all of them, for the "breath" <gloss>vanity</gloss> of wisdom is within it.

There is a "vanity" that emerges from those upper vanities upon which the world stands, and this is "done upon the earth," and it is strengthened in its existence and strengthened in its power like the deeds of the wicked. And in the ascent that rises from the earth, this is done upon the earth, and all its strength and existence are like those souls of the righteous who are removed from the earth while they are still meritorious, before they have labored [in sin], while they still give off a good fragrance. Such was Enoch, of whom it is written:
> "And he was not; for God took him." (Genesis 5:24)

He [God] took him before his time arrived, and this was done to him. And so it is with the other righteous of the world who are taken for two reasons: the righteous are removed from the world before their time arrives, first, because of the sins of the generation. For when the sinners are found in the world, the righteous who are found among them are seized for their sins. And immediately, when it is revealed before the Holy One, Blessed Be He, that they might turn to evil later, He raises them from the world before their time arrives. This is what is written: "there be righteous men, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked," because He saw that above it is as if they had committed the sins and deeds of the wicked <note>Meaning, God foresees potential future sins and takes them while they are still pure.</note>. For Rabbi Yose asked: when Jacob said "I have been small" <note>original: "Katonti"</note>, did they merit in the time of Rabbi Akiva and his companions who were removed from the world and died? And in that same manner, Rabbi Meir? Is this written in the whole Torah? Heaven forbid! Rather, Solomon said: "there be righteous men, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked."

And there are wicked men to whom it happens according to the work of the righteous: they sit in tranquility and goodness as if the suffering of the world does not reach them, as if they performed the deeds of the righteous. But this is because it is revealed before the Holy One, Blessed Be He, that they will eventually return in repentance, or that a righteous seed will come from them into the world—such as Terah, from whom came the righteous seed of Abraham, or Ahaz, from whom came Hezekiah, and other sinners of the world. And because of this, on this side and on that side, the "vanity" of which we spoke is "done" and strengthened upon the earth as we have said.

Come and see: "There is a vanity which is done upon the earth," as we said, which is strengthened over the world because "there be righteous men, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked." There reaches them those deeds of the guilty, such as those who hold onto deeds that are slightly wicked, yet they stand before those who blaspheme and do not desire rest at all. Like many righteous of truth to whose hands come such deeds, and they are "mighty in strength" who do the will of their Master and do not sin. And because of this, "all is done upon the earth" and strengthened in its power.

"And there be wicked men, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous." There reaches their hand a spark of life, a deed of the righteous, and they merit in it and perform it. For example, there was a bandit who used to rob in the mountains; he found poor people there, and when he knew [their plight], he would help them pass through, protecting them and saving them from others. Rabbi Akiva would read over him: "there be wicked men, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous." And because the end proves that it was to his merit...

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic commentary on the Book of Exodus. The previous section concluded a discussion on the nature of divine justice and the balance between good and evil forces. This page transitions into the mystical interpretation of the birth of Moses.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

In its hidden mysteries, when he encountered that woman who was fit for him, his daughter, he sought to strengthen her. Her Master said to her: "Be careful of your Master and do not sin with her." He ascended and did not return to her. Come and see, it is hinted: **"There are wicked people to whom it happens according to the work of the righteous... I said that this too is vanity"** <note>Ecclesiastes 8:14</note>. Just as the Holy One associates with all these sins of the righteous who encounter the deeds of the wicked but do not sin, so too He associates with those living wicked ones who encounter the deeds of the righteous and perform them. The Holy One, blessed be He, created righteous and wicked in the world, and just as His power is glorified in the world through the deeds of the righteous, so too His power is glorified through the wicked when they perform a good deed in the world; then it is received and "beautiful in its time." Woe to those when one makes himself evil and associates with sin, for then it is said: **"Woe to the wicked, for it shall be ill with him"** <note>Isaiah 3:11</note>.

He opened again and said: **"I have seen everything in the days of my vanity"** <note>Ecclesiastes 7:15</note>. See the verse, for so it is in the wisdom of the companions. For every person, according to how the world conducts itself at the time when the Moon <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note> is needed. **"There is a righteous man who perishes"**—this is the Pillar of the World <note>The sefirah of Yesod</note>, and he perishes entirely. The Righteous One perishes at the time of exile **"in his righteousness"** <term>Tzedek: The feminine aspect of justice/Shekhinah</term>, because she is the <term>Shekhinah</term> cast to the dust. This "Righteousness" <note>Tzedek</note>, all the time she is guarded in exile, He dwells with them in exile. And because of this, the "Righteous One perishes in his righteousness," for those supernal blessings do not reach him. **"And there is a wicked man who prolongs his life in his evildoing"**—this refers to <term>Samael</term> <note>The primary figure of evil/Satan in Kabbalah</note>, who prolongs quiet and tranquility for himself alone through his evildoing. Through that "Evil" below, which is so strong, for quiet and tranquility do not reach them except because he associates with that female <note>Lilith</note>. This continues until the end of his kingdom, until the Holy One, blessed be He, raises from the dust that "fallen Tabernacle of David," as it is written: **"I will raise up the Tabernacle of David that is fallen"** <note>Amos 9:11</note>.

---

# And He Went (Vayelech)
**"And there went a man of the house of Levi"** <note>Exodus 2:1</note>. Rabbi Yose opened: **"My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices"** <note>Song of Songs 6:2</note>. "My beloved has gone down to his garden"—this is the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>Knesset Yisrael, another name for the Shekhinah</note>, for she is like a bed of spices, comprised of all the types of spices and scents of the <term>World to Come</term> <note>Alma d'Atay</note>. At the hour when the Holy One, blessed be He, descends to this garden, all those **souls of the righteous** <note>Nishmathon d'Tzaddikaya</note> who are crowned there all give off a scent. And the scent is like that of apples—these are the souls of the righteous. For behold, Isaac—all the living souls of the righteous who were in this world, and all the living souls destined to descend to this world, all of them stand within this Assembly in the Garden of Eden. They all stand in the image and form <note>Diyukna</note> in which they existed in this world. And this secret is handed over to the wise.

The spirit <note>Ruach</note> that descends to this assembly, which is from the "Female" side, is always engraved with an **engraving** <note>Galupa</note> like a **seal** <note>Chotam</note>. The form of the body of a human in this world is visible on the outside, and the spirit is joined within. When the spirit is divested from the body, that spirit is gathered into this Assembly in the exact way and image of this world, because it was always within the "seal." And regarding this it is said: **"Set me as a seal upon your heart"** <note>Song of Songs 8:6</note>. Just as a seal is engraved with an engraving on the inside and forms an image facing outward, so too is the spirit which is bound to it. In this very manner in this world, it is engraved with an engraving inside when it is divested from the body, and it returns to the Assembly where that engraving is gathered, which was formed on the outside, and it is formed in an image facing outward, like the image of the body in this world. Above, it joins with the "Living" from the strength of the "Living" that is always there above, in that same image, and it delights in the "pleasantness of the Lord," all of it to "behold the pleasantness of the Lord and to visit His Temple."

---

# And He Went (Vayelech)
**"And there went a man of the house of Levi"**. Rabbi Gabriel said: This refers to Gabriel who went and returned... **"From the house of Levi"**—this is the Assembly of Israel which comes from the side of <insert>the Left</insert> <note>The original text mentions Samael here, but the context of Levi usually refers to the Left Side of the Sephirot</note>. **"And he took a daughter of Levi"**—this is the soul that comes at the hour when the body of a righteous person is born into this world.
