## Main Text (Zohar)

The Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: *Kadosh Baruch Hu*</note>, called to Nebuchadnezzar and took that garment of the righteous which is in the Garden <note>Eden</note> and gave it to him to destroy the bodies of the righteous who were born into this world; and his embrace was appointed over it and guarded it. And if you say that this king who was placed over the heights of the righteous and learned his name, and there is no other whose embrace is suppressed—it was certainly so because he comes from the side of impurity <note>original: *sitra de-tuma*</note>, and anyone who comes from the side of impurity is called thus.

**And a man went.** This refers to Amram. **And he took a daughter of Levi.** This refers to Jochebed. A Heavenly Voice <note>original: *Bat Kol*</note> descended and said to him to mate with her, for the time of the redemption of Israel was drawing near through the son to be born from them. And the Holy One, blessed be He, assisted him, as we have learned: the Divine Presence <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note> rested upon their bed, and their will was in a single attachment <note>original: *devekuta*</note> with the Divine Presence. Because of this, the Divine Presence never departed from that son they fathered, to fulfill that which is written:
> Sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy (Leviticus 11:44)

When a person sanctifies himself from below, the Holy One, blessed be He, sanctifies him from above. Just as their will was attached to the Divine Presence, so too the Divine Presence attached itself to the very act they performed. Heaven forbid <note>that it be otherwise</note>, for the meritorious and the precise are invited, and their will is in an attachment that stands eternally; and just as they are always attached to Him, so too He is attached to them and never leaves them. Woe to the wicked whose will and attachment are distant from Him. And it is not enough that they are distant from Him, but they attach themselves to the "Other Side" <note>the realm of evil/impurity</note>. Come and see: Amram, who attached himself to the Holy One, blessed be He, produced a "fountain of the eye" <note>a metaphor for Moses</note> because the Holy One, blessed be He, never departed from him, and the Divine Presence was constantly attached to him, and all was perfected.

**And the woman conceived and bore a son, and she saw him, that he was good.** What is the meaning of "that he was good"? Rabbi Hiyya said: he was born circumcised, because the spirit of the Covenant <note>the sign of circumcision</note> is called "Good," as it is written:
> Say of the righteous that he is good (Isaiah 3:10)

Rabbi Yose said: it refers to the light of the Divine Presence that shone within him. For at the moment he was born, the entire house was filled with light, as it is written, **and she saw him, that he was good**, and it is written elsewhere:
> And God saw the light, that it was good (Genesis 1:4)

Therefore, **that he was good** and the light are one and the same. **And she hid him for three months.** Why is "three months" mentioned? Rabbi Yehuda said: it is a hint that Moses was not recognized in this world until three months had passed, as it is written, **In the third month**, for then the Torah was given through his hand, and the Divine Presence was revealed upon him before the eyes of all, as it is written:
> And Moses went up to God, and the Lord called to him (Exodus 19:3)

**And she could no longer hide him.** For until that time, the dwelling place of the Holy One, blessed be He, was not known. And it is written, **And remembrance and peace shall answer us with a voice.** She prepared for him an **ark of bulrushes**, a hint of the Ark of the Tablets which would stand within it. The "ark of bulrushes" is the Ark of the Covenant. **And she daubed it with slime and with pitch.** For that ark, which is the Ark <note>of the Covenant</note>, was plated from within and from without. Rabbi Yehuda said: this refers to the strength of the Torah, which the Holy One, blessed be He, fortified with positive commandments and negative commandments. **And she put the child in it.** These are the people of Israel, as it is written:
> For Israel is a youth, and I love him (Hosea 11:1)

**And she placed it in the reeds <note>Hebrew: *Suf*</note>.** These are the commandments of the Torah, the stringencies to be performed until the end <note>Hebrew: *Sof*</note> of the world, and Israel was to be fed at the end of forty years. **By the river's brink.** Upon the word of the Torah, for from them the Torah goes out to Israel.

### And He Went
**And a man went.** This is the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written: *The Lord is a man of war*. **From the house of Levi.** This is the Holy One, blessed be He, the place of Wisdom <note>the Sefirah of Chokhmah</note>, where the river flows and is drawn out as one, never separating. **From the house of Levi.** This refers to the "Leviathan" <note>the primordial sea monster, here a mystical symbol</note> who gives everything... the extra letter *Vav* is to erase, etc. **And he took a daughter of Levi.** This is the Holy One, blessed be He, the place of light from the side that shines.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Exodus (Shemot), specifically focusing on the infancy of Moses and the symbolic roles of the women who protected him. It connects the literal narrative to the Sefirotic realms.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

...And she opened it; so have I learned below, that before the union of the "daughter of so-and-so" with the "son of so-and-so" <note>A common Rabbinic idiom for destined marriage partners</note> occurs, the sun joins in the connection, and thus the "daughter" is considered as one degree in the embrace.

**And she hid him** for three months <note>Exodus 2:2</note>. These are the three months in which harsh Judgment <term>Midat HaDin: the divine attribute of strict justice and law</term> dwells in the world, which are the months of Tammuz, Av, and Tevet <note>Summer and winter months associated with historical tragedies in Jewish tradition</note>. What does this teach us? That before Moses descended into the world, he was present above, and the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the immanent feminine aspect of God</term> was revealed and joined with him from the day he was born. From here, **Rabbi Shimon** said: The souls of the righteous are watched over on high even before they descend into the world.

**And when she could** no longer hide him, etc. <note>Exodus 2:3</note>. What is the meaning of "she took for him an ark of bulrushes"? She protected him with a covering to endure in the mountains <note>original: "tur"</note> from the "stars" and the "waters" that strike between the Great Sea and the sea where it is written, "therein are creeping things innumerable" <note>Psalm 104:25</note>. And why did she protect him? To be a shield for them against the side of the Jubilee <term>Yovela: representing the higher world of Binah/Understanding</term> which investigates two colors, black and red <note>Symbolizing the blend of Mercy and Judgment</note>, and these were for her to plant among them, and from here she joined him to receive the desolation.

**And the daughter of Pharaoh came down** to wash at the river <note>Exodus 2:5</note>. This refers to the one who comes from the Left Side <note>The side of Gevurah/Strength and Judgment</note> of harsh Judgment; then she "comes down to wash at the river." It says specifically "at the river" and not "at the water." And if you say, "But is it not written: 'and the rod wherewith you struck the river'?" <note>Exodus 7:17</note>, yet the rod did not strike the sea, but it is called "river." Rather, the river that Aaron struck by means of the rod is changed by the verse. In this same way, the salt of the seven days of investigation struck it, and "the river" is lacking "struck it," except that because it came from the side of "Hardness," it is called "Ice" <note>original: "Kerach"</note>, and afterward it is called "Impure" like the rod. **And her maidens walked along the riverside**—these are the other appointed powers that come from this side. **And she opened it and saw him, the child, and she had compassion on him.** "She had compassion on him" <note>original: "Vatachmol"</note>—this refers to his eyes. **Rabbi** said: You have no word in the Torah that does not contain high and precious secrets. Rather, thus have I learned: that the King and the Matronita <term>Matronita: The Divine Mother/Shekhinah</term> were found in him, and they are the likeness of God, the Secret of Wisdom <term>Sodah de-Chokhmah</term>. Immediately, "she had compassion on him," etc. Up to this point refers to the upper realms; from here onward refers to the lower realms, except for this verse:

**And his sister stood afar off** etc. <note>Exodus 2:4</note>. "And his sister stood"—this refers to the sister of the one who called the Assembly of Israel <term>Knesset Yisrael: the spiritual community of Israel, often identified with the Shekhinah</term> "My sister," as in: "Open to me, my sister, my love" <note>Song of Songs 5:2</note>. "Afar off"—as in: "From afar the Lord appeared to me" <note>Jeremiah 31:2</note>. For what reason? Because they are meritorious, but in this way they are known to the world above regarding everything, and especially the Rod. And it implies that the wisdom of the righteous is extended; "his sister" rose up as we have established. And the spirit of the matter we have learned is that Father and Mother <note>Chokhmah and Binah</note> made the body on earth, and it implies that all sides, both above and below, come from Male and Female and are found there. And they established the secret of what is written: "rebuke" is lacking the "palm of the hand." This lack is the **Assembly of Israel**. "The palm of the hand"—like the palm of the First Man <note>Adam Kadmon</note> that rose up as was said. **Rabbi Abba** said: Blessed is he! He said: Certainly you have spoken well, and so it is surely. Blessed is the portion of Moses the Faithful Prophet over all the rest of the world. "And his sister stood"—this is **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah</term>, as in: "Say to Wisdom, you are my sister" <note>Proverbs 7:4</note>. **Rabbi Isaac** said: The decree of Judgment is never removed from the world, for at every hour that Israel turns away, Judgment prosecutes them, and then "his sister stands afar off"—this "afar off" is as in "From afar the Lord appeared to me."

**And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash at the river**—this corresponds to the claim that when Israel ceased from the Torah, immediately "the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash at the river." The **Attribute of Judgment** descended to strengthen itself...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And These are the Names**<-

To remove the likeness of Israel because of the grievance of the Torah. *“And her maidens walked along the riverside”* <note>Exodus 2:5</note>—these are those who pursue them by the riverside, at the gateway of the grievance of the Torah, and those who teach falsely within it and forge its meanings. Rabbi Judah said: All those who provoke the Torah, and a congregation that has no man to receive it, and everyone who sheds tears in their exile—there is no gate through which those tears do not enter. What is written? *“And she opened it and saw him, the child”* <note>Exodus 2:6</note>. *“And she opened”*—this refers to the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often depicted as a motherly figure</note> who stands over Israel like a mother over her children; she opens always for the merit of Israel. Once she opened, *“she saw him, the child”*—these are the inner meanings of the Torah that appear before kings, and they all constantly return in repentance, standing before Him like a son who cries before his father. What is written? *“And behold, a youth was crying.”* As soon as he cried, <margin>(Page 163)</margin> all the accusers of the world were stirred. What is written? *“And she had compassion on him.”* Mercy was stirred for him, and she pitied him. And come and see: the words of the Hebrews are those that are difficult and hard <note>original: "kashu kzal"</note>, and not the words of Esau which are hard like a bark <note>original: "kashu nevach"</note>. The words of the Hebrews are such that when one is worthy, he inherits, and they are among those who appear before the <term>Matronita</term> <note>The Noble Lady/Divine Mother</note>. *“And she called the name of the child”*—the Shekhinah is weeping: *“A voice was heard in Ramah... lamentation and bitter weeping, Rachel weeping for her children”* <note>Jeremiah 31:15</note>. He was a doll <note>or "beloved child"</note> and she pitied the child; he was a joyful doll for Judah for the time to come. What is written? *“With weeping they shall come, and with supplications [I will lead them]”* <note>Jeremiah 31:9</note>. Who are those who *“with weeping shall come”*? By the merit of the weeping of the one who pitied the child, Rachel’s [tears] will be completed and they shall be gathered from the exile. And Rabbi Isaac said: The <term>Redemption</term> of Israel depends only on weeping; when the tears shed by Esau before his father are finished and completed, as it is written: *“And Esau lifted up his voice and wept”* <note>Genesis 27:38</note>. Rabbi Yose said: Those cries that Esau cried and those tears brought Israel down into their exile. Once those tears are finished, through the weeping of Israel they shall go out of exile: *“With weeping they shall come, and with supplications I will lead them.”*

**And he turned** this way and that way, etc. <note>Exodus 2:12</note>. *“This way and that way”*—Rabbi Isaac said: *“This way”* <note>Hebrew: "Koh"</note>—there were deeds of the "other side" <note>evil forces</note> in him; and *“that way”* <note>Hebrew: "Koh"</note>—a worthy son was destined to come out of him. Immediately, *“he saw that there was no man.”* He saw through the <term>Holy Spirit</term> that no worthy son was destined to come out of him. Rabbi Abba said: How many guilty people are there in the world who produce a worthy son, more so than all others? And that worthy son who comes from a guilty person, his life is found to be more significant, showing the pure from the impure—like light out of darkness, or wisdom out of folly. And this life is the most excellent of all. *“And he saw”*—he saw here through the Holy Spirit; he looked and struck. And because of this, he looked at him and killed him, for it was difficult. He surrounded everything to strike, just as Jacob went to that well, as it is written: *“And he sat by the well”* <note>Exodus 2:15</note>. Like Jacob, it is written *“and he saw,”* and he struck with the sword, as it is written: *“And he dwelt in the land of Midian, and he sat by the well,”* because Moses, even though they were on the same level, ascended from this *“Koh”* more than him.

**Rabbi** Yose and Rabbi Isaac were walking on the way. Rabbi Yose said: That well that Jacob saw and where Moses struck—it is the same well that Abraham and Isaac dug. It is ready to give water to him when it descends to the earth; the world took hold of this well. And at the eve of the Sabbath at twilight, its mouth was created, and it is the well that Jacob saw and where Moses [sat].

**Mishnah:** Those who are masters of truth, those who contemplate the <term>Secret of Faith</term>, those who are prepared with the <term>Incense</term> of spices—all those who know the ways of the Supreme King, tie the knot, spread out, and hear. When two ascend and go out to meet one, they receive him between two arms. They call to those coming to the bride's canopy; there are two, one on the right. Two are sitting, and it is found that in the gates <margin>(Page 186)</margin> they weep. One is on the right; he says to the whole, they are the nullification of the whole.

## Main Text (Zohar)

That holy host <note>original: *chila kadisha*</note> stands before their words, a balance of holy apples <note>A Zoharic metaphor for the Divine Presence or the field of sacred souls</note> for them from this side, to arrange the flocks. For behold, the staff that is mentioned from this side is for the arrangement of the flocks that Jacob selected when they were separated into his portion. All those chariots <note>original: *ratchin*; celestial vehicles or angelic assemblies</note>, all those masters of wings, three stand as a fourth over this well. From those, it is filled with the water that is called "upon four," as it is written:
> The **mercy** <note>original: *chesed*</note> of the Lord fills the earth, etc. (Psalms 33:5)
And it is written:
> But the **mercy** of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear Him (Psalms 103:17)
To judge all the multitude; all these are then ready to judge all the earth. In it is hidden the holy source of which it is written that it is always before the Lord, to call Him "Blessed be He" forever and to all eternity.

# And to the Priest
of Midian there were seven daughters, and they came and drew water, etc. <note>Exodus 2:16</note> Rabbi Judah said: If this well is the same well of Jacob, behold it is written of it:
> And thither were all the flocks gathered, etc. (Genesis 29:3)
But here, the daughters of Jethro did not need this [assistance], rather "they came and drew water" without the help of another. Rabbi Hiyya said: Jacob removed [the stone] from the well, for behold it is written that when all the flocks gathered there, they rolled the stone. But regarding Jacob, it is not written that he "returned" the stone, for it was not needed after that. At first, the waters would not rise, but once Jacob came, the waters rose toward him. And with Moses, the waters likewise rose toward him, and that stone was not upon the mouth of the well. Because of this, "they came and drew water" [easily].

Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Abba were traveling from Tiberias to Sepphoris. While they were walking, a certain Jew met them to join them. Rabbi Eleazar said: Let each one say a word of Torah. 

He [the stranger] opened and said: "And He said to me, smite it thus with the sword, rest the pain of the sword and the heat of God to slay, etc." <note>A homiletic expansion on Ezekiel 21:19</note> From this verse I know the place from which the spirit flies out, etc. Can one be silent and strong for the congregation upon the throne? For behold it is written:
> No man has power over the spirit to restrain the spirit (Ecclesiastes 8:8)
Rather, when one cannot rule over the spirit, the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note>, rules over all, and by His word it was delayed. Furthermore, the Voice is the spirit in the body in this world, and because of this, it is built upon the four winds/directions of its strength, and the spirit from that place below is supported like the four sides of the world. 

Since that Jew was before him, Rabbi Eleazar said to him: What is your name? He said: A word that proves itself. He said to him: What is it? He said to him: The spirit gathered five and lived, and the weight of the throne of the image is like the body of this world. It should have been written:
> Thus says the Lord God: Come from the four winds, O spirit (Ezekiel 37:9)
What is "from the four winds"? It means the spirit does not descend to this world until it ascends and is struck by the four [corners] of the Throne <note>original: *korsaya*</note> which stands on four pillars. Once it ascends there, it is sent from within that Throne of the King and descends to this world in a body that is adorned from the four sides of the world. The spirit is likewise nullified from the four sides of the Throne that is prepared for them. 

He said to him: While I am walking straight before you, here is a wondrous thing from this side. For one day I was walking in the desert and I saw a tree that was desirable to look at, and a cave beneath it. I approached it and saw that place from which scents of all kinds of fragrances of the world arose. I strengthened myself and entered that cave, and I saw steps and the likeness of a platform where there were many teachings, spirits, and hidden things <note>original: *razin*</note> that I could not comprehend. And there I saw a man with a scepter in his hand. He was standing at a certain entrance. When he saw me, he was astonished and stood toward me. He said to me: What are you doing here and who are you? I was afraid and began to tell him of my companions here. Thus I saw in the desert, and we entered this cave and stayed here. He said to me: Since the time of the proclamation has come, go before the scribes and give it to be proclaimed. Those who know the secrets <note>original: *razin*</note> for the hints of the righteous <note>original: *tzaddikaya*</note> shall prevail...

He struck him with that staff while I was sleeping. Meanwhile, I saw many hosts and camps <note>angelic or spiritual groupings</note> within the hidden firmament that were coming along the path like a merit. And that man struck with that staff and saw the way to the milk and went. Meanwhile, as they were going, they spread out into the air and ascended, and I did not know to which place. I heard the voices of many camps and I did not know who <margin>Books 31: to which place</margin> the vision was prepared for, and I did not see the words and I was afraid in that place. Meanwhile, I saw as he poured wine for me, I saw a single vision, I saw within the hidden firmament such and such. He said: In that way go the spirits of the righteous into the Garden of Eden above there. And what you heard from them is that they stand in the Garden in the image <term>Diyukna: a spiritual form or prototype</term> of this world, and they see with their spirits the righteous who enter there. Just as the body is built in this world from the connection of the four elements <note>fire, air, water, and earth</note> and moves in this world, so too the spirit <term>Ruach</term> is built in the Garden from the connection of the four winds <note>original: "arba ruchin," playing on the double meaning of spirit and wind</note> that stand in the Garden. In that spirit, it is clothed there and appears clearly in the image of the body that was built in this world. And if not for those four winds, which are the hosts of the Garden, the spirit would not be formed in any shape at all and would not be clothed in them. And those thirty spirits are tied to one another as one. And in that spirit, it is formed and clothed in them in the likeness of the body built by the connection of the four elements of the world. And because of this, "From the four winds, O breath, come" <note>Ezekiel 37:9</note>, for it is clothed and formed by them. And he opened and went and stood before us to write and saw the way and gave it to those behind him. Rabbi Eleazar came and the companions were wise and they checked him with a garment. Rabbi Eleazar said: The Merciful One wrapped your arrangement, a male worker, this is the clarity of the matter and it stands at times for the mouth to see the verse. He gave them a fine penalty for writing. When Rabbi Eleazar approached him and opened for him the palm of the hand of the brother, and it was hidden from him there like that which was struck and flew from his hands. Rabbi Eleazar wept and said: Who can endure among the children of the King?
> "Who may dwell in Your tent? Who may live on Your holy mountain?" <note>Psalms 15:1</note>
Blessed is this way and the clarity of mind that we encountered thus. And from that day on, Rabbi Eleazar meditated and said nothing to the companions. Until they were walking and encountered a single well of water; they stood over it and drank from the water. Rabbi Eleazar said: Blessed is the portion of the righteous! Jacob fled from before his brother and a well was prepared for him. As soon as the water saw him in the way, they recognized their master and rose up toward him and rejoiced with him, and there his soulmate was joined to him. Moses fled from before Pharaoh and a well was prepared for him, and the waters saw him and recognized their master and rose up toward him, and there his soulmate was joined to him. What is the difference between Moses and Jacob? Regarding Jacob it is written:
> "And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel... Jacob went near and rolled the stone..." <note>Genesis 29:10</note>
Regarding Moses, what is written?
> "The shepherds came and drove them away; but Moses stood up and saved them..." <note>Exodus 2:17</note>
When he saw, Moses knew that since the waters rose toward him, his soulmate would be prepared for him there. Furthermore, the Holy Spirit <term>Ruach HaKodesh</term> never departed from him, and through it, he knew that his soulmate would be found in that deliverance. Moses said: Surely Jacob came here and the waters rose toward him; it was prepared for him as he recognized it for his house and he gave him all that was needed, so too here. That man said: Wait, I have learned there is no priest for the goat <note>referring to Jethro, the priest of Midian</note>. Since he struck the goat, there is no cup from him that is separated from the worship of the idol. They stood with her and her jugs. When they stood in the house, they were driving them away, for at first they were trembling over them. Since he struck the staff through the Holy Spirit regarding the matter of the goat they were doing, immediately "Moses stood up and saved them and watered their flock," and everything was done corresponding to one another. Rabbi Eleazar said to him: You have been wise toward us, but I do not know your name.

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Book of Exodus (Shemot) in the Zohar. It follows the conclusion of Genesis, transitioning from the deaths of the Patriarchs to the exile and redemption of the Children of Israel.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

A wise man approached, and his son helped him, and his son-in-law Jacob and the companions raised him up. They said, "What is the right path? We did not know it was so." They stayed together as one all that day. At another time, they encountered three matters that remained for the end.

---

### And they said
**And they said**: Life comes from themselves. Rabbi Chiyya said, "The companions have already established that in all of them there is a holy mystery; they spoke, yet they knew not what they said." This is like a man who lived in the desert, and there were times they had nothing to eat. One day, the time came to eat a certain lamb; it fled, and he pursued it until they reached that man of the desert. He stood in the way, overpowered it, and they ate. <note>original: "Lishana Achra" — another version of the story exists.</note>

---

### And these
**And these** are the names of the children of Israel. Rabbi Yehuda opened his discourse and said:
> I am black but comely...
<note>Song of Songs 1:5</note>
"I am black but comely." This refers to the Assembly of Israel <term>Knesset Yisrael: a mystical personification of the Jewish people and the Shekhinah</term>, who is "black" from the darkness of exile, yet "comely" through their study of Torah, their commandments, and their righteous deeds. The Assembly of Israel is such that when they merit below, there is a spiritual expansion above. This is the meaning of the verse "And these are the names of the children of Israel"—their deeds were like the "curtains of Solomon," like the curtains of the King to whom peace belongs <note>original: "Shelomo" is read here as "She-ha-shalom shelo," the King of Peace/God</note>, for everything is His.

---

### Rabbi
**Rabbi** Chiyya the Great was traveling to the masters of the Mishnah to learn from them. He came to the house of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and saw a certain curtain <term>Paragod: a mystical veil or divider separating the holy study space</term> that was spread across the house. Rabbi Chiyya was astonished; he said, "I will hear a word from his mouth from right here." He heard him saying:
> Flee, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag...
<note>Song of Songs 8:14</note>
All the longing of the Assembly of Israel is for the Holy One, blessed be He, that He should not distance Himself from Israel. The moon <note>symbolizing the Shekhinah</note> is a light that does not depart or distance itself except like a gazelle or a young stag. Just as a gazelle runs, and no other animal in the world acts like the gazelle or the young stag—for when it flees, it moves a little and then turns its head back to the place it left, always turning its head behind it—so Israel said: "Master of the Universe, if we cause You to depart from among us, may it be Your will to flee like a gazelle or a young stag, who flees but turns his head back to the place he left." And even this is a miracle:
> And yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not cast them away, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly...
<note>Leviticus 26:44</note>
Rabbi Chiyya heard this and cried out, "Woe! The heavenly ones are separated!" <note>original: "Sefarim acherim" (other versions) read: "The depths are in the house"</note>. He saw the companions sitting there and he wept. He trembled and said, "Surely the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> is within; I shall go out." Rabbi Eleazar, the son of Rabbi Shimon, said, "If the light is here, I am not light; for the Divine Presence is within, let the Divine Presence enter and its rectifications below be completed." He heard a voice saying, "Before the supports are supported and the gates are prepared, and while the scent of the spices of Eden has not yet gone out..." Rabbi Eleazar did not go out. Rabbi Chiyya sat, wept, and sighed. He opened his discourse and said, "Turn, be like a gazelle, my beloved, or a young stag." The gate of the curtain opened, but Rabbi Chiyya did not enter. He lifted his eyes and said, "A vision comes to the booth to see the vision of the companions, and we shall sleep." Rabbi Shimon rose and went from his place until he reached Rabbi Chiyya. He saw Rabbi Shimon as a spark of light <note>original: "Kotzita de-nehora"</note> shining outward. He said, "The mouth of Rabbi Chiyya has been milked" <note>meaning he has produced sweet Torah</note>. When he came before the pious one, he lowered his eyes and did not raise his head. Rabbi Shimon said to his son Rabbi Eleazar, "Rise and pass your hand over his mouth, for he is not used to this." Rabbi Eleazar rose and passed his hands over Rabbi Chiyya's mouth. Rabbi Chiyya opened his mouth and wept for what his eyes had seen. He stood before them and said, "It is better to die in a skin of gold, a good light in a place where the coverings throw light to every side. And every single covering rises to three hundred and sixty..."

It features a dramatic scene where Rabbi Chiyya approaches the mystical study circle of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, experiencing the overwhelming power of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) hidden behind a curtain.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And These Are The Names**<-

And the chariots rise, and all those who are able to spread out pass through thousands and tens of thousands until they reach the **Ancient of Days** <note>A name for the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note> who sits upon the throne. And the throne trembles before Him at various times, and sixty worlds [tremble] until it reaches the place of the "narrow path," until it is heard in all the firmaments and all the upper and lower realms. And all of them at once are shaken and terrified. This is **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai**, who would make all these matters tremble, and who was able to stand before Him. This is <term>Rashbi</term> <note>Acronym for Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note> who, when he opened his mouth, secrets were delivered to the angels like a brightness. All the thrones, all the firmaments, all the chariots, and all those appointed over their masters come toward him; none open their mouths, for those who are marked as silent remain still until a voice is heard in all the firmaments above and below. When Rabbi Shimon finishes speaking these bright words, they see mountains of words; they see the Primordial One who is found by His masters; they see voices traveling through all the lower firmaments. All those within the "thirty-nine pedestals" bow and prostrate before their Master. The spirits of the longing ones of Eden ascend to the Ancient of Days, and all those within the "forty" [pedestals].

**Rabbi Shimon opened** his mouth and said: Six levels descended with Jacob to Egypt, and each and every one consisted of ten thousand myriads. Corresponding to them were six levels for Israel, and corresponding to them were six levels for the Throne Above, and corresponding to them were six levels for the throne below, as it is written:
> Six steps to the throne <note>1 Kings 10:19</note>
The sound of the chariot is like the gift of <term>Metatron</term> <note>The highest Archangel, often associated with the governance of the physical world</note> as it is written, etc. Read "six," and corresponding to them it is written:
> And the children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty, etc. <note>Exodus 1:7</note>
Come and see: when he ascended to the courtyard, they were coming—those who were estranged, who were in the surroundings of the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence, viewed as feminine</note>. And those chariots that went out with Israel from exile and that entered with Jacob into exile were coming. Rabbi Hiyya said to him: And what is this that is written:
> Now there arose a new king, etc. <note>Exodus 1:8</note>
Shimon said to him: [The light] burst forth from here, and not everything is as it appears. The elder gathered his strength and decided with the reed-pen. This one and that one stood in stillness, as it is written:
> Toward the face of the lampstand shall they give light, etc. <note>Numbers 8:2</note>
While they were sitting, Rabbi Elazar said to Rabbi Shimon: Show me, why did the Holy One, Blessed be He, bring Israel down to Egypt in exile?
He said to him: Master of the lower realm, this is a secret of two. He said to him: Why two exiles, and why for this duration? He said to him: They are two that return to being one. He said to him: Arise in your standing, your building shall be established forever; let your voice speak the word, my son, speak. He opened and said: "Sixty are the queens and eighty concubines." "Sixty are the queens"—these are the words from above, from the power of the light from below, before the "husks" <note>Klippot; the forces of impurity or shells that conceal holiness</note> of the holy living beings of Israel. And "eighty concubines" are those appointed over the exiles beneath them, and of worlds there is no number. As it is said, "Is there any number to His armies?" And despite all this, it is written:
> My dove, my undefiled, is but one; she is the only one of her mother <note>Song of Songs 6:9</note>
This is the **Holy Shekhinah** who goes out from the twelve lights of the crown, and all of them rejoice to be called "one." In this manner, the Holy One, Blessed be He, acted on earth: He cast out to all the nations, to every root, and placed over them great ministers without lack. But the portion of the Righteous Lord is not like that of all the nations, as it is written of His portion, the **Assembly of Israel**: "For the Lord's portion is His people; Jacob is the lot of His inheritance." And He called her: "My dove, my undefiled, is but one; she is the only one of her mother"—this is the precious Shekhinah who dwells among them, she is one and unique to Him.
> The daughters saw her and called her blessed <note>Song of Songs 6:9</note>
All the many daughters of Esau performed valiantly, but you have ascended above them all. "The queens and the concubines, and they praised her"—these are the ministers of the nations who are abandoned over them. Furthermore, the spirit of the matter is as we have learned: "By ten utterances was the world created." And when you look, there are three, and the world was created through them: through <term>Wisdom</term> (Chokhmah), through <term>Understanding</term> (Tevunah), and through <term>Knowledge</term> (Da'at). And the world was only created for the sake of the children of Israel. When He desired to establish the world, He acted to join [the patriarchs] in the spirit of Wisdom; Isaac in the spirit of Understanding; Jacob in the spirit of Knowledge. And this is what is written: "And by knowledge shall the chambers be filled." And the Throne was a burden to include the whole world, and from below they descended to Jacob.

## And These Are The Names

For Jacob, the side was always perfected entirely in the likeness of that which is Above. When the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note>, saw the great joy that the world had taken on, being perfected in the likeness of Above, He said: "Perhaps, Heaven forbid, they will mingle with the rest of the nations and the inner essence of all the worlds will become defiled." What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He moved them all from here to there until they descended to their dwelling place, like a drop of pitch <note>an image of the dark, sticky nature of the material exile in Egypt</note> that aims for their horses and aims for them to be found among them and to mingle with them. And foreign servants defiled them, and they were oppressed by them with a yoke, until everything was perfected as the "Holy Feet." And meanwhile, God proves the status of the other nations, as it is written:
> *For the iniquity of the Amorite is not yet full* (Genesis 15:16).
And when they went out, they went out as holy righteous ones, as it is written:
> *The tribes of Yah, a testimony for Israel* (Psalms 122:4).

Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse and prostrated his head upon a stone: "While you exist, a terror exists for you." Rabbi Shimon sat, and Rabbi Eleazar his son sat before him, and he revealed words of the secrets of wisdom <note>original: *razei de-chokhmata*, referring to Kabbalistic mysteries</note>. And they were covered as if by canopies in the sun, and the words were flying through the firmament. They sat for two days and did not eat or drink, and they did not know if it was day or night. When they came out, they realized it had been two days that they had tasted nothing. Rabbi Shimon applied this verse to the situation:
> *And he was there with the Lord forty days and forty nights; he did neither eat bread...* (Exodus 34:28).
If this happened to these men in a single hour, how much more so for Moses, of whom the scripture testifies, "And he was there with the Lord," and so on.

When Rabbi Hiyya came before Rabbi Yose, there was an incident involving him. Rabbi [Shimon] was sharp, and Rabbi Eleazar his son sensed the scent of Rabbi Shimon like a mountain of purity <note>original: *tur charivuta*</note>. Concerning him it is written:
> *The lion has roared, who will not fear?* (Amos 3:8).
And so on. If the upper worlds tremble because of him, how much more so should we? Let us flee so that the fire of the worlds' suffering does not consume us because of what we have seen. But rather, he decrees and the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills; the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees and the righteous one annuls. And this is what we have learned, what is the meaning of that which is written:
> *The righteous one rules over men* (2 Samuel 23:3).
The Holy One, blessed be He, rules over man, but who rules over the Holy One, blessed be He? The righteous one, for He issues a decree and the righteous one annuls it.

We have learned: Rabbi Judah said, there is nothing as beloved before the Holy One, blessed be He, as the prayer of the righteous. And even though it is pleasing to Him, sometimes He grants their request and sometimes He does not. Our Rabbis taught: Once the world was in need of rain. Rabbi Eleazar came and decreed forty fasts, but the rain did not come at all. Rabbi Akiva came, stood, and prayed. He said: "He who causes the wind to blow and the rain to fall," and immediately the rain came. Rabbi Eleazar felt weak in his mind <note>he felt discouraged or slighted that his long fasts failed while Akiva's short prayer succeeded</note>. Rabbi Akiva looked at his face and stood before the people and said: "I will tell you a parable; to what is this matter comparable? Rabbi Eleazar is like the King’s beloved friend, whom the King loves exceedingly; whenever he is before the King, it is pleasing to Him, and the King does not want to grant his request immediately because He does not want to be separated from him, for He enjoys speaking with him. But I am like the King’s servant who asks a request, and the King does not want me to enter the palace <note>original: *paltorin*</note> or to speak with Him. The King says: 'Give him his request quickly so he doesn't come in here!'" Thus, Rabbi Eleazar is the King's beloved, and the King wants to speak with him every day and not be separated from him, while I am a servant and the King does not want me to enter the gates of the palace. Rabbi Eleazar’s mind was eased.

Akiva said to him: "May this matter that appeared to me in a dream be a comfort to you. Behold, it is written:
> *As for you, do not pray for this people, nor lift up a cry or prayer for them, and do not intercede with Me* (Jeremiah 7:16).
Come and see: twelve mountains of pure balsam <note>original: *afarsamona*</note> enter... [the one] who is clothed in... and a shadow from the Holy One, blessed be He, to give to the world, and until now it hangs and stands." If so, why did Rabbi Eleazar feel weak in his mind? Because of the shame, for they did not know the reason. Rabbi Eleazar said: "Eighteen mountains of pure upper balsam are the souls of the righteous, and forty-nine scents rise in every..."

## Main Text (Zohar)

->And These Are The Names<-

Every day, until reaching that place which is not called "Eden" <note>referring to a level of hidden divinity beyond comprehension</note> until we receive this, the Torah is increased by twenty-eight facets of impurity and twenty-eight facets of purity. Why do we learn them in doubt? Because they perform forty-nine days to receive the Torah—forty-nine holy days. Upon them, they sit and stand to take permission; every day they rub and dwell to strike with that key. And just as the likeness of the "garment of the nose" <note>a metaphorical reference to a specific divine emanation or "Partzuf"</note> sits on the holy throne and calls to four fallen ones who stand looking at the key, by their words they go up and by their words they go out. They lift their eyes and look to the nourishment of the forgiveness of the pleasantness that burns in the depths of the brain. They produce an embryo, and the holy vessel ascends upon it, shaking and dividing the knots on the sides of the holy right, which squeezes like dew in the hands of the blind support, answering to the light and hidden like the book of *Santis* <note>an obscure or celestial book title</note>. Rabbi Akiva said: What is the meaning of that which is written:
> I went down into the garden of walnuts <note>Song of Songs 6:11</note>
He said to him: Come and see, the "garden" goes out from Eden, and this is the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>the Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note>. The <term>walnut</term> (Egoz) is the <term>Holy Chariot</term> <note>the Raitika Kadisha</note>, which are the four heads of the rivers that branch out from the garden, just like this walnut has four sections inside. And as for what he said, "I went down," it is like when a certain person "descended to the <term>Chariot</term>" <note>Merkavah; a term for entering a deep meditative state of mystical ascent</note>. Rabbi Akiva said: If so, he should have said "I went down to my gardens"; why "to the garden of walnuts"? He said to him: Because it is the surrounding of the garden. Just as a walnut is hidden and closed from all its sides, so is the Chariot that goes out from the garden closed from all its sides. Just as there are four shells in the walnut that join on this side and separate on that side, so the Chariot joins in unity, in joy, and in perfection, and each one separates according to its deeds, concerning which it was said: "And he was the promise of all the land of awe." It was that which was before and behind, and so all of it. Rabbi Akiva said: See the dirt that is on the shells of the walnut, what does it hint at? He said to him: A person with a discharge <note>Zav; one who is ritually impure</note> is not revealed the Torah in this garden. Come and see: some of them are bitter and some are sweet, and there is a hint in them. Some have a harsh image and some have a mountain-like quality. For every hint revealed in the Torah, we see an image, and so it is for the visionary to see it in the image, as it is written:
> I see a rod of an almond tree <note>Jeremiah 1:11; the Hebrew word for almond, 'Shaked', also means 'to be watchful'</note>
What is "Shaked"? It means actual watchfulness. And so "the bud blossomed and yielded
> almonds" <note>Numbers 17:23</note>
And from the word itself, it is understood that there is a harsh image, as it is written: "And the Lord watched over the evil," and so "visiting the guilt of the fathers upon the children," and so all of it. Rabbi Akiva said: This implies that everything the Holy One, Blessed be He, made was so that we might learn wisdom from it in awe, as it is written:
> The Lord has made everything for His own purpose <note>Proverbs 16:4</note>
Rabbi Eleazar said: From here, as it is written:
> And God saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good <note>Genesis 1:31</note>
What is "very"? To learn from it higher wisdom. Rabbi Yehuda said: As it is written:
> God has made even the one as well as the other <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14</note>
In the likeness of the firmament, the Holy One, Blessed be He, made the earth, and all of them are hints to that which is above. For when they were before Rabbi Abba, he spoke of a hidden tree that was made, and its branches were divided... <note>The text here describes a complex mystical vision of trees and branches representing divine structures</note> ...to strike hints. They were lacking their dates until their navels, to strike so that wisdom could be understood from them, such as what the Holy One, Blessed be He, did on earth. Rabbi Jose said: So that wisdom could be prepared from them, such as the many stalks of the pistachio and similar things. All of them were planted in soft soil. All those that produce fruit, when they are opened, are of one spirit, except for the intelligent ones that are separated. All those that do not produce fruit are great, but outside the order of awe, for a spirit moves them alone, in the likeness of that which is above—blight and mildew—and each one of them pushes and strikes. When they are seen in a single dream, all the herbs of the earth are born, over which are appointed great and powerful ministers in heaven. Each and every one has a spirit to itself, in the likeness of that which is above. And because of this, it is written:
> You shall not sow your field with diverse seeds <note>Leviticus 19:19</note>
For each and every one enters alone and comes out alone, and as it is written:
> Do you know the ordinances of the heavens? Can you establish their dominion over the earth? <note>Job 38:33</note>
And so it is written in all.

## Main Text (Zohar)

For all of them are called by His precious Name. And why all of them? Because in this world, they are merely spirit, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to reveal them and mention them by name. Thus, they are called by their names—Jacob and the holy tribes—corresponding to the foundation of the world. Regarding this, the verse repeatedly cries out: **"And these are the names of the sons of Israel."** Rabbi Yose, son of Rabbi Yehuda, said: If the text had only said "These are the names," it would imply these alone. But now that it is written **"And these are the names,"** <note>The Hebrew prefix "Vav" (And) usually implies an addition to what came before.</note> it implies that it adds to the first ones; just as the first ones were the sons of Jacob, so too these are the sons of Jacob. Rabbi Yehuda further said: The reason is that the Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
> **"I will go down with you to Egypt"** (Genesis 46:4)
Because the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed in the Zohar as the feminine aspect of God that accompanies Israel in suffering.</note> would descend with him at that hour. Rather, it is written: **"I will go down with you to Egypt"**—literally with you. At the moment there was a descent for the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>Knesset Yisrael; the spiritual archetype of the Jewish people.</note>, the Shekhinah descended with her. **"I will go down with you to Egypt, and I will also surely bring you up again."** As long as you have an ascent, as it were, I have an ascent; and at the time you have a descent, as it were, I will go down with you. And until Joseph and all his brothers died, and the final time of descent arrived, the Shekhinah stood and descended with them. Just as these descended, so too those descended.

Rabbi Yehuda said: What is written just before this? "And Joseph died, being a hundred and ten years old," etc. And at that moment, the children of Israel descended into exile, and the Shekhinah went over them because He said "with them, with them." **"And these are the names of the sons of Israel"**—for they were added to the first ones to be in exile. He said to him: If so, had Jacob died or not? He replied: He had died. He said to him: Then what is the meaning of that which is written, "I will go down with you to Egypt"? Was Jacob alive? How many times was it "with Jacob" while he was alive? After he died, He brought Jacob out from there. He said to him: Come and see, the verse says: **"Who came into Egypt with Jacob."** <note>Exodus 1:1</note> For until this point, there had been no descent for Jacob, but here we go with him; with Jacob they went. Until these descended into exile, those [heavenly powers] descended with them. This is what is written: "And these are the names," etc. Rabbi Dostai said: Every single day they would come and go before the Holy One, Blessed be He, from Egypt, and the text is not written with any deficiency regarding them. This is why it is written **"Who came into Egypt"** as at the first time, **"with Jacob."** And afterward, when they had a descent, **"every man and his household came."** And come [see], the sons of Jacob were all brought at that time, and both these and those descended. Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Eleazar said: This section contains supreme matters. For we have learned: At the hour these descended, the holy <term>Chariots</term> <note>Angelic hosts or divine vehicles.</note> and high officials—the images of the tribes that are engraved above—all ascended to dwell with them. This is what is written: "Every man and his household came," and it is written: "Reuben, Simeon," etc.

->**"And these are the names of the sons of Israel who came into Egypt with Jacob, every man and his household came: Reuben, Simeon, Levi..."**<- 
---

Let us return to this section: Why did Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Yehuda say this? And it was all so. And come and see, Rabbi Eleazar arranged all these matters... <note>The text here becomes more mystical and difficult to parse due to the Rashi script and Aramaic idioms.</note> when the Shekhinah was enriched and spread out in exile, they all gathered by their names to dwell in the Cave of Machpelah <note>The burial place of the Patriarchs in Hebron.</note>... not like the exhaustion of this world... they perform vengeances of the world. At that hour, the spirit of that foolish one was awakened... the Holy One, Blessed be He, called to all His Chariots and officials and their hearts in their mercies, and they all descended with Jacob and with his tribes. The tribes were like the giving of wine with the company of the tribes; they descended with them, with their fathers. This is: **"And these are the names of the sons of Israel who came into Egypt,"** etc. And it is written: "Reuben, Simeon, Levi," etc. And come and see... and it is written: "And Joseph was in Egypt." Rabbi Abba said: In this verse, he is called the throne of the father over the children. Rabbi Yehuda bar Shalom was walking on the way, and Rabbi Abba was with him. They arrived at a certain place and stayed there. They ate, and when they wished to lie down, their resting places were all on the ground where there was a single grave. Until this... a single voice from the grave said: "Earth, earth! Do not... twelve years was..."

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And These Are The Names**<-

...that it was not decreed except in joy for a person who merits the eighth <note>likely a reference to the eighth day of circumcision or a specific mystical level</note> here. Rabbi Yehuda said: Who is this? He said to him: My father was a Judean, and he sat in the cave of my father. I did not want to go because of that evil one whose eyebrow hair was long <note>original: "דגבגיה", a physical description often used in the Zohar to denote a sorcerer or an individual with an "evil eye"</note>; that goat, his whole lap was small, and they divided for him every day. And his fire pushed me to go to my place, and in this place, it was not decreed except in joy. He went and they were holding the youth of life. He went and began at the grave of the living; if in our hour for life they will not endure half a day, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, is in death. Rabbi Yehuda said: What is your business in that world? The grave was agitated and said: Levi, arise! For the righteous shall go in joy, they shall prophesy and flash from there words of hunger. They sat by the river Euphrates. They rose to go and saw a man who was running and flashing, and his shoulders were closed. They reached him and he told them the story. They said to him: What is your name? Aldanza son of Lyocha. They said: And what of this? Lyocha son of Nachman was that dead man, and I am afraid that I was not circumcised more in the holy... they did not pierce. Rabbi Abba said: This is the master of the poverty of the dead who shield the living, from here as it is written: *And he went up against... until Hebron* <note>original: "ויגנו כנגד ויכח עד חברון", a play on the word "Hebron" and the protection of the Patriarchs</note>. Rabbi Yehuda said: Come and see, two crowns, a crown that surrounded Jacob; one, the image of rain upon him like a garden, and one, his disk from his grave to see the joy of the holy company who dwell with his children, as it is written: *Your people shall be willing in the day of your power* <note>Psalm 110:3</note>. The sages said: *Your people* are in exile, and they shall dwell with you now as a whole, and I will protect you from your graves with Me, and it is written: *Rejoice...*

**Now there arose a new king over Egypt, etc.** <note>Exodus 1:8</note>. Rabbi Shimon opened and said:

This is *While the king was at his table*—while the Holy One, Blessed be He, was standing on Mount Sinai to give freedom to Israel, *my spikenard sent forth its fragrance*, as it is written: *And they made a calf*. Rabbi Phineas said: Every strength and power has a limit for Israel, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives dominion to this one and a spear to that one, and when He gives dominion to that celestial prince, he has no dominion over Israel unless they change for the worse.

## Main Text (Zohar)

There are no nations that deny and yet praise before the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: *Kadosh Baruch Hu* (קב"ה)</note> like those of the East. The **Holy One, Blessed be He** gave them dominion for the sake of Israel, for "a handmaid that is heir to her mistress" <note>A reference to Proverbs 30:23, interpreted here as Hagar (the mother of Ishmael/the East) gaining temporary power over Sarah's descendants</note>, referring to Hagar who gave birth to Ishmael. 

Rabbi Isaac was going up to Jerusalem and was traveling on the road. He saw an Arab traveling on the road with a camel. They encountered a man named Yoḥai. One said to his fellow: "Look, I see a flash in the vision..." <note>The text here uses Aramaic/Arabic dialectal variations to depict a conversation between travelers regarding spiritual omens</note>. He spat in his beard, the old man, and they responded: "The sickness of the throat is pushed away." I know that the seventy nations are despised through them. His son went and showed his beard... Rabbi Yehuda said: "Secrets are hidden within the heights that wait below." Because of this, they were swallowed up after them.

Rabbi Isaac opened his discourse: "Until the day breathes and the shadows flee..." <note>Song of Songs 2:17</note>. This verse refers to the exile of Israel. They are sealed in the depths and despised in exile until that time of the dominion of the nations—which is harsh—is completed. Even though the nations had dominion over them, and Gehenna is a wall so that death shall not be wrought upon them, Heaven forbid, as it is written: "And it shall be one day which is known to the Lord..." <note>Zechariah 14:7</note>. 

"Until the day breathes"—before the thorn blows, the day of heat. "And the shadows flee"—these are the rulers over them. Even so, "I will get me to the mountain of myrrh." The **Holy One, Blessed be He** said: "I will go to the mistress of heat." From Jerusalem, it shall be the "Mountain of Myrrh," as it is written: "In Mount Moriah which is in Jerusalem," and the "Hill of Frankincense"—this is the Holy Temple which is built there, of which it is written: "Beautiful in elevation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion..." <note>Psalms 48:3</note>.

Rabbi Yehuda said: "At the end of days, He shall take hold of the ends of the earth, and the wicked shall be shaken out of it." The filth shall be nullified and burned away. Rabbi Joseph said: "In the future, the **Holy One, Blessed be He** will reveal Himself in the lower Jerusalem and purify it from the filth of the nations until not a trace remains." On that day of heat, after life, the "seers" <note>referring to the spiritual representatives of the nations</note> shall have no dominion over Israel, not even for a single day. Everything is conditional on Heaven: "All the day faint" <note>Lamentations 1:13</note>—one day and no more. Rabbi Yose said: "They shall be enslaved even more by the decree of the King, even if they do not deserve it." And it is written: "And it shall come to pass, when all these things are come upon thee, the blessing and the curse..." <note>Deuteronomy 30:1</note>. And it is written: "If any of thine be driven out unto the outmost parts of heaven, from thence will the Lord thy God gather thee..." <note>Deuteronomy 30:4</note>.

---

> **And he said** unto his people: "Behold, the people of the children of Israel are too many and too mighty for us." <note>Exodus 1:9</note>

Rabbi Shimon opened: "In every instance, the table of dominion is appointed over the East." And so it is in this portion: "A king of Egypt" is mentioned plainly, referring to the great appointee <note>The celestial guardian or angel</note> over the East. "Pharaoh, King of Egypt" refers to the actual Pharaoh. Rabbi Shimon said: "Therefore it is written 'And he said,' meaning he spoke in his heart." For every 'saying' that does not specify to whom it was said refers to the heart's thought. Similarly, "And Haman said in his heart," and "And Esau said in his heart." Here too, they spoke their thoughts in their hearts: "too many and too mighty for us." What does "from us" <note>original: *mimenu* (ממנו)</note> mean? It means they are mightier than our celestial source. They said in their hearts that Israel's strength and power were greater than their own spiritual dominion. 

Rabbi Isaac said: "All the 'seers' of the world, except for the poor, draw strength from their guardians, while Israel's voice is accepted by their Father in Heaven." Rabbi Yehuda said: "Here they are called 'his people,' as it is written 'And he said to his people.' But elsewhere it is written 'I have surely seen the affliction of My people'—'My people' literally. Israel is called the people of the Lord, while the other nations are called the 'people' of their specific celestial ruler. As it is written: 'For all peoples will walk every one in the name of his god, and we will walk in the name of the Lord our God for ever and ever.'" 

Rabbi Abba said: "The verse should have said 'Behold, the people of Israel.' Why 'the people of the *children* of Israel'? This refers to the literal children of the 'Israel' above <note>The sefirah of Tiferet, often called 'Israel' in Kabbalah</note>. Because they were the children of the Supernal Israel, they were with the Lord. Thus it is written: 'And they were grieved because of the children of Israel' <note>Exodus 1:12</note>, and it does not say 'because of the *people* of the children of Israel.'"

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **And these are the names** <-

...with the Children of Israel, but rather because of the actual Children of Israel. Rabbi Yochanan was standing before Rabbi Isaac and said: "What did Balak see that led him to say, *'Behold, the people of the Children of Israel are more numerous and stronger than we'* <note>Numbers 22:5</note>, and he did not simply say 'Behold, the Children of Israel'?" <margin>3</margin>

Rabbi Isaac said: "Balak was a great sage <note>In the Zohar, 'sage' often refers to mastery of the dark arts or sorcery</note>, and such is the way of sorcerers: they take a matter in which there is no sin. They would always mention the name of a person's ancestors, but they would silence their own memory because of sin. For such is the way of the 'Other Side' <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of evil or impurity</term>; they gaze into that portion which we leave for them, and if they see a lie, they announce false things. But if it is the truth, everything they say for a short time is true—all the more so when performing their work."

Rabbi Isaac said: "Balak took the path of disgrace, saying *'Behold, the people of the Children of Israel,'* as if to say they have no known ancestors." Rabbi Yochanan asked: "Why did they make knots <note>Magical bindings or spiritual accusations</note> for the great ones, but for the Holy One, Blessed be He, they did not make knots?" Rabbi Isaac said: "A poor man is not like a rich man. A poor man is in the eyes of his own side; a rich man does not 'knot.' And the goodness of Israel is that they are a *'kingdom of priests and a holy nation'* <note>Exodus 19:6</note>. One who is diligent acts like a man before Him, as it is written that He desires them to be bound to Him more than all others. This is what is written: *'You only have I known of all the families of the earth, therefore I will visit upon you all your iniquities'* <note>Amos 3:2</note>."

Rabbi Yose was walking along the road and Rabbi Isaac was following him. While they were walking, Rabbi Yose remained silent and reflected on worldly matters, while Rabbi Isaac reflected on matters of Torah. As they were walking, <margin>3</margin> a snake <note>original: "kulsa" / "chivya"</note> appeared before Rabbi Yose, running after him. Rabbi Yose said to Rabbi Isaac: "Do you see this snake running after me?" Rabbi Isaac said to him: "I do not see it at all." Rabbi Yose ran, and the snake was behind him. Rabbi Yose fell and was bitten a second time, and he was silent from his nose <note>likely meaning he was breathless or stunned</note>. He heard them saying: *'You only have I known of all the families of the earth...'* Rabbi Yose said: "Certainly, what is the reason for this? Is it not because one who is elevated has his sins held against him?"

He opened his discourse and said: *'For the Lord your God has blessed you in all the work of your hand; He knows your walking...'* <note>Deuteronomy 2:7</note> and *'Who led you through... the great and terrible wilderness, wherein were fiery serpents and scorpions...'* <note>Deuteronomy 8:15</note>. Why is the 'fiery serpent' mentioned here? It is only to take the punishment from Israel whenever they separate themselves from the **Tree of Life** <note>The Torah</note>, as it is written: *'For it is your life and the length of your days'* <note>Deuteronomy 30:20</note>.

Come and see: Rabbi Hiyya said: "It is written, *'The rod of his scepter bears it...'* and it is written, *'To strike the one who strikes you, says the Lord,'* and it is written, *'And the house of Esau for stubble.'* What is 'stubble'? As it is written, 'The rod of his scepter bears his son,' meaning I have sent his fear, and therefore I have cut down the scepter of violence. All the more so for **Torah scholars** <term>Talmidei Chachamim</term>, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not want them to be separated from the Tree of Life for even a moment."

**And he said** to his people. He gave them counsel to do evil to them. Rabbi Isaac said: "They were all divining through their calculations that their end would be to suffer because of Israel, and therefore he prioritized giving them dominion to do evil to them."

Rabbi Isaac happened upon a certain mountain and saw a man who was holding the image of a certain power sitting there. He was sitting in the hollow of the earth which was beginning to shake. That power broke and doubled over, and he saw cracks and pits in the earth, and the earth rose and was crushed. A voice of a man cried out toward Rabbi Isaac and said to him: "They shall be moved and the teeth of that power shall be broken! They stand in the firmament; a great prince of the nations has dominion over it, and he is prepared to do evil to you because the wrath of the earth is at its end. For all the time the wrath of the earth is full, he will do evil to you."

Rabbi Isaac was astonished and said: "It is written, *'Under three things the earth quakes... under a servant when he reigns'* <note>Proverbs 30:21-22</note>. From the time that he was waiting under the dominion of the lower power, and now they have given him dominion to rule over Israel." Rabbi Hama bar Guria said: "When he sees Israel under the dominion of the nations, he sits and groans, and thus the Holy One, Blessed be He: *'My soul shall weep in secret places'* <note>Jeremiah 13:17</note>." Rabbi Yose said: "Specifically in 'secret places'." Rabbi Joseph went to Rabbi Eleazar of Bagdad, who was sitting and whispering to himself and was sad. He said to him: "In what..."

## Main Text (Zohar)

An ancient sage rose and said to him: It is written <note>Proverbs 16:15</note> *“In the light of a king’s face there is life,”* etc. He acts with patience, even toward those who deserve punishment. Just as the wicked strike and act, the Holy One, blessed be He, allows these "bands of destruction" <note>term: *Chabulin* — destructive angels or spiritual forces of judgment</note> to strike at first, but He remains with His children. They are found in the "inner chambers" and they are found in the "outer chambers." What are these "inner chambers"? Rabbi Isaac said: They are associated with two kings. *“The angels of peace weep bitterly”* <note>Isaiah 33:7; original: "Malachei Shalom mar yivkayun"</note>. Is it possible for kings to be concerned with peace? He said to him: Yes. Come and see: the dwelling of grace is small, and there is no dwelling of grace that is not expansive and soft, and where there is a dwelling of mercy, there is no Judgment <note>term: *Din* — the attribute of strict justice</note> at all. These are called the "Kings of Peace." Regarding those below, it is written *“Melchizedek”* <note>Genesis 14:18; literally "King of Righteousness/Justice"</note>, who is a priest, and he is like a covering. And it is written that all possessions are before Him. If so, all those rulers who are appointed over the other nations, when they strike their masters, they act as a curtain for His children. Rabbi Eleazar said: They only strike as they are commanded, and they perform the will of their Master. Rabbi Dostai said: Whenever the children of the Holy One, blessed be He, are handed over to the rulers of the nations, twelve bands of judgment are subdued, and a great preparation is made... <unclear>textual corruption</unclear>... The Holy One, blessed be He, drips from the "Great Abyss" and they roll down below to the lower levels... The Holy One, blessed be He, casts down snow; who can stand before it? Come and see: at the time the Holy One, blessed be He, handed Israel over to the master of Egypt, he saw seven decrees to enslave them. Therefore, the Holy One, blessed be He, acted: <note>Exodus 1:14</note> *“And they embittered their lives with hard labor, in mortar and in bricks,”* etc. And corresponding to this: <note>Exodus 1:7</note> *“And the children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.”*

---

**"Come,** let us deal wisely with them" <note>Exodus 1:10; original: "Hava nitchakma lo"</note>. Rabbi Yose said: Look, the word *Hava* ("Come") is always an invitation to do evil, as in "Come, let us build" <note>the Tower of Babel</note> or "Come, let us go down." Rabbi Yochanan said: *Hava* is a language of agreement and preparation, like "Come, let us build us a city," or "Give (*havu*) your word and counsel," or "Ascribe (*havu*) unto the Lord, O ye sons of the mighty." Rabbi Isaac said: "Come, let us deal wisely with him"—this refers to the wisdom they used against Him <note>God</note>, regarding the phrase "Lest he multiply" (*Pen yirbeh*). But the Holy Spirit says: "So he shall multiply and so he shall spread" (*Ken yirbeh ve-ken yifrotz*). *“And they were grieved because of the children of Israel”* <note>Exodus 1:12</note>—they were like thorns (*kotzim*) in their eyes. Rabbi Yehuda said in the name of Rabbi Isaac: What was the thought of the Egyptians? To prevent Israel from being fruitful and multiplying, and to overcome the celestial rulers appointed over them. He said to them: Know that through a single secret, one will emerge from Israel through whom Judgment will be made heavy upon them. Rabbi Yochanan said: At the time He said He would execute judgments against all the gods of Egypt, Duma <note>term: *Duma* — the angel in charge of the souls of the dead and the Prince of Egypt</note>, the minister of Egypt, went and walked four hundred parasangs. The Holy One, blessed be He, issued a decree before him, as it is written: <note>Isaiah 24:21</note> *“The Lord shall punish the host of the high heaven on high,”* etc. At that moment, his dominion was nullified. And with wisdom, Duma, the minister of Gehenna <note>Purgatory/Hell</note>, came to judge the souls of the wicked. Rabbi Yehuda says: They dealt wisely regarding the dead. Rabbi Hanina said: It is written, "I will execute judgments." Were they all made of silver and gold? Those of silver and gold melted, and those of wood rotted. Rabbi Eleazar said: The "lamb" of Egypt <note>the sheep worshipped as a god</note> was what the Holy One, blessed be He, intended to execute judgment upon, to consume it in fire... so that its smell would spread, its head with its legs and its innards. This was harder for the Egyptians than anything else—the judgments of the Holy One, blessed be He. Rabbi Yehuda said: This refers to their actual Prince <note>spiritual patron</note>, to fulfill "The Lord shall punish the host of the high heaven on high." All this was known to their wise men and their Prince. Therefore it is written, "Come, let us deal wisely with him." Rabbi Yochanan said: There were many idols in Egypt, and in all of them, their power was broken.

->**And these are the names**<-

<note>The text begins with a complex Aramaic discussion on the nature of the Egyptian exile, using metaphors of "clinging" and "spreading."</note> It ascended within him and within all of them, and it looked closely and answered in everything, and five were spread out. One Isaac son of Salka flashed at first and then returned, thus he feared the clinging. This is what Rabbi Yose and the others say: the wall of Egypt itself was not a dream to them, since it is written: *there remained not so much as one of them* <note>Exodus 14:28</note>. And before this, at the hour when it spread in the clinging, etc., it is written: *Come, let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war...* <note>Exodus 1:10</note>. They wrote this concerning the future according to what would happen to them, and *he also join unto our enemies* refers to the Heavenly Kingdom that dwelt among them. *And fight against us* refers to what is written: *The Lord shall fight for you* <note>Exodus 14:14</note>. *And get them up out of the land* as it says: *the children of Israel went out with a high hand* <note>Exodus 14:8</note>.

**And there went** a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi <note>Exodus 2:1</note>. Rabbi Eleazar opened his discourse: *The Song of Songs, which is Solomon's* <note>Song of Songs 1:1</note>. We have learned: when the Holy One, blessed be He, created His world, it arose in desire before Him, and He created the heavens with His right hand and the earth with His left. It arose in desire before Him at the end of the day and the night, and He created the angels appointed over acts of kindness by day, and He created the angels appointed to utter Song by night. This is what is written: *The Lord will command His lovingkindness in the daytime, and in the night His song shall be with me* <note>Psalms 42:9</note>.

These are on the right and these are on the left, and these arrange the song of the day; the song of Israel is "Holy." Rabbi Isaac said: the protection of His surroundings is Song at night; they arrange the song of Israel by day as "Holy," declaring and arranging for your Creator. Rabbi Simeon said: the daughter of the wall of her completion <note>a mystical reference to the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> completes the strength of the Song at night. This is what is written: *She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household* <note>Proverbs 31:15</note>.

Rabbi Eleazar said: Ten things were created on the first day, and among them the attribute of Night and the attribute of Day. And concerning the attribute of Night it is written: *She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household*, as it is said, "they snatched the prey," and it is written: *He hath given meat unto them that fear Him* <note>Psalms 111:5</note>. *And a portion to her maidens* as it is said, "statute and ordinance" <note>original: "chok u-mishpat"</note>. From here we learn that the "Living Creature" <note>Chayah - a high level of angel</note> rules at night. And we have learned: those who utter Song at night, these are the princes over all masters of song. And like their drops, the Living Creatures add strength to the upper ones to know, to recognize, and to perceive that which they had not perceived; face and earth add to the daughter who cuts the Song. 

Rabbi Chamya said: Happy is the one who merits to know the secret of the Song, for we have learned: he who merits the secret of the Song knows the matters of the Torah and Wisdom, and he shall increase and be strengthened, and add power and might in what was and what is destined to be. And in this way, Solomon merited to know; for Rabbi Simeon taught: David, peace be upon him, knew this and prepared many songs and praises, hinting in them at the things to come in the future. He added power and might through the Holy Spirit <note>Ruach ha-Kodesh</note>, knowing the matters of Torah and Wisdom, and he saw and searched and added power and might in the Holy Tongue. But Solomon merited even more in the secret of the Song; he knew Wisdom, saw and searched, and prepared many parables. He made a book from the literal secret of the Song, and that is what is written: *I got me men singers and women singers* <note>Ecclesiastes 2:8</note>, meaning: I acquired for myself the knowledge of the Song from the secret of the supernal Songs and that which is under them. And that is why it is written *Song of Songs*, meaning: the Song of those supernal Princes, a Song that includes all matters of Torah and Wisdom, and power and might in what was and what is destined to be—the Song that the supernal Princes sing. 

Rabbi Eleazar said: These Princes stood until Levi was born; but from the time Levi was born and onward, they uttered Song. When Moses was born, and Aaron in truth, and the Levites were sanctified in the order of the Song, the Princes were then assigned to their watches.
