<meta>This page continues the Zohar's mystical commentary on the Book of Exodus (Shemot). It transitions from the general spiritual state of the Israelites in Egypt to the specific circumstances surrounding the birth of Moses and the eventual downfall of the spiritual "Prince" of Egypt.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

It is found that just as below they did not merit, and so on. Since the singers from the tribe of Levi <note>The Levites were the designated musicians and singers in the Holy Temple</note> rested upon the bed and were all sanctified, they stood at their watch and were sanctified for prophecy, as were all their companions; and they were found as one, with one King dwelling over them. Solomon came and composed a book from his accompaniment, a "Song of the Seal" <note>referring to the Song of Songs</note> which spreads over the Assembly of Wisdom, etc. Rabbi Judah said: Why are the songs below called "Levites"? Because they surround and give strength on high, each one [according to its station], and whoever hears all this, his soul cleaves to the heights. And some say: Why did Joseph take such a sickness? Rabbi Tanchum said: In every accompaniment, the seed of Levi was with the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the feminine, indwelling presence of God</term> upon the bed, shining and providing, and all his seed called out and approached the Lord to serve Him. Come and see: at the hour when the singers stood above, they also stood at their watch until the holy Solomon was born, a staff for the horn and provider. Immediately the staff and the lack of provision—why? Rabbi Yose said: He prepared and labored for all, and gave them provision.

Come and see: at that hour when Levi was born, the Holy One, blessed be He, took him and called him from among all his brothers and settled him in the land. And he fathered Kohath, and Kohath fathered Amram, and he fathered Aaron and Miriam. And he was separated from the rectification, but in the return at that hour, the celestial singers were standing and singing. The Holy One, blessed be He, rebuked them and the song was removed until He planted His "Right Line" and provided for Amram. Why was Amram's name not mentioned [initially]? Because he would come from him with power over all, yet his name is not mentioned. Why is his name not mentioned? Rabbi Judah said in the name of Rabbi Chakka: Because he went in humility and returned to his sickness in humility so that the public would not recognize him; he went like a commoner, as it says, "And Amram went in secret." "And he took the daughter of Levi"—she too returned in humility and her name was not mentioned.

**And there went** a man. <margin>A man went</margin> Rabbi Chisda said: "And there went a man"—this refers to the angel Gabriel, as it is written <note>Daniel 9:21</note> "the man Gabriel." He brought her up and returned her to Amram. Rabbi Judah said: It was literally Amram, and his name was not mentioned because this Divine Presence was not from him to pair with his sickness, but from above. Another explanation: In the window and on high, it was not like a commoner's union for the Assembly of the Torah; and below it is written, "And he took the daughter of Levi" to teach that the Divine Presence is called by the name of Levi. Amram was not worthy to father [Moses] below until he took a portion in the Divine Presence and fathered the congregation below. "And he took the daughter of Levi," and therefore it is written, "And she saw him, that he was good." Rabbi Eleazar said: Amram merited that a son should come from him who merited a "Great Voice," as it is written, "And the children shall serve with a voice." And Amram merited a "Daughter of a Voice" <term>Bat Kol: a heavenly echo or divine resonance</term>, as it is written, "And he took the daughter of Levi," meaning the *Bat Kol*. Therefore it is written "And he went," meaning he ascended to this spiritual degree. Come and see: when Moses was born, the Holy One, blessed be He, unified His Name upon him, as it is written <note>Exodus 2:2</note> "And she saw him, that he was good," and it is written <note>Psalms 145:9</note> "The Lord is good to all," and it is written <note>Psalms 34:9</note> "Taste and see that the Lord is good."

---

**And it came to pass** in those many days. <margin>And it was</margin> Rabbi Judah of Sakhnin said: "And it came to pass in those many days"—this was the end of their exile, for Israel was enslaved in every kind of labor. "In those many days"—for they were many for Israel in Egypt. And when the end of their exile was completed, what is written? <note>Exodus 2:23</note> "And the King of Egypt died." Why? Because the Prince <note>The spiritual guardian or patron angel</note> of Egypt was cast down from his rank and fell from his pride. And once the King of their companions fell—who is the Prince of the heights—the Holy One, blessed be He, remembered Israel and heard their prayer. Rabbi Judah said: Come and see, as long as their Prince was given dominion over Israel, the cry of Israel was not heard. Once the Prince of the heights fell, it is written, "And the King of Egypt died," and immediately, "and the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up unto God." Until that hour, they were not answered in their crying. Rabbi Eleazar said: Come and see the mercy of the Holy One, blessed be He; for He has mercy on Israel, He subdues [the enemy] and brings him down and has mercy on them. This is what we have learned: that the Holy One, blessed be He, sheds two tears into the Great Sea. What are these two tears? Rabbi Yose said: It is not a [simple] matter.

It also explains that the Israelites' prayers were only heard after the spiritual "Prince" of Egypt was toppled from his heavenly position.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Exodus (Parashat Shemot). It focuses on the spiritual mechanics of the Exodus, specifically how the cries of the Israelites triggered a shift in the divine realms from Judgment to Mercy, and the downfall of the spiritual "Prince" of Egypt.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And These are the Names**<-

A clear word was revealed to prove to his people that he was a liar and spoke falsehoods. Rabbi Elazar said: Following this, he proved to his people that the portion of the "clear word" is as we have learned: among the ten crowns of the King <note>The Sefirot, or divine attributes</note>, He shed two tears, and these are the two **Attributes of Judgment**. For all their activity is according to Judgment, as it is taught: "Behold, your voices," and how much does **the Holy One, Blessed Be He**, remember? There is no weeping; rather, the Voice brings them down to the Great Sea, which is the **Sea of Wisdom** <note>Yam ha-Chokhmah</note>, to sweeten them. Thus, He turns the **Attribute of Judgment** into the **Attribute of Mercy** and has compassion upon them. Rabbi Yehuda said: "Two tears" is a general term; all tears represent the source of all Judgment.

Rabbi Yehuda said: It is written, *“And behold, Egypt was marching after them”* <margin>Exodus 14:10</margin>. And Rabbi Yitzchak said: This refers to the **Prince of Egypt** <note>The guardian angel or spiritual representative of the nation in the heavenly court</note> and his legions with him. "The King of Egypt" refers specifically to this Prince of Egypt. Rabbi Yitzchak said: This matter seems difficult compared to what was said above. Here it is written, "And behold, Egypt," while elsewhere it is written, "The King of Egypt." This teaches us that now he was no longer a "king," for they had cast him down from his greatness; therefore, it is written "Egypt" and not "the King of Egypt." And regarding what is said, "And he died," this is as in the verse: *“For all the men are dead who sought your life”* <margin>Exodus 4:19</margin>.

Rabbi Yitzchak said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua: All the kings of Egypt were named Pharaoh, yet the text does not always call them by name, but simply "the King of Egypt," and in its place "Pharaoh," for he was the actual Pharaoh. Come and see: there is no authority below unless there is authority above. When the authority above is removed, the authority below is likewise removed.

Rabbi Yossi said: It is written, *“Come, let us deal wisely with him”* <margin>Exodus 1:10</margin>. <unclear>...</unclear> Rabbi Abba said: This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed Be He, executed judgment upon the Prince above. What is written? *“For My sword has drunk its fill in heaven”* <margin>Isaiah 34:5</margin>. Does God possess a physical sword? Rather, Rabbi Yitzchak said: A "sword" is not a literal object, as it is written, "And His sword against all flesh." Rather, the "sword" is the Judgment that ascends, as it is written: *“And David saw the angel of the Lord standing between the earth and the heaven, with a drawn sword in his hand”* <margin>1 Chronicles 21:16</margin>. Was there a physical **drawn sword** in the hand of the angel? Rather, it means that the authorization was written in his hand to execute judgment. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: The Angel of Death said to him, "If I did not cherish the honor of the Creator, I would collect from them the house of visitation." Why? Rabbi Abba said: Whenever the authorization is in his hand to carry out the final judgment, it is called a "drawn sword in his hand"—the permission is written in his hand to perform judgment. If so, why does he return his sword to its sheath? Rabbi Abba said: The judgment returns to the Master of Judgment, and the authority to Him to whom authority belongs.

*“And the children of Israel sighed”* <margin>Exodus 2:23</margin>. It does not say "they sighed" <note>in a simple sense</note>, but "And they sighed," meaning they looked toward the One Above. Their sighing was a cause for the awakening Above. Rabbi Berachiah said: These were the "Children of Israel" from Above <note>a reference to the spiritual source of the souls of Israel</note>. And what is "And the children of Israel sighed"? It refers to those who are called the children of the service, meaning those who were under the bondage Above.

*“And their outcry rose up to God”* <margin>Exodus 2:23</margin>. Until that hour, their outcry had not ascended before Him. Rabbi Yitzchak said: There are three matters here: **Sighing** (*Anacha*), **Outcry** (*Shuah*), and **Wailing** (*Ze'aka*). Each one is distinct from the other. "Sighing" is written: "And the children of Israel sighed." "Groaning" (*Na'aka*) is written: "And they cried out." "Outcry" is written: "And their outcry rose up." Each one is explained individually, and Israel performed them all. Rabbi Yehuda said: They performed groaning and outcry, but they did not perform sighing. It is implied by the text "And they sighed" that it was an awakening of Wisdom. What is the difference between "Wailing" and "Outcry"? Rabbi Yitzchak said: You have no "Outcry" except in prayer, as it is said: "Hear my prayer, O Lord, and give ear to my outcry." "Give ear, O Lord, to my outcry." "I cried out to You and You healed me." "Wailing" is when one screams but says nothing at all. Rabbi Yehuda said...

<summary>This page discusses the mystical mechanics of the Exodus, explaining how the different types of cries from the Israelites (sighing, crying, and wailing) caused a shift in the divine realm from Judgment to Mercy and led to the spiritual downfall of Egypt's heavenly protector.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Exodus (Shemot). The previous section likely concluded the discussion on the bondage in Egypt, transitioning here into the power of prayer and the beginning of Moses's leadership.</meta>

## And These are the Names

It is known that **crying out** <note>Hebrew: *Tze'akah*</note> is greater than all other forms of prayer, for crying out is in the heart, and it is more effective than anything else before the Lord. **Crying out** and **shouting** <note>Hebrew: *Ze'akah*</note>—as it is written: *And he cried out with a great and bitter cry* <note>Esther 4:1</note>—are closer to the Holy One, Blessed be He, than formal prayer or wisdom. For it is written: *And it shall come to pass, when he cries out to Me, that I will hear; for I am gracious* <note>Exodus 22:26</note>. Rabbi Berechiah said: At the hour when the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses: *Why do you cry out to Me?* <note>Exodus 14:15</note>, I knew that I had made Saul king. What is written there? *And Samuel was grieved, and he cried out to the Lord all night* <note>1 Samuel 15:11</note>. Here it is the same.

And it is known that crying out is closer to the Holy One, Blessed be He, than all of them; this is what is written: *And now, behold, the cry of the children of Israel has come to Me* <note>Exodus 3:9</note>. Furthermore, one who weeps and cries out until they are unable to move their lips—this is a **perfect prayer** <note>Aramaic: *Tzelota Shelimta*</note> which is in the heart, and it never returns empty. Rabbi Judah said: Crying out is so great that it tears up a person's [heavenly] decree for their entire life. Rabbi Isaac said: Crying out is so great that it rules over the **Attribute of Judgment** <note>Hebrew: *Middat HaDin*</note> on high. Rabbi Yose said: Crying out is so great that it rules in this world and in the World to Come. Because of crying out, one inherits this world and the next, as it is written: *Then they cried out to the Lord in their trouble, and He delivered them out of their distresses* <note>Psalms 107:6</note>.

---

**And Moses** *was shepherding the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian* <note>Exodus 3:1</note>. Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse: *My beloved is mine, and I am his; he who grazes among the lilies* <note>Song of Songs 2:16</note>. Come and see: the creatures are changing, yet they know that at the hour when the Holy One, Blessed be He, looks upon the whole world, all the worlds arose in **Thought** <note>The mystical level of *Machshavah*</note> and were made into a single creation. Were they not all made with **Wisdom** <note>The Sephirah of *Chokhmah*</note>? And in this Thought, which is Wisdom, He created this world and the world above. He extended His right hand and created the world above; He extended His left hand and created this world which has an end. *My hand has laid the foundation of the earth, and My right hand has spanned the heavens; when I call to them, they stand up together* <note>Isaiah 48:13</note>. They were all created in a single moment. And this world corresponds to the world above; everything that exists above has its likeness below. And everything that exists below has its likeness in the sea and in the dry land, according to the mystery of the upper beings and the kings. He created human beings in this world; He created animals in it—all so that the Holy One, Blessed be He, might be joined together to be One. It is written regarding **Kindness** <note>Hebrew: *Chesed*</note> that in the soul he abandoned kindness, and it is written: *For You have made him a little lower than the angels* <note>Psalms 8:6</note>. The lives of precious human beings are all in subjugation, and they are found from a drop of the male, as we have learned to praise Him. Like the upper beings, and like Israel—to the upper beings He did not call "children," but to the lower beings He called "children," for *You are children to the Lord your God* <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note>. He called them children, and they called Him Father, as it is written: *For You are our Father* <note>Isaiah 63:16</note>, and it is written: *My beloved is mine, and I am his.* He chose me, and I chose Him.

*He who grazes among the lilies*—He shepherds among the lilies <note>The Hebrew *Shoshannim* can mean lilies or roses</note> of the face, whose fragrance surrounds them. And who can shepherd among the lilies like Him? Another interpretation: *He who grazes among the lilies*—just as this lily is red but its water is white, so the Holy One, Blessed be He, guides His world through the **Attribute of Judgment** and the **Attribute of Mercy** <note>Hebrew: *Middat HaRachamim*</note>. And it is written: *Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow* <note>Isaiah 1:18</note>. Rabbi Eleazar was walking among the lilies, and Rabbi Isaac was with him. They rejoiced and went along until they encountered those roses. Rabbi Eleazar took one in his hand. As he was walking, he encountered Rabbi Yose, who said: "Surely the **Divine Presence** <note>Hebrew: *Shekhinah*</note> is here! And I see joy in the hands of Rabbi Eleazar, who teaches pleasant wisdom. For I know that Rabbi Eleazar did not take this [flower] except for the sake of Wisdom."

Rabbi Eleazar said: "Sit, my son, sit." They sat. Rabbi Eleazar said: "The Holy One, Blessed be He, surely sees that the world is sustained only by **scent** <note>Hebrew: *Reyach*</note>. For the strength of the soul is sustained only by scent and by the blood at the entrance of the Sabbath." He opened his discourse and said: *My beloved is mine, and I am his; he who grazes among the lilies.* What caused me to be His and my Beloved to be mine? Because He guides His world with lilies. Just as a lily has scent and is not [only] red but is cleaned to white, and its scent transforms [the heart], so too the Holy One, Blessed be He, guides His world in this way. For if Kindness did not exist even in a small measure, the "bed" would be called "red" without mercy. *Though your sins be as scarlet... they shall be white.*

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the mechanics of atonement, specifically how the physical elements of sacrifice (blood and fat) correspond to divine attributes. It transitions from the conclusion of the previous section into the opening of the Book of Exodus (Parashat Shemot), focusing on the symbolism of Moses as a faithful shepherd.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And These Are The Names**<-

To merit [divine favor], one offers a sacrifice to the Name <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> which is red. One sprinkles the blood around the altar, which is red—representing the Attribute of Justice <note>original: *Midat HaDin*</note>, which is red and burns with judgment. Then the smoke rises entirely white, and thus the judgment in the red is transformed into white; the Attribute of Justice is transformed into the Attribute of Mercy <note>original: *Midat Rachamim*</note>. Come and see: everything that required judgment, if a person [sins], it is as if they [spilled] blood. This is what Judah said: "The hand of the Lord is like a judgment..." until blood is visited upon them. Even the hands of the wicked [are judged], but His right hand is only with kindness. Furthermore, red and white are like the sacrifice of the world; the foul odor of the rising smoke is rectified. Just as the Accuser <note>Satan</note> is red, so too the scent of the sacrifice comes from red and white, strength and mercy. From the scent of the incense—some of its ingredients are red and some are white, such as frankincense which is white and pure myrrh which is red—the scent rises from red and white. Regarding this, He sustains His world in His dwelling, which is red and white. And it is written: *to offer to Me the fat and the blood* (Ezekiel 44:15). Corresponding to this, a person offers their own fat and blood [through fasting] and is atoned for; this is red and this is white. Just as the simple [sacrifice] is red and white, and the fires turn it all white, so too with sin. Now, one who sits in their fast and offers their fat and blood, their palate is parched so as to return entirely white from sin. For Judah said: through a person's fast, their limbs turn red <note>from the heat of hunger</note> and the red prevails over them. At that moment, one must offer their fat and blood like the matter of that place called the Altar of Atonement. This is what Rabbi Eleazar said when he sat in his fast; he would pray and say: "It is revealed and known before You, Lord my God and God of my fathers, that I have offered before You my fat and my blood, and I have heated them through the heat of my body's weakness. May it be that the scent rising from my mouth at this hour be like the scent rising from the sacrifice on the altar fire, and may You accept me." Like whom? Through the kindness of one who offers the fat and blood in their fast, and the scent that rises is the Altar of Atonement. Therefore, the Sages established Prayer in place of the Sacrifice, provided that they focus on what we have said. For we have learned: from the Priest onwards it is written, *everything that passes through fire, you shall pass through fire and it shall be clean* (Numbers 31:23). In the days when the Holy Temple stood, a person would offer their sacrifice in this manner and be atoned for. Now, a person's prayer atones for them in place of the sacrifice, as in this case. This is: *My beloved is mine and I am his, who browses among the lilies* (Song of Songs 2:16). Just as lilies are dyed with colors within them, so the Holy One, blessed be He, leads His world with prophets and the wicked. Just as with lilies, were it not for the thorns, the lilies would not survive; so too, were it not for the wicked, the righteous would not be recognized. For Judah said: how much are the righteous recognized because there are wicked people? For if there were no wicked, the righteous would not be known. This is *He who browses among the lilies*—He who leads His world with goodness... and in the eighth... the Tabernacle of Levi. Another explanation: *among the lilies*—like the repetitions <note>a play on the Hebrew *shoshannim* (lilies) and *shonim* (those who study/repeat)</note> of the Torah.

---

**And Moses** was shepherding the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian (Exodus 3:1). Rabbi Hiyya opened and said:
> A Psalm of David: The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want (Psalms 23:1).

Meaning: The Lord is my shepherd, and I am His sheep. Just as a shepherd leads the flock and brings them to good pasture, to fat pasture, to a place of water streams, and straightens their path with righteousness and justice, so too the Holy One, blessed be He—as it were—*He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside still waters; He restores my soul* (Psalms 23:2-3). Rabbi Jose said: It is the way of shepherds to lead their flocks with righteousness, to keep them far from theft, to bring them into the plain, with the staff in hand so they do not stray right or left. So the Holy One, blessed be He, shepherds Israel to bring them into the plain, and at all times the staff is in His hand so they do not stray right or left. Another explanation: *And Moses was shepherding*—Rabbi Jose said: You should know that as long as the shepherd is wise and [leads] his dog, he is ready to receive the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven. But if the shepherd is a fool, he is called "a snare for the fool." Rabbi Judah said: Moses was wise and expert in leading his flock. In the clarity of... and he led the flock to the wilderness, to teach you...

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of Moses's early life, specifically focusing on his role as a shepherd and his initial encounter with the Divine at the Burning Bush. It corresponds to the Zohar, Exodus (Shemot), Folio 21a.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

From a great power he came, and in the end, because he tended the flock with justice and proper conduct, the Holy One, Blessed be He, crowned him as king over all Israel. And why with sheep and not with cattle? Rabbi Judah said: Israel is compared to sheep, as it is written: *“And you are My sheep, the sheep of My pasture, you are Man”* (Ezekiel 34:31), and it is written: *“As the holy flock, as the flock of Jerusalem.”* Just as the sheep, when one offers it upon the altar, earns for its owner the life of the World to Come, so too the leader of Israel who leads with justice and proper conduct earns for himself the life of the World to Come. Furthermore, regarding one who tends the flock: when the sheep give birth, the shepherd takes the lambs in his bosom so they do not grow weary or exhausted, and he leads them after their mothers and has compassion for them. So too, the leader of Israel must lead them with mercy and not with cruelty. And thus Moses said:
> *“That You should say to me: Carry them in your bosom”* (Numbers 11:12).

And so on. Just as the shepherd of the flock, when he is a good shepherd, saves the flock from wolves and wild beasts, so too the leader of Israel, if he is good, saves them from the idolatrous nations, and from the judgment of below and the judgment of above, and guides them to the life of the World to Come. Thus Moses was a "Faithful Shepherd" <note>Hebrew: *Ra'aya Meheimna*</note>, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to bring him out to kingship over Israel by the merit of the very justice with which he tended the flock—giving to the ewes according to their need and to the young according to their need. Therefore it is written: *“And Moses was tending the flock of Jethro his father-in-law,”* and not just anyone. Rabbi Yose said: Did the one who gave him his daughter separate from him and not give Moses sheep and cattle? Rather, Jethro was a wealthy man, but this is a parable for a man who loved his daughter; so that they would not be burdened, because the flock was with him, he tended his father-in-law's flock well. Therefore it is written *“the flock of Jethro his father-in-law”* and not someone else from Midian. Rabbi Tanchum said: Even though Jethro was an idolater, because he performed acts of kindness for Moses, Moses tended the flock with proper care in a good, fat, and rich pasture.

**And he led** the flock behind the wilderness. Rabbi Yose said: From the day the staff was created, the Holy Spirit <note>Hebrew: *Ruach HaKodesh*</note> never departed from it. The spirit in the heights of holiness was his aspect; the wilderness was prepared to receive the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven upon him. What is the meaning of the verse *“the flock behind the wilderness”*? Rabbi Isaac said: Literally "behind the wilderness" and not *in* the wilderness; he wanted them to enter within it, but they began to distance themselves behind the wilderness.

**And he came** to the mountain of God, to Horeb. Rabbi Judah said: This refers to the merit of receiving the Veil <note>The *Pargod*, the celestial curtain separating the Divine from the lower worlds</note>. When he saw it reaching his level, thus Moses and the [Divine] Glory <note>original: *Yakar*</note> as they ran toward one another, he leaped upon the approach and *“came to the mountain of God, to Horeb.”* Rabbi Hiyya said: The three days of creation were brought together with one another, and their appearance was like a crown <note>original: *targes*</note> facing the staff. Once he saw into its midst, he leaped into it and the mountain stood still. This teaches that they were marvelling at one another and trembled. And Moses knew that this was the mountain of God, Horeb, as it is written: *“And he came to the mountain of God.”* For we have learned: how far was the distance of Moses's level? The mountain was so far that birds that were flying and spreading their wings would not enter... Rabbi Isaac says: The birds would fly far from there and, being impure, would fall at the feet of Moses. Immediately he sensed this and stationed the flock behind the wilderness, and he remained there alone.

**And an angel** of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of the bush. Rabbi Tanchum says: It was the hour of the afternoon prayer <note>Hebrew: *Mincha*</note>, when the Attribute of Justice <note>Hebrew: *Midat HaDin*</note> prevails. Rabbi Yochanan said: It is written *“And he saw,”* and the darkness flees... His kindness, the Attribute of Mercy <note>Hebrew: *Midat HaChesed*</note> is what is meant, and not [Justice]. Rabbi Isaac says: He makes the white frost forgotten until it is late to descend, like the cold of the day, and that is the simple Attribute of Mercy that descends in the cool of the evening. And in the end, what is it? This is what is written:
> *“And God called the light Day”* (Genesis 1:5).

Rabbi Yochanan said: It was the hour of the afternoon prayer, from the decline [of the sun] and downwards. For Rabbi Isaac taught: What is the difference between the evenings? You shall include the flesh, for you have already been subdued by every "between the evenings," for that is the hour of Judgment.

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Book of Exodus (Shemot), focusing on the symbolic relationship between the Patriarchs, the times of prayer, and the divine attributes of Mercy and Judgment.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **And These Are The Names** <-

The night begins to fade into the rest of the day, and it is written: "The eagle ascends between the knife and the leaf." <note>A cryptic Zoharic metaphor for the transition of spiritual forces.</note> The Lord’s anger burned because of your rebelliousness. The power of the Kingdom <term>Malchut: the tenth Sefirah, representing divine sovereignty</term> rules, and "in the morning you shall be filled with bread" <note>Exodus 16:12</note> because that time is called **Chesed** <term>Loving-kindness</term>, which is a shining light. As it is written: "The **Chesed** of God endures all day long," and it is written: "And God called the light Day," which is explained as such. Rabbi Tanchum said: This is red and not white; red is "between the evenings," as it is written: "Between the evenings you shall eat meat," and white is in the morning, as it is written: "And in the morning you shall be filled with bread." <note>Exodus 16:12</note> Regarding the attribute of **Chesed**, it is written: "And the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it," which is the hour of **Chesed**, corresponding to the attribute of the Holy One, blessed be He. Rabbi Judah said: The first light of **Chesed** emerges in the morning, and it is not written "the first light" but rather the light of **Chesed** is established against the attribute of **Chesed**, for in every place where it is mentioned, it says "that it was good." Rabbi Tanchum said: Therefore, Isaac established the Afternoon Prayer <term>Mincha</term> which corresponds to the attribute of the Holy One, blessed be He <note>Here referring to Gevurah/Judgment</note>. And regarding Isaac, from here we learn: "Woe unto us! For the day declines, for the shadows of evening are stretched out." "For the day declines"—this refers to the attribute of **Chesed**. "For the shadows of evening are stretched out"—for the attribute of Judgment has already prevailed. Abraham established the Morning Prayer <term>Shacharit</term> corresponding to the attribute of **Chesed**.

When the light shone, Moses approached Mount Sinai because it was revealed to him in a flame of fire, which is Judgment. Jacob's portion was like the end of the hour. Rabbi Yose says: All of them met and participated as one. It is written: "And he came to the mountain of God," <note>Exodus 3:1</note> where mercies abound. And it is written: "And in the greatness of Your excellency You have overthrown them," and it is written: "And the angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush." <note>Exodus 3:2</note> Out of the "midst," because there they were destined to be in a Sukkah <term>Tabernacle/Booth</term>, as it is written: "He made his pavilion [Sukkah] round about him." Rabbi Judah said: From here we learn His compassion for the wicked; even in a place of the wicked, it is written: "And behold, the bush burned with fire" to execute judgment upon the wicked, "and the bush was not consumed" so as not to make a total end of them. It burned with fire—this is a reference to the fire of **Gehinnom** <term>Purgatory/Hell</term>, but "the bush was not consumed," so that they would not be totally destroyed. Another interpretation:

### And He Appeared
"The Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire." Why "in a flame of fire" and not in His full power? Rabbi Judah said: It was revealed below in a flame of power, for we have learned: whoever approaches fire is burned by it, yet Moses approached the fire and was not burned, as it is written: "And behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed." <note>Exodus 3:2</note> And it is written: "And the angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of the bush." Rabbi Abba said: This matter of Moses cannot be looked upon except through Higher Wisdom. It is written: "Because I drew him out of the water" <note>Exodus 2:10</note>—he who is drawn from the water does not fear the fire. For it was taught: Rabbi Judah said, from the place where Moses was "fired" <note>refined/tempered</note>, no other human was ever "fired." Rabbi Yochanan said: He looked through ten degrees, as it is written: "He is faithful in all My house," <note>Numbers 12:7</note> and not just "faithful in My house." Happy is the portion of the man whose Master testifies thus for him! Rav Dimui said: But is it not written, "And there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses" <note>Deuteronomy 34:10</note>? And Resh Lakish said: "In Israel" none arose, but among the nations one did arise—and who was it? Balaam. He said to him: Certainly you have spoken well. He was silent. When Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai came, they brought this matter before him. He opened and said: The sap of the ground is mixed with balsam to make a paste; but certainly it was so: "none arose [in Israel]," and who was it? Balaam. Moses's works were Above, and Balaam's were below. Moses used the **Holy Crown** <term>Keter Kadisha</term> of the High King Above, while Balaam used the lower crowns that are not holy below. And in exactly that manner it is written: "And Balaam the son of Beor, the soothsayer," who brought near the flesh. And if you wish to know more, go and ask what is found. Rabbi Yose came and covered his hands and said: This is the measure for my garment, and he went outside. For here it is implied that there are higher and lower, right and left, mercy and judgment. Israel and the uncircumcised: [Israel] uses the higher holy crowns, while the worshippers of stars and constellations use the lower crowns that are not holy, between the demons and those there—no. And here they are divided by higher powers and lower stars, by holy powers and by their own powers of holiness. Rabbi Judah said: In the manner that was **Moses**...

<meta>This page concludes the commentary on the Torah portion Shemot (Exodus 1-6:1) and begins the portion Va'era (Exodus 6:2-9:35). It continues the mystical comparison between the prophecy of Moses and other forms of revelation.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Moses was set apart from all other prophets like the high holy assembly <note>original: "Kenesset Ila'ah," referring to a celestial spiritual gathering or the Sefirah of Binah</note>; likewise, Balaam was set apart from the rest of the prophets of the nations like the lower assembly <note>the "Kenesset d'Lattata," often associated with the physical world or the "other side"</note>. In any case, Moses was above and Balaam was below, and many degrees of separation lie between them. Rabbi Isaac said: Moses called out from the mountain <note>likely Mount Sinai</note> and the Lord said to him: "Pity Israel, for they are exhausted by this harsh labor." This is as it is written:
> **"And Moses implored the Lord his God... and said, 'Lord, why does Your anger burn against Your people...'"** (Exodus 32:11)
And the spirit [of God] was appeased regarding the fire burning within you, meaning: they are enslaved in harsh labor, go and set a limit to their days. In general, Israel are meritorious, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, set them apart from all the nations and called them "children," as it is written:
> -> **"You are children of the Lord your God."** (Deuteronomy 14:1) <-

---

-> # Portion of Va'era <-

**And God spoke** to Moses and said to him, "I am the Lord. I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as God Almighty <note>El Shaddai</note>..." (Exodus 6:2-3). Rabbi Hezekiah opened his discourse:
> **"Trust in the Lord forever and ever, for in Yah, the Lord, is an everlasting Rock."** (Isaiah 26:4)
All people of the world should trust in the Lord in order to find strength in Him, the Holy One, Blessed be He, so that His love may be upon them. And if you ask, what is the meaning of "forever and ever" <note>original: "Adei Ad"</note>? It is so that a person's strength shall be in the place that is the sustenance and bond of all. It is called **Ad** <note>literally "Until" or "Witness," here used as a mystical name for the Sefirah of Wisdom</note>, and this is Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>, as it is said:
> **"A path which no bird of prey knows."** (Job 28:7)
And this "Ad" is the place that shows itself to all sides, to guard this and to protect that, to sustain and to bind a bond that shall never pass away. It flows until the very bottom of all; through it, everything exists down to the "everlasting hills" <note>original: "Giv'ot Olam"</note>. These are the springs of the world, and they are two mothers <note>referring to the creative forces</note> and dwellings that search out the world, all of them "from world to world" <note>from eternity to eternity</note>. Truly, each one is called a "world," and these search the everlasting hills, and their foundation is in this **Ad**, the sustenance of all sides. What is the foundation of all? That which is worthy to be crowned by Him, to guard the blessings upon it, and to pour upon it from the ancient springs. This is as it is written:
> **"Go forth, O daughters of Zion, and behold King Solomon with the crown with which his mother crowned him."** (Song of Songs 3:11)
The foundation of the hidden place is to be blessed by Him and to be illuminated by Him, and this is "until the bottom of the everlasting hills." Therefore, "Trust in the Lord forever and ever" <note>Adei Ad</note>, for from that point upward is a place hidden and concealed that cannot be grasped—the place from which the worlds emerge and are formed. This is as it is written, **"For in Yah (Y-H), the Lord, is the Rock of worlds."** This is a place concealed and sealed. Therefore, "Trust in the Lord forever and ever." Up to this point, a person has permission to contemplate; from here onward, a person has no permission to contemplate, for it is hidden from all. And what is **Yah**? It is the Foundation <note>Yesod</note> from which all worlds were formed, and no one can stand upon that place. Rabbi Judah said: The verse itself proves it, as it is written:
> **"For ask now of the days that are past..."** (Deuteronomy 4:32)
Up to here, there is a secret for a person to contemplate; from here onward, there is no one who can stand upon it. "Trust in the Lord forever and ever"—all the days of a person's life, he must find strength in the Holy One, Blessed be He, for so David said:
> **"To You, O Lord, I lift up my soul; O my God, in You I trust..."** (Psalms 25:1-2)
And whoever places his sustenance and strength in Him properly, all the people of the world cannot harm him. For whoever places his strength in the Holy Name is sustained in this world, because the holy world is sustained by Him. This is as it is written: **"For in Yah, the Lord, is the Rock..."**

<summary>This page discusses the unique spiritual status of Moses compared to Balaam and provides a mystical commentary on Isaiah 26:4, explaining the divine name "Ad" as the source of cosmic sustenance and the limits of human contemplation of the Divine.</summary>

<meta>This page translates the Zohar's commentary on the opening of the Torah portion "Va'era" (Exodus 6:2). It continues the mystical exploration of Moses's complaint to God at the end of the previous portion and explains the transition from the divine name of Judgment to the name of Mercy.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And I Appeared**<-

The mountain of the worlds is hidden, for the lower crowns <note>The lower *Sefirot* or divine emanations</note> were gathered together, world upon world, Judgment and the World to Come. She heard it; in purity it was created and upon purity it stands. This is like a ewe in the secret of secrets, bringing forth children who were gathered because of her in purity, so they would not go out to the sword outside. Come and see: **"And God [Elohim] spoke to Moses"** <note>Exodus 6:2</note>—this is the decree of Judgment that stood over him. What is written next? **"And He said to him: I am the LORD [YHWH]."** He came to the level that does not judge, the *Yod* <note>The first letter of the Name YHWH, representing Wisdom</note> from the waters of strength that waters the Torah. In prophecy, not all of His will was in this place. One said:
> "Why have You dealt ill with this people..." <note>Exodus 5:22</note>
And Pharaoh struck after him: "...to speak in Your name, he has done evil to this people; neither have You delivered..."
> "...Your people at all." <note>Exodus 5:23</note>
Who would be so foolish as to say such a thing? Rather, Moses knew that another level was destined to be revealed to him. Rabbi Isaac said: In the Torah that was given to him, it is written that he was appointed like a man who is appointed over his house and says whatever he wishes without fear. Outside, he watches over the watering of his house and is not afraid.
**"And God [Elohim] spoke"**—this is the decree of Judgment. Because of this, **"He said to him: I am the LORD [YHWH]"**—the level of Mercy. And behold, everything is bound together as one, Judgment and Mercy; this is what is written: **"I am the LORD."** Come and see, it is written: **"And God spoke to Moses."** It should have said "The LORD spoke." However, it is written **"And God spoke to Moses"** first, and afterward **"He said to him: I am the LORD,"** to give a taste of level after level. Rabbi Yose said: The watering of the world that turns away from the sharpness of the house—there is service that is done because of what he said, but because of this, he was not punished. Except when he doubled the quarrel in speech and said other words to complain. Since the word was stirred up, the Kingship <note>The *Sefirah* of *Malkhut*</note> was there. The King ceased the word and stood, and she stopped speaking.
The King was revealed, etc. If he had known where the Kingship was, he would have prepared higher words. Not everyone is like this, watering and doing good. Moses said: **"And he said to him: Why have You dealt ill..."** Immediately, **"And God spoke to Moses."** He was foolish to complain. Immediately the King ceased the word and **"He said to him: I am the LORD."** And Moses knew where the King was and prepared higher words.

---

->**And I Appeared**<-

> "And I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, as God Almighty [El Shaddai]..." <note>Exodus 6:3</note>
Rabbi Hezekiah spoke thus of higher matters: Oh, it is like a king who had a daughter who was not yet married, and he appointed a beloved friend for her. When the king wanted to speak with that beloved friend, he would arrange for his daughter to speak with him, and the king would speak with him through his daughter. The time came for his daughter to be married. On the day she was married, the king said: "Call my daughter the Princess, the Matronita <note>A term for the *Shekhinah*, the Divine Presence, as a noble Queen</note>." Until now, I spoke with you as the King's friend; from here on, I am the love of your husband, and he will say what is needed.
Sometimes her husband would say words before the King until he was moved to speak. The King ceased one word for another, and he, the King, came—who until this day had not spoken or gathered with me except through you, my daughter—until she was married. And here: **"And I appeared to Abraham... as God Almighty [El Shaddai]"**—when she was in my house and not yet married, and the wise ones did not speak with me face to face as I do with you. And you, by the authority of the King, I spoke to my daughter before me with higher words. Because of this: **"And I appeared to Abraham... as God Almighty, but by My name LORD [YHWH] I was not known to them"**—to speak with them in this level that I speak with you. Rabbi Yose opened:
> "A Psalm of David. The earth is the LORD’s, and the fullness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein." <note>Psalms 24:1</note>
"The earth"—this is the Holy Land of Israel, which stands to be prepared from Him and to be blessed from Him first, and afterward the whole world is prepared from it. "The world and they that dwell therein"—these are the other lands that are nourished from it, from everything. For it is written:
> "And He shall judge the world in righteousness [Tzedek]." <note>Psalms 9, 9</note>
"For He has founded it upon the seas, and upon..." <note>Psalms 24:2</note>

->the rivers<-

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the divine names and the levels of prophecy. It specifically addresses the transition from the revelation given to the Patriarchs to the higher revelation granted to Moses, using the symbolism of the Sefirot (divine emanations).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The seven pillars of the earth are supported by them, and these are the seven seas, and the Sea of Galilee <note>original: "Yam Kinneret"</note> rises above them. <note>Refers to the seven lower Sefirot and the Malchut (the feminine divine presence)</note>
Rabbi Judah said: Do not say that it rises above them, but rather that it is below them, as it is written, "And He established it upon the rivers." And
what are these rivers? They are all the holy rivers of His name, and these rivers within it are all proper,
and "a river goes out from Eden to water the garden," and because of this, "He established it upon the rivers." Come and see: Abraham,
Isaac, and Jacob are the foundation of the earth, yet each one did not rule individually, for it is written: "And I appeared <note>original: "Va'era"</note> to Abraham, to
Isaac, and to Jacob" as *El Shaddai* <note>God Almighty</note> and no more. However, Jacob established everything as a reflection below,
and from him the House above was perfected. And through the House below, the House above was established with twelve
boundaries and seventy branches, and this is the establishment. What supports the House above? Ultimately, the House below.
And regarding Jacob it is written: "with *El Shaddai*." With *El Shaddai* the Holy One, blessed be He, spoke with him and no more. "But by My name *YHVH* <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> I was not known
to them"—to speak with them in this degree which is above them.

**"And I appeared** <note>original: "Va'era"</note> to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob." Rabbi Hiyya said: This is a wonder of wisdom.
Jacob was the perfection of them all, yet for all of them it is written "to <note>Hebrew: "el"</note> Abraham, to Isaac."
But for the child <note>Jacob</note> there is an extra letter, as it is written "and to <note>Hebrew: "ve-el"</note> Jacob."
The letter *Vav* <note>meaning "and"</note> was added to him to show that he is a greater perfection than all of them. And despite all this, he did not merit to use it <note>the higher Name</note> as was fitting. "And I have also established My covenant with them
to give them the land of Canaan," because they were circumcised; for whoever is circumcised inherits the land, as the
land is only inherited by a "Righteous One" <note>term: Tzadik - the Sefira of Yesod</note>, and whoever is circumcised is called "Righteous," as it is written: "And Your people are all righteous, they shall
inherit the land forever." Whoever is circumcised and guards this sign of the covenant is called "Righteous." Come and see: Joseph
was not called "Righteous" all his days until he guarded that holy sign of the covenant; once he guarded it, he was called
"Joseph the Righteous." Rabbi Shimon was sitting one day and Rabbi Eleazar his son was with him. Rabbi Eleazar said:
Look at the verse that is written: "And I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob," etc. What is "And I appeared" <note>original: "Va'era"</note>?
And he mentioned it to him. Rather, it is to awaken the supernal spirit. Come and see the colors that are seen,
and there are colors that are not seen, and these are the supernal spirit of faith, and because of all this, they do not know Him
nor gaze upon Him, and they are established; they did not merit them until the wise came and stood upon them.
And regarding this it is written "And I appeared," for he saw those colors that are revealed, and which colors are revealed? They are *El Shaddai*,
which are colors in a supernal mirror, and these are seen. But the colors above are hidden and are not seen; no one
stood upon them except for Moses. And regarding this it is written: "But by My name *YHVH* I was not known to them"—I was not revealed to them
in the supernal colors. And if you say that the wise did not know them, even though they are those that are revealed,
it is written: "And the wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament, and those who turn many to righteousness as the stars forever and ever." "And the wise
shall shine." Who are the wise? They are the sages who contemplate on their own things that a human
cannot speak with the mouth, and these are called "the wise." "They shall shine as the brightness of the firmament"—what is the "brightness of the firmament"? This
is the firmament that reaches and stands in its perception, and in this brightness it is hidden and not revealed, and it stands upon
that firmament in which colors are seen. And those colors are outside, to be seen in it, but not the brightness like the brightness
of those hidden colors. Come and see that at the time when those three colors are hidden and one is revealed,
it is like a brightness that is doubled, like the brightness of radiance, and those lights are like the brilliance of a sapphire that is pure and flies to its degree, and this
is what nullifies all lights. Like a brightness that does not shine, it gazes toward these, and those lights are seen
in the mountains, a precise depth toward where it reaches. And these three that we mentioned are hidden and stand upon this
which is revealed.

<note>Handwritten note in a Sefardic/Italian cursive hand: This note explains that the "colors" represent the different ways God's light is filtered through the Sefirot. While the Patriarchs perceived God through the "revealed colors" of the name *El Shaddai* (associated with the Sefira of Yesod and the physical world), Moses achieved a higher state of prophecy, perceiving the "hidden colors" of the name *YHVH* (Tiferet), which represents a more direct, unmediated divine light.</note>

It also emphasizes the connection between the Sefira of Yesod (Righteousness), the covenant of circumcision, and the merit of inheriting the Land of Israel.</summary>

--- Page 50 ---
<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Va'era (Exodus 6:2). It focuses on the distinction between the prophetic visions of Moses and the Patriarchs, using the metaphor of the "luminous" and "non-luminous" mirrors. It then transitions into the creation of Man from the four elements.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Va'era (And I Appeared)**<-

...that was overcome. And this spirit <note>referring to the visual spirit of the eye</note> is poor in its vision, containing colors that are engraved and marked within it, yet they do not shine because they stand like that which does not illuminate. These are like the hidden things that stand over them; they are what appear as a covering to know those hidden things that shine from within those that do not shine. Those that shine and are hidden are revealed to the body like its own firmament. These stand over those colors that appear in the "poor" vision. This spirit closes the eye according to the movement of the eyeball, and those shining colors are revealed and appear over those colors that appear but do not shine. Regarding this, we call them **Staff** <note>Hebrew: *Mateh*</note> and **Thus** <note>Hebrew: *Koh*</note>, like a luminous mirror <term>Aspaklaria de-Nahara: a clear lens of prophecy</term> that stands over that which does not shine. The children of the world go around that which does not shine. We find that there were appointees within six colors that were formed, and they are hidden, standing over those that do not shine. Regarding this, it is written:
> And I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as God Almighty [El Shaddai], but by My name, the Lord [YHWH], I was not known to them. <note>Exodus 6:3</note>

These are the supernal, hidden colors that Moses was privileged to gaze upon, because the spirit of the eye is both closed and revealed. It is closed from the aspect of the luminous mirror, and revealed from the aspect of the non-luminous mirror <term>Aspaklaria de-la Nahara: a dim lens of prophecy</term>. Therefore, **"And I appeared"** refers to the non-luminous mirror, where the word "vision" <note>Hebrew: *Re'iyah*</note> is written. Regarding the luminous mirror, the word "knowledge" <note>Hebrew: *Yedi'ah*</note> is used, as it is written: **"I was not known."** Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Abba approached and kissed his hands. Rabbi Abba wept and said, "Woe, when you depart from the world, the world will be left an orphan without you; who will be able to illuminate the words of the Torah?" Rabbi Abba opened his discourse and said:
> And thus shall you say to him that liveth: "Peace be both unto thee, and peace be to thy house, and peace be unto all that thou hast." <note>1 Samuel 25:6</note>

"And thus shall you say to him that liveth" <note>original: *v'amartem koh le-chai*</note>—did David not know at all the "Living One" who is called Life, that he had to say "Thus to the Living One"? Rather, that day was the day of **"Thus"** <note>referring to the Divine attribute of Malchut/Koh</note>, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, sat in judgment over the world. Therefore, he said "Thus to the Living One" facing "Thus," for all life depends upon it. **"And peace be unto thee."** Why "And thou" <note>Hebrew: *Ve-Atah*</note>? This seems to be addressing him directly. Rather, he said it all correspondingly, to face the "Faith" <note>the Shekhinah</note> as is proper. From here we learn that a person should speak to a male <note>the masculine aspect of the Divine</note> when the Altar is ready to offer him peace. And "Life" must be offered first, as David did, blessing him correspondingly, appearing to speak in his favor. You might say "Life" was far off? No. For all things that ascend to Him are corresponding, and it appears he spoke in his favor; "To the Living One" is not distant. Whoever offers peace to the righteous, it is as if he offered it to the Holy One, for the Master of Life is Peace above and below.

->**Va'era (And I Appeared)**<-

Rabbi Hezekiah opened:
> Happy is the man unto whom the Lord imputeth not iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile. <note>Psalms 32:2</note>

How many people are "blocked" <note>spiritually deaf/insensitive</note>, not knowing or observing upon what they stand in the world! For when the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world, He made Man in His own image <term>Dyokan: Divine form</term> and established him with proper arrangements. For when Adam was created, he was formed from the dust of the Sanctuary below, and the four directions of the world were joined in that place. Those four directions of the world joined like four crowns which are the foundation of the world: Fire, Air, Water, and Earth. They joined in the four directions of the world, and from them, the Holy One, Blessed be He, prepared one body of supernal arrangement. This body was joined from two worlds: from this lower world and from the world above. Rabbi Shimon said: Come and see, there are four primary mysteries of the Faith. They are the "Patriarchs" of all the worlds. And the spirit of the supernal holy ancient one—they are Fire, Air, Water, and Earth. These are supernal, and these are the Patriarchs of all the worlds to oversee everything. From them emerge gold, silver, copper, and iron, and beneath these...

## Main Text (Zohar)

These are found to be types that resemble them in this manner: **Come and see**, Wind <note>Ruach: also translated as Air or Spirit</note>, Water, and Earth are the primary ones and the foundations of above and below; and the lower and upper beings stand upon them. These correspond to the four directions of the world and stand as these four: North, South, East, and West. These are the four sides of the world and they stand as these four: Fire <note>original: אשא (Asha)</note> to the side of the North; Wind to the side of the East; Water to the side of the South; and Earth to the side of the West. These four are bound as those four, and they are all one. And these produced four types corresponding to them: Gold, Silver, Copper, and Iron. Behold, they are twelve, and they are all one.

**Come and see**, Fire is found at the side of the North, for Fire has the strength of heat within it. And because it is strong, its opposite emerges from it: cold and <unclear>darkness</unclear> together as one, and it is Fire. Water is to the right and goes to the side of the South. And to balance them, He made this vessel in this manner: North is cold and lacks heat, and it joins them toward the side of the South. South is hot and calm. Water is cold, and therefore He balanced and mixed them as one. Water emerges from the South and makes its dwelling in the North, and from them the brain is formed. Fire emerges from the North and goes with the strength of the South, and from the South the strength of heat emerges to the world. Because the Holy One, Blessed be He, strengthened this one with that one, and each one holds onto its fellow as is fitting for it. In this manner, Wind and East [are paired], because each joins its fellow to be created and to be included one in the other, to be united as one.

**Come and see**, Fire is from this side, and Water is from that side, and they were in conflict <note>original: מחלוקת (Machloket)</note>, until the Wind came and took hold of both sides. This is what is written:
> And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters.
<note>Genesis 1:2</note>
For behold, Fire is thin and sent to this side, and Water stands upon the face of the earth. The Wind entered between them and took hold of both sides and separated the conflict. Earth stands upon it, and the Wind is found and received from all of them like a bride <note>or "vessel"</note> of these three that stand upon her. **Come and see**, and the East: the East is hot and moist. Wind is cold and moist from the side that it properly takes hold
<column-break/>
of Fire. From the side that is cold, it takes hold of the Wind and maintains a balance between them, separating the conflict of Fire and Water. Earth is cold and dry, and for this reason, it receives all of them upon itself, and all of them perform their work through it. It receives from all of them to bring forth through their power sustenance for the world. Because the West is associated with Earth, which is cold and dry, like the North which is cold and moist—for cold is associated with cold. Likewise, Copper is associated with the West, like the side of the South which is hot and dry; in that dryness of its own, it takes hold of the dryness of the West like the side of Fire. Thus the West is joined on two sides. And so the South is associated with the East, for the heat of the South is associated with it like the heat of the East. And the East is associated with the North, for its moisture is associated with the moisture of the North. Now it is found that there is South-East, East-North, North-West, and West-South. And they are all included one in the other to be perfected as one. The North produces Fire; from the side of the strength of Fire, Gold is made. And this is what is written:
> Out of the north comes golden splendor.
<note>Job 37:22</note>
Fire is associated with Earth to make Gold, and this is what is written:
> And it has dust of gold.
<note>Job 28:6</note>
This Wind <unclear>melts</unclear> and Gold [is formed]. Water is associated with Earth, and the coldness in its moisture makes Silver. Now Earth is associated with two sides, with Gold and with Silver, and is placed between them, and the Wind takes hold to return...

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the elements and their relationship to the physical world and the soul. It follows the previous discussion on the creation of the material world from spiritual foundations.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> Leviticus <-

A flame goes forth and emerges, appearing like the color of burnished copper <note>original: *nechoshet kalal*; see Ezekiel 1:7</note>. And the **dust** <note>The element of Earth</note> of which we spoke, its nature is to be subdued and cold, and it produces iron; it is red in hue like iron, etc. <note>Ezekiel 1:4</note>. And this dust is joined with all the other elements, and they all act upon it according to their own colors and qualities. Come and see: **Dust** contains within it the potential for gold, silver, and copper; each one is grasped by the other to be bound together, and the dust is unified with them all because it is held by two sides. **Fire** and **Air** <note>or Spirit; original: *rucha*</note> draw near to it because these two ascend and perform their work within it. It is found that when the dust is joined with the heat of the flame, it works and gives birth to other "dusts" <note>minerals/metals</note> according to their own likeness. In the likeness of fire, it gives birth to a red-green dust which is exactly like the appearance of gold. In the likeness of silver, it gives birth to lead. In the likeness of copper, it gives birth to tin <note>original: *kasitra*</note> which is like copper but better. In the likeness of iron, it gives birth to iron, and your sign for this is: "Iron sharpens iron" <note>Proverbs 27:17</note>.

Come and see: **Water** and dust are all grasped one in the other and bound together, never truly separated. And the dust alone gives birth, but afterwards they are not bound together by heat without a body and fruit <note>referring to the alchemical process of formation</note>. Because this dust, when it gives birth through the power of the three elements above it, it brings forth four rivers, and there are found precious stones and one pure gold, as it is written: "There is the bdellium and the onyx stone" <note>Genesis 2:12</note>. And these precious stones are twelve, and they are the thirty-six sides of the world <note>referring to the 36 hidden righteous ones or cosmic directions</note> corresponding to the twelve tribes, as it is written: "And the stones shall be according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve according to their names" <note>Exodus 28:21</note>. And these are the twelve oxen that were beneath the molten sea <note>The large basin in Solomon's Temple; 1 Kings 7:25</note>.

Come and see: the four supernal sides <note>the four elements/archangels</note> of which we spoke are knotted one to another, and they stand above and below as the foundation of the world. But **Air/Spirit** is the most essential, for everything exists because of it. The soul <note>original: *nefesh*</note> cannot stand except through the Spirit <note>original: *rucha*</note>; for if the Spirit is withdrawn for even a single moment, all is consumed and cannot exist. And regarding this Spirit, it is written: "The Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil" <note>Genesis 2:9</note>. "Good" is when it is filled with Spirit; without Spirit, it is not good and cannot endure.

And come and see: the twelve stones we mentioned are the twelve oxen beneath the sea. Therefore, they are all twelve, as in "all the oxen for the burnt offering were twelve..." <note>Numbers 7:87</note>. And the Spirit is over them all. Whoever gazes into these matters will know through the spirit of Supernal Wisdom <note>original: *chokhmata ila'ah*</note> that the root of everything is within it. And this is the secret that Rabbi Eleazar said: When the **Holy One, Blessed Be He** <note>original: *Kadosh Baruch Hu*</note> created Adam from the dust of the Sanctuary <note>the Temple site</note> which is called "below," he was found to be from the dust of the Sanctuary that is "above." He placed a soul <note>original: *nishmata*</note> within him. Just as when he was created from the dust below, three sides of the world's elements were found in him, so too when he was created above, the three sides of the world's elements were found in him and gathered as one. And this is what is written: "The mercies of the Lord are not consumed, for they do not fail" <note>Lamentations 3:22</note>.

**Therefore** <note>original: *Lachen*</note> say to the children of Israel: "Therefore... I will bring you out" <note>Exodus 6:6</note>. Rabbi Judah said: This verse is an opening, as it is written: "I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians" first. And afterwards: "I will deliver you from their bondage." And afterwards: "I will redeem you." Should it not have said "I will redeem you" at the very beginning and then "I will bring you out"? Rather, the root of everything is that at first, the **Holy One, Blessed Be He** wanted to announce to them the consolation of everything at the start. And the end of it all is: "I will take you to Me for a people, and I will be to you..."

## The Faithful Shepherd

**And I will take** you to me for a people, and I will be to you a God, and you shall know that I am the Lord your God, etc. <note>Exodus 6:7</note>. This is the first commandment of all commandments. It is the primary authority of all commandments: to know the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: Kudsha Brich Hu</note>, as a general principle. To know that there is a supreme Ruler who is the Master of worlds, and He created all worlds, heaven and earth and all their hosts. And this is as a general principle. And at the end of everything, as a particular principle, to know Him in particular and in general. And these [principles] and the end are the mystery of Male and Female <note>original: Dechar ve-Nukba; referring to the union of divine attributes</note>. And "with you" <note>referring to the Hebrew word 'etchem'</note> is only when one strives in that which is occupied with the general and the particular; in this world, it is general and particular. The restoration of this world is through the general and the particular, because it is shown that everything is for the purpose of knowing that we have a Ruler and a Judge, and He is the Master of all worlds. He created the body and that which is distinct, and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life. And this is all within the general outline.

When Israel went out of Egypt, they did not know the Holy One, blessed be He. Once this first commandment came to them, it taught them, as it is written: *And you shall know that I am the Lord your God who brings you out...* <note>Exodus 6:7</note>. Had it not been for this commandment, Israel would not have endured through all those miracles and mighty deeds that He performed for them in Egypt. Once they knew this commandment in its general outline, miracles and mighty deeds were performed for them. And the end of the letter *He* <note>The final letter of the Tetragrammaton, associated with the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> is that they should strive in all those commandments of the Torah. He taught them from between those things that are conducted as one, and those that are conducted outside of the boundary. Then He taught them as a specific engraving, for "and you shall know Him" and "you shall know in your heart."

<note>The following section contains highly compressed Kabbalistic abbreviations and phonetic Rashi script variations typical of the Mantua/Cremona printings</note>

For the Lord is the God of gods, as a specific engraving. How many mysteries and secrets are hidden here. And the first knowledge is entirely from the side of the general and not the particular. And if you say that it is written "And I will take" <note>Ve-laqachti</note>, this implies knowledge as a specific engraving, to know the Living King. And this knowledge is not for every person to contemplate until he knows. And here it is written "to know," to know Him, for there is the knowledge to know Him as a specific engraving. Therefore, the first commandment is to know the Holy One, blessed be He, in general and in particular, in the beginning and in the end. And this is "to see" and "to do." "To see" in general and "to do" in particular. And everything is in the general.

But once one knows Him in general, one must know Him in all the "limbs" <note>original: shayfin; referring to the parts of the Divine Chariot or the human form</note>. And these are the 248 commandments <note>term: Ramach Pekudin; the 248 positive commandments corresponding to the 248 limbs of the human body</note> which are the 248 limbs. For once a person contemplates them in general, then he will know in a specific way that there is no equality in all of them. He will know all the days that are calculated to bring healing to all the limbs. And so it is above and below. And He is destined to establish and give healing to all limbs of the world at the time when the limbs are refined before the Lord. Then healing and life depend upon them, and they shall not move and they shall not depart from the King.

So it is also below: when a man perfects his body with those commandments shown to him, then all his days he comes to contemplate Him. And when they are blessed by Him, then life and healing hang upon him from above. From there, He reveals to them the Lord, the Lord... they are one, just as they are blessed from the Supernal mystery.

<summary>This page discusses the first of all commandments: the obligation to know God in both a general sense (as Creator) and a specific sense (through the 248 positive commandments). It links the redemption from Egypt to this foundational knowledge and compares the commandments to the limbs of a body that receive divine healing.</summary>

<meta>This page transitions from the general mystical significance of the human form and the commandments into a specific discourse on the opening of Parashat Va'era. It explores the metaphysical reasons for Moses' speech impediment as a reflection of the Divine Speech being in exile.</meta>

# Va'era
## (And I Appeared)

-> And I Appeared <-

...to be blessed from below through the mystery of "Man" <note>Adam</note>. All of these are the foundation in this world for the sake of the commandments of the Torah, which are called "Man," as it is written: *You are called men* <note>Babylonian Talmud, Yevamot 61a</note>. You are called "Man," <term>and not</term> the idolaters. Because Israel is called "Man," they must be rectified through those commandments of the Torah to make everything one within the mystery of "Man." When the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave the Torah to Israel on Mount Sinai, the first word was *I* <note>Anochi</note>; my palate rises to the supernal mysteries. And here lies the mystery of the first commandment: to know Him in a general sense, as it is written, *And my palate...* <note>referring to the sweetness of Divine knowledge</note>. The "Voice" alludes to the Living Creature <note>Chayah</note> that took the supernal dominion, which is the first commandment as a general principle. Specifically, because it is written: <quote>I am the Lord</quote> <note>Exodus 6:2</note>, this is the specific detail of the first commandment which one must know clearly and fundamentally, as we have established. Until here. <margin>Until here.</margin>

**And he spoke** <note>Moses</note> thus to the children of Israel, but they did not listen to Moses because of <term>shortness of breath</term> <note>Exodus 6:9</note> and hard labor. Rabbi Yehuda said: It was because they were not submissive or at ease due to the knots of the spirit. Rabbi Shimon said: "Because of shortness of breath" means that the <term>Jubilee</term> <note>The Sephirah of Binah, representing liberation</note> had not yet bent down to bring out their souls and the spirit behind them; it had not yet gained the authority to act in its days, and thus there was a constriction of the spirit. And who is this "latter spirit" we mentioned? Come and see, it is written: <quote>Behold, the children of Israel have not listened to me; how then shall Pharaoh listen to me, for I am of uncircumcised lips?</quote> <note>Exodus 6:12</note>. What does <term>I am of uncircumcised lips</term> mean? For previously it was written: <quote>I am not a man of words... for I am heavy of mouth and heavy of tongue</quote> <note>Exodus 4:10</note>. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, answered him: <quote>Who gave a mouth to man?</quote> <note>Exodus 4:11</note> etc. Yet here he says, "I am of uncircumcised lips." This implies the "Mouth" was not assisted <unclear>to speak</unclear>. If so, was Moses trying to contradict the Holy One, Blessed be He, who had previously reassured him? Rather, the "Spirit" comes from the side of the "Voice," and <term>Speech</term> <note>The Sephirah of Malchut</note>—which is the Word—was in exile. It was blocked from expressing words. Therefore, Moses argued: "How will Pharaoh hear me as long as my Word is in his exile?" For he had no "Word" <note>articulate speech</note>; he felt the lack of the Word because it was in captivity. Therefore, the Voice was silenced from expressing itself through the Breath.

Come and see: whenever "Speech" is in exile, the "Voice" is withdrawn from it and the Word is incomplete. Without the Voice, everything comes from the lower side. The Voice and the Word were both in exile. As long as Speech was in exile, the Voice remained a voice without articulate speech. This continued until they approached Mount Sinai and the Torah was given. At that time, the Voice was united with Speech, and then the Word spoke. This is what is written: <quote>And God spoke all these words</quote> <note>Exodus 20:1</note>. Then the Word was found to be perfect, as is fitting—Voice and Speech together in perfection. Because of this, Moses complained that the Word was lacking from him while it was in exile. But when he spoke to complain at the time it is written, *Since I came to Pharaoh to speak in Your name, he has done evil to this people,* immediately <quote>God spoke to Moses</quote>.

Come and see that this is the way of the Word: to speak and then pause. Because the time had not yet arrived for that which is written, <quote>And God spoke</quote> <note>in full revelation</note>, the Word paused and was hidden. This is what is written: <quote>And He said to him, I am the Lord</quote> <note>Exodus 6:2</note>. Because Speech was in exile, the time to speak fully had not yet come. And come and see: for this reason, Moses was not "complete" at first, for it was ordained that he be the "Voice" <note>Tiferet</note> who strives for "Speech" <note>Malchut</note> to bring it out of exile. Once it emerged from exile and Voice and Speech were united as one at Mount Sinai, Moses was perfected, and Voice and Speech were established together. Come and see: all the time that Moses was by himself trying to bring the Word out of exile, the Word did not speak. Once it emerged from exile, that Voice which is Speech turned and spoke to Israel. But it did not speak fully until they approached Mount Sinai and he opened with the Torah, as is proper. And if you say that Shalom ben Yitzchak <note>likely a scribal or student reference</note> said 119, it does not say "He spoke" <note>Dibur</note> but "He said" <note>Amirah</note>, which refers to the will of the heart, as we have established.
