<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Va'era (Exodus 6). It focuses on the transition from the revelation given to the Patriarchs to the higher revelation given to Moses, specifically exploring the divine names and the sanctity of the Covenant.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Va'era (And I Appeared)**<-

**And God spoke** to Moses and said to him, "I am the Lord" <note>Hebrew: YHVH</note>. Rabbi Yehuda opened the discussion with the verse: *I rose to open for my beloved, but my beloved had turned away and was gone...* <note>Song of Songs 5:5-6</note>. Come and see: the Assembly of Israel <note>The *Knesset Yisrael*, representing the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> experiences all the expressions of love from the Holy One, blessed be He, for she clings to Him and He clings to her. And we have learned: what is meant by *my beloved had turned away and was gone*? It means He was not to be found in His usual dwelling or in His commands; the entire matter and the Divine speech had withdrawn. There was a pause and a silence. Afterward, the Holy One, blessed be He, returned and said to Moses: *I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as God Almighty* <note>Hebrew: El Shaddai</note>, *but by My name "The Lord" I was not known to them* <note>Exodus 6:3</note>. This was due to the "pressure" and "concealment" of Wisdom. All of these—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—were found within that pressure. Because of the concealment of Wisdom, all of them—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—were found at a single level, as it is written: *I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as God Almighty.* It does not say "I said to them, 'I am the Lord.'" Here it is written that He appeared to them as *El Shaddai* <note>God Almighty</note>, for He was not revealed to them through the Name <note>YHVH</note>. This was because it was not yet fitting while Jacob was alive; He joined Jacob [to the others], and even when he died—for as long as a person is alive in this world, the Holy Shekhinah <note>Divine Presence</note> does not rest upon them [in that specific way]—therefore He joined him with Isaac. Now that Jacob had died, the whole matter stood in its fulfillment, as it is written: *I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, **and** to Jacob*—with the addition of the letter "and" <note>The Hebrew letter Vav, signifying a connection to a higher spiritual flow</note>. In all of these, I did not seal them with the "weapon" <note>A metaphor for a specific level of divine power</note> in which they were found as she is. Nor did I seal them from within the "Luminous Mirror" <note>The *Aspaklaria HaMe'irah*, a term for the highest level of prophecy, unique to Moses</note>. And come and see: they were perfected in life as was proper and no more. Come and see that they are never separated, for they stand in their levels as a seal, for the Covenant <note>Brit</note> is with them. They receive a person to accompany them, for the Holy One, blessed be He, is theirs, as it is written: *I also established My covenant with them* <note>Exodus 6:4</note>, in order to maintain existence in a single unity. *I also established My covenant with them*—it has been said: whoever merits the Covenant inherits the Land. Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yose were present one day before Rabbi Shimon.

**Rabbi Shimon** opened and said: *Be afraid of the sword, for wrath brings the punishment of the sword, that you may know there is a judgment* <note>Job 19:29</note>. The word for "judgment" <note>Shaddun</note> is written [alluding to the name Shaddai]. *Be afraid of the sword*—what is this "sword"? This is the "sword that executes the vengeance of the covenant" <note>Based on Leviticus 26:25</note>. For this sword is difficult to behold for one who is false to the Covenant. For anyone who is false to the Covenant, vengeance upon vengeance is taken from him by this sword, as it is written: *for wrath brings the punishment of the sword.* What is the reason? Because one who is false to the Covenant blemishes his repentance and does not remember the One who guards [him], and does not give to his [spiritual] level, for he does not awaken toward his level. But anyone who guards this Covenant causes that Covenant to be awakened toward its level. Then the worlds are blessed, both the upper and the lower. Whoever awakens this Covenant toward its level: all are found to be righteous in the world. From where do we know this? From here, as it is written: *I also established My covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings* <note>Exodus 6:4</note>. What is meant by *their sojournings* <note>Hebrew: Megureihem</note>? It is as you say: *Be afraid* <note>Goru</note> *of the sword.* Because it is a place of fear <note>Dachilu</note> and "sojourning" <note>Gor</note> in the world. Therefore: *Be afraid of the sword.* They returned and "sojourned" in it. From this, they were found before the Holy One, blessed be He, in fear—both a lower fear and a higher fear—to keep His commandments. For the Holy One, blessed be He, hints upon hints that a person should fear the Holy One, blessed be He, forever. Come and see: through the "Awakening from Below" <note>Human initiative or prayer</note>, when Israel awakens toward the Holy One, blessed be He, and remembers—what is written? *And I have remembered My covenant* <note>Exodus 6:5</note>. When it concerns the Covenant, there is "remembrance." And then they are found to be crowned, everything in one bond. Once this Covenant is awakened, the bond of all is awakened. *And I have remembered My covenant*—to pair it with its level. And therefore: *Say therefore to the children of Israel, "I am the Lord."*

**And the Lord spoke** to Moses and to Aaron, and gave them a charge to the children of Israel and to Pharaoh, king of Egypt <note>Exodus 6:13</note>. They established this: He said to the children of Israel to lead them gently, as is proper.

<summary>This page discusses the transition from the Patriarchs' perception of God as 'El Shaddai' to the higher revelation of the name 'YHVH' given to Moses. It emphasizes the spiritual power of the Covenant (Brit) and the 'Sword of Justice' that guards it.</summary>

# Va'era

->**And I Appeared**<-

And as for Pharaoh, no honor entered into him to raise him up. Rabbi Yose said: To what is this comparable? Is it not like the authority of a synagogue? Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: "Remember now the children of Israel, in how much distress they dwell in hard labor; they are kings, the sons of kings." **These are the heads of their fathers' houses**—this refers to the lineage of their fathers' houses. Rabbi Hiyya said: All of them guarded their customs <note>original: "nimuseihon" - laws or social customs</note> and did not intermingle with other nations. These are the ones who stood by their holy merit and did not look to mingle with the Egyptians. 

Rabbi Isaac said: Because the midwives were below and were honored, we see that from there they were brought out to the Side Above. Regarding Pharaoh, he was skipped over from the path because in all the shouting <note>or "stirring"</note> of Israel, none were found like them, Heaven forbid. And regarding the zeal of Phinehas <note>Cf. Numbers 25:7-11 regarding Phinehas</note>, he took for himself, and in the weeping of Phinehas, he took fire and gave... **these are the heads of the fathers of the Levites.** And then, when they were found, it was all for mercy, except that Phinehas stood with many faces and will from the Side, and he stood for the heads of the fathers so that the matter would be written concerning him. **And Eleazar took him a wife... and she bore him Phinehas; these are the heads of the fathers of the Levites.** This is to show what was found in him, and how they were diminished and enslaved, yet the spirit was within him, and he gained their priesthood and the spirit within it. For the departure of the two of them <note>Nadab and Abihu</note> was a loss to the heads of the Levites that was found in him. And who were they? Nadab and Abihu. They separated from the other establishment, and he came and repaired them. Because of this, the inheritance of both of them was given to him. And this is mentioned here for what would happen later. 

And come and see what is mentioned here regarding Phinehas: the Holy One, Blessed be He, saw to honor him according to the thought that said:
> **"And I have remembered My covenant"** (Exodus 6:5)

For the two sons of Aaron were destined to damage this covenant, and he arranged it to know the strength that was made for him. Once they died, Phinehas acted piously and established this covenant, as the translation says, and he straightened their crookedness. Immediately, **"This is that Aaron and Moses."** The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Aaron that he should be first.
> **"This is that Aaron and Moses, to whom the Lord said: 'Bring out the children of Israel...'"** (Exodus 6:26)

**This is that Aaron and Moses.** Behold, Aaron and Moses are equal here. Rather, it is to include this one like that one, as if they were one. **"This is that Moses and Aaron"**—to include the strength in the spirit, and regarding this it is written "This is" <note>singular</note> and not "These are" <note>plural</note>. 

Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Hakha were present one night at the inn of Usfinia. They rose to labor in the Torah. Rabbi Eleazar opened and said:
> **"Know this day, and lay it to your heart, that the Lord He is God"** (Deuteronomy 4:39)

Is this how the verse should be? It should have said: "Know this day that the Lord He is God, and lay it to your heart." Rather, blessed is the portion of one who labors in the Torah. Come and see: "And lay it to your heart" is required. Rather, Moses said: "See, you need to stand upon this and to know that the Lord He is God, and lay it to your heart, and then you will know Him." **Your heart** refers to the <term>Good Inclination and Evil Inclination</term> <note>original: "Yetzer Tov and Yetzer Ra"</note> which are included one in the other to become one. Then you will find that the Lord is God, for they are included as one and He is one. And regarding this, "lay it to your heart" to know the matter. 

Furthermore, Rabbi Eleazar said: The sinners create a separation above. See, the inwardness of the spleen is not included in the Right. And the Evil Inclination is not included in the Good Inclination because of the sins of the sons of men. And they do not cause a blemish except to themselves, truly... as if it were possible, they act and do not act. They act so that the blessings from above are not drawn down upon them, as it says:
> **"And He will shut up the heaven, so that there shall be no rain"** (Deuteronomy 11:17)

And they do not act, for they have blocked their own channels from the necessary blessings. And it is not that a blemish is found below, but that they themselves are the cause. Furthermore, the Right is not included in the Left so that blessings are not drawn to those below. All of them, for it is not that it is not found below. Who raises it below? Because the sinners separate the Evil Inclination from the Good Inclination and become established in the Evil Inclination. Let Judah come, who comes from the side...

He brings them near to their dismissal as we have said. Because of this, Judah—who comes from the side of the Left—clings to the Right and reigns toward the Right. # Va'era

## Main Text (Zohar)

Eleazar, from the side of the **Upper Right**, thirteen supreme fountains emerge, and deep rivers flow and ascend. These groups enter one into another. One emits its scent and travels through two bodies: one body of the river is cast perfectly above and separates below. Their transformations emerge to the four sides from those rivers. Thirteen fountains are divided into thirteen, and they are white to the eye. Waters emerge numbering four hundred and ninety-nine and a half white ones from this side, and three hundred and ninety-nine and a half white ones from that side, as if salted. A half remains from here and a half from there, and they are made into one. This is the white between the colors and the whites, and it becomes pure white.

The head is red like a rose; its scales are as strong as iron. Its wings beat, grinding and separating for all those colors and whites. When it ascends, it is refined and pure, and it gazes toward the stars; none can stand before it. Its mouth is a flame of fire. When it travels through all those colors and whites, the surrounding serpents tremble and flee, entering the sea. Once every seventy years, they sing to this side, and once every seventy years, they sing to that side. It passes, and the whites join one of eighty from it. This is the **Great Dragon** <note>Aramaic: Tannina; a primordial cosmic force often representing judgment or raw power that must be sweetened</note> that lies between the colors and the whites.

When it moves, a spark of fire emerges like wings; they all stand and rage. In its rage, the colors and the whites are arranged toward the blue eye of Wisdom, and the spheres cast dew to the four sides of the world. It lifts its tail, striking above and striking below; they all flee before it until a flame of fire stands at the North side. A herald cries out: "Lift up the stakes! Be scattered to the three corners!" This awakens the One who pairs the Holy One <note>The Divine Presence or Shekhinah</note> over the face of the Dragon, as it is said: <note>Ezekiel 29:4</note> > *I will put hooks in your jaws...* < Then they are all subdued, and they emerge for the Dragon, going out to cover the upper side. They bring it into the star of the Great Abyss until its scales are awakened. Then they return it to its rivers. Once every seventy years they do this to it, so that it does not stray toward the two firmaments and their appointees. Upon it, all are entwined, circled, and bound, all of them like a wall and like a fortress before the Lord. The upper dragons (the upper chariots) stand above, those that are entwined, as it is said: <note>Genesis 1:22</note> > *And God blessed them* <. These rule over all the surrounding stars, for it is written: <note>Genesis 1:22</note> > *And fill the waters in the seas* <. And regarding this it is written: <note>Psalms 104:24</note> > *How manifold are Your works, O Lord! In wisdom You have made them all.* <

## Commentary (Tosefta)

->**Addition**<-

**A cluster of henna** <note>Song of Songs 1:14</note> > *My beloved is to me a cluster of henna* <. This "cluster" <term>Eshkol: literally a cluster of grapes, here symbolizing the gathering of divine attributes</term> is the **Upper Mother** <note>Imma Ila'ah, the Sephirah of Binah/Understanding</note>. Just as a cluster is divided into many branches and many vines that support one another, so the **Upper Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence</note> is divided into many harvests, supporting her vessels from many horns and many types of "dishes" that provide atonement for the Assembly of Israel. The "horn" <note>symbol of strength/royalty</note> stands before the King, and its garment is to remember the eternal covenant. Her dominion sits with blessed forces that prepared the Divine Will in exile to enter before the King.

The righteous are the life; all the scents of the Shekhinah are spread. The "beloved" and the "King" are transformed into Mercy. In this manner, the name **Y-H-V-H** <note>The Tetragrammaton, usually associated with Mercy</note> exists to fulfill: *If your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow* <note>Isaiah 1:18 paraphrased</note>. The name Y-H-V-H becomes like a leopard <note>representing fierce judgment</note> in all these ways, which are clothed in the Upper Shekhinah. Let the Shekhinah be **the flaming sword which turned every way, to guard the way to the Tree of Life** <note>Genesis 3:24</note>.

The Rabbis established that it "turns"—sometimes to Mercy and sometimes to Judgment. Sometimes it is crushed, sometimes whole. Sometimes it is not in this manner. My beloved is sometimes Mercy, in the manner of Y-H-V-H, the voice of Kindness from the side of the "Length of Days" <note>Atika Kadisha/The Ancient One</note> to sustain all; these turn to Mercy. But from the side of the **Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil**, all Mercy turns to Judgment to nourish those who transgress the words of the Torah. And because of this, in the World to Come, there will be rest; all tastes of Judgment will turn to purity. Therefore, they established the Divine Will for us, like this world and the World to Come. And we know that **Understanding** <note>Binah</note> shall be the "flaming sword which turns"—turning from the start toward Mercy for the righteous, to give them rest in the World to Come. **Kingship** <note>Malkhut</note> is the "flaming sword which turns" to nourish with Judgment the wicked in the world.

## Main Text (Zohar)

In this world, every matter has a side of good and a side of evil. To the outward sight, things appear to change—from a throne for the righteous to a seat for the eunuch <note>referring to shifts in spiritual status or fortune</note>. Because of this, it is written: *And Jacob told Rachel...* and so on, to establish a will that a person does not possess until he takes up a matter with strength or in the flesh. Because they possess both a good and an evil side, things flip from good to evil and vice versa. This was observed by Pharaoh, as it is written: *And the magicians did the same with their secret arts.* They were turning their cups <note>original: "kisin," likely referring to vessels or hidden arts</note> from one side to the other, and their masks <note>original: "pukin"</note> likewise, until this point.

->**And you shall say**<-
to Aaron: "Take your staff." What is the reason it was Aaron’s staff and not Moses’ staff? It is because that staff was exceedingly holy, having been carved with the Holy Name. It descended into the form of a crocodile <note>Exodus 7:9; original: "tanina," often translated as serpent or sea-monster</note>. The Holy One, blessed be He, did not want to defile Moses' own staff with those sticks of sorcery. Furthermore, it was meant to subdue all those who come from the "Left Side" <note>the side of judgment and impurity</note>, because Aaron comes from the "Right Side" <note>the side of mercy and priesthood</note>, and the power to subdue lies in the Right. Before the Holy One, blessed be He, those magicians made crocodiles. What greatness is there in making crocodiles before Pharaoh? It is because that was the beginning of their portion—the awakening of the Great Crocodile which is his dominion. Then all the magicians rejoiced, for this is the head of all their wisdom. Immediately, that crocodile of Aaron turned back into a serpent <note>original: "nachash"</note> and swallowed them. Because of this, they were astonished and realized that a Higher Dominion exists on earth; for they had thought that beneath them, there was no power capable of doing anything. Then *Aaron’s staff swallowed...* specifically "Aaron’s staff," which had turned into a serpent and swallowed them. Thus, Aaron performed two signs: one above and one below. One above: a supernal crocodile that rules over theirs. One below: ruling over their physical crocodile. Pharaoh was wiser than all his sorcerers; he gazed and saw that a Higher Dominion rules over the earth—ruling above and ruling below. Rabbi Yose said: See how the sorcerers, in all they did, could only see what was below and no further. "Take your staff and it shall become a serpent," for it is written: *and they became crocodiles.* Rabbi Yose said: Even their crocodiles turned back into serpents, and the "eye" of Aaron’s serpent swallowed them. It is written here:

> "Behold, I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great crocodile that lies in the midst of his rivers." <note>Ezekiel 29:3</note>

From there is the beginning of their dominion below, for all their wisdom is below the totality of the spiritual grades. Come and see: their wisdom is in the lower grades, and see how those grades—the heads of their authority and their root—are subdued below by that crocodile. It is found that through the crocodile, the power of their supernal serpent was nullified. This is the meaning of the verse: *a rod for the back of the fool.* Rabbi Hiyya was sitting one day before the gate of Lod. Rabbi Eleazar approached him like a weak and poor traveler <note>original: "katopira," a Greek-derived term for a traveler or perhaps a specific type of garment</note>. He said to Rabbi Eleazar: I hear that in your path, many boundaries of impurity surround you. He turned his head and saw him. He said: You have a worthy mission, for the Voice performs its mission in everything. How many messengers does the Holy One, blessed be He, have! Do not say that only things with a spirit <note>breath/soul</note> act as messengers; even things without a spirit do so. He opened his discourse and said:

> "For the stone shall cry out of the wall, and the beam out of the timber shall answer it." <note>Habakkuk 2:11</note>

How much must a person be careful of his actions so that he does not sin before the Holy One, blessed be He! <unclear>illegible</unclear> and see, it is written that sometimes the Holy One, blessed be He, performs His mission through them. Come and see: the staff of Aaron, which had no spirit, the Holy One, blessed be He—the Root of all—acted through it. Two missions were performed through it: one while it had no spirit, and one when it turned into a creeping reptile <note>original: "ruchsha"</note> with a spirit to perform its deed. Rabbi Eleazar said: Go out...

->**Va'era**<-

The spirits of the righteous say: is it not so that the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to revive the dead? And how will anything be made of them <note>the decayed bodies</note>? For those fools who are far from wisdom and far from everything come and say: "Come and see, how can this be the truth?" But the Holy One, blessed be He, at the end of time, will renew for Himself a new creation. And the bodies? Those are the very bodies in which the holy spirits and souls resided, those who kept the commandments of the Torah and labored in the Torah day and night. The Holy One, blessed be He, hid them in the dust until the time when the world rejoices; how much more so will He then make a new creation! Rabbi Hiyya said: Not only that, but that same body which existed will rise, for it is written, *Your dead shall live* <note>Isaiah 26:19</note>, and it is not written, "Your dead shall be created." This implies they are the same beings for all time. For there is one bone <note>the "Luz" bone</note> that remains under the earth, and from that bone, it will never rot or decay in the dust forever. And at that time, the Holy One, blessed be He, will soften it and make it like dough with leaven, and it will rise and expand to the four sides, and from it the body and all its limbs will be built. Afterward, the Holy One, blessed be He, will place a spirit within it. Rabbi Eleazar said to him: It is so. And come and see how that bone is softened: it is by the dew, as it is written: *For Your dew is like the dew of lights* <note>Isaiah 26:19</note>.

## Main Text (Zohar)

**And the Lord said** to Moses: "Say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, over their canals, over their ponds, and over all their pools of water...'" <note>Exodus 7:19</note> Rabbi Judah said: This verse must be looked into. Could he really strike every single place? Furthermore, it is written: *And seven days were completed after the Lord had struck the Nile.* Come and see: it is written "the Nile," yet it also says "over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, over their canals, and over their ponds." Rather, "the waters of Egypt" refers to the source of them all. From there, all those rivers, streams, springs, and all their waters are filled. Therefore, Aaron did not stretch out his hand to strike anything but the Nile alone <note>the source of the Egyptian deity and water supply</note>. And come and see that it is so, for it is written: *And the Egyptians could not drink water from the Nile.*

Rabbi Yose said: Come and see, the lower waters are divided into several higher sides. For the higher waters gather together then, just as it is said: 
> And God said, "Let the waters under the heavens be gathered together into one place." <note>Genesis 1:9</note> 
And it is written: *And the gathering of the waters He called Seas.* This verse has been established by the colleagues. And come and see: that voice of the firmament which contains the sun, the moon, the stars, and the constellations—their life is like the gathering of the waters. For it collects all the waters and they go out to the four sides of the lower world. Once it collects the water, it then divides them to every side, and from there everything is sustained. And when the secret of the lower world's path rests, it draws from that firmament which rests on the left side; then they are called "guilty" and the waters are salty <note>representing judgment or bitterness</note>. Woe to those who suckle from there and are sustained by it! At that time, it was divided into two parts: white and red <note>mercy and judgment</note>. And then the portion of the Matron <note>the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> was protected for Israel, part of it above and part of it below. Because of this, the water opened for Israel. And regarding the blood: see the wonder, it was a boiling of the waters and nothing more. Come and see: the water turned aside and entered their <note>the Egyptians'</note> innards, descending and seizing them until they were bent over, and the water was revealed as proof. Then the water opened... such was the rot of their portion... Rabbi Isaac opened with this verse: 
> I will exalt You, my God the King, and I will bless Your name forever and ever. <note>Psalm 145:1</note> 
Come and see: David said this in relation to his own degree <note>his spiritual level</note>, as it is written: "My God." Because he desired to take his praise and bring it into the light of the world, to mix one with the other so they become all one. Because of this: *I will exalt You, my God the King...* For all the days of David were destined to prepare the Throne and to illuminate the moon <note>the Shekhinah</note>, so that it would protect him and be constantly appointed as a wall of strength, like the moon.

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Va'era** <-
<note>Exodus 6:2 - "And I appeared"</note>

Through the High Priest above <note>referring to the Sefirah of Hesed or the Archangel Michael</note>, all becomes one. When there is great peace below, the world is encompassed by it, and the lower side <note>the Sitra Achra or "Other Side"</note> does not need to be troubled to receive blessing. Come and see: at the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires to execute vengeance upon the idol-worshipping nations, Samael <note>the primary angelic figure of severity and judgment</note> is aroused, and the Moon <note>the Shekhinah/receptive divine presence</note> is filled from that side. Then, blood gushes from its springs, and all those below who belong to the Left Side <note>the side of Judgment</note> are affected. Their judgment is through blood. Come and see: when blood is aroused against a nation, it is the blood of those slain, for another nation shall rise against them and kill them. Regarding all that enslavement [in Egypt], the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not want another nation to be aroused against them with blood. Because Israel was in their merit and would not sin, and because they dwelt in their own land, they did not receive another nation with their priests who could not repeat [the miracles]. Because their dominion ruled over that side, the Holy One, Blessed be He, first commanded their dominion, so that their god should be struck first. For the Nile was one of their gods. And so, the rest of their gods gushed blood. This is what is written:
> And there shall be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood and in vessels of stone. <note>Exodus 7:19</note>

Rabbi Hiyya rose one night to labor in the Torah, and Rabbi Yose was with him. Rabbi Hiyya opened the discourse and said:
> Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart; for God has already accepted your works. <note>Ecclesiastes 9:7</note>

What did Solomon see that he said this verse? Rather, all of Solomon's words were spoken with wisdom. This that he said, "Go, eat your bread with joy"—at the time when a man walks in the ways of the Holy One, Blessed be He, the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings him close to Himself and gives him peace and rest. Come now and wait, and be like a lamp that burns, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, delights in his works. And to strengthen the living spirit greatly, for you have seen that all of Solomon's vessels were in wisdom. To us, he is the Ancient Wisdom. Heaven forbid <note>original: "Chas ve-Shalom"</note> that we should cease your cooking <note>metaphor for deep study</note> and you shall see this verse. Heaven forbid, even before your "cooking" I knew. Heaven forbid, they prepare for you. Heaven forbid, I heard a voice from here, for the voice is the "wine" of this verse. And Solomon warned man to guard the Assembly of Israel <note>the Shekhinah</note> with the joy of the Right Side <note>Mercy</note>, as is fitting to be crowned in joy, and afterwards to be crowned with the wine of joy from the Left Side <note>Judgment sweetened by Mercy</note>, so that the joy of all should be sweetened in perfect faith and be filled. And when you are both thus, then all blessings dwell in the world. And all this is when the Holy One, Blessed be He, is pleased with the works of human beings, as it is written: "for God has already accepted your works." Rabbi Hiyya came and stood up. I will show you the secret of this matter regarding the Holy One, Blessed be He, and your children. And now I know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires you to be needed in the Torah. Further, the master opened and said:
> And the Lord said unto Moses: Say unto Aaron: Take thy rod, and stretch out thy hand over the waters of Egypt. <note>Exodus 7:19</note>

The word "rod" <note>matteh</note> is missing a letter <note>spelled defectively</note>. And not "his rod." And it did not receive the "wine" of deficiency; the waters stood in their place and were filled like... sealed. To Aaron, who comes from that side <note>the Right/Priestly side</note>, it shall be aroused. And when Samael strikes them, they turn to blood. Come and see that all the levels beneath the first magicians from below, the Holy One, Blessed be He, troubled them... from all wisdom and to seek it. And when He reached the highest level of all levels, He executed judgment upon them and acted in the land of Egypt and killed them all. And because of this, He killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, because he <note>the firstborn/Pharaoh</note> is the highest level and the crown of all. And come and see, Pharaoh's dominion was in the water, as it is written:
> The great crocodile that lies in the midst of his rivers. <note>Ezekiel 29:3</note>

Because of this, the river turned to blood. Afterwards, there went out a [plague] that confounded them with hidden voices, croaking in their innards, and they came out of the river and went up onto the dry land, and voices were heard on all sides until they were doubled like the dead inside the house. And the spirit of all kinds... which the Holy One, Blessed be He, made, all were from within this strength and hardness, and this to cast upon the levels...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Va'era (And I Appeared)**<-

All of their [the Egyptian sorcerers'] powers were intended to confuse their own minds, so that they would not know how to re-enter their spiritual levels. Once they went out to perform anything to fix the whole, they were unable to do anything afterward. He saw them when a powerful moon dwelled upon them, as it is written <note>original: "V'saran sichur tzfarde'im v'ozan v'kochan" — a non-biblical formula likely referring to the removal of the frogs' strength</note> (and the turning away of the frogs' sorcery and their strength and power) in your house. Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse with the verse <note>Jeremiah 31:14</note> > "A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping; Rachel is weeping for her children..." < Come and see: this verse has been established in several places. Yet this verse is difficult. Why "Rachel is weeping for her children"? As you might say <note>Lamentations 2:19</note> > "Pour out your heart like water," < but why did Rachel specifically weep? Is something missing from the text? Why does it show that Rachel wept and not Leah? This is what they said: it is written <note>Genesis 29:17</note> > "And Leah’s eyes were weak." < Why were they weak? Because every day she would go out to the crossroads and ask about Esau. And they would tell her, "The deeds of that wicked man are evil." She feared falling into his portion [in marriage] and she would weep and pray every single day until her eyes became soft. And the Holy One, Blessed be He <term>the Creator; literally 'The Holy One, Blessed be He'</term> granted her merit because of that testing, and she was not established in the portion of that wicked man. By your life! A woman shall stand outside at the crossroads and weep over the exile of Israel. And you [Leah] shall stand inside and not weep over them—while Rachel is seen later! The exile of Israel is seen through this entire verse according to what they say. The secret of the matter is that Rachel and Leah are two worlds. One is the <term>Concealed World (Alma d'Atkasya)</term> and the other is the <term>Revealed World (Alma d'Atgalya)</term>. Because of this, Leah was buried and covered inside the cave [of Machpelah] and remained hidden, while Rachel stands at the crossroads in the revealed. Everything is according to the Supernal pattern. For this reason, Jacob did not bring her into the cave, nor into any other [burial place], as it is written <note>Genesis 48:7</note> > "when there was still some distance to come to Ephrath," < and he did not bring her to the cave. This is because he knew that this place was strong in the lower realm. Come and see: the <term>Assembly of Israel (Knesset Yisrael)</term> is thus called "Rachel." Just as it is said <note>Isaiah 53:7</note> > "and like a sheep (Rachel) before her shearers is silent," < to show that in the exile of all the rulers of the other nations, the voice does not cease from her, yet she takes on silence. And this is what is written: "A voice is heard in Ramah, bitter weeping." "A voice is heard in Ramah"—this refers to the Jerusalem Above. "Rachel is weeping for her children." Whenever Israel is in exile, she weeps for them and their distress. The King does not enter to His children because they are not there. For she certainly weeps, but because she desires to rise up from her state and is not broken by this. And come and see: it is not just one hour that she weeps for Israel, but at every single time that they are in exile. And because of this, the Holy One, Blessed be He <term>the Creator</term> makes a voice heard from afar, as it is written <note>Cf. Exodus 11:6</note> > "And there shall be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as there was none like it..." < At times there are other voices, all of them frogs, who hinted at voices in their bellies; they were doubling the distress among the dead, and this was the place of birth, and it was filled with the noise of their children. And they all surrendered their bodies to the heat, as it is written <note>Exodus 7:28</note> > "and into your ovens and into your kneading bowls." < And see, they were meant to be measured in fire and water and given to the spirit. And if you say, "If so, why did it matter to them from afar that all those frogs entered the heat?" Rather, they all entered the heat and went into the oven and did not die. And those that did die, she [the plague's power] worked with that froth in the oven, and they entered into it and were stuck, and other offspring came out of them and were cast out in great numbers. They [the Egyptians] came to eat from it, and he [the frog] opened and sent a frog into their bellies, and they would croak and hint at voices until they died. And this was harder for them than anything. Come and see, it is written <note>Exodus 7:28</note> > "And the river shall swarm with frogs, and they shall go up and come into your house, and into your bedchamber, and upon your bed." < Pharaoh himself was the first portion of them all, and more than them all. Let it be certain that the blow comes from the Blessed One from world to world, for He oversees the deeds of the sons of man in all that they do. It is written <note>Genesis 12:15</note> > "And the princes of Pharaoh saw her and praised her to Pharaoh, and the woman was taken into Pharaoh’s house." < He called to the level that is below. Three "Pharaohs" are mentioned

## Main Text (Zohar)

Here, what happened in that time, and what happened in the time of Joseph, and what happened in the times of Moses when Pharaoh was struck with his staffs? This verse was entirely fulfilled in the first Pharaoh of all: at the time Sarah was found with him, they placed <term>images</term> <note>original: "dyoknin" - spiritual or physical representations/portraits</note> and they carved that image of Abraham over his bed on the wall. His mind was not at rest until they made an image like her own form, and whenever he went up to his bed, she went up with him. Every earthly king after him, behold, they saw that image from the light of the lamp and they would rejoice before it in those forms. When he went up to his bed, he was seen in that image; because of this, the king was struck here more than all of them. Come and see, this is what is written: "And into your bedchamber, and upon your bed, and into the bedchamber of your servants, and upon your people," but for all of them it does not say "upon their beds," only for him alone.

Rabbi Abba opened:
> **"All the rivers flow into the sea, yet the sea is not full; to the place where the rivers flow, there they flow again."** 
<note>Ecclesiastes 1:7</note>

This verse has been explained, and the companions have spoken of it. In every place, how many times do they enter and are hidden? The sea gathers them and draws them in because the waters emerge from the midst of the sea. And that river washes all the brains <note>or "inner essences"</note> that enter it, and afterwards the waters emerge with the strength of the South and water all the beasts of the field; everything is sustained, all the beasts of the Almighty. And come and see, the frozen sea is strengthened by the power of the South, as has been said, and it draws in all the essence. Thus "it is not full." And the companions have awakened a discussion on this: "to the place where the rivers flow, there they flow again"—why "there"? Because that river which flows and emerges from Eden never ceases for all eternity, and it brings forth water to the sea. Therefore, the waters merit to go and return, to be seen and return, and they never cease. And when the vision is set to go, it is in order to go and water everything. And the place of the North wind freezes the water, but the South wind pushes with heat to send them to every side. Therefore, the vision and the essence sit between these two sides, and their structures stand and increase on this side and that side.

Come and see, when the King comes to his bed at the time when the night is divided, the North wind is awakened. This awakens the love toward the <term>Matronita</term> <note>The Divine Matron or Queen, representing the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note>, for if not for the awakening of the North, the King would not unite with her. For the North arouses love, as it is said:
> **"His left hand is under my head"**
<note>Song of Songs 2:6; the "Left" corresponds to the North/Gevurah</note>

And the South embraces in love, as it is written: **"and his right hand embraces me."** Then, how many forms awaken in song until the morning comes, as it is written:
> **"When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy"**
<note>Job 38:7</note>

And when the morning comes, they all go and take up the song, chirping in this manner below, as it is written:
> **"You who remind the Lord, take no rest for yourselves"**
<note>Isaiah 62:6</note>

"Take no rest for yourselves"—this is the image in the night. When the night is divided, those whose praise is to remind the Holy One, blessed be He, do not keep silent. They merit to go and stand to remind the Holy One, blessed be He. When the morning rises, the Assembly of Israel rises early and praises the Holy One, blessed be He. And so too after midday, and so too in the night when the night settles in darkness and the "blind daughter" <note>a reference to the night or the moon/Shekhinah in a specific state</note> rules. Regarding these it is written, "You who remind the Lord, take no rest for yourselves," and this refers to the holy people of Israel.

And because of this, the Holy One, blessed be He, remembered them in Egypt and brought up against Pharaoh those who do not keep silent day or night. And who are they? The <term>frogs</term> <note>original: "urdai'aya" - Aramaic for frogs</note>, whose calling never ceases. This was because he [Pharaoh] had strengthened himself against the holy people who do not keep silent day or night from praising the Holy One, blessed be He. And there was no man in Egypt who could hear anything at that time. From them [the frogs], sparks and will were received by the Shepherd, and they were both dead and alive. You might ask: how could they not be killed? Rather, they were a living creature of a different side <note>the "Other Side" or Sitra Achra</note>, and even if one tried to kill them, they would split open and six would emerge from their innards, and they went and swarmed the land until they were too many to approach. Come and see how many circles and how many turnings emerged from this, and the brain was struck when the waters were silenced and divided into many parts.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Va'era, specifically focusing on the spiritual significance of the ten plagues. ## And I Appeared (Va'era)

->**And I Appeared**<-

How many streams flow to how many sides, and how many splendors and how many lights there are! From a high vantage point, one looks toward the side of Egypt: those waters stir with secular powers, for there are no waters emerging from the sea that do not provide fish for their various species. Those "fish" <note>A metaphor for spiritual entities or lower-level angels</note> rise through the worlds, appointed to carry out the will of their Master, appointed with a spirit of wisdom. Regarding this, we have learned: there are waters that grow wise men, and there are waters that grow fools, according to those rivers that divide to every side. And here in Egypt, they grow masters of sorcery. These "fish" are like small, broken shards, acting as treasurers for the lower levels, as it is written <note>Isaiah 3:2</note> **"the diviner, and the prophet, and the sage."** From silver and gold, from power and goodness, from sin, from the necromancer and the one who consults the dead—from all these, the splendors of the wisdom of Egypt shone. 

At that time, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>Hebrew: HaKadosh Baruch Hu; the standard Rabbinic name for God</note> increased His own wisdom and confused those streams and rivers of Egypt, and the "fish" of their wisdom died. One stream turned to blood, and another caused the "fish" to rise up <unclear>shriveled</unclear> without any use, and the spirit of those wise men did not rest upon them. The **Swarms** (Arov) functioned in this same way: He confused the species of their wisdom so they could not be clarified. Furthermore, the wisdom of the earth itself destroyed them within the land and brought vanity to their strongholds. 

What is this **Swarms** (Arov)? It is a "mixture" (Irbuvya), just as it is said regarding "forbidden mixtures of garments" <note>Kilayim</note>. It was a mixture that they could not untangle, for they had cut themselves off through their own "wisdom." Come and see how many heavenly hosts were cast out as one, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, confused them all together because they had confused their own powerful forces above. All those mighty deeds that the Holy One, Blessed be He, performed in Egypt were done before God, and He cast them down above and below. From that moment, the wisdom of Egypt was outsmarted, as it is written <note>Isaiah 29:14</note> **"The wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid."** 

Come and see, it is written "and from the sorceries of Egypt in Egypt." There is an "Egypt" above and an "Egypt" below <note>The Zohar posits that every earthly nation has a corresponding spiritual representative or "Prince" in the heavenly realms</note>. Because those forces appointed above were over the forces below, they were all cast out. They were cast out above so they would not be remembered, and so they could not connect to their renewals like those who are meritorious, who were previously joined but were now confused. Not only this, but He brought upon them the judgment of the "Swarms," where they were mixed into one another so that the "morning of the earth" <note>Likely referring to the dawn of redemption or the clarity of the land</note> could rise. 

Come and see: wherever something is born on earth, its power comes from above to the earth upon its bosom. Everything was mirrored according to the pattern above. Come and see: the Holy One, Blessed be He, made the nature of the heavens just as He made the nature of the earth, and those boundaries spread out in their places. He fixed the heavens above, and He fixed the boundaries of the earth above. In this same manner below, the levels are spread out; He fixed the heavens and He fixed the boundaries of the earth. The companions have established this: like the nature of the earth, like a garment folded one over the other, so are the boundaries of the earth above, each one spreading into seventy sides, appointed over seventy ministers, who are over seventy nations. 

And that land is the boundary of every single nation, standing before the Holy Land of Israel. Thus did Solomon, the "hammer of the mighty," teach—not regarding the mighty of Israel, but regarding the hidden things left within them, those natures appointed over the Holy Land. It was not the same above as it was below. Come and see that boundary which is raised up as a portion of light: at that time, the Holy One, Blessed be He, increased His wisdom and "scribes" <note>Spiritual agents</note> were born in that boundary, and all those "chariots" that were mounted with "brain" <note>Intellectual/spiritual essence</note> were confused. And all the greenness of the seventy waters then appeared below as images from the morning to the earth. 

Come and see the seal of their deficiency: He saw that all their "buildings" were striking out to the right. The Holy One, Blessed be He, broke their pride, as it is written <note>Exodus 15:6</note> **"Your right hand, O Lord, shatters the enemy."** In this manner, the Holy One, Blessed be He, brought His "beasts" against the city, as it is written <note>Isaiah 34:9</note> **"And its streams shall be turned into pitch, and its dust into brimstone."** And all this happened: "all the dust of the land became lice throughout all the land of Egypt." 

<term>Rabbi Yehuda</term> and <term>Rabbi Hezekiah</term> were walking on the road. Rabbi Hezekiah said: "Companions, all those children [...]"

It describes a cosmic hierarchy where earthly Egypt reflects a spiritual "Egypt" above, both of which were dismantled during the Exodus.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

When the King is destined to go out, he is greeted with joy and praise. Those who are sinners or half-hearted, the members of the household who are not truly of the King’s palace, seek to separate themselves from the rest. How do we know this? From Caleb, as it is written:
> **"But My servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him and followed Me fully..."** <note>Numbers 14:24</note> 
What is this "another spirit"? It means he separated himself from those spies. He opened [his discourse] and said:
> **"And they went up into the South, and he came unto Hebron..."** <note>Numbers 13:22</note> 
<note>The verse uses the singular "he came" rather than "they came," which the Zohar attributes specifically to Caleb.</note>
He went to separate himself from those spies and to come to the burial place of the Patriarchs, to prostrate himself upon the graves in Hebron. And Hebron was given to him as a portion to gather strength within it, <term>as it is said</term> <note>original: k'di amei</note>, and to bring down a holy portion. And see, they gave him Hebron. He lived there in order to prostrate himself at the graves of the Patriarchs, to find counsel from that place and to be saved from the counsel of the spies. In this same manner, it is written:
> **"And David inquired of the Lord, saying: 'Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah?' And the Lord said unto him: 'Go up.' And David said: 'Whither shall I go up?' And He said: 'Unto Hebron.'"** <note>2 Samuel 2:1</note> 
Here we must look closely: since Saul had died, and David had already been anointed in the days of Saul to receive the kingdom, why—once Saul was dead—did they not immediately make David king over all Israel? Why did he not receive the kingdom over all Israel, but instead went to Hebron and received the kingdom there alone for seven and a half years? Why all those seven years? Only after Ish-bosheth died did he receive the kingdom over all Israel in Jerusalem. Rather, this is all a mystery before the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: Kudsha Brich Hu</note>. Come and see: the Holy Kingdom <note>The Shekhinah or the concept of Malchut</note> does not receive dominion until it is first joined with the Patriarchs. Once it is joined with them, it is established for their children in the perfection of the Upper World. And the Upper World is called "seven years" because everything is contained within it. Your sign for this is the gathering of seven years. Not just the Upper World, but as it is written:
> **"And he built it in seven years."** <note>1 Kings 6:38</note> 
Thus, "for in six days the Lord made the heavens and the earth"—these are hidden and not revealed, as it is written:
> **"These are the generations of the heavens and of the earth when they were created..."** <note>Genesis 2:4</note> 
<note>The Zohar reads the Hebrew word "Be-hibaram" (when they were created) as an anagram for "Be-Abraham" (through Abraham).</note>
Through Abraham. And Abraham is called "seven days," and because he is the "seven days," the world was built. In that same way, "he built it in seven years." Come and see: David desired to be joined to the Upper Kingdom, but he could not be joined until he went and joined with the Patriarchs [in Hebron]. He stayed there seven years to be joined among them. After those seven years, the House was built and his kingdom was established so that it would never pass away. If he had not prepared himself in Hebron to be joined to his proper place, his kingdom would not have been established as is fitting. In this same way, Caleb sought to clothe himself in the spirit of wisdom, so he went to Hebron to join with the Patriarchs, and then he went to his own place.

Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Hezekiah were traveling from Cappadocia to Lydda, and with them was a certain Jew who was carrying a load of poultry. As they were walking, Rabbi Yose said to Rabbi Hezekiah: "Open your mouth and say a word of the excellent matters of the Torah, which you review every day before the Holy Lamp <note>A title for Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note>." He opened [his discourse] and said:
> **"Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace."** <note>Proverbs 3:17</note> 
"Her ways are ways of pleasantness"—these are the ways of the Torah. For whoever walks in the ways of the Torah, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> spreads over him the pleasantness of the Divine Presence <note>original: Shekhinah</note> so that it never departs from him. "And all her paths are peace"—for all the paths of the Torah are peace. Peace for him above, peace for him below, peace for him in this world, and peace for him in the world to come. <note>The text here contains a difficult anatomical/mystical metaphor regarding the foundation (Yesod) and the body.</note> He said to him: "May it be so for you, <term>Heaven forbid</term> <note>original: Chas v'Shalom</note> that I should mock, for I have learned this matter." He opened and said: "This verse is interpreted in two ways and two sides. It says 'Ways' and it says 'Paths'; it says 'Pleasantness' and it says 'Peace.' What are 'Ways' and what are 'Paths'? What is 'Pleasantness' and what is 'Peace'? Rather, 'Her ways are ways of pleasantness' is as it is written: 'And the pleasantness of the Lord be upon us.' For every place called a 'Way' of the Lord is a road open to all. In this road, it is open to every person. So 'Her ways' are those ways that are open from here, mentioned in the Great Sea."

<summary>This page explains that spiritual leadership, exemplified by Caleb and King David, requires a foundational connection to the Patriarchs in Hebron. It also begins a mystical discourse on the "ways and paths" of the Torah, equating them with divine pleasantness and peace.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Exodus from Egypt, specifically focusing on the divine attributes (Sefirot) and the symbolic meaning of the plagues, transitioning into the origins of Abraham.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Through them and upon them, the children are built. From the hidden places to the coverings, they open to every side and to all directions of the world. And that light which emerges from the **World to Come** <note>The Sefirah of Binah/Understanding, the source of divine flow</note> divides, and from the World to Come all the stars shine and the lights are separated to every side. And that goodness and light of the World to Come, which nourishes them, is called **Pleasantness** (*Noam*). For every **Kindness** (*Chesed*) of the World to Come is called Pleasantness. And when the World to Come is awakened, all goodness, all joy, all lights, and all freedom in the world are awakened. And because of this, it is called Pleasantness.

And regarding this, we have learned: they stand and shine at the hour when the world—all of them—stand, and their life and their sanctification are in the Book. Once the Book goes forth, we must awaken a supernal joy over it, for in the Book is that goodness of the vision from below, from that hour and onward. And we must awaken and say: <note>Psalm 90:17</note> *“And let the **pleasantness** of the Lord our God be upon us...”* This is the supernal Pleasantness, the portion of all. And regarding this: <note>Proverbs 3:17</note> *“Her ways are ways of **pleasantness**, and all her paths are **peace**.”* What are "her paths"? These are the trails that emerge from above, and the **Single Covenant** <note>The Sefirah of Yesod/Foundation</note>, which is called **Peace**—the peace of the home—gathers them all and leads them to the Great Sea <note>The Sefirah of Malchut/Kingship</note> when it is at its strength. And then He gives it Peace. This is what is written: *“And all her paths are peace.”*

Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Hezekiah bowed and prostrated themselves. "To such an extent are these supernal, hidden matters a fountain, and we did not know!" He said: when they saw a certain man of the field, they saw cattle of the field lying dead. They said, "Worthy is the memory of the cattle in this place." That Judean said: "This is the aftermath of the plague in Egypt." All those worlds, all of them were cattle; three dwellings were cattle. One male, and one those that the hail killed, and one the foreign cattle, and their dwelling was there. But is it not written previously: *“The hand of the Lord is upon your cattle”*? <note>Exodus 9:3</note> It is written like a staff lacking in the book. To show them all, it does not say "the hands of the Lord," but **"the hand of the Lord,"** which is the whole—five fingers. For as it was written previously: <note>Exodus 8:15</note> *“It is the **finger of God**.”* And behold, all of them are five fingers; every single finger killed one [type], and they were five, as it is written: <note>Exodus 9:3</note> *“Upon the horses, upon the donkeys, upon the camels, upon the cattle, and upon the sheep.”* These are five kinds, five fingers, which are called "Hand." When it says "The hand of the Lord," it was a **pestilence** (*Dever*), a very heavy matter, for they died on their own.

And they were found dead after they did not return from their own radiance; those five returned and killed all those that remained. **Pestilence** is Kindness (*Chesed*). **Hail** (*Barad*)—what is the difference between this and that? Behold, this was not like the living force or the strength of anger. And these two were in one place like marrow in a skull. Come and see: those that were in their strength dwelt in the house and died on their own. The hail was sent down in the strength of anger and killed all of them. They sat in that field and saw the cattle in one place, dead there. That Judean stood toward that place and opened two gates of words of the fortress.

He opened and said: It is written <note>Genesis 12:2</note> *“And I will make of you a great nation, and I will bless you, and make your name great...”* This is the portion of Rabbi Eleazar, who said: *"And I will make of you a great nation"* corresponds to *"Go forth"* (*Lech Lecha*); *"And I will bless you"* corresponds to *"from your land"*; *"And I will make your name great"* corresponds to *"from your birthplace"*; *"And you shall be a blessing"* corresponds to *"from your father’s house."* But it is not only according to this. Rabbi Shimon said: The **Spirit of Wisdom** (*Ruach de-Chochmah*) is here. *"And I will make of you a great nation"* corresponds to the **Right Side** <note>Chesed/Kindness</note>. *"And I will bless you"* corresponds to the **Left Side** <note>Gevurah/Strength</note>. *"And I will make your name great"* corresponds to the **Side of Warmth** <note>Tiferet/Beauty</note>. *"And you shall be a blessing"* corresponds to the **Side of the Foundation** <note>Yesod</note>. And the whole Spirit of Holy Wisdom stood in the lower preparation to be awakened above. For until it is awakened below, it is not awakened above to rest upon him. What is written in the book? <note>Genesis 11:31</note> *“And they went forth with them from Ur of the Chaldeans.”* *"And they went forth with them"*—it should have said *"And they went forth with him."* For it is written: *"And Terah took Abram his son..."* Why does it say *"And they went forth"* below? Rather, Terah and Haran went out with Abraham, and the part of the understanding was that Abraham was saved from the fire, and Terah turned to do his will, and because of this—

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the life of Abraham, specifically focusing on the spiritual implications of the birth and circumcision of Ishmael. It connects the biblical narrative to the future geopolitical and spiritual destiny of the Land of Israel.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

When the spark comes • Since they were awakened at first, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: **"Go forth"** <note>Genesis 12:1</note>. Rabbi Shimon said: "Go forth" for your own restoration, for yourself, from your portion of that <term>Crown</term> <note>original: Keter</note> of the end where you were strengthened so that you should not go and take possession of it. "And from your kindred"—from that progeny of yours. "And from your father’s house"—for you were strengthened by their crown. "To the land that I will show you"—there will be revealed to you what you seek, that power which waits for it to be deep and hidden. Immediately, **"So Abram went, as the Lord had spoken to him"** <note>Genesis 12:4</note>. And we seek to proceed from here to know the spirit of wisdom.

Rabbi Abba opened and said: **"For then I will change the speech of the peoples to a pure speech, that all of them may call on the name of the Lord and serve Him with one accord"** <note>Zephaniah 3:9</note>. And it is written: **"On that day the Lord shall be one and His name one"** <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>.

Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Hiyya were walking on the road. Rabbi Yose said to Rabbi Hiyya: "I see you are silent, and a portion [of the soul] is only restored through words of Torah." Rabbi Hiyya sighed and wept. He opened and said: **"But Sarai was barren; she had no child"** <note>Genesis 11:30</note>. Woe to that time! Rabbi Yose said to him: "Look, she gave birth later and everything became a holy soul." He said to him: "Woe for that time, because since that side [Sarah] was delayed, it is written: **'But Sarai was barren, etc.'** All this was at the opening, etc. And because of this, the hour stood for Hagar to inherit the side of the firstborn, and she had a son from [Abraham's] joy and love. He said to Him: **'O that Ishmael might live before You!'** <note>Genesis 17:18</note>."

And even though the Holy One, Blessed be He, was guarding him until the holy seed [Isaac] came out, the love for Ishmael was so great until the Holy One, Blessed be He, answered him: **"As for Ishmael, I have heard you"** <note>Genesis 17:20</note>. Afterward, he was circumcised and entered into the <term>Holy Covenant</term> <note>original: Kiyuma Kadisha</note> before Isaac came into the world.

And for four hundred years, that appointed celestial minister of the children of Ishmael stood and pleaded before the Holy One, Blessed be He. He said to Him: "Does one who is circumcised have a portion in Your Name?" He said to him: "Yes." He said to him: "Behold, Ishmael was circumcised! And not only that, but he was circumcised when he was thirteen years old. Why does he not have a portion in You like Isaac?" He said to him: "This one [Isaac] was circumcised as is proper and according to its requirements, but that one [Ishmael] was not so. Furthermore, these [Israel] are attached to Me at eight days, while those [Ishmael] are far from Me for many days [thirteen years]."

He said to Him: "And despite all this, since he was circumcised, shall he not have a good reward for it?" Woe to that time when Ishmael was born into the world and was circumcised! What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, do? He distanced the children of Ishmael from the <term>Supernal Attachment</term> <note>original: Devekuta</note> above, but gave them a portion below in the <term>Holy Land</term> <note>original: Eretz Yisrael</note> because of that circumcision within them.

And the children of Ishmael are destined to rule over the Holy Land when it is empty of everything for a long time, just as their circumcision is empty and without perfection. And they will prevent the children of Israel from returning to their place until that merit of the children of Ishmael is exhausted.

And the children of Ishmael are destined to stir up fierce wars in the world, and the children of Edom <note>The Western/Christian world</note> will gather against them and stir up war—one on the sea, one on the dry land, and one near Jerusalem. They will rule over one another, but the Holy Land will not be handed over to the children of Edom. At that time, a nation from the end of the world will be stirred up against them and stir up fierce wars, and nations will gather there and fall into their hands until all the children of Edom gather against it. Then the Holy One, Blessed be He, will be stirred up against them, as it is written: **"For the Lord has a sacrifice in Bozrah, etc."** <note>Isaiah 34:6</note>. And after this, what is written? **"To take hold of the corners of the earth, etc."** <note>Job 38:13</note>. He will destroy them from below and break all the celestial hosts above, and no power will remain above over the nations of the world except for the power of Israel alone. This is what is written: **"The Lord alone did lead him, and there was no strange god with him"** <note>Deuteronomy 32:12</note>. Because He is holy in His oneness and His planting is in oneness, and therefore everything depends on the Right Hand. And we have learned that they must raise the Right over the Left, as they established it, for it is written: **"From His right hand went a fiery law for them"** <note>Deuteronomy 33:2</note>. And the merit of this holiness—"Your right hand shall support me."

Blessed be the Lord forever, Amen and Amen.

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Zohar's commentary on the Torah portion "Bo" (Exodus 10:1). It establishes the mystical framework of divine judgment and the role of human actions in influencing the heavenly realms.</meta>

# ## Portion of Bo: "Go to Pharaoh"

## Main Text (Zohar)

**And the Lord said** to Moses: "Go to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart..." <note>Exodus 10:1</note>. Rabbi Yehuda opened the discussion and said: "Happy is the people that knows the joyful shout; O Lord, they shall walk in the light of Your countenance" <note>Psalms 89:16</note>. How much do people need to walk in the path of truth and to keep the commandments of the Torah <note>original: "Pikudei Oraita"</note> so that they may merit through them the World to Come <note>original: "Alma De-Ate"</note>, and so that they may be acquitted from all the accusers <note>original: "Kitigorin" - prosecuting angels</note> above and below. For just as there are accusers found in the lower world, so too are there accusers found above who stand over people. Those who perform the commandments of the Torah and are seen to be under the protection of their Master—how many defenders <note>original: "Sanigorin" - advocating angels</note> stand over them above! As it is said: "If there be for him an angel, an intercessor, one among a thousand..." <note>Job 33:23</note>. And it is written: "Then He is gracious unto him, and says: 'Deliver him from going down to the pit, I have found a ransom'" <note>Job 33:24</note>. Therefore, happy is the portion of those who keep the commandments of the Torah. Come and see: those paths of the righteous <note>The text likely intends "righteous" despite the OCR "sinners" (chata'ei), as the context describes protection</note> are guarded by their King, who acts as a defender for the person. And of this it is written: "For the Lord shall be your confidence, and shall keep your foot from being caught" <note>Proverbs 3:26</note>. And it is written: "The Lord shall preserve you from all evil" <note>Psalms 121:7</note>. For the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kadosh Baruch Hu"</note>, sees everything a person does in the world, whether good or bad. And so He says: "Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? says the Lord" <note>Jeremiah 23:24</note>. And Rabbi Yehuda said: Everything is revealed and seen before the Holy One, Blessed be He. But it is also written: "But touch his bone and his flesh" <note>Job 2:5</note>, and it is written: "And you moved Me against him, to destroy him without cause" <note>Job 2:3</note>. This is to show that a secret was handed over to the Other Side <note>original: "Sitra Achra" - the realm of evil</note>, and permission was given over the matters of the world to test those who should not have been handed over into his hands. There are hidden weapons before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and there is no permission for the Fearful One <note>the Accuser</note> to investigate them, because they are the pride of the Holy One, Blessed be He, hidden away. These are the mysteries <note>original: "Razin"</note> that those who are truly righteous—who know the secrets of the Torah—investigate, and they are like a vessel of wisdom to know those hidden matters of the Torah.

**Rabbi** Elazar opened and said: "Now it fell on a day, that the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them" <note>Job 1:6</note>. "Now it fell on a day"—this refers to the day when the Holy One, Blessed be He, stands to judge the world. In the same way it says: "And it fell on a day, that he came thither" <note>2 Kings 4:8</note>. That day was the festival of Rosh Hashanah <note>The Jewish New Year and Day of Judgment</note>. "The sons of God came"—these are the great ministers and messengers in the world who are present to witness the deeds of humanity. "To present themselves before the Lord"—as it is said: "And all the host of heaven standing by Him on His right hand and on His left" <note>1 Kings 22:19</note>. But "to present themselves before the Lord" implies a state of accusation <note>original: "Kitigoria"</note>, to see if the love of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is present for Israel. For thus the living beings <note>angels</note> who are appointed over the deeds of humanity ascend, and they wander and roam <note>original: "Satan ve-Satan"</note> through all those deeds. And when the judgment comes to stand and judge the world, they become accusers to stand against humanity. And come and see: out of all the nations of the world, they do not stand to investigate their deeds as they do with Israel alone, because Israel are close to the Holy One, Blessed be He. And when the deeds of Israel are not as they should be, as it were, the strength of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is weakened. But when they perform proper deeds, they give strength and power to the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His House of Judgment. It is written: "Ascribe strength unto God" <note>Psalms 68:35</note>. Just as there are proper deeds, "Satan also came"—all the great ministers gather "against the Lord." "Against the Lord" certainly, for since they gather against Israel, they gather against Him. "And Satan came also among them"—the word "also" <note>original: "Gam"</note> is to include all of them coming to be accusers against Israel, and this...

<meta>This page continues the Zohar’s commentary on the Torah portion *Bo* (Exodus 10:1–13:16). It explores the mystical reasons behind the suffering of Job, framing it as a divine strategy to distract the Accuser (Satan) from prosecuting the people of Israel during their redemption from Egypt.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And this was added to them because their fear was as one, all of them being accusers. When the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: *Kadosh Baruch Hu*</note>, saw that they all came to accuse, immediately: *“And the Lord said to the Satan, ‘From where do you come?’”* (Job 1:7). Did the Holy One, blessed be He, not know from where he came? Rather, it was to bring understanding to his will. *“And the Lord said to the Satan...”* and *“The Satan answered the Lord and said, ‘From roaming the earth...’”* From here we learn that there are times when the sword is given over to the "Other Side" <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of evil or impurity</term> when the Land of Israel is alone. Once he saw him "roaming the earth," even though <note>original: *af al gav*</note> the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: *Kadosh Baruch Hu*</note>, desired to be a guardian over Israel, He immediately said: *“And the Lord said to the Satan, ‘Have you set your heart upon My servant Job, for there is none like him in all the earth?’”* (Job 1:8).

He saw the hour was right to give him a portion <note>a "bribe" or distraction</note> so that he would be occupied and separate himself from the children of Israel. And we have established that His will was to act like a priest <note>who offers a portion to appease</note>, etc. Immediately, that Satan became occupied with him [Job] and did not accuse Israel. *“Then the Satan answered the Lord and said, ‘Does Job fear God for nothing?’”* (Job 1:9). Is it not the way of a servant to his master that he desires all his will so that he should fear him? Remove Your protection from him and see if he fears You. And Heaven forbid, at the time of the plague, when a single portion is given to this side to be occupied with, it then separates from all the rest. This is like the "Two Goats" <note>original: *shnei se'irim*</note>—the goat of Yom Kippur—which is given so that he [the Accuser] will be occupied with it and leave the King’s children alone, and the elder [the Accuser] arrives and takes his portion from all the seed of Abraham on the Other Side, as it says: *“Milcah also has borne children... Uz his firstborn...”* (Genesis 22:20-21).

And come and see: at the time he saw him "roaming the earth" from everything and seeking to perform judgment on Israel—for he had a claim of judgment against Abraham to demand from the Holy One, blessed be He, because judgment was not fully executed upon Isaac when he was offered upon <note>original: *al gabi*</note> the altar. For one should not exchange a sacrifice once it is on the altar, and so in every aspect of judgment, they should not be exchanged. And here Isaac stood upon the altar, yet the sacrifice was not completed through him and judgment was not executed on him. He [the Accuser] demanded this from the Holy One, blessed be He, just as he demanded the judgment of Joseph for many generations. And everything he demanded, the sword of judgment was upon it.

From that time when Isaac was returned and his sacrifice was exchanged, the Holy One, blessed be He, prepared that Accuser to take his portion from all the seed of Abraham so he would not approach the Other Side. And all of them were in the exact form that came to the prophet, for the advice of Pharaoh was his. And when Pharaoh rose against Israel and sought to kill them—Heaven forbid <note>original: *chas v'shalom*</note>—he did not take their sustenance but ruled over their bodies with hard labor. "But do not kill them," Heaven forbid. The Holy One, blessed be He, by Your life, just as the judgment reached Noah... what is written? *“And he reached out and took...”* and he moved against himself and against his flesh, etc. Just as he pushed us to be judged, and he thought that in every place he feared the Holy One, blessed be He.

Come and see what is written: *“And his soul went out...”* (Genesis 35:18) like a bird, because of the spirit, as it is written: *“The end of all flesh has come before Me”* (Genesis 6:13). And we have learned: "before Me" means he pushed and there was strength. "The end of all flesh" and not the spirit. And it is said that he pushed the "Lower End" from the side of darkness, which is the "End of the Angel of Death" <term>Samael/Death</term>. *“He searches out to every limit”* (Job 28:3) because he pushed another "End," which is called the "End of the Right" <term>Ketz HaYamin: the holy redemption</term>. And he did not push the other "End" from the side of impurity, which is darkness. And because of this, he was given permission over the skin and the flesh... and he swallowed it. If so, was it not exactly as that Accuser said, that he saw him and strengthened him? Everything was exact. He waited to say to him, to take him, *“For the work of a man He will pay him, and according to the way of a man He will find him”* (Job 34:11). And so it was, as the heat of the fire is to the oven, so far. And regarding that which was said: *“And you incited Me against him to destroy him without cause”* (Job 2:3)—it is not written "without cause" [regarding the inciting], but *“you incited Me... for in him it stands,”* according to his knowledge that he pushed... for *“you incited Me”* is as he said. And regarding the "turning of the wicked," he said he was obligated to turn by the word of that Accuser. In this manner: *“They enticed Him with their mouth, and with their tongue they lied to Him”* (Psalm 78:36). It does not say "they enticed Him and lied to Him," but *“they enticed Him with their mouth”*—this word stands as a compromise, that he was enticed, Heaven forbid.

It links Job's suffering to the incomplete sacrifice of Isaac and the mystical concept of the "End of All Flesh" versus the "End of the Right."</summary>
