<meta>This page continues the Zohar's mystical commentary on the Torah portion "Bo" (Exodus 10:1). It transitions from the plagues of Egypt to a broader discussion on the nature of the Accuser (Satan) and the testing of the righteous, specifically using the story of Job as a primary example.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Come to Pharaoh**<-

Rabbi Isaac said: Everything was well-ordered in all that we have learned, for we have taught that he <note>The Evil Inclination/Satan</note> ascends and makes his calculations, and it is in his hand to lead people astray. For he is the "old and foolish king," as it is written: *Better is a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king* <note>Ecclesiastes 4:13</note>. And because of this, he is able to lead everyone astray. What is the reason? Because he is entrusted over the deeds of humankind.

Come and see: This examination of Ezekiel <note>original: "Yechizkel," likely a scribal error for the general concept of Divine inspection</note> is written regarding the secret of the world: *And the Lord came down to see the city* <note>Genesis 11:5</note> etc. And the way of the world is that trust is given into his <note>the Accuser's</note> hands alone, for [God] does not wish to mention the word of that Accuser, as his abomination is always toward impurity. From this we learn what is written: *He sets an end to darkness, and searches out every limit* <note>Job 28:3</note>. Regarding impurity, he searches out everything, and this is the meaning of *The end of all flesh has come before Me* <note>Genesis 6:13</note>, certainly because of him.

And you see: *Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord* <note>Job 1:6</note>, as it has been said. On that day, two sides stand together against the world: all those who come before Him with merit and good deeds to be written before Him—who is Life—and to bring forth holy offspring and matters from His side, as it is written, *for life* <note>Isaiah 4:3</note>. And all those who come with evil deeds belong to that <term>Other Side (Sitra Achra)</term> <note>The realm of evil or "the other side" of holiness</note>, which is Death and is called Death, and in which Death dwells. And in the book of the blotted out it is written: *Let them be blotted out of the book of the living* <note>Psalms 69:29</note>.

And these two sides, Life and Death—there is no one who takes hold of the side of Life and no one who takes hold of the side of Death [exclusively], for the pillars of the world are in the middle. If one righteous person stands in the world to tip the scales for them, they all stand and are written for Life. But if one guilty person tips the world, they are all written for Death. At that time, the world stands in the balance, and that Accuser seeks to prosecute immediately. What is written? *Have you considered My servant Job, that there is none like him on the earth...* <note>Job 1:8</note>. Once he was singled out alone, the Accuser immediately grew strong against him.

And behold, we have learned that a person should not praise themselves from the general collective, so that they are not singled out alone and prosecuted above. As it is written regarding good things, it was said: *I dwell among my own people* <note>2 Kings 4:13</note>. She did not wish to remove herself from the collective, for there is safety among the people. But here, regarding Job, once he was singled out above and distinguished, the Accuser immediately grew strong against him and said: *Does Job fear God for nothing?* <note>Job 1:9</note>. Anyone who fears You and You strengthen them and make them victorious, he makes a sound below [saying] "The Sabeans fell upon them and took them away" <note>Job 1:15</note>. For all the ascent of this praise that [God] made for him, the Accuser sought to diminish him, saying: *He will surely curse You to Your face* <note>Job 1:11</note>. He will leave You and cleave to the Other Side. For the bread on your table is for everyone; remove Your table from him and see if he still cleaves to You. Immediately, *The Lord said to Satan, "Behold, all that he has is in your hand"* <note>Job 1:12</note>. This shows that his judgment was before the Holy One, blessed be He; He did not simply hand him over to the Other Side [without cause].

And from here we learn that all those who fear the Holy One, blessed be He, only because of their wealth or their children—this is not proper fear. And this is why that Accuser prosecuted, saying: "Does Job fear God for nothing?" A voice below said "The Sabeans fell upon them," etc. *You have blessed the work of his hands* <note>Job 1:10</note>, and it was because of this that he was given permission to prosecute him, to show that he did not serve his Master out of love. For once he was tested, he departed from his path and did not stand in his steadfastness. What is written? *In all this, Job did not sin with his lips* <note>Job 2:10</note>. He did not sin with his lips, but in his will (thought) he sinned, and later he sinned in everything.

And yet, a person is not tested unless it is written: *The Lord tests the righteous* <note>Psalms 11:5</note>. And because Job was singled out—even though he did not stand in his steadfastness as was proper—he did not completely leave the authority of his Master to cleave to the Other Side. And you see that his suffering lasted twelve months, which is the duration of the dominion of the Other Side, just as we have learned that the judgment of the wicked in Gehenna <note>Purgatory/Hell</note> is twelve months. And because he did not cleave to the Other Side, it is written: *And the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning* <note>Job 42:12</note>.

<summary>This page discusses the spiritual mechanics of the Accuser (Satan), explaining how singling oneself out for praise can invite divine prosecution, using the trial of Job as a cautionary tale about the nature of true fear of God versus fear motivated by material reward.</summary>

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Torah portion "Bo" (Exodus 10:1). The previous section concluded the plagues in the portion of Va'era. Here, the Zohar transitions into a deep mystical analysis of the "Great Dragon" and the spiritual roots of Pharaoh's power, contrasting the "End of Days" with the "End of the Right."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Come to Pharaoh** <-

I have spoken of the union of their wills. The mystery of the matter is that the serpent <note>original: *chivya*</note> acts in the same manner as one who builds in shame, circling in a likeness. For it is not written, "And God tested the serpent," as it is written <note>Genesis 22:1</note> **"And God tested Abraham."** For when he cast the serpent into his hand to draw near to Him, his words were directed toward the Holy One, Blessed be He. But the serpent gave nothing, nor did he surrender anything to the Holy One, Blessed be He, nor did he seal anything for Him. For it was revealed before Him that he could not endure within it, and so everything was delivered into the hand of the Accuser <note>The Prosecuting Angel/Satan</note>. Thus, the judgment of the Holy One, Blessed be He, was carried out, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, was awakened to justify the law, just as this Accuser acts toward the prophets of old. Therefore, look at the works of the serpent, etc.

He opened and said: <note>Genesis 4:3</note> **"And it came to pass at the end of days"** <note>original: *mi-ketz yamim*</note> and not at the "End of the Right" <note>original: *mi-ketz yamin*</note>. The serpent is compared to the "End of Days," but one should draw near to the "End of the Right." As Daniel said <note>Daniel 12:13</note>: **"But go your way till the end be: for you shall rest, and stand in your lot at the end of the right."** <note>The "Right" represents the side of Mercy/Chesed, while "Days" here refers to the side of Judgment/Malchut</note>. He did not say "End of Days," but rather "End of the Right." Furthermore, David was afraid and said <note>Psalms 39:4</note>: **"Lord, make me to know my end, and the measure of my days, what it is."** This refers to the "End of Days" and not the "End of the Right." And here, what is written? "And it came to pass at the end of days," and not the "End of the Right." Because of this, Cain's sacrifice was not accepted, for it all came from the "Other Side" <note>the realm of evil/impurity</note>.

Come and see what is written: <note>Genesis 4:4</note> **"And Abel, he also brought."** From where did he bring it? For his pleasure. For when his sacrifice was for the Holy One, Blessed be He, it was everything. He uprooted his sacrifice for the Holy One, Blessed be He, and gave a portion to the "Other Side." But Cain uprooted his work from the "End of Days"—the mystery of the "Other Side"—and gave the [remaining] portion to the Holy One, Blessed be He; therefore, it was not accepted.

Regarding the serpent, what is written? <note>Job 1:4</note> **"And his sons went and feasted..."** and <note>Job 1:5</note> **"And it was, when the days of their feasting were gone about..."** and they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and drink with them. When the Accuser is filled every day, he watches him but cannot prevail against him. How do we know this? As it is written <note>Job 1:10</note>: **"Have You not made a hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he has on every side?"** For he [Job] did not give a portion at all to the "Other Side." But is it not written <note>ibid.</note> **"and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all"**? He sent a portion Above, but did not give a portion to the "Other Side" to weaken it. Had he given it a portion, it could not have prevailed against him later, and all that was destroyed of his would not have been destroyed.

And if you say that the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives him a portion—it is like giving a portion to a weakling to turn his face away, so that he departs from the Sanctuary, allowing the side of Holiness to ascend higher and higher. But the serpent did not do so, and therefore he challenged the Holy One, Blessed be He, in judgment. Come and see: just as the serpent was separated and did not eat "Good and Evil," He judged him in that same way—giving him good, then evil, and then returning him to good. For it is fitting for a person to know good and to know evil, and then to return to the good; this is the "Mystery of Faith" <note>original: *raza de-meheimanuta*</note>.

Come and see from the servants of Pharaoh: this is what is written of him <note>Exodus 9:20</note>: **"He that feared the word of the Lord among the servants of Pharaoh."** A mystery is said now: there is a need to reveal secrets that are attached Above and Below. Come and see that the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not wish to uproot the serpent from its hole, for the serpent was covering Pharaoh, since Below he [the serpent] executed vengeance upon Pharaoh.

What is written? <note>Exodus 10:1</note> **"Come to Pharaoh."** It should have said "Go to Pharaoh." See, all the strength that the Holy One, Blessed be He, brought, chamber after chamber, was against a certain Great Dragon <note>original: *Tanin ha-Gadol*</note>, supreme and mighty, from whom many levels hang down. He is the mystery of the "Great Dragon." Even the staff [of Moses] was afraid of him and did not draw near to the serpents. His levels are a destruction to the prophet, and he did not draw near because he takes from the side of the upper bellies. When the Holy One, Blessed be He, saw that Moses was afraid, and He had sent other messengers from Above who could not face him, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said <note>Ezekiel 29:3</note>: **"Behold, I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon that lies in the midst of his rivers."** The Holy One, Blessed be He, had to wage war against him, and not a mere staff, as it is said: "Behold, I am against you." This is the elevation of the mystery of Wisdom: "The great dragon that lies in the midst of his rivers." This is for the masters of measure who know the mysteries of their Lord.

He opened the mystery and said: <note>Genesis 1:21</note> **"And God created the great dragons, and every living creature that moves, which the waters brought forth abundantly, after their kind."** This verse has been established for all: "And God created the great dragons," as we have established, this refers to:

-> **Leviathan** <-

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Come unto Pharaoh**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion, Exodus 10:1.</note>

The Leviathan and its mate: the word for "sea monsters" <note>Hebrew: *Tanninim*</note> is written in a deficient form <note>Missing the letter 'yod'</note> because the Holy One killed the female and preserved her for the righteous in the time to come. There are nine holes <note>or "caverns/channels"</note> where the waters press greatly between them, and one hole surrounds them all. These are the circuits of the waters that descend into it three times a year. When it is blessed twice, that hole is filled, but not always is it so. Because of this, the Sea Monster stands in that river which is mighty and powerful, and it emerges and strikes and swallows many kinds of creatures. It sits in that hole and watches, and those nine holes watch as well; they go up and increase the number of the wicked who labor within them.

The first hole emerges from the nostril of **Samael** <note>The primary figure of evil/severity in Kabbalah</note> like a single spark that strikes and emits three drops. Each and every drop is divided into three more drops, and from each drop, a single hole is formed. These are the nine holes that grow strong, moving and striking and surrounding all those lower firmaments. From those drops, when they stand ready to emerge below, one drop emerges like a discharge <note>semen-like emission</note> that falls between them, and from it, one more hole is made. This hole is the one we called "the discharge." When that river strikes and emits other great drops from the right side—those that are from the blessings below—one drop falls into that hole which is entangled, and this hole is superior to them all.

When those four rivers that go out from the Garden of Eden emerge and spread out, the one that is traced in the "Double Python" <note>A cryptic term for a specific force of the *Sitra Achra* or "Other Side"</note> is included in that hole, reaching until the level of **Kingship** <note>Term: <term>Malchut</term> - the final Sephirah, representing the manifest world and the Shekhinah</note>. Through this hole, all those other holes are nourished and filled. One Sea Monster rules and strikes over the nine, and each one is like a female in its desire, as it is said: *“You crushed the heads of the sea monsters...”* [Psalms 74:13]. Even the "Great Sea Monster" is thus, for all spirits are bent toward it, and it is below in its authority. It is written: *“Behold, I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great sea monster...”* [Ezekiel 29:3]. Corresponding to every deed of the "Ten Crowns of Impurity," there stand these ten holes.

One Sea Monster pants like a wind toward each one, and because of this, all species tremble and the world shakes. For when this Great Sea Monster raises its fins and trembles, then all those in the holes tremble, the whole world shakes, and the "Sword" is filled. They are all included in this Great Sea Monster. They surround the state of **"Unformed and Void"** <note>Hebrew: *Tohu wa-Bohu* from Genesis 1:2</note>. A wind passes through them all; the world was a ruin, and they know it, but few are those who know the secret of the work—how it strikes with the breath of the Great Sea Monster. The shadow of the Sea Monster is such that all the worlds are not even equal to its fins.

"Unformed and Void": The Sea Monster was far away because when it enters that first hole we mentioned, it becomes filled and rises, knowing the directions below in those worlds that were initially cast out. Those other sea monsters we mentioned existed and yet did not exist, for their strength was established so they would not wander the worlds. Once every seventy years, they strengthen themselves through the power of this Great Sea Monster. This is the "learning" to grow strong. Had its mate remained established for her children, the world could not have endured them. It is written that until He killed the female, the world was "Unformed and Void." After He killed her, it was ready to be illuminated, but before there was light, she labored to exist.

What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He struck the heads of the male above and subdued him, because the deep below was not illuminating. Why did it not illuminate? Because the Great Sea Monster was crouched over the deep, licking it, and would not pant below. Then another Spirit passed above, as it is written, and through that Spirit, the Holy One purified it: **"And the Spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters"** [Genesis 1:2]. This is what we learned: that the Holy One clashed spirit against spirit and created the world. And see: "Let there be light, and there was light"—the light of the upper world shone, as it is written...

Once those lights were engraved within the surrounding circle below, the wicked of the world knew of them and would worship the surrounding circle. <meta>This page continues the Zohar’s commentary on the Torah portion "Bo" (Exodus 10:1–13:16). ## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Go to Pharaoh**<-

It ascends toward visions and sights, and all their affairs are entangled like a thicket where that forest is found, and they see revelations on every side. Then that infant <note>likely a reference to a nascent spiritual force or the "youthful" stage of a cosmic power</note> ascends and is raised among them, returning to every vision. The breasts shall ferment and there shall be a strike in the firmament; the death-beast is weakened because it is closed off on two sides and does not emerge to the worlds except for one time a day. In the ancient books, this is the "weakness of the coils" of the beast, which is always in a state of crookedness, and living curses are upon the world when this Measure <note>The Divine Measure</note> breaks the strength of that infant. It cannot stand until it consumes souls, because its stomach bends it within the sea when it enters it. And He shall tread upon the strength of the sea; and the strength of the sea is this beast, the infant, and He "treads upon the heights of the sea." And when this serpent stands, what is written? "And He shall slay the crocodile that is in the sea" <note>Isaiah 27:1</note>, this is the beast, "the great crocodile," etc.
<note>Isaiah 27:1</note>
It is written: "Behold, I am against you," and this is the weakness of the beast that undermines with curses for all, because the beast is strong against it with the strength of that great officer <note>The spiritual prince of Egypt</note> who is carved from the palm tree. That power of the beast is a star; when it is hungry, it prepares to be fixed constantly, because all its sorceries and strengths are gathered by the beast. It eats the earth and its dust constantly, as it is said: "And dust you shall eat all the days of your life" <note>Genesis 3:14</note>. This one grows like dust and this one grows
<note>Genesis 3:14</note>
just as that which grows in the water is not strong enough to grow like the dry land. Concerning this, it is written that the "undermining of the officer" is not revealed to a prophet; it is not revealed to a prophet, but only to the Holy One, Blessed be He, alone, who kills it from within the sea, as we have established, because He takes the spirit that is within it; then He strikes him and his descendants.

**"And the Lord will pass** through to strike the Egyptians," etc. Rabbi Yose taught: This verse is difficult, and others like it.
<note>Exodus 12:23</note>
First this, and afterward "and He will pass over" <note>Exodus 12:23</note>. The support is that it should be done, and their life-force [preserved], because the beast flees from being seen in a place, and from being seen in three places that are open. And this is what is written: "And the blood shall be [a sign] for you," etc. Why was it necessary to put the blood on the lintel and on the two doorposts? Rather, it is written:
"And the Lord smelled [the soothing aroma] and forgot..." <note>A paraphrase of Genesis 8:21</note> and "for the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth." Preparation is not only for those below, but also for those above. Even for those at the very bottom, an action must be performed. An action is required, and until then they do not look to eat, except for the "chirping" of the Commandment, as it is written: "Take heed to yourselves, lest your heart be deceived" <note>Deuteronomy 11:16</note>. Since an action is performed for comfort,
<note>Deuteronomy 11:16</note>
it awakens [mercy] above. Therefore, everything—whether for good or for evil—depends upon an action. Rabbi Yose said: All the marketplaces of Egypt were full of sorceries, and furthermore, in every single house there were "slaughterers of splendor" who were bound in their knots of lower crowns <note>impure spiritual emanations</note> below, and they awakened an impure spirit through them. Therefore it is written: "And you shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and strike the lintel and the
<note>Exodus 12:22</note>
two doorposts." A bunch of hyssop? Why a bunch of hyssop? In order to purge the impure spirit from among them, and to seal their entrances in these three places of perfect faith: one here, one there, and one between them. By this, "the Lord will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come into your houses to strike you." What is this?
<note>Exodus 12:23</note>
The Holy Name is marked upon the entrance. Rabbi Judah said: Come and see, what is this blood? It is the blood of the circumcision and the blood of the Passover lamb. One is included within its colors. These were two types of blood: one of circumcision and one of the Passover. Circumcision is Mercy <term>Chesed/Rachamim: the expansive, loving aspect of God</term>, and the Passover is Judgment <term>Din: the restrictive, legalistic aspect of God</term>. Rabbi Judah said: It is not so, but as we have learned, the Holy One, Blessed be He, turned it to Mercy as if it were white, as it is written: "And I saw you wallowing in your blood, and I said to you: In your blood, live!"
<note>Ezekiel 16:6 (with variations)</note>
And I say that it was red below for Mercy, as it is written "In your blood, live," and because he marked the entrance on three sides: one here, one there, and one between them. Come and see, the two types of blood were prepared to correspond to the two crowns <note>Sefirot</note> that are crowned above at that hour. Rabbi Yose said: One crown is included in two hidden sides, like embroidered work...

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Exodus, specifically the portion "Bo" (Come). It focuses on the night of the Passover in Egypt, interpreting the physical signs on the doors through the lens of the Sefirot (divine emanations).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Come to Pharaoh** <-

With compassion and judgment. There is one secret <note>original: "Chad Raza"</note> found in many places: The Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>, had pity on His children and performed all this for the house, sanctifying the [divine] host. As it is said: He placed [a sign] at the opening, and the "Chet" <note>The Hebrew letter Chet, representing life or protection</note> rested inside the house, while there was a "cutting" outside at the opening to guard you. Here, the blood alludes to the opening, the secret of His faith; the "Chet" rests inside the house while there is a guard for you outside. For it is written: **"And none of you shall go out of the door of his house until morning"** <note>Exodus 12:22</note>, and it is written: **"And he shall take of the blood and put it on the lintel and on the two side posts... and the Lord will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come in unto your houses to smite you"** <note>Exodus 12:22-23</note>.

Furthermore, there is one secret regarding the form of the Holy Name that they made at that hour. Just as the Holy Name is above, so it was below at that hour. Judgment <note>term: Din - the divine attribute of strict justice and limitation</note> hovered here below at that hour, as it is written: **"And he shall take of the blood and put it on the lintel and on the two side posts."** This mark was entirely red below, for below it is the nature of Judgment to execute vengeance and to weaken [the enemy's] life. It is written: **"Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah?"** <note>Isaiah 63:1</note>, for He is destined to appear entirely in Judgment to execute vengeance. The secret of the matter is that just as it was above at that hour, so it was required below: compassion for compassion, and judgment for judgment. Then you shall consider the blood... and you shall strike [the lintel] etc. **"And none of you shall go out of the door of his house until morning."** What is the reason? Because of the [divine] preparation.

Rabbi Isaac said in the name of Rabbi Jeremiah: A person should not go out into the street or be found in the market at a time when Judgment is stretched out. For since the "External Ones" <note>term: Chitzonim - demonic or chaotic forces that exist outside the realm of holiness</note> have permission to consume, they may strike whoever they encounter and he will be harmed. Even if the Judgment is not intended for him, he should not go outside. It was taught that Rabbi Yose said: At that time when Judgment was found to strike [the Egyptians], at that very moment Compassion <note>term: Rachamim - the balancing attribute between Mercy and Judgment</note> was found for Israel. Thus it is written: **"And when I see the blood, I will pass over you"** <note>Exodus 12:13</note>. For all the holy crowns <note>The Sefirot</note> above act as one; Judgment is found and Compassion is found, and all of them at the same hour.

Rabbi Hezekiah taught: It is written, **"And the Lord shall smite Egypt: he shall smite and heal it"** <note>Isaiah 19:22</note>. Smiting for the Egyptians and healing for Israel. What is "healing"? Healing from a wound, for all [Israel] required healing. And it was taught: At that hour He smote them... with the seal... for Israel. As Rabbi Yose said, and Rabbi Hezekiah said: What is meant by **"And the Lord will pass over the door"**? It should have said "pass over *you*." Rather, it means "over the opening"—literally over the opening, and the "opening of the body." Rabbi Yose said: The "opening of the body" refers to Circumcision <note>term: Milah</note>.

Rabbi Simeon said: At the hour when the holy crown below is stirred by the Male. And who is the Male? It is the Supernal Kindness <note>term: Chesed - the attribute of expansive love and benevolence</note> that reaches the entire generation... and in this manner, this one strikes and that one protects, and all at the same hour. And it is written: **"And the Lord will pass over the door"**—over the *known* opening. Why is it called "the opening"? Because it is the opening and the purification of the spirit and the body. Come and see: before a man is circumcised, he is closed off from all sides; once he is circumcised, he is opened to all and is no longer blocked and closed as before. This is the spirit that is prepared, and the "Foundation" <note>The Sefirah of Yesod</note> becomes the opening... because the [letter] *Yod* is revealed. What does this mean? Rabbi Isaac said: They struck [the blood] to reveal this Kindness <note>Chesed</note> as Justice <note>term: Tzedek - often associated with the Sefirah of Malchut/Kingship</note>, and this is the opening of the holy supernal dwelling. As it is written: **"Justice, Justice [shalt thou follow]"**—the well-known [Justice]. Rabbi Eleazar said: When the [letter] *Yod* is revealed, it flows to atone and to bless the opening of **Justice**, for this **Justice** is covered by Kindness. This was the secret of that hour: Kindness, which is the portion of Abraham. And the fact that this opening of **Justice** was covered... as it is written: **"And the Lord blessed Abraham in all things"** <note>Genesis 24:1</note>, for it was covered in Kindness until the *Yod* was revealed. Rabbi Abba said: This is the "Foundation" <note>Yesod</note>, the opening of **Justice**, as it is written: **"And the Lord blessed Abraham in all things,"** and this is the final holy opening... in the secret of how the Crown of Kindness was given...

<meta>This page begins the commentary on the section "Bo el Pharaoh" (Come to Pharaoh), specifically focusing on the mystical events of the Midnight of the Exodus. It follows the previous discussions on the plagues, transitioning now to the final stroke against Egypt and the nature of Divine judgment versus mercy.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

->**Come to Pharaoh**<-

**"And the Lord will pass through** to strike the Egyptians." What is the meaning of "And He will pass through"? It means to pass over the guards of judgment <note>original: *natorei dina*</note> who are crowned and bound with other crowns that are inclined toward evil. He did not remove their authority from their positions, but rather "passed over" His own mercy in order to execute judgment upon them and to avenge Israel. Thus, every instance of "And He passed," "And I will pass," or "And He passed over" regarding the Holy One, Blessed be He, means He bypassed His usual ways—sometimes for judgment and sometimes for mercy. Here, "And He passed through" was for the purpose of executing judgment. Elsewhere, "And He passed by" <note>referring to Exodus 34:6</note> was for the purpose of mercy.

<note>Exodus 12:23: "And the Lord will pass through to strike the Egyptians"</note>

**"And it came to pass** at midnight, that the Lord struck all the firstborn, etc." It is written:
> "But as for me, let my prayer be unto You, O Lord, in an acceptable time..."
<note>Psalms 69:14</note>
Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yose were traveling on the road toward Ganda Zapua. Rabbi Hiyya was riding on a donkey. Rabbi Yose said: It is written here "and we have arrived," for the time of the Afternoon Prayer <term>Mincha: the daily afternoon service associated with the attribute of Stern Judgment</term> has come. A person should always be careful regarding the Afternoon Prayer, to be seen and to be careful, because it is a time of judgment when it prevails, and a person must focus his intention. Rabbi Hiyya wrote and revealed [this matter]. While they were traveling, the sun began to set. Rabbi Hiyya said to Rabbi Yose: Sit. Rabbi Yose said: I was contemplating in my mind that the world only endures through the secrets of the people. When the leaders of the people <note>original: *reisha de-ama*</note> are righteous, it is good for the world and good for the people, and they live. If they are not righteous, woe to the world and woe to the people. Rabbi Hiyya said: And why is it so? From where do we know this? As it is written: "I have seen all," and he expounded on the verse regarding the herald: all those who have hunger and wine, the Lord did not bring them to the portion of the inhabited world, they shall return alive by their merit in peace. "They shall return, they shall dwell"—He brings him in. "To his house, in his house"—He brings him in, for they stand in both. Rather, thus we have learned: if the head of the people is not worthy, the people are seized for his sins. From where do we know this? As it is written: "And David was distressed, etc." and "It is I who have sinned and done very wickedly." What did they do? David sinned and Israel suffered. But if the head of the people is worthy, even if the people are seized for their sins, they are saved. For judgment does not rest upon them, as it is written: "And the Lord did not bring them to destruction," meaning He had pity on them; they were not the leaders of the people who strayed from the path. "They shall return alive by their merit in peace"—all of them are saved while their leaders are seized. Even Jehoshaphat had a decree issued against him to be punished because he joined with Ahab, but he lived, as it is written: "And Jehoshaphat cried out."

While they were traveling, night fell. They said: What shall we do? For the kindness of the night is like a scroll. It is written that it is a palm tree. They turned from the road and sat under a certain tree, and they sat and spoke words of Torah. When they slept until the dividing of the night <term>Midnight: Chatzot, the time when the North Wind blows and the Holy One enters the Garden of Eden</term>, they saw a certain hind passing before them, resting and letting out cries. Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yose rose and saw that it was trembling. They heard a voice proclaiming and saying: "Awakeners, rise! Those who stand, awaken! The worlds are prepared to meet your Master!" For a voice goes out, as it is written: "The Hind of the Dawn" <note>Psalms 22:1</note> and it opens. As it is written:
> "The voice of the Lord makes the hinds to calve, and strips the forests bare"
<note>Psalms 29:9</note>
For your Master goes out toward the pressure of the Palace to be punished with the righteous, as it is written:
> "And in His palace everyone says: Glory"
<note>Psalms 29:9</note>
Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yose sat. Rabbi Hiyya said: Now it is exactly midnight. Fortunate is the portion of those who merit to hear this! And come and see the secret of the matter: at the moment when the Holy One, Blessed be He, comes to the Garden, the whole Garden gathers and does not separate from Eden. And from this Eden, springs go out to many paths and trails, and the whole Garden is called the "Bundle of Life" <note>original: *Tzeror HaChayim*</note>, for the life therein is the delight of the righteous in the World to Come. And at that moment, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is revealed upon them. Rabbi Yose said: How many are the merits of those who wait, as it is written: **"And it came to pass at midnight, that the Lord struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt."** He said to him: Go out like the day that is revealed to all publicity, to see the radiance of all those kings of the Crown of Mercy, and those messengers of submission. And their kingdoms did not die, for His decree drew near, just as it was with Sennacherib, as it is written:
> "And the angel of the Lord went out and struck the camp of Assyria, etc."
<note>Isaiah 37:36</note>
And it shall be in the heart of kings, sons of kings, *Rufinum* and *Pardeski* <note>These appear to be mystical titles or names of angelic/spiritual governors, possibly derived from Latin *Rufinus* or Greek terms</note> were established there.

## Main Text (Zohar)

To show the power of his Master, his ascent was greater than what had been seen of him before, becoming even more elevated. He said to him: "The merit of the Patriarchs was not found in what I sought and did not see, but I have merited all the holiness that is prepared before us." <term>Rabbi Hamnuna the Elder</term> <note>A prominent, often mysterious figure in the Zohar, representing ancient wisdom</note> said: "From the time you went out, I acted in the manner of 'Come [unto Pharaoh],' and they sat until the morning light shone." When the light rose, they stood and went. When they reached him, they found him sitting with a book of *Aggadah* <note>Homiletic or narrative traditions</note> in his hands. He opened his discourse and said: "All that is hidden is like this; when He strikes, He opens and gives according to His kindness." Since he said "all that is hidden is like this," why did he say "He searches and gives according to His kindness"? Rather, we have learned that the <term>Ancient of Days</term> <note>Aramaic: Atika De-Atikin; refers to the most hidden, primordial aspect of the Divine</note> made the world of <term>Faith</term> <note>Aramaic: Meimanuta; refers to the realm of the Shekhinah or the structured spiritual reality</note> for them so they would not gaze upon it, and there appeared before them a false faith. Everything was rectified and given according to His kindness, like this world which is surrounded by wind and revolves in smoke like the firmaments; everything and all the inhabitants of the earth are unified.

He opened again and said: **"In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth"** <note>Genesis 1:1</note>. The word *Et* <note>The untranslatable Hebrew particle pointing to a direct object</note> refers to the days of the <term>Holy One, blessed be He</term>, and *Et* refers to the offspring. We have learned that the <term>Holy One, blessed be He</term>, turned and added, and created the heavens; He turned His name and created the earth. Everything is "also," as it is written: "My hand laid the foundation of the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens; when I call to them, they stand up together."
> "Indeed, My hand founded the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens; I call to them, they stand together." <note>Isaiah 48:13</note>

What is the meaning of "they stand together"? Heaven and earth—not (as those who err say, that He calls one and then the other—it is not so) but they are joined and rejoice to assist one another, *Et* and *Et*. And how do they "stand together"? This refers to the intention of that which is hidden at the division of the night, when all are *Et* and *Et*. And we have learned it is written: **"He has made everything beautiful in its time"** <note>Ecclesiastes 3:11</note>. This *Et* refers to the other. Everything is a whole, and the Lord blessed the *Et* with everything. And you see that He is the Crown who rejoices to be called, and the *Et* of everything is renewed. And He turns at the division of the night to His two sides, in <term>Mercy and Judgment</term>, hinting to the binding and the crushing for the sake of the Crown.

<term>Rabbi Hiyya</term> opened and said: "I have the strength before my Master, for it is pleasing to me to speak of what we have come for." It is written:

-> **And it came to pass** <-
**at midnight, that the Lord smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt** <note>Exodus 12:29</note>. And regarding what the Master said to strengthen this verse with that word below—we have seen the land that is prepared before us to come and ask before you. He opened and said: **"Who is like the Lord our God, who dwells on high, who humbles Himself to behold the things that are in heaven and in the earth?"** <note>Psalms 113:5-6</note>. Who is like the Lord our God, who ascends and is not found below, like a holy Crown that rules over all the gatherings of His throne with two crowns? He who prepares the rest of His strength in His crowns, from crown to crown, from light to light, from His throne to His throne, from foundation to foundation, to gaze upon the upper and lower beings. Everything, and the Lord humbles, He humbled the children of... etc.

Come and see the writing: "About the middle of the night." <margin> { </margin> It should have said "At midnight." And this is like the vision, like the glowing coal that Moses spoke of. And there is no blood of which we spoke that is blessed, so that they should not say: "We found the portion leaning when he saw the bush." Behold, the standing is like twelve, standing like a canopy to cover and dwell; they will say thus. First, if it were so, he should have said "And he said: Leaning toward the vision of the night." <margin> { </margin> And you see it says: "Thus says the Lord," just as he did not intend the exact hour, for it cannot be split like a hair or a thin line, because he said "Thus says the Lord," etc. Second, for Moses said: "Even unto the firstborn of the maidservant that is behind the mill," but it was not so; rather, it was "unto the firstborn of the captive that was in the dungeon." <margin> { </margin> In any case, even Israel—who would say such a thing? For the words were not clarified. Third, if he said "leaning" of the Patron, like a vision, yet it is written: "And it was at the middle of the night." <margin> { </margin> And further, your question is more than the burden that a blind man can bear. Rather, everything is the Spirit upon him, for the sake of the joy of the voice, and everything is bound in the faithful strength. Blessed is the portion of Moses, of whom it is written:
> "You are the most handsome of the sons of men; grace is poured upon your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever." <note>Psalms 45:2</note>

To strike the spark that is not evil:
> "Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness." <note>Psalms 45:8</note>

Gladness.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Come to Pharaoh**<-

"You are the most beautiful of the sons of men; grace is poured upon your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever." <note>Psalm 45:3</note> This refers to wisdom and establishment. <note>original: "Chokhmah and Koneni"</note> "Therefore God has blessed you forever"—this refers to the sweetness and the law <note>original: "nimus," from the Greek *nomos*</note>; the good oil that benefits. "From your sweetness"—this refers to the lack or the covering, etc. A man who ascends to the upper degrees <term>Sefirot: levels of divine emanation</term>, where no other man has ascended, does not even know what he says.

So we have learned: this latter part, which is the portion of "This" <note>Zoharic shorthand for the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> below, which is considered the totality of "This." It is called the honor of the lack, "my bread of my portion," for from life he took "This." From grace it was simple for him, the portion of the Name <note>original: "YH"</note>. And this is the Kindness <term>Chesed: the attribute of mercy</term> of the male, for this is the portion of the remnant. He escaped into it, and he apportioned to him "This" and "That" to him. And "This" is for the turning from "That" which is called "Male."

And because of this, she is a Palm Tree <note>Tamar</note>, male and female, for this one ascends and that one ascends. The Palm Tree is a bride in the bitterness of the goat. Just as the goat ascends in whiteness and wears a covering, so here everything is included at the midnight hour to perform His laws <note>nimusoi</note> as one. One hour is white for Israel and a garment of darkness for Esau <note>representing Rome/Egypt/Oppressors</term>. Furthermore, the night stands and is not divided until His laws are performed.

What is the meaning of "their lack"? As it is written: "And the night wrapped over them," for it was divided to perform His laws. Here, it is below other writings. What is the "preparation"? It is like the rising of the mortar, like the rising of the grain-heap. Here, the preparation is like a bit <note>bridle</note>. And who knows that He does not perform His laws until it is divided? And so it is: the night performed His laws until it was divided at the latter division, as it is said: **"And it came to pass at midnight."** <note>Exodus 12:29</note> The words "at the half" <note>Kachatzot</note> refer to the latter division, like the tradition that she rules and is found capable of performing His laws continually. And every law that is performed in the night is performed at the division, at the latter part.

**"And the Lord struck every firstborn"** at the hour when He arose and was awakened in the Garden of Eden to delight with the righteous. A herald goes out and calls: "Awake, O north wind, and come, O south; blow upon my garden, that its spices may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden and eat his choice fruits." <note>Song of Solomon 4:16</note> The words "eat his choice fruits" refer to the offerings that are brought before Him from the souls of the righteous; these are the midnight offerings, while at another time they are actual sacrifices.

"And the Lord" <note>V'Adonai</note>—this refers to Him and His House of Judgment; "And the Lord"—this is Him and His laws. Here, "every firstborn"—here it reaches to the other side of the slain and they died. Why is it that here He did not awaken until the preparation of the staff, as it is written: "And He struck them in my name until now"?

And you should know that Pharaoh was wiser than all his sorcerers, and he looked upon this one who performed judgment upon him, and who was destined to have mercy on his degree, as it is said: "By this you shall know that I am the Lord." <note>Exodus 7:17</note> And see what is written: "And Pharaoh turned." What is "and he turned"? That he turned his heart from this side entirely. "And Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he did not set his heart even to this." <note>Exodus 7:23</note> The word "even" <note>gam</note> comes to include that which was destined to have mercy on his degree, yet he did not set his heart to receive "This."

"Every firstborn"—for even the upper and lower degrees were broken from their dominion. All those who rule in their wisdom, as it is written: "From the firstborn of Pharaoh"—all the upper and lower degrees that were broken from their dominion, all of them were according to the mouth of that place, as it is written: "From the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne, to the firstborn of the maidservant who is behind the millstones, and all the firstborn of the cattle." <note>Exodus 11:5</note> Behold, all of them are seen according to the mouth of the hidden one who teaches: "From the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne"—this is the first crown of the foundations of the upper kingdom. "Until the firstborn of the maidservant"—this is the lower first crown, below the foundations, from the crown of the degree of their dwelling, the degree of the residence of the impurity, as it is written: "behind the millstones" and not "from the millstones."

"And all the firstborn of cattle"—these are the lowest of the low, the female of the females found among the lower ones like beasts, as it is written: "they were struck and received their blow," strangers and elders. "Until the firstborn of the captive who was in the dungeon"— <note>Exodus 12:29</note> these are those who go out from the doubt that is in them, who work to dig so that they will be enslaved forever and never go out to freedom. In their spirituality, these are the tangled degrees from which they made a smoke-screen for Israel so they would never leave their service. And in this, the might and dominion of the Holy One, Blessed be He, was shown, and this crushing will be shown to Israel in the final generations.

<meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Bo (Exodus 10:1–13:16), specifically focusing on the mystical mechanics of the Exodus from Egypt. It explores how the Holy One broke the "knots" or "crowns" of the Egyptian sorcery through the merit of the Patriarchs.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

...after them, and showed them the strength and might of the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: HaKadosh Baruch Hu</note>. All the kings of the nations and all the sorcerers of the world and the wise men of the world were not able to save them from the servitude of the side of their "knots" <note>referring to the spiritual bonds or "crowns" of impurity that held Israel captive</note>, until He struck all those crowns in order to bring them out. Concerning this, it is written:
> Who would not fear You, O King of the nations? For it is Your due; for among all the wise men of the nations and in all their kingdoms, there is none like You. <note>Jeremiah 10:7</note>

The verse does not say this in vain, but opens and speaks of the "knot of the resin" <note>a metaphor for the sticky, binding nature of Egyptian magic</note> which was revealed and surrounded, for the Holy One, blessed be He, surrounded it with many merits: "Who brought you out of the land of Egypt," "The Lord your God who brings you out from Egypt," "And the Lord your God brought you out from there," "I brought out your fathers," "Remember this day on which you went out from Egypt," "And He brought you out in His presence with His great power from Egypt," "The Lord who brings you out from this."

But come and see: there are seven crowns below <note>in the realm of the "Other Side" or impurity</note> corresponding to the pattern above, and all of them are hidden within three lower branches. Three knots were knotted into them upon three levels, through which they worked so that Israel would never go out from their servitude. Blessed are the Patriarchs—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—for in their merit these knots were untied. The Holy One, blessed be He, remembered the three knots of their faith. This is what is written <note>original: Hada Hu De-Khtiv</note>:
> And God remembered His covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob. <note>Exodus 2:24</note>

"With Abraham"—this is the first knot of Abraham. "With Isaac"—this is the second knot of Isaac. "With Jacob"—this is the third knot of Jacob. Praise be, for at all times and seasons, these memories are brought forth, and upon this all things are sustained. For if not for this, the "Side" <note>the Sitra Achra or Evil Side</note> would have controlled the times and seasons. Because of this, the memory of Egypt is found in all times and seasons. Come and see the holy place, the path and the scratch of the Torah, and all the holy ones and all the faith of the community of Israel.

Furthermore, why was the completion of the redemption not immediate? We have learned that it is written: "Today you are going out," and it is written: "The Lord your God brought you out of Egypt by night." But come and see: the essence of the redemption of Israel was only at night, for at night He broke the knots and performed vengeance, and by day He brought them out publicly. This is what is written: "The children of Israel went out with a high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians." Furthermore, at night He broke the knots and performed vengeance and judgments, and the day revealed and publicized the miracle and the vengeance that was done. This is what is written:
> The children of Israel went out with a high hand. <note>Exodus 14:8</note>

And it is written:
> While the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn, whom the Lord had struck down among them. <note>Numbers 33:4</note>

This is the publicizing of the miracle. Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yose taught: they prostrated themselves before Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai. They spoke and said: the engraved ones of above and below lift their heads because of you! The Holy One, blessed be He, made Jerusalem below in the pattern of the one above. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai made a wall around the Holy City and its gates; those who enter do not enter until the gates are opened. He who ascends does not ascend until the steps of the wall are prepared. And it is written:
> Three times a year all your males shall appear before the face of the Master, the Lord. <note>Exodus 23:17</note>

Who is "the face of the Master, the Lord"? This is Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>A bold Zoharic statement suggesting the Divine Presence is reflected through the Tzaddik, the righteous leader</note>, for whoever is a male among males must appear before him. He said to them: until now I have not finished the matter of your endeavor, for we have learned: "The Lord struck every firstborn"—"every firstborn" plainly, as we said, and so it was. And those who died were the "knots of knots" who were used in their sorcery like those crowns. From here they used the upper ones and from there the lower ones, even though they are all lower. All the magicians of Egypt were a matter of vanity. And it is written: "For there was no house where there was not someone dead." And it was made clear to all of them in their minds, for they were all struck in their houses and were not scattered in the desert or the field, but were all found in their houses. And this was aimed at the righteous, and He made the night like that hour. 

And the light of the night shone like the day of the summer solstice <note>original: Tekufat Tammuz</note>, and all the people saw the eyes of the Holy One, blessed be He. This is what is written:
> And the night shines as the day; the darkness is even as the light. <note>Psalms 139:12</note>

And at the time they went out, all the dead were found in the streets before the eyes of all those who were rushing to bury them, but they could not find a place, and this was the hardest thing of all for them: seeing Israel going out before their eyes...

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Exodus, specifically the portion of "Bo." It transitions from the mechanics of the Exodus to a broader philosophical inquiry into the nature of justice and the vanity of the world as expressed by King Solomon.</meta>

->**Come to Pharaoh**<-

## Main Text (Zohar)

...before their eyes many miracles, and at times they appeared as a single miracle. Everything was publicized in a way that had not occurred since the day the world was created. And come and see, it is written: <note>Exodus 12:42</note> **It is a night of vigil for the Lord to bring them out... this is that night for the Lord, a vigil for all the children of Israel.** This verse is difficult: since it says "night" <note>original: *layil*, masculine form</note>, why does it say "vigil" <note>original: *shimurim*, plural</note>? Why does it not say "guarded" <note>singular</note>? Why is the word repeated twice? And it is written "This is that night for Him"—it mentions the first part and then His own. Rather, thus we have learned: it is written <note>Deuteronomy 22:19</note> **Because he has brought out an evil name upon a virgin girl <note>na'arah</note>.** Up to this point in the Torah, the word is written deficiently <note>without the final 'h', reading as 'na'ar' or youth/boy</note> because as long as she has not received the male principle, she is called "youth" <note>na'ar</note>. Once she receives the male, she is called "maiden" <note>na'arah</note>. So too here, it is called "night" <note>layil</note> until it receives the male principle. And even though it is written "vigil" <note>shimurim</note>, the male was destined to be united with it. 

And after he was united with her, it says of the male: **This is that night for the Lord, a vigil.** "Vigil" <note>plural</note> refers to the male and the female <note>the union of divine attributes</note>. For this reason, it is written "This night." And after the male and female are united, there is no praise except for the male. And in this manner we, Israel, descend—we descend toward the male and not the female. All this is **This is my God and I will glorify Him** <note>Exodus 15:2</note>. There is no praise except after the male and female have united, and then for the male. Regarding this, Israel is seen to say: <note>Isaiah 25:9</note> **This is the Lord; we have waited for Him, we will be glad and rejoice in His salvation.** For the Ancient One is destined to act for them, as it is written: <note>Micah 7:15</note> **As in the days of your coming out of the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders.** And this secret is as follows: it is "night" <note>layil</note> and "nighttime" <note>laylah</note> when the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to act for them, as it is written: <note>Isaiah 21:11</note> **Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?** <note>original: *shomer mah mi-layil, shomer mah mi-leyl*</note>. What are these "guarding" and "night"? All of them are guarding and night. And "nighttime" <note>laylah</note> is established upon the male; everything is established in honor and strength. Then comes the morning: **And Abraham rose early in the morning** <note>Genesis 22:3</note>, which is the actual attribute <note>of Mercy/Chesed</note>, and it is written: <note>Psalms 5:4</note> **O Lord, in the morning You shall hear my voice.** Literally in the morning. And our Rabbis taught: they stood, etc., and the secret of the Priestly Torah was prepared for them, and they arranged it every day and sat before Him.

One day he went out and they did not see him clearly; they reached a certain clearing and sat. Rabbi Isaac opened and said: Come and see, it is written <note>Ecclesiastes 7:15</note> **All have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man who prolongs his life in his wickedness.** Solomon, whose wisdom was greater than all—why did he say this verse? Rather, Solomon was hinting at Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>. For we see the mercy of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is directed thus, as it is written: "to give to every man according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds." Yet there are two matters hinted at here: we have learned that when the eyes of the Holy One, Blessed be He, seek to gaze upon the world and look into it—as it is written: <note>Zechariah 4:10</note> **The eyes of the Lord, they run to and fro through the whole earth**—and He finds the guilty in the world, that righteous man who is found there is then seized for their sins. But for the wicked, the Holy One, Blessed be He, prolongs His anger with them until they repent. And if not for the righteous, there would be no one to plead for them. Thus, **there is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness** because that merit-worthy one is removed from the world. 

For this reason, we have learned: A person should never dwell except in a place where people of pious deeds dwell. Why? Because woe to the one whose dwelling is among the guilty, for he is seized for their sins. But one who dwells among the righteous, their merit gathers him in. For Rav Hisda originally dwelt among the Cappadocians, and the hour was pressed for him, and creditors pursued him in his wandering. But when he moved his dwelling among the "Masters of Shields" <note>term for great scholars</note> who guard, he ascended and merited many good things, much wealth, and much freedom. He said: I merited all this because I entered among those whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, gazes upon to do them good. 

Another explanation: **All have I seen in the days of my vanity.** Did Solomon, about whom it is said his wisdom was above all his generation and his lineage was like freedom to do good and truth—as it is written: <note>1 Chronicles 29:23</note> **And Solomon sat on the throne of the Lord**—how could he say **in the days of my vanity**? And it is written: <note>Ecclesiastes 1:2</note> **Vanity of vanities, says Kohelet, all is vanity.** And we find seven names for him: Solomon, Jedidiah, Agur, Bin Yakeh, Ithiel, Lemuel, and Kohelet. Kohelet corresponds to them all. And all of them are as Kohelet. Look into this.

## Main Text (Zohar)

They desired to ascend above in the holy assembly of the house of the crown <term>in this manner</term> <note>original: "k'gavna de'da" - a common Zoharic phrase meaning "in this way" or "correspondingly"</note>, a congregation of living beings in the manner of a crown, and a congregation of those who scoop from this, and the "Assembly" (Kohelet) of all, for she is the Bride, the Assembly of Jacob. And the living beings are gathered according to the order of Wisdom, which are called <term>in this manner</term> the three books Solomon made: Song of Songs, Ecclesiastes (Kohelet), and Proverbs. And all of them were made to complete Wisdom.

Song of Songs corresponds to **Loving-kindness** <note>Chesed</note>.
Ecclesiastes corresponds to **Judgment** <note>Din</note>.
Proverbs corresponds to **Mercy** <note>Rachamim</note>.

This was in order to complete Wisdom, and behold, he did all that he did to complete Wisdom. And corresponding to the lower world, he observed it and said: "The days of vanity, vanity of vanities." However, the spirit of "breath" <note>Hebel - also translated as vanity</note> is precious. It is the breath that issues from the mouth, and from the spirit of the breath that issues from the mouth, a voice is made. And the living beings gather, for the world is sustained only by the breath of the mouths of school children who have not sinned. Or rather, [even if] they actually sinned, the voice is made into a spirit through the breath. And whatever is made through the breath and spirit of these children, a voice is made that spreads through the world, and they are the guardians of the world and the guardians of the city. Unless the "Breath" <note>referring to God/the spiritual source</note>, Heaven forbid, guards the city... <note>Psalm 127:1</note> etc.

Come and see: He is "Breath" (Hebel), He is the "Stalk" (Kelach). What is the difference between *Hebel* and this *Kelach*? It is thin and frail like the food that comes from a stalk. A literal stalk is thin in its standing, not producing anything else. And it was the "breath" that came from his Wisdom; when he looked at the city, he called it "vanity" (Hebel), and from it comes everything that exists. And even though they are assisted by other higher revelations, they were his, and it is known from this that he said: "the days of my vanity," for from it they do not sin below. And the spirit from it is the "Breath of the All."

"There is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:15</note>. This is the spirit of the matter that he revealed and published. "The days of my vanity"—meaning, at the time when this "Breath" draws from the Spirit to execute Judgment, "a righteous man perishes in his righteousness." And at the time when this "Breath" draws from Mercy, "a wicked man prolongs his life in his evil." Both of them depend on this "Breath." And because of this, it is written "as the days" and not "in the days," for all depend on the days of the Living Breath. One who is stricken by Judgment is like wax; one who is stricken by Mercy is like mercy. And if you say, "there is a righteous man who perishes" <note>obed</note> and it does not say "is lost" <note>abud</note>, it is because he is literally perishing; for the destroying Judgment goes and removes the righteous man from the world and pushes him away. And "there is a wicked man who prolongs his life in his evil"—literally prolongs; for that Judgment of the "All" draws from Mercy and performs mercy for that wicked man and prolongs his life.

While they were sitting, they saw a smoke that was ascending upward and bending downward. He said: This protection that is protected like the clay of the earth, from within the mixture that smoke ascends, a scent of all spices. He said: It is written here that the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> is with us to be sustained, because of the "fragrance of a field which the Lord has blessed." He opened and said:

> "And he smelled the fragrance of his garments, and blessed him, and said: See, the smell of my son..." <note>Genesis 27:27</note>

"And he smelled the fragrance of his garments"—this implies that those garments were emitting a good scent to the Most High. It was removed from the covering. Now, Wisdom descends to him; it is written "the fragrance of his garments" and it is written "the fragrance of my son." Rather, he said "the fragrance of his garments" which is "the fragrance of my son." Even the moisture, once it is gathered, it draws as his people are gathered. And we have learned: those garments belonged to the first man <note>Adam HaRishon</note>, as it is written:

> "And the Lord God made for Adam and for his wife <term>garments of skin</term> and clothed them." <note>Genesis 3:21</note>

And we have learned: if you say it is written "and they sewed fig leaves," if so, why is it written "and the Lord God made" and it is written <term>garments of skin</term> <note>Ketnot Or - spelled with an Ayin, meaning skin/leather</note>? It should have been fig leaves. Rather, it is as the Translation <note>Targum</note> says: <term>garments of honor</term> <note>Lebushin de-Yakar - associated with Ketnot Or spelled with an Aleph, meaning garments of Light</note>. And they emitted fragrances from the spices of Eden. And we have learned: when he went, they were made, as it is written "And the Lord made"—completing what was not made by the hand of Samael <note>the accuser/angel of death</note> and the earth. They were revealed, and behold it is written regarding the garments: "Lord God..." [they were] pure and hidden. It is not a difficulty. Rather, all that were made for her were made as a covering. But when they did not endure as a covering, they endured [differently]. And what they said—that those garments came to that wicked one, Esau, as it is written of them from the priest—so we have established it... but if so, behold it is written "for Adam and his wife," for their covering and for the covering of death, garments of significance, what became of them? Thus they all...

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Come to Pharaoh** <-

By what are all the arms <note>The Sefirot of Hesed (Mercy) and Gevurah (Strength)</note> and shoulders bound together? They are bound so that they may have holiness, specifically the garments in which Mercy and Strength are clothed. These are like a staff for the life of those garments, mirroring the pattern above; all the arms are clothed in them. Come and see, it is written: *He put on righteousness as a breastplate* <note>Isaiah 59:17</note>, and it is written: *The Lord reigns, He is clothed with majesty* <note>Psalms 93:1</note>, and it is written: *Splendor and majesty are before Him* <note>Psalms 96:6</note>, and *Who covers Himself with light as with a garment* <note>Psalms 104:2</note>. Once He is clothed in what He is clothed, He performs what He performs. Below, in the Holy Temple, the royal garments were fashioned after the pattern above. The portion of the world belongs to Him, and they cast honor upon the glory of their garments. Come and see: *And he smelled the smell of his garments and blessed him, and said: "See, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field which the Lord has blessed"* <note>Genesis 27:27</note>. From where did Isaac know the "smell of a field which the Lord has blessed"? Rather, these are two matters that are actually one, as it is written: *And Isaac went out to meditate in the field toward evening* <note>Genesis 24:63</note>. He had a specific "house" where he prayed, and he saw that this field was the <term>Field of Holy Apples</term> <note>original: "Hakal Tapuchin Kadishin"; a mystical name for the Shekhinah or the Sefirah of Malkhut</note> near the cave, as it is written: *The field which Abraham purchased from the sons of Heth* <note>Genesis 25:10</note>. At the time Isaac entered it, he saw the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence</note> over them, and all the "arms" and all the words were received and bound there where he prayed. The Holy One, blessed be He, established the primary order there. No other scent was ever changed to be like this scent. Why was it called Moriah? After the name of the "Good Myrrh" <note>original: "Mor ha-tov"</note>. He knew all this deeply in its enclosure. Therefore, he did not attribute the matter to the physical garments, but rather in Jacob he saw what he saw—that the essence was within him—and the blessing descended and was realized. Rabbi Isaac said: The Torah only needed to write "from the field" to be understood. Why then [the extra words]? To show that the Holy One, blessed be He, is bound to that which is bound to Him, as it is written: *And this field...* <note>Genesis 23:17</note>. All life is bound as one, and the Crown <note>Keter</note> is for Him like male and female as one; it is only found through the Male, and for this reason, his soul loved it. Rabbi Judah said: Why did Isaac say this twice? To humble [the sitra achra] and diminish it further, as it is written: *For the Lord’s portion is His people*—this binding is for you and not for the other nations.

-> **Speak** <-
*unto all the congregation of Israel, saying: In the tenth day of this month they shall take to them every man a lamb...* <note>Exodus 12:3</note>. On the tenth. Rabbi Isaac said: This is the time when power is established, as it is written: *On the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement* <note>Leviticus 23:27</note>. *They shall take to them every man a lamb according to the house of their fathers.* This was to prove that the "crowns" <note>referring to the Egyptian powers</note> are hanging, and against them He spread a net. He said: "Draw out and take for yourselves," as it is written: "Withdraw [your hands from idols] and take." The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "Perform an action below, and I will break their strength above." Just as you deal with fire, so I will give... on the tenth, it enters like a sword of ten. Rabbi Isaac said: Israel was bound for four hundred years. See that for four hundred years they were not enslaved [entirely], but in order to be bound to Him and strengthened over [the nations], all those 400 years were accounted for. For this reason, they delayed the lamb for four days <note>from the 10th to the 14th of Nissan</note>, bound to the bed, until *the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it at twilight* <note>Exodus 12:6</note>. This is to take hold of the needs within the mystery of the night, when the matter is strengthened.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Exodus from Egypt, specifically focusing on the transition from the "Other Side" (the domain of impurity) to the "Holy Domain" of God. ## Come to Pharaoh (Bo)

This matter is not in the hands of others, as it is written:
> And it came to pass, as the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, a dread, even a great darkness, fell upon him... <note>Genesis 15:12</note>

After this, there was one darkness, and after that, a "great darkness." For even though we have established this verse as referring to the other enslavements of Israel <note>the four future exiles</note>, everything follows this pattern. As we have learned, they are purified from Above. A teacher taught: Israel was confined in Egypt until all the celestial powers governing them were broken, and Israel departed from their domain and entered the Supernal Holy Domain of the Holy One, blessed be He, and were bound to Him. This is what is written:
> For unto Me the children of Israel are servants; they are My servants... <note>Leviticus 25:55</note>

What is the reason it says "they are My servants"? It is their deed of manumission <note>freedom papers</note> from Egypt, to take them out of the **Other Domain** <term>Sitra Achra: the side of impurity or "the other side"</term> and to bring them into My domain. And this is what Rabbi Shimon said regarding what is written:
> ...even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses; for whosoever eateth leavened bread... <note>Exodus 12:15</note>

It shall not be found among you. We have said that this **leaven** <term>Se'or: sourdough starter</term> and **leavened bread** <term>Chametz</term> are of the same level; they all hint at one thing. They represent the powers and appointees over the other nations, and we call them the **Evil Inclination** <term>Yetzer Hara</term>, which is an "other" that is not like their own. So too here, leaven and leavened bread are all one. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "All this time you existed under the Other Domain, serving another. From here on, you are free men." Therefore: "on the first day you shall put away leaven from your houses," "no leavened thing shall you eat," and "no leaven shall be seen with you."

Rabbi Yehuda said: If so, this should apply all the days of the year as well! Why specifically the seven days as it is written:
> Seven days shall there be no leaven found in your houses... <note>Exodus 12:19</note>

Seven days and no more? Rather, whenever a person is required to show himself as a free man, this is necessary. When he is not so required, it is not necessary. It is like a king who made a triumph <note>original: *rufus*, likely referring to a Roman-style celebratory procession</note> for a man; all those days that he ascends to this rank and wears garments of honor and this crown, he must set aside all other burdens. So too, those days when Israel ascends to this glory and wears the garments [of freedom] etc. Every single year, in this manner, it is written for Israel: "Seven days leaven shall not be found," for these are the days of the **Moon** <term>The Shekhinah/Divine Presence</term> when she is destined to ascend to this glory, and they left the other enslavement and entered the Holy Domain. Therefore it is written: "Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread (Matzot)."

Rabbi Shimon said: **Matzat** <note>unleavened bread</note> is written without the letter *Vav* <note>מצת instead of מצות</note>, certainly. And why is it called *Matzat*? Because it is the female principle <note>the Shekhinah</note> without the male principle, not yet united in the holy brain, for she was not yet strengthened by all. And from here, in their likeness, are Israel; for she stands in poverty <note>diminished</note>. And because she stands in this poverty, it is written: **Bread of Affliction** <term>Lechem Oni</term>. Why is she in poverty? Because the "uncovering" <note>circumcision</note> had not yet occurred for this nation, for it was a decree of "it shall be," and the rages were not yet pacified... <note>The text here uses cryptic terms like *sam sam* possibly referring to the "poison" of the serpent or medicinal herbs</note>. And even though we established this verse in another matter, it is all one. And if you say: in the days of Joshua they were uncovered <note>circumcised</note>, as it is written: "And all the people that were born in the wilderness by the way..." <note>Joshua 5:5</note>.

After they were circumcised, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: "At first, you ate Matzot because the Moon <note>Shekhinah</note> was in poverty, and it was called 'Bread of Affliction.' From here on, the bread is from another place, which is from the Brain <note>the higher intellect/Heaven</note>," as it is written:
> Behold, I will cause to rain bread from heaven for you... <note>Exodus 16:4</note>

This was not from the Moon, but truly from Heaven, as it is written:
> So God give thee of the dew of heaven... <note>Genesis 27:28</note>

And the holy Israel, during those days above, are under the wings of the **Shekhinah** <term>The Divine Presence</term> and they guard that Passover of theirs from this side. Therefore it is written:
> The feast of unleavened bread shalt thou keep... <note>Exodus 23:15</note>

And it is written: "And you shall guard the Matzot." My hope is that "guarding the Matzot" and "guarding the covenant" <note>circumcision</note> all rise as one level and are unified. And if you say: how did the Matzah not "uncover" them? It was so that Israel would not be mixed there until they were transformed. Therefore it is written:
> ...seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread therewith, even the bread of affliction... <note>Deuteronomy 16:3</note>

What is the reason for "Bread of Affliction"?...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Torah portion "Bo" (Exodus 10:1–13:16). It transitions from the general narrative of the Exodus to the specific spiritual mechanics of the Matzah (unleavened bread) and the commandment to retell the story of the departure from Egypt. The text maintains the Zohar's characteristic symbolic language, where physical objects like bread and the moon represent divine emanations.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Come to Pharaoh**<-

<note>original: "Bo el Par'oh"</note>

My servants, because they were snatched away and changed, as it is written: *and they could not tarry.* <note>Exodus 12:39</note> Come and see: all the Israelites who entered Pharaoh's domain entered into decrees and were enslaved by him. It is written: *You shall eat no leavened bread with it; [seven days you shall eat] the bread of poverty.* <note>Deuteronomy 16:3; original: "lechem oni"</note> What is this "bread of poverty"? It is the bread of affliction. It is meant to show the state of the "Poor Soul" <note>A reference to the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence, in her state of exile</note>. This is because the Moon <note>The Shekhinah</note> stood in a state of diminution <note>original: "pegimuta"</note>; she was not blessed by the Sun <note>Tiferet, the masculine divine principle</note> and did not receive light from the Sun at all, for everything was like darkness and gloom, without any light shining. Why then is it called the bread of "repayment" <note>A wordplay on "lechem tipre'u"</note>? Rather, it is so that Israel would be circumcised and "uncovered" <note>A reference to the covenant of circumcision, "peri'ah"</note> so that they would lack nothing, as it is written: *in which you shall lack nothing.* <note>Deuteronomy 8:9</note> And because of this, *you shall eat the bread of poverty.* Why "you shall lack nothing"? Just as they were told in Egypt. In every place and time, Israel performs the remembrance of Egypt; they eat and do not change from generation to generation. Because of this, to be "uncovered" here in Egypt, they lacked the manifestation of "All" <note>The divine grade of Yesod</note>, and the Moon stood in diminution, in the state of the "Poor Soul"—"poor" as the translation <note>Aramaic Targum</note> renders it: "poverty." And what they ate there in Egypt was for a remembrance of Egypt, a law for all generations. And for the time to come, it is written: *Your sun shall no more go down, nor shall your moon withdraw itself...* <note>Isaiah 60:20</note> Come and see, Rabbi Shimon said: It is written "clarification" like a hammer, and it is written "but the clarification of the bread of the poor." On the Day of Atonement, it is diminished as it was said, for it is written: *on the tenth of the month, a statute.* What is this speaking of? Rather, "clarification" <note>original: "be'ur"</note>—this matter depends on clarification. *For the month, a statute.* Like the new moon, a statute; from here, examine closely. But when it comes to the day that corresponds to that level, it is written specifically *for the month, a statute.*

### **And they shall take**
> *to them every man a lamb, according to the house of their fathers, a lamb for a house.* <note>Exodus 12:3</note>

To teach of three knots. These are three knots that all "blackness" is tied to; they are all three colors of the night. And in all these that are called "grace" <note>original: "chen"</note>, everything is tied together. They are all included together to be tied in grace, and it is impossible to be separated from its knots. They were all tied up, and regarding this it is written: *And it shall be for you to keep* <note>Exodus 12:6</note>—tie him up in his own accusations <note>original: "kitrunia"</note>, and he shall be delivered into your hands when you are ready, until you take him and perform judgment upon him. And for the time to come, it is written: *Who is this that comes from Edom...* <note>Isaiah 63:1</note> and it is written: *For the Lord has a sacrifice in Bozrah* <note>Isaiah 34:6</note> and it is written: *And the Lord shall be king over all the earth; in that day shall the Lord be one, and His name one.* <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>
