## Commentary: Faithful Shepherd

->**The Faithful Shepherd**<-
<note>The "Raya Mehemna" is a later layer of the Zohar, often attributed to the soul of Moses, focusing on the mystical reasons for the commandments.</note>

### **And they carried**
> *The people took their dough before it was leavened...* <note>Exodus 12:34</note>

This is the commandment to remove leaven <note>Chametz</note>, for this commandment was handed over to Israel. This is "the people took their dough before it was leavened." And it is written: *[leaven] shall not be found in your houses.* The companions have established this, and the secret we have established is the difference between leaven <note>representing the evil inclination/pride</note> and Matzah <note>representing humility/purity</note>, just as they merit—this is the greater will, the greater good. The commandment following this is to tell the praise of the Exodus from Egypt, to show the vitality of a person who speaks of this praise forever. Thus we have established: every person who speaks of the Exodus from Egypt and rejoices in that story, the Holy One, Blessed Be He, rejoices with him. It is a time to rejoice with the Shekhinah in the World to Come, which is the greatest joy of all—to have joy when one rejoices in his Master. And the Holy One, Blessed Be He, rejoices in that story at that very hour; the Holy One, Blessed Be He, assembles all His celestial retinue <note>original: "pamalyya"</note> and says to them: "Go and hear the story of My praise that My children are telling, and how they rejoice in My redemption!" Then they all gather and come and join with the Israelites, and they hear the story of praise, and they rejoice in the spirit of the redemption of their Master. Then they come and give thanks to the Holy One, Blessed Be He, for all those miracles and mighty deeds, and they thank Him for the holy nation that He has on earth, who rejoice in the joy of the redemption of their Master. Then, strength and might are increased above. And Israel, through that story, gives strength to their Master, like a king whose strength and might are increased when they praise his might and give him thanks. And all are silenced before Him, and His glory is exalted above all. And because of this, it is an obligation to speak of the story...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Exodus from Egypt, specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of confession and the symbolic power of the Passover sacrifice and circumcision.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

Because it is said that this "theft" <note>referring to the hidden nature of sin</note> should not rule over a person, one must always speak before the Holy One, blessed be He, in every training <note>or "habitual practice"</note> regarding what they have done. And if you say: why show one's sins before Him? Does the Holy One, blessed be He, not already know everything—all that was and all that will be? Why then must one publicize this before Him when He already knows? Indeed, a person must publicize and speak before Him regarding everything they have sinned and every wrong they have committed. Because those words ascend, and all the Heavenly Family <note>the angelic hosts</note> gather and open them, and they all give thanks to the Holy One, blessed be He. And His glory is uplifted over them above and below, in this manner of one who speaks and specifies his sins for all that he has done.

And if you say: why is this necessary? It is because the Accuser <note>original: *Samael* or the Satanic force</note> stands constantly before the Holy One, blessed be He, to speak of the sins of humankind and to gaze upon them for evil. Once a person anticipates this and specifies his sins one by one, no opening of the mouth is left for that Accuser, and he cannot gaze upon him for evil. For the Accuser always demands judgment first, and afterward he speaks and accuses: "So-and-so did such-and-such." Therefore, a person must be proactive and specify his sins. Once the Accuser brings his case, he has no opening of the mouth against him, and thus he is separated from him entirely. And if he returns in repentance <note>original: *teshuvah*</note>, then the Accuser is not found over them, except to say: "So-and-so sinned before You with strength," but the person has already covered his sins through this confession. For this reason, he is not remembered for evil because he is found as a servant standing before the Holy One, blessed be He.

The commandment after this is to eat Matzah <note>unleavened bread</note> like the Passover offering, so that it shall be a remembrance for generations upon generations regarding the secret of faith. And this has been established: that they went out from the "bread of poverty" <note>original: *nan d'anya*</note> at that time, from the spirit of those who wander and err, and they entered into the Spirit of Faith. And this has been established as the "Pure Spirit," as it is written and clarified.

**And the Lord said** unto Moses and Aaron, etc.: "This is the ordinance of the Passover..." <note>Exodus 12:43</note>. This commandment is to slaughter the Passover lamb between the evenings, as a weeping remembrance of what was done with the Passover of Egypt. And this is the supplication over all: "And the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it between the evenings." This decree was required to be on the tenth day <note>of the month</note> to crown the Right Side <note>the attribute of Mercy/Chesed</note> and to begin, as it is written: "On the tenth day of this month they shall take for themselves..." <note>Exodus 12:3</note>. Why? Because then is the beginning of the foundation of Kindness <note>Chesed</note> which crowns the Right, until it is completed on the fourteenth, so that it may be like a purse <note>or vessel</note> against the claim of the Accuser that hangs over the world. This spirit is to remove the filth from before the Holy One, and to find in that spirit that the Righteous One <note>the sefirah of Yesod</note> is vacant of judgment. And any uncircumcised person shall not eat of it. For one who possesses the Holy Covenant <note>circumcision</note> may eat of it. One who does not possess the Holy Covenant may not eat of it, for through the Covenant, the strength of the profane is broken to remove the "foreskin" <note>the *klipah* or shell of impurity</note> from before the Covenant. Thus, only those of the Covenant may perform the service, and not those of the foreskin.

When the Holy One, blessed be He, came to Egypt, He saw the blood of the Passover which was smeared on the entrance, and the blood of the Covenant <note>circumcision</note> standing together at the entrance. It is written: "And you shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and strike [the lintel]..." <note>Exodus 12:22</note>. This hyssop, we have established, is what removes the evil spirit. Every side of the evil spirit is removed through its awakening, like the supernal redemption of Israel. To show that the glory of the Heart comes to... and He opened with this redemption, as it is written: "And the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it..." <note>Exodus 12:6</note>. A remembrance of the time to come in that supernal redemption upon the doorposts and the lintel, like the marking of the letter *Dalet* and the letter *Yod* <note>forming the name of God or the word for "Hand"</note>, to show the marking of the Holy Covenant and to break the foreskin before it. The blood of the Covenant is marked over all, and below, blood upon blood. When that is found, the Destroyer sees the mark and [passes over] all, "and He will not suffer the Destroyer [to come into your houses]" <note>Exodus 12:23</note>. By the life of the Holy One, He was the one who killed, yet it says "He will not suffer the Destroyer," which implies the Destroyer was going and not the Holy One. But certainly, the Holy One, blessed be He, was killing and descending... to be found...

## Main Text (Zohar)

It was found regarding Israel that when that <term>Destroyer</term> <note>The angel of death or judgment</note> saw the sign upon which the two sides were crowned, he would flee and separate from them. Because the Holy One, blessed be He, killed all those firstborn of that "other side" <note>The realm of impurity/Sitra Achra</note>, He gave the firstborn to Israel for their redemption. <term>Metatron</term> <note>The supreme angelic prince</note> offered praise over them, mentioning the world in general, and in all things the Holy One, blessed be He, guarded them as a father guards his children.

->**In one**<- house it shall be eaten; you shall not carry any of the flesh outside the house, etc. <note>Exodus 12:46</note>. This commandment is to eat the <term>Passover offering</term> <note>Pesach</note> with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. Why is it written "unleavened bread" <note>Matzah</note>? It corresponds to the "bread of poverty," so that the "engraving of poverty" should be found with them, so they would know the bitterness they endured, as it is written:
> And they embittered their lives with hard labor, etc. <note>Exodus 1:14</note>

And when they ate this Passover sacrifice, it was to make manifest all that the Egyptians had done to them, like the engraving of that servitude. What is written? "And you shall not break a bone in it" <note>Exodus 12:46</note>. This was to bring shame upon all the idols of the Egyptians. For the bones were cast into the streets, and they saw dogs dragging them from courtyard to courtyard. This was not difficult for the Israelites <note>to leave the bones whole</note> because the bones represent the structure of the body, and it resembles the "other" bones. Seeing them in the street was a disgrace <note>to the Egyptian gods, often depicted as animals</note>. Furthermore, it is written "you shall not break a bone in it"—it appeared as though you should not break them, but the dogs would come afterward and see those bones which were discarded, and they would crush them and taste them like dust. This was so the dogs would not find them <note>whole</note>, and this is the reason for the extra wood from their side. When the Holy One, blessed be He, rose in His glory, all those "others" were subdued. By this hand, the "nullification" from their side was further subdued, and for Israel, they do not nullify them, as it is written: "And you shall not break a bone in it."

->**Sanctify**<- to Me every firstborn, whatever opens the womb, etc. <note>Exodus 13:2</note>. This commandment is to sanctify the firstborn of the animals. Two matters depend on this: one, that it be redeemed from under the authority of the <term>Evil Inclination</term> <note>Yetzer ha-Ra</note>, who is its master, just as Jacob said to Esau:
> Let my lord pass on ahead of his servant <note>Genesis 33:14</note>

In this world, for judgment from all the debts that cover the body, as we have established: "The Evil Inclination comes stripped," while the <term>Good Inclination</term> <note>Yetzer ha-Tov</note> is also stripped. For the "intermediate" person, both of them judge him. The "intermediate" is the "You" of the Evil Inclination and the "You" of the Good Inclination. "My brother, keep what is yours." When merits are suppressed, the pressure breaks the two watches—which are the "morning stars" crying out—and it rises to the next watch in which "Man" <note>Adam/the spiritual human form</note> is arranged. When they come, he arranges them: "And I have oxen, donkeys, flocks, male and female servants," and he rises to the level of "Man" of whom it was said:
> And let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the heavens, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, etc. <note>Genesis 1:26</note>

And when merits are intermediate, "And a man wrestled with him" <note>Genesis 32:25</note>. Thorns and thistles embrace to strengthen the battle from the side of merits. "And when he saw that he could not prevail against him" from the side of sins, "he touched the socket of his hip," corresponding to the soul-flesh of the body. For God dismissed all his toil. This is the language used for one of the seven dwellings... there he prophesied from the ruins of Memphis... before the light... the world was dimmed. And he shall go out from there to the outside. "And a man wrestled with him"—this refers to the "stranger" <note>the shadow side</note>, like that embrace of dust of which it was said:
> And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground <note>Genesis 2:7</note>

And he exchanged it for their kick. Because of this, "And He formed" <note>Vayietzer, spelled with two 'yods'</note>—one for the Good Inclination, which is of a pure nature, and one for the Evil Inclination that wrestled with him, of which it was said: "Because he touched the socket of Jacob’s hip at the sinew of the thigh-vein." It was found that their nature was weakened, for the Good Inclination was exchanged for him. Before all this, four angels from below fought with him: one gives him merit, the voice of <term>Michael</term> <note>The angel of mercy</note> through the merit of Abraham; the second is <term>Gabriel</term> <note>The angel of strength</note> through the merit of Isaac; the third who fought with him is <term>Nuriel</term> through the merit of Jacob; and the fourth is <term>Raphael</term> <note>The angel of healing</note> through the merit of the First Man. The Good Inclination is above him for the World to Come. Therefore, it is established: "The wicked—the Evil Inclination judges him; the righteous—the Good Inclination judges him; the intermediate—both judge him." Therefore, the "intermediate" lives by <term>Gabriel</term>, who is the Good Inclination, and <term>Samael</term>... <note>The text cuts off as it begins to discuss the angelic representative of the Evil Inclination</note>

# Come to Pharaoh

And their side is the **Evil Inclination** <note>Hebrew: *Yetzer ha-Ra*</note>; this is the "Serpent" that judges him. For every human being who possesses an Evil Inclination, his right side is weakened by four angels from the right and four from the left. The four from the right are **Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, and Nuriel**, and the four from the left are **Iniquity, Destroyer, Anger, and Wrath**. From the aspect of the body, **Metatron** <note>The supreme angelic scribe and mediator</note> descends upon him from the right and the left. And regarding a person who has an Evil Inclination, his right side—according to the unity of the Holy One, Blessed be He—perceives these four "Holy Living Creatures" <note>Hebrew: *Chayot ha-Kodesh*; the highest order of angels in Ezekiel's vision</note> according to his guiding star.

The sign is: **Michael** and his crown, **Gabriel** and his crown, **Nuriel** and his crown, **Raphael** and his crown. If his guiding star is the Holy **Loving-kindness** <note>Hebrew: *Chesed*</note>, then it is **Raphael** and his crown, Michael and his crown, Gabriel and his crown, Nuriel and his crown. If his guiding star is the Holy **Might** <note>Hebrew: *Gevurah*</note>, then it is **Gabriel** and his crown, Michael and his crown, Nuriel and his crown, and Raphael and his crown. If his guiding star is the **Crown** <note>Hebrew: *Keter*; the highest Sefirah</note> of the Holy One, Blessed be He, then it is Michael and his crown, Gabriel and his crown, Raphael and his crown, and Nuriel and his crown. These are all from the side of the right; all four are Mercies, in the manner of the "Bestowal of Loving-kindness."

From the side of **Michael**, who is bowed, there is whiteness and purity; every miracle is an act of kindness. A pious and wise man <note>Hebrew: *Chassid ve-Chacham*</note> strives to excel in piety. But if not, the reverse occurs from the side of the **Evil Inclination**: a robber and a predator who possesses no kindness. For "an unrefined person cannot be pious" <note>A reference to Ethics of the Fathers 2:5</note>. From the side of **Gabriel**, his four aspects are the attribute of Judgment against the wicked; he prevails over them, as we have established, appearing as a shield in the world. In this, one is "mighty in Torah," a "fearer of sin," and a "judge" who shall live and occupy himself with piety for his students. Conversely, from the side of the **Evil Inclination**, he is aroused against the righteous to be hard toward them, "mighty in transgression" to do evil, not fearing sin, etc., and using his mouth for theft and bloodshed like Esau.

One whose guiding star is **Crown** <note>*Keter*</note> does not hate the attribute of Judgment, for he balances between the good and the evil like the scales of a balance; he has white and erased aspects. One whose guiding star is **Loving-kindness** <note>*Chesed*</note> from the side of Good is included in all good traits: pious, wise, mighty in Torah, fearing sin, and restrained in all good qualities. From the side of the **Evil Inclination**, he is filled with all evil traits... until all the guards of the Evil Inclination depart from him, and he crowns over his limbs the Intellect and all its guards. If merits prevail, the guards of the **Good Inclination** rule until all the guards of the Evil Inclination depart from him, and the guards of the Good Inclination rule over all his limbs. At that time, he is saved... Victory and Strength stand over him from his right and his left; these on the right to merit him, and these on the left to find him liable. Therefore, the Masters of the Academy established: "A person should always see himself as if the entire world depends upon him" <note>Talmud, Kiddushin 40b</note>.

From the side of **Michael**, he is called "Firstborn" <note>Hebrew: *Bechor*</note>; his level is Silver, which is whiteness. Because of this, the **Redemption of the Firstborn** <note>Hebrew: *Pidyon ha-Ben*</note> is performed with five silver coins, corresponding to the five of **Wisdom** <note>*Chokhmah*</note>, which is Wisdom in the Torah. One adds to it the letter *Yod* of "fear" <note>*Yirah*</note>, as it is written: "One must sanctify the firstborn of the cattle," which is "Israel is holy to the Lord." Through this, one must crown the offspring... from the side of the "Son of Yah" <note>The first two letters of the Tetragrammaton</note>... for all life comes from the "Holy Living Creatures" below. Regarding the Holy Name, it is written:

> "Everyone who is called by My name, and whom I have created for My glory, whom I have formed, even whom I have made." (Isaiah 43:7)

All creatures below are within them, and there is no creature that does not move within this structure to know Him who created it. The image of all creatures is the letter *He* and *He* <note>The two *He*s of the Divine Name</note>; the image of the *He* is found on the right and the *He* on the left, and the image of the body. Because of this:

> "To whom then will you liken Me, that I should be equal? says the Holy One." (Isaiah 40:25)

There is no creature that truly looks like Him, even though I created it in the likeness of My vision, so that the righteous one can perceive that Creator and act many times... but no one can truly see My image.

<meta>This page continues the discourse of the "Faithful Shepherd" (Raya Mehemna) within the portion of Bo. It addresses the central paradox of Kabbalah: how a formless, infinite God is described using human imagery and names. It connects to the previous themes of divine revelation and the nature of the Sefirot (divine emanations).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Come to Pharaoh**<-

<note>The title of the Torah portion</note> my image; and because of this, it shall not be for you according to your own manner, for your thrones and visions are divided. "And you grasped a man," it is written, *for you saw no form* <note>Deuteronomy 4:15</note>. They will answer him: but this "form" exists, for it is written, *and he beholds the form of the Lord* <note>Numbers 12:8</note>! However, [He is] not in any form of male or female, for He created and formed everything and is prepared [to appear in them]. And because of this, it says: *To whom then will you liken Me, that I should be equal?* and *To what likeness will you compare Him?* <note>Isaiah 40:18, 25</note>. For even this "form" He does not possess in His own place, but only when He descends to rule over [His creations] and spreads Himself over the creatures, appearing to each one according to the appearance, vision, and imagination [of the recipient]. And this is what is meant by: *And through the hand of the prophets I used parables* <note>Hosea 12:11; original: "adameh" - I will be likened</note>. And because of this He said: even though I appear to you in your images, *to whom will you liken Me that I should be equal?* For before He created any image in the world and sketched any form, He was alone, without form or likeness. And for one who perceives Him before the creation—where He is beyond any image—it is forbidden to make for Him any form or image in the world, not with the letter *He* (ה), nor with the letter *Yod* (י), and not even with the Holy Name, nor with any letter or point in the world. And this is the meaning of *for you saw no form*—anything that possesses form or likeness, you did not see. 

But after He made this image of the Chariot of the <term>Supernal Man</term> <note>Adam Ila'ah: the primordial spiritual structure of the Sefirot in human form</note>, He descended there and was called by that image "Y-H-V-H," so that they might perceive Him through His attributes. And they called Him <term>God, Almighty, Lord of Hosts, I Shall Be</term> <note>El, Elohim, Shaddai, Tzevaot, Ehyeh</note> so that they would perceive Him in every single attribute—how the world is guided by Kindness (Hesed) and Judgment (Din) according to the deeds of human beings. For if His light did not spread over all creatures, how would they perceive Him? And how would the verse *the whole earth is full of His glory* <note>Isaiah 6:3</note> be fulfilled? 

Woe to one who equates Him with any attribute, even one of His own attributes, and certainly not with human beings *whose foundation is in the dust* <note>Job 4:19</note>, for they are all temporary and perishable. Rather, the "likeness" is only according to His dominion over that specific attribute, and even over all creatures. But above that attribute, when He withdraws from it, He has no attribute, nor likeness, nor form. 

This is like the spreading of the waters of the sea over the land. When the water covers the land, it takes on a shape, and we can make a calculation there: 
1. The **Source** of the sea—this is one. 
2. A **Spring** according to its spreading out in that land in a circle, which is the letter *Yod* (י). This Source is one, and the Spring that comes out of it makes two. 
3. Afterward, He makes from it a great vessel, like one who digs a great pit, and it is called **Sea**. This is the third vessel. 
And that great vessel is divided into **seven streams**, like long vessels. Thus the water spreads from the sea into seven streams. And behold: the Source, the Spring, the Sea, and the seven streams make ten. 

If the Master breaks these vessels that He fashioned, the water returns to the Source, and only the broken vessels remain, with nothing in them. 

In this way, the Cause of Causes made ten <term>Sefirot</term> <note>Divine emanations</note>. He called the **Crown** (Keter) the "Source," and in it there is no end to the flow of light. Because of this, He called Himself the <term>Infinite</term> <note>Ein Sof</note>. In this state, He has no likeness or form, and there is no vessel there to grasp Him or to have any knowledge of Him at all. Regarding this, they said: "Do not seek what is too wondrous for you" <note>Ben Sira 3:21</note>. 

Afterward, He made a tiny vessel, which is the letter *Yod* (י), and it was filled from Him. He called it a "Flowing Spring" and called it <term>Wisdom</term> (Hokhmah), and in it, He called Himself "Wise." 

Afterward, He made a large vessel and called it "Sea," and He called it <term>Understanding</term> (Binah). He called Himself "Understanding" within it. He is Wise by His own essence and Understanding by His own essence; for Wisdom is not called "Wisdom" on its own, but because of the Wise One who is Wise through it and gives to it from His own. If He withdraws from it, it remains dry. 

Afterward, He "struck it into seven streams" <note>Isaiah 11:15</note>, into seven precious vessels, and called them: <term>Greatness, Power, Beauty, Victory, Splendor, Foundation, and Sovereignty</term> <note>Gedulah (Hesed), Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut</note>. 
He called Himself: 
- "Great" in Greatness (Kindness). 
- "Mighty" in Power. 
- "Glorious" in Beauty. 
- "Victorious" in Victory (as in battles). 
- In Splendor, He called the name "Splendor." 
- In Foundation, He called His name "Righteous" (Tzaddik), for the Foundation supports everything, all the hosts and all the worlds. 
- And in Sovereignty (Malkhut)...

# Come to Pharaoh (Parashat Bo)

## Main Text (Zohar)

Blessed is the portion of those kings, Levites, prophets, and priests, and those who are the children of the King of All. And regarding what they said, that there is nothing etc., and all that is similar, for they are righteous. For us, the Kingdom is pressed <note>original: "dehika," meaning constricted or pressured</note>; all kingdoms are within His authority to deliver, like kings, and to add to them those around Him, and to be called according to His will. In Him, there is no change or transformation to the spirit that He adds to it; let one see and know it. Afterward, He made ranks <note>original: "tastatin," likely from the Greek 'taxis' for order/rank</note> of these kings, thrones like four pillars, and six steps to the throne. And this is all precisely like the likeness of the cup of the capital <note>original: "kosa de-kharkha"</note> in which they established a crown of memory, like the ox that was placed in the crown of memories, like a world of pressure, an act of mercy that was created in the crown beneath it. And He prepared for the throne groups to flank it, which are the four kingdoms: **Living Creatures (Chayot)**, **Wheels (Ophanim)**, and **Electrum-Beings (Chashmallim)**. The hosts: **Sons of God (Bnei Elohim)**, and **Men-Beings (Ishim)**. And for the count, He made surrounding ranks, and all His groups are in the clouds to ride upon them for strength, for they are like horses to them. And from where do we know that clouds are called a chariot? As it is written: *Behold, the Lord rides upon a swift cloud and shall come to Egypt* <note>Isaiah 19:1</note>. And it is not from what he flees, but immediately when they saw the sand, they spoke of their words; they saw Him like a horse beneath His holy chariot immediately, and the idols of Egypt moved, seeking their dream-visions, and their heart melted like wax. And as for the donkeys etc., until now our speech was like a horse; He sought for them from their melting, and like water, like wax. And from where do we know that his water is like the melting of wax? *My heart is like wax; it is melted in the midst of my bowels* <note>Psalms 22:15</note>.

**And** *every firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb* etc. <note>Exodus 13:13</note>. This commandment is to redeem the firstborn of a donkey and to break the neck of the firstborn of a donkey; for if he does not redeem it, it shall be so, and heaven forbid <note>original: "v'chas"</note> you do not redeem it, then *you shall break its neck*. And this secret is the "excess of evil," and all of it is male in its rectification. And afterward, the "excess of good," just as we have established: "heaven forbid" and "here," a "helper" <note>Genesis 2:18</note>. If he does not merit, it is "against him," because they are of one image—one in goodness and one in the donkey <note>The word for donkey, 'Chamor,' shares a root with 'Chomer,' meaning matter or physical substance</note>. And if he merits, the male is in rectification. The heart is pressed; the donkey with the "stripped one" <note>referring to the soul or a specific spiritual state</note> you shall redeem from the exile. In it are pressed the "winepress" and the "foreskin," and the sand returns in rectification. *And you shall break its neck*—equate it with the "end," the voice that is destined to be erased from the Book of Life, for they went up to the palm tree; whoever is lacking or small, let them be erased from their book.

**And** *it shall be for a sign upon your hand and for frontlets between your eyes* etc. <note>Exodus 13:16</note>. This commandment is the commandment of **Tefillin** <term>Phylacteries: black leather boxes containing Torah scrolls worn during prayer</term>, which are engraved in the male likeness. And this is to engrave a commandment that is not holiness, and these are the Tefillin: the Prayer of the Hand and the Prayer of the Head. The rectification is the beauty of the supernal canopies. And the "Hand" is called **Frontlets (Totafot)**; all of it spreads out, lacking thus for the Tefillin. And it is written: *For like a youth he spreads out and his palate...* Spreading out and smallness, spreading out from the power of the beauty of the canopies above and below. **Joseph** ascended and was crowned with two colors: at first like a youth and a longing for the Righteous One. Just as there are colors in him to show, and this secret is: *And Joseph was beautiful of form and beautiful of appearance* <note>Genesis 39:6</note>—beauty on two sides, above and below. It is written: *And you shall do that which is right and good* <note>Deuteronomy 6:18</note>. "The Right" is the Prayer of the Hand, which is below the Prayer of the Head, and I will crown it so that there is no separation between them at all. And he who is crowned with Tefillin, a herald of the canopy calls out over him, and he takes those two secrets that are spoken in the spirit that acts in heat and the covenant of the son of his unity. And these are the Prayer of the Hand and the Prayer of the Head. And they are all one; any separation is a sword. The **Portions (Parshiyot)** <term>The four specific sections of the Torah written on parchment inside the Tefillin</term> of the Tefillin are as written in the Tefillin of the Head and the Hand. Just as there are four portions in the Tefillin of the Head, so too are they all in the Tefillin of the Hand; for the Prayer of the Hand has nothing of its own, except what it receives from above. And this secret is: *All the rivers run into the sea* <note>Ecclesiastes 1:7</note>. And because it receives them, it is called "Prayer" and is sanctified with their holiness. And all of it is a law of holiness. And then the Kingdom is called a support, a ladder of four portions: the first is *Sanctify unto Me all the firstborn* <note>Exodus 13:2</note>, which is the driving out of the spirit of the side.

## Footer Notes
The handwritten text at the bottom explains that the Tefillin represent the binding of the physical world (the Hand) to the divine intellect (the Head). It emphasizes that Joseph represents the "Righteous One" (Tzadik) who unites the upper and lower worlds, which is why the text links his beauty to the beauty of the Tefillin. The commentator notes that "breaking the neck" of the donkey symbolizes the destruction of stubborn materiality that refuses to be elevated.

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Torah portion "Bo." It focuses specifically on the spiritual architecture of the Tefillin (phylacteries) and how their four internal parchment scrolls correspond to the divine emanations (Sefirot) and the unity of God's name.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Come to Pharaoh** <-

The supernal [light] is included in all that is written in the spirit of the supernal light that emerges from the Brains <note>The "Moachin" or mental faculties of the Divine</note>. And all these are the four seals here. **"Sanctify"** <note>Exodus 13:2, the first portion of the Tefillin</note>—this is the supernal holiness. It is the spirit of supernal Wisdom <term>Chokhmah: the first flash of divine intellect</term> from which everything was prepared in the spirit of the supernal hiddenness, which is called **"Sanctify to Me."** This is the spirit of the Higher World, the Inner Palace. And this spirit is [referenced in]: **"For the children of Israel are servants to Me,"** **"For every firstborn is Mine,"** and **"You shall be a treasure to Me."** All of this is the spirit of Mercy <term>Chesed</term> as it is written both above and below. The "Firstborn" is **"My firstborn son,"** as it is written, **"Israel is My firstborn son."** This firstborn son includes all sides and all colors, and thus the verse includes all four [portions] in the spirit of supernal Wisdom. This is the general Covenant, to know that all are included in this. This is the first section which includes all other sections.

The second section is **"And it shall be when He brings you..."** <note>Exodus 13:11</note>. It is not like the first, for in this section there is the Exodus from Egypt, which came from the side of the Jubilee <term>Yovla/Binah: the source of liberation</term>. Regarding its secret, the word "And it shall be" <note>Hebrew: *Ve-haya*</note> existed in the Jubilee. Because of this, Judgment <term>Din</term> is below it. "And it shall be" implies that there is no existence except in this place, and it is destined to be drawn downward to illuminate the branches and to strengthen the lower level. "And it shall be," as was said regarding the King, is destined to be drawn downward to illuminate the various kinds. All of them are in one spirit. And because they are called the "Creation of Heaven," they are not called by their names in this second [seal] except to let the wise know. Until the gates [of understanding], this matter is hidden and holy.

The third section is **"Hear [O Israel]"** <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note>. This is the spirit of the Right Side, which is called Supernal Mercy <term>Chesed</term>. It offers and confesses that all belongs to the four directions. The Holy One, blessed be He, arranges through it the dwelling of the whole world. This [section] spreads to all sides, even into the lower boundaries. The Holy One, blessed be He, created the world when He wrapped Himself in a garment of light, and this is what unifies the Unity. Because of this, "Hear" is adjacent to "And it shall be" [the second section], for it is the unity of all, and the mouth tastes and confesses the verse. Let our hearts precede it; the letters Y and H <note>The first two letters of the Tetragrammaton</note> are all one. And it is called "One."

Behold, there are three names [in the verse: *YHVH, Eloheinu, YHVH*]; how are they one? Even though we call them "One," they are [truly] one. Rather, through the vision of the Holy Spirit, it is known, and they are in the vision of the eyes to know that these three are one. This is the mystery of the Voice that is heard. The Voice is one, yet it consists of three elements: fire, spirit <note>or air</note>, and water. All of them are one in the spirit of the Voice, and they are nothing but one. So too here: **"The Lord, our God, the Lord"** are one. Three colors <note>aspects</note> that are one. It is the Voice that a person makes, and at its end is the unity of all things, from end to end, in this Voice that makes these three into one. This is the daily Unity revealed by the spirit of the Holy Spirit. Many types of unity are awakened, and all are truth. What this one does, that one does. Everything is the Unity that is awakened from below in the spirit of one Voice, which is one in the dwelling of the word.

Afterward [comes the fourth section]: **"If you will surely listen"** <note>Deuteronomy 11:13</note>. This is the detail of Supernal Mercy as we said. And this fourth section was the spirit of "Hard Judgment" <term>Dina Kashya</term> that we mentioned to you. It is necessary to subdue them every day so that a man may be in the Supernal Image. Regarding this it is written: **"And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you"** <note>Deuteronomy 28:10</note>—this refers to the Tefillin of the arm in this manner. They have been arranged, and all are one. The knot of the Tefillin of the head is the letter *Dalet*, and regarding this it is written: **"And you shall see My back"** <note>Exodus 33:23</note>. This refers to the back [of the head], and there everything is tied in one knot. When one puts on these Tefillin of the arm, the blue crown is tied, the spirit of holy creatures. This spirit, as awakened in many places, is all one spirit. Happy are Israel, who sow this spirit upon themselves! It is written: **"And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall be afraid of you."**

Blessed be the Lord forever, Amen and Amen.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Beshalach. The previous section likely concluded the preceding portion, and here the Zohar transitions into the narrative of the Exodus, specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of hospitality and the recognition of holiness through the story of the Shunammite woman.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**44**<-
->**Portion of Vayehi Beshalach**<-

**And it came to pass** when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not by the way of the land of the Philistines, etc. <note>Exodus 13:17</note>. Rabbi Isaac opened his discourse:
> A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet upon Shigionoth. O Lord, I have heard the report of Thee, and am afraid; O Lord, revive Thy work in the midst of the years... <note>Habakkuk 3:1-2</note>.

"A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet"—this is unique among all the other prophets of the world, for it is not written "A prayer of Isaiah the prophet," or "of Jeremiah," or "of Ezekiel," or "of Joshua," or any other prophets. Rather, we have learned that there are five <note>referring to specific prophetic ranks or instances</note> in which a deed was done that no other prophet merited: to be one who shows mercy. He acted and sought to stir mercy from his Master. What is written?
> And it fell on a day, that Elisha passed to Shunem, where was a great woman; and she constrained him to eat bread <note>2 Kings 4:8</note>.

She was "great" in her deeds, for she was found more worthy than all the people of her generation, and she was the mainstay of the house. And because her husband did not merit for the house to be established through him, the text mentions only her. And see how she was "great"—greater than all other women of the world. For all other women, when they see a guest in the house, they are troubled by him and press him to leave, but she rejoiced in the guest and spent her money on him. As soon as she saw the man, she rejoiced greatly and brought him into her home. Therefore, you see she was "great," greater than other women.

And come and see, she said here:
> Behold now, I perceive that this is a holy man of God <note>2 Kings 4:9</note>.

How did she know? Our colleagues have established that she placed a fine white sheet on his bed and never saw a nocturnal emission upon it, nor did a fly ever pass over his table. Thus they have taught. But if you say she did not see an emission, that is something revealed to all people; what is unique here? And if you say a fly did not pass over his table, why is it written "I perceive"? She knew, and no other, yet all those who saw him eat at his table would have seen that!

Rather, it is well explained here: "I perceive"—she knew and no other, because she would prepare his bed at the time he lay down at night and when he rose in the morning. And she said that she placed a fine white sheet on his bed, and it was so. And it is known in the way of the world that when a man rises from his bed, the sheet is taken up to smell its fragrance. And she saw that from this sheet, from his bed, there rose scents upon scents like the fragrances of the Garden of Eden <note>Hebrew: Gan Eden</note>. She said, "This man is holy, and the holiness of his Master is upon him, for such a holy scent rises from him." For this reason, she wanted him to stay in her house, and no man is as cherished as when he is in the home.

But see the deed:
> Let us make, I pray thee, a little chamber on the wall; and let us set for him there a bed, and a table, and a chair, and a candlestick <note>2 Kings 4:10</note>.

Why these four? It was to prepare the arrangement of the Assembly of Israel <note><term>Knesset Yisrael</term>: a mystical term for the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note>. For thus it is called: Bed, Table, Chair, and Lamp. And they are not arranged all at once, for one must seek the first levels, and afterwards they rise to the Crown <note><term>Keter</term>: the highest emanation of the Divine</note>—the Lamp to the Crown, the Bed to the Crown. Why is it called a "Bed"? Because she rested upon it more than all of them. And a person should marvel at what is written concerning it: "And it fell on a day, that he came thither." "And it fell on a day"—which day was this? As they have established, come and see: that day was not like any other, for on it the foundation of the world was to go forth, and the people of the world were to be remembered by the call of the Divine Presence <note><term>Shekhinah</term></note>. And it says here: "Behold, thou hast been careful for us with all this care"—because of this, we must look into your matter <margin>for the world</margin> before the Holy One, blessed be He, who is destined to provide for her.

<summary>Rabbi Isaac explores the spiritual greatness of the Shunammite woman, explaining that she recognized Elisha's holiness through the scent of Eden on his linens. The four items she provided for him—bed, table, chair, and lamp—are revealed as mystical symbols for the Shekhinah.</summary>

to the world. And because the *Segol* <note>A Hebrew vowel mark consisting of three dots, used here as a mystical symbol for a specific divine configuration</note> is separated, this Crown is bound; we must therefore look into the mysteries of the world. **"Is there anything to be spoken for you to the king, or to the captain of the host?"** <note>2 Kings 4:13</note> etc. This "King" refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He, for it was necessary for this woman—who did not go out or attend prayer in the King’s palace—to be considered. For that day was the New Year <note>Rosh Hashanah</note>, the head of all the years of the world, when all sit in Judgment. And on that day, they call the Holy One, Blessed be He, "King"—the King of Judgment. He <note>Elisha</note> said to her: "Do you have need of the Supreme King concerning the deeds that are in your hands?" **"And she answered: I dwell among my own people"** <note>2 Kings 4:13</note>. What does this mean? It means that at a time when Judgment is hanging over the world, a person should not separate themselves to stand alone, so as not to be specifically marked out above or individually recognized. For in a time when Judgment hangs over the world, those who are recognized and marked out individually—even if they are righteous—are seized first. Therefore, a person should not seek to be separated from the community, for at all times the mercies of the Holy One, Blessed be He, are upon His people all as one. A person should never seek to be separated from the people. And because of this, she said, "I dwell among my own people," meaning: I do not wish to be separated from them, just as I have done until now. **"And Gehazi said: But she has no son..."** <note>2 Kings 4:14</note>. Elisha said: "This is certainly a valid claim, for the day itself caused it." **"And he said: At this season, when the time comes round, you shall embrace a son"** <note>2 Kings 4:16</note>. **"And the woman conceived, and bore a son at that season, when the time came round, as Elisha had said to her"** <note>2 Kings 4:17</note>—at the time that was to be. And afterward, he died. Why did he die? Because he was given to *her* and not to her husband. And he was attached to the aspect of the Feminine <note>term: *Nukva* - the lower divine attribute associated with manifestation and sometimes strict Judgment</note>. And whoever is attached to the Feminine, death is prepared before him. To her he was given, as it is written: "You shall embrace a son." Come and see: in the blessing [of others] it is written **"May the Lord give you..."** <note>referring to a masculine source of blessing</note> and it does not join to "you" [feminine], for that is joined [to the masculine] and not to the Feminine. What comes and binds to the Feminine is the "brain" that is called "at her feet." **"And she went up, and laid him on the bed of the man of God"** <note>2 Kings 4:21</note> because she prepared holy life for him from the All. **"And he said to her: Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with the child?"** <note>2 Kings 4:26</note>—of all of them, she is the mainstay of the house, yet she did not go to the physician but to his "Crown," rather than her husband. "And Gehazi came near to thrust her away." This has been established. "And the man of God said: Let her alone." Why is he called "the man of God" here, whereas before he was called "Elisha"? It is because here he came as "the man of God," for here is the place [of power] and not in death. Rather, the claim was that her weeping was before him. **"And the Lord is righteous from us..."** Just as the Lord testified over Sodom and Gomorrah, this is when Judgment descends. **"And the Lord has hidden it from me"** <note>2 Kings 4:27</note>. What did Elisha not know? Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "If this righteous man kills this one, if I revive him for him, he shall not die, for he is in the power of Judgment." Certainly, he revived him from death. And he came down as the "embraced son" <note>note: The name Habakkuk is derived from the Hebrew word *Chibuk*, meaning "embrace"</note>, and from the place of the Feminine, death is stirred; therefore, he did not see it. And he said to Gehazi: "Gird up your loins, and take my staff in your hand, and go." This has been established, but wisdom was hidden from him. **"As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you"** <note>2 Kings 4:30</note>. Why, since Gehazi was already going? Rather, there was knowledge of the destruction of that wicked one [Gehazi], but he was struck by this which was praised by his hand. **"And he put his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes..."** <note>2 Kings 4:34</note>. And what of this? Elisha listened and knew that this breath was what caused him to be bound now. "And he put his mouth upon his mouth and his eyes upon his eyes" and bound another [spirit] upon him from behind. The place of life was found in him, and he could not uproot him from the place where he was bound by Judgment at first. Until a new spirit was awakened from above and bound in this place, and his soul lived. He pushed them thus; Noah stood for the images. And he sneezed seven times, and no more, corresponding to "the days of our years are seventy years." And he is Habakkuk in his entirety. Thus: **"You shall embrace [Chobeket] a son."** If so, "Embrace" [Chabuk] is his name. Regarding Habakkuk, he was twice [embraced] before he came.

It explains that the boy died because his soul was initially rooted in the "Feminine" attribute of Judgment, requiring Elisha to perform a mystical restoration to bind him to the "Masculine" source of Life.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

...one for life and one for death, to be restored with him. Two embraces were within him, both for this side and for that side <note>referring to the two "sides" of spiritual influence: mercy and judgment</note>. One embrace was after he was first doubled within it. An embrace that we see raised him to higher levels, and because of this, "Habakkuk" <note>original: *Chavakuk*</note> is doubled <note>The name Habakkuk shares a root with *Chibuk*, meaning "embrace"; the name contains the letter 'Kaf' twice, hinting at a double embrace</note>. **A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet** <note>Habakkuk 3:1</note>—what is this "prayer"? Rather, this is the place to which he was first bound, and it was not a prayer except **upon Shigionoth** <note>errors or musical wanderings</note>. For on that day when he was bound to it, the errors of the world were hanging before the Holy One, blessed be He, and He was ruling. And because of this, he was bound to this prayer: "A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet." A prayer of Habakkuk, because Habakkuk acted like a violin <note>or a musical instrument</note>: **O Lord, I have heard the report of You, and I am afraid...** <note>Habakkuk 3:2</note>

Come and see: when the spirit of prophecy was awakened upon him, it came upon this place which is "prayer," and he was afraid and trembled. From the things he saw there, as it is written: **Our King, Your possessions...** and he trembled. **O Lord, revive Your work in the midst of the years.** What is "Your work"? He was speaking of himself, for he is His "work" <note>referring to Habakkuk being a direct creation of Divine intervention/revival</note>. **In the midst of the years revive it**—thus they are the life for this "work" of which the high deputies spoke. **Revive it** so that he should not die as he did at first. **Upon Shigionoth**—what is "upon Shigionoth"? Upon errors. Since all of them were errors, what could be established? Not all of them were for all errors; all of them were "A Shigaion of David." Worthy are they, for when the spirit of prophecy was about to rest upon them, they all began with praise and joy from wisdom, and before them were **the drum and the flute...** <note>1 Samuel 10:5</note> and afterwards they stood to praise. And everyone like Habakkuk needed more than all of them to calm the spirit and to cleanse that place so the spirit of prophecy would be found upon him. And so it was for all the prophets in this manner, except for Moses, who rose above every place of the world's prophets, and all was his portion.

Come and see: when Israel went out of Egypt, their spirits were broken within them. They were carrying their burdens and were unable to rejoice. But at the time when all the hosts and chariots went out with the Shekhinah <note>the Divine Presence</note>, they all rejoiced and praised and went down before the Holy One, blessed be He. And the Holy One, blessed be He, awakened their spirits, and they carried their burdens and their praises, and they were within them so that they did not fly away. When a person has much life within him, then he knows the breaking of his bones and the breaking of his spirit. So it was with Israel: when they went out of Egypt, they then tasted the taste of death. And the Holy One, blessed be He, saw them, as it is written: **And the Lord went before them by day...** <note>Exodus 13:21</note> and all the paths sent up scents of wisdom and entered into them, and they were built up. A voice was found for them; they heard, and they were calmed and rested in their spirits. And Pharaoh and all those hosts of his were seeing after them to push them until they went out from the land of Egypt. And so all those princes who were appointed over them and over the rest of the nations saw the Shekhinah and Israel, all of them, until they flew in their grace like a white reed.

**And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had sent the people...** <note>Exodus 13:17</note> When that time drew near to grant a vision of mercy for the kindness that the Philistines did for Habakkuk, as it is written: **With kindness, kindness I have done with you, you shall do with me and with the land where I have sojourned.** <note>A mystical interpretation linking the Philistines to the narrative</note>

**And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had sent the people**—what is written above? **And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he and all his servants.** <note>Exodus 12:30</note> Come and see the vengeance that the Holy One, blessed be He, performed in Egypt. There were three times. One that they all did in Egypt, killing all the camps of Egypt. And one where the Holy One, blessed be He, killed like the terrors of the night. It says that when Pharaoh saw the plague in his house, and in his sons, and in his servants, he rose and hurried himself and killed the taskmasters and the lords, and everyone he saw who was a taskmaster over the people, until he saw—he saw it happen to him in his own life—he rose in the very night. Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, like the terrors of the night, killed the firstborn and performed vengeance, so Pharaoh rose in the land of Egypt and killed and performed vengeance upon his own leaders, his taskmasters, his chariots, and all those light riders.

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Torah portion Beshalach (Exodus 13:17). It continues the narrative of the Exodus, focusing on the spiritual distinction between the Children of Israel and the "Mixed Multitude" (Erev Rav) who joined them. The text transitions from the literal departure from Egypt to a mystical dialogue between Rabbi Isaac and Rabbi Yehuda.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Beshalach**<-
<note>Beshalach: "When he sent," the opening word of the Torah portion describing Pharaoh sending the Israelites away.</note>

This is what is written: *And Pharaoh rose up in the night* (Exodus 12:30). "In the night" literally, to kill and to go and cast them down. For all of them, all the beasts <note>referring to the Egyptian sorcerers or spiritual forces</note> saw in their hearts a seal that had taken hold of him. So Pharaoh later saw and looked at his end, and he was crying out and saying: *Rise up, go out from among my people, both you and the children of Israel* (Exodus 12:31). At all times they appeared as killers, harassing and disturbing me and all my household. This is what is written: *And he called for Moses and Aaron by night.* Since everything was in your hands, *and bless me also* (Exodus 12:32), so that you do not kill me. And afterward, he saw them like the likeness of beasts, and he sent them out from the taking of the voice <note>the sound of the plague</note>, and so *Pharaoh sent the people away* (Exodus 13:17).

**And God led the people around** by way of the wilderness of the Red Sea (Exodus 13:18). To strengthen the sword against the "Other Side" <note>the forces of spiritual impurity</note>. Rabbi Yehuda says: What is the praise when Israel were like a leader? As it is written: *God did not lead them* (Exodus 13:17). For He had pity on their words below regarding "My people," "Israel My firstborn son." And at that time they were not yet circumcised and had not sanctified themselves in Him as is proper. But here, where they were circumcised and performed the Passover sacrifice and sanctified themselves in Him, He calls them "the people." Rather, because of that **Mixed Multitude** <term>Erev Rav: A group of non-Israelites who joined the Exodus, often blamed in mystical texts for later sins like the Golden Calf</term> who cleaved to them and mixed among them, He calls them "the people" plainly. This is as it is written: *And the Lord repented concerning the evil which He thought to do unto His people* (Exodus 32:14) <note>referring to the sin of the Calf</note>. *And the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron* (Exodus 32:1). *And the people saw that Moses delayed* (Exodus 32:1). And so with all of them.

Rabbi Isaac and Rabbi Yehuda were walking on the road, and with them was **Yosi the Merchant** <note>original: "Tayya," an Arab merchant figure who often reveals deep secrets in the Zohar</note>, with his camel's saddle-bags wrapped over his shoulders. While they were walking, that Yosi the Merchant found a certain merit, for he said: "Nations that are bound by the inspections of the field to be moved from their burning..." and he took hold of it and brought it down. Rabbi Isaac and Rabbi Yehuda were astonished and said: "Let us sit from the path, for the Holy One, Blessed Be He, desired to show us that it is not written explicitly 'Give rest.'" As it is found afterward, as it is written: *The horse and its rider He has thrown into the sea* (Exodus 15:1). And wisdom ceased the seed. They said: "Blessed is the Merciful One who paired us together."

Rabbi Isaac opened and said: *Do not fret because of evildoers, neither be envious of those who work unrighteousness* (Psalms 37:1). It is written "wicked ones" elsewhere, but here "evildoers" <note>original: "meraim," which can also mean "those who make friends"</note> to exclude them from their own bodies, and those who are joined with them. Rabbi Yehuda says: "Evildoers"—thin your own body out from evildoers so that you do not become "friends and companions" <note>a wordplay on "meraim" (evildoers) and "re'im" (friends)</note> as one, so that their deeds do not become bad for you and you be caught in their sins.

Come and see: it was not those Mixed Multitude who were found among Israel—that deed <note>the Golden Calf</note> would not have been found, and none of Israel would have died, all those who died, and it would not have caused Israel all that it caused. And come [see], that very deed and that very sin caused the Exile for Israel. For we have learned: The Holy One, Blessed Be He, desired that Israel should be gathered at that time like supreme kings, and to make them free from everything: free from death, free from the [evil] species, free from the subjugation of all other nations. *Engraved (charut) upon the tablets* (Exodus 32:16)—do not read it as "engraved" (*charut*) but as "**freedom**" (*cheirut*). Once that deed was committed, they caused everything: they caused death; they caused the subjugation of kingdoms; they caused those first Tablets to be broken; they caused many thousands of Israel to die. And all this because those Mixed Multitude joined with them. Even here, in their journey, they are not called "the Congregation" or "Israel" or "His People," but "the people" plainly. And *the children of Israel went up armed* (Exodus 13:18)—when they went up and that Mixed Multitude had not yet joined with them, He calls them "the children of Israel." Once they were mixed with them, He calls them "the people."

Rabbi Yosi said: It is written, *For the Egyptians whom you have seen today, you shall see them again no more for ever* (Exodus 14:13). If so, all the time they were seeing that Mixed Multitude! Rabbi Yehuda said: "Egyptians" is written, and not the Mixed Multitude, for many other nations lived in Egypt. And not only that, but they [the Mixed Multitude] were circumcised, and once they were circumcised they were no longer called "Egyptians." And by the word of Moses, he accepted them, and that is what he said...

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the Torah portion Beshalach, specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of the Exodus and the transition into the wilderness. It bridges the narrative of carrying Joseph's remains with the mystical significance of the Pillar of Cloud and Fire.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

As the scripture says: **"Go, get down, for your people have corrupted themselves."** They have turned aside quickly from the way which I commanded them; they have made themselves a molten calf <note>Exodus 32:7-8</note> and caused sin. The children of Israel went up "armed" <term>Chamushim (armed/fifty)</term> from the land of Egypt. They were redeemed from violence. But Rabbi Yose says: they were redeemed from the sins of Israel. Rabbi Yehuda understood this to mean they were redeemed from their own corruption. Heaven forbid! Rather, because the "filth" <note>referring to spiritual impurity or the 'Other Side'</note> ascended with them from Egypt, for that reason the children of Israel went up from Egypt with sins, and it was not easy for them. Because of this, they were delayed fifty days until they could receive the Torah. From that place <note>the fiftieth gate of understanding</note> freedom and their liberation emerged, and for this reason the word "armed" <note>Hebrew: *Chamushim*</note> is written deficiently <note>spelled without the letter Vav, hinting at the number fifty, *Chamishim*</note>. Because of this, the children of Israel went up from Egypt.

**"And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him..."** <note>Exodus 13:19</note> Why did he bring up his bones? He said: because he [Joseph] is the head of the Assembly in exile. Furthermore, they were a sign of redemption for him and for all of Israel. Regarding this, it is written: **"For he had strictly sworn the children of Israel..."** as was stated.

**"And the Lord went before them by day..."** <note>Exodus 13:21</note> Rabbi Yose opened the discussion with the verse: **"To the Chief Musician, upon the Doe of the Dawn, a Psalm of David."** <note>Psalms 22:1</note> How beloved is the Torah before the Holy One, Blessed be He! For anyone who exerts themselves in the study of Torah is beloved above and beloved below. The Holy One, Blessed be He, listens to his words; He does not abandon him in this world, and He does not abandon him in the World to Come. One is required to labor in the Torah by day and by night, as it is written: **"And you shall meditate on it day and night."** <note>Joshua 1:8</note> And it is also written: **"If My covenant be not with day and night..."** <note>Jeremiah 33:25</note> This is fine for the day, but for what purpose is the night? So that the Holy Name may be found complete within him. Just as there is no day without night, and it is not complete except for one with the other, so too must the Torah be found with a person day and night, so that there may be completeness for the person day and night. And it has been taught that the essence of the night is from midnight onwards.

Even though the first half is included in the general category of night, at midnight the Holy One, Blessed be He, enters the Garden of Eden to delight with the righteous. At that time, a person is required to rise and labor in the Torah. It has been taught that the Holy One, Blessed be He, and all the righteous in the Garden of Eden all listen to his voice. This is what is written: **"O you who dwell in the gardens, the companions listen for your voice; let me hear it."** <note>Song of Songs 8:13</note> This has already been established: "You who dwell in the gardens" refers to the Assembly of Israel <note>the Shekhinah</note>, who praises the Holy One, Blessed be He, through the assembly of the Torah at night. Fortunate is the portion of one who joins with her to praise the Holy One, Blessed be He, through the assembly of the Torah. When the morning comes, the Holy One, Blessed be He, delights in him and extends to her <note>the Shekhinah</note> the scepter of Lovingkindness <term>Chesed</term>. And not upon her alone, but upon her and all those who join with her. This is as it is written: **"By day the Lord will command His lovingkindness, and in the night [His song shall be with me]."** <note>Psalms 42:9</note>

Regarding this, she is called "The Doe of the Dawn." Rabbi Shimon said: At the time when the light seeks to shine, it becomes dark and the light is obscured, and blackness is found. Then she <note>the Shekhinah</note> joins below with the Assembly to delight with Him and ascends to His palace. Afterward, the sun seeks to enter and shine, and the night departs. At that time, all the gates are closed; the donkeys bray and the dogs bark. When the night is divided <note>at midnight</note>, the King and the Queen <term>Matronita</term> enter to sing. The King comes and stands at the gate of the palace and says: **"Open to me, my sister, my love..."** <note>Song of Songs 5:2</note> Then He delights in the assembly of the righteous. Fortunate is the portion of one who awakens at that time with words of Torah, because all those of the Queen's palace must praise the King, and they all offer praise before Him. A sacrifice that rises from this world, which is so far away, is more pleasing to the Holy One, Blessed be He, than anything else. When the night is divided and the morning comes, and it is dark and obscured, then the King and the Queen are as one in spirit, and He bestows gifts upon her and all the children of His palace. Fortunate is the portion of one who is found in that preparation.

**"And the Lord went before them by day"** — The Holy One, Blessed be He, and His court of judgment...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Beshalach**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion, meaning "When he sent out"</note>

Rabbi Isaac said: This is what we have learned, that the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note> is present in all the paths. **"And the Lord went before them by day"** <note>Exodus 13:21</note>—this refers to Abraham <note>Associated with the quality of Mercy/Chesed</note>. **"In a pillar of cloud"**—this refers to Isaac <note>Associated with the quality of Strength/Judgment/Gevurah</note>. **"To lead them on the way"**—this refers to Jacob <note>Associated with Beauty/Tiferet, the balance of the two</note>, as it is written: **"And Jacob went on his way"** <note>Genesis 32:2</note>. **"And by night in a pillar of fire to give them light"**—this refers to King David <note>Associated with Sovereignty/Malchut</note>. And all of these are holy <term>chariots</term> <note>Spiritual vehicles or structures</note> upon which Israel traveled in total perfection. **"To go by day and by night."** Now, did they actually see these by day and by night? Did they travel by day and not by night like ordinary people who flee? Since the dawn rose for them to travel, they went by day and by night. Rather, it was so that total perfection would be found in them, for there is no perfection except in the union of day and night.

Rabbi Abba said: Blessed is the portion of Israel, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, brought them out of Egypt to be His portion and His inheritance. And come and see: just as the burden of the <term>Jubilee</term> <note>The Sefirah of Binah, representing the source of liberation</note> was found to be heavy for Israel <note>referring to the spiritual intensity of the process</note>, so too in the time to come, as it is written: **"And it shall come to pass in that day, that a great shofar shall be blown..."** <note>Isaiah 27:13</note>. And because of that supernal <term>Jubilee</term>, they were destined to receive the Torah and to approach Mount Sinai. And since they saw by day and saw by night, it was as if the day and night were one single day, and no separation was found. Furthermore, they all traveled together according to the desire of their souls, according to the law of the Torah they received. There were twenty worlds <note>referring to spiritual dimensions</note>, and day and night were elevated as is fitting, for there is no day without night and no night without day. And night and day are called "One" corresponding to the day of the Jubilee. And just as those twenty days of the Jubilee surrounded them, from the side of the Jubilee the Torah was established for them, and because of this, they traveled by day and by night.

<margin>And the Lord</margin> **"went before them by day."** Rabbi Hiyya said: This is how we established it: "And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of cloud"—this is Abraham. "And by night in a pillar of fire"—this is Isaac. But if so, where is Jacob? Rather, it is like the first word that was said, and there they surrounded him, as it is written "And the Lord" <note>The name 'And the Lord' (V'Adonai) implies God and His Heavenly Court, including the attribute of Jacob/Tiferet</note>. And the night was like a protection on this side and that side. And Rabbi Abba said: It is written, **"And it came to pass, when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see"** <note>Genesis 27:1</note>. We have established that this was from the heat of the spirit that consumed him. And come and see: at the time when night is established, the night does not shine, and regarding this, "his eyes were dim from seeing"—it is all one mystery. Rabbi Isaac opened and said:

<margin>And it was told</margin> **"to the king of Egypt that the people had fled"** <note>Exodus 14:5</note>. Who told him? Our colleagues have established that his assembly of wise men and magicians gathered through prophecy and informed him that the people had fled. And why did they say this? Because they saw through their wisdom that the Israelites were traveling day and night, which is the way of those who flee. Furthermore, they saw that they were traveling toward a place of death, as it is written: **"that they turn back and encamp before Pi-hahiroth"** <note>Exodus 14:2</note>. **"And he took six hundred chosen chariots"** <note>Exodus 14:7</note>. Six hundred of what? If you say it corresponds to the number of Israel, as it is written: **"six hundred thousand on foot"** <note>Exodus 12:37</note>. **"Chosen"** corresponds to the men who are the essence of the whole army. **"And all the chariots of Egypt"**—these are the other chariots that are secondary, following behind, corresponding to the children, as it is written: **"besides children"** <note>Exodus 12:37</note>. And all of this was done through the counsel of his magicians and wise men. **"And captains over all of them"**—this is interpreted through wisdom as corresponding to the supernal levels, two and one. Rabbi Isaac said: according to the Aramaic translation, they were "armed"—they were all prepared. "And he took six hundred chosen chariots." Rabbi Hiyya said: It is written, **"The Lord will punish the host of the high heaven on high, and the kings of the earth upon the earth"** <note>Isaiah 24:21</note>. At the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives dominion to the princes of the nations above, He gives it to the people below. And at the time He brings them down from their levels above, He brings the people down below. **"And he took six hundred chosen chariots"**—this refers to their appointed celestial minister; they established that he remembered the chariots of the "donkey" <note>A symbol of the Egyptian spiritual source</note> and they all doubled as a fortress for the side of the Crown <note>referring here to the 'Crown' of the impure side</note>. And this is the meaning of "chosen." **"And all the chariots of Egypt"**—it is written: **"I have compared thee, O my love, to a steed in Pharaoh's chariots"** <note>Song of Songs 1:9</note>. This is like a female horse below compared to the horses of Pharaoh, as they have established. Rather, "to my steed in the chariots of Pharaoh..."

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the Torah portion Beshallach, specifically focusing on the events at the Red Sea and the spiritual significance of the Sabbath. The text transitions from describing Pharaoh’s pursuit to the merit of Moses and the sanctity of the Sabbath.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

When Pharaoh was pursuing after Israel, what did he do? He took a female horse and bound it to his chariot, and the male horses he bound behind them. The males were prepared to face the females, but they did not want to split apart or move forward <note>The Zohar describes Pharaoh using animal instincts to drive his cavalry forward in a frenzy</note>. As he drew near to Israel, he took the female horse and placed it behind, and the male horses in front, to weaken them and to prevail in battle against them. In this manner, "the way was before them" <note>original: "ויהי הדרך"; the text notes this may be a variant for "the cloud" (Exodus 14:19)</note> and the Angel of God moved, and so on. For this reason, [it is written]: "I have compared you, my love, [to a mare among Pharaoh's chariots]" (Song of Songs 1:9), and this verse we have already established.

**And Pharaoh** drew near. Rabbi Yose said: It has already been stated that he brought them closer to repentance. It is written, "And Pharaoh drew near," and it is already recorded: "O Lord, in trouble they have visited You" <note>original: "יהוה בצר פקדוך"; Isaiah 26:16</note>. Israel "visits" the Holy One, Blessed be He, only in a time of distress; then they all visit Him and pour out a prayer before Him. When is "Your chastening upon them"? At the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, visits them with His rods. Then the Holy One, Blessed be He, has compassion on them with mercy, and that voice is pleasing before Him, so that they may be separated from their foolishness and He may be appointed over them with mercy. This is like the parable of a king with his son, etc. So too, Israel was approaching the sea; they saw the sea before them, raging with its waves rising upward. They were afraid. They lifted their eyes and saw Pharaoh and his armies, with spears and bows. Then they were very afraid. What did they do? "And the children of Israel cried out." See how Pharaoh brought Israel closer to their Father in Heaven; this is what is written: "And Pharaoh drew near," as has been stated.

**And Moses said** to the people: "Fear not, stand still and see the salvation of the Lord." How worthy is the portion of Israel, for the Faithful Shepherd <term>Faithful Shepherd: A title for Moses, "Raya Mehemna"</term> walked among them. It is written:
> Then He remembered the days of old, Moses His servant (Isaiah 63:11).

"He remembered the days of old"—this refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He. "Moses His servant"—from here we learn that Moses was equivalent to all of Israel. We learn that Moses, as the Faithful Shepherd, was truly with them. If the leader is worthy, the whole nation is worthy; if the leader is not worthy, the nation is not worthy and they become like weeping ones. And we have established: "Stand still and see"—you do not need to wage war, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, will wage the war for you, as it is written: "The Lord shall fight for you, and you shall hold your peace." Come and see: on that night, the Holy One, Blessed be He, assembled His heavenly entourage <note>original: "פמליא"; from the Latin 'familia'</note> to look into the judgments of Israel and to have compassion, for the merits of Israel preceded them and they were not abandoned to judgment. Rabbi Judah said: The merit of Jacob protected Israel; this is what is written: "If it had not been the Lord who was on our side, let Israel now say" (Psalm 124:1)—this refers to "Israel the Elder" <note>Jacob</note>.

**The Lord shall fight** for you, and you shall hold your peace. Rabbi Abba opened: "If you turn away your foot from the Sabbath, from doing your pleasure on My holy day" (Isaiah 58:13). Blessed are Israel, whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to cling to more than all other nations of the world. Out of His love for them, He brought them close to Him and gave them the Torah, and gave them the Sabbath, which is the holiest of all other days, a rest and a joy for all. The Sabbath is weighed against the entire Torah. See how the Sabbath is weighed as the fear of the entire Torah. "And you shall call the Sabbath a delight"—the delight of all, the delight of soul and body, the delight of the upper and lower worlds. "And you shall call the Sabbath"—this means one should invite it as one invites a guest <note>The word "call" (ve-karata) is interpreted as "inviting" the Sabbath Queen</note>. From here we learn that just as one invites a guest, so one must prepare a set table properly, and prepare the house properly with food and drink, more so than on other days. "And honor it, not doing your own ways."
