## Main Text (Zohar)

Your ways, as we have established, [come] from those paths of yours, and "speaking a word" <note>Refers to the prohibition of mundane speech on the Sabbath</note> has already been discussed. Because that word ascends and awakens a matter that goes up to the High Faith, [the sages] established that one must labor in it [the Torah] and not in anything else. Come and see: that word which goes out from a person's mouth ascends and awakens an **awakening** <term>Itaruta: the Kabbalistic concept that human action triggers a reciprocal divine response</term> above, whether for good or for evil. And one who sits in the "clouds of the Divine Presence" <note>The Shekhinah</note> is forbidden from awakening a word that wanders, for it causes a blemish on the Holy Day. One who sits at the King’s wedding feast should not turn away from the King to occupy himself with something else. In all things, one must show action and awaken an awakening of that which is necessary. In the matters of the Sabbath and the holiness of the day, one must awaken [spiritually] and not with any other word.

Come and see: here, when Pharaoh drew near to wage war, there were many merits among Israel. And who would not want the merit of Israel crying out? There was no need for an **awakening from below** <term>Itaruta de-Ltatat: human initiative</term> at all, because the **awakening from above** <term>Itaruta de-Le'ila: divine initiative</term> was already present. For they were worthy of the holiness of the awakening from above, and their merit stood before Him. To awaken this awakening, He did not require the merit of Israel or an awakening from below at all, for the Crown was standing above. Thus it is written: **"The Lord <note>original: יהוה (YHVH)</note> will fight for you, and you shall hold your peace"** <note>Exodus 14:14</note>. "You shall hold your peace" certainly—do not awaken a word that is not necessary for you.

And here the Holy Name was revealed in seventy hidden ways. Our colleagues, Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Yehuda, were walking on the road. Rabbi Yehuda said: "Certainly we have learned that the name *Lord* <note>YHVH</note> in every place signifies **Mercy** <term>Rachamim</term>. Yet here He approaches to wage war and execute **Judgment** <term>Din</term>! This was a 'Judgment within Mercy.' Here it is written 'The Lord will fight for you,' and it does not appear like a judgment of mercy at all, for it is written unlike any other miracle."

Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said to him: "Shimon <note>Addressing himself or the group</note>, I say that here it was Judgment within Mercy. For even though the sea covered them [the Egyptians] and they died, they were treated with honor and buried. For the earth did not want to receive them until the Holy One, blessed be He, extended His right hand and she received them, as it is written: **'You stretched out Your right hand, the earth swallowed them'** <note>Exodus 15:12</note>. Because of this, it was Judgment within Mercy. And for this reason, the Holy One, blessed be He, did not want Israel to awaken any word at all. For if Israel had awakened a word, they would have awakened the Name of Mercy, and Judgment would not have been executed within Mercy. Therefore, 'The Lord will fight for you and you shall hold your peace'—do not awaken anything, for the Name of Mercy needs to be awakened over them to perform Judgment within Mercy. For if you [Israel] act, you will cause a blemish and awaken another matter, Heaven forbid."

And is it not written: "And the Lord was seen among the nations"? If so, this was Judgment within Mercy. He said to him: "It was certainly so. It was Judgment within Mercy, for their death was not found to be like that of other nations. Rather, vengeance was taken upon them so they would not be like the rest of the world's people who are killed, but rather [it was unique]. This is Judgment within Mercy. In every place, this Name [YHVH] is Judgment within Mercy, except for one place where it is written: **'The Lord shall go forth as a mighty man'** <note>Isaiah 42:13</note>... and even with all this, it is Judgment, yet the cord of Mercy is in it, as it is written 'as a mighty man' and not 'a mighty man,' 'as a man of war' and not 'a man of war.' For certainly, even though He executes Judgment, it is upon His works. 'And the Lord will fight for you' certainly, 'and you shall hold your peace.' Happy is the portion of Israel before the Creator, for their portion and their inheritance, as it is written: **'For the Lord's portion is His people; Jacob is the lot of His inheritance'** <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>."

->**And the Lord said**<- to Moses: "Why do you cry out to Me?" <note>Exodus 14:15</note>. This matter has been established in the *Book of Concealment* <term>Sifra De-Tzniuta: a highly cryptic, foundational Kabbalistic text</term>, and there is its secret. "And the Lord said to Moses"—Rabbi Yehuda opened and said: **"Then Jonah prayed unto the Lord his God out of the fish's belly"** <note>Jonah 2:2</note>. What is written above? **"Now the Lord had prepared a great fish"** <note>Jonah 2:1</note>. "Prepared" <note>original: וימן (Vayman)</note> is as it is said: **"And the king appointed for them a daily provision"** <note>Daniel 1:5</note>...

## Main Text (Zohar)

He brought him in. **"And the Lord appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah"** <note>Jonah 2:1</note>. This corresponds to the side of the female <note>original: "Sitra de-Nukba," the feminine aspect of the divine emanations</note>. However, that fish was certainly prepared to swallow Jonah to protect him from the great surrounding [danger], and what a structure was inside it! Once he entered it, he saw inside its mouth something like a great palace, and the two eyes of that fish shone like oil, and its heart was thick. He saw in its innards that it was bright for him, and he saw all that was in the sea and in the deep. And if you say: if so, why is it written, "I called out of my distress"? It does not seem like he had all this room. Rather, once that fish showed him all that was in the sea and the deep, it was more than he could bear. Then it became narrow for Jonah, for he saw that he was being guarded. When Jonah saw all that space, he was happy. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "What more do you seek? I brought you in here [for a purpose]." What did He do? He killed that fish and it died, and all the other fish surrounded the carcass of that fish, and this one bit him from this side and that one bit him from that side. Then Jonah saw himself in distress; immediately **"Jonah prayed to the Lord"** <note>Jonah 2:2</note>. At first it was a "fish" <note>original: "Dag," masculine</note> and now it was a "female fish" <note>original: "Dagah," feminine</note>; everything was like a block, lacking strength, like a vision of death. And then it is written, "I called out of my distress." It does not say "I was in distress," as if I sat in distress, but "I called" from that distress that pressed upon me. From here we learn my claim that it [the fish] had died. And it is not written "from the belly of the fish" <note>masculine</note> but "from the belly of the female fish" <note>feminine</note>, for it had certainly died. Once he accepted his exile, the Holy One, Blessed be He, revived that fish and it brought him out to the dry land before everyone. And they saw the work of the Holy One, Blessed be He. What is written? **"And Jonah prayed to the Lord his God from the belly of the female fish"** <note>Jonah 2:2</note> after he was bound, as it is implied by the writing "his God" <note>Elohav</note>—it does not just say "prayed to the Lord" but adds "his God" <note>invoking the attribute of Judgment/Justice</note>. So too here: **"And the Lord said to Moses: Why do you cry out to Me?"** <note>Exodus 14:15</note>—"to Me" specifically. "Speak to the children of Israel that they go forward." "Go forward" from dragging these matters out until the lower exile. "And they shall go forward"—to where did He command them to go, since they were already camping by the sea? Rather, it means to arrange [the spiritual realms] above, for it is written "Why do you cry out to Me?" since they all stand as one, and because of this "they shall go forward" and take from this, for it is ready.

---

**"And you,** lift up your staff..." <note>Exodus 14:16</note>. "Lift up your staff" which has the engraving of the Holy Name upon it; incline your hand toward the holy side, and once they see the power of the Holy Name, they will flee from it and from before it. And because of this, "stretch out your hand" toward the "Other Side" <note>original: "Sitra Achra," the realm of impurity or judgment</note>, for that staff was made for you for other waters. Rabbi Eleazar said: We see that sometimes this staff is called "the staff of God" and sometimes it is called "the staff of Moses." He said to him: There were two, and so we have established it. But in the book of Rav Hamnuna the Elder, he says well that it is all one, whether you say it belongs to the Holy One, Blessed be He, or you say it belongs to Moses; and this staff below is on the side of Strength <note>term: Gevurah - the divine attribute of judgment and restriction</note>. And because of this, "stretch out your hand"—the left hand—to show the side of Strength. Rabbi Shimon said: Woe to those who do not show the Torah [properly]; it is read before them and they do not know and do not look! Come and see: from the side of Strength, waters are stirred in the world and waters go out, and now the Holy One, Blessed be He, wants to dry up the water. And it shows "stretch out your hand," which is the left. Rather, "lift up your staff" to dry the water, and "stretch out your hand" below the water to arouse the side of Strength and to cut the water over the Egyptians. For this reason, there are two matters here, as it is written: **"Lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it"** <note>Exodus 14:16</note>. And come and wonder: the Holy One, Blessed be He, made it like a cup, then the depths congealed in the heart of the sea. And in them, they saw the dry land. This is what is written: **"And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea on the dry ground"** <note>Exodus 14:22</note>.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on Parashat Beshalach, specifically focusing on the crossing of the Red Sea and the divine dismantling of the Egyptian chariots. ## Main Text (Zohar)

**"And He took off** the wheels of their chariots" (Exodus 14:25). Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse: "And behold, one wheel was on the earth beside the living creatures" (Ezekiel 1:15). This verse has already been established and explained. For everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created, He established His dominion over it; His dominion shall never pass away, and it is for all eternity. He performs His will on earth just as He does in the heavens. He established the world through man, as it is written: "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created" <note>original: *be-hibare’am*</note>. Our sages established that this word can be read as "through Abraham" <note>original: *be-Abraham*—a classic wordplay suggesting the world was created for the sake of the patriarch's merit</note>. Because of him, the world exists, for he is the foundation of the worlds. He is certainly the "cutting of the covenant" <note>a reference to circumcision and the union of male and female principles</note>. When Isaac was bound before Him, he was wrapped in this attribute and departed through it; the Holy One, blessed be He, rested His **Kindness** <note>the Sefirah of Chesed</note> upon him, and thus he departed.

And Jacob took hold of all of them; he lived such that death never touched him, for all life flows through that path in which all things are included. He gives life to all who take hold of him. For this reason, "Jacob did not die" <note>referring to the Talmudic teaching that as long as his children live, he lives</note>. And when did he "die"? At the moment it is written: "And he gathered his feet into the bed" (Genesis 49:33). "The Bed" is as we have said: "Behold the bed of Solomon" (Song of Songs 3:7). Regarding that bed, it is written: "Her feet go down to death" (Proverbs 5:5) <note>The "Bed" or "Couch" represents the Shekhinah (Divine Presence) in its lower aspect, which touches the realm of mortality</note>. Therefore, it is written: "And he gathered his feet into the bed." Then, "he breathed his last and was gathered to his people."

The Holy One, blessed be He, performed a wonder to house that Jacob <unclear>within the chariot</unclear>. This is the "Supernal Holy Living Creature" <note>Chayah</note> upon which all other living creatures depend. They gaze upon it to receive life. These ascend and those descend; all are levels upon levels, higher and lower, that travel and sail through the sea. This is the "great and wide sea, wherein are creeping things without number" (Psalm 104:25). Higher and lower beings all travel and sail in the sea. When the day breaks, all four <note>the four primary angels or directions</note> roll forward and ascend with their wings. A storm is found, and a mighty wind moves over them in silence. During the day, they are scattered to every side: these to the East, these to the West, these to the North, and these to the South. All the inhabitants of the world who see them <note>perhaps referring to clouds or celestial phenomena</note> whisper over them; they are like dew, swallowing them like dust-caps. No swords are taken up against their companions; they simply ascend and descend.

Except for that error <note>or "straying one"</note> where a "Male" comes into the sea and knows how to subdue the storm-wind of the sea. Once he ascends, the sea rejoices, its anger is stilled, and a calm is found. Then all four travel straight ahead, turning neither to the right nor to the left. Those of merit shall walk there. "**Leviathan**, which You formed to sport with" (Psalm 104:26)—this is precise. All the stars of the sea gather to their places, and all those creatures are afraid. The Supernal Living Creature is prepared, and "all the beasts of the field shall play there" (Job 40:20).

Come and see: just as it is above, so it is below. Just as it is below, so it is in the sea. Just as it is above, so it is in the Supernal Sea. Just as it is above, so it is below; just as it is below, so it is in the Lower Sea. The breath of that sea is stirred to bless the path. It spreads its head, arms, supports, and body—everything as it should be, and everything is called by His name. Similarly, in the Lower Sea, there is a "Head of the Sea," "Arms of the Sea," and "Body of the Sea." It is written: "Zebulun shall dwell at the shore of the seas" (Genesis 49:13). He is at one end... <note>The text links the tribes of Israel to the limbs of the Divine Chariot</note>. It was proclaimed by a supernal herald: "And his flank shall be toward Sidon." This is all a "Fish" <note>Nun</note>. The "thigh of Jacob" and Zebulun were the right leg of the body.

**"And He took off"** <note>Vayasar</note>—this means He cut them off, like a servant. From here we find the division of the end. Come and see: Chariot upon Chariot was found. The wheels of the chariot were moving in this manner and were not delayed. Those who were beneath the chariot were like dew upon it. So it was for all of them. Come and see: a chariot that is lower than its fellow. You might say it was not a complete chariot, but it is written: "And He took off the **wheel** of his chariots." How many chariots were there? They were all moving upon a single support, a "Wheel" that was appointed over them. Once this one was removed from its dominion, all the chariots were removed from their dominion and could not move. Then all those below were removed from their dominion, as it is written: "...against Pharaoh, and against those who trust [in him]."

It explains Jacob's "death" as a transition into the eternal Merkavah and describes the spiritual ecology of the "Sea" as a reflection of higher divine realms.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Beshalach (Exodus), specifically focusing on the crossing of the Red Sea. The previous discourse likely touched upon the spiritual preparations for the Exodus; here, the text explains the metaphysical collapse of Egypt's power in the celestial realms before its physical defeat on earth.</meta>

# Beshalach

...and so on. Since the Holy One, blessed be He, granted the dominion of Egypt power over all other nations, once the strength of Egypt was broken, the strength of all other nations was broken as well. How do we know this? As it is written: ->**"Then the chiefs of Edom were dismayed..."** (Exodus 15:15)<- and it is written: ->**"The peoples heard and trembled..."** (Exodus 15:14)<- This is because all of them were attached to the worship of Egypt and relied on Egypt to assist them. The Holy One, blessed be He, summoned them all together to assist Egypt so they might be strengthened. Therefore, once they heard of the mighty deeds the Holy One, blessed be He, performed in Egypt, their hands grew weak and they could not stand. They all trembled within their dominions, and their strength faded everywhere above <note>in the spiritual realms</note>, and the power of all those who held onto it was shattered. Once the strength of them all was broken above, they were all broken below, because of that strength that was shattered first.

And because of this, it is written: ->**"And He took off their chariot wheels"** (Exodus 14:25)<- **"and He drove them heavily."** For when this <note>the celestial power</note> was broken, they could no longer move. Come and see that it is so, for it is written "He took off the wheel <note>original: *Afen*</note> of his chariots"—the word "wheel" is written defectively <note>without the letter Vav, implying a singular or diminished state</note>. It is written "bitter" <note>a wordplay on the Hebrew letters</note> because all those who were attached to it are called by this name.

Come and see: "And He took off the wheel of his chariots." Fortunate is the portion of Israel, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to be attached to, making them His portion and inheritance. They are His portion because they are attached to Him. As it is written: ->**"But you who held fast to the Lord..."** (Deuteronomy 4:4)<- and it is written: ->**"For the Lord has chosen Jacob for Himself"** (Psalms 135:4)<- and it is written: ->**"For the Lord’s portion is His people..."** (Deuteronomy 32:9)<- For He brought them out of the holy inheritance to be His own portion. On account of this, He gave them the holy, supernal Torah, which was hidden for two thousand years before the world was created, and of which it is said <note>that it was His delight</note>. Out of His love for them, He gave it to Israel so they might draw near to His Crown and be attached to it. Come and see: all the <term>Matronin</term> <note>Divine feminine powers or "Ladies" of the court</note> above, and all those <term>Rethichin</term> <note>Celestial Chariots or spiritual structures</note>, are all attached to one another—levels upon levels, some higher and some lower. And these are the "living creatures" of which it is written: ->**"There is the sea, great and wide..."** (Psalms 104:25)<- and all the creatures and "Ladies" are all included under His hand; for His Name and for His sake they labor. At that time, they were all held by Him because they all cling to Her <note>the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note>.

Rabbi Isaac said: At the moment the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to destroy the hosts of Pharaoh below, He first broke their strength above, as we have established. What did He do? He removed and withdrew that holy supernal place which guides all those Chariots. Once it was withdrawn, they all trembled and could no longer drive. When they saw this, the ministering angel of the Egyptians could not prevent his dominion from being removed or their crowns from being taken away; and then the dominion of the Egyptians passed away.

Rabbi Isaac said: At the moment Israel approached the sea, the Holy One, blessed be He, called to the Angel of the Sea. He said to him: "When I created this world, I appointed you over the sea and made a condition with you that the sea should dry its waters before My children." Now the time has arrived for My children to pass through. Therefore, what is written afterward? ->**"And the sea returned to its strength [Le-Eitano] as morning appeared"** (Exodus 14:27)<- What does "to its strength" <note>Le-Eitano</note> mean? It means "to its condition" <note>Le-Tena'o</note>—the agreement it had with the Holy One, blessed be He, when He created the world. And as Israel approached the sea, and they were afraid, with the sea rising and falling, they lifted their eyes and saw Pharaoh and his hosts. They were terrified and cried out in that hour. What did the sea see? It saw the coffin of Joseph and fled from before it. Why? Because it is written of Joseph: ->**"And he fled and went outside"** (Genesis 39:12)<- and because of this, ->**"The sea saw and fled"** (Psalms 114:3)<-. And it is written: "And He took off the wheel of his chariots..." ->**"Let us flee from before Israel."**<- Why? Because they saw the spiritual essence of Egypt—all their crowns were burned. Then they said, "Let us flee from before Israel."

Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yose were walking in the desert. Rabbi Hiyya said to Rabbi Yose: Come and see, when the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to remove a dominion on earth, He does not do so until He removes their dominion in the heavens. He does not remove the ruler until He strikes the scepter against their scepter, so that their dominion in the heavens is diminished.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Beshalach**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion: "When he sent," referring to Pharaoh sending the Israelites out of Egypt.</note>

...in the firmament in order to fulfill that which is written: *to divide between the day and between the night.* Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Hezekiah were walking along the way. Rabbi Yose opened his discourse and said:
> *O Lord, our Master, how mighty is Your name in all the earth!* (Psalms 8:2)

"O Lord, our Master"—this is said when the Holy One, blessed be He, seeks to mention the matter of the mighty nations to execute powerful judgment upon them, breaking them and subjugating the strength of their dominion.
> *You will give truth to Jacob, kindness to Abraham...* (Micah 7:20)

...over the nations. It should have said "He performed kindness" or "He will give kindness." What is the meaning of *You will give kindness to Abraham*? Rather, this refers to the "wind" from the side of the North, the depth of all things. <note>The North usually represents Gevurah (Judgment), but here it is being sweetened by Chesed (Kindness).</note> And David sought in his prayer to subdue the nations through this, and this is "Kindness" when it returns to being sharp and potent. At the time when everything is gathered as one into the "depth of all," then they all rejoice, and the **Matronita** <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence as a Queen or Matron</note> is crowned by the **King**, and all the nations are subdued, and the dominion of the mighty nations is removed from before the Matronita. Then, all those who hold fast to Her lift up their heads.

They turned and saw a man who was coming with a load in front of him. Rabbi Yose said, "Certainly, perhaps this man is 'mighty'; he is a 'kindness' to us and a 'pious one' <note>A wordplay on the Hebrew 'Chesed' (Kindness) and 'Chasid' (Pious)</note> prepared before us on the road." They looked at the verse and saw what kind of great man he was. He passed before them, walking with difficulty because of the load he was carrying. He waited and said, "I know another path, for I see with my eye that there is a danger for you [on this one]. Do not be found guilty through us, and let us not transgress that which is written:
> *And before a blind man, do not place a stumbling block* (Leviticus 19:14)

...and let us be of assistance on this path so that you do not endanger your lives." Rabbi Yose said, "Blessed is the Merciful One who brought us here." They joined with him. He said to them, "Do not be distressed by anything until we pass to this other side by the other path." 

After they emerged from the "Other Side," <note>The Sitra Achra, the realm of spiritual impurity or danger</note> he told them that on that other path they had been traveling, a murderer had once stood in that place and killed a pious man. From that day on, anyone who passes through that place endangers his life. For there, destructive spirits are stationed who kill people, and those who are wise do not pass there. And this is because of the Holy One, blessed be He, [avenging] what happened to that Priest every day. He opened and said:
> *This very day he shall halt at Nob...* (Isaiah 10:32)

The masters of the Academy have already established this. But come and see, they did not show you this: that the spirit of the matter passes through "this very day." Which day? The Day of Judgment. Rather, so it is written: *And he arose and took the ephod...* <note>original: "את הפרן את חניבעל בת עמינדב" - likely a scribal variant or Zoharic reference to the priestly garments or lineage involved in the Nob incident</note> and a spirit is over all of Israel, for it is their "ornament" <note>term: טויטירא (Totira) - a protective or decorative covering</note> to prepare the House, to hide it, and to bring it to the King in joy as one. From that point forward, anyone who serves in the Sanctuary [is affected]. In this manner:
> *So have I envisioned You in the Sanctuary* (Psalms 63:3)

For she was above him, and all those holy priests were the **grooms** <note>term: סוסכינין (Sosikinin) - attendants or best men at a wedding</note> of the Matronita. Once the "loaves" <note>referring to the Showbread or the priestly portions</note> of the Matronita were prepared together to beget and to honor the House, and no one was found to serve before Her and prepare the House and gladden Her in the vision with the King—then, from that day, the kingdom was removed, they died, and a "covering" stood over the world. Because of the slaughter and the covering, the kingdom of Israel was diminished by many thousands and tens of thousands. And until now, that "sin" hangs in the balance until Abraham and his merit arrive. And when it says *This very day he shall halt at Nob*, this refers to the Supernal Day. And what is this? The twenty-four <note>Hebrew: כ"ד</note> loaves of her grooms that were permitted, and the death that occurred because of the joining of the Priest's loaves... and because of this, one should not cling to the "waste." Therefore: *This very day he shall halt at Nob.* 

Come and see: "Gibeah of Saul"—how much of "Sheol" <note>The underworld/grave</note> took hold there because he killed the priests and crushed the people, and from there he was uprooted from the world. So too here, from that day on, no man passes through that "breach" without endangering his life. Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Hezekiah said to him, "You have gladdened us; certainly, you are a great man." He opened and said:
> *Happy is the man who finds wisdom* (Proverbs 3:13)

They lacked kindness because...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Beshalach 50**<-

In order that it should be found for you, and that the King of Wisdom should know of you. And this child goes forth. Just as I have waited for you to be joined with you. And this is when the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> is compared to him, like the way of the hungry at the mill, and concerning this it is written: *And he smelled the fragrance of his garments... like the fragrance of a field* (Genesis 27:27). That man opened with a secret and said: *A Psalm of David. The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof...* (Psalms 24:1). "A Psalm of David" is said in one place, and in another it is translated as "To David, a Psalm." What is the difference between this one and that one? Rather, "A Psalm of David" is the song that David said concerning the **Community of Israel** <note>The mystical archetype of the Jewish people, the Sefirah of Malkhut</note>. "To David, a Psalm" is the song that David said concerning himself. *The Lord’s is the earth and its fullness*: "The Lord’s" refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He. "The earth and its fullness" refers to the Community of Israel and all its hosts that are joined as one and are called "its fullness," and this is the Assembly of the Torah, to say *the whole earth is full of His glory*. *The world and those who dwell therein*: this is the lower land which is called "the world" <note>Tebel</note> and the inhabitants of the world who are within it. As it is written: *And He shall judge the world in righteousness* (Psalms 9:9), because whether for one nation or for the whole world, it is judged by this spirit. Come and see: Pharaoh sucked from this spirit until he and all his people were destroyed. Once this spirit was awakened against him, that **appointed minister** <term>Memuna: a celestial angel overseeing a specific nation</term> who was below them in authority was removed and passed away; then all those below were destroyed, as it is written: *And He took off their chariot wheels* (Exodus 14:25). What are "their chariot wheels"? The chariots of Pharaoh. And who is their "wheel"? That **appointed minister** who ruled over them, and because of this they all died in the sea. My brother, it is like this. Rather, the world was awakened against them and they were prepared by His hand. And because of this, it is written they "drowned in the Red Sea." Rabbi Yose said: It is certainly so, and therefore it is written "in the Red Sea" <note>Yam Suf</note>, the end of the levels. Rabbi Hiyya said: *And He made them drive heavily* (Exodus 14:25). What is "heavily"? Rather, from here we learn that when a male is remembered, he is remembered by that which he himself remembered. Regarding Pharaoh it is written: *And Pharaoh’s heart was heavy* <note>Hardened</note>. With that same word, the Holy One, Blessed be He, remembered him with literal "heaviness." The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: "Wicked one, you made your heart heavy; I will remember you with the same." Therefore, *He made them drive heavily*. *And Egypt said: Let us flee from before Israel* (Exodus 14:25). "And Egypt said" refers to the **appointed minister** over Egypt. Rabbi Yose said: This matter is difficult; since he was removed from his authority, how could he pursue after Israel? Rather, it is certainly all one. This refers to the Egypt below, for once their power was broken from above, then their power and **strength** <note>Tukpa</note> were broken below. This is what is written: *For the Lord fights for them against Egypt* (Exodus 14:25). Specifically "against Egypt"—this is their strength from above. And this is what they established: who is "Egypt" without further description? Here, "And Egypt said: Let us flee from before Israel," for they saw that their power and their strength from above were broken. Come and see: when this **Community of Israel** is awakened, all those who are dependent on her are awakened, and they all take hold below, and Israel is above all of them, for they are all to her like a body to a soul, as has been established. Because of this, Israel cleaves to her more than all other nations. And when they are awakened, all the nations who are **idolaters** <note>original: "ovdei avodah zarah"</note>, their strength and the power that rules over them is broken. Come and see: this minister who polished the Egyptians oppressed Israel with many labors, as it is said and established. After that first one was broken, those below were broken. This is what is written: *For the Lord fights for them against Egypt*. As is fitting for the flame, certainly.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Beshalach<-
<note>The portion of the Torah describing the Exodus and the parting of the Sea.</note>

Those wise ones follow seventy and two <note>The 72-letter Name of God derived from Exodus 14:19-21</note> levels, and thus three and [eighty] were fixed and established for the names of the Awesome One. They were engraved and hidden within the levels and were made like a body to the voice. Afterward, they divided and became two paths; half of them were revealed and half were submerged. These ascended and those descended. From here, the world spread out to divide into another side. There is a supernal end to the engraving, the seal of a powerful signet, and it strikes the wheels of the sea. All sides divided into four corners. One half ascends and one half descends. One half to the North side and one half to the South side. All are joined as one, coals and flames, all of them standing as a covering for the other which turns. One stands like a son, and what a perfect level for length and breadth! The whole world stands high above to bear and hold the knot for the tongues of the flames of the sea. Who has seen the wheels that ascend and descend, and the spirit that is written of them? And how many swords are on every side of the world! That level, all the power of the work stands with a wing on its right and a wing on its left. He returns and sits in the chambers like a king on his throne, looking out over all sides of the sea, to the four sides of the world. With Him, she <note>The Shekhinah</note> goes out; she is the King’s stability. Then speeches go forth, riches of the eyes, and they open them high above. From their chambers, those who strike shall arise in their positions; they awoke to the wise ones, appointed until it is written "as those who wander." Then: *And the angel of God moved.* <note>Exodus 14:19</note>

**Rabbi** Chiya opened: *She is like the merchant ships; she brings her food from afar.* <note>Proverbs 31:14</note> "She is like the merchant ships"—this is the Assembly of Israel <note>The Shekhinah</note>. "She brings her food from afar"—everything is increased there, for "from afar" refers to the [level of] Jubilee. "She brings her food" as one level that merchants travel upon, and through it are drawn all those rivers and springs that go into the sea, as it is said: *All the rivers run into the sea... to the place where the rivers go.* <note>Ecclesiastes 1:7</note> Even though they are all drawn to that level, and that level brings them to that sea, do not say that it releases them and they do not return as before. Rather, it says *to the place where the rivers go, there they return to go*—to that level, because of those new times, there they return to go from that place of the world and they never cease. They all gather in that place. And why "to go"? To that place of the sea, as has been stated. What is the name of that level? It is called "Righteous" <term>Tzadik: the ninth Sephirah, Yesod, which funnels divine blessing</term>. Rabbi Yehuda said: It is written, *There go the ships, and Leviathan, which You formed to sport in it.* <note>Psalm 104:26</note> "There go the ships"—they travel in that sea of portions and pressures until they are seen to join in that level. Then it is written: *Leviathan, which You formed to sport in it.* Rabbi Yitzhak said: High above there is a union of merchants in constant succession that is never separated. Rabbi Yehuda said: Who [merits] that union? He said to him: Whoever has a portion in the World to Come. Specifically in the World to Come. He said to him: And this we have learned from here, as it is written: *Leviathan, this (zeh) You formed to sport in it.* This implies "this," and "this" refers to those who are known <note>The level of "Zeh" often refers to the prophetic clarity of Moses or the level of Yesod</note>. He said to him: Here, both of you have spoken well, and Rabbi Yehuda has analyzed it well. And the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to delight the righteous with them, as it is written: *Then you shall delight in the Lord.* <note>Isaiah 58:14</note> Rabbi Chiya said: How many shifts, how many myriads of holy camps does the Holy One, blessed be He, have! Some are for the wise, some for the eyes, some for the meritorious, some for the students, some for the male principle, some for mercy, and some for judgment. And over them all, He appointed the Matronita <term>Matronita: The Divine Matron or Queen, a title for the Shekhinah</term> to stand before Him like a palace. Corresponding to the armor, the Matronita has armed helpers with joyful faces. There are others found, and all of them shine... how many go out, how many eyes are covered by wings, protecting the whole world. Before each and every one are coals of burning fire. A flaming canopy covers them. In the inner mechanism of the gate, it flames throughout the whole world toward the front side.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Beshalach**<-
<note>Beshalach: "When he sent," the name of this Torah portion (Exodus 13:17–17:16).</note>

145. This is what is written: **"And the flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life"** (Genesis 3:24). For the "way of the tree of life" is the Matronita <note>Aramaic: *Matronita*, the Queen or Matron, representing the Shekhinah</note>, for she is the path to that great and mighty Tree <note>The "Tree of Life" refers to the central divine emanations, specifically Zeir Anpin</note> to partake of it. This is what is written: *Behold the bed of Solomon; sixty mighty men are around it, of the mighty men of Israel* (Song of Songs 3:7). "Israel" refers to the Supernal Israel <note>The divine realm</note>. They all grasp the sword when the Matronita travels; they all travel with her. This is what is written: **"And the angel of God moved..."** (Exodus 14:19). Is she called "the angel of God"? Or rather, is she not Life itself? Come and see: A person prepares a city before a palace, a holy palace for the Holy One to enter. The Holy One, Holy One, Holy One <note>The threefold holiness of God</note> enters it, and it is called Jerusalem, the Holy City. Anyone who wishes to enter to the King can only enter through this holy city, just as one goes to a king—the King below. This is what is written: *This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter into it* (Psalms 118:20). Every mission that the King desires reaches out from the Matronita, and every mission from below to the King enters first into the house of the Matronita, and from there to the King. Thus, the Matronita is the messenger <term>shlicha</term> <note>The word for "messenger" or "agent" is the same as "angel" (malakh) in Hebrew/Aramaic</note> for everything, from above to below and from below to above.

And because she is the messenger for all, it is written: **"And the angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, moved and went"** (Exodus 14:19) above. Regarding the "angel of God," it is written: **"And the Lord went before them..."** (Exodus 13:21), as we have established. Is it not the honor of the King that the Matronita should go? There was a war, and she went as the messenger. To a King who was joined with a Matronita: the King saw her glory was above all other queens in the world. He said, "All of them are like animals compared to this Matronita; her beauty shall rise above all. What shall I do for her? I will place my entire legion in her hand." The King issued a proclamation: "From here on, all the King's matters shall be handed over to the Matronita." What did he do? The King entrusted her with all his weapons, all his types of shields for war, all the King's precious stones, and all the King's treasuries. He said, "From here on, anyone who needs to speak with me, the King, will not be able to speak with me until he makes it known to the Matronita."

So too, the Holy One, blessed be He, out of the greatness of His love and affection for the Assembly of Israel <note>The Shekhinah</note>, entrusted everything into her authority. He said, "Behold, the other nations are as nothing compared to her." He said, "The kingdom is established..." etc. *My dove, my undefiled, is but one* (Song of Songs 6:9). "What shall I do for her? I will place my entire legion in her hand." The King issued a proclamation: "All the King's matters shall be handed over to the Matronita." He entrusted to her hand all his weapons: spears and swords, bows, arrows, and catapults, engines of war, stones, and all types of shields for war. This is what is written: *Behold the bed of Solomon; sixty mighty men... they all grasp the sword, experts in war* (Song of Songs 3:7-8). The King said, "From now on, my war is handed into your hand; my weapons and my masters of shields are in your hand. From now on, you be the guardian of them." This is what is written: **"The Guardian of Israel"** (Psalms 121:4). From now on, whoever needs Me will not be able to speak with Me until he makes it known to the Matronita. This is what is written: *With this [Zot] shall Aaron come into the holy place* (Leviticus 16:3) <note>The word "Zot" (This) is a mystical name for the Shekhinah</note>. She is the messenger for all, as we have established; thus, everything is for the honor of the Matronita. This is what is written: **"And the angel of God moved..."** as has been said.

And they went out from their wine <note>A metaphor for divine judgment/rigor</note> to the war, because before her were the masters of shields, masters of catapults, masters of spears and swords, and they ascended before her. And behold, they were coming with their remnants to wage war against Israel from above. And at that time, that great prince who is appointed over the Egyptians <note>The guardian angel of Egypt</note> was exhausted, and he covered the matter... chariots of accusers, and over every single chariot there are appointed rulers and officers. This is what is written: **"And he took six hundred chosen chariots..."** (Exodus 14:7). Were there only six hundred chariots in all of Egypt? Heaven forbid! Rather, "and all the chariots of Egypt." Even so, Samael <note>The primary archangel of evil/accuser</note> was seen joining him; there were chariots of accusers to assist him. This is what is written: **"And he took six hundred chosen chariots..."**

<summary>This page explains that the "Angel of God" leading Israel is the Shekhinah (the Matronita), who acts as the sole gateway to the Divine King and commands the celestial armies. It describes how God entrusted all His "weapons" and authority to her out of love, making her the "Guardian of Israel" and the necessary intermediary for all prayer and divine action.</summary>

## Beshalach
->**Beshalach**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion, meaning "When he sent," referring to Pharaoh releasing the Israelites.</note>

When is the Holy One, blessed be He, joyful? It is when He strikes in the battle against the "Other Side" <note>The forces of spiritual impurity or evil</note>, for the Holy One, blessed be He, bound all those celestial chariots and delivered them all to the Matron <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence in its feminine aspect</note>. This is as it is written:
> *The brook Kishon swept them away, that ancient brook...* (Judges 5:21)

And to break the wicked, they were all delivered [to her], as it is written:
> *Who is this that comes from Edom, with crimsoned garments from Bozrah...* (Isaiah 63:1)

And regarding this, it says: *And it moved from behind them*—**"And the pillar of cloud moved from before them and stood behind them"** (Exodus 14:19). What is this "pillar of cloud"? Rabbi Yose says: This was the cloud that is always found with the Shekhinah, and this is the cloud that Moses entered <note>referring to Moses ascending Sinai</note>. Rabbi Isaac said: It is written,
> *And the Lord went before them by day...* (Exodus 13:21)

And He accompanied the support of the "Righteous One" <note>The sefirah of Yesod</note> and the spread of His firmament, and therefore He went before the cloud by day. And it is written:
> *By day the Lord commands His lovingkindness* (Psalms 42:9)

From the side of Lovingkindness <term>Chesed: the divine attribute of expansive benevolence</term> this came, and it is called "Chesed." And the cloud that traveled, traveled at night and was called a "pillar of fire."

Rabbi Shimon said: The "pillar of cloud by day" is Abraham <note>representing Chesed</note>. The "pillar of fire by night" is Isaac <note>representing Gevurah/Judgment</note>. And both of them were found within the Shekhinah. And what Rabbi Isaac said is correct, for because of this, the levels of this [mystery] are found and established: **"And the angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, moved and went behind them"** (Exodus 14:19). For it is written that it moved from the side of Lovingkindness and attached itself to the side of Power <term>Gevurah: the divine attribute of strength and judgment</term>, because the hour had arrived for [the Egyptians] to be struck.

Come and see: At that hour, the Moon <note>The Shekhinah</note> was perfected by all those seventy holy crowns from three sides. One side was clothed in the crowns of Lovingkindness (*Chesed*) upon her, with engraved rings of light that the cloud merited to illuminate for her. The second side was clothed in the spear of Power (*Gevurah*) with the strength of the "Male Torah" <note>The written Law or the sefirah of Tiferet</note>, and the side of the bucket <note>referring to the drawing of judgment</note> as it is written from the side of "Awe" <note>Fear of God</note> upon her with hidden engravings. The third side was clothed in garments of purple that the Holy King wears, which are called Beauty <term>Tiferet: the attribute of harmony and balance</term>, the inheritance of the holy moon through seventy supernal crowns from the side of "Father and Mother" <note>The higher sefirot of Chokhmah and Binah</note>. And what is the inclusion of this side and that side?

We have learned: From the side of Lovingkindness (*Chesed*) there are seventy-two witnesses. From the side of Power (*Gevurah*) there are seventy-two scribes. From the third side, there are seventy-two colors for Glory (*Tiferet*). And the Holy One, blessed be He, sparkles as one and the Holy Name of the Chariot ascends. Here, Wisdom was engraved to be joined as one, and it is the Holy Name engraved in its arrangement, a collection of letters.

These first letters <note>referring to the first of the three verses, Exodus 14:19</note> were inscribed in their [forward] order, all of them established because they are found for the first rectification, like Lovingkindness (*Chesed*) which travels and is established in forward order. The second letters <note>Exodus 14:20</note> were inscribed opposite them, in reverse order, because all these second letters are found in Power (*Gevurah*) to strike judgments and weapons that come from the side of Samael <note>The primary figure of evil/prosecution in Jewish mysticism</note>. The third letters <note>Exodus 14:21</note> are inscribed to show the colors of Lovingkindness to be crowned by the Holy King, and all of them are joined and tied within Him. He is awakened by His crowns... like a king crowned with all strength, and two holy supports engraved with the 72-letter Name <note>The Name of God derived from the 72 letters in each of the three verses of Exodus 14:19-21</note> which are crowned by the Patriarchs and the holy Chariots upon Him.

And if you say that the third letters are not written alone, some in forward order and some in reverse, for we have learned below: when the Holy One, blessed be He, delivers [the protection] to Israel from this side and that side, He makes a shield of two sides. And it is written:
> *And the middle bar in the midst of the boards...* (Exodus 26:28)

This is the Holy One, blessed be He. Rabbi Isaac said: This is Jacob <note>representing Tiferet, the middle bar</note>, and they are all one. It is like a King who is perfect from all his sides... what is the way of that King? His face shines like the sun constantly because he is perfect. When he turns for good, he turns; when for evil, [he turns]. And the legions seek to look upon him. He who is a fool sees the face of the King and does not look [deeper]. But he who is wise sees the face of the King shining like wine; the King is certainly perfect...

<summary>This page explains the mystical significance of the Pillar of Cloud and Fire, linking them to the divine attributes of Chesed (Lovingkindness) and Gevurah (Power). It introduces the derivation of the 72-letter Name of God from three consecutive verses in Exodus, explaining how their letter orders (forward and reverse) reflect different spiritual forces used to protect Israel and judge Egypt.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Do not be ashamed to appear before the Living One, for if it were not so, the King would not be complete. On this account, in order to be protected, so the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kadosh Baruch Hu"</note> is always complete in this manner. In all of this, He is not seen except through the light of the lamps. And because of this, those guilty ones must not be protected from Him. Those who are wise and possess the strength of wine <note>likely referring to the "wine of Torah" or mystical intoxication</note> know the King is complete, even though He subdues the cold darkness. Let there be no shame within Him, so that one may be protected by Him. Rabbi Judah said: From here we learn that a knife does not divide into another place except to include everything. Thus there are two colors to be included; therefore, everything is established as one below. And even though those below take hold of this side and that side, they are written in their proper order.

---

**And the angel of God, which went before the camp of Israel, removed and went behind them; and the pillar of the cloud went from before their face, and stood behind them.** <note>Exodus 14:19</note> Until here is one side: <term>Loving-kindness for Abraham</term> <note>The first of the three verses corresponds to the attribute of Chesed/Mercy</note>. Rabbi Shimon said: My son, come and see. This spirit, when the Holy Ancient One <note>Atika Kadisha, the highest aspect of Divinity</note> shines upon the King, He strengthens him with holy, supernal crowns. When they reach him, the Patriarchs are crowned. At the moment the Patriarchs are crowned, then everything is in perfection. Then the <term>Matronita</term> <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Feminine presence</note> takes up her burden in that perfection of the Patriarchs. And when she is crowned by them, then she is blessed and the desire of all is in her hand. Behold, in this manner, the Holy Name is engraved in its letters, galloping upon the holy supernal Chariot, the crown of the Patriarchs.

---

**The commentators have said** here that the King wrote the verse *And he traveled* <note>Vayissa - Exodus 14:19</note> in order, every single letter in a separate house like a garden bed, with this language until all the rows are arranged in order by the wind of Loving-kindness <note>Chesed</note>, not turning to the right. And on the other side, the King wrote the verse *And he came* <note>Vayavo - Exodus 14:20</note> backwards, likewise every single letter in a separate house like a garden bed, with this language until all the rows are arranged backwards by the wind of Strength <note>Gevurah</note>, all of them surrounding on the right. Afterward, the King wrote the verse *And he stretched out* <note>Vayet - Exodus 14:21</note> in order, likewise every single letter in a separate house like a garden bed, with this language until all the rows of the Holy King are joined in Beauty <note>Tiferet</note> and in the Crown <note>Keter</note>; Wisdom was joined and they became the Holy Name. And afterward, the King produced the 72 <note>The text has a typo "62", corrected here to 72</note> Names emerging from these three verses in a square, every single name consisting of three letters emerging from these three verses: forward, backward, forward. The sign for this is "Beautiful Light" <note>The Hebrew word for beautiful, YaPeH, serves as a mnemonic for Yashar (Straight), Hafuch (Inverted), Yashar (Straight)</note> with this language. Behold, in this manner, the Holy Name is engraved in its letters, galloping upon the holy supernal Chariot, the crown of the Patriarchs. And we have not printed it <note>the actual grid of names</note> because of the precious glory of our greatness.

---

**Rabbi Yose said:** I have found this secret in the arrangements of the Rav in Babylon: three here, and here, and here, corresponding to these three. And such is the order. Rabbi Yose said: Everything is to be included in this holy perfection and to be aided by it; it is found that the perfection of the Holy Chariot is within it. Rabbi Shimon said: This is the Holy Name, the crown of the Patriarchs, which they wear as their very bodies, as a single union, to be included in the forty-eight arrangements that establish the perfection of all and the essence of the lines. Come and see: the body of the flame is thus: it raises the letters *Nun* and *Yod*. The head of all the branches of the tree is *Vav* and *Vav-Pe*. And these awaken the union of all the branches, the body and the blossom, in forty-eight words. And this is marked in three worlds below, corresponding to: ->Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord of Hosts<- <note>Isaiah 6:3</note>. "Holy" above. "Holy" in the middle. "Holy" below. "Holy" is <term>Loving-kindness</term>. "Holy" is <term>Strength</term>. "Holy" is <term>Beauty</term>. And all of them are engraved in seventy-two, as has been said. Blessed is He and blessed is His Name forever and ever, Amen. Come and see: at the hour that Israel stood by the sea, they saw many wonders.

## Beshalach
->**Beshalach**<-

The multitudes of many armies and many officers from above and below all gathered against Israel. They troubled them with all their strength. At that moment, the **Holy Ancient One** <note>Aramaic: *Atika Kadisha*; the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note> was revealed, and **Favor** <note>Aramaic: *Re’ua*; Divine Will or Grace</note> was found in all the upper worlds; then the light of all things was illuminated. Rabbi Isaac rejoiced at that moment, seeing how the light surrounded them from all sides. And what of the clouds that stood before them? Behind them were all those multitudes, all those officers who stir up trouble above, many accusers who labored against the light. Then it was written: *And the Lord said to Moses, "Why do you cry out to Me?"* <note>Exodus 14:15</note> And we learned in the **Book of Concealment** <note>Aramaic: *Sifra Detzniuta*; a foundational, highly cryptic section of the Zohar</note> that the beard of the Ancient One supports everything; then everything is illuminated as one, and the upper laws are arranged and handed over into the hands of the upper and lower beings. Because of this, everything was open before the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, at the splitting of the Red Sea, and all was done with **Wisdom** <note>Hebrew: *Chokhmah*; the primordial point of creation</note>. What is the reason? Because the splitting of the Red Sea depends upon the Ancient One.

Rabbi Simeon said: There is a certain **doe** <note>Aramaic: *Ayaltah*; a recurring Zoharic symbol for the Shekhinah or the community of Israel</note> on the earth. When the world is in need of mercy for water, she lets out cries, and the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, hears her voice and accepts her prayer. Then the world is sustained, as it is written: *As the doe pants for streams of water...* <note>Psalms 42:2</note> And when she needs to give birth, she is closed up from all sides. Then she comes and places her head between her knees and cries out with many voices, and the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, has mercy on her and summons a certain serpent to her, which bites her at that place <note>the womb</note> and opens it, tearing that place so she may give birth immediately. Rabbi Simeon said: Regarding this matter, do not ask and do not test the Lord, for it is precisely so.

### And He Saved
*And the Lord saved Israel on that day... and Israel saw the Egyptians dead...* <note>Exodus 14:30</note> That prince <note>the celestial guardian angel</note> appointed over the Egyptians—the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, saw him and passed him through the **River of Fire** <note>Aramaic: *Nehar Dinur*; a river of fire in the heavens that purifies or punishes souls</note>. His horse was at the brink... for what reason? There are many matters of Wisdom regarding how He removed him from his dominion.

### And He Saw
*And Israel saw the great hand...* <note>Exodus 14:31</note> Rabbi Hiyya said: It is enough that the Hand was raised, and all were humbled. The Hand was established and included all the "days," as we have learned: the "Bride" is included in the "days," and depends upon the "days." This is what is written: *Your right hand, O Lord, is glorious in power; Your right hand, O Lord, shatters the enemy.* <note>Exodus 15:6</note>

And Rabbi Isaac said: There was never a person whose heart was as hardened against the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, as Pharaoh. Rabbi Jose said: Was it through pride and pleasure? He replied: Not so. It was because the prophets of Israel were strengthened against all the prophets of the nations, just as Pharaoh was strengthened in his height... and they struck his strength, yet he did not repent. Rabbi Judah said in the name of Rabbi Isaac: Pharaoh was wiser than all his sorcerers. He looked into all those astrological signs and all those sciences, and in all their sides he did not see a redemption for Israel. For indeed, all the celestial knots were tied against Israel. But Pharaoh did not remember that there is another "Knot of Faith" <note>the Divine connection</note> that rules over everything. Because of this, his heart was hardened. Rabbi Abba said: Pharaoh's heart was only hardened by what he heard; for when Moses said, "Thus says the Lord," that very word hardened his heart, as it is written: *And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh.* For in all his wisdom, he could not find a basis for this Power ruling on earth. Rabbi Jose said: Later he said, "I have sinned against the Lord"—the same mouth that said one thing said the other. Rabbi Hezekiah opened and said: *It is all one; therefore I say, He destroys the innocent and the wicked.* <note>Job 9:22</note> The masters of the Academy established this through the spirit of Wisdom...

<summary>This page discusses the splitting of the Red Sea as an act originating from the highest Divine level (the Ancient One) and uses the allegory of the "doe" to explain how Divine mercy is birthed through crisis. It also analyzes Pharaoh's hardening of heart as a result of his reliance on astrology over the supreme "Knot of Faith."</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Exodus, specifically the portion of Beshalach. It transitions from the miraculous crossing of the Red Sea to the spiritual mechanics behind the Song of the Sea.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Beshalach**<-
<note>original: "בשלח" - The name of the Torah portion meaning "When he sent," referring to Pharaoh releasing the Israelites.</note>

And these [heavenly forces] awaken redemption constantly for Israel. **And Israel saw the Great Hand which the Lord did in Egypt** <note>Exodus 14:31</note>. But did He only do it now? Surely it was done from the very beginning. What is the meaning of "the Great Hand which the Lord did"? Rather, this "Hand" is usually called "less than ten fingers," but it is called "Great" because five others were included within it, and then they are called "Great." All fifteen fingers ascended to gaze upon the mystery of glory that He made for them. Now all the levels were established for the throne of the <term>Matronita</term> <note>The Matronita is a Zoharic term for the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence, often depicted as a Queen or Matron.</note>. From this point forward, one may gaze upon that which is written regarding the love before Him. It is written, "And He hardened the heart of Pharaoh." Once these fifteen were completed, the matter was within the power of Pharaoh; then it is written, "And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh." And regarding this, "And Israel saw the Great Hand," and it is written, **"And the Lord saved"** <note>Exodus 14:30</note>. Was there no salvation until now? And it is written, "And the people believed... and they believed etc." and they saw all those mighty deeds that <term>the Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> performed for them in Egypt. But what is the meaning of "And they believed"? It refers to that matter which was said: "And Moses said to the people, 'Do not fear, stand firm and see...'" <note>Exodus 14:13</note>. Rabbi Yose said: It is written, **"And Israel saw the Egyptians dead"** and it is written, **"You shall not see them again forever"** <note>Exodus 14:13</note>. Rabbi Yose said: We have learned that they saw them. He said to him: If it were written "You shall not see them [at all]," I would have thought so. Rabbi Abba said to him: You have spoken well. But come and see, it is written "From the world unto the world" <note>Psalm 106:48</note>, and we have learned there is an Upper World and a Lower World. The Upper World is where the beginning of the lighting of the lamps occurs. The Lower World is the conclusion, where everything is mingled together, and from this world, the mighty deeds are conducted below. And through this world, <term>the Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> performs signs for Israel and enacts miracles for them. Every place where "World" stands to perform miracles, they all shine and are sanctified through this world, and the miracle occurred for Israel like this world. And regarding this, it is written "You shall not see them again until the World" <note>The Zohar interprets "Ad Olam" (forever) as "Until the [Lower] World" acts in judgment</note>—until that "World" stood and its judgments were prepared. Once they were completed within it to be judged, then it is written, "And Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the seashore." This is what is written, "From the world unto the world," for glory is within it, and from that power it is written, **"And they believed in the Lord and in Moses His servant"** <note>Exodus 14:31</note>.

---

**Then** [Az] Moses sang. Rabbi Yehuda opened: **"Before I formed you in the womb I knew you"** etc. <note>Jeremiah 1:5</note>. The entire portion of Israel is that <term>the Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> desired them more than all other nations. From the treasure of the love with which He loved them, He established over them a true and faithful assembly. The <term>Holy Spirit</term> rested upon them more than any other faithful assembly, and He brought them out from their portion specifically to the "digging of Jacob" <note>A cryptic reference to the spiritual lineage of the Patriarch Jacob</note> from his designation for <term>the Holy One, Blessed Be He</term>. Since he belonged to Him, <term>the Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> took him and crowned him with many crowns, and gave him a holy greatness above. Then He brought forth from His designation a Holy Spirit to the world and gave it as a holy faith—a mystery of faith—and testified to his nation below. He merited to kiss the entirety of faith. <term>The Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> brought forth a Holy Spirit from the sapphire light, for he is a prophet who gazes through its lattices and descends. Crowns were gathered and stood before him, and He entrusted him with all that was His, giving him the staff and the key, and three [other] keys. He crowned him with five crowns, and each and every crown ascended and surrounded the portion of the worlds, like rivers and stars for radiance, like a prophet to the High Holy King. Then he was conceived in all the directions of the Assembly of Eden and revealed in His palace. "Then" [Az] was opened; it ascended and was crowned in preservation. He crowned it with three words and protections and five crowns, and placed the key in his hands. He was needed for all these hosts and legions of His. Then all the births opened and said, "Your kindness," and it surrounds the side of sides, for <term>the Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> awakened a spirit to rule and arrange the worlds. A voice went out and said: What is this, that all these keys are in his hands?

## Main Text (Zohar)

In his hands. A voice broke out and said: "Receive him among you! This is the time for him to descend among the sons of men. The hidden Torah is destined to be delivered into his hands, and the four worlds shall be ruled and governed through him." At that moment, all the celestial beings were stirred and filled with joy. They opened their mouths and said: **"Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place"** <note>Ezekiel 3:12</note>. "Come, come, O righteous one!" Then that spirit ascended and stood before the King <note>The Holy One, Blessed be He</note> to be crowned with twenty-eight <term>holy crowns</term> <note>original: "atrin kadishin"; these represent the 28 letters of the first verse of Genesis or the 28 times mentioned in Ecclesiastes</note>. All the keys of the King were entrusted into his hands, and he was appointed the faithful member of His household. The letter *He* <note>representing the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> ascended and was adorned with her ornaments; she received him and brought him to the King. That spirit called out like those who pour from a vessel, "The Unique One rides!" She received him and revealed the King to him, and she gave him gifts and nourishment to distribute to Pharaoh and all his land. And in the time of wrath, when he ascended to the King, all the engraved letters were investigated and supported. At that hour, when he sought to subdue Pharaoh in the land of Levi, four camps were established, and five canopies were prepared for the King... and five engravings were prepared to provide for that other spirit. When he went out into the world, the letter *He* shone in his face, and all were filled with his nourishment. At that moment, the Holy One, Blessed be He, called out over him: **"Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations"** <note>Jeremiah 1:5</note>. Rabbi Isaac said: At that moment, the Holy One, Blessed be He, slew the prince <note>the guardian angel</note> of the Egyptians, and Moses and Israel saw him... then they sang the song with all joy: **"Then Moses and the children of Israel sang."**

->**THEN**<-
**Moses and the children of Israel sang this song...** <note>Exodus 15:1</note>. Rabbi Abba opened and said: **"The wrath of a king is as messengers of death, but a wise man will pacify it"** <note>Proverbs 16:14</note>. Come and see: he saw all the power and all the mighty deeds that were performed for Israel. All that was carved out from the light of the <term>Holy Ancient One</term> <note>original: "Atika Kadisha"; the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note> with his engraved and marked crowns... it shone in the darkness and illuminated every side. The word "will sing" <note>the Hebrew "Yashir" is in the future tense</note> implies that this matter is suspended and stands for the time to come, for Israel is destined to sing this song in the future. Moses and the children of Israel—we see that even though the ancient righteous ones have ascended to the highest levels above and are strengthened in the bond of the <term>Light of Life</term> <note>original: "nehora d'chayye"</note>, they are all destined to appear in the body and see the miracles and mighty deeds that the Holy One, Blessed be He, performs for Israel. This is the meaning of "Moses and the children of Israel *will* sing." Rabbi Shimon said: It is from here: **"The Lord will set His hand again a second time to recover the remnant of His people"** <note>Isaiah 11:11</note>. "To recover" <note>Hebrew: "liknot," to acquire</note> is as it is said: **"The Lord acquired me at the beginning of His way"** <note>Proverbs 8:22</note>. "The remnant of His people"—these are the righteous who are called the "remnant" of the people, and the merit of the righteous will protect them. Consider that this world only exists for the sake of those who make themselves like "remnants" <note>meaning those who are humble or self-effacing</note>. And if you say: since they are bound in the Light of Life and delight in the supernal delight, why would the Holy One, Blessed be He, bring them down to the earth? Go and see... the spirit of the dead who were in a high degree above, the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings them down to the earth below... for as it is said: **"For there is no righteous man on earth who does good and does not sin"** <note>Ecclesiastes 7:20</note>. And if you speak of those buildings that are written of... they shall rise and be happy... Moses is destined to say the song in the time to come. Why? Because it is written: **"As in the days of your coming out of the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders"** <note>Micah 7:15</note>. It should say "I will show *them*." Rather, "I will show *him*" refers to showing Moses the wonders he saw at first... and this is "I will show him My salvation" <note>Psalm 91:16</note>. And then—

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on Parashat Beshalach, specifically focusing on the Song of the Sea (Exodus 15). ## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Beshalach**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion, meaning "When he sent," referring to Pharaoh sending the Israelites out of Egypt.</note>

Fortunate are the people of Israel who are found below in the surroundings of the **Matronita** <note>The Shekhinah, the feminine Divine Presence, depicted here as a Queen</note> to receive her. For this reason, anyone who takes hold of the surroundings of the Matronita—since all the people of the world who focus upon her and everything [they do] is to give her benefit—behold, they have life in this world and life in the World of Life <note>The World to Come</note>. Through her, they have the life of the bonds of faith. There is no day when the King <note>The Holy One, Blessed be He</note> unites [with her] that he does not ascend through her, and they are found beneath the upper and lower scepters.
The "Other Side" <note>The forces of spiritual impurity</note> surrounds mankind, except for the Torah which finds the Matronita of the King. And from where is she found above? It says: **"And take this staff in your hand"** <note>Exodus 4:17</note>. This is in order to return the King to her, so that the King's footsteps are found toward her. Rabbi Yose said: For all those watches that were standing against [Israel], the Holy Kingdom went out to meet them; because of this, they find the Matronita. Rabbi Yehuda said: If so, why is it written "staff" and so on? Israel needed to find the Matronita. Rather, it was the merit of the Patriarchs that [empowered] the staff and Israel, for they knew how to find the King for the sake of the Holy Matronita, because all that strength and might of hers she inherits from the King.

Rabbi Hiyya opened and said: **"Arise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the watches"** <note>Lamentations 2:19</note>. "Arise, cry out" refers to the Assembly of Israel <note>The Shekhinah</note> in the night of exile. Rabbi Yose said: "In the night" refers to the time when [the attribute of Judgment] rules and they awaken "at the beginning of the watches"—He makes it like the Beginning <note>Genesis/Creation</note>. Rather, "at the head/beginning" is as it is written: **"Above my chief joy"** <note>Psalm 137:6; literally "at the head of my joy"</note>. And we have established that **"the head of the staff"** <note>Genesis 47:31</note> refers to **Yesod** <note>The Sefirah of Foundation, the channel of divine procreation</note>. So too here, "at the head" refers to Yesod, by which the Matronita is blessed. "The head of the watches" refers to the head of the assembly and the praise. Rabbi Yose said: This is the head of the King's crowns and the conclusion.

Rabbi Abba said: It is written "at the head of the watches" as a tradition, and this is the head of the staff, and everything is within the High Holy King who is hidden and not [revealed], etc. Rabbi Isaac said to him: This is the light that goes out from above, from which all the oil and greatness <note>Anointing and abundance</note> goes out to his portion... and it implies that the Crown <note>Keter</note> of which it is written "kindness to the Lord" <note>original: *chasidah l'Hashem*</note>, this is the High Holy King, and regarding this it is not written "kindness to him." "And they shall be troubled"—he said this refers to the generations of generations, so that his intention shall never be forgotten; for whoever merits this Torah in this world merits the World to Come and everything, to find her in the days of the King Messiah in the joy of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Then it shall be said:
It was said at that time. It was said like a holy healing, like the time Israel was at Marah <note>Exodus 15:23</note>. It was said in exile. It was said in the redemption of Israel. It was said regarding the World to Come. "Kindness to the Lord" is written... But because of the finding of the Matronita, they sought to find the Lord, who is the Holy King.

**"For He is highly exalted"** <note>Exodus 15:1; literally "He is proud, proud"</note>. Just as He ascended and was honored with His crowns of blessings, praises, and strengths to bring them all out. **"For He is highly exalted"**: Exalted in this world, exalted in the World to Come. "For He is exalted" at that time, so that He may be crowned with His crowns in perfect joy. **"The horse and its rider He has thrown into the sea"** <note>Exodus 15:1</note>. This refers to the dominion below and the dominion above that go [together]; the Holy One, Blessed be He, acts below until their dominion passes away above. This is what is written: **"The Lord will punish the host of heaven on high, and the kings of the earth on the earth"** <note>Isaiah 24:21</note>. "Thrown into the sea"—Rabbi Yehuda said: "In the sea" refers to the exile, about which it is written: **"And the Lord drove the sea back with a strong east wind"** <note>Exodus 14:21</note>, which is the powerful force of **Gevurah** <note>The Sefirah of Might/Judgment</note>, as it is written "strength all the night." At that time, the Matronita requested from the King that all those hosts below and all those rulers above be delivered into her hand; and they were all delivered into her hand to execute vengeance upon them. This is what is written: **"The horse and its rider He has thrown into the sea."** "Into the sea" plainly refers to both above and below.

**"The Lord is my strength and song"** <note>Exodus 15:2</note>. Rabbi Hiyya opened and said: Search, search, and man shall precede and see upon him... just as men are found for the glory of the Holy One, Blessed be He, when He created the world to look...
