## Main Text (Zohar)

He looked upon Adam so that he would be a ruler with **two faces** <note>original: "du-partzufin" – referring to the mystical concept that Adam and Eve were originally created as a single, back-to-back being</note>. There was a fear of him among the upper and lower beings, for he descended in a precious likeness. When the creatures saw him, they gathered toward him and prostrated themselves before him. A fear and trembling doubled over them, as it is written: *And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth and upon every bird of the heavens* <note>Genesis 9:2</note>. They approached him from the side, as it is written that he should have a vision before him. But when they sinned with him, he was cast out, and those who were salt-like and covered in darkness appeared before him. Afterward, He commanded him concerning a certain tree, but he did not stand by the command of his Master.

->**We have found**<-
In the **Book of Enoch** <note>A mystical text attributed to the biblical figure Enoch, often cited in the Zohar for ancient secrets</note> it says that after the Holy One, Blessed be He, took him up and showed him all the upper and lower treasures, He showed him the Tree of Life and the tree that Adam was commanded concerning. He showed him the place of the pious one who descends to Eden, and he saw that if Adam had kept this command, he would have been able to exist perpetually and be eternal. But because he transgressed the command of his Master, he went out to judgment and was punished. Rabbi Isaac said: He was created with **two faces**, and we have already established the meaning of *And He took one of his ribs* <note>Genesis 9:2</note>. The Holy One, Blessed be He, covered them and cut them into two, from East and West. This is what is written: *Behind and before You have hedged me in* <note>Psalms 139:5</note>. "Behind" refers to the West, and "before" refers to the East. Rabbi Hiyya said: What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, do? He prepared that **female** <note>original: "nukva"</note> and perfected her beauty above all else and brought her to Adam. This is what is written: *And the Lord God built the rib which He had taken from the man into a woman* <note>Genesis 2:22</note>. Come and see what is written above: *And He took one of his ribs*. What is "one"? It is as you say: *My dove, my perfect one, is but one; she is the only one of her mother* <note>Song of Songs 6:9</note>. The mechanisms from his sides were all-encompassing, and the Tabernacle was filled. Rabbi Judah said: The Supernal Holy One made Adam beautiful and included within him **Supernal Wisdom** and understanding to know from which place he was given. Rabbi Isaac said: What is the meaning of "as my likeness"? Holy ones are coming. Rabbi Judah says: From here, as it is written: *And the earth brought forth a living soul*. From them is their portion, and from them to the place of the Sanctuary to be found within it. A "living soul" went out—what is it? It is the power of the **First Man** <note>original: "Adam Kadmon"</note> which includes all. Rabbi Hiyya said: Adam knew Supernal Wisdom more than the ministering angels above. He would gaze at everything and knew and recognized his Master more than all other inhabitants of the world. After he sinned, the springs of wisdom were closed off from him. What is written? *And the Lord God sent him forth from the Garden of Eden to till the ground* <note>Genesis 3:23</note>. Rabbi Abba said: The **First Man** was created **male and female**. This is what is written: *And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness...* <note>Genesis 1:26</note>. They were created as one and separated afterward. And if you say, "What of that which is said, 'He took one'?" This and that are the female, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, partnered with him, and this is **male and female**, and the whole matter is one. Rabbi Yosei said: What is *His strength and song is Yah*? That is to say, in the Garden of Eden they were never separated from one another in rebuke, but in a single will. Dead ones were found, the darkness of them all, and established to find everything and bless everything. This is like the grace of the waters of the springs, and like the waters that *his waters shall not fail* <note>Isaiah 58:11</note>. And regarding this, *He has become my salvation*, as it is written thus, facing the pious one, and they see below. And the fire descended to perform wonders. *Yah*—they waited and merited this, for his light shines, blessings go out in a pair, and the pious one is in that place where the foundation is found. And this is the Sanctuary... what does it say? Not toward the place of the gracious radiance of that side, for there was the perfection of everything in that place. Isaac said: *And He has become my salvation*—this is the **Holy King**. And so it is understood from another verse that is found: *For Yah is my strength and song, and He has become my salvation* <note>Exodus 15:2</note>, for *He has become my salvation* is adjacent to it.

->**Beshalach**<-
->**This is the Holy King**<-

## Main Text (Zohar)

**The Lord is my strength** and song, etc. <note>Exodus 15:2</note> Rabbi Hezekiah opened the discussion and said: It is written in this verse, "At every time the evil is searched out, and if it prevails, a child." <note>This appears to be a homiletic interpretation of a proverb or a specific mystical teaching regarding the timing of judgment and birth.</note> "At every time the evil is searched out"—this refers to the Holy One, blessed be He, of whom it is written: "Your friend and your father’s friend, do not forsake." <note>Proverbs 27:10. The Zohar often identifies "Friend" (Re'a) with the Divine.</note> "And if it prevails, a child"—at the time they listen to your praise, what does the Holy One, blessed be He, say? "For the sake of my brothers and my friends, let me now speak peace within you" <note>Psalm 122:8</note>, for Israel are called "brothers" and "friends" to the Holy One, blessed be He. What is "a child"? Is it a child now? Rather, at the time that a righteous person is born in Israel, behold, He gives to you for your benefit, more than all those who distressed you. Rabbi Judah says: "A child" of the Holy King is more than this "strength" <term>Oz: strength/power</term> for your cleaving, from the strengthening on that side; all of it is "The Lord is my strength and song," a help for me to be crowned with mighty deeds <term>Gevurot: the divine attribute of Judgment/Strength</term> against the sins above.

Rabbi Yose opened and said: How much a person ought to love the Holy One, blessed be He! For there is no service <term>Avodah: worship/service</term> of the Holy One, blessed be He, except through love. And anyone who loves Him and performs His service with love, the Holy One, blessed be He, calls him "Beloved." Thus it is written: "Be strong and let your heart take courage, all you who hope in the Lord" <note>Psalm 31:25</note>, and "your father’s friend do not forsake." And it is written: "Make your foot rare in your friend’s house." <note>Proverbs 25:17</note> Rather, this is a decree—what does this verse proclaim in my world? It is written now: "Your friend and your father’s friend do not forsake"—to serve Him, to be found in Him, and to perform His commandments. "Do not forsake" certainly! And it comes to be said: "Make your foot rare in your friend’s house." That is to say: make your preciousness rare <note>original: "Hokar Yekarcha"</note>, so that he shall not tremble before you, and shall not rule over you, and you shall not perform another [sinful] thought from "your friend’s house." Who is "your friend’s house"? This is the Assembly of Israel <term>Knesset Yisrael: the mystical personification of the Jewish people, often identified with the Shekhinah</term>, who emanated to you your Friend and gave you your son. "A child"—this is the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, to love Him above all, as it is written: "And you shall love the Lord your God." <note>Deuteronomy 6:5</note>

And this love—all of Israel stood at the Sea [and saw] what Ezekiel did not see in prophecy; even the embryos in the wombs saw it! They were all praising and glorifying the Holy One, blessed be He, and all of them were saying: "This is my God and I will glorify Him; my father’s God and I will exalt Him." <note>Exodus 15:2</note> All of these were in blessing. Rabbi Yose said: By the life of the Firmament! What is "and I will exalt Him" <note>original: "Ve-aromemnehu"</note>? It is like one who rises to bless with a voice. He said to him: His commandment is thus required, and it is all one word. "And I will exalt Him" in everything, to include whoever knows how to contemplate the Great Holy Name, for that is the service of the Holy One, blessed be He.

For Rabbi Judah was sitting before Rabbi Shimon and was reading what is written: "The voice of your watchmen! They lift up their voice, together they sing for joy." <note>Isaiah 52:8</note> "The voice of your watchmen"—from those watchmen. These are those who look forward for mercy, that the Holy One, blessed be He, will have mercy to build His House [the Temple]. All of them "together shall sing for joy"—it should have said "a voice," why "together"? Rather, whenever one weeps and hopes <unclear>longs</unclear> over the destruction of the House of the Holy One, blessed be He, etc., because it is written "together they shall sing for joy," he will merit to see it when he merits in joy, "for eye to eye they shall see when the Lord returns to Zion." "For eye to eye they shall see when the Lord returns to Zion"—it should have said "at the goodness of the Lord to Zion," but it is "at the Lord's return to Zion" certainly.

Come and see: at the time that Jerusalem below was destroyed and the Assembly of Israel was expelled, the Holy King ascended, as it were, and revealed Himself to her. Because the Assembly of Israel was expelled, now that He is revealed, He raises her up to Him. When the Assembly of Israel returns to her place, then the Holy King will sit on His throne to unite one with one, and this is: "For eye to eye they shall see when the Lord returns to Zion." And then Israel is destined to say: "This is my God and I will glorify Him." And it is written: "This is the Lord; we have waited for Him, let us be glad and rejoice in His salvation." <note>Isaiah 25:9</note>

---

**The Lord** is a man of war, the Lord is His name. <note>Exodus 15:3</note> Rabbi Abba opened: "Therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of the Lord: Eth and Heb in Suphah, and the valleys of Arnon." <note>Numbers 21:14</note> How much we must look into the words of the Torah! How much we must listen to every word! For you have no word in the Torah that is not hinted at in the Supreme Holy Name, and you have no word in the Torah that does not contain many secrets <term>Razin: mysteries</term>, many reasons, many paths, and many branches, for all is [contained within it].

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on Parashat Beshalach, focusing on the spiritual warfare involved in the Exodus and the Song of the Sea. It transitions from the general concept of "God's wars" to the specific destruction of Pharaoh's chariots.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Beshalach** <note>The name of the Torah portion, meaning "When he sent"</note><-

Here one must look into the verse: **"It is said in the Book of the Wars of the Lord"** <note>Numbers 21:14</note>. Does the Lord truly have a book of wars? Rather, we have learned this from the Throne: all matters below that involve battle are found in the Torah. And if you look for peace, at the end of all the "battles" of the Torah, there is peace and love. However, the battles of the world result in strife and the sword. Thus, it returns to: **"Therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of the Lord, Eth and Heb in Suphah"** <note>Numbers 21:14</note>. This means: to the Holy One, Blessed be He, at the end <note>original: "be-sophah" - a play on the word "Suphah" (storm) and "Soph" (end)</note>. You have no wisdom or peace except from this side that strikes at the crowns. Regarding **"It is said in the Book of the Wars of the Lord,"** this refers to the Law of the Wars of the Lord. From here we derive the counting: the spirit of the world, the voice. The Holy One, Blessed be He, has a place to investigate the dust, as it is said, which hovers over the dust of the Lord. All the matters and mighty deeds <term>Gevurot: Divine judgments or displays of power</term> that the Holy One, Blessed be He, performed are suspended in that place and emerge from it. **"Eth and Heb in Suphah"** refers to war. Rather, all those matters and all those mighty deeds that the Holy One, Blessed be He, performed are suspended in that dust. And when the Holy One, Blessed be He, wages His battles in that place, it is "at the end" <note>Suphah</note> of the levels and investigations, and through it, everything reaches the highest elevation. "In Suphah" means at the end of the levels it is found. In "Suphah" there is a "Soph" (end), to call to those who are the end of all levels. **"And the streams of Arnon"** <note>Numbers 21:14</note> refers to the types of all those who are found and inherited from that high place of investigation and Arnon. Life and Arnon are the supernal pair of love that are never separated, as it is said: "And a river went out of Eden." And in every rain, its leaves and branches are prepared to benefit His battles in every place, to kindle forces and mighty deeds, and to seal the precious dominion of all. Come and see: when the mighty deeds and battles are awakened for the Holy One, Blessed be He, how many pure weavers <note>angelic forces</note> are awakened on every side! Then there are the points of spears and swords, and the mighty deeds are awakened, and the place of the giant is blotted out. All the revelations rise and descend, and the night-spirits and the dominion in the sea are silenced on every side. Blessed is the battle, the strength of the vessels of the armories of life, of spears and swords; then the nine stars are strengthened. The Holy One, Blessed be He, participates in His appointments; the Lord is for the grace of the Holy King, and He watches over the battle for them. Then it is written: **"The Lord is a man of war"** <note>Exodus 15:3</note>. From here, there is grace for the time, and the life of the frost emerges from the mountains of battle to grace the guilty who struck the opening. They are suspended for the grace of the life of truth, and through them His words are explained. And as for what is said: **"The Lord is a man of war, the Lord is His name"**—since it is written **"The Lord is a man of war,"** do I not know that **"the Lord is His name"**? Rather, it is as it is written: **"The Lord rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah sulfur and fire from the Lord out of heaven"** <note>Genesis 19:24</note>. Everything is suspended in this; all of them are His names... and a sword is established for Him. And because of this, by the will of the Holy One, Blessed be He, battle is awakened in the upper and lower worlds, and they are uprooted from their wanderings as we have established. And in the time to come, the right hand of the Holy One, Blessed be He, will rest a supernal and powerful battle upon the nations in order to honor His name, for it is written "The Lord," and all of them are for the sake of the Holy One as in the day He fights in the day of battle. And it is written: **"Thus I will magnify Myself and sanctify Myself and make Myself known"** etc. <note>Ezekiel 38:23</note>.

## **Chariots**
**"Pharaoh’s chariots and his host He cast into the sea"** <note>Exodus 15:4</note>. When the Holy One, Blessed be He, awakens battle, then the upper levels and the lower levels below are awakened, and then **"Pharaoh’s chariots and his host He cast into the sea."** Rabbi Yehuda opened and said: **"Salvation is far from the wicked"** <note>Psalms 119:155</note> etc. By the will [of God], when the orphaned Israel passed through, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to the angel appointed over the sea: "Divide your waters." He said to Him: "Why?" He said to him: "Because My children are passing through you." He said to him: "The redemption that was received, spread forces and forces." He said to him: "For this I made the sea when I fled." What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, do? He awakened His might and the waters were shriveled. This is what is written: **"Is not salvation far from the wicked?"** Rather, kill all of them, the males, and the crown banned them... the crown was poured out upon them, this is **"Pharaoh’s chariots and his host He cast into the sea."** Rabbi Eleazar said: Come and see how many chariots <term>Rethichin: Aramaic for Divine structures or chariots</term> the Holy One, Blessed be He, made above, how many portions, how many armies, and all of them are bound together.

It also begins a commentary on the Song of the Sea, describing the metaphysical process by which God subdued the sea and destroyed Pharaoh's forces.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on Parashat Beshalach (Exodus), specifically focusing on the Song of the Sea. ## Main Text (Zohar)

These are bound one to another, and from them all the celestial chariots <note>original: *ratichin* — refers to the Divine Chariot or Merkabah structures</note> learned to be bound together, level upon level. From the "Left Side" <note>The side of Judgment or Severity in Kabbalistic thought</note> the holy chariots are awakened and ascend, and all are known levels above. Through them, the throne of Pharaoh was arranged—which is a specific level that the Holy One, Blessed be He, killed. He broke his level from within a powerful thousand, placing his rank under His dominion. Many chariots and many hosts stand below that level; some are attached to this side, and some are attached to the Kingdom Above. Some are attached to these four thrones <note>Zohar reference: page 86</note> as has been stated, and all were delivered into His hand. Then, the Kingdom Above cast them down to drive them from their levels. When they were broken above, all those below were likewise broken and destroyed like the lower sea, as it is written:
> Pharaoh’s chariots and his host He cast into the sea. <note>Exodus 15:4</note>

The word "sea" is stated plainly, and it is spoken of in the language of nature as the "Reed Sea" <note>Red Sea</note>. Afterward, the verse divides them, saying: "the horse and his rider He has thrown into the sea." "Sea" is stated plainly twice, and this one corresponds to those, just as it is patterned above. All were delivered to be broken and moved, these and those. Come and see: it is said that Pharaoh knew and recognized all ten signs <note>plagues</note> that the Holy One, Blessed be He, performed in Egypt. These ten sections are included one within the other, corresponding to the Ten Utterances <note>The ten creative words by which the world was made</note> by which the Holy One, Blessed be He, is called. Corresponding to all of them is this one who is strong and cast down, whose dominion was over all, and finally the Glory, as it is written: "Pharaoh’s chariots and his host He cast into the sea," etc. And in the time to come, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to kill the officers, the commanders, <note>Alternative version: some say "the sorcerers"</note> and the governors of Edom <note>Edom represents the final exile/Rome in Jewish mysticism</note>, as it is written:
> Who is this that comes from Edom, with crimsoned garments from Bozrah? <note>Isaiah 63:1</note>

---

->**The Chariot**<-
"Pharaoh’s chariots and his host He cast into the sea." Rabbi Isaac opened his discourse:
> At the sound of His giving a multitude of waters in the heavens, and He causes the vapors to ascend from the ends of the earth; He makes lightnings for the rain, and brings forth the wind out of His treasuries. <note>Jeremiah 10:13</note>

Come and see: we have learned that the Holy One, Blessed be He, made seven firmaments. In every single firmament, stars are fixed and run. Above them are the overseers of *Arabot* <note>The highest of the seven heavens</note>. In every firmament, they have measures: its height is forty thousand measures, and between one firmament and the next is five hundred measures. This *Arabot*—its color is like a smooth, polished glow, and its width is one thousand five hundred measures. From within it, all those firmaments shine. Within them, we have learned, are the celestial arrangements of the firmament, the "feet" of the Holy Living Creatures <note>original: *Chayot HaKodesh* — a high order of angels</note>. Their height is equal to all that is above them. Above them are the ankles of the Creatures, then the legs of the Creatures, the knees of the Creatures, the thighs of the Creatures, the waists of the Creatures, the bodies of the Creatures, their wings, the necks of the Creatures, and their faces. Every part of the Creatures corresponds to seven boundaries, seven palaces <note>original: *heichalin*</note>, and corresponds to the ground of the firmament and the space from firmament to firmament. The measure of them all and their height are crowns, divided into thousands of portions according to the measure of the Holy One, as we have established. Furthermore, there is one firmament above the ankles of the Creature: "And the likeness of a firmament was over the heads of the Creatures." This firmament diminishes like the chariots on the right, and from under its hand, it spreads a curtain <note>Zohar reference: page 120</note>. All the stars of the sea are gathered like the pattern of four crowns in their levels. All are chariots for the approach of the Names; beneath them are hosts, dominions, and "Watchers" <note>a type of angel</note>, level upon level, as it is written:
> This is the sea, great and broad, in which are swarming things without number, living creatures, small and great. <note>Psalms 104:25</note>

And come and see: we have established the matter of the "number" below the three who stand before the Throne, at the beginning of the upper windows. They were written to be broken by the holy, powerful strength, just as Pharaoh’s chariot and his host were crushed.

**Your right hand**, O Lord, is glorious in power. Not after the assistance that spreads light, for the sand stands in its place, arranged on this side, and it ascended in the words of the King's palaces. A man who exerts himself at midnight...

It then describes the vast, structured dimensions of the seven heavens and the angelic "Living Creatures" that support the Divine Throne.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Beshalach**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion: "When he sent."</note>

At the dividing point of midnight, at the hour when the North Wind <note>The North Wind represents the attribute of Gevurah or Judgment</note> is aroused, a longing for the Holy One awakens in the world. She <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note> comes to stand before the King. At that hour, when the moon falls, a single thread of Loving-kindness <note>Chesed</note> stretches over those in need. One who gazes into the firmament sees the radiance of the holy Supernal Knowledge <note>Da'at</note> rising upon it. A person should wrap themselves in this [holiness], for then they are called a "son" who is invited to receive the King’s palace of Sovereignty <note>Malchut</note>. Regarding the hour when the King's breath is upon him, it is written:
> **The Lord is near to all who call upon Him, to all who call upon Him in truth.** <note>Psalms 145:18</note>

What does "in truth" mean? As we have established and learned: **"Truth to Jacob"** <note>Micah 7:20</note>. One must know how to unify the Holy Name <note>original: "Shema Kadisha"</note> in the world as is fitting; this is the service of the Holy King. Whoever knows how to unify the Holy Name is called a "servant of the Lord," and of him it is written:
> **And who is like Your people Israel, a nation that is One on earth?** <note>1 Chronicles 17:21</note>

Regarding this, we have established that any Priest who does not know how to unify the Holy Name properly, his service is not a true service. For everything depends on this: the upper service and the lower service. One must direct the heart and the will <note>original: "Re'uta de-Libba"</note> so that the upper and lower worlds may be blessed. It is written:
> **When you come to appear before My face...** <note>Isaiah 1:12</note>

It should have said "to see My face." However, for anyone who comes to unify the Holy Name but does not intend it with heart and will—neglecting the purpose of blessing the upper and lower worlds—the Mercy of the Lord proclaims of him: "Who requested this from your hand?" The text reads **to see** <note>original: "Lira'ot"</note> My face, but it should be read as **to be seen** <note>original: "Leira'ot"</note>. What does this mean? All those hidden coverings of the King are concealed in the depths of darkness. But those who know how to unify the Holy Name properly break through all those walls of darkness and coverings of the King so that He may be seen and shine upon all. When they are seen and shine, everyone—upper and lower—is blessed. Then blessings are found in all worlds. Thus it is written "to see My face," followed by **who requested *this* from your hand?** <note>Isaiah 1:12</note> What is being discussed here? Whoever comes to unify the Supernal Holy Name must unify it starting from "This" <note>original: "Zot," a term for the Shekhinah</note>, as it is written:
> **With *this* shall Aaron come into the Holy Place.** <note>Leviticus 16:3</note>

This is so that the two may be joined as one: the Righteous One and Righteousness <note>original: "Tzadik v'Tzedek," referring to the union of the Sefirot Yesod and Malchut</note>. In this manner, blessings reside upon them, and they are called "All," as it is written:
> **Happy is the one You choose and bring near to dwell in Your courts.** <note>Psalms 65:5</note>

If a person comes to unify the Holy Name but does not intend it with the heart's desire as is fitting, a prosecutor stands before him and pushes him away, preventing him from beholding the blessings. Come and see: from the side of the Holy One, blessed be He, all lights, all blessings, and all holiness are aroused. Everything is included in Him. As we have said, there is the Right and the Left <note>Chesed and Gevurah</note>. The Left is meant to be included in the Right, for the Right includes everything. When the Right is aroused, the Left is aroused with it, for it is grasped by it and included in it. Come and see: when a person raises his hands in prayer, he directs his fingers upward, as it is said: "And his mouth like a rod..." <unclear>textual variant</unclear>. For everything depends on the Right. It is written that when the Right is raised above, woe to those below, for all assistance and blessings are withdrawn from them. How do we know this? As it is written:
> **He has drawn back His right hand.** <note>Lamentations 2:3; the manuscript notes a scribal error in the citation</note>

What does "He has drawn back His right hand" mean? The translation <note>The Aramaic Targum</note> renders it as "He removed His right hand." Immediately, the enemy consumed. When the Right is withdrawn, the Left remains alone, and then Judgments <note>Dinim</note> rule in the world, Heaven forbid. Because the Right is withdrawn, the Left is ready, and then Judgments are aroused in the world and a foul spirit prevails over all. When the Right is removed, it is as if it is written: "He has drawn back His right hand." Is it possible? <meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Song of the Sea (Exodus 15) from Parashat Beshalach, focusing on the divine "Right Hand" and the transition into the Messianic era. It follows the previous discussion regarding the splitting of the sea and the revelation of divine power.</meta>

# Beshalach

It is written: *The Lord is my strength and song, and He has become my salvation* <note>Exodus 15:2</note>. All those who are righteous before the King are not found to be so except through two sides. First, that blessings do not labor within them as they should at first; and second, that his **female partner** <note>original: "bat zugia," referring to the feminine aspect of the soul or the Divine Presence</note> is found with him, who is etc. It is found that the **Righteous One** <note>term: Tzadik—the foundational divine grade that channels blessing</note> is found in every way more than all else. And in the time to come, it is written: *Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is righteous, and having salvation* <note>Zechariah 9:9</note>. It does not say "a righteous one and a savior," but *righteous and saved is he*. "And saved" is a mystery that has been explained.

**Thy right hand**, O Lord, is glorious in power <note>Exodus 15:6</note>. Why does it say *is glorious* <note>original: "nedari," a plural or intensive form</note>? It should have said "is glory." Rather, at the hour when joy is found to unite with Him, then it is written *is glorious* in two gates, and it is always so because it is found in the **Right Hand** <note>original: "yamina," representing the attribute of Mercy/Chesed</note> and included within it. Come and see, Rabbi Shimon, as we have established, so it is: whenever it is found to be divided, it is in order to receive his female partner with him so they become truly one body. Just so, "Thy right hand" is found to be divided in order to receive the **Left Hand** <note>original: "smala," representing Judgment/Gevurah</note> with it. And so, all is one in One. And because of this, as one, the Holy One, blessed be He, strikes and heals: *Thy right hand, O Lord, dashes the enemy in pieces*. Come and see, this "dashing" was not said only for that time [of the Exodus], but for the time to come, in the days when the **Messiah King** <note>original: "malka mashiacha"</note> shall awaken, as it is written: *Thy right hand, O Lord, shall dash the enemy*. It does not say "dashed" [past tense], but *shall dash* [future tense]. Just as it was written previously: *He hath drawn back His right hand from before the enemy* <note>Lamentations 2:3</note>, at that time [the future], "Thy right hand" shall dash the enemy, and all is one. The deep was before You. It does not say "You stood," but *the deep*. *Thou sentest forth Thy wrath, it consumed them as stubble* <note>Exodus 15:7</note>—all this refers to the time to come. *Thy right hand, O Lord, is glorious in power*—to seize judgment in the world of judgment. *Thy right hand, O Lord, shall dash the enemy*—at the time when the Messiah awakens. *And in the greatness of Thine excellency Thou overthrowest them that rise up against Thee*. This is for the house of our rest and protection. *Thou sentest forth Thy wrath, it consumed them as stubble*—this refers to the **Resurrection of the Dead**, as it is written: *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to reproaches and everlasting abhorrence* <note>Daniel 12:2</note>.

At that time, Rabbi Shimon said: Blessed are those who labor in the world. And who are they? Come and see, nothing remains for the children of the world except those who received the **holy covenant** <note>referring to the sign of circumcision</note> to maintain it in holiness, for they shall inherit the holy standing in those two portions as we have established. He who merits to guard that <term>covenant</term> <note>original: "kayis/kayama"</note> and does not bring it into a place where it is not permitted, is among those who labor and are found in the "Life of the Worlds." From here we learn what is written: *And it shall come to pass, that he that is left in Zion, and he that remaineth in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, even every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem* <note>Isaiah 4:3</note>. This implies that whoever is circumcised in these two levels enters and inherits that covenant as is fitting, and remains within it; of them it is written, *he that is left in Zion and he that remaineth in Jerusalem*. These shall be joined at that time, and then the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to renew the world and rejoice in them. Regarding that time it is written: *Let the glory of the Lord endure for ever; let the Lord rejoice in His works* <note>Psalms 104:31</note>.

Rabbi Hiyya was walking to see Rabbi Elazar, and found him sitting with Rabbi Yose, the son of Rabbi Lakunya, his father-in-law. When he [Rabbi Elazar] raised his head, he saw Rabbi Hiyya and said: *In that day shall the Lord be one, and His name one* <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>, to speak and decree a blessing in the midst of the earth. He said: *Blessed be the Lord of Hosts, saying: Blessed be Egypt My people, and Assyria the work of My hands, and Israel Mine inheritance* <note>Isaiah 19:25</note>. How foolish are the people of the world who do not know and do not look into the words of the **Torah** <note>original: "Oraita"</note>, for the words of the Torah are the way to merit that world, as it is written: *Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace* <note>Proverbs 3:17</note>. "Ways of pleasantness" certainly. It strikes down anger, as it is written: *to cause a blessing to rest on thine house* <note>Ezekiel 44:30</note>. And we have established that because of this, the Torah and its paths come from those hidden longings, and they are paths spread out within it, and therefore *all her paths are peace*. Rabbi Hiyya said: We have learned that at the hour when the Holy One, blessed be He, gave the Torah to Israel, light went forth from that **Throne** <note>original: "kise," the Divine Throne of Glory</note> and the Holy One, blessed be He, prepared Himself within it, and from that Throne, the radiance of all their worlds was watered.

<summary>This page interprets the Song of the Sea as a prophecy of the Messianic era and the Resurrection, emphasizing that the "Right Hand" of God will eventually defeat all enemies. It also stresses the importance of guarding the holy covenant (circumcision) as the key to being "written for life" in the future Jerusalem.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar on the Torah portion Beshalach. It focuses on the celestial ascent of Moses to receive the Torah and the cosmic power of Torah study to subdue the spiritual forces of the nations.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

To all the firmaments and all the crowns. Regarding that time, it is written: "straightforward and broad." <note>A reference to the spiritual expansion of the Temple's influence.</note> This was the case when King Solomon reigned and so on, and all the time that the Sanctuary was built, the Holy One, blessed be He, was adorned with that crown and sat upon His throne and was crowned with His crowns. But from the time the Sanctuary was destroyed, the Holy One, blessed be He, has not been adorned with His crowns. And that anger <note>The divine wrath resulting from the exile</note> is spoken of until it shall be rebuilt.

Rabbi Elazar saw: At the time Moses entered into the midst of the cloud, as it is written: **"And Moses went into the midst of the cloud"** <note>Exodus 24:18</note>, he was already following the Spirit. He was met by a great and mighty angel named Kemuel, who is appointed over twelve thousand messengers. He sought to harm Moses. Moses opened his mouth with the twelve engraved letters of the Holy Name <note>original: "שמא קדישא"</note> which the Holy One, blessed be He, had passed to him, and he became stronger than the angel's strength by many thousands of parasangs <note><term>parasang</term>: an ancient Persian unit of distance, used here to denote vast celestial reaches</note>. Finally, Moses went into the cloud, his eyes flashing like sparks of fire, until he was met by a great and honored angel, even mightier than the first, named Hadarniel. He rises above his fellow angels by one thousand and sixty thousand parasangs, and his voice goes through the firmaments that surround the white glow.

When Moses saw him, he was unable to speak. He sought to throw himself out of the cloud. The Holy One, blessed be He, saw Moses and said: "Is it you who spoke so many words with Me? As it is written, to know the spirit of the Holy Name, and now you have come to this matter and are silent because you fear a single messenger?" When Moses heard the voice of the Holy One, blessed be He, he was strengthened. He opened his mouth with the twenty-two letters of the Supreme Name. When Hadarniel heard the vibration of the Holy Name from the mouth of Moses, he trembled. He approached him and said: "Happy is your portion, Moses, for that which was not granted to the high angels has been granted to you." He then went with him until they reached the mighty fire of a certain angel who is flaming with sparks, the mighty Sandalphon. He rises above his fellows by a distance of five hundred years' journey. He ties the crown of the <term>Pargod</term> <note>The celestial curtain or veil before the Divine Presence</note> which was entrusted to him, and he ties crowns from the prayers of Israel. At the time this crown reaches the head of the Holy King, He receives the prayers of Israel, and all the living creatures <note>original: "חיוון" - the Chayyot, a high order of angels</note> and hosts tremble and they all sing: **"Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place"** <note>Ezekiel 3:12; original: "ברוך יקרא יי' מאתר בית שכינתיה"</note>.

Hadarniel said to Moses: "Moses, I cannot stand with you, lest the mighty fire of Sandalphon consume me." At that moment, Moses was strengthened by the Holy One, blessed be He, who placed him before Him and taught him the Torah. He clothed Moses in that light and splendor of that "anger" <note>referring here to a specific divine radiance</note>, and the face of Moses shone like all the splendors of the firmaments. All the hosts of heaven trembled before him when he descended with the Torah. Once it was found below, the Holy One, blessed be He, took a thousand portions of that radiance back. At that hour, the high angels and all those hosts sought to strike him down when the Holy One, blessed be He, said: **"Go, get thee down; for thy people... have dealt corruptly"** <note>Exodus 32:7</note>. Moses trembled and could not speak until he saw the bride <note>the Torah/Shekhinah</note> and the pleas before the Holy One, blessed be He. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: "Moses, take hold of My throne!" The Holy One, blessed be He, rebuked all those hosts and all those living creatures, and Moses took hold of the two stone tablets and brought them down. This is what is written: **"A wise man scales the city of the mighty and brings down the strength of its confidence"** <note>Proverbs 21:22</note>. From that radiance that remained in him, the face of Moses beamed. And what is written? **"And they were afraid to come nigh him"** <note>Exodus 34:30</note>; they were unable to look at his face because he had ascended from this world.

Rabbi Hiyya said: **"Thy right hand, O Lord, is glorious in power"** <note>Exodus 15:6</note>—this refers to the Torah. **"Thy right hand, O Lord, dasheth in pieces the enemy"**—for there is nothing in the world that breaks the power of the nations who worship stars and constellations <note>original: "עכו"ם" - acronym for star-worshippers</note> except for the time when Israel occupies itself with the Torah. For as long as Israel occupies itself with the Torah, the power and strength of the idolaters is broken. Therefore, the Torah is called "Strength" <note>original: "עז" - Oz</note>, as it says: **"The Lord will give strength unto His people"** <note>Psalms 29:11</note>. But when Israel does not occupy itself with the Torah, the power of the idolaters is strengthened, and they rule over them and decree decrees upon them that they cannot withstand, and because of this, the children of Israel were exiled and scattered among the nations, etc.

<summary>This page describes Moses' dramatic ascent to heaven, where he overcomes the terrifying angels Kemuel, Hadarniel, and Sandalphon using the power of the Holy Name. It concludes by explaining that the Torah is the "strength" of Israel, and its study is the only protection against the dominance of foreign nations.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Zoharic commentary on the Torah portion Beshalach, specifically focusing on the mystical interpretations of the Song of the Sea (Exodus 15). ## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Beshalach** <-
<note>Beshalach: "When he sent," the name of the Torah portion covering the Exodus and the parting of the Sea.</note>

On what basis should they be forgiven, etc. And the Lord will have compassion <note>I believe it should read: "will have pity"</note> upon those who occupy themselves with the Torah <note>original: "A.T." - an abbreviation for *Oraitah*, the Aramaic word for Torah</note>. For as long as Israel occupies itself with the Torah, the strength and power of all the idol-worshipping nations will be broken before them, and the Lord will grant them life. Rabbi Elazar said: Blessed is he who, at all times, ensures the Holy One, blessed be He, is heard in his house, in gatherings, and in the houses of study, etc. As we have learned:
> **"The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau"** <note>Genesis 27:22. A classic rabbinic motif: when the "voice" of Jacob is heard in prayer and study, the "hands" of Esau (military power) cannot prevail.</note> 
And this we have already established.

**"And in the greatness of Your majesty, You overthrow those who rise against You"** <note>Exodus 15:7</note>. Rabbi Hezekiah opened:
> **"Why, O Lord, do You stand far off? Why do You hide Yourself in times of trouble?"** <note>Psalms 10:1</note>
At the time when the sins of the world cause it, the Holy One, blessed be He, ascends on high and hides His various colors <note>A mystical reference to the Divine Attributes or *Sefirot* withdrawing</note>, and the springs of judgment descend upon them. Even <note>I believe it should read: "Also"</note> because He <note>I believe it should read: "He is"</note> ascends higher and higher, and repentance is withheld from them; then it is written: "And in the greatness of Your majesty, You overthrow those who rise against You." Rabbi Isaac said: This verse refers to the time when the Holy One, blessed be He, clothes Himself in majesty against the nations who gather against Him, as it is written:
> **"Why do the nations rage... against the Lord and against His anointed"** <note>cf. Psalms 2:1-2</note> 
And three times those seventy chieftains <note>The seventy celestial patron angels of the seventy nations</note> from every side are destined to gather at that time, when the whole world comes to wage war against Jerusalem, the holy city, and to take counsel against the Holy One, blessed be He. And what do they say? "Let us attack the Patron first, and afterward His people and His Temple." At that time, the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to laugh at them, as it is written:
> **"He who sits in the heavens laughs; the Lord mocks them"** <note>Psalms 2:4</note> 
At that time, the Holy One, blessed be He, will cast His majesty upon them and they will be destroyed from the world, as it is written:
> **"And this shall be the plague wherewith the Lord will smite all the peoples that have warred against Jerusalem: their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet"** <note>Zechariah 14:12</note> 
Rabbi Hiyya said in the name of Rav Yosef: In every single age, the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to bring back to life all those kings who caused suffering to Jerusalem—Sihon, Og, Sennacherib, and all those kings of the nations who destroyed His House—and to curse them first. Then the rest of the nations will gather with them, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to take vengeance upon them for the destruction and the rebellions of Jerusalem. Thus it returns to: "And this shall be the plague wherewith the Lord will smite all the peoples that have warred against Jerusalem." It does not say "who *will* war," but "who *have warred*" <note>The Zohar notes the past tense, suggesting that even ancient enemies will be resurrected to face final judgment</note>. Then it is written: "And in the greatness of Your majesty, You overthrow those who rise against You"—and this refers to the time to come, which the Assembly of Israel praises; this is the departure toward the World to Come.

**"And with the blast of Your nostrils the waters were piled up"** <note>Exodus 15:8</note>. At that time, and because of this, there was song <note>or: "life"</note> at that time, and for the time of the King Messiah, and for the time of Gog and Magog, and for the time of the World to Come, which gives life to the dwelling of all worlds.

**"The enemy said: 'I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoil'"** <note>Exodus 15:9</note>. He said: See, this refers to that appointed minister <note>The celestial prince of Egypt or the Accuser</note> who snorted when authority was given to him over Israel; he thought they would be destroyed under his rule. But the Holy One, blessed be He, led the mountains of the world <note>The Patriarchs</note> to be shields for them. And do not say this of him alone, but of all those great ministers appointed over every nation: when permission and authority are given to them over Israel, they all become angry and seek to destroy Israel under them. And because of this, those nations under their authority—those who are appointed—all decree to plunder them when the Holy One, blessed be He, has mercy on them. And when the time came that none could be found to stand against Him, it was said: "Who is like You among the mighty, O Lord?" He said: There is a certain tree <note>A metaphor for the Divine structure or the Tree of Life</note>... <note>The text here becomes highly metaphorical, describing the "seventy branches" (nations) sucking from the roots, and how they seek to destroy the "root" (Israel) when their time of dominion arrives, but the Holy One, blessed be He, sees and takes action.</note>

<meta>This page continues the Zohar’s commentary on the Torah portion Beshalach (Exodus 13:17–17:16). The previous discussion likely focused on the Song at the Sea. Here, the text transitions from the praise "Who is like You among the gods" to a philosophical and mystical inquiry into the value of human actions, drawing heavily on Ecclesiastes.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The portion of that side <note>referring to the "Other Side" or the forces of impurity</note> is a breath of a portion that they seek to take and receive as a portion among all those seventy <note>The 70 nations/guardian angels</note>... to take a portion for the seventy branches. And regarding this, it is written: **"Who is like You among the gods, O Lord?"** <note>Exodus 15:11</note>. What is this "portion"? It is as it is said <note>original: "כמה דאת אמר"</note>, "For they sacrificed to the dead," <note>referring to idols</note> which is the portion of those who worship a breath that fails its children. Therefore, regarding this portion: **"Who is like You"** who can act as You act, and have mercy upon all? **"Who is like You"** among all those extensions of the portion where the guilty rule... but You do not wish to perform a complete destruction. **"Who is like You, majestic in holiness"** <note>Exodus 15:11</note>. In that supernal Holiness which is called "Holy." In the literal Holy, which is called the Throne of the Lord, the Anger of the Lord. And we have established these words.

---

**"Who is like You among the gods, O Lord?"** Rabbi Yose opened his discourse:
> "I have seen all the deeds that are done under the sun, and behold, all is vanity and a chasing after wind." <note>Ecclesiastes 1:14</note>

King Solomon, who possessed wisdom greater than all the people of the world, how could he say that all deeds are vanity and a chasing after wind? Even the act of <term>Charity</term> <note>Hebrew: Tzedakah; also implies "righteousness"</note>?
For behold, it is written:
> "And the work of righteousness [Tzedakah] shall be peace." <note>Isaiah 32:17</note>

Rather, they have established: "All the deeds that are done **under the sun**" is what is written. This excludes the act of Charity, which is **above the sun**. "And behold, all is vanity [breath] and a chasing after wind"—what is this speaking of? If you say "all," it is as we have established, that they exist in the spirit of wisdom, all is a "breath" <note>The Hebrew word 'Hevel' means both vanity and breath/vapor</note> that comprises the seven "vanities" of Ecclesiastes, which are the supernal vessels. But if you say it is as written, "all is vanity and a chasing after wind," this matter does not apply to what is "under the sun." Rather, thus they established it, and so it is:

Come and see: at the time when deeds are proper below, and a person exerts himself in the service of the Holy King, that deed creates a force that is made from it above. There is no "breath" <note>Hevel</note> that does not have a voice, which ascends and is crowned above, becoming an advocate before the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: "קודשא בריך הוא"</note>. But all those deeds that a person exerts himself in which are not for the service of the Holy One and His commandments—the "breath" created from them goes and wanders through the world. And when the soul of that person departs, that "breath" rolls him through the world like a stone in a sling, as it is written <note>original: "כמה דכתיב"</note>:
> "And the soul of your enemies, He shall sling it out as from the hollow of a sling." <note>1 Samuel 25:29</note>

What is "He shall sling it"? It is that "breath" <note>Hevel</note> that leads him through the world. Therefore, all things that are done "under the sun" which are not for the service of the Holy One, a "breath" is made from them that breaks the spirit... a vanity and a chasing after wind. But that matter which is for the service of his Master, this is called "above the sun," and from it is made a **Holy Breath**. This is the seed that a person sows in that world, and what is its name? **Charity** <note>Tzedakah</note>, as it is written:
> "Sow for yourselves for righteousness [Tzedakah]." <note>Hosea 10:12</note>

This [Charity] leads the person when his soul departs from him, and brings it up to the place of supernal Glory, to be awakened in the Light of Life. This is what is written:
> "And your righteousness [Tzedakah] shall go before you." <note>Isaiah 58:8</note>

Because it is necessary to raise you from place to place, as it is written: **"The glory of the Lord shall gather you."** All those souls of that Holy Breath, that portion of the "Glory of the Lord" leads them, gathering them within it, and they are illuminated by it. This is "The glory of the Lord shall gather you," and it is not called a "chasing after wind" like that other vanity. Happy are the righteous, for all their deeds are "above the sun," and they sow deeds that are the seed of Charity to merit the World to Come. And regarding this, it is written:
> "But unto you that fear My name shall the sun of righteousness [Tzedakah] arise." <note>Malachi 3:20</note>

Rabbi Shimon said: Come and see, at first when the Holy Temple was built below, it was built only with Judgment and Wrath, as it is written:
> "For this city has been to Me as a provocation of My anger and My fury." <note>Jeremiah 32:31</note>

And so on, because the side of Wrath dwelt there. But in the time to come, the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to build it and establish it on another, higher level called **Charity** <note>Tzedakah</note>, as it is written: **"In righteousness [Tzedakah] shall you be established."** Because of this, it shall endure forever.

## Main Text (Zohar)

And regarding this it is written: **Out of the depths I called to the Lord** <note>Psalm 118:5; original: "Min ha-metzar karati Yah"</note>. This teaches that one must call from a narrow place of distress, representing the masculine side, like the breath of a spirit that does not swerve to the right or the left. In the Sanctuary, the voice could not dwell in this way, for the masculine aspect is like the sound of the Shofar, which binds everything together, emerging from a narrow and weak place to pierce the heavens and ascend, just as the awakening of the spirit ascends above. Regarding this it is written that Isaac rested and took to himself like a crack in the milk <note>This is a highly cryptic metaphorical passage regarding the "wine" of Isaac—the attribute of Gevurah or Judgment—and how it is sweetened</note>. Isaac placed wine within it, such as was not found in all the world, and gave of this verse to them; and for this reason, he pushed it like a crack to the place where it was revealed and stood.

**It was taught** in a Baraita: Rabbi Isaac said, all the service of the "outer" ones <note>referring to the lower spiritual realms or the nations</note> is such that they merit to say this Song as in this world. For the Holy One, blessed be He, granted them the merit to say it in the form of a hidden protection that was not built with crowns. But the two holy lower letters <note>referring to the final letters of the Divine Name YHVH</note> are engraved and crowned with severity, and all of them are marked with the Holy Name, and all of them are the inner dimensions of the Holy Name. And from where does this awakening come? 

Rabbi Shimon said: At that moment when Israel stood by the sea and sang the Song, the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, viewed as the feminine aspect of God</note> was revealed with all Her hosts and words, so that they might know Her sovereignty—for He performed all those miracles and mighty deeds for them. Each and every person knew and perceived what the other prophets of the world did not know or perceive. For if you were to say they did not know or attach themselves to the Supernal Wisdom through this Song, come and see: they all perceived through Wisdom and knew the matters they spoke. If it were not so, how could they speak words of Wisdom without making a single error? And when it says "This is my God" <note>Exodus 15:2</note>, it refers to the Holy One, blessed be He, the King of all. They all spoke with a single insight, the Holy Spirit in the mouth of each and every one, and the words were spoken as if emerging from a single mouth. Even the embryos in their mothers' wombs sang the Song together, and they all saw what the prophet Ezekiel never saw. Because of this, they were all looking and seeing eye to eye. 

And when they finished the words, they were all sweetened as if by <term>pure clarity</term> <note>original: "kasofia," likely from the Greek 'sophia' (wisdom) or 'sappheiros' (sapphire/clarity)</note>, and they remained hanging there to look and perceive. He concealed His glory outside in the wilderness. Then, out of the greatness of that desire and will to perceive, they moved. And we have learned: the Holy One, blessed be He, is called "Torah." There is no water but Torah, and no Torah but the Holy One, blessed be He.

They were not sweetened with that initial clarity. Not only that, but the powers of judgment came to prosecute them. <meta>This page continues the commentary on the Exodus narrative, specifically the events at Marah (Exodus 15:25-26). It focuses on the mystical transformation of the bitter waters and the spiritual requirements for the Israelites to receive the Divine Presence.</meta>

->**Beshalach**<-
<note>original: "בשלח" - The name of the Torah portion, meaning "When he sent."</note>

"And He showed him a tree" <note>Exodus 15:25</note>. This refers to the Torah, as it is written: "It is a **tree of life** to those who hold fast to it" <note>Proverbs 3:18</note>. And there is no "Torah" other than the Holy One, Blessed be He. Rabbi Abba said: This "tree" is indeed the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: "For man is a tree of the field" <note>Deuteronomy 20:19</note>—this is certainly so. This refers to the "Man of the Holy Apple Orchard" <note>A Kabbalistic metaphor for the Sefirah of Tiferet or the Divine Countenance</note>. When the radiance of the glory of the **Kingdom** <term>Malchut: the tenth Sefirah, representing the Divine Presence in the world</term> was revealed upon them, then "he cast it into the waters, and the waters were made sweet." What is the meaning of "the waters were made sweet"? It means that the **Accuser** <term>Katigora: the spiritual force of judgment or prosecution</term> was turned into an **Advocate** <term>Sanigora: the spiritual force of defense and mercy</term>.

Rabbi Abba said: Come and see! At first, all the eyes of Israel were looking to be sustained by the Holy One, Blessed be He, but they did not "eat" <note>experience the Divine</note> as was proper. What was the reason? Because they were circumcised, but the **holy impression** <term>Reshima Kadisha: the spiritual mark of the covenant of circumcision</term> had not yet been fully revealed <note>referring to the transition from the initial cut to the full uncovering/healing required for spiritual maturity</note>. Once they arrived here, "there He made for them a statute and an ordinance" <note>Exodus 15:25</note>. There, Israel ascended into two holy portions in the same manner that their "impression" was revealed, and these are called "statute" and "ordinance." "Statute" <note>Chok</note> is as you say: "She gives food to her household and a **statute** <note>allotted portion</note> to her maidens" <note>Proverbs 31:15</note>. "Ordinance" <note>Mishpat</note> is as it is said: "An **ordinance** for the God of Jacob" <note>Psalms 81:5</note>. "And there He tested them"—in that holy place, for everything is "a statute for Israel." In the book of Rav Yeba the Elder, he spoke a word regarding that holy staff.

**"And he said:** If you will diligently heed the voice of the Lord your God." What is the meaning of "And he said"? This word was written first. Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, spoke it. Rabbi Hezekiah said: "Heed" <note>Shamoa</note> refers to water in a general sense. What does "water in a general sense" mean? As it is written: "But he who heeds counsel is wise" <note>Proverbs 12:15</note>. Rabbi Eleazar said: The word "voice" is not written here <note>in the first part of the phrase</note>. Rabbi Yose said: "Diligently heed" <note>Shemoa Tishma</note> is written because it says "And he cried out to the Lord, and the Lord showed him a tree." The literal meaning of the verse implies "And He said" and "And He heard"—who spoke the word? "To the voice of the Lord your God." It should have said "To *My* voice." Rather, it refers to that specific **Voice** <note>The Sefirah of Tiferet</note> that entered into him. 

Rabbi Abba said: After the holy impression was revealed in them, they entered into two holy portions as we have said. And once they entered these two, they ascended through two other portions so that when they look upon these other two matters, they shall be joined as one and not be separated. Because of this, they all reach until the **Holy Kingdom** <note>Malchut</note>. And the end of the verse makes the matter heard, as it is written: "And he said: If you will diligently heed." "And he said" refers to the **Holy Kingdom**. And what does it say? "If you will diligently heed the voice of the Lord your God"—this is the **Assembly of Israel** <term>Knesset Yisrael: the spiritual archetype of the Jewish people, often identified with the Shekhinah</term>. "And do what is right in His eyes"—this is the **Righteous One** <term>Tzadik: the Sefirah of Yesod, the foundation</term>. "And give ear to His commandments"—this refers to **Endurance and Splendor** <term>Netzach and Hod: the seventh and eighth Sefirot</term>. "And keep all His statutes"—this is **Foundation** <term>Yesod</term> <note>Some versions say Hod</note>. Since they have entered all of these, they have reached the **Holy Kingdom**. 

Afterward, what is written? "None of the diseases which I put upon Egypt will I put upon you, for I am the Lord your healer." For "I" <note>Ani</note> is the **Holy Kingdom**. This is all derived from what is written: "To the voice." The holy impression rises from it until the **Supreme Holy Kingdom**. What does this imply? It implies those two <note>Netzach and Hod</note> in which the "seed" is gathered, and from there holiness descends to the dwellings... <unclear>damaged/obscure text regarding the sun and angels</unclear>... and because of this they were sanctified like the angels of the Supreme Kingdom through the Lord, and He shall mend it for him. Therefore, since they entered into these two and were later bound to the other two, they reached the **Holy Kingdom**. 

Rabbi Isaac said: Whoever merits the **Righteous One** <note>Yesod</note> merits the **Assembly** <note>Malchut</note> and **Splendor** <note>Hod</note>. These are the three through which the Assembly of Israel is blessed. And whoever merits them merits the **Holy Kingdom**. They all enter into the Master of the Universe... <note>The text here uses complex metaphors of "knots," "saddles," and "ships" to describe the structural integrity of the Sefirot</note>. When the "knot" of the **Righteous One** is guarded, the "ship" <note>Malchut</note> is protected. The "knot" of **Endurance** <note>Netzach</note> is the protection of the "eye." The "knot" of **Splendor** <note>Hod</note> is the protection of the "vessel." Therefore, "to the voice of the Lord your God" is the **Assembly of Israel**. How meritorious are the Israelites to receive the face of the **Divine Presence** <term>Shekhinah</term> by guarding themselves from the [five] impurities. Therefore we have learned: "Do not approach to uncover her nakedness" <note>Leviticus 18:6</note>. What is "to uncover her nakedness"? This refers to the **Assembly of Israel**, and to this they cling, and other matters are prepared for the Assembly of Israel to be bound to them. And what of the "statutes"? "And do what is right in His eyes"—this is the **Righteous One**, as it is written: "The eyes of the Lord are toward the **righteous**" <note>Psalms 34:16</note>, to be guarded from the four...

## Main Text (Zohar)

And we have already established these matters, as it is said: *Attach me, I pray you, to the priestly office* <note>original: "וספחתני נא" from 1 Samuel 2:36</note>. The Torah is the gift of your mouth for the favor of the **Righteous One** <note>The sefirah of Yesod</note>, to cling to the gateway and the perfection of all things, so that he is found not to be false within it. For the conclusion is not found where falsehood dwells, as it is written: *and his strength had not fled* <note>Deuteronomy 34:7; the Zohar links "strength" (koach) to spiritual vitality</note>. No transgression shall be found, for he stands upon the Living Mountain of his dwellings, as it is written: *For you shall worship no other god.* And observe every commandment with majesty <note>Hod</note>, to be guarded from the "stranger" and from sickness, just as we have learned.

Rabbi Judah said: What is the meaning of the verse, *Gird your sword upon your thigh, O mighty one, your glory and your majesty*? <note>Psalm 45:4</note> Rather, anyone who arms himself with the secret signs and prepares the blade of the sword—the mighty **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence</note>—against those who oppose him "upon the thigh." What does "upon the thigh" mean? That it is not distant, but close; everything is a swift power, "thigh under my thighs." No, *Gird your sword* is a mystery: prepare your "thigh" to be a companion to His "sword upon your thigh," referring to that Holy Beloved of the **Right Side** <note>The attribute of Mercy/Chesed</note>. Then it becomes a crown for him, and then "Might" <note>Gevurah</note> and "Strength" are searched out and encompass him like garments. And we see his garment is like a hard mountain and victory <note>Netzach</note>, as it is written: *You are clothed in glory and majesty.* <note>Psalm 104:1</note> So too here: *Your glory and your majesty.* And then a man may cling to the **Holy King** as is fitting. From this point forward, anyone who gives pleasure to another is like one who brings an offering; *I will put none of these diseases upon you, for I am the Lord who heals you.* And because of this, they lacked that very word which He gave and sprinkled upon them and no more; the Torah was not yet settled within them until it was written: *There He made for them a statute and an ordinance,* and immediately, *And He said: If you will diligently listen...*

Come and see: when the **Holy One, Blessed Be He**, desired to lead Israel toward the Torah, He drew them with many matters, with many "sufferings" <note>original: "מסכני" (miskeni) - poverty or trials</note> of fatherhood, like a father who draws his son to the schoolhouse. And come and see: the Holy One, Blessed Be He, did not want to give them the Torah until they drew near explicitly. And how much did we read in this... <margin>From here we see: one who has no bread</margin> ...as it was said. Rabbi Judah said: Israel did not arrive at Mount Sinai until they entered into the portion of the **Righteous One** <note>Tzadik/Yesod</note> and merited it. From where do we know this? As it is written: *On this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai*—"this day" specifically. And it is written elsewhere: *And it shall be said on that day: Behold, this is our God; we have waited for Him...*

**And He said** etc. Is it possible that the staff of a commoner <note>original: "mamzer"</note> could reach the heights of the Heavenly Family? <note>original: "Pamalia"</note> Rabbi Judah opened and said: *Blessed is he who considers the poor; the Lord will deliver him in the day of evil.* <note>Psalm 41:2</note> This verse was established for the time when a man lies ill, when his sickness takes hold of him. The King’s side is at his head... his feet are in chains... many illnesses surround him... all of them in the image of those who dwell in the window, all of them impure. At that time, his deeds are made into advocates <note>term: "epitropos" - a legal guardian or advocate</note> to seek merit before the King. At that hour, blessed is the portion of the man who comes to him and sees how to teach him to be drawn away from **Judgment** <note>Din</note>. The congregation returns to *consider the poor.* And can he really grant him merit? To teach him what? To be found before his Master... <margin>explained in Beshalach</margin> ...to pass as an advocate for him above. What is the grace? *In the day of evil, the Lord will deliver him.* For the "one who considers the poor" does not realize how much power a poor man has before the Holy One, Blessed Be He.

Rabbi Hiyya said: The strength of this verse is as it is written: *For the Lord hears the needy...* <note>Psalm 69:34</note> He hears the needy and no other? Rabbi Shimon said: Because they are closer to the King, as it is written: *A broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.* <note>Psalm 51:19</note> And you have no one in the world with such a broken heart as the poor man. Furthermore, Rabbi Shimon said: Come and see, all the people of the world appear before the Holy One, Blessed Be He, with body and soul, but the poor man appears only with the **soul** <note>Nefesh</note> alone, and the Holy One, Blessed Be He, is closer to the soul than to the body. The poor man is unique in his "adornments"... Rabbi Yose... was not looking at him, and he was bold and strong...

## Beshalach

->**Beshalach**<-

Once, a great weakness overcame Rabbi Yose. He heard a voice saying: "This soul is ascending, this soul is flying toward Him, for his days are not yet fulfilled. Woe to the inhabitants of the city <note>original: "kaso matya"</note> among whom no one is found who sits at the table <note>term: "kefatora" - a table or seat of honor</note> before Him." Rabbi Yose arose and placed water in his mouth, along with grains of a small measure <note>note: the text suggests a very small amount of food, perhaps bran or a husk</note>. He humbled himself, his face trembled, and his spirit returned to him. After he had rested and his spirit was restored, Rabbi Yose said: "My soul departed from my nostrils and reached before the Throne of the King. It was not yet time to be crowned there, but the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to grant you merit and to proclaim concerning you: 'Rabbi Yose is destined to have his spirit ascend and to be strengthened as one of the Holy Companions <note>term: "Chavrayya" - the inner circle of Zoharic sages</note> who are destined to be crowned on the earth.' And for this, three thrones were prepared for you and your companions." From that time on, they looked upon him as one who had returned from the dead.

Furthermore, another poor man passed before Rabbi Isaac, holding half a silver coin <note>original: "ma'ah"</note> in his hand. He said to Rabbi Isaac: "Have pity on me, and on my heart, and on my daughters with a piece of bread." He replied: "How can I have pity? A dry hunger is upon me, and I have nothing with me but half a coin." The man said to him: "With this, I will find the other half to sustain myself and my household." He embraced him and kissed him. 

Later, he was shown in a dream that he was passing by the shore of the Great Sea and they wished to cast him into the depths. He saw Rabbi Shimon extending his hands toward him and toward the two pieces of the poor man's coin; he embraced them and kissed the hands of Rabbi Shimon and was saved. When he awoke, he repeated the verse: "He who considers the poor, the Lord will deliver him in the day of evil." <note>Psalms 41:2</note>

And come and see: every single day, the dew drips from the **Holy Ancient One** <note>term: "Atika Kadisha" - the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note> to the **Small Face** <note>term: "Zeir Anpin" - the manifest aspect of God</note>, and all the **Holy Apple Fields** <note>note: a mystical metaphor for the Shekhinah or the community of Israel</note> are blessed. From that side which is not drawn down to those below, the holy angels are nourished, each according to his capacity for eating. This is what is written:
> **"Man ate the bread of the mighty; He sent them provision to the full."** <note>Psalms 78:25</note>

When Rabbi Shimon would bless, many members of the synagogue would grow faint at that time. The supernal angels are the "Companions" who labor in the **Torah** <note>original: "Oraita"</note> day and night. And would it enter your mind that this is actual physical food? No. Rather, it is like that very food, but doubled in its spiritual essence. Come and see: when Israel ascended and cleaved to the Holy King, the children of the chambers of the Holy Chariot, they then merited to eat from this other supernal food, even more so than at first. When Israel went out of Egypt, they ascended in that investigation of the Manna and they opened etc., and they ascended to eat from that other supernal food, higher than the highest, as it is written:
> **"Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you."** <note>Exodus 16:4</note>

Literally "from heaven." And from that time, Israel merited to find sustenance from this place. The Companions who labor in the Torah are nourished from this supernal source. As it is written:
> **"Wisdom preserves the life of him who has it."** <note>Ecclesiastes 7:12</note>

This is even more sublime. Rabbi Eleazar said to him: "If so, why is the sickness in their mouths greater than that of other people? It should be more substantial, providing strength to be seen and found!" He replied to him: "It is a sickness of longing." Come and see: all the nourishment of the people of the world comes from above. That nourishment which comes from heaven and earth is the nourishment of the whole world, and it is coarse and heavy. But the nourishment that comes from further above is the nourishment that is hidden and refined, coming from the place of Judgment; it is a more subtle nourishment. The nourishment found for Israel at that time from the supernal world was a most subtle nourishment that enters the innermost parts more than anything else and spreads through the body. 

The most supernal nourishment of all is the nourishment of the Companions who labor in the Torah, for they eat the **nourishment of the spirit and the soul** <note>original: "mazuna de-rucha ve-nishmata"</note> and do not eat the nourishment of the body at all. This is from the most precious supernal place called **Wisdom** <note>term: "Chokhmah"</note>. Because of this, the bodies of the Companions are weaker than other people, for they do not eat the food of the body at all, but rather the food of the spirit and soul from that distant, supernal, and precious place.

...most precious of all. And in repentance, that nourishment is the most subtle of the subtle, more than anything else. Fortunate is their portion, as it is written: **"Wisdom preserves the life of its possessor"** <note>Ecclesiastes 7:12</note>. Fortunate is the portion of the body that is able to be nourished by the nourishment of the soul. Rabbi Elazar said to him: "Certainly it is so; all those who find these types of nourishment are meritorious." The first type of nourishment is the nourishment of the whole world, which is below the heavens and the earth, and it is the nourishment for everyone. "Doing kindness" implies that through his merit, he completes and brings <term>Chesed</term> <note>Loving-kindness</note> to completion, and then it becomes Mercy.

A nourishment higher than these is the supreme and precious nourishment from the place where it is engraved; it is the most subtle of all, and it is the ultimate nourishment for the sick. This is what is written: **"The Lord will support him on his bed of illness; You have turned over his entire bed in his sickness"** <note>Psalms 41:4</note>. This is precise, because these sick people are only nourished by that very subtle essence. And what is it? "Milk and blood," as it says, "to offer Him the fat and the blood." This is nourishment from the place called "Heaven," and it is precious, supreme, and the most subtle of all.

The holy and precious supreme nourishment, the nourishment of the spirit and the soul, is the nourishment that comes from afar, supreme and more precious than all. It is the nourishment of the spirit that is seen in a vision, and it is the nourishment that comes from the Supernal <term>Chokhmah</term> <note>Wisdom, the second Sefirah</note>, from that place. Because the Torah goes forth from the Supernal Wisdom, those who labor in the Torah enter into the essence of the Root, and therefore their nourishment comes from that holy, supreme place. Rabbi Elazar came and kissed his hands, saying: "Fortunate is my portion that I have attained these words. Fortunate is the portion of the righteous who labor in the Torah day and night, for they merit it in this world and in the World to Come, as it is written: **'For He is your life and the length of your days'**" <note>Deuteronomy 30:20</note>.

---

**"Behold, I will rain down bread from heaven for you."** Rabbi Yossi opened his discourse: **"You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing"** <note>Psalms 145:16</note>. What is written above this? **"The eyes of all look expectantly to You"** <note>Psalms 145:15</note>. All the inhabitants of the world wait and lift their eyes to the Holy One, blessed be He. Therefore, all "people of faith" <note>original: *benei meheimanuta*</note> must ask for their sustenance from the Holy One, blessed be He, every single day, and offer their prayer for it. For whoever offers his prayer to the Holy One, blessed be He, for his sustenance, causes every day to be blessed through that portion of sustenance he prayed for. The reason for this is: **"Blessed be the Lord, day by day"** <note>Psalms 68:20</note>.

Even if a person has food with him, he should ask before the Holy One, blessed be He, and offer a prayer for sustenance every day, so that blessings may be found with him every single day Above. Therefore, a person should not cook food from one day to the next, nor delay it from day to day, as it is written: **"And the people shall go out and gather a day's portion every day"** <note>Exodus 16:4</note>. "Every day" is precise—except for the eve of the Sabbath for the Sabbath, as we have established. Then the Holy One, blessed be He, is found full of blessings every day, and then it is written: **"You open Your hand... and satisfy the desire of every living thing."** That "desire" <note>original: *ratzon*</note> is found in the <term>Atika Kadisha</term> <note>The "Holy Ancient One," the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note>, and from Him issues the Will to water and provide sustenance to all. And what is it that provides sustenance every single day? That is called the "Faithful Well," and through the secret of the assembly, blessings are found Above.

Rabbi Chaba opened: "And the kindness of the Lord is upon those who fear Him, those who hope for His kindness." How much must people follow after the Holy King and walk in the paths of the Torah, so that blessings may be found for all, above and below! For we have learned: What is the meaning of that which is written, "May He send your help from the Sanctuary, and support you from Zion"? What does "from Zion" imply?...
