## Main Text (Zohar)

All these things happened to them only because they were not people of faith <note>original: *benei mehemanuta*</note>. In this same way, those who do not establish themselves in holiness do not wish to gather in the Land; they wish to trouble themselves at all times after their sustenance, day and night, yet it does not succeed in their hands. The verse begins by saying that they gathered these things because they were not people of faith. So too here: **"The people went about and gathered it"** <note>Numbers 11:8</note>—they abandoned their own souls and chose to trouble themselves over it. For it is written: **"and ground it in mills"** <note>Numbers 11:8</note>; after all this trouble, it did not result in anything more than what is written: **"and the taste of it was like the taste of a cake baked with oil"** <note>Numbers 11:8</note> and nothing more. What caused this for them? Because they were not people of faith. Rabbi Yose asked: What is "a cake baked with oil" <note>original: *leshad hashemen*</note>? Some say it refers to "moisture" as in the Aramaic translation. Others say it refers to <term>Chesed</term> <note>The Sefirah of Lovingkindness</note> which transforms into many colors; so too here, it transformed into many colors. Rabbi Yehuda said: *Leshad hashemen* refers to the essence of the oil. Rabbi Isaac said: **"every man according to his eating they gathered"** <note>Exodus 16:16</note>. Does this mean one who eats a little gathered a little, and one who eats much gathered much? But it is written: **"he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack"** <note>Exodus 16:18</note>. Rather, they gathered according to those who were to eat. This implies that everyone would eat it, and for this reason, it does not say "his eating" <note>singular</note>. What is this speaking of? A person holds onto his wisdom and honor as if it were his own. A case came before the <term>level</term> <note>original: *darga*</note> of <term>Metatron</term> <note>The supreme angel and "Prince of the World"</note>. He said to them: "How many souls are in his house, and how many souls are in your house?" This one said such-and-such, and he gave his claim. He said to them: "Let them gather a measure tomorrow, and each of you take it and come to me." The next day they went out and gathered and came before him. He measured before them. He saw that servant who had worked for that Manna, and found one <term>Omer</term> <note>A biblical unit of dry measure</note> for every single soul of his household. He measured for the other and found the same amount of food that he had worked for in his Manna, and one Omer for every single soul of his household. He said: "This is the servant." This is what is written: **"every man according to his eating they gathered"** and it is written: **"an omer a head, according to the number of your persons"** <note>Exodus 16:16</note>. Rabbi Hiyya said: It is written:

->**Evening**<-
> **"At even, then ye shall know that the Lord hath brought you out from the land of Egypt; and in the morning, then ye shall see the glory of the Lord"** <note>Exodus 16:6-7</note>

"At even ye shall know"—by what do they know? Rather, it was said thus: Every single day, look at the days of the Holy One, blessed be He. When the morning awakens, <term>Chesed</term> <note>Mercy/Lovingkindness</note> is awakened in the world. At that time which is called "evening," <term>Din</term> <note>Judgment</note> hangs over the world and is established over His children. Thus Isaac instituted the <term>Mincha</term> <note>The afternoon prayer, traditionally associated with the patriarch Isaac and the attribute of Judgment</note> prayer. What does "At even ye shall know" mean? When Judgment awakens in the world, you shall know that at that time the Lord brought you out of Egypt. "And in the morning ye shall see the glory of the Lord," for at that time <term>Chesed</term> awakens in the world and gives you food to eat. Rabbi Hiyya said the opposite: regarding what was above when they looked upon the generation of the wilderness, etc. At the hour that evening awakens, which is the time that Judgment awakens, <term>Chesed</term> also awakens in the world. This is what is written: "ye shall know that the Lord hath brought you out from the land of Egypt"—you shall know that <term>Chesed</term> which He did for you, that He brought you out of the land of Egypt. "And in the morning ye shall see the glory of the Lord"—this is well known. And why all this? **"For that the Lord heareth your murmurings"** <note>Exodus 16:7</note> etc. Rabbi Yosa said: The Holy One, blessed be He, does not find merit in His days except for those who sustain the world, for because of them He turns <term>Rachamim</term> <note>Compassion/Mercy</note> into Judgment <note>The text likely implies turning Judgment into Mercy through prayer</note> as has been said. Come and see, Rabbi Eleazar: from this faith, those who are worthy will go to the World to Come. And if you say it is in this manner? No. It is even more, for it was never so in all the worlds. And if you say as we have established, as it is written: "to be in the evening of the Lord and in the morning in His palace." And it is written: **"Neither hath the eye seen, O God, beside thee"** <note>Isaiah 64:3</note> etc.

->**See**<-
> **"For that the Lord hath given you the sabbath"** <note>Exodus 16:29</note>

Rabbi Hezekiah opened: **"A Song of Ascents. Out of the depths have I called Thee, O Lord"** <note>Psalm 130:1</note>. "A Song of Ascents" is stated plainly, without specifying who said it. Rather, it is a Song of Ascents that all are destined to sing...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Torah portion Beshalach, focusing on the mechanics of prayer and the sanctity of the Sabbath. It transitions from the general requirements of prayer to the specific cosmic structure of the Sabbath and the concept of the Divine "Place."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Beshalach**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion, meaning "When he sent," referring to Pharaoh sending the Israelites out of Egypt.</note>

All the worlds look upon this mountain to be repaid for the generations of the world. And what is this? **"Out of the depths I have called You, O Lord"** <note>Psalm 130:1</note>. Come and see: anyone who offers their prayer before the Holy King must seek their request and pray from the depths of the heart, so that their heart may be found complete with the Holy One, blessed be He, and they may focus their heart and will. Did David not say this? For it is written: **"With my whole heart I have sought You"** <note>Psalm 119:10</note>. Why then did he need to say "out of the depths"? Rather, come and see: every person who seeks their request before the King must focus their mind and will on the Root of all Roots <note>The ultimate divine source, often associated with the highest Sefirah, Keter</note>, to draw down blessings from the depths of the Pit <note>original: *be'era* - referring to the deep wellspring of Binah/Understanding</note>, so that blessings may be given from the Source of All. And what is that place from which that River emerges and is found? As it is written:
> **And a river went out of Eden** (Genesis 2:10)
And it is written:
> **There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God** (Psalms 46:5)
And they do not investigate "out of the depths"—the depth of all, the depth of the Pit from which the springs emerge and flow to bless everything. This is the beginning of drawing down blessings from above to below. Rabbi Hezekiah said: When the Ancient of all Ancients <note>original: *Atika de-kol Atikin* - the most hidden, ancient aspect of the Divine</note>, the most Hidden of all, desires to draw down blessings to the worlds, He rests everything and includes everything within this Supernal Depth. From here, it descends and flows by way of streams and springs that are drawn from it and established by it. Therefore, one who prays must focus their heart and will to draw blessings from that Depth of All, so that their prayer may be accepted and their will fulfilled.

Rabbi Judah said: Every single day the world is blessed from that Supernal Depth of All. The six days <note>of the week</note> are blessed from the Seventh Day, and each day gives from that blessing which it received on its specific day, flowing down below. For thirty days, thirty days from them until morning. Why? Because this day does not give to or sustain its fellow; rather, each one rules alone on its own day, for one day does not rule during the day of its fellow. Because of this, all those five days rule by themselves, and what was commanded is found within them, but on the Sixth Day, more is found. 

With the secular <note>weekday</note> it is not so, for there are other levels. As it is written, **"The Sixth Day"** <note>Genesis 1:31</note>—and it is not said this way regarding any of the other days <note>which lack the definite article "The"</note>. Rather, they have established it thus: this letter *He* [The] of "The Sixth" refers to the Matron <note>original: *Matronita* - the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> who prepares the table for the King. Because of this, two portions are found on it: one for its own day, and one for the preparation for the King, in the joy of the Matron. On that night and day, the Matron is like the King, and all six days are blessed, each one individually. Therefore, a person must arrange the table on the night of Sabbath, because blessings from above rest upon it, and blessing is not found upon an empty table. On 그 night is the joy of the Matron as the King, and their Union <note>original: *Zivvuga*</note>. Therefore, come and let us make known this secret: their Union is from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve. 

Another matter: **"For the Lord has given you the Sabbath"** <note>Exodus 16:29</note>. What is "Sabbath"? The day upon which the other days stand, and it is the sum of all those other six. Rabbi Yose said: Likewise, the Congregation of Israel <note>the spiritual essence of the Jewish people</note> is called "Sabbath," because she is His partner. This is the secret of the Bride, as it is written:
> **And you shall keep the Sabbath, for it is holy unto you** (Exodus 31:14)
"Unto you," and not to the other nations. This is what is written: **"Between Me and the children of Israel,"** and it is an eternal inheritance for Israel. And it is further written: **"If you turn away your foot because of the Sabbath..."** <note>Isaiah 58:13</note> and afterwards they explained the matter.

---

It is written:
# **Let No**
man go out of his place on the seventh day <note>Exodus 16:29</note>. "From his place"—we have learned: from that "Place" <note>original: *Makom* - a name for God/Shekhinah</note> which is below, for whom? And a spirit for the matter, as it is written:
> **Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place** (Ezekiel 3:12)
Let it not be "Place" and let it not be "Spirit," for it is written:
> **For the place whereon you stand is holy ground** (Exodus 3:5)
A known site we call "Place," where the Supernal Glory is made known. Because of this, it is a warning to a person that they should not be crowned with the holy crown <note>the Sabbath soul</note> only to go outside and leave their house, for by the mouth of the King, one who leaves his house is cursed.

<meta>This page transitions from the conclusion of the Sabbath laws and mystical significance into the beginning of the Torah portion *Beshalach*. It focuses on the divine response to Israel's distress at the Red Sea and the mystical identity of the "Rock" (Tzur).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

From every day of the Sabbath, all are in the service of the sons of man to call out. When they pass, they see all the windows of the Sabbath; it is a precious place of holiness that stands alone from other secular days. It is the "Glory from below," which is the spirit of the crown of the Sabbath. Because of this, "No man shall leave his place" <note>Exodus 16:29</note>. Fortunate is the portion of one who merits the glory of the Sabbath; he is complete in this world and in the world to come.

**And the Lord said** unto Moses: "Why do you cry out to me?" etc. <note>Exodus 14:15</note>. Rabbi Hiyya opened his discourse: "The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear Him, and delivers them" <note>Psalms 34:8</note>. Fortunate are the righteous of the Holy One below, for their honor is even greater than those above. Come and see how many people in the world blaspheme and revile the One Above, such as Sennacherib, who blasphemed and reviled and said, "Who among all the gods of the lands..." <note>Isaiah 36:20</note>, yet the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not immediately demand retribution from him. Once he set himself against His Law, what is written? "And the angel of the Lord went out and struck the camp of Assyria" <note>Isaiah 37:36</note>. Pharaoh was the same; when he served <term>idolatry</term> <note>original: "Avodah Zarah"</note>, offering incense and praising it, the Holy One, Blessed be He, sought nothing from him. Even when He brought all the plagues upon him, he increased his wickedness and did not accept it. What is written? "Immediately his hand... and he could not do good." Regarding his service to idolatry, the Holy One did not demand an accounting. Pharaoh drew near and blasphemed <margin>and Moses saw</margin> saying, "Who is the Lord?" etc. <note>Exodus 5:2</note>. Yet the Holy One did not demand retribution until he touched Israel, as it is written: "Still you exaltest yourself against my people" <note>Exodus 9:17</note>. Here, "The hand of the Lord is upon your cattle," etc. Thus, in every place, the Holy One demands the grievance of the righteous more than His own. Here, Moses was offering his prayer, <margin>and Moses saw</margin> that the Holy One said to him: "Moses, it is not the time to demand your grievance; rather, pass before the people and show their strength, and let his hand be increased against you." Were their thrones poured out, or his throne? "And the staff with which you struck the Nile, take in your hand and go." What is this staff? It is engraved with the Name, and the holy medicine was hinted at within it from the beginning, as it was said: "The way of a man is upon the Rock." As you are informed, in what place was it revealed? Here it was revealed, as it is written: "Behold, I stand before you there upon the rock" <note>Exodus 17:6</note>. And who is the "Rock"? All of them are "The Rock, His work is perfect" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>. There Moses knew how the praise was written "upon the Rock," and thus we have established the matter. Rabbi Yehuda said to him: "The verse is pleasant, but is it not written: 'And you shall strike the rock, and water shall come out of it'?" He said to him: "Fortunate is your portion! For every secret of the holy secrets of the Holy One is not made for empty things. He brought everything out for the need of the world. This was not just to bring out water; rather, if so, is it not written: 'Behold, He struck the rock and waters flowed'?" <note>Psalms 78:20</note>. Who strikes to wonder? Rather, a <term>sharp hammer</term> <note>original: "Patisha Charifa" - a metaphor for sharp mystical insight</note> is known by its knots, and you have the strength to hang this. Come and see: in every place, "Rock" refers to <term>Severity</term> <note>original: "Gevurah" - the divine attribute of judgment</note>. When the Holy One wished to forgive them and bring forth [water], He awakened this Severity, and with that Severity, He struck and tapped. Is it not written: "Behold, He struck the rock and waters flowed"? If He had not awakened this Rock and struck in the place where it was needed, water would not have emerged. He said to him: "If so, is it not written: 'You neglected the Rock who begot you'?" <note>Deuteronomy 32:18</note>. And we have learned: "He struck and tapped," meaning you weakened Him. Rather, it is thus: for a time I knew from the day of this Rock that it was ready to awaken against them and to pour upon them, to prevent war before Him. But the matter is in their eyes, since they do not look at it and are not established in their wisdom <insert>another version: in their thrones</insert>. And because of this, "You neglected the Rock who begot you." Rabbi Isaac said: "There is a Rock and there is a Rock. From the side of the upper Rock, another Rock emerges and strikes. The upper Rock endures in every generation, and it strikes that which goes down to the remainder, as it is written: 'You neglected the Rock who begot you.' For it strikes from the side of the upper Rock, and another Rock emerges from the 'Other Side' of the serpent, emerging as Severity and sickness. This is what is written: 'Who can utter the mighty acts (Gevurot) of the Lord?' <note>Psalms 106:2</note>. He strikes the mighty acts of the Lord to consume. It is not upper, for even though it is not the essence of judgment, from its side it approaches, for from its side comes Severity."

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Exodus, specifically the transition from the miracle of water at Rephidim to the attack by Amalek. It maintains the Zohar’s characteristic focus on the symbolic meanings of "Rock" and the internal structure of the Divine realms.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And in His throne they are found, and because of this He is called the "Rock of the Worlds" <note>original: *Tzur Alama*</note>. And it is found that His words were not shining, for He did not strike it like the "Kindness of the World" <note>Chesed</note> which is the light of Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>. Furthermore, Rabbi Abba said: "Water" in every place is well-known, yet it is difficult—how can this "Rock" awaken the way of water, since water is only seen to emerge from the side of Power <note>Gevurah/Judgment</note>? And this is the mystery of the "Nest" <note>referring to a specific kabbalistic configuration of divine attributes</note>. And concerning this, David praised and said: *Who turned the rock into a pool of water...* (Psalm 114:8). And what is this "turning"? For it is not the natural way of a rock to do so. And because of this, the Creator of the world brings forth water from the lowest of the low, and from the heavens to the cliff below. As it is written: *And you shall strike the rock, and water shall come out of it, that the people may drink* (Exodus 17:6). And here, the "Rock" and "Cliff" brought forth water through the power of the "Rock Above." This is what is meant by: *The Rock, His work is perfect* (Deuteronomy 32:4), for the Rock was commanded to make His work perfect. And what is this? It is Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>, as it is written: *Walk before Me and be perfect* (Genesis 17:1). (And this is "Who turned the rock into a pool of water," and when His work is withheld from water, this is the pain of the soul that was commanded to be "perfect" at the time when the "End of all Ends" was made from her. And now, to bring forth water from this Rock in the midst of Israel, the water was not arranged as it was at first. At that time, the pen of Moses was weakened, and he said: *You neglected the Rock who begot you* (Deuteronomy 32:18). That is to say, you weakened Him from what He was at first, and because of this, He was not found "perfect" at that hour to act within it, for He was not as in the time of "He begot you"—meaning, when He first brought you forth).

Rabbi Abba said: What is the meaning of that which is written: *Is the Lord among us, or not?* (Exodus 17:7). Were the Israelites so foolish that they did not know this? For they saw the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> before them and the Clouds of Glory above them surrounding them, yet at that time they said, "Is the Lord among us or not?" Even the heathens, who are the "woe" of the call of their kings, and the strength that was strengthened against the wood—what did Rabshakeh and Ezekiel send? Even they were found to be fools when they said, "Is the Lord among us or not?" Rather, this is what Rabbi Shimon said: They sought to know the difference between the <term>Ancient Hidden One</term> <note>Atika Stima'ah; the most concealed, transcendent aspect of God</note> who is called **"Nothing"** <note>Ayin; the Infinite source beyond comprehension</note>, and the <term>Small Face</term> <note>Ze'ir Anpin; the revealed, emotive attributes of God</note>. And because of this, it is not written "Is the Lord among us or *no*" <note>Hebrew: *Lo*</note> as it is written elsewhere, *Whether they will walk in My law or no* (Exodus 16:4). Rather, it says "or **Nothing**" <note>Hebrew: *Ayin*</note>. If so, why were they punished? Because they created a "separation" <note>Piruda; a spiritual rift between the different levels of the Divine</note>. And thus, at the time when it is written, *Because they tested the Lord, saying...* Israel asked if He is "One" in this manner. And because they spoke in this way, immediately: *Then came Amalek.*

---

->**Then came** Amalek and fought with Israel in Rephidim<-

Rabbi Yose opened with the verse: *Happy are you who sow beside all waters, who send forth the feet of the ox and the donkey* (Isaiah 32:20). "Happy are you who sow beside all waters"—there we have learned how many "waters" and what kind of "waters" were found. Meritorious are Israel, for they have no "seed" except upon the Water, as it is written: *And they camped there by the waters* (Exodus 15:27). These were the branches of Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note> of the "Nest." For we have learned: There is a Tree above, and it is a Great and Mighty Tree, and when it is found providing rest for all, it is prepared in twelve boundaries, established in three directions for the twelve winds of the world, and other branches are within it. And Israel is found in the breath of that Tree, and they are the seventy branches surrounding them. And this is what is written: *And they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees* (Exodus 15:27). And this has been established and said in many places. They camped and were established there "by the waters." Even at that time, Israel merited those waters, which are the branches of the Tree called "The Meritorious Waters." And regarding this: "Happy are you who sow beside all waters, who send forth the feet of the ox and the donkey." These are the two "Crowns" <note>Ketarim</note> of the left side to which the idolatrous nations cling, which are called "Ox" and "Donkey." And this is what is written: *I have acquired ox and donkey* (Genesis 32:6). Because for the simple man, he was like one who stirs them up and pushes them into the two lower realms. And at the time they sought to prove to Jacob, as it is written: *A wandering Aramean was my father* (Deuteronomy 26:5), and in the end it is said: when Israel is meritorious, they "send them forth" so they cannot rest upon them—meaning "sending forth the feet of the ox and the donkey" so they do not rule over them. When they are joined as one, they cannot prevail, just like a ritual bath <note>Mikveh</note> like this. And regarding this it is written...

<meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Beshalach, specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of the war with Amalek and the metaphysical nature of "Evil Sickness" as described in Ecclesiastes.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Open for him <note>original: *tamrus*</note> like a mountain and like myrrh together. "Together" is emphasized. And they prepare for him, giving the merit of his education to those who borrow from the pockets, for in the action he awakens what is not needed. And when they are joined as one, they cannot stand before them. From their side, they are bent by their strength, for he sees a "dog," and this is the most hypocritical of them all. **And against any of the children of Israel, a dog shall not sharpen its tongue.** <note>Exodus 11:7</note> The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "You said, 'Is the Lord among us or not?' <note>Exodus 17:7</note> Behold, I am handing you over to the dog." Immediately, **Amalek came.** <note>Exodus 17:8</note> Rabbi Judah said: **Amalek was the first of the nations, but his end shall be destruction.** <note>Numbers 24:20</note> Was Amalek truly the first of the nations? Were there not many bandits, nations, and peoples in the world before Amalek arrived? Rather, when Israel went out of Egypt, fear and awe fell upon all the nations of the world. How do we know this? As it is written:
> The nations heard and trembled; pangs seized the inhabitants of Philistia. <note>Exodus 15:14</note>
And there was no nation that did not fear the might of the Holy One, Blessed be He. But Amalek did not fear. This is what is written:
> And he did not fear God. <note>Deuteronomy 25:18</note>
He did not fear to draw near to you. And because of this, **Amalek was the first of the nations.** He was the first who came to wage war against Israel. And because of this, **his end shall be destruction,** as it is written:
> For I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek. <note>Exodus 17:14</note>
"You shall blot out the remembrance of Amalek"—this corresponds to "his end shall be destruction." Does "until destruction" mean he angers Him? Rather, until the Holy One, Blessed be He, comes and destroys him; that is to say, until the Holy One, Blessed be He, causes him to perish, as it is written:
> For I will utterly blot out. <note>Exodus 17:14</note>
Rabbi Eleazar said: Come and see, <term>The Rock, His work is perfect</term> <note>Deuteronomy 32:4; a title for God emphasizing justice</note>, and He performed kindness with them to take them out of the hand [of Egypt], yet His judgment did not cease, for it is written, "And Amalek came." Rabbi Abba opened and said:
> There is a sickening evil I have seen under the sun. <note>Ecclesiastes 6:1</note>
How many people are closed-hearted because they do not look into the <term>Torah</term> <note>Divine Law/Wisdom</note>! "There is a sickening evil." Is there an evil that is "sickening" and an evil that is not "sickening"? Indeed, there is a "sickening evil," for we have learned that from the <term>Left Side</term> <note>The realm of harsh judgment and spiritual impurity</note> many officers of decrees emerge, and they are established in "sickness." And when they wish to go out, they go and are found in the planet **Mars**, where all the chambers of decrees join together as one. They burst through the air, fly through the world, and draw near to human beings. Each one says "Evil," and all of them say, "No evil shall befall you," because below they are in strength upon the **Throne of Yah**. "Sickening" <note>Hebrew: *cholah*</note>—it takes hold of a sickness. When this rests upon people, it makes them stingy with their money. The charities of the Holy One, Blessed be He, come under his hand, and [the sickness] says to him: "Do not let anything go out from what is yours." The poor come, and it strikes his hand. He comes to eat from his own wealth, and it strikes his hand because he is guarding it for someone else. And from the time it rests upon him, it is "sickening," just as one says of a sick person <note>Hebrew: *marea*</note> who does not eat or drink. And regarding this, it is a **sickening evil guarded for its owner to his own hurt.** <note>Ecclesiastes 5:12</note> May the Merciful One save us! It says: **And God gives him wealth, possessions, and honor, etc.** <note>Ecclesiastes 6:2</note> This verse is a profound secret... it is written: **And God gives him wealth and possessions... but God does not give him power to eat from it.** If so, is it not in the person's power? Rather, it is written: **God does not give him power to eat from it.** The support says this: He does not give him power because he is prepared for that "Evil," and he takes hold of it. The Holy One, Blessed be He, does not rule over it to cast it down, as it is written of a sick person, but he stays close to his money and does not let it out, guarding it until he leaves the world. Then another comes and takes it out, and that person is the "owner." King Solomon cried out and said: **Wealth guarded for its owner to his own hurt.** Who is this "owner"? This is the other person who inherits it. And why did he merit to be the owner of that wealth? Because the first one clung to that "Evil" and desired it "to his own hurt"—by the killing of your neighbor <note>metaphorical for the spiritual harm caused by stinginess</note>—the other person attached himself to it and stands to be the owner of that wealth "to his own hurt," meaning because of the evil he clung to, he gained this. "There is a sickening evil"—this refers to one who sits in a good portion like his father's house, yet he goes toward his sins.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Beshalach**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion, meaning "When he sent," referring to Pharaoh sending the Israelites away.</note>

In those times, these matters were meant to cling to that evil constellation <note>The Zohar often discusses "Mazal" or constellations as spiritual conduits</note>... as mentioned previously, a sick person is protected in his times, one way or another. So too, Israel: the Holy One, blessed be He, carried them on eagles' wings and surrounded them with clouds of glory. His *Shekhinah* <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</note> traveled before them, He brought down Manna for them to eat and brought forth sweet water for them, and they saw Him in His power. Immediately, "Then came Amalek" (Exodus 17:8).

**Then came** Amalek. Rabbi Shimon, the spirit of wisdom, the pure lamp, approached and a voice was heard above and below. There is not a single word in the Torah that does not contain high secrets of wisdom that are bound to the Holy Name. As it were, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: "When they are worthy below, My strength prevails over all. But when they are not found worthy, they—as it were—weaken the strength Above, and the power of harsh Judgment prevails." Come and see: at the time Israel was worthy below, what is written? "Then came Amalek and fought with Israel." Below, the Accuser sought to challenge Mercy with Judgment. And all of this was reflected both Above and Below. "At Rephidim"—this implies *Rippui Yadayim* <note>A Hebrew wordplay: Rephidim sounds like "weakening of the hands"</note>, for their hands weakened from the study of Torah to provoke [the Divine], as we have established. Rabbi Judah said: Twice did Amalek come to wage war with Israel; once here, and once where it is written, "Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites came down..." (Numbers 14:45). Rabbi Shimon said: It happened Above and Below. The accusation against the Holy One, blessed be He, was Above, as has been said. Below, it was against the Holy One, blessed be He, for they [the Amalekites] acted like strangers; they cut off the "sign of the holy covenant" <note>The circumcision</note> from the Israelites, threw them upward, and said: "Take for Yourself what You desired!" Therefore, the zeal was over everything. <margin>(Section 8, page 158)</margin>

**And Moses said** to Joshua: "Choose men for us and go out, fight with Amalek" (Exodus 17:9). Now, what did Moses see that caused him to remove himself from this first battle that the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded? Rather, Moses—blessed is his portion—looked and knew the root of the matter. Moses said: "I see myself designated for that battle Above, and you, Joshua, prepare yourself for the battle below." And they assisted one another, as it is written:
> And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed (Exodus 17:11).

This refers to the [spiritual] prince Above. For this reason, Moses withdrew from the battle below in order to exert himself in the battle Above, and it was settled by his hand. Rabbi Shimon said: Was the war of Amalek a small thing in your eyes? Come and see: from the time the world was created until that time, and from the end of time until the King Messiah comes—and even in the days of Gog and Magog—nothing is found like it. Not because of powerful armies or weapons, but because it involved all "sides" of the Holy One, blessed be He. "And Moses said to Joshua"—why to Joshua and not to Moses? At that time, he was a youth, as it is written: "And Joshua the son of Nun, a youth" <note>Hebrew: *Na'ar*</note>. Were there no stronger men in Israel than him? Rather, Moses looked with wisdom and knew. What did he see? He saw that the one who was the Accuser Above was assisting Amalek below. Moses said: "Certainly, the battle must appear this way." Joshua at that time was found in a very high degree. And if you say he was found within the *Shekhinah* at that time—rather, it is because he was attached and clung to it, and the Joshua below was beneath it, etc. Rabbi Shimon said: In the place called "Youth" <note>A reference to the angel Metatron, often called the "Youth" in mystical literature</note>, Joshua was there, for Judah strikes, as it is written:
> Your eyes shall see Jerusalem, a peaceful habitation, a tent <term>Ohel: a tent or tabernacle, often symbolizing a spiritual dwelling</term> that shall not be moved; its stakes shall never be plucked up (Isaiah 33:20).

Jerusalem—the Jerusalem Above—is called "a tent that shall not be moved," for it shall no longer go into exile. And this is the spirit of what is written: "And Joshua the son of Nun, a youth." A "youth" certainly! "He departed not out of the tent" (Exodus 33:11). That which is called "a tent that shall not be moved" teaches that every single day he would suckle from the *Shekhinah*. Just as the "Youth" Above <note>The celestial Metatron</note> does not depart from the Tent and suckles from it constantly, so too this youth below.

It highlights Moses' role in the celestial battle while Joshua, linked to the divine "Youth," fought the physical war below.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Beshalach, specifically the battle against Amalek in Exodus 17. It explores the cosmic significance of the physical battle led by Joshua and the spiritual battle led by Moses.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The lower world shall not falter from the balance! And it is constantly damaged by it <note>referring to the spiritual impurity of Amalek</note>. Therefore, "I will utterly blot out" <note>Exodus 17:14</note>—to strike like this, to strike Amalek. Moses certainly stood against him and prevailed over him to defeat him. Immediately:

**And Moses said to Joshua: "Choose men for us and go out, fight against Amalek"** <note>Exodus 17:9</note>. This battle below is yours, while I shall prepare myself for the battle above. "Choose for us men"—righteous men, sons of righteous men, who are fit to go out with you. Through the movement of the hand, Joshua was awakened from the side above and was equipped with many adornments and many weapons that were prepared for him for this battle—this is to avenge the **vengeance of the Covenant**. And this is what is written: **"A sword that shall execute the vengeance of the Covenant"** <note>Leviticus 26:25</note>. And this is the meaning of what is written: **"And Joshua weakened Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword"** <note>Exodus 17:13</note>.

"With the edge of the sword" certainly—and not through mere love or physical weapons, but rather as it stands, they took the **sword that executes the vengeance of the Covenant**, and from there he was prepared for the battle above. **"And the staff of God shall be in my hand"**—the staff of the precious, holy ones that was handed over to the worlds. Precious ones who were appointed to wage the battle above. **"And they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat upon it"** <note>Exodus 17:12</note>—because of the two Israels <note>the celestial and the earthly</note>, he sat with them as in their youth.

**"And Aaron and Hur supported his hands, one on this side and one on that side, and his hands were faith"** <note>Exodus 17:12</note>. "Faith" <term>Emunah: faithfulness or spiritual steadfastness</term> certainly. But was it because Aaron and Hur supported his hands that his hands became "faith"? Rather, everything was done with **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah: the sefirah of divine intuition</term>. What he did with Aaron and Hur—this one from his side <note>Right/Mercy</note> and that one from his side <note>Left/Judgment</note>—and his hands were entirely in faith. And because of this, "his hands were faith." Aaron, because he was awakened from his side, and Hur, because he was awakened from his side, and they held his hands from here and from there so that the supernal assistance would be found.

---

**"And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed"** <note>Exodus 17:11</note>. When he raised the form <note>of his hands</note> above all Thought, and focused his intent in the spreading of his hands, then the Supernal Israel prevailed. **"And when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed"**—at the moment when Israel below looked down and were unable to stand upright, then Amalek prevailed. From here onward, see that the Priest spreads his hands in battle to prepare himself; all Israel needs to be found in their prayers with him. Come and see: in this battle of Amalek, they were in danger both above and below, and therefore "his hands were faith," and faithfulness as is fitting. "And his hands were <note>singular</note> faith"—it should have said "his hands were <note>plural</note> faiths." However, because everything depends on the **Right Hand**, it is written "it was" <note>singular</note>. And it is written "his hands" because they are the essence of everything. And it is written: **"Your right hand, O Lord, is glorious in power; Your right hand, O Lord, shatters the enemy"** <note>Exodus 15:6</note>.

---

**"And the Lord said to Moses: 'Write this as a memorial in a book...'"** <note>Exodus 17:14</note>. Come and see, it is written above: **"And Joshua weakened Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword."** "Weakened"? It should have said "killed"! Rather, "weakened" is as you say: **"who didst weaken the nations"** <note>Isaiah 14:12</note>. Joshua was weakening them, and that **sword that executes the vengeance of the Covenant** was killing them, as it is written: "with the edge of the sword," as has been said. "Write **this** as a memorial"—"this" <note>Zot: a name for the Shekhinah</note> specifically. "And place it in the ears of Joshua"—for he was destined to kill other kings. **"For I will utterly blot out"** <note>literally: blotting I will blot</note>—"blotting" above, "I will blot" below. "The remembrance"—the memory above and below. Rabbi Isaac said: It is written "For I will utterly blot out" and it is also written **"You shall blot out the remembrance of Amalek"** <note>Deuteronomy 25:19</note>. Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: "I will blot his memory below, and you <note>Israel</note> below shall blot his memory above." Rabbi Yose said: Amalek and Ammon lived for destruction with him. And all those who stood for battle as one against Israel... and because of this, Joshua was weakening them. Rabbi Yose said: "And Joshua weakened"—meaning their supernal power was broken.

---

**"And Moses built an altar and called its name 'The Lord is my Miracle'"** <note>Exodus 17:15</note>. Is an altar proof against that which is above? "And he called its name..." as one who says "The Lord is my Miracle" because here the vengeance of that **Holy Sign** <note>the Covenant/Circumcision</note> was taken.

...holy, that there should be in him the male [principle] of poverty. And from where do we know that it is called "a sword that executes the vengeance of the covenant"? And we have learned that once a male child is circumcised, etc., and that holy mark is revealed in him, he stands before that which is called the **Altar** <term>Mizbe'ach: the focal point of sacrifice and atonement, here linked to the Divine Presence</term> to atone for him. And what is its name? "The Lord is my Banner." In this manner: "And he built there an altar and called its name The Lord is my Banner." Israel—to whom? To that place called Altar. Rabbi Yose said: What is the meaning of that which is written <note>Exodus 24:10</note> "And they saw the God of Israel..."? Did they actually see? Is it possible to see the Light of the [Divine] Smallness? For behold, it is written: "For no man shall see Me and live." But here it says, "And they saw the God..." Thus we have learned: any matter that involves gazing even slightly is like a matter of gazing into the **Luminous Mirror** <term>Aspaklaria ha-Me'irah: a technical term for clear prophetic vision, usually associated with Moses</term>. It is lacking. And because of this, it is forbidden for a person to gaze at the fingers [of the Priests] when the Priest spreads his hands to pray. And to gaze even slightly at the matter—what is "slightly"? Rabbi Abba said: because of "slightly" literally. What is "slightly" in general? He said to him: at the "slightness" above and the "slightness" below. At the "slightness" above, because of the protection of every matter that he might gaze upon; for he who gazes at the "back" of the higher realm commits a disgrace against the **Shekhinah** <term>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God dwelling in the world</term>. At the "slightness" below, what is it? That sign of the covenant below... for anyone who gazes at it commits a disgrace above.

Rabbi Isaac said: Come and see, it is written <note>Genesis 24:2</note> "Put your hand under my thigh," for he was adjuring him by this sign [of circumcision]. And because of this, the higher Sages were protective, for they are not like the rest of the world. Furthermore, "Put your hand under my thigh" is written, and it is not written "Ride under my thigh"... to gaze at the "slightness" in general, as we have learned.

"And they saw the God of Israel"—that a "slightness" was revealed to them like beautiful, radiant colors, flaming from every side. It is significant that it is written "*et* [the] God of Israel" and not simply "they saw the God of Israel." Rabbi Yose said: like the brilliance of the Shekhinah... and it strikes there to hide the Shekhinah, which is called "within the Sanctuary." And [God] took it and placed it as the repair for the feet of the Shekhinah, and it stood before Him until the Sanctuary was established below, as it is written: "And all that is before His feet."

Rabbi Hiyya said: "The sapphire brick" is the radiance of the sapphire... engraved on high, flaming with sparks. And two branches of glory: "I will lay your foundations with sapphires." Rabbi Abba said: Just as the essence of the heavens is engraved with seals, and two branches fly from it, flaming from every side, so here the vision of that "essence of the heavens" was like the vision of the actual sky.

Rabbi Yehuda said: Everything is to be interpreted by that light of the Living Creatures <note>The Chayyot/Angels</note> that are engraved from the side of the Shekhinah. Rabbi Hezekiah said: Come and see, and so you shall judge regarding the **Chariots** <term>Merkavot: the divine vehicles or structures of the celestial realm</term> of the Shekhinah, as it is written <note>Song of Songs 3:7</note> "Sixty mighty men are around her." So it is certainly thus: these are the sixty that shine in twelve borders, and they never move from their ranks. For we have learned: twelve borders are engraved upon them in the balance, rising in the holy portion. Rabbi Hezekiah said: All those lights of the Chariot are like the King below. And this is the "essence of the heavens"—the actual "essence" that supports [everything]. And all those lights ascend and shine within it, in the radiance of the **Matronita** <term>The Matron/Queen; another title for the Shekhinah</term>. ## Main Text (Zohar)

...melting the powers of judgment, the blue thread of the fringes ceases there, and thus "he inclined all that he had done," etc.
> **"And Moses built an altar and called its name: The Lord is my Miracle"** (Exodus 17:15).

<note>original: "Adonai Nissi"</note> It truly means "The Lord is my Throne," <note>The Zohar plays on the phonetic similarity between 'Nissi' (my miracle) and 'Kissi' (my throne)</note> to show that because Amalek took all those who were circumcised but had not uncovered the flesh <note>referring to the ritual of 'priah', the second stage of circumcision</note>, he cut them off and threw them upwards. Afterwards, regarding what happened below at that hour, what is written?
> **"And he said: Because a hand is upon the throne of God, the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation"** (Exodus 17:16).

"From generation to generation" <note>Hebrew: "mi-dor dor"</note> is written deficiently <note>missing the letter 'Vav' in the original Hebrew text</note>. In every single generation, and in all generations to come into the world, there is no generation that does not contain some of that evil seed, and the Holy One, blessed be He, wages war against them. Rabbi Isaac said: From the dwelling below to the dwelling above, and concerning them it is written:
> **"Let sinners be consumed from the earth..."** (Psalms 104:35).

"From the earth" refers to this world and the world to come, and regarding all of it, it is written:
> **"Bless the Lord, O my soul. Hallelujah!"** (Psalms 104:35).

->**The Portion of "And Jethro Heard"**<-

**And Jethro heard**, the priest of Midian, Moses' father-in-law, all that God had done, etc. Rabbi Hezekiah opened and said:
> **"Lift up your hands to the Sanctuary"** <note>Psalms 134:2</note>

It is written "hand" <note>singular in some mystical readings</note> because one must lift it up and strike the adversary so as not to let the spirit of impurity stand. We have found in the Book of King Solomon that anyone who raises his hands upward when it is not for the purpose of prayer or supplication, this <term>human being</term> <note>Aramaic: bar nash</note> is cursed by ten rulers for no reason. And these ten rulers are:
> **"Which were in the city"** (Ecclesiastes 7:19).

These are the ten who are appointed over the <term>spreading of the hands</term> <note>Aramaic: perisu yadin; the priestly blessing or prayer posture</note> above. When the hands are raised in prayer or with the voice of blessing, they give strength to it so that the <term>Holy Name</term> <note>Aramaic: Shema Kadisha</note> may be honored and blessed from below. Once it is blessed from below through that spreading of the hands, it is then blessed from above and honored on all sides. Those ten rulers are appointed to receive those blessings from above and to heal below, and to bless the one who offers the blessing, as it is written:
> **"And I will bless them"** (Numbers 6:27).

Therefore, a <term>human being</term> must be careful at the time he raises his hands upward to acquire merit through prayer, blessings, or supplication. He must not raise his hands for no reason, because those ten are prepared and ready for that spreading of the hands. If it is for nothing, those ten curse him, and he becomes weak and cursed. Regarding such a person it is written:
> **"He loved cursing, and it came unto him"** (Psalms 109:17).

And then a <term>spirit of impurity</term> <note>Aramaic: ruach mesava</note> rests upon those hands, for it is forbidden to rest upon an empty place, and blessing does not dwell in an empty place. Regarding that spreading of the hands, strength rests upon them when engaged in prayer. In the spreading of the hands, there is a high mystery at the time of their separation and their exchange above, and a <term>human being</term> honors the Holy One, blessed be He, with several high mysteries. Come and see: there is no spirit that performs a desire except to praise everything, so that the <term>Holy Name</term> is blessed on all sides and everything is unified as one, above and below. He opened and said:
> **"And they shall not appear before me empty-handed"** (Exodus 23:15).

This refers to the spirit of the raising of the fingers. When a <term>human being</term> raises them upward, they must not be raised <term>empty</term> <note>Aramaic: reikam</note>, but rather with prayer, supplication, and blessings, or at least one of them.
> **"And they shall not appear before me empty-handed"**

It does not say "before Him," but "My face" <note>the Hebrew 'panai' can mean 'My face' or 'before Me'</note>, referring to the spirit of the raising of the fingers, so as not to trouble the heights by raising them for no reason, as has been said. The ten rulers we mentioned are the ten utterances below, like the spirit of the letters that are hidden in the body above, and these stand as before regarding that raising of the fingers.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the arrival of Jethro (Yitro) at the Israelite camp in the wilderness. It explores the cosmic necessity of a high priest of idolatry acknowledging the true God before the Torah could be revealed at Sinai.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Jethro Heard** <-

And through this, every **Side of Holiness** <note>Aramaic: *Sitrah de-Qedushah*; the realm of divine light and purity</note> is unified above and below; then all other sides are subdued and they all give thanks to the **Holy King**. Come and see: this Holiness is a King, and here is found the herald of Holiness both above and below. There is a King above, who is the Spirit of the Holy of Holies, and He is the Supreme King. Beneath Him are many spirits of the primordial light who serve before Him, and this is the great portion of the **Right Side** <note>The side of Mercy and Grace in the Sefirotic tree</note>. There is a King below, who is in the likeness of that Supreme King, and he rules over all; beneath him are many who serve him, the mystery of **Michael the High Priest** <note>The archangel Michael, seen as the celestial high priest</note> who is on the right. And so, on the Side of Holiness, there is a King and a foundation, and this is the spirit of perfect **Faith**.

On the **Other Side** <note>Aramaic: *Sitra Achra*; the realm of evil or "husks" (Kelipot)</note> which is opposite the Side of Holiness, there is a spirit who is a king, and we have established that this is the **"Old and Foolish King"** <note>A reference to Ecclesiastes 4:13, interpreted as the Evil Inclination or *Yetzer Hara*</note>. Beneath him are many beasts, and this is the spirit of which it is written: *And afterward I will explain to you my ten gifts of grace* <note>This appears to be a mystical interpretation or a specific manuscript variant regarding the actions of Jeroboam</note>, for this matter ruled over that deed which **Jeroboam** performed; had this word not been found, he would not have been able to endure in that deed. And this is the matter: when this king and his foundation stand together, they are subdued and broken and give thanks to Him; then the **Holy One, Blessed Be He**, rules alone above and below, as you have said:
> *And the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.* <note>Isaiah 2:11</note>

In this same manner and with this very spirit, the Holy One, Blessed Be He, acted with **Pharaoh**. At the time when Moses came to Pharaoh and said:
> *The God of the Hebrews has met with us,* <note>Exodus 5:3</note>

He opened and said:
> *I do not know the Lord.* <note>Exodus 5:2</note>

But the Holy One, Blessed Be He, desired that His Name be honored on earth just as it is honored above. Since he [Pharaoh] and his people were divided, he eventually came and gave thanks to the Holy One, Blessed Be He. Afterward, that foundation which serves beneath him was broken and subdued until he came and gave thanks to the Holy One, Blessed Be He. And this is the foundation from the side of the **Spleen** <note>In medieval physiology and Kabbalah, the spleen was often associated with melancholy or the "Other Side"</note>; and this is the "glory" <note>A play on the word *Yeqara* (glory) and the heaviness of the spleen</note> of which Rachel spoke at the beginning of her death, as it is written:
> *Ben-Oni (Son of my sorrow).* <note>Genesis 35:18</note>

And because of this, Jacob turned and called him **Benjamin** <note>Son of the Right Hand</note>, for the Spleen is not so; it is the **Right Side**. And once that king and his foundation gave thanks to the Holy One, Blessed Be He, and were broken before Him, then the Holy One, Blessed Be He, ascended in His **Glory** over everything, above and below. And until the Holy One, Blessed Be He, had ascended in His Glory through all those times before Him, the **Torah** was not established. Only after Jethro came and gave thanks and said:
> *Now I know that the Lord is greater than all gods,* <note>Exodus 18:11</note>
> *Blessed be the Lord, who has delivered you,* <note>Exodus 18:10</note>

—then the Holy One, Blessed Be He, ascended in His Glory above and below, and afterward He gave the Torah in the perfection of His dominion over all. He opened and said:
> *Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You.* <note>Psalms 67:4</note>

Then he [Jethro] rose and sacrificed and gave thanks to the Holy King. When He ascended through the Torah, which is the "Taste," then a spirit went out and came below and rose in the morning of the "sharp ones" <note>Possibly referring to the diligent students or the morning light</note>, like the days when **David's harp** would play and say, etc. And what was it saying? Come and see: at the time when the Holy One, Blessed Be He, awakens toward all those celestial chariots to give them their sustenance, as we have established, for it is written:
> *She rises while it is yet night and provides food for her household and a portion for her maidens.* <note>Proverbs 31:15</note>

Then they are all in joy. They opened and said:
> *May God be gracious to us and bless us and make His face to shine upon us, Selah.* <note>Psalms 67:2</note>

When the **North Wind** <note>Associated with the attribute of Gevurah/Strength and the awakening of the night</note> awakens, then it is for the world, as you have said:
> *That Your way may be known upon earth, Your salvation among all nations.* <note>Psalms 67:3</note>

Afterward, at the time when He gathers that spirit into Himself, He opened and said:
> *Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You.* <note>Psalms 67:4</note>

When David arose and the **Holy Spirit** was awakened upon him, he opened and said:
> *The earth has yielded its harvest; may God, our God, bless us. May God bless us, and let all the ends of the earth fear Him.* <note>Psalms 67:7-8</note>

Because the goodness of the Holy One, Blessed Be He, was found from above to below. Afterward, David came with the Holy Spirit and arranged them together; he looked at everything in this verse of the harp, because it is the ladder of the Glory of the Holy One, Blessed Be He, above and below. At the time when he mentioned the other nations coming and giving thanks to Him—once they said "Let them praise You"—then the Glory of the Holy One, Blessed Be He, ascended above and below. At the time when Moses saw Pharaoh...

## Main Text (Zohar)

To Pharaoh, he said: "The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us," etc. <note>Exodus 5:3</note>. He opened his discourse and said: "I do not know the Lord" <note>Exodus 5:2</note>. But the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>Aramaic: Kudsha Brich Hu; the standard rabbinic name for God</note> desired to honor His Name just as it is honored above. Once He had dealt with Pharaoh and his people, Jethro came and gave thanks to the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, as it is written: "And Jethro rejoiced" <note>Exodus 18:9; the Zohar interprets this as Jethro acknowledging God's greatness</note>. He gave Him honor, for Jethro was a great king <note>original: "Krupinos," likely a corruption of a Greek term for a high official or ruler</note> over the whole world. Once he gave honor, all the other kings turned and saw, as it is written:
> **"Then the chiefs of Edom were dismayed"** (Exodus 15:15)

Jethro came—he who was a priest of idolatry and the chief of all the ministers of all other false gods—and he acknowledged and gave honor to the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, saying: "Now I know that the Lord is greater than all gods" <note>Exodus 18:11</note>. At that moment, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> was uplifted in His glory above and below, and afterward, He gave the Torah in His dominion over all. Come and see what Rabbi Eleazar, his son, wrote concerning this:
> **"Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You."** (Psalms 67:6)

Rabbi Eleazar came and kissed his hands. Thus are the masters of wisdom. He said: "A daughter sins against her children, but grace and mercy are upon her children." <note>A cryptic proverbial expression regarding the transmission of merit</note> Rabbi Eleazar hid his words, for he was a son of the Merciful One. Blessed is your portion, for you have merited to hear these words before Him, of which one will not be ashamed in the World to Come. Rabbi Abba said: Regarding this "Priest"—if it were not written "Jethro, the Priest of Midian," it would be written differently. Everything is one, as before. See that Joseph was "Priest of On" <note>Genesis 41:45</note> and later we see that Moses' father-in-law was "Priest of Midian." This is all one mystery. For these two are from the side of Joseph, standing in the same level of spirit. And what is said of the "Priest of Midian" is a mystery below... from the side of Joseph, they stood in one spirit, this spirit and Jethro as one. Rabbi Abba placed his hand upon his head and wept. He said: The light of the Torah rises to the height of the firmament of the Upper Throne! After whom will the light of the Torah shine? Woe to the world that will remain an orphan without you! All the words of my Master will be hidden from the world until the King Messiah comes, and then it shall be written:

**And Jethro heard**, the priest of Midian. Rabbi Yose opened:

What is the praise of all the other verses? In all of them, two words change the house... but because the six sides were completed in this secret. This corresponds to the three redemptions of Israel, excluding the first redemption. The verse calls "wine" <note>likely a metaphor for the secrets of Torah</note> in place of the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings, and everything depends on this Wisdom. <meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Yitro (Exodus 18). The previous context likely discussed Jethro’s arrival and his recognition of the God of Israel. ## Main Text (The Zohar)

-> **And Jethro Heard** <-

And they were humbled before the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kadosh Baruch Hu," the standard rabbinic title for God</note> and he [Jethro] drew near to His fear. Rabbi Chakla saw: in many places we have learned that everything the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> made above and below is all truth, and the praise of truth. There is nothing in the world that a person should look upon with contempt or view as shameful, for all of them are truth and all are necessary in the world. 

For one time, <term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> <note>The son of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note> was walking on the road, and <term>Rabbi Hezekiah</term> was walking with him. They saw a snake, and <term>Rabbi Hezekiah</term> moved to kill it. <term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> said to him: "Leave it be, do not kill it." He replied: "But this is an evil thing that kills human beings!" He said to him: "Hezekiah, it is written—Heaven forbid—that a sin occurs without cause? It is not written that a snake [attacks] a person until they whisper to it from Above and say to it: 'Go and kill so-and-so.' And sometimes, just as the snake does this, it also saves a person from other things. Through it, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> performs His will <note>literally: "throws a cup of silver"</note>, and everything is suspended in the hands of the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>. All are the work of His hands and the world has need of them. If the world did not need them, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> would not have created them. Therefore, a person should not look with contempt upon anything in the world, for all are the works of the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>." He opened his discourse and said:

> **"And God saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good"** (Genesis 1:31)

<term>And God saw</term>—this refers to the <term>Living God</term> <note>Elohim Chayim, a divine name associated with the flow of life</note>. "And He saw" means to look upon and to illuminate them and to be found by them. "Everything that He had made"—this includes everything together, above and below. <term>And behold, it was good</term>—this is the <term>Right Side</term> <note>The side of Mercy and Light</note>. <term>Very</term>—this is the <term>Left Side</term> <note>The side of Judgment and Severity</note>, and thus they have established it: <term>Good</term> refers to the Angel of Life; <term>Very</term> refers to the Angel of Death. Yet it is all one spirit. This is a mystery for those who gaze into the secret of wisdom. "And God saw everything that He had made"—regarding every individual work of creation it is written "And God saw that it was good," but here it says "And God saw *everything* that He had made." "God" below rules over the lower beings; "God" above rules over the upper beings. This is all the <term>Living God</term> who illuminates and causes all those stars, upper and lower, to sparkle, and from there all those lights go forth to shine.

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **And Jethro Heard** <-

Let this be established by the verse that is written: **"So he listened to the voice of his father-in-law and did all that he had said"** <note>original: "shamoa tishma..." - a reference to Exodus 18:24</note> and **"And Jethro heard..."** <note>Exodus 18:1</note>. He opened his discourse and said: **"Therefore I will give thanks to You, O Lord, among the nations, and sing praises to Your name"** <note>Psalms 18:50</note>. King David spoke this through the Holy Spirit at the time he saw that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called and exalted with a supreme exaltation—to be honored in the whole world specifically from the side of the other nations. And if you say that the Holy One, blessed be He, is only honored in the world because of Israel, that is certainly true, for the Holy One, blessed be He, took them as His portion and heritage above all other peoples. But when the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is recognized by those outside of Israel, then the foundation of the earth is strengthened and all His works are strengthened in a single path. Then the Holy One, blessed be He, ascends in glory above and below. In this manner, dread and fear fell upon all the world before the Holy One, blessed be He. And once Jethro came—who was the high priest <term>komra; a high-ranking pagan priest</term> of all the false gods—and bowed down, then the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, was strengthened and revealed over everything. For when all the world heard of the mighty deeds of the Holy One, blessed be He, they trembled; and they were all looking toward Jethro, who was the wisest of the wise and the chief appointee over all the false gods of the world. Once they saw that he came and worshipped the Holy One, blessed be He, and said, **"Now I know that the Lord is greater than all the gods"** <note>Exodus 18:11</note>, then they all distanced themselves from their own worship and knew there was no substance in them. Then the glory of the Holy Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, was honored on all sides. For this reason, this section of the Torah was set apart, and the conclusion of the section was named for him. Jethro was one of the three advisors of Pharaoh. Pharaoh had three advisors: one was Jethro, one was Job, and one was Balaam. Jethro was such that there was no form of worship, appointee, false god, or star ruling over a cult that he did not know; he knew the worship below and its hidden source. Balaam was the head of all types of sorcery <term>charshin; magical arts or enchantments</term>, whether in action or in speech. Jethro was one who served through "awe" <term>dechilu; a state of religious dread or focused intent</term> and "observation" <note>original: "sichuta"</note>, which was his primary root. For a matter from Above—whether from the side of Holiness or from the "Other Side" <term>Sitra Achra; the realm of impurity or evil</term>—a person cannot draw down a spirit from Above to below or approach it except through awe, directing his heart and will as is fitting, and humbling his heart. Then the spirit from Above and the desired will is drawn down and dwells within him. If he does not direct his heart and will as is fitting for that side, he cannot attach his will to it, except for those "thin forms" <term>tupsa; spiritual imprints or shells</term>, and even then not all of them. For there are those on the side of good that require the will of the heart and awe, just as there are matters on the other side that require awe, love, and will. Jethro was wise in the worship required for that side, including the "confrontation" <note>original: "kenucha"</note> required of a man. Because that side clings to a person at the time he needs it. Balaam, in his sin, used sorceries as has been said, to join with the "hidden ones" of that awe. And fear was lacking in Egypt to tremble before the Holy One, blessed be He, even when they saw the wisdom, might, and miracles that the Holy One, blessed be He, performed in Egypt. Jethro did not return <note>meaning: did not convert or repent</note> through all of that until Israel went out of Egypt and all those sides and "forms" <term>tupsa</term> that were bound in fear were revealed as nothing and were subdued. After he heard all of them, then he turned and returned to the worship of the Holy One, blessed be He. He almost did not return, for the "form" <note>from the word for "shell" or "imprint"</note> of the Other Side was clinging to him. Yet even so, he looked from a distance, looking through that "form" <note>from the word for "shell"</note> and the attachment of the Other Side. For even in the Other Side there is a single thin light that shines from its place upon everything, and because of it, it is written that "the end sees from afar." And when all things reach their end, he saw a small matter from that light, as if from behind a wall. He would speak and not know what he was saying, looking as if at a light that is hidden from the eye, where the eye is not revealed but sees for a moment a hidden light and then does not see. This is the spirit of the "closed eye" <note>referring to Balaam</note>, which they established as "closed yet open," and it is all one, for there is no "Other Side" that does not have some light within it.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of Parashat Yitro (Exodus 18), focusing on the spiritual dynamics of Jethro’s arrival and the nature of prophetic vision. It bridges the gap between the "Other Side" (impurity) and the "Holy Side" (purity).</meta>

## Jethro Heard

A thin, minute light from the side of holiness—like the spirit of a flame in a lantern—exists in such a way that no human can perceive it by their own power. For there are powerful, subtle forces that surround it, all acting as one. They recognize the merit and the portion of the side of supernal life, belonging to all the high holy ones; these are things that no other person in the world is given permission to gaze upon. Just as the wicked prophet Balaam used to see only a tiny, thin light as if from behind a wall from within that "Other Side" <note>original: *Sitra Achra*, the realm of spiritual impurity</note> • so too Moses, from within a great and abundant supernal light, would look downward as if from behind a wall, through a single thin screen that appeared to him. Yet, while Balaam could not look upon that light at all times • the merit and portion of Moses was established differently. What is written of him? *And the angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of the bush* <note>Exodus 3:2</note> • The bush was certainly within that holiness and attached to it, for everything is attached to one another: the pure and the impure. There is no purity except that which emerges from within impurity. This is the mystery of the verse: *Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean?* <note>Job 14:4</note> • The "shell" <note>original: *Kliffah*, the outer layer of impurity</note> and the "brain" <note>the inner essence or fruit</note> rise together. This shell will not be removed or broken until the time when the dead rise from the dust; then the shell will be broken, and light will shine throughout the world, and all hidden things will be healed from their blemish. Righteous are the just in this world and in the World to Come.

**And** you have learned: Rabbi Hiyya said, etc., "his sons" and yet they were not the sons of Moses? <note>Referring to the phrasing in Exodus 18:5 regarding Jethro's arrival with Moses' family</note> • Rather, because they were worthy to be given over to the study of the Torah, the Torah calls them "his sons" even if they were not biologically his <note>A common Rabbinic theme: a student is like a son</note>. This means to say that on the festival days, the sons of Moses were truly "men of truth," his sons indeed. Rabbi Eleazar said: Was it not that Moses was joined as one to the high holy Grade <note>the Shekhinah</note>? Therefore, it was fitting for his glory to call them "his sons." Now, even though they were his biological children, because of the glory of that place to which he was joined, the text calls them "sons" without further specification. Later, it calls them "his sons." Why? Because at that moment Moses was ascending to speak in the assembly; but after he separated and went out to meet his father-in-law, then it is written: *And Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came with his sons and his wife to Moses.*

**And Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came with his sons and his wife, etc.** <note>Exodus 18:5</note> • Rabbi Shimon said: Eleazar, Eleazar! I see in this section that you are speaking words as is fitting, and the support of the Living God is with you. Certainly, for the sake of the glory of the Divine Presence <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note> and the supernal union that Moses was joined with, it is written "his sons." And if you say, "But look, it is written: *And Jethro... came with his sons and his wife*," [implying they were Jethro's sons]—know that regarding Moses, it is all one portion. These children were like Jethro's because after they came to him, they were like sons to him. We find a similar case with Jacob, who when he came to Laban, Laban's household became like his own sons. So too here: because Moses was joined to the Great One, Jethro had "sons," and his entire household was ready to enter under the wings of the Divine Presence <note>Jethro's family converting and seeking shelter under God's protection</note>. And Jethro said to Moses: "I have heard that Jethro, the strength of your God and your handmaid and the elders with you..." It is written "captives of captivity" and not "his grandsons." Because of Jethro, it is written: *And the children of the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law, went up from the city of palm trees* <note>Judges 1:16</note>. His children ascended through the waters and Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, merited this. Open your eyes and see: *Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord...* <note>Isaiah 2:3</note>. This verse has been established in several places. In the future, the other nations are destined to wear out their feet to enter under the wings of the Divine Presence. "Come and let us go up"—for all idols of foreign worship have no ascent, only descent, and those who cling to them have no exhaustion-free rising. "To the mountain of the Lord"—this refers to Abraham, as it is written: *On the mountain of the Lord it shall be seen* <note>Genesis 22:14</note>. Abraham called it a "mountain," and just as a mountain is open to anyone in the world who desires it, so too is this holy place open to receive anyone in the world who desires to convert. "To the house of the God of Jacob"—for Jacob called this place a "house," as it is written: *This is none other than the house of God.* From the "mountain" to the "house," they all rose to one single degree.

**Secrets of Secrets**

This wisdom is to be told at the time of the King, and he saw it and wrote it in a sapphire. To... to establish it... to give the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> and to exchange it... and the selection of every vision of strangers to be seen in the countenance <note>Partzufa</note>. And from the exchange of the labor of this wisdom... "thou shalt provide out of all the people" <note>Exodus 18:21</note> as it is written... and like your image it will be helped. And to engrave an engraving for the purpose... and to engrave and to contemplate... and this is to know and to do and to sustain, like the living beings of the throne, the covenant of the rains. One must look at the images <note>Diyukna</note> of human beings to know the wisdom in its clarity. And these are the signs: in the **hair**, in the **eyes**, in the **nose**, in the **lips**, and in the **cheeks**.

## Main Text (Zohar)

### Column 1 (Right)

->**And Jethro Heard**<-

The scripture contains one secret of the upper worlds <note>spiritual realms</note> and one secret of the lower worlds <note>the physical realm</note>. "Adam" <note>Man</note> is a secret of the upper worlds, established in the structure of the verse as male and female in a single spirit, as it is written: *This is the book of the generations of Adam* <note>Genesis 5:1</note>. Male and female are as one; since they produce generations together, He called them "Adam," as it is written: *the generations of Adam*. After the matter was revealed from within the first supreme hiddenness, the verse descends with mercy below, as it is written:
> In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made He him. <note>Genesis 5:1-2</note>

"In the likeness" does not mean in the same manner that spiritual images appear within Him. For those images do not endure in that vision as we have established their existence, but rather they pass away immediately. So too, "in the likeness of God" does not mean a complete likeness of the image, which is male and female in the secret of "behind and before." "Behind" refers to the spirit that is hidden, and "before" refers to the spirit that is remembered <note>the masculine aspect</note>. All the commandments of the Torah depend on Him, the King, and all the commandments of the Torah depend on the whole of Him. We have prepared "behind" for the Work of Creation and "before" for the Work of the Chariot <note>Ma'aseh Merkabah, the highest form of Jewish mysticism</note>, and they all depend one upon the other. "In the likeness of God" means exactly according to that image, and this is what the Master established.

**They taught:** *This is the book of the generations of Adam* refers to the images of a man. For the images of the male are for the purpose of recognizing those generations of the male, according to the image of the male secret. For example: by the hair, the forehead, the eyes, the face, the lips, and the hands—the hands and the joints—by these natural signs one may recognize him. Regarding the hair: there are those whose hair is curly and rises upward on the head; this indicates a person whose level is <unclear>bent</unclear> like a mold, and if his deeds are not corrupted, one should still distance oneself from partnering with him. If the hair is straight and hangs down, this is good for partnership and a spirit of peace is found in him. But in his studies, he is not so. This is a master of secrets in those mysteries above him. <unclear>When they do not stand...</unclear>

<column-break/>

### Column 2 (Left)

...faces, <unclear>lines</unclear>, and these sides, it is written: *And you shall provide* <note>Exodus 18:21, the source for Jethro's advice to Moses to choose leaders based on their appearance/character</note>. *And you shall provide*—like wool in small bundles—to look at those signs above the eyes. From all the <unclear>hair</unclear> in the eyes, the spots, the delays, and the points to see his eyes. It is necessary that there be strength in them to stand in the recognition of the world, in the light of the eyelids, in the coverings, in the bundles of the coverings, and in the lines of the hands by which he is examined. And these are the foundations in the lines of the hands, the markings within them. All six sides are hinted at here, which were handed over to Moses to gaze upon and to know the hidden wisdom. This wisdom is inherited by the righteous of truth as is fitting, and all their <unclear>reward</unclear> is written: *Remember, do not forget*, etc. In this manner, the Holy One, blessed be He, made levels upon levels above, these upon those, hidden and revealed. These are the veins and the sinews, and these are the bones that stand in the structure of a man's bones. These are engraved in the secret of the levels and the dominion of all flesh. All of these are found from the crown of the spirit of the <unclear>firmament</unclear>, and the <unclear>rulers</unclear> who rule like a crown. Above all is the skin and the covering of the expansion of the firmament, and this is the skin of the covering. Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, made the stars and constellations in the expanse of the firmament to be received, so He made in the skin <note>the human skin</note> hints and bundles like the stars and constellations, to know and to receive through them the **Wisdom of the Face** <term>Physiognomy: the art of judging character from facial features</term> and to gaze into the body. Just as the stars and constellations in the expanse of the firmament change according to the deeds of the world, so these markings and bundles in the covering of a man change according to his deeds. These are ready and prepared not for the <unclear>arrogant</unclear>, but for the righteous of truth, to know and to exchange through the Wisdom of the Face.

*This is the book of the generations of Adam*—one gazes at a person according to his deeds; thus they are engraved and marked, and he walks in them. For at the time when the Holy Spirit dwells within him, he produces "generations" <note>spiritual fruits</note> and one sees the markings of the spirit. But at a time when the Holy Spirit is removed and an impure spirit comes, the markings of that impure spirit <unclear>clash</unclear> between them, and they are engraved on the outside. Those who know can recognize him by the wrinkles in his coverings on the outside...
