# The Secret of Secrets: Reading the Forehead

**[Right Column]**

A person whose deeds are sometimes proper and sometimes not, and whose life hangs in the balance below <note>referring to earthly instability</note>, and who does not err regarding his fear of his Master—he feels shame for his actions when they are not proper. When good deeds are before him, he may fail to perform them, and his life is lacking in the necessary awe. Such a person treats the matters of the world as vanity, yet also treats the matters of his people as such. Anyone who draws near to him will find that the higher secrets are not revealed to him, for he is a mix of secrets and waking thoughts. It is good to correct such a person through speech, for a small word can do much. His words are hidden, and his spirit is like the letter *Zayin* <note>original: ז'</note> which leans toward the lower measurements.

Regarding the forehead <term>Sa'ara: the forehead or hair-line area</term>, if the wisdom shines more brightly in the hollows of all his deeds, both in worldly matters and in those that fly above, there is an advantage to this hollow for those who seek to know who is connected to him. Sometimes this hollow is present, and sometimes it is not. In that emptiness, his spirit takes flight. This spirit exists within the general rule of the letter *Zayin*. 

The wisdom of the forehead sometimes shows a hollow and sometimes not. This person is prone to being a partner or a snatcher. It is good to be with him for a short time, but not for a long time, for in the long run, he will return to his own calculations. To ensure he does not separate from the good, stay close for a short duration. He may appear healthy in his looks, but look closely at his "crown" <note>the top of the head or spiritual aura</note>; they will see that he lacks the spirit for the long term. He is pressed for time, and his thoughts are like sparks that cannot be contained. His heart is thin, and his spirit does not stand within the general rule of the letter *Zayin*, but rather the letter *Yod* <note>original: י'</note>. 

When the forehead is smooth <term>Marit: smooth or plucked</term>, he is capable in his deeds. He is tall and bows like a reed. Before he reaches old age, his forehead is smooth, but the crown of old age transforms him from how he was at first, whether for good or for evil. So it is with the words of a smooth forehead between the eyes, upon the brain, in the place of the Wisdom of the Phylacteries <term>Tefillin: ritual leather boxes containing scripture worn on the forehead</term>.

---

**[Left Column]**

Regarding the forehead, the nose, and the eyes: all these signs stand upon their foundations and do not cease. This is the secret of the wisdom of the letter *Zayin* which stands in the forehead. It humbles the *Zayin* and looks toward the battle in the forehead, so that the whole does not divide against him. The forehead stands to be known and revealed; it stands under the letter *Yod* and is joined by the letter *Lamed* <note>original: ל'</note> which is above, producing the letter *Pe* <note>original: פ'</note>.

In this forehead, there hang wisdom and time. There are three lines <term>Sirtutin: the engraved lines or wrinkles on the forehead</term> on the right side <margin>two on the left, and they do not connect</margin>. On the right forehead, there are three thin, trembling lines that pass over the main lines. These indicate a person who is prone to crossing over the boundaries of his masters. On the left side, there is a small mark, like a spark. This stands between the letter *Vav* <note>original: ו'</note> and the letter *Zayin*. 

In this case, we see strong "horns" <note>prominent ridges or veins</note> above the corners of the eyes that connect. Such a person is a master of anger, and he is not humble. He is one who learns through hard work and carves into himself a place of refuge. He constantly bows his head, and his master comforts him from without. He is not easily satisfied. He cannot be consumed by words of weeping, for heavy words are written upon them. 

When the "horns" are not balanced, the right side has two thick lines and one small one, with two trembling lines that enter into his days. On the left side, there are two: one large and one small, and one trembling mark. This person is a master of anger according to the hour; his rage rises and falls quickly. He is a person of a quiet spirit in the world, yet he possesses a hidden strength. He is accepted by others, but he is wrinkled in his movements and resembles a dog <note>original: כלבא; likely referring to tenacity or a specific facial set</note> in his persistence. His will is to be weighed in his purity, but he is easily tossed aside. In his efforts, he licks the dust. Here the letter *Zayin* is exchanged for the letter *Tav* <note>original: ת'</note>. If these "horns" are separated, he is a good man, and the lines of his master enter between them. He is a man of a small, dark face, but he is good and ancient in his soul.

## Commentary

A wrinkled eyelid: eyes that do not see... <margin>one line on the forehead</margin> and he thinks sharp and wakeful thoughts, there is no faithfulness in him. A man should not partner with him so that he does not shave his debt to kings in all his deeds; he has a birthmark and a wakeful sign on his left thigh... and even four **lines** <note>original: *sirtutin*, often referring to lines on the palm or forehead</note> on his forehead, every small thing is in him but he has no offspring. And if there are three large ones and small light ones, it is good, and let him rise and stand in his craft. Until the secret of the taste... the forehead is explained by the eyes. The eye is explained like the taste and thirty sides. Like the pupil in the colors of the eye, the light of the eye in the wisdom of the eye, all for gazing, to gaze at all those signs that are deep... to distinguish the Holy Spirit from the spirit of impurity. Except for the lines alone, for the lines are between the wakeful and the great: they change constantly, and so regarding all of them it is written:
> **"And Moses chose capable men out of all Israel, etc."** <note>Exodus 18:25</note>
For he looked upon those signs... and so "wise and discerning men, known to your tribes" <note>Deuteronomy 1:13</note>—these are "known" to be recognized by these signs... red hair. If the prophets are white, a man would not need the priestly house to be warned by him... his forehead is large and not round. Two large, weak markings in the breadth of his forehead from side to side and four wakeful ones; his hair hangs down, his brain is cold and strong, and because of this he is alert...

## The Secret of Secrets

### Column A (Right)

He sees shames in that trial; a shame that rises from below <note>original: "kisupha salik letatun"</note>. Below, they do not rise on their own from the chosen ones and the priests. Other thin marks are present, and these are within the category of the letter *Samekh* <note>The Zohar often uses Hebrew letters as archetypal categories for human features</note>. Whenever the letter *Samekh* is present, the eyes are green and surrounded by whiteness. When that greenness mingles with that whiteness, he is a man of mercy. Such people always think of their own benefit, yet they never think of doing evil to others. 

Wisdom is hidden within him below, and he does not send forth evil. The "Evil Side" <note>the Sitra Achra</note> does not take hold of him or dwell within him. He is faithful, as we have said above. Even when he is not recognized, he remains faithful. He is a Master of Secrets. In what way? His spirit is modeled after that spirit which, like wine, when one hears it, everything is revealed. Yet he does not listen to the spirit of others at all, for their words are not pleasant to him. 

The arches of his eyes <note>eyebrows</note> turn with light and greenness; this indicates a spirit below that is included in the letter *Samekh*. When the eyes are smiling and green, there is much within him. Because of this abundance, he is not a man of great talk, yet he conducts himself like a great man with grandeur. Whoever partners with him will find him exhausted; do not reveal a secret to his path, for he does not hold it firmly in his heart. He is not a faithful spirit when he makes himself great in this way. He is not in the spirit of the letter *Samekh* when it is included in the *Samekh* alone. 

Do not distance yourself from the letter *Samekh*, for because he acted with grandeur, the letter *Samekh* will not be far from him, yet do not draw near to him. When he speaks, he makes wrinkles <term>wrinkles: kmitin, often used in the Zohar to denote lines of judgment or character on the forehead</term> in his colors and on his forehead. His eyes are white, turning and waking with greenness. He prolongs the secret and is a man of mercy to the spirit at times. But when anger is stirred, there is no love in him at all, and he turns to cruelty. He is not a Master of the Secret. He is not in the spirit of the letter *Mem* that is included in the letter *Samekh*. Green and white eyes together, with a small amount of black in them—this is a Master of Secrets, and he is tied to them. Woe to the master of his degree <margin>on his own</margin>.

### Column B (Left)

The marks of the desire <note>or "Abiyan"</note>: these are red marks that return to the small one to do good, and it is sustained in him. He delivers and saves, yet returns to his corruption. Who is the small one who turns to the opposite? He inherits the generation of the world. This one has a beautiful redness <note>original: "pumka shapira"</note> to perform judgment and to do good in his deeds. His eyes are eyes of tears, sitting upon their fullness, rising and descending. One is of a green hue and goes in their garden. At the hour when the "horn" is angry, it is inclined downward. 

In its perfection, the redness is like a rose. When this is in the "horn," the thread returns to be round like an Alexandrian. Like doors were his eyes, such as those that are supported to see points in three colors; all of them were happy in the heart. All of his face is such that people gaze at them. The eyes of these rise in their sockets to the right, and a casting down descends at night. A great circle in the sapphire, and all those below rise. These rise and those descend. Those who are wise rise and give remembrance to one another. 

Because of this, his marks rise in length upward. The depths of his eyes hint at mercy—not blackness nor redness, but between two colors. The "daughter of the eye" <note>the pupil</note> pushes away all the countenances of the world. The redness is inclined, the moon is for him, and he who walks round and round—all is the secret of the life of the guilty. They are commanded to see his openings; they see in them a hidden mercy. 

He arranges for the Crown <term>Crown: Keter, the highest of the ten Sefirot or divine emanations</term> strength, and casting down, and gift, and anger. The beauty of his eyes is full and meritorious for those who serve them, a covering for their life. All this he acquires for his fellow. And it is written: "His eyes move" <note>cf. Proverbs 6:13</note>, drawing near and distancing all the countenances of the world. All of them are included in the covering of the hair of the dew. It was moist with the nuances of the taste. 

The color of his countenance is like a dream of the first ones. Afterward, the countenances of the first study: his color is greenish-gold. Like the palms of the hands is his color, and beautiful gold in the collections. His color is gold like the depths. And like the nests upon his eyes, his color is closed gold. Like a moist violet, his color is gold inclined upon the shaved parts of his heart. His color is Tarshish-gold <note>a precious stone, possibly chrysolite or aquamarine</note> upon the two arms. All these various colors were marked.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And Jethro Heard**<-

The spirit of this [feature] is the master of the spirit. Blessed are those wise ones to whom all is handed over, to know until this point the spirit of the wise. From here onwards, it is through the secret of the lips. Following the letter *Dalet* <note>The fourth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, often representing the "poor" or "doorway" in mystical thought</note> which is included in this spirit:

If the lips are large, this is a man who is a "hurler of stones" <note>original: *ma'il bilista*; an idiom for someone who speaks recklessly or aggressively</note>, lacking wisdom and lacking fear of his Master. He is a master of dispute; everything between this [lip] and that [lip] speaks words that despise the "utterance of the lips." For such a person, he destroys the spiritual levels. Even when he labors in the Torah, he hides secrets from every master of the *Lutcha* <term>Lutcha: a Zoharic term for specific physical traits that reveal the soul's character</term>; his cup is hidden and he does not hate what is in his heart. This relies on the letter *Pe* <note>The letter representing the mouth (*Peh*)</note> which is included after the letter *Lamed*, but is not included after the letter *Samekh*. This is one who appears to be righteous and fears the dew <note>original: *metala*; possibly meaning he fears Heaven or is cautious</note>, but he does not know how to labor [in Torah] because all his words are in his mouth and not in his body. If the lips are old and moved <note>perhaps wrinkled or displaced</note> and they are thin, this is a man of excessive anger, a master of willfulness. He cannot endure a word. He is a master of an evil *Lutcha*, like a merchant <note>original: *praktein*</note> without any support at all; at times he engages in mockery. This is a man one should distance oneself from.

When his image is filled with hair, which is an evil *Lutcha*, he is like a merchant who has no support and engages in dispute. He dreams of worldly vessels. One can see in his lips that he "winks with his eyes"; regarding this it is said: **"A wicked man hardens his face"** <note>Proverbs 21:29</note>. This is in the spirit of the letter *Pe* in its teachings, and it is not included after the letter *Samekh* at all. And sometimes it joins after the *Dalet*. After the letter *Lamed* it is included. One whose [lips] are large and thick, he has a palm <note>or "clapping"</note> in his heart and an abundance in his spirit. One whose [lips] are small and stand upon the foundation of the heart in their awakening, he merits to labor in everything. This spirit is the letter *Yod* which is included in all other letters.

Until here are the secrets of the countenances <note>original: *dioknin*</note> for a man. From here onwards are other secrets in the "lower signs" of the Master, which do not stand within the face, but are to know the secrets that are divided among the higher levels in the times and seasons for this world, though [most] do not merit them. Rabbi Shimon said: "My sons, you are meritorious in this world and in the world to come, and my eyes are meritorious to be able to see this until I enter that world to come." For from the "Coming World" <note>a play on the word *Ati*, "coming," and *Atik*, "Ancient"</note> the Ancient of Days <note>The highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note> is called. This is the meaning of the verse: **"You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows"** <note>Psalms 23:5</note>. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, calls out concerning us: **"Open the gates, that the righteous nation which keeps faith may enter in"** <note>Isaiah 26:2</note>.

They also opened [the discussion] and said: It is written, **"And they had the hands of a man under their wings"** <note>Ezekiel 1:8</note>. The companions established this verse as referring to the hands that receive the masters of repentance <note>those who return to God</note> which are under the "wings" of the Holy One. These hands are the memories and the higher secrets of the "measuring reed" <note>original: *kanya*</note> in a man. When they are found outside and inside, and in that palm <note>original: *kaf*</note> and reed, when a man opens it, all the forms of the higher secrets from above and all the forms of the secrets of the world below are arranged within it. Everything is engraved in man, who is the "collector" <note>original: *kaos*</note> of all the names of God <note>original: *Elohim*</note>. Because of this, it is called a "Palm" (*Kaf*), and the spirit of the palm is the letter *Dalet* which engraves. Regarding this it is written: **"So God created man in His own image"** <note>Genesis 1:27</note>. This is the secret of the letter *Kaf* <note>The Hebrew letter *Kaf* also means "palm"</note>. This letter contains higher secrets and higher forms. In this palm hang the Ten Utterances <note>The ten phrases by which the world was created</note> from the Speech and the Word—five on the right and five on the left—and they are one in one spirit.

We have learned: It is written, **"And I also will strike my hands together"** <note>Ezekiel 21:22; original: *kaf kapi*</note>. This refers to the division [of the hands], and they will cry out in their spirits from the world that passes away, and the descent of Israel to destruction among the nations. But when they are joined as one, it is written: **"One gold pan [palm] of ten shekels, full of incense"** <note>Numbers 7:14</note>. This hints at a single source. And when they were in a single source, it is written: **"So God created man in His own image..."** "God created man"—this is the division that joins in the inner spirit. "The man"—this is the spirit of male and female as one, in the likeness of God. We have spoken of the spirit of the palm. When he was created to be clothed, what is written of him? **"You have clothed me with skin and flesh..."** <note>Job 10:11</note>

## Jethro (Yitro)

And so on. And this is what is written: what is the "complete" man? If you say he is merely skin, flesh, bones, and sinews—it is not so! For truly, the "Adam" <note>The Hebrew word for "Man," referring here to the spiritual essence</note> is nothing other than the soul. These things mentioned—the skin, flesh, bones, and sinews—are all nothing but a garment. They are the "vessels" of the human being, but they are not the Adam himself. 

When this Adam departs <note>at death</note>, he strips off these garments that he wore. The skin that the human was clothed in, and all those bones and sinews, are all based on the secret of Higher Wisdom, modeled after the pattern Above. 

The **skin** is modeled after the pattern Above, just as the Master established in the heavens: "You stretch out the heavens like a curtain" <note>Psalm 104:2</note>. These are the "skins" of the garments Above that cover the upper realms—the expansion of the heavens, which is the outer garment. The "curtains" are the inner garments, the membrane that covers the interior. 

The **sinews and bones** are the Chariots <note>term: Chariots (Merkavot); the divine structures or vehicles that carry the Divine Presence</note> and all those hosts that stand within. All of these are garments for the innermost part: the Spirit of Adam, which is the interior essence. 

So it is with the spirit below. Adam is the interior essence within; his garments are modeled after the pattern Above. The bones and sinews are like what we said: they are considered the Chariots and the Legions. The **flesh** covers those legions and chariots and stands on the outside. And this spirit of Adam, when it is drawn toward the "Other Side" <note>term: Other Side (Sitra Achra); the realm of evil or impurity</note>, the skin that covers everything is like those firmaments that cover everything. All these are garments to be looked upon <note>to gain insight</note>. The interior within is the spirit of Adam, and the entire spirit below is modeled after the pattern Above.

> And for this reason: "God created man in His own image, in the image of God He created him" (Genesis 1:27).

The word "God" appears twice here: one corresponding to the Male and one corresponding to the Female. The spirit of Adam below is entirely life-force, like the Spirit Above. 

The **firmament** that covers everything has marks engraved upon it, so that one may look and know through those marks the hidden matters and secrets. These are the marks of the stars and constellations that are engraved and fixed in this firmament that covers the outside. 

The **skin**, which is the outer covering of a human being, is likewise a "firmament" that covers everything; it contains marks and lines. These are the "stars and constellations" of the skin. It is a firmament to be looked upon to know hidden matters and secrets—just like the stars and constellations—and the "wise of heart" <note>Exodus 35:10; those with intuitive spiritual wisdom</note> gaze at them. They look at them to gain knowledge by observing the face through the secrets we have mentioned, when they are radiant and exist without anger. This spirit is white, red, or dark-red like the stars. 

In a time when anger rules over a person, no investigation is permitted to know anything, for permission is not given to rule or know at a time when the [angry] eye rules the firmament. But the observation of the face must be in the way of truth, at a time when the face is radiant and the person is stable. Then those marks and all that observation can be found with greater clarity—even though in all states, all those wisdoms can be found.

The **lines of the hands** and the **lines of the fingers** within all stand upon other secrets to know hidden things. These are the "stars" that shine, and one looks at them as "constellations" in the higher lights. The fingers stand upon higher secrets. 

The **fingernails** that stand at the ends on the outside: it has already been established that they are in those secrets of the "back side" <note>the external, less holy dimensions</note> facing outward. In them are secrets for those who gaze at the nails by the light of "the other thing" <note>a euphemism for the Sitra Achra</note> that rules over them, and those lines lead to another path. 

On the nails, there are times when thin white spots appear on them; these are like the "offspring of lentils" <note>small, round spots</note>, and they are sunken into the nail. These white spots are different from others that are not sunken but remain forever. In those that are not sunken, there is no substance. But those that are sunken, white like a lentil-shape, have substance. This is a sign for a person regarding what will happen to them and the power of the hour that has arrived. A decree has been decreed upon him, and he should settle his mind because of it. The lines of the hands are based on higher secrets.

## Fifth Section: Yitro

->**The Fifth: Yitro**<-

In the folds <note>Aramaic: *atchafayin*, referring to the creases of the forehead or palms</note> within all of them, there are large lines and small lines, and very fine, sublime lines between them. Just as in those folds where there are small lines tucked away and hidden, sometimes these fine markings are not visible in the folds at all. This person stands constantly over deeds that are on the side of <note>Psalm 29</note> **the Merciful One**. In this fold, there are lines that are added to be doubled within them. This is how they are to be looked at: only if they are added. If two knots <note>Aramaic: *chumrechin*, likely small bumps or intersections of lines</note> are added upon that line that is doubled, a path will not be prepared for him, and if he acts, he will not succeed. Except for those that stand in the space between one marking and another; when he turns to look back and those markings are found to be recognizable to them, he will succeed in his path. And this is the sign: three and three, open and long in length, and the spirit of those who have small thoughts. And one time in length and two and two open: the path and the hearing of words will be in a near time, but he will have no benefit from them. Four markings in length and four markings open: a path is prepared for him, he will labor much in the path, and in the end, there will be benefit and profit. The sign of the *Chutma* <note>Aramaic: *Chutma* usually means nose, but here serves as a category for a specific facial feature or line type</note> shows to the knowledgeable that between the small and the large it is narrow, and small markings open below and four above like a palm, and four in length: in his days he will be in his house and [wealth] will enter to him. And the path is prepared before him, yet he does not wish to act; but if he lives and acts, he will succeed in that path. No harm will be done to him, and the entry is established. The sign of the *Chutma* which is thin and straight: in the fold that is folded, for this fold stands to perform a deed in that [matter] to achieve merit. *Chutma*: one line stands in length between the lines of his olive-shape <note>referring to the shape of the eyes or a specific facial mound</note>; those who see look and depart from him, and he is afraid and does not act, and the thought arises not to do it. *Chutma*: two lines in length that stand when stretched out; he looks back and they are not established in him, and he desires thoughts for the moment not to do it. And he does not think of the Moon <note>symbolizing the Shekhinah or the receptive spiritual realm</note> at all, but sees from a thought of double pressure and toil; harm is in the reflection, and he does not merit the *Chutma*. And he lives. Three markings in length and his palms are two or three; when stretched out he looks back in his walking; a man of open pressure <note>Aramaic: *pachicha*, meaning wise or alert</note> and he thinks thoughts, and all those thoughts for those on the side of the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note> are established in his hand, and the knots are established for them thus. *Chutma*: four, not five, in length when they are stretched out as we said; the *Chutma* is the fruit of the laborers <margin>Look! Open</margin>. *Chutma* in three, *Chutma* in length: they are not secret and not moist. This is a man whose merit for bread is not found in them, and his *Dikanos* <note>Greek: *dekanos*, here meaning the facial appearance or "governor" of the face</note> and the space between his eyes are red. And the secret of this is to be included in it the letter *Yod* <note>The first letter of the Divine Name, representing the point of wisdom</note>, and these are the judgments in the fold of his day.

## Jethro (Yitro)

The small is like the great, and the sign for this is: **"You shall hear the small as well as the great."** <note>Deuteronomy 1:17</note> These two wisdoms are within this secret, and they come from the secrets of the changes of the Master, and they are not among the secrets of the broken decrees. From all of them, the <term>lines</term> <note>original: "shartutin" - the creases or markings on the palm or forehead</note> are not known except to those who investigate the generations of man, as it is written: **"This is the book of the generations of Adam"** <note>Genesis 5:1</note> from the day he was created. For all of them are spirit, not in the manner of human offspring, but in all those <term>images</term> <note>original: "dyoknin" - spiritual likenesses or archetypes</note> of the wise and in all those things we have said. And in these generations of the lines of the hands, which are seen in the inner secrets as they appear. **"This is the book of the generations of Adam"** refers to the lines and the turning of secrets for the wise of heart. There are five letters like five gates to know the wisdom in its clarity.

### The First Gate
The letter *Resh* <note>The Zohar often uses Hebrew letters as codes for specific personality types or palm configurations</note> is found in the secret of thin lines and large lines, and they are all mixed with one another. The large lines contain all those two as one and two as a pair, joined to one another. This is the secret of the "Woman of Valor" and the secret of the letter *Dalet* and the letter *Resh*, and it pushes away the *Dalet* and the *Vav* and kills these two wisdoms. The pair is killed as one, killing the *Resh*, and its sign is the letter *Heh*. This person has a hidden circle facing these large lines. And all those small lines on the entire right side do not circle it. Sometimes there is one thin line above as one, and one thin line below that holds those two large lines of the pair; there is one thin line that crosses over it and strikes it, and in its lowliness, it is like a window and like a spider. Behold, sometimes he comes in weeping and sometimes in joy. This person's heart is not sufficiently open; all his weeping is dependent on joy, and when he is in joy, he is dependent on weeping. He is always steady in joy and sometimes in weeping; this is a stone in whiteness, and it is worthy for others to look upon them. This stands in change. He does not wish to fight. He is quick to embrace the matters of the world. The letter *Aleph* awakens to do good for him from above. And on the right, this embrace is beloved, and his beauty is spread out; the eye stands toward his direction and is heard. It rises in love. This person's embrace sometimes consumes his heart to the point of gnashing. And then three small lines are found that pass through that thin line below, over those two of their pairs, and the spirit that joins with the *Resh*. This is the craftsman of the house, from this spirit, this matter, this benefit, this haste, this good eye, this beloved one who spreads wealth; this one consumes his heart and returns to gnashing.

### The Second Gate
The letter *Dalet* is on the right, hinted at in the summer heat. And on the right, when three large lines are found as a pair, and two large ones as one, and one hot one below that holds those two of their pairs, and one for the Master does not hold them—this person has a defect in his seed from the side of his father or the side of his mother. And then there are found below those three lines of the pair, two thin lines that hold them from below. This person's embrace is like a vessel; he fixes his deeds before men, but his heart is not truth. And sometimes he goes out and returns to fix things; then those two lines are found as one, holding those of the pair. And then we say they are burdened in their furrows, thin ones as one, and three thin ones as a pair, and this spirit joins with the letter *Resh*. And when his embrace is good and he returns as we said, his embrace is fixed as this herald, and it joins with the letter *Dalet* for the <term>Crown</term> <note>original: "Keter" - the highest of the ten Sefirot, representing Divine Will</note>. When this embrace is fixed, all his threads and all his deeds are always in study; he eats them in his embrace in the day as is proper, because that defect has not yet been attributed to him. From all the changes, these whose seed is disqualified for three generations are not attributed to that defect in the writing.

## Main Text (Zohar)

And because of this, we require in every translation a complete man, complete in everything. Thus, all the works of the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> are complete in the world as a perfect existence. It was taught that Rabbi Yose said: One day I was standing before Rabbi Yehuda and I asked him about what is written: 
> Who has ascended into heaven and descended? Who has gathered the wind in his fists? etc. <note>Proverbs 30:4</note> 

What is he saying when he says "Who" <note>original: "Mi"</note>? He said to me: What is the perfection of the holy faith <note>original: "Meimanuta"</note> that is found in that place? Just as it is above, in every place where perfection is found, it is called **"Who"**. I said to him: If so, why did they translate it as "judgment" and not "perfection"? He said to me: There is no awe except in a place where perfection is found, and in every place where perfection is found, it is called **"Who"**, as it is written: 
> Lift up your eyes on high and see: **Who** created these? <note>Isaiah 40:26</note> 

See, there is no lack; it implies that where he sees a lack [it is not there], but in a place where there is no lack, perfection is found. Therefore, "Who has ascended into heaven and descended?" Rabbi Yose said: This is Moses, as it is written: 
> And Moses ascended to God. <note>Exodus 19:3</note> 

"Who has gathered the wind in his fists?" This is Aaron, as it is written: 
> And his fists full of finely ground incense. <note>Leviticus 16:12</note> 

"Who has wrapped the waters in a garment?" This is Elijah, as it is written: 
> There shall not be dew nor rain these years, except according to my word. <note>1 Kings 17:1</note> 

"Who has established all the ends of the earth?" This is Abraham, as it is written: 
> These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created <note>Genesis 2:4</note> 

Do not read it as "when they were created" <note>original: "be-hibare'am"</note> but rather "through Abraham" <note>original: "be-Abraham"</note>. He taught and opened his discourse, saying: "Who has ascended into heaven?" This is the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term>, as it is written of Him: 
> God has ascended with a shout. <note>Psalms 47:6</note> 

"Who has ascended" is a rectification. In the secret of "backwards" and "five" with a shout, and "descended" in the secret of "and they were finished," we have distinguished it for him... with a shout. "Who has gathered the wind in his fists?" This is the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term>, as it is written: 
> In whose hand is the soul of every living thing. <note>Job 12:10</note> 

"Who has wrapped the waters in a garment?" This is the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term>, of whom it is written: "He binds up the waters in His thick clouds." "Who has established all the ends of the earth?" This is the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term>, of whom it is written: "He establishes strength and there shall be peace for earth and heaven." And further, he said: "Who has ascended into heaven and descended?" These are the four foundations of the world: **Fire, Air, Water, and Earth**. Rabbi Yose said: I am amazed by Rabbi Yose, for all these words were not established so well until Rabbi Shimon [bar Yochai] placed his hands on the head of Rabbi Yose and blessed him, saying: You have spoken well, and so it is. He asked him: From where do you know this? He replied: Thus I learned from the Sage, who said that the support of the way of faith is found [here].

Once, Rabbi Shimon was sitting at the gate of Sepphoris. Rabbi Yitzhak said to him: Regarding Elijah, of whom Rabbi Yose said "Who has ascended into heaven and descended," etc.—one time he said this refers to Moses, another time he said it is the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term>, and another time he said these are the four foundations: Fire, Air, Water, and Earth. Yet, [Rabbi Shimon] blessed him for it! He replied: Certainly he spoke well, and so it is; they are all one matter, and all these words are fulfilled in the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term>, and they all rise in one scale of the balance. Rabbi Yitzhak was moved by the beauty of Rabbi Shimon's words and said: Certainly it is so, and I have learned this from the Master once before. See: "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created"—do not read "when they were created" but "through Abraham," as it is written: 
> I said, the world shall be built with kindness <note>Psalms 89:3; "Kindness" or "Chesed" is the attribute associated with Abraham</note>. 

But all is well. What does the end of the verse mean where it is written: 
> What is His name, and what is His son’s name, if you know? <note>Proverbs 30:4</note> 

"What is His name" is immediate, but "what is His son's name"—what does this mean? He said to him: I am teaching the spirit of the matter to my son, Rabbi Eleazar. He said to him: Let the Master tell us, for we are thirsting for the teaching before the Master. He said: These and those are words [of truth] and it is not hidden. See if it is fit to be remembered. He said to him: Certainly, on this day you have said it. He said to him: The secret of the matter is that which is written: 
> Israel is My son, My firstborn. <note>Exodus 4:22</note> 

And it is written: 
> Israel, in whom I will be glorified <term>Beauty/Tiferet</term>. <note>Isaiah 49:3</note> 

And he is like the spirit <note>Air/Ruach</note>, and this is why he is called "My son." He said: In the day to come, for I know this spirit... Rabbi Yitzhak did not remember it, but his mind went to his house and he slept. They showed him in his dream a book of Aggadah <note>homiletic traditions</note> in which was written: **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note> and **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note> are like the Sanctuary. He woke up and went to Rabbi Yitzhak, and what he saw, he saw in the world, and from here he said: From within it, the book is given.

It concludes by linking the concept of the "Son" to the people of Israel and the Sefirah of Tiferet (Beauty).</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And Jethro Heard**<-

As a flower of beauty that is shown before **YHWH** <note>original: "יהוה", the Tetragrammaton, the four-letter Name of God</note>, it is written that **Wisdom** <note>original: "Chokhmah", the sefirah of divine intuition</note> is forever, and **Beauty** <note>original: "Tiferet", the sefirah representing the heart and harmony</note> is below, as a call to their prophets. And so it was found according to his mouth. Rabbi Shimon said to him: Until now you have been riding to know the difference between the brain and the scale <note>likely referring to the balance between different mystical faculties</note>. And behold, everything has been shown to you, as it is written: *What is His name, and what is His son’s name, if you know?* <note>Proverbs 30:4</note>. **Wisdom** is His name, and **Beauty** is His son.

**And Moses** went up to God. Fortunate is the portion of Moses, who merited this glory—that the Torah was given through his hand. When Rabbi Judah appeared, he said: Come and see the difference between Moses and the rest of the world's inhabitants. When other people "ascend," they ascend to wealth, they ascend to greatness, or they ascend to royalty. But when Moses ascended, what is written of him? *And Moses went up to God* <note>Exodus 19:3</note>. Fortunate is his portion! Rabbi Yose said: From here the companions have taught: "He who comes to purify himself is assisted from Heaven," for it is written, *And Moses went up to God*, and what is written immediately after? *And the Lord called to him*. For whoever desires to draw near, they draw him near. *And the Lord called to him from the mountain, saying: Thus shall you say to the house of Jacob, etc.* Rabbi Isaac opened with the verse: *The kindnesses of Your people shall be remembered; Your companions shall be established.* Fortunate is the portion of that man whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires and brings close to the Master of the Palaces, the Holy Temple. For anyone whom He desires for His service is marked by signs from above to know that he has been chosen before the Holy King. He ascends to the Master of the Dwellings, and anyone found in him is marked for reward in all the upper gates, and no one can stay his hand. Rabbi Judah said: Fortunate is the portion of Moses, of whom it is written: *The kindnesses of Your people shall be remembered and brought near*, as it is written: *And He called to him from the mountain*. He reached out his staff to take hold of the Lord, and he stood and took it. And behold: *And the Lord called to him from the mountain, saying: Thus shall you say to the house of Jacob*—these are the **Females** <note>original: "Nukva", the feminine aspect of the divine or the women of Israel</note>—*and tell the children of Israel*—these are the **Males** <note>original: "Dechrinin"</note>. Rabbi Shimon said: "Thus shall you say" refers to the whole, as in "Thus shall you bless," and it is written, *And Your pious ones shall bless You* <note>Psalm 145:10</note>, meaning they shall bless "Koh" <note>The word "Thus" (Koh) is also a mystical name for the Shekhinah</note>. *Thus shall you say to the house of Jacob* in a whisper, for this is from the side of the **Female** aspect. *And tell the children of Israel* in a whisper, and he shall tell the council of His covenant, as it is written: *I have declared this day to the Lord your God* <note>Deuteronomy 26:3</note>. To the children of Israel, the **Males**, who come from the side of Mercy. Rabbi Isaac said: That phrase, what is its meaning? *I have declared this day to the Lord your God*—it should have said "to the Lord *our* God." Rabbi Shimon said to him: Does this stand as your learning? Come and see what is written: *For the Lord your God brings you into a good land...* and *which the Lord your God gives to you*, and *For the Lord your God is a consuming fire*. All of them are like this. Rather, thus we have learned: Anyone who dwells in the Land of Israel is like one who has a God, and anyone who dwells outside the Land is like one who has no God. What is the reason? Because the holy seed ascends to the Holy Land. And its writing is like a release. And this depends on that. And he says "Your God" to those who were destined to enter the Holy Land and receive even the **Divine Presence** <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note>. And the reason he did not say "Our God" is because Moses did not merit to enter the Land, and therefore "Your God" is certainly used in every place because they were destined to enter there. But here it is written: Fortunate is the portion of the priest who shall be in those days, and the desire of these: *I have declared this day to the Lord your God*. They are as one, and they say "Your God" and not "Our God." Rather, they need to show and confess that because of **Lovingkindness** <note>original: "Chesed"</note> they merited all this, and they entered that land, and He did all those good things with them. And because of this, they would say these words to the priest and not to another man, as it is written: *I have declared this day to the Lord your God*. This is certainly because he comes from the side of **Lovingkindness**. *Thus shall you say to the house of Jacob*—to that place which is below them. *And tell the children of Israel*—to that place of peace that is prepared for them. For behold, Jacob and Israel are two **Levels** <note>original: "Darjin"</note> to be established, and they ascend in one degree, but Israel is called the perfection of all.

## Main Text (Zohar)

69

->**And Jethro Heard**<-

They investigated. "And tell the children of Israel" <note>Exodus 19:3</note>—this is to show wisdom and to seal the hidden things of wisdom, the goodness and truth that the Holy One, Blessed be He, performed for them, as it is written: **"And He declared to you His covenant"** <note>Deuteronomy 4:13</note>. It was taught: Rabbi Yose said, "Once I was traveling on the road and Rabbi Hiyya my son was with me. While we were walking, we found a man who was holding herbs in his field. We approached him and said to him, 'Man, why do you have this bundle of herbal knots?' He raised his head and said nothing. I asked a second time, and he did not return a voice nor say anything. I said to Rabbi Hiyya my son, 'Is this man a fool, a sorcerer, or a sage?' He remained silent near us. Afterward, he gathered those herbs, turned them over, and blew upon their leaves. They flew off. He said to us, 'I see those who would lower themselves below, and donkeys would carry them—those who consider themselves wise teachers. I am concerned for you; now, stay a hundred paces away from here!'"

We distanced ourselves from everything. Behold, we saw that the spirit of one herb that was near you rose up in your cloaks. You must remain distant for three days, or eat these cloves of garlic and you will be healed. We were all stunned by them, for they were standing before us and we did not know them, and we were bound in a trance <note>original: *za'afa*, a state of spiritual agitation or stupor</note> for a long time. Afterward, we woke up. That man said to us, "The paths are twisted with you, for you were found by me, and behold, you saw that your bodies were changed." While we were walking, he said to us, "Any man who does not converse like another man is according to the measure of his 'nets' <note>original: *hermoy*, likely referring to spiritual traps or the 'nets' of one's character/disposition</note>, for one must establish a man according to his nets, and a stranger according to his nets." I said to Rabbi Hiyya my son, "This is what is written: **'Thus shall you say to the house of Jacob, and tell the children of Israel'**" <note>Exodus 19:3</note>.

He said to us, "You saw that I did not raise my head and did not converse with you because here is the wisdom of herbs from the gardens of desire <note>original: *dakni derakhi*</note>. I go here among the 'nets' of all the herbs, in which there is truth and wisdom in everything. There is a dwelling place among them. And this herb that you saw me blowing on its leaves—those that flew off—they are 'weeping life' <note>original: *bekiti chait*</note>, a single hole, and it guards the scattered and the empty place for the sake of one scent and a mixture. From that scent, a man emerges with two streaks <note>or 'runners'</note>, and a path is found in his hand. Every day he shakes us, and here I gather these herbs. Look after this, and you will see the division of this herb and what higher teaching is revealed in the world, though there is no one who knows its 'nets'."

We followed him until we were walking in a dark forest. He saw a hole in the dust and turned toward it. He found a <unclear>creature</unclear> and a snake came out, and its head was very large. He took a palm branch and tied it to a dead kid <note>young goat</note>. He said to us, "Follow the snake to its house." We saw that place like a <unclear>hidden chamber</unclear> behind a wall. He took a branch and lit the gathered herbs of that place for their scent. He said to us, "From what you see, do not imagine or speak anything." Meanwhile, the snake was bound by its knots <note>or 'incense'</note> like a <term>Kosta</term> <note>an aromatic plant/root used in incense</note> from that herb, and it turned the belly of life. It entered that eye of desire, and we heard a voice that made every place tremble. We wanted to leave, but that man grabbed our hands and said, "Do not fear, come close to me." Meanwhile, he bent over the water and drank. That man took some of that herb and turned it in his hand as before. He entered that eye of desire through a small opening. We saw a man emerge from before the eye with two streaks and a <unclear>shroud</unclear> surrounding him. He entered that eye of desire and emerged three times. He was saying, "A knot, a knot! Woe to the snake that shall be a place of wisdom for him." Meanwhile, the scent was uprooted from its place, and the man and the snake emerged; they bent over and both died. We were very afraid. That man said to us, "Is it not the power of the herb that I gathered before you? Because of this, I did not converse with you and did not raise my head when you approached me." He said to us, "It is a profane thing and we know it."

The narrative emphasizes that true wisdom requires silence, specific conditions, and protection from spiritual contamination.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And human beings should know that everything the Holy One, Blessed be He, planted on the earth and all His matters are not revealed to the world, and their forms are words that change through His great wisdom. The Holy One, Blessed be He, hid this wisdom from human beings so that they would not stray from His paths and become arrogant through that wisdom and conceal Him. When we returned and looked at the words before Adam, we saw that he was wise; he knew it and left it to be feared. For there was not great wisdom in him, and his voice was like a great blindness <note>original: "כסמיה" - likely referring to a lack of clarity or a hidden state</note>. Come and see from Enoch, for in every place where the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires to purify a person, they are purified from the side of the "Dinur" <note>The River of Fire</note>, the upper matters that were entrusted to him. For that matter which was entrusted to him, when it was mixed with the filth of the impure spirit, the person was looked upon and a warm prayer [was offered]—blessed be the Merciful One for the assistance.

->**You**<-

**You** have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself <note>Exodus 19:4</note>. It is with Mercy <note>The "Heavens" often represent the Sefirah of Tiferet, which is the attribute of Mercy</note>. Just as the eagle is found to have mercy toward its children but judgment toward others, so the Holy One, Blessed be He, is found with mercy toward Israel and judgment toward the nations who worship idols. Rabbi Eleazar was traveling from Cappadocia to Lydda, and Rabbi Yossi and Rabbi Hiyya were traveling with him. They rose at dawn when the day brightened and were walking. Behold, the lion is on the right, the ox is on the left; the eagle is the place of the male <note>The balancing central pillar</note>. Rabbi Eleazar said to him: In this matter, it is precisely clarified: just as the flight of the eagle is entirely mercy for its children and judgment for others, so the Holy One, Blessed be He, guided Israel with mercy and with judgment toward others, as it is written: "I bore you on eagles' wings." And it is written: "As an eagle stirs up its nest"—from here we learn that the eagle is called Mercy. For it is written: "The way of an eagle in the heavens"—literally in the heavens. And because of this, the lion is to the right, the ox is to the left, and the eagle is between them, and He desired for them Kindness <term>Chesed: the attribute of expansive love</term> which includes them all, and all were perfected in it, as it is written: "And upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man above it" <note>Ezekiel 1:26</note>.

"We have a little sister"—this is the Assembly of Israel <note>The Shekhinah</note>, who is called "sister" to the Holy One, Blessed be He. "And she has no breasts"—this is what we have learned: that in the time they approached and drew near to Mount Sinai, they had no merits or good deeds to protect them, as it is written "she has no breasts," for these are the strength and the beauty of the lower realm. And there is no beauty below except for these [merits]. "What shall we do for our sister"—what will be done as a miracle in the hour that the Holy One, Blessed be He, reveals Himself on Mount Sinai to speak the words of the Torah, and their souls fly out from them? Rabbi Yossi said: At that hour when Israel approached Mount Sinai, on that night they gathered three times, for they did not see their own worthiness, and angels came upon them and received Israel with love—those angels above and Israel below. And Israel was crowned with seventy crowns on that night, and the supernal angels were saying: "We have a little sister and she has no breasts," for they have no merits or good deeds. "What shall we do for our sister"—meaning, what honor and greatness shall we perform for this sister of ours on the day the Holy One, Blessed be He, reveals the Torah to her?

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Yitro (Jethro), specifically focusing on the Revelation at Sinai. It explores the interplay between the divine attributes of Judgment (Gevurah) and Mercy (Rachamim) during the giving of the Ten Commandments.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And Jethro Heard**<-

On Mount Sinai, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: HaKadosh Baruch Hu</note> called to all His heavenly entourage. He said to them: "Now Jethro, who was a priest to idolatry, has come. The nations did not know My laws, and I desired to reveal Myself to them. Had I descended upon them with the power of **Strength** <note>Gevurah - the attribute of strict justice</note>, they would not have been able to endure it. But I shall reveal Myself to them with **Mercy** <note>Rachamim</note>, and they shall receive My laws." This is the meaning of "And it came to pass on the third day"—like the third day of creation, where Mercy was not suppressed. From where do we know this? As it is written:
> And the Lord descended upon Mount Sinai (Exodus 19:20)

And it is written that the Holy One, Blessed be He, revealed Himself to Israel and strengthened them with Mercy at first, and afterwards the Torah was given to them from the side of Strength. On the third day, it was seen that for this reason He would take them. **"When it was morning"**—as it is written, "morning" corresponds to the merit of Abraham. At first, a thick cloud was found and **Kindness** <note>Chesed</note> was not revealed. And when is Kindness revealed? When "the morning is light," for when it shines, Kindness goes out into the world and judgments are removed. But at the time when the morning does not shine, the judgments are not yet removed, as it is written:
> When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy (Job 38:7)

Once those stars pass and the brilliance shines, as the verse says "morning," the darkness is gone and Kindness is awakened in the lower world. At that hour, it is written **"When it was morning"**—up to this point, "when it was morning." And once the morning passes, it is not found after three days. "When it was morning" was the time the Holy One, Blessed be He, prepared to reveal Himself on Mount Sinai. Three times "when it was morning" occurred when the merit of Abraham was awakened, as it is written of him:
> And Abraham rose early in the morning (Genesis 22:3)

**"And there were thunders and lightnings"**—Rabbi Abba said: These are two voices that returned to become one. This one emerges from that one: wind from water, and water from wind. Two that are one, and one that contains two. Rabbi Yose said: "Thunders" <note>literally "Voices"</note> is one, which is a mighty sound that never ceases. For we have learned: in the four seasons of the year, the voice is interrupted and then judgments are awakened in the world. But this Voice, which includes other voices, never ceases and never passes from its perfect existence and its strength. It is the Voice of voices, the Voice of the Voice, the Voice that includes all other voices. Rabbi Yehuda said: There is no voice except from the side of wind and water, and a voice creates a voice, and they do not overlap. And it is written "thunders and lightnings." Rabbi Yose said: This is what is written:
> He makes lightnings for the rain (Psalms 135:7)

God is like the crown of the knot of Mercy in wisdom that does not sink. We have learned that Rabbi Yehuda says: The Torah was given through the "rain" of Strength. Rabbi Yose said to him: "If so, it would be from the Left Side <note>the side of Judgment</note>." He replied: "It returned to the Right," as it is written:
> From His right hand went a fiery law for them (Deuteronomy 33:2)

And it is written:
> Your right hand, O Lord, is glorious in power (Exodus 15:6)

And so on. We find that it appeared on the Right, and at times on the Left—for Strength is on the Left. **"And a thick cloud upon the mount"** etc. (Exodus 19:16)—a strong cloud, powerful in darkness that does not cease. "And the voice of the shofar exceeding loud"—from where did that strong cloud emerge? That voice. Then:
> And it came to pass, when you heard the voice out of the midst of the darkness (Deuteronomy 5:20)

Rabbi Yehuda said: There were three darknesses, as it is written:
> Darkness, clouds, and thick darkness (Deuteronomy 4:11)

And that Voice emerged from them, from all of them. Rabbi Yose said: It was the innermost of them all, as it is written of it:
> A great voice, and it did not cease (Deuteronomy 5:19)

Rabbi Isaac said: It is written:
> And all the people saw the voices (Exodus 20:15)

"Saw"? It should have said "heard"! Rather, we have learned: those voices were engraved <note>original: mitgalfi</note> in that darkness, cloud, and thick darkness, and they appeared as a body is seen. They saw what they saw and heard what they heard from within that darkness, thick darkness, and cloud. And from within that vision they saw, they were illuminated with a supernal light and knew what later generations would not know. They all saw "face to face":
> The Lord spoke with you face to face in the mount (Deuteronomy 5:4)

And they truly saw. We have learned from Rabbi Yose: From the light of those voices—for there was no voice that did not shine with a light—all the prophets and all the wise men and all the generations to come until the King Messiah gazed upon it. And for this reason it is written, "And all the people saw the voices." They truly saw.

<summary>This page discusses the mystical mechanics of the Revelation at Sinai, explaining how God balanced Judgment and Mercy so Israel could receive the Torah. It highlights the miracle of "seeing the voices," where the Israelites perceived divine sound as visual light, granting them a level of prophecy surpassing future generations.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion "Yitro" (Jethro), specifically focusing on the Revelation at Mount Sinai. It transitions from the general awe of the Israelites to a deep analysis of the "voices" and "sounds" heard during the giving of the Ten Commandments, drawing parallels to the prophetic vision of Ezekiel.</meta>

->And Jethro Heard<-

## Main Text (Zohar)

Truly far off. Rabbi Eleazar said: "And all the time, far off." It was far because it was distant from them—those voices which they did not see, which resembled the other two <note>Likely referring to higher spiritual emanations or "Sefirot"</note>. **The voices** <note>Exodus 20:15</note>—all of them, and one was **with the Lord** <note>The Hebrew word "Et" (את) is interpreted here as an inclusionary particle, suggesting something additional joined to the Divine Name</note>.
It is not written "the sword of the Lord," but "with the Lord." So too here, "and all the people saw the voices"—it does not just say "voices," but "with [Et] the voices." This is like the phrase **"the [Et] heavens and the [Et] earth,"** for they are seen as one and were given together. Just as it says **"your [Et] father and your [Et] mother,"** and **"the [Et] Lord your God."** All of these are to be looked upon as one single place. So too here, "with the voices" comes to include that other voice which is written of for the prophets, through which they see and contemplate with great wisdom, and every generation and the nations and the cycles of time that are to come into the world.

**And the torches**—as before, in the radiance of the torches. They are all one, but from here they were established in their proper forms to be seen below, and so it was. **And the sound of the Shofar.** Rabbi Isaac taught: It is written, "And the word of God we have heard"—this means we heard everything, and it was meritorious, and it did not leave you. Rabbi Judah said: "The sound of the Shofar." Why the Shofar? Rather, it is that voice which is called "Shofar," as it is written:
> Then you shall sound the Shofar-blast in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 25:9)

At that time, it is called a Shofar. Rabbi Yose said: Just as a Shofar brings out sound, breath, and moisture <note>original: "v'rucha v'maya"</note>, so too here, everything is included in this, and from this, other voices emerge. Rabbi Eleazar said: The voice that comes out of the Shofar implies that the Shofar is one thing and the voice comes out of it, yet the Shofar remains in its existence; therefore it is written "the sound of the Shofar." Rabbi Judah said: When "the sound of the Shofar" is written in a deficient form <note>referring to Hebrew spelling variations</note>, it refers to the time before the kings reigned, and the Shofar is over you to improve <note>A wordplay on "Shofar" and "Shefer" (to improve/beautify)</note> before Me to be nourished. Rabbi Shimon said: "The sound of the Shofar" is the place from which the voice emerges, and it is called Shofar. Furthermore, Rabbi Shimon said: Come and see, "the sound of the Shofar" below is the voice of which it is written:
> For man does not live by bread alone, but by everything that proceeds out of the mouth of the Lord (Deuteronomy 8:3)

What is "that which proceeds out of the mouth of the Lord"? This is the sound of the Shofar; it is greater than all other lower sounds and stronger than all of them, as it is written, "and the sound of the Shofar was very strong," whereas regarding all other voices, "very strong" is not said. Rabbi Shimon said: Like this sound of the Shofar, everything is repeated, and it is written "a great voice." A "still small voice" <note>1 Kings 19:12</note> is like a light that is pure, thin, and more refined than anything. "Stillness" <note>original: "Demamah"</note>. What is "stillness"? Rabbi Shimon said: Blessed is the person who keeps silence and muzzles his mouth, as it is said:
> I said, I will guard my ways, that I sin not with my tongue; I will guard my mouth with a muzzle (Psalms 39:2)

Stillness is a silence that is not heard outside. **And the people saw, and they trembled, and they stood far off**—they feared what they saw. "And they trembled"—all of them, and those who trembled were the "Mixed Multitude" <note>The non-Israelites who left Egypt with the Hebrews</note> from the sound of the voices. Come and see what is written in Ezekiel when he saw the mighty acts of the Holy One, blessed be He, in his days, as it is written:
> And I looked, and behold, a stormy wind came out of the north (Ezekiel 1:4)

It was all-encompassing and caused a storm to be seen. Rabbi Yose said: This was to subdue the four kingdoms. Rabbi Judah said: This wind is what awakens the colors of "Gevurah" <term>Gevurah: The Divine attribute of Strength or Judgment</term> above. "From the north"—it does not say "from north," but "from *the* north," referring to that which is known above, the side that is hidden and concealed above. **A great cloud, and a fire flaring up**—which was attached to it and yet not attached. It was attached to its sides to awaken judgment, which is prepared three times a day; that harsh judgment is nourished by the engraved teeth from the side of that Gevurah and the "fire flaring up" because it is awakened in the world. And what covers it? That of which it is written, **and a brightness was round about it**—for that radiance which surrounds it from all sides covers it and prepares it so that the judgment should not be too harsh, so that one can look upon it. **And from the midst of it as the color of the Chashmal**—from the midst and the inside, like the color of the Chashmal. What is Chashmal? Rabbi Judah said: "Living creatures of fire that speak" <term>Chayyot Esh Memallelot: A traditional acronym for Chashmal, suggesting angelic beings that are sometimes silent and sometimes speak</term>. Come and see, Rabbi Yose said: From what was there to be covered? As it is written:
> From the midst of it as the color of the Chashmal, out of the midst of the fire (Ezekiel 1:4)

And not "the Chashmal" alone. "Out of the midst of the fire"—from there, the silence <note>original: "Chash"</note> and the speech <note>original: "Mal"</note> are within the Chashmal. This Chashmal comes after four levels, as it is written: "a stormy wind," "a great cloud," "a fire flaring up," and "a brightness round about it."

<summary>This page provides a mystical analysis of the sounds heard at Sinai, identifying the "Sound of the Shofar" as a supreme divine voice. It links the imagery of the Revelation to Ezekiel's vision of the Chariot, explaining the four elements (wind, cloud, fire, and brightness) as stages of Divine judgment and revelation.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on Parashat Yitro, specifically focusing on the Revelation at Mount Sinai. It draws a sharp contrast between the direct, communal vision of the Israelites at Sinai and the individual, mediated prophetic vision of Ezekiel by the river Chebar.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And Jethro Heard**<-

He is good and delights like one who rises out of the fire; that is what is written concerning it: **and a fire flaring up** <note>original: "v'esh mitlakhat"; Ezekiel 1:4</note>. It was taught that Rabbi Yose bar Yehuda said: Israel saw what Ezekiel did not see, and they all cleaved to the Higher Wisdom <term>Chokhmah: the second Sephirah, representing the flash of divine intuition</term> through the levels of the voices. Israel saw them as a solid mountain. And through these levels, the Torah was given, for it is written: **the sound of the shofar** <note>Exodus 19:19</note>. Ezekiel, in contrast to them, saw five levels which are described as: **a stormy wind, a great cloud, and a fire flaring up, and a brightness was around it, and the color of the Chashmal** <note>original: "Chashmal" refers to a glowing metallic luster or angelic being; Ezekiel 1:4</note>.

Rabbi Eleazar said: It is written **as the appearance of a man** regarding the Glory of the Lord, but in Ezekiel it is written **as the appearance of the likeness of a human form** <note>Ezekiel 1:26</note>. There were many partitions, like a person who sees a man behind a wall. Rabbi Yehuda said: What Israel saw, no other prophet saw; and all that Moses saw, no other prophet or any other person saw. And all their portions were unique, as it is written of him: **and he was there with the Lord** <note>Exodus 34:28</note>, not like other seers, as it is said, but through riddles.

Rabbi Yose said: Come and see, it is written: **The word of the Lord came expressly** <note>Ezekiel 1:3</note>, coming like a reflection to awaken. Rabbi Yehuda said: This was to establish the "voice from below" <note>The physical or earthly manifestation of prophecy</note> which was necessary for the sake of Israel, to make it known that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not abandon them; in every place where Israel is scattered, the Shekhinah <term>Shekhinah: the Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</term> is with them.

Rabbi Eleazar said: The double expression **came expressly** <note>original: "Hayoh Hayah"</note> confirms that he saw and yet did not see; he heard voices in those words but did not grasp the essence. But regarding Israel, what is written of them? **And all the people saw the voices** <note>Exodus 20:15</note>. Each and every one saw according to what was fitting for him. For it was taught: they all stood in rows upon rows and boundaries upon boundaries, and as was fitting for them, each one saw.

Rabbi Shimon said: The heads of the people were all precise, the heads of the elders were all precise; they were all precise—sixty levels to the right and sixty levels to the left. Then the prophets were all before the Lord, in a chariot-like arrangement <note>original: "ribas ratikas," likely referring to the celestial chariot/Merkavah</note> surrounding Him. Five levels to the right and eight levels to the left they saw. This is what is written: they surrounded the center, and one was in the midst of it... these five levels to the left, all levels were established for the sake of the world.

In exchange for these, Israel will inherit five worlds, a coveted crown upon which all commandments, all merits, and all inheritances depend, which are found in the good portion of Israel. It was taught: at that hour, the Holy One, blessed be He, was revealed like a mountain of their doubts <note>or "mountain of their clarity"</note>; each one saw as one sees light through a glass lamp <note>original: "ashishita"</note>. And from that light, each and every one saw what Ezekiel—as it were—did not see. From the nine levels of those supernal voices, they were awakened as one, as it is said: **And all the people saw the voices.**

He said to him: Like the appearance of the stars they were revealed in His chariots and no more, and he saw as one sees behind many walls. Rabbi Yehuda said: Blessed is the generation of which it is written: **the Lord came down in the sight of all the people upon Mount Sinai** <note>Exodus 19:11</note>. Come and see, it is written: **from His right hand went a fiery law for them** <note>Deuteronomy 33:2</note>. From the right side, that which was revealed was revealed. What is the difference between the voice and the trembling?

Rabbi Yose said: Everything at Sinai was the movement and beauty of the King, as it is written: **He bowed the heavens also, and came down; and darkness was under His feet** <note>Psalms 18:10</note>, like the form of the living creatures of the body. But in Ezekiel it is written: **and the hand of the Lord was upon him** <note>Ezekiel 1:3</note>, meaning a hand was revealed but not the "body." And we have learned: the "Hand of the Lord" above and the "Hand of the Lord" below.

Come and see, it is written: **the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God** <note>Ezekiel 1:1</note>. The word **visions** <note>original: "mar'ot"</note> is written defectively <note>missing a letter in the Hebrew scroll</note> to show it refers to the Shekhinah, for the vision was a single vision. Rabbi Yose said: All of them are the Shekhinah, who is the Bride. Rabbi Yose said: The movement of the King is not like the feet of the King, but within the Bride, it is like the body of the King. Come and see, it is written: **and the anger of the Lord was kindled**, and in Ezekiel it is written: **and the anger of the vision of God was kindled** <note>The text here interprets the prophetic experience as a manifestation of divine attributes</note>. Everything is there in the "vision." What this one saw, that one saw. But the portion of Moses was unique, for there was no faithful power as strong as his. **And the anger of the Lord** is precise; **and the anger of the vision of God** is precise. And it was as one level. But rather thus:

It uses the imagery of the "Hand of God" and the "Shekhinah" to explain the different degrees of divine manifestation.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on Parashat Yitro (Exodus 18:1 - 20:23). It focuses on the distinction between the prophecy of Moses and other prophets like Ezekiel, and the spiritual preparation for receiving the Ten Commandments.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And Jethro Heard**<-

Thus I have seen, though it is not fully explained, I know where it stands. One child <note>A reference to a young student or a mystical "youth" figure often found in Zoharic literature</note> included this and explained it. What is the reason he explained his vessels? Ezekiel and all the other prophets saw their visions for the sake of Israel, so that they would know the belovedness with which the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note> regards them; for the **Divine Presence** <note>original: *Shekhinah*—the feminine, indwelling aspect of God</note> and Her arrangements would dwell among them even in exile. One living creature <note>original: *Chayah*—referring to the angelic beings in Ezekiel's chariot vision</note> was like a throne, and it is written that there were two "sponsors" <note>original: *sandik*—likely referring to supporting angelic forces</note>; this Name was not seen by the students of the Divine Presence there. And if you say it was for the sake of Israel, it was good that the two aspects of the Divine Presence were within them so that the void would not be revealed. This proves that what was revealed to them, they did not previously know. And regarding that which was revealed, what is written? "By the river Chebar" <note>Ezekiel 1:1</note>. Why is it called "Chebar"? Because it had "already" <note>Hebrew: *k'var*</note> been the place where the Divine Presence rested, as it is written, "and the hand of the Lord was upon him there." But not all of them were a crown for the Master. One living creature is written of, "and the likeness of their faces was the likeness of a human" <note>Ezekiel 1:10</note>. First, in the supernal spirit, there are four pillars for the living creatures within, like a holy palace; and they are before the **Ancient of Ancients** <note>original: *Atikin d'Atikin*—the most hidden, primordial level of the Divine</note>, the holy totality of the supernal crown. And Ezekiel saw the likeness of the supernal structures that stood before him from a place that was not so luminous. This proves that just as there is a "knot" above, there is one below them, and so in all the worlds, they are all grasped one within the other. And if you say he saw even higher, we have learned that he stood before the **shining mirror** <note>original: *aspaklaria de-nahara*—the clear, direct prophetic vision unique to Moses</note>, yet all the other prophets only stood within the **mirror that does not shine** <note>original: *aspaklaria de-la nahara*—an indirect or clouded vision</note>, as it is written, "in a vision" <note>Numbers 12:6</note>. And it is written: "If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make Myself known to him in a vision... My servant Moses is not so... mouth to mouth I speak with him" <note>Numbers 12:6-8</note>. One lesson teaches that all prophets compared to him are like a female to a male, as it is written "mouth to mouth I speak with him" in a clear "appearance," whereas for other prophets it says "in a vision (*be-mar'ah*) I make myself known," using a term for a reflected vision. When Ezekiel came, "vision" is not written with the full spelling, but a diminished form, to show it was not a direct sight but a matter of clarity. And all those of that generation of the prophet called out. Because of them, "Joseph lives" <note>a metaphor for the preservation of the righteous foundation</note> and all of Judah were protected; Israel saw the radiance of the glory of the Kingdom. There were no blind, deaf, or crippled among them, as it is written: "And all the people saw the voices" <note>Exodus 20:15</note>, and it is written "they stood at the foot of the mountain." The crippled were healed, for regarding that time it is written: "Then shall the lame man leap as a deer, and the tongue of the dumb sing" <note>Isaiah 35:6</note>...
<note>Biblical quotes: Numbers 12:6-8 regarding Moses' prophecy; Exodus 20:15 regarding the Sinai revelation; Isaiah 35:6 regarding the healing of the infirm.</note>

## **And He Spoke**
"God spoke all these words, saying..." <note>Exodus 20:1</note>. Rabbi Judah opened his discourse: <term>Who can utter the mighty acts of the Lord? Who can show forth all His praise?</term> <note>Psalm 106:2</note>. In how many ways does the **Torah** <note>original: *Oraita*</note> lead a person to the Holy One, Blessed be He, so that he may stand before his Master? In how many ways does it give him counsel so that he does not stray from his paths to the right or to the left? In how many ways does it give him counsel on how to stand before his Master and find favor? For we have learned: there is a King, and the Torah gives thirteen types of counsel to a person to be perfect with his Master. For his Master desires to do good for him in this world and even more so in the **World to Come** <note>original: *Olam Ha-Ba*</note>. For we have learned: everything the Holy One, Blessed be He, does for a person is from those merits he earns for the World to Come. And if you say this world is not for pleasure, we have learned that this world compared to the World to Come is nothing but like a **vestibule** <note>original: *prozdor*</note> before a **palace hall** <note>original: *traklin*</note>. Therefore, the World to Come is for the Holy One, Blessed be He, like a treasure and a dwelling. As it is taught: "Therefore Levi had no portion or inheritance with Israel, for the Lord is his inheritance." And the portion of one who merits to strengthen himself in this supernal dwelling is great. Just as in this world, so in the World to Come, in the supernal holy greatness, as it is written: "I will give them in My house and within My walls a monument and a name (*Yad Vashem*)..." 
<note>Exodus 20:1 begins the Ten Commandments. The Zohar quotes Psalm 106:2 and discusses the paths of Torah and the relationship between this world and the world to come (Olam Ha-Ba) using the analogy of a vestibule and a palace (Pirkei Avot 4:16).</note>

<summary>This page contrasts the indirect prophetic visions of Ezekiel with the direct "shining mirror" prophecy of Moses. It also discusses the spiritual healing of Israel at Mount Sinai and the Torah's role in preparing a person for the World to Come.</summary>
