## Main Text (Zohar)

Fortunate is the portion of that servant whose dwelling is with the King in His palace. <note>Rabbi Hiya begins here</note> Rabbi Hiya said: Fortunate is the portion of that righteous person, as it is written: *Then you shall delight in the Lord.* <note>Isaiah 58:14</note> It does not say "with the Lord," but rather "upon the Lord." What does "upon the Lord" mean? It refers to the place where the upper and lower worlds are supported and depend upon—that place of which it is written, *Water shall flow from his buckets,* and it is written, *A river went out from Eden.* It stands before the Holy One, Blessed be He, as the most ancient of repairs <note>original: "tikkun vatikin"</note>, because they gaze upon that hidden radiance from which all those crowns are gathered and hidden.

Come and see, said <term>Rabbi Shimon</term> <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the central figure of the Zohar</note>: We have learned regarding this verse, *Then you shall delight in the Lord*, that the continuation of the verse says: *And I will cause you to ride upon the high places of the earth.* This refers to that place called the "Upper Earth." And that place which is "upon the earth" is the "Heaven" <note>original: "Shamayim"</note>, and this is the meaning of *upon the Lord.* Rabbi Hiya said: If it were not written *Then you shall delight*, but rather *Then you shall delight upon the Lord*, it would mean the Heaven, as it is written: *Who rides the heavens to your help.* *And I will cause you to ride upon the high places of the earth* refers to the "Land of the Living." This implies that the Children of Israel ascend to their place, which is the Upper Heaven and the Upper Earth. And the word that <term>Rabbi Shimon</term> spoke is indeed so, and all is one, as it is written: *And he came to the Ancient of Days...* <note>Daniel 7:13</note> and all these matters ascend to a single place.

<term>Rabbi Abba</term> said to Rabbi Shimon: Let the Master tell me about this entire verse and how you establish it, as it is written:
> *Then you shall delight in the Lord, and I will cause you to ride upon the high places of the earth, and I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father.* <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>

He said to him: All of this refers to the lower realm, that it should be strengthened so they may merit "upon the Lord," the place of Upper Life. And it is written, *And he came to the Ancient of Days,* "upon the high places of the earth," as has been said. *And I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father,* as it is written:
> *May God give you of the dew of heaven...* <note>Genesis 27:28</note>

And this is the "heritage of Jacob." For the blessing with which Isaac blessed Jacob refers to this "Heaven." And he blessed him with a blessing that is destined for the children of Jacob to see at that time, as it is written: *May God give to you.* To "you" and not to another. *From the dew of heaven*—for by it the dead are destined to be brought to life, for it issues from the "Ancient One" <note>Atika, the highest aspect of Divinity</note> to the "Small Face" <note>Zeir Anpin, the emotive attributes of God</note> and is prepared in this Heaven. Rabbi Abba was found saying: Now everything is understood, and it is found that Isaac's blessing was more sublime than we had thought. *A Psalm of David: I will extol You, O Lord... who can utter... who can declare His mighty acts.* <note>Psalm 145:1, 106:2</note>

<term>Rabbi Hiya</term> said: All is like "plucking ears of grain with your hand," for His mighty acts <note>Gevurot</note> clash and emerge from a single <term>Gevurah</term> <note>The attribute of Strength/Judgment</term>. And come and see: one Upper Gevurah is a crown of crowns; they are crowned and emerge from it as eight weapons <note>or gates</note> from here and from there. They emerge in a hidden manner. Each one is called a "Mighty Act" <note>Gevurah</note>, and each one is guarded in a carved, shining chamber <note>original: "kardituta"</note>, and all are called "the mighty acts of the Lord." <term>Rabbi Hiya</term> said: "His mighty acts" <note>Gevurotav</note> is written defectively <note>missing a letter</note>, because they are all included in One. *Who can show forth all His praise?* This refers to the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence</note>, for she is the glory of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: *His praise fills the earth.*

<term>Rabbi Shimon</term> said: It is written, *And a river went out of Eden to water the garden...* <note>Genesis 2:10</note> [The text discusses the names of the rivers]. These are the names they are called. And so said Rav Hamnuna the Elder: When it goes out, it is heard. What is the "Heaven" of that river that goes out? Rabbi Shimon said: *Yukhal* is its name, as it is written *Until he is able [yukhal] forever...* and it is written, *It shall not cease from yielding fruit.* What is the reason it does not cease? Because it is "able forever." And regarding this it is written: *And like a spring of water, whose waters do not fail.* And because of this it is written, *And it flows,* and it does not stop. Come and see, said Rabbi Shimon, it is written:

**And God spoke** all these words, saying... <note>Exodus 20:1</note> "And He spoke" was in order to announce the words. For come and see: at the moment the Holy One, Blessed be He, revealed Himself and arranged the King, the upper and lower beings trembled, and the souls of Israel departed. And come and see: that Word was flying from the firmament downwards, engraved in the four directions of the world, ascending and descending. When it ascended, it was found awakening to be proclaimed.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And Jethro Heard**<-

In that upper world, wisdom was found through hints to Israel, and their souls and wisdom returned to them, and they were engraved after them in the laws of wisdom. And so it was with every single word. Rabbi Shimeon said: Every single word that was spoken was accompanied by all those musical accents <note>The "Ta'amim" or cantillation marks, which in Kabbalah represent the highest level of textual meaning</note>, and all those hidden, stored, deep mysteries and secrets, in such love that no word was left out of the collective whole. And at the moment that word went out to be established, every image was engraved after it below. In that word were seventy branches that ascended into the body, and fifty crowns minus one <note>49 crowns, corresponding to the 49 days of the Counting of the Omer</note> from the male side, and sixty minus one from the other side, like a hammer that strikes with joy, like a pen upon a crown—as it is said: 
> "Is not My word like fire, says the Lord, and like a hammer that breaks the rock in pieces?" <note>Jeremiah 23:29</note>
And all of Israel saw with their eyes and perceived, and they all judged after them; all was strength below, and they all received the Torah at Mount Sinai, as it is written: 
> "With him that stands here with us this day... and also with him that is not here with us this day" <note>Deuteronomy 29:14; a reference to the souls of all future generations being present at Sinai</note>
and each and every one saw it as was fitting for him. And they all saw and received the words of God. This is **Strength** <note>Gevurah</note>. The word <term>Et</term> <note>A Hebrew grammatical particle that the Zohar interprets as a sign of inclusion</note> is included in the Right side, as we have learned: <term>Et Ha-Shamayim</term> (the Heavens) refers to the lap and the Right, <term>Ve-Et Ha-Aretz</term> (and the Earth) refers to the lap and the Left, as it is written: 
> "My hand has laid the foundation of the earth, and My right hand has spanned the heavens" <note>Isaiah 48:13</note>
And from my days, the voice of <term>Et</term> was never [just] anything; it is to include all the other crowns of the males that are tied one to another—the Bride, the Bride—all those accents, all those mysteries, all those hidden secrets and depths. To the place—to acquire an inheritance for the Bride, as it is written: 
> "Moses commanded us a law, an inheritance" <note>Deuteronomy 33:4</note>
And if you say He revealed it, why is it necessary for every man? It is written: "The wisdom of your God." Just as wisdom is hidden and concealed, so should these words be hidden and concealed in the heart. So that "God" shall not be mentioned as one [alone], but to include the males in the Bride, to the place where other levels are struck. 

Rabbi Yehuda said: "And God remembered" refers to <term>Strength</term> <note>Gevurah</note>; <term>Et</term> is the Right. This and that are included—the Bride—these are the lower ones, as it is written: 
> "And all the people saw the voices" <note>Exodus 20:15</note>
Each one was silent to include Abraham, as it is written: 
> "And the Lord blessed Abraham in all things (Bakol)" <note>Genesis 24:1</note>
And the males are to include the other crowns that are to be covered. The Bride—these are the lower ones, as it is written: "And all the people saw the voices." To the place, do not rest, as it is written: "A crown of strength is her husband's strength." And it is written elsewhere: "He sent quickly to the lower one." 

Rabbi Isaac said: I saw the seal of the Torah in heat and darkness, as it is written: "And darkness like a cloud that hovered over the heart of heaven, darkness, cloud, and thick fog." For anyone who labors in the Torah is saved from "the other thing" <note>Sitra Achra, the side of evil/impurity</note> that damages and confuses, which all other nations intend for Israel. For by the merit of Abraham, he is saved and protected from the damaging thing. As it was taught: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Abraham: "As long as your children labor in the Torah, they will be merit-worthy [to be saved] from illnesses and [suffering]." It is not the power of Gehenna <note>Purgatory/Hell</note> that rules over them or their enslavement among the nations. He said to Him: "The tied crowns do not raise words; it is better before You that they be consumed by the fire of Gehenna and be enslaved among the nations until they become refined." He said to him: "It is certainly right; vanity, spare him, spare him, for the fire is from the Throne." Life is this fire, the voice of Abraham, as it is written: 
> "Look to the rock from which you were hewn" <note>Isaiah 51:1</note>
And the Lord brought [them] in—this is the Holy One, Blessed be He, who agreed by His hand. 

Rabbi Yehuda said: From the day Israel went out of Egypt until the day the Torah was given, there were fifty days. What is the reason? Rabbi Yehuda said: Because they are the years of the Jubilee, as it is written: 
> "And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year" <note>Leviticus 25:10</note>
The power of that <term>Jubilee</term> <note>Binah, the 50th gate of understanding</note> brought Israel out of Egypt. And if you say it was the literal Jubilee—no, it was from the side of the Jubilee, and from the side of the Jubilee the place was illuminated for its sides. And because of this, these fifty days belong to the Jubilee. Come and see: corresponding to this, fifty times it is mentioned and remembered in the Torah: <term>The Exodus from Egypt</term>. And they were all purified, except for <margin>the one who waits</margin>.

# And Jethro Heard (Vayishma Yitro)

When they descended, the flowing waters <note>original: "nozelim"</note> were strengthened for you. And all those fifty times <note>referring to the fifty gates of understanding or the days of the Omer</note> were for you and no more, because the Bride <note>the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> was adorned and crowned on the day she was completed. And for this reason, the Torah—which comes from **Power** <term>Gevurah: the attribute of judgment/strength</term>—was adorned by the **Right Hand** <term>Chesed: the attribute of mercy/kindness</term>, as it is written: <note>Deuteronomy 33:2</note> **From His right hand went a fiery law for them.** We have learned that there were five voices, and all of them were distilled and included within her, and the Bride was crowned by them. <term>Rabbi Shimon</term> said: At that time when <term>Israel</term> received the Torah, the Bride was never so announced by the crowns of the Holy One, Blessed be He, like a king who is adorned by his son. As it is written: <note>Song of Songs 3:11</note> **Go forth, O daughters of Zion, and gaze upon King Solomon, even upon the crown wherewith his mother hath crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.** This refers to the giving of the Torah, which is the Bride. And the Bride is adorned with five [voices] through His mercies. <term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> said: This is the Bride. <term>Rabbi Judah</term> said: It is written: <note>Song of Songs 1:2</note> **Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth...** Who gives the kiss? May the Merciful One save us, as the companions established: <note>Leviticus 18:9</note> **The nakedness of thy brother and the nakedness of thy mother thou shalt not uncover.** Woe to him who uncovers their nakedness <note>a mystical warning against improper study of the divine secrets</note>.

Come and see: <term>Rabbi Isaac</term> said: At the moment the Holy One, Blessed be He, revealed Himself on Mount Sinai, the mountain trembled. And when Sinai trembled, all the other mountains of the world trembled and were rising and falling until the Holy One, Blessed be He, stretched out His hands over them and they were settled. A herald went forth and proclaimed: <note>Psalm 114:5</note> **What aileth thee, O thou sea, that thou fleest? thou Jordan, that thou turnest backward? Ye mountains, that ye skip like rams?** etc. And at the end: **Tremble, thou earth, at the presence of the Lord.** <term>Rabbi Isaac</term> said: "At the presence of the Lord, tremble, thou earth"—this refers to the Living Creature <note>the Chayah/Holy Beast of the Chariot</note>. "At the presence of the God of Jacob"—this was the Bride for the sake of her children, the double <term>Israel</term>.

It is written: **With the crown wherewith his mother crowned him.** What is this crown? <term>Rabbi Isaac</term> said: As it is written, "and his brothers crown David." Because he is adorned with colors—with red and with green—and all the colors are included in him and awakened in him. <term>Rabbi Judah</term> said: "With the crown wherewith his mother crowned him." Who is the crown? As it is written: <note>Isaiah 49:3</note> **Israel, in whom I will be glorified.** And it is written: "And the olive tree is my glory." <term>Rabbi Isaac</term> said: The Torah comes from fire—**Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah</term> upon **White Fire** <note>representing Mercy</note> to include the Right in the Left, and this Left shall return to the Right, as it is written: **From His right hand went a fiery law for them.**

<term>Rabbi Abba</term> said: At the time we learned, before Him went forth, ascended, and was adorned that smoke in this perfection; it ascended and came, and all the spirits and perfumes of the Garden of Eden ascended in that smoke in a vision of white and red, as it is said: <note>Song of Songs 3:6</note> **Perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant.** Who was that smoke? <term>Rabbi Isaac</term> said: It was the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>Divine Presence</note> who was revealed there as the Bride: <note>Song of Songs 3:6</note> **Who is this that cometh up out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke?** <term>Rabbi Judah</term> said: Why do you need this? The verse itself teaches us: <note>Exodus 19:18</note> **And mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because the Lord descended upon it in fire: and the smoke thereof ascended as the smoke of a furnace.** And the people saw the sign and knew it.

<term>Rabbi Hiyya</term> said: When it was revealed, they were covered and seen as surrounding crowns from this side and from that side. They were revealed and covered in **White Fire**, and their laws were from **Black Fire**, and they were wrapped in surrounding crowns from this side and from that side. <term>Rabbi Abba</term> said: They were in their eyes, and they were peeling back and appearing as these crowns—White Fire and Black Fire—to be strengthened as one, Right and Left, as it is written: <note>Proverbs 3:16</note> **Length of days is in her right hand; and in her left hand...** and it is written: **From His right hand went a fiery law for them.** Rather, it was from the side of **Power** <term>Gevurah/Left</term> and was perfected in the **Right** <term>Chesed</term>. And because of this, there is White Fire and Black Fire. Come and see, it is written: "And you shall take from the soul of the blood there..." <term>Rabbi Judah</term> said: "And you shall take"—one and two they were, but they appeared as one. <term>Rabbi Isaac</term> said: Of their hands they were...

and two...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And Jethro Heard**<-

There were two white stones, and they were written upon internally. The <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kadosh Baruch Hu"</note> wrote with His spirit, and they expanded and were carved into two tablets. Rabbi Judah said: They appeared as sapphires, which are precious stones, as it is written <note>Exodus 32:16</note> **"They were the work of God."** He said to him: If so, if they were sapphire, which is a precious stone from the side of physical stones, they would not be the "work of the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>" <note>i.e., they would be natural rather than supernatural</note>. Rather, how do we establish that "they were the work of God"? The word "They" <note>Hebrew: *Hemah*</note> is precise. <term>Come and see</term> <note>original: "Ta Chazi" - a standard Zoharic opening to a teaching</note> it is written: **"And the writing was the writing of God."** It is written **"The Tablets,"** but it is not written "And the tablets were the work of God." Rabbi Simeon said: It is all one. These two tablets existed before the world was created, and they rose up on the eve of the Sabbath, and the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> made them; they were His own handiwork. How were they made? We have learned: from that <term>Dew</term> <note>original: "Tal"</note> that descends from the <term>Holy Ancient One</term> <note>original: "Atika Kadisha" - the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note>. And when it flows and is drawn toward the Field of Holy Apples <note>a mystical name for the Shekhinah or the Garden of Eden</note>, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> took two drops from it, and they congealed and became two precious stones. He blew upon them and they expanded into two tablets; everything was the "work of God." And the writing was the writing of God, as it is written <note>Exodus 31:18</note> **"written with the finger of God."** This defines these tablets. That flaming fire protected them, as it is said, "It is the finger of God." And each fire rose and protected until a path of perfection was made, as it is written, "And Israel saw the great sea." Rabbi Judah said: **"Engraved [Charut] upon the tablets"**—through their points many wise things were seen from both sides; it was an engraving of engravings. Rabbi Isaac said: From this side the letters were seen, and from the other side what was written on the other side was seen <note>referring to the miracle that the letters were bored through the stone but could be read normally from either side</note>. Rabbi Eleazar said: It was a miracle they were written so that all people could read them, even the cracks, for it was the writing of God. And the spirit of the light—all the people of the world could not know them as they truly were. For those who say they were seen in the points, look, it is written "Engraved *on* the tablets" <note>Hebrew: *Charut al ha-luchot*</note>. <term>Come and see</term>: there are three voices at times: the Right, and the Middle. And those that are found are all in the Right, and from the Right they were established. And those that are found and deposited are all seen, and from there they are included in these tablets; in the end, from this side one sees, and from the other side, and he reads the visions and the repetitions. For we have learned that the fire turned to the Right, as it is written <note>Deuteronomy 33:2</note> **"From His right hand went a fiery law for them."** And because of this, it is the writing of God and His spirit. How so? Whoever was from this side would read the whole: "I am the Lord your God." And through the repetitions he would see and read **"You shall not murder."** He would read **"You shall have no other gods,"** and he would see and read **"You shall not commit adultery."** And he would read **"You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain,"** and he would see and read **"You shall not steal."** And everything was from this side, and likewise for all of them. And then from the other side, and they were all included one in the other, for all was the writing of God. The writing of God and His spirit. <note>Exodus 19:25</note> **"So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them."** Rabbi Jose said: What did he say to them? For it is written "and he spoke to them," but it is not written *what* he said. Rather, <term>come and see</term>: it is a new thing in the world—when joy comes to a person, or a joy that follows pain, he cannot contain it, for his soul would faint. But when he knows it beforehand, he is strengthened in his existence and can endure it. How much more so here, for they saw all that was remembered, and their hearts were strengthened by it, otherwise they could not have endured. How much more so if he had said nothing to them; therefore, "he spoke to them" first so their hearts would be strengthened. And afterward <note>Exodus 20:1</note> **"And God spoke,"** and even so they could not endure. For we have learned: Rabbi Judah said in the name of Rabbi Hiyya, who said in the name of Rabbi Jose: When they heard the word of the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, their souls flew out of them, and the souls of Israel ascended to His <term>Throne of Glory</term> <note>original: "Korsi Yekara"</note> to be found there. Rabbi Hezekiah said... [the text continues regarding the "Leader" and the creation of the world].

<summary>This page describes the supernatural creation of the Ten Commandments from divine "Dew" and fire, explaining how the tablets could be read miraculously from both sides. It also notes that Moses had to prepare the Israelites' hearts before the Revelation so they would not die from the overwhelming joy and awe of the Divine voice.</summary>

# And Jethro Heard

## Main Text (Zohar)

There are those from here and those who spread out, and from the revealed within it. And all the children of Israel shall remember to say: "For the children of Israel are servants to Me." These children of Israel belong to us. At that hour, when the Torah returns, as each and every one of Israel returns to their place, the Torah strengthens and takes hold of them as they return to restore Israel. This is what is written:
> **The Torah of the Lord is perfect, restoring the soul** (Psalms 19:8)
It literally restores the soul. Come and see, it is written: **And Solomon sat on the throne of the Lord as king** (1 Chronicles 29:23), just as it is written that there were six steps to the throne. Rabbi Abba said that the moon <note>original: *siyahra*; a symbol for the Shekhinah or the Divine Presence</note> stood in its fullness. For we have learned that in the days of Solomon, the moon stood in its fullness. And when was it in its fullness? When it stood at the fifteenth generation, as we have learned the lineage: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Judah, Perez, Hezron, Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon, Salmon, Boaz, Obed, Jesse, David, and Solomon. When Solomon came, the moon stood in its fullness. This is what is written: **And Solomon sat on the throne of the Lord as king.** 

In the days of Zedekiah, the moon stood in diminishment <note>original: *pegimuta*; a state of spiritual blemish or waning</note> and was eclipsed, as you said:
> **And the moon shall not cause her light to shine** (Isaiah 13:10)
For we have learned that in the days of Zedekiah, the moon was diminished and the faces of Israel were darkened. Go and count the generations: Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, Ahaziah, Joash, Amaziah <note>The text lists Uzziah</note>, Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, Manasseh, Amon, Josiah. And when Zedekiah came, the moon was diminished and stood in its blemish, as it is written:
> **And he blinded the eyes of Zedekiah** (2 Kings 25:7)
At that time, the sun departed and grew dark. It began to pass away from before the sun, and its light was seized from it and turned toward the sword. This means the moon stood in diminishment. Come and see, at the time when Israel stood at Mount Sinai, the moon began to shine, as it is written:
> **He bowed the heavens and came down** (Psalms 18:10)
What is the meaning of "and came down"? That the sun <note>symbolizing the Holy One, Blessed be He</note> drew near to the moon and the moon began to shine, as it is written:
> **The standard of the camp of Judah toward the east** (Numbers 2:3)
Like Mount Sinai, Judah extended his rule in his kingdom, as it is written:
> **But Judah yet ruleth with God, and is faithful with the saints** (Hosea 11:12)
What is "faithful with the saints"? When the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel: **And you shall be unto Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation** (Exodus 19:6). They were all there, and Judah was there to receive the kingdom, and the moon turned to shine.

---

· **I am** <note>Hebrew: *Anokhi*</note> the Lord your God, who brought you out, etc. (Exodus 20:2). Rabbi Eleazar opened:
> **Hear, my son, the instruction of your father, and forsake not the law of your mother** (Proverbs 1:8)
"Hear, my son, the instruction of your father"—this refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He. "And forsake not the law of your mother"—this refers to the Congregation of Israel <note>the Shekhinah</note>. Why the Congregation of Israel? Because it is the "Congregation" of which it is written, "to prepare the words of understanding." Rabbi Judah said: "The instruction of your father"—this is Wisdom <note>the Sefirah of *Chochmah*</note>. "And forsake not the law of your mother"—this is Understanding <note>the Sefirah of *Binah*</note>. 

Rabbi Isaac said: Both are one and the same matter. For we have learned that the breath comes from Wisdom and the tongue brings it forth. Rabbi Yose said: It comes from Understanding, as it is written, "to prepare the words of understanding," and it is written, "and forsake not the law of your mother." Rabbi Judah said: The Torah is comprised of Wisdom and Understanding, as it is written, "Hear, my son, the instruction of your father, and forsake not the law of your mother." 

Rabbi Abba said: All are included; since these two are included, all are included—in Kindness <note>*Chesed*</note>, in Judgment <note>*Din*</note>, and in Mercy <note>*Rachamim*</note>. In all of them is the perfection that the matter requires. Where the King and the Matron <note>the male and female aspects of the Divine</note> are found, all are found; in the place where these are found, all are found. 

Rabbi Yose said: "Wise" <note>Hebrew: *Chacham*</note> refers to the Shekhinah, as it is written: **the cunning artificer and the eloquent orator** (Isaiah 3:3). "The Lord your God"—this is the Congregation of Israel, "and forsake not the law of your mother." Rabbi Isaac said: "Wise" refers to the Shekhinah and her keen taste, as in "all the wise men of Esau on the way." "The Lord your God," as it is written:
> **Out of heaven He made thee to hear His voice** (Deuteronomy 4:36)
And it is written:
> **You have seen that I have talked with you from heaven** (Exodus 20:19)
"From heaven"—literally from heaven, which is the Holy One, Blessed be He. "Who brought you out of the land of Egypt." "Who" <note>Hebrew: *Asher*</note>—for all things are bound up in Him, as it is written...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar on the portion of Yitro. The text focuses on the "Jubilee" (the 50th gate of understanding) as the source of freedom.</meta>

->## And Jethro Heard<-

From where do we derive the service of freedom? This is the **Jubilee** <note>original: *Yovela*. In Kabbalah, this refers to the Sephirah of Binah (Understanding), the source of liberation</note>, as we have learned: from the side of the **Female** <note>Nukva/Malchut</note> it goes out to the **Male** <note>Zachar/Zeir Anpin</note>, and it went out from Egypt. And because of this, the Exodus from Egypt is mentioned fifty times in the Torah; fifty days to the receiving of the Torah; fifty years for the freedom of servants; "from the house of bondage," as it is written:
> He struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt. <note>Psalms 135:8</note>
And these hanging crowns were established, through which they were distanced from Egypt. Just as there is a house above, there is a house below. The holy house above, as it is written:
> Through wisdom a house is built. <note>Proverbs 24:3</note>
The lower house below is entirely holy, as it is written, "from the house of bondage." The inner meaning of the matter is that all those commandments of the Torah that are distributed on this side were all included in this word. As we have learned: all the commandments of the Torah are distributed within the **Body of the King** <note>The structure of the Sephirot</note>; from here is the belly of the King, and from here the torso, and from here the hands of the King, and from here his legs. And there is no one who goes outside the Body of the King. Therefore, one who sins against the commandments of the Torah is like one who sins against the Body of the King, as it is written:
> And they shall go out and look upon the corpses of the men who have rebelled against Me; for their worm shall not die. <note>Isaiah 66:24</note>
Woe to the guilty who transgress the words of the Torah and do not know what they are doing! For Rabbi Shimon said: "The portion of the wise is greater than that of the prophet," for he is in the place where the hidden joy truly resides. And Rabbi Shimon said: The Holy One, blessed be He, truly hides His joy. With one voice, one voice, the Holy One reveals, as it is written:
> The heavens shall reveal his iniquity, and the earth shall rise up against him. <note>Job 20:27</note>
"The heavens shall reveal his iniquity"—this is the Holy One, blessed be He. "And the earth shall rise up against him"—this is the **Assembly of Israel** <note>Knesset Yisrael/Shekhinah</note>. You find the heavens revealing the joy of the Male, etc., and at the time of freedom, the joy is revealed, and the earth acts softly like a man, as it is written, "and the earth shall rise up against him" to act softly within him. Rabbi Yose said: We have learned from the "heavens" of Rabbi Shimon, for Rabbi Shimon said: Let us say it is like a ladder that is found, as it is written, "this one brought in the sun."

---

**I am** the Lord your God. My wise ones, as we have learned: Abraham had a daughter and her name was "In All" <note>Talmud, Bava Batra 16b</note>, and this is the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence</note>, and she is the Daughter. "The Lord your God," as it is written:
> Israel is My son, My firstborn. <note>Exodus 4:22</note>
And it is written:
> She is a tree of life to those who lay hold of her. <note>Proverbs 3:18</note>
This is the **Mother** <note>Binah</note>. Your service was removed from Egypt from the covenant, as it is written, "And He finished..." <insert>it shall be holy to you</insert>. And it is written, "this one brought in the sun." "And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout the land"—she is the Mother, and because the Mother dwells, the children dwell. And all the worlds are as one in perfection. If the Mother is removed, they are all moved from their places. And it is written:
> You shall not take the mother with the young. <note>Deuteronomy 22:6</note>
And we have learned: a man should not commit a sin below, so that the Mother is not removed from over the children. Rabbi Isaac said: The Bride <note>Kallah</note> is a light voice <note>Kol Kal</note>, the Bride is one, and these words are to gladden the **Field of Apples** <note>Malchut/The Garden of Eden</note>. Blessed are they in this world and in the world to come. Come and see, Rabbi Eleazar said: It is written:
> In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. <note>Genesis 1:1</note>
And it is written:
> On the day that the Lord God made earth and heaven. <note>Genesis 2:4</note>
According to the secret of the explanation, we have learned these verses: that both were created as one. This teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, created in one time the heavens, and created in one time the earth. At first, "the heavens and the earth," and afterwards, "earth and heaven." We have learned: it is written, "In that day I will respond, says the Lord, I will respond to the heavens, and they shall respond to the earth." "I will respond to the heavens" literally, from what is written, "The heavens are My throne." "And they shall respond to the earth"—the earth literally, as it is written, "and the earth is My footstool." The heavens are over them, the earth. And the earth, the earth is over them. For it was taught: when the heavens were established in their arrangements to be prepared over against this earth, and its desire was toward it as one level, which is called **Righteous** <note>Tzadik/Yesod</note>, as it is written: "The righteous is the foundation of the world" <note>Proverbs 10:25</note>. And he cleaved to this earth, and the authority of the King was over the garment... for if the Righteous comes as one, this holy one...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on Parashat Yitro, specifically focusing on the revelation at Mount Sinai and the spiritual definition of "Man" (Adam) as it relates to the Covenant and the Commandments.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->And Jethro Heard<-

The Holy One, blessed be He, pours out tenderness and takes up a great desire in this holy union <note>original: *hadan*, referring to the mystical joining of divine attributes</note>, and He receives everything within this union. Afterwards, from this union below, everything above and below is like a male; for when his desire is to cleave to the female, he brings forth the seed of tenderness from the brain into that place <note>the reproductive organ</note> and bestows it upon the female. From this, the female becomes pregnant. It is found that all the parts of the body are attached to the female, and the female holds everything. In this likeness, everything was established below to crown the first ones; the House of Assembly <note>the *Shekhinah* or the community of Israel</note> receives toward all of them. Rabbi Yose said: Corresponding to all of them. Rabbi Isaac said: It is written, *And the sun set and it went down* <note>Genesis 15:17</note>, and it is written, *And the Lord descended before the eyes of all the people upon Mount Sinai* <note>Exodus 19:11</note>. Come and see: *He bowed the heavens and came down* <note>Psalms 18:10</note>—to where? If you say He descended in His glory upon Mount Sinai, it is written "upon Mount Sinai," but it does not say "before the eyes of all the people *in* Mount Sinai." Rather, *He bowed the heavens and came down*—to where? Rabbi Yose said in the name of Rabbi Judah, who said in the name of Rabbi Hiyya: He descended degree by degree, and moved through the crowns until He cleaved to this union, and then the vision was bound and stood in perfection. Then *He bowed the heavens and came down* to this union, and then it is written *upon Mount Sinai*. What is the "standing" upon Mount Sinai? I would say this is the *Shekhinah* <note>the Divine Presence</note>. Rabbi Chizkiyah said: From here, *Because the Lord descended upon it* <note>Exodus 19:18</note>, and it is written, *For the Lord your God is a consuming fire* <note>Deuteronomy 4:24</note>. And it is written, *And the Lord rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah sulfur and fire from the Lord out of heaven* <note>Genesis 19:24</note>. *And the Lord rained*—this is the union. From what place did He take it? The end of the verse proves it, as it is written: *from the Lord out of heaven*. Literally from heaven. Rabbi Hezekiah said: From here it is written, *And God spoke all [these words]* <note>Exodus 20:1</note>. "All" refers to the totality of everything, for all things depend on "All" <note>the sefirah of Yesod</note>.

**You shall not** have other gods before Me. Rabbi Isaac said: "Other gods" serves to exclude the *Shekhinah*. "Before Me" <note>literally "upon My face"</note> serves to exclude the "Face of the King," through which the Holy King is seen, and these are the Heavens. And He is them. Leave the Heavens, for it is written: *The voice of the Lord is upon the waters* <note>Psalms 29:3</note>. He is the Heavens, the end of the blessing of the Name forever and ever. Come and see, Rabbi Simeon said: Happy are Israel, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, called "Adam" <note>Man</note>, as it is written: *And you My sheep, the sheep of My pasture, are Adam* <note>Ezekiel 34:31</note>. And *When a man [Adam] brings an offering from among you* <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>. What is the reason He called them "Adam"? Because it is written: *But you who cleave to the Lord your God* <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>. *You*, and not the other nations. And because of this, *you* are called "Adam." For it was taught, Rabbi Simeon said: Once a man is separated and set apart, entering into the Covenant <note>the *Brit Milah* or circumcision</note> that was cut with Abraham—as it is written, *And the Lord blessed Abraham with all [Bakol]* <note>Genesis 24:1</note>, and it is written regarding Abraham that he sought to save his soul below—once he merits to fulfill the commandments of the Torah <term>Pekudei Oraita: the 613 religious obligations</term>, he enters into this likeness that is prepared in the body of the King, and then he is called "Adam." And the congregation of Israel is called "Adam." Come and see, it is written regarding Ishmael: *And he shall be a wild man [Pere Adam]* <note>Genesis 16:12</note>. A "wild man," but not "Adam." A "wild man" because he was circumcised <note>separated</note>, yet the Torah of "Adam" was not in him. For it is written: *And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin* <note>Genesis 17:25</note>. Since he was circumcised, he entered into this outer shell <note>original: *sirota*, a lower spiritual level</note>, yet *he shall be a wild man* and not "Adam." *His hand against everyone*—his hand is against all, and he casts down but does not increase, because he did not receive the commandments of the Torah. The outer shell is in him because he was circumcised but was not perfected through the commandments of the Torah. But the children of Israel, who are perfected in all of them, are called "Adam" in truth. And it is written: *For the Lord's portion is His people; Jacob is the lot of His inheritance* <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>. Rav Yessa said: All other matters are merely external garments of "Adam." Rabbi Isaac said: When it is made below, the body is a garment of perfection. Rabbi Judah said: This is what people say, "A knot of beauty in the soul we have merited." Rabbi Judah was traveling from Cappadocia to Lydda to see Rabbi Simeon who was there, and Rabbi Hezekiah was traveling with him. Rabbi Judah said to Rabbi Hezekiah: That which we learned before Rabbi Simeon, that the Foundation <note>the sefirah of *Yesod*</note> flies...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And Jethro Heard**<-

A weak spark flew, and this spark is the secret of the letters *He-Yod-Yod* <note>original: הי"י; likely a permutation of a Divine Name or a mystical acronym</note>. And this is within the secret of the matter. At the end of the verse it is written:
> He shall dwell in the presence of all his brothers (Genesis 16:12)

What is the meaning of "He shall dwell in the presence of all his brothers"? He said to him: Do not err and do not say that these are mere exchanges <note>referring to the exchange of spiritual states or letters</note>. It is written:
> And this is the Torah which Moses set (Deuteronomy 4:44)

The word "set" <note>Hebrew: *Sam*, spelled Shin-Mem</note> is missing a letter; could one say it refers to Moses's wife? <note>A play on *Sam* (set) and *Shem* (name/reputation) or *Simah* (placement)</note>. No, "Moses set" refers to the living woman <note>the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note>. Rabbi Judah opened his discourse and said:
> For it is your life and the length of your days (Deuteronomy 30:20)

How meritorious are those who labor in the Torah and do not separate from it, for they merit two lives: one in this world and one in the world to come. This is why it is written "your life" <note>original: *chayyekha*, which can be read as plural</note>, implying two. And anyone who separates from the Torah is as if he separates from life itself. And one who separates from Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, it is as if he separates from everything! 

When they saw this verse, he opened a gateway, but I was not able to enter it. If the words of the Torah that are hidden are so profound, how much more so is this! Woe to the generation from which Shimon bar Yochai departs! For when Rabbi Shimon is present, he is focused toward the gates of every side and all secrets are revealed. But when we are separated from him, we know nothing and all the springs are stopped up. 

Rabbi Hezekiah said: This is what is written, "And he stopped appearing to him" <note>alluding to the withdrawal of inspiration</note>. A prince was over him and placed a holy covering over his face like a veil <note>Reference to the veil of Moses, Exodus 34:33</note> from which many stars shine, and he is found in his standing. So too is Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai; he is the Master of Stars, he shines for all, and the light never departs from him nor falters in his presence. 

They watched until they reached him. When they reached him, they found him sitting and laboring in the Torah, and he was saying:
> A prayer of the poor man, when he is faint, and pours out his plea before the Lord (Psalms 102:1)

Every prayer of Israel is a prayer, but this one <note>the poor man's</note> rises above them all. What is the reason? Because this prayer ascends to the Throne of Glory of the King and is crowned upon His head. And the Holy One, blessed be He, is certainly found within that prayer. "A prayer of the poor man" is a prayer of "calling" <note>a play on *Ani* (poor) and *Kari* (calling/happening)</note>. "When he is faint" <note>Hebrew: *ya'atof*</note>—this wrapping is not a wrapping of clothes, for he has none. Rather, it is written here "when he is faint/wrapped" (*ya'atof*), and it is written elsewhere:
> The faint ones belonged to Laban (Genesis 30:42)

"And before the Lord he pours out his plea"—that it should be accepted before his Master. This is a word for him before the Holy One, blessed be He; from the side of the world, all this is sustained in him, so that the kindness that sustains the world may be found in the world. The prayer of that poor man—He takes it upon Himself to fulfill it because the poor man is closer to the King than anyone else, as it is written:
> And it shall come to pass, when he cries out to Me, that I will hear; for I am gracious (Exodus 22:26)

Regarding others, sometimes He hears and sometimes He does not hear. What is the reason? Because the fire of the King is with those who are recognized, as it is written:
> With him that is of a contrite and humble spirit (Isaiah 57:15)

And it is written:
> The Lord is near to those of a broken heart (Psalms 34:19)

> A broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise (Psalms 51:19)

From here we have learned: whoever is bent in the end <note>humbled</note>, as in the case of a marriage contract <note>Ketubbah</note>, as it is written: "And this is the contrite and humble spirit." And it is written:
> For the Lord will plead their cause (Proverbs 22:23)

Because their Advocate <note>term: *Apotropas* — a legal guardian or protector</note> is powerful and rules over all; He needs no witnesses and needs no judge to see, nor does the poor man need to wait after a judge. And if one robs the poor, it is as if he robs the soul of a human, as it is written:
> And He will despoil the soul of those that despoil them (Proverbs 22:23)

Furthermore, he said: "A prayer of the poor man"—in every place where "Prayer" is mentioned, it is a high matter, for it ascends to the place where the Holy One, blessed be He, chooses. The Prayer of the Head <note>Tefillin</note> is for the life of the King's prayers. 

Rabbi Shimon the Pious greeted and filled <note>welcomed</note> Rabbi Judah and Rabbi Hezekiah who had reached him. After he finished, he looked at them. He said to them: "Arise, stand up, and let us look at your intentions." They said to him: "Certainly, the Master has opened a high gateway, and we were not able to hear it clearly. What was that sound?" They said to him: "The weak spark flew, and we wish to know the end of the verse where it is written: 'And he shall dwell in the presence of all his brothers.' What is 'in the presence of all his brothers'? For we know the secret of the spark's vessel, but we do not know the vision, for the end of the verse was not visible at its beginning." 

He said to them: "By your lives, it is all one matter, and it ascends degree by degree. Come and see: how many 'Faces' does the Holy One, blessed be He, have? Faces that shine, faces that do not shine. Upper faces, lower faces, faces that are

...for the holy faces are engraved: the inner faces, the male faces, the female faces, and the faces of the left side <note>original: "pinnin"; these refer to the *Partzufim* or Divine Aspects/Countenances in Kabbalistic thought</note>. It is written "Behold, I have blessed him" and it is written there "And he shall be a wild man," "his hand against everyone," etc. And regarding this, it is written "He shall dwell in the presence of all his brothers." For all his other relatives were circumcised and called "righteous converts" and no more, but he was more and rose above them all. Certainly, those who were not circumcised and stand in those engraved faces, those lower faces. And they are dwellings forever from all their faces and from all the faces of the idolatrous nations. This is what is written: "He shall dwell in the presence of all his brothers." ->**YOU SHALL NOT MAKE FOR YOURSELF AN IDOL OR ANY IMAGE**<-

This has been stated and we have established it: all faces <note>images</note> are permitted except for the face of a human being. For that face is said to be the image of the male <note>the Divine Masculine</note>.
**You shall not make for yourself an idol or any image, etc.**
Rabbi Isaac opened:
> Do not let your mouth bring your flesh into sin (Ecclesiastes 5:5) 
How much must a person be careful regarding the words of the Torah! How much must he be careful not to err in them, and not to bring forth from the Torah that which he does not know or did not receive from his teacher. For anyone who says something in the words of Torah that he does not know or did not receive from his teacher, regarding him it is written: "You shall not make for yourself an idol or any image, etc." And he is separated from Him in the World to Come <term>Olam Ha-Ba: the spiritual afterlife</term>, just as it is written regarding this punishment for giving a memory to the image of a man; they give him from that place to be dragged like the dragging of that place whose name is *Kasmaton* <note>A name of a destroying angel or a place of spiritual punishment</note>. Rabbi Yehuda says from here: As we have learned, "Why should God be angry at your voice?" This refers to the soul of a person. Rabbi Hiyya said: It is written, "For the Lord your God is a consuming fire" (Deuteronomy 4:24). What is the reason? Because He is jealous for His Name in general. If because of the faces <note>idols</note> he brings accusation against His Name, it is because he lies against His Name. If because of the Torah we have learned, the Torah is entirely the Holy Name. For you have no word in the Torah that is not included in the Holy Name. And because of this, one must be careful not to err in the Holy Name and not to lie in it. And one who lies against the Supernal King is not allowed into the King’s palaces <note>Divine chambers</note> and is destroyed from the World to Come. Rabbi Abba said: It is written, "You shall not make for yourself an idol or any image." And it is written simply, "Idol."

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the mystical secrets of the Torah, specifically focusing on the sanctity of the Sabbath (Shabbat) and the spiritual mechanics of the Three Meals. ## Main Text (Zohar)

For the Holy Name <note>original: "Shema Kadisha," referring to the Tetragrammaton</note> is not mentioned in the Torah until after two things, as it is written that blessing is found in Him and through Him. Rabbi Shimon said: The Holy Name is not mentioned except over a complete world. As it is written: *In the day that the Lord God made earth and heaven.* <note>Genesis 2:4</note> From here we learn that His Holy Name is not mentioned over emptiness. And it is written: *You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain.* <note>Exodus 20:6</note> And we have learned that Rabbi Yose said: What is the blessing of the Holy Name? It is because from Him, blessing is found for all worlds. And blessing is not found in an empty place, nor does it rest upon it, for it is written: *You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain.*

**Remember** *the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.* <note>Exodus 20:7</note> Rabbi Yitzhak said: It is written, *And God blessed the seventh day...* <note>Genesis 2:3</note> and *Six days you shall gather it, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there shall be none in it.* <note>Exodus 16:26, referring to the Manna</note> Since sustenance <note>Manna</note> was not found on that day, what "blessing" is found in it? Rather, we have learned thus: All blessings of the upper and lower realms are dependent upon the seventh day. And come and see: sustenance is not found on the seventh day because from that day all six days are blessed, as well as the "Upper Days" <note>the higher spiritual emanations</note>, and each one gives sustenance to the lower realm on its own day from the power they received from being blessed on the seventh day.

And because of this, one who is on the level of faith <note>term: "Meheimanuta" — mystical adherence to the divine truth</note> must arrange a table <note>term: "Petura" — the Shabbat table set for a meal</note> that includes the beauty of the Sabbath, so that his table may be blessed all those six days. For at that time, blessing is ready to be found for all six days of the week, and blessing is not found on an empty table. Therefore, one must arrange his table with the completion of the Sabbath with bread and food. Rabbi Yitzhak said: Even on the day of the Sabbath itself. Rabbi Yehuda said: One must take delight in this day and eat three meals on the Sabbath, so that satisfaction and delight may be found in this day in the world.

Rabbi Abba said: [These meals are] to unite with those Upper Days that are blessed from this day. And this day is the "Head" of the *Lesser Countenance* <note>term: "Zeir Anpin" — the emotional attributes of the Divine, centered on Tiferet</note> from the dew of the *Holy Ancient One* <note>term: "Atika Kadisha" — the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine, Keter</note>, the most hidden of all. And He unites with the *Holy Apple Field* <note>term: "Hakla de-Tapuchin" — a mystical name for Malchut, the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> three times from the onset of the Sabbath, so that they may all be blessed as one.

And for this reason, a person must take delight in these three times, for the Upper Faith depends on the *Holy Ancient One*, the *Lesser Countenance*, and the *Field of Apples*. A person must delight in them and rejoice in them. And one who diminishes even one meal from them shows a flaw above, and the punishment of that man is great. Because of this, one must arrange his table three times from the onset of the Sabbath, and his table should not be found empty, so that blessing may rest upon it all the other days of the week. By this act, he shows and establishes the Faith above.

Rabbi Shimon said: One who completes three meals on the Sabbath, a voice goes out and proclaims concerning him: *Then you shall delight in the Lord.* <note>Isaiah 58:14</note> This refers to the first meal, corresponding to the *Holy Ancient One*, the holiest of all. *And I will cause you to ride upon the high places of the earth*—this is the second meal, corresponding to the *Holy Field of Apples*. *And I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father*—this is the perfection of the lower realms <note>the third meal, corresponding to Zeir Anpin/Jacob</note>. One must complete his meals and delight in all of them and rejoice in each one, because it is the Perfect Faith. Therefore, the Sabbath is more precious than all other times and festivals, because everything is found within it, which is not the case for all other times and festivals.

Rabbi Hiyya said: Because in the "tasting" <note>the mention of the day</note> everything is mentioned three times, as it is written: *And God finished on the seventh day... And He rested on the seventh day... And God blessed the seventh day.* <note>Genesis 2:1-3</note> When Rabbi Abba would sit at the Sabbath meal, he would rejoice in each one. He would say: "This is the holy meal of the *Holy Ancient One*, the hidden of all." At the other meal he would say: "This is the meal of the Holy One," and so with all the meals, rejoicing in each one. When he concluded them all—

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And Jethro Heard**<-

Prepare the meal of the faith as the preparation for the King’s meal. • When he would sit, they would proclaim 
over him <note>Isaiah 58:14</note> >Then you shall delight in the Lord, and I will cause you to ride upon the high places of the earth, and I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father.< • 
<term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> said: We have seen how the times of the meals are established. • He said to him: Regarding the night of the Sabbath, it is written, "and I will cause you to ride upon the high places of the earth." • On that night, the <term>Matronita</term> <note>The Divine Presence or Shekhinah, personified as a Queen or Noble Lady</note> is blessed, as are all the <term>Fields of Apple Trees</term> <note>A mystical name for the Garden of Eden or the Shekhinah in her receptive state</note>, and the table of a person is blessed, and the additional soul <note>The "Neshamah Yeteirah" believed to inhabit a person during the Sabbath</note> arrives; that night is the joy of the Queen. • And a person must rejoice in that joy and eat the meal of the Queen according to the custom of the Sabbath. • Regarding the second meal <note>The Sabbath morning meal</note>, it is written, "Then you shall delight in the Lord." • "In the Lord" specifically, for at that hour the <term>Holy Ancient One</term> <note>Atika Kadisha, the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note> is revealed, and all worlds are in joy and perfection; it is the joy of the Precious Ancient One and it is truly His meal. • Regarding the third meal of the Sabbath <note>The afternoon meal</note>, it is written, "and I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father." • This is the meal of the <term>Small Face</term> <note>Zeir Anpin, the aspect of the Divine that interacts more directly with the world, associated with the patriarch Jacob</note> which is then in perfection, and all the times of sustenance are blessed from that perfection. • 
And a person must rejoice in his meal and complete these meals, for they are the meals of perfect faith of the holy seed of Israel; they are a supreme support belonging only to them and not to the idolatrous nations, and because of this it is said <note>Exodus 31:17</note> >It is a sign between Me and the children of Israel.< • Come and see: through these meals, Israel are recognized as the children of the King, that they are from the King’s palace, children of faith. • And one who diminishes even one meal among them shows a flaw Above, and shows himself to not be among the children of the Supreme King, nor from the King’s palace, nor from the holy seed of Israel; and the severity of three things—the judgment of Gehenna <note>Purgatory/Hell</note> and so on—is invoked against him. • And come and see: at all other times and festivals, a person must rejoice himself and also bring joy to the poor. • And if he rejoices alone and does not give to the poor, his punishment is great, for he rejoices alone and gives no joy to others. • Concerning him it is written <note>Malachi 2:3</note> >I will scatter dung upon your faces, even the dung of your festivals.< • But if on the Sabbath he rejoices and celebrates and does not give to others, they do not place a punishment upon him as they do on other times and festivals where it is written "the dung of your festivals." • It says "the dung of your festivals" and not "the dung of your Sabbaths." • And it is written <note>Isaiah 1:14</note> >Your New Moons and your appointed seasons My soul hates.< • But it does not say "Sabbath." • And because of this, it is written, "between Me and the children of Israel." • And since all faith is found on the Sabbath, a person is given an additional soul to illuminate the higher soul—a soul in which all perfection exists, in the likeness of the World to Come. • And because of this, it is called "Shabbat." • What is "Shabbat"? • It is the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, who is perfect from all His sides. • Rabbi Yose said: Certainly it is so. • Woe to the person who does not complete the joy of the Holy King. • And what is His joy? • These three meals of faith. • The meals of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are all within them, and they are all joy upon joy, perfect faith from all sides. • These three days <note>The three meals representing the three patriarchs</note> are crowned by them, and all other days draw nourishment from them, which is not the case with all other festivals and times. • On this day, those days are meritorious; on this day, all judgments are suppressed and are not aroused in the world. • On this day, the Torah is crowned with perfect crowns. • On this day, joy and delight are heard in the strength and power of the worlds. • Come and see: on all six days of the week, when the time for the afternoon prayer arrives, harsh judgment rules and all judgments are aroused. • But on the Sabbath day, when the time for the afternoon prayer arrives, the <term>Will of Wills</term> <note>Ra'ava d'Ra'avin, a moment of supreme Divine favor and grace</note> is found, and the <term>Holy Ancient One</term> reveals His will, and all judgments are suppressed, and favor and joy are found in everything. • And in this Will, Moses the holy, faithful prophet departed from the world, so that it would be known that he did not depart through judgment; and at that hour, through Will...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Sabbath (Shabbat) from the Zohar, specifically focusing on the connection between the Sabbath, the soul of Moses, and the "Ancient Holy One" (Atika Kadisha). It transitions into an interpretation of the "eunuchs" mentioned in Isaiah as a metaphor for Torah scholars.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

In the mystery of the **Ancient Holy One** <note>original: Atika Kadisha; the highest, most hidden emanation of the Divine</note>, his soul went forth, and concerning this it is said: **"And no man knows his burial place"** <note>Deuteronomy 34:6</note>. Just as the Ancient Holy One is the most hidden of all hidden things, unknown to those above or below, so too is this soul—which is the mystery of the lower world according to the supernal knowledge of the Sabbath rest—of which it is written: **"And no man knows his burial place."** It is hidden from all the hidden things of the world, and judgment has no power over it.

This is the portion of Moses. Come and see: on this day [the Sabbath] when the Torah was given, everything was protected—all those commandments, all those decrees and punishments, branches of light that surround every single side. Come and see: the branches that emerge from every single branch, fifty stand because of it, and all branches take hold of them. Come and see: those gates that open on every side, all of them are transmissions and crowns within that light which goes forth and never ceases.

A voice of a herald goes forth: "Awaken, supernal holy ones! Awaken, holy nation that is protected above and below! Awaken the joy of the Primordial Master! Awaken in the joy of the Torah!" Our portion is in three joys, in three [attributes]: Kindness, Wisdom of the Primordial One, and the Faith of the joy of all joys. This is the portion of the holy people of Israel in this world and in the world to come; this is your inheritance above all the nations who worship stars and planets. And concerning this it is written: **"Between Me and the children of Israel"** <note>Exodus 31:17</note>.

Rabbi Judah said: It is certainly written, **"Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy"** <note>Exodus 20:8</note>. And it is written, **"You shall be holy, for I the Lord am holy"** <note>Leviticus 19:2</note>. And it is written, **"And you shall call the Sabbath a delight, and the holy of the Lord honorable"** <note>Isaiah 58:13</note>. Come and see: on this day, all the souls of the righteous delight in the delicacies of the Ancient Holy One, the most hidden of all hidden things. And a spirit from that delight spreads through all worlds, ascending and descending, spreading to all the holy children, to all the guardians of the Torah. In them is perfect rest, and all anger, all judgments, and all harsh labors are gathered away from them. This is what is written: **"On the day that the Lord gives you rest from your sorrow, and from your fear, and from the hard bondage"** <note>Isaiah 14:3</note>.

For this reason, the Sabbath is weighed against the entire Torah, and whoever keeps the Sabbath is as if he kept the entire Torah. And it is written: **"Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who holds it fast; who keeps the Sabbath from profaning it, and keeps his hand from doing any evil"** <note>Isaiah 56:2</note>. It is found that one who keeps the Sabbath is like one who keeps the entire Torah.

Rabbi Yudai was walking to see Rabbi Shimon, and in his hand was a traveler's staff to walk with him on the way. Rabbi Elazar said to him: It is written regarding the atonement of the Sabbath of the Ancient of Days <note>original: Atik Yomin</note>, where it says: **"Thus says the Lord to the eunuchs who keep My Sabbaths... I will give them in My house and within My walls..."** <note>Isaiah 56:4-5</note>. My brother, the voice speaks. He said to him: This commandment is a level tied to the throne, descending from the King of the Torah who desires joy. Furthermore, let us turn to the desire and the crowns and intend toward this. He said: For the sake of the Master, make the way, and the crown of the Master shall gaze upon the **Divine Presence** <note>original: Shekhinta</note>.

He said: You are the King! Here is Hezekiah his companion, and the King did not explain what is meant by **"the eunuchs."** My brother, these "eunuchs" are the companions [the scholars] who gaze upon the Torah and "castrate" themselves <note>i.e., practice sexual abstinence</note> all six days of the week, toiling in the Torah. But on the eve of the Sabbath, they provide themselves for their marital union, because they know the supernal mystery according to the mind of the **Matron** <note>original: Matronita; the Shekhinah</note>, the joy of the King. And those companions who know this mystery direct their hearts to the faith of their Master and are blessed in the strength of their waters [offspring] on that night. And this is what is written: **"Who keep"**—just as it is said, **"And his father kept the matter"** <note>Genesis 37:11; meaning he waited expectantly</note>. And they are certainly called "eunuchs" because of the wisdom of the Sabbath, to find the will of their Master, as it is written: **"And choose that which I desire"**—simply stated. My brother, "that which I desire" refers to the union of the Matron. **"And hold fast to My covenant"**—all kindness is in "My covenant," simply stated. Blessed is the portion of one who strengthens himself in this holiness and knows this mystery.

Come and see, it is written: **"Six days you shall labor and do all your work"** <note>Exodus 20:9</note>...

<meta>This page continues the exposition on the mystical secrets of the Sabbath from the Zohar, specifically focusing on the transition from the six days of labor to the spiritual union of the Sabbath. It follows the previous discussion on the Ten Commandments in Parashat Yitro.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

"...your work; but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God, etc." <note>Exodus 20:10</note>. All your work is prepared during the six days of the labor of the sons of men. And because of this, the companions <note>The circle of scholars surrounding Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> do not discuss these matters except at a time when the labor of the sons of men is not found, but only the labor of the Holy One, Blessed be He. And what is His labor? The **union of the Matronita** <term>The Matron/Queen, referring to the Shekhinah or the Divine Presence in its feminine aspect</term>.

And because of this, the companions occupy themselves with the holiness of their Master and direct their hearts to the commandment of the eve of the Sabbath; for the Sabbath is for rest and for striving on behalf of the King and the Matronita. And because of this, regarding the spirit of the King, it is written of them: "You are children of the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note>. And they shall live, for they are called His children because of the King and the Matronita. **Come and see** <term>A standard Zoharic opening for a mystical exposition</term> that the ancient companions knew how this spirit is prepared.

And for this reason, they are called children of the Holy One, Blessed be He. And thus, those of the world, their buildings are sustained. And when the world rises in **Judgment** <term>Dina: the divine attribute of severity and law</term>, the Holy One, Blessed be He, looks upon those children and has mercy on the world. And regarding this, it is written: "A seed of truth" <note>Jeremiah 2:21</note>—a seed of truth indeed. What is "truth"? It is the holy depth from below. Just as it is said: "You will give truth to Jacob" <note>Micah 7:20</note>. This "truth" is the Holy One, Blessed be He, and all is one. And because of this, it is a seed of truth indeed.

Rabbi Judah said to him: Blessed be the Merciful One who arranged for me to be here! Blessed be the Merciful One who opened my heart to this matter I have heard from your mouth. How great is Rabbi Yochai! Rabbi Shimon said to him: Look at what is in the house. He said to him: I have merited to see. Woe to the children of this world whose ways are like those of beasts; they do not know and do not look, and it would have been better for them had they not been created. Woe to the world when the Master <note>Rabbi Shimon</note> leaves it! Who will be able to reveal **secrets** <term>Razin: the hidden mysteries of the Torah</term>, and who will know them, and who will look into the paths of the Torah?

He said to him: Go out; the world exists only for those companions who strive in the Torah and know the hidden things of the Torah. Indeed, in a bond, the companions should dwell among the people of the land who distort their paths and do not know between right and left, for they are like beasts for whom it is fitting to perform judgment upon them even on the Day of Atonement. And regarding their likeness, it is written: "For they are foolish children" <note>Jeremiah 4:22</note>—literally like the ignorant.

Rabbi Eleazar said: One must be precise in his ways. It is written: "I will give them, in My house and within My walls, a monument and a name better than sons and daughters; I will give **him** an everlasting name" <note>Isaiah 56:5</note>. It should have said "I will give **them**." Why does it say "I will give **him**"? He said to him: Come and see. "I will give them in My house"—what is "My house"? Just as it is said: "In all My house, he is faithful" <note>Numbers 12:7</note>. The name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is called "House." "And within My walls"—as it is said: "Upon your walls, O Jerusalem, I have set watchmen" <note>Isaiah 62:6</note>. "A monument and a name" <note>Hebrew: Yad va-Shem</note>—meaning that holy souls drip from this place, and in that "monument" <note>Yad: literally 'hand' or 'portion'</note> is a portion in perfection, good and full, gathered and stored. "An everlasting name I will give **him**"—to that hidden portion. Kindness shall not be cut off for generations upon generations.

Another explanation: "I will give him"—to the one who knows the spirit of the King and will give them as they ought to be directed. Come and see, Rabbi Shimon said: It is written: "You shall kindle no fire throughout your settlements on the Sabbath day" <note>Exodus 35:3</note>. What is the reason? Because there is no fire below like on this day. And if you say, "But it rises to the Most High?" It says "in all your settlements," and not to the Most High. And that which rises to the Most High rises to subdue the Judgment below. For we have learned: there is a fire that consumes fire, and the fire of the Altar consumes other fire. And because of this, the **Ancient Holy One** <term>Atika Kadisha: the highest, most merciful aspect of the Divine</term> is revealed on this day more than all other days. And at the time when the Ancient One is revealed, no Judgment is found at all. And all the upper and lower worlds are found in complete joy, and Judgment does not rule.

Come and see, it is written: "For six days the Lord made the heavens and the earth" <note>Exodus 20:11</note>. "Six days," and not "*in* six days." And these holy upper days are called the days of the Holy Name; it is included in them and they are included in it. Blessed is the portion of Israel above all the nations who worship idols; concerning them it is written: "But you who held fast to the Lord your God are all alive today" <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>.

It emphasizes the superior spiritual status of those who study the secrets of the Torah compared to the 'ignorant' who live like beasts.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Ten Commandments, specifically focusing on the fifth commandment (Honor your father and mother) and the structural symmetry between the two tablets of the Law.</meta>

# Jethro (Yitro)

**Honor** your father and your mother. Rabbi Hiyya opened his discourse with the verse: <note>Genesis 2:10</note> *And a river went out of Eden to water the garden.* This "river" refers to the gathering of the celestial springs that flow perpetually without ceasing. From the waters of this river, the entire Garden of Eden is irrigated. This river of springs is called **Father** <note>Aramaic: *Ab*. In Kabbalah, this refers to the Sephirah of Hokhmah (Wisdom), the seminal source of flow.</note>. Why is it called this? Because it is the gathering point for the Garden of Eden. Rabbi Abba said: Eden itself is actually called **Father**, because this Eden is found in the place called **Nothingness** <note>Hebrew: *Ayin*. This refers to Keter, the highest, unknowable crown of the Divine.</note>. For this reason, it is called **Father**, and we have established that from the place where everything is found, it is called **You** <note>Hebrew: *Atah*</note>, as it is written: <note>Isaiah 63:16</note> *For You are our Father.*

Rabbi Eleazar said: *Honor your father*—this refers to the Holy One, blessed be He. *And your mother*—this refers to the Assembly of Israel <note>The *Knesset Yisrael*, a mystical term for the Sephirah of Malkhut or the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence.</note>. The word *et* <note>A Hebrew grammatical particle that is untranslatable but often interpreted by the Zohar to include something additional.</note> before "your father" is specifically included to encompass the **Shekhinah**. Rabbi Judah said: *Honor your father* and *your mother* are stated plainly to show that they are as one. The word **Et** serves to include everything above and below.

Rabbi Yose said: What Rabbi Abba said—that everything is found in that place—is correct. For we have learned that regarding the Hidden One who cannot be measured, we say **He** <note>Hebrew: *Hu*</note>. But from the place where measurement begins to be found, we say **You** <note>Hebrew: *Atah*</note>, and He is called **Father**. It is all one. Blessed be His Name forever and to all eternity, Amen.

Rabbi Isaac said: Certainly it is all one. *Honor your father* is the Holy One, blessed be He, and *your mother* is the Assembly of Israel. And the teacher Rabbi Shimon said: It is written <note>Deuteronomy 6:13</note> *You shall fear **et** the Lord your God.* That place is called **Et**. Therefore, the text is phrased cryptically: *Honor your father and your mother* to include everything above and below. Rabbi Isaac said: It also includes one's teacher, who teaches him the way to the World to Come.

Rabbi Judah said: According to the general principle of the Holy One, blessed be He, these first five commandments are as one. The other five were engraved to correspond to them—five within five, like the fingers of the hand. The Sages said they correspond to one another. For we have learned that Rabbi Isaac said in the name of Rabbi Judah: These two are engraved as a single principle. One who kills <note>The 6th commandment: *You shall not murder*</note> diminishes the likeness and the treasure of his Master, as it is written: <note>Genesis 9:6</note> *For in the image of God He made man.* And it is written: <note>Ezekiel 1:26</note> *And upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man.*

Rabbi Hiyya said: It is written <note>Genesis 5:1</note> *This is the book of the generations of Adam, in the day that God created...* One who sheds blood is as if he diminished the celestial likeness and treasure; that is to say, he did not honor this likeness, but rather another likeness. This is implied by what is written: <note>Genesis 9:6</note> *Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed.* What does "by man" mean? It refers to the inner essence that is lost from that blood. Why? Because *in the image of God He made man.* Therefore, these two depend on one another.

**You shall have no other gods** <note>2nd Commandment</note> corresponds to **You shall not commit adultery** <note>7th Commandment</note>. For such a person lies against the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is impressed upon man. And just as there are many merits and treasures dependent on this, one who lies against the Holy One, blessed be He, lies against the King, as it is written: <note>Hosea 5:7</note> *They have dealt treacherously against the Lord, for they have begotten strange children.* And it is written: **You shall not bow down to them nor serve them.**

This also applies to **You shall not take the Name in vain** <note>3rd Commandment</note> which corresponds to **You shall not steal** <note>8th Commandment</note>. It is written: <note>Proverbs 29:24</note> *Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul; he heareth the adjuration and uttereth nothing.* If you say they depend on one another, it is because a thief does not hesitate to swear a false oath; whoever does one, does the other.

**Remember the Sabbath day** <note>4th Commandment</note> corresponds to **You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor** <note>9th Commandment</note>. For Rabbi Yose said: The Sabbath is called a "testimony." A man must testify to it, as it is written: <note>Exodus 20:11</note> *For in six days the Lord made...* The Sabbath is the sum of everything. And Rabbi Yose said: What is the meaning of the verse <note>Micah 7:20</note> *You will give truth to Jacob*? It is as you say: <note>Exodus 31:16</note> *And the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath.* One who bears false witness lies against the Sabbath, which is the testimony of truth. And one who lies against the Sabbath lies against the entire Torah. Therefore, these two depend on one another.

**Honor your father** <note>5th Commandment</note> corresponds to **You shall not covet your neighbor's wife** <note>10th Commandment</note>. And Rabbi Isaac said: *Honor your father* means your literal father. For one who covets a woman and begets a son—that son will honor someone else and not you.
