<meta>This page continues the commentary on the Torah portion Yitro (Jethro), specifically focusing on the mystical significance of the Ten Commandments and the revelation at Mount Sinai. It explores the unity between God, the Torah, and the Divine Name.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And Jethro Heard**<-

"Remember" is written, and it is written "Honor your father..." and "You shall not covet your neighbor’s house..." and this—it is written here concerning "all these words" <note>Exodus 20:1</note> that were spoken before you and now for you. That which was given to you is fitting for you, and you shall not covet that which belongs to another. Certainly, this depends upon that. These first five [commandments] include the other five. Because of this, "From His right hand went a fiery law for them" <note>Deuteronomy 33:2</note>, for all of them were made into a "Right Hand" <note>The 'Right Hand' symbolizes the attribute of Mercy/Chesed</note>. For this reason, the Torah was given as five voices. Rabbi Judah said: All of them were five within five. Corresponding to them are the Five Books of the Torah. Rabbi Eleazar taught: All ten utterances revealed the commandments of the Torah, the decrees and the punishments, the pure and the impure, the branches and the roots, the trees and the herbs, death and life, the sea and the depths. For the Torah opened in a manner corresponding to the [Divine] Name. Just as the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He <term>Aramaic: Kudsha Brich Hu</term>, was revealed through the ten utterances, so too the Torah was revealed through the ten utterances. These ten utterances are the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the Torah and He are all one; it is truly the Holy Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Blessed is the portion of one who merits it! One who merits the Torah merits the Holy Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, itself. Rabbi Yose said: It is truly the Holy One, Blessed be He, for He and His Name are One. Blessed be His Name forever and to all eternity, Amen.

---

**You** shall not make with Me gods of silver and gods of gold <note>Exodus 20:20</note>. Rabbi Yose said: Why is this? Because it is written, "The silver is Mine and the gold is Mine" <note>Haggai 2:8</note>. "With Me" <note>Hebrew: Ati</note> means "under Me" <note>Aramaic: Choti/Tachoti</note>. Rabbi Isaac said: It is written, "Who is mighty like You..." <note>Psalm 89:9</note> and "You are great and Your Name is great in might..." <note>Jeremiah 10:6</note>. "You are great and Your Name is great"—this refers to "The silver is Mine." "In might"—this refers to "The gold is Mine." These two colors <note>The mystical 'colors' or attributes of Mercy (Silver/White) and Judgment (Gold/Red)</note> are not seen and are not separated except when they are engraved in one place. Because of the place where they were revealed to Israel, the colors are seen and not separated; all of Israel saw them and were thus awestruck. Rabbi Judah opened: "The goodness of His kindness..." <note>The text here uses shorthand for a verse regarding joy and salvation</note>. Blessed is the portion of Israel among the idolatrous nations, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, provides them with joy and delight, as it is written, "The goodness of His kindness." Since it says "kindness," why does it then say "as the slain"? Rather, thus said Israel: "When He comes to us with mercy, the goodness of His kindness is upon us; when He comes with judgment, we shall still rejoice." Why? Because these [attributes] are engraved in Him, as it is written: "For He has clothed me with the garments of salvation" <note>Isaiah 61:10</note>. What are "garments of salvation"? They are the colors that were revealed to be gazed upon, as it says, "They shall look upon the Lord." "They shall look"—meaning to gaze [mystically]. One who desires to gaze upon the colors, let him gaze. Why? Because it is written, "He has covered me with the robe of righteousness," precisely because the colors are revealed in Him. "As a bridegroom decks himself with a garland"—this is one color. "And as a bride adorns herself with her jewels"—this is another color. And when the colors are united in Him, the hour is prepared and all take hold to perceive and gaze upon Him. Rabbi Yose said: "The goodness of His kindness" refers to two joys: one in mercy and one even in the portion of judgment. Rabbi Judah said: All of it is joy upon joy and strength. For in the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to sanctify Israel with an adornment greater than all, as it is written: "And the ransomed of the Lord shall return and come to Zion with singing..." <note>Isaiah 35:10</note>. "The ransomed of the Lord shall return"—that is one. "And come to Zion with singing"—that is two. "And everlasting joy shall be upon their heads"—that is three. "They shall obtain gladness and joy"—that is four. These correspond to the four times Israel was scattered among the nations...

---

**And** God spoke all these words <note>Exodus 20:1</note>. "All the words"—all of them are the "Voice," for everything is included within it and established by it. He gathered the spirit of the world... by the spirit of the Holy Name it was born. Wisdom was revealed and gathered; it was revealed by the Holy Spirit of the Throne of Glory... as it is written, like a horse in flame and the moon...

It emphasizes that studying the Torah is equivalent to connecting with the Divine Essence itself.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Ten Commandments from Parashat Yitro. It specifically bridges the concepts of divine wisdom (Chokhmah) with the practical prohibitions against idolatry, linking the structure of the soul and the "Twelve Precepts" to the commandments of "Remember" (Zakhor) and "Keep" (Shamor).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

For all is bound together above in **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note> in the perfection of the secrets of the ascents of the **Throne** <note>Korsaya/The Divine Throne</note> below. The holy visions and the vision established in its arrangements ascended. When the vision is beautiful, like a vision from above reflected below, then it is called **Wise**—the **Wise of Spirit** <note>Chachmei Ruach</note>—where all is as one, including all the letters as the burden of the Torah that emerges from the supernal secret. Within this "pouch" hang secrets upper and lower. The "Wise of Spirit" provide a good place for the righteous who wait for Him and keep the **precepts** <note>Pekudin/Commandments</note> of the Torah as is fitting for them, in goodness as is worthy for the World to Come. And your sign for this is: "No injury." **Wise** <note>Chachmei</note> and **"You shall have no [other gods]"** are stated in the secret of the Torah, and they did not deviate from **Remember** <note>Zakhor - the positive commandments</note> and **Keep** <note>Shamor - the negative commandments</note>.

The "Wise of Spirit" is hidden and concealed like all those levels of the upper world in one general principle. Since it is said "Wise" to connect everything as one in one secret, the "Wise of Spirit" refers to the two thrones. The "Wise" [represented by the letter] *Kaph* of the Throne; "Wise" that is purified from the Sanctuary, and its surroundings are approached by the Holy One. The Sanctuary shines with the teachings that were nullified in that difficult hour. When evil [is removed] from the world, the Holy One, blessed be He, ascends in His glory alone. Then it is said: **Wise**. **"The Lord your God"** is the spirit that ascends in the **Holy Name**.

The letter **Aleph** [of *Elohecha*] is the sea; this is the spirit of the Holy Name in its levels, that it should be one. For example, let there be a spirit of "Wise" to fear the Holy One, blessed be He, and to know that there is a Law and there is a Judge. It descends to bring good to the righteous and retribution to the wicked, because His spirit is the "Lower Hey" [of the Tetragrammaton].
The letter **Kaph** is to sanctify His Holy Name every day, to be sanctified in holy levels, and to forgive the exile toward Him at all times, to ascend to the upper crown. This is the spirit of the Upper Throne over the upper visions as is fitting, and His spirit is the "Upper Hey."
The letter **Yod** is to labor in the Torah day and night, and to decree a decree in the secret of the Mishnah and the "Right Hand," and to draw near with strength. [This includes] the **Tefillin** <note>phylacteries</note>, the **Tzitzit** <note>ritual fringes</note>, and the **Mezuzah**, and to surrender one's soul to the Holy One, blessed be He, and to cleave to Him.

These are the **Twelve Upper Precepts** that are included in three other precepts which are in the spirit of the "Wise," the general principle of **Remember**. This does not change as one, because the *Chayah* [living essence] is the letter **Yod**, the upper spirit, the principle of **Freedom**. Corresponding to the twelve [precepts], there are **Twelve Attributes of Mercy** <note>Michilin de-Rachamei</note> that hang from them, and one that rules over them to make thirteen.

> **You shall have no [other gods]** <note>Exodus 20:3</note>

This is written as a word and hidden, reaching the precepts of the Torah.
The letter **Lamed** [of *Lo*, "No"]: The spirit of not giving honor and greatness to another.
The letter **Aleph**: A tower of fear that ascends like a compass needle that does not swerve here or there to submit to it, just as there is a spirit of a star-tower for another side <note>Sitra Achra/Evil side</note>.
The letter **Lamed**: Not to turn to the image of **idolatry** <note>Avodah Zarah</note>, to meditate on it or to be prideful, so as not to bow down and not to humble oneself to another "god."
The letter **Aleph**: Not to teach the unity of his Master as if it were other errors.
The letter **Aleph**: Not to meditate on another fear to be purified except through Him.
The letter **Aleph**: Not to stray after [false] judgments and to remember the secret of the Image of Man, and not any other image.
The letter **Aleph**: Not to inquire of the dead and not to perform sorcery.
The letter **Aleph**: Not to swear with a mouth in impurity to push away the Other.

Up to here are twelve others which are the precepts of **Keep** <note>Shamor</note>. Corresponding to these twelve hang three hundred and fifty-three precepts of "Keep" which are included in the essence of the twelve. And this spirit is "Wise." Rabbi Shimon said: Furthermore, we have established "Wise" as the general principle of Above, the principle of the upper and lower beings; all of them are holy living beings included in it. Everything is a "Voice in the Spirit" of the Wise. "You shall have no" refers to the spirit of the thirteen lower waters below.

> **You shall not make for yourself a graven image** <note>Exodus 20:4</note>

"Graven image" <note>Pesel</note>—[it is carved] from that upper place, from that holy place. "Pesel" also implies the **refuse** <note>Psultet</note> of holiness, which are the spirits of other errors. This spirit is entirely a "spirit of coldness" and a "stormy wind," like that which comes from the vine, etc. And **"any likeness"**—Heaven forbid—they are ignited. For "Wise" is intended to prevent intermingling, so as not to approach the upper or the lower, and not to draw near to the door of her house. God forbid that one should take a portion in that place. This spirit is under the dominion of anger and wrath. And the prohibition is: "You shall not make for yourself" (one), "a graven image" (two), "and any likeness" (three)—one upon the other.

->**And Jethro Heard**<-

Another interpretation: *Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the third and fourth generation of those who hate Me* (Exodus 20:5). And regarding this, *those who hate Me* refers to the side of the "Serpent" <note>The personification of evil or the 'Other Side' in Kabbalah</note>. It is visited twice and four times, and the previous sins are accounted for—Heaven forbid—even unto the third and fourth generations.

## Main Text (Zohar)

**Do not**—Come and see: *You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain* (Exodus 20:7), and so forth. This cannot be repaired, nor is it fitting to be repaired. Likewise, the atonement for this is through an oath; a person includes themselves in it at times when they are pushed down below as is fitting for them, for they have gone before and become entangled in them, and they stand upon their existence. *You shall not take*—this refers to the spirit. When we see a person who is afraid of the "crawler" <note>The primordial serpent or forces of chaos</note>, the companions have established that it is as if they have accepted everything that is included within it. And this is an oath that sustains the world, which was sunk within the depths of light to sustain the **Holy Name** <note>original: "Shema Kadisha"</note>, as it is written. And upon this, it is engraved in the Name that was revealed within it, as it is written: *And you shall swear, "As the Lord lives"* (Jeremiah 4:2). And whoever fears, fears the abyss. And when the waters seek to rise, they see the engraving and look upon the place where the spirit of the **Holy Name** is engraved, and it is sustained as it is written. It is a gravity to fulfill the **commandment** <note>original: "pekuda"</note> of light, and they return and are fixed and turned back, for the oath mentions the life that turns everything backward. And whoever sees what more the spirit does within that **Evil Inclination** <note>original: "Yetzer Hara"</note> which accuses a person and entices the depths, and seeks to make them fear so that they stumble and transgress the **commandment** of the one who mentions [the Name], and the existence is found. To cut off that light, it rises and shines for the person to see in their tomorrow, and they receive that gravity and return and are sustained by this, and their merit lives. And it stands over the abyss and rises and is sustained, and that gravity is praised through it, like Boaz, of whom it is written: *As the Lord lives, lie down until the morning* (Ruth 3:13), for he conquered his **Evil Inclination** and stood by the oath. At the hour when the **Evil Inclination** cries out with this gravity to look upon that light, it accuses him and watches over this. When life rises to receive the vision, then above, the King appoints a spirit for the dwelling of the drops. That light that rose returns backward, twelve drops according to the count of the vessel. And regarding this, they see the window and the drops, and they err regarding that light which is more grave than an oath. See that the King who gives the established redemption within the depths, they return and seek from all these drops, and they are burned thus because of the heat, to rise and strike the world and to return life to it, descending from above to below to that source as at first. Until the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "Kadosh Baruch Hu"</note> summons one of the kings of life. And from that source, they descend below, and He appoints for him a king over seventy keys for all those drops, an oath for the existence of the spirit of the **Holy Name**. And until it reaches that which is below, it is the spirit of the **Holy Name**. And let the light not be called [vain], for the letters are engraved in it as at first, the King Himself of the spirit, the world, and His body. And then the world is sustained, and the waters return to guard His own name which is hidden above in its place. And regarding this, it is written: *You shall not take the [Name]...* Thus, whoever sees the standing of the entanglement, he sustains *the name of the Lord your God in vain*. To that place, and when he takes the life of the place, he sustains the whole world, when it dwells upon all.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Ten Commandments, specifically focusing on the Fourth Commandment: the Sabbath. It maintains the dual-column structure typical of early Zohar editions, contrasting the main Zohar text with the "Faithful Shepherd" (Raya Mehemna) commentary.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

**Remember** the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. This is the secret of the Holy Covenant <note>The "Covenant" refers to the Sefirah of Yesod, the foundation of the spiritual body and the site of circumcision</note>, and because all the limbs of the body stand upon this Covenant and are all included within it, so too is the Sabbath the summation of the Torah. All the secrets of the Torah hang upon it, and the preservation of the Sabbath is the preservation of the entire Torah. Whoever guards the Sabbath is as if he has guarded the entire Torah.
<margin>Remember</margin> <note>original: "Zechor". Catchword for the continuation of the main text below.</note>

## Faithful Shepherd (Raya Mehemna)

**The Faithful Shepherd** <note>A section of the Zohar traditionally attributed to the soul of Moses, who is the "Faithful Shepherd"</note>
The commandment is to be mindful of the Sabbath day, as it is said: **"Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy"** (Exodus 20:8). We have already established the secret of the Sabbath in all those other places; it is the day among the days of the world that represents the summation of the Torah, and whoever guards the Sabbath is as if he guards the entire Torah. Regarding what is said about the "remembrance" of the Sabbath to sanctify it with all types of sanctifications: whoever mentions the King must bless Him. And it is said that "Remember" <note>original: "Zechor"</note> refers to the male aspect, while "Observe" <note>original: "Shamor"</note> refers to the female aspect. This and that are entirely as one.

---

<note>The text continues in full-width lines.</note>

The Sabbath day is the secret of Faith, which hangs from the Supernal Head <note>The highest Sefirah, Keter</note> down to the end of all levels. The Sabbath is everything. There are three levels, and all are called "Sabbath": the **Upper Sabbath** <note>The Sefirah of Binah, the "Divine Mother"</note>, the Sabbath of the Day <note>The Sefirah of Tiferet</note>, and the Sabbath of the Night <note>The Sefirah of Malkhut/Shekhinah</note>. All are one, and all are called Sabbath. Because of this, every vision rules as one with its fellow, and He appoints them in order according to His dominion. When all this comes into the world, they all bow and submit before Him. When night comes, that "Sabbath of the Night" is prepared, and it is prepared as a Palace <note>The Shekhinah is often called the Palace for the Divine King</note> to be spoken of with Him. Once the Upper Sabbath arrives, it is drawn over it, and all things are hidden as at the end of the night. For this reason, the meal of the night is as beloved as that of the day. When the day comes, it is prepared along with these two to remember the upper level and the lower level, so as not to diminish it or be hidden from it. All together is called Sabbath, and they rule on the Sabbath day. These three levels are the summation and the secret of the entire Torah—the Written Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings. Whoever guards the Sabbath is like a mountain of the entire Torah. There are two pearls, and one script is with them in concealment, which holds between this one and that one. The upper pearl has no color and no life-force like the plantings. This pearl turns all its surroundings into various changes. They are engraved, protruding, gathering, bursting, and splitting, and they shine each and every one. Below them are two engraved supports like that pearl, and on the Sabbath day they gather and shine and open gates, and they emerge in abundance. They gather into the thirty-four hands <note>original: "L-L-D yado" - a cryptic numerical or symbolic reference</note> and return to gather them... they shine one to another. And when they shine, they do so in two colors: one color is white <note>representing Mercy</note> and one color is red <note>representing Judgment</note>. From these two, two other medicines are made until they rise below to spring forth red... and because these are as one, they both shine in two colors. These are two medicines: one is called "Offspring" and one is called "Sand" <note>original: "Ch-L"</note>, and they shine as one. The letter *He* emerges and they gather, and upon the Sabbath they both shine in two colors... the secret of the thirty-four. They shine as one... they gather as one and rise one upon the other, both engraved and carved as one. They surround the head like mountains, gathering branches that rise from this side and that side, and they are called "Master of Branches." These two below are all prepared one for the other, offspring upon offspring, shattered by the wind that binds the measures of mercy. These two below are prepared for one another, and when they cleave to one another and rise together, they lift their heads and shine and gather over all, like the Master of Branches who bursts forth in all...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse from the Zohar on the portion of Yitro. It transitions from a complex description of the celestial "Chariot" and the union of divine lights to the specific mystical significance of the commandment to "Remember the Sabbath."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The lower side <note>referring to the feminine aspect of the Divine, the Shekhinah</note> ascends to unite as one with them, so they become a single entity. All those supports and rulers go forth and govern on this day. Once these govern, that supreme pearl <note>original: *margala*; a metaphor for a high divine spark or Sephirah</note> emerges in a single gathering. And what is its gathering? These are the hidden seals. When it emerges, it strikes those supports; one swims between them, a living creature, the seventh, who is crowned and enters like a pearl beneath, while another swimmer descends under it, and they become one. That supreme pearl is hidden within it, and that gathering is crowned because of this swimmer. After it enters this swimmer, seventy branches emerge from within it to every side, and they all join as one. Thus, a Chariot <note>original: *retheka*; the divine vehicle of God's manifestation</note> and a Throne are made for that supreme pearl, which rules with the King’s crowns like a Throne on this day, and all are joyful. Once all this is established, the King sits upon the Throne of Judgment, and the seventy branches of the Throne ascend as we have said.

And those two "grooms" <note>metaphorical agents of divine flow</note> are the totality of the Torah on the sides of the crowns. The first grooms ascend, one to the house of the tribes and one to the gathering of the tribes that are lacking. These are the twelve tribes of the Supernal Israel. Furthermore, these two grooms ascend and descend, flying to the crowns of the grooms at the end of all grooms; one ascends like sixty degrees and the other like sixty degrees. They are the help for the life of the totality of all grooms—the twelve tribes, the first crowns—and they crown the ascent of the two grooms at the end, which is the end of the Torah.

The mystery of this is that the supreme pearl inherits that Throne of seventy-two <note>referring to the 72-letter Name of God</note>, and all the grooms shine. Then, that lower pearl we mentioned gazes at that hidden light to strengthen those lower grooms... <unclear>at the priest's mouth for inquiry</unclear>. Then that light is closed and ascends, entering the entire arrangement of the upper grooms, bringing that pearl toward it and spreading light to the twelve sides. Once this pearl gathers and gives life to those grooms, the witnesses of the supreme pearl are mixed as one, and pearl is joined with pearl. Everything becomes one spirit that is found. We have established these grooms as hidden from the side of the swimmer; and from this side, this is the "peg" between them, between pearl and pearl. Then everything becomes a spirit of holy joy of the seventy-two grooms of the Supernal Chariot, and everything stands and receives the offering. This is the Spirit of the Sabbath. Until here.

->**Remember**<- <note>Hebrew: *Zakhor*; the first word of the Fourth Commandment</note>

"Remember" is the masculine spirit. It is the masculine spirit that takes hold of all the limbs of the upper world. This is "the Sabbath Day" <note>Exodus 20:8</note>, which comes to include the Eve of the Sabbath, which is the night. This is the secret of sanctification <note>original: *kiddush*</note> that is required from the holy people, to be crowned by them as is fitting. "Remember" is for that which has no wisdom of its own and in which wisdom does not stand; for there is no wisdom below except through the upper masculine—the letter *Vav* <note>the symbol of the masculine divine flow</note>—and the hiddenness above and below. There is no wisdom below except that which requires "Remembering." Regarding this it is written: *Do not remember against us the iniquities of our forefathers* <note>Psalm 79:8</note> etc. There are those appointed there to remember, and since there is no wisdom before the Holy Throne, it ascends before Him.

And whoever is before Him, "Remember" is hidden above, because everything is the masculine spirit. There, the spirit of holy joy is engraved. For the *Vav* and for the lower realm, it is necessary to be sanctified, and it is necessary to be sanctified through "Remembering," for from it one takes all sanctifications and all blessings. This occurs when the Eve of the Sabbath crowns the holy people with the <insert>garments</insert> and coverings and prayers of holiness. And if you say that "Remember" does not need to be sanctified—Heaven forbid!—for from it emerge all the sanctifications of the world. Even so, it does not need to be sanctified during the day <note>in the same way as the night</note>, for it is necessary to be sanctified at night, and all sanctifications are hidden for Israel afterward, to be sanctified with the sanctification of all.

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Ten Commandments from the Zohar, specifically the section known as the "Faithful Shepherd" (Raya Mehemna). It focuses on the Fifth Commandment: honoring one's parents.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And Jethro Heard** Page 93<-

**The Faithful Shepherd**
**Honor** your father and your mother <note>Exodus 20:12</note>. Just as it has been established that all the works of the Holy One, blessed be He, are hidden, so too it is established that one must merit to give honor to their Master. "Honor your father and your mother" refers to the Assembly of Israel <note>The Shekhinah</note> and the Foundation of the World, which is the secret of the honor of the Supernal Father and Mother <note>The Sefirot of Chokhmah (Wisdom) and Binah (Understanding)</note>. It is written: "Honor the Lord with your wealth" <note>Proverbs 3:9</note>; this refers to the Torah. And who is the "Assembly"? It is "Length of days in her right hand, and in her left hand riches and honor" <note>Proverbs 3:16</note>.

> Honor the Lord with your wealth (Proverbs 3:9)

Know that a person’s life comes only from the Torah and the commandments. It is made known that from the Crown of Wisdom <note>Keter of Chokhmah</note> flow the gifts of life to those who occupy themselves with the Torah and the commandments. Therefore, "Honor the Lord with your wealth" <note>The Hebrew word for wealth, *Me-honekha*, is homiletically linked to *Me-hinneka*, meaning "from that which is graced to you"</note>—do not separate yourself from the Torah in order to aggrandize yourself through it, as is the way of some associates. Do not make the Torah a crown to grow great by, nor a spade to dig with for the sake of your own honor. Rather, give glory to Him, as it says, "Honor the Lord with your wealth." For a person is obligated in the honor of his father and mother because he is a partner with them; from two drops a person is formed. From the father’s drop come the eyes, bones, and sinews; from the mother’s drop comes the light in the eyes, the hair, the skin, and the flesh. <note>This reflects ancient embryological theories used here to illustrate the physical partnership of parents</note>. Just as a person is obligated to teach his son Torah, if he does not teach him the Torah and the commandments, it is as if he has made him into an idol. Regarding this, it says, "You shall not make for yourself a carved image." Such a son is destined to be "stubborn and rebellious," and he causes strikes against the Divine Mercy. He is like one who robs his father and mother, and he is joined with the "Destroyer" <note>A name for the demonic or destructive forces</note>. This applies to all things, even to bloodshed and forbidden unions.

**Honor** your father, as it is said: "Honor the Lord with your wealth." "With your wealth" means with your money. "With your wealth" also means from your very essence <note>original: *mi-mochak*, from your marrow/brain</note>, to call upon the Holy One. For the Holy One, blessed be He, is present in all the works of the world. One must provide for the father and mother from one's wealth and money for all that they need. Just as one is required to honor the Holy One, blessed be He, so is one required to honor the father and mother. For a holy partnership exists between them and the Holy One, blessed be He. Just as one must fear the Holy One, blessed be He, so must one fear his father and mother and honor them.

> So that your days may be lengthened (Exodus 20:11)

Because there are Supernal Days upon which a person’s life in this world depends. It has been established that a person’s days in this world are mirrored Above, and they all stand before the Holy One, blessed be He, and through them, a person’s life is known. "Upon the land which the Lord your God gives you." This refers to the vision that is like a "Luminous Mirror" <note>The prophetic clarity associated with Moses</note>. The secret of "Upon the land" refers to the "Mirror that does not shine" <note>The Shekhinah, which receives light from above</note>, which receives from those Supernal Days that shine from the Essence of All. What merit is there in these two commandments of the Torah where it is written "that your days may be lengthened"? These are the honoring of parents and the "Sending of the Nest" <note>Shiluach HaKen</note>. These two commandments are both suspended on high. Father and Mother are the secret of "Remember" and "Observe" <note>The two aspects of Sabbath</note>. Therefore it is written "that your days may be lengthened." Regarding the nest, it is written:

> You shall surely let the mother go, but the young you may take for yourself; that it may be well with you, and that you may prolong your days (Deuteronomy 22:7)

This is the secret of the Upper World <note>Binah</note>, where permission is not given to gaze, and one must only ask and contemplate within it. "But the young you may take for yourself" refers to what is written: "For ask now of the days that are past... from one end of heaven to the other" <note>Deuteronomy 4:32</note>. Everything above the "end of heaven" is hidden, and you shall not send your thoughts to profane it. Thus it is written, "that it may be well with you, and that you may prolong your days." "That it may be well with you" refers to the place that is good to all <note>The world to come</note>. And what is that? It is the hidden and concealed world where days are truly prolonged.

<summary>This page provides a mystical interpretation of the commandment to honor one's parents, linking physical parents to the divine emanations of Chokhmah and Binah. It explains that honoring parents is equivalent to honoring God and connects the reward of "long life" to the attainment of spiritual heights in the Upper World.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Yitro (Jethro). The previous sections likely dealt with the preparation for the Revelation at Sinai. This page focuses on the spiritual mechanics of performing commandments (mitzvot) and the specific cantillation of the Ten Commandments.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And Jethro Heard**<-

And from that day, as it is written: "it shall be established for you" <note>original: *tequm lakh*</note> by the permission of all. When a person performs a deed and focuses his will <note>term: *re'uta* — the mystical intention or "will of the heart" required for a spiritual act to ascend</note> upon it, he is meritorious and his portion is great. Even if he does not focus his will, he is still meritorious because he has performed the commandment of his Master. However, it is not the same as one who performs the "will" for its own sake <note>term: *lishmah* — performing a holy act purely for the sake of Heaven without ulterior motives</note> and focuses his will upon it to gaze at the glory of his Master. Even if he does not know how to fully grasp the reasoning, the matter depends upon that will for its own sake. Through the deed below performed for its own sake, the deed ascends above and is repaired in a fitting manner. This is like the action of the body which is repaired by that external deed according to that will. For the Holy One, blessed be He, desires the heart and the will of man. And even so, if the will of the heart—which is the essence of everything—is not present, regarding this it is written: **"And may the work of our hands be established upon us..."** <note>Psalm 90:17</note>. For not every man is wise enough to set his will and heart in the proper repair <note>term: *tikkun* — the process of spiritual rectification or "repairing" the world through holy acts</note> while performing the deed of a commandment; therefore, this is written: **"And may the work of our hands be established upon us."** What is the meaning of **"established upon us"**? Establish and prepare Your repair above in a fitting manner. **"Upon us"** means even though we do not know how to set the will, but only the deed alone, **"the work of our hands, establish it"** to that level which needs to be repaired. **"Establish it"** <note>original: *konenehu*</note> as a single union, to be repaired through this deed as is fitting.

## No
**Thou shalt not murder. Thou shalt not commit adultery. Thou shalt not steal. Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbor.**
**No.** <note>original: *Lo*</note> There is a "pause-mark" <note>term: *ta'am* — refers to the musical cantillation marks which also serve as punctuation; here, the Zohar notes a specific pause after the word "No"</note> in all these three. If there were no pause-mark, there would be no existence for the worlds, and Mercy <note>term: *Chesed* — the divine attribute of loving-kindness</note> would be added to us even if one were killed in this world, Heaven forbid, for transgressing the Torah. But because the pause-mark separates it, there is Mercy and Mercies.

## No
**Thou shalt not commit adultery.** If there were no pause-mark, there would be Mercy even for the portion of grace <note>original: *chen*</note> to be called into the lower dwelling of the adulterer. But because the pause-mark separates it, there is Mercy and Mercies.

## No
**Thou shalt not steal.** If there were no pause-mark, there would be Mercy even for the property that one is destined to acquire through the Torah, the grace of knowledge that is hidden to be gazed upon, so that he could be purified before the claim of the property he is destined to receive from the Merciful One; and for the property of knowledge, both of which bring purity to the light. But because the pause-mark separates it, there is Mercy and Mercies.

## No
**Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbor.** Here there is no pause-mark, because Mercy is the totality of all. And in all matters of the Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, placed secrets within them and a portion for the heart in the Torah to be repaired by it and to grasp it. As it is said: **"I am the Lord your God, who teaches you for your profit, who leads you in the way you should go"** <note>Isaiah 48:17</note>. See, etc.

## No
**Thou shalt not covet.** There is no pause-mark at all. One might say that even the "coveting" of the Torah is forbidden since there is no pause. Come and see: all the deeds of the Torah are general principles, and all these are details: **"your neighbor's house, his field, his servant, etc."** like all worldly matters. But the Torah itself is a constant "coveted" thing, a delight, the essence of life, a sword of days in this world and in the world to come. Thus, the gravity of the Torah is established for you, for all the commandments of the Torah are both above and below, and all are weighty matters that are hidden. They were engraved upon the stone tablets, and all the colors that were in them appeared before the eyes of all, to know and to gaze into the spirit of the 613 commandments of the Torah, which are all as one. They all appeared to the eyes; they all saw with a vision to gaze at the Bride <note>note: a mystical reference to the Shekhinah or the Torah itself</note> who gazes at all, and the word was shining before their eyes. At that moment, all the secrets of the Torah and all the supernal secrets were revealed to them, to remove the veil from their eyes because they were seeing.

## Main Text (The Zohar)

Come and see! The radiance and glory of their Master was present in a way that had not been seen since the day the world was created. The Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself in His glory upon Mount Sinai. And if you should say, "But have we not learned that at the crossing of the Red Sea, even a handmaid saw what the prophet Ezekiel did not see?" <note>original: "כביכול" - as if it were possible to say</note>—it was not the same as that day when Israel stood at Mount Sinai. For on that day when Israel stood at Mount Sinai, the filth <note>original: "זוהמא" - the spiritual impurity or "slime" of the primordial serpent</note> was removed from them, and all their bodies shone with a brilliance like the angels <note>original: "כלכוסי" - likely a reference to celestial hosts or 'helicoses'</note> who perform the mission of their Master. In that victorious kingdom, they were like those who eat the bread of angels. They were not like a king’s subjects who merely see him when he passes, but rather they ascended to His Name, as it is written: **"God has ascended with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a horn"** (Psalms 47:6).

And because that filth was removed from them, the bodies of Israel were transparent and shining, without any opacity at all. They were like the brightness of the firmament, prepared to receive the light. Thus were the people of Israel; they saw and gazed upon the glory of their Master in a way they could not at the Sea, for the impurity had not yet been removed from them at that time. But at Sinai, the impurity ceased from them, and even the embryos in their mothers' wombs saw and gazed upon the glory of their Master. Each and every one received the revelation according to what was fitting for them. This day was more precious before the Holy One, blessed be He, than the day the world was created, for the day the world was created did not have a firm foundation until Israel received the Torah, as it is written: **"If My covenant be not with day and night, I have not appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth"** (Jeremiah 33:25). Once Israel received the Torah on Mount Sinai, the world was established, heaven and earth were sustained, and the essence of both the upper and lower worlds was fixed. His glory was exalted over all. Regarding that day it is written: "The Lord reigns, He is clothed in majesty; the Lord is clothed, He has girded Himself with strength." And there is no "strength" but the Torah, as it is written: **"The Lord will give strength to His people; the Lord will bless His people with peace"** (Psalms 29:11).

---

-> # The Portion of "And These are the Laws" <-

**Rabbi Shimon opened** his discourse and began: **"And these are the laws which you shall set before them"** (Exodus 21:1). The translation <note>The Aramaic Targum Onkelos</note> is: "And these are the judgments you shall arrange before them." These are the arrangements of the souls <note>term: "סדר דנשמתין" - the mystical order of how souls are judged and reincarnated</note>; the judgments of the souls that are judged, each one according to its deeds.

**They said:** <unclear>The signs from the beginning of the books...</unclear> <note>This appears to be a cryptic scribal note or mnemonic regarding the textual layout</note>.

**"If you buy a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years, and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing"** (Exodus 21:2). Rabbi Hiyya opened: **"The secret of the Lord is for those who fear Him, and His covenant to make them know it"** (Psalms 25:14). **"If you buy a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years."** When a soul is sentenced to reincarnation <note>term: "גלגולא" - Gilgul; the transmigration or "rolling" of souls into new bodies</note>, God forbid, it becomes a "servant" to Metatron <note>note: The supreme angel who governs the lower worlds of action</note>. This state is comprised of six sides <note>the six directions of the physical world</note>, which is why it is written "six years he shall serve" in his reincarnations. He is not released until he completes the six levels... <unclear>after they are stirred</unclear>... from the side of the "Seventh" <note>The mystical realm of Binah or the Sabbath, representing freedom</note>. What is written? "And in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing." For then he is joined to the place where there is no earthly kingship, and since there is no earthly kingship over him, there is no longer any bondage. This is the conclusion of the matter.

## Main Text (Zohar)

In her, is it not the strength of the **Living God**? Thus, my Master, what is the addition of the soul of the **Living One** <note>Hebrew: *Chayah*, the second highest level of the soul</note> from which it is known when it says: *You shall not do any work, you, your son, your daughter, your servant, etc.* <note>Exodus 20:10</note>? The Old Man <note>The "Saba," a recurring mysterious elderly sage in the Zohar</note> said to him: Old man, old man, you have merited this! For this certainly refers to the soul of the **Righteous** <note>The *Tzadik*, often associated with the sephirah of Yesod</note>, of whom it is said that a servant who is obligated to be refined through **reincarnation** <note>Literally "the cycle" or *gilgul*</note> like all those who are in service like a servant or a maidservant; and the beginning of their freedom is through the grace found in all living beings who are poor, like the souls of the **Assembly of Israel**. It is written of her: *You shall not do any work*, and it calls to him: *You shall not make him work as a bondservant*. Regarding the **Righteous**, who is the **Sabbath day**, *you shall not make him work as a bondservant*, for that refers to a **weekday**. But, Old Man, Old Man, she is the **Only Daughter** <note>The *Bat Yechidah*, a level of the soul or the Shekhinah</note> and she is the mate of the **Righteous**, who is the **Sabbath**. What then is the meaning of *if he takes another for himself*? He said to him: Take note, for this pushes away the Bride; see the surroundings below, for she is called the **weekday of the Sabbath**, but rather the **weekday of the joy of the Sabbath**. He said to him: And what is this "weekday of the Sabbath"? He replied: This is the **handmaid**, who is the body of the **Only Daughter**, concerning whom it was said: *He shall not diminish her food, her clothing, or her marriage rights* <note>Exodus 21:10; the Zohar reads "another" as a lower manifestation</note>. Come and see: the **Divine Presence** <term>Shekhinah: the feminine aspect of God dwelling in the world</term> is sometimes called a "handmaid" and sometimes called a "servant-girl." And the **Shekhinah** is sometimes called the **King's Daughter**. So too there is a **Living Being** <note>Chayah</note> of whom it is said "and God is **Gabriel**," and there is a **Living Being** of whom it is said "Yod-Vav, the **Living Beings of War**." And because of this, the soul that is drawn into **reincarnation**—Heaven forbid—she is the daughter of the **Holy One, blessed be He**. If you say she happens to be in a body that is offensive, which is the dominion of the **Evil Inclination** from the side of the "servant-girl"—Heaven forbid! Woe! *My name and My glory I will not give to another*, etc. *And if a man sells...* (He said to him: And behold, this body of the **Righteous** is the **King's Daughter**; if you say it happens to be from the lower crowns of impurity—disgrace! Heaven forbid! Regarding her it is said: *She shall not be sold as the men are sold*, for you have bound her to Him. Who is the body of the **King's Daughter**? This is **Metatron** <note>The highest Archangel, often described as the "garment" or "body" of the Shekhinah</note>. And this body is the place of the **Shekhinah**, the **Radiance of Life**, the soul, the **King's Daughter**; she surrounds it there like a cycle below. And what is written of her?

# And if he sells
-><-

*And if a man sells his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out as the menservants do* <note>Exodus 21:7</note>. Furthermore, *And if he sells*—Heaven forbid—this refers to the **Holy One, blessed be He**. *His daughter*—these are **Israel**, for they are from the side of the **Only Daughter**, as He calls them "His daughter." And if you say they are like those from the side of the **servant**, which is **Metatron**, who went out as a gift from Egypt, *she shall not go out as the menservants do*. This is what is written: *For you shall not go out in haste, nor go by flight* <note>Isaiah 52:12</note>. Come and see: when a person is born, they give him a **Spirit** <note>Ruach</note> from the side of the "Beasts" <note>the *Chayot*, holy creatures</note> from the Crown of Purity, from the side of those called "Handfuls." If he merits more, they give him a **Soul** <note>Neshamah</note> from the side of the **Throne**. And these three are the "maidservant," "servant," and "servant-girl" of the **King's Daughter**. If he merits more, they give him a soul by way of **Emanation** <term>Atzilut: the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, representing pure divinity</term> from the side of the **Only Daughter**, and she is called the **King's Daughter**. If he merits more, they give him a soul from the side of the **Central Column** <note>The middle path of the Sephirot</note>, and he is called a **Son** to the **Holy One, blessed be He**, as it is written: *You are sons to the Lord your God* <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note>. If he merits more, they give him a soul from the side of **Father and Mother** <note>the Sephirot of Chokhmah and Binah</note>, as it says: *And He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life*. What is "Life"? These are the letters **Yod-He**, of which it is said: *Let every soul praise the Lord [Yah]* <note>Psalm 150:6</note>, and it is completed with the letter **Yod**. If he merits even more, they give him the name **Y-H-V-H** in its full spelling of the letters **Yod-He-Vav-He**; this is the **Voice**, which is **Man** in the way of the Supernal **Emanation**, and he is called by the **image** of his Master. Of him it is said: *And have dominion over the fish of the sea, etc.* This refers to the **Living Being** <note>Chayah</note> and dominion over all the firmaments, and over all the **Ophanim**, **Seraphim**, and **Holy Creatures**, and over all the hosts and powers above and below. And because of all this, they merited, etc. According to the plain meaning, from the side of the **Only Daughter** it is said of him: *She shall not go out as the menservants do*. Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yose happened to meet one night at the **Tower of Tyre**. They joined together there and rejoiced in one another. Rabbi Yose said: How beloved is the Torah, for just as the **Shekhinah** is like a woman in every place, this companion is needed as one. An old man, a deep thinker, who was walking...

<meta>This page continues the narrative of Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yose encountering a mysterious old man (the "Saba") on the road. ## Main Text (Zohar)

All his paths were like a hundred with a sword and a nut with iron. In between, there is space for one like a hundred who lies between two mountains of copper and a sign in iron. And what is this? Like a scent received in its strength that was not among those destined to be cut, nor was it the time in judgment to be forced, like a secret that was not forced. All go up and go down; when they go down, they go up—two that are one, and one that is three. What is the **fair maiden who has no eyes**, whose body is hidden and revealed? She comes out in the morning and disappears in time. She is wrinkled in a vision that was not; all this he asks in silence and was enslaved. And a secret he has in a vision, for he stands in the measure of those who occupy themselves with the matters of the **Torah** <note>original: "Oraita"</note>, those which are in other words. There, Rabbi Hiyya saw that traveling man <note>The "Tayya" or Arab traveler, often a disguised sage in the Zohar</note> and asked: Do you know anything of him? He said to him: I know that there is no substance in his words, for if he knew, he would open like a hole, and there would be no way in their emptiness. Rabbi Hiyya said: That traveler is here, for sometimes bad sparks exist, and an old man is ready to be purified. He said to him: Stand here and there and prepare the donkeys with food. He called to him and he came before them. He said to them: I will join two that are three, and three that are as one. Rabbi Yose said: Did I not tell you that all these vessels are empty, and they remain in their emptiness? He sat before them and said to them: Bow down here, for a traveler has been made, and eyes are invited, for at first I did not see a traveler for every son; I have one small one, and the children of the book <note>students</note> urged him, and like a time to look into the hole. Remember this: we found one of the Rabbis who went in silence and went in his crown and was defiled, and he arrived and found that he heard new words in the hole, and I heard nothing. Rabbi Yose said: In all the words you have said, do not be troubled except by one. Either you spoke here in error, or they are empty words. That **Elder** <note>original: "Saba"</note> said: And what is the joke? He said: **The Fair Maiden** <term>Fair Maiden: A mystical metaphor for the Shekhinah (Divine Presence) or the Torah itself, which reveals its secrets only to its lovers</term>, etc.

**The Elder opened** his discourse and said:
> "The Lord is for me, I will not fear; what can man do to me?" (Psalms 118:6).
> "The Lord is for me among my helpers, and I shall see [the defeat of] my enemies" (Psalms 118:7), etc.

How good and pleasant and precious and high are the words of the **Torah**, and here Rabbi Hiyya stands bowing, for I have not heard from their mouths until now even a single word. But I must say that there is no end at all to speaking words of **Torah** before everyone. That **Elder** wrapped himself [in his prayer shawl], opened, and said:
> "And if a priest's daughter be married unto a stranger, she may not eat of the offering of the holy things" (Leviticus 22:12).

This verse relies even on another verse:
> "But if a priest's daughter be a widow, or divorced, and have no child, and is returned unto her father's house, as in her youth, she shall eat of her father's bread; but there shall no stranger eat thereof" (Leviticus 22:13).

These verses are according to their literal meaning, yet all words of **Torah** are hidden matters. And how many are the words of wisdom hidden in every single word of the **Torah**, known to those [who seek], for the **Torah** is not composed of worldly words. They are given to the one who interprets them, and it is said: "after the mouth," and it is a burden to guard them to interpret them according to their ways. And if these words which I announced are a burden to guard to interpret them according to their ways, the words of the **Torah**, which are the tastes of the **Holy King** <note>original: "Malka Kadisha"</note>, how much more so <note>original: "v'al achat kama v'kama"</note> is it a burden to look into it simply, as it is written:
> "For the ways of the Lord are right" (Hosea 14:10), etc.

And it is written:
> "Lo, all these things does God work, twice, yea thrice, with a man" (Job 33:29).

To bring back the first to the converts, and what purifies the **soul** <note>original: "Nishmata"</note> below and above. He opened and said: we must see what is the difference between the verse that says "and a priest's daughter" and the verse that says "and a priest's daughter" and "man" is not written. Rather, "and a priest's daughter" refers to one called a **Priest** <note>original: "Kohen"</note> but not a literal priest. And in this way, he was a priest, and in the end a deputy, and he was a High Priest, and he was a priest who was not called "Great." A deputy is generally a master more than that priest. And how is there a purification of sparks...

<meta>This page continues the "Sava de-Mishpatim" (The Elder of Mishpatim) discourse from the Zohar. The previous section likely introduced the mystical interpretation of the laws of Hebrew servants as allegories for the soul's journey. This page specifically addresses the "holy soul" falling into the "Other Side" (evil) and the mystery of the scales of judgment.</meta>

->Laws<-

And I saw the spirit and I saw the soul. **"And if a priest’s daughter is married to a stranger"** <note>Leviticus 22:12</note>—this refers to the holy soul <note>original: *nishmata kadisha*</note> that is found rising from below to above and enters into the dwelling of the portion of life. And every spirit of the High Priest <note>The "High Priest" here is a mystical reference to the archangel Michael or a high emanative force</note> gives a portion from there; those souls fly out and enter as one. Woe to the world, for the children of men do not know that they are found becoming defiled by vanity and by the "Evil Son" <note>A reference to the personification of the *Sitra Achra* or the "Other Side" of evil</note> who is cursed and plagued. 

The priest’s daughter <note>the soul</note> flies downward and is found in a place that is "strange" <note>the material world or the realm of impurity</note>. Because it is the will of her Master, she acts there and is suppressed; she is unable to straighten herself or reach perfection in this world. When she departs from it, **"she is like the holy offering <note>terumah</note>; she shall not eat"** <note>Leviticus 22:12</note> among the rest of the souls that reached perfection in this world. 

Furthermore, I saw in this verse: **"And if a priest’s daughter is married to a stranger"**—the poor thing! The holy soul is given over to a stranger! This refers to the soul found on the "Scale of the Balance" <note>original: *tikla*; a mystical mechanism of judgment and reincarnation</note> and it flies upon it. The Priest <note>the Divine</note> is open to the wisdom of the West <note>the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note>; she was given to a "stranger." Furthermore, it is certainly the High Spirit, greater than all, in the Pillar that stands for restoration. The air of the soul strikes one side of the Scale, and strikes the other side of the Scale. On this side are the **Kings of Righteousness** <note>original: *malkhei tzedek*</note> and on that side are the **Kings of Deceit** <note>original: *malkhei mirmah*</note>. 

This Scale never stops turning, and souls ascend and descend and return. There are no "old" souls <note>meaning souls that have finished their task</note>; everything is weak in the darkness, as it is written:
> **"Until the time that man ruled over man to his own hurt"** (Ecclesiastes 8:9).

"To his own hurt" certainly—destruction to this soul that was in the "Other Side," the "stranger." It was distressed by him; this is the secret of "to his own hurt." It is cursed and strange, and **"of the holy offering she shall not eat"** until the Holy One, blessed be He, does with it what He does.

He opened the verse and said: **"And if a priest’s daughter is married to a stranger"**—so it is here. I saw the spirit, how souls are occupied. Rather, in this world, everything is conducted in the portion of the "Knowledge of Good and Evil." When the people of the world conduct themselves on the side of Good, the Scale stands and tips toward the side of Good. When they conduct themselves on the side of Evil, it tips toward that side. All the souls that were in the Scale at that moment are taken and seized "to their own hurt." Those souls are forced into whatever is found on the evil and foolish side. This is the holy spirit that was occupied in the palaces, and they ruled over it "to its own hurt." So too, the souls occupied by the Other Side, "to their own hurt" is what is done to those souls. 

We have seen in the Early Books <note>Ancient mystical texts often cited by the Zohar</note> that those who were like the "Pious of the Nations of the World" and those "Disciples of the Sages" who preceded the High Priest are destined to suffer in the world, even though they entered the innermost sanctum. This Elder wept; his heart rejoiced, his limbs trembled, and they said nothing. That Elder opened and said:

**"If** she is displeasing in the eyes of her master, who has not betrothed her, then he shall let her be redeemed; to a foreign people [he shall have no power to sell her]" (Exodus 21:8). This section is supreme! It is said: **"And if a man sells his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out as the menservants do"** (Exodus 21:7). 

"If she is displeasing..." Master of the Universe! Who would not fear You? For You have the merit of dominion over all the kings of the world! Who would not fear the **"King of the Nations"** <note>Jeremiah 10:7</note>, for it is befitting You? How many are there in the world who find this verse and all say: "Woe! This verse is not established upon its strength!" Is the Holy One, blessed be He, the "King of the Nations"? Is He not the "King of Israel"? For it is written:
> **"When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance..."** (Deuteronomy 32:8).

And it is written:
> **"For the Lord’s portion is His people"** (Deuteronomy 32:9).

And certainly, He is the King of Israel! If you say He is the "King of the Nations," is this their praise—that He rules over them? For it is said they were handed over to His appointees and deputies. Furthermore, the end of the verse says:
> **"For among all the wise men of the nations, and in all their kingdoms, there is none like You"** (Jeremiah 10:7).

Is all this praise only to compare Him to the nations? This is a difficult question—how do they not rise in this verse to the height of the firmament?

He also questions the title "King of the Nations," arguing that God's true sovereignty is over Israel, while other nations are governed by intermediaries.</summary>

## Laws (Mishpatim)

The fifth firmament that stands before them is of such density that they do not know it at all, for that which is there is more severe than all of them; they see only "chaos and void." As it is written: **"All the nations are as nothing before Him; they are accounted by Him as less than nothing and void"** <note>Isaiah 40:17</note>. This world is uprooted and called "waste" by the verse. 

<term>Rabbi Hiyya</term> <note>A prominent sage in the Zohar's circle</note> said: It is certainly written, **"God reigns over the nations"** <note>Psalm 47:9; original: "Elohim malakh al goyim"</note>. He said to him: The wisdom of the <term>Crown</term> <note>Keter, the highest and most hidden emanation of God</note> was hidden and emerged in this verse to assist them, but in the end, it is not found at the beginning as it is found later. But since it was revealed to you at the end, I will pass it before you, and from there we shall see how to pass it all. 

Come and see: all the arrangements and all the descriptive titles <note>kinnuyim</note> that the Holy One, Blessed Be He, possesses—they all spread out in their paths and clothe one another. They are all divided into known paths and streams, except for the **Unique Name** <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note> which is set apart from all other names. It belongs to the Unique Nation, blessed above all other nations, and these are the letters <term>Y-W A-H</term> <note>A mystical permutation of the Divine Name</note>. This is what is written: **"For the Lord’s portion is His people"** <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>. And it is written: **"But you who held fast to the Lord your God are all alive today"** <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>. 

Beside this, I have seen that there is one name among all the other names that is permitted to spread out and divide into many "swords and knives" and investigations of <term>Elohim</term> <note>original: "Al-dis," a substitution for the name Elohim to avoid profanation</note>. This name is investigated and divided among the lower levels, which are their worlds. This name is divided among the sides and the appointed ministers of the other nations. Thus: **"And God came to Balaam at night"** <note>Numbers 22:20</note>; and **"And God came to Abimelech in a dream by night"** <note>Genesis 20:3</note>. Likewise, every minister and authority there receives from the other nations through this name. Even idolatry is investigated through this name. 

This name "reigns over the nations," but this is not the name that reigns over Israel. For the Unique Name is for the unique people of Israel, the Holy Nation. And if you should say, based on this wisdom, let us establish the verse that says: **"Who would not fear You, O King of the nations?"** <note>Jeremiah 10:7</note>, implying that He is the King who reigns over the nations through the name <term>Elohim</term> <note>Al-dis</note>, in whom authority and place reside—it is not so. For if it were so, even idolatry would be included in this. 

Rather, since the scripture was close to the "Crowns of Wisdom," the verse calls out regarding His existence according to the city's arrangement: **"Who would not fear You, O King of the nations?"** And if you say that "King of the nations" refers to the Holy One, Blessed Be He—it is not so. Rather, who is the "King of the nations" who does not fear You or tremble before You? Who is the "King of the nations" who does not flutter like a fledgling? These "gods" are all servants of the Lord. 

One who hears this might not understand what is being said. Since it says "God" <note>Elohim</note> in this context, these are "gods who are servants of the Lord." It should have written "the servants of the Lord are gods," but instead it placed the Name here. It should have written: "Who is the King of the nations who does not tremble?" Rather, everything is stated according to its arrangement: **"For among all the wise men of the nations and in all their kingdoms, there is none like You"** <note>Jeremiah 10:7</note>. What is this "King"? His power spreads through their wisdom, saying "there is none like You." They all cease at this point. When they see Your works and Your might in their wisdom, this King's power spreads, and they say "there is none like You." The heralds stood and were silent, saying nothing. 

He opened and said: "And the fire began to join them..." <note>A mystical reference to the soul's refinement</note>. The heralds awaken the mistress of the flame to crush it until it is written: **"Whatever Sarah tells you, listen to her voice"** <note>Genesis 21:12</note>. Here it is written: **"And if a man sells his daughter"** <note>Exodus 21:7</note>. This refers to the <term>soul</term> <note>Neshama</note> which is sold into this world because of bad deeds. It is like a debt to the Master, like a scale that turns. One must labor to bring her out from there. 

It was taught: Like the descent of slaves, all those souls who labor are there. Here is the spirit; these are like the sucklings and the "watchers" <note>angels</note>. All those who suckle from the strength of the heat. The Holy One, Blessed Be He, sees that if they remain in the world, their scent will become foul and they will be scorched by this heat. He gathers them while they still give off a pleasant scent. What does He do? He leaves them to be occupied by the hand of this <term>Serpent</term> <note>The physical world or the Inclination toward Evil</note>, and they do not fear... for once they are given over...

...which was denied by the authority of that female <note>referring to the feminine aspect of the *Sitra Achra* or "Other Side"</note> who oppressed it and snatched it from the world while it was still nursing in the strength of its mother. And if you say that those souls will perform good in the world, regarding this it is written: **"If she is pleasing in the eyes of her master"** <note>Exodus 21:8</note>, for it is destined that if this man, after many days, fulfills his obligation through her, he shall not neglect her, but shall rejoice in her. This is the meaning of **"If she is pleasing in the eyes of her master, who has not <term>betrothed</term> her"**: the word "not" is written with an *Aleph* <note>original: "לא" (not) vs "לו" (to him). The Zohar notes the traditional scribal variant where the text says "not betrothed" but implies "betrothed to him."</note>. If you say that from that Other Side, the Holy One, blessed be He, sometimes provides comfort—behold, in the cycle of <term>reincarnation</term> <note>original: *gilgula*</note> He attaches her to him and betroths her in a way that was not possible before. **"Then he shall let her be redeemed."** What is the meaning of **"he shall let her be redeemed"**? The Holy One, blessed be He, redeems her at the gate of ascent, so that she may be seen before she sees, and she ascends to the heights of heights as is His custom. And if you say: since she was enslaved by that Other Side and He gave her over—as we have said—to the pious of the other nations, or sometimes to a Torah scholar, the verse comes and adds: "honor her and speak to her." To sell her is certainly "against him" <note>referring to the spiritual damage</note> for one who occupies her with the business of the cycle of the <term>Scale</term> <note>original: *tikla*, a mystical mechanism of judgment and reincarnation</note>, except for Israel certainly, and not for others. And when she emerges from this Scale, she is under the wings of the Divine Presence <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note>, but she is crowned with her crowns like a mistress over a worm. And if you say that this side is above her in that female—it is not so. Rather, He takes her and rejoices with her, and she flies from the hand and enters that place, seeing the command of that female, and rejoices in it and smiles, gazing upon that crown until later the Holy One, blessed be He, takes His soul and it stands in its body. And after all, it is under the authority of the Holy One, blessed be He.

Come and see. It was taught: "The wings of the Divine Presence." What is this? At the hour she emerges from the Scale and from that side, the Holy One, blessed be He, cherishes her and returns her like a fledgling into His own precious garment, showing her how holy she is to her companions. And this is the precious rest that the King spreads over her, and then she is like a treasure that was given only to Israel alone. This is what is written: *“For who is God...”* and regarding this it is written: **"To a foreign people he shall have no power to sell her"**—"against her," for as long as the King’s precious garment is upon her, **"to a foreign people he shall have no power to sell her."** How much greatness does that side have? Come and see: all the inhabitants of the world are under the authority of the Holy King at the time He desires to remove them from the world, and this [Other Side] has no place there, yet she smiles at them and rejoices in them. A warning to man in this world is contained in these verses, and how many high benefits are prepared in all these matters of the Torah, and all of them are in the path of truth and are known to the wise who know the truth. At the time the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to create the world, it rose in His will before Him, and He formed all the souls that were destined to be given to human beings later. And they were all formed before Him in the very same image they were destined to take in the human being. He hides and shows each one, and there are those among them destined to corrupt their way in the world. When the time arrives, the Holy One, blessed be He, calls to that soul and says to her: "Go, enter such-and-such a place, in such-and-such a body." She replies before Him: "Master of the Universe, I am content with the world in which I dwell, and I do not wish to go to another world where they will enslave me and I will be defiled among them." The Holy One, blessed be He, says: "From the day you were created, you were created only for this—to be in that world." Once the soul sees this, she descends and enters there against her will. The Torah, which gives counsel to the whole world, saw this and called out to the children of men, saying: "See how much the Holy One, blessed be He, has pitied you! A precious pearl that He had, He gave to you for free, that you might be served by it in this world." **"And if a man sells"**—this is the Holy One, blessed be He. **"His daughter"**—this is the holy soul. **"To be a maidservant"**—to be an enslaved handmaid among you like this.

## Judgments

In this world, at the time when a person is destined to come [into the world] and eventually to depart from this world, [the soul] does not descend with ease like servants, but is commanded and wrapped in the Supernal Mind <note>original: *mochin*, referring to divine intellectual energies</note>. She shall go out as a free woman, clarified and expert, so that she may be like "this" <note>original: *koh*, a mystical name for the Divine Presence</note> and be found as "this." And He gives her a good reward, unlike the children of a stranger who all enter and turn away with their wings folded in hunger and exhaustion. When she goes out clarified and expert, as it is written: *He shall let down a cord* <note>interpretive reading of the soul's descent</note>, He has pity on her in the eyes of the poor, she is wrapped in the wings of the Mind so as not to be defiled before Him. As it is written: *He shall let down beauty* to that body which was wise through that soul of the Divine Image. For all souls ascend clarified and go out standing from this world; every single soul enters into the King's Book of Life, and they are all supported. And this word stands: "The soul of so-and-so, at such a time, shall belong to that body which is found," and then it is written: *In it he shall be justified* etc.

But when she goes out "evil in the eyes of her master" <note>referencing Exodus 21:8</note>, because she was defiled by sins and in the wings of transgressions, then He does not delight in her, and she is not settled in that body. From her, life and health depart, except for that portion of the two sparks given to the body. Then it is written: *Then he shall let her be redeemed* <note>Exodus 21:8</note>—He redeems his soul from passing into the pit. *Then he shall let her be redeemed*: He preserves his life as a person who speaks a foreign tongue <note>original: *la'az*, meaning a foreign language or a difficult situation</note>; he redeems her and returns in repentance. And she stands between two sides: the Master, the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the redemption <note>original: *purkana*</note> after he returns in repentance, He redeems her from the bread of Purgatory <note>original: *Gehinnom*</note>. *To a foreign people he shall have no power to sell her*: What is "a foreign people"? These are the "other sides" <note>original: *sitra achra*, the forces of impurity</note>. The life of every soul that departs from the world and the person has sinned is far off; she is destined to be taken above by the holy sides. Because the holy sides stand in this partition for the souls, the stars stand in that partition of Purgatory. And how many souls, how many holy sides are given to her to be sold with her and to enter her into the [lower realms]? No. And how many, how many sides and stars are given in the partition of Purgatory? And so the sides that lick the dust and merit to make for her openings below... *To a foreign people he shall have no power to sell her*: these are the lickers of dust. Against him, like the enclosure that the Holy One, Blessed be He, made for her, a fortress so that they shall not be absolute in her—the "foreign people"—within that spread of the fortress over her.

**And if** *he designates her for his son* <note>Exodus 21:9</note>. Come and see how much life there is for a person who happens upon this! May His mercies be aroused in this world. When a person in this world is worthy of the soul, as it is written: *He shall let down in their lives*, when the Holy One, Blessed be He, delights in him and is found in him every day, in hunger and in thirst, and says: "See my holy son, who has life in that world, such and such he does, such and such his deeds are prepared." And every such soul departs from this world in merit, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, calls out to recognize her with many lights every day, and proclaims over her: "This is the soul of so-and-so, she is clarified!" This is what is written: *And if he designates her for his son, he shall deal with her according to the judgment of daughters.*

What is *the judgment of daughters*? Here there is a secret of life for the wise: in the good, powerful, hidden firmament, there is one Palace called the **Chamber of Love** <note>original: *Heichal Ahavah*</note>. There, hidden treasures are found, and all the secrets of the King's love are there. And those souls of the King enter there. Once she enters there, into that Palace of the King, it is written: *And Jacob kissed Rachel* <note>Genesis 29:11</note>. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, is found there for that holy soul; He immediately comes forward and kisses her and embraces her and raises her up with Him. He does not treat her with the distress of below, but *he shall deal with her according to the judgment of daughters*—just as a father acts toward his beloved daughter, he kisses her and embraces her and gives her gifts, so the Holy One, Blessed be He, does for the worthy soul every day, as it is written: *he shall deal with her according to the judgment of daughters.* This is what is written: *Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth* <note>Song of Songs 1:2</note>. When He sees His daughter, He delights His eyes in the life of the world. So too, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gathers with her to see her in the World to Come, as it is written: *No eye has seen, O God, beside You, what He acts for the one who waits for Him* <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>. And here it is written: *Isaac* <note>referring to the laughter/joy of the soul</note>.

## Laws
