**If** he takes another for himself, etc. <note>Exodus 21:10</note>
And he shall do for her, etc. That Old Man delighted in the study and did not abandon it as before, nor did he diminish it. **If** he takes another for himself, etc. What does "if another" mean? Is the Holy One, Blessed be He, destined to bring *another* soul into their sheaths <note>the body</note> in this world, and not the specific soul that was destined for this world by the will of her Master? For there is no change for the righteous at all! What then is "if he takes another for himself"? That Old Man opened his discourse and said: >**"And the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it"**< <note>Ecclesiastes 12:7</note>. Our colleagues have established this verse in the context of the Holy Temple. And we have learned: "And the dust returns to the earth as it was." This refers to that which is written, "and he returns to his dust." "As it was" implies it returns to its source. "And the spirit returns to God who gave it." What is this "spirit that returns"? This is the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note> which is the Holy Spirit. When she comes from the Throne, from those ten groups that she leads, and they do not wish to be hidden but to return in repentance before the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, the "Other Side" <note>the forces of evil/impurity</note> takes hold upon the Holy Land, as the colleagues have established. Come and see: the spirit of a person is entirely crowned in the image of that which is below. Through all merits and festivals, the spirit and spirits are crowned; they spread out and ascend on high. Just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, acts with that holy soul above, so He acts with this spirit that ascends before Him. He says of it, "Let it be the spirit of such-and-such a body." Immediately, the Holy One, Blessed be He, crowns this spirit with several crowns and delights in it. And if you say that for the sake of this spirit of the "children" of the Holy One, He does what He does for the soul—it is not so. Rather, "another" like her: **"her food, her clothing, and her marriage rights he shall not diminish"** <note>Exodus 21:10</note>. These are the three supernal names belonging to the level that corresponds to the lower realm. All of them are sealed in the World to Come like a signet ring. One of them is **"her food"** <note>Hebrew: *She'erah*</note>, from the hidden goodness and the light that shines in hidden joy, concealing for us the radiance of all; it is called <term>Yesod</term> <note>Foundation, the ninth Sefirah</note> in the point of the Hidden Wisdom. **"Her food"** (*She'erah*) is an anagram of "Happy" (*Asher*), and its name is never diminished. It is "another" like her, the spreading of the King; this is the goodness of the "other" that shines and guards her constantly. The spreading of the King's garment that spreads over her is that which is hidden in him constantly, never departing from her. **"And her marriage rights"** (*Onatah*)—this is from the goodness of the World to Come in which everything exists. The Lord is the directness of her life, shining like all the hidden upper lights which are the life-force, containing the hidden humility that emerges from the teaching. All of this is in the clarity and longing for the World to Come. These three things shall not be diminished for her when she lives and merits as is proper. But if she does not live properly, these three are diminished from her, and a crown is not made for her from even one of them. Come and see what is written: >**"And if he does not do these three for her..."**< <note>Exodus 21:11</note>—referring to the lower levels. **"Then she shall go out for nothing, without money."** She shall go out from before the Living One. "Without money" <note>Hebrew: *Keseph*, also meaning "longing"</note> means she has no longing and no ornaments at all. Up to this point, merit and freedom depend on all the counsels within it—from where does good counsel come to all people? From here onward, he returns to the previous words regarding that supernal crown which the Holy One, Blessed be He, spreads over her, so that she is not taken outside in judgment, for all are guarded by her life constantly.

## Main Text (Zohar)

That righteous person reaches thirteen years and is transformed from being called the son of a stranger <note>original: *bar nokhri*, referring to the uncircumcised or spiritually unrefined state</note>. And all those who see from here on, he crowns his years above and merits them, and is certainly called a son to the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written: <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note> **"You are children to the Lord your God."** When David reached thirteen years, he merited on that day above to be marked [with holiness]; then it was written: <note>Psalms 2:7</note> **"The Lord said to me, 'You are My son; today I have begotten you.'"** What was the case before this? He was not yet a "son," and the supernal soul <note>original: *nishmata ila'ah*</note> had not yet rested upon him, for he was still within the years of the "foreskin" <note>the first thirteen years are seen as a period of spiritual concealment</note>. Thus, **"Today I have begotten you"**—today, and not before this. And regarding this "Other Side" <note>original: *sitra achra*, the realm of impurity</note>, as it was until now, so it remains alone. Except for the crowning of years, what is written of Solomon? <note>Proverbs 4:3</note> **"For I was a son to my father, tender and the only one before my mother."** And now, from thirteen years and onward, since he has departed from the domain of Samael <note>the personification of evil/the accuser</note> and comes into His kingdom, what is written? <note>Exodus 21:9</note> **"He shall deal with her according to the law of daughters."** What is **"the law of daughters"**? We have learned: Every single day the Holy One, blessed be He, sees that youth who was called the son of a stranger, a "foreskin," and a bent serpent; he is snatched away to the schoolhouse and breaks [the power of the Other Side], and goes to the synagogue and breaks it. What does the Holy One, blessed be He, do for that soul? He brings her into His chamber and gives her gifts and revealed ornaments, and adorns her with supernal adornments until they reach the wedding canopy <note>original: *chuppah*</note> when that boy is thirteen years and older. <note>Exodus 21:10</note> **"If he takes another for himself."** Here lies a <term>Secret of Secrets</term> <note>original: *raza de-razin*; profound mystical insight</note>; do not hand it over [to the unworthy], for it is a power to renew her at first as something new. Come and see: On the Sabbath day, at the hour when Israel sanctifies the day in the synagogue, souls go out from within the <term>Tree of Life</term> <note>original: *ilana de-chayye*; the source of holy souls</note> and blow <unclear>graciously</unclear> holy souls, and they rest within him all through the Sabbath day. After the Sabbath departs, all those souls ascend and are crowned with holy crowns above, and all are crowned by that Sabbath; they are certainly the masters of that goodness. So too, the Holy One, blessed be He, sees that person, and behold, the power of "another soul" hovers over him, though it was not prepared for him immediately from the start like her, yet **"her time of duty he shall not diminish,"** as has been said. Just as He commanded from the beginning, and said to him at the end: "Old man, old man! How much you yearn to embrace holy words!" See and attend to them with us for the sake of a "new man." Come and be zealous for them, for these words do not stand alone, as it is written: <note>Proverbs 3:27</note> **"Do not withhold good from its owners when it is in the power of your hand to do it."** What is **"Do not withhold good from its owners"**? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He—are they not here? For in every place where words of Torah are spoken, the Holy One, blessed be He—are they not there? And let us bring to mind that Tree of Good and Evil; at the time when the profane [days] are nourished, those words rest. That <term>Side</term> <note>original: *sitra*</note> of Good is transformed and ascends above, and the Holy One, blessed be He, etc., are crowned with that Good, and they are the masters of that Good. "Old man, old man! Are there other words than these? I did not know!" By the life of the Holy One, blessed be He, and by the life of these who stand here, all these are the words. Do not fear, old man! For you have been in many battles with mighty men and did not fear, and now you fear? Speak from yourself, for certainly the Holy One, blessed be He, and those who are here are present, and by their lives, I am pleased with them and do not need [other] words. Speak your words as I say everything for the sake of the profane. He opened and said: <note>Psalms 104:1</note> **"O Lord my God, You are very great; You are clothed in glory and majesty."** "O Lord my God"—this is the joy of faith, the ascent of the Supernal Thought to bring a single spirit without separation. **"You are great"**—this is the joy of the first day of all, the side of the Right <note>the attribute of Mercy/Chesed</note> prepared by the Ancient Ones. **"Very"** <note>original: *me'od*</note>—from that Crown <note>Keter</note> which is hidden. **"You are clothed in glory and majesty"**—these are the two "willow branches" <note>the sefirot of Netzach and Hod</note>. Until here, because they reached into the Tree of Life to be spoken of, but they were not yet established to be as they were at first, because it is a [hidden] matter. From what is "Very"? A garment for all the branches below, and including one bitter branch; and because of this, that Tree of Life was hidden and did not wish to build as at first, until it returns to its original state and slaughters in another manner. And he said: "Now return to its name; this is the beginning for this day."

<meta>This page continues the discourse of the "Saba de-Mishpatim" (The Elder of Mishpatim), focusing on the mystical journey of souls, specifically the relationship between holy souls and the souls of converts, and how they are "clothed" in spiritual garments within the Garden of Eden.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Laws**<-
<note>original: "Mishpatim" (Exodus 21:1). This section of the Zohar uses the legal portions of the Torah as a springboard for mystical secrets.</note>

Of the primordial spirit. Like that water here, for the purpose of the vessel and for the living being, from one side for the purpose of the vessel on the right, to be illuminated in all that is hidden. **"Who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters"** <note>Psalms 104:3</note>. Here it emerges in strength, for it is the standing tree that emerges from Eden and spreads out within its waters; those two willow branches <note>referring to the Sefirot Netzach and Hod</note> which grow in the waters of "all who lay the beams of His upper chambers in the waters." Who are "His upper chambers"? These are the willow branches, and this is what is written: **"And spreads out its roots by the river"** <note>Jeremiah 17:8</note>. And this is the spirit of which it is written: **"There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God"** <note>Psalms 46:5</note>. Who are "its streams"? These are its roots when they are called out. "His upper chambers" means his roots. Its streams are all watered from the waters of that river. **"Who makes the clouds His chariot"** <note>Psalms 104:3</note>—these clouds are the angels Michael and Gabriel. **"Who walks on the wings of the wind"** <note>Psalms 104:3</note>—to go with intention into the world, and this is the angel Raphael. From here onward, **"He makes His angels spirits..."** <note>Psalms 104:4</note>.

"Old man, old man! See how much you know, yet you do not fear? Speak your words, and let the words of your mouth shine!" The companions stood and kissed him because of his holy words. He said, "By the life of the Elder! Not for nothing did you bring yourself in; you entered into the thickness of the spirit, it lived for you on the side, and you emerged from there." If he prepared for us several ancient reincarnations <note>term: gilgulim (cycles/reincarnations of souls)</note> here that had not been revealed until now, they are all the truth as is fitting, for one cannot deny a word of truth even by a hair’s breadth.

At first, he lived to awaken the souls of converts <note>term: geyrim (proselytes)</note>. They all fly from within the Garden of Eden together in secret. When they are completed from this world, the souls that were empty within the Garden of Eden—to what place do they return? Rather, we have learned: one who was nullified and profaned among the stars, and converts at first, etc. Even so, all those holy souls enter into the place the Holy One, Blessed be He, has prepared for them in the Lower Garden of Eden. As we have said, they all go out at appointed times and ascend to delight in the Upper Garden of Eden. There they encounter those souls of converts. Whoever profaned them—from these souls that ascend, he is hidden in them, merits them, is intertwined with them, and they ascend. They all stand in this garment <note>term: levusha (a spiritual vestment earned through deeds)</note> and descend into the Lower Garden. This is because in the Garden of Eden, they do not stand there without a garment—all who stand there [must be clothed].

If you say that because of this garment these souls lack any of the delight they had previously—come and see what is written: **"If he takes another wife, her food, her clothing, and her conjugal rights he shall not diminish"** <note>Exodus 21:10</note>. In the Garden, they stand in a garment, not as before. To return to them and merit them; and when they ascend above, they strip themselves of it, for there they do not stand in a garment.

That Elder wept as before and said, "Pay heed, Elder, Elder! Surely it lived for you to build; surely it lived for you to strive, for you delve into every single word, as it is revealed before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Indwelling Presence <note>the Shekhinah</note>." The holy ones above bow to him, and all their companions wait, for they rejoice in every word and are crowned by them. For all those holy souls, when they descend to this world to watch over their bodies to repair them... they all descend and clothe themselves in those souls that are red <note>perhaps referring to the material/animal soul</note>, and thus they cover the holy seed. And in this kingdom <note>the Sefirah of Malkhut</note> they stand to strive for the life of this world.

And all the rulers of the words of this world look upon them; those holy souls return from the fragrance they inherited from within these garments of theirs. The Holy One, Blessed be He, made all hidden things pressed together above, and He sustains them in holy freedom <note>term: cheruta (referring to the Sefirah Binah, the source of liberation)</note>. Everything is found there. And the moon <note>Malkhut</note> is a hidden matter; Freedom reveals her, and immediately she clothes herself in another garment and is hidden there and not revealed. And their standing is for life, full of eyes; even though <note>original: "a'g" (af al gav)</note> that matter is melted into the garment there, they see it from within the garment. Just as that matter was revealed before it entered the garment, they see it with an opening of the eye; and even though it was immediately melted, it was not hidden from their eyes. And just as they merit to see the Holy One, Blessed be He, over them, so that the holy seed shall be cast into it. And afterward, the hidden word emerges from the silence. And since—

<meta>This page continues the famous "Saba de-Mishpatim" (The Elder of Mishpatim) discourse. It follows the Elder's mystical teachings on the soul and transitions into the celebrated allegory of the Torah as a maiden in a palace. This section is a cornerstone of Kabbalistic hermeneutics, describing the four levels of scriptural interpretation (Pardes) through the lens of a romantic pursuit.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And as soon as she is revealed, she immediately returns to her place and withdraws there. Since she is hidden, all those who are worthy see a word emerge from the crown <note>original: *kotereta*, referring to a divine emanation or a crown on the letters</note>, and it is revealed, saying: *And you know the soul of the stranger* <note>Exodus 23:9</note>. Immediately, she enters her place and returns to her longing and hides herself, as it is written: *For you were strangers in the land of Egypt* <note>Exodus 22:20</note>. This is the conclusion of the verse: once she is revealed, that which she sinned with regarding this "soul of the stranger" is no longer there. And the holy hiddenness is known through the matters of this world, yet remains concealed from them.

That Elder opened his discourse and said: *And Moses went into the midst of the cloud, and went up into the mount...* <note>Exodus 24:18</note>. What is this "cloud"? This is the power of which it is written: *I have set my bow in the cloud* <note>Genesis 9:13</note>. We have learned that this "bow" <note>the rainbow, a symbol of the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> stripped off its garments and gave them to Moses, and in that garment Moses ascended the mountain, and through it, he saw what he saw and enjoyed everything.

At the end, heralds came and stood before that Elder, whispering and covering their faces, saying: "The power has not been given to the world to hear these words from your mouth; enough for you!" The Elder said: "Heaven forbid that one should take it for himself alone." The heralds did not say this because the word is needed for him alone, for a father among his children does not speak with words but makes a small sign <note>original: *kit kit*, a clicking sound or gesture</note> and does not call out.

How many people in the world are in confusion regarding their own sovereignty and do not see the path of truth in the Torah! And the Torah calls out every day with longing toward human beings, but they do not wish to turn their heads. And even though I say that the Torah—a word—emerges from the crown and is seen for a moment and immediately hides itself, it is certainly so.

Happy is the portion of that person who is the beloved of the Torah! The Torah only does this for those who know her and are acquainted with her. To her beloved, she is beautiful in appearance and beautiful in form <note>a reference to Rachel in Genesis 29:17</note>, and she is hidden in the depths of her palace. She has a single lover whom people do not know, but he is in hiding. Who is this lover? It is the one who loves her. He passes by the gate of her house constantly, lifting his eyes to every side. And she knows that her lover is constantly circling the gate of her house. What does she do? She opens a tiny door in that hidden palace where she dwells, reveals her face to her lover, and immediately returns and hides.

All those who were near the lover did not see and did not look, except for the lover alone; and his innards, his heart, and his soul go out after her. He knows that out of the love she has for him, she revealed herself to him for a single moment to awaken love toward her.

So it is with a word of Torah: she does not reveal herself except to her lover. The Torah knows that the "wise of heart" <note>the dedicated mystic</note> circles the gate of her house every day. What does she do? She reveals her face to that wise of heart from within the palace, hints to him with a sign <note>original: *remiza*</note>, and immediately returns to her place and hides. All those who are there do not know and do not look, except for him alone; and his innards, his heart, and his soul go out after her. Therefore, the Torah is revealed and hidden, and goes in love toward her lover to awaken love with him.

Come and see: the way of the Torah is thus. At first, when she begins to reveal herself to a person, she hints to him with a sign. If he knows, it is well; if he does not know, she sends for him and calls him "simple." The Torah says to the fool that she sent for: "Let the simple one turn in here," and she speaks with him directly. As it is written: *Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither; as for him that void of understanding...* <note>Proverbs 9:4</note>. She calls to him from behind a curtain <note>original: *parokhta*</note> to speak with him, and she arranges words according to his way until he looks little by little—and this is the "secret" <note>the level of *Sod*</note>.

Afterward, she speaks with him from behind a thin veil <note>original: *sotafia*</note>, words of riddles, and it is not yet full delight. After he has become accustomed to her, she reveals herself to him face to face and speaks with him of all her hidden secrets and all the hidden paths that have been concealed in her heart from the earliest days. Then...

<meta>This page continues the discourse of the "Old Man" (Saba de-Mishpatim) regarding the mystical laws of reincarnation and the nature of the soul. It specifically addresses how the soul (Neshamah) and spirit (Ruach) interact, their judgment before entering the world, and the mechanics of the "levirate" mystery where a spirit is redeemed.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Laws (Mishpatim)**<-

When a master of the Torah enters <note>into these mysteries</note> and is drawn to the members of his household <note>the inner circle of mystics</note>, all her secrets are revealed to him; she does not distance herself or withhold anything from him. She says to him: "See, from the word I hinted to you at first, such and such secrets were there, and such and such they were." Then they see that all those words are neither to be added to nor subtracted from their intended meaning. And then the literal meaning of the verse is as it is, without adding or subtracting even a single letter. And for this reason, people must be careful to pursue the Torah to acquire her love, as has been said. **Come and see**: "If he takes another for himself" <note>Exodus 21:10</note>—these are the reincarnations <note>original: *gilgulin*</note> that cycle through this verse. How great and lofty they are! For indeed, all souls enter into reincarnation, yet human beings do not know the ways of the Holy One, Blessed be He, nor how the scale <note>original: *tikla*, the balance of judgment</note> stands, nor how human beings are judged every day and at every moment. They do not know how souls enter into judgment before they come into this world, and how they enter after they depart from this world.

How many reincarnations and how many hidden deeds does the Holy One, Blessed be He, perform! How many naked souls and how many naked spirits wander in that world, unable to enter through the King’s Curtain <note>original: *pargoda de-malka*, the celestial veil</note>. How many worlds are overturned by them, and the world is overturned by many hidden wonders, yet human beings do not know and do not observe how souls roll like a stone in a sling <note>Cf. 1 Samuel 25:29</note>, as it is written: "the soul of your enemies He shall sling out as from the hollow of a sling" <note>original: *kaf ha-kela*</note>.

And that precision in the cycle opens for him a carving <note>a revelation</note>, for indeed all souls go out from that great and mighty river that flows out from Eden. And all spirits go out from their place and are awakened, emerging in a drop from above, a spirit from below, and they join as one in the manner of male and female. When they all join as one, they then shine with the radiance of the world <note>Cf. Daniel 12:3</note>. And in the single union of the two of them, it is called "Son" <note>original: *Bar*</note>. <margin>The lamp of the Lord is the soul</margin> As in "The lamp of the Lord is the soul of man" <note>Proverbs 20:27</note>. What is "Son" <note>Bar</note>? It is the numerical value of <term>Spirit (Ruach)</term> <note>The Hebrew word *Ruach* (214) equals the word *Bar* (202) plus the 12 months of the year or similar mystical calculations</note>. And regarding the union of the two of them as one, it is called "Son." For it is written: "The lamp of the Lord is the soul of man." Soul <note>Neshamah</note> and Spirit <note>Ruach</note> are male and female to surround as one; this one without that one does not shine and is not called "Son." But when they join as one, they are called "Son." And then the Soul is wrapped in the Spirit to stand there above in the hidden palace, as it is written:
> For the spirit shall wrap itself before Me <note>Isaiah 57:16</note>
It does not say "it shall wrap" <note>passive</note> but "He shall wrap" <note>active</note>.
What is the reason? Because the Soul is the garment of the wrapping. There above, in the hidden Soul, the Soul is wrapped and clothed in the Spirit, as we have said. For since the Soul is a palace for it, it only makes use of the Spirit. And the Soul is not given except when clothed in that Spirit. And when it descends into the lower Garden of Eden, like this world, it is clothed in that other spirit which is grasped from that which goes out from there. And through all of them, it clings to this world and is clothed in that spirit which goes out from this world, which was not raised and did not spread in this world except through reincarnation. It finds no rest and repeats in reincarnation in the world like a stone in a sling, until it finds that redeemer who shall redeem it in that very "king" <note>the deceased brother in a levirate marriage context</note> who used it and to whom his spirit was always attached. And his wife was the spirit within the spirit, and that redeemer builds it as at first. And that spirit which was left behind and attached to that "king" is not lost, for there is not even a tiny thing in the world that does not have a place and a location to be preserved and gathered, and it is never lost. And because of this, that spirit which was left in that matter is there, and it pushes and pursues after its root and its foundation from which it emerged, to accompany it and build it in its place. After that, the spirit of his mate, which went out in light, is established there as at first. And no man knows that now in the world there is a new spirit and a new body. And if you say it is the same spirit that was—it is so, but it was only established because of that other spirit that was left in that "king" here...

It describes the "hollow of the sling" as a state of wandering for unrectified souls and hints at the mystery of levirate redemption where a deceased man's spirit is reclaimed.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the laws of reincarnation (Gilgul) and the restoration of bodies at the time of the resurrection, specifically focusing on the "Faithful Shepherd" (Ra'aya Mehemna) section of the Zohar. It addresses the metaphysical mechanics of how multiple bodies inhabited by the same soul are treated in the afterlife.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Judgments**<-

The spirit of life opened (this is the spirit of rest that ascends the worlds) in the **Book of Enoch** <note>A mystical text attributed to the biblical figure Enoch, often cited in the Zohar for secrets regarding the soul's journey</note> regarding this: those who were found were not built except through that spirit which was left there in that altar. And when they ascend to be found, this one draws after it that naked spirit that is powerful, and it harms him toward it. And there are two likenesses there that are one after the other: one is spirit and the other is a garment <note>original: *kesufa*, referring to the spiritual "clothing" or vessel of the soul</note>. And both of them are one, living and dead, to be found as is fitting. And both of them are one in which another higher soul <note>original: *neshamata achra ila'ah*</note> is found, just as exists for the children of the world. The spirit through which souls merit are those that precede and go within them, and another spirit from above, and in the holy soul to be found within them. So too, like a literal filling, there are two spirits in order for the higher soul to be found in them; He gave to this another body that is now found as a measure. In the end, the first breath that was left—what is made of it? Or so, both are empty in their spit <note>A metaphor for the lack of spiritual substance or "moisture" in a body without a soul</note>. According to human understanding, it is heard that the first one who went to be grasped first was destroyed before Him and did not merit. If so, why did he strive in the commandments of the Torah? Even in one of them! And they see and know that even the forms in her sides, all these things are portions; except for this infant, even though they were not found to be purified and to purify in the world other commandments of the Torah, so that they would not be lost from him. And why for nothing would they proclaim the proclamation: "Open your eyes!" For behold, here they know that so they are; the masters know that all those bodies are living in emptiness, having no existence forever? It is not so! Far be it from us to be found in these words <note>A common Zoharic expression meaning "Heaven forbid we should think such a thing"</note>. He opened and said:
> Who can utter the mighty acts of the Lord? Who can show forth all His praise? <note>Psalms 106:2</note>
Who is there in the world who can speak of the mighty deeds that the Holy One, Blessed Be He, does in the world constantly? That first body which was left is not destroyed, and it shall have existence for the time to come <note>The Resurrection of the Dead</note>. For behold, all are hidden in His treasures, and the Holy One, Blessed Be He, does not withhold the reward of any creature, for all are living beings that emerged from the faith of the Master, and there is no end to the good in them forever. And every matter that did not bow like a *Modai* <note>A reference to the "Modim" prayer of thanksgiving; here implying submission to Divine will</note>, the Holy One, Blessed Be He, makes from it other callings, so that the end—the body of the infant—is not built later when the spirit shall rise forever. But rather, is it not so that the Holy One, Blessed Be He, makes the spirit live now? And to be found in this world in that other body, what does the Holy One, Blessed Be He, do? That redemption which He redeems in the end, his spirit that goes there and is strong, and it mixes with that spirit that was in that altar. Certainly it is not to be destroyed. And what is made? For behold, three spirits are there: one that was in the book and wisdom and was prepared there; and one that was found there which was naked; and one that is from above there, that redemption, and it mixes with them. To exist in three spirits, or to depart. Rather, such are the higher mighty deeds that the Holy One, Blessed Be He, performs. That spirit from above there, that redemption, in it is found that other soul to sweeten the colors and the voice. And that naked spirit that returned there to be found shall be for a cover for the higher sweetness. And that spirit which was in the beginning, which remained in that power, redeemed there. And the Holy One, Blessed Be He, will prepare for it a place like the dwellings of the males behind the shoulders of the **Garden of Eden**, and it remains there and ascends to that first body that was in the beginning. And in that spirit, that body shall rise. And this is one of the living, two that we mentioned above. For all that breath, until there arises a great hidden thing, for behold, children who were not found like him are placed in the ban of the destruction that is near to being poured out, and are judged there, and afterwards they raise him to this blue <note>original: *techelet*, perhaps referring to a specific heavenly firmament</note>. Now you have seen, and now it ascends; behold they have ascended and live. You have seen he has no one around him except for the danger-dwellers, and like equal days and the carvings of months, and those who sleep in the dust of the earth.

<meta>This page continues the famous discourse of the "Saba de-Mishpatim" (The Old Man of Mishpatim) from the Zohar, Section II. The previous context involves the "Old Man," a hidden sage appearing as a donkey-driver, revealing deep mysteries regarding the transmigration of souls (reincarnation) and the laws of the Torah as they apply to the spirit's journey.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Judgments** <-
<note>original: "Mishpatim" — the title of the Torah portion dealing with civil laws, here interpreted mystically.</note>

**The earth of decay:** crumbling dust. And concerning these it is written <note>Daniel 12:2</note> **"And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to reproaches and everlasting abhorrence."** All these are those who did not merit to be rectified <note>term: rectified/tikkun — the process of spiritual repair or completion</note>. But if they did merit, that naked spirit <note>original: "rucha artila’ah" — a soul wandering without the "garment" of its good deeds or a physical body</note> which returns as it was before to be rectified, and all of it is that same spirit found within it, for whose sake it shall be rectified in that body. And concerning these it is written, **"some to everlasting life, etc."** and to reproaches, etc. All those who do not merit to be rectified. And these are the supernal powers of the Holy High King, and He does not overlook anything, even the breath of one's mouth. Below, there is a place for it, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings about what He does, and even a word <unclear>is not lost</unclear> and this exchange does not happen in vain; there is a place and a station for everything. My brother, those who were found at the opening and went out into the world, he checks the opening and has no partner, and because of this they proclaim that his soulmate was taken from him; his soulmate that he had was enslaved to another, and there is bread for all.

**Old man, old man!** <note>The text addresses the "Saba," the mysterious elderly sage</note> What have you done? Silence would have been better for you. **Old man, old man!** Thus I say: the world is a great house, all are consumed and all are as nothing—what will you do? If you say you will ascend above, you cannot. If you say you will descend below, that is the depth of the great abyss—what will you do? O **living Old Man**, **Old Man**, you have no way to turn back. In those times you were not present, and you did not stir to be rectified in your strength, for you knew that <unclear>another</unclear> like all this generation did not enter into this depth where you have gone. Blessed be the Image <note>The Divine form/Tzelem</note> and He knows them; reproaches were spoken, and he lives above in the deep day of the <unclear>hated one</unclear> at first. How shall he act at once? And he shall improve well in the day before he enters, and the merit of the **Old Man** was not found at first.

The **Old Man** opened at the brook and descended there; do not bend the whole path to stray to the right or to the left, to the length or the breadth, to the depth or the height—do not fear! **Old Man, old man**, strengthen yourself in your strength! How many mighty men have you broken in their might, and how many wars have you conquered? He opened and said: to grace and beloved companions, such as King Solomon in the crown <note>original: "atarah" — referring to the Sefirah of Malchut/Kingship</note> with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, the day of his gift, and like the cup of his heart's joy. My brother called out wisely and said this: Woe for the grace and the beloved, etc. A vision, etc. to see King Solomon, who is the King to whom peace belongs <note>note: a common Zoharic play on the name Solomon/Shlomo, meaning "The King of Peace," referring to God</note>, and He is hidden from all high matters from above in that place <note>Isaiah 64:3</note> **"No eye has seen a God besides You."** And you speak of grace and beloved companions like King Solomon? Furthermore, regarding His glory, all the supernal angels tremble and are in turmoil over "the place of His glory." Rather, that which was said regarding grace and beloved companions like King Solomon **"in the crown"**—it is written "in the crown" and not "and in the crown," for whoever sees that crown sees the <unclear>delight</unclear> of the King to whom peace belongs. A crown—his mother-in-law calls it, a daughter calls it, a mother-in-law calls it—Heaven forbid!—and it is all one, and all was for one who gazes and will know at first, and then precious wisdom.

He opened <unclear>to work</unclear> the living of the beast, this hidden secret <note>original: "raza setima"</note> must not be revealed. I will not say "living" and they will be provoked, and these will be finished from this spirit. Like that **Old Man** on his knees, and to the one who wraps to visit the hints <note>Psalm 31:6</note> **"Into Your hand I commit my spirit; You have redeemed me, O Lord, God of truth."** From here, that which is below—how shall it be made above? As that which was above—how shall it be overturned and become that which is below? His soulmate was enslaved to another. Wonder at the wonder! To see the furnace. To me belonged the merit of the beginning, he shall redeem him properly for all to merit the furnace, etc. I have not seen a wonder; I have seen the world as an upside-down thing. And those who were above are below, and those who were below are above. But "Let the name of God be blessed from world to world, for wisdom and might are His." And he goes out from here <unclear>until</unclear> and brings out, etc. <note>Daniel 2:22</note> **"He knows what is in the darkness, and light dwells with Him."** He stood watching those who travel in the caravan; he could not look to examine in the darkness. But a voice, my brother, weep and know.

<summary>The "Old Man" (Saba) reveals the mystical secrets of the "naked spirit" and the trials of reincarnation, explaining how souls are rectified through successive lives and the mystery of soulmates being "enslaved" to others. He uses the imagery of King Solomon's crown to describe the hidden nature of Divine glory and the "upside-down" nature of the spiritual world compared to the physical one.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discourse of the "Elder of Mishpatim" (Saba de-Mishpatim), focusing on the mystical mechanics of reincarnation (Gilgul) and the soul's transition between the masculine and feminine spiritual realms.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And know that even though the light labors with the filth <note>original: *metuna*; referring to the physical body or the "husk" of existence</note>, the light gazes into the filth and knows all that is there. Here we must first establish a matter that the ancients spoke of regarding the balance: Woe to those who see a matter but do not apply understanding <note>original: *binah*</note> to it, as it is written: **For God has deprived her of wisdom** <note>Job 39:17</note>. Here one must look closely, for if he descends, his end will be as written: that he who sees the matter will merit Understanding. But if one comes upon his vision to sin, then the supernal spirit—at the time it is transformed above—ascends from below to above. As it was at first, once it ascends above, the path is reversed; he becomes part of the supernal world, rules over it, and merits Understanding. At first, when he ascends, he is placed among the thirty-three <note>possibly referring to the 33 years of a specific spiritual cycle or the 33 paths</note>, and above what is written?

> **The Lord said to me: "You are My son; today I have begotten you."** <note>Psalms 2:7</note>

Then he is below it. Once he ascends upon it, he is from the supernal worlds, for he has ascended to the level of **Joseph** <term>Joseph: representing the Sefirah of Yesod, the "Foundation" and the procreative force</term>, and this (God forbid) merits Understanding. So too, the King washed at first; he was like the foot of Joseph seeking a path beneath him, standing by his will and ruling over it. For every female is in the image of the Female <note>original: *Nukva*</note>, the path stands beneath her. Since he then sought to stand in that level of Joseph but did not succeed in reaching it—to bring forth into the world and produce offspring—then he is like a death below, and she becomes a burden. And with the voice of redemption, he inherits the inheritance of Joseph, which he had at first, and he is like a death below. Once he descends below, then it is fulfilled in him: *The Lord said to me: "You are My son; today I have begotten you."* The path is reversed; that which was finally beneath him and he ruled over it, the path returns to rule over her, and he is like a death below. 

Since he is like a death below, that one who went to the inheritance—the place of Joseph—is called "the one who strikes," and he gathers into himself all offspring, and he is upon his restoration and pushes away as is proper. At first, he ends from the **Male world** <term>Dikhra: the masculine spiritual principle of giving/emanation</term> and is uprooted from there, and he is viewed from the **Female world** <term>Nukva: the feminine spiritual principle of receiving/manifestation</term>. He goes out and rules over it, and it returns to being in the Female world. Furthermore, he has no soulmate <note>original: *bat zug*</note> at all. No announcement is made regarding a woman for him, for he is arranged from the Female world. He is the "first body" to the "widowed elder," and they shall know and look upon the weeping of the world—a youth who has nothing when he is uprooted from the Male world and returns to the Female world. And they shall know that there is no "youth" in the world like the coverings of a youth. He has no soulmate because he does not stand in the place of the Male; no announcement is made for a woman for him because he is from the Female world. But a living one has a soulmate through mercy, even though the female has washed, for until now she has no man. And regarding this we have learned that **reincarnation** <term>Gilgul: the cycle of the soul returning to a new body to achieve perfection</term> is more precious than the place when it arrives. Another teaching: everything is according to its restoration, and regarding this it is written:

> **"But if a priest’s daughter is widowed or divorced and has no child, and she returns to her father’s house as in her youth, she may eat of her father’s food."** <note>Leviticus 22:13</note>

"A priest's daughter"—we have established this matter. "Widowed"—from that first body. "Divorced"—because she did not enter the King's Curtain <note>original: *pargoda*; the celestial veil</note>, for all those who do not stand in the Male world have no portion; he slipped away and was uprooted by a hint from the Male world and has no portion in it. Therefore, she is "divorced and has no child," for he did not sow and was not uprooted from it, and it was not like a death to the Female world. "And she returns to her father's house"—what is "her father's house"? This is the Female world, for that world is called "her father's house." And when he is the King who was to restore and be restored in it, the descent is reversed like a death below, and that King ascends above. "As in her youth"—like that time of which it is written:

> **"You are My son; today I have begotten you."** <note>Psalms 2:7</note>

And he is purified and merits the days of his youth as he was at first, afflicted by the blade; and above, the merit of restoration lives. And since "she returns to her father's house," she shall eat of her father's bread—

->**She shall delight.**<-

<meta>This page continues the discourse of the "Saba de-Mishpatim" (The Old Man of Mishpatim), a famous section of the Zohar where an elderly donkey-driver reveals profound mysteries. The focus here is on the laws of Levirate marriage (Yibbum) and the mystical journey of the soul (Nefesh) and spirit (Ruach) during reincarnation (Gilgul).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Laws (Mishpatim)**<-

His soul shall delight in the pleasure of the world that is gathered to his portion, and he shall enjoy the joy of the righteous above. However, to gaze and to enjoy as the other righteous enjoy, he is unable, because he was a "stranger" there <note>original: "zar" - referring to one who has not yet rectified his soul through the mysteries of procreation</note>. And as long as he has not eaten of the **Holy**, it is not beloved before the Living One who established the world. And because of the life of the world that He established, he does not eat of the "Challah" <note>The portion of dough given to priests; here a metaphor for spiritual sustenance</note> that is included, as it is written:
> And no **stranger** shall eat of the **holy thing**. <note>Leviticus 22:10</note>
The holy things are for his comfort. For before he is favored by the male world <note>The higher spiritual realm associated with the "male" aspect of divinity</note>, the Challah is not seen by him during the day. And because of this:
> **Israel was holiness unto the Lord, the first-fruits of His increase.** <note>Jeremiah 2:3</note>
The supernal fragrance of the entire male world is "Holiness" <note>Kodesh</note>. And Israel ascends through this Holiness. Because of this, "Israel is Holiness" within his portion of the "increase." All spirits are deposited in their strength, and they go out to the graves, but they are not "deposited" <note>in the higher sense</note> because they did not merit the world of Holiness, as it is written: "And no stranger shall eat of the holy thing." And if that spirit did not merit to be repaired as is fitting, when it returns in **reincarnation** <term>Gilgul: the transmigration of souls into new bodies</term>, even in this place of his "heave-offering" <note>Terumah</note> he does not eat, and he is called a "stranger" even to the lower world, and he does not eat of the Holy at all in this mystery.

Thus he opened: Since he has turned aside <term>taken in his days</term>, go according to your will to all sides that are pleasing. Now, life is toward him, for to see that this **redemption** <term>Peruka: the mystical "redemption" of a deceased brother's soul through Levirate marriage</term> comes and returns in that King whom we saw above there. And the spirit of the female world is purified there like this poor one, and nothing is lost, even the "breath of the mouth" <note>The spiritual residue left by a husband in his wife</note> was fitting, and so it was.

Open, open! Speak life and reveal warmth without fear! Other human beings in this world who depart from it should know what a generation leaves below, what was his, and what is pleasant above. What is done with the **hidden essence of his life**? Stand thus and see below what is done with this **spirit** <note>Ruach</note> that the first husband left in her <note>his wife</note>, for she is now married to another who has sealed her. To establish the spirit in a mystery, he did not depart; for he who seals her now, a spirit comes and is considered here. And so that first one who departed, a spirit above... that first one who departed because they hoped for him, and this one who is now their living **redemption**.

The spirit that the first one left in her is weakened, and another descends and sweeps it away, and it returns and returns when the spirit pushes it. And both of their spirits are gathered to be established in that body below. As it is said: Life is like that which is lost, life departs. What is made of it? Even so, their life is not suppressed. That spirit which her husband left in her—what is made of it? Life is like that which is lost—is it not so? Everything must be illuminated now. Open, open before Him! What have you done, and how much have you pained yourself? Arise, open for the spirit that descends! Arise, open and protect yourself before your Maker!

That **Old Man** <note>The Saba</note> opened and said:
> **Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty...** <note>Psalms 131:1</note>
King David said this because he was a king and a ruler over all the supernal kings and rulers from the East to the West, yet he did not allow his heart to become arrogant or to dwell apart from his Master. And when he labored in the Torah, his spirit was eventually moved, and his eyes were always lowered to the earth in awe of his Master. And when he walked among the people, there was no haughtiness of spirit in him at all. Regarding this it is written: "Lord, my heart is not haughty..." My heart was not haughty to act as a king ruling over all other kings of the world. "Nor mine eyes lofty" at the time I stand before You laboring in the Torah.
> **Neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too wonderful for me.** <note>Psalms 131:1</note>
In the sense that he walked among the people. And see, King David said this for the rest of the people of the world until now. And see how much he merited to beautify his heart and lower his eyes before the Holy King. And he said to me that with the holy words of the Torah, his heart would return in this, and his tears would fall upon his beard. Then he opened with life: How beautiful are the tears upon your beard, just as it was beautiful:
> **Like the precious oil upon the head, running down upon the beard, even Aaron's beard...** <note>Psalms 133:2</note>
Living are your words! Open, for behold...

## Main Text (Zohar)

For the Holy King is here! He opened his discourse among us, for those who have departed from the world and have prepared their spirit <note>Hebrew/Aramaic: *Ruach*</note> with that strength they used to employ. It was hidden, and he came to see and enter into that spirit that rests in another. What becomes of that first one, as has been stated? Come and see how many humiliations the Holy King performs, and we are obligated to speak of them. 

When this second husband comes and enters his spirit into that vessel <note>The "vessel" refers to the wife</note>, the first spirit prosecutes <note>or "contends with"</note> this spirit that has entered, and they do not settle together. Because of this, down below, she does not settle properly with the second husband because the first spirit is rustling <note>or "gnashing"</note> within her. Then she remembers him constantly and weeps for him, or is found sighing over him, for his spirit rustles in her innards like a serpent. It prosecutes against the spirit that entered her, hindering the second one for a long time. They prosecute one another, and the one who entered awakens to stand, and to awaken that which was first. 

Afterward, this first one departs and goes his way. Sometimes, this first one pushes away the second one and becomes an adversary to him until he removes him from the world. And the second one wanders from then on; a man should not join himself to her below, for the Angel of Death has strengthened himself in her. Then the world does not know that this spirit, once it has strengthened, seizes that other second spirit. From then on, a man should not mix with her below, as if fleeing. I know that in this daughter, you have the power to kill and to live. He does not die by the judgment of this second one, nor do they judge him from Above. 

Come and see all those who say "So-and-so, son of So-and-so" <note>A reference to naming conventions in prayers or incantations</note> so that So-and-so does not prosecute against him. And who is it that is written as "sickles" <note>Aramaic: *Charmashin*; likely a metaphor for destructive forces or the "sickles of death"</note> regarding the one who enters in his days with a strong spirit? They all consume and do not know life, passing through the dew or drowning in the depths. And this living one who entered, who is the second spirit, strengthens and confronts that first one; that first one departs from there and goes his way. 

To what place does it go, and what is done with it? Old man, old man, what have you done? You have remained to praise a little and went out to this; you entered a place where no other man has entered since the day of the spirit. And they have asked questions, like those four hundred questions they used to ask about the "tower flying in the air," and no man answered them until King Solomon came and explained each one according to its proper arrangement. Old man, old man, spirit of the world that is hidden, you have come to reveal! What have you done? Old man, old man, at first you should have looked at the silent eagle and gazed at the image <note>Aramaic: *Dyokan*, the spiritual archetype or "face"</note>. Alas, this is not the time to be told! Old man, return to your strength. 

That spirit that went out, where does it go? He wept and said: Friends, all these tears I weep are not for our sake, but for the strength of the Master of the World, for the hidden heights, the sons of the heights. Alas, I have revealed before Him—not for my honor have I done this, nor for the honor of my father, but my will is for His service. May we be worthy to see the glory of the Master in that world. And they said: We know that it is so. 

Alas, it was not revealed before him, and his wisdom appeared. We have learned: they push a man away because of another man with many hidden bans <note>or "nets"</note>. And it is likened to that first spirit that was seized before the second one. Where does that spirit go? It goes out and wanders in the world, unknown. It goes into the graves of that man, and from there it wanders the world and is found in dreams by many people. It shows them in a dream the image of that man and informs them of things according to his way. For that spirit is preserved by the power of how it was in that world; thus it wanders in this one, and thus it informs in this one. It constantly visits that grave until the time when spirits visit the graves of the bodies. Then this spirit joins with his spirit, clothes itself in it, and goes its way. When it enters its place to spread out from it, it has the merit to see, like those spirits in the Garden of Eden, like those...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the laws of marriage and the soul from the perspective of the Zohar's commentary on the Torah portion Mishpatim (Exodus 21-24). It specifically addresses the mystical mechanics of the "first" and "second" husband and the fate of the spirit left behind with a widow.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Judgments**<-
<note>original: "Mishpatim"</note>

Those who are worthy of it, each according to their own ways, and there it is explained. When they are summoned to this world, sometimes they are provided for during their life, provided with that drawing forth of the spirit, and within it, another spirit is clothed. And if you say: if so, what is the benefit to that spirit? And from this woman, she has performed a benefit for all of them. It is not so, for if she marries another, she is not pushed away from before that first spirit. The other man has another benefit in another manner, and he did not give to them in the world as they were, and he was exacting regarding the life of this world as it was from the higher tastes and the merit. If so, the second marriage of this woman was not from Above? But you said that a man stands before another man <note>meaning, one replaces another</note> and to have mercy, for this second husband—of whom it is written below—this one is her actual soulmate <term>Bat Zug: a predestined spiritual partner</term>. And that first one was not her actual soulmate. And in this second one, he was hers. And when his time arrived, this one was pushed away from before him. Certainly, it is so, for that first spirit that was in this woman did not endure except because this second one is her soulmate. This second one, and all those second ones who push away the first ones—the first ones were not their soulmates, and because of this, they have no permanence with them.

And the second spirit is pushed away from before the first spirit, and because of this, regarding one who is called a widow <term>Armenta</term>, we read concerning him: *(And he knows not that it is for his life. For a wise king scatters the wicked, etc.)* <note>Proverbs 7:23; 20:26</note> and he does not know if she is his actual soulmate or not. * A widow who is not covered <note>perhaps meaning one who has not remarried</note>, even though her soulmate comes and has pity on her now, it is found that **the Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>The standard Rabbinic name for God</note> is like a guide to her <margin>Correction: (And from your right hand we will not ride upon a horse, as in the portion of Balak)</margin> from the judgment. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, prepares that person when a woman belongs to another and did not enter properly like this one in this world. And even though she has no son—for a woman is not commanded regarding "be fruitful and multiply" as they have established—this woman who did not marry a second time, that spirit which her husband left in her, what becomes of it? It dwells there for twelve months, and every single night it goes out and visits the grave and returns to its place. After twelve months, when the image of that man is to depart—for all those twelve months the spirit is gathered in his eyes every day—after twelve months it goes out from there and goes and stands at the gate of Eden and visits this world at that **altar** <term>Mizbe'ach: referring here to the feminine Divine Presence or the site of the soul's sacrifice</term> from which it emerged. And when the woman is to depart from the world, that spirit goes out and clothes itself in her spirit, and she goes with it to her husband, and then both of them are as is fitting, like a single entity. Since we have come to this place, the **Other Side** <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of evil or impurity</term> seeks to confuse the hidden paths of the Master of the world, which human beings do not know. And all of them go in the path of truth, for:
> *For the ways of the Lord are right, and the just shall walk in them: but the transgressors shall fall therein.* <note>Hosea 14:10</note>
Worthy are those who do not know and do not gaze upon how many worlds are the works of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and how they go, and the children of the world do not know, and all of them are in the path of truth, not straying to the right or the left. These who are reincarnated <note>Gilgul</note>, who were cast out by divorce from that world and have no soulmate who happens upon them in this world, who are they? They are children who are paired with them in this world, for he is a divorcee and has no soulmate like all the men who were not divorced and are paired with their own, and all of them have a soulmate except for this one. Come and see how great and high are the powers within this. We have learned: whoever divorces his first wife, the altar sheds tears over him. Why? Rather, this is the life of all the houses of this world, which stand in the image of this altar, and for this reason, they inherit seven blessings, for all of them are the **Congregation of Israel** <term>Knesset Yisrael: the mystical personification of the Jewish people, often identified with the Shekhinah</term>. And if he divorces...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the laws of marriage and divorce from the perspective of the soul's journey. It specifically addresses the spiritual mechanics of "re-marriage" and "reincarnation" as reflected in the laws of Deuteronomy 24.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

He raises an objection and returns to the matter of divorce <note>Aramaic: *terukhin*</note> and the witnesses, for the secret of this is written:
> "And he shall write her a scroll of severance and place it in her hand... and she shall depart from his house and go and become the wife of **another** man." (Deuteronomy 24:1-2)

This implies that when it says "and she shall go," I do not know if she goes back to her husband who divorced her. Why does it say "to **another** man"? Rather, it is as we have said: "after this" <note>Aramaic: *achar*</note> and "afterward" <note>Aramaic: *acharon*</note> are written, and we read it as "Another." As it is written:
> "And from **another** dust they shall sprout." (Job 8:19)

And the divorces are joined as one—the divorce of that upper world and the divorce of this world. And that which was below was in the **supernal image** <note>The divine archetype</note>; he looks at the lower image and calls it "Another" <note>Aramaic: *Achar*</note>, and we read it as "The Last" <note>Aramaic: *Acharon*</note>. From where do we know "The Last"? As it is written:
> "And **the last** shall rise upon the dust." (Job 19:25)

And in all these, it is "The Last." Furthermore, "if that **last** man dies." This "Last" is more significant than what came before, and it is a wonder that she should not be paired even with this crown after that one. It is not so. For if she does not pair with her husband nor with another, what is this "Last"? Rather, this is what we have said, and they are one. And it is called "The Last" because the "Other" <note>The side of impurity or the 'Other Side'</note> rolls within the box <note>A reference to the body or the cycle of reincarnation</note>. The "Other" who strikes and calls out thus, for the entire building is doubled and returns to its dust; nothing remains of what was. And to the "Other" who strikes, we call him "Another." So too, for the striker, they call him "The Last." And is "The Last" his law? This living one shall be punished and shall not return, nor be reincarnated, nor be planted as at first. For the striker, they call him "The Last." Woe to those who do not see what is written:
> "And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was **very good**." (Genesis 1:31)

"Good"—we have learned this is the Angel of Good. "**Very**"—this is the Angel of Death. And for all of them, the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, has prepared rectifications. Come and see, it is written:
> "And a river went out from Eden to water the garden." (Genesis 2:10)

This river never ceases from emerging, building, and producing fruit. But any "Other" that is there has nothing, as it is written "forever," and it does not produce fruit; for if it produced fruit, it would destroy the whole world. Because of this, a man who clings to that side <note>The *Sitra Achra* or "Other Side"</note> which is called "Evil" in the world will never see the face of the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence</note>, as it is written:
> "Evil shall not dwell with You." (Psalms 5:5)

This man who is rolled in this **reincarnation** <note>Aramaic: *gilgula*</note> and passes away without rectifying that "Other" space that does not produce fruit or benefit the world—because of this, he is called "Another." And when does he cling to life? "Another" and "Another" they call him, and they call it the "Kindness of the Living." From the beginning and onward we call him "The Last," and for "The Last" they search. Immediately they search for "The Last," and thus the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, calls him "The Last" because he was prepared to be the final one and not return as at first a second time. And so at all times, from the beginning and onward, he is called "The Last," and it is necessary to call him "The Last" because he is called immediately "the second." This is the **opening of the mouth** to return as at first, and he is remembered in the manner of the binding. From where do we know this? From the Second Temple, as it is written:
> "Greater shall be the glory of this **latter** <note>Aramaic/Hebrew: *Acharon*</note> house than the first." (Haggai 2:9)

From the beginning and onward they call it "The Last," for there will be no "opening of the mouth" there in that manner, to be doubled and return as at first. So too, we call this "The Last," and because of this it is written:
> "Her first husband, who sent her away, **shall not be able** to take her again." (Deuteronomy 24:4)

"He shall not be able"—it should have said "he shall not take her." Why "he shall not be able"? Rather, since this woman was established in this state and in her end to be subjugated to a **lower level**, the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, does not want them to return from his level to eat for free <note>A reference to "bread of shame" or unearned spiritual light</note> and to cling to that level which is not his. And come and see: if this woman had not married another, she would return like all people of the world; if her husband wanted, he could return to her. Everything is attached to life as is fitting. But after this, "he shall not be able" to return to the **former level** that he had with her at first. He shall certainly not be able to rest in that level forever, for she is "defiled." We have learned that "she is defiled" is inclusive. Or so, she would be rectified and merit everything as at first. But since she clung to "Another," she received upon herself the portion of that side, and her first husband [cannot return].

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Laws**<-

Initially, the serpent <note>original: *chivya*; representing the primordial forces of evil or the "Other Side"</note> from the side of darkness was good for him; he shall have a portion in the worlds and shall not perish at all from that place. Behold, he spared his own body, and the latter lent to him, for when he dies, the thread of deficiency returns to the beginning to return everything to its place. Perhaps it will be found below as before, and the deficiency will arise to be paired with it. He who possesses this, because of the first and the sin, he sinned for the sake of his house on that day to cling to the side of sin which turns about because of two sides: one, for there are two that judge all, and the third is the side of the serpent. Furthermore, the constellation <note>original: *mazla*; destiny or celestial influence</note> that was made through him is another, and it shall come to him to give within him a spirit of falsehood, and it shall partner with it and cling to it. It is not that the serpent's deficiency is hidden within it. For his house and to support himself as they see. Rabbi Yosta cursed <note>original: *layit*; a common Zoharic expression for a sharp disagreement or a mystical rebuke</note>... he was smiling and mocking at what is below, before the one who was to pair with it, and he would say: *And she shall laugh at the time to come* <note>Proverbs 31:25</note>. "Deficiency" is written; he who clings to it through the sin of deficiency is able to reach the Crown <note>original: *Keter*; the highest of the ten Sefirot or divine emanations</note>. Now he descends to return and to leave for one great place and a world that is in the world, a planting and a mark of truth. And this was the work of Obed <note>the son of Ruth and Boaz</note> for the house of Jesse and the house of David. For behold, you might say to me what the Old Man <note>original: *Saba*</note> said: "And behold, the mark of truth emerged from that place," but rather the work was to be repaired through a supernal repair, and the mark of the serpent returns, which turns over its repairs to ascend within it and be repaired as is fitting. And he called the name "Obed" <note>meaning "servant" or "worker"</note> because he merited what the rest of the world's inhabitants did not. And below, the serpent labors and the root is uprooted, and the mark of the serpent emerges from bitter branches and returns to be repaired in the body of the serpent. His son came and they restrained him and repaired him, so that he would not return to the branches of the other, higher serpent, and from there comes strength like the sand, to be covered one with the other. Once David came, those portions were covered and divided one into the other; then he inherited the dominion as at first, and Obed raised this up. Thus said that Old Man: "Woe, Old Man, Old Man! It was not revealed to you that you entered like a soft one; now you have descended into the great depths to be repaired and to ascend." Old Man, Old Man, you were the cause of the world, you were ancient at first... now you were unable, and there is no one to return like you, but your desire shall arise, Old Man, to ascend in the ascent. This work is to be repaired and from it emerged the law. You are in a state of hidden things, and like a son to repair and the strength is uprooted. And this work is a spirit of... and I do not know if I saw it or did not see it. I saw from you, Old Man, that I did not see as I know all other subjects of reincarnation <note>original: *gilgula*</note>. Obed is our strength to repair all that is below. King David is our strength, the boundary of the female <note>original: *nukba*</note> below, and it was necessary to receive "waters" from below. And if this one is to repair and repairs everything, so too the rest of the world's inhabitants who sin in reincarnation, who are unable to be repaired thus—on them, in all sides, to turn in reincarnation. They sought this: so was the work, so it was. And as a whole, our strength emerged from the side of... and it clung to the Crown <note>Keter</note> in the side of Good. At first, *And Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked* <note>Genesis 38:7</note>. They were strong also from those, also thus and not so. Destruction was made into evil, and Good emerged to the Crown; that emerged which is written: *For his goodness and his life are with him.* Here our strength stands at first upon its repair, and a complete king... from the root and the foundation of the supernal male. The levels of merit ascended: Simeon, Levi, and Judah. What is written of him? *This time I will praise the Lord* <note>Genesis 29:35</note>, and it is written: *and she stopped bearing.* And in the Book of Enoch: "and she stopped bearing"—this refers to the root that did not give birth, for when Judah was born, the female emerged clinging to the male <note>original: *dechura*</note> and she was not in her proper repair... they did not reach the Crown to give birth. Once the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: *Kudsha Berich Hu*</note>, separated her and repaired her, then she was tied to conceive and to give birth. And in the Book of Enoch: "and she stopped bearing" to be designated for this woman, concerning Rachel the wife of that one...

## Main Text (Zohar)

Regarding such a matter that was found in Joseph and Judah, a thing was performed that had not been rectified at first. The supernal image was broad <note>original: "rhuban," referring to the expansion of divine light</note> in another way, as it is written: "the fat of kidneys" <note>Deuteronomy 32:14</note>. And Judah and Simeon are like the sun in that sign which eats directly the "poison of iniquity" <note>a wordplay on the name Simeon/Shimon as "Sam Avon" - poison of iniquity</note>. Levi is clarified for all to be found from two sides.

Judah is the market <note>or "street/pathway"</note> where the speech is directly attached. **Y-H-W-D-A** <note>The Hebrew spelling of Judah: יהודה</note>: the **Y-H-W** is the male aspect, and the **D** <note>Dalet</note> is the female aspect, which is arranged like the letter **H** <note>Heh</note> to show this in this order. And it is not that they were left to desire as one, so that there would be no poverty. They were stirred below like a cycle <note>Gilgul</note> to be consumed in the light and to be rebuilt in the dust, and afterwards to be wiped away like the good rain, and to go out from a dwelling to wealth. And then the letter **H** [is revealed].

And regarding this, Judah: go out and look! Go out from the depths! Do not fear, for many swords are prepared for you in the hour that you will need them, to spit with them just as before. And the wine of the masters of the worlds—perhaps they will say they are helping him—is alive thus. And like a deep valley, it is revealed before you, for he acted for your honor and did not act for my honor. For at first, he had to hide so as not to enter the Great Sea. But now, since he has grasped it, he has life for the [Side] in all sides, and from it emerges **Y-H-W-D** below.

This is what we said: "Blessed are you to the Lord." "Blessed" and "to the Lord" are below for all his children. Jacob did not say "You" <note>Hebrew: *Atah* (אתה)</note> except for the "You" that was needed for this, for the Lord below. This name **Y-H-W-D** <note>Judah without the final Heh</note> grasps them all. Your portion is upon this name, and it pushes downward. "Your hand shall be" <note>Genesis 49:8</note> grasps upon this name to ascend and to be subdued like the letter *Tet* which is missing, because when it was created, behold, you bent the **Other Side** <note><term>Sitra Achra</term>: The kabbalistic term for the realm of evil or "the other side" of holiness</note> like a myrtle. Since they said "You" (*Atah*), we have dominion and greatness, and the Other Side is to be subdued and not to exist there. And he pushes like a bow toward Tarshish.

He was freed from the Other Side, and this is to rectify, and its dominion shall be broken. And a cup for the Other Side, since "your hand grasps," and upon this name below, then "your hand shall be on the neck of your enemies" <note>Genesis 49:8</note>. Immediately they are subdued before you, and this name causes it. The companions know, and I know, that this name is below for us. And they say to another supernal place, as it is written: "You are a priest forever" <note>Psalm 110:4</note>. The supernal is good for the Lord. Since Rabbi Shimon has a portion in the upper and lower worlds and is wise in everything, all that they fear for the Master is fitting and beautiful. But when you reach him, let them say to him and to his throne: "May it be wiped out," for we have learned that all seed is divided into fifty-two kinds. For here the **Cup of Blessing** <note><term>Kos Shel Berakhah</term>: The cup of wine used for sanctification, representing the Sephirah of Malchut</note> is bound to the right, not separated at all. And in this "You are a priest forever," it turns to bind the cup to the right as is fitting.

And regarding this, the scripture says: "Judah, you..." <note>Genesis 49:8</note> to praise below. And "your hand grasps," and it is not written "Judah and your hand grasps" and no more, but rather upon the name "You" (*Atah*). This place is needed to show this and not another. Judah grasped the first and grasped the second, and there was no "Chief" <note>Aluph/Letter Aleph</note> in him forever. And in this, Perez <note>The son of Judah</note> was strengthened with his strength, which was not the case for all the people of the world. And because of this, David was struck by the good from Perez. And it is not necessary to say that the Old Man <note>The Sabba</note> subdues, crying out: "Living ones! Rectify for them hidden words!" For laughter and for a tongue, these words are hidden. And regarding the spirit of this name called "You" (*Atah*), it stands on its health, from the first strength and from the second strength, to be found forever. And the nickname of Judah and his seed are profane, and they say: "For You are our Father" <note>Isaiah 63:16</note>, which is not the case for the rest of the children forever. It ascends in twenty children of reincarnation. Two protections of Haman <note>possibly a reference to a specific demonic force or a scribal error for a similar sounding word</note> they have for nicknames, and they are weapons in the depths. And who is the herald? And all of them are for standing. Who can take them out?

Arise, Old Man, to be recognized and to be strengthened in your strength! Bring out the complainers from the depths! They sought to rectify the letter *Kof*. The Old Man bent all the hollows for the deed of the *Kof*. The deed was like a danger to them; thus it was for the children. He sought, and he grasped the first who did not use a knife. And if you say it was for the Lord, he pushed when to the place of this deed, the thorn of the constellation was strong in his son, and the daughter-in-law <note>referring to Tamar</note> was the end in him, so as not to leave...
