## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Judgments (Mishpatim)** <-

Let it be hidden in a fenced-in storehouse, and let the "What" <note>original: *Mah*, a mystical name for the Divine Presence</note> be sanctified for the primary root, so that all shall be one King, one peace, and all shall be one. There was no protection like the cycle of the seed of the generation, and upon this, He sealed from the beginning to the end; all is hidden. A general opening emerged from the Ancient Elder <note>original: *Saba de-Atika*, referring to the highest emanations of the Divine</note> for all time. The **Foundation** <term>Yesod: the ninth Sephirah, representing the generative organ of the Divine body</term> was certainly sealed from the beginning to the end. They did not seal every side so that it would not be learned to be called a "seal." All the portions of the generation of the elders were clarified, and to the side of the radiance, the root of human beings as is fitting. His brother shall cast away all the children of the world... "I shall be" <note>original: *Ehyeh*</note> is not like a man; all the children of the world do not intend for reincarnation <term>Gilgul: the transmigration of souls</term> except from the side of the brothers. And it comes like yourself to the duty of the levirate marriage <note>original: *yibbum*, the practice of a man marrying his deceased brother's childless widow</note>. The Elder holds them all as one, so that no human being shall look upon the ladder of the kingdom. If he sealed in your learning, he sealed from the beginning to the end. You performed the seal, and the entire curl and the body emerged—what is the image and the body? For they are not your children, but children of the free, who were not conceived as children of your midst; they were not established forever, neither to the side, nor to the front, nor as a spark of another image. Rather, freedom surrounds the building, and freedom finishes the structure. All your curls are children of freedom in the joy that fills the reincarnation. From the side of the lower world, all images shall be changed and intermingled. If it is correct and perfect by your hand, it is held so that not one of them was like the cycle of the curl, as it is written: "Your hand is raised," so that there was no other mixture in you. And they are from the prey of the children of the upper chamber, which was not prey for another on your table. Through the death of our masters, like the death of our elders, he is afterwards recognized as one who stands for the redemption. Who shall raise him? As it is written: *And he knew her no more* <note>Genesis 38:26</note>. The flow ceased. Who shall raise him from the voice of the sea? The lower deficiency of the letter *He*, from which the voice of the sea was diminished, and the treading rose to her. I needed you more, and just as the ladders... she did not need you more, and she was established to be separated from him. But "who shall raise him" and push from there onwards? The physician of judgments, for he emerges from the one who stirs the bowels. The hidden spirit, the Elder, is added outside with strength to strike. It is a thin burning... even the burning that stirs in the bowels. Who is the one who is equal to him? He accuses him with accusations on all sides, seeking to bring him out. Once he emerges, he is ready for another, a disqualification of another spirit, and they come above as at first, until he cries as at first, like the pain of a strong accusation. From there onwards, the woman is spoiled, not for him. And all the portions of the Foundation <note>Yesod</note> were at first a dwelling, but afterwards, freedom was recognized and spread in its portion. Afterwards, freedom finishes the whole on every side. The children of the world shall be thus, and regarding this, it shall be said as we have stated: Reuben, Simeon, and Levi—these three are as we have said. Judah was joined with them, and all is as it should be.

And the living beings: Issachar and Zebulun are the two thighs for the two images in the house of the smallness of the right thigh. It is written: *Issachar, men who had understanding of the times* <note>1 Chronicles 12:33</note>, and it is written: *Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out* <note>Deuteronomy 33:18</note>. And in the great crown it is written: *Zebulun shall dwell by the shore of the sea; he shall be a shore for ships* <note>Genesis 49:13</note>. What is the reason? Just as the thighs are upon the body... until the body. Sometimes he is surrounded above between the thighs, for Joseph's image was like the leg, and he was not measured in this world. And now, the truth of Moses: *And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him* <note>Exodus 13:19</note>. Sometimes he ascends above in the right, like the image of the world... below. Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher are like the left thigh. Dan reaches the joint of the standard; the joint of the standard is Naphtali. And behind Naphtali is a perfect strength, light in his standards. In the right thigh is Gad, and he *shall be raided by a troop, but he shall raid at the heel* <note>Genesis 49:19</note>, reaching the joint of the heel. The joint of the right heel is missing. *And Asher, let him dip his foot in oil* <note>Deuteronomy 33:24</note>, and it is written: *Your bolts shall be iron and bronze, and as your days, so shall your strength be* <note>Deuteronomy 33:25</note>. All these are supernal images, images from above. And because they were actual creations in the foundation of the world, the **Divine Presence** <term>Shekhinah: the feminine, indwelling aspect of God</term> was repaired through them.

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic discourse on the mystical construction of the Divine Name Elohim. It builds on the previous themes of the separation of the Name during exile and its reunification in the messianic future.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

At the time when the redemption is raised up, you shall be raised up below, specifically from Israel, as it is written: *All these are the names of Israel* <note>original: "כל אלה שמי ישראל"</note>. The sum of the ten elevations of Israel is "These" (*Eleh*), which are called below from that which is comparable to the gathering, as is fitting for Israel to exist within the totality of the Name *Elohim*. "These" (*Eleh*) and the foundation shall be within the totality of "Who" (*Mi*). Just as "These" (*Eleh*) is Lovingkindness (*Chesed*), it is clearly so, and it is like the pattern of the rectifications of the single Name. This is what was said to Jacob, who was of humble mind, as it is written: *For you have striven with God (Elohim) and with men and have prevailed* <note>Genesis 32:29</note>. And furthermore, in the upper realms, in the first rectifications, in the first pattern, "All these" are certainly like the first pattern for the Foundation (*Yesod*). Because of this, Israel is never found wanting for all eternity. And furthermore, if you gaze upon it, this Name would not exist [without them], as it is written: *And they will cut off our name from the earth; and what will You do for Your great Name?* <note>Joshua 7:9</note>. This "Great Name" is like the first pattern, the first Name, *Elohim*, for there the souls of Israel are like a garden. When it is possible for everything to be like a double pattern, then in the time to come, when **the Holy One, blessed be He**, redeems His children from exile, "Who" (*Mi*) and "These" (*Eleh*)—which were separated in exile—will be joined together. They will be joined as one, and the Name *Elohim* will be complete in its rectifications, and the worlds will be established. The voice of "Who" (*Mi*) and "These" (*Eleh*) [will cry out]: *Who are these that fly like a cloud, and like doves to their cotes?* <note>Isaiah 60:8</note>. And because it is a single Name, it is written "Who" (*Mi*) and "These" (*Eleh*).

Rather, "Who" (*Mi*) and "These" (*Eleh*) are a single Name in its entirety. The explanation is that now, in exile, "Who" (*Mi*) has ascended above, as if it were possible to say, away from the children. And the children are doubled. And when the Name is complete, the Supernal Name of the first city is doubled. Therefore, they are counted and sanctified, as it is written: *Like thrones upon this Name*. It will not be built as it once was, and they say: *May His Great Name be magnified and sanctified. Amen, may His Great Name be blessed.* What is this "Great Name"? It is the first of all, for it has no pattern like "These" (*Eleh*); this "Who" (*Mi*) will never be diminished. "These" (*Eleh*) is the whole, and therefore at that time: *Who are these that fly like a cloud*, and the whole world will see that the Supernal Name has been established in its rectifications. By the life of His Great Name, this is to be rectified, and they shall be joined in their rectifications. Israel shall rule over all, and all other names shall return to their rectifications, and Israel shall rule over all, for they all hang upon the Great Name, which is prior to all structures. And this spirit, when He created the worlds, was prior to all structures. This Name is to be called upon, as it is written: *Lift up your eyes on high and see: Who (Mi) created these (Eleh)?* <note>Isaiah 40:26</note>. God (*Elohim*) is His Name in its rectification, as is fitting. When "These" (*Eleh*) was created, His Name was according to the full count that is seen for Him, to establish His Name in its rectification as is fitting, as it is written: *He who brings out their host by number* <note>Isaiah 40:26</note>. What is "by number"? "These" (*Eleh*) created one who clarifies the numbering of the worlds until the ends of the world. **The Holy One, blessed be He**, possesses the end of the great and mighty strength; the goodness reaches the house of His Name, and its end is seen. His labors and their digging are like holy dust, and the number of His Name and the revelation of the supernal spices. And from that which they exist, they hang from Him until the end of the number. And all of them, all of them, are this Name in its gathering, as it is written: *The heavens declare* <note>original: "כסמים מספרים" - likely a variant of Psalm 19:2</note>. Just as the end of the number, all of them are the heavens, the expansions of this Name in its gathering. And therefore: *He who brings out their host by number*, for through this number, the hosts and the offspring are sustained for eternity. And therefore it is written: *Who can count the dust of Jacob, and the number of the fourth part of Israel?* <note>Numbers 23:10</note>. These two [Who and Number] protect you and us, as if by their hands, so that the Evil Eye shall not rule over them. *Who can count the dust of Jacob*—this is one who performs the observation; *and the number of the fourth part of Israel*—this proves the other. And because of these two, the Evil Eye does not rule over them. For *Who can count the dust of Jacob*—these are the holy ones among you from the service of the wise, who are like water to the world. And further it is written: *And your seed shall be as the dust of the earth* <note>Genesis 28:14</note>. Just as that dust of the world is blessed through its children, so too *all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in your seed*, literally like the dust of the earth. And the "number" is for the spirit placed in the gathering, waiting for the fourth part, all those stars and pearls upon which Israel is written and waits.

<meta>This page continues the discourse of the "Saba de-Mishpatim" (The Old Man of Mishpatim). The previous context established the mystical nature of the soul's journey. ## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Laws** <-

And henceforth there shall be rest for all, because of the vision of the "good eye" <note>original: "tov ayin" - referring to a benevolent spiritual gaze</note>. For it is written: *He counts the number of the stars* <note>original: "moneh mispar la-kokhavim"</note>. What does this mean, "He counts the number of the stars"? It means that through His hands, all pass by in the count. And in the time to come, *the flock shall again pass under the hands of the one who counts them*, and we do not know who he is. But because it is in this manner, everything is as one; just as the Foundation <note>term: "Yesod" - the ninth Sephirah, associated with the procreative force and the covenant</note> is the end of the separation, so shall they all be, and all shall be a single count. Arise, Old Man, and strengthen yourself like a lion! He traversed the sea, opened his mouth, and said:
> **Who can count the dust of Jacob, and the number of the fourth part of Israel?** <note>Numbers 23:10</note> 
At the hour when the Holy One, blessed be He, shall awaken to revive the dead, thus they shall return in reincarnation <note>term: "Gilgul" - the cycle of souls or reincarnation</note>. Two watchers in one spirit, two merits—for whom? How many reincarnations revolve through this hand! Even though it has been stated, and so it is, yet *who can count the dust of Jacob*? He prepares and repairs everything, and nothing shall be lost, and everything shall arise. For it has been stated and explained:
> **Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake** <note>Daniel 12:2</note> 
"Dust of the earth"—this is as was stated regarding the flight of Enoch. When the companions look into your life, those who are hidden in your life, in him and your life forever. He opened and said:
> **And I praised the dead who have already died** <note>Ecclesiastes 4:2</note> 
"Dust of the earth" is given to you, and a voice awakens and trembles. And thus he said in the assembly of the wise: the first "dust" refers to the first [body], and "earth" to the second, which comes to repair the root of the first. The waste matter is cast aside, but the "dust of the earth"—all of them shall awake. *These* are those repaired for eternal life. Which "world" <note>note: the word "Olam" means both "world" and "eternity"</note>? This is the lower world; for if they did not merit to be in the upper world, then *these* who did not merit are for "reproach and eternal abhorrence." Why for reproach? Only because the Other Side <note>term: "Sitra Achra" - the realm of evil or impurity in Kabbalah</note> shall be removed from the world, and the Holy One, blessed be He, shall purify those who were suppressed by that side, to cleanse them like a priest cleanses all the people of the world. All of this—who caused it? He who did not wish to bring forth [children] into the world and did not wish to maintain the Holy Covenant <note>term: "Brit Kadisha" - the sign of circumcision and sexual purity</note>. This caused all that it caused, and all these reincarnations that we have seen until now. At this point, the Old Man was silent for a moment, and the companions were astonished; they did not know if it was the end of the day or if it was night, or if they were standing there or not. That Old Man opened again and said:

**If** *you buy a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years, and in the seventh...* <note>Exodus 21:2</note> This verse proves everything that has been said. Every male stands in the likeness of the Male World <note>note: the spiritual realm of giving/influence</note>, and every female stands in the likeness of the Female World <note>note: the spiritual realm of receiving/manifestation</note>. While he is a servant of the commandment below to cleave to it, and this ancient power dwells before him, if he uproots himself from his service, the Holy One, blessed be He, uproots him from those "six years" of the world. He is handed over to a man who is from the "six sides" <note>note: the six directions or emotional attributes</note>; he shall serve him six years, and be uprooted from the six supernal years above. And after he dies from there, he is handed over to the Female World. Since he did not want to be established in the Male World—which is the life and sustenance in the Source below—the Seventh [Year/World] receives him. From that point onward, from the Female World, he did not want to be established in her, and like a pampered child he descends below to cleave below and to be made heavy by the Other Side. From then on, he is uprooted from the Male World and the Female World. He is transformed into those "servants" who are from the Other Side. Now, since this is so, a defect <note>original: "pegam"</note> is required, to make in him a sign of the defect, for every defect is from the Other Side. And from then on, he returns to reincarnation and returns to the world as at first, to cleave to that Female World and no more. And if he produces offspring in the world, they are those of whom it is written "his progeny after him," his domain is brought to you. Happy is he when he is repaired and merits this. But if he does not merit, he goes in the cycle of reincarnation. He must return, not to learn, but to wait in the world and produce offspring. What is written?
> **If he comes in alone, he shall go out alone** <note>Exodus 21:3</note> 
If he enters this world solitary, without offspring, he departs solitary.

He describes how a soul is cycled through different spiritual realms (Male and Female) to repair its past failures.</summary>

## Laws (Mishpatim)

->**Laws**<-

He appointed Mercy over him, and He was filled with mercy for all His works; His mercy is upon all His creations, even upon the cattle and the birds, He provides mercy through sustenance. If He provides mercy through sustenance for them, how much more so for human beings who know and recognize their Master, that He provides mercy through sustenance and guards over them. Regarding this, David said: *Your mercies are great, O Lord; according to Your laws, grant me life* <note>Psalms 119:156</note>. If He provides mercy through sustenance for the guilty, how much more so for the righteous. If one asks: who desires to be sustained from the side of sins? <note>The text asks if God sustains people even while they are in a state of sin</note>. And who is sustained from the side of sins? These are the sins that stand before Him, yet the mercy of the Holy One, blessed be He, is upon them so they will not be abandoned by Him, and He does not withdraw from them. He places Himself before them; when the Holy One, blessed be He, brings one near, He brings them near with the Right Hand <note>The side of Chesed/Kindness</note>, and when He pushes away, He pushes with the Left Hand. Even at the moment He pushes away and rebukes, He brings near from this side; He pushes with one hand and brings near with the other, for the Holy One, blessed be He, never withholds His mercy from them. Come and see what is written:
> *And he went on frowardly in the way of his heart,* and it is written afterward, *I have seen his ways, and will heal him; I will lead him also, and restore comforts unto him and to his mourners* <note>Isaiah 57:17-18</note>.

*And he went on frowardly*: even though they do everything they do willfully, following the path of their own hearts and acting in darkness, will they be healed? They do not even seek to cry out to Him! But at the moment they return in repentance <term>Teshuvah: literally "returning" to God</term> and take the good path of repentance, the Holy One, in His compassion, is ready to meet them. He opens a way for life and for observation. If you look at the verse regarding "life," the verse speaks of the living; regarding the "dead," the verse speaks of the dead. The beginning of the verse refers to the living, and the end of the verse refers to the dead. This verse was seen while a person is still alive, and thus it is: *And he went on frowardly in the way of his heart*, because the Evil Inclination <term>Yetzer HaRa</term> within him is strong, and it overpowers him, and he continues to go frowardly and does not wish to return in repentance. The Holy One, blessed be He, sees in His mercy that he is walking toward total destruction. The Holy One, blessed be He, says: "I will guard you to strengthen you," as it is written: *I have seen his ways and will heal him*—though they walk in darkness, I will guard him to bring him back to repentance and I will heal him. The Holy One, blessed be He, is prepared to enter into his heart the mercy of repentance and the thought of consolation, and His consolation strikes with love. How fortunate is he whom the Holy One, blessed be He, guides with the way of discipline, like one who grasps the hand of another and pulls him out of the darkness. *And I will restore comforts unto him and to his mourners*: it has been said that he who is meritorious is called "living," while the wicked is called "dead" even while alive. Because he went in his ways, the wicked is dead; but I will restore comforts to him and to his mourners. See, the Holy One, blessed be He, performs kindness with human beings. Once they enter the side of merit and onward, He appoints with him two guardian angels who guard him, one on his right and one on his left. When a man walks in the path of discipline, they support him and strengthen him with joy, proclaiming before him: "Give honor to the image of the King!" But when he walks in a crooked path, they mourn over him and depart from him. Once the Holy One, blessed be He, strengthens him and settles him in the path of discipline, then it is written: *And I will restore comforts unto him and to his mourners*. *I will restore comforts to him* as at first; he is comforted for what he did previously and for what he does now, and he returns in repentance. And afterward, *to his mourners*: these are the angels who were mourning over him when they departed from him, and now they return. This is certainly the intention for all sides... he is alive. He opens with life on all sides, in the portion of life, and the intention is for the portion of life. Then he is called a "Master of Repentance" <term>Ba'al Teshuvah</term>, for he was in a state of impurity and now is greatly beloved; he is a true Master of Repentance. And concerning this, our predecessors said:
> *In the place where Masters of Repentance stand, even the perfectly righteous cannot stand* <note>Talmud, Berakhot 34b</note>.

King David said:
> *Against You, You only, have I sinned, and done that which is evil in Your sight...* <note>Psalms 51:6</note>

*Against You only*: why "Against You only"? Because there are sins that a man commits against the Holy One, blessed be He, and against the Assembly <note>The Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note>, and there are sins that he commits against fellow men and not against the Holy One, and there are sins he commits against the Holy One alone and not against any man. And King David sinned against the Holy One, blessed be He, alone and not against men <note>The Zohar here offers a mystical defense of David's conduct regarding Bathsheba and Uriah</note>. And if you say he sinned...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Judgments**<-

Good was that altar <note>referring to Bathsheba as a spiritual foundation</note> that Bathsheba built from the types of trials that came upon her husband <note>Uriah</note>. She had a desire for the Master of All, and she showed compassion for her companion, and compassion for the Holy One, blessed be He. It is not as people say regarding the King <note>David</note>, that he was strong and his passion was within him. Rather, she had a bill of divorce from her husband before he went out to battle, for such was the custom for all of Israel: everyone who went out in the army gave a conditional divorce to his wife. Thus did Uriah do for Bathsheba. After the time had passed and she was released from all obligations, David took her. After that, he did all that he did. If she were a widow, it would not have been a reproach. The Prophet <note>Nathan</note> came before him and helped to establish the ruling: *And David comforted Bathsheba his wife.* <note>2 Samuel 12:24</note>

He saw the visitation of the widowhood and the pushing away of the groom. She was the soulmate of David, destined for him since the day the world was created. The spirit of the matter is the Supernal Kingdom <term>Malchut: the tenth Sefirah, representing the feminine divine principle</term>, which is made the fourth leg of the Supernal Chariot. She is not called "Bathsheba" <note>literally "Daughter of Seven"</note> until she finds grace in the "Seven Eyes." This is the decree: that David did not sin except against the Holy One, blessed be He, as we have seen, and not against another. For he killed Uriah with the "sword of the children of Ammon" and did not kill him with his own intent. This is the secret: David was leaning upon him <note>Uriah</note> and showed compassion, turning him into a merit. For it is written that the sin of the "likeness of the firstborn" was a sin for David, but he did not sin like Saul, nor did he kill him by his own hand, but killed him by the sword of the children of Ammon.

And the Scripture says: *He did not turn aside from anything... except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.* <note>1 Kings 15:5</note> The word "except" comes to exclude; he sinned in the *matter* of Uriah, but not against Uriah himself. It is a light thing in your eyes that "you have slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon"? Every sword of the children of Ammon is the image of the Dragon <note>the primordial serpent</note> engraved upon it, a "coiled serpent" <note>original: *chivya akis*</note> seen upon them. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "You gave strength to that Samael <term>Samael: the primary figure of evil/the accuser in Kabbalah</term> because, through the error of the children of Ammon killing Uriah, they took from the children of Israel who were with him." At that hour, the sword of the children of Ammon prevailed. By what power did it prevail? By the power of Samael.

And if you say Uriah was not righteous because he is called "Uriah the Hittite"—it is not so. He was righteous, but he took hold of that "Hittite" <note>the shell of impurity</note> to subdue it. Then Samael opened a breach upon the horse of the Hittite. Because of this, "in the matter of Uriah the Hittite," the Samael of the children of Ammon prevailed over the camp of the Chariot, which was the very image of David's guard above. At that hour, the face of David's guard was covered. This is the "other face" above the guard. Regarding this, David said: *Against You, You alone, have I sinned.* <note>Psalm 51:6</note> Against You alone, and not against another. This strengthened that debt he owed to the Prophet, and this strengthened the "matter of Uriah." This was like the sword of the children of Ammon. It is written of him: *His eyes roam through all the earth*—these are the windows of the female. And it is written: *The eyes of the Lord roam*—these are the windows of the male, and they know these things. David said: *And I have done what is evil in Your eyes.*

> **Against You, You alone, have I sinned, and I have done what is evil in Your eyes.** <note>Psalm 51:6</note>

"In Your eyes"—it should have said "before Your eyes." Rather, it means "within Your eyes." David said: "In that place where Your eyes are found, the Holy One knew that Your eyes were prepared and standing before me, yet I did not look at them." This was the rebuke. "And Your servant is in that place which is 'in Your eyes,' *so that You are justified in Your speaking and blameless in Your judgment.*" Thus, I will have no opening of the mouth to speak before You. Come and see the piety: when he spoke in his piety, David spoke as the image of the King. Even though he was among the youths, since he was before the King, he returned to his joy in order to cleave to the King. He said: "The Master of the world sees with wisdom, and there is no other who can stand in Your concealment." This is the wisdom: *so that You are justified in Your speaking.* Let the King of Truth see, for if there were no rebuke, the word would not be true. Let the King see in his lower image that there is a rebuke, so that He may be a King of Truth, sitting in the place of victory. Thus did David do, *so that You are blameless in Your judgment.* David was pious toward his form and said: "Among the youths I shall dwell," for his joy was in the King. David prepared these things below to rectify them. We see this action and he said: *And my heart is hollow within me.* We see that it was already hollow within me <note>meaning he had conquered his evil inclination</note>.

## Laws (Mishpatim)

->**Laws**<-

It is within my inner parts. But David said: in my heart there are two chambers, one containing blood and one containing spirit <note>original: *rucha*</note>. That one which is full of blood is where the Evil Inclination <term>Yetzer Hara: the innate human impulse toward selfishness or sin</term> can dwell. But my heart is not so, for it is empty; I did not give a dwelling place for blood within it for the Evil Inclination to be found there <margin>The Assembly</margin> and "my heart is hollow within me" <note>Psalm 109:22</note> without the dwelling of blood. And since it was so <gloss>translation: like a light and pressed collection</gloss>, David was not destined for that death <note>spiritual expiration</note> like Saul. This was in order to provide an "opening of the mouth" <note>a precedent</note> for people to say: David the King sinned and returned in Repentance <term>Teshuvah: literally 'returning' to God</term>, and the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: *Kudosha Brich Hu*</note>, forgave him. How much more so <note>original: *Kal va-chomer*</note> will He forgive other human beings. And regarding this he said: "I will teach transgressors Your ways, and sinners shall return to You" <note>Psalm 51:15</note>. And it is written:
> And David went up by the ascent of the Mount of Olives, and wept as he went up, and had his head covered, and he went barefoot <note>2 Samuel 15:30</note>
This hinted at his covering and being barefoot to show how he made himself like a collection <note>of sorrows</note> to receive punishment. And see, he stayed four cubits away from his house. Blessed is the servant who thus serves his Master and recognizes his rebuke to return to Him in complete Repentance. Come and see: what Shimei ben Gera did to him was harder than all the troubles that passed over him until that day, yet David did not answer him a word, for thus it was fitting for him, and in this way his sins were atoned for. Now we must look: Shimei was a Torah Scholar <note>original: *Talmid Chacham*</note> and wisdom was in him, yet he saw the decree against David and did to him all that he did. Another pious person might have taken this matter to heart, but all this was for David's benefit. And that line which Shimei took with him caused him to return in complete Repentance; it broke his heart into pieces, and he poured out many tears from his heart before the Holy One, Blessed be He. Regarding this he said: "For the Lord said to him: Curse" <note>2 Samuel 16:10</note>. He knew that his sin was being struck by the word. David gave two commands to Solomon his son: one regarding Joab and one regarding Shimei, along with other commands. Regarding Joab it is written: "Moreover, you know also what Joab the son of Zeruiah did to me" <note>1 Kings 2:5</note>. This was a hidden matter, for Solomon was not supposed to know it except that others had made it known to Solomon; therefore he said "And you also know," meaning what was not apparent for you to know. Regarding Shimei it is written: "And behold, you have with you Shimei the son of Gera" <note>1 Kings 2:8</note>. What does "behold, he is with you" mean? It means he is constantly available to you. He was a neighbor. For this reason, he did not say regarding Joab "behold, Joab is with you." But Shimei, who was found with him constantly, he said "behold, he is with you." "And the king sent and called for Shimei, and said to him: Build yourself a house in Jerusalem" <note>1 Kings 2:36</note>. Behold the wisdom of King Solomon in this! Rather, he did everything with Wisdom <term>Chokhmah: divine or inspired wisdom</term> and found justification on all sides, for Shimei was a pious man. Solomon said: I want his merits to increase all at once through Shimei's own actions, and that he should not go outside. Furthermore, Solomon found through his wisdom that it is written "And he came and he cursed." Why "he came" and why twice? "And he came and cursed" would be enough. Rather, one was the lewdness that went out from the House of Study toward David, and one was the lewdness that went out from Jerusalem toward his servant <unclear>in the likeness of his eyes</unclear>. The first lewdness was against the King, and the second was against the servants. Solomon saw all this and discovered through the Holy Spirit <note>original: *Ruach HaKodesh*</note> that second lewdness. Regarding this he said: "And it shall be on the day you go out... you shall surely know that you shall die" <note>1 Kings 2:37</note>. And what of "dust like dust"? Solomon said: regarding me, he was like dust; regarding Shimei, it was like him, as it is written: "And it shall be on the day you go out and cross the Brook Kidron." Dust there and here is brain. Solomon judged both to be dust and brain, like a woman suspected of adultery <note>the Sotah ritual</note> to test the paths of his sins. It is written: "And he cursed me with a grievous curse" <note>1 Kings 2:8</note>. And it is written: "And I swore to him by the Lord, saying: I will not put you to death with the sword." <unclear>He struck with a bitter thing</unclear>. Was Shimei a fool to see these things? But he waited for him with a sharp arrow. Rather, there are two matters here. One says: and the power of the covenant of the star... <unclear>the power of his shells</unclear>.

## Main Text (Zohar)

...that they rise to the spirit of the clouds. The wall of King David, everything <term>YHVH<note>The four-letter Name of God, associated with the Attribute of Mercy.</note></term> desires to lend to his chariot's division, for there His Name was engraved and carved, and there it is seen. And so he acted for His Name, as it is written: *And I swore to him as in the days of my comforting, I have spared your pity, your crown.* As one who says, in the end, this is lent to your crown, your crown is seen. And another matter: Solomon spoke with a voice to the prophets and the wise, like words—"take words with you"—and the Explicit Throne <note>The Divine Throne of Glory</note> was slain, and not your crown; and because of this, Solomon acted thus. Now come and see: since David saw it to strike and slay those below, which is lent from the Supernal YHVH to the heart and the mouth, they were as one. David did not slay the profane or the jaw. And it is known that all the limbs of the body receive everything, but the heart does not receive even as much as a thread of a hair. King David later was and received what was lent to him to receive, and because of this it is written: *And you shall know that I have done kindness for him.* Furthermore, this tree is large, to place on the side and take vengeance like a serpent, as it is written:

> **For You do not desire sacrifice, or I would give it; You do not delight in burnt offerings. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.**
<note>Psalm 51:18-19</note>

*For You do not desire sacrifice etc.*—The Holy One, Blessed Be He, does not desire that they should bring a sacrifice before Him, for it is easy to prepare a sacrifice for sinners so they may bring it and have their sins atoned. However, David spoke before <term>Elohim<note>The Name of God associated with the Attribute of Judgment.</note></term>. One does not bring a sacrifice to the Name *Elohim*, but rather to the Name *YHVH*. And even then, regarding harsh judgment, one does not bring a sacrifice to the Attribute of Judgment, as it is written:

> **When any man of you brings an offering to YHVH...**
<note>Leviticus 1:2</note>

To *YHVH*, and not to *Elohim*. And: *When you bring a meal offering to YHVH.* *A sacrifice of thanksgiving to YHVH.* *A peace offering to YHVH.* Because King David spoke toward *Elohim*, it was necessary to write: *For You do not desire sacrifice, or I would give it; You do not delight in burnt offerings.* For to this Name, one does not offer sacrifices, but only a "broken spirit," as it is written: *The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit.* The sacrifice for *Elohim* is sadness and the breaking of the heart. Therefore, one who goes toward the "Evil Side" <note>The Sitra Achra or forces of impurity</note> must show sadness, for he stands within the Attribute of Judgment. A sacrifice to the Attribute of Judgment requires sadness, a broken spirit, and a horse of sadness and patience below, as was seen; for the matter of judgment is upon him, and the sacrifice of those below is to be brought before the Attribute of Judgment. *A broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.* What is meant by *You will not despise*? This implies there is a heart that is not like this, which is alive. This is the heart that is revealed, a heart like the slumber of the spirit; this is the heart that is built of everything—*a broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.*

> **Do good in Your favor unto Zion; build the walls of Jerusalem.**
<note>Psalm 51:20</note>

What is *Do good*? To repair the goodness that was in it. And now, *Do good* refers to the end of the goodness of the living. For from the day the Holy One, Blessed Be He, strove with the wings of the Temple above until now, that "goodness of favor" has not rested upon that building, and therefore it has not been completed. For at the time when the Supernal Favor is awakened, the radiance and sparks of light of that building and that work—which are hidden from the comforters above—they will not be able to look upon it, neither the Temple nor that building; and then the Temple will be fully completed. *Build the walls of Jerusalem etc.*—from the day He strove with the building of the Temple until now, He has not built them. Or come and see: the walls of Jerusalem have not been built until now, because the Temple is above. The Holy One, Blessed Be He—all His works are not like the works of human beings. When human beings built the Temple below, they first made the city walls and finally made the Temple. They made the city walls first in order to protect themselves, and afterward the building of the House. The Holy One, Blessed Be He, is not so; He first deals with the Temple, and finally, when it is extended and sits in its place, then He will *build the walls of Jerusalem* to protect the city's surroundings. Therefore, David said in the verse: *Do good in Your favor unto Zion* first, and afterward *build the walls.*

It also describes the spiritual rebuilding of Jerusalem, noting that God builds the Temple before the city walls, reversing human logic.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar on Parashat Mishpatim. It focuses on the cosmological struggle between the "Marrow" (the holy essence) and the "Shell" (the forces of the Other Side), leading into the laws of the Hebrew servant from Exodus 21.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Laws (Mishpatim)** <-

See and observe the hint: all the works that <term>the Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> <note>original: "Kadosh Baruch Hu"</note> performs are first for the sake of man, and after death, they return to Him. In this, the Divine Presence was present in all those works that <term>the Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> performed and engraved. Except for death, which is outside of holiness in thought and action; for every <term>Shell</term> <note>original: "Kliphah" - the outer husk that conceals the light</note> comes from the <term>Other Side</term> <note>original: "Sitra Achra" - the realm of evil or impurity</note>, while the <term>Marrow</term> <note>original: "Mocha" - the inner spiritual essence</note> comes from the Marrow. The Other Side always pursues holiness, growing and destroying and binding there. Once it has grown, they crush it outward, as it is written: "The wicked prepares it, but the righteous shall wear it" <note>Job 27:17</note>; they strike and cast away that Shell and bless the righteous of the world. Everything is like the construction of the Temple, where the Evil Side shall be removed from the world, for it will no longer be needed as a Shell for the Marrow. At first, the Marrow is primary, as it is written:
> Do good in Your favor unto Zion <note>Psalms 51:20</note>
This is first, and afterward: "Build the walls of Jerusalem." That wall on the outside was literally its Shell. As it is written:
> For I, says the Lord, will be unto her a wall of fire round about <note>Zechariah 2:9</note>
"I" and not the Evil Side. Israel is the Marrow within the world. But sin caused a blemish in the initial thought. The idolatrous nations, who are the Shell, preceded them, as it is written:
> And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Israel <note>Genesis 36:31</note>
Yet sometimes <term>the Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> brings forth the Marrow without a Shell, as it is written:
> Israel is the Lord's hallowed portion, His first-fruits of the increase <note>Jeremiah 2:3</note>
The holy Marrow precedes the Shell, and it is destined that the Marrow shall stand without a Shell. Who are those who stray and do not merit to eat? For "all that devour him shall be held guilty; evil shall come upon them" <note>Jeremiah 2:3</note>. Like this wall, a time will come when you will not be swept away, for then everything will be removed like a fading sound. Then the youth <note>Metatron or the rejuvenated soul</note> shall open with all his rectifications, and then the youth shall be brought near to the Lord God. The filth of the serpent shall not be joined to the sacrifice; for if it were joined, many youths would ascend to be joined there. At that time:
> For You are great, and do wondrous things; You alone are God <note>Psalms 86:10</note>
And there is no "god" of the <term>Other Side</term>. And at that time it is written:
> See now that I, even I, am He, and there is no god with Me <note>Deuteronomy 32:39</note>
"See now." See that "I, even I, am He" refers to the Divine Face. Rather, He is holy to "I," and from His power shall be the life of <term>the Holy One, Blessed Be He</term>. "Now see" what you were unable to see previously. "I, even I"—twice—"I kill and I make alive." This specifies that there is no god there but Him. Many times death and life occurred while the <term>Other Side</term> still existed there. But here it says "I" and "He" and "there is no god with Me," for every other side shall be removed, specifically by "I" who gives life. "I kill and I make alive"—previously death came from the Other Side, but from now on, "I kill and I make alive." For at that time, all those who have not tasted the taste of death, life shall be theirs; death will be instantaneous and He will raise them immediately. This is so that they shall not be left with any of that worldly filth at all, and the world will be renewed by the hands of <term>the Holy One, Blessed Be He</term>.

**"If** he comes in by himself..." <note>Exodus 21:3</note>. This refers to the servant going out free. Just as it was said, his inner self meets him. "His wings are with him" <note>a play on the word 'gapo' - by himself/with his wing</note>. What does "his wing" mean? It means, as the translation suggests, "alone." And this is the secret: the whole world does not grasp this "by his wing" <insert>on his own</insert>. This spirit exists in the secret of <term>Male and Female</term>. <term>The Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> created them male and female, and in everything that sustains the world, we know that if <term>the Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> had lacked the creation of the female, the world would be confused. Therefore, they produce offspring. "By himself he shall come" refers to that breath that does not produce offspring above. And since it is so, "by himself he shall come" means they come below and not above to be separated at all, and he shall not be crushed or driven from that world, "his wings are with him." Come and see what is written:
> They shall die childless <note>Leviticus 20:20</note>
"Childless" is written to include male and female in the spirit of the male above. And in the spirit of the female, she shall go out. He enters with this and goes out with this. Pity the one who does not cling to Him in that world, for <term>the Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> does not wish to take before Him anyone who has made himself a eunuch in this world. Come and see from the sacrifice that was not...

<meta>This page continues the discourse of the "Saba de-Mishpatim" (The Old Man of the Laws), a famous section of the Zohar where an elderly sage reveals deep mystical secrets to Rabbi Chiya and Rabbi Yose. The previous pages established the laws of the Hebrew servant as a metaphor for the reincarnation of the soul. ## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Mishpatim (Laws)**<-

They would bring before him spices and take them out so that they would not be recited before him <note>referring to the blessings over fragrances</note>, and he would command and bring wine, and all who tasted of it found its flavor. And so, for generations upon generations, it is difficult for the high beings, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, is entirely holy in the world. For all the heights of the watchmen are wine. He lived to strive, and it is written below, but he did not produce offspring and did not desire to, even though he had a wife, she did not become a mother. And he entered that world without offspring. What is written? "If he is a master of sin" <note>original: *ba'al chata*; a mystical play on Exodus 21:3, "if he is the husband of a wife"</note>, he is one who did not happen to prepare his hands, which are destroyed. And he is taken below... and he comes in with his body <note>original: *be-gapo*; meaning alone or with his own physical essence</note>. "If he comes in by himself, he shall go out by himself" <note>Exodus 21:3</note>, as it has been said, everything is according to its restoration. If his portion is diminished, he is punished for the sin, as it was said, so that his portion should not be the joy of all the earth. He gives him sin. From here, for all of them, it stands according to the will of a man to give below.

A world without blemish, and his judgment is for the Lord, without the mockery of scoffers. He gives him sin, for according to their will they are judged. And who is he who is small for his own, and no dream is within him? And who is that image? And he returns to the place and to the beginning. He comes with mercy and takes for himself this wife who did not seal him, and she was cheapened for him. He sees the thinness and sees that woman below who was destined to produce offspring in the world. The Holy One, Blessed be He, lives in mercy and his decree is able, and He makes judgments and stirs below **(pity on the soul)** for his own in a son and a daughter, and the strength of his heart gives birth, and he shall be "with his body" <note>alone</note>.

The poor man lies down, for he strove with his will for this, but did not strive to produce fruit in the daughter that was his, and he went out empty. First by first in times **(behold, in years)**, if she was at your feet, she is like one who is good in the ground without strength for the scent below, and a refuge in the garden that he cannot. He is like his feet; the Old Man <note>the Sage</note> shall be strengthened and shall not fear. Behold, the poor man who strove in emptiness has done so; he returns to live like one who sows in the daughter that was his. If so, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives him that daughter to sow in her, for his desire did not take her.

But come and see: all the words of the Holy One, Blessed be He, are all in truth, and no word is in vain. This one whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave to him below, and he produced fruit in her, they are required for this canopy of the wedding chamber. And it is not similar to one who strove in this world without a person and a child, to one who did not want to find and to strive, and uprooted the leaves for another, and his love returned. This one who gives to him below as if to make judgments, he did not strive at first because he did not inherit the portion and was not able. And since he has so much, he does not have **(behold, he has no building)**. For if he had been worthy as he should have been, he would have returned in reincarnation <term>Gilgul: the transmigration of souls</term> like a dog in a box. For it is written:
> I will give them, in My house and within My walls, a monument and a name better than sons and daughters <note>Isaiah 56:5</note>
And now that he was not worthy, the Holy One, Blessed be He, sees that he had pity and strove but was not able; see their portions, "He gives him sin" as it was said. And since the Holy One, Blessed be He, had pity on him and gave to him in mercy, the Holy One, Blessed be He, also takes from his own at first and takes what was lacking from that spring. And like the sin, she shall be the birth of his portion, and afterward he shall return and strive for himself to complete his deficiency. Until here is the secret of the verse. "He who strikes, he who strikes" <note>referring to Exodus 21:12</note> is said regarding the attachment of one who strove but was not prepared. The evening of this examination goes as we have said, for Korah pursues your Crown <term>Keter: the highest of the ten Sefirot or divine emanations</term>, which hides the entire building that was built until they came. And this one thought that the sea would not be found for your will... as it is written, "pity is lacking," the servant returns to write the portion of this one below. And the blow is found that has no portion from her. What will you do now, so that there will not be a window to pursue your Crown? And if this Korah pursues your Crown and goes out from the Crown to the wall, like a blue thread in the field, from the inside to the vessels of your Crown, he will finish the vessels for the mockery of your Crown and will embrace you. What will you do, Old Man? Now you have become like yourself, for you were a mighty hero until this day. First by first, remember and see what is revealed when the beans are fresh, and wait for how many heroes have conquered the strength.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Judgments**<-

There is strength before you, and power for you alone. Now, thirteen mighty men, when the shadow falls, each one of them is slain. There is joy until life can no longer sustain your life—thirteen men below. So too, there are thirteen who have no strength; all words concerning them are "Life, Life, Life" <note>The Hebrew letter Chet repeated thrice, often symbolizing 'Chai' or life</note>. It is written that then the Holy One, Blessed be He, distances Himself to perform judgment for each one. When the time arrives for one to descend below to find a soulmate, what does He do? He kills this one and kills that one, his soulmate, and he is not bent before the world, remaining solitary and alone. "Binding his foal to the vine, and his donkey’s colt to the choice vine" <note>Genesis 49:11</note> according to the plain meaning of the verse. And he binds the donkey in the mountain-range of the secret knives, and binds the silver in the secret knives, until the satiety of all living things enters. 

Wine, when it is dug on the day of satiety, the loans are cancelled. Regarding the servant, it is written: while you still have life, he works in the sixth conversation. Wine in the mountain-range of the secret knives, and he binds at the end of the secret knives—it is nothing. And because of two times of life, he shall ferment and be watchful while yet living in this lower realm, before my poverty and like the poor. Every day, the Holy King is with me; just as there was a turning toward mercy, so the voice of the monkey is in mercy, and not the voice of wine. He shall ferment the donkey as at first; all the praise is in mercy. He shall ferment at the Altar and be sanctified as before, to lead me to your paths, like a harp and like the treasure of my exile. 

The Holy One, Blessed be He, is far off, to mend his deeds and to be mended. And you, to lead me to your paths, I have sealed my lips and did not open my mouth. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, accepted him like the acceptance of repentance. And all the grace of the exiles—what does the Holy One, Blessed be He, do? That which was destined to return him in reincarnation <term>Gilgul: the transmigration of souls</term> and to weigh his deeds in this world for what he did, so that he should not return to the Life of Worlds. What does He do? He brings him close to the Court of the Heavenly Academy <term>Metivta de-Raki'a: the celestial study house where souls and angels learn</term>, and they judge him and hand him over to the earthly kingdoms. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, hides him so that he is not handed over to the place of punishment, and He meets him to show him under the dominion of the Jubilee <note>The 50th gate of understanding/liberation</note> until a known time. 

Afterward, He redeems him to life, like the assembly of the righteous who perform inner work for him. Life reaches the Jubilee; even one day in the Jubilee is considered for him as if the righteous one was cast out until the Jubilee. Thus he is punished and no more, until the Jubilee, and he is redeemed. And they enter him into the Garden of Portions. 

Until here, that Old Man <note>The Saba, a recurring mysterious master in the Zohar</note> lowered his eyes, struck once, opened his discourse and said: "Hear, O mountains, the Lord’s controversy, and you firm foundations of the earth; for the Lord has a controversy with His people..." <note>Micah 6:2</note>. Life is here until the hidden things are concealed in the depths of the sea. And a path opens in the mighty mountains to wage war with them, to be profaned and to be witnessed. Now my strength is firm, descending to all until the labor in the depths. And what do you seek in your life, you mighty mountains who built and reached and stormed? This opening is yours to fight the war in the depths. And in those mountains, where is the strength? Our portion shall be overturned as you have seen. And for all this, one deed was done, one killing. 

He opened: You have no strength to wage war and to finish it all, and not to turn back. Strengthen yourself with your power, gird your sword, and do not fear the stranger. Thus the mountains will not prevail against you. Say to them: "Mountains of spears! Mighty mountains! How are you strengthened?" Two verses are written. One writes: "Arise, contend with the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice" <note>Micah 6:1</note>. And one writes: "Hear, O mountains, the Lord’s controversy." Rather, there are mountains and there are not mountains. There are mountains that are "mountains of spears" high, high above—of these it is written, "Hear, O mountains, the Lord’s controversy." And there are mountains that are lower mountains, beneath them—of these it is written, "Arise, contend with the mountains," for a pursuer of blows is against them. Therefore, there are mountains and there are not mountains. 

And if you say: "Behold, here it is written, 'and let the hills hear,'" those hills are all those that are below. And now, why does He make them mountains? Rather, it is thus: relative to those "mountains of spears," they are called "hills." When they are by themselves, they are "mountains" and are called "the Mound of Life." It is written: "and the firm foundations of the earth." Since it is written, "Hear, O mountains," what is...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar on the Torah portion of Mishpatim (Exodus 21-24). The previous context likely involved the "Elder" (Saba) engaging in a spiritual debate or "battle" of Torah interpretation regarding the celestial hierarchies.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Mishpatim 110** <-

Who are these **chariots** <term>Rethichin: the celestial vehicles of the Divine Presence</term>? And what are these **living beings** <term>Chayot: the holy creatures supporting the Divine Throne</term>? Rather, in the secret of the **mighty ones** <term>Eitanim: a term for the Patriarchs, meaning "enduring ones"</term>, all of these are one. However, there are three upper ones above their secrets, and three lower ones beneath them. And they are all one in the supernal secret. Regarding them, King David (peace be upon him) said: **Wait for the horse** <note>original: "Chaku el ha-sus". This may be a mystical allusion to a verse comparing the Chariots to horses, perhaps related to Psalm 83 or Habakkuk 3:15</note>. These are the first three. And "the mighty ones, the foundations of the earth," these are the three lower ones beneath them: two pillars of truth and one holy one that contains three, and these are called the "foundations of the earth." They are the "mighty ones" and they are called "living beings."

This Elder wept. "Do you know that he who is below in battle, if he does not know how to guard himself, he will not win the wars? He needs to brace his hands and guard his legs. What he gives is considered for the place; what he gives is considered for the Right." And the secret of the **resting** <note>original: "minach"</note> is always ready to brace. And from the Left, the secret of the **releasing** <note>original: "machaletz"</note> is always ready to receive and to guard, and it proves everything.

He opened and said: "The living beings and the mighty ones are below, and they are arranged above." It was said to the Elder: "Behold, we have reached the place facing you, as it is written: **A Maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite** <note>Psalm 89:1</note>. This refers to Abraham the Elder, who is called 'Ethan' (Mighty). And if Abraham is 'Ethan,' then Isaac and Jacob are also called 'Eitanim' (Mighty Ones). Arise, O Elder, for you know our will regarding this was to reach your thought."

**"And he looked on the Kenite, and took up his parable, and said: Strong is thy dwelling place, and thou puttest thy nest in a rock"** <note>Numbers 24:21. Note: 'Strong' is 'Ethan' in Hebrew</note>. This 'Ethan' is the "Morning" of Abraham, and this is the "Morning" of **Kindness** <term>Chesed: the Sephirah of Mercy associated with Abraham</term>, the pillar upon which the whole world stands. And the Priest who learns from Abraham inherits the **Crown** <term>Keter: the highest Sephirah</term> which is the "delight from Eden" and is so called.

"O Elder, Elder! Behold, we have reached the place facing you, but you did not know how to guard yourself; is this how one leaves a battle? Elder, your strength was not sufficient, and it pushed away the might of war." It is written: *A Maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite*. **Maskil** <term>A musical or contemplative heading in Psalms, here interpreted as 'Enlightenment'</term> is the Crown, the delight from Eden, which is the "interpreter" for David to make known to him those hidden, supernal matters. If *Maskil* (some say *Maski*) is the Crown that goes out from Eden, then *Ethan the Ezrahite* is Abraham above—and I know it pushes it away. And even though the Elder's strength was not established in his thought, *Ethan the Ezrahite* refers to two levels: **Morning** and **Light**. "Light" is for Abraham; "Morning" is the Crown. So too is *Ethan the Ezrahite*: "Ezrahite" <note>In Hebrew, 'Ezrach' can mean 'native' or 'shining'</note> is for Abraham, and "Ethan" is as we have said—this is the Crown that gathers and bends from Eden.

Look, O Elder! Arise, for it is difficult for your mind; the woman is beginning and will not be able to stand up. Behold, the King of the world comes with his hair, his chariots, his commanders, and his officers, and he comes toward you. Arise, go out from the field so that he does not find you there! It is written: **"And all the men of Israel assembled themselves unto king Solomon at the feast in the month of Ethanim..."** <note>1 Kings 8:2</note>. This is the month in which the "Mighty Ones" (Patriarchs) were born. And who are they? Abraham and Isaac, the mighty ones of the world. And this month is the guardian of the "Alpha," returning everything from below to above.

Gather your strength and go out from the field so you are not found there! If it were written "A Maskil *for* Ethan the Ezrahite" as you said—but now that it is written "A Maskil *of* Ethan," your battle is nothing, and you must leave the field against your will and not be seen there. O poor Elder, how will you go out? If so, they will defeat you, and all the people of the world will wake up from the field and pursue you, and you will have no lodging to show yourself before any man forever! Here you established that I should not leave the field, and here he appears in the face of King Solomon and all the men of Israel, and his commanders, his officers, and his chariots. May the verse assist you, Elder, for there is no strength left. Arise, Elder, strengthen yourself with all your might, for until this day you were known to be as strong as giants!

He opened and said: *A Maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite*. If it were written "A Maskil for David" as you said—but it says "A Maskil of Ethan." There is a *Maskil* and there is a *Maskil*. There is a *Maskil* above and there is a *Maskil* below. "A Maskil of Ethan" is like one who goes, a man who stands in desire, and all the holy limbs are gathered to him and honored...

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Zohar on the Torah portion "Mishpatim" (Laws). It focuses on the emanation of wisdom from the Supernal Mind and the structural relationship between the Written and Oral Torah, personified through King David and the "Eitanim" (Foundations).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Mishpatim (Laws)**<-

It ascends until it reaches the **Supernal Mind** <note>original: *Mocha Ila'ah*; the highest level of divine consciousness</note>, which is appeased by it, rejoices in it, and receives it. Then, it becomes a **Maskil** <note>A term meaning "Enlightened" or "Wise Instructor," often used in the titles of Psalms</note> for the "living ones." It grants him understanding and informs him of the heights of wisdom, his beloved, and everything that is necessary. That Supernal Mind acts as a **Maskil** for the "living ones." And when King David was established in his proper arrangement before Him, He became a **Maskil** for David, just as the Supernal Mind is a **Maskil** for him. Regarding this, there is one type of *Maskil* and another type of *Maskil*. There is a *Maskil* through the spirit of the **Eitanim** <note>original: *Eitanim*; literally "Strong Ones," referring to the ancient foundations or pillars of the world</note> who were born on the sides of the moon. These *Eitanim* are in a state of rest, mirroring the pattern above, and they were born among the ten mountains. The "Mountains" are hidden, while the "Eitanim" are the strong thighs, like a rushing stream, and that "Strong One" (*Eitan*) is between them.

Arise from your place! Come and see that from all sides, at the hour when Moses ascended to receive the Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, handed over to him the seventy keys of the Torah. When he arrived to be crowned—and your sign is "Arise, rejoice"—one key was brought to him that was hidden, which had not been handed down below before him. He saw before him a staff <note>The Staff of Moses</note> containing all the keys, upper and lower, like a master key. He saw before him the joy of the world. What was hidden there? He said to him: "Eitan," and all those *Eitanim* hang from it and stand through it. From the "Torah of Comfort" <note>referring to the teachings of Rabbi Menachem</note>, they are of the **Written Torah**, and he is the essence of the Written Torah. He informed him and gave him understanding (*Maskil*) that he is the essence and the key to the Written Torah.

And when the **Oral Torah** was established because of them, the essence of the path and its key were certainly with him. Then it is a "Maskil for David," and the shield of the Torah—the Oral Torah—is nourished from what preceded it. And these are the words of the "Inquiries of the Torah": *Tashar* <note>A mystical permutation of letters</note> is what he ate, because he is the holy spirit of heaven... <note>The text here transitions into complex letter-mysticism and references to Tractate Chagigah 5a regarding the altar</note>. One was Deborah, and she was established in the seven, as it is written: "And Deborah arose." And after this, they brought the holy name in which Joseph was established, and this is the key. When the Oral Torah is opened, we require that it be recognized by him, and this is the teaching: "An *Eitan* (Strong One) carves a path for the son of comfort."

The **Eitanim** are the **Tannaim** <note>The Sages of the Mishnah</note>; they are the pillars and supports for the "Son of Comfort." Now it must be made known: when they go toward the **Written Torah**, they are called *Eitanim*. Regarding the **Oral Torah**, they are called *Tannaim*. *Eitan* relates to the Written Torah; *Tanna* relates to the Oral Torah; and everything is as it should be. The *Baraita* <note>External oral tradition</note> is like a field. King Solomon and the mighty men... and one of them merited to rejoice like a strong man. It is recognized in the "tearing of the garments." Behold, I know that he came and stood after the restoration was prepared, and he was found in it, and the point of my strength stands like a field in his heart...

**"Hear, O mountains, the Lord’s controversy, and you strong foundations (*Eitanim*) of the earth"** <note>Micah 6:2</note>. "Hear, O mountains," as we have said. "And the *Eitanim*," as it is written from the voice. "Foundations of the earth"—these are certainly the foundations, for from them the earth is nourished and from them it receives every day. **"For the Lord has a controversy with His people"**—who is it that can uphold the covenant of the Holy One, blessed be He, with Israel? And in another place: "Hear, O mountains"—this is one resting place. "Arise, contend with the mountains"—this is a second resting place where the Holy One, blessed be He, built all those disputes for Israel and all those rebukes... to establish it like Jacob. It is written that at the time He sought to rebuke him directly, what is written? **"The Lord also has a dispute with Judah, and will punish Jacob"** <note>Hosea 12:2</note>. What is this dispute? As it is written: **"In the womb he took his brother by the heel"** <note>Hosea 12:3</note>. Regarding that which is below, it is a rebuke. And all those disputes—is it not a great matter, "In the womb he took his brother by the heel"? Is it a small thing, what he did in the womb? Did Jacob really act in the womb? Heaven forbid! Rather, this is the voice...

## Introduction (Upper Columns)

**[Right Column]**
As you say, even that one who cleanses the spirit <note>original: *rucha*</note> up to two times, it is written in this verse: "And for you, a covering." One is from within and is obligated, and one is from the side of the spirit. And if you merit that one, you shall have mercy, and you will speak as if you did not see those internal struggles of yours, for they are all forgiven with you from below. From here on, I will not remove from here those who wait for your midst, as it is said, "to mention My name." That spray of saliva stands at the opening like a dog.

**[Left Column]**
Regarding Jacob, who as an infant was assisted by mercy from his mother’s womb to help in the claim below him, and was grasped by his hands; his life was sustained <note>original: *t-t*, likely a shorthand for "good" or a mystical cipher</note> because there was no strength for the "Dominant Man" <note>referring to the primordial or fallen state of Adam</note>. And until now, the one who was his strength was not yet born. From the strength of this Dominant Man, you are the one who stands in the image of the Dominant Man from his mother’s womb, as it is written: "And he begot in his likeness, after his image, and called his name Seth." Two things: "in his likeness" and "after his image," for he was born circumcised.

## Laws (Mishpatim)

In the beginning, He concealed all the **striking** <note>original: *batishu* - a term for the emanative "striking" or impact of divine lights</note> so that the **serpent** <note>the primordial snake/evil inclination</note> would gather and toil over it. Like a dog that licks a drop of blood, it nourishes itself until it is broken below. When a man emits [seed] from himself afterward, it becomes for him a light from his own bones, and all is for benefit. Thus, the masters of counsel said: they extract from that **womb** and snatch from it the **side of the thigh**, and afterward they give him a single bone. That womb and that thigh are male and not female. Behold, the bone that they give him for his portion is a cup that is mixed for him. And regarding all those who do not know or gaze upon the Holy One, Blessed be He, and all of them together are truth. Behold, **piety** <note>original: *chasidut*</note> causes the bone to burn, as it is said: -> *She who abandons the companion of her youth* <- <note>Proverbs 2:17</note> etc. So too below, in the same manner as it is above.

Come and see: whoever is inscribed as a tenant-farmer <note>original: *chachra* - one who leases land</note> like him, acts according to his deeds in the world that he has, and clings to the [Other] Side and does kindness with it. Woe! The **Other Side** <note>original: *Sitra Achra* - the realm of evil/impurity</note> is not so. Since one who is meritorious is inscribed on the **Side of Holiness** of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and acts according to His deeds and clings to Him, then He desires to nourish him and to remove him from the world [to the afterlife]. Come and see: below, she acted according to her deeds and clung to him; see what she did when she was inscribed on the Side and her thigh fell. The Holy One, Blessed be He, is not so; whoever is meritorious toward the Other Side and clings to it, the Holy One, Blessed be He, then loves him and does for him all the good of the world <note>This likely refers to the "wicked who prosper" in this world as their reward for any small merit, so they have no portion in the next</note>. Now, here, prepare yourself, for the serpent goes toward him and seeks to incite you, but he cannot.

He opened and said: -> *What profit has a man in all his labor wherein he labors under the sun?* <- <note>Ecclesiastes 1:3</note> Did King Solomon not come to teach everything? If he had said "in his labor wherein he labors," it would be fitting, for the **labor of Torah** remains in him as a profit. But since it is written "in **all** his labor," it implies everything, that nothing remains in which there is profit. Rather, King Solomon did not say this of every man, but there is a man in the world whom the serpent gazes upon, and he does not sin, yet he does not strive in the good even for a single moment.

And regarding this, it is written **"his labor"** (*amalo*) and it is not written **"his toil"** (*yegia'o*). "His labor" is entirely nourished by labor with mercy, and he does not push away the labor that he toils. "His toil" is as in: -> *When you eat the toil of your hands* <- <note>Psalms 128:2</note> etc. And it is written: -> *This is the toil of the hands of the wicked...* <- <note>Job 20:18</note>. Woe! "His labor" is written, and in this striving of his, he is clothed until his life is "under the sun." On the side of this **sun** <note>original: *cheres* - a term for the sun, often associated with the harsh side of judgment</note> where he strives in evil, regarding this it is written: -> *He shall have neither son nor grandson among his people* <- <note>Paraphrase of Job 18:19</note> etc. For the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires that he should produce **offspring of wisdom**, but he produces offspring that are a law that dulls the world.

And regarding this it is written: *What profit has a man in all his labor.* Come and see: one who does not strive to produce offspring and clings to the "dull side" <note>original: *kehi sitra*</note> which is called a "cup," and upon the likeness of its wings is **another spirit** <note>a spirit of impurity</note>. And -> *Spread your wings over your handmaid* <- <note>Ruth 3:9</note> in order to mate in holiness, to go out and produce offspring. And the Holy One spreads His wings over that power in order to bring out into the world [souls]. One who does not want to produce offspring, his "wing" etc. The wing of that "cup of life" sees the barrenness like this serpent for the lonely fool. His wing etc. As it was said, now his life—that he did not strive to produce offspring—all that is necessary has been said.

The **dispute** <note>original: *riv*</note> that the Holy One, Blessed be He, made is stated. The dispute of which it is written: -> *Arise, contend with the mountains* <- <note>Micah 6:1</note>. What is this? Rather, it refers to the mountains below. Why this dispute? Because upon them depends all the "brain" <note>original: *mocha* - the intellectual/spiritual essence</note> of those who act and toil toward their wisdom of "striking." What is the reason? Because they were toiling and knew the "blindness" <note>or hiddenness</note> of all the supernal kings who give life, and he did not make them wise according to their names. And all their support and the "crowns" of the sides were wandering to their crowns. First, because they knew how to draw down their strength which is in power and the constellations together. And second, because they knew how to warm them with everything they needed. And regarding this, the Holy One, Blessed be He, sought to make a dispute and judgment against them. And since there shall be dispute and judgment against them, all their dominion is doubled so that there shall be no profit in it. And because of this: *Arise, contend... and let the hills hear your voice.*

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Judgments**<-

Come and see: these souls are those levels that joined with the "maidens following her" <note>Psalm 45:15</note>, and because of this, "the young women hear your voice." Come and see that this path has many ancient aspects, for this is what Israel did until they were joined with the lower levels. Regarding the "thigh" <term>Yerech: often a euphemism in Kabbalah for the lower sefirot or foundations of strength</term> that they spoke of, they strengthened them greatly, and Israel is within that thigh. Mordecai saw and concealed the desire of Haman, which was his "thigh," and because of this, he was angry at the matter that was prepared for him. The companions saw what is written: "And Rebecca took the garments of Esau her elder son, the precious ones..." <note>Genesis 27:15</note>. With these garments of his, she took his spoils and removed him from all his blessings. Because of this, the voice they found was his chariots, to ride upon them in their covering, to see your ways constantly in their thighs and their teeth and their laughter. These were two matters from the "Other Side" <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of evil or impurity</term>, and all this was because they robbed them; they have no voice except to ride. Therefore, they laugh at their riders, for they are consumed by their coverings, and thus their blessings were taken from them—the voice and the push—and they were kings. From those like the upper clouds, and from that which was their strike, they desired their riding, all of them swimming in the day of their disgrace. For this reason, there is no ascent without an ascent, and no word without a memory, and every thing returns to its place.

Solomon said: "And I praised, and I saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun; and behold the tears of the oppressed, and they have no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power, but they had no comforter" <note>Ecclesiastes 4:1-2</note>. This verse was cast into this and explained. But I praised, etc. From what place did Solomon return to life? After this matter lived, it returned as before, and he spoke another word and brought it: "But I returned and saw under the sun..." <note>Ecclesiastes 9:11</note>. At all times, Solomon would investigate with atonement <note>original: "bekhapara," likely referring to a state of ritual purity or a specific mystical method</note> and would go on his palms toward the East and see what he saw. Afterward, he would return to the North side and stand there, closing his eyes and lifting his head in this argument: Behold, a pillar of fire and a pillar of cloud were below. Upon that pillar of cloud, a certain man would come, and that man was great and strong. Likewise, he would come driven and rebuked upon the pillar of fire, and he blew and was driven like a fool upon the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire. That man was over them, and they would prostrate themselves before King Solomon.

Then the man would come and laugh before him and give him those leaves. King Solomon would take them and smell them, and he would know by them a sign. He would say: "This is the bosom of the double, and this is the bosom of the open-eyed." When there were two leaves, he knew that both the "double" and the "open-eyed" <note>References to the fallen angels Aza and Azael, who are said to be chained in the Mountains of Darkness</note> wanted to inform him of things. What did he do? He would set his throne like a great eagle <note>original: "gontafna," a legendary bird or mechanical throne-eagle</note> upon which the Holy Name was engraved. He would take the ring <term>Ezka: the legendary Seal of Solomon</term> upon which the Holy Name was engraved, go up to the roof, ride upon that man, and travel with him. That man would ascend to the height of the clouds, and in every place where he performed a movement, he was beneath him. According to the path of his wisdom, in that place where the table was joined, they knew and would say: "Behold, King Solomon is going and passing here," but they did not know to which place he was going. The spirits that were there would say: "These are the serpents that go and encompass the world." The man struck out directly and flew four hundred parasangs <note>An ancient unit of distance</note> until he reached the Mountains of Darkness.

And there he would take his rest as in a desert in the ruins, and he would hide there and lift his head and see the Mountains of Darkness. He knew there everything that was necessary, and he knew that he should enter there. He rode upon the man as before, and he flew and leaped into the mountains until he reached the place of the dwelling. There he called out with strength and said: "Woe, the thigh is cast down..." and he saw everything. He went there until he drew near to that place, holding the ring before them, and he approached. There he knew all that he desired of those hidden wisdoms that he sought to know. Once they told him all that he desired, he would then ride upon that man...
