<meta>This page continues the discourse of the "Saba de-Mishpatim" (The Old Man of the Section of Laws). The previous section likely introduced the mysterious old donkey-driver who reveals himself as a master of secrets. Here, he discusses the profound mystery of "the oppressed"—the souls of infants who die before their time.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

When he returned and came back to his place, as soon as he sat upon his chair, his mind became settled. He began to speak words of wisdom in his mind, and at that moment his voice said: "Fortunate is my portion! Fortunate is your portion! For surely from this path, one is privileged from the side of wisdom and for goodness, as it is written <note>Proverbs 24:4</note> **'And by knowledge [the rooms are filled]'**." And then: "And I returned and considered all the oppressed." Are there so few in the world that he says "all the oppressed"? <note>Ecclesiastes 4:1</note> Furthermore, what is meant by "the oppressed"? These are the infants who die by the power of oppression <note>meaning they are taken prematurely by divine decree</note>, who are oppressed from several sides: oppressed in this world above, and oppressed below. 

Come, friends! They awoke and stood before him, and they all bowed to him. He said, "Rise, Old Man! Awaken with your strength! Old Man, say your words, for surely in all the words you say, there is no business like these 'oppressed' ones." For there is no break at first—Heaven forbid—from comfort to be said of them, as it is written <note>Exodus 34:7</note> **"Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation."** How could such a one be "oppressed" <note>The Saba asks: if they die for their fathers' sins, are they truly 'oppressed' innocents or just receiving justice?</note>? King Solomon cried out and said: "And I returned and considered all the oppressed that are made, etc." and "they have no comforter, etc." Since they are oppressed as you said, a voice is seen in them, and thus they shall be oppressed in the balance. As it is written, until they have not yet spoken, they have no comforter... until he is like a small vessel, just an infant under the Holy Hand, and they have no comforter in this world. Since they are oppressed as you said, have pity on them! And the Shepherd <note>God</note> shall let them be oppressed from that side of the Master. There is no oppressed one like the one who returns; all of them are [included in] **"You shall not oppress your neighbor."** <note>Leviticus 19:13</note> And they shall be like a servant and a maidservant of the bosom, oppressed as a nickname from that side of freedom. And therefore he said, "all the oppressed."

Solomon said: It is a logical inference <term>Kal Va-Chomer: a 'light and heavy' logical argument</term> regarding all those oppressed from every side of oppression. And why are they oppressed? They lack a "Cano" <note>The Saba uses a cryptic term, likely referring to a base or foundation</note> and are under the "Kums." "Lacking a Cano"—he should have said "lacking a Nun" <note>A linguistic play on the Hebrew word</note>. What is "lacking a Cano"? If the lack is great enough to cause praise, it is not their sin, but rather true Grace from Above. To all, it is certainly a "Cano." How is it a "Cano"? Rather, because they are oppressed from your spirits there, to strike the living of this world. To the spirits, he pushes the "Cano." They are made like likenesses in this world, for as soon as their body is contemplated and that spirit is made in the body—pure and clean, without any filth of those who find grace in that world—then the body is oppressed just as the spirit was oppressed. It takes a form <term>Dyukna: the spiritual image or blueprint of a person</term> to enjoy it more than anything. 

And there are other oppressed ones of several kinds of spirits there, who are not made into bodies; for all these, they are "oppressed lacking a Cano." There are others "lacking a Cano" whose surroundings are like a barrier to their words. And they see the lack. The brain of the Ancient One <term>Atik: the highest, most hidden level of the Divine</term> is below, which is destroyed when they are compared in revelation. And the command for the child to be born draws from the Ancient One; have pity, for all is the will of their Master. And the person in this world does not know that they are the destroyers, the oppressed, and the lack for the Holy One, Blessed be He, to make them a body and to light for them a furnace. These are the "oppressed lacking a Cano." They lack a "Cano" and their bodies are against their will. 

And therefore King Solomon said: "And I returned [and considered] all the oppressed"—he meant all types of oppressed. You said they lack a "Cano" and were made as "afflicted ones." Just as it is so, they are oppressed who are already like the "uncircumcised" <note>referring to the foreskin/spiritual blockage</note>, etc. Go and move the body and make it, and afterwards they oppress them from the palm and kill them. Behold, they are "oppressed lacking a Cano." And regarding all of this, King Solomon said: "And I returned and considered all the oppressed lacking a Cano." And he saw the "tears of the oppressed"—they are all those who are squeezed with a claim before the Holy One, Blessed be He: "Behold, we are the pious ones of tears!" The "uncircumcised" <note>the forces of judgment</note> is soft to them and grows them until twelve years, and afterwards they oppress them from the "uncircumcised" and the Holy One, Blessed be He, kills them. "Take for Yourself the oppressed who lack a Cano like a loaf." If one committed a sin, they kill him. They have a claim and they laugh, saying: "Master of the Universe! An infant of one day old—has he sinned? In one day, can he be guilty?" Like a one-day-old who is like a voice of laughter, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, calls to him, as it is written: "And He said, 'Behold, I have come to you...'"

<margin>**Commandment**</margin> One [commandment] is to set aside Cities of Refuge for one who kills inadvertently, because of the "stone-throwers" and those who kill in the West <note>The "West" often symbolizes Malchut/Shekhinah</note>, for there was the Ancient Gate. ## Main Text (Zohar)

This state was like the mixture of good and evil; a servant and an atonement. He was supported previously, but became defiled like a darkened star, acting in a lowly way. Not so is my servant **Metatron** <note>The text uses "Mata" (Staff/Metatron) as a code for the chief angel who serves the Divine</note>; in all my house he is faithful. He is the companion of the "Evil" side in judgment, but "Good" in essence. It is taught to you to labor in the mystery of the "Staff" <note>Metatron</note> that was given to you, which was of the mixture of good and evil—tasting the good and erasing the evil. And because you have returned in repentance and are found in the "Living" state, you have gone out from being a servant and have been restored as a son to the Holy One, Blessed be He. The "Staff" given into your hand is the **Tree of Life**, which is life itself. And he shall take up the 49 aspects <note>The 49 gates of Understanding/Binah</note> of your judgment as a free man, and it shall be established and fulfilled in you:
> **He will never allow the righteous to be moved.** (Psalms 55:23) <note>The word for "moved" (Mot) is a pun on "Mata" (Staff/Metatron)</note>

The 49 aspects correspond to the 49 letters in the verse **"Hear O Israel"** <note>The Shema and the following response "Blessed be the Name..." contain 49 letters combined in certain traditions</note>. "Blessed be the Name of His glorious kingdom forever" consists of six words of the Higher Unity, which is **Tiferet** (Beauty). There are a second six words in "Blessed be the Name..." and the whole is completed by the **Tzaddik** (The Righteous/Foundation). The number 49 represents the prevention of the "Righteous" from falling before the "Wicked." Who caused this? The letter *Het* is missing from the "Staff" <note>M-T-H</note> to reach the 50 gates; for 50 gates of **Binah** (Understanding) were given to the Staff. Look at the beloved vision: the *Het* is missing from the count, leaving 49. This is the secret of "The righteous man falling before the wicked"—strike the wicked one, who is Samael <note>The Accuser</note>, and take the 49 from your "Staff" (Mata), of which it is said:
> **And the staff of God was in his hand.** (Exodus 4:20)

For the "Other Staff" is for you the staff of the lower world. Because the life of **Binah** (Understanding) has returned to you according to the measure of wisdom, as in our Mishnah, even Understanding has returned to you through repentance. It shall enter between the letters *Vav* and *Yod* and bring life, fulfilling for you and for Israel the promise: "With great mercies I will gather you." From there, your life will be sustained in you; "He will never allow the righteous to be moved." At that time, two commandments will be fulfilled in you: one, **"You shall surely help him to lift it up"** and **"You shall surely release it with him."** <note>Exodus 23:5 regarding a fallen animal</note> "Lift up" (Haqem) with the Higher *Yod* and the Merciful Staff; "Lift up" (Taqim) with the *Vav*. "With him" refers to the Son of Amram <note>Moses</note> who ascended to Understanding, which is the letter *Heh*. Therefore, "You shall surely lift up" refers to the *Heh* that had fallen. **"You shall surely release it with him"**: "Release" (Azov) refers to the 72 names <note>original: "Ayin-Bet" (72)</note> and the letter *Vav*. This is the secret of the 70 names.
<margin>Refers to the 72 names derived from Ex. 14:19-21</margin>
**"And he moved... and he came... and he stretched out"** <note>Exodus 14:19-21</note>. This is the secret of life. There, the "Skin" (Or) is transformed into "Light" (Or). "You shall surely release"—in its time, he shall inherit the Kingdom. "And you shall gather your grain, your wine, and your oil," which are for Israel. Regarding the forgotten sheaf and the corner of the field: "For the poor and the stranger you shall leave (Ta'azov) them." Here we change to the third commandment. It is necessary to return to them, for they are the "Staff" for the Righteous. "Release, release." "You shall release" the Righteous "with him"—this is the Son of Amram. Take his portion: "For the poor and the stranger you shall leave them." You were a "stranger" (Ger) at first, as it was said of you: "For I was a stranger in a strange land." But now your wisdom is according to your level. "Lift up" the lower *Vav*, "Raise him up" with the Son of Amram in your higher level.

**The Commandment** of the Crown: This is to redeem the **Hebrew Servant**. Why is he called "Hebrew" (Ivri)? Because he comes from the side of the "Passage" (Ever). Regarding the acquisition of a Hebrew servant, "You shall surely furnish him" (Ha'aneq Ta'aniq):
> **If you buy a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years.** (Exodus 21:2)

What is his "acquisition"? It is through the Crowns of the Torah. **Metatron** is the "Servant of the Lord," comprised of the number nine on each side, totaling the six letters <note>Metatron in some spellings has 6 letters</note> and the **Six Orders of the Mishnah**. Through them, there is life for every person to labor in His service, to become "his money-acquisition." For "Money" (Keseph) is the Right Hand, the level of **Abraham** and **Hesed** (Kindness). From that level comes freedom and wealth. Why does he labor in this? So that he may merit the **World to Come**, which is called "the acquisition of his money"—the world of longing (Kissupha). This acquisition is over the 49 levels. The Supreme One is the "Acquirer of Heaven and Earth." "Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding." The Crown that he acquired for himself shall be his forever. The "Life" that is acquired for six years—look, the "Life" that is acquired forever, it is written of him:
> **And his master shall pierce his ear with an awl, and he shall serve him forever.** (Exodus 21:6)

There is no "Forever" (Olam) except for the World <note>note: Refers to the concept of 'Olam' as the Jubilee year or eternity</note>.

->**Mishpatim (Ordinances)**<-

...of the Jubilee <note>Hebrew: *Yovel*</note>, which consists of fifty [years], and this is the secret of the *Shema* prayer <note>The central declaration of Jewish faith</note> as we have learned: "Twenty-five, twenty-five" <note>referring to the 25 letters in the first verse of the Shema and the 25 in the response "Blessed be the Name..." totaling 50</note>. As we have learned regarding the laws of uncircumcised fruit and purities: there are fifty **Gates of Understanding** <term>Gates of Understanding: *Sha'arei Binah*, the fifty levels of divine wisdom through which the world was created</term>.
After one achieves unification through them, he accepts upon himself his Master as the yoke of the *Tefillin* <note>phylacteries</note> upon his head, and he sees his Master's 
open strap, ready to hear the Voice <note>original: *Qal*</note>, just as every tongue that is bowed hears—that is, the hearing of the one who seeks his redemption. It was taught in the five [books of the Torah] that the spirit of the fifty [gates] allows no redemption for another, like a garden of rest.
Regarding his sale, it was not said "He shall be struck," but rather "His uncle or his uncle’s son shall redeem him" <note>Leviticus 25:49</note>. And in the exile <note>original: *Galuta*</note>, it is mentioned 
that he is like a servant below. The "Heavenly Voice" <note>original: *Bat Kol*</note> of prayer says: "Six years he shall serve" <note>Exodus 21:2</note>, and between the labor of prayer, "Six years he shall serve."
There are three [attributes of] mercy, and the final matter of speech brings him out, as it is mentioned that he fulfills his obligation. For one who does not know how to revolve 
within them, the **Righteous One** <note>The Sefirah of *Yesod*</note>, the Life of the Worlds, prepares them for the Heavens, just as the Righteous One is the body, close [to the Divine], as it is written: "The Lord is near to all who call upon Him" <note>Psalms 145:18</note>.
And it is good for a person to be there, for a neighbor is near and not far—that is, the **Central Column** <term>Central Column: *Amuda d'Emtaita*, the balancing force in the Sefirotic tree, often identified with the son of God/Tiferet</term>, which is the "Son of Yah" <note>The Divine Name YH</note> that ascends

In the five [books] it is said of him: "The high praises of God are in their throat" <note>Psalms 149:6</note> 
"and a double-edged sword in their hand." For the Lord is certainly the head of the sword, to complete your lip; the *Yod* is to the right of your chariot,

certainly like your pan that brings out these fifty from your mouth... because of these things that

of Israel. And because of this, as much as you were wealthy... and the vision is held above...

## Main Text (Zohar)

And the end of the wall, as it is written: *five hundred reeds all around, to separate between the holy and the profane* <note>Ezekiel 42:20</note>. This refers to the Lower Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence in its most immanent form</note>, which is its Western Wall. It stands upon six <note>referring to the six directions or the six sefirot of Zeir Anpin</note>, a "mound" (*tel*) toward which all faces turn, for a "mound" is born, etc. The Shekhinah is his mound, upon which are his *six locks of hair, wavy and black as a raven* <note>Song of Songs 5:11</note>. And upon every single point <note>literally "thorn" or "tittle" of a Hebrew letter</note> there are heaps upon heaps of laws. If the "thorn" of the letter *He* (ה) is missing, it becomes a "mound" (*tel* - תל) toward which all turn. And it is difficult to separate between the profane and the letter *Shin* (ש) of the name *Shaddai* <note>Almighty</note>, for He is "all that is in heaven and on earth." Furthermore, one should desire "heaven and earth," and the masters of the academy established: "Upon what does the world stand? Upon a single pillar whose name is **Tzadik** <term>Tzadik: The Righteous One, associated with the Sefirah of Yesod</term>," as it is said: <note>Proverbs 10:25</note> **"The righteous is the foundation of the world."** And all of this is the Covenant of the Oath through which even the four <note>elements or directions</note> of heaven and earth exist, as it is written: <note>Jeremiah 33:25</note> **"If not for My covenant day and night, I would not have set the statutes of heaven and earth."** He is the "Heaven" which is above, and the eight <note>referring to numerical values or specific emanations</note> of heaven; the four is "Earth," which is *the earth is My footstool*. Because the Covenant connects heaven and earth, and the oath stands within it, it surrounds until the morning. One who reveals [this secret] to another <note>unworthily</note> is as if he blemishes the Shekhinah of heaven and earth and returns the world to "chaos and void." If a man were to remove the "thorn" of the letter *Dalet* (ד) from the word *Echad* (One), there would remain *Acher* (Other/Stranger) <note>Changing "One" (אחד) to "Other" (אחר) implies idolatry</note>. Heaven, which is the Covenant, would become "Other," and all would be delayed. A man who [sins] causes heaven and earth to rest upon "Other." And the Holy One, that "Other" voice is harsh, for it is the Shekhinah [in exile], and heaven and earth fall. It is as harsh as if *He cast down from heaven to earth* the **Tiferet** <term>Tiferet: Beauty/Glory, the central Sefirah</term>. For who puts "earth" in "heaven" that it says *He cast down from heaven to earth*? Rather, this is certainly the **Shekhinah** <term>Shekhinah: The Divine Presence</term>, and Tiferet is with her so as not to be separated from her, like her double, to fulfill in her: *My name is the Lord, and My glory I will not give to another.* From here we learn that the "double" is upon her, as it is written: *And it cast truth to the ground.* And one who shows the truth fulfills *Truth shall spring from the earth*, which is the Middle Pillar <note>Tiferet</note> upon which the Shekhinah stands, which created "God" (*Elohim*) and clarified "the Heavens and the Earth." Because the "Oath" is the Shekhinah, and this world has no existence without the Foundation (*Yesod*), which is a thing of substance...

Since the World to Come <note>Olam Ha-Ba</note> is above the "Oath" of cleansing and watering, it is not based on physical substance but on the blessing of **Yesod** <term>Yesod: Foundation, the Sefirah of procreation and connection</term> which stands upon it, which is the **Covenant** <term>Berit: The sign of the covenant, circumcision</term> through which marital relations occur. Because of this, on Yom Kippur—which represents the World to Come where all vows are submerged—marital relations are forbidden. There, the "Sign of the Covenant" is elevated according to the law of the *Tzadik*, as the sages established: "In the World to Come there is no eating, no drinking, and no marital relations, but the righteous sit with their crowns on their heads," etc. And because there is no [physical] use in the World to Come, the teachers established: "Whoever makes [mundane] use of the Crown passes away." For the teacher of the world that is below... the point of use is for healing. In the world of "his sister" <note>a metaphor for a high level of sanctity</note> there is no [mundane] use. Because of this, a Torah scroll has no vowel points on its letters, only crowns (*tagin*). Therefore, one who makes [mundane] use of the Torah scroll passes away. Likewise, regarding one who makes use of one who studies the laws (*halakhot*), the Rabbis established: "He who makes use of a teacher (*Tanna*) passes away."

**They came**, all the masters of the academies, and prostrated themselves before him and said: "Certainly a voice speaks through your mouth! We are not worthy, and we cannot comprehend these words, for no other 'foundation' or 'mouth' besides yours could speak them." Certainly, those who judge testify thus, for it is said of him: <note>Numbers 12:8</note> **"Mouth to mouth I speak with him."** There is no delay; Elijah is with you, but only to appease the Holy One, blessed be He, and he will serve you regarding the ten words of the exile for you. **Faithful Shepherd** <note>Moses</note>, a servant is bound to you, a "Hebrew servant" <note>referring to the portion of Mishpatim</note>... to his children with these hidden words from your granary. Your Torah is your "granary and winepress" <note>referring to the tithes mentioned in the portion</note>. As they established: "from the refuse of the granary and the winepress." Is it not written: "wilderness," "winepress," "foundation," "holiness"? A blessing to the Holy One, blessed be He—this is the Shekhinah, who is a blessing to the Holy One, blessed be He, supporting you. And He is holiness with him, and He is the Foundation in the supports... and thus the verse rises...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the "Faithful Shepherd" (Moses) within the Zohar's commentary on the portion of Mishpatim (Laws). It focuses on the transition from physical perception to spiritual vision, contrasting the "garments" of the soul with the "shells" of sin.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Laws (Mishpatim)**<-

The Holy One, Blessed be He, gives life and sustenance to those who exist within His Law <note>Hebrew: *Halakhah*</note>, which is the Divine Presence <note>Hebrew: *Shekhinah*</note>. The Holy One, Blessed be He, is with her in a permanent bond. From this, they shall be His forever, for there is a Law that is His daughter, from the side of the "Maiden" <note>A reference to the Shekhinah in her youthful aspect</note>. Regarding her it is said: "The Law is double." To every Law of yours, O Faithful Shepherd <note>The title for Moses in the Zohar</note>, it is said: "A Law given to Moses from Sinai" <note>original: *Halakhah le-Moshe mi-Sinai*</note>. From the mouth of the Power <note>Hebrew: *Gevurah*</note>, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave you His daughter. Because of this, regarding other laws it is said: *Many daughters have done valiantly, but you excel them all* <note>Proverbs 31:29</note>. Regarding your Law, it is said that you have prevailed over all, through the strength of the Lord who is with you, a mighty man of valor. He established it so, and my windows are focused on the heart, to give life to His structures through your mouth.

**The Faithful Shepherd opened** his discourse and said: *The angel who redeemed me from all evil* <note>Genesis 48:16</note>—this gives life to the Divine Presence, of whom it is said: *And the angel of God moved* <note>Exodus 14:19</note>. May He bless you in the World to Come, and may you be *in the midst of the earth* in this world, so that your authority may be sustained in both worlds. For you are the living ones who draw life from this "World of Life," as it is written: *She is a tree of life to those who lay hold of her* <note>Proverbs 3:18</note>. Life is found there, for all that belongs to them is filled with life. But the garments of the worn-out "shells" <note>Hebrew: *Klipot*—the forces of impurity</note> of skin, flesh, bones, and sinews are merely secondary to the spirit. That state is called "death"; there, one sees but does not perceive, hears but does not understand, speaks but has no movement like his companions. So too, such a spirit is considered "dead" above, for their debts are counted against them. "Know what is above you: a seeing eye, a hearing ear, and all your deeds are written in a book" <note>Pirkei Avot 2:1</note>. Many secular angels are with him, of whom it is said: *For He shall give His angels charge over you* <note>Psalms 91:11</note>. At times, the body is given permission to look at them and use their properties, for they are the living "beasts" <note>Hebrew: *Chayot*—a high rank of angels</note> who speak, sanctify, unify, and bless the Holy One, Blessed be He, together with Israel.

The Holy One, Blessed be He, gives life from above His Divine Presence, through which He receives the prayers of Israel. Because of sins, they were clothed in these "shells" of decree. Man's wisdom is in his hands, and it is called "living" when they establish the path of the Mishnah <note>The core text of Jewish oral law</note>, seeing the merit of their deeds in their hands. Because of these shells of sin, the verse says: *But your iniquities have separated between you and your God* <note>Isaiah 59:2</note>. Because of these shells, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is hidden, like the Seraphim of whom it is said: *With two he covered his feet...* <note>Cf. Isaiah 6:2</note>. In the time to come, *your Teacher shall not be hidden anymore, but your eyes shall see your Teacher* <note>Isaiah 30:20</note>. You shall live in this world without shells or skins; you will have permission to gaze into this world and all worlds, and the external forces will have no permission to gaze at you. Therefore, it is said of you that life and peace have come to you from the World of Life. This entire world is secondary to that; this is the "World of the Dead," for all generations apart from the Lord are considered dead.

**Rabbi Shimon said:** Holy Intention! Despite all this, one has no permission to gaze at the children of the World to Come with physical eyes, nor at their garments, as long as they are within the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Divine Presence. However, use the intelligence of your heart to see that the children of the World to Come and their service are witnessed by the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Divine Presence. Regarding this, Solomon said (of whom it is written: *And he was wiser than all men* <note>I Kings 5:11</note>): *And my heart saw much wisdom and knowledge* <note>Ecclesiastes 1:16</note>. The intelligence of the heart has no permission to gaze upon the Glory directly, but rather through the eyes of life—the vision and sight of their eyes. Everything is made known through the "breadth of the heart." Furthermore, in your vision: "sight" is by day and "vision" is by night, and both are through the eyes, not the intellectual eye of the heart. The eyes are the two mediators of the heart and its servants, and the King's vision is between them. Therefore, "a wise man is superior to a prophet." So it is with the two ears, the two "hearers" of the heart. In every instance, the Sages say: "The heart sees and the heart hears." Not only that, but it is said: "In the heart of the wise, it is established," and "The heart knows." *And in the hearts of all that are wise-hearted I have put wisdom* <note>Exodus 31:6</note>. Behold: Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge <note>Hebrew: *Chokhmah, Binah, Da'at*</note> are in the heart. Through them, heaven, earth, and the depths were made, and through them, the Tabernacle was made. Everything...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Raya Mehemna (The Faithful Shepherd) section of the Zohar, focusing on the spiritual anatomy of the human head and its correspondence to the Divine Sefirot, specifically through the imagery of the Song of Songs. It transitions into the legal and spiritual responsibilities of judges (Dayanim) as discussed in the Torah portion of Mishpatim.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

That one who is filled at times with the **Spirit of God** in **Wisdom**, in **Understanding**, and in **Knowledge** <note>Exodus 31:3</note>, and contains within him everything we seek. And the scent and the faith depend upon all of this; and this resides in the heart even more than in a prophet. Anyone who gazes to learn from him finds no end. And through it, the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, who is without end, grants what you did not previously have permission to behold with those eyes. And for the wicked who turned away and turned back, "they shall not see." These "drops of the heart" are dead and blind, as if they were husks <note>term: Kelipot; the spiritual shells or forces of impurity that conceal the Divine light</note> on every side. They see nothing; they are darkened and do not intervene between you and the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, and His **Shekhinah** <note>term: Shekhinah; the Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</note>. For all of this lower world and the angels shall ascend to you in a vision through the "windows" of the eyes, and the "tunnels" of the stars, the nose, and the mouth—like a king who enters the inner chambers to dwell with his son. And because of this, the constellations of Israel depend on it; through that constellation, the whole generation is relaxed, like gardens, and the heart and the life of every thing in the world shall be from you.
Afterward, the world is "peering through the windows" etc. <note>Song of Songs 2:9</note>. And these are the windows of the eyes, and the tunnels and stars of the nose and the mouth. And these are the seven openings that are redeemed through seven types of incense, and thus one learns of the ascent through them. Incense for life: "Spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices" <note>Song of Songs 4:14</note>. Through that, and from all that is below, thus ascends the "perfume of myrrh and frankincense" etc.
The **Holy One, Blessed be He**, ascended: "Who is this that comes up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense" etc. <note>Song of Songs 3:6</note>. "Who is this" <note>original: "Mi Zot"</note> refers to the totality of "Who" <note>Mi - associated with the Sefirah of Binah/Understanding</note> and "This" <note>Zot - associated with the Sefirah of Malkhut/Kingship</note>. It is comprised of seven types of spices, and nothing comes from the poor. Two of them are spikenard and saffron from the seven kingdoms, like an eagle—dead before her and one behind her; and like a raven—dead before her and dead behind her. And these are **Greatness** (Chesed), **Power** (Gevurah), **Beauty** (Tiferet), **Victory** (Netzach), and **Splendor** (Hod), until "Yours, O Lord, is the Kingdom" <note>1 Chronicles 29:11</note>, which is **Malkhut**, comprised of three spices. "Perfumed with myrrh"—this is not **Keter** (Crown); "and frankincense"—this is not **Chokhmah** (Wisdom). "From all the powders of the merchant"—this is **Binah** (Understanding), the full cup, the commandment of your Master.

---

"**You** shall not follow a multitude to do evil... to pervert justice" <note>Exodus 23:2</note>. "Follow the majority to incline." There is no "multitude" less than three. And if there is no judgment in it, it is because she <note>the Shekhinah</note> follows the judgment, for the judgment of the **Shekhinah** is in three. These are the three types of her **Chariot** <note>term: Merkavah; the Divine assembly or vehicle of manifestation</note>. And she is the Law of Truth, the "Middle Pillar" <note>term: Amuda d'Emtaita; the central balance of the Sefirotic tree, usually Tiferet</note>. And any judge who does not judge a true judgment in its absolute truth, it is as if he causes the **Shekhinah** to depart, as one who profanes the world, and it shall rise to be destroyed—God forbid—and the **Shekhinah** is with him. And **Gehenna** <note>term: Purgatory or the realm of spiritual retribution</note> shall arise as the mate of the profaner, with the profaner, through the permission of a judge who upholds a "lying lip." A true judgment is the Middle Pillar. A "lying lip" is **Gehenna** and the profaner. And opposite every judge who judges, **Gehenna** is open before him by his own taste, the mate of Death, riding upon his snorting from above—Death like a profaner behind him and upon his nostrils.
But **Eden** is open to his right, and the **Tree of Life** is open before him upon his head. And this is the one who judges the judgment for the tree of the vision; the Angel of Death rules over him <note>if he judges falsely</note>, and that is his crown. But if he judges a true judgment, it is holy, and he shall enter into **Eden** and taste from the **Tree of Life**, as it is written of it: "And take also of the **Tree of Life**, and eat, and live forever" <note>Genesis 3:22</note>. And he is created like a free man below; in it was the **Tree of Life** for those who hold fast to it. The **Tree of Life** is **Tiferet**; its life is **Chokhmah** and **Binah**, the life of the King. And to "live forever" is the judgment for the Kingdom. The moon and the judgment are in the heart, and in the palm tree was the spirit. And because of this, "a judge has only what his eyes see." And thus there is no judge but the Holy One, and what his eyes see, for "the eyes of the Lord run to and fro" <note>2 Chronicles 16:9</note>. His eyes are upon all the ways of man, and through them He "peers through the windows"—the spirit of the openings of a person in the two eyes, the two tunnels <note>nostrils</note>, and the two openings of the nose and the mouth. Behold, these are the seven below that are upon them. And thus, like the action that is included in the seven of the **Shekhinah**, she is embraced by twenty hands, and the surrounding three, and the Covenant <note>Yesod</note> is two... two legs. Seven: Yah, Yud-He, in her seven judges, which are included in the seven openings of the head.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Ra’aya Mehemna (The Faithful Shepherd) within the Zohar on the Torah portion of Mishpatim (Laws). It focuses on the spiritual anatomy of the human soul, the hierarchy of the Sefirot (divine emanations), and the struggle between the Good and Evil Inclinations.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Laws<-

This commandment is regarding this: just as the hidden point <note>The Sefirah of Chokhmah/Wisdom</note> corresponds to the letters Y-H <note>The first two letters of the Tetragrammaton</note>, and this Y-H is like its natural seal to look upon the natural arrangements and visions that descend. These are the arrangements for the body of the Priest. The performance of the commandments is like the garment of the altar. Because of this, the commandments are called "friends." And because of this, the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> is the body, while the "Other Side" <note>the realm of evil</note> is the clothing consisting of skin and flesh and kindness. <term>You have clothed me in skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews</term> <note>Job 10:11</note>. After the Divine Presence is within, that body is called nothing but a garment; a garment for the dream, a garment for the Torah. And this is the Torah: <term>This is the law: when a man dies in a tent</term> <note>Numbers 19:14</note>. In the Beauty <note>Tiferet</note>, "Man" sits in the house. And in the place where the commandment is given, it is called a "body" for the Man, such as the "bodies of the laws" <note>essential legal principles</note> and the commandments of statutes. The Holy One, Blessed be He, is the Judge from the side of the Central Column <note>Tiferet</note>, from the side of Understanding <note>Binah</note>. A judge <note>Dayan</note> is from the side of Sovereignty <note>Malkhut</note>. An officer is from the side of the one who exacts justice; the officer is the ruler. And from the side of Joseph the Righteous, the Mishnah is taught, for "Joseph was the ruler." All the emanations <note>Sefirot</note> are judges: from the side of Kindness <note>Chesed</note>... for Beauty <note>Tiferet</note> he is a Judge. And they are officers from the side of Sovereignty <note>Malkhut</note>, teaching "officer and constellation." And in the commandment following this, "Judges and officers you shall appoint," which we will explain in the portion of Shoftim.

**Keep** far from a false matter; and do not slay the innocent and righteous, etc. <note>Exodus 23:7</note>. This is a commandment to treat litigants equally and to distance oneself from a false matter, so that they shall not say a word of partiality in the matter. For the Holy One, Blessed be He, comes as a cup that "does not show partiality and does not take a bribe." The secret of the word "One" <note>Echad</note> is similar: a judge must be like the color of "One," which is a unity for the One. He shall not take a bribe—this is His law. He should be like His example, making the two litigants equal. He shall not tilt the judgment to one more than the other, but rather keep them in a single balance according to the image of Justice. Afterward, each one is judged according to his deeds. The masters of the Mishnah taught: "A righteous man who suffers" <note>Tzaddik ve-ra lo</note>—the Good Inclination judges him. "A wicked man who prospers" <note>Rasha ve-tov lo</note>—the Evil Inclination judges him. A "middle-of-the-road" person—both judge him. One who is entirely for praise has no judgment at all; he has no Evil Inclination, for he is a "perfectly righteous man." This is "a righteous man who prospers" <note>Tzaddik ve-tov lo</note>, and there is no "Good" <note>Tov</note> other than Torah, as it is written: <term>For I give you good doctrine; do not forsake my Torah</term> <note>Proverbs 4:2</note>. And "a righteous man who suffers" <note>Tzaddik ve-ra lo</note> is from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. He is called "righteous" even though he "suffers" <note>literally "evil is to him"</note> because the Evil Inclination is in his lap; however, because the Good rules over it, he is called a righteous man who suffers. That "evil" is held under his authority like a slave under his master. And even though the evil in his lap hides the righteous man, a perfectly righteous man can be punished... for that good which is there. His feet... he has nothing in his lap, and he returns in repentance... and they shall be dust under his feet. From the side of the "modest" evil, the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note>... <insert>and he uncovered her feet and lay down</insert>—read it as "and He lay down" <note>Ruth 3:7</note>. For a handmaid <note>the Evil Inclination</note> shall not inherit the mistress. The Evil Inclination is female, the Evil Inclination is male... and from the side of the "righteous man who suffers," the Divine Presence shall be a crown upon the head of the man, and the handmaid—the Evil Inclination—is suppressed under the mistress. But from the side of the "perfectly righteous man," there is no stranger and no Evil Inclination. From the side of the "completely wicked man," he has no portion in the Divine Presence. A man has no portion in the Divine Presence except from the side of Good. Not every "Divine Presence" that they call "Divine Presence" is the same; there is the Tree of Good and Evil, and this is the throne for the entire Divine Presence... for "evil shall not dwell with You." Because it is within it, and "Sovereignty rules over all." ... jealousy for the Holy One... the shame of the Matron <note>the Shekhinah</note>... as long as the handmaid is at the gate... wherever the "Face" is, the Matron does not dwell there, but she opens her lap within... a blemish in a man... to look upon the Matron...

Until all his companions are awakened. The Holy Lamp <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> said: Faithful Shepherd <note>Moses</note>, because of this you labor in this Torah, which contains commandments to crown the Holy One, Blessed be He, over all the "companions" of the Shekhinah <note>the Divine Presence</note> through every single commandment, and you do not turn to your right. Blessed is your portion, for because of you the Shekhinah is found to crown the Holy One, Blessed be He. The companions of the Shekhinah among all Israel are the masters of the academies, and they are the companions of the Shekhinah. Thus does the Holy One, Blessed be He, do for the "Chamberlain of Heaven" <note>Metatron/Moses</note> over you: He shall crown you over all the upper and lower worlds.

Arise, Faithful Shepherd, to arrange the laws regarding the statutes of damages (*Nezikin*) in the arrangement of this Samael <note>the personification of evil/Satan</note> who lies in wait for the guilty, riding the "snail," the "crooked one," and the "face of darkness," which are the Ox, the Donkey, the Lion, and the Serpent. For he prosecutes at the right hand of the south, thirty beasts. Such are the beasts of their arrangement: the "silent," the "sun-scorched," the "bound," the Ox, and the "doubled serpents," which are such beasts that fly. And the arrangement of the beasts is to labor for destruction, and the beasts of damage belonging to Samael are thus arranged, and they are seven. And because of this, you are bound to them by every merit like sparks: the Pit, the Goring Ox, the Grazer <note>Maveh</note>, and the Fire <note>the four primary categories of damage</note>, and their blindness is a breach of trust.

**Arise**, awaken in purity. **Open**, Faithful Shepherd, and say:
> O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth shall declare Your praise. <note>Psalm 51:17</note>

These are those who labor in the commandment to purify. And because of this, the Masters of the Mishnah said: <term>The law of the kingdom is law</term> <note>original: "Dina d'malchuta dina" — a legal principle here applied mystically to the Divine Kingdom</note>. All judgments in this Name are purified in the Assembly of the Shekhinah, corresponding to the three Patriarchs. He is a Judge of Truth, and the foundation of the Judge is to judge from the side of the "God of the South" <note>Chesed/Mercy</note>; He is a Judge of Truth. And from the side of the "Elohim" <note>Gevurah/Judgment</note>, God is the Judge of all.
> For God is the Judge. <note>Psalm 75:8</note>

And what are the living judgments arranged to judge? Like the damage of the **Pit**. Second, to judge like the damage of the **Goring Ox**. Third, to judge like the damage of **Grazing**. Fourth, to judge like the damage of **Fire**. And their companions are to judge according to the law of the **Four Guardians**: the Unpaid Guardian, the Paid Solicitor, the Borrower, and the Renter. And the "Small Wage" corresponds to them. Against them are the laws for four: the law of the division of partners, the law of the division of lands, the laws of male and female servants. To you belong the "Mover" and the "Claimant" in several kinds of claims regarding money, theft, and seizure—if one damages his fellow or involves him in one of the four capital punishments of the court.

The "Window" is the Holy One, Blessed be He, when He comes to judge with all kinds of laws to issue a verdict, for "Power" <note>Gevurah</note> is feared. And from it, all damages are found to be living "Angels of Destruction," from whom come the souls of the wicked, as the Masters of the Mishnah established: "The souls of the wicked, they themselves are the damagers in the world." Even after death, the wicked man flows and writes, and his dwelling is the "Secret of Death," the "Wound of the Sabbath," and the "Healing of the Shekhinah." And such is the Sabbath, for at the time when the debts of human beings are found, and the "Healing" that you caused them—that they should be stirred by the words of Torah—is hindered by several damages of the Angels of Destruction: "Destroyer," "Anger," and "Wrath." And the "Lying Down" <note>impurity</note> that they intended for the Shekhinah, as the scripture calls to them and they were saying:
> Where is your God? <note>Psalm 42:4</note>

And how much exile comes from this "Evil Maidservant" <note>the Sitra Achra/Other Side</note>, of whom it is said "the exile of the handmaid." And it is written how many blessings are an "exile" for the Shekhinah. The Evil Maidservant, with the weight of the "Ham" and the weight of several sparks, is sold for a pittance. And how many sacrifices are received! For at the time when the Matron <note>the Shekhinah</note> is below, the Matron is hidden, stripped of the "Garments of Gold," the "Priests," the "Mountains of Stone," the "Serpents," and the "Purple." She enters with several "Vines and Pomegranates" and her "Garments of White" in which the Matron was adorned before the King of All and His mysteries.
> To remember the everlasting covenant. <note>Genesis 9:16</note>

And she is an "exile" to her Mistress. How many sacrificial foods—the "Ox" betrays its master, even to the King's heart, leaning on his four primary categories of damage, which are beasts. And the "Ox" turns from the pure to the four beasts: "Iniquity," "Destroyer," "Anger," and "Wrath," for all of them are prone to spoil with his breath, leaning upon the vessels, turning from the table, and the merchants wait and run upon them and their thoughts. And in his "Pit" are destroyed all the sacrifices from the table, and with his "Foot" he tramples and crushes everything. And the "Beasts" are donkeys and mules and "Mountains of Covering"—he tramples with his foot. And with his "Horn" he kills and perverts. He lifts everything, a void from the Kingdom.

-> **Mishpatim (Ordinances)** <-

And in the book where it is said that He is the Spirit (Ruach) and the Seven, it is stated regarding it: "Thus says the Lord your God," tablets in heart and spirit. Praised is he who elevates it through the "sustenance" which is the commandment of Tefillin, in which there are four sections <note>The four biblical passages written on parchment inside the Tefillin</note> containing the births: <term>Sanctify to Me every firstborn</term>, <term>And it shall be when the Lord brings you</term>, the letter *Vav*, <term>Hear O Israel, the Lord</term>, and <term>And it shall come to pass if you surely hearken</term>. The hand and their grace are in the four sections and in the two arms; the arm is seven, and the two supports are nature, and the knot of the strap is the crown of the sections. For the Lord says, "My field is the Shekhinah." Regarding the prophet, it is said: <quote>"Into Your hand I commit my spirit"</quote> etc. <note>Psalms 31:6</note> The spirit is committed to the Lord and the Holy One, Blessed be He, as one, to receive it and toward the Shekhinah. For Beauty (Tiferet) is the level of Moses that falls, and Kindness (Chesed) is his arm, and the Staff is shortened by the 72 <note>The 72-letter name of God associated with Chesed</note> which is Kindness for the companion. ## Laws (Mishpatim)

The light shines through two distances. Through them, the Masters of the Assembly prepare two [Messiahs] who are destined to reveal themselves and remove the "chaos and void" <note>Tohu and Bohu</note>. This is so that the Messiah son of Ephraim shall not die, for he comes from the side of the Right Hand's glory. The Passover is the Right Arm, established through the verse: <note>Micah 7:15</note> **"As in the days of your coming out of the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders."** And these are the "living creatures" <note>Chayot</note> of Benjamin in his inheritance. In the end, they are destined to be revealed to fulfill the verse: <note>Isaiah 54:8</note> **"But with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on you, says the Lord your Redeemer."**

Afterward, all of them will draw from the might of the Messiah—the Messiah son of Ephraim—to be victorious in the vengeance of our remembrance. For thus it is necessary to conquer the labor of the "living creatures" of Israel with the Right Hand, and afterward to establish the standing that existed at the very beginning. Regarding him it is written: <note>Obadiah 1:18</note> **"The house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them and devour them."** At the time of this labor, the Central Column <note>The middle path of the Sephirot, often associated with Jacob or Moses</note> departs toward them and hastens to His house—this is the Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence</note>—for everyone in the grade of the Messiah son of Joseph. He takes the exalted letter *Yod* and the "horn" <note>The power of the Messiah</note> devours all our surroundings, just as the green of the field is consumed, of which it is said: <note>Psalm 103:15</note> **"As for man, his days are like grass..."** From Passover until Shavuot <note>The Feast of Weeks/Pentecost</note> shall be the redemption of the "living creatures" until that point, and from then on shall be the destruction [of the wicked]. For the language of redemption is "forever and ever." Anyone who guards the "living creatures" will find the dross removed from Israel in the days of the "living creatures." The Lion <note>The first of the four celestial faces</note> shall stand for them in the body. This "living creature" is the one for whom everyone bows; one bows at the word "Blessed" to the Righteous One, of whom it is said: <term>Joseph the Righteous</term> <note>The archetype of the Sephirah Yesod, associated with the Messiah son of Joseph</note>. And your sheaves bowed down, and they appeared to my sheaves, and I was strengthened by them. They shall merit the morning, and every "vav" <note>The letter Vav, representing the connection between heaven and earth</note> is in the name of the grade of the Messiah. We bless above and below; through him all Israel shall rise as companions of the body. Through him, they all stand upright in the resurrection. He stands among them in terror, for of him it is said: "And you shall be strengthened."

There will be the Messiah son of David, who is the Lion <note>Arieh</note> on the right, and the Messiah son of Joseph, who is the Ox <note>Shor</note> on the left. On the right is <term>Abraham</term> <note>Representing Loving-kindness/Chesed</note> and on the left is <term>Isaac</term> <note>Representing Might/Gevurah</note>. Holiness is sent to you from the side of the Lion. From the side of Abraham, they are called "Lions of the Morning." From the side of the Messiah, they are called "Bulls" from the wings. From the side of the center, they are called "Eagles," and of them it is said: <note>Exodus 19:4</note> **"And I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you to Myself."** These are the seventy trees. And over the "beasts," which are like the house of Esau. Then shall be fulfilled: "He shall have dominion from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth." So it is with the two Messiahs, and so it is with all Israel, all in the merit of what was given to Moses.

The Messiah son of David is from Judah, the Lion who crouches over him. As it is said: the Lion to the right, the Ox to the left, the Eagle in the middle, and Kindness <note>Chesed</note> over them all. <meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic discourse of the "Faithful Shepherd" (Ra'aya Meheimna) within the section of the Zohar dealing with the Torah portion of Mishpatim (Laws). It focuses on the symbolic refinement of Israel through the metaphor of agricultural processing—separating grain from chaff—and the spiritual significance of the first fruits and tithes.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Laws (Mishpatim)**<-

The pressure of the serpent reaches from Judah, of whom it is said <note>Genesis 49:9</note> **“Judah is a lion’s whelp; from the prey, my son, you have gone up.”** He shall arise over the sins of the world, crouching and lying down like a lion to prey upon them as in that time. And the sacrifice, as seen from them, rises on the path that stands to rule over them. At that time, the King shall awaken and be distinguished, scattered over the mixture of sins, which are the Amalekites and the "Mixed Multitude" <note>term: Erev Rav; the group of non-Israelites who joined the Exodus and are often blamed in mystical texts for causing spiritual setbacks</note> who are the evil within Israel. He shall prey upon them until not one of them remains, to fulfill what was said in the song of David <note>Deuteronomy 32:12</note> **“The Lord alone did lead him, and there was no strange god with him.”** From that time forward, we do not accept converts; as the masters of the Mishnah established: "Converts are not accepted in the days of the Messiah."

And the "serpents" of Esau <note>note: symbolic of the Roman/Western exile</note> of the world who remain—the Holy One, Blessed be He, shall immediately awaken to kindness to rescue [Israel], to fulfill what is said: "For behold, I uphold kindness." They [the nations] shall serve you and be destroyed, to fulfill for Israel: "And they shall have dominion over the fish of the sea, etc." and "The fear of you and the dread of you, etc." And from the side of the "End" <note>note: the final redemption</note>, five species are supported from all of them, and they are: **wheat, barley, spelt, oats, and rye.** These five belong to Israel, as it is written <note>Jeremiah 2:3</note> **“Israel is holy to the Lord, the first fruits of His increase.”** Just as there are five [species], when they go out from exile, so shall they be recognized until the grain is clarified, and the olive is known, and the secret of their nicknames.

And until they are clarified from among them, the serpent shakes itself against the letter *He* <note>note: the final letter of the Divine Name YHVH, representing the Shekhinah or Divine Presence in exile</note> with pressure, as it is said, to fulfill the verse <note>Exodus 17:16</note> **“For there is a hand upon the throne of the Lord [Yah].”** And because of this, the straw and the chaff are obligated in the tithe until the grain is clarified. After it is clarified, they are gathered to that place called Jerusalem. Just as wheat, after it is clarified from the straw and chaff, is brought into the storehouse, so shall Israel—who are the "pure grain"—be gathered to Jerusalem. The pressure is against the Mountain of the Lord, as it is written <note>Psalms 24:3</note> **“Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord? And who shall stand in His holy place? He who has clean hands and a pure heart.”** "Pure" like grain that has been clarified from its waste. At that time, it will be as it was at first, of which it was said: "They shall go up and strengthen his mouth."

At that time, the image shall be repaired to uphold the "grain" from within the straw and the rotting chaff that covers them. He shall call them "Israel, My firstborn son." And so it is with all trees: there is no breaking like the vine, for in its pruning it is broken. Like its grapes, they are broken and crushed between the feet. So too the olive; its olives are crushed in exile. Israel is compared to these: <note>Psalms 80:9</note> **“You brought a vine out of Egypt.”** And so in the fourth exile <note>Isaiah 5:7</note> **“For the vineyard of the Lord of Hosts is the House of Israel.”** And within this, there is no protest for Israel <note>Jeremiah 11:16</note> **“The Lord called your name a leafy olive tree, fair with goodly fruit.”** And because of this, there remains <note>Psalms 128:3</note> **“Your wife shall be as a fruitful vine in the innermost parts of your house; your children...”** etc. Close to this is Leah, who represents those recognized in exile.

And after they are established, they shall be sanctified for the Holy Temple, to be offered upon the altar, and the olives for the portion of the lighting of the lamps for the following day. And the merit for this: wine that shall not be used for libations [of idolatry]. And of Israel it is said <note>Psalms 106:35</note> **“But they mingled themselves with the nations and learned their works,”** because they were trodden under their feet in exile and were not clarified from them. Regarding them, David, peace be upon him, said <note>Psalms 49:6</note> **“Wherefore should I fear in the days of evil, when the iniquity of my heels compasseth me about?”** And of them Solomon said <note>Song of Songs 1:8</note> **“Go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock.”** Like Jacob, of whom it was said regarding the ancient vision... after they go out from exile like baskets of apples and all good spirits, in the manner of the exodus from the womb, as it is written <note>Song of Songs 8:5</note> **“Under the apple tree I awakened you.”**

The commandment after this is to bring the **First Fruits (Bikkurim)**, and after that to make the **Confession over the First Fruits**, and after that the **Confession over the Tithe**. The Mishnah establishes regarding the tithe that the obligation [starts] before its picking, and it takes effect after its picking for its processing. For example, the Etrog (citron), of which it is said that its status follows its picking for the sake of the fruit. And the Etrog's growth is similar to [other] trees, but its acquisition is like grain, for it is like seeds of which it is said that the processing is not complete until the end of its harvest.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on Parashat Mishpatim from the Zohar, Volume II. It focuses on the distinction between the Hebrew terms "Kadosh" (Holy) and "Kodesh" (Holiness/Holy), exploring how Israel’s identity is linked to the highest emanations of divinity.</meta>

->Mishpatim<-

## Main Text (Zohar)

"Holy" <note>Hebrew: *Kadosh*</note> and above even higher is "Holiness" <note>Hebrew: *Kodesh*</note>. Rabbi Isaac was traveling on the road, and Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Hiyya were traveling with him. 
Rabbi Hiyya opened a discourse on the verse: <note>Exodus 22:30</note> **"And ye shall be holy men unto Me"** <note>original: *ve-anshei kodesh tihyun li*</note>. From here, Rabbi Yose said that all the companions have spoken well, and so it is. From here it is written: <note>Jeremiah 2:3</note> **"Israel is holiness unto the Lord, the firstfruits of His increase."** "Firstfruits" <note>Hebrew: *Reshit*</note> certainly refers to Wisdom <note><term>Chokhmah: the second Sephirah, representing the first point of divine revelation</term></note>, which is called "Beginning" <note>Reshit</note>, as it is written: <note>Psalms 111:10</note> **"The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord."** And because Israel is called "Holiness" <note>Kodesh</note>, which is the level of the perfection of all, it is written: <note>Exodus 22:30</note> **"neither shall ye eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field."** For behold, Israel, who are perfect above all, do not draw nourishment from the side of harsh Judgment <note><term>Din: the attribute of divine justice and restriction</term></note>. **"Ye shall cast it to the dogs"**—certainly to the outside. For that is a very, very powerful judgment over all. 
Since powerful judgment rests upon it, and if they were to sin by partaking in it, it would cause a deficiency for those who are called "Holiness." Therefore, "ye shall cast it to the dogs" certainly, for the dog represents powerful judgment. It is a judgment more powerful than all, as it is written: <note>Isaiah 56:11</note> **"And the dogs are greedy of soul."** Come and see: when the text ascends in its path, it is written of Israel "Holy" <note>Kadosh</note> and not "Holiness" <note>Kodesh</note>. Here it is written: **"And ye shall be holy men unto Me; neither shall ye eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field,"** but there, regarding a carcass <note>nevelah</note>, it is written: <note>Deuteronomy 14:21</note> **"Ye shall not eat of any thing that dieth of itself; thou shalt give it unto the stranger that is in thy gates... for thou art a holy people"**—"Holy" <note>Kadosh</note> and not "Holiness" <note>Kodesh</note>. For all of them are from the side of Israel, and this is not disqualified <unclear>...</unclear> and because of the colors/aspects within the carcass, there are many who are afflicted. 
The Rabbi opened: It is written here, **"And ye shall be holy men unto Me,"** and it is written there, **"For thou art a holy people unto the Lord thy God."** "Unto the Lord" <note>referring to the Tetragrammaton</note> extends to Him and causes Him to be known. Rather, there it refers to the highest of the high <note>the upper Sephirot</note>, but here it refers to the Divine Presence <note><term>Shekhinah: the immanent, feminine aspect of God</term></note>. And it is written: <note>Isaiah 4:3</note> **"And it shall come to pass, that he that is left in Zion, and he that remaineth in Jerusalem, shall be called holy"** <note>Kadosh</note>—and not "Holiness" <note>Kodesh</note>. All of them are "Holy," but above them is "Holiness," as it is written: **"Israel is holiness unto the Lord, the firstfruits of His increase,"** with power, as we have established. And this is to say: **"And ye shall be holy men unto Me"**—certainly.

Rabbi Isaac was sitting before Rabbi Shimon. He said to him: It is written, **"Israel is holiness unto the Lord,"** and at the end of the verse it is written, **"all that devour him shall be held guilty."** What does this teach? He said to him: You have spoken well. **"All that devour him shall be held guilty"** is just as it is written: <note>Leviticus 22:14</note> **"And if a man eat of the holy thing unwittingly..."** and it is written: <note>Leviticus 22:10</note> **"There shall no stranger eat of the holy thing."** And because Israel is called "Holiness" <note>Kodesh</note>, it is written: **"all that devour him shall be held guilty."** Rabbi Isaac came and kissed his hands, saying: Long live the teacher! I only came to hear this word. 
He said to him: Rabbi, we have learned that "Holiness" <note>Kodesh</note> is higher than "Holy" <note>Kadosh</note>. If so, behold, "Holiness" is written in the Eighteen Benedictions <note>the Amidah prayer</note>, and this is the perfection of all. He said to him: Come and see, they all join together as one, and they are not made one until "Holiness" is within them. Even though all of them are "Holy," "Holiness" is the sum of all, for everything is included within it. And when Israel is included in them through strong faith <note>Aramaic: *meimanuta*</note>, they are all called "Holiness," as it is written: **"Israel is holiness unto the Lord."** And because of this: **"And ye shall be holy men unto Me."** 
Regarding the one who asked the Rabbi a wise question: Is it not written, **"neither shall ye eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field"**? If so, what of that which is written: <note>Psalms 111:5</note> **"He hath given food to them that fear Him"**? <note>The word for "food" here is *Teref*, the same root as "torn flesh" or *Treifah*</note>. Does He give "torn flesh" to the dogs? Why does it say He gives it to those who fear Him? He said to him: Empty one! Does it say He gives *Treifah* <note>forbidden torn meat</note> to those who fear Him? It says *Teref* <note>prey/food</note>. And if you say *Teref* is like *Treifah*—He certainly gives it to those who fear Him. Why? So that the sick should not be fed <unclear>...</unclear> for you know that this is from Him and all the sides of His commandments. And because this word is from the Master of the Torah, who wishes to warn us, it is written "to those who fear Him" certainly, and not to others. And all the stringencies of the Torah were not given by the Holy One, blessed be He, except to those <unclear>...</unclear> for these are His portions and these are His commandments, and not for you. 
See, Rabbi, it is well written: **"And ye shall be holy men unto Me."** Why does it say "men" <note>Hebrew: *Anshei*</note> and then "Holiness"? If they are "men of holiness" certainly, it is because when Israel went out <note>from Egypt</note>, they were from the side of the Jubilee <note><term>Yovel: representing the Sephirah of Binah/Understanding and ultimate liberation</term></note>. After they went out to freedom, they were called His men, like His own. And it is written of the Jubilee: <note>Leviticus 25:12</note> **"It shall be holiness unto you."** "Holiness" certainly. And because of this: **"And ye shall be holy men unto Me"**—truly His men. And the Holy One, blessed be He, said this concerning...

It explains why Israel is forbidden from eating "torn flesh" (treifah), associating such meat with harsh external judgments and "dogs."</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the sanctity of the community of Israel and the spiritual gravity of civil laws (Mishpatim). It connects the legal prohibitions against verbal abuse to the high celestial standing of the soul.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And because of this, Israel merited to be called "not female" <note>referring to a mystical state of active spiritual influence rather than passive reception</note>, as it is written: *For the sake of my brothers and my companions* (Psalms 122:8). Afterward, they are called "Holy," from what is written: *Israel is holy to the Lord, the firstfruits of His harvest* (Jeremiah 2:3). They are "Holy" itself, and not merely "the fat of the holy" <note>original: "chalvei kodesh"</note>; for just as all fat and dreams <note>perhaps a scribal variant for "fat and choice parts"</note> are set apart, so too are they. And it is written: *No stranger shall eat of the holy thing* (Leviticus 22:10). Come and see: *If a man eats of the holy thing unwittingly...* Israel is destined to be called "Holy," and because they are holy, it is forbidden for one to call his fellow by a name of a carcass <note>a derogatory or "spiritually dead" name</note>, nor should he call another a "carcass," for his punishment is great. And this is even more true regarding other words.

Come and see, it is written: *A lyre for those who are sick from our companions.* What is "sick"? It refers to those who are afflicted by an evil eye, which brings two types of sickness to the world. Every day, anyone who calls his fellow by a name that does not apply to him, or rebukes him for a fault he does not possess—if it were not so, what would we say? Rabbi Hezekiah said: Anyone who calls his fellow "wicked" <note>Hebrew: Rasha</note> is himself brought down to Gehenna <note>Purgatory/Hell</note> and lowered for eternity, except for those who are truly rebellious and deserve to be called wicked. 

There was a man who cursed another in the presence of Rabbi Yose; he said to him, "You have crossed the line." He brought him before Rabbi Yehuda, who said, "I am calling him 'wicked' because of the leg <note>the action</note> I saw, not because he is inherently wicked." Rabbi Yehuda opened a discourse and brought the case before Rabbi Eleazar, who said, "Certainly, he is not liable." From here we learn what is written: *He is the Lord our God* (Psalms 105:7), and not "He is like our God." For if it were not so, no remnant of the root of Israel would remain in the world. In this manner, it was "like a dream" and yet not a dream; like a dream that goes after its interpretation.

Rabbi Hezekiah said: For this reason, the voice is the essence of everything, as it is written: *And upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man* (Ezekiel 1:26). It says "as the appearance of a man," and not "the appearance of a man" <note>emphasizing the distinction between the Divine manifestation and physical humanity</note>. Rabbi Isaac said: It is written: *As an apple tree among the trees of the wood* (Song of Songs 2:3)—"as an apple tree" and not a literal apple tree. "As an apple tree" which spreads out into various colors, and in those colors the word is unified. Rabbi Yehuda said: Look, we are only here to hear these words of the Lord. Come and see, it is written: *And the throne was as a throne on that day, like a circle* <note>original: "k'dur"</note>. Like a circle and not a generation <note>a play on the Hebrew words 'Dor' and 'Dur'</note>. Like a circle that encompasses the garden of the House of the Lord. And he was a king over kings, yet he called himself thus. Rabbi Abba said: Happy are Israel, for the Holy One did not call them "as holy" <note>k'kodesh</note>, but "Holy" <note>Kodesh</note> in essence, as it is written: *Israel is holy to the Lord, all who devour him shall be held guilty* (Jeremiah 2:3).

Come and see, Rabbi Yose said: What did the Holy One, blessed be He, see that He gave the laws of judgment <note>Din</note> to Israel immediately after the Ten Commandments? Rather, we have learned: The Torah was given to Israel from the side of Power <note>term: Gevurah - the Sephirah of strength and judgment</note>. Therefore, they needed to place a ladder between them so that the Torah would be guarded on all sides. For Rabbi Abba said in the name of Rabbi Isaac: The world only endures through Judgment <note>Din</note>, for without Judgment, it would not stand. But was the world created and sustained only by Judgment? Come and see, it is written: *Judgment and morning justice* (Amos 4:13)—one merits the "morning," but not every day. 

Rabbi Aha said: To the Lord! Rather, "to the morning" means before they eat, for the judges should not eat until they have rendered judgment. For anyone who renders judgment after he has eaten and drunk—it is not a clear judgment. As it is written: *You shall not eat over the blood* (Leviticus 19:26). What does "over the blood" mean? It is a warning to the judges that they should not eat until they have judged the case. For anyone who judges after eating and drinking is as if he is guilty of blood, for he has declared a verdict that belongs to another. This is not like the judgments of the commoners who require weapons to protect themselves; rather, they should not judge until they have eaten and drunk <note>Note: The text here contrasts the holy requirement of fasting before judgment with the mundane world</note>. And regarding this it is written: *Judgment in the morning* and it is written: *For I, the Lord, love justice* (Isaiah 61:8) and *righteousness in the land, for in these things I delight, says the Lord* (Jeremiah 9:23). It was taught that Rabbi Yehuda said: Whoever lies in judgment lies against the "Arrangements of the King" <note>the Divine structures</note>. What are the Arrangements of the King? Those of which it is said: *The strength of the King loves justice* (Psalms 99:4). And all these things are dependent on one another. Rabbi Yose said: These are the "Arrangements of the Throne," as it is written: *Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne* (Psalms 89:15), and it is written: *And the throne shall be established in mercy* (Isaiah 16:5).

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic exposition of the Divine Countenance (Partsuf) of Zeir Anpin (the "Short-Faced" or Microprosopus), often referred to as "the King." It follows the anatomical-mystical descriptions common in the Idra sections of the Zohar.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

<note>original: "Mishpatim" — the name of the Torah portion</note>

Just as it is in the mystery of the spirit, the **Head of the King** is established as the spirit stands in fire. The **hairs** hang, side by side, and all the divisions <note>or "ranks of angels"</note> are attached to them, above and below. These are the masters of lamentation, the masters of truth, the masters of the balance, the masters of howling, the masters of clanging, the masters of judgment, and the masters who see and taste the desolations and the mysteries of desolation; and all of them are scrutinized <note>or "engraved"</note> in the hair of the King. That is to say, the divisions that extend from the Holy King, and all of them are established in him through the holy opening.

The **Brain of the King** is the visitation of life when [souls] are remembered for their deeds and when their sins are revealed. Then the Brain of the King is scrutinized—that is to say, **Severity** <term>Gevurah: the divine attribute of judgment and restraint</term> is strengthened in its judgments and spreads to its sides, and it is not found to be from the Brain of the **Ancient Holy One** <term>Atika Kadisha: the highest, most merciful aspect of the Divine</term> which is called **Will** <term>Ratzon</term>.

The **Eyes of the King** are the supervision over all, the supervision of those above and those below. All those who are masters of supervision are thus scrutinized in the eyes. Colors are found there, and those colors scrutinize all those masters of the King's supervision, each according to his way. All the colors of the eye are scrutinized, as we have said, as the supervision of the King. Thus the colors are awakened in the eyes, scrutinized in the place that gives supervision to all the colors of the masters of supervision. Thus they look toward the place where the light of lights comes to supervise, and a place emerges to be drawn from that river that surrounds the Brain of the Ancient One. From the place where the Brain shines, all Severity spreads, and the eyes flame like glowing red. But when the **Ancient Holy One** shines His whiteness, it looks with the vision of **Mercy** <term>Rachamim</term> and is filled with milk, and it provides nourishment to all. Then all the eyes are found to be like this pure milk that is poured out and emerges constantly, returning to love like milk. As it is said, it moves constantly and never ceases.

The **Nose of the Holy King** is the restoration of the Countenance. When the Severities spread and are joined as one, they are the Nose of the Holy King. Those Severities are scrutinized and emerge from a single Severity. When the judgments are awakened and they overpower from their side, they are only sweetened by the smoke of the Altar. And then it is written:
> And the Lord smelled the soothing aroma.
<note>Genesis 8:21</note>
This excludes the Nose of the Ancient One, which is not needed <note>for sweetening</note>, for the Nose of the Ancient One is "Long-suffering" <note>original: "Erech Apayim"</note>; all are scrutinized there, and the light of the **Hidden Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah Stima'ah</term> shines and scrutinizes His nose. And the support is the "balance," as it is written, "a balance for David," and it is written:
> And for My praise, I will restrain it <note>literally: "muzzle/nose-ring"</note> for you.
<note>Isaiah 48:9</note>
And regarding the awakening of the King's anger: "a balance for David," etc.

The **Ears of the King**: when favor is found and Mercy overpowers, and the light of the Ancient Holy One shines, the light of the two brains and the light of Wisdom are awakened. All those who scrutinize the Brain of the King flame as one. And when they flame as one, they are scrutinized as the "Ears of the Lord," for the prayer of Israel is accepted. Then there is an awakening for good and for the cup <note>of blessing</note>. Through this awakening, the "masters of wings" <note>angels</note> are awakened, who carry all the voices of the world, and all of them are scrutinized as the "Ears of the Lord."

The **Arms of the King** are the binding of Wisdom and Mercy, and their spreading out, which binds and strikes and flames like this scent of the King. Then the visitation is found in the King from the image of the King's glory. From all the "masters of kindness" <note>original: "Chasidim"</note>, Kindness <term>Chesed</term> is missing from them, but through Severity and the light of Wisdom and Mercy, the light of Wisdom is divided into three arms and three crowns. The letter *He* is five: Kindness and Severity as one light. The *He* comes to the crown, Kindness is crowned to be found in two lights, and they are perfect. And Severity shines as one, the *He* of the nine. And when all the arms are joined as one, they scrutinize the image of the King. And then it is written:
> The Lord shall go forth as a mighty man, He shall stir up jealousy like a man of war, etc.
<note>Isaiah 42:13</note>

The **Lips of the King** likewise proceed when the light of Wisdom shines. Wisdom shines in three lights. From one light, the light of Supreme Kindness shines. From one light, the light that scrutinizes the Brain of the King shines. And one light repeats until the light of the cheeks shines. And when it shines, it shines in five lights. In those, it shines from one path, as it is written: "And his sons who were attached..."
