<meta>This page continues the discussion of the mystical anatomy of the Divine (the Sefirot) within the context of Parashat Mishpatim. It specifically explores the "Palate" and "Mouth" as sources of speech, wisdom, and the emanation of the Hebrew letters.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

To cleave to Him, but it is written: *“Man knows not the price thereof”* <note>Job 28:13</note>. Just as the male cleaves to the female and she conceives and gives birth, she brings forth five lights and five kindnesses <note>The five "Chasadim" or benevolent energies</note>. Within them are engraved fifty gates leading to many lights. Corresponding to them are fifty aspects of the pure and fifty aspects of the impure. From these fifty, one ascends. One stands and is made into the whole, appearing in the place where it is suspended. When they are joined as one and settled in the King, they are called the "Hidden Treasures of the King." Because of this, He decrees words of truth.

The mouth depends upon them; the opening of the mouth. What is this "Mouth"? It is **Knowledge** <term>Da'at: the Sefirah that balances Wisdom and Understanding</term> hidden in the mouth of the King. It is not **Beauty** <term>Tiferet</term>, but the opening where all colors are united, as it is written: *“By knowledge shall the chambers be filled”* <note>Proverbs 24:4</note>. And that Knowledge was hidden in the vision, filling all the chambers and their wisdom. When the light within it is awakened and goes forth, it is then called **The Mouth of the Lord**.

The secret of those two lights—milk and salt—is like the Knowledge that meets in that light of Knowledge; they join as one, and words are decreed in truth, through **Wisdom**, **Understanding**, and **Knowledge**. Then all words of truth are decreed by these three lights. They enter into one another and are crowned as one. When they join as a single crown, they are called "The Sweeteners," and they are the **Palate of the King**. They are called the "Sweetness of the King," and of this it is written: *“Taste and see that the Lord is good”* <note>Psalms 34:9</note>. Upon this Palate depend all the rulers and officers of the King, as it is written: *“And by the breath of His mouth all their host”* <note>Psalms 33:6</note>. In this Palate, the perfection of all is found.

Therefore, all the letters associated with this place <note>The guttural letters pronounced from the throat/palate</note> appear in their perfection: **אחה"ע** (Aleph, Chet, He, Ayin).

**א** (Aleph): The light of the Holy Ancient One, the most hidden of all hidden things.
**ח** (Chet): The covering of Wisdom which is not found and cannot be grasped, as it is written: *“Man knows not its value”* <note>Job 28:13</note>.
**ה** (He): The light of the "Muzzle" <note>A mystical term for a specific concealment of light</note> which is like a light that flows and goes forth, watering everything and suckling the "children" <note>The lower Sefirot</note> until that abundance reaches and fills the Prophet. The vision is bound to the Lower Female <term>Malchut/Kingship</term>, and they are blessed by it. They do not separate from one another—the white within the red—as it is written: *“The mountain He desired”* <note>Psalms 68:17</note>, the hill of Lebanon.
**ע** (Ayin): The light of the **Seventy Branches** that are nourished by this spirit going out from the Mouth. Then there are seventy supports for the Holy One, Blessed be He, corresponding to them, just as the count of the whole Assembly of the House of Jacob that came to Egypt was seventy <note>Genesis 46:27</note>. For Jacob is the strength of them all, and those seventy branches hang [from him], extending to the four directions.

From the **ח** (Chet) shines the light of the **ג** (Gimel), the vision of **Kindness** <term>Chesed</term>, which is good for the righteous and is called "Reward." Of this it is written: *“The kindness of the Lord... you shall delight in the Lord.”*
From the **ח** (Chet) shines the **י** (Yod), which is **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah</term>. Everything is hidden in the Yod, which is concealed on all sides; therefore it is not found, as it is written: *“And it is not found in the land of the living”* <note>Job 28:13</note>.
From the **ה** (He) shines the **כ** (Khaf), which is the light and the measure of abundance that pours from the vision to that place called the "Horn," specifically the "Horn of the Jubilee." This is the **Kingdom of David** <term>Malchut</term>. Therefore, the Messiah comes only through the spirit of the *Khaf*.
**ק** (Qof): Just as there are seventy, so there are one hundred (Qof=100) from the Kindness of Wisdom's perfection. Thus, in this Palate is the perfection of all. Whoever knows this secret and dwells in it, blessed is his portion!

The **Body of the King** is the extension of **Beauty** <term>Tiferet</term>, in which all colors join.
The **Arms of the King** are the lights of **Kindness** <term>Chesed</term> and **Strength** <term>Gevurah</term>. Therefore, there is right and left.
The **Inwards** are established in **Knowledge** <term>Da'at</term>. It enters the belly to be established and spreads within.
The **Thighs** of the body are divided into two lights, and they are literally two lights.
The **Thighs** and the two **Kidneys** all hang from one place where all the abundance and "oil" of the body is gathered. There, all that abundance is funneled to the place called the **Foundation of the World** <term>Yesod</term>.
"Foundation" comes from that place called "World," "Nourishment," and the vision of **Victory** <term>Netzach</term> and **Splendor** <term>Hod</term>. Therefore, "And the Lord..." as His name is finished. Blessed be He and blessed be His name forever and ever. All these "Repairs" <term>Tikkunim/Arrangements</term> come to join as one until all the holy abundance flows from the **Living One** <note>The Sefirah of Yesod</note>, the Foundation and the Kindnesses, to the Female, and they are blessed by Him. I have seen [them] blessed by Him.

Come and see: at the hour when the judgments below are established <note>original: *dinim d'letata*</note>, and as judgments are established below, they are established above. All the rectifications of the King are in joy when they are within the holy circle, and everything is one; then He is upon them and within them, as it is written: 
> *God stands in the congregation of God; in the midst of the judges He judges.* <note>Psalms 82:1</note>
But when judgments are not established below, as it were, it is the same above; for all the rectifications do not appear as they should, because He withdraws from the children. Because of this, the Glory [is affected], for the Foundation <note>the sefirah of *Yesod*</note> does not rest within the Female <note>the sefirah of *Malkhut*</note>, and all the judgments are awakened, and the powerful serpent rules. As it were, the King’s rectifications are withdrawn from His judgment. Since this Female is not blessed, she is pressed like a mountain, and the powerful serpent rules—woe to the world whose judgments are thus awakened! 

Rabbi Eleazar said: All these rectifications are [written] without the letter *Nun*, so that one should not take it as a shame in the World to Come, now that these things have needed to be revealed. And it is written: 
> *And they shall know that I am the Lord.* <note>Ezekiel 6:7</note>
This is so that these words shall not be found lacking, and from here on, the words are hidden within you. Blessed is the portion of those in this world and in the World to Come, for until this point the Holy Stroke was crowned with these words among the children. 

Come and see: Rabbi Hanina said at the end, and I asked before Rabbi Simeon: "Behold, I have learned before the Master that she is Wisdom <note>*Chokhmah*</note>, and it is so, but why is she concealed?" He said to him: "Come and see, for it is written:

What is this river that goes out of Eden? This is Understanding <note>*Binah*</note>. And within that river, the lower assembly enters, for the river flows from all its sides and brings forth strength under the arm. In this manner, the letter *He* is for the Crown <note>*Keter*</note> which gave birth and brought forth this Son, and took him before her. For this reason, the *Yod* and the *He* sit to nurse him. Thus we have established in our Mishnah: this *He* was a *Dalet* from the lower part, and the Male was pregnant with her from one side, and she is called *He* for the hollow Crown, and she brought forth the *Vav*—that is the Son—who stands before her. Regarding this it is written: *And a river went out of Eden*—from there it goes out, and is it not *to water the garden*? To nurse him." 

I was holding his hand and I wept with a great weeping; my heart was certainly stirred in this world. There were three days that I ate nothing when [the vision] was closed off from me, for I was not worthy to see him or anything else. Yet with all this, one must be constantly attached to Him. For when the teaching is preserved for us, we see the forms that stand before Him. Happy are the righteous in this world and in the World to Come; regarding them it is written: 
> *Surely the righteous shall give thanks unto Your name; the upright shall dwell in Your presence.* <note>Psalms 140:14</note>

Thus will be fulfilled that which is written:

Lest it be "and in all that I have said to you be circumspect."

David spoke these verses through the Holy Spirit, and they must be looked into. "Hear, O My people"—as we have learned, the Torah calls to a person in many places and says "Hear, O My people," and all of it is for the benefit of the person, so that he may awaken to the commandments of the Torah. <meta>This page continues the discussion of the spiritual laws found in the Torah portion of Mishpatim (Laws), specifically focusing on the mystical significance of the Three Pilgrimage Festivals and the sanctity of the male assembly before God.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The remembrance of mercy is linked to "Freedom" <note>Aramaic: *Chiruta*; a mystical term for the Divine Mother or the world of Jubilee</note>, and one should labor in it as one who labors in the Holy Name. For we have learned: Freedom serves the Holy One, Blessed be He, and whoever labors in it is as if he labors in the Holy Name itself, because Freedom and the Name are entirely one Holy Name. It is the Supernal Name, the Name that includes all other names. And anyone who subtracts even one letter from it, it is as if he caused a blemish in the Holy Name.

Come and see: **"And the name of other gods you shall not mention"** <note>Exodus 23:13</note>. This means you shall not add to the concept of Freedom, nor subtract from it. Rabbi Hiyya said: "The name of other gods" refers to anyone who occupies themselves with "other books" <note>External or secular wisdoms</note> that do not originate from the side of Freedom. **"It shall not be heard upon your mouth"**—it is forbidden even to mention them or to learn a single reason from them, and certainly not to compare them to the Torah of Freedom.

Rabbi Yehuda taught: Why is it written, **"And the name of other gods [you shall not mention]"** and immediately followed by **"The Feast of Unleavened Bread you shall observe"**? It is because anyone who does not guard this festival is as if he does not guard the Faith of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Why? Because the word is written in connection to Freedom. Rabbi Isaac said: This applies to all other appointed times and festivals, for they are all grasped within the Supernal Holy Name.

And regarding this we learned, why is it written **"Three times a year"**? Because the Faith <note>The Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> depends upon them. **"All your males shall appear"**—to see [the Divine] and to be seen. Rabbi Eleazar said: "All your males" is meant literally, because the males are the blessing of the home. From here we learn that every son of Israel who is circumcised must appear before the Holy King, because he includes the blessing from the wings of all [the Sefirot]. This is what is written: "To the righteous, kindness is written for you." And it is written: **"Before the face of the Lord, HASHEM"** <note>Exodus 23:17; original: *Adon YHVH*</note>. This is like water to the thirsty, for from there blessings are poured out and blessings are received. And all of Israel are gathered from among all other nations.

Worthy is the portion of Israel, to be nourished by Him and to be mixed with Him in holiness. And He takes them to restore blessing to the world. Look, they sent to Rav Hamnuna the Elder; he said to them: "Have you seen the sign in the ancient valley?" They said to him: "We once saw that when the clouds gathered, all the paths were blocked by water and mist, and from within it, it was found that those who ascended there could not walk. Furthermore, at the hour they entered to appear [before God], even the heavens were found to be moved and joyful."

He said to them: "Surely, life lives within them! When they took this path to be revealed to them, they ascended as in the beginning. For no one was blessed at that hour except for those of Israel who were present. And upon that holiness, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gazes and blesses them."

Below, they called out as they ascended, and those who were mixed in as in the beginning, when they were finishing their offerings, they saw their cheeks turning red from the smoke of the altar. They decreed that all should be blessed, but those [outsiders] were not blessed. They went down and spoke to the Head of the Academy to have mercy on them. They asked: "What portion do you have in this? What sacrifice was yours?" It was not fitting. They checked and found their cheeks were pale, and they removed them. They said: "Blessed is the Merciful One who saved His people, for surely blessing only dwells within Israel and within the Holy Master, according to the Faith and according to the Truth." And a path was opened to bring blessing to the world as at the conclusion. They opened their mouths and said: **"Surely the righteous shall give thanks to Your name..."** <note>Psalms 140:14</note>.

Rabbi Hiyya said: In the merit of Israel, their enemies are humbled beneath them and they inherit their estate. Come and see what is written: **"All your males shall appear,"** and it is written immediately after: **"For I will cast out nations before you and enlarge your borders"** <note>Exodus 34:24</note>. He uproots the inhabitants from their dwellings and settles others in their place. And because of this, **"All your males shall appear before the face of the Lord, HASHEM."**

Rabbi Yehuda said: "They shall see," as it is written, "For the kindness of the Lord, HASHEM, is straightforward," and it is all one—uprooting inhabitants and settling inhabitants. Rabbi Isaac said: There is no separate portion, and they all hang as one. Rabbi Yehuda said: It is a change that has no equal, as in **"He strikes the edge of His paths"** <note>Job 26:14</note>, a cutting off.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Mishpatim. It focuses on the transition from the laws of the Sanctuary to the promise of the Divine Messenger (Angel) in Exodus 23:19-20, exploring the concept of spiritual union (Dveikut) through the metaphor of a kiss.</meta>

## Laws (Mishpatim)

->**Mishpatim**<-

That which is pressed, as much as it is pressed, it is written [another version: "it is a camel"]. Rabbi Yose says: "The gall of asps" <note>Job 20:14</note> is written as "bitterness." And what is the "gall of asps"? For everyone knows this and not that. The "gall of asps" is life; this has no end. The Name of the Lord is searched out according to its writing, and "life" is searched out according to its writing, and because of this, they are searched out in secret, and regarding this, "gall of asps" is written. Rabbi Yehuda said: Sometimes the higher realms are called by the name of the lower realms, and sometimes the lower realms are called by the name of the higher realms. He opened with the Name of the Lord in His high name, and we have established it; they remain and are like their treasures which are separated, yet all is one. Blessed be the Merciful One, blessed be His Name forever and to all eternity.

**Behold,** I send an angel before you, etc. <note>Exodus 23:20</note>. Rabbi Isaac opened: "Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth," etc. <note>Song of Songs 1:2</note>. The Community of Israel <term>Knesset Yisrael; the mystical personification of the Jewish people and the Shekhinah</term> said: "Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth." Why does it say "from the kisses" <note>original: *mi-neshikot*</note>? It should have said "Let him kiss me." However, we have learned: What are kisses? They are the cleaving <term>Dveikut; mystical attachment or union</term> of spirit to spirit. Because of this, a kiss is on the mouth, for the mouth is the source and wellspring of the spirit. Therefore, kisses are on the mouth in love, and spirit cleaves to spirit so that they do not separate from one another. Because of this, one whose soul departs in a "kiss" <note>The "Kiss of God," a peaceful death for the righteous</note>, the spirit is left with its Master and does not separate from Him; this is the secret of the kiss. And regarding this, the Community of Israel said: "Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth," to cleave spirit to spirit so that one shall not separate from the other. "For your love is better than wine"—what is the need for "wine" here? For it is written, "and your kiss like the best wine" <note>Song of Songs 7:10</note>, and it is written, "Do not drink wine or strong drink, you and your sons" <note>Leviticus 10:9</note>. Why is "wine" mentioned here? Rabbi Hiyya said: This refers to the wine of the Torah. Rabbi Hezekiah said: This is as it is written, "And wine gladdens the heart of man" <note>Psalms 104:15</note>. And regarding this, it is written, "For your love is better than wine," for the joy of all. From where do we know that this [the kiss] is greater than all? Rabbi Yehuda said: It is written, "And Jacob kissed Rachel and lifted up his voice and wept" <note>Genesis 29:11</note>. Why did he weep? It was found that this spirit could not bear [the intensity] and he wept. And if you say, it is written [of Esau], "and he kissed him and they wept" <note>Genesis 33:4</note>, and we learned: why did he weep? It was because the spirit did not cleave to him at all. Regarding this, it is written, "But the kisses of an enemy are deceitful" <note>Proverbs 27:6</note>. What is "the kisses of an enemy are deceitful" <note>original: *na'atarot*, often translated as "profuse" or "deceitful"</note>? Rather, one who kisses in love, his spirit cleaves to the other's spirit in the attachment of love. But one who does not kiss in love, it is not a cleaving at all, but rather "deceitful." What is "deceitful" <note>*na'atarot*</note>? It is a coarseness where that kiss does not cleave to his spirit and does not attach to him at all. Because of this, it is written, "Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth," for this is the cleaving of spirit to spirit. Come and see: when the Holy One, blessed be He, goes on the way, in this manner the spirit can cleave to the spirit. Regarding this, it is written, "But you who cleave to the Lord your God are all alive today" <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>—a cleaving where one does not separate from the other. When it was written, "Behold, I send an angel before you," Moses knew it was a separation. He said: "If Your presence does not go, do not bring us up from here" <note>Exodus 33:15</note>. Rabbi Abba said: What is written just before this? A secret at the end of the section: "The first of the fruits of your land you shall bring to the house of the Lord your God; you shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk" <note>Exodus 23:19</note>. What is this dealing with? It means not to mix the lower matter with the higher. And the male side <term>Sitra de-Dkhura</term> should not seek from the female side <term>Sitra de-Nukba</term>. What is the difference between this and that? This is the male from the side of the angels, and this is theirs from the holy side. Who is "his mother"? This is the Community of Israel, who is called "Mother." "In its mother's milk"—for strength from this side for one who does not need it. And afterward it is written: "Behold, I send an angel before you." Moses said: "Behold, in everything there is love from You, but what is this? If Your presence does not go, do not bring us up from here." And as they stood well... Rabbi Eleazar said: The Holy One, blessed be He, only said this word out of love for Israel and to be reconciled with them, like a king who wanted to go with his children and did not want to leave them. His son came and was reconciled...

## Main Text (Zohar)

And they should seek the Holy King as is fitting • to sanctify the King and to be light before Him. This is like a king who said to his son, "Behold, I send a messenger <note>original: "malakh" (angel/messenger)</note> before you to guard you." Afterward, he said, "Be mindful of him..." <note>The Zohar is comparing the warning in Exodus 23:20-21 to a father cautioning a son about a high-ranking escort.</note>
The son said, "If so, either let him stay here, or You come with me and do not separate from me." So <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kadosh Barukh Hu"</note> first said, >Behold, I send an angel before you to guard you on the way< (Exodus 23:20). And afterward, it says, "Be mindful of him..." When Moses became afraid, he said, >If Your presence does not go with us, do not bring us up from here< (Exodus 33:15). <term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> came and agreed with this in the assembly.
He said, "Eleazar my son, you have spoken well. But come and see: after this, Moses said nothing more and did not return a word to the Holy One, Blessed be He. What is the reason? Because the wise man did not agree to the spread of the covering <note>likely referring to the protective canopy or the veil of the Tabernacle</note>. And we have established this matter among the companions. Some teach it the opposite way, but the first explanation is the correct one."

And when all the words are intended well, they all say their reason in one word. When did Moses reply? Like that which is written, >And I will send an angel before you<; the matter is spread out, and regarding this, it is written here, >But if you truly obey his voice and do all that I speak< (Exodus 23:22). It specifically says "that *I* speak" <note>implying that even if an angel is the messenger, the voice must be recognized as the Divine "I"</note>. And it is written, "And I will remember My covenant," and "I will establish a covenant," and everything depends on Him.
Rabbi Judah said, "If you say that both refer to a literal angel, why is it written about them that he did not see the place?" When did he reply? As it is written, >If Your presence does not go...<
Rabbi Shimon said, "The rule of the matter is that Moses did not want an angel at all, as it is written, >Now therefore, I pray You, if I have found grace in Your sight, show me now Your way<."
Rabbi Judah said, "That which is written, >You shall not seethe a kid in its mother's milk< (Exodus 23:19), Rabbi Abba said: cooking milk makes it fit <note>referring to the chemical/spiritual change in the mixture</note>. What is the reason? If you say the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>The Shekhinah, the feminine Divine Presence</note> is the 'mother' on the side of the Angel, it is not so. For I have heard Rabbi Shimon say: The Assembly of Israel is the holy mother of Israel, for to Israel below it is written, >For the Lord's portion is His people<."

Rabbi Shimon said, "You have spoken well, and this is a beautiful point, for everything depends on the Son. Come and see: it was prepared for them above on this side. There are two: one to the right and one to the left. Because of this, from here to the right and from here to the left, and all of them are cut from this <term>Kindness</term> <note>The Sefirah of Chesed</note>, the holy vision. And they are weighed in this balance. At the time when this one does not suckle from the other side, and the Sanctuary is defiled, and the 'strong hair' <note>a metaphor for harsh judgments/external forces</note> surrounds to reveal itself, then the 'kid' <note>the forces of judgment</note> suckles from the mother's milk, and <term>Judgments</term> <note>The Sefirah of Gevurah/Din</note> are awakened.
Therefore, Israel brings the firstfruits. And at the time we nourish them, we must say and open with the blessing that seeks mercy to increase for Jacob and the holy branch, so as not to give them into the hand of 'that side' <note>the Sitra Achra/evil forces</note>, and that Israel should not be delivered to that side.
And regarding this, it is written, >The first of the firstfruits of your land... you shall not seethe a kid in its mother's milk<. So that 'that side' does not suckle from the mother's milk, for then the Sanctuary is not defiled and Judgments are not awakened. Therefore, all the holy seed cannot be ruled by that side or the King.
And anyone who comes from that side—they give place to those who are not needed. For the matter depends on action: the action below awakens the action above. <term>Meritorious are Israel</term> among the fierce nations, for their Master calls them His own, as it is written, >The Lord has chosen you to be a precious people unto Himself<. And it is written, >For you are a holy people to the Lord your God<—it is all one matter. And it is written, >You are children to the Lord your God<.
Come and see: at the time when Israel's deeds are not in order, what is written? >My people are like gleanings...< as we have established the words in the secret of the Book of King Solomon.
Furthermore, we find that anyone who eats this food <note>milk and meat together</note> to join them as one, whether at one time or in one meal: for forty days, that 'kid' <note>the demonic force</note> is sustained in its husks <note>klipot</note> against those above, and he is distanced from the Holy King."

<meta>This page continues the Zohar’s mystical commentary on the Torah portion *Mishpatim*. ## Laws (*Mishpatim*)

->**Mishpatim**<-

The holy ones draw near and study to involve themselves in the world so that they may be holy. If it were not for your intention, the Holy One would not be ready to invite a holy soul to fill what is lacking, as it is written: *And you shall sanctify yourselves, and you shall be holy...* <note>Leviticus 11:44</note>. One who comes to be defiled, they <note>the spiritual forces of impurity</note> defile him certainly. It is written: *And you shall be defiled by them* <note>Leviticus 11:43</note>, where the word is written without the letter *Aleph* <note>The Zohar notes that without the Aleph, the word "v’nitmetem" (and you shall be defiled) can be read as "v’nitamtem" (and you shall be dulled/blocked). Impurity blocks the heart.</note>, implying a total blockage of the heart, where there is no permission to be purified. This is more severe than other types of impurity that can be cleansed. Furthermore, such a person should fear evil visions, for in their eyes a great darkness grows and they can be harmed, because the **Image** <term>Tzelem: the spiritual aura or divine "form" that protects a human being</term> of the person departs from him.

Rabbi Yosef said: This refers to one who destroys a rooster or a chick and eats it <note>likely referring to eating limbs from a living creature or improper slaughter</note>. Rabbi Shimon said: If you lack [holiness], you give an opening to evil species. To you they say: Like a closed vineyard, stay closed; do not approach the vineyard. Certainly, if you lack this, the blemish is in you, just as a beast requires proper slaughter. And one who is repulsive is like a "shell" <term>Kliphah: an outer shell of evil or impurity that conceals holiness</term>; it is written: *And the land vomited out its inhabitants.* One who acts repulsively is like those who are foul, and it is written: *You shall not eat any abominable thing* <note>Deuteronomy 14:3</note>. This means anything that causes the soul to be consumed. You should eat only that which is pure... so as not to be defiled by their food.

Rabbi Elazar said: It is written: *But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king's meat...* <note>Daniel 1:8</note>. We have learned in the secret of the Mishnah that the food of that wicked man <note>Nebuchadnezzar</note> was like a snare for all, and it was mixed with impurity, unlike other foods. And Daniel, who guarded himself from all these heights, sat in the lions' den and was revealed in the **Image** of the Other <note>the Divine</note>, and he did not allow his body to take on a deficiency. Because of this, the lions recognized him and did not eat him. But the wicked [king] lost the "taste of royalty" and his dwelling was with the beasts of the field, for the **Image** was removed from him. From that day on, he did not appear as a human being to the animals. For every beast that comes to look at a man sees him in his **Image** and fears him; they all come and bow. Many times they hoped to build a wild kingdom, but his deeds were cut off, for it is written: *And they shall be like kings.* Because of this, they were all praised in him during that time.

Come and see what is written: *And at the end of ten days their countenances appeared fairer and fatter in flesh than all the children which did eat the portion of the king's meat* <note>Daniel 1:15</note>. Their countenances appeared better because the **Image** of the Other <note>the Divine</note> was not removed from them, while from the others it was removed. What caused this? Because they did not defile themselves with the laws of their food. Happy is the portion of Israel, as it is written: *And you shall be holy men unto Me* <note>Exodus 22:30</note>.

**And** unto Moses He said: *Come up unto the Lord...* <note>Exodus 24:1</note>. "And unto Moses He said"—who said it? This is the **Shekhinah** <term>The Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</term>. "Come up unto the Lord," as it is written: *And the rod of God in my hand.* And if you say he stood with them, it is because they were now "uncovered" <note>referring to the completion of the covenantal rite</note>, which they did not do when they left Egypt; for then they were circumcised but the *priah* <note>the uncovering of the corona during circumcision</note> was not performed. But here, they were uncovered and entered into the Covenant of Existence, as it is written: *There He made for them a statute and an ordinance* <note>Exodus 15:25</note>. And He placed the Throne like this holy sign that is revealed... established by the hand of Moses to maintain the path, as it is written: *And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people...* <note>Exodus 24:8</note>.

Rabbi Yitzhak said: What is the meaning of that which is written, *And they gave the blood and sprinkled it upon the altar*? It does not say "in" the altar, but specifically "upon" the altar. And the change was "from afar." What does "from afar" mean? As it is said elsewhere: *The Lord appeared from afar unto me* <note>Jeremiah 31:2</note>, and it is written: *And his sister stood afar off* <note>Exodus 2:4</note>. My teacher explained to me that the Moon <note>symbolizing the Shekhinah</note> stood in deficiency, but once Israel entered into the holy portion and cut the holy Covenant with the **Holy One, blessed be He**, [the light returned]. "And unto Moses He said: Come up unto the Lord"—what is the reason? The **Shekhinah** said to him to ascend above, for he was worthy, and Israel was joined as one in the radiance through your hand, which had not happened until now. What is written? *And Moses took half of the blood...* <note>Exodus 24:6</note>. He divided it into two: half of the blood he sprinkled on the people, and half of the blood he sprinkled on...

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Torah portion Terumah. It focuses on the structural correspondence between the spiritual realms, specifically how the "Upper World" (the hidden divine source) and the "Lower World" (our manifest reality) are bound together as a single unity.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Terumah (Offering)**<-

**For the Lord’s portion is His people** <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>; He turned to give the nations great rulers appointed over them, but He took Israel for His own portion. Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse: **Who is she that looks forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and awesome as an army with banners?** <note>Song of Songs 6:10</note> This matter refers to two worlds joined as one, and this is "world and world" <note>referring to the phrase 'from world to world' or 'forever and ever'</note>.
"Who" <note>Hebrew: *Mi*</note>—this we have established as the high level above the Foundation <term>Yesod: the sixth of the lower Sefirot, acting as a channel</term> that stands in the realm of questioning and inquiry, as it is written: **Who created these? Lift up your eyes on high and see: Who created these?** <note>Isaiah 40:26</note>. And "This" <note>Hebrew: *Zot*</note> is the level far below, the Lower World. And both are two worlds in a single vision, in a single bond as one. "Looking forth as the morning"—the two of them join together as one like the morning. When the dawn breaks, the light begins to shine, and afterwards it shines upon the moon; all the weight of the sun's light is within her, and afterwards the moon stands in her fullness. "Awesome"—powerful over all to wage war. For then the strength of the moon is empowered to produce hosts, and strength strikes from the Upper World through the "Perfect Isaac" <note>referring to the attribute of Gevurah/Strength</note> to join them as one. He joined them as one above, and joined them as one below. And from them emerged the twelve holy tribes, modeled after the pattern above. Jacob, who is "perfect," entered into two crowns—two worlds—as we have established. "Morning"—because he exerted himself in the law <note>original: *din*</note>, revealing ornaments above and below. He labored with weeping in two worlds... <note>The text here uses dense Aramaic metaphors regarding the separation from "strangers" or "enemies" to maintain the purity of the divine union</note>. And if you say Rachel was strong as a wall, it is certainly so, for the Lower World and all its boundaries are certainly intended to be like the pattern of the Upper World, to inherit the male principle... just as the "tradition of the scribes" <term>Kabbalistic reference to the oral transmission of wisdom</term> is for their children, so is the tradition of the scribes because there is a "Book" and a "Scribe," and their treasure is the essence of the Supernal Wisdom. Even Jacob did not sin against them... "Morning"—so too the world of those who cast enmity and cause separation, revealing the nakedness of all above and below. And this secret is that these "ornaments" are pushed away and flee in a single spirit. "Who" and "This" are called "Groom" <note>The union of the divine attributes</note> because they are in a joyful embrace and in a bond of will... one who reveals their nakedness has no portion in the World to Come and no portion in Faith. Come and see:
**For the Lord has chosen Jacob for Himself** <note>Psalm 135:4</note>. A supernal spirit from above, once he was perfected and called "Israel," then he took everything on all sides; he took from above and took from below and was perfected in all. Rabbi Shimon said: We have learned that when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He engraved engravings of Faith within the Primordial Purity for the sake of the worlds. He engraved above and He engraved below, and all was in a single spirit... the Holy Foundation that teaches through its unions above and below. And in this secret, we contemplate the worlds: the Upper World and the Lower World. The Upper World is contemplated through the spirit that possesses the "Upper Point"—the first point that emerged from the Hiddenness and burst forth from the Unknown. It cannot be known and is not known at all. The ascent of this spirit is from the Infinite <note>original: *Sof*</note>, and from within this Hiddenness, a light shines. One light, thin and hidden, containing everything within it—all lights and splendors. A hidden Groom strikes within it, yet does not strike. A Groom shines within it, yet does not shine. And then he brings forth a single light for the vision of the "Circle" <note>original: *Idra*</note> to play and delight in—a thin light hidden within that light. And that light pressed the Circle for the delight of the "Hundred" <note>or "measure"</note> that it might be established and perfected. Within it were hidden things that are not known, except to that thin light. When it ascended to delight the Circle in the refinement of light, there stood a light that emerged from within the thin light, possessing "Awe and Love" <note>original: *Dechilu u-Rechimu*</note> and great strength. This expanded and became a single world that shines to all worlds. A hidden world that is not known at all, and its "children" dwell in secrecy; all of them are camps and hosts and upper princes. And once he brought them forth and they were perfected as one, then he...

<meta>This page begins the portion of Terumah (Exodus 25:1). It continues the mystical exploration of the relationship between the upper and lower worlds, specifically focusing on the construction of the Tabernacle as a mirror of the divine realm.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

They are one union and they are the secret of the three, and this is to participate in that hidden world. And when they are unified, it is written: *For the Lord has chosen Jacob for Himself* <note>Psalms 135:4</note>. All is established from within the letters *Yah* <note>The first two letters of the Tetragrammaton, representing the upper hidden realms</note>, and then Israel is His treasure. He surrounds this world, for permission was not given to take it thus, except for His treasure—the place where it is written, *In the day He created* <note>Genesis 2:4</note>. And it is not that which is below, but rather it is like dew from above in the concealment of the clouds, to include them in the revealed world, as it is written: *And Jacob was...* **And they shall take for Me an offering.**

---

**And they shall take for Me an offering.** Rabbi Judah opened with the verse: *How great is Your goodness, which You have hidden for those who fear You; which You have wrought for those who trust in You in the sight of the sons of men* <note>Psalms 31:20</note>. This verse has already been established and discussed. However, we have established this secret: at the time when the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to create the world, the will arose before Him and He created the world from the highest level of that spirit of the upper world. It rose to the secret of the All, and the upper realm is called **"Who"** <note>original: *Mi* (מ"י). In Kabbalah, *Mi* represents the hidden, questioning aspect of the Divine Mother/Understanding</note>. The lower level of that spirit of the lower world is called **"What"** <note>original: *Mah* (מ"ה). *Mah* represents the revealed, physical world or the Shekhinah</note>. And we have learned: why is it called "What"? Because all the upper levels in their perfection are found here. And come and see, it is called "What." Even though the goodness of the hidden Cause is not revealed until it is revealed here—which is the place of the end of all levels, the end of the thought of all, standing in revelation—even though it is revealed more than anything, it stands in the question of "What?" What have you seen? What have you known? All are distant from any grasp. And because of this, *How great is Your goodness*—this is the Foundation of the world which is called "Great Good," as it is mentioned: *Good to the House of Israel*, because it stands as Great Good. The primordial light is called "Sweet Light," and it was hidden for the male and female as one. *Which You have hidden for those who fear You*—because the primordial light was shown only to be revealed and then hidden. *Which You have wrought*—this refers to the Mother of all, the Mother of all the world, the desire of longings and spirits. Through this spirit, the Holy One, blessed be He, made the desire of all the world, and with this spirit in His authority, *God created the heavens and the earth*. Through this spirit, the Tabernacle <term>Mishkan: the portable sanctuary in the desert</term> was made and prepared, for it was in the image of the upper world and in the image of the lower world. This is what is written: *And they shall take for Me an offering*—"For Me," "An offering," two levels joined as one.

---

**And they shall take for Me an offering, etc.** Rabbi Shimon, Rabbi Eleazar, Rabbi Abba, and Rabbi Yose were sitting one day under the trees in the valley of the Sea of Ginosar <note>The Sea of Galilee</note>. Rabbi Shimon saw how beautiful the shade of these trees was over them, and said: "We must crown this place with words of Torah." Rabbi Shimon opened and said: *King Solomon made himself a palanquin of the wood of Lebanon* <note>Song of Songs 3:9</note>. This verse we have already established and discussed. But this **palanquin** <term>Appirion: a covered litter or bridal carriage, here a metaphor for the Tabernacle or the Shekhinah</term> is the Palace below, which was made in the likeness of the Palace above. The Holy One, blessed be He, called it the Garden of Eden, which He planted for His pleasure and His desire to delight in it among those souls of the righteous who are there. All of them stand and are hinted at within it—those souls that have no body in this world, they all ascend and are crowned there, and they merit to see and delight in the upper delight called "The Pleasantness of the Lord" <note>Psalms 27:4</note>. And there they are filled with all the longings of the light of pure balsam. This balsam is the upper Palace, hidden, supreme, and concealed. This palanquin is the Palace below, which has no support <note>original: *Samakh* (סמך), which means "support" and is also the name of the letter S</note> until it is protected from within the upper Palace. And because of this, the letter *Samekh* (ס) is closed on all its sides, in the form of a closed circle. What is the difference between this and that? It is in the taste of concealment and for delight, in the likeness of the upper Point above; then it stands in the image of the closed letter *Samekh*, and it is prophesied within it to receive from above. And in the taste of the order, she sits as a fourth over the children below to nourish them; then she stands in the image of the letter *Samekh* resting within the four sides of the world, and for this reason, it is called a Palanquin.

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of Parashat Terumah, specifically focusing on the "Appiryon" (Palanquin) from the Song of Songs as a metaphor for the Divine Tabernacle and the structural blueprint of the universe. It links the "Trees of Lebanon" to the six days of Creation.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Terumah (Offering)**<-

The Palanquin <note>Hebrew: *Appiryon*; a bridal litter or canopy</note>, this is the Palanquin. And after the two who are established, the six rivers of pure-scented balsam <note>original: *afarsamona*</note> stand ready to receive all the spirits that come from within the sixty-four blessings. Sixty correspond to the sixty sides that emerge from the seal of the letter *Yod*. Ten <insert>princes</insert> correspond to the four sides of the branch, and all of them complete the brain <note>the higher consciousness or *Mocha*</note>. And the Lord <unclear>is there</unclear>. A spirit for the brain in the likeness of that which is above. And regarding this, this balsam and that balsam are the rivers that flow from this celestial balsam. Like the supernal sides that have no body, like these sparks, a light is formed that emerges from those rivers of pure balsam. They sing in this supernal manner, and like the sides that ascend and have no body like this world, they ascend and suckle from that light of the Palanquin. Then they give spirit from those measures to their crowns, which are filled like this world. And then, from that scent which is gathered there, all the wings <note>of the angels</note> are gathered... the blessing of the Lord is lacking. This scent is gathered there in that reception, and all stand in that flowing spring; these delight above and those delight below. **King Solomon made for himself** <note>Song of Songs 3:9</note>—he occupied himself with his own essence. And if you say, "Behold, these are spices for the righteous to delight in," yet you say "he made *for himself*"? It is certainly so! Because this Palanquin and all those spices for the righteous all stand to provide delight before the **Holy One, Blessed Be He**.

**King Solomon made himself a palanquin** — "King Solomon" refers to the King to whom peace <note>Hebrew: *Shalom*</note> belongs, which is the Supernal King <note>Binah or Tiferet</note>. It has been established that "The King" mentioned without qualification refers to the King Messiah; this is the world of the Male and this is the world of the Female. **Of the wood of Lebanon** — these are the planted trees that the **Holy One, Blessed Be He** uprooted and replanted in another place. These are called the Cedars of Lebanon. All the Cedars of Lebanon <note>minus sixty-nine</note> were built into this Palanquin, and this was perfected within that. "Of the wood of Lebanon"—these are the Days of Creation, for each and every day arranges within this Palanquin the **Arrangement** <note>original: *Siddura*</note> that is fitting for it.

The first **Arrangement** is from the side of the Right: the Primordial Light that was hidden, to flow down from the side of the Right. It entered this Palanquin by way of the Foundation <term>Yesod: the Sefirah of connection and procreation</term>, and he made a sign within it. Afterward, that Palanquin brought forth a single image in the likeness of this light, and this is the spirit of which it is written: **"Let there be light, and there was light"** <note>Genesis 1:3</note>. Since it said "Let there be light," which is written, and then "there was light," the verse did not need to write "and there was light" <note>as a repetition</note>. Rather, from that light, He brought forth another light for those below it, and this is the first day of those "Trees of Lebanon."

The second **Arrangement** is from the side of the Left: the spreading of the waters by means of the powerful fire, to flow down from the side of the Left. It entered this Palanquin and made a sign within it, and it divided between the waters on the right side and those waters on the left side. Afterward, that Palanquin brought forth a single image in its likeness, and this is the spirit of which it is written: **"Between the waters which were under the firmament and the waters which were above the firmament; and it was so"** <note>Genesis 1:7</note>. This is the second day of those "Trees of Lebanon."

The third **Arrangement** flows down from the Central side: a third day that makes peace in the world. From there, they were supported for all, and this made a support in this Palanquin. It brought forth "kind after its kind" and was able to work through its revelation, and there was <insert>light</insert> for those below it. All of these were gathered and went with many hosts, and the image was fixed there. It brought forth "kind" in that Palanquin in the exact same likeness. This is the third day, which was perfected from twenty sides of those "Trees of Lebanon."

The fourth **Arrangement** flows down to illuminate the light of the sun, to illuminate this Palanquin within its darkness. It entered it to illuminate, but did not make a support until the fifth day, when it brought forth into this Palanquin that support of the light that entered it on the fourth day. That Palanquin brought forth in that exact likeness that light from those "Trees of Lebanon."

The fifth **Arrangement** flows down as a single drawing out to the distance of the waters...

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the mystical significance of the Tabernacle offerings (Terumah). It transitions from the cosmic order of the six days of creation to the sanctity of the Sabbath, and then addresses the necessity of personal effort and "cost" in attaining holiness versus the "free" nature of impurity.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The light was established and the service was broken to bring forth that light from the dwelling of the day. His will acted as one who takes books <note>original: "sifrin" - likely referring to the heavenly records or emanations</note> of the sun and brings forth sparks and kinds according to their kind, to be seen in that very same manner. The day of the sun <note>Sunday/The first day</note> took more than all other days, and they all depend on it until the seventh day, which brings forth and sees the books of all that was within it. For it is written: *“Let the earth bring forth a living soul according to its kind...”* <note>Genesis 1:24</note>. And this "living soul" <note>Chayah</note> is the day that rules from the beginning until the Lebanon. **The sixth arrangement** is the "living soul" of the day, which is the restoration of all the books, and it has no restoration or outlet except through this living day. When this day comes to restore them, it sees the books with many spirits, many souls, and many beautiful worlds, appearing in their beauty to dwell in the King’s Palace. So too, it restored in beauty all the other days that existed previously, and they were restored in a single desire and a single will, a restoration of the above and the below as one. Then the vision of the books was strengthened with supernal holiness and was crowned with its crowns until it ascended in the ascent of the pure crown and was called by the High Name, the Holy Name of life: **Sabbath**. This is the rest of all desires, where all things cling together, both above and below as one. And then it is written: *“King Solomon made himself a sedan chair <note>Apalirion/Chariot</note> from the wood of Lebanon”* <note>Song of Songs 3:9</note>. Rabbi Shimon said: Worthy is the vision of these books, etc., all of them to dwell in the pure radiance of the Holy One, blessed be He. The Bride gathers all desires and I have improved and beautified my dwelling in this which stands to give us life and to gaze upon. And they do not dwell there except as the assembly of the Holy One, blessed be He, within those books, to give us life and to crown us with supernal crowns until the trees of those books are awakened to come upon us as a new assembly. Rabbi Shimon opened with relief and said:

->*“And they shall take for Me an offering (Terumah) from every man whose heart prompts him, you shall take My offering.”* <note>Exodus 25:2</note><-

"And they shall take for Me"—this is the life of the vision that one must strive for in a vessel and strive for it as the Holy One, blessed be He, requires them to strive for it in His image and as a resting place. However, it is necessary for a person to strive for it properly, according to his strength. And we have established this matter in several places: that a person must take that labor for the Holy One, blessed be He, entirely connected as in the Mishnah, etc. And if you say, behold it is written: *“Come, buy and eat; come, buy wine and milk without money and without price”* <note>Isaiah 55:1</note>, implying that this is a resting place and a labor without money or cost for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He? 

Rather, the labor of the Torah is for anyone who wishes, etc., according to the labor for the Holy One, blessed be He, to know Him—anyone who wishes may engage in it without any payment at all. But the labor that stands in the commandment <note>Mitzvah</note> is considered as a sacrifice for a resting place. And in their images we have learned that one should not [be found] in that deed at all without the Holy Spirit being found upon them, but rather it ascends like a flame. In the Book of Sorcerers <note>original: "Sifra de-Chartaya"</note> which was sent to King Solomon, it says: anyone who wishes to strive to be blessed by the **spirit of impurity** <term>Ruach Mesava: The "unclean spirit" or side of evil</term> and to subdue the "other spirit"—that deed which he must strive in, he must acquire it like a rising flame with all that is required of him, whether small or great. For the spirit of impurity is always found in rest and in emptiness, and it goes without price and is wise to draw them in and entices them to dwell with them with many enticements and many sorceries, in order to cheapen its dwelling with them. 

But the **Holy Spirit** <term>Ruach Kodsha: The Divine Presence or Shekhinah</term> is not so. Rather, it is like a rising flame, requiring great and vast effort, and the preparation of oneself, and the labor of one's arrangements, and the will of his heart and his mouth and his spirit, so that he may merit to have its dwelling with him. And with everything he gives from his choice, he should strive to buy and to praise. And if not, it immediately departs from him and distances itself from him, and he cannot merit it as he did at first. And regarding this it is written: *“And they shall take for Me an offering from every man.”* From he who is called "Man" <note>Ish</note>, who has overcome his [evil] inclination. For such a vision, to overcome his inclination, he is called by our Sages of blessed memory: *“whose heart prompts him.”* Take the staff of "whose heart prompts him." But—

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on Parashat Terumah (Exodus 25), specifically interpreting the "offering" not merely as a physical gift, but as the elevation of the human heart and the reclamation of spiritual sparks from the "Other Side."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Offering (Terumah)**<-

Through this, everything is awakened toward the Holy One, Blessed be He. **"To You, my heart has said"** (Psalms 27:8). **"The stirring of my heart"** (1 Samuel 1:7). **"And a good heart makes a cheerful heart"** (Proverbs 15:15). All of these verses refer to the Holy One, Blessed be He. And this is the meaning here of **"Whose heart makes him willing"** (Exodus 25:2). From here, they established "My offering," for there [in the heart] it is found and hidden in another place. And how do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires him and makes His dwelling within him? When we see that the will of that person is at one with the will of his heart—to pursue and to labor after Him with his heart, his soul, and his will. Certainly, then it is known that the Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</note> dwells within him. Then, one should seek to "acquire" that person with full silver <note>original: "kesef," meaning both money and "longing"</note> and to strive after him, to connect with him, and to learn from him. Of such a person, the ancients said: "And acquire for yourself a friend" (Mishnah Avot 1:6). One must acquire him with a "perfect tongue" <note>sincere speech</note> in order to merit the Shekhinah. <note>Eccl. 10:1 reference</note> For this reason, one must pursue the righteous and acquire them. Conversely, the righteous person must pursue the guilty and "acquire" them at a full price, so that he may turn them into righteous people, thereby subduing and humbling the "Other Side" <note>Sitra Achra; the forces of spiritual impurity</note> and removing the <term>Captivity</term> <note>original: "Kaftia," referring to the spiritual sparks held captive by evil</note> so that the Creator may be praised above them all. This is the praise through which the glory of the Holy One, Blessed be He, ascends more than any other praise; it is an ascent above all else. What is the reason? Because he caused the subduing of the Other Side and the ascent of the glory of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Regarding this, it is written of Phinehas: **"And he turned many away from iniquity"** (Malachi 2:6). And it is written: **"My covenant was with him"** (Malachi 2:5). Come and see: anyone who takes the hand of the guilty and strives with him to leave the evil path, he ascends through three ascents that no other man achieves. He causes the subduing of the Other Side, he causes the Holy One, Blessed be He, to be elevated in His glory, and he causes the whole world to be sustained in its existence, both above and below. Regarding this, it is written:
> **"My covenant was with him, of life and peace"** (Malachi 2:5)

And he merits to see children born to his children's children; he merits in this world and merits in the World to Come. All the masters of judgment cannot judge him in this world or the World to Come. He enters through thirteen gates, and there is no one to protest against him. Regarding this, it is written:
> **"His seed shall be mighty upon the earth; the generation of the upright shall be blessed. Wealth and riches shall be in his house, and his righteousness endures forever"** (Psalms 112:2-3).

And the secret of **"Unto the upright there arises light in the darkness..."** (Psalms 112:4). In the cycle of the world, there stand three sides of colors, and they burn within a lower flame; that flame emerges from the side of the south, which is the Right <note>The attribute of Mercy/Chesed</note>. And those colors are divided into three sides: one ascends above, one descends below, and one remains as an <term>Aspect</term> <note>original: "Gvanna," a color or spiritual hue</note>, and within it is like a vessel that purifies the color. The one that ascends above emerges, and those colors are a hue whiter than any other white. This is what is said in Ecclesiastes (10:1) regarding "folly"—it should be forgotten and not found, while that color stands above at the head of that "newness." And at the time when Israel enters the synagogue and offers their prayers, when they reach "The Redeemer of Israel" and join Redemption to Prayer <note>The practice of not interrupting between the blessing of Geulah and the start of the Amidah</note>, then that color ascends to the head of the "newness" and becomes a crown for it, to sustain it with fragrance and wine. Then the holy people are "wedded" <note>joined</note>, they who do good before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and this is the secret of **"And I have done that which is good in Your eyes"** (Isaiah 38:3). One joins Redemption to Prayer because at that moment when this color ascends to the head of that "newness," the "I Am" <note>Divine Name</note> is awakened to burn and connect with the "Eternal" in love and affection as one will. And all the "drops" are joined in one desire, strength within strength, and those below and all the righteous are illuminated and kindled, and they all stand in one union like that Righteous One <note>The Sefirah of Yesod</note> who is called "Good," as it is said: **"Say of the righteous, that he is good"** (Isaiah 3:10). This connects them all in one union. Then they are all in a state of desire, above and below, longing for the Will, and the matter stands like the affection of a wedding canopy. Once they reach "Grant Peace" <note>Sim Shalom, the final blessing of the Amidah</note>, then the conclusion is made, which is the Crown that bows...

## Terumah
### Page 129

Rather, it is necessary to double the coverings over the face, because at that time when they <note>the forces of judgment</note> are moved, every person must cover themselves before their Master and bow their face in shame before Him. One must include this bowing within that assistance of the "bowed ones," so that the heavenly assembly is included from above and below through bowings and spirits. Then, another hidden treasure from below is revealed and descends like a bird <note>original: "zippori"</note> that comes to the assembly; and in a mystery, a herald goes out and calls, saying: "Ascend and give witness to this! See the life of the one who merited bowings and merited to establish that knowledge of the Kingdom <term>Malchut: the tenth emanation representing the Divine Presence</term> upon his head, who is now below and above before the King and the Matronita <term>The Matronita: the feminine aspect of the Divine, the Shekhinah</term>, for the King and the Matronita rejoice over him."

Then two witnesses are prepared from those "eyes of the Lord that roam through all the world" <note>Reference to Zechariah 4:10: "The eyes of the Lord, they roam through all the earth"</note> and they stand behind the Curtain <term>Pargod: the celestial veil separating the Divine from the lower realms</term> and bear this witness, saying: "Behold, we testify concerning so-and-so, son of so-and-so, who shared his portion; for they waited and remembered him for good." This is the life of one who creates a "folding" <note>original: "kefna," likely referring to subduing the animalistic nature</note> below, a folding of the guilty ones who were troubled by the "Other Side" <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of evil or impurity</term>. Then the Holy One, Blessed be He, is honored with perfect joy.

At that hour, a certain appointee is prepared, whose name is remembered over the **images** <term>Dyokan: the spiritual archetype or "image" of a person</term> of the righteous, in the spirit of the movement of the letters that are called "in the spirit." They make it known in the crown of the movement that reaches the holy place. The Holy One, Blessed be He, gives a sign, and that appointee brings the image of that person who performed the "folding" of the scoffers, and stands it before the King and the Matronita. He sees and gazes upon it with favor and will, for at that hour they hand over that image to Him. For you have no righteous person in this world whose image is not engraved above under the hand of that appointee, and they deliver into his hand seventy keys to all the hidden treasures of the Matronita.

Then the King blesses that image with all the blessings with which He blessed Abraham when he performed the "folding" of his scoffers. The Holy One, Blessed be He, signals to the Matronita concerning him, and they crown that image and share portions with him. There shall be for us worlds because of them, which no other person merits except for those hidden treasures for the living who perform the "folding" of their scoffers. And from this study, they knew how much benefit and merit they cause for the righteous; and the meritorious among them would see their crowns and pursue them like a vision that pursues life.

A poor man merits the strength of possessions—how many good things, how many supreme hidden treasures! It is not like the life of one who merits through his own scoffers. What is the difference between this and that? If they see one who exerts himself after the poor man, it is a life of tranquility to search and study it to sustain it, and he merits because of it many good things for that world. But one who exerts himself after the guilty, his life is even more tranquil. He acts to guard the "Other Side" so that the "End of Days" <note>or "the latter end"</note> is subdued and does not rule. And he who removes it from its dominion causes the Holy One, Blessed be He, to be exalted upon His Throne of Glory. He causes the Holy One, Blessed be He, to ascend, and the "Other Side" departs and shares its portion.

Another color from below shall not be seen at the time when Israel takes up the **Sanctification** <term>Kedushah: the prayer "Holy, Holy, Holy"</term> of the order. Then a prophetic color emerges, because this is the holiness with which Israel sanctifies more than the supernal angels who proclaim holiness. And see, a hidden color shall not be seen at the time when Israel is sanctified, for behold, Israel stands upon this, and the angels open above them and act for them on high so that they shall not be prosecuted.

Then a herald goes out and says: "Higher and lower beings, come and see! See the life of the humble spirit, like white garments. See the life of one whose garments are all prepared to be covered in white garments." For we have learned that a person should strive to be humble in this world in white garments, for there is nothing as beautiful as the white of the World to Come. In this holiness, we need to be careful and not to swallow it like a force, so that the holiness may be sanctified in it clearly and with more bowing than those sanctifications said by the priestly angels of the worlds. The holiness that we sanctify on the Sabbath, wherein we find the King upon it—because of this danger, they suffice for us to enter within the gates of the Most High, and regarding this, this holiness...

## Main Text (Zohar)

...in the Holy Tongue <note>Hebrew</note>, and they rise up through our will to enter the upper gates, for they <note>the angels</note> assist them in their proper order. Because of this, they perform more sanctifications and enter the highest gates. And if you say that the matter is otherwise—that the high angels are holier than we are and they perform more sanctifications—it is because if they did not assist and help us in sanctification, they would not be able to be companions in holiness. Thus, the glory of the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>, is heard above and below as one. For this reason, they strive to gain companions among [mankind], so that the glory of the Holy One, Blessed be He, may rise above and below as one.

The sanctification <note>Kedushah</note> that is at the end [of the service] should be in Aramaic <note>original: "Targum"</note>, as we have established. This [Aramaic version] even an individual may say. These words of the Aramaic translation, unlike all words of the Holy Tongue used in sanctification, are only said in a quorum of ten <note>a Minyan</note>. This is because the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> joins itself with the Holy Tongue. In every sanctification where the Shekhinah comes, it must be among ten, as it is written: *And I will be sanctified in the midst of the children of Israel* <note>Leviticus 22:32</note>. "The children of Israel" refers to the Holy Tongue, and not to the other nations who have other languages.

And if you ask: if this gathered sanctification is in Aramaic, why is it not said by an individual? Come and see: this sanctification is not like the other sanctifications we have learned. Rather, this sanctification rises on all sides, above and below, and through all the sides of faith. It breaks iron locks and seals and evil husks <note>term: "Kelipot" — the spiritual shells or rinds that conceal divine light</note> so that the glory of the Holy One, Blessed be He, may rise above all. We must say it in the language of the "Other Side" <note>note: Aramaic was considered the language of the mundane or "backside" of holiness</note> to subdue the powerful strength of the "Other Side." [When we say] *May His great Name be blessed forever* <note>the central response of the Kaddish</note>, the strength of the Other Side is broken, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, rises in His glory over all. When the strength of the Other Side is broken by this sanctification, the Holy One, Blessed be He, rises in His glory and remembers His children and remembers His Name. And because the Holy One, Blessed be He, rises in His glory through this sanctification, it must only be in ten. All of this is done so that the Other Side is forced to be subdued and its strength broken. To raise the glory of the Holy One, Blessed be He, one must break the locks, seals, powerful ladders, and evil husks. Then the Holy One, Blessed be He, remembers His Name and His children. Worthy are the holy people to whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave the holy Torah, to merit through it the World to Come.

Come and see: regarding the Queen <note>note: the Matronita or Shekhinah</note>, they are worthy of the World to Come. Since these are words regarding the crown of the upper Kingdom, this Mother <note>the Shekhinah</note>, as it were, says: "It is fitting for you, O companions, in this world." May the speech of your mouths rise above in awe as you awaken these words. He opened and said:

-> **And this** is the offering which you shall take from them: gold, and silver, and brass. <note>Exodus 25:3</note> <-

This verse is established for the upper watch and for the lower watch. It belongs to the upper side in the realm of holiness, and it belongs to the lower side in the manner of the "Other." Come and see: when the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world, He surrounded it from the side of Samael <note>note: the primary figure of evil/prosecution in Jewish mysticism</note>... because that stool was from above. And as the work was found to be in his image, he surrounded it from the side of Samael and afterwards from the side of the Right <note>the side of Mercy</note>. Because it was found to be from the side of Samael, he surrounded it here from the side of Samael and afterwards from the side of the Right. "And this is the offering..." and it is written: *Evening, and morning, and at noon...* <note>Psalm 55:18</note>. This verse we have established... for there was no "Eden" yet... and from its surrounding they were awakened in these three times. "Evening" was the looking that does not shine. "Morning" was the looking that shines. "Noon" is the place called Kindness <note>Chesed</note>, but it is a place that stands between this and that. Woe to the time of exile, for the strength of the place called Kindness is seized by the "Evening," and they stand one with the other. And that which is said of "Noon," which is the strength of Samael, is found from above... and such is the way of a man...

# Terumah

## Main Text (Zohar)

They call it white, yet its greatness is removed from it like a spark; and sometimes they call the white "black," as it is written: *For darkness is like a cup of affliction.* <note>original: "כי חשך כוסית לקי" - a play on the word 'Keri' and darkness.</note> Is it not in this manner that the image of "Evening" comes? This is the "Exile of the Evening." And because in this evening, the **Other Side** <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of evil or impurity in Kabbalah</term> of darkness is mixed in and rules at night, it has authority, yet it has no fixed time. Donkeys and mules are found at this time, and from here are seen many **bands of destructive spirits** <term>Chavilei Tehirin: literally 'bands of noon-day demons,' here referring to harmful spiritual forces</term> who go out and rule in the night.

And if you say: If so, have we not learned that all those masters of the **Other Side** do not rule in the **Holy Land**? Yet here they are awakened! But in this place, they do not mix to dwell upon the **Holy Land**. Behold, at night, that smoke rises and does not rise, in the manner of the other sacrifice where the smoke would rise in a specific place. Here, that smoke would rise to every side of the **Northern Cavity**, for there are all the dwellings of the evil spirits.

And once that smoke rises and twists the path of that side, they all gather and stand in their places and do not go out to rule in the world. One appointee stands over that side, over that **Northern Cavity**, among all those bands of spirits; his name is **Sanigora** <note>A name implying a defense or a specific spiritual function within the dark realms</note>. The claim of that smoke twists his path, and this appointee rises and claims ten thousand camps for the paths; they are all prepared to receive it and to laugh at it. They stand in 그 cavity and enter through one gate called **Keri** <term>Keri: literally 'accidental' or 'chance,' referring to ritual impurity or nocturnal emission</term>, which is not a prohibition, as it is written: *And if you walk with Me in "Keri" (contrary/chance), then I will also walk with you in "Keri."* <note>Leviticus 26:21-24</note> This is the mystery that emerges from the gate of **Keri**, and these are the ones who roam at night.

And the claim of that smoke: they go out to ascend from below to above. These go out and prosecute them so they cannot ascend, except for those high, holy pious ones who are at the edges of the heavens; they return and ascend. And these bands of spirits go out and arm themselves with false words for human beings, appearing to them in the likeness of paths and mocking them until they return to their senses. They cast the matters of **Keri** because those who emerge from the gate of **Keri** cause it for them.

And at the time when donkeys and mules are found, that smoke would cast sustenance to them according to their honor; thus is their sustenance, whatever is fitting for them. And by this, they do not go out or roam in the **Holy Land**. "Evening" is a bride <note>A wordplay on 'Erev' (evening) and 'Kallah' (bride)</note>, and also a "Mixed Multitude" <note>Erev Rav</note> ascended there, for all those bands of spirits are mixed into the dominion of the night. For this reason, the "Exile of the Evening" was left as a resting place, for there is no set time that can strengthen itself against **Jacob**, for the image was found by the King and he prepared it as is fitting.

And because of this, this is the mystery of this exile: it is to protect us from the *terror by night* <note>Psalm 91:5</note>. From the terror of many sides, a fear takes hold; this is that claim that pursues to stand. For one, it stands for two.

And because of this, Israel hastens to say: *And He, being merciful...* <note>The "Ve-hu Rachum" prayer preceding the evening service</note> because of the fear that takes hold. And on the Sabbath, when the fear of judgment is not found, nor the judgment of the "Other," it is forbidden to mix it below, for there is no permission on the Sabbath to pass judgment from the world. And the fear of the prosecution of that smoke—all its anger is to ascend above to appear before its Master.

And therefore <note>original: בגין כך</note> we hasten to say: *Who guards His people Israel forever, Amen.* Just as there are many damagers and prosecutors found at night who have permission to harm one who goes out from the door of his house to the outside, so too <note>original: וכהאי גוונא כן</note> we hasten to say: *Guard our going out and our coming in.* And above all this, we entrust our bodies and souls to the Supernal Kingdom, which has dominion over everything. And for this reason, the "Exile of the Evening" occurs every single night. Now that sacrifices and altars are no longer found, we perform all the rectifications that we do for the spirit of the house at midnight, when the **North Wind** <note>The 'Ruach Tzafon' which awakens the heart to study</note> awakens with all those dwellings of evil spirits, and breaks one strong male [force], and enters and roams above and below. And all those bands...
