## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Terumah (Offering)**<-

Pure hidden ones <note>referring to angelic forces or celestial observers</note> enter their places, and their hosts are scattered and no longer rule. And then the Holy One, Blessed be He, enters to delight with the righteous in the Garden of Eden, as has been stated. All those rivers of light that fly and ascend are all gathered before the light of the Mother <term>Mother: The Sephirah of Binah, the source of divine understanding</term>, and then the **Morning** rules, and the dominion of the Evening passes away. And then this morning is the "First Morning" <note>The light of Chesed/Mercy associated with Abraham</note>. This morning is the inheritance of our beloved for all worlds. From here onwards, the upper and lower realms are established. This inheritance of the gardens is the beam <note>support structure</note> of the entire world.

Here is a <term>Secret</term> <note>original: "Raza"</note> for those who know measures: One who wishes to go out on a journey should gather his cloak and plant himself in his inheritance at the hour before the mountain <note>dawn</note>, and he shall see a likeness of what we have seen—that which strikes in the firmament, neither ascending nor descending. There are windows that are the gathering of what we have seen, through which the heavens and the earth were created. He who lives knows by the spirit of your life that they come to those spirits of holy purity for the forty-two letters <note>The mystical 42-letter Name of God</note>; and he should remember them as is fitting with the desire of his heart. Then he shall see within the radiance of the light of the firmament six *Yods*, three to the right side and three to the left side, and three *Vavs* that ascend and descend, and all of them are in the firmament; and you shall see the letters of the Priestly Blessing.

And then he shall reveal his prayer and go out on his way, and the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence</note> shall precede him, and all shall be his portion. All these belong to this morning, a single pillar like a beam that treads within the paths of the firmament... <note>The text here describes complex celestial imagery involving colors and pillars</note> it is not illuminated with the radiance of the three colors embroidered into purple. Like that pillar, a single branch stands, and by it three birds are awakened by the breath of praise. The first opened and said:
> Hallelujah! Praise, O servants of the Lord, praise the name of the Lord. <note>Psalms 113:1</note>
The second opened and said:
> Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth and forevermore. <note>Psalms 113:2</note>
The third opened and said:
> From the rising of the sun to its setting, the name of the Lord is to be praised. <note>Psalms 113:3</note>

Then a holy herald calls out a second time: "O high holy ones, those who slaughter <note>sacrifice their ego</note> for their Master, be prepared in the ranks of the day!" Then the day is separated from the night, and all those whose portion is the brain <note>wisdom</note> are found with the Torah, having labored in it at night at the time when the light breathes. It is written:
> The watchman said: "The morning comes, and also the night; if you will inquire, inquire; return, come." <note>Isaiah 21:12</note>
This verse contains wisdom regarding the exile of Israel who dwell among the children of Seir <note>Edom/Rome</note>. They weary the Master, the Holy One, Blessed be He, asking: "What will be of us in the exile which is like the night?" What is written? "The watchman said"—this is the Holy One, Blessed be He, who sees the morning already shining... I have given you the service so that you may merit eternal life... "and also the night," I have not abandoned you in exile as in former times. "If you will inquire, inquire"—all of you seek the morning of the Lord and call out, and there you will find how long the exile hangs over you... return in <term>Complete Repentance</term> <note>original: "Teshuvah Sheleimah"</note> and immediately "come" and draw near to Me. And the herald who stands and calls... <note>The text concludes with a dense mystical description of the "Spirit of Faith" and the "Voice" that sustains the world</note> ...the voice of the <term>Spirit of Faith</term> <note>original: "Ruach de-Meimanuta"</note>.

## Main Text (Zohar)

All of them are a consuming fire to them, and it is written: *And the sun rose upon him* <note>Genesis 32:31</note>, for the spirit of faith is thus. These are levels within levels; they are internal, consisting of the "husk" <term>Klipah: the outer shell or spiritual impurity that conceals holiness</term> and the "brain" <term>Mocha: the inner essence or light</term>. We have established this from what is written:
> And I looked, and behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it (Ezekiel 1:4).

This level is "a great cloud," that level is another. "And a fire infolding itself" is a third level. "And a brightness was about it" is a fourth level. And afterwards, "and out of the midst thereof as the color of amber <note>Hebrew: Chashmal</note>." And afterwards, "out of the midst thereof the likeness of four living creatures." These are levels within levels. So too here, when the Holy One, blessed be He, is revealed, He is revealed only from within these levels. From here we learn the mystery of the most hidden end. Afterwards, it was necessary to be revealed, and the place of "consuming fire" is another level that is more revealed—the "husk" that strikes against the "brain." And afterwards, "He shined forth from Mount Paran" <note>Deuteronomy 33:2</note>, which is another level. And afterwards, "He came with ten thousands of saints," which is the arrangement of all that is revealed from all these levels, from that place which is the root of all that is destined to be revealed from Him. From that place come the holy Chariots <term>Merkavot: the spiritual structures that carry the Divine Presence</term>, which are the high levels, up and up. So too here, "a consuming fire" comes from that level we mentioned that clings high above. **The watchman said: "The morning comes, and also the night"** (Isaiah 21:11-12). This "Watchman" is Metatron <note>The supreme angel and heavenly scribe</note>, the guardian of Israel, as it is written: "He who guards His months," and he is the mystery of the one who rules in the night. And "to the night"—what is the difference between this and that? Rather, all is one, but in this division the "Other Side" <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of evil or impurity</term> rules, and in this division it does not rule at all. "Night" <note>Hebrew: Layil</note> requires guarding, as it is written: **It is a night of watching** (Exodus 12:42), and it is missing the letter *He* <note>The Hebrew word for night is usually 'Laylah' (ending in He); here it is 'Layil'</note>. This refers to when the night goes on until it is divided. From the division of the night onwards, "Night" <note>Laylah</note> rules, as it is written: **And it came to pass at midnight** (Exodus 12:29), **that same night**. **And the night shines as the day** (Psalms 139:12), and so on. Thus: "The watchman said: The morning comes, and also the night."

The Watchman said: We found in the Book of Adam, what is the difference between "And he said" and "And he said"? One "And he said" is above, and one "And he said" is below. Rather, Metatron said it. What did he say? He said "Watchman"—this is Metatron below. **Morning**—this is the Morning Prayer <note>Shacharit</note>, which is the dominion of the day, that which rules over the night. And if you say that it comes alone and is separated from the Female <term>Nukva: the Shekhinah or Divine Feminine</term>, behold it is written: **and also the night**. Both are as one and are never separated from one another. And "Morning"—he calls to these people: "Behold, morning and also night are both ready for you." From now on, **if you will inquire, inquire**. If you seek your requests, seek them before the Holy King; seek and ask your requests and return to your Master. **Come** <note>Hebrew: Ateyu</note>—like one who is ready to receive you and have mercy upon you. So too, the Holy One, blessed be He, called "Morning and also night" and said "Come."

Happy is the holy people whose Master seeks them and calls them to bring them close to Him. Therefore, the holy people must gather in the synagogue. And whoever arrives first to join in the synagogue in one group—come and see: that first one <margin>Another version: who arrives</margin> who is found in the synagogue and waits in the synagogue, happy is his portion! For he stands in the level of the **Righteous One** <term>Tzadik: the Sefirah of Yesod</term> within the level of the **Divine Presence** <term>Shekhinah: the Sefirah of Malchut</term>. This is the mystery: "and you shall be found," for he rises in a supernal ascent. And if you say: "But have we not learned that at the time the Holy One, blessed be He, comes to the synagogue and does not find ten there, He is immediately angry?" Yet you say that this one individual who arrives first to join the synagogue stands in the level of the Righteous One? Rather, it is like a king who ordered all the townspeople to be found with him on such-and-such a day in such-and-such a place. While they were preparing themselves, one of the townspeople hurried to arrive first and went down to that place. When the king arrived and found that man had arrived there first, he said to him: "Where are the people of the town? Where are they?" He said to him: "My lord, they are coming after me, and I have come first to wait for the king's command." Then the king is pleased with him and sits there with him, and he is awakened with him to do the king's will. In the meantime...

## Terumah (The Offering)

->**Terumah**<-

And so it is that all the people come and the King is reconciled with them, and He arranges for them a place of dwelling. For all the inhabitants of the city, if they do not come, not one of them may draw near to speak before the King or to offer praise on their behalf, for they all come immediately in a state of anger and the King is provoked. So too here, since the Holy One, blessed be He, is One and is found in the Synagogue, and the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often depicted as the feminine aspect of God</note> comes and is found there, then everyone must gather and be found there. For He does not wait for them there; immediately the Shekhinah joins with Him and they sit as one, and He is known as the <term>Tzadik</term> <note>The Righteous One; specifically the Sefirah of Yesod which channels divine flow</note> and His dwelling is like the level of the Tzadik. And if He is the only One—the Holy One, blessed be He—and is found there alone, what is written? *“Why, when I came, was there no man?”* <note>Isaiah 50:2</note>. It does not say "there were not ten," but "there was no man," to be found in his place <unclear>as a support</unclear> for all the living beings of the world, to be at the level of the Tzadik. And not only that, but He is recognized as the Tzadik and includes within Himself life and rest; but if no one comes, as we have established, it is written:
> *“Who among you fears the Lord and obeys the voice of His servant...”* <note>Isaiah 50:10</note>
To be stirred like that which is written:
> *“One calls to me from Seir...”* <note>Isaiah 21:11</note>
For there is level after level; the level of the "Watchman" calls out with power <margin>from the heights</margin> and with ease, yet no one "obeys the voice of His servant." This "servant" is the **Matronita** <note>original: "Matronita"; the Divine Queen or Shekhinah in her royal aspect</note>. Therefore, happy is he whom the Holy One, blessed be He, finds in the Synagogue to rise to this high level we have mentioned. When he comes, he goes out and is recognized, and those found in the Synagogue must be found in <insert>orderly</insert> rows and arrangements. We have established that the order of prayer is to stir the love of the Above and the Below, to prepare the rectifications and to awaken joy. For because of this, the eyes are awakened to stir love and joy above among the living beings, the rows, and the arrangements.

But one who speaks <note>mundane talk</note> in the Synagogue causes a rift in the service. Woe to him, for he diminishes the faith! Woe to him, for he has no portion in the God of Israel, for he shows that there is no God and He is not found there, and he has no portion in Him and does not fear Him; he treats the supreme Rectification (others say: the supreme Power) of Above with contempt. For at the time when Israel arranges the order of the rows and arrangements and the order of prayer in the Synagogue, then three "Queens" <note>referring to groups of angels serving the Shekhinah</note> of the Kings gather over the **Matronita**. The first are those holy supreme angels who dwell and go out by day; for there are others who dwell opposite her by night, and others who dwell and go out and others in rows and arrangements according to the order of Israel by day. The second "Queen" consists of those holy angels who are found in every "Sanctification" <note>the Kedushah prayer</note> that Israel sanctifies below, and according to their authority, all those who are awakened in all those firmaments correspond to that prayer of Israel. The third "Queen" are those supreme authorities who are prepared with the **Matronita** and prepare her to bring her before the King; these are the supreme camps over all of them. And all of them are prepared through the order of Israel who prepare themselves below in living rows and arrangements and in the order of the prayer that Israel completes.

When these three "Queens" are ready, then Israel opens with song and speaks before their Master. And those of the **Matronita** who fear to be found <unclear>lacking</unclear> in their words by day, they prepare themselves over them and speak with them as one in the living praises of King David <note>The Psalms or Pesukei D'Zimra</note>, as we have established the matter. At the time when Israel finishes the living and arranged praises of David, then the praise is for the "Form of the Image" <note>the Divine Countenance</note> as we have established. And if you say: what is this praise for? It is for the second rectification after the praises of David. And take the Written Torah which was written and preceded the Oral Torah, and preceded the Synagogue, and preceded the Writings; and just as it preceded them, so it is necessary to bring it forward. However, since it is only rectified through the Written Torah, so it is necessary at the time of the rectification to take the supreme praise from all other praises in the world. And let it be that she is not rectified by all of them as much as she is rectified by this praise.

## Terumah

-> **Offering** <-

From the perfection of this <note>Zohar II, 132b</note>. And because of this, the vision is close to the revelation of the Altar, as we have established. At the time when the day is spoken of, the Assembly of Israel <note>The Shekhinah</note> is adorned with that crown which the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to place upon the King Messiah. That crown is engraved with holy names from the depths, just as it was adorned on that day when Israel crossed the sea and tasted the praise of all the chariots of Pharaoh and his horsemen. For this reason, the Priest <insert>the leader of prayer</insert> must set his will upon this Song <note>The Song of the Sea, Exodus 15</note>. Anyone who merits it in this world will merit to see the King Messiah in his preparations and with that crown; because of it, he merits and will merit to surround the joy of the song there.

We have established these matters: as soon as a person reaches the point of preparation, the Holy One, Blessed be He, takes that crown and places it before Him, and then the stench of your exile comes before the High King <note>meaning the suffering of exile is transformed or addressed through this mystical act</note>. It is necessary to include her <note>the Shekhinah</note> in the **Thirteen Attributes** of Mercy from which she is blessed. These are the thirteen supernal spices, all as one: *Saffron, calamus, and cinnamon* etc. <note>referring to the ingredients of the Incense/Ketoret</note>. And this is the secret for you: blessed is **His voice** <note>original: *kolo*, numerically 136</note>, and quickly strength and dominion. The Great Assembly. And Might. Praise. And Beauty. Holiness. Holy books. And to crown her with their crowns and to say "And the Kingdom," because the Vision <note>Shekhinah</note> is blessed by them.

On this account, it is necessary at the time of completion in their days to set one's heart and will upon this, and not to speak at all, nor to interrupt between them. If one interrupts between them, a gift that pushes the Cherubim aside, a single flame is cut off, and it calls out with power: "The wine of his neighbor!" If he interrupts, the descent of the Holy One, Blessed be He, changes and is cut off, so that they do not see the descent of the Holy King, the Bride. And all her month is the descent of the Lord, because these thirteen are the descent of the Lord. From all of them to the three of the completion etc. This is the High King of the world, to whom everything belongs, because all the elders of praises are toward Him, for everything is found in the Matronita <note>The Queen/Shekhinah</note> below. All is a secret of secrets, *Kindness to Solomon*, to the King of the world to whom it belongs.

From there onwards, it is more white, and all is Kindness, dealing in peace, and all is "the All" <note>Yesod</note>, and she is mixed into Him. And the sources are awakened, for such are the rectifications of the Upper World. <margin>Some versions read as follows:</margin> "Blessed God" <note>the start of the blessing before Shema</note> are the rectifications of the Lower World, which are the **22 letters** and the Watchers. For there are Great Letters and Small Letters. The Small Letters are from the Lower World. The Great Letters are from the source of the World to Come <note>Binah</note>. Like a bride, they are great. Their palate is great in itself. When they come, they will rejoice; their palate is great, for when they are not spread out further, their palate is small, each one according to the chariot that is fitting for it. As it is written of the Sabbath, that their palate is small: "God, the joy over all works." "Blessed and praised by the mouth of all that breathes." These letters are in the very essence of the words, for their palate hints at the gates of the World to Come.

The other two letters at the end, this is their palate in six and six words, which are the six sides of the World to Come, and they emerge from there, such as "Sabbath they give to Him, all the opposite of the heights." "Beauty and Greatness," *Trifos* and *Chofkis* <note>mystical angelic names or ciphers</note> and the Holy Living Creatures. These two letters are in six and six. The first two letters are in *mashi mashi* <note>a cipher/permutation</note>. All the circuits and the letters in the Mishnah are all four by four. And because their palate is in the spirit of the supernal chariot, you have the first letters and the palate at the end, the completion of the 22 letters. For there are 22 words corresponding to the 22 Supernal Letters. To complete the eighteen other letters that rise in their midst, four by four, to **seventy-two words**, which are the secret of the **Explicit Name**, the holy engraving of 72 letters with which the Holy One is crowned. And just as this Vision crowns the heart and rises in the spirit that is crowned by them within the ascent of the *Midcharis*. And the support of these letters that are crowned according to the supernal form: these are the first and the last that rise in their crowns for Him. *Pat* <note>cipher</note> instead of *mashi mashi*. *Tiz* in six. *Bayit* in *mashi mashi*. *Tin* in six. Because of this, the spirit that is in it is all 7, 17, 4, the Lord.

## Main Text (Zohar)

The totality of the **22 letters** <note>The standard Hebrew alphabet</note> are the crown of the "tags" <note>The decorative crowns found on letters in a Torah scroll</note> and the two paths. A sign for these is that they descend to the "lattices" <note>A reference to Song of Solomon 2:9, implying divine glimpses</note> and ascend in their chariots. They circle like a ship's pilot and a horseman, and all of them are the spirit of the **Holy Chariot**.
The secret of the **22** is the spirit of the holy circuit. The spirit of the **Holy Chariot** ascends above and descends below to be crowned from the side of the hidden dwelling, just as it is in the Supernal Chariot, as it is written: *As Your name, O God, so is Your praise* <note>Psalm 48:11</note>.
Because of this, they all circle about like a wind that blows here and there, swirling and fluttering. Through them, she <note>The Shekhinah</note> is crowned to become a holy circuit and a supernal spirit, like those upper pillars of the higher world that are below. This applies above and below. And until this supernal circuit exists, all its spirit is King David, who is crowned with this secret of the **42 letters**. His spirit is here and there, crowned in the supernal world.
And it shall sprout above just as it is below. Because of this, it ascends and does not descend, to be crowned within the supernal dwelling. All of this is the portion of one who knows it and the secret within it. The circuit of the **22 letters** is the generation that is crowned with this, and its spirit ascends and descends in the manner of **Mantzapakh** <note>The five Hebrew letters that have a different form when appearing at the end of a word: Mem, Nun, Tzadi, Pe, Kaf</note>.
The circuit of the **thirteen attributes of mercy** <note>The 13 modes of Divine compassion</note> are the twelve spirits of the **Holy Chariot** that emerge from the one who exerts effort over them. Because of this, they ascend and descend. All of them ascend and descend except for that which ascends and does not descend. The circuit of the **22** ascends and descends; it ascends from this side and descends from that side. The circuit of the **thirteen attributes** ascends from this side and descends from that side. The circuit of **28** <note>The number of letters in the first verse of Genesis</note> exists so that goodness may be found below.
Because of this, all the first letters ascend like a dwelling, and the other letters descend like a dwelling, so that goodness is found above and below. The circuit of **42** is crowned for the **Supernal Chariot**. The circuit of **72** <note>The 72-fold Name of God</note> is crowned for the **Lower Chariot**. Blessed is the portion of one who strives to know his Master, for everything will be his in this world and the world to come.
Therefore, the "Praise of Sabbath" <note>Psalm 92</note> praises the King who ascends in His glory. He is praised with the goodness of the **72** and with **22 words**, the spirit of the **22 letters**, so that she may be crowned by it to ascend on high like the praise of the Letter *He*.
Because of this, the praise of the world to come belongs to it, the spreading of the **Supernal Chariot** which is crowned to ascend on high, and the spreading of the **Assembly of Israel** <note>Knesset Yisrael/Shekhinah</note> which is crowned to ascend within the **Supernal Chariot**. They ascend and descend as has been said; they ascend and do not descend. This supports the Feast of Tabernacles (Sukkot) and the Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur). The spirit ascends higher and higher until the whole is crowned as far as the "End of Vision."
The word *Blessed* (*Barukh*) is the circuit of the letters and the mountains in their preparation, like a bride. Because these letters are "small," there is no space between them; they are the adornments of the maidens <note>the lower spiritual forces</note> of the letters with the **Matronit** <note>The Queen/Shekhinah</note> before the Holy Supernal King.
This is what the supernal angels sanctify in the "Unification" <note>The Kedushah prayer</note>. Every holiness that exists in the **Holy Tongue** <note>Hebrew</note> must be said alone <note>without translation</note>.
The **Targum** <note>Aramaic translation</note> is never used for the "Unification" <note>The core declaration of God's oneness</note>, nor for the "Sanctification" (Kedushah). The Unification is its own preparation and life, and they do not multiply it. The sign for this spirit is: "One portion of Scripture and one portion of **Targum**." The sum of the language of the many is far from the holy "Unification." For the **Holy Tongue**, it must be said as a Unification. The holiness of the **Targum** is said in the plural, not as a Unification, ever.
Regarding the **Targum**, we have learned: "One [person reads], and not two or more." The **Targum** comes to diminish, and so it is required. The **Holy Tongue** comes to increase, and so it is required, for "one elevates in holiness and does not lower it." But in **Targum**, one lowers and does not elevate. For one person we have learned, and no more, and they do not elevate at all. This holiness is the holiness through which the **Shekhinah** is sanctified, and all her chariots are strengthened toward the Supernal King. And because it is the holiness of the lower world, it is said while sitting and not while standing.

## Main Text (Zohar)

Another sanctification <note>The *Kedushah* prayer</note> from below: prayer is the sanctification of the upper world, and for this reason, it is performed while standing, so that it may be found below. All matters of the upper world are performed while standing and not while sitting. Despite all this, the sanctifications of Israel are sanctified through them below. Israel is sanctified by the sanctification said while sitting below, and by the sanctification that is higher, said while standing. 

Another sanctification is the "added sanctification" <note>The *Kedushah de-Sidra* or "Uva Le-Zion" prayer</note>; for this reason, it comes after the main prayer. Because it is an addition of holiness over other sanctifications, it follows the prayer service. And because every single person needs to find that addition upon themselves, the "Sanctification of the Translation" <note>The Aramaic *Targum* of Isaiah 6:3 and Ezekiel 3:12</note> was established for each individual. 

And if you say: "But it contains the sanctification in the Holy Tongue <note>Hebrew</note>?" That is for the inner aspect, to sanctify everyone collectively in that added holiness. But because an individual does not have permission to recite it <note>the communal Kedushah</note> in the Holy Tongue and be sanctified alone, they established it for him in the language of Translation <note>Aramaic</note>. It is set in its time so that every single person can be sanctified by that addition, to find extra holiness upon themselves. All these are the rectifications of Israel who are sanctified with upper sanctifications because they cleave to the One Above, as it is written:
> *But you who cleave to the Lord your God are all alive today.* (Deuteronomy 4:4)

**It is written:**
> *Behold now, I perceive that he is a holy man of God who passes by us continually.* (2 Kings 4:9)

And it is written:
> *Let us make, I pray you, a small walled upper chamber; and let us set for him there a bed, and a table, and a chair, and a lamp...* (2 Kings 4:10)

In this verse, we have a support for the world. "Behold now, I perceive"—this refers to the permission of a human being to speak of Her <note>the Shekhinah</note> by a nickname. "That he is a holy man of God"—this refers to the Upper World <note>Binah</note> which sits upon the Throne of Glory, and all sanctifications emerge from it, and it sanctifies all worlds. "Who passes by us continually"—from that holiness which sanctifies all worlds above, it also sanctifies us in this world. For there is no holiness above unless there is holiness below, as it is written:
> *And I shall be sanctified in the midst of the children of Israel.* (Leviticus 22:32)

And it follows: "Let us make, I pray you, a small walled upper chamber"—this is the dwelling place for the rectification of the *Shekhinah* <note>the Divine Presence</note>, who is the "upper chamber of the wall." All their statutes are "his face toward the wall."

"Small"—because She is small, as in "a small city" <note>Ecclesiastes 9:14</note>. And it is written "for him there"—in this rectification, for them we prepare our dwellings in the mountains, settlements, and exile. And in this rectification, they prepare for the Prophet <note>Elisha, representing the flow of prophecy/divinity</note> according to his intention: **a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp.** 

These four are all within the *Shekhinah*, and She is the Bride. All these rectifications are prepared for the Upper World in the dwelling place where they arrange the Evening Prayer (*Arvit*); in its rectification, it is the **Bed**. Like the dwelling of the sacrifices and burnt offerings which they arrange in the morning, which are the rows and preparations, it is the **Table**. And in that dwelling of the prayer said while sitting <note>the blessings of the Shema</note>, and in the rectification of that Unity <note>the Shema itself</note> which they prepare, it is the **Chair**. In that dwelling of the prayer said while standing <note>the Amidah</note>, and for those sanctifications and the added holiness and blessings which they arrange, it is the **Lamp**. 

And the whole is a blessing, for this was His will: to cleave to his Master every day and to be prepared before his Master with rectifications. Then, certainly, the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices and rejoices and rejoices—as it were—every day. And it is all in this world, and it is all in the World to Come. For these four are the rectifications of the *Shekhinah* to be prepared for Her Husband, like these four rectifications that are prepared in her beauty, her joy, and her adornment by the mouth of the holy people every day. 

The **Bed** was given to Jacob to be rectified, and until Jacob, for the rectification of the Evening Prayer. The **Table** was rectified by King David with those rows and provisions, for he rectified the Bride: "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies." The **Chair** was rectified by Abraham through his binding of kindness and peace, which are prepared for all people of the world; and there is no rectification of the Chair except through Kindness (*Hesed*), as it is written:
> *And a throne shall be established in kindness.* (Isaiah 16:5)

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Contribution (Terumah)**<-

He prepared and brought forth what was engraved, that which is hidden from the eyes of all worlds, and the light of the Supernal Assembly shone within this holiness. Because of this, the holy people must unify and direct their will to arrange the Supernal Altar, which is the dwelling of Understanding <note>Binah</note>, the thread of kindnesses below, and the table, the throne, and the lamp, so that they may draw from them every day above and below. At the time when Israel proclaims the Unity and the mystery of <term>Metatron</term> <note>The celestial prince or mediator</note> with a perfect will, then a single light emerges from the hiddenness of the upper world. This light strikes the wall of darkness and splits into seventy <note>original: ע'</note> lights, and these are seventy flames in the seventy branches of the **Tree of Life**. Then that Tree emits fragrances and spices, and all those branches of the Garden of Eden emit fragrances and praise their Master. For then the <term>Matronita</term> <note>The Divine Matron or Shekhinah, representing the feminine presence of God</note> is prepared to enter the bridal canopy with her Husband. All those supernal limbs are joined in one desire and one will to become one without any separation at all. And then her Husband is prepared to enter the bridal canopy with her in a single unity, to be unified with the Matronita, and concerning this, they awaken her and say:

> Hear, O Israel, prepare yourself, for your Husband comes to you in His finery, ready to receive you. **The Lord our God, the Lord is One.** <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note>

In one unity, in one will, without separation, for all those limbs are made one and enter into the secret of Unity. Once they say **The Lord is One** with the will of the six sides <note>The six emotional attributes or directions: Chesed through Yesod</note>, then all those six sides are made one. And the mystery of this is the letter *Vav* <note>numerical value 6</note>, a single extension by itself, all of it a cleaving, not to call out to Him but He alone extends from everything and He is One. At that moment, the Matronita is prepared and adorned, and they bring her in secretly and quietly to her Husband, and they say:

> Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.

This is said alone, for thus it is necessary to bring her to her Husband. Blessed is the people who know this and arrange the supernal arrangement of faith. At that moment when the Husband and Wife are joined as one, then a herald goes out from the side of the lower arm with words and gifts that reveal love toward your Master. Then a **Supernal Altar** is awakened, containing many gifts, and in its hand are four keys that include the kingship of the sides of the world. One key is marked with the letter **Y** <note>Yod</note>, another key is marked with the letter **H** <note>Heh</note>, another key is marked with the letter **V** <note>Vav</note>, and another key is marked with the letter **H** <note>Heh</note>. He placed them under the Tree of Life. Those three keys marked with these three letters were made one. Once they were made one, that last key <note>the final Heh</note> rises and stands and joins with that other one, the bride, and all those gifts and hosts enter those two keys within the Garden, and all are unified just as it is below. And this mystery is hinted at in the "Supernal Head" mentioned in the ancient books: **Our God** <note>Eloheinu</note> is the mystery hinted at by the letter *Heh* of the upper world, the hidden foundation in the holy book. And this mystery is the drawing down from below to the very bottom through the mystery of the letter *Dalet* <note>the final letter of 'Echad' (One)</note>, and those two letters are drawn out to be after this, and He is One. All these three are one in a single unity. Once all this is made one in a single unity and everything is joined in the mystery of the letter *Dalet*, the Master of the Spring rises and receives her innermost parts and the secrets of the heart and the Mother. Then they bring the Matronita in with this holiness; He opens and is filled with all supernal goodness and is able to nourish her and give her sustenance and provision as is fitting. And all His limbs are all one. Then they bring her to Him alone, to appear alone so that no stranger shall mingle in the holy congregation, as it is written:

> And a stranger shall not share in its joy. <note>Proverbs 14:10</note>

Just as He is unified above in six sides, so too she is unified below in six sides, to be called children of a single vessel.

## Main Text (Zohar)

One above and one below, all is the Lord and the Lord, "The Lord is One and His Name is One." One above in the six directions, as it is written <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note> **Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is One**. These six words correspond to the six directions <note>The six spatial dimensions: North, South, East, West, Up, and Down, representing the six sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</note>. One below in the six directions: <term>Blessed be the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever</term> <note>original: "Baruch Shem Kavod Malchuto L'olam Va'ed"</note>. These are another six directions in six words. The Lord is One above, and His Name is One below. And if you say, "Behold, it is written 'One' above, but below it is not written 'One' but rather 'Forever' <note>original: "Va'ed"</note>," the secret is that the letters of the speech do not change. The letters of the Female <note>The Shekhinah or Malchut</note> change. And this is the praise of the speech over the Female. And so that the "Evil Eye" shall not have power, the letters are changed, but they are seen as "One" in revelation. And in the time to come, the Evil Eye will be removed from the world and will have no power over her; then she will be called "One" in revelation. Because now, that <term>Other Side</term> <note>original: "Sitra Achra" — the realm of evil or impurity</note> is silenced with her, but it is not his. "One" is ours, but we unify her in a whisper, in the secret of other letters, and we say "Forever" <note>Va'ed</note>. But in the time to come, when that Side is separated from her and removed from her, then she will certainly be called "One," and there will be no partnership or other attachment with her. On that day <note>Zechariah 14:9</note> **the Lord shall be One and His Name One**—entirely, and not in a whisper, and not in the secret of "Forever." Therefore, we unify her from that Other Side many times. We see the need to unify like this at night so that the Other Side does not take charge of us, for the Other Side has no life in itself. And so that there should be no separation from that Side, when she comes, we bring her to the wedding canopy to her husband, the Upper King, with all the will and intention of the heart, until she becomes "One." At the time when there is life below in her world, and she seeks to separate from the Other Side below, she is seen covered in the glory of the King and no more. And thus the heralds go out to see the glory of the King. Then the Other Side has no power to see or to separate from her, all in joy and love. When the King ascends, they go out to see. When she comes, all those sides bring her to the canopy with the King in a whisper, in a secret, for if not, that Other Side would separate from her and mingle with her pain. For whenever that Other Side is separated from her, then "on that day the Lord shall be One and His Name One." When she enters the canopy and is with the King, then the joy of the union is awakened, and the Bride is bathed, and it is written <note>Deuteronomy 6:5</note> **And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, etc.** and "If you shall diligently hearken, etc." All of this is because the Other Side cannot approach there and has no permission. All of this is because they seek to bring her up to the King. To the support, it is necessary to speak in a whisper, in secret, so that no man is found near "Forever" <note>Va'ed</note>, to cast off the Evil Side so it does not cleave to her, and no blemish or defect shall be found at all. And thus Jacob said to his sons: "Perhaps there is a defect in my bed?" <note>Referring to the Midrash where Jacob worries his sons aren't fully committed to God</note>. They said: "Just as there is only One in your heart, so too we have no attachment to the Other Side at all, for your bed is pure." And they joined in the unification before the Upper King, having no attachment to the Other Side, for in the separation of the Other Side, our will is found. When he knew that the Other Side was not attached there at all, then she entered below to her husband in the whisper of the secret of the unification of the six directions. He opened and said: "Blessed be the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever," for she lives in the spirit of "One" in her world, without any confusion or partnership with the Other Side. Furthermore, see that at that hour, Jacob and his sons were like the Upper Image below with the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence</note>. Jacob took hold of the spirit of the six directions of the Upper World in one spirit. His sons were like the image of the six directions of the Lower World. And he desired to reveal to them that "End," as we have established that there is an "End" and a "Conclusion of the End." There is the <term>End of the Right</term> <note>original: "Ketz HaYamin" — the holy redemption</note> and there is the <term>End of Days</term> <note>original: "Ketz HaYamim" — often associated with the end of the physical world or the side of judgment</note>. The End of the Right is the spirit of the Kingdom that supports the End of Days.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on Parashat Terumah (Exodus 25:2). The text explores the unity between the upper and lower worlds through the concept of the "offering" (Terumah) and the devotion of the "Righteous One" (Tzadik).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Terumah<-

This conclusion is the spirit of kingship to the Master, the spirit of rain to the Master of research, the end of all flesh and the limit of the laws of wisdom. Since it is extended, the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the indwelling feminine presence of God</term> departs from him, etc. They are prepared for their Master, for there is no end to the Kindness <note>original: Chesed</note> to walk in the spirit of the upper world, and they are one. And the end of wisdom and therefore in the spirit of the lower world, it is one. And because they remembered two to honor: the spirit of the upper world, which is the heart <note>original: lev</note> of Jacob, and the spirit of the lower world, which is for all his children, then he brings her into his fellowship. And just as they are unified—the spirit of the upper world in one and the spirit of the lower world in one—so too must the upper be unified in one and the lower world be unified in the spirit of one. This covers the sides and that covers the sides. And because of this, there are words here in the spirit of the sides and words here in the spirit of the sides, and "The Lord is one and His name is one." Blessed is the worker and his portion, whoever sets his will <note>original: re'uta</note> to live in this world and in the world to come. Rav Hamnuna the Elder said: All the pleasures of song are good for them, and the spirit of speech from below, we have already established it. And these words are destined to be mixed before the Ancient of Days <term>Atik Yomin: an aspect of the Divine associated with ancient mercy</term> without any shame at all. He opened and said:

->**And they shall take** for Me an offering <note>Exodus 25:2</note>, etc. Here it says:<-
->Unity in one general whole<-

Above and below. It is not written "And they shall take an offering," but rather "And they shall take **for Me** an offering"—above and below in one general whole without any separation at all. The word "All" <note>original: Kol</note> is Kindness <note>Chesed</note>, and "whose heart prompts him, you shall take My offering." This verse <note>original: kra</note> should have said: "from every man whose heart prompts him." What is the meaning of the word "Every man"? Rather, it is the spirit of the Elder, those masters of judgment. Blessed are the righteous <note>original: tzadikaya</note> who know how to place their will toward the Holy Upper King. All their will is not toward this world and its vain desires, which they do not know; rather, they strive to direct their will and to cleave above, in order to draw their will through their thought to their prophecy from above to below. And whoever searches for that nullified will of their Master to be found for his prophecy, then the Holy Upper Master crowns him, from whom all holy wills emerge. And who is "Every man"? This is the Righteous One <term>Tzadik: the foundational soul that connects heaven and earth</term> who is called "All" <note>Kol</note>, and then "the profit of the earth is in all." Therefore, "all the precepts of all." It is so.

---

The Righteous One—this is "All." His words are as it is written: that his will is always toward the Matron <term>Matronita: the Divine Mother or Queen, synonymous with the Shekhinah</term> like a husband who loves his wife always. "Whose heart prompts him"—this refers to her, and "his heart" is his Matron, who prompts him to cleave to him. And they are in great love, such that they are never separated from the side of his love, as it is written of the Matron: "from him you shall take My offering." This is the Torah <note>original: d'Oraita</note> of the Most High; whoever desires it...

## Commentary (Ray'a Mehemna)

->**The Faithful Shepherd**<-

The commandment to study Torah every day, which is the spirit of the upper faith <note>original: meimanuta</note>, to know the mercies of the Holy One, Blessed be He. For anyone who strives in the Torah <term>Oraita: the mystical and legal body of Jewish law</term> merits this world and merits the world to come, and is saved from all evil accusers. Because the Torah is the spirit of faith, whoever engages in it engages in the upper faith. The Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> surrounds him within, so that she does not depart from him. Whoever knows a word of Torah and strives in it must pursue it and learn that word from Him to sustain it, as it is written:
> "From every man whose heart prompts him, you shall take My offering."

The Torah is a tree of life; that is to say, life for all who engage in the Torah, to be strengthened by the Torah. Then, "it is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it." And wisdom provides for them and sustains them. One who strives in the Torah merits to be bound to the Torah of above, which is this world, and this is remembered in the world to come. Even in the grave, his lips move with the Torah, as it is said:
> "Moving the lips of those who sleep" <note>Song of Songs 7:10</note>, etc.

## Main Text (Zohar)

When a person seeks to find [the Divine Presence] below, she is hidden and does not leave him. For all of them, even though all her love is toward Him and His love is toward her, they take her from Him to be among them from that supernal place where all love, below and above, dwells.

> **"You shall take My offering (Terumah)"** <note>Exodus 25:2</note>

Happy is the portion of Israel, and happy are all those who merit this.

**"And this** is the offering which you shall take from them" <note>Exodus 25:3</note>. Now, you might say: if so, it should have said "which you shall take from *you*"; what is the meaning of "from *them*" <note>original: *me-itam*</note>? It comes from two sides. Rabbi Yosef taught: From here it is said "from them" <note>*me-itam*</note>—from the letter **S** <note>Samekh</note>, which is the spirit of the Supernal Circle, the dwelling place of the Holy One, blessed be He, the Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds. From the letter **K** <note>Kaf</note>, from there all the worlds below receive life, and all of them find joy in her, a spirit for the wise below. For when they merit their portion, those who take her here can only do so as the Throne of the Husband and His footstool, performing the service of love toward Him; thus they merit His mercy [through the words] "you shall take My offering." And all of this is achieved through the service of prayer, the rectification, and the order that Israel arranges every day. **"From this"** <note>*me-zot*</note> refers to the inclusion of the six supernal sides, and all are one. "From them" refers to those merits and virtues, and all are a spirit of joy.

**"Gold, and silver, and copper; and blue, and purple, and scarlet wool; and fine linen, and goats' hair."**

**Gold:** This corresponds to the spirit of the day of Rosh Hashanah, which is a day of gold <note>representing *Gevurah* or Judgment</note>, and this smoke rises, included in the blowing [of the Shofar], and it becomes gold.

**And silver:** This is Yom Kippur, when the sins of Israel are made white like snow, as the pious ones make their garments white like snow, and regarding this whitening it is written:
> For on this day He will atone for you, to cleanse you <note>Leviticus 16:30</note>

**And copper:** These are the days of the sacrifices of the Festival <note>Sukkot</note>, which correspond to the chariots of the idolatrous nations <note>the 70 bulls offered for the 70 nations</note>, and they are called the spirit of the "mountains of copper." Because of this, their colors diminish every day.

**And blue (Tekhelet):** This is the end of the dominion of the spirit of faith, the spirit of the blue light. And because it is blue <note>associated with the word *tikhla*, meaning "end" or "destruction"</note>, it does not rule until the "speckled one" is removed, as it says:
> And the Lord will pass through to smite the Egyptians <note>Exodus 12:23</note>

For this reason, all colors are good in a dream except for blue.

**And purple (Argaman):** This is Shavuot, the spirit of the purple of the Torah, of which it is written that it is life; it is a crown included from all sides, from the right and from the left—all of it is from the right, this for "yes" and this for "no," and for the commandments.

**And scarlet wool:** This is the "living creature" <note>*Chayah*</note> which is the Crown, as it is written that Israel is covered in its protection... through the "worm" <note>the *tola'at* or scarlet</note>. Up to here are six times, and further on is the spirit of the days of Hanukkah.

**"And fine linen, and goats' hair, and rams' skins dyed red, and tachash skins, and acacia wood; oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the sweet incense; onyx stones, and stones to be set."**

Up to here are nine items, corresponding to the nine days [of repentance] until Yom Kippur, which is the tenth. And from all of these, we take the offering of the Lord at every specific time so that He may dwell upon us. Thus we take the offering of the Lord, and it is the spirit of the "Head" below from the side of gold. Like Yom Kippur, we take her, and she is the inheritance of Yom Kippur in the spirit. On Sukkot we take her, as it is written:
> On the eighth day you shall have a solemn assembly <note>Numbers 29:35</note>

And this is the offering of the Lord. On Passover, she is the "end," and this we have established as the spirit of the way of blue. On Shavuot we take her, as it is written:
> And God spoke all these words, saying <note>Exodus 20:1</note>

And we take from the Torah, as it is written, the "Oral Torah." Furthermore, everything is a holy standing for the daughters of Israel. "All that is found" is for the circuit of the Passover, and regarding "what they take from them" it is written: just as they are unified above, so here she is unified below in the spirit of "One" with them above, one corresponding to the other. Everything is above; He does not sit upon His Throne of Glory until she is made into the spirit of "One" in His likeness, to be "one within one." And this we have established: He is One and His Name is One. The spirit of the Sabbath is the Sabbath below, like the spirit of "One."

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Terumah (Offering)**<-

For kindness to rest upon it, the spirit of kindness. The soul of the Sabbath, in which there are three divisions: the precious holy throne, the herald of Oneness, and it is prepared for the High Holy King to rest upon it. When the Sabbath enters, she <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note> becomes unified and separates from the "Other Side" <note>Sitra Achra; the realm of evil or impurity</note>, and all judgments are removed from her. She remains in the unity of holy light and is adorned with many crowns for the Holy King. All the dominions of wrath and the masters of judgment all flee, and there is no other dominion in all the worlds. Thus, there is a supreme light, and she is crowned below by the holy people, and they are all crowned with new souls.

Then is the beginning of the prayer to bless her, like the light of a covering, and to say: **"Bless the Lord who is blessed."** **"The Lord"** <note>original: "Et Adonai"</note> specifically, in order to open the spring with blessing. And it is forbidden for the holy people to open the spring with a verse of "remembrance" <note>referring to verses of judgment or weekday petitions</note> such as: <note>Psalm 78:38</note> > And He, being merciful, etc. < because she has already separated from the spirit of the Other Side, and all the masters of judgment have separated and passed away from her. From here onward, what stands below is arranged below just as it is above.

And their holy blessing cannot be crowned with the crown of holiness as long as they awaken below the "remembrances" of the male <note>the weekday forces of judgment</note> that were mixed in. They all go to hide within the hole of the dust of the great abyss; they are all required to hide in their places so that the holy place of the "Mistress of the House" <note>The Shekhinah/Sabbath</note> may be engraved within them. And do not say that she is prepared alone, for there is no awakening above to be crowned until Israel awakens below, as we have established, for it is written: <note>Psalm 81:4</note> > At the hidden time, on the day of our feast <. It does not say "the day of the feast," but "the day of *our* feast."

Therefore, it is forbidden for the holy people, who are being crowned with holy crowns, to mention [judgment], lest they awaken the spirit of those "remembrances." Rather, all should be with great will and love, to awaken blessings above and below as one. **"Bless the Lord"**—**"The"** <note>original: "Et"</note> specifically, as we said, this is the Sabbath of the Sabbath eve. **"Blessed is the Lord who is blessed"**—this is the drawing forth of blessings from the Source of Life, the matter from which all watering issues forth to water everything. And because He is the Source, like a spirit that stands firm, we call Him "The Blessed One" <note>original: "Ha-Mevorakh"</note>; He is the male fountain. Once they reach there, behold, the Well <note>The Shekhinah</note> is certainly filled, and its waters never cease for eternity.

And for this reason, we do not say "Blessed are You, Lord, who is blessed," but rather **"Blessed is the Lord,"** for the fullness does not reach there [the lower realm] unless it is drawn from the supreme Source, for the Well is not filled at all [on its own]. And regarding this, **"The Blessed One"**—why is He "The Blessed One"? Because of the drawing and the kindness that increases forever and ever. **"Forever and ever"** <note>original: "Le-olam va-ed"</note>—this is the Sabbath of the Sabbath eve, and there the blessings are fixed in the place called "Blessed." Once they reach there, they are all **"forever and ever,"** which is **"Blessed is the Lord who is blessed."**

Up to this point, the blessings reach from the upper world, and they are all "forever and ever" to be blessed and watered, and to be complete as is fitting, with spirit from all sides. **"Blessed"** <note>original: "Barukh"</note>—this is the supreme Source from which all blessings issue. And the entire order below, we call it thus in relation to the lower ones, but "Blessed" is the supreme Source as we said. **"The Lord"** <note>the Tetragrammaton</note>—this is the center of all the upper sides. **"The Blessed One"**—this is the peace of the palace, the male fountain to complete and water everything. **"Forever and ever"**—this is the lower world <note>Malchut</note> which needs to be blessed. And from here, they continue to bless the Lord and the Blessed One; everything is "forever and ever." "Blessed" is the whole, like a small portion.

And for this reason, all the people are required to say this blessing, and on the eve of the Sabbath with the will of the heart and with joy, they must guard this crown to be blessed by it—the Sabbath that enters at night from the holy people as is fitting. Through this blessing, when Israel exerts themselves to bless, a voice goes through all the firmaments that are sanctified with the holiness of the Sabbath eve. And they say: "Fortunate are you, holy people, who bless and sanctify below, so that many upper levels may be blessed and sanctified above."

<meta>This page continues the kabbalistic exposition of the celestial mechanics and the divine union, specifically focusing on the mystical interpretation of Psalm 19. It bridges the concepts of the "Upper Chariot" and "Lower Chariot" with the biblical figures of Adam and Eve (Chavah) as archetypes for divine emanations.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The heavens shine upon that Glory <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note>, and this is the secret of what is written: *“Night unto night declares knowledge”* <note>Psalm 19:3</note>. His Chariot <term>Merkavah; the divine vehicle or structure</term> consists of the "body" and the "throne," and all of these are called "nights." Thus it is written: *“Even at night my kidneys instruct me”* <note>Psalm 16:7</note>.
The Upper Chariot is called "days," as in *“Day unto day”* <note>Psalm 19:3</note>. The Lower Chariot is called "nights," as in *“Night unto night.”* *“Declares knowledge”* <note>original: *Yechaveh Da'at*</note>—this means it reveals and gives life <note>A wordplay on *Yechaveh* (declares) and *Chayah* (living/life)</note>. It brings forth offspring like those heavens. And the Living One <note>The Divine</note> gives life, but not to their embrace and life. Come and see:
It is written: *“And the man called his wife’s name Eve [Chavah], because she was the mother of all living [Chai]”* <note>Genesis 3:20</note>. *Chavah* (Eve) and *Chai* (Living) arise as a single word. Because the letter *Yod* [י] was removed and the letter *Vav* [ו] entered, she became *Chavah*; and then there is righteousness and merit, for the *Yod* is *Chayah*—life for the living.
Regarding *Chavah* and *Chayah*, and the taking of life from the *Yod*, so too here: *“He declares”* [*Yechaveh*] means "He shall give life." *Knowledge* [*Da'at*] is the "Living One" [*Chayah*], the secret of the Heavens. Just as the Heavens have six sides <note>The six directions/Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</note>, so too this has six sides, like those offspring that emerge in its likeness. Therefore, *“Day unto day”* is included in the upper level. And it says *“Night unto night”* in the secret of the Masculine, which departs so that there shall be no "humming" of Knowledge. And because of this, it says the Upper Spirit is "Living" [*Chayah*] and not like these others. The verse is careful regarding it and says "Living" in the masculine sense, unlike other harsh things of the world. A light and bitter voice—the Upper Spirit is like the upper levels where there are no harsh or masculine sounds heard like other levels. These are the secret of Faith, which is a voice that is heard; but all these [upper ones] are never heard. This is what is written:
*“There is no speech, and there are no words; their voice is not heard. Their line goes out through all the earth”* <note>Psalm 19:4-5</note>. Loving-kindness and Strength <note>Chesed and Gevurah</note>, which are the hidden upper ones that are never known—from their movement and their drawing-forth, [the voice] is heard and made below. And because the voice is drawn forth, we do not have perfect Faith like in this world; yet all the inhabitants of the world speak of the secret of the Faith of the Holy One, blessed be He. All those levels are extended and were not hidden or concealed, and this is: *“And their words to the end of the world”* <note>Psalm 19:5</note>.
From the beginning of the world to the end of the world, those wise ones speak, and they are all like those hidden levels, even though they are not known. But just as they are recognized below, He engraved a Name like the structure of the Holy Body of the Living One; they find the kings, the holy upper levels, revealed in order. As it is written, all the rows and structures are drawn forth, and their establishment below is Faith for all the world. Whoever enters to bathe in the brain/oil <note>referring to the flow of divine wisdom</note> as it is written for all the levels. Because the oil/anointing and the voice look upon everything and take the Bride and the Living One, it departs through all those colors in order below. Therefore: *“And he is like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber”* <note>Psalm 19:6</note>, like the radiance and the establishment of all the hidden lights. For all of them, with desire and perfect will, give him their will and their brightness. Just as below, the Bride has no will or desire except to stand for him in the star and be established; therefore: *“He is like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber.”*
What is his "chamber" [*Chuppah*]? This is Eden; and this Spirit, and the river and the brook from Eden. Eden is the embrace from the mouth of the "Apple" <note>A kabbalistic metaphor for the divine countenance</note> upon the Bride. *“He rejoices as a strong man”* <note>Psalm 19:6</note>. He rejoices from the side of the initial White <note>Chesed/Mercy</note> where no judgment is found at all. *“As a strong man”* [*Gevurah*]—from the side of Strength. And even though Strength is perfect judgment, it is written "as a strong man" and not "a strong man," because the heat can strike, yet he takes the Bride in order, with desire and perfect will. Therefore: *“To run the course”* <note>Psalm 19:6</note>—the Bride supports his hand and strives to praise him in the masculine order in all sides, and to open in her a path to crown her below.
*“From the end of the heavens”* <note>Psalm 19:7</note>—from the edge of those Upper Heavens we mentioned, he goes out. Just as the longing of the living body goes out, in that place it is recognized between Masculine and Feminine. This is the secret of what is written: *“And from one end of the heavens to the other end of the heavens”* <note>Deuteronomy 4:32</note>. The "End of the Heavens" is the Upper World. "And from the end of the heavens" is the King of his world. As we said, he includes all lights and all are in him. So too here, the voice includes all lights and all are in him, and the vision goes out *“from the end of the heavens. And his circuit”* <note>Psalm 19:7</note>—which surrounds all those holy bodies that are below him.

## Main Text (Zohar)

The cows ascend <note>original: "parot olot"</note> and all is as it should be. These are the "cows" <note>A reference to the kine that carried the Ark in 1 Samuel 6, interpreted here as celestial powers</note> that are awakened by this praise, and they "went straight on the way." And what song did they sing to the Master? "Sing to the Lord a new song, for He has done wonders" <note>Psalm 98:1</note>. This spirit is modeled after the pattern above. At the hour when all the Living Beings <note>term: Chayot - the high-ranking angels that carry the Divine Throne</note> prepare the way for Him above, they sing this praise to the Master. And if you ask why it is written "His holy arm" <note>Psalm 98:1</note> and that this praise is always before Him? It is certainly because of "knowledge" <note>madda</note>, and it is only called "knowledge" when it is beneath the Moon <note>term: Shekhinah - the Divine Presence</note>, for whenever it is hidden from the Sun <note>term: Zeir Anpin - the masculine aspect of the Divine</note>, it is called "knowledge" and not a "new song." The "hiddenness of the right" and "His holy arm" refer to the awakening of the Right and the Left to receive Him. When they travel and ride, they find this praise; when they ascend to Beth-Shemesh <note>literally "House of the Sun"</note>, just as the wagons ascended to Beth-Shemesh, they all ascend in one spirit. Because of the covering of the throne, the throne ascends higher. The arrangement of this praise and these songs were all established for the Sabbath, to find the unique nation in the world.

---

**A Psalm,** a song for the Sabbath day <note>Psalm 92:1</note>. Adam the first man uttered this praise when he was driven out of the Garden of Eden; the lower world offered praise, as the companions have established. This praise is the lower world praising the King of the upper world, the day that is entirely Sabbath—the King whose peace <note>Shalom</note> belongs to Him. It does not say "A Psalm, a song" and it does not write who said it, as we have established. "For the Sabbath day"—this is the Upper Day, the Upper Sabbath. This is a Sabbath and that is a Sabbath; what is the difference between them? Rather, "Sabbath" mentioned plainly refers to the Eve of Sabbath <note>Friday night</note>, while "The Sabbath Day" refers to the Sabbath above. This is Day and that is Night. "The Children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath" <note>Exodus 31:16</note>—this is the Night, the spirit of the Canopy <note>the Sukkah/Shekhinah</note>. "Remember the Sabbath day" <note>Exodus 20:8</note>—this is the Day, the masculine aspect. For this reason, it is "A Psalm, a song for the Sabbath day." We find in many places that the lower world does not ascend by name but is mentioned plainly, such as here, and "And He called to Moses" <note>Leviticus 1:1</note>, and "He said to Moses, 'Come up to the Lord'" <note>Exodus 24:1</note>. In all these, the name is hidden and does not ascend. This is because it contains a high degree, and since it sprouts from a high degree, it does not ascend by name. Like the light of a lamp that does not rise as high as the light of the sun, and therefore the sun ascends by name. All these praises of the Sabbath are a praise higher than all other days.

---

**The Soul** of every living thing <note>term: Nishmat Kol Chai - a central prayer in the Sabbath morning liturgy</note>—the companions have awakened true words regarding this. But we must remember that this soul flies forth from that "Life of the Worlds" <note>term: Chai HaOlamim - a designation for the divine attribute of Yesod or Binah</note>. Because it is His, all blessings and creatures emerge through it, and He sustains and blesses below. The soul that emerges from Him is what moistens and blesses this place. Therefore, the hidden ones spread out from that "Life." Like the Eve of Sabbath, those souls which are actual blessings bless this place which is called "Name" <note>Shem</note> from below. And the place from which they emerge blesses it from above. Thus the "Name" receives blessings from below and from above and is included from all sides. On weekdays, she receives blessings from the Grace <note>Chesed</note> of the souls that bless her from below. On the Sabbath day, she receives blessings from those upper souls that bless her when they dwell [within]. And the middle weight is balanced, as we have established, in the spirit of "What" <note>term: Mah - representing the lower world/Malchut</note> and in the secret of "Who" <note>term: Mi - representing the upper world/Binah</note>. This is the Upper World and this is the Lower World. Therefore, "Who are these" <note>Isaiah 60:8</note>... and from before Him the praise of the "Other" ascends until fifty words <note>note: referring to the 50 Gates of Understanding</note>. Even though it does not stand there fully as a support, the darkness ascends until the spirit of "Who." From there, another praise ascends to find "What" from these words, the completion of all, and one chariot over that which is lacking, which is the completion.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Terumah (Offering)**<-

For the sake of the heights of unification. And corresponding to these, he engraved and established the staff of **Twenty-Five** <note>original: "Koh" (כה), the numerical value of 25</note> letters in the spirit that goes forth for unification, as it is written: **Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is One** <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note>. And these are twenty-five letters engraved and carved in the supernal spirit. And the essence sought to be established below in the spirit of unification, and it was established with **Twenty-Four** <note>24</note> letters in those words: **Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.** And it did not complete the count to twenty-five because the Tabernacle <note>Mishkan</note> was not yet established. Now, to establish the Tabernacle, there were found the eight kings <note>referring to the kings of Edom/shattered vessels</note>... when it was completed, it was not profane, but rather twenty-five letters to show that this was completed in the likeness of the supernal realm, as it is written: **And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying** <note>Exodus 6:10 and elsewhere</note>. And until this point <note>the word "Koh," meaning "thus" or 25</note> they are to show that the restoration of the Sanctuary is complete, and all these letters were established by those engraved letters that we learned from the Master. And because these eight creations were found, this is called "Koh" <note>25</note> in the unification that was completed to be found, and concerning it is written: "May He bless you," for "Koh" <note>25</note> is written as the spirit that completes the whole Tabernacle and its restoration. Twenty-five corresponding to twenty-five letters, in freedom and in longing, and they are written as one collective and one spirit. Regarding the flavor of Israel, the unification is discussed in the holy portion in the spirit of twenty-five letters, which are: *Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.* And these twenty-five letters are found, and each person should meditate upon them, that all those letters connect as one and rise in one union from the gates in the spirit... and then one must ascend even further into the hidden chambers. And then the gates are opened, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, considers that person as if he fulfilled the entire Torah, which comes in **Forty-Nine** <note>49</note> aspects <note>faces</note> in total. And for this, one must direct the heart and the will toward it, and to raise them up with the will of the heart to the forty-nine gates that we mentioned. Since they are found in this, one should meditate on this unification that the Master said, *Hear O Israel*, and they are found to be the entirety of the whole Torah. And in that emergence, they see that they should meditate on them, for certainly they are the whole of the Torah above and below. And this is the spirit of the "Complete Man," in male and female, and the spirit of all faith. The dispute of Shammai and Hillel <note>famous Talmudic sages</note> concerns the standing and the goodness, as it is written "in Your goodness and Your standing." For Shammai says [one should recite] in the evening [leaning], which is the inclusion of the **Female** <note>the Sefirah of Malchut/Kingship</note>... which is necessary regarding the Female... And in the morning when the **Male** <note>the Sefirah of Zeir Anpin</note> rules in the dominion of the world, one must stand before the Male, just as is required in the Standing Prayer <note>the Amidah</note> and in every place where the Male comes. But the House of Hillel said: If it were that the lower was alone and this was alone, it would be so required. But since we connect them as one and they ascend as one like a union in forty-nine aspects from forty-nine gates, we do not need to separate this one alone and that one alone, but rather everything is found to be one, all in a single compass. And just as his portion is Male, so is the day, for both are as one union as we have it, and so it must be shown. And for this, the Male is [represented] in nine words in the verse of *Hear O Israel* <note>counting the words in the mystical expansion</note> which are nine words, and the Female in nine words in "*Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever*" <note>abbreviated as Baruch Shem</note> which are another nine words, and they rise in one union in the spirit of the forty-nine gates. And the law follows the House of Hillel in every place. Rabbi Shimon raised his hands and blessed Rabbi Eleazar his son. He opened and said: **"Who has aroused [one] from the East"** etc. <note>Isaiah 41:2</note>. This verse we have established... the spirit of wisdom is "Who" <note>Mi</note>, the spirit of the upper world, for from there goes forth the illumination for the spirit of faith, as we have established. Furthermore, "Who" <note>Mi</note> is the most hidden of all hidden things, which is not known or revealed at all. The glory is hidden to be known from that place called "East," for from there is the beginning of every spirit of faith and light to shine. And after he examined (he said to them), the level of the horse... revealed the supernal **Strength** <note><term>Gevurah: the divine attribute of judgment and power</term></note> and the dominion of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and to move His dominion over all the worlds to lead them and to restore them as is fitting. And regarding this: **"He gives nations before him, and makes him rule over kings"**...

And behold, all those in the world exist under the authority of this **Justice** <note>Hebrew: *Tzedek*, a name for the Shekhinah or Divine Presence in her aspect of judgment and law</note>, and "He shall judge the world with justice" <note>Psalm 9:9</note>. And **Justice** stands constantly at his feet, never departing from there, calling out and never ceasing: "O God, do not be silent; do not hold Your peace, and do not be still, O God" <note>Psalm 83:2</note>. And now the verse is missing the letter *Lamed* <note>a grammatical/mystical observation on the word 'silent'</note>... and Rabbi Eleazar was reading by the supernal light and did not cease, for such is the portion of the righteous in this world and the world to come.

Rabbi Isaac opened the discourse and said: "A Psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah" <note>Psalm 63:1</note>. Why is this different from all other places of his poverty <note>or distress</note> where the text does not mention the specific place where King David dwelt? Why here does it say "when he was in the wilderness of Judah"? It is not for this reason alone, for we find similar instances as it is written: "when he changed his behavior before Abimelech," or "when the Ziphites came." All these are to show that all people of the world found David trembling <note>or fluttering</note> among the daughters <note>perhaps referring to his soul's yearning</note> while they pursued him. He would occupy himself with many songs and praises to the Holy One, Blessed be He. And David, even though they pursued him and he was in his youth, never ceased songs and praises from his mouth, to show his strength over all. Once David came, he found the "body" <note>the spiritual vessel</note> prepared as is fitting, and it rested upon him. And the end of the matter is like this world, to show the Master and King of all, because this world was prepared for the sake of the world above. For David was a man of peace, a man who prepared, a man of stature. And in this, David was not alone, but they are found forever. "When he was in the wilderness of Judah"—he did not forget David even though he was in his youth, and even though they pursued him. And what was "found"? It says he was found to be the "first of the first-fruits," and he found his own. What was it? He saw a dream. It says "dream" plainly. Once it says "dream," it shows a dream here of his own level—three levels: "Dream," "Dream," "Vision" <note>Aramaic: *Chalam, Chalom, Chata*</note>. And even though we see three, they are one level: a vision in the spirit, a living dream <note>Hebrew: *Chai*</note>, a dream from above. A dream that lives without interruption unto the end of the heavens—that is his level.

And the spirit is called "the Reckoner" <note>or "the Thoughtful"</note>. For there is a mirror that does not shine <note>Malchut</note> and a mirror that shines <note>Tiferet</note>. "My soul thirsts for You" <note>Psalm 63:2</note>—just as one who hungers to eat and also to drink... because he is in the wilderness, which is not a portion of clarity and not a place for the Holy... and because...
