## Main Text (Zohar)

And all this sustains the world for a single unified service of will. There is the joy of the second level and the sharpness like that of a seed that produces offspring and sowings; these are prepared and worthy for the restoration of the world in this exile, from which one does not emerge as from the [ordinary] world, yet it sustains everything. And upon this, the **Holy One, blessed be He** <note>Hebrew: *HaKadosh Baruch Hu*</note>, nourishes the world. In every place above, there is a light that shines; one [ray] emerges from it, prepared, then returns to be hidden, and is constantly ready for those above, like this voice and its hearing. There are times when one is made poor; what is written? "And not..." and every word here is not—God forbid—far from us, for the cloud dwelt upon it. What have we learned? There was one from that side of the first light that emerged in the joy of all, until it descended to the poor one below. And from that first time, which was not revealed to any appointed official, it is made heard in the world; and the work of His will and the purpose shall not be preceded at any time.

**Rabbi Yose** was traveling on the road, and **Rabbi Isaac** and **Rabbi Hezekiah** were with him. **Rabbi Isaac** said: Behold, we have learned that the work of the Tabernacle <note>The *Mishkan* described in the portion of Terumah</note> is like the work of Heaven and Earth. The companions have awakened to their secret and their beginning—that a person is unable to eat with his mouth, or put his hand into his mouth to swallow [spiritual wisdom without help]. **Rabbi Yose** said: These words ascended into the garden <note>The celestial Garden of Eden</note> as a holy, hidden longing; they prepared ornaments with restorations just as they were prepared for them by the **Holy Ancient One** <note>Aramaic: *Atika Kadisha*, referring to the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note>, the most hidden of all internal things. And they prepared ornaments such that there is no place to say of them, "to show the peoples" like a king. Furthermore, a person is able to eat and drink and delight himself as is fitting, until the meritorious of the world are crowned; and the purse shall be established, and he shall set it before them, "and they shall eat and leave over, according to the word of the Lord." <note>2 Kings 4:44</note> He opened [his discourse] and said:

> "And the Lord gave wisdom to Solomon, as He promised him; and there was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a covenant." <note>1 Kings 5:26</note>

This verse has been explained in many places, and the entire secret of the **Wisdom** <note>Aramaic: *Chokhmah*</note> from above is according to its vision and its judgment. We have learned: "Wisdom" is mentioned here like one who walks in self-nullification and gives in love, like a crown that was remembered for him—the peace of Wisdom like a crown—and it takes and is sweetened, this within that. "And there was peace between Hiram and Solomon"—because they knew one another, the hidden nature of the words they would say. And they wept, for like those in Hebron, they did not know how to look and to know all those below, before Solomon made it known in every word. King Solomon looked, and it was before him; for even in that generation, which was a time of peace more than all generations that were destroyed, it was not the King's will that Wisdom be so revealed, nor that the **Torah** <note>Aramaic: *Oraita*</note>, which was hidden as before, be known; yet he opened portals for it. And for the opening of these hidden things, it is only for those wise ones who walk and slumber in the houses [of study], and he opened his mouth with the secret of the Supernal.

All were astonished at the wise men of the generation—how they could leave off even for a single moment from toiling in the Torah. For as long as Rabbi Shimon exists in the world, all this Wisdom shall not be covered from the world. Woe to the generation when he shall depart, and the wise shall be diminished, and Wisdom shall be hidden from the world! **Rabbi Isaac** said: And they were spared, for this voice that he sighs travels with him in his portion. He opened his mouth with the Torah, and you might say a pillar of cloud [appeared] as if from above to below, and a bright spark within the pillar of food, for they were zealous for the meritorious food. > "And all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the door of the tent; and all the people rose up and worshipped, every man at his tent door." <note>Exodus 33:10</note>

And this is to find mercy like a faithful purse for all the inhabitants of the world. And the secret of this is what the generations acquired at Mount Sinai; and they were given like water within Wisdom, their might like an entrance and on the right. All is within them, for in this generation, the supreme merit of **Rabbi Shimon** works below, and thus [Wisdom] is established through him.

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Tabernacle's materials from the Zohar, Volume II, Parashat Terumah. It focuses on the symbolic meaning of the colors, specifically blue (Tekhelet), linking them to the second day of Creation and the balance between Mercy and Judgment.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

**And blue:** Rabbi Isaac said: Blue comes from the side of the "Female" <note>The Sefirah of Malchut, the Divine Presence</note> who draws nourishment from the portion of the "Male" <note>The Sefirah of Zeir Anpin</note>. This color was necessary for the work of the Tabernacle below. Regarding this color, he opened his discourse and said:
> "And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters."
<note>Genesis 1:6</note>
This firmament was created on the second day of the Work [of Creation]. It is not the same as the "Heavens" mentioned [on the first day]. On the second day, we learn that the Left Side <note>The side of Gevurah or Judgment</note> was created. From it emerged a flash, like an open shield of hidden fire. On that day, the color blue was found within it, which is the **Throne of Judgment** <note>original: "Koursaya de-Dina"</note>. This "sea" took the waters that were from the Right Side <note>The side of Chesed or Mercy</note>, but the waters from the Left Side were not revealed until the second day. On their own day, the waters were only revealed below because they were included in one another and gathered into one another.

He returned to the first day: the first light shone from every side, white and standing firm. It returned to the side of Mercy <note>Chesed</note>, as it is written: "And there was light." It then returned to the Left Side, which is the "Mercy of the Left" <note>a tempering of judgment</note> that comes from the Right Side and is included within it. On the first day, the Moon was strengthened by the Right, by the "Living Waters." This was not literally the work of water, but the work of Light, which comes from the side of Fire. This day is great, showing that the Holy One, blessed be He, established the world only upon Mercy, and everything follows that path. On the first day, everything He made was from the side of Mercy.

On the second day, acting through the power of the first day, He leveled the wall and planted within it all the pigments, like the work of a tapestry, to show that they are all included in one another. On the third day, it stood between the two of them, and within it was purple <note>Argaman</note> and so on, as it is written "that it was good" three times <note>referring to the double mention of "good" on the third day plus its completion of the previous days</note>.

This blue was found on the second day on the side of the colors red, black, and blue. Red belongs to our side from the second day itself, like the color of fire; this is purple. It is a single color. Blue emerges from that red color. When it descends below, the red color moves away from the place of burning, and the blue color takes on its nature. That redness enters the days and its color changes, turning into blue. This teaches that its Mercy is not as strong as it was at first.

Black: This color emerges from the intensity of the red when it opens and spreads below, as it is written: "and darkness was upon the face [of the deep]" <note>Genesis 1:2</note>. It emerges from that red color when its strength is unleashed. There is a powerful time below for the black, and all of it comes from that primary red below. All of this was created on the second day, and they rose and called it "the Throne."

This black is so deep a red that its [original] color is not visible due to its intensity. As the Holy Lamp <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> said: this black color is found below, but all the red pigment below is within the blue. The colors mixed below in the hidden images within the boundaries, and from within them were made mire and clay. From the right come mire and clay, and at the time when the mud of the depths emerges, that darkness—which is black—appears. Yet it is not truly black, but an intensified red. Thus: "and darkness was upon the face of the deep." They searched the depths of darkness because its color is dark, and it is hidden from the wisdom of created beings. This is the red and the black. For this reason, "that it was good" is not written regarding it <note>The second day of creation lacks the phrase "it was good" because Judgment/Division was created then</note>.

And if you say, "But it is written 'very good'?" <note>Genesis 1:31</note>. This refers to the Angel of Death. And why is the Angel of Death called "good"? It is better than the bad, because all the people of the world know they will die and return to the dust; therefore, they set aside their [sinful] lives and return in repentance to their Creator. If they did not hear the voice [of mortality], they would not fear to sin before Him. It is like a King who hangs a strap <note>for punishment</note> before them. Just as that strap is for the benefit of people to make them good and upright in their ways, so too "Death" is "very good." This is a great mystery...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the soul's journey, specifically focusing on the mystical garments it wears in different realms. It transitions from the general nature of life and death to the specific mechanics of the Garden of Eden as a prototype for the physical world.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The secret of the children of change <note>original: "b'nin d'cholofna," referring to the cycles of life and death</note> is like a holy species, and the "Good Priest" is the Angel of Life. The "Sickly One" is the Angel of Death, who brings distress and excess. And why does he change? When the **Holy One, blessed be He** <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> created the world, everything was established upon high, and there was kindness for life from the King of the world's life. Once they joined together, he became weak; He made him established in the truth of the light of kindness, wrapping this kindness and goodness. "But they sought out many schemes" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:29</note>; he made for himself an evil inclination, and subsequently sinned and was expelled from the **Garden of Eden**.

**The Garden of Eden** is in the likeness of the supernal pattern, a planting that the **Holy One, blessed be He** planted, as it is said: -> "And the **Lord God** planted a garden in Eden from the east" <- <note>Genesis 2:8</note>. And He planted it in peace, in the likeness of that which is above. All the supernal forms are embroidered and fashioned in this lower Garden of Eden. There, the Cherubim are found, engraved with the engravings of the "Children of the Throne." Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, [created] from the word of the Master, so all the sides above are engraved and fashioned in an embroidered likeness, the work of His hands. The portion of the Holy One, blessed be He, is all carved there; all the forms and images of this world are all fashioned there, engraved and carved there, all in the likeness of this world.

This place is the dwelling for holy spirits, both those who have come into this world and those who have not yet come into this world. All those destined to come into this world—all those spirits are clothed in **garments** <term>Levushin: mystical coverings or "bodies" that allow a soul to exist in a specific realm</term>, bodies, and countenances in the likeness of this world. There, they gaze upon the radiance of the glory of their Master until they descend to this world. At the time they depart from there to come to this world, those spirits strip off that body and garment from there, and clothe themselves in the body and garment of this world. They make their dwelling in this world in this garment and body, which is formed from a drop [of seed].

When the time arrives to depart and go out from this world, the soul does not leave until the **Angel of Death** comes and strips it of this bodily garment. Once this body is stripped from that spirit by the hand of that Angel of Death, the spirit goes and clothes itself in that body in the Garden of Eden which it had stripped off when it came to this world. There is no joy for the spirit except in that body which is there; it rejoices that it has been stripped of this body of this world and has clothed itself in another garment of peace, in the likeness of this world. In it, the spirit sits and sees, perceiving in its higher knowledge that which it could not know or perceive in this world while in this body.

When the **Soul** <term>Neshamah: the highest level of the human soul</term> is clothed in that garment of that world, how many delights and how many longings are hers there! What causes this body to be clothed by the spirit? It is the one who stripped those garments from it. The Holy One performs a kindness with His creatures, not to strip them of these garments until He has prepared for them precious and good garments in exchange.

As for the wicked of the world who did not return in **repentance** <term>Teshuvah: literally "returning" to God</term> to their Master: they came naked into this world, and naked they shall return there. Such a soul goes in shame among its companions, for it has no garment at all. It is judged in that **Hell** <term>Gehinnom: a place of spiritual purification or punishment</term> by that fire from above.

There are some among them who find rest and ascend. These are the wicked of the world who intended to return in repentance and died before they could complete it. These suffer there in Hell, but afterward, they find rest and ascend. See how great is the mercy of the Holy One toward His creatures! Even if one is a great sinner, if he chose repentance but could not complete it before death, the Holy One accepts the potential action. Because he departed without repentance, but had the will to do so, the King's wisdom does not pass over him. The Holy One prepares for that soul a place of remembrance, a dwelling of rest, and there the good is stirred up. For that will is before the Holy One; He breaks all the types of gates of the dwellings of Hell until he reaches that place where that "altar" is, and He stirs up that original will...

<summary>This page explains that the soul possesses a celestial "garment" in the Garden of Eden which it sheds upon birth and regains after death. It also discusses the fate of the wicked, noting that even an unfulfilled sincere intent to repent can eventually trigger divine mercy in the afterlife.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of spiritual purification and the consequences of human desire. It transitions into a detailed description of the structure of Gehinnom (Purgatory) and the specific fate of those who neglect the sanctity of the Sabbath.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Terumah**<-
<note>The title of this Torah portion means "Contribution" or "Heave-offering."</note>

At that opening, one exits from the dwelling of the **spleen** <note>In Kabbalistic anatomy, the spleen is often associated with the "Mixed Multitude" and the source of melancholy or dark impulses.</note>, and there is no good will found before the Holy King at such times. All who live and harbor sinful thoughts are drawn toward another side; for even if one cannot fulfill the act, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> considers the bad intention as if the deed were done. This applies to all evil desires, except for the worship of <term>idolatry</term> <note>original: "Avodah Zarah"</note>, regarding which the companions have established that those who did not contemplate repentance as they should are ruled by the spleen. These souls descend, and concerning them it is written: 
> As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away, so he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no more. (Job 7:9)

But regarding the former ones, it is written: 
> The Lord killeth, and maketh alive; He bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up. (1 Samuel 2:6)

Rabbi Judah said: In the place where they pass through Gehinnom, those who are destined to dwell there are shown why they are being judged by the fire of Gehinnom. In this Gehinnom, there is a furnace that burns day and night, just as the physical body is heated by the fire of the <term>Evil Inclination</term> <note>original: "Yetzer HaRa"</note> to act against the words of the Torah. With every "hammer blow" and heat by which they were inflamed by the fire of the <term>Evil Inclination</term>, so too burns the fire of Gehinnom. And what fuels it? The <term>Evil Inclination</term> itself in this world, which acts like a bellows of iron. When that <term>spirit</term> <note>original: "Ruach"</note> departs, all that time the furnace of Gehinnom burns, yet it is never fully consumed. 

The <term>Evil Inclination</term> returns to its place, and the eyes of the world seek to be warmed by it; thus they surround the furnace of Gehinnom to be burned. For behold, Gehinnom only burns through the heat and strength of the <term>Evil Inclination</term> of the wicked. And in that heat of Gehinnom, it burns day and night and never cools. There are seven gates to Gehinnom and seven dwellings there. Seven times they are called by names: <term>Evil</term>, <term>Worthless (Belial)</term>, <term>Sinner</term>, <term>Wicked</term>, <term>Destroyer</term>, <term>To Him</term>, and <term>Haughty</term>. Corresponding to each of these, there are dwellings in Gehinnom, each one as is fitting for it. According to the level of the sin one committed, so is the standing and the dwelling in that assembly. 

In every single dwelling, there is an appointed angel over that place, and under the hand of <term>Dumah</term> <note>The angel of silence who has charge over the souls of the departed</note> are many thousands and tens of thousands who judge the guilty, each one as is fitting for him in the dwelling where he resides. However, the fire of Gehinnom reaches down from the fire of the Gehinnom above, and it reaches this side below to burn through the awakening of the heat of the wicked who heated themselves through the <term>Evil Inclination</term>. 

All those dwellings burn there. There is a place in Gehinnom and levels there called the "Trembling Serpent," and there is the filth of those who are drunken, who are covered in all the filth of this world. They are covered and they ascend, and that filth is left there. Those evil levels called by these names all tremble and melt over that filth. All of Gehinnom rules over that filth that is left behind. 

There are the guilty who are constantly covered in stains and were never cleansed of them, dying without repentance. They are below, and the "hammers" embrace them; they were stiff-necked and never broke themselves before their King in this world. These are judged there in that filth and by that Trembling Serpent, and they never leave there—those who cast their venom upon others and did not care for the honor of their Master in this world. All of these are judged there for generations upon generations. They do not even leave on <term>Sabbaths and Festivals</term> <note>original: "Shabbatai u-Moadei"</note>. In many other places, the furnace burns and they are not purified, but they do not leave from there, for they bear a permanent brand. 

All those who desecrated Sabbaths and appointed times and did not care for the honor of their Master at all—because He protects them—but instead desecrated it publicly; just as they did not observe the Sabbaths and times in this world, so they have no rest in that world. Rabbi Yose said: Do not say so, but rather they *do* observe the Sabbaths and times there in Gehinnom, just like all those who flee. Rabbi Judah said: These are the ones who were not commanded, yet because they did not keep the Sabbath in this world, they keep it there against their will every Sabbath day when the time arrives...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the mystical secrets of the Sabbath and the afterlife from the Zohar, Parashat Terumah. It focuses on the respite granted to souls in Gehenna during the Sabbath and the specific judgments faced by the body and soul after death.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

They go through all those dwellings of Gehenna <note>The place of spiritual purification or punishment</note>; the judgments of the Unified One ascend, for the Holy King comes to be unified with His Bride <note>The Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note>, and the day is sanctified. Grace and kindness rest upon everyone, and immediately the judgments are removed, and the guilty find rest. But all those who spoke idly on Sabbaths and times of atonement, who turned away and ascended from their paths—to every side of Gehenna, the fire is never extinguished from upon them. All those who dwell in Gehenna surround them from the outside; these are the ones who have no rest among all the guilty here. They are the "slippery ones of the male" <note>referring to specific types of spiritual transgressions</note> who return to them. These are the guilty who denied the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kadosh Baruch Hu"</note>, and acted against the entire Torah because they did not keep the Sabbath. Therefore, they have no rest forever. All those guilty ones go out from their places, and permission is given to look and see them.

And one [angel] whose name is *Spetira* <note>A punishing angel mentioned in Zoharic literature</note> comes and takes that body of theirs and brings it into Gehenna before the eyes of the guilty, showing them that tomorrow it will be food for worms. He joins it to the end of the circuit of Gehenna, and all those guilty ones there tremble at that body and proclaim over it: "This is so-and-so, the denier, who did not have pity on the honor of his Master; he denied the Holy One, Blessed be He, and denied the entire Torah. Woe to him! It would have been better for him had he not been created and had not come to this weapon and this shame." This is what is written:
> And they shall go forth and look upon the carcasses of the men who have rebelled against Me; for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorrence unto all flesh. <note>Isaiah 66:24</note>

"For their worm shall not die"—this refers to the body; "and their fire shall not be quenched"—this refers to the soul <note>original: "Neshama"</note>. "And they shall be an abhorrence unto all flesh"—they shall be a stench until all the guilty of Gehenna who are there shall say, "Keep this distant one away!"

Rabbi Yose said: It is certainly so. Because they removed themselves from the entire Torah, and the Torah is "Life" <note>The Hebrew word for life, Chai, has the numerical value of 18</note>, because they transgressed the eighteen [principles] of the Torah, this is the "Life" <note>the 18 levels</note> of Gehenna that burns and is not extinguished from them forever.

Rabbi Yehuda said: After the Sabbath departs, that angel comes and returns that body to its grave, and both are judged—this one in its place and that one in its place. All this occurs while the body still exists, for once the body is consumed, all these judgments are silenced, and "He will not stir up all His wrath" <note>Psalm 78:38</note> is written of him. All the guilty of the world, as long as the body is whole in all its parts in the grave, the body and spirit are judged as one, a judgment as is fitting for it. Once the body is consumed, the judgment of the spirit is silenced. Some require further atonement, and some require their matter to be "ashes and dust under the feet of the righteous" <note>Malachi 3:21</note>; to each and every one, it is done as is fitting for him.

Therefore, how good it is for the meritorious, for the righteous! For as soon as they die, their body is attached to the earth and is silenced within its dust in a short time, so that they do not remain in that state for a long time while the body and spirit are found together every day. For you have no righteous person in the world who does not face the Judgment of the Grave <note>term: Din ha-Kever; the initial spiritual adjustment after burial</note>, because that angel appointed over the graves stands over the body and judges it every single day. If it is so for the righteous, how much more so for the guilty! As long as the body exists and is not consumed in the dust, the judgment is not silenced from it.

Except for those pious ones of the world whose lives were seen to ascend to their dwellings in their likeness to that high place which they saw. And they are the "living" in the world. All those who die in the world [outside the Land], except for those who die in the Holy Land <note>The Land of Israel</note>—all of them die by the hand of the appointed angel, who is the Angel of Death. But all those who die in the Holy Land do not die by his hand, but rather by the hand of the King <note>God</note> who yearns for them in an instant.

Rabbi Yitzhak said: If so, what is the difference for Moses and Aaron, of whom it is written "by the mouth of the Lord" <note>Numbers 33:38, Deuteronomy 34:5</note>, implying they did not die by the hand of that impure angel? Yet you say that everyone who dies in the Land of Israel does not die by his hand? He said to him...

It also explains the "Judgment of the Grave" and asserts that while most die via the Angel of Death, those in the Holy Land die through a direct act of God.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the sanctity of the Land of Israel, specifically focusing on the metaphysical mechanics of death and the unique status of the city of Luz.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Terumah (Offering)** <-

To Him it is certainly so, and the praise of the lower world is to be established and elevated more than all the people of the world who die outside of the Holy Land <note>Eretz Yisrael</note>, for there they are lacking and diminished. Outside of the Holy Land, death prevails, and all die by the hand of that "king" <note>the Angel of Death</note>, except for those who are below and diminished, who do not die except by the hand of the Holy One, Blessed be He. For all those who die in the Holy Land do not die through that "king," since even the Holy Land does not stand under any other authority, but under the authority of the Holy One, Blessed be He, alone. And because of this, it is written: *Your dead shall live, my corpses shall arise; awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust...* <note>Isaiah 26:19</note>. "Your dead shall live" refers to those who die in the Holy Land, for they are His dead and not the "king's," as the <term>Other Side</term> <note>Sitra Achra; the realm of evil/impurity</note> does not rule there at all; therefore it is written "Your dead." "My corpses shall arise" refers to those who died in another, foreign land by the hand of that "king," and therefore they are not called by the same name, for everything there is defiled, just as those who die outside the Holy Land are defiled. And regarding all of them, every release <note>Shemitah</note> is disqualified because life from the Other Side ceases in it, and as soon as it is disqualified, the Other Side rules over it. And because it belongs to him and he is cast upon it, they are not called by the same name. And this spirit is in every place, and everything is with him, and in every place where he is cast, they are not called by the same name, for he is only cast in the place of his command. And regarding a child who is disqualified, he belongs to him and is called by his name. Because of this, those who die outside the Holy Land—their soul dies to the "other" and the Other Side is cast upon them, and they are not called by the same name. "Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust"—"dwellers" implies those who are sleeping and not dead. These are the ones who died in the Land, for they are not dead, but merely sleeping. And it is written of them that their bodies remain, just as we have learned that the "living beast" <note>Chayah</note> stands within it for the other. So too, the four pairs in Hebron <note>the Patriarchs and Matriarchs in the Cave of Machpelah</note> are sleeping and not dead, and they all remain in their existence within those bodies of theirs, and they know hidden secrets more than all other people. Because they were there within the entrance of the Garden <note>of Eden</note>, those bodies of theirs are the "dwellers of the dust." Therefore, all those whose souls departed in the Holy Land did not depart by the hand of that "king," and he does not rule there; rather, it is by the hand of the King of Mercy, for the Holy Land stands in its own worth.

There is one place in the inhabited world where that "king" <note>the Angel of Death</note> has no dominion, and no permission has been given to him there. All who dwell there do not die until they go outside the city. And there is no person among all who dwell there who does not eventually die, but they all die outside of it, for they cannot remain there forever; some go out and some enter, and therefore they all die eventually, but that destroying angel has no dominion there. If you say that it does not stand under His authority—behold, the Holy Land does not stand under any other authority, yet people die there. In <term>Luz</term> <note>A legendary city mentioned in the Talmud (Sotah 46b) where the Angel of Death has no power</note>, the place of Luz, they do not die. If you say it is because it is not a place of total holiness and the praise of the Land of Israel—and if you say it is because of that man who built it, how many people had merits greater than his? Rabbi Isaac said: Here it is not found, nor is the wisdom. They went and asked Rabbi Shimon. He said to them: Certainly, the Angel of Death has no dominion over that place, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not desire that a person should ever die in that place. And if you say that before it was built, people died in that spot—it is not so; rather, from the day the world was created, that place was prepared for endurance. And the spirit of the spirit is here for those who look into the root of wisdom. When the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world, He created it with a spirit of life to circulate into living beings. And now the world is in the bodies of the holy blindness to circulate into living beings, and they brought the world down into its body. When the world circulated and expanded and was created, and they became living beings, afterwards the kindness of the Holy One, Blessed be He, was completed according to the law, and it remained below, suspended in that place.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the construction of the Sanctuary (Mishkan) and the spiritual significance of the Hebrew alphabet. It specifically focuses on the letter Tet (ט) and the appointment of Bezalel.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

They hang in the white <note>referring to the white light or the "white" of the parchment/supernal realms</note> because the Holy One, blessed be He, took hold of it, in whom no [imperfection] is found. And the letter *Tet* (ט) was exchanged; all those hang in the white until that point of merit. The *Tet* stands for them; therefore, whoever sees a *Tet* in their dream, it is a good sign for them <note>A traditional Talmudic teaching (Berakhot 59b) because the word "Tov" (Good) begins with Tet</note> and things are set right for them. And because it was hanging until that place, death does not rule over it. When the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to establish the world, He cast a fire into the brain <note>or "innermost essence"</note> and it was enveloped within it. All the letters circled to stand, and the fire circled them, and a place was found to be established. Then, when the Holy Land [was formed], the waters were going around it until that fire reached beneath the **Altar**, and there it was submerged, and the whole world was established. And if you say: if so, that in that place waters dwell, why were they not extinguished? Because the Sanctuary was to stand, life was to be doubled. Rather, here in this place, it is established because of this one [force] that spreads over it. In the Sanctuary, all of them go within it, and here life alone was created, in the likeness of all the worlds. Furthermore, the Holy Land gives life and atonement to be subdued in that world; but this place is not so—it gives life to that place in this world and in the world to come. And because the Sanctuary is bowed from there, it is because there is a teaching to discipline in this world and not in the world to come. Therefore, the Sanctuary stands to atone for sins and to merit them for the decree of the world to come. Come and see: the Priests who live in every place, and when the verse opens with "that it was good," as it is written:
> **And God saw that it was good** <note>Genesis 1:4 and others</note>
They opened and fled from here. It did not stand, it fled, even though permission was not settled for it there. This letter is mentioned under the 135 [levels]; it is not settled at all in its place in the world, and the tongue is joined to it as one. The letter *Tet* is settled in every place and was prepared to be settled as is fitting. And because every place that has a *Tet* has no suffering to be prepared there to dwell in it. And because of this, the **Other Side** <note>The Sitra Achra, or forces of evil/impurity</note> does not rule over this place at all, and it gives the life of this world to this place. And it shall not go out; and when it goes out, the Other Side has no permission to rule over it. Just as it does not rule in this place, so the letter *Chet* (ח) <note>original: "את חרס" likely referring to the sun/destruction or the letter Chet</note> does not rule in the place of rest. And who covers the letter *Kof* (ק) and was delivered into the hand of the **Altar** all around? Are they not the two letters *Pe* (פ) and *Tet* (ט)? And because of this, they were not written among the sages of the secret... to the hearing; and the tribes of Israel, two letters were hidden to be withheld from them, so that the letter *Kof* (ק) <note>often associated with "Kelipah" or impurity</note> would not be trampled among them. In the place of the Sanctuary, all the letters of the Alphabet hang, like bodies, holy, bound, joints upon them, and the whole world above and below—all of them are as the letters are defined and struck, and the Holy Spirit is enveloped upon them. Like the Tabernacle that was engraved and the letters were formed as was fitting. In this manner, [Bezalel] knew how to combine the letters with which heaven and earth were created; and through his wisdom, they were supported by all the works of his hands, and he was chosen from all the people. And just as He desired to choose him above, so the Holy One, blessed be He, desired that he be chosen below. As we have learned:
> **See, I have called by name Bezalel** <note>Exodus 31:2</note>
Below, the verse sees the letter *Vav* (ו) in the name of Bezalel. And his name is a supernal secret, a commandment thus in everything, in the inheritance and the giving of strength. This is the **Tzadik** (Righteous One) who lives and dwells in all that which is searched by the Most High, and a vision more so in the likeness of that [letter] *Aleph* (א). That one is the Tzadik of the two sides, for he is the Tzadik who nullifies them... so that one should not be lacking above... to be lacking below. And that is the "God" (El) in the building of all those who die on the sides; that Tzadik, all of them gather in him. **The son of Uri, the son of Hur.** The first "son of Hur" is when the Holy One, blessed be He, [acted] like the Work of Creation. "Son of Hur" is the son of the Master of All. This "son of Hur, son of Hur" is from all the colors... below, and the Holy One, blessed be He, as is fitting, all the colors dwell... except for the **Blue** (Tekhelet) as the likeness of below. Because the life of the Throne is for the matters of judgment... and it takes hold of the color for it, except at the time it stands in the place where it is bound, then it takes the color of Blue, and this is the establishment.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Tabernacle furnishings, specifically transitioning from the spiritual significance of colors and the Cherubim to the laws and esoteric meanings of the Table (Shulchan) and the provision of sustenance.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And we have established that at the time a **human being** <note>original: "bar nash" - a person or son of man</note> sees these colors, they serve to remind the person to perform the commandments of their Master. This is hidden in the secret of the serpent of wisdom: at the time they saw it, they would fear before the **Holy One, blessed be He**, and humble themselves. When that fear of the Holy One, blessed be He, rose upon them, they were immediately healed. What caused this? That serpent which was fixed there; by looking at it <note>referring to the Bronze Serpent in Numbers 21</note>, they were healed. So too is the *Techelet* <note>the biblical blue dye</note>: "And you shall see it and remember all the commandments of **the Lord**" <note>Numbers 15:39</note>. From that fear of Him, one reaches the blue. Rabbi Isaac said: This blue that you see is like a pale green, and when it stands in this color, then it is ready to judge a judgment like flax <note>a metaphor for harsh or thin judgment</note>. And my vision was in mercy. He said to him: At the time the Cherubim turn their faces toward one another and look face to face, since those Cherubim look face to face, then all the colors are rectified. The blue color turns into a white color, and the green color turns into the color of gold. Because of this, through the overturning of the colors, judgment is turned into mercy, and likewise from mercy to judgment—everything depends on the changing of the colors according to their levels. And their side of rectification before the Holy One, blessed be He, stands thus, and thus it is arranged. Regarding this it is written:
> "Israel, in whom I will be glorified" <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>

Like those colors that are included in one another, which is the beauty of them all.

---

->**And you shall make**<-
**And you shall make** a table of acacia wood, etc. <note>Exodus 25:23</note> Rabbi Isaac opened:
> "And you shall eat and be satisfied, and you shall bless the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 8:10</note>

And so on. How virtuous are Israel, for the Holy One, blessed be He, desired them and brought them close to Him from among all the nations. The deeds of Israel are further proof, bringing satisfaction to the whole world. Because of this, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not give sustenance to the world except through Israel; the satisfaction of Israel descends upon all of them, providing double sustenance. In the time when Israel were in the Holy Land, they gave a portion beneath them to the nations who worship stars and constellations—mere vinegar and dregs <note>original: "pota chala" - crumbs or worthless leftovers</note> from the residue—while the feast of Israel was in tranquility. But now it has turned the other way. It is like a king who prepared a feast for the honor of his house: as long as the children do the will of the king, the feast is with the king, and they give the dogs a portion of bones <note>original: "garmin"</note> to gnaw. But at a time when the members of the household do not do the king's will, the king gives the entire feast to the dogs and leaves the bones for the children. In this same way, as long as Israel do the will of their Master, they are at the Table <note>original: "ptura"</note> of the King; they eat, and the whole feast is prepared for them. From their joy, they give the "bones" to the beasts below—to the idolaters. But whenever Israel do not do the will of their Master, behold, the feast is for the dogs, and only the bones are left for them. Just as the children once ate, now there is no taste to be found in the hidden parts, for they eat the residue from above. Woe to the son who leaves his place and falls to the table of the servant to eat what is left over from a crowded table! King David said:
> "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows." <note>Psalms 23:5</note>

"You prepare a table before me"—this is the feast of the King. "In the presence of my enemies"—these are the dogs who sit before the table, panting for their portion of bones, while he sits with the King in the delight of the feast at the table. "You anoint my head with oil"—this is the abundance of the feast where everything is found and provided. The King’s table <note>The "King" here refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He</note> is such that only the King himself is needed, and all those who are blessed are blessed by Him from that very source. He replied: Although the wisdom is great, and our brothers are like water and springs compared to them, I have not merited to hear this wisdom until now. He opened his discourse and said:
> **"Who gives bread to all flesh..."** <note>original: *Noten lechem le-chol basar*; Psalms 136:25</note>
What did David see that he concluded the Great Hallel <note>A specific sequence of Psalms of praise</note> with this particular verse?
It is because there are three rulers above through which the Holy One, Blessed be He, is known, and they are His precious spirit. These are: the **Brain**, the **Heart**, and the **Liver**. They function in a manner opposite to this world. Above, the Brain is contained within the Head, and as a Crown, it gives to the Heart. The Heart receives and gives to the Liver. Afterward, the Whole gives a portion to all those lower sources, each one as is fitting for it. Below <note>In the physical human body</note>, the Liver receives first, and afterward, it brings everything near to the Heart and it receives it. Once it has received and been strengthened from the "strong side," and the desire of what it received is established, it gives and awakens toward the Brain. Afterward, the Whole returns and distributes sustenance to all the sources of the body.
On a day when one awakens with lower delights toward the Upper World, it is exactly in this manner. But on the Sabbath day, it is not so. On a day of fasting, a person brings food and drink near to the Liver, and his life-force strikes out from his heart, his blood, and his will. That Liver receives everything according to its will. Once everything is seen by it, it receives and brings everything before the Heart, which is the master and ruler over it. Once the Heart receives and is strengthened with will, it brings everything near to the Brain, which is the supreme ruler over the entire body. Afterward, the Whole returns and distributes portions to all those lower sources and limbs.
At another time, when the Brain receives first, and afterward gives to the Heart, and the Heart gives to the Liver, the Whole then gives to all the lower sources. Afterward, when it desires to distribute the sustenance of this world, it gives to the Heart, which is the King whose crown and Table are awakened first, before all other inhabitants of the world. Blessed is the portion of one who is like a storehouse for the King’s table, for through him, this supernal goodness is made known. And because of this, it was a deed of goodness and truth that David performed for Barzillai, as it is written:
> **"...and let them be among those who eat at your table."** <note>2 Samuel 19:29</note>
And if you should say that another person eats from the King’s table besides Him—no. Rather, the King eats first, the Crown of all the people. Those who eat "with" the King eat of the same essence that He eats; they are those who are more beloved to Him than all others, and they are found at the King’s table. And if you should say, is it not written:
> **"He ate at the King’s table continually"** <note>referring to Mephibosheth; 2 Samuel 9:13</note>
This is because all his sustenance was not considered significant elsewhere, but only at the King’s table, for from there his sustenance and food came; this is the meaning of "he ate at the King’s table continually."

For words of Torah should be arranged in this place.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Terumah <note>Portion: "Offering"</note>**<-

We see the laws: *And you shall eat, and be satisfied, and bless.* These belong to the Lord. Can a human being truly eat? Rather, it is like this: his will and desire should be focused upon it, so that the essence of his food becomes "satisfaction." This is what is written: <note>Psalm 145:16</note> **"You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing."** For every living thing, it is written—not just food, but *desire* <note>original: "ratzon"</note>. That same will/desire rests upon that food to bring satisfaction. We learn that when a person has only that table before him and he is troubled by it, he must increase his will for satisfaction to rest upon it. Because of this, it says "satisfies the desire," for "desire" is written and not "eating." And because of what is written and pushed down below, a person must bless the Holy One, Blessed Be He, because through this, joy is awakened above.

**Rabbi Hezekiah opened** by discussing the verse that follows and said: *And you shall eat, and be satisfied, and bless.* From here we learn that a person is permitted <margin>2:153</margin> to say the Grace After Meals <note>Birkat HaMazon</note> while intoxicated, which is not the case with the Prayer <note>The Amidah</note>. Regarding the Prayer <margin>2:163</margin> it is not so, for one must pray it without having eaten or drunk. What is the reason? Because the Prayer ascends higher and higher to a place where there is neither eating nor drinking. It is for the sake of the world's repair that eating and drinking were pushed down... but other levels exist below. In the Grace After Meals, a different and superior color is concluded, and that blessing is found in satisfaction. Because the Grace After Meals comes through eating and drinking, sustenance <note>original: "mazona"</note> issues forth below. Therefore, one must show satisfaction and joy before Him. And because of this, it must be in a place where eating and drinking exist, and sustenance issues forth below, and one must show satisfaction and joy before Him. The crown of the Prayer is not so, for it ascends further higher and higher, and therefore an intoxicated person may not pray. But regarding the Grace After Meals, an intoxicated person is permitted to bless the Grace After Meals, as implied by the verse which is written: <note>Deuteronomy 8:10</note> **"And you shall eat, and be satisfied, and bless."** "And you shall eat"—this is eating. "And you shall be satisfied"—this is drinking. For satisfaction is associated with drinking. Wine certainly brings satisfaction. And regarding this, an intoxicated person [is permitted], for it is written "and you shall bless," specifically implying that the Grace After Meals requires joy and satisfaction. As we have learned: "The Good and He who does Good" <note>The fourth blessing of the Grace After Meals</note> requires the goodness of total satisfaction, like the satisfaction of bread and the light of abundance. Because of this, joy and satisfaction are required. Rabbi Isaac opened and said:

**"And you shall make** a table of acacia wood..." <note>Exodus 25:23</note> This Table stood inside the Tabernacle. What is the reason? Because from it, sustenance issues forth to the entire world. And this Table must not be empty even for a single moment; rather, food must be upon it. For a blessing is not found in an empty place. Because of this, bread must be upon it constantly. And so that a constant blessing may be found in the world, from that Table blessings and sustenance issue forth to all other tables in the world, which are blessed because of it. Every person's table must be constantly before him at the time he blesses the Holy One, Blessed Be He, so that the blessing from above may rest upon it, and it should not appear empty. For the blessings of the world do not rest in an empty place, as it is written: <note>2 Kings 4:2</note> **"Tell me, what do you have in the house?"** And what did the companions conclude? This table, when words of Torah are spoken over it, regarding it is written: <note>Isaiah 28:8</note> **"For all tables are full of vomit and filth, without a place"** <note>The Zohar interprets "without a place" as a table lacking the presence of the Divine "Place"</note>—it is a grave matter to bless over such a table. What is the reason? Because there is a "Table" and there is a "Table." There is the Table that is arranged before the Holy One, Blessed Be He, above, which stands constantly to arrange within it the words of Torah and to include them. For we have learned that words of Torah are gathered within it, and it includes them all, and then it is perfected and rejoices and possesses holiness. And regarding this table it is written: <note>Ezekiel 41:22</note> **"This is the table that is before the Lord."** "Before the Lord" and it rests "before the Lord." But there is another table that has no portion in the Torah and has no portion in the holiness of the Torah, and that table is called "vomit and filth," and this is "without a place."

When that table is removed from before a person, two holy angels are present there, one on the right and one on the left. ## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Contribution (Terumah)**<-

It is one. This Table is arranged in relation to that Bread. They ascend below and the bread is upon them. However, this matter is the essence of His dwelling place: to receive blessings and to provide nourishment and sustenance to the world. And from the spirit of this Table, sustenance goes out to the world, as we have established regarding it above; and in that bread, there is the connection and the sustenance that goes out from this Table to show that this sustenance emerges like fruit. And they are meritorious, providing sustenance to the world. If the cluster of grapes <note>A metaphor for the source of divine abundance</note>—which are the obligation that emerges from it—were not found, they would not be found at all. And if the obligation were not an obligation, it would not be found in the world; therefore, the Table is the essence.

The sustenance that goes out from it shall be that bread. And in this way, they would gather the "debt" <note>original: *chova*, likely referring to the spiritual sparks or the specific requirements of the Table</note> of the Table from among the people, to show that higher sustenance goes out from within that Table. Because it is the sustenance they gathered, in this way every single external sustenance is blessed. And it is given to the Accuser <note>The Prosecuting Angel/Satan</note> to occupy the Evil Inclination <note>term: *Yetzer Hara* — the innate drive toward self-interest or physical desire</note> with them; for the Evil Inclination is not found except through food and drink. This is what is written:
> And you shall eat and be satisfied... and you shall turn away to other gods <note>Deuteronomy 11:15-16</note>
For through food and drink, the Evil Inclination grows within the innards of a person. Take this: the sustenance that goes out from the Table blesses the [ordinary] sustenance, so that no accuser shall be found among them to prosecute them, [allowing them] to perform perfect service to the Holy One, Blessed be He. And this is necessary for this [Table] more than for all the world. And for this reason, the Table is the essence and the obligation, and the sustenance that goes out from it shall be that bread. This Table needs its arrangement to be established on the side of the North, as it is written:
> And you shall set the table on the north side <note>Exodus 26:35</note>
Because from there is the beginning of sustenance. The letter *Vav* and the secular <note>original: *chala*</note> take from the Brain <note>term: *Mocha* — the highest level of divine consciousness/wisdom</note> constantly at first, and afterward it awakens toward the Female <note>term: *Nukva* — the receptive, feminine aspect of the Divine, often associated with the Shekhinah</note>, and afterward she approaches him, and the Brain is toward him and she cleaves to him. These are the "Living Waters" from the Brain, and he is saturated; immediately he gives to the beginning, and these waters cleave to him and they fear him. And afterward, he is included in the Right Side <note>The side of Mercy/Chesed</note> to awaken the Female with that joy and food, as it is written: "His right hand embraces me" <note>Song of Songs 2:6</note>, like the first food to pour water at the beginning. He is in the beginning and does not pour to the Right, for behold, the water from the Right—he takes them and pours. And because of this, waters are not found except from the side of the pouring; once the waters are taken toward him, behold, they awaken toward the Female like those waters. And regarding the "Mighty Deeds of the Rain" <note>A liturgical reference to God's power in providing rain</note> we have learned: and for this reason, "you shall set the table on the north side," for from that side they are prepared in it more than from the Other Side <note>term: *Sitra Achra* — the realm of evil or impurity</note>. When they awaken in its foundation at first, everything pours under the arm, and afterward:
> And his right hand shall embrace me <note>Song of Songs 2:6</note>
The table of a person needs to be found in the purity of the body, and one should not approach to eat his sustenance except in the purity of himself. And for this, a person needs to sanctify himself first before he eats the sustenance that is found within it; for with that sustenance, to prepare it in him, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is pleased. This is so that he does not approach that Table [while] entirely standing from the spirit of the Other Side, so that the Other Side shall not receive anything at all from that sustenance of this Table. And after a person eats and enjoys himself, he needs to give the portion of the "dregs" to that Side; and these are the "Final Waters" <note>term: *Mayim Acharonim* — the ritual washing of fingers after a meal</note> which are the cleansing of the hands. And one needs to give to that Side the portion that is necessary for it, and for this, these are his waters. They are the Brain, and after the Brain, we call [them]. And it stands over a person to give it this portion. And for this, it is necessary to bless generally, for behold, blessing is not in that Side. And because of this, a person must not give sustenance that is on the table [to the Other Side], for that is entirely established, and everything in his innards and everything that is good for a person—in them is the repair of his body. And therefore, the Table is for eating upon it in this way, as we have said. This Table stood in the Holy Temple in order to strengthen sustenance within it and to bring sustenance out from it, and for every moment.

Because that "Glory" of Mine is to be established by them as pillars to support it, and to grasp it with perfections and bonds below, so that this Glory of Mine shall be uplifted with the honor of the firmament that is on the earth.

Because of this, "I created him" corresponds to the Supernal Glory <note>the higher divine realm</note> whose repairs are within him. In the spirit of the left side, and therefore he returns and wanders <note>or "is humbled"</note> on the earth and has nothing. To repair that "Glory," He made in him the repairs of the Supernal Glory which has in it a great secret in the spirit, and therefore "I created him." Just as in that Supernal Glory there is "Formation" <note>Yetzirah</note>, so too "I formed him." The repair of his existence in him on this side is as he is on the earth, in the likeness of that Supernal Glory. Just as in that Supernal Glory there is "Action" <note>Asiyah</note>, so too "even I made him" was written to make him in the likeness of that Supernal Glory which prepares and blesses the Lower Glory.

From where do we know that the Supernal Glory has these three? As it is written: "Former of light and Creator of darkness, Maker of peace" <note>Isaiah 45:7</note>. "Former of light"—this is Formation (*Yetzirah*). "And Creator of darkness"—this is Creation (*Beriah*). "Maker of peace"—this is Action (*Asiyah*). And this is the Supernal Glory that prepares and blesses and provides with all its blessings to the Lower Glory. In this manner, He created Man on earth, who is in the likeness of that Supernal Glory, to be prepared before the [Lower] Glory. And behold, he is sustained from all sides. Just as the Supernal Glory has these three, Man below has these three, to include that Glory from above and from below, to make it complete on all sides. Happy is the person who merits through his deeds to act in this manner. And regarding this it is written: "Let your garments always be white, and let oil not be lacking upon your head." Just as for the Supernal Glory, that supernal anointing oil <note>divine flow/blessing</note> is never withheld from the Spirit of the Living World, so too for the person whose deeds are always prepared...

And so forth; thus page 155 <note>original: *qof-nun-he* (155)</note> is saturated with all those delights from the side of the Supreme Will, which is hidden and always rests upon that Supernal Glory. Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Hiyya were walking on the road, and a merchant <note>original: *tayya’a*; often depicted in the Zohar as a simple traveler who reveals profound secrets</note> was leading his pack behind them. Rabbi Yose said to Rabbi Hiyya: "We must engage and strive in words of Torah, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, walks before us, and therefore it is time to prepare for Him the proper arrangements on this path."

Rabbi Hiyya **opened** his discourse and said:
> **"It is time to act for the Lord, for they have made void Your Torah"** (Psalm 119:126)

This verse has been discussed and established by the companions. However, "It is time to act for the Lord" means that whenever the Torah is sustained in the world and people strive in it, as it were, the Holy One, Blessed be He, rejoices in the work of His hands. There is joy in all the worlds, and heaven and earth stand firm in their existence. Not only that, but the Holy One, Blessed be He, gathers all His heavenly host <note>original: *pamalya*; the divine entourage of angels</note> and says to them: "See the holy nation I have on earth! The Torah is crowned because of them. See the work of My hands, about whom you once said:
> **'What is man that You should remember him?'** (Psalm 8:5)"

And when they see the glory of your words with Him, they immediately open their mouths and say:
> **"And who is like Your people Israel, a unique nation on earth"** (2 Samuel 7:23)

But at a time when Israel neglects the Torah, it is as if the Divine strength is weakened, and then "It is time to act for the Lord." Those children of the world who are righteous and strive [in Torah] must draw their swords and perform deeds of restoration <note>original: *uvadin de-vatlehon*; deeds to counter the neglect</note> so that the Holy One, Blessed be He, may be strengthened through them, like His guardians and wise ones. Why? Because "they have made void Your Torah," and the people of the world do not strive in it as is fitting.

That merchant who was leading behind them said to them: "I beg of you, I have one question to ask regarding this matter, to know its meaning." Rabbi Yose said: "Certainly, the path is prepared before us; ask your question." He said: "This verse that is written, 'It is time to act for the Lord'—and now you have explained it thus—what is this 'Time' <note>original: *Et*</note>? And furthermore, 'to act for the Lord' Himself? Does the Lord <note>original: *Y-H-V-H*</note> need a deed to be 'acted' for Him?" Rabbi Yose said: "In several ways the path is prepared before us: one, that we are two and it is Sabbath; yet we are three, and the Divine Presence <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note> is included with us. And another, that the Torah was like a weakened and shamed thing, and you were hungry for it. And another, perhaps you asked because you have a word to say; speak!" He <insert>the merchant</insert> opened and said: "'It is time to act for the Lord, for they have made void Your Torah.' 'It is time to act for the Lord'—there is 'Time' and there is 'Time.' 'A time to love and a time to hate.' 'Time' is a decree from above... 'Time' is the treasury of Faith <note>original: *mehemanuta*; often a reference to the Shekhinah</note>, and this is called the 'Time of Favor.' And this is why a person is obligated to love the Lord always, as it is said, 'And you shall love the Lord your God,' reaching 'a time to love'—this is the time a person is obligated to love. And there is 'a time to hate,' which is the mystery of 'other gods,' and a person is obligated to hate it and not let his heart be drawn after it, reaching 'a time to hate.' And because of this it is written regarding Aaron your brother, 'that he come not at all times <note>original: *be-khol et*</note> into the holy place.' And everything depends on the time when Israel strives in Torah; then that 'Time of Faith' is prepared in its arrangements and adorned with prayers as is fitting. But at a time when Israel neglects the Torah, as it were, that 'Time' is not in its proper arrangement and is not found in prayer as is its way. Returning to 'It is time to act for the Lord'—what is 'to act' <note>original: *la'asot*</note>? As it is said:
> **'Which God created to act'** (Genesis 2:3)

What is 'to act'? To repair the bodies that are lowly, to repair the day... to be made and repaired to crown the heights, everything... 'A time to act'—everything is found in restoration and everything is complete. Why? Because 'they have made void Your Torah,' because Israel is found below [neglecting] the words of Torah; because of this, that 'Time' stands thus, or ascends, or is like a balance for the children of Israel." Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Hiyya came...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the significance of the Sabbath afternoon prayer (Mincha). It focuses on the transition from the weekday judgment to the Sabbath "Time of Favor," explaining why specific verses are recited to justify Divine judgment upon the passing of three great leaders: Joseph, Moses, and David.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

"See and go out in anger." Rabbi Yose said: "Certainly there is no time like this to enter the Crown <note>The highest Sefirah, Keter</note>, for all is one. Whether we have merited to see it or not, the hidden things of Rabbi Shimon’s heart, which bend between the mountains of wisdom, are found there." Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Hiyya wept, and the three of them went as one. He opened his discourse and said: **"But as for me, let my prayer be unto You, O Lord, in a time of favor; O God, in the abundance of Your mercy, answer me with the truth of Your salvation"** <note>Psalm 69:14</note>.

We have learned: When is it called a "time of favor"? At the time when the songs of praise <note>original: "nechora," likely referring to the angelic or liturgical melodies</note> are victorious. And it is truly so, for then the singers arrange and prepare the repair of this "time of favor," and they themselves are the "time of favor." Therefore, one must offer prayer, as it is written: **"O God, in the abundance of Your mercy, answer me with the truth of Your salvation,"** for then it is necessary to offer prayer. **"But as for me, let my prayer be unto You, O Lord"**—herein lies the secret of Unity. And this refers to <term>King David</term> <note>original: "David Malka"</note>, the place called "Prayer" <note>The Sefirah of Malchut</note>. "My prayer" is the Prayer itself, and here it is joined to "Redemption" so that they are one. When one joins Redemption to Prayer, then it is a "time of favor." "Time of favor"—likewise, they are all as one. "Time" is one, "Favor" is one; they are included in each other and become one. And King David sought to unify this verse into a single Unity.

And if you should ask: Why is this verse recited during the exile of the Sabbath afternoon <note>Mincha</note>? It is the time to recite it on the Sabbath during that Mincha prayer, and not during the exile of the weekdays, for certainly the time of Sabbath Mincha is not like a weekday. Because during the weekday afternoon, judgment hangs over the world and it is not a "time of favor." But on the Sabbath, all anger passes away and everything is included as one. Even though judgment is awakened, the "Serpent" <note>The source of evil/judgment</note> is subdued. Therefore, a verse of Unity is required to unify all levels, for when they are unified, judgment is covered and included within Mercy, and all is found to be a "time of favor." "Time of favor" includes everything as one, and David was subdued at that time and hoped for the holiness in everything.

Moses the Pious departed from the world at that hour of the Sabbath Mincha, at the hour when the "time of favor" is found. At that hour, there is Will above and rebuke below. And until now, the gates are humbled <note>original: "kna'anu," a play on the word for Canaanites/merchants and being humbled</note> on the Sabbath from the time of Mincha onwards. Which gates? The gates of the House of Study. For we remember that through the staff of Will, the standing of freedom was subdued because of it. In the book, it is found that the House of Study of the city was subdued by nine swords. Who has seen the gates of the House of Study of the city that were humbled? For they were not humbled, but destroyed. The freedom of the city is humility... and the cantor places it for the poor.

Because of this, all the gates of the House of Study are humbled, and all are required to justify the Holy One, Blessed be He, in the path of merit. These are the verses of **"Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains"** <note>Psalm 36:7</note>. There are three who departed from the world at this hour, and all are included in Moses: One is Moses, the faithful supreme prophet; one is Joseph the Righteous; and one is King David. Therefore, there are three justifications of the Divine Decree <note>original: "Tziduk HaDin"</note> here. One is for Joseph, the holy righteous one who was the "all," and this is: **"Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains, Your judgments are like a great deep..."** <note>Psalm 36:7</note>. This is Joseph, who is like the mighty mountains—all the high mountains. And one is Moses, the faithful prophet, and this is what is written: **"Your righteousness also, O God, reaches to the high heavens, You who have done great things"** <note>Psalm 71:19</note>, because he includes all sides, from below and from above. And one is King David, and this is what is written: **"Your righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and Your Torah is truth"** <note>Psalm 119:142</note>. This is King David. Then everything is gathered into the Book and the power of the Torah, as it is written, "Your Torah is truth."

At the hour when Joseph the Righteous died, the sources and springs were covered, and all sides fell into exile. They opened and said: **"Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains, Your judgments are like a great deep."** At the hour when Moses died, His name was strengthened in the morning, and the wisdom of the Torah, the intellect, and the testimony were given... At the hour when King David died, the moon was gathered in its fullness and freedom...

It links the three "Tzidkatkha" verses recited in the liturgy to the passing of Joseph, Moses, and David, who all represent different aspects of Divine Righteousness.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And the whiteness within it <note>original: "Chivurta"; referring to the white space or the hidden light of the Torah</note> is like the colors of the Torah. And who are those who take on the burdens of fasts that we decree? For every death of a certain person, one decrees a fast. When it is so, he decrees thus, and he gathers more from the sweetness of the Torah, as it is written: "And the Torah which is in him." At that time, it is necessary for them to make gates for the Torah. And because of this, we say these are the proven ones, just as it was stated. Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Hiyya went and traveled on their way, and it was like the weight of water and milk <note>likely a metaphor for the blending of Mercy and Severity</note> on this path. And that strength and power—from what place is it strengthened? He returned and said: **"More than ten rulers"**—these are the Ten Utterances <note>The Ten Commandments</note> written in the Torah, which are the rulers over all miracles, to be strengthened by them in this world and in the World to Come. Blessed is the portion of one who strives in the Torah to be strengthened by the strength of the World to Come. "Ten rulers"—these are ten types of wisdom when the Torah is engraved with ten names and they are included in one Name of crowns; and two second names are engraved with the secrets of the World to Come, which are lights that no eye has been permitted to see, and even the angels cannot know or gaze upon them. <term>Eden</term> <note>The ultimate source of divine pleasure, distinct from the Garden of Eden</note> and the longing of the voice are lacking for the righteous until the World to Come, then:
> **"No eye has seen, O God, besides You, what He will do for those who wait for Him"** (Isaiah 64:3).
The opening of the world is when one merits to eat at another table, like the time of that world, as it is said:
> **"For he ate at the King's table regularly"** (2 Samuel 9:13).
And King David said:
> **"You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies"** (Psalms 23:5).
And the arrangement of the table in that world exists, for then there is life, delight, and the longing of desire to be prepared for them in the World to Come. And do souls have a table in that world? Yes. For the nourishment and the supply of delight pass through that world in the manner that the supernal angels eat. And do the supernal angels eat? They live! In the manner that the tongue eats, as Israel mentions. And that nourishment is the spirit of life that dwells on the wings, to be strengthened by the secret of the World to Come. And its palate is the nourishment of the memory of the bed of holy greatness, and the place of the righteous is below there in the Garden of Eden, and their partnership is there. For from there, the souls of the righteous are clothed in the lower Garden of Eden in the likeness of this world. And the garments and the radiance spread out and ascend to see the essence of what is behind them and to delight in the supernal delight as is fitting, as it is written:
> **"And it shall be that from one New Moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh shall come to prostrate themselves before Me, says the Lord"** (Isaiah 66:23).
And is it truly "all flesh"? It should not have been written this way, but rather "all spirit" or "soul." What is "all flesh"? Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, makes for every person in this world a likeness of the supernal glory of the Glory above. That supernal Glory shall be spirit and wisdom for the Assembly <note>referring to Knesset Yisrael/the Shekhinah</note>.

## Main Text (Zohar)

Until it reaches a certain place below called the **body**, and it covers it. A single spirit enters from the source of life which is called "All" <note>Hebrew: *Kol*</note>; this is the living being, the merit, the sustenance, and the entire satisfaction of that body. And this spirit is the "advantage of the land" <note>Ecclesiastes 5:8</note>; in everything it is the life, it is "All," and it is the spirit of that body. In this same manner, when the world is observed, it is a body, and the spirit that rules over it is like that spirit which rules over the body called "All," and she is called "All-Preserving." Concerning this it is written: *And all the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing before Him* <note>Daniel 4:32</note>. The Holy One, blessed be He, said regarding that prepared arrangement, which is like the grass of the field, "Look to it!" The companions rejoiced in this clarity.

When they reached a certain mountain, Rabbi Hiyya said to a certain Arab traveler <note>The *Tayya'a* or Arab traveler is a recurring character in the Zohar who often reveals deep hidden wisdom</note>: "What is your name?" He replied, "Machin." He said to him, "May the Holy One, blessed be He, establish you <note>A wordplay on the name Machin and the Hebrew root *K-W-N*, meaning to establish or prepare</note> and hear your voice in the hour of your need." Rabbi Yose opened the discourse and said: *“And you shall eat and be satisfied, and you shall bless the Lord your God for the good land which He has given you.”* <note>Deuteronomy 8:10</note> How is it that the people of Israel bless for another portion above all others? For in this manner it was not necessary. Rather, when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He divided the earth and gave merit to one side, while the rest of the earth was for the other side <note>The "Other Side" or *Sitra Achra* refers to the realm of spiritual impurity or shells</note>. He divided the merit and surrounded the world around a single point, and that point is the **Holy Land**.

The Holy Land is the "fatness" <note>the choice part or essence</note> of the world. And within the fatness of the Holy Land is Jerusalem. The fatness of Jerusalem is the House of the Holy of Holies, and all goodness and all sustenance for the entire inhabited world descends from there, from above. There is no place in the whole inhabited world that does not receive from there. He divided the earth, and no "strong land" <note>harsh or desolate land</note> was found in the whole world except for that wilderness where Israel broke its strength and its power. That land is desolate, as it is said: *“Who led you through the great and terrible wilderness...”* <note>Deuteronomy 8:15</note>. From that wilderness rises the **Other Side**, and against its will, Israel returned to it and broke its strength in many lands.

If Israel had been found worthy in those many lands, that Other Side would have been removed from the world. But because they provoked the Holy One, blessed be He, all those times, that Other Side grew strong, and they all fell there under its authority. Now, if you say: "Behold, Moses, who rose above all people in the world—how did he fall there?" It is not so, for Moses the **Faithful Shepherd** was not under its authority, but rather at Mount Abarim. What is "Abarim"? It refers to the "divisions" <note>A wordplay on *Abarim* and *Hevrim* (divisions/sides)</note> where the supernal rulers above were divided, and he was not delivered into the hand of the lowly one or the Other Side. He remained there until, below, Moses the faithful servant ruled over it. He was buried there, and no one occupied themselves with his burial except for the Holy One, blessed be He, alone. This is what is meant by: *“And He buried him in the valley.”* <note>Deuteronomy 34:6</note>

Who buried him? It is the same One of whom it is written in the hidden decree: *“And He said to Moses,”* and it does not say who He is. *“And He called to Moses,”* and it does not say who He is. So too here, *“And He buried him,”* and it does not say who He is. But certainly, this place is known to the companions. Therefore, on that mountain, no one rules except for Moses alone who is there. And in order to protect all the other generations of the world—those who are the "Dead of the Wilderness"—that Shepherd will lead them and gather them to exist together in the awakening of the resurrection for the World to Come. And if you say: "If that wilderness is the strength of the Other Side, why did the Holy One, blessed be He, command that the goat <note>The Scapegoat of Yom Kippur</note> be sent to the other mountain?" To the end... [text continues]

The Cup of Blessing is blessed like silver; it is the blessing that a man recites over it to the Holy One, blessed be He, and therefore it is the Spirit of Faith. One must guard it like a sapphire upon him, like the vision and merit of the King, for the building of his table is blessed with the taste of the blessing—the sustenance that this man blesses his table with. It must not be empty, for blessing is not found upon an empty table, as they established from what is written:
> **Tell me, what do you have in the house?** <note>2 Kings 4:2, where the miracle required a small amount of oil to begin</note>

> **He gives wisdom to the wise** <note>Daniel 2:21</note>

->**The Faithful Shepherd**<-
