<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the construction of the Tabernacle, specifically focusing on the Menorah (the Candelabrum) as a symbolic representation of the Divine structure and the Sefirot (Divine emanations). It transitions from the general laws of contribution (Terumah) to the specific mechanics of how the Menorah "makes itself" through Divine will.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Terumah 158**<-

A difficulty is raised regarding the verse **the Menorah shall be made** <note>Exodus 25:31. The Hebrew "Te'aseh" is in the passive voice, implying it was made automatically or by itself.</note>. Certainly, the Holy One, blessed be He, intended for the *Shekhinah* <note>The Divine Presence, often associated with the feminine principle and the Sefirah of Malchut.</note> to be the King’s name above, to be His recognized sign. Concerning this, it is said: **Seven times a day I praise You** <note>Psalms 119:164</note>, which refers to the seven Sefirot: *Gedulah* (Greatness), *Gevurah* (Power), *Tiferet* (Beauty), *Netzach* (Victory), and *Hod* (Splendor), all resting upon *Malchut* (Kingship). All seven pass through seven levels to ascend and establish the branches of the Menorah. The first Menorah <note>The central shaft</note> is the body and the two arms of the King; let it be a Hanukkah lamp to shine through them. The branches of the Menorah then ascend; the second Menorah consists of the two legs and the kidneys <note>Symbolizing the Sefirot of Netzach and Hod</note>, and let it be the Western Lamp to shine through them, to be called the recognition of the King. And let it be **Thus** <note>Hebrew: *Koh*, numerically 25, a name for the Shekhinah</note> to shine within it, for of the Menorah it is said: **The commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes** <note>Psalms 19:9</note>.

The partitions of the Menorah—the Lord covered them to show her three branches in this image: **ו ו ו** <note>Three of the Hebrew letter Vav</note>. These three *Vavs* represent the three merits <note>The Patriarchs: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob</note>. The second *He* <note>The final letter of the Tetragrammaton, representing Malchut</note> has three second branches in the image of **ו ו ו**, which correspond to *Hod*, *Yesod*, and *Malchut* in their awakening. And upon the secret of the crown, let it be included as six branches below, according to the count of His six branches <note>The six directions/Sefirot of the Zeir Anpin</note>. This is the strength of the "Crown of her Husband." It was taught that the Torah scroll is in the form of seven from the side of the World to Come <note>Binah</note>. They shall be from the power of the Prophets; certainly, it flows to the Prophet, but the Crown is upon the head of my Beloved. Let it be the strength of the King, their hope, His staff in every Sefirah of His, in every side of His, in every measure of His.

Because of this, this *Vav* sometimes serves as their hope, sometimes it is upon the head, and sometimes in awakening upon the head. The Lord is wise and strong; the stone which the builders rejected **has become the chief cornerstone**. This is the secret of "kindling the lamp continually," so that the *Vav* shall be over the *Yod* from the side of the recognition in the awakening of the "camp of the stone" <note>A reference to a specific mystical configuration or angelic camp</note>. As it is written, they shall give in this manner, moving like a longing, like a poor man in this bowing. My Beloved is five cubits <note>The letter He</note> from this side, and five cubits wide from the lower side; five is *Yod* and five is *Yod* <note>The numerical value of the letter Yud is 10, often split into two fives in Kabbalistic math</note>. All of it is hinted at in the letter *Chet* and *Yod* <note>Spelling *Chai*, meaning Life</note>. This is the secret of the "Living One" for the hidden ones. All is life... hinted at in this... the *Vav* and the *He*... and the one who rules over the fifty gates of the Female <note>The 50 Gates of Understanding</note> shall be from the left side.

After these crowns, it is in the Body in this manner: *He*, *He*. They are prepared for the Spirit and the Female... because we did not perform the unification below as the unification above, which is a perfect unification as it should be. But the Holy One, blessed be He, who knows all thoughts, said: Since they did not intend for the good to perform the unification, **the Menorah shall be made** <note>Exodus 25:31</note>—it shall be made of itself. Just as the *Shekhinah* is made of itself by the Holy One, blessed be He, without separation.

In every place where the lower *Shekhinah* is, let there be a Crown, a Pillar. When the *Segol* <note>A Hebrew vowel/cantillation mark</note> of grace—which is *Binah*—becomes the World to Come, there is no knowledge for anyone except the Holy One, blessed be He, and His attributes, until one enters this lower gate. Regarding this it is said: **This is the gate of the Lord** <note>Psalms 118:20</note>. It contains every Sefirah and every letter that supports it. Let it be like a point for every letter, a movement like a leaf, and let it be a Crown upon the head from the side of the musical accents (*Te'amim*). For example: the *Segola* point is beneath the "thighs of the King," called **His footstool**. And in the awakening from the depths of the "camp of the stone," like the *Zarka* <note>A cantillation mark whose name means "sprinkling" or "throwing"</note>, let it be a Crown upon the head from the side of the *Segolta*, *Zarka*, *Maqaf*, and *Shofar Holekh*. The *Segolta* shall be like a Crown upon the head of the King. Concerning that which is hidden from you, do not seek it <note>A famous Talmudic/Ben Sira warning against over-speculation into the Divine Essence</note>. For through this, you may know that He is merciful above... and whoever clings to Him below, He raises him above, and whoever seeks to separate... has no portion in Her.

## Main Text (Zohar - The Faithful Shepherd)

For Him and for His children; and what is it that they should not seek to take for the higher level? The nourishment of their lives, all of them, above and below. And their nourishment is here: **"And this is what their father spoke to them"** <note>Genesis 49:28</note>, as if to say He was recognized when He was present. And He said to the wise of the Torah—the wise ones, the mighty in strength, and those rich in it, who are happy with their portion—for the sake of their prophecy, He said regarding it: **"Thus says the Lord: Let not the [wise man] glory..."** <note>Jeremiah 9:22-23</note> **"But let him who glories glory in *this* (Zot), that he understands and knows Me."** David, who knew her <note>The Shekhinah, often referred to by the feminine pronoun "this" (Zot)</note>, said: **"Though a host should encamp against me... in *this* (Zot) I trust."** <note>Psalms 27:3</note> And Jeremiah was in the exile of destruction, sun and darkness, and all the depths of the seventy nations whose chariots crushed Israel; and the voice of that One called out and said: "Holy!" **"And yet for all *this* (Zot), when they are in the land of their enemies..."** <note>Leviticus 26:44</note> And afterward He subdued [the enemies], and *this* (Zot) was his merit... and it was said of her: **"A senseless man does not know, and a fool does not understand *this* (Zot)."** <note>Psalms 92:7</note> And *this* (Zot) is the voice, as it says: **"Hear, O Lord, the voice of Judah."** <note>Deuteronomy 33:7</note> Because of the speech that reached him, he merited to see; and David, because of her, ascended to the kingdom, for he pledged all his days for her. The Holy One said regarding her: **"And *this* (Zot) is the Torah which Moses set before the children of Israel."** <note>Deuteronomy 4:44</note> Through her, He binds Israel at the time of your fear; through her, He blessed Israel, every single tribe, on the mountain: **"And *this* (Zot) is the blessing with which Moses blessed..."** <note>Deuteronomy 33:1</note>

And for the sake of the companions, masters of the Mishnah, I have answered: **"This (Zot) is the Torah: when a man dies [in a tent]..."** <note>Numbers 19:14</note> And they said regarding this: What is "when a man dies in a tent"? The Torah is only sustained in one who kills himself for it. And there is no "death" like the poor man, for the poor man is considered as if dead, and his poverty is like a sacrifice. And he rises from the side of the ten <term>Sefirot</term> <note>The ten divine emanations</note> to ascend above all the wealthy. All the good that they do is all to merit them for the World to Come... like the one who serves to merit in two worlds... like the portion of the <term>Afikoman</term> <note>The broken matzah eaten at the end of the Passover Seder</note> hidden under the cloth after the meal... and from the side of the heart, He says: **"Whatever your petition, it shall be granted you; and whatever your request, even to half of the kingdom, it shall be performed."** <note>Esther 5:6</note>

Everything depends on the poor man who "kills" himself for her <note>the Torah/Shekhinah</note>, just like your way, O Faithful Shepherd <note>Moses</note>. And he shall be a sacrifice to mend your repair... for one who exerts himself for the sake of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) which is holy, and is like dead for her, it is he of whom it is said: "Prepared in the hand of the Lord." And it was said by the High and Lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: **"I dwell in the high and holy place, and also with *this* (Zot) one who is of a contrite and humble spirit."** <note>Isaiah 57:15</note> Because of the "blackness" <note>suffering/poverty</note>, he is enslaved, contrite, and humble of spirit for the sake of my Shekhinah, to take her from the fringes... a crown for your throne... to dwell with him. And the crown of her husband, the Shekhinah... and he shall be like him upon his head, and he gives a level below to her husband, and she descends to the feet of the Kingdom. And the secret of the matter: **"The heaven is My throne, and the earth is My footstool."** <note>Isaiah 66:1</note> From the day he inherited the portion, he receives, and his Shekhinah raises his plea... as the verse says that David spoke in the Book of Psalms: **"I will tell of the decree: The Lord said to me, 'You are My son; this day I have begotten you.'"** <note>Psalms 2:7</note>

To the Holy One, the Faithful Shepherd: What is "this day I have begotten you"? Rather, for your sake, David said through the Holy Spirit: "Behold, this day is great," as it was said of him: **"And there has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses."** <note>Deuteronomy 34:10</note> You stand with the Shekhinah... and you shall love with all your heart—which is the Soul (<term>Nefesh</term>)—and with all your soul—which stands below. For she has five names: **Soul (<term>Nefesh</term>), Spirit (<term>Ruach</term>), Breath (<term>Neshamah</term>), Living One (<term>Chayah</term>), and Unique One (<term>Yechidah</term>).** And with all your might—with all your wealth—the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah shall be nourished by you through all of these. You are the partner... all the strength of your greatness was given to them to raise the Shekhinah from the dust and to make Him king with His Shekhinah over all types of nations... the Holy One, blessed be He, is yours, included in all attributes... above and below, and over all Israel, whoever merits...

## Main Text (Zohar)

Happy is the portion of the one who turns a shovel into a work of the **Crown** <note>Hebrew: Keter; the highest emanation of the Divine</note> for **Wisdom** <note>Hebrew: Chokmah</note>, which is delved into by all thought for your Master. Place it upon your hand and do not move from it forever, but let it be like the image of a bride. And she waits in exile, established in the covering of the bride. And Wisdom from this world is the peace of the Holy One, blessed be He, to say these words before you. And Wisdom is within Him so as not to move. Thus, at every time and hour when there is no need for darkness, and all the ornaments and the connection of the Academy, arise and pray the commandments of the King. He opened and said: **"And they shall make an ark of acacia wood"** <note>Exodus 25:10</note>. The secret of the matter is the Middle Pillar <note>The central balance of the Sephirotic tree</note>; the Ark is the **Divine Presence** <note>Hebrew: Shekhinah</note>. **"From within and from without you shall overlay it"** <note>Exodus 25:11</note> to receive the longing. The house is from within it, and all is one. That which is not so, all of them are of this world of whiteness from within, waters of grace, and another from the "Other Side" <note>The realm of evil or impurity</note>. This is with the writing of ink, and this is the wood of the body. And this is certainly the whiteness struck from the bride; the moon—gold and glass cannot equal it. And from the "Other Side," even like this world, it takes hold, for all is one judgment and an eye that was established so that you should not make them now. And all the things that were from then are still here. Furthermore, this is Wisdom from without and returning from within; so they are outside to the stump. And the wise men and wise women are like this world, for this is to all the beautiful ones like that world, to the life within us and the children. This is the law of the chamber that belongs to the servant, to be His throne, and until His hand are **Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge** <note>Chokmah, Binah, and Da'at</note> which He wrote when it was in His hand at that time. Until here. He opened:

# **And See**

Rabbi Yose opened and said: In those supreme mysteries of **Metatron** <note>The supreme angel and heavenly scribe</note> it is written:
**"And now, according to their pattern"** and it is written **"And you shall set up the Tabernacle according to its fashion"** <note>Exodus 26:30</note>. This is the exchange that the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: all the repairs and all the forms of the Tabernacle, each and every one as is fitting for it. And He showed it to Metatron, who showed the soft Throne within. And if you say that the Tabernacle was not established above until the day the Tabernacle was established below, it was not at that time like the one above until the day it was established below like this other Tabernacle. Rather, it is not so, for the Tabernacle was not established above until the Tabernacle was established below. But you might wonder that the whole Tabernacle was not established in its permanence until the Tabernacle was established below. And He showed it to Metatron from the left of the **Crown**; not that he was on the left, even though he serves the Crown. And not like that other time did the Holy One, blessed be He, say to Moses what the Tabernacle is and what the pattern is; everything was delayed until the voice was established below. And if you say he is Metatron, he is the one who serves her, and his appointee is him. And **Michael**, the High Priest, he is the one who serves within that Tabernacle of Metatron, who serves in this upper soft throne above. Within, another internal one is found which is not revealed in the spirit of the world below. There are two Tabernacles: one is the upper internal one, and one is the Tabernacle of Metatron. There are two priests: one is the Primordial Light and one is Michael, the High Priest below. From here are the hidden mysteries of the House of the Tabernacle from the mouth of the Lamp <note>A reference to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note>. The upper ones were found established upon twelve pearls, supreme limbs. And Michael and the staff, the staff and Michael—there are three supports, they are finished as one. And this enters, and this enters into this. The first one said to him, and it was established in their mouths. He is the first of the life, and Michael and the angel, and he was converted in the spirit of Michael. And when he enters and serves within, he is established like this, and he is called by his spirit "El" <note>God/Might</note>, for he is from the spirit from above within the Holy of Holies. It does not go out from there as an angel, but rather when the angel goes out, the throne is established. For when he goes out from the spirit of the world below, he is an angel and they prevail. Even so, he said to him: to the servant of the life, the spirit from above does not become an angel until it goes out. Then he said to him: and this is the spirit of Michael, the priest; this is included in the beauty of Michael, and he winds the wick before him, and is included like this, and when they are included like this...

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Portion of Terumah (Exodus 25:1–27:19). The text focuses on the cosmogonic process where the Hebrew letters act as building blocks of reality, emerging from the interaction of the Divine Spirit (Ruach) and the primordial elements.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Terumah (Offering)**<-

The light that calls to them <note>The letters or celestial powers</note>... and the secret of this matter is that the Holy One is comprised within the Spirit of the lower image. Certainly, it is so. Rather, all the levels that emerge through the Spirit of the letters <term>Atvan: the Hebrew alphabet viewed as creative forces</term> from within the lower world require this assistance to be unified and gathered, to be joined to that place from which they emerged, and to be established by this Name within. For behold, it was said <note>original: א"ל - amar leh</note> at first on the Right Side to be included within the Left, and through it, he has completion and the "Mercy of Abraham" <note>Chesed Avraham: the divine attribute of loving-kindness associated with the patriarch Abraham and the Right Side</note>. And this is the Spirit of the Right, the Name of *Elohim* <note>original: אלהים</note>. Regarding this secret, wherever there is "Spirit," it is hinted at there, for it includes the soft and the moving, to be gathered and to be seen, to emerge from there to its appointed place like a shadow for both of them. And they were perfected and called "Perfection"—this is the perfection of the letters from the Spirit of the Upper World, all to be included one within the other.

Once it reaches its appointed place, it is perfected; the Holy Name, the key to all, which is called *YHVH* <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter ineffable Name of God</note>, hovers over it. Then there is a shadow for all sides: above and below, right and left, and for all other sides. And when it is perfected from the Spirit of the two sides, from the right and from the left, they are called "Perfection," for here are the right and the left, and its appointment is according to the totality of this Name.

And this is seen: the Spirit of the letters is gathered and emerges from there in this manner, to be gathered and established in every single place. They are included on this side, and like a shadow in the word of the Right. It proves that Grace <note>original: חן - Chen</note> is included like the form of the word, for the Spirit of the Right and the Spirit of the Left are proven. But when it is included and proven in the Left, and like a shadow in the word of the Right... and they are called **Water** <note>original: מים - Mayim</note>.

Is it truly so? Rather, at the time of gathering to that place from which they emerged, like a shadow to be filled with two letters. One is proven as a shadow from the Spirit of the lower world... two, and they are then called **Water**. It is proven to be included like the form of the beginning, and like the shadow of the letter that follows it, the *M* <note>The letter Mem</note>, and like the shadow of the *L* <note>The letter Lamed</note> that was in the Left. The *M* is like its form, to be gathered thus: **Water** <note>M-Y-M</note> in that which is a shadow and more. Then it is proven to be included in it, to begin according to its form.

To the Crown <note>Keter</note>, the letters are gathered: the *A* <note>Aleph</note> which was as at first on the Right Side, it stayed and brought forth the letter *Sh* <note>Shin</note>, included in three sides. It partnered with the letter *A* and **Fire** <note>original: אש - Esh, formed from Aleph and Shin</note> was made.

Furthermore, the letters moved and stayed within the striking of these two sides, and they drew near as one in a "dispute" <note>A mystical tension between opposing forces</note>. And from this dispute of **Water** with the letter... just as the letters were born, they brought forth the letter *R* <note>Resh</note>, the letter *V* <note>Vav</note>, and the letter *Ch* <note>Chet</note>, and **Spirit** <note>original: רוח - Ruach</note> was made. The two sides entered into it, and then the first letters were settled in their places, each one according to its form.

Furthermore, the letters moved and revolved as one. *A* <note>Aleph</note> brought forth *M* <note>Mem</note>, which is from the Right Side, for it is established as the Right. *M* brought forth *Sh* <note>Shin</note>, because *M* is included as at first from the letter of Mercy <note>Chesed</note>, and it was included in the Crown as the Right, and was perfected in two sides. Once they were perfected, they moved and gave birth as one and were included in two sides. *M* was strengthened and showed to the "Five" <note>original: לחמ"ש</note> three letters, and they ascended and gave birth to three others within the revolution. *M* was strengthened and moved and returned to *R*. *A* moved and returned to *V*. *Sh* moved and returned to *H*, and all was included.

Furthermore, these letters moved—the Spirit of Mercy <note>Chesed</note>—and they revolved as before. *A* moved and returned and brought forth the letter *B* <note>Bet</note> on the West side; then it settled on the South side. *M* moved and returned and brought forth the letter *D* <note>Dalet</note> on the North side; then it ascended between North and South and hung in the air. *Sh* moved and returned and brought forth the letter *G* <note>Gimel</note> and settled on the East side, and for it, it ascended between West and East and hung in the air. It was found that two letters, *M* and *S*, were hanging in the air. *A*, which was hidden, ascended between West and East in its place and went up above and was crowned with the *Y-H* <note>The first two letters of the Divine Name</note>. All of them were strengthened and moved and returned... and stood in its place. Then it was crowned and shone, and spread light, and returned as a radiance, and brought forth the letter *T* <note>Tet</note>... the Spirit of the Upper World in the assembly.

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Tabernacle (Terumah), transitioning into a deep esoteric analysis of the "Shema Yisrael" prayer. It connects the physical construction of the Tabernacle to the spiritual unification achieved through prayer.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Terumah (Offering)**<-

They brought her out to the daughter within the mystery of the letter *Bet* <note>The second letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing the home or the feminine principle</note> in the spirit of the Garden. These three, for he was occupied, etc. The letters were as before below in the general spirit, included and gathered as the "brain" for the lower level, as it is written: **"Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place"** <note>Genesis 1:9</note>. <note>original: "עכ"מ בהעתק" - This is a scribal note meaning "Up to here I found in the copy," indicating the end of a source manuscript section.</note>

**"And** the Tabernacle you shall make with ten curtains..." <note>Exodus 26:1</note>. Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Yose were walking on the road; as they were walking, they saw the house of Yose at the entrance with remnants and a vaulted chamber reaching the path.

Rabbi Yose opened his discourse and said: Regarding the reading of the *Shema* <note>The central declaration of Jewish faith: "Hear O Israel..."</note>, why is it written **"Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one"** <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note>, while it is also written **"Hear, O Israel: this day thou art become a people"** <note>Deuteronomy 27:9</note> and it is written **"Hear, O Israel: thou art to pass over the Jordan this day"** <note>Deuteronomy 9:1</note>? Regarding all these instances of "Hear, Hear" that are said—what do they signify? For the "Hear, O Israel" of the Unification <note>The prayer declaring God's oneness</note> is the one that strikes the primary level. Thus it is concentrated; look and see. Rather, all of them refer to the primary level. The "Hear, O Israel" of the Unification certainly stands and sits at that level. And here is hinted and placed the Unification of the Supernal Wisdom <note>term: Chokhmah - the highest spark of divine intellect</note>. The letter *Ayin* of the word *Shema* <note>Hear</note> is large from below, representing power and strength. Rather, it casts its light to include the above and below as one in a single Unification. *Shema* (Hear) is composed of *Shem* (Name) and *Ayin* (70). Here this Name is included as the vision of the seventy supernal Names, for the Name is blessed by them and included in them. And it is necessary to include them as one in a single Unification, with the light of the Ancient One <note>term: Atika - the most hidden, ancient aspect of the Divine</note> within them. For see, the seventy Names are in the spirit of the Supernal Ancient One, and from that Supernal Point this Name is blessed and included in their splendor, to crown Israel in general.

But we have learned that this is "Israel the Elder" <note>A mystical name for a specific divine configuration or Sefirah</note> so that Israel may be a single whole, the knot of the bond of all. And because of this, "Hear, O Israel" is now attached below as a gathering, and everything becomes a single inclusion. This is the "Hear, O Israel" of the Unification. "Israel" unifies three sides: "The Lord, our God, the Lord" to make everything one. The "Hear, O Israel" that surrounds them all is in this manner for all of them; they are for the primary level and all are attached as one to the gate: "Hear, O Israel: thou art to pass over the Jordan this day." "Hear, O Israel: this day thou art become a people." All are attached to the lower level: "Hear, O Israel: this day thou art become a people." "Hear, O Israel" and you went. What is "thou art become (*nihyeta*) a people"? It should have said "thou wert (*hayita*) a people." What is *nihyeta*? Rather, as in every place when the children are concentrated for the service, it is like a "becoming" and a "renewal." This is what is written: **"Hear me, my brethren, and my people"** <note>I Chronicles 28:2</note>. If they are "my brethren," why "my people"? And if "my people," why "my brethren"? Rather, David spoke with the desire of the heart: "My brethren," and if they are my brethren, they are "my people" to be blessed in their hearts for my service. So too, "this day thou art become a people"—you were prepared for the service of the King. "Hear, O Israel: thou art to pass over the Jordan this day"—all is according to the lower level.

What is the difference between this and that? Rather, that "Hear, O Israel" of the Unification—not all of them were in this manner, for those were the mystery of the above and below as is fitting. And in every place, a person must take upon themselves the Yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven <note>term: Malchut Shamayim - accepting divine authority</note>. Because of this, a man must be ready in that *Shema* at that time to unify the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and to accept upon himself the Yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven. And in the copy that I saw: when the Name is accepted as the Yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven, then the *Shekhinah* <note>term: Shekhinah - the Divine Presence, often viewed as feminine</note> comes and rests upon his head and stands over him as a witness to testify the testimony before the Holy King, that this man is unifying His Name and the Unification is completed above and below as is fitting. And because of this, the *Ayin* of *Shema* and the *Dalet* of *Echad* (One) are large <note>In Torah scrolls, these two letters are written larger than the others</note>, to form the word *Ed* (Witness) before the Holy King. "The Lord, our God, the Lord"—this is the mystery of the Unification in three sides as they have established it in the holy intention. And Wisdom is awakened in its places, and we have no permission to awaken it further, except when one is unifying the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

## Main Text (Zohar)

...that the Holy One, Blessed be He, [is the male aspect] and the Woman is considered the Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note> below. He labors over His path and blesses her like a male [blesses a female] with blessings, and it is said of him: "And he said to Jacob, now He shall bless you," which refers to the attribute of Beauty <note>Tiferet, the central sefirah associated with Jacob</note>. What is this "drawing near"? Rather, when Israel went out of Egypt, they did not know the **Secret of Faith** <note>Aramaic: Raza de-Mehemanuta; the mystical understanding of Divine unity</note> of the Holy One, Blessed be He, at all. This was because they had all served foreign worship in Egypt, and afterwards, because of the exile, they forgot the entire root of faith that was in them previously—that which all the **twelve tribes** had inherited from their embrace of Jacob. And when they arrived [at the Exodus], their strength was weak, for there was no kindness in the world, as we have established. Afterwards, they saw all those miracles and mighty deeds at the Sea, and all the miracles and mighty deeds He performed for them in the wilderness. Afterwards, they saw many mighty acts and many merits, and they followed after the Holy One, Blessed be He, until they reached this time. Moses said to them: "Until now, I needed to speak to you like one who teaches a child. From here onward, 'draw near to know'—change your habit to use your intellect to know, to observe, and to enter into the **Secret of Faith**." And what is seen? <term>That the Lord is God</term> <note>The unification of the name YHVH (Mercy) and Elohim (Judgment)</note>. If you say this is a small matter to know, behold it is written: ->"And you shall know this day and settle it in your heart, that the Lord is God"<- <note>Deuteronomy 4:39</note>. If you say it is a small matter, behold it is written: ->"In the heavens above and on the earth below, there is none else"<- <note>Deuteronomy 4:39</note>. Here hangs the entire **Secret of Faith**: to know the spirit of all secrets from within this; to know the hidden spirit of all hidden things, the <term>Unity</term> <note>Yichud: the mystical union of the Divine</note> of the six words <note>Likely referring to the six words of the Shema: "Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One"</note>, and all is one. "Draw near to know"—here is the secret of those who are worthy, they know their Master. For worthy are all those who labor in the **Torah**. When the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world, He looked into the **Torah** and created the world. And through the **Torah** the world was created, as we have established, for it is written: ->"Then I was beside Him as a nursling [Amon]"<- <note>Proverbs 8:30</note>. Do not read it as *Amon* (nursling), but rather as <term>Uman</term> (Craftsman/Architect). Through me, the **Torah**, He was a craftsman. It is like a king who wishes to build **palaces**; if he does not have a craftsman, he cannot build the **palaces**. Once the **palaces** are made, the name of the craftsman does not leave the heart of the king who made the **palaces**. The king is greatly praised because of those **palaces**. So too, the Holy One, Blessed be He, to create the world, looked into the **Torah**. And because the craftsman made the **palaces**, the name of the King does not depart [from them]. If the King made the **palaces**, certainly the King [is known by] how many **palaces** the **Torah** prepared and helped graciously so that the Holy One, Blessed be He, could create the world. However, before the world was created, the **Torah** was engraved for two thousand years before the world. And when the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to create [the world], He would look into the **Torah** at every single word and perform the craftsmanship of the world accordingly. For all the words and deeds of all the worlds are in the **Torah**. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, looked into it and created the world. It was not for the **Torah** that He created the world, but rather the Holy One, Blessed be He, through this looking into the **Torah**, created the world. It is found that the Holy One, Blessed be He, is the Craftsman, and the **Torah** is opposite Him and with Him as the craftsman: "And I was beside Him as a craftsman." It is not written "I was a craftsman," but "beside Him," for the looking into it was "beside Him" as a craftsman. And if you say the craftsman is a single entity, he is a craftsman to the prophet <note>Meaning the Torah acts as the intermediary/tool</note>. Rather, the looking of the Holy One, Blessed be He, was in this manner: In the **Torah** it is written: ->"In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth"<- <note>Genesis 1:1</note>. He looked at this and created the heavens. It is written in it: ->"And God said, let there be light"<- <note>Genesis 1:3</note>. He looked at that word and created the light. And so with every single word written in the **Torah**, the Holy One, Blessed be He, looked and performed that word. And because of this, "go and see." In this manner, the entire world was created. Once the world was created, every single thing was not sustained until it arose in His will to create Man, who would labor in the **Torah**, and for whose sake the world would be sustained. Now...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Terumah <note>The portion of "Offering" or "Contribution"</note>**<-

Everyone who exerts themselves in the Torah, it is as if they sustain the entire world. The Holy One, Blessed be He, looked into the Torah and created the world; a human being looks into the Torah and sustains the world. Thus, it is found that the action and the preservation of the entire world is the Torah itself. Therefore, happy is the person who exerts themselves in the Torah, for they are the one who sustains the world. When it arose in the will of the Holy One, Blessed be He, to create man, [the man] stood before Him in his form and stature exactly as he appears in this world. Even all the people of the world, before they come into this world, all of them stand in their stature and their preparation exactly as they stand in this world, in that material <note>The Zohar suggests a spiritual "matter" or substance in the higher realms</note> where all the souls of the world are clothed in their forms. 

And at the time they are destined to descend into this world, the Holy One, Blessed be He, calls to a certain appointee <note>An angel or celestial official</note> whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, has placed in charge of all the souls destined to descend to this world, and says to him: "Go and bring me the spirit of so-and-so." At that moment, that soul comes clothed in the form of this world, and the appointee presents it before the Holy King. Then, the Holy One, Blessed be He, speaks to it and adjures it <note>original: "סהדה" - warns or charges it</note> that when it is down in this world, it must exert itself to know Him and to know the secret of the faith. For anyone who is in this world and does not exert themselves to know Him, it would have been better for them had they not been created. For this reason, [the soul] is prepared before the Holy King: to know in this world and to exert itself in the Holy One, Blessed be He, through the secret of the faith. This is what is written:

> You have been shown to know that the Lord <note>YHVH</note> is God <note>Elohim</note> <note>Deuteronomy 4:35</note> 

This refers to what [the soul saw] before the Holy One, Blessed be He. "To know"—to know and to gaze in this world into the secret of the faith, into the secret of the Torah; for it is for this purpose that the Holy One, Blessed be He, brought the human being into this world. What does it mean "to know that the Lord is God"? This is the sum of the entire secret of the faith, the sum of everything above and below, the sum of the entire Torah. In this secret is the sum of the entire secret of the faith, and it is certainly the sum of the entire Torah. This is the secret of the Written Torah and this is the secret of the Oral Torah, and they are all one sum of the spirit of faith, for it is the side of the King; this is the spirit of faith. And who is this?

> The Lord is one and His name is one <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>

"The Lord is one"—as in "Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one" <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note>—this is the holy unification. In all of these, there is another unification to establish His name as one. And this spirit is "The Lord is God" when they are in a single unification. And if you say: if so, just as it is written "The Lord is one and His name is one," is it not all one? For it is written "The Lord is one and His name is one." I would have said so, but it is only written "The Lord is one and His name is one," and it is necessary to say in this manner: "The Lord is God" is He, and they are found to be "The Lord is one and His name is one." 

Rather, all is one. For when these two names are unified—this one in a single unification and that one in a single unification—then these two names become "He and His Name" as one, and the whole becomes a perfect Name in a single unification. "The Lord is God"—then everything is perfected as one to be one. And until each one is unified on its own, they are not perfected and not included one in the other to become all one. The sum of the entire Torah is thus, and this is the Torah: it is the Written Torah and it is the Oral Torah. The Written Torah is that which is written as "The Lord" <note>YHVH</note>. The Oral Torah is that which is written as "God" <note>Elohim</note>. And because the Torah is the secret of the Holy Name, it is called thus: Written Torah and Oral Torah, all one without separation. The whole needs the part, and the part needs the whole, and they are unified with one another to become all one. And the sum of the Torah is the sum of the upper and lower [worlds], because this Name is above and below. This is the secret of the upper unification and this is the secret of the lower world, and concerning this it is written: "You have been shown to know that the Lord is God."

<summary>This passage explains that the purpose of the soul's descent to Earth is to study Torah and recognize the mystical unity between the Divine Names YHVH (Written Torah) and Elohim (Oral Torah). It emphasizes that the world is sustained through the human effort of Torah study, which mirrors the Divine act of creation.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

These generations <note>referring to the spiritual lineages or emanations</note> are the life of all, and this is what a person needs to know in this world. And if you should ask: where are the commandments of the Torah found in this general principle? It is rather that this "life" is the secret of *Remember* <note>the masculine aspect of the Sabbath</note> and this "life" is the secret of *Observe* <note>the feminine aspect</note>, and all the commandments of the Torah are included within them in the mystery of *Remember* and the mystery of *Observe*, and everything is one.

Rabbi Yose opened and said: Regarding that which we have learned, that the Evening Prayer is "optional" <note>original: *reshut*. In Jewish law, the evening prayer was historically considered voluntary compared to the mandatory morning and afternoon prayers</note>—why is it different, and when is this so? It is because the recitation of the *Shema* in the evening is an obligation, a reception of the yoke to be unified at night just as it is unified during the day. Thus the attribute of Night is included in the Day, and the attribute of Day is included in the Night, so that a single Unity is made. And the one who said it is "optional" refers to the burning of the sacrificial fats and limbs which are consumed on the altar at night, as we have established.

It is written: *And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul...* <note>Deuteronomy 6:5</note>. We have established this verse, and the colleagues have established it. But one must look at this: in this Unity of "Hear O Israel" <note>the *Shema*</note>, everything is included. And those [verses] that follow, it is written *And you shall love* and *If you will surely listen*, for they were already included in the Unity. Rather, here is the General Principle and there is the Detail, and so it is necessary to be mixed into the mystery of this Unity.

This Unity is like the form of the **Head-Tefillin** and the **Arm-Tefillin**. Like the Head-Tefillin, where the parchment sections are below <note>inside the housing</note>, and here there are three Names <note>The names of God in the first verse of the Shema: *YHVH, Eloheinu, YHVH*</note>. There, in the Tefillin, there are four sections, each one alone, but here there are three Names—what is the difference between this and that? 

Rather, those four sections [of the Tefillin] are awakened by:
1. One Supreme Primary Point <note>the level of *Chochmah* or Wisdom</note>.
2. One Spirit of the World to Come <note>the level of *Binah* or Understanding</note>.
3. One Right Side <note>Mercy</note>.
4. One Left Side <note>Judgment</note>.
These are the spirit of the Head-Tefillin. 

And here, in the mystery of this Unity [of the Shema], there are three Names, and they correspond to those four sections:
* **The first *YHVH*:** This is the Supreme Point, the beginning of all.
* ***Eloheinu* (Our God):** The Spirit of the World to Come.
* **The final *YHVH*:** The inclusion of the Right and the Left together as one.
And these are the Head-Tefillin, and this is the Primary Unity.

**The Arm-Tefillin** is the totality of all these together, and this is the spirit of "Blessed be the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever" <note>original: *Baruch Shem Kevod Malchuto Le'olam Va'ed*, the phrase whispered after the first verse of the Shema</note>. Here is the totality of those Head-Tefillin as they are included within the Arm-Tefillin. 
* **Blessed (*Baruch*):** This is the spirit of the Supreme Point, for it is "Blessed," and all blessings flow from there. And if you say the World to Come is called "Blessed"—it is not so, for the Supreme Point is Male and the World to Come is Female. He is "Blessed" (*Baruch*) and she is "Blessing" (*Berachah*). 
* **Name (*Shem*):** This is the World to Come, which is the "Great Name," as in "What will You do for Your great Name?" 
* **Glory (*Kevod*):** This is the Supreme Glory, which is Right and Left. 
And all of them are included in this Prayer of the Hand <note>the Arm-Tefillin</note>, which is *Kingship* <note>the sefirah of *Malchut*</note>, and it takes everything for its sake. In this "His Kingdom" (*Malchuto*), all worlds are included, to give to them and provide for them all that they need.

This is the Unity of the Head-Tefillin and the Arm-Tefillin. Just as the spirit of the Unity of the Tefillin is, so is the Unity of everything, and this is the mystery of the matter. 

When the Unity is arranged in its totality from the head of the Supreme Point, it is then necessary to draw it down from the head of the Primary Light to the life of all. *And you shall love*: this is the love of the Right Side, to hint to the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: *Kudosha Brich Hu*</note>, with the love of His attachment. And who is the Right Side? This awakens love. Whoever loves the Holy One, Blessed be He, awakens and proves his love to Him...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Terumah [Offering]<-

In love, all things in the world depend solely on the will. Spirit draws spirit and brings it forth, and it is proven that this and that [the human and divine spirits] assist one another. At the moment when a person awakens love toward the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: HaKadosh Baruch Hu</note>, the awakening of the Right Side [Mercy] is only aroused through three colors: "With all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might." These are three distinct aspects. Do not say it is this *or* that *or* that, for it is not written "or with all your heart, or with all your soul." Rather, all are required: heart, soul, and might. Then, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> awakens His Right Hand toward him, stretches it out to meet him, and receives him. Regarding this it is written, "The kindness of the Lord is forever," and that spirit which takes hold of Him is lengthened within him. For King David stood upon his four legs [of the Divine Chariot] when he was bound to the Right Side. We have learned that the commandments here in the Right Side <note>Deuteronomy 6:5</note> **"And you shall love the Lord your God"** consist of three words. "With all your heart" makes two more. "And with all your soul" makes three. "And with all your might" makes four. "And you shall speak of them" makes three more. <note>Deuteronomy 6:7</note> **"And you shall teach them diligently"** is written, making seven. "And when you walk by the way" makes eight. "And when you lie down" makes nine. "And when you rise up" makes ten. "And you shall bind them for a sign upon your hand" makes eleven. "And they shall be as frontlets between your eyes" makes twelve. "And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your house and upon your gates" makes thirteen. These thirteen commandments depend on the Right Side, corresponding to the thirteen attributes of mercy which are greatly needed. Whenever the Left Side [Judgment] is aroused, the Right Side testifies for him, as it were. Therefore, the one who is meritorious is included in the Right, and this secret is proven: the Left is included in the Right, and the Left rules and supports this and that, as it were, like one who says "Walk in my place." In every place, the Left is awakened in love by the spirit of the Right, and afterward the Right is strengthened. This is necessary in every place, and the companions have discussed these matters. Rabbi Hiyya came and kissed him. He opened his discourse and said:

**"And** you shall make the Tabernacle with ten curtains..." <note>Exodus 26:1</note> Here we find the <term>Spirit of Unity</term> <note>original: Ruach de-Yichuda</note>, for the preparation of the Tabernacle is as the sages judge it, as it is written, <note>Exodus 26:6</note> **"And the Tabernacle shall be one."** This is to unite all the limbs of the body so they all become one spirit of the body. Just as a human being has many limbs, higher and lower, some internal and hidden and some revealed on the outside, yet all are called "the body" and the person is called "one"—so too is the Tabernacle. It has these limbs corresponding to the pattern above, and when they are all joined as one, then it is written, "And the Tabernacle shall be one." The commandments of the Torah are all limbs and organs in the Supernal Spirit, and when they all join as one, they all ascend into one spirit. In the spirit of the Tabernacle, those organs and limbs all ascend to a single spirit, just like the commandments of the Torah. For the commandments of the Torah are all within the spirit of "Adam" [Man], male and female, who when joined as one are the single <term>Secret of Adam</term>. One who diminishes even a single commandment of the Torah is considered to have diminished the Image of Faith, for all are limbs and organs in the Image of Adam. Because of this, everything ascends in the Spirit of Unity. Regarding this, the Secret of Faith is one, as it is written, <note>Song of Songs 7:10</note> **"And your palate is like the best wine..."** and it is written, "For wine rejoices the heart of man." Rabbi Isaac was conversing before Rabbi Eleazar and said to him: "Certainly, the love of the Holy One, Blessed be He, for a person who loves Him is only awakened from the heart, because the heart is the catalyst for the awakening of love toward Him, and the Merciful One desires the heart. If so, why is it written 'with all your heart' and afterward 'with all your soul'? This implies two different entities: one the heart and one the soul." He opened his discourse: 

"Certainly, the heart and the soul are two, yet they are bound as one. For the heart, the soul, and one's wealth are all bound to one another, and the heart is the foundation of all. That which is said, 'with all your heart' [written with a double 'bet' in Hebrew] refers to two hearts—the Evil Inclination and the Good Inclination... and they are two, yet each one is called 'heart'..."

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the portion of Terumah (Exodus 25:1-27:19). The previous section likely discussed the commandment to love God with all one's heart, soul, and might. This page provides a profound Kabbalistic justification for the existence of the "Evil Inclination" (Yetzer Hara), explaining it not as an independent enemy of God, but as a servant performing a difficult task to test and elevate humanity.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

It is called a "good heart" and not a "bad heart." And because of this, the verse says "your hearts" <note>original: *levavecha* (plural form of heart)</note> to include those two: the **Good Inclination** and the **Evil Inclination**. And "with all your soul"—it should have said "with your soul," but "with all your soul" comes to include the *Nefesh*, *Ruach*, and *Neshamah* <note>The three primary levels of the soul in Kabbalah: the vital/animal soul, the emotional spirit, and the higher divine breath</note>. This is the meaning of "with all your soul"—everything that is attached to the soul. "And with all your might"—this also refers to many types of money and possessions, all of which are encompassed by these words and called "all." The love of the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, requires a person to love Him with every single one of these.

And if you should say: since the **Evil Inclination** exists, how can a person love God with it? For the Evil Inclination is an accuser <note>term: *mekatreg* (prosecuting angel/accuser)</note> and it prevents a person from drawing near to the service of the **Holy One, Blessed be He**—so how can one love Him with it? 

The answer is: this is the highest service of the **Holy One, Blessed be He**—when the Evil Inclination is subdued out of love for the **Holy One, Blessed be He**. For when the Evil Inclination is subdued and a person breaks it, that is the true love of the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, because he knows how to bring that Evil Inclination into the service of the **Holy One, Blessed be He**. 

This is the secret of the matter: everything that the **Holy One, Blessed be He** made, both above and below, was all made to show His glory and all is for His service. Now, who has ever seen a servant who acts as an accuser against his master and opposes everything his master desires? The desire of the **Holy One, Blessed be He** is for human beings to always be in His service and walk in the path of truth, so that He may reward them with many goods and merits. Yet the desire of the **Holy One, Blessed be He** [is expressed through] an "evil servant" who acts as an accuser by the very will of his Master! He misleads human beings toward an evil path and distances them from the good path, causing them not to do the will of their Master. 

But surely he is doing the will of his Master! 

It is like a King who had an only son whom he loved dearly. Out of his love, he commanded him not to go near an evil woman, for anyone who goes near her is not worthy to enter the King's palace. The son, out of love for his father, desired to do his father's will. Outside the King's palace, there lived a harlot who was beautiful in appearance and form. One day the King said, "I want to see the devotion of my son toward me." He called that harlot and said to her, "Go and entice my son, to see my son's devotion to me." 

What did that harlot do? She went after the King's son and began to embrace him, to fondle him, and to entice him with many seductions. If that son is worthy and follows his father's command, he rebukes her, does not listen to her, and pushes her away. Then the father rejoices in his son, brings him into the inner chamber of his palace, and gives him gifts, presents, and great honor. 

Who caused all this honor to be given to the son? You must say it was that harlot! And does this harlot deserve praise for this or not? Certainly, she deserves praise from all sides. First, because she fulfilled the King's command. Second, because she caused the son to receive all this goodness and all this love from the King. 

And regarding this it is written:
> And behold, it was very good.
<note>Genesis 1:31</note>

"And behold, it was good"—this refers to the Angel of Life. "Very"—this refers to the **Angel of Death** <note>The Zohar identifies the "very" in the creation story with the Angel of Death/Evil Inclination, arguing it is "very good" because it enables human choice and reward</note>. For he is certainly "very good" for one who listens to the commands of his Master. 

Come and see: if there were no such accuser, the righteous would not inherit those supreme hidden treasures that they are destined to inherit in the World to Come. Happy are those who encounter this accuser and happy are those who are not led astray by him. For then, those who encounter him for the sake of building [their character] will inherit all those goods and delights and all those desirable possessions of which it is written:
> No eye has seen, O God, besides You.
<note>Isaiah 64:3</note>

Happy are those who are not led astray by him, for because of him they inherit rest and a portion from the Master in life. And as for the wicked who do not listen to their Master and are found following [the accuser]—the righteous should actually credit him for their own rewards, for because of him they inherit all those goods, delights, and desires in the World to Come. The benefit of this accuser is when the wicked follow him...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar on Parashat Terumah, focusing on the spiritual mechanics of the "Other Side" (the forces of judgment) and the symbolic encounter between Jacob and the Angel of Esau.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

See, I have seen that even though the "Prosecutor" <note>original: *mekatreg*; the spiritual accuser or Satan</note> gains no benefit from the commands of his Master, he must still perform them to grow strong. For just as a sickness or a bad ailment grows strong when it acts upon a person's body—not because it wishes to kill the person, but because once it kills human beings, it is then strengthened and prevails in its illness and finds no rest—so too the Prosecutor is not satisfied in his sickness until he ensnares human beings, accuses them, and kills them. Then he finds rest and is strengthened and prevails in his sickness. 

Just as the side of life strengthens all good people and leads them in the straight path, so too this Prosecutor is strengthened and prevails when the wicked are judged and he finishes them off. May the Merciful One save us! 

Fortunate are the righteous, the "Assembly of Israel," who subdue him for the sake of the World to Come. Strength comes when the Assembly of Israel dwells [in holiness] until it is said of them: "His kindness is with His strength." Thus, "the paths are in their hearts" <note>Psalm 84:6</note> and they are powerful in this world and in the World to Come.

Rabbi Yose, Rabbi Yehuda, and Rabbi Hiyya were walking on the road when they encountered Rabbi Elazar. When they saw him, his face was shining like the whiteness of the sun. Rabbi Elazar said: "Surely I see the wise men of the Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</note>, for all those righteous people who merit it, it is as if they are sown within her; they are surely the 'palms' <note>or 'wings/covers'</note> of the Shekhinah. And why are they called the 'palms' of the Shekhinah? Because the Shekhinah is hidden within them." 

See, they are in secret while they are also revealed. Because the Shekhinah is close to them, they are called her "face." And these are they. They shall be strengthened like them to appear before the Supreme King. And now that I have descended here, surely the Shekhinah is established over you, as it is taught regarding her "face." He opened his discourse and said:

> "Please take my blessing that was brought to you..." <note>Genesis 33:11</note>

When Jacob saw that the Prosecutor had wrestled with him all night, he saw him in the image of Esau, but he did not recognize him until the dawn rose. Once the dawn rose and he gazed at him, he saw him with a face both hidden and revealed. He looked at that image, which was like the image of Esau, a man of sin, and he knew he was the guardian angel of Esau. He took hold of him. What is written? "And he said, 'Let me go, for the dawn has risen'" <note>Genesis 32:27</note>. He broke him because the time had arrived for the angels to say and sing praises to the Holy One, Blessed be He. 

"And he said, 'For the dawn has risen.'" One must look into this: the time for his [the Prosecutor's] authority to be sick <note>or "to act"</note> is only at night, amidst the darkness, as "the spirit does not fear in the nights." This refers to the fear of Gehenna <note>Purgatory/Hell</note>. And why does it say "nights" (plural)? To include him and his female counterpart. For this reason, he only rules at night. And this is why he said:

> "Let me go, for the dawn has risen." <note>Genesis 32:27</note>

See, "for the dawn has risen." Because when the morning comes and the authority of the night-ruler passes, then he and his hosts go like the "female of the great abyss" to dismiss the souls, until they enter the hidden places. They rule and mislead at night until the morning comes. And this shadow was pressing to say "for the dawn has risen," for he has no authority during the day. 

In this same manner, the Exile of Israel is compared to the night and is called "Night." A lesser king rules over Israel until the morning comes, when the Holy One, Blessed be He, will shine for them and their [the oppressors'] authority will pass. And regarding this, "for the dawn has risen"—he was pressed in his hand and his strength melted, for the night had passed. Therefore, Jacob strengthened himself against him and struck his image, which was like the image of Esau, as we have learned. And then he returned to him regarding the blessings. What is written afterward?

> "...for I have seen your face as one sees the face of God, and you were pleased with me." <note>Genesis 33:10</note>

For he saw in a vision the "palms" <note>the angelic forces</note> in the image below. Everywhere a male is not established in this way, they saw in his face that the Shekhinah was with them, and they bowed as if bowing to her. Fortunate are you! He said, "If I were a common traveler, I would see you as such; I would sit with you. Now that I have seen your lives, I have come to call out to be separated from your presence like this toward the light."

## Main Text (Zohar)

For the Torah. He opened and said: **"A Song of Ascents for Solomon: Unless the Lord builds the house, its builders labor in vain; unless the Lord watches over the city, the watchman stands guard in vain."** <note>Psalm 127:1</note> Did Solomon actually say this praise regarding the building of the Holy Temple? Not so; rather, King David said it concerning his son, King Solomon, when the Holy Spirit came to him and spoke to him about Solomon. Afterwards, King David showed his son Solomon the "image" <note>The spiritual blueprint or mystical form</note> of the Holy Temple. Once David saw the image of the Holy Temple and all its arrangements, he returned to sing a song for his son Solomon and said: "Unless the Lord builds the house..." for he saw **"A Song of Ascents for Solomon"**—referring to the King to whom Peace belongs <note>A common Zoharic wordplay: Solomon (Shlomo) is linked to Peace (Shalom), often referring to the Divine King/God</note>. And what song is this? It is a song and praise above all other songs, for it rises above them all. **"Unless the Lord builds the house"**—for King David saw all those seven pillars upon which this Holy House stands, mountains upon mountains to build this House above, and they all stand by the power of the Supernal House upon them, which gives them strength and might, each one as is fitting. And concerning this, the King to whom Peace belongs lives to strengthen the power of this House, because regarding this House, **"its builders labor in vain"**—referring to those who stand over this House <note>The lower spiritual forces or human efforts without divine aid</note>. **"Unless the Lord watches over the city"**—this is the King to whom Peace belongs. **"The watchman stands guard in vain"**—this refers to a certain "foundation of the world" <note>Likely referring to a specific angelic or sefirotic guardian</note> that is established over it and is ready to inspect it, for he guards this city. We find that regarding Moses, Joshua was always standing and guarding it, for there was no guarding of it except through him, as it is written: **"And Joshua the son of Nun, a youth, did not depart from within the tent."** <note>Exodus 33:11</note> Later we find that he [the guardian] is called a "youth" <term>Na'ar: A title for the angel Metatron, signifying a high-ranking servant or youth</term>, as it is written: **"And the youth Samuel ministered"** <note>1 Samuel 2:11</note>; he ministered there because no guarding was found except through a "youth." But the Holy Temple is not so; its guarding is only through the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: **"Unless the Lord watches over the city, the watchman stands guard in vain."** And who is this "watchman" who guards? We have found it to be <term>Metatron the Youth</term>. But you, high holy ones, your protection is not like the protection found elsewhere; rather, your protection is the Holy One, Blessed be He, alone, as it is written: **"The Lord shall guard your going out and your coming in from this time forth and forevermore."** <note>Psalm 121:8</note> For the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to provide a portion for the righteous in His courtyard, protecting us always, as it is written: "The Lord shall guard your going out and your coming in." They followed after him and accompanied him for three miles and then returned to their place. Concerning them it is written: **"For He shall give His angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways."** <note>Psalm 91:11</note> "They shall bear thee up in their hands..." and **"Let thy father and thy mother be glad, and let her that bore thee rejoice."** <note>Proverbs 23:25</note>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Tabernacle (Mishkan) from the portion of Terumah. The previous context likely established the Tabernacle as a physical mirror of the celestial realms.</meta>

# Main Text (Zohar)

The Holy One, blessed be He, comes to the synagogue <note>original: "Beit Knesset"</note> and this is before the time [of prayer]. All the people follow after Him, as has been said, and they go and find the Holy One, blessed be He, there. Then He shines forth as a King; and "King" without further specification refers to the Holy King who is joined in atonements and prepared for the illumination above. And with five [people present], the spirit is struck <note>This refers to the mystical requirement for a quorum; while ten is the standard, the Zohar often discusses the significance of smaller groupings as well</note>. But when He is in the fields <note>A metaphor for the Divine presence waiting in the synagogue</note> near the synagogue and the people do not come to Him to gaze upon the Holy One, blessed be He, then all that supernal dominion and all those appointed over them and the guards are broken from that height which is established in the arrangements of the King. 

Why? Because at that hour when Israel below arranges their prayers and requests and finds the Supernal King, all those supernal guards surround the throne and are established in that holy arrangement. For the supernal guards are all companions, like a lamp below, to be found with the Holy One, blessed be He, as one, so that the ascent of the Holy One, blessed be He, may be above and below as one. 

But when they are prepared to announce like a crown, and Israel below does not come to arrange their prayers and requests to be found with their Master, all the holy guards and the supernal dominion are broken from their arrangements. For they do not ascend in the ascent and cannot rise to their Master as is fitting. Because the merit of the Holy One, blessed be He, requires being as one, above and below, supernal and lower beings at one time. And for this reason, the spirit is struck, and the King is not struck. Even if there are not many in the synagogue, but only ten, those ten are prepared so that the supernal guards will be joined with them. What is the reason? Because all the arrangements of that King are in ten, and for this, He requires ten or more. Come and see, it is written:

> **"And the Tabernacle you shall make with ten curtains"** (Exodus 26:1)

Ten, because the arrangement of the Tabernacle is in ten so that it may be as is fitting. "Ten" <note>Hebrew: *Eser*</note>—why "ten" and not "ten-ness" <note>The Zohar is distinguishing between the masculine and feminine forms of the number ten in Hebrew</note>? Come and see: "Ten" in every place refers to the *Shekhinah* <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note>, which is not like a [standard] count. For example, "standing upon ten oxen"—she surrounds them as a count, for she stands above. As it is written:

> **"The blessing of the Lord, it makes rich [Ta'ashir], and He adds no sorrow with it"** (Proverbs 10:22) <note>The word "makes rich" (Ta'ashir) shares a root with "ten" (Eser) in Hebrew</note>.

To the "Other Side" <note>term: *Sitra Achra* — the realm of evil or impurity</note> is attributed a surplus count. And regarding this, it was said: from here we learn that the *Shekhinah* is a count that is not like a [standard] count. To the Other Side is attributed a surplus count, and it is like a flaw, like the word *Ashtei* <note>referring to *Ashtei Esreh*, eleven. In Kabbalah, eleven represents the "Other Side" because it exceeds the holy number ten</note>, and thus they established it. In every place where we find an addition, it is for the sake of a deficiency. <margin>The addition of a letter in the Other Side indicates a lack in holiness.</margin> But in the side of holiness, where a letter is missing, it is actually an addition. 

Rabbi Hiyya opened: "And the ten..." <note>unclear: likely referring to the curtains</note> like the colors of the heavens like a curtain. This verse was established: that when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He wrapped Himself in that primordial light and created the heavens with it. And come and see: light and darkness were as one. Light from the right side and darkness from the left side. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He struck them together and created the heavens from their power. What are the heavens <note>Hebrew: *Shamayim*</note>? Fire <note>Esh</note> and Water <note>Mayim</note>. He arranged them as one and made peace between them, and when they were included as one, He stretched them out like a curtain; He spread them and made from here a sign, and this is called a "curtain." 

And "curtains" as it is written—this spread out from it in this manner and they became curtains. And there are seven firmaments marked in the manner through which they were built, as they established it, and one firmament that stands above them. And this [highest] firmament has no color and has no place to be gazed upon, and it does not stand to be gazed into. This firmament is hidden and concealed from all, and it covers them in their ascent, each one as is fitting for it. From this firmament and beyond, there is no one who knows or tastes, and it has no mention except to stop one's mouth from praising or gazing with [human] intellect. Whoever gazes to arrange [this] backwards—there is no one who can know it. 

The ten curtains are the ten firmaments, and these are the firmaments of the Tabernacle which are ten, standing to be known before all. Whoever knows how to gaze into them [finds] great wisdom and the secrets of the world, to gaze above.

<summary>This page explains the mystical significance of the number ten in the Tabernacle's curtains, linking them to the ten holy Sefirot and the creation of the heavens from the union of fire and water. It contrasts the "holy ten" with the "impure eleven" of the Other Side and describes a hidden, unknowable firmament above the visible heavens.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the structure of the heavens and the requirements for prayer, specifically focusing on the seventh firmament, Arabot, and the paradox of approaching God with a broken heart versus the requirement for joy.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Above, in that place where each and every one is attached, when there are two who stand on the right and the left, and they are within the colors of faith. Thus, the day is established, planting the firmaments; and they and the "Stewardess" <note>Hebrew: *Sokhent*, a term for the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> are crowned. If you say it is because it is written "He crowns all poverty," <note>A play on words between *Sokhent* (stewardess) and *Miskenuta* (poverty)</note> is she then called "Stewardess" because she stands over the crown? Rather, certainly they are "plantings," and these plantings are many, and the "Spread-Out Secret" is not hidden. And when is she crowned? In this manner: the Tabernacle is "ten curtains," <note>Exodus 26:1</note> and ten curtains correspond to ten firmaments. This is a southern wind <note>or spirit</note> that is not handed over except to those who know wisdom, and all of them are within the secrets of the Holy Writing, where the secret of every firmament is revealed. And they are hidden, reaching into each and every one. There are seven firmaments above, and there are seven firmaments below, corresponding to those above. There are seven firmaments in which there are stars and constellations to examine this world according to its way, as much as is needed for it. And all of them are of a superior nature when they are unified, for He guides them all and stands over them all. It is written: **Extol Him who rides upon the clouds [Arabot]** <note>Psalms 68:5. The word *Arabot* refers to the highest of the seven heavens.</note>. Who rides in *Arabot*, and what are these *Arabot*? Rather, this *Arabot* is the seventh firmament, which is called *Arabot* because it is composed <note>Hebrew: *Kalil*, also meaning "included" or "crowned"</note> of everything. However, it is as one from the side of the South and from the side of the North, and behold, it is a "mixture" <note>Hebrew: *Ma'arav*, a pun on *Arabot*</note> from two sides. And if you say, if so, there are two *Arabot* that are joined as one? Therefore, it says "Extol Him who rides in *Arabot*." If so, who and what? Do they bear fruit in their body, or is their body like thighs? For this one produces fruit and those do not, or this one produces fruit and those... rather, certainly all is the secret of *Arabot*, for all of them are *Arabot*, for all is one. Water was not fixed in the spirit... and which is the seventh? This is the Law <note>Greek/Aramaic: *Nomos*</note> included as one in one secret. And because *Arabot* is the whole of it, which others kindle, it is the Supernal Spirit. And He <note>The Holy One</note> desires this firmament more than all other firmaments, and His desire is always to prepare that firmament with supernal radiance. And regarding this: "Extol Him who rides in *Arabot*." And who is He? That hidden and concealed firmament that stands upon the foundation, which is the "Rider of *Arabot*." And "come before Him"—it is not written "from before Him," but "before Him," for there is no one who can know anything of Him. But "before Him": whoever enters before this firmament must enter with **joy** and not with **sadness** at all. Because this firmament demands that sadness and anger do not dwell there at all, for there, everything is in joy. Even the High Priest who stands before Him would not have anything on the Holy Face except joy and desire... and regarding this it is written: **Serve the Lord with gladness; come before His presence with singing** <note>Psalms 100:2</note>. For it is necessary not to show sadness in Him. And if you say: if so, what of the man who is in pain and distress, who cannot gladden his heart, and out of his distress he must seek mercy before the Supernal King? If so, can he not pray at all? Can he not [approach] in sadness at all, since he cannot gladden his heart and it does not rise before Him as a proper preparation? There is a remedy for this man: rather, he comes and breaks all the gates with sadness and brings [his prayer] in. And the "Gates of Tears" are never closed, and there is no tear except from out of pain and sadness. And all those appointed over those gates, they all break the bolts and cancel [the restrictions] and let those tears enter. Then that prayer rises before the Holy King. At that time, that place <note>The Divine</note> feels the distress of that sadness and the pressure of that man... for the desire of that Upper World toward this place is like a male whose desire is always toward the female, like a King toward the Matron <note>The Shekhinah</note>. When He sees her in sadness, then whatever she asks is granted. And why so much? Because at all times He does not withhold from the "Beard" <note>A Kabbalistic metaphor for the flow of Divine Mercy</note> and the Holy One, blessed be He, stands over him.

<summary>This page discusses the seventh heaven, Arabot, as a place of absolute joy where the Divine resides. It addresses the spiritual paradox of prayer: while one should approach God with joy, the "Gates of Tears" remain open for those in deep distress, as the Divine responds with compassion to the "sadness" of the Shekhinah.</summary>
