<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the inner meaning of the Torah's commandments, specifically linking the structure of the human soul and body to the 613 precepts. It follows the previous discussion on the Tabernacle (Terumah) and the elevation of the soul through sacred service.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Terumah (Offering)**<-

...upon it. And all these garments that a person is seen to wear are like their inner garments before the Holy One, blessed be He. In this same manner, it is like a blue-violet thread <note>original: *techelet*</note>. One who dwells in the matter of this blue-violet thread within his dwelling, his eyes behold it. And this blue-violet thread rules that supernal firmament, which is not seen in sickness, but rather as joy and gladness for all. He who dwells in its matter, because it is the ruler that commands that person regarding that work from which he must abstain, as it is said: **Extol Him who rides upon the clouds** <note>Psalms 68:5; the Zohar reads "clouds" (*aravot*) as a specific celestial level</note>, for He is joy, and He gladdens all. The firmament is named after Him when His name is mentioned, for in that place, "His name is Joy" <note>original: *Shemo Simchah*</note> to the ultimate degree. And his face shines because it is not necessary to show sadness before Him, as has been stated. Rabbi Elazar said: This verse should have said "Extol the One who rides *upon* the clouds"; what is meant by "extol Him who rides *in* the clouds"? And "in Yah is His name"—how can He be called by His name? Rather, the verse refers to the Hidden of all Hidden, the <term>Ancient of all Ancients (Atika de-Atikin)</term> <note>The most primordial, hidden level of the Divine Crown (Keter)</note>, that which is not revealed and not known at all, who is the "Rider of the Clouds." And if you say that He comes and rides upon it, Heaven forbid! Even though it is written that He stands in the <term>Crown (Keter)</term> <note>The highest of the ten Sefirot or Divine emanations</note> to be revealed. Rather, "Extol the One who rides in the clouds" refers to the Ancient of all Ancients, the Hidden of all Hidden, who is unknown. And just as He rides in the clouds, in Him is the first secret that emerges before Him, and this is His name from that unknown Hidden One—His name which is <term>Yah (Y-H)</term> <note>The first two letters of the Tetragrammaton, representing the initial flash of Wisdom and Understanding</note>. To them, He is "He," but He is "He" because of that veil <note>original: *parokhta*</note> that is spread and emerges from before Him. For this entire veil, He is "His Name," and this is the <term>Chariot (Merkavah)</term> <note>original: *Ratika*; the Divine vehicle or structure through which God interacts with the world</note> for Him, which is not known at all. And this is His Great Name, because He is Joy, which is not like a flowing stream in this, even though there is an addition of letters. For He is "Joy-Rider." And the letter *Ayin* in this "Joy" (*Simchah*) is a stone they bring forth from Him. In this, it goes to them at all times and reaches the "Other" that was given to them. And "Yah is His name, the Blessed Rider." For when Joy ascends to be established, everything is in its perfection and all worlds rejoice in gladness. When Joy is washed, all the upper and lower beings are included in that Joy, comprising the six hundred and thirteen <note>613 Mitzvot</note> commandments of the Torah, which include all the upper and lower secrets, the inclusion of the Male World above and the inclusion of the Female World below. And all the commandments are all bodies and limbs in which the secret of <term>Faith (Meimanuta)</term> <note>The mystical system of the Sefirot as a unified structure</note> is seen. One who does not labor and does not look into the secrets of the commandments of the Torah does not know and does not observe how the limbs are established in the Supernal Spirit. The limbs of the body are all established upon the secret of the commandments of the Torah. And even though there are limbs that are large and small, upper and lower, if one of them is missing—even a small one—a person is called "blemished." How much more so for one who diminishes even one commandment from those commandments of the Torah; he causes a blemish in "This" <note>The Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> where no blemish should be. Come and see what is written: **And the Lord God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and to keep it** <note>Genesis 2:15</note>. They established "to work it and to keep it" as referring to the sacrifices, and it is all one. But this is the secret of the commandments of the Torah: "To work it" refers to the <term>248 upper limbs</term> <note>Positive commandments, corresponding to the 248 limbs of the human body</note>. "And to keep it" refers to the <term>365 lower limbs</term> <note>Prohibitive commandments, corresponding to the 365 sinews/days of the year</note>. These are the upper ones of the Male and these are the lower ones of the Female, and it is all one. Happy is he who walks in this path. The commandments of the Torah guard a person, to watch over his spirit and his soul in this world and in the world to come. For the Torah merits a person to find two worlds: this world and the world to come. Anyone who labors in the Torah is seen as a refuge. He is pitied in this world and pitied in the world to come, and is saved from all evil punishments so they cannot rule over him. If this is so for his labor, how much more so for one who performs the deed. Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Abba were before Rabbi Shimon; they arose at midnight to labor...

## Main Text (Zohar)

...to labor in the Torah. His daughter <note>Likely a reference to the Shekhinah or a metaphorical representation of the soul/community</note> poured herself out before them and showed them the way, and afterwards she stood to crown them so they might hear the words of Torah. Rabbi Abba opened the discourse and said:
> For the commandment is a lamp and the Torah is light, and reproofs of instruction are the way of life. (Proverbs 6:23)
"For the commandment is a lamp": anyone who labors in this world in those
commandments <term>Mitzvot; religious obligations</term> of the Torah, there is prepared before him for every single commandment a single lamp to illuminate for him in that
world. "And the Torah is light": one who labors in the Torah merits that light from which the lamp is kindled,
for behold, a lamp without light is nothing. Just as light without a lamp likewise cannot shine.
It is found that each of these needs the other. Action is needed to prepare the lamp <note>The physical performance of a commandment</note>, and it is necessary
to know the Torah to kindle the lamp. Happy is he who labors in it, for through this lamp and through this light
"reproofs of instruction are the way of life." The "way of life" for the World to Come <note>The afterlife or spiritual realm</note> is found in those reproofs
that a man accepts in this world, which cause him to turn away from destruction and to go out upon the good path. Furthermore, "the way of life"
refers to those reproofs of instruction that the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>Original text: קב"ה (Kadosh Baruch Hu)</note>, brings upon them; for when they do not fear Him, He admonishes them with all these reproofs.
Happy is he who receives them with the willingness of his heart. For "the lamp of the commandment" is the preparation of this lamp for a man
in the time of David, who is the master of the preparation of the Oral Torah <note>Original text: דבע"פ (Torah she-be’al Peh)</note>, which must be found constantly, and life
is not lacking. Conversely, from within the [Written] Torah, it is written of the Oral Torah <note>Original text: דבע"פ</note> that it has no light except from within and upon

said: those who are despised <note>perhaps meaning the humble or those who suffer</note> do not merit the Torah, yet behold, they are remembered as meriting the Torah and they call to this lamp, for those who are despised
are prepared through this commandment. Because the preparation of the "backwards" <note>a mystical term for the lower or external dimensions</note> is remembered in the Torah to illuminate all this
preparation of the commandment through which they were prepared. He placed the commandment below and within all of them. Pure is the
merit of the one below who is before us and entered into his days, and his daughter stood to crown them and in all things
he ascended and lacked nothing. Rabbi Elazar <note>Original text: ר"א</note> related to him the story of that one below, who was also living and meritorious.
Rabbi Abba <note>Original text: ר"א - likely a scribal error for Rabbi Abba or Elazar</note> said to him: perhaps the husband will be restored, as it is written "he did not merit the Torah." Heaven forbid! <note>Original text: ח"ו (Has ve-Shalom)</note> It is not so.
And while they were weeping thus, the father was constantly being cut off. And because he was passing away, he said one thing: that in the future, a man

## Main Text (Zohar)

Because of this, he covers [himself], and therefore he rises with this supreme name called <term>Adam</term> <note>Man; in Kabbalah, this refers to Adam Kadmon or the primordial spiritual structure of humanity</note>, who is complete in everything, which no other human is called—only he is truly "Adam." And because he rises with this name, he is sanctified as supreme over all. Regarding this, it is said: the father descended to the waters. From the waters, he is sustained. Who are the waters? Rather, it says the father descended, and his warmth generated the waters for the sake of the person who has waters available to him. Why? Because I said that the waters shall remember him! This father descended, and his warmth generated waters within me, and goodness and kindness were brought down to you. Therefore, a portion of my wife's knowledge was awakened. I said:
> "Days should speak, and many years should teach wisdom." <note>Job 32:7</note>
Truly, "But it is a spirit in man, and the breath of the Almighty gives them understanding."
And because the elder rabbis came with this desire to speak until this day, when the letters of the Elder are ready to open the Torah before you. He opened [his discourse] and said:
> "For the commandment is a lamp, and the Torah is light, and reproofs of instruction are the way of life." <note>Proverbs 6:23</note>
"For the commandment is a lamp"—this is the <term>Mishnah</term> <note>The first major written collection of the Jewish oral traditions</note> without the "And the Torah" and the faith. "And the Torah"—this is the <term>Written Torah</term>. And the faith—this is the Mishnah, which is the wick of the lamp that stands to be kindled. When it comes, it is called a "lamp." However, it receives everything from between the two arms <note>The sefirot of Chesed (Mercy) and Gevurah (Strength)</note>, and these are the supreme edges, for she is the opening toward them, her two arms. Then the two arms are included within her, and she is called a "lamp." "And the Torah is light"—for it illuminates that lamp and kindles from it, from the side of the <term>Primordial Light</term> <note>Or Kadmaa; the first light of creation</note> which is the <term>Right</term> <note>The side of Mercy/Chesed</note>. For the Torah was given from the side of the Right, from the Primordial Light, as it is written:
> "From His right hand went a fiery law for them." <note>Deuteronomy 33:2</note>
It was given from the side of the Right, even though the <term>Left</term> <note>The side of Judgment/Gevurah</note> is included within it, for then it is considered the perfection of all. This light is included in three and seven worlds, which are in the structure of that light, and they all spread out. Beneath the supreme hidden Throne, there are two worlds on the side of that Right; three from this side and four from those, making seven on the side of the Right. Three and three are on the side of the Left, and they are three from one side and one [central]. These are what he constantly prepares, and the words spread into many other delights, all within the structure to be integrated from here as a reflection of the <term>World to Come</term> <note>Alma de-Atei; the realm of Binah or the future spiritual reward</note>. And regarding this, it is written:
> "That I may cause those that love me to inherit substance (Yesh); and I will fill their treasures." <note>Proverbs 8:21</note>
And regarding these it is written:
> "No eye has seen, O God, beside You..." <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>
"Substance" (Yesh) refers to those three hundred and ten <note>The Hebrew word 'Yesh' (Yod-Shin) has the numerical value of 310</note> worlds in the structure of the World to Come. And regarding those [four] and seven that are from the side of the Right, they are called the <term>Primordial Kindness</term> (Chesed). For even the "kindness of the left" is called kindness, but the Primordial Kindness is the Right, to produce offspring for the World to Come. And if you say that the World to Come produces more—even at every single moment, if this light were not present, the world could not stand, as it is written:
> "I said, the world shall be built by kindness (Chesed)." <note>Psalms 89:3</note>
This Kindness is a holy seed, like the Garden of Eden, and he made for it rows, the seed of Jacob, who is the <term>Righteous One</term> (Tzadik) <note>The sefira of Yesod, the foundation and procreative force</note>, who enters and descends, and it is written "to sow for the light," and he sowed for him a seed of truth. And he made for him rows upon rows like a garden, and he gave birth and desired to produce fruit, and from them came the worlds, the assembly of kindness, "sown for the righteous," etc. And it is written: "And as a garden causes the things that are sown in it to spring forth." What is "the things sown in it"? These are the "arms" of the Primordial Light, which is the constant "arm" that the Lord planted, making delights. And now it is sown at the beginning until the world can [sustain it]; there is one who gives birth to this "arm" and the fruit is hollow and does not emerge. And until [the end of] times they are nourished by the sufficiency of that gardener called "Righteous" (Tzadik); he is at rest and never ceases, except during the time of Exile. And if you say that during the time of Exile it is written:
> "The waters fail from the sea, and the river decays and dries up." <note>Isaiah 19:5</note>
How then does he produce offspring? Rather, it is written "and his arm"—he sows for him constantly, and from the day the sackcloth was separated, like this garden, he did not enter—

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the creation of light from the Zohar, Parashat Terumah. ## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Terumah <note>The portion of "Offering"</note>** <-

In it is that soul and the moon, the **Light** <note>Hebrew: *Ohr*</note> that belongs to it. The seed constantly produces sins and rest, and from itself they returned as at first. It is never still in the descent that produces offspring. From that seed, it is doubled within its place from itself, and it produces offspring as it did at first. And if you say that these offspring are the same as those that exist at the time of the descent there—it is not so. Rather, this seed is withheld forever. In this manner, "the Torah is light" <note>Proverbs 6:23</note>. This light constantly circles the world and produces offspring, and they are never still. From here comes its vitality to the world below. **"And the way of life is the reproof of instruction"** <note>Proverbs 6:23</note>. There are two paths: one is the path of life, and the other is its opposite. When it is "life," who is it? It is the "reproof of instruction." For whenever the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires to guard a person to follow the path of life, He places that portion upon him and performs "reproofs of instruction" for the inhabitants of the world. And who is this? As it is written:
> **"And the flaming sword which turned every way, to guard the way of the Tree of Life"** (Genesis 3:24)

And so on. The "way of life" is the "reproof of instruction." And what is this reproof? Certainly, they awaken it for the one who was on the path of life, for the "reproof of instruction" dwells there. This verse is not head-to-tail or tail-to-head <note>meaning it is not inverted or disorganized</note>. Everything is the Spirit of Faith <note>Aramaic: *Ruach de-Meimanuta*</note> according to this verse. **"For the commandment is a lamp"**—this is the spirit of the time <note>referring to the feminine aspect/Malkhut</note>. **"And the Torah is light"**—this is the spirit of "Remember" <note>referring to the masculine aspect/Zeir Anpin</note>. **"And the way of life is the reproof of instruction"**—these are the fires and branches of the Torah, and all is the Spirit of Faith. One is needed for the other to become the spirit of the whole as is fitting. And because of this, this light burns and shines as it is written concerning it:
> **"When you light the lamps"** (Numbers 8:2)

For example, light comes from the side of this light. Regarding this light, it is written:
> **"Let there be light, and there was light"** (Genesis 1:3)

Since it says "Let there be light," why is it then written "and there was light"? Surely the first part was enough. Rather, **"Let there be light"** refers to the primordial light, which is the Right side <note>the attribute of *Chesed* or Lovingkindness</note>. **"And there was light"** means that from the Right emerged the Left <note>the attribute of *Gevurah* or Judgment</note>. From the spirit of the Right emerged the Left, and "and there was light" refers to this Left. From here we learn that the beginning of the Torah was from the side of the Left <note>referring to the harshness of the law</note>, and for this reason, there is no sign of blessing in the letter *Tet* <note>the 9th letter</note>, because from it emerged that darkness which darkened the world for the inhabitants of the earth. And at that time, the spirit was revealed, wrapped in its clouds like this smoke. "And it was wrapped... and the lamp was established in the spark..." <note>The text here uses obscure Aramaic idioms regarding the formation of matter from spirit</note> to open for the inhabitants of the world so they may walk without rain.
> **"And God saw the light, that it was good"** (Genesis 1:4)

This is the Central Pillar of Truth <note>the attribute of *Tiferet*, which balances Right and Left</note>, which is praiseworthy and pious toward this side and toward that side. All is the perfection of the three sides. It is written of it "that it was good" because this was not the case with the others; there was no perfection until the third light arrived, which completed all sides. And once this third one arrived, it then separated the conflict between the Right and the Left, as it is written:
> **"And God divided between the light and between the darkness"** (Genesis 1:4)

And because of those five levels that were separated, "Light" is mentioned five times in the account of the first day. All were divisions of the Right and were included within it. And when they were included in the Left side, they were included in the spirit of the "Waters" which are in the secret of the Right; therefore, "Water" is also written five times. And when they were perfected in the Middle Spirit, it is written:
> **"Firmament"** (Genesis 1:6)

Five times. And regarding the three, they are Light, Light, and Firmament, corresponding to these three levels. All five levels were included equally; it is written five times for each one. Everything is the spirit of this in the three waters, carved and sparkling on the wings of the spirit in the image of the one. The vision of the first light, then the water, then it spread out in abstinence, and the "Firmament" which is the vision of the body of the bodies, the image of *Chesed* <note>Kindness</note>. Just as the body is in the radiance of the image of *Chesed* in its offspring, for in the offspring of every first cup is the seed of the vision of light. This is the radiance of all that moves, breathing life into that seed. Therefore, they lived by the light, and that light is called "seed," as it is written:
> **"Light is sown for the righteous"** (Psalms 97:11)

And so on. After this seed of the vision of light spread out, it became
water...

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the creation process found in the Zohar, specifically focusing on the transition from the primordial "thought" to the physical manifestation of the human form. ## Main Text (Zohar)

**Also**, at the time when he engraved, he engraved further and spread an expansion within the "bosom of the waters," a physical expansion toward all sides. Once it was perfected and the form of the body’s image was revealed, it was called "He." This expansion was not yet a firmament within the waters. But after it congealed, it is written:
> And God called the firmament Heaven (Genesis 1:8)

For that lower part of the body that was within the "bosom of the waters" had not yet congealed. Once it was stirred, it went out and was carved into a hollow, for that which was left over and remained was the dross <note>original: *psollet* — the waste material or "husks" left over from a refining process</note> produced during the smelting. These were the "castrated" or murky waters, and from here was created the accusing dross for the whole world, male and female. Later, when those murky waters weakened and turned downward toward the side of the **spleen**, they went out to accuse the whole world. Happy is he who is saved from this. Once the accuser emerged, it is written:
> Let there be lights (Genesis 1:14)

The word is written deficiently, lacking the letter *Vav* <note>The word מארת (lights) is written without the letter Vav, which Kabbalistically implies a lack or a curse (me'erah).</note> and it was found to be a "choking" for the small children, and the moon was handed over to be diminished. Later, it says "and they shall be for lights" regarding their days, both of them as one. Just as that firmament which we mentioned, when it was taken and joined like the firmament of the heavens, then "they shall be for lights" — they both became complete as one, with no inner part at all. They circle the vision of the serpent, riding and rejoicing. 

He said to them: That which we saw, that the wind stirred to the loins in the mud, that was the evil and hidden thing made from the water. And what are those waters where the firmament of the **Image of Man** <note>original: *Dyokan d'Adam* — the spiritual archetype or "blueprint" of the human form</note> spread out, as we have awakened? It is fine when this is done within the lower intestines, for the seed is only revealed within the female's intestines to spread into the image of man. But if these are from the higher levels, where is the place where this image was carved and spread within the "bosom of the waters"? 

If you say it was within the "Female" <note>referring to the Sephirah of Malchut or the "World to Come" (Binah)</note>, it is not so, for the form and image were not revealed until they went out to the lower ones, male, and were later completed. Furthermore, the "World to Come" already existed at the time it was written:
> And God said, Let there be light, and there was light (Genesis 1:3)

"Let there be a firmament" — this was the warmth. If you say it was like the lower female, it is not so, for she did not yet exist, and all this Image of Man emerged with her. The Image of Man was not revealed in this way. If so, in what place was this seed revealed and manifested? In the "intestines" of the body of the Image of Man. Rather, this is the spirit of **Primordial Man** <note>original: *Adam Kadma'ah* — the first and highest spiritual stage of creation</note> that was revealed and completed without a second female. The brain and the seed of this one were engraved and revealed within the female. 

The Primordial Man, the engraving of the form and the image of the body, was not like a female and was without a female at all. It was revealed and engraved below from the World to Come without male or female. For those lower ones, they were completed within the **Thought** <note>original: *Machshava* — the divine consciousness where all things are first conceived</note> and revealed and engraved as the spirit of Man. They were in a straight path like the arrangement of the tongue. From the spirit of the Primordial Light, they rose to be revealed and to be formed for the lower ones, and they returned that light as a reflection within the Thought. Everything that was stretched within the Thought returned from it into the "Brain," and the firmament spread out in the form of the Image of Man as is fitting. 

After the Female was adorned for him and they were arranged face-to-face, this Image of Man entered into a desire for the Female, and there he was engraved and revealed in his own likeness, and concerning this it is written:
> And he begot in his own likeness, after his image (Genesis 5:3)

This was revealed within the female, which was not the case with that first one <note>the Primordial Adam</note> who was revealed within that first reflection according to his measures in the Thought, as has been said. In this manner it is below. Below, what is written?
> And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain (Genesis 4:1)

The "stench of the ape" <note>The "stench of the ape," referring to the impurity of Cain's soul origin.</note> was brought to the birth by the action of the constellation and the help of Adam. Afterward, the female received from this "ape," and therefore it does not say "and he begot," but rather "and he knew, and she conceived, and she bare," and the dross emerged within the female.
> And she again bare his brother Abel (Genesis 4:2)

And regarding him, it also does not say "and he begot," even though he was from the side of the male. But the accuser, the serpent, came and cast **husks** <note>קליפין - shells/husks of impurity.</note> for they rose up without end.

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the primordial generations from the Book of Genesis, specifically focusing on the lineage from Seth to Noah and the restoration of the world’s spiritual form. It transitions into a discussion on the laws of the table and the blessing over bread.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The lower world was ready to give birth. Once the dross <note>spiritual impurities or "husks"</note> was observed at the beginning below, it was ready to give birth from the secret of **Seth** <note>Hebrew: *Sheth*</note>, who was the restoration of male and female in a single union. And then it is written, *he begot in his own likeness, after his image* <note>Genesis 5:3</note>, and it is written *and he called* <note>Hebrew: *Vayikra*</note> and not *and she called*. He called him, and not she. He called his name Seth, the restoration of male and female as one, in a single union. Furthermore, they sparkled below and returned to give birth in place of Adam, and these are the two ends of heaven. And these are three, and later seven, and not five, for the [letter] *He* was removed from the Palace <note>Hebrew: *Heikhal*</note>; because of this, the letter *Chet* was nullified, followed by the *Zayin*, and it ended in the confusion of the letter *He* and he was called **Enosh**. 

What is the difference between the name Enosh and the name Adam? Rather, Enosh was not in the strength of the first restoration. As Rabbi [Simeon] said: *What is man <note>Hebrew: Enosh</note> that You are mindful of him?* <note>Psalms 8:5</note>. It is written: *You visit him every morning and test him every moment* <note>Job 7:18</note>. And regarding this it is written, "Woe to the desire," for all these things are the breaking of the body and the strength of the palm. The portion of Seth to Enosh was an inheritance that he was meant to receive, and it is like the hollow of the palm. Furthermore, they sparkled below to fix the crookedness and returned to give birth to **Kenan**, who is the restoration of Cain; he was restored beneath him, and they returned below to sustain the worlds from the crookedness that existed. **Mahalalel** is the lower end of Adam, the *He* for the restoration of the lower Palace. And because there was no humility in Cain, they did not change below except for one side. And later, the two ends of the *He* were for the vessels of restoration until the world was established and the crookedness from the impurity of Enosh was fixed—except for the filth of Adam, which was not settled until Israel stood at Mount Sinai. 

The darkness was the restoration of the crookedness of Cain, and in everything the whole world was restored and established, even in youth and sorrow, until the restoration of which it is written: *This one will comfort us from our work and from the toil of our hands, because of the ground which the Lord has cursed* <note>Genesis 5:29, referring to Noah</note>. Up to here, he returned to be restored as before. 

And now, my masters, here is the general rule: in all the ways I have recounted, I have not merited to know the wisdom, and I was troubled here, and I said that the inhabitants of this land are simpletons in their holes, and it weighed upon me that I did not speak words of Torah before the Master of all this. He removed the greenness <note>pallor/sickness</note> and rest, and these things were completed. Blessed is my lot that you have been removed to here. Rabbi Yose raised his voice in prophecy, and they all stood and kissed him on his head. Rabbi Yose said: Blessed is our lot that we have merited on this path to hear words of the **Ancient of Days** <note>term for the highest aspect of Divinity</note> from your mouth, which we have not merited to hear until now. They all sat. He said to them: My masters, since I see the youth before me, and I have clarified the fine points and guarded them like a vault, for I did not know the **Blessing of the Food** <note>Grace after meals/Birkat Hamazon</note>. I said to them: until this Blessing of the Food is clarified, I will not turn to the wisdom of all the people of the world; and even though I am able to taste everything, I do not wish to transgress their opinion, since I was not able to say anything for two days. Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Hiyya rejoiced, and they stood and prepared and covered the gathering before him. Rabbi Yose said: In a moment, as soon as you have forgiven us, give us bread; blessed is our lot like the living mountain.

->He opened for him<-

with the Blessing of the Food and said: One verse says, *And you shall eat before the Lord your God* <note>Deuteronomy 14:23</note> and another verse says, *And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God* <note>Deuteronomy 16:11</note>. Thus all of Israel are seen before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and they were sustained. Now, how are they sustained? Can a man eat "before the Lord" and rejoice "before the Lord"? Rather, certainly it is so: initially, when a man sits at the table to eat, he blesses **"Hamotzi"** <note>The blessing: "Who brings forth bread from the earth"</note>. What is the reason it says *Hamotzi* <note>with the definite article "the"</note> and not *Motzi* <note>without "the"</note>? For it is written, *Creator of the heavens* <note>Isaiah 42:5</note> and it is not written *The Creator*. It is written *Maker of earth* <note>Psalms 146:6</note> and it is not written *The Maker of earth*. What is the reason here it is *Hamotzi*? Rather, all things that are from the secret of the Upper World are hidden; the letter *He* is removed from them so they are not seen, for that world is concealed and hidden.

->And in all<-

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the mystical dimensions of the Tabernacle (Terumah), specifically transitioning into the spiritual requirements of the table and the Grace After Meals (Birkat HaMazon). It connects the physical act of eating to the Sefirotic realms of Chesed (Mercy) and the Right Side.</meta>

## Terumah

->**Terumah (Contribution)**<-

And all things that are from the lower world are more revealed, as it is written: "Thus" <note>original: *Koh*</note>, as it is written <note>Exodus 25:31-40</note> regarding the Menorah, according to the number of all the holy things. To whom does it face? It is from the spirit of the lower world, and it is a living being <note>original: *Chayah*</note>, as it is written that it is like an attachment; it is "Thus" <note>*Koh*</note>, just as "The Great" <note>referring to the Great Name or Great Mercy</note>.

And the secret of the bosom is in a hidden silence <margin>in order to be revealed</margin> from the spirit of the lower world. Once a person recites a blessing, the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the feminine, indwelling aspect of God</term> comes before him. And as for what is said <note>Deut. 14:23</note>, "And you shall eat before the Lord your God," here it is gathered to speak words of freedom, for so it is necessary to learn before Him to fulfill what is written <note>Ezekiel 41:22</note>, "This is the table that is before the Lord."

And it is written, "And you shall eat there before the Lord your God." Since a person offers praise before his Master, he must show grace to the poor and give to them, just as He gives to him to eat; like one who eats before the Holy King. And it is necessary that nothing [wasteful or unholy] be found upon his table, for then the blessing would be from the "Other Side" <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of evil or impurity</term>, and that spirit says <note>Gen. 25:30</note> "Feed me" <note>original: *Hal'iteini*, associated with Esau's gluttony</note>. Every person must [be careful], and it is written, "And the Lord your God shall bless you." You might think [this applies even to] a merchant, but it is written "And you shall eat before the Lord your God," and not before the Other Side. And it is necessary not to engage in idle words [during the meal].

And regarding the blessing of the meal, it is well. All words of freedom [should be spoken], for when words of freedom are said over the table, the Holy One, blessed be He, gives powerful strength to his portion. And the "Soul before the Lord" is like the Cup of Blessing <term>Kos Shel Beracha: the cup of wine over which Grace is recited</term>. When a person blesses over the Cup of Blessing, he must rejoice and show gladness, and no sadness at all. Since it is written regarding the Cup of Blessing, the Holy One, blessed be He <note>Kadosh Barukh Hu</note>, speaks of the prophet, and he must wrap his head in joy. And to bless over the cup with the goodness of three things: his food, his destiny <note>mazal</note>, and in his wrapping of life. This requires the will of the Supernal, toward the Ancient of Ancients <term>Atika d'Atikin: the most hidden, ancient aspect of the Divine</term>, and concerning Him, it is in hidden silence.

And [we say] "In His goodness" <note>original: *u-ve-tuvo*</note> and not "From His goodness" <note>original: *mi-tuvo*</note>. "In His goodness" refers to the Right Side <term>Yamina: the side of Mercy/Chesed</term> of the world, while "From His goodness" refers to another level that comes from the Right Side, which is a lower level. Because through that "Good," the world was gathered and by it, it is nourished. And its strength is called "Good" <note>Tov</note> and its delights are called "Mercy" <note>Chesed</note>. It is "Good" when it includes all things within itself and does not spread outward below. It is "Mercy" when it descends below and performs kindness for all creatures, for the righteous and the wicked alike; and the Seer and the Pious One are of one level.

From here it is written <note>Psalm 23:6</note>, "Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me." Why "Goodness"? And why "Mercy"? For they go as one. Rather, "Goodness" includes all within it and does not spread below. "Mercy" nourishes and spreads below, nourishing all—righteous and wicked alike—as one. And here, since it says "In His goodness we have lived," it then says "Who nourishes the whole world in His goodness, in Mercy" <note>referring to the liturgy</note>. It turns to <note>Psalm 136:25</note> "He gives bread to all flesh, for His mercy endures forever" <note>original: *Ki L'Olam Chasdo*</note>. And because of this, "He nourishes all," both righteous and wicked; therefore, this is called the Blessing of the Right. This praise is not like [other] blessings of food.

And because of this, the Left should not assist the Right. For once one blesses, he blesses the Right; it is necessary to cleave to the other [side] so that from the Right it is found, and from there it breaks forth to provide nourishment for all. And therefore, the structure of the "Blessing of the Land" requires that one mentions within it the Covenant and the Torah: "For Your covenant which You sealed in our flesh, and for Your Torah which You taught us." This is to show that in that "Good," He sealed the Covenant and the Torah, which is the rectification found in this "Good." From here we learn that [women] are exempt from the Grace After Meals <note>note: a legal discussion regarding the specific phrasing of the liturgy</note> to fulfill their obligation, for they do not [possess the sign of] the Torah and the Covenant. And do not add "For the Land and for the food," for this is a cleaving together in Mercy. "For the Land"—this is the Land of the Living. "And for the food"—this is Mercy. This inclusion of one in the other is like a cleaving that is not a spreading out; it is the "Good" that is born, which is called "Mercy."

And for all this, we thank You, for this and for that, in our completions that are unified from the side of "Good." And "Life shall be wiped out" <unclear>textual variant</unclear>, and "Thus" it is written <note>Psalm 16:11</note>, "Delights are in Your right hand forever." This is from the Right side. It is not so, but rather each and every one looks toward that place from which he emerged. And "Life shall be wiped out" like Noah in his days. It is written "Delights," and it is written <note>2 Sam. 23:1</note> "The sweet singer of Israel," and this is praise...

# Terumah

## Main Text (Zohar)

And every side that is included in the spirit of the **Right** receives a portion and joy from the Right to be strengthened, for from there it emerges. And this is the spreading of **Good** to extend into the path of life. This is because there is no end to be found, for the "Other Side" <note>The *Sitra Achra*, or the realm of impurity</note> has no portion at the time when the Right is awakened. But if one awakens from the Other Side, it awakens with him, and those who are worthy in their blessings find the portion of Jacob. 

Therefore, we give a portion to that Accuser <note>Samael/Satan</note> like water for washing <note>referring to *Mayim Acharonim*, the final waters used to wash hands after a meal to satisfy the "Other Side"</note>. For if there is no filth, there is no portion for that burden which we call "Judgment." Because of this, he has no portion in the foundation and wanders about, having no part in this holiness. For in all his portion, we have no desire to awaken or be attached to him at all, so that the Accuser does not awaken and take two portions—one below and one above—like a firstborn. For we find that those worthy in their blessings belong to Jacob; his portion is below, and the Accuser has nothing above. Israel is nullified above and Esau is nullified below, and therefore he shall not approach to be attached at all to a pure blessing.

Once the blessing is made, the "Other Side" is removed from before the side of the Right, and one receives from the pure source. Then, mercies are stirred for all: *“Have mercy, O Lord our God, upon Israel Your people, and upon Jerusalem Your city...”* <note>original: "Rachem Hashem Eloheinu..." - a central plea in the Grace after Meals</note> for from that purity emerges the removal of the "Other" from before the Holy House. And the Holy Temple shall be built below through those mercies. 

And so that one is not found empty, for what purpose was it built? One prays to say a song of praise and to grant us the fulfillment of both: *the sure mercies of David* <note>Isaiah 55:3</note>. Regarding this, it is said: *“Let not the blessing of an ordinary person be light in your eyes,”* for the song and the thanks are the "mercies of David," and also the "Peace" which we speak of in the exile in the blessing: *“He who makes peace in His heights, may He in His mercy make peace upon us.”* 

**The Good and He who does Good** <note>The fourth blessing of Grace after Meals</note>—everything comes from the side of the Right, and from the side of Samael <note>The Angel of Death/Evil Inclination</note> nothing at all. He who blesses the Grace after Meals takes blessings first from all, to be blessed within the general Grace after Meals, and therefore he possesses the path of life. Sweet words regarding the **Cup of Blessing**: one takes it and blesses over it, as it is written: 
> *I will lift up the cup of salvations* (Psalms 116:13)
What are "salvations"? This is the Right, which saves from all the accusers of the world, as it is written: 
> *His right hand... has worked salvation for Him* (Psalms 98:1)
And it is written: 
> *Save with Your right hand and answer me* (Psalms 60:7) 
For in this way, he is guarded and strikes down those who stand against him. 

Rabbi Yose said: There was a time when a sickness fell upon the city until all the wise men of the town were weakened. This was a sickness of the gut that affected them. They took their wisdom and blessed it with many blessings; they acted so that the sister <note>perhaps a reference to the Shekhinah or a specific soul-root</note> would repair the other side to return in prayer all the wise men of the town to this judgment. They all called out and struck with them all that day, and he called out with them in words of Torah. He opened his discourse at the table and said:

**“And you shall make** the planks for the Tabernacle of acacia wood, standing up” <note>Exodus 26:15</note>. It is written here “standing,” and it is written there: 
> *Seraphim stood above Him* (Isaiah 6:2) 
Just as there they are Seraphim <note>fiery angels</note>, so too here they are like Seraphim. These stand in the rectification of all things, acting as the supports of the Canopy <note>the *Chuppah*</note> to guard within it the secret of the Canopy—the Supernal Spirit. Just as everything below requires the preparation of a beautiful canopy for the glory of the "Other" <note>the Shekhinah</note> to dwell there in the joy of all that is below. 

And for the sake of the glory of that Supernal Bride, one must make a beautiful canopy with every beautiful preparation to invite the Supernal Bride to that joy. In this manner, regarding every type of Covenant <note>the *Brit*</note> below, it must be prepared with beauty to gladden the "Covenant of Existence" <note>the sefirah of *Yesod*</note> that comes there. So too here, every canopy requires beautiful rectifications for the glory of the All, for this is the likeness of the established world. This one rises with **Seven Blessings** <note>the *Sheva Brachot* of a wedding</note>, and that one rises with seven blessings, and the one rises with seven blessings—then she is called "Bride." Therefore, it is forbidden to gaze upon her until she is included in those seven blessings in the supernal likeness. Those seven blessings are the inheritance of the Bride from the Supernal Spirit.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Terumah (The Offering)**<-

The place from which all blessings flow. There are six blessings from which everything is blessed, and you should count them <note>literally: "string them together"</note> as seven. Indeed, the "Oath" <note>Hebrew: *Shevuah*, a wordplay on *Sheva* (Seven)</note> is what sustains everything. The majority of blessings rest upon the foundation <note>the Sefirah of Yesod</note>, which is the side called "Bride" because of that wine which constantly changes its appearance. For this reason, the first blessing of these seven is the mystery of wine. Wine produces fruit both above and below. The Vine <note>the Shekhinah</note> receives everything and brings forth strength to the world, awakening the holiness of the embrace, as it is written:
> His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.
<note>Song of Songs 2:6</note>
"Embraces me." And the moon <note>the feminine divine presence</note> produces fruit and life through this awakening. This is the holy blessing of the Bride. The second is that "everything was created for His glory," the holy male spirit, the holiness of the male who receives all blessings to produce strength in that Vine. For initially, His Kindness <note>Chesed</note> produces fruit like life from above to below, flowing and drawing toward the Holy Covenant <note>the sign of the circumcision/Yesod</note> to include them in that Vine. This is from the Right side, for joy is found on the Right. The Left awakens and the Right acts. To crown the inclusion of the Left within the Right, and from them the soul is established as the Spirit of Kindness <note>Chesed</note>; therefore, the third is "Preserver of Kindness" <note>Exodus 34:7</note>. Jacob is certainly the Central Pillar, the very image of Kindness. The fourth is the pillar of the right thigh <note>Netzach</note>. The fifth... <note>The text here describes the gathering of the holy household from the four sides of the world</note>... this is the spirit of the other thigh <note>Hod</note>, which is sold like the left thigh to provide and gather from all sides... The sixth is "You shall surely open" <note>Deuteronomy 15:8</note>, the place of authority... where the Pillar of the World is found, who is called the Righteous One <note>Tzadik/Yesod</note>. The Righteous One and Righteousness <note>Tzadik and Tzedek</note> are companions and friends, waiting for one another for this delight. Up to here are the six blessings from which the Bride is blessed. The "Oath" <note>the seventh</note> is what sustains the Bride, and from this Oath, all are certainly blessed... for this includes both above and below. Furthermore, it includes the seven merits of the Holy Sabbath... to strengthen the Bride with peace and shepherds, to bring the Bride to her perfection. Worthy are Israel, for they have merited below just as it is above. Concerning them it is written: "And who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth."
<note>1 Chronicles 17:21</note>
They all rejoiced all that day in words of Torah... On another occasion, Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Hiyya stood up, blessed them, and went on their way. When they reached a certain path, [a child] lifted his eyes and saw them. He said to them: "I have been watching you this day, and I have seen you for two days and one night, how you were near the Tabernacle of the Holy One, Blessed be He... high secrets of the Torah were revealed to you, and this is your portion, my sons." They recounted all the matters before him and told him the story. He said to them: "Worthy are you, and worthy is my portion... for all your children are taught of the Lord."
<note>Isaiah 54:13</note>
"And all your children shall be taught of the Lord," etc. All the children of Israel, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives them a portion of the grace of the Torah. For when these children labor in the Torah, the Shekhinah <note>Divine Presence</note> rests upon them and gives them word and strength to know the Torah. For without the help of the Holy One, Blessed be He, those children would not be able to endure it. Rabbi Simeon was present one day at the entrance of Lod, and Rabbi Hiyya was with him. A certain child <note>Yanuka</note> met him. Rabbi Simeon said: "Certainly the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires the world..."

That child said: "It is a wonder in its merit," and they praised them with intention. And what verse arises and stands above them all? And they are certainly "taught of the Lord," and everything from them is with an open eye <note>insight</note> which is not the case for the rest of the world, but for Israel alone, of whom it is written: "And all your children shall be taught of the Lord." And because of this, everything from them is with an open eye. Rabbi Shimon came and kissed him, saying: "From this day I have heard that this son of the opening <note>perhaps a reference to a brilliant student or a specific lineage</note> has a command that is worth a hundred."

And if you say: "But all the hosts of heaven are standing," as it is written: > I will give you a place to walk among these who stand by <note>Zechariah 3:7</note>, for they all have a fixed station and no joints <note>in their legs, meaning they do not sit or kneel</note>, and they all remain standing. It is written: > A Psalm of David. The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want <note>Psalm 23:1</note>. It has already been stated: what is the difference between "A Psalm of David" and "Of David, a Psalm"? Here, the Divine Presence <note>Hebrew: *Shekhinah*</note> preceded him and came and rested upon him first. "The Lord is my shepherd"—and when he saw the Divine Presence first here, David needed to precede it first with Lovingkindness and request sustenance <note>Aramaic: *mezoni*</note> from the Holy One, blessed be He. Because the Holy One, blessed be He, desires to bring down sustenance to the world below, She <note>the Shekhinah</note> precedes first and rejoices in the gift of sustenance for all the worlds. And because of this, She precedes this matter of sustenance and rested upon David. "The Lord is my shepherd"—His will is like this shepherd who leads his flock to a place of delight, to a place where they fear nothing and are covered so that they lack for nothing. So too, the Holy One, blessed be He, is my shepherd to feed me with all that I find and need. Another explanation: "The Lord is my shepherd"—it is taught that a person's sustenance is as difficult before the Holy One, blessed be He, as the splitting of the Red Sea. Here there are two aspects, and both are as one truth. One is because the Holy One, blessed be He, performs all His works with justice <note>Hebrew: *din*</note> and truth, and upon justice and truth the whole world is established. And every single day and at every single time, He judges the whole world with justice—the righteous, the wicked, and all people of the world, as it is written: > The Lord loves righteous deeds <note>Psalm 11:7</note>. And when He judges human beings and the Accuser <note>the *Sitra Achra* or prosecuting angel</note> shows how many are guilty and how many sin before Him, then it is "difficult" in His eyes to give them sustenance at all times, because it is not fitting to feed those who sin. But He acts with them beyond the line of strict justice and feeds and provides for them according to the Lovingkindness from below. And it is done for all people of the world, and through it, He feeds and provides for all—for the righteous, for the pious, and for all people of the world, and for every species and beast from the ends of the heavens, from the horns of the wild oxen to the eggs of lice. And He does not turn away from the world, for He feeds and provides for all, even though it is "difficult" before Him according to the deeds of human beings, like the splitting of the Red Sea. But is the splitting of the Red Sea difficult before Him? Is it not written: > He rebukes the sea and makes it dry <note>Nahum 1:4</note>, and > He calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth <note>Amos 5:8</note>? For as soon as His will arises...

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Terumah (The Offering)** <-

His authority is before Him; everything is before Him, and there is no other. The splitting of the Red Sea was "difficult" before Him, for even at that time, they passed before Him, and the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> desired to split the Red Sea below. This was because the appointed celestial minister over Egypt sought justice before the Holy One, Blessed be He. He said before Him: "Master of the Universe, why do You desire to execute judgment upon Egypt and split the sea for Israel? Behold, they are all guilty before You, and all Your ways are justice and truth. These [the Egyptians] are idolaters, and those [the Israelites] are <term>idolaters</term> <note>original: "Avodah Zarah"</note>. These are guilty of forbidden sexual unions, and those are guilty of forbidden sexual unions. These are shedders of blood, and those are shedders of blood." At that moment, it was "difficult" before Him according to the path of strict justice. And why did He exert Himself for them then? Because of that which is written: *And the Lord said to Moses, "Why do you cry out to Me? Speak to the children of Israel, and let them journey"* <note>Exodus 14:15</note>.

It was difficult before Him to act against strict justice and split the Red Sea for them, until it was revealed that the Holy One, Blessed be He, looked upon the **merit of Abraham**, who had risen early in the morning to perform the command of his Master and His will, as it is written: *And Abraham rose early in the morning* <note>Genesis 22:3</note>. All of them were considered as one day, because throughout that entire night, the Holy One, Blessed be He, was pushing off the matter of Israel. For we have learned: what is the meaning of that which is written, *And one did not come near the other all the night*? <note>Exodus 14:24</note> This teaches that the supernal angels came to offer praise as is the custom of the night before the Holy One, Blessed be He. He said to them: "The works of My hands are drowning in the sea, and you wish to arrange a song before Me?" Thus, *one did not come near the other all the night.*

What is written? *And the angel of God moved...* for the Holy One, Blessed be He, looked upon the merit of Abraham who had preceded in the morning to do the will of his Master, as it is written, *And Abraham rose early in the morning.* Then the sea was stirred and the waters fled before Israel, as it is written: *And the sea returned to its strength at the turning of the morning* <note>Exodus 14:27</note>. And we have learned: "to its strength" <note>Hebrew: "le-eitano"</note> refers to its "condition" <note>Hebrew: "le-tenao"</note>—the condition that the Holy One, Blessed be He, made with the sea when He created the world. It is written here "to its strength" <note>le-eitano</note> and it is written there, *A Maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite* <note>Psalm 89:1; "Ethan" and "Eitano" share a root</note>. Therefore, "at the turning of the morning," when the merit of Abraham arrived to do the will of his Master, then the sea was split here and threw the camp of Egypt into confusion. For this reason, it was "difficult" before Him like the splitting of the Red Sea.

In this same manner, **sustenance** <note>original: "mezonin"</note> is as difficult before the Holy One, Blessed be He, as the splitting of the Red Sea. Just as the splitting of the Red Sea killed these on this side and sustained those on that side, so too it is written: He rebukes the lacking... And we have learned: children, life, and sustenance do not depend on merit, but on **constellation/destiny** <note>original: "mazla"</note>. He gives to those below—to this one who is not worthy, and to another who is righteous He gives from his merits below, and not according to the law of the bosom. All these are hidden mysteries, and what the companions have awakened is certainly so.

Regarding what they awakened concerning "before Me" and "not from before Me": "Before Me" refers to that which stands directly before the Holy One, Blessed be He, prepared before Him. Therefore they said that a person's sustenance is difficult for the Holy One, Blessed be He. It is "before Me" and not "in front of Me" for all these things, because they do not stand according to His will to perform an act of mercy. Rather, even though He performs mercy, He does so according to another will. It is written: *That soul shall be cut off from before Me* <note>Leviticus 22:3</note>. What is "from before Me"? This refers to the **World to Come** <note>original: "Alma de-Atei"</note>, where all the waters stand. <term>Another explanation</term> <note>original: "Davar Acher"</note>: This is the Supernal River whose waters never fail, and everything is enriched by it, for it takes all the delights of the World to Come. Sustenance and supernal delights are prepared in that place... and this is "from before Me."

And if you say: If so, behold it is written, *And Jonah rose up to flee to Tarshish from before the Lord* <note>Jonah 1:3</note>. For the Sages knew that it was "from before the Lord," but he thought... and he fled, etc. Is it possible for a man to flee from before the Holy One, Blessed be He? Rather, he went and fled to leave the Holy Land, for the **Divine Presence** <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> does not dwell outside the Land of Israel. Because he did not want the Shekhinah to rest upon him, he fled from the Holy Land, for the Shekhinah does not dwell there [outside], as you say: *Your wife shall be as a fruitful vine in the innermost parts of your house* <note>Psalm 128:3</note>. The lot went out...

# Terumah

Similarly, below, the fountain never ceases from the gate through which the daughter <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note> is nourished by the holy seed. It is written "from before" and not just "before," or "a voice from before," because the spirit of all does not come from within the Shekhinah herself, but rather "from before" her—from those two levels that, as it were, rest upon the Shekhinah. From that place above, the holy seed is raised up. Regarding this "from before," it is said: "For from before Me the spirit shall fail" <note>Isaiah 57:16; original: *ki milfanai ya'atof*</note>, and not just "before the Lord." For He knows that the sustenance does not come except from "before." Therefore, it is said that a person's sustenance is as difficult <note>original: *kashin*, meaning difficult or weighty</note> before the Holy One, Blessed be He, as the parting of the Red Sea.

King David linked his sustenance to the higher realms because there, it never ceases; but here below, it can be interrupted. Sustenance does not depend on the lower world but on the higher. Thus it is written: "The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want" <note>Psalm 23:1</note>—sustenance shall never cease, because that river which flows and goes out from Eden <note>The flow of divine wisdom/Chokhmah</note> never ceases.

Come and see: when this place <note>the Shekhinah</note> receives sustenance from above, all those who are sanctified for her service are awakened. They raise their wings when the Shekhinah arrives with that sustenance so that they do not gaze upon her. They stand in three sides, and as they rise, one group calls to the other: "Holy." These are the "beams" <note>original: *kerashim*, the wooden beams of the Tabernacle</note> for the second Matron <note>a mystical level of the Divine Presence</note>. They raise their wings—these are the first and these are the second. And after these second ones, these "beams" are holy to the third Matron. They raise their wings on three sides as one, and all of them say: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts, the whole earth is full of His glory" <note>Isaiah 6:3</note>.

They all look at one another, these higher ones and those higher ones, just as it is written: "Each one facing its sister" <note>Exodus 26:3</note>. "So shall you do for all the clasps of the Tabernacle" <note>Exodus 26:11</note>. The clasps <note>original: *karsim*</note> stand perpetually in their positions and do not bend, just as the angels are called "those who stand" <note>Zechariah 3:7</note> because they do not bend; they have no joints and always stand. Thus it is written: "The beams standing up" <note>Exodus 26:15</note>. What is written? "Two tenons for each beam" <note>Exodus 26:17</note>. So too, they are all in two modes, each and every one of them, joined and bonded together.

They are intertwined with one another, as it is written regarding Wisdom: "For her merchandise is better than the merchandise of silver, and her harvest than fine gold" <note>Proverbs 3:14</note>. There is no division or change; they are made to interlock with one another. They are led "beside the still waters" <note>Psalm 23:2</note>. These are the "forces" <note>original: *kochot*</note>, for these are the supernal sources from which all sustenance and satisfaction come. These are called the "forces of Jacob." Do not be surprised that it is written "Let the earth bring forth grass" <note>Genesis 1:11</note>, for that is below, but these "forces" are below only because they are born from the brain of Wisdom. Therefore, "He leads me beside the still waters"—these are the waters of Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note> that flow from that place which "goes out from Eden." These waters are called "still waters" <note>original: *mei menuchot*, literally waters of rests</note> according to their plain meaning. David did not seek to strengthen himself or his level except through these "rests" and "stillnesses" which shine forever to the lower realms, as it is written: "And the Lord shall guide you continually..." <note>Isaiah 58:11</note>.

**And you shall make** fifty clasps of copper... <note>Exodus 26:11</note>
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Abba were sitting one night. Throughout the evening, a scent of the Garden <note>Eden</note> entered the world. They rose and saw two [celestial] lights, as it were, one from here and one from there, and they were praising one another. Rabbi Abba said: "How great are the works of the Holy One, Blessed be He! Like the waters from above and the [earth] from below." They marveled at these two lights that went out, one from here and one from there, praising each other. Rabbi Elazar said: "We have not seen them [directly], but we have found their traces in many other works."

## Main Text (Zohar)

...which the Holy One, blessed be He, does continually. He opened [his discourse] and said: > **"Great is our Lord, and abundant in power..."** <note>Psalm 147:5</note>. May the Holy One, blessed be He, be great, abundant, and strong. But do we not already know that the Holy One, blessed be He, is great and abundant in power? Why did David say this here? Rather, in every place, he says "great and abundant in power" to offer praise for His glory. Just as there where he says > **"Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised"** <note>Psalm 48:2</note>, he stands at a high level <note>referring to a higher Sefirah or spiritual emanation</note>, so too here where it is written "Great is our Lord," he speaks of a lower level <note>the Sefirah of Malkhut/Kingship</note>, for He is the **Master of all the earth** <term>Adon Kol Ha-Aretz: a title for God emphasizing His immanence and rule over the physical world</term>. What is written just before this verse? > **"He counts the number of the stars; He calls them all by their names"** <note>Psalm 147:4</note>. All the people of the world are destined to be created, and all those who intended to count the stars were unable to count them all, as it says: > **"and count the stars, if you are able to count them"** <note>Genesis 15:5</note>. But regarding the Holy One, blessed be He, it is written: "He counts the number of the stars; He calls them all by their names." Why? Because it is written, "Great is our Lord, and abundant in power..." Just as there is no number for the stars of heaven when they are humbled, so too it is written of Him: **"and His understanding is infinite"** <note>literally: "has no number"</note>.

Come and see, it is written: > **"He who brings out their host by number..."** <note>Isaiah 40:26</note>. All the legions, camps, and stars—the Holy One, blessed be He, brings them out by name, each and every one, and not even one is missing. Among all the stars and constellations, even the tiny ones, all are numbered and appointed to sustain <note>original: *le-akma* (to establish/sustain)</note> the world, each one as is fitting for it. There is not a single blade of grass or well in the entire world that does not have a star and constellation ruling over it in the firmament. And over that star, there is one appointed official who serves before the Holy One, blessed be He, each as is fitting for him. All the stars in the firmament serve this world, and all are appointed to measure out every single thing in this world. Herbs, trees, grasses, and wild plants do not sprout or grow except by the power of the stars that stand over them and gaze upon them face-to-face, each one as is appropriate for it. The majority of the stars and constellations go out by the authority of the night until three hours minus a quarter. From then on, they do not go out except for the small ones. And all those stars do not serve in vain, nor do they appear in vain. There are stars that serve all night in order to sprout and grow all those things they are appointed over. And there are stars that serve until midnight, sprouting and growing by the authority of the night until that hour all those things they are appointed over. And there are stars that serve and "speak" <note>perhaps a reference to celestial music or influence</note> between the lower realms, and with that herb... and that one which sleeps for three hours and does not stir further in that night—even those do not stand in vain. Once they have completed their service, they are no longer seen in this world and they enter their place.

In the **Book of Wisdom of the Easterners** <note>Sifra de-Chokhmata de-Bne Qedem: an ancient source often cited in the Zohar for its astrological and botanical lore</note>, they say regarding all those stars of the "extended rod" <note>original: *tarbita* - likely referring to a specific planetary alignment or a "stretching" of light</note> that arrange a path in the firmament: they say there are herbs on earth from those called "medicine of life" and "healing balms," and there are sights on earth that are revealed within the Mountains of Mercy, like water covered by a casing so as not to be moved. The dominion over all these belongs to the stars of the *tarbita*. A window is opened in their gardens, and all their preparation and greatness is only through this, and the height of that *tarbita* which that star arranges in the firmament; then all those things are prepared and grown. There are illnesses in the liver, such as jaundice and *kasterin* <note>likely a Greek-derived medical term for a specific ailment</note>, for which the **healing** <term>Asvata: Aramaic for medicine or healing</term> depends only on a single thing that flies, like a spark... and it has the power to strengthen the sick person. This does not apply until that flying thing passes, and to this side in the manner of the *tarbita*... like a flash of lightning... and in that optimal moment of the lightning... healing comes to him. So too, all those things over which those stars rule have no preparation or greatness in this world except through that extension of the *tarbita*, and through this they are prepared in appearance, such as...

## Main Text (Zohar)

In the same blue manner as below, a vision is woven. For this manner was hinted at in the Book of King Solomon, regarding the wisdom of the precious sages, which was hidden from them—like the manner of the brilliance and flaming of known stars. These stars were not established by them, nor can they ever be fixed by them; rather, they were all established before Him for the restoration of the world, all of them to shine upon the earth as much as is needed to restore this world. It is written:

**And you shall make** fifty copper hooks, and it is written, *And you shall make fifty gold hooks* <note>Exodus 26:11 and 26:5</note>. We have learned: whoever has not seen those hooks has never seen the light of the stars in the firmament, because that vision and that manner resemble them to anyone who gazes upon them. Living stars in their firmament emerge from that firmament where all the stars shine. In that firmament, there are fifty <note>original: "חמש" (five), but contextually "חמשים" (fifty) based on the hooks</note> windows that are recessed, some on the eastern side and some on the southern side. In each and every window, there is one star. All the nations see through those windows and recesses in the firmament, which are like stars. And those stars emerge to be revealed from that gathering which was gathered and mixed in a blue manner; some are green like the color of gold, and therefore some are red and some are green. There are fifty in those windows on the other sides: on the eastern side they are green, and on the southern side they are red, like the initial redness that is found. All those stars that emerge from that firmament mingle at night, and they flame and rule in this world. Some rule over the blue and some over the green gold, and they are established and lead according to their power. These stars rule here and there <note>original: "פלוני" (so-and-so/specific place)</note> like the loops of the curtains for those moments of the hour. And those that lead the blue, they are like hooks and flame; and if their vision is seen three times on the eastern side, or five, or seven—kings of the nations will come against that side, and all wealth and gold will be removed from that side. But if they gather two, four, or six, one after the other, then wrath and visitation will fall and dwell upon that side with a good gathering and clarity. Wars will be stirred up but will not be carried out, for at that time there is an awakening above before the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> <note>original: קב"ה</note> regarding those ministers who rule over the other nations; and so it is in this manner on the other side.

He opened and said:
> Let the name of God be blessed from eternity to eternity, for wisdom and might are His. <note>Daniel 2:20</note>

And He changes the times and the seasons, and all visions are like His garment. He uncovers the deep shell <note>original: קליפא (Kliphah) - the "husk" or "shell" of impurity in Kabbalah</note> from the sand and the crushing of the stars, and fills them, because those others are a burden; but not so is the Portion of Jacob, for He is the Creator of all. There is a firmament above all these firmaments, a hidden and concealed life. And wonder of wonders <note>original: גנוטפכא (a cryptic Zoharic term for a hidden treasure or vessel)</note> is found ruling over this firmament, and this firmament is called the "Skin of the Tabernacle." In this firmament are all those windows from this side and that side, and all those arrangements are strictly ordered. There are six windows that are greater than all of them, and one stands to rule over them. One window is called the "Window of the Double Cave" <note>original: וכיף כפלא (resembling Machpelah)</note>; one star is engraved to be seen there, and this is a living opening to receive from the flow below, like the sovereignty of Judah. The other nations have no portion in it, for the tribes of Israel have no portion or inheritance in them <note>the other stars</note>, except for the tribe of Judah who rules over this. And they are like hooks upon it, and all the kindness of Judah is to distance it from the Holy Crown <note>original: כתר (Keter)</note>. The Holy One, Blessed Be He, began to make known the <term>Crown</term> <note>The highest of the ten Sefirot, representing Divine Will</note> of this window. And the star stands in its fullness, for this is what gathers the rest of the nations, as it is written of him: *he shall go like a city of your grace* <note>alluding to the strength of Judah</note>. They give to him service and worship, and concerning this it is written:
> Then Judah approached him. <note>Genesis 44:18</note>

He drew near between them, for when this star emerges, it spreads one hand with five fingers, shining and gathering into that window.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of celestial mysteries within the portion of Terumah, specifically detailing the seven "windows" (Chalonot) in the heavens and the stars that emerge from them to govern earthly affairs. ## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Terumah**<-

The masters of sorcery and divination <note>original: "qosemin ve-chartin"</note> are seized by this place, for at the time when this [celestial power] rules, they all stand in confusion and their divinations do not succeed in their hands. And if you say: that hidden spirit which is seen in the firmament, how do they know it? Rather, they have a sign outside, and they know that this one rules over all of them, and this is born constantly from here, and those sorceries and divinations do not succeed in their hands. And yet there are times when people follow it, and times when they do not. Because of this, those masters of sorcery and divination are diminished in their works, because they do not know the root when they are struck so that [the power] does not succeed in their hands. Regarding this, the ancients knew and looked outward at that sign which they knew.

**The second window** is called the "Nail Window" <note>original: "Chalon Tofra"</note> because it is shaped like a fingernail. Through it emerges a single star which the wise call "The Scatterer," for it rules with a powerful dominion like a hammer. In its secret and its movement, it has sparks like a collection of smithereens. From that window emerge six hundred thousand hidden spirits that rule over the fingernails of people when they are thrown away, as is revealed in this; through these, the sorcerers and diviners perform their works, all those who know them. At the time when this star rules, all those who throw away their nail parings cause sorcery to bring death to the entire world, and the sorcery succeeds in the hands of those who perform it.

**The third window** is called the "Altar Window." Through it emerges a single star called Binah <note>The text reads "NB"Ch," but a note suggests it should be "Binah," meaning Understanding</note> which is hidden. This is like a building, and it stands over every spirit and direction, and merit is found within it. There is no accusation <note>prosecuting angel</note> in it at all. When it rules, all rest and all light rule in the world, great goodness, and all [blessings] rule in the world.

**The fourth window** is the window called "The Gaze" <note>original: "Navit"</note>. Through it emerges a single star which the wise call "The Inverse," because it is bent like a hook, with broken structures like spiders or like blossoms. Through this, love is awakened in the world, distancing and bringing near the offspring of those who serve [the idols of] deficiency in the world. The people of the world are not careful when they are needed and do not rule, and from this, [strife] is awakened in the world.

**The fifth window** is the window called "In the Sea" <note>original: "Be-Char"</note>. Regarding the star that emerges through it, it rises and bends so that it never rules. In this, the wise of heart cannot stand upon the true appearance, because it does not remain in its standing and is never still. And they still labor in their deceptions to gaze into this place, but there is nothing to learn.

**The sixth window** is the window called "The Gathering" <note>original: "Kanacha"</note>. Through it emerges a single star called "The Throat" <note>original: "Giron"</note>, because all its rule over the world is harsh, with many decrees and many punishments. Each and every kind of decree is renewed upon the world, and before these are finished, others are renewed. This rule does not [usually] stand in the world. All this is close to the days of the Messiah, and this long [star] rules like this star over the world. And because of this, the masters of divination will be despised in the world, and evil types [of decrees] will be renewed one after another, and they will be troubled in their hardships. All will be crushed within the darkness. Then the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>, will prepare for them a light that will wipe them out, and the high holy ones will receive the kingdom. And then **the seventh window** will open to all the world, and its star will shine to the four corners. And when the King Messiah is revealed, all the nations of the world will gather to the King Messiah, then the scripture will be fulfilled as it is written:

> **"And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious."** <note>Isaiah 11:10</note>

He opened and said: He did not say it except to the one whose eyes are fixed on the melodies of all. This verse has been established and explained. Everything requires great strength <note>original: "azti"</note>, but the medicine of the birth, the medicine of everything, is to prepare the beginning and its house of judgment. This is a complete medicine that includes male and female... He established all the melodies because she is the one who constantly praises the King of the world, like a gathering that is never still, in order to receive the holy light upon all the teachings.
