<meta>This page continues the discussion of the spiritual mechanics of the night, specifically focusing on the transition from the songs of the stars to the emergence of the "Other Side" (Sitra Achra) and how both angels and Israel must navigate this impurity to reach the Divine.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Joy. And all those songs of all those stars that shine in the firmament, all of them go and praise the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note> throughout the entire time they are visible in the firmament. Because the high angels all go and praise and say songs of praise during the three watches of the night. At night, many sides are divided under the authority of the Night; when He signals to the Night, all those evil spirits and evil judgments are drawn out, spreading and roaming throughout the entire world. The "Other Side" <note>The *Sitra Achra*, representing the forces of impurity or evil</note> separates itself and prepares its nets <note>or "traps"</note> away from the King’s palace and from all those holy sides. Once that Other Side is awakened, all the inhabitants of the world taste the taste of death <note>A reference to sleep being one-sixtieth of death</note>, as it hovers over them and ascends upon them. Then, since they find themselves separated above, and they rule and descend below, they then divide into three sides to oppose the Holy One, blessed be He, corresponding to the three watches of the night as they are all awakened. While they find the Holy One, blessed be He, the Other Side goes and roams below in all the regions of the world. And until the Other Side is removed from there, they cannot unite with their Master—a spirit for the wise. The high angels and Israel below all press against that Other Side. When the high angels desire to unite with their Master, they cannot until they push her <note>the Other Side</note> outside. What do they do? They produce sparks of fire—those holy angels—and they sweep goodness over all the inhabitants of the world. And when they push her outside and give her this world with that "goodness" <note>referring to the physical husks or distractions</note>, then they ascend and receive additional holiness. Except for Israel alone, over whom she does not rule, because she is separated from them; they look toward their Master, praising and trembling before Him. In this same manner, Israel below cannot unite with their Master until they push that Other Side away from them and give her a portion <note>A reference to certain rituals, like the scapegoat or the washing of fingers, intended to "bribe" the accuser</note> as has been explained, so that those who draw near to their Master are divided and no accuser is found above or below. And if you say, "That is fine for below, but above, what accusation could there be?" Rather, above, because it is an impure spirit, and those are holy spirits—until they remove the impure spirit from among them, they cannot draw near to their Master, for the Holy One, blessed be He, never mixes with impurity. And so it is for Israel below. Both sides, above and below, when they seek to draw near to the Holy King, push her outside. At the onset of the night, when the holy high angels arrange themselves in rows upon rows to draw near to their Master, they push that Side outside as before and perform the will of the Holy One, blessed be He. Therefore, when night begins, all the evil spirits, sparks, and judgments are made impure and appear outside, and they squeeze the heavenly kingdom within the holiness. This is like a King who had precious wise men and many treasures engraved in chests. And that King was wise; so that no one would approach the King's hidden treasures—the chests of the precious wise men where the "dew of wisdom" is stored—he placed a powerful serpent <note>original: *chivya*</note> in his wisdom, and it coiled around that chest. Anyone who sought to stretch out his hand toward the chest, this serpent would fall upon him and kill him. The King had one friend; the King said to him, "Whenever you wish to enter and use the chest, do such-and-through to that serpent, and you shall open the chest and use my hidden treasures." So the Holy One, blessed be He, coiled the "husk" of the Holy Chariot <note>The *Merkavah* or Divine Assembly</note> below, and the high angels above within the holiness—behold, the serpent is there, and it is difficult to look upon it. And if you say, "Behold, they all sin and do not receive their lack," come and see what is written:
> "He makes the winds His messengers, flaming fire His ministers" <note>Psalms 104:4</note>
"He makes the winds His messengers"—these are the angels who stand outside. "Flaming fire His ministers"—these are the angels who stand within the serpent, the impure spirits, and they are spirits. Spirit does not enter into spirit; an impure spirit and a holy spirit do not mix.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->Terumah<-

They are intermingled with one another, and likewise, those who are darkened <note>original: "קדרין", referring to those in spiritual darkness or distress</note> are unable to enter within because that entrance is narrow. Those who are within are in grace and mercy, and in that grace, it resembles that entrance which does not lean inward. Because of this, they are all pushed outside so as not to mingle with them. On account of this, they wait for the living; they stand poor before **the Holy One, Blessed Be He** <term>Kadosh Baruch Hu: The standard rabbinic name for God</term>, who is the Crown that is likened to the outer key. Three shofars <note>ritual rams' horns</term> are included corresponding to them, three sides that are divided just as they are below. And concerning the desire of them all, it is a mercy like that of David, who did not rely on the worlds; mercy is a constant joy, and he finds the Supernal King. In his hand, he prepared songs included in this, and he did not say to Him "God of my strength" as it is below, because from above and below they were included together.

And it is made like a canopy, a body from two sides, from male and female. So too is the spirit, a living spirit included from male and female. On account of this, the male was established when the throne was engraved like a body and a spirit. And because life is included in this spirit, and like this action as it is below, until he comes and returns in perfection like a single branch, like a whisper, like our likeness. And here below, it is included, saying this is like it is below at night. All those types of evil spirits are awakened in the world; how can life be pushed away? We have learned that from the side of the North <note>The North is associated with Gevurah/Judgment</note> emerge all types of evil spirits. And come and see, **Rabbi [Abba]** said that when it is spread at the division of the night, then all those evil spirits and evil sides gather and are cast down from above into the hole of the Great Abyss. If so, it is from the side of the South <note>The South is associated with Chesed/Mercy</note> that life is on the right, for from the side where evil types live, the South wind does not rule. But certainly, were it not for that side of the South which withholds and subdues that evil side, the whole world would be blurred, and the world would not be able to endure the destruction. But the awakening of that side of fear <note>The North/Left side</note> awakens only by the side of the West wind which rules there. And the life of the world is gathered and precedes to help the world in this manner, just as it is below.

Happy are Israel in this world and in the world to come, for **the Holy One, Blessed Be He** <term>Kadosh Baruch Hu</term> desired them out of all the other nations of the world. He gave His name to the **Assembly of Israel** <term>Knesset Yisrael: The mystical personification of the Jewish people, often identified with the Shekhinah</term> and cherished her. Here, when the night is divided, it is known as the whiteness. **Rabbi Abba** said: Now certainly it is the time of the delight of **the Holy One, Blessed Be He**, and many visions are mingled. This is for **the Holy One, Blessed Be He** at the hour when the night is divided; He enters among those righteous in the **Garden of Eden** to take delight in them. Happy is he who delights in the soul <insert>to labor in the Torah</insert> at this time.

**Rabbi Eleazar** said: This delight that **the Holy One, Blessed Be He** takes among the righteous in the **Garden of Eden**—how does He delight? Rather, at that time when the night is divided, He is awakened with love for the planting toward the **Assembly of Israel**. For there is no love except from the **Left Side** <term>Sitra d'Smala: The side of Judgment/Gevurah, which provides the "fire" for passion</term>, and the Assembly of Israel has no breath or good satisfaction except through those spirits of the righteous. For **the Holy One, Blessed Be He** stands before them, crowned with many good deeds and many merits. And this approach and zeal is more pleasing to Him than all sacrifices and burnt offerings, for **the Holy One, Blessed Be He** carves in them a pleasing aroma that Israel produces. Then the light is illuminated, and all those in the **Garden of Eden** say a song, and the righteous are crowned there with those delights of the world to come. When one is awakened at that hour, his portion is canceled with the righteous who are built in the Garden. One struck Name and thirty-two letters are awakened there, and life is within the secrets of the righteous. He opened and said: <note>Psalm 111:1</note> > Hallelujah! I will praise the Lord with all my heart < etc. It was said and the companions were awakened by it. And such is the life of this mercy, a praise that rises above all those songs and praises that David said in the crown of praises. He said that it includes everything and is found as one, and all of it is the **Holy Name** <term>Shema Kadisha</term> that rises. "Praise the Lord with all my heart"—after this, King David said the spirit of the Alphabet.

## Main Text (Zohar)

The house is a vision of the lower spirit, engravings that emerge through the engravings of the thirty-two paths <note>The 32 paths of Wisdom (Chokhmah) from the Sefer Yetzirah</note>. Over them is the spirit from the supernal world; it descends to the four spirits which are the "Tannin" <note>serpents/monsters</note> and the "Watchers." And thus is the vision of the spirit that passes through the house of the lower world. And this is "with all your heart" <note>Deut 6:5</note>, with the good inclination and the evil star <note>the evil inclination</note> which are hidden away. For over everything, one must give thanks to the Holy One, blessed be He, for the good and for the bad. Just as the hand that comes from the right side is good, and good comes to every cup, and one must bless the Holy One, blessed be He, with the "Good and Beneficent" blessing. And from the left side comes the evil, and the accusation comes to every cup, and one must give thanks to the Holy One, blessed be He, for the bad just as for the good, in everything that comes upon a person from this side and from that side. "His glory shall recognize them and the congregation." In the secret of "they shall depart by their tongue," for they knew the Holy One, blessed be He, for they knew all the secrets. And they are the spirit that learns. And regarding "glory, sufferings, and the congregation," these are the "sufferings of love" <note>term: sufferings of love (yissurin shel ahavah) - trials sent by God to a righteous person to increase their merit</note> when they gather in the flock to give thanks to the Holy One, blessed be He, and with every living thing to give thanks to the Holy One, blessed be He, for the good and for the evil, and to publicize everything. For if you say the heart speaks, it knows and lives, for it is necessary to publicize it. For then the Holy One, blessed be He, is honored in the world by publicizing how much. And regarding the Holy One, blessed be He, it is written: "And I will magnify Myself, and sanctify Myself, etc." <note>Ezekiel 38:23</note>. Rabbi Yehuda said: What is the meaning of that which is written, "Let every soul praise the Lord" <note>Psalm 150:6</note>? Because with the breath, all souls are given from this holy body, and they are stirred like the children of the throne, and they move from that place which is called "the Hand of the Lord" from this place. Rabbi Yehuda said: It is written, "How manifold are Your works, O Lord! In wisdom You have made them all" <note>Psalm 104:24</note>. Come and see, from this Wisdom which gathers the pulses into the thirty-two paths, everything was perfected, both all that is above and all that is below. And behold, the Holy Spirit was established, for all spirits were included in it. Come and see, Rabbi Isaac said: In the days when Rabbi Shimon explained this matter, clouds like water appeared, and he would say: All the treasures of the Supernal King are guarded as one key and are hidden in the chest of the "Korditi" <note>likely a reference to a specific celestial chamber or vessel</note> with engravings upon them. But thus, who is able to recognize and to be included in what the prophet saw from the outside? For Moses did not reveal this in his days when he revealed the secret of death to Israel, even though they were all complaining against him. But at that hour when the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to bring him up to the Supernal Holy Academy and to bring him in from the "Many," as it is written: "I am a hundred and twenty years old today; I can no longer go out and come in" <note>Deut 31:2</note>. For on that day his time was completed to draw near to this place, as it is written:
> Behold, your days approach that you must die (Deuteronomy 31:14)

> And Moses died there (Deuteronomy 34:5)
Thus in every place, regarding the righteous, it calls it "death." What is "death"? From our side it is called so. For it was taught: Rabbi Shimon said, and so it is here, that he who passes like the lamps of the holy faith, it is suspended in him. Death is not suspended in him, and he did not die, just as it was with Jacob, in whom there was the perfection of faith. For Rabbi Shimon said: "Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name," and He called his name Israel <note>Gen 35:10</note>. What is "Israel"? The perfection of all, as it is written:

He said to him: Yes, for "with me" is not written, but rather "for I am with you," for from his strength he comes to be joined, his dwelling with him. <note>gloss: Rabbi Abba said well</note> For behold, "And Jacob shall return, and shall be quiet, and at ease, and none shall make him afraid." "And Jacob shall return" to draw near in security. He said, as it is written: "Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel." This is because Jacob is in the place below, and from there he goes out in this world, and is "at ease" in the World to Come. "And none shall make him afraid"—from the Angel of Death, for from him everything was covered. Rabbi Isaac said: This conclusion they established, as it is written: "And your seed from the land of their captivity"—just as his seed is alive, so too he is alive.

**Rabbi Yehuda opened** his discourse: "Happy are you, O land, when your king is a free man and your ministers eat at the proper time." And it is written: "Woe to you, O land, when your king is a youth and your ministers eat in the morning." These verses have been established according to their interpretation. Rabbi Yose said: Do they not gaze upon the nation as the mouth of the Matron <note>The *Matronita*, a term for the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note>? For the Matron goes on their behalf to the accounting and merits before them the words of the Torah, yet they do not gaze. For we have learned one foundation: a man is required to perform three things for his son: circumcision, redemption <note>The *Pidyon HaBen* or redemption of the firstborn</note>, and to compel him toward the Torah; and likewise for Israel. Regarding circumcision, it is written: "And the good fortune of the group," and regarding Israel it is written: "And so on the eighth day shall every male among you be circumcised." Regarding redemption, it is written: "And the <term>Lord</term> <note>original: *YHVH*</note> your God redeemed you from the hand of Pharaoh, king of Egypt." And regarding compelling him toward the Torah, it is written: "Male and female He created them," and it is written: "And God blessed them and said to them: Be fruitful and multiply." Furthermore, He carries them like that eagle who carries its young on its wings, as it is written: "And I bore you on eagles' wings."

**Then Rabbi Yose said:** She is a bride and a crown to the whole Torah, to return before Israel and to apportion to them more than a bride. Come and see: there is no praise of the male like this world, and in the world to come, the Torah is the joy, as it is written: "By me kings reign." For we have learned that Rav Huna disagreed there; he found the Rabbis who were expounding this verse: "And I will punish all the oppressors and I will take his swallow out of his mouth, and the nations shall no longer flow to him." But Rav Huna did not pay attention to it, for it was not known to him at first because he was small. Until he went to the House of Study and found the Rabbis saying: This verse must be looked into, whether the goodness and the portion of the star is like kindness, for it is blind; all this is written in it, and regarding the latter over the former, for all is mine, to be clarified as my portion. And furthermore: "And I will take his swallow out of his mouth."

Rav Huna stood between the pillars and saw the vision of Huna like two rows of teeth for this verse. They did not pay attention to him. He stood a second time and said this word. Rabbi Yolchi bar Rav came and his appearance was before him. He said: I have seen a spring of the sea for the words of Torah; it is written: "A priest like the right-hand runner shall be called," etc.

**He opened and said: Thus we have learned:** In the early days, before Jacob came, a man would be sneezing in his house and his time would pass, and he would die without illness. When Jacob came, he prayed before the <term>Holy One, blessed be He</term> <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note>, the Master of the Universe: "If it is pleasing before You, let a man be weakened by illness for two or three days, so that he may speak to his children and command his household and return in repentance." He said to him: "You have spoken well, and you shall be a sign for the world." Come and see what is written of him:

> "And it came to pass after these things, that one told Joseph: Behold, your father is sick."
<note>Genesis 48:1</note>

Is it not written what had never happened to a man before this? After it was written, there was no man who had illnesses and did not die until Hezekiah came. What is written of him?

> "In those days Hezekiah was sick unto death..."
<note>II Kings 20:1</note>

Come and see what is written: "And Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the <term>Lord</term>." He said to Him: "Is it pleasing before You that men should recover from their illnesses, so they may know Your name and recognize You and return afterward in complete repentance, and praise You in this world and stand before You?" The <term>Holy One, blessed be He</term>, said to him: "It is a merit; you shall be a sign for the world." And so it was, for it was not so previously. "The writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he had been sick, and was recovered of his sickness." And we have learned: At that time the sun returned ten degrees. And you should know that for their entire dwelling, they would eat every day at the fourth hour, and they would rest until the ninth hour, and it was comfortable until the fourth hour; when he looked, he saw the hour was like all the hours. He said: This is like the knot of the binder... They said to him...

...darkness, and until it shines, that which rules does not rule. Come and see, the Rabbi said:

holy Jacob, the "perfect man," as we have established, for it is written: <note>Genesis 25:27</note> **"And Jacob was a

for he takes hold of this side and that side, to show that he is the "middle" [bolt]; he is "perfect," as the Aramaic translation renders it: "complete"—complete on every side,
between the two sides of the *Ancient Holy One* <note>Atik Kadisha/Keter</note> and the *Lesser Countenance* <note>Zeir Anpin</note>. He is complete between Supreme Lovingkindness <note>Chesed</note> and Supreme Power <note>Gevurah</note>,
taking hold of this side and that side. And the secret of the matter is that *Wisdom* <note>Chokhmah</note> includes everything. From the Supreme Flowing Source, Wisdom emerges.
Power <note>Gevurah</note>, which comes forth with strength, emerges from *Understanding* <note>Binah</note>. Jacob takes hold of both sides. Just as Wisdom includes
everything, so Jacob includes the Patriarchs. Come and see: now, when Wisdom shines and is gathered into the Spirit—which is [the Spirit] that does not change
its waters—into one place, to open the fifty gates of Understanding, paths emerge and are crowned in two
[directions], in greatness and glory, and the crowns and the two paths are sent forth. When that Spirit is in the midst of the paths,
and the fifty gates of Understanding are opened, the crowns and the two [paths] are drawn through the fifty gates toward the "Dove" <note>a symbol for the Shekhinah or the community of Israel</note>,
and they are crowned with the seventy-two letters of the Holy Name. These open to the sides and these crowns are crowned,
and the two [paths] in the two [aspects] of Mercy are included in the *Ancient of Days* <note>Atik Yomin</note>, who shines for them, each on its side.
And the fifty engravings are crowned, just as they are holy in their hearts; the Name and the Gate are joined. And there are drawn
into their bodies eight gates which are the "perfect ones," which are of Mercy, as it is written: <note>Exodus 34:6</note> **"The Lord, the Lord, God, merciful and gracious,"**
which emerges from the Ancient One to the Lesser One. And they are joined in these two holy ones, Wisdom and Supreme Understanding, which ascend.
Supreme Lovingkindness <note>Chesed</note> emerges from this side, and Judgment <note>Din</note> for Power <note>Gevurah</note> from this side. Below is the merit of Jacob,
who takes hold of both of them; he takes hold of them because he is the supreme perfection. Come and see: "Man" <note>Adam</note> is called by an extra [name]
because of the three: the lower Jacob and the upper Israel. "Jacob" is not [full] perfection; "Israel" is the perfection
of all. And so, come and see: David—when David is alone, it is not perfection, for he is after this. And when there is distress, there is no perfection. And this is what we have learned: Israel was not exiled from their land until they denied the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Kingdom
of the House of David, as it is written: <note>1 Kings 12:16</note> **"We have no portion in David, nor inheritance in the son of Jesse; every man to his tents, O Israel."** Woe, woe!
"To his tents"—the place where idolatry dwells through contact; that is the meaning of "to his tents." Rabbi Judah said: Every word of wisdom is to engrave
engravings, all of them in two brains, in two places. He said to him: Like that which is below, Understanding <note>Binah</note>. In Understanding,
everything is revealed, and because of it, fifty gates are opened within it, and it is found that everything was drawn from Wisdom, and this is what is written: <note>Psalms 104:24</note> **"In wisdom You have made them all."**

### The Parable of the Wheat

A parable of a man who lived in the fields and did not know the ways of the city-dwellers. He sowed wheat and ate the wheat in its raw form <note>as plain kernels</note>. One day he entered the city, and they brought him a good fine bread. He said, "What is this for?" They said, "It is bread to eat." He ate it and found it very pleasant. **The Rabbi said**: "From what is this made?" They said, "From wheat." Later, they brought him cakes kneaded in oil. He tasted them and said, "And what are these made of?" They said, "From wheat." Later, they brought him royal pastries <note>delicacies</note> made with honey and oil. He said, "And what are these made of?" They said, "From wheat." He said, "Surely I am the master of all these things, for I eat the essence of all these, which is wheat!" Because of that... <note>The parable illustrates that while the simple man thinks he knows the "essence" by eating raw grain, he misses the refined beauty of the "garments" or "preparations" (the commandments and mystical insights) that turn the raw essence into a royal feast.</note>

<summary>This page explores the mystical unity of the Divine attributes through the symbolism of the Cherubim and concludes with a famous parable about a villager who fails to appreciate refined bread because he only knows raw wheat, illustrating the depth of the Torah's hidden meanings.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

He revealed Himself as a small point below, like a crown that changes years from all of them. Seven runners bear witness, yet they do not stay in their places. He goes and covers, sitting among the branches, and birds nest there. My vision is a shadow from the day of prayer; a voice goes through twelve paths to rest upon seven pillars surrounding it, like four corners rolling toward four sides. <meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Exodus, specifically the opening of the Torah portion Tetzaveh. The previous sections likely dealt with the construction of the Tabernacle; here, the focus shifts to the specific instructions given to Moses and the mystical significance of the word "And you" (Ve-Atah).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Portion of Tetzaveh (And You Shall Command)**<-

**And you** shall bring near to yourself the children of Israel, etc. And you, bring near to yourself Aaron your brother, etc. <note>Exodus 28:1</note>. Rabbi Hiyya said: Why is it different here than in every other place, that it is written: "And you, bring near to yourself"; "And you, shall speak to all the wise-hearted"; "And you, shall command the children of Israel"; "And you, take for yourself the finest spices, flowing myrrh"? Rather, these are all a supreme mystery <note>original: "raza ila’ah"</note> intended to include the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the feminine aspect of God that dwells among humanity</term> together with them. Rabbi Isaac said: Just as it is in the upper realm, so it is in the lower vision, included in measure and investigation is the word "And you" <note>Hebrew: Ve-Atah</note>. As it says, <term>And You give life to them all</term> <note>Nehemiah 9:6</note>. And because of this, it is not simply written "Bring Aaron your brother near," or "Command the children of Israel," or "Speak to all the wise-hearted." Because the commandment is a time of goodness that surrounds and strengthens everything as one, to rest upon the faithfulness of the deed. Rabbi Eleazar said: From here we learn, "in whom the Lord has put wisdom and understanding." Rabbi Shimon said: From here, "And you shall speak to all the wise-hearted, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom" <note>Exodus 28:3</note>. It should have said "whom I have filled *them*" <note>plural</note>. Rather, it says "whom I have filled *him*" <note>singular</note>—referring to that specific Heart. I filled him with a spirit of wisdom at that time, as it is written: "The spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, a spirit of wisdom." And because of this, "whom I have filled him with a spirit of wisdom" means that goodness dwells in the Moon <term>The Moon: a common Zoharic symbol for the Shekhinah, which receives light from the "Sun" or the higher Sephirot</term> in the perfection of all, and therefore it is marked in every place. Rabbi Eleazar said: If so, how are these instances of "And you" and "And you" settled in the verses? He said: The body of them all is settled in the foundation. "And you, bring near to yourself"—to unite with Him and to sanctify in the secret of the spirit that rests, the Holy of Holies. "And you shall speak to all the wise-hearted," because they all belong to Her <note>the Shekhinah</note> for restoration. To perform the service until the Holy Spirit <note>original: "Ruach HaKodesh"</note> speaks within them and gives to them with a burning glow, and then they perform the work.

**And you** shall command the children of Israel <note>Exodus 27:20</note>. The Holy Spirit commands them and doubles the charge upon them to perform the work with a complete will. "And you, take for yourself," as we have established, is like that which is written, "And you, bring near to yourself." And so all of them here, in the work of the Tabernacle <term>Mishkan: the portable sanctuary in the desert</term>, everything is awakened through this Spirit. Rabbi Shimon opened and said: <term>But You, O Lord, be not far off; O my strength, hasten to help me</term> <note>Psalms 22:20</note>. "But You, O Lord" <note>Ve-Atah Adonai</note>—all is one. "Be not far off"—to depart from here and leave it empty, just as the upper light departs from the lower when the upper light is reflected and not found in the world at all. And because of this, "be not far off," for the Holy Temple in the days of Jeremiah was going to be hidden, and afterwards the light returned to its place as is fitting. And because of this, this is the secret of that lamentation Jeremiah recited over the departure of the supreme light, which ascended higher and higher and did not return to its place afterwards as was fitting. Jeremiah departed and did not return to his place, and the Holy Temple was destroyed, and the lights were darkened for all. And the "Spleen" <note>a reference to the forces of darkness or melancholy</note> sought to grind away the redemption and the remembrance of the supreme light to its place. And it is necessary to remember that supreme light, to bring about redemption, and to build the Holy Temple. And all the elders and all the lights shall return as they were at first. And because of this, their prophets stand constantly, this one against that one, because the "Spleen" grinds, and the movement of those below, one with the other, causes the effect, whether for good or for evil. And regarding this spirit in the movement of those below, who are holy supports, so too the letters in themselves cause the revelation of supreme mysteries, just as the holy support below in their very selves cause holy mysteries to be revealed through them. The first spirit and the first commandment that stands.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Tetzaveh**<-
<note>The name of the Torah portion, meaning "You shall command."</note>

It was made as a hidden, concealed treasury of the spirit, which stands upon five others for four hidden things. They are one point <note>original: *nekudah*; referring to the primal point of creation or the Sefirah of Wisdom</note> that stands within the structure <note>original: *hamni'uta*; a technical Zoharic term for the divine measuring scale or structural framework</note>. These are five, and it is the letter *He* (ה) that stands below upon four; it is a point upon four that stands within the structure. The end here is like one who stands upon five pillars; so it is. And by itself, like the Supernal Point, it exists in two ways: one alone, and one hidden and concealed from the **Secrets of Enoch**. <term>He (ה)</term> <note>The fifth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing the Shekhinah or the feminine divine presence</note> stands upon five pillars that emerge from the spark <note>original: *bozina*; the primordial lamp or spark of divine light</note>.

And then five emerge from the right, and they were thirteen attributes of mercy after they rested to be added upon them. And these are the twelve that stand within it; sometimes they are forty-two, and sometimes they are seventy-two. <note>These numbers refer to the mystical Names of God: the 42-letter Name and the 72-letter Name</note>. Everything is seen below, and here they are divided and surround every side, which are thirty-two <note>referring to the 32 Paths of Wisdom</note>, and they are divided into forty-two... and they were empowered by forty-two letters upon them, which are the **Large Letters** of the Torah, for there are <term>Large Letters</term> and there are <term>Small Letters</term>. The Large Letters are above <note>in the higher spiritual realms</note>, and the Small Letters are below. Everything below is in the likeness of that which is above. For there are supernal holy pillars that stand by the will of the spirit, and everything is included from within.

And there are lower holy pillars that stand by the word, and according to the measure of thought, they are diminished. And there are other pillars below that are from that <term>Other Side</term> <note>original: *Sitra Achra*; the realm of evil or impurity</note>, which is from the side of impurity. These do not stand except by the will of an action below and by the sound of that action that gathers toward it. For the Other Side is nothing but like the deeds of this world to look upon them, in the manner of a sorcerer, and they are the "Children of the East" and all those who occupy themselves with that Other Side. They do not stand like the markings from the heart of the Torah... and these are the letters *Resh* (ר) and *Kof* (ק), and they support them with the support of the letters of falsehood. <note>The letters Resh and Kof form the word "Rak" (only/empty) or are part of "Sheker" (falsehood)</note>. Vanity—these are recognized by them even more.

And because of this, in the "Psalm of Praise by David" <note>Psalm 145, known as *Ashrei*</note>, the letter *Vav* (ו) is written with every single letter, except for two places where *Vav* is not written, for it is the radiance of the Holy One, Blessed be He. And because of this, those forty-two letters with which the world was created do not stand to be gazed upon. The Supernal *He* (ה) stands to ascend to ninety-two steps... and this spirit... everything is according to the calculation of ninety-two. And when the level of the male spirit is added, which is the firmament of support, it stands to support the right. *He* (ה) is five, and these are certainly the five blessings every day that the **Assembly of Israel** <note>The *Knesset Yisrael*, representing the Shekhinah</note> needs to be crowned with.

And everything is in the spirit of the *He*; she is <term>He (ה)</term>, her image is in two ways: the spirit of five, which are the five pillars of the sockets that emerge from the spark, and those other five that emerge from her. Therefore, the image is like the form of the *He* in two ways, and the voice that stands as the structure. Because of this, the *Vav* (ו) stands as a constant direction like the form of the *Het* (ח)... for here is the place to be crowned. And other secrets are like the secret of the *He*; all this is according to the secrets of the **Book of Enoch**, and so it is certainly. And when they are established in these truths, all their measures are a commandment that stands in the spirit... like the form of the *He*, the colors of holiness like the structure rule over them, and all is one spirit. Happy are those who know the way of the Torah to walk in the path of truth! Happy are they in this world, and happy are they in the World to Come!

The thirteenth spirit, *He* (ה), is the letter of the image of the spirit of Adam <note>Man</note> as it has been said. And we have established that this letter stands upon twelve chariots. And when the union is divided, two chariots are included in this letter, the step of the image of a human being corresponding to the arms, the thighs, and the body.
->**End**<-

## Main Text (Zohar)

The ends of them all—those arms, thighs, and the soul—have already been discussed. However, they are all hidden within the body, and the soul stands within all twenty-four <note>referring to the twenty-four ornaments of the Shekhinah or the limbs</note>, and all are "chariots" included within the body. Because they are all included in it, they stand and extend as one body, one included in twenty-four chariots. These are the secret of the hidden soul within. And even though all the chariots are twelve on each side, they all stand within the soul. All of them act, and four are the secret of the spirit, which are the drops used to crown the spirit. The eighteen vertebrae <note>the "thumni srei chulyan"</note> where the spirit stands are the spirit of the side. Therefore, the measurement of the lower world and the spirit on that side is exactly like the secret of the commandments; the body is eighteen, and in this manner, all these secrets are explained—that the arms and thighs are all "buildings." Therefore, they are all included in the lower spirit and its image.

And when the lower elements are perfected, which is their seal, then all the evil sides are muzzled and separated from the Moon <note>the Shekhinah</note>. They cannot grow strong because they feel the striking of all the strikes of the heavens to illuminate her, and the accusers cannot oppose Wisdom at all. But when it <note>the light</note> departs, then he <note>the Accuser</note> rises and is hidden and grows, and is able to accuse all the people of the world, for he is the **old and foolish king** <note>original: "melech zaken ve-kesil" — a traditional Zoharic term for the Evil Inclination, citing Ecclesiastes 4:13</note>.

And the voice of wisdom is not like the Moon that shines to the surrounding area; even though the lights that are placed are included in it like the Moon that shines to the surrounding area, one quick extension is made for her. This is the secret of the "impure bird" in all those secrets, and when it shines to the Moon with the spirit that illuminates her. In the Book of Adam the First, regarding the forms of the letters, one is like the holy above and exactly like the holy below. And such is its measurement in this manner. In every point stands the spirit of the crown, for you have no point that does not strive for the crown, for every point has planted supports, chariots, and the Moon is a point striving for the crown. The commandment of the right plants supporting chariots for her, and the quickening is the crown; and so to the left, and so to all sides.

Furthermore, all the commandments are each a general rule of the crown, its embrace, and its chariot. All are included in that lower extension. When the support enters the Moon as a commandment from this, one extension of the spirit of the male is in this manner—the "living vein" <note>the Yesod</note> to enter the female. Everything is included without agitation in the extension of the letter *Vav* <note>ו</note>; then it stands to support the female. And this is the spirit of which it is written: **"And you, bring near to yourself Aaron your brother"** <note>Exodus 28:1</note> to be found as a quickening in the body. And the "You" <note>Atah</note> is like a seal. These are all his chariots and supports. The arm of the support for the prophet, as it is written: **"Take the Levites"** <note>Numbers 8:6</note> to be found including everything as one extension, to be a new thing to be repaired in this, and from here is the support. To prevent it, all is one life, and therefore one extension is made. Search for one and you will find nothing but one extension alone, and that is "One." The letter *He* <note>ה</note> at the end becomes one body in that commandment to sustain it, and above it is the *Vav* <note>ו</note>. The *Vav* is established between two commandments, one above and one below. Then the upper world is established like the lower world, and it is one life, as we have established.

Rabbi Eleazar came and wept and raised his hands. Rabbi Chama wept and said, "Woe to the world when the staff is gathered and the world is snatched away!" Rabbi Eleazar said, "The thighs are below in this spirit of the *Vav*; these are included in this below." He said to him, as it is written: **"Remember the Torah of Moses My servant"** <note>Malachi 3:22</note>, and it is not written "with my strength," to find that everything is included in this spirit. And the letter *Vav* is the law of the hanging, and it is one life... and one extension, as has been said.

It does not say "to be a priest for him," but "to be a priest to Me" <note>original: "le-kaheno li"</note>—for His supports, for the lower support, for the inner support. And this "to Me" <note>Li</note> has the *He* for the upper and the support of the *Vav* so that all shall be one. Blessed are the people of Israel.

# Tetzaveh

->**Tetzaveh**<-
<note>Exodus 27:20, "And you shall command."</note>

Israel, who are present and know the secrets of the mercies of the Torah, walk in the path of truth. It is from within the "wings of Israel" <note>a reference to the community of Israel or the Shekhinah</note> that everything is brought near to become one as is fitting. For the children of Israel stand below to awaken the love of the High Holy Ones, to illuminate the paths, to raise the sparks, and to bring everything near from below to above so that all is made one. Regarding this it is written:
> **But you who held fast to the Lord your God are all alive today.** <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>
And it is written:
> **And you, bring near to yourself Aaron your brother.** <note>Exodus 28:1</note>
Indeed, all these are "bringings near" <note>a wordplay on *Korban* (sacrifice) and *Karov* (near)</note> for the one who knows how to unify the Holy Union and to assign the portions. For just as it is below, when the sacrifice is offered properly, all things are unified and the "shining of the countenance" <note>divine favor</note> is found. But when the sacrifice is not found to be proper, the union is not right; then the countenance is sad, the light is not found, the moon is covered, and the <term>Other Side</term> <note>Sitra Achra; the realm of evil or impurity</note> rules. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "Let it not be so," and He did not come with him in assembly like the assembly of the righteous below. For it is not written regarding Job that "God tested Job" as it is written regarding Abraham, **"And God tested Abraham,"** where the matter was in his own hands to sacrifice his son and bring union to Him. Even though He did not give him or hand over anything to him <note>the Accuser</note>, yet he was handed over to him—that <term>Accuser</term> <note>the Mekatreg; Satan</note>—because the Holy One, blessed be He, saw that he [Job] failed to awaken that Accuser toward himself [with a portion of the sacrifice]. For at all times that Accuser comes to mingle among men. And here, the Holy One, blessed be He, awakened him [the Accuser] against him, as it is written: **"Have you considered my servant Job?"** But this is a deep secret. He opened and said:
> **And it came to pass at the end of days, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering to the Lord.** <note>Genesis 4:3</note>
"And it came to pass at the **end of days**"—this is a secret. It says "end of days" (*Ketz Yamim*) and not "end of the right" (*Ketz Yamin*). For the "end of the right" is near, as it is written:
> **But you, go your way till the end; for you shall rest, and will arise to your inheritance at the end of the right.** <note>Daniel 12:13</note>
The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Daniel: "And you, go to the end." Daniel asked Him: "To the end of the right or the end of days?" until He told him: "To the end of the right." And because of this, David was afraid, as it is written: **"Lord, make me to know my end"** <note>Psalms 39:5</note>, which the sages established refers to the "end of the right." But here, what is written? "And it was at the end of days," and not the "end of the right." Because of this, his [Cain's] sacrifice was not accepted, for it was all from the "Other Side." Come and see what is written: **"And Abel, he also brought."** What is the meaning of "he also"? It is to include everything, this and that; the sacrifice was a whole, and its essence was for the Holy One, blessed be He, but he gave a portion to the Other Side so that all would be satisfied. But Cain made the "end of days" the essence, and gave a [mere] portion to the Holy One, blessed be He; therefore, he and his sacrifice were rejected. Regarding Job, what is written? **"And his sons went and feasted..."** and it is written, **"And it was, when the days of their feasting were gone about..."** and it is written, **"And they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them."** This shows that the essence was for the Other Side, and only afterward did he offer burnt offerings. He changed the order and did not have the right intention to ascend above, and he did not offer the sacrifice to include [the Other Side] properly. Come and see: if one gives a portion to the Accuser, he cannot prevail against him afterward. And if you ask, why did the Holy One, blessed be He, see him [Job] this way? Because he was negligent in his fault, and to hide the light he did not offer another sacrifice to subdue the others, but only a "burnt offering" (*Olah*) which ascends only upwards. Regarding this it is written: **"Thus did Job continually,"** for the Other Side was not found in his portion, and thus it [the Other Side] was removed from the Sanctuary and ascended away from it, while the side of Holiness ascended higher and higher. But Job did not want the "Other" to be below in his sacrifice, and he removed himself from it. From this we learn what is written: **"And he turned away from evil."** Therefore, he always offered a burnt offering, for the Other Side never takes a portion from a burnt offering. Because of this, all that he [the Accuser] took [from Job later] was because his dwelling was canceled. Therefore, Job "gnashed his teeth" against the Covenant, for he had not removed [the Accuser] from himself [with a gift]. Because of this, the Holy One, blessed be He, awakened that Accuser, as it is written: **"Have you considered my servant Job?"** Come and see, everything that the
->**Holy One, blessed be He**<-
desires...

<summary>This page discusses the mystical requirements of sacrifice, explaining that a proper offering must unify the divine realms while also "satisfying" the Accuser (the Other Side) with a portion to prevent interference. It contrasts the sacrifices of Cain and Abel and critiques Job for offering only burnt offerings, which excluded the Other Side and ultimately led to his suffering.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar on Parashat Tetzaveh. The previous themes likely touched upon the Tabernacle service, which now transitions into the spiritual significance of the Passover sacrifice and the internal struggle between the holy soul and the "Evil Inclination."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The Holy One, blessed be He, <note>original: "Kadosh Baruch Hu"</note> is below all of them in the Foundation <note><term>Yesod</term>: the ninth Sephirah or divine emanation, often associated with the generative principle and the covenant of circumcision</note>, which does not stand for a moment because the foreskin <note>original: "orlah"</note> covers it as a secret, until the time that the Accuser is nullified and laughs. Because of this, the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded to consume it through the Priests, who represent the side of Lovingkindness <note><term>Chesed</term>: the Sephirah of mercy and expansion</note>. One should strive for it with joy. He commanded to remove the foreskin from them, and then the Holy One, blessed be He, is established in the Foundation. That "Other Side" <note><term>Sitra Achra</term>: the realm of evil or demonic forces in Kabbalah</note> is then separated from the Holy, and one strives in it with joy and the nullification of its own power. Then He opens for him and pushes him away until that opening is made for him, and then those who know the unifications of their Master do so properly. It is written: *And the wise-hearted among those who perform the work shall make for you* <note>A variant or specific Kabbalistic reading of a verse related to the Tabernacle craftsmen or the prohibition of leaven</note>. And it is written: *The Feast of Unleavened Bread you shall keep.* What does one have to do with the other? Rather, they have established it thus: anyone who eats leaven <note>original: "chametz"</note> on Passover is as if he practiced idolatry <note>original: "avodah zarah"</note> for himself. For the spirit of purity was pressed on Passover, like one who worships idols, for it is an idol. And when Israel went out of Egypt, they left their authority—the authority of that wicked one who is called "leaven," like evil leaven. Therefore, it is called idolatry, and this is the spirit of the Evil Inclination <note>original: "Yetzer HaRa"</note>, a foreign worship. It is called leaven because it is dark, and this is the Inclination, for such is the "Evil Son" to a person, like leaven in the dough <note>A classic Rabbinic metaphor for the Evil Inclination which causes the heart to "swell" with pride and sin</note>. It enters a person's innards little by little, and afterward grows strong in him until the whole body is mixed with it. This is idolatry, and regarding this it is written: *There shall be no foreign god within you* <note>Psalm 81:10</note>; certainly, *The Feast of Unleavened Bread you shall keep.* Rabbi Yehuda opened: *Cease from the man in whose nostrils is breath; for of what account is he?* <note>Isaiah 2:22</note>

*Cease from the man*, etc. They have established this verse. But what does it mean, *from the man*? If a person is lacking, should one refrain from trading with him? Or if those who are counted with him are found, should people never draw near to them? Rather, they established it regarding one who considers his friend's entrance to give him a greeting of peace. And here we establish it regarding another matter, as it is written: *He who blesses his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him* <note>Proverbs 27:14</note>. This is taught well. But what is *Cease from the man in whose nostrils is breath*? Here the Holy One, blessed be He, commands a person and warns him to guard himself from those people who have diverted their ways from the good path to the evil side and defiled their souls with that other impurity. But when the Holy One, blessed be He, created man, He made him in the Supernal Image <note>original: "dyokna alaah"</note> and breathed into him a holy spirit comprised of three levels, as we have established: Soul, Spirit, and Breath <note><term>Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah</term>: the three primary levels of the soul in ascending order of spirituality</note>. The *Neshamah* <note>the highest level</note> entered, which is the supernal strength to know and recognize the commandments of the Holy One, blessed be He. And that holy *Neshamah* lives above. If he defiles it with foreign worship, he leaves the service of his Master. Because the three strengths are all one like a body—*Nefesh*, *Ruach*, and *Neshamah* are joined as one and directed as one, and all are like the body of the Supernal Spirit, until he joins *He who walks with the wise*, etc. <note>Proverbs 13:20</note>. And we see that this man who had all these levels within him has not yet stood in his permanence to know who he is. By what is a holy man known? By refraining from his anger; in his very anger one knows him and recognizes who he is. If that holy *Neshamah* departs at the time of his anger, and he does not uproot it from its place to settle that "foreign god" in its stead, then he is a man as he should be. He is a servant of his Master; he is a complete man. But if that man does not guard it, and he uproots this holiness from its place to settle the "Other Side" in its place, certainly he is a man who rebels against his Master, and it is forbidden to draw near to him or join with him. This is *He tears his soul in his anger* <note>Job 18:4</note>; he tears and uproots his soul because of his anger and settles a foreign god in his body. Regarding this it is written: *Cease from the man in whose nostrils is breath*, for he tears that holy *Neshamah* and ruins it because of his anger <note>The Hebrew word for "anger" (af) is the same as the word for "nose/nostril"</note>, *in whose nostrils is breath.*

<summary>This page interprets the prohibition of leaven on Passover as a rejection of idolatry and the Evil Inclination. It further explains that a person's spiritual integrity is tested through anger, which can uproot the holy soul and replace it with "foreign" unholy forces.</summary>
<keywords>Passover, Leaven (Chametz), Evil Inclination (Yetzer HaRa), Idolatry, Soul levels (Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah), Anger, Sitra Achra, Yesod</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the inner spiritual state of man, specifically focusing on the destructive nature of anger and its connection to idolatry, before transitioning into the sanctity of the Festival of Unleavened Bread (Passover).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Tetzaveh**<-

As is his body, so is his covering. For how much is he diminished by his own wrath, that man. And one who becomes intoxicated by wine <note>original: "chamarah"</note> <note>See Zohar II:182a regarding the comparison of anger to drunkenness and idolatry</note> and one who becomes intoxicated by anger—it is exactly as if he became intoxicated by actual idolatry <note>original: "avodah zarah"</note>. What is the reason? Because of this, an impurity actually dwells within him. And not only that, but he uproots the supernal holiness from its place and settles a "strange god" <note>original: "el zar"</note> in its place. Regarding what is written of a strange god, "Do not turn to idols" <note>Leviticus 19:4</note>, it is forbidden to gaze upon the face of such a person. And if you say, what of the anger of the Sages? The anger of the Sages is good for a person in all aspects, for we have learned that the Torah is fire, and it is the Torah that boils within them, as it is written: "Is not My word like fire? says the Lord" <note>Jeremiah 23:29</note>. The anger of the Sages is in matters of Torah. The example of the Sages is to give honor to the Torah and is considered like the service of the Holy One, blessed be He. But if it is in other matters, it is not the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, because in all his aspects a man must be careful of the impurity itself and forbid himself from drawing near to it.

And if you say, "But he only did it for a moment and then he repented?" It is not so. For once he has uprooted the holiness of his soul from its foundation and its place, and cast a strange god into that place, it cannot be repaired or dwell there again. Except when a man comes with everything he has and uproots that [evil] forever, and afterwards strives to be sanctified; then holiness may rest upon him and he can take hold of sanctity. Rabbi Yose said: He is truly restored. He said to him: Come and see, at the moment he uproots the holiness of his soul and that strange god rises in its place, the man is defiled and called "unclean," and he defiles anyone who draws near to him, for that holiness has fled from him. And once it has fled from him all at once, how much must a man do until it returns to its place! He said to him: If so, how many wretched people are found [in this state]? He said: If they found a path, they would not be able to do more. But this is the merit of all, and the whole body is diminished by it. And the soul and everything is surrounded. And the surrounding of the world is nothing but the body alone, and because of this it is written: "The wings of a dove are covered with silver, and her pinions with shimmering gold" <note>Psalm 68:14</note>. The holiness of the Matronita <note>The Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> is because of the covering that is not defiled, which cleanses everything. For just as he was diminished, so much strength is needed to humanize him.

Come and see: this anger is from the "Other Side" <note>original: "Sitra Achra," the forces of evil</note> as we have said, and a man must guard himself from it and separate from it, and regarding this it is written: "You shall make for yourself no molten gods" <note>Exodus 34:17</note>. "For yourself"—meaning, so as not to deny your own essence. And it is written: "The Festival of Unleavened Bread you shall keep" <note>Exodus 34:18</note>. "You shall keep"—this is the side of holiness that a man must guard, and he should not exchange it for the Other Side; for if he exchanges it, he becomes defiled and defiles all who draw near to him. "The Festival of Unleavened Bread you shall keep"—this is the place to draw near and guard, and therefore it is written: "The Festival of Unleavened Bread you shall keep; seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you." These seven days are like the seven days of Sukkot <note>The Festival of Booths</note>, which are supernal and are lower, and because of this, in the latter we recite the full Hallel <note>Psalms of praise</note> and in the former [Passover] we do not recite the full Hallel <note>referring to the last six days of Passover</note>. And because they are below, it is written "seven days you shall eat unleavened bread" <note>original: "matzot"</note>. The word "Matzot" is written deficiently, without the letter *Vav*, for those supernal days—the mystery of the Woman—have not yet ascended.

Come and see: once the spirit of the Festival of Unleavened Bread comes to repair that which is below, for we have learned: "One ascends in holiness and does not descend" <note>original: "Ma'alin BaKodesh ve-lo moridin"</note>, the heat from below is like those lower days. Come and see, it is written: "And he shall make atonement for himself and for his house..." <note>Leviticus 16:6</note>. Who makes atonement for him? He first needs it for himself, and then for his house. In this manner, there is another level to be sanctified and to go out in holiness to atone for him. And once he is sanctified, he must atone for his house and sanctify them, and therefore he descends below to sanctify his house. And how much does he sanctify them? A measure below. And once they are sanctified, we need to ascend above, for when the house of the Matronita is sanctified, then she ascends above to be sanctified like those supernal days above.

<summary>This passage warns that uncontrolled anger is spiritually equivalent to idolatry because it uproots the divine soul and replaces it with an "alien god." It then links the preservation of holiness to the observance of Passover, explaining the mystical significance of the "seven days" and the principle of ascending in holiness.</summary>
<keywords>anger, idolatry, Sitra Achra, Matronita, Passover, Matzah, holiness, atonement, Shekhinah</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the sacred calendar, specifically the transition from the Exodus (Passover) to the receiving of the Torah (Shavuot). It focuses on the counting of the Omer as a process of purification and elevation.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Above, and because of this, we perform the action upon the covenant, for these days are supreme days <note>The "days" refer to the mystical emanations or Sefirot that govern time</note>. They are within the Assembly of Israel <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note> as we have said, which stands upon legs, thighs, and the body as one. There, the thighs and the body stand like a "speech" <note>A masculine principle of active revelation</note> that stands by its words, and not like a "female" of whom it is said "to sit." Furthermore, because the world and the children are the secret of speech, it is written that they are "exempt from this tractate" <note>A metaphorical way of saying certain feminine aspects are not counted in this specific masculine alignment</note> and are not seen to be counted, except for the males, to be sanctified each one as is fitting. In this manner, the thigh is always an upright male and not "houses" <note>feminine vessels</note>, because the secret of the Covenant is masculine and not feminine. And because the secret stands above, they are not obligated.

The secret of what we learned here is that in every seven days, the supreme days speak as a holy unit and are unified with these lower ones. This lower one is called a "week" <term>Shavuot/Week: implying a completion of seven</term> to be sanctified by the seven supreme days. And so, in every seven and seven, the fifty days are grasped until the end.

When the forty-nine supreme days are found, seven days are found below to be sanctified by them, for each one is called a "week" entering into the seven living beings. Regarding this it is written: *Seven complete Sabbaths shall they be* <note>Leviticus 23:15</note>. Because they are feminine <note>original: "Nukvin"</note>, [the impurity] is removed to take the feminine aspects, and when they are sanctified as it is written, they are found to be joined below like a husband. Then it is called "from the weeks," grasping the feminine aspects that surround them, those supreme days, to be sanctified by them. Because of this, it is written *in your weeks* <note>Numbers 28:26</note>—meaning those that belong to you—and it does not simply say "in the weeks," because in this way Israel below is sanctified with them.

Therefore, when they reach forty-nine days, that supreme day is called the "fiftieth day," which rules over the forty-nine days. This is the secret of the whole, which is "Liberty" <term>Dror: a specific biblical term for the freedom of the Jubilee year</term>, like forty-nine branches. Then that supreme day, the day of liberty, brings out liberty for all, like forty-nine aspects. **Rabbi Elazar** opened his discourse:
> *Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow [Dror] a nest for herself, where she may lay her young—even Your altars...* <note>Psalms 84:4</note>

"Even the sparrow has found a home"—these are the birds of heaven that many times have their dwelling outside, but from here on many have their dwelling in a house. For example, the *Dror* <note>The word for "swallow" in Hebrew is the same as "liberty"</note> is a bird that dwells in the house of every man and does not fear. Why? Because everyone calls it *Dror*. What is *Dror*? It is the liberty of all, as in *And you shall proclaim liberty [Dror]...* <note>Leviticus 25:10</note> and the Aramaic translation is *Hori* <note>Free/Noble</note>. This is the "bird of liberty." From the day it makes a nest in the house and brings out its young, it dwells in the house for sixty days with them, and after they separate, these and those, it is called the bird of liberty/freedom. Come and see what is written:
> *And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty [Dror] throughout the land* <note>Leviticus 25:10</note>

Liberty goes out to all. And because freedom <note>original: "Hori"</note> comes from it—the liberty that comes from it is like a "free man." Therefore, liberty is over the "maiden" <note>The Shekhinah</note> who is called liberty, and this liberty is called freedom because of what this supreme day brings out; it is called liberty and it is the freedom of all. This supreme fiftieth day—because there is a lower freedom and an upper freedom—this upper one is its crown. Upper freedom and lower freedom, the Sun and the Jubilee, are as one. They are the two priests of all Israel: one when they went out of Egypt, and one as it is written, one like Passover and one like Shavuot. For it is written: *Who is good to you, bread from heaven.* Therefore, the sacrifice of this day is like this, and it is offered upon this. In all other sacrifices, the hundred is the essence, as it is written: *And you shall offer with the bread seven lambs...* and it is written *From your dwellings you shall bring bread for a wave offering...* for it is not like that which Israel became wise in, the supreme wisdom of liberty, and they entered into liberty. Now we must look at Passover: Israel went out from the exile to be rectified, as it is written *No leaven shall be seen with you* and it is written *For with the bread of wisdom...*

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the spiritual nature of the Exodus and the commandments. It specifically addresses the transition from the "Bread of Affliction" to the "Bread of Healing" (Matzah) and the subsequent permission to eat leavened bread (Chametz) once the soul is fortified. It then transitions into a classic Zoharic narrative structure where Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai encounters a traveler with hidden wisdom.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Tetzaveh** (Command)<-

What is the reason? Because the scripture calls that bread *Matzah*. Now that Israel has merited to eat a higher food, it should not be abolished from them or from below at all. Furthermore, the Holy One, Blessed be He, saw that it was written: *“They shall be baked as leavened bread”* <note>Leviticus 23:17, referring to the Shavuot offering</note>. Moreover, on this day, the Evil Inclination and the "other side" <note>The Sitra Achra, or forces of impurity</note> below are subdued. 

This is like a king who had an only son. One day the son fell ill. They checked for a remedy for the king's son, and until he ate that remedy, no other food or sustenance was found in the master's house. They did so; once he ate that remedy, <term>afterwards</term> from then on, he could eat whatever he desired and it could not harm him. 

So it was with Israel: until they subdued Egypt, they did not know the essence and the spirit of faith. The <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, tasted [their heart] and saw that Israel needed a remedy. Until they ate the remedy, no other food was prepared for them. Once they ate that remedy—which is the Matzah—it became a healing for them to enter and know the spirit of faith. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "From now on, prepare leavened bread (<term>Chametz</term>) for them and let them eat it, for it can no longer harm them." 

And just as it is written regarding the day of Sukkot, they are refined by that higher light which is for healing. And because of this, leavened bread is brought to be burned upon the Altar. Two other breads are brought, and the leavened bread is consumed by the fire of the Altar so that it cannot dominate or harm Israel. 

Because of this, holy Israel clings to the Holy One, Blessed be He, like a seal to a signet on this day. Israel guarded their portion on two sides, so that these [harmful forces] would never enter into judgment against them. On the day of Rosh Hashanah, which is a day of judgment, the Holy One, Blessed be He, sits in judgment over all. Therefore, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, gave Israel the merit to taste of that bread from that [holy] place. From that bread, they knew and gazed into the secrets of the Torah to walk in the straight path. With this wisdom, a herald goes forth to proclaim these matters we have spoken of.

**Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Elazar** his son were traveling on the road, and **Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Yose** were going with them. While they were walking, they encountered a man leading a donkey <note>original: *pater chamor*, a play on the "firstling of a donkey" and a "traveler with a donkey"</note>, and the donkey was carrying a young boy. Rabbi Shimon raised his eyes and saw him. He said to Rabbi Abba: "Surely new words of Torah are with us here in this opening." 

When they reached him, Rabbi Shimon said: "The shadow of your donkey's load <note>meaning the hidden wisdom the traveler carries</note> has arrived before you." The man said to him: "I know that here are masters of donkeys <note>a metaphor for those who carry the 'burden' of Torah</note> and surely new words are with us today." Rabbi Shimon asked him: "Where is your home?" He replied: "My dwelling was in the reaches of the wilderness, for there I labored in the Torah. And now I have come to the inhabited settlement to dwell in the shadow of the Holy One, Blessed be He, because of the season of this seventh month <note>Tishrei, the month of the High Holidays</note>." 

Rabbi Shimon rejoiced and said: "It is written that the ways of the Holy One, Blessed be He, are directed toward us." He said to the man: "Let a word from your mouth be heard, new and ancient words, for you have come from the wilderness to the settlement in this seventh month to see the rewards." The man said to him: "You have opened with this question, and I know that a spring of wisdom flows from you, and your words reach the heavens of wisdom."

**He opened** his discourse and said: *“And in the wilderness, where you saw how the Lord your God carried you, as a man carries his son...”* <note>Deuteronomy 1:31</note>. This verse should be understood: "And in the wilderness *also* which you saw." What does this mean? That the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, remembered Israel in the wilderness—a harsh wilderness, as it is written: *“A place of snakes, fiery serpents, and scorpions”* <note>Deuteronomy 8:15</note>. This wilderness was harsher than all other wildernesses in the world. What is the reason? Because of the reason that Israel went out...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar regarding the spiritual dynamics of the Moon (representing the Shekhinah or Divine Presence) and the forces of Judgment. It specifically addresses the period of Rosh Hashanah and the symbolic "covering" of the moon.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The moon <note>original: *sihara*; a reference to the Shekhinah, the feminine aspect of the Divine</note> shines and is completed to give authority to strengthen the Holy Kingdom <note>original: *malchuta kadisha*</note> and to shine upon all. At that time, the guilty kingdom is subdued and the moon shines. The Holy One, Blessed be He, brought them out to bind them like a mighty desert—a dark desert and a ladder of the guilty kingdom—and He goes into its very lap in order to break its strength and power, to subdue it and bow its head so that it shall not rule. Fear and sin were appointed; the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to remove it from the world, and for this reason, He passed them through His darkness and confusion and actual distress. Since they went many times, it is written of them: "they saw," and then the secret was established of "the runner was reversed," etc. <note>A mystical reference to the reversal of spiritual forces.</note>

What is the "head of the beginning"? They did not know how to guard themselves from it, and afterward they lived like the latter ones and all fell as in the desert. Thus was fulfilled the "heel's supplement," and for forty years they received their portion corresponding to the kingdom of the head. Concerning this it is written: *which you saw with your eyes*—they were appointed over that sin of the desert. Go and subdue it before them! They took His darkness and confusion from all, as it is written:
> **Then the chiefs of Edom were affrighted** <note>Exodus 15:15</note>
The strength of the vision of the "fiery serpent and scorpion." Therefore, sustenance was provided for the mighty desert to look there in its paths in order to subdue that "Other Side" <note>original: *Sitra Achra*; the realm of evil or impurity</note>. The offspring settle there, the strength of the Torah is there, for there is no way of strength except that which is bent out of darkness. For when this Side is subdued, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is elevated on high and honored in His glory. Therefore, the perfection of all is good and evil together, only to be elevated afterward as good. And there is no "good" except that which is bent out of the midst of evil. When the covering of the good is removed, His glory is elevated, and this is a complete service. Therefore, until now, the dwelling is there all the days of the year, in order to subdue that Side below like a desert. For the time of the holy service of the Side of Holiness has arrived; on the contrary, at the time when the service is there, the time has also arrived for that sustenance to demand Judgment <note>original: *Dina*</note> before the Holy One, Blessed be He. Those below are complete, and therefore they appear as open-eyed and to rebuke. That Elder opened his discourse and said:
> **Blow the Shofar at the new moon, at the covered time [Keseh] for our feast day** <note>Psalms 81:4; the word *Keseh* implies the moon is hidden or covered</note>
For here is the time to awaken the mighty Supernal Spirit. And when it is awakened, another spirit departs to strengthen the Chaldeans. Once it is strengthened, it rises and covers the moon so that it is not seen as a mountain, and it is completed from the side of Judgment. Then the entire world is in Judgment, and those below—and a man—a herald calls out in all the firmaments: "Prepare the Throne of Judgment!" For He desires to judge. A mystery is here: they shone for us like the desert to see the awakening of the Supernal Bear on this day. Rather, all secrets and all precious holy things are all dependent upon the Oath. And that Supernal Oath is the "World that is Searched" <note>The hidden realm of Binah/Understanding</note>, the World to Come, from which all lamps and all holy things and all blessings shine. 

When the time arrives to extend blessings and holiness to the end, He desired to establish the repair of all worlds. All those repairs to be established rise from the lower realm. If they are like a sin, they are like a sin. And then it stands not like a mountain until the debts are separated from the merits. Then Judgment is awakened, and from that spirit, the Other Side is strengthened, and the Accuser shines because those sins are given to him. For concerning him it is written:
> **He searcheth out all perfection** <note>Job 28:3</note>
And he covers the moon to look, because it is not the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He, to remember the works of His hands [negatively]. And that Other Side stands as a mighty shell <note>original: *Kelipah*</note> that cannot be broken except by that counsel which the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave to Israel, as it is written:
> **Blow the Shofar at the new moon, at the covered time [Keseh] for our feast day** <note>Psalms 81:4</note>
In order to break that "covering" <note>original: *Kesa*</note> that covers the moon so it is not seen. And when we awaken below with the Shofar, that voice which is bent from the Shofar flies in the air and cleaves the firmaments until it rises to that mighty crown that covers the moon to break it. Then it causes the awakening of Mercy <note>original: *Rachamim*</note> to rise.

<summary>This passage explains the mystical significance of Rosh Hashanah, describing how the "Other Side" covers the moon (the Shekhinah) to bring Judgment upon the world. The blowing of the Shofar is presented as a spiritual tool to break this "shell" and awaken Divine Mercy.</summary>
