<meta>This page continues the discussion from the previous section regarding the spiritual mechanics of prayer and the Shofar. It focuses on the mystical relationship between the "Precious Stone" (the Sefirah of Malchut) and the "Other Side" (the realm of judgment), specifically during the rituals of Yom Kippur.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

When the sound rises and stands above, it becomes intermingled. Then that voice stands and passes through that firmament, and once the awakening of Mercy arrives, so too is another supreme Beauty awakened above. It brings forth a voice of love, and voice mingles with voice, mercy with mercy, and they descend. Just as the awakening begins below, so too is it awakened above. And if you should ask: how can the female below <note>referring to the Sefirah of Malchut, the feminine aspect of the Divine</note> awaken the heights? It is because the awakening starts below.

**Come and see:** The lower world is constantly prepared to receive, and it is called the **Precious Stone** <note>original: *Even Taba*. This represents Malchut, the vessel for divine light</note>. The upper world only gives to it according to the state in which it stands. If it stands in the **Illumination of the Face** <note>original: *Nehiro de-Anpin*, meaning a state of joy and favor</note> from below, then they shine upon it from above in the same way. But if it stands in sadness, they give to it accordingly. This is the meaning of: *Serve the Lord with gladness* <note>Psalm 100:2</note>. The joy of a human draws toward them another supreme joy from above. So too, this lower world: according to how it is crowned, so it draws from above.

For this reason, Israel acts first and awakens the sound of the Shofar, a voice which is a breath of Mercy, encompassing all. It strikes and forgives, and it becomes joy and rises above. The **Precious Stone** flies like a bird and is colored with the living colors of that voice. Then, just as the awakening was, so it draws from above. Once she is prepared by this voice, mercies emerge from above and rest upon her, and she is perfected from below and from above.

At that moment, the **Other Side** <note>original: *Sitra Achra*, the realm of evil/judgment</note> becomes confused. He looks and sees the Illumination of the Face; he is stunned by its strength and is unable to act as an accuser. This Precious Stone then stands in the light of all sides—in the light from below and the light from above. And when does she stand in the light from above? You must say: on the Day of Atonement <note>Yom Kippur</note>.

Since that Precious Stone is illuminated on the Day of Atonement by the light from above through the light from below, and that **Informer** <note>original: *Deltora*, the accusing angel/Satan</note> is confused, Israel below prepares a **Goat** <note>original: *Se'ir*, the Scapegoat</note> for that mighty desert-dweller who rules over it. That Other Side is a point in the middle of the masters of the world, for all his greatness comes from that Other Side ruling over him.

And there is a point in the middle of all merits, the side of Holiness, which belongs to Him. Upon this it stands, a weight to prevent every righteous person who enters into the two commandments. The Kingdom of Heaven <note>Malchut</note> is separated from the Mountain of Holiness—one part for her and one for the World to Come. This is a supreme, hidden commandment, and therefore it stands upon two commandments. Her commandment is strong, a weight to prevent every righteous person. The commandment of the Husband is a supreme, hidden seal, belonging to the "N" and "G" <note>likely referring to the initials of *Nefesh* and *Guf* (Soul and Body) or specific mystical ciphers</note> that stand forever in the middle of the whole world and all sides of greatness and merit. Therefore, in the middle of the Garden of Eden stands a commandment of hidden and concealed joy that is not known. And one pillar, like a vision from below to above, extends from that commandment, and from there waters gush forth to be divided into the four sides of the world. Thus, three commandments are found in the world, standing one upon the other, mirroring the three commandments of the Torah.

**Come and see:** The goat that Israel offers to that desert is intended to give a portion to that **Other Side**, so that he may be occupied with it. And if you should ask: why two goats? One for the Lord and one for that Other Side? The goat for the Other Side is understood, but why one for the Lord?

It is like a king who was angry with his son. He called for the **Executioner** <note>original: *Santiora*, an officer of punishment</note> who constantly carries out judgment on people, so that he would be ready to execute judgment on his son. That executioner was glad; he entered before the king and waited there. When the son saw him, he said: "I wish this executioner had not entered!" He wept in fear because the king was angry with him. What did he do? He went and reconciled with his father. Once he had reconciled with him, the king ordered a supreme feast to be made for himself and his son, and he ordered that the executioner should not know about it. Later, the executioner entered. The king said: "Now, if this one finds out about the supreme feast I have prepared..."

It introduces a famous parable of a King and an Executioner to explain why a "portion" (the Scapegoat) is given to the forces of judgment to distract them from accusing Israel.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar on Parashat Tetzaveh, specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of Yom Kippur (the Day of Atonement). It explores the relationship between the "scapegoat," the purification of the Sanctuary, and the numerical significance of the "tenth" and "seventh" levels of the divine hierarchy.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Tetzaveh**<-
<note>Exodus 27:20-30:10</note>

Judgments hang more heavily than a sieve of life; the lower arm is extended, but his thought is not below, for all is joy. The Kingdom is the field of the King of All; from this side, his bosom is included more than his thought of judgment. And the thought does not ascend like this appearance—this is the **goat** <note>Hebrew: *Sa'ir*; refers to the scapegoat of Leviticus 16</note> of the hair <note>A wordplay between *Sa'ir* (goat) and *Se'ar* (hair), representing the "hairy" or "rough" forces of judgment</note> of Leviathan; it does not hang and does not err. It does not err, for that is his thought; and it does not hang, for his thought is strengthened in it like this appearance—and not this or that. This is the **goat** and no other. It is called *Kippur* <note>Atonement/Wiping away</note> to erase and to call it *Kippur*, but because it cleanses every thought and passes it from before him on that day. Therefore, it is called the Day of Atonement (*Yom Kippur*), the day of cleansing, and so we call it. It is written:
> **For on this day He shall atone for you, to cleanse you** <note>Leviticus 16:30</note>
For "this day" prepares him. Why "on this day"? This is so that the Sanctuary above may be purified and prepared. It is written, "For on this day He shall atone for you," and then "and he shall atone," etc. First, "on this day" so that they may be purified, and afterward "for you." Furthermore, "He shall atone on this day" and prepare him first, and because of this "for you"—for your sake it is necessary to appoint him and cleanse him as before. "And he shall atone" means he wipes away and atones for what is his, so that it is clear and clean for all (everything that is in this world is remembered and cleaned for all). And until all the evil sides are removed, for they have searched the constellations <note>Hebrew: *Mazzalot*</note>... and just as those constellations hang, so too the side of judgment hangs; it is their side. And the storm <note>Hebrew: *Sa'arat*</note> of that side does not err. In this manner it is written:
> **And he shall atone for the Holy Place, because of the uncleanness of the children of Israel, and because of their transgressions, even all their sins** <note>Leviticus 16:16</note>
So that the Accuser <note>The Prosecuting Angel/Satan</note> cannot rule over them. Therefore, on the Day of Atonement, which is the punishment for all sins, and their cleansing, they seek to uproot the Serpent itself for those who bring their feet forward to the upper Altar. There are **five afflictions** <note>The traditional prohibitions of Yom Kippur: eating/drinking, washing, anointing, wearing leather, and marital relations</note> in order to be found in the five supernal sides of the Day of Atonement; He commanded them, and they are his gates. And the lower life is considered to be from the side of Isaac <note>Representing the attribute of *Gevurah* or Severity/Judgment</note>; behold the olive and the protection, even though in the general rule of all is the Law. And then these are the olive and the afflictions in the perfect return, in the established staff, and in the lower level it is found. And corresponding to them, they perform this affliction. It is written: **And on the tenth of this seventh month** <note>Leviticus 23:27</note> and it is also written **on the tenth of the month, on the tenth, in the tenth**—it should have said "in the tenth-ness." Why **on the tenth**? Rather, because below on this day, all the supernal levels come down to watch over the Moon <note>Symbolizing the *Shekhinah* or Divine Presence</note> and to give her an inheritance, and all of them are the spirit of the wool until it ascends to the brain. And when it stands in the spirit of the brain, then all is one and it is called "Ten." Therefore, it says **on the tenth**, just as it is said **"Remember" and "Keep"** <note>The two versions of the Sabbath commandment</note>; all of them come to guard and to give inheritance in the spirit of the ten.

He turned his head toward Rabbi Simeon. Rabbi Simeon said to him: "Behold, I know that below you seek the meaning of this **'on the tenth of the seventh month'** and its rejection. It was like the tenths, and so it is that it ascends to the brain. And this scripture was only established so that it ascends to seventy, as it is written: **'on the tenth of the seventh month.'** When they crown the seventh with ten, behold, it ascends to seventy." He said to him: "Because of this, I turned my head to you, for I know that you are wise. Come and see two mysteries here: one is the Atonement (*Kippur*) and one is the Seventh. And it is called the 'Seventh Month' because it receives from the ten lights that pass through. And further, see from what you said, that it ascends to seventy on this day, and it is in the level of seventy, and in the level of the brain it is hushed, to block and to inherit in the level of seventy. For on this day, it is decreed for all the people of Israel to be judged, and they all stand as a gathered assembly more than a body. For on this day, the soul of the Atonement is a light and not a body, as it is written: **'And you shall afflict your souls'** and **'For any soul that is not afflicted.'** And this day is decreed for every soul, and they were in turmoil, and life does not stand in the spirit of seventy; this is for the soul that stands atoned in the spirit of seventy."

## Main Text (Zohar)

Crowns of knives are above; he sees them, yet they are unseen, passing over your chambers where they listen. Come and see: the likenesses below, in this way, decree judgment on every cup up to thirteen knives. What is the reason? Because they leave seven knives to assist all who behold the glory. A human being has no permission to use those seven. And those seven only labor over the thirteen below, in the way that those thrones are toward Him. Therefore, all decrees and all judgments below come from those seven knives below, all of which are crowns of knives of protection. And the spirit of the whole world is by the hand of this level, which is the very life of protection, standing in a likeness such as this world, in order to be purified toward the Upper World; for it has no help to be cleansed and purified except from the lower beings. And when he marks protection like the marking of days, then he is ready to spread his wings over them and to say with them—and concerning this it is written: <note>Leviticus 23:40</note> **"And you shall take for yourselves on the first day the fruit of a majestic tree."** These are the portion of the fruit tree, and you will find them like the fruit of a majestic tree, for all "splendor and majesty are before Him." Why is it called <term>Majestic (Hadar)</term>? And who is this "Majestic" one? This is the <term>Righteous One (Tzadik)</term> <note>The Sephirah of Yesod, the foundational procreative force</note>. Why is he called "Majestic"? For he is a hidden place that has no revelation and must always be covered, and "majesty" is only a vision that is revealed and seen! However, even though he is a hidden level, he is the majesty of the whole body, and the majesty of the body is found only in him. What is the reason? The nations see him, my brother; a level that has no majesty cannot enter the assembly. The voice is for the nations like a male, and the majesty of the voice spreads from him. The beard and the majesty of the beard are for the nations, and to remove the assembly, that level—all the majesty of the body is in it; it emerges, is hidden, and is revealed. Therefore, the <term>Majestic Tree (Etz Hadar)</term> is the tree upon which all the majesty of the body depends, and this is the "tree that produces fruit." <term>Palm branches (Kapot Temarim)</term>: Here she is included below like her husband; the bride is separate, but the "palm branches" are as one. <term>And branches of thick trees (Anaf Etz Avot)</term>: These are his three branches, this one on this side, that one on that side, and one that mediates over them <note>Representing the Sephirot of Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet</note>. <term>And willows of the brook (Arvei Nachal)</term>: Two that have neither scent nor taste, like the legs of the body. Therefore, the <term>Lulav</term> includes them all, in the likeness of the arrangement that stands in the body. And that which bends outward—so he saw, for the sake of the soul, to provide for all and to wash as is proper. And therefore, with these species, a person must appear before the Holy One, blessed be He. The leaves and foliage of these palms are all majestic matters that are grasped in those colors, for we require the below to be in the likeness of the above. There is nothing in the world that does not have a prototype above. As it is above, so it is below. And Israel must appear in the <term>Spirit of Faith (Ruach de-Meimanuta)</term> before the Holy One, blessed be He. <note>Leviticus 23:42</note> **"In booths (Sukkot) you shall dwell for seven days."** This is the Spirit of Faith. My brother, the verse speaks of the Upper World. And so we have learned: when the world below is awakened, my brother, when the Upper Wisdom (Chokhmah) labors to bring forth a matter that is unknown and unseen, then a single measurement goes forth. And the Upper Wisdom placed a covering within it and it spread to all sides in a spirit that is found above. And the covering was found upon it, bringing forth six sides. And then the covering was like a bright measurement, and it is written: "In booths (Sukkot) you shall dwell for seven days." Who is the "Sukkah"? It is Kindness (Chesed), and this is found below, standing to be seen in all directions. And then "In booths you shall dwell seven days"—behold, seven days from the Upper World to the lower, for they all stand in the existence of Wisdom, corresponding to the Sukkah. And who is this? This is the "fallen Sukkah of David," the "Sukkah of Peace." And the holy flock must sit beneath the wing in the Spirit of Faith. Whoever sits in this shadow sits in those upper days, and they all act as a single support of peace, to show that whoever sits in this shadow sits in those upper days, to cover him and protect him in the hour of need. And come, they are all called "Sukkot" <note>plural</note>, as it is written, yet it is written defectively as "Sukkah" <note>singular</note>. This refers to the lower world, like these seven holy days.

...holy ones, to be for all of them a source of blessings above. While they [the celestial powers] are all in joy as is the way of the world, the Accuser <note>original: *katigora*, the spiritual prosecutor or Satan</note> shall not bring charges. And because they occupy themselves with that Altar of sacrifices for those gatherings more than on other days, it is so that they [the "other side"] should be occupied with them and not later interfere with the joy of Israel. And what is the joy of Israel? This is the day of **Atzeret** <note>The holiday of Shavuot, the "Assembly"</note>. And come and see: while the other appointed ministers receive their portions and shares from that Altar which Israel prepares for them, they [Israel] are preparing the Throne for the Holy One, Blessed Be He, from below, to cause Him to ascend above in joy. And the meritorious merit, and in joy, to bring forth purities. Then she [the Shekhinah/Divine Presence] ascends and takes blessings and joy as is the way of the world, and surrounds herself with kinds of blessings, a source and portions, prepared and overflowing. And they are like a knot tied in the clouds above, as has been said. Once she descends, and within her is like a knot of all blessings and all holinesses and all delights. And Israel thus for seven days would invite her through the portions of the deeds they perform and offer therein; then, like a groom toward a bride, they call them "one day." And that day is a day of desire, because all the other seven days were in holiness, and regarding this, it is the perfection and the completion of days as one. And because of this, it is called **Atzeret**—a gathering. All are gathered on this day, and it is called "the eighth," yet there is no "eighth" except from within the seven. It is written: *Let the name of the Lord be blessed* <note>Ps. 113:2</note>. What is "blessed"? Rather, all know that all this is so, but one of the companions knew, as he mentioned what a priest showed him, and Rabbi Isaac Caphtora was his name. What is "blessed"? A beginning that is hard <note>original: *kata*, meaning harsh or constricted</note> and its end is soft. What is "hard and soft"? It is certainly so for him. And afterward, soft. In this manner, this day is soft. What is this that is written: *And by the breath of His mouth all their host* <note>Ps. 33:6</note>? To show the world was created, and for this, it was created in harshness. Afterward, it was soft. And regarding this we have learned: every beginning is hard and their end is soft, like the day that wipes away sin. What is "hard in purity"? Like the day of **Atzeret**, which is soft in this. Come and see: when purity ascended to life, purity. Purity ascended, a beginning whose end is hard, and it is not seen that he should be crushed by it, and all that he saw was to strengthen. And after they were purified, he did not go up from there until he ate and turned aside everything so that nothing remained. But purity, the wine from below, the beginning is hard, and whoever sees to prepare it until it is clear, they are bent. In this manner is the portion of the Holy One, Blessed Be He. Sometimes purity is awakened above to watch over the world, like the days of the **Flood** <note>The Great Flood in the time of Noah</note>, and because of this, nothing remained in the world except for that Ark of purity which lived in a manner that it could endure that strength. And sometimes the Holy One, Blessed Be He, looks with mercy upon the world and the whole world is treated with loving-kindness, as it is written: *The Lord sat at the Flood* <note>Ps. 29:10</note>. And because of this, purity did not labor above over the worlds, for the worlds could not endure it even for a single moment. Meanwhile, Rabbi Shimon was weeping and rejoicing; he lifted his eyes and saw before him those veils that the companions were wont to seek for him. They stood and saw Rabbi Shimon on this side, and facing him was **Rav Hamnuna the Elder**. He said: "As the way of the wise, for in another way they were drawn." Rabbi Shimon and those companions with him saw three things. Rabbi Shimon said: "To your lives, travelers, what is this way before you?" They said: "To seek him, to find the waters of wisdom we have come." Rabbi Shimon came and kissed him, saying to him: "The way is supported, the way is wise, and the way dwells with you." Rabbi Shimon opened and said: "*He reveals deep and hidden things; He knows what is in the darkness, and light dwells with Him*" <note>Dan. 2:22</note>. The verse says "He reveals deep and hidden things"—the Holy One, Blessed Be He, reveals the deep and hidden things of all the hidden supernal depths; He reveals them and strikes the taste of their revelation. Because "He knows what is in the darkness," for he [man] does not know the way. But He knows what is in the darkness, and because of this, He reveals deep and hidden things, for if not for the darkness, the deep and hidden things would not be searched out. "And light dwells with Him"—what is this light? This is the light from below.

# Portion of Ki Tissa

## Main Text (Zohar)

**And the Lord spoke** to Moses, saying: "When you take the sum of the children of Israel according to their number..."
> **"And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: When you take the sum <note>literally: 'lift the head'</note> of the children of Israel according to their number, then every man shall give a ransom for his soul to the Lord when you number them, that there be no plague among them when you number them."** (Exodus 30:11-12)

Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Assi were walking, and Rabbi Yossi was with them, traveling toward Tiberias. While they were walking, they saw Rabbi Elazar coming toward them, and Rabbi Hiyya was with him. Rabbi Abba said: "Surely the *Shekhinah* <note>the Divine Presence</note> is here now." They all walked together until they reached one another. When they met, Rabbi Elazar said: "It is surely written:
> **'The eyes of the Lord are toward the righteous, and His ears are open to their cry.'** (Psalms 34:16)

This verse is difficult..." etc. *(You will find this discourse in the portion of Pekudei, page 262, section 66, in its proper place)*.

Come and see: It has been established that a blessing from Above does not rest upon a thing that has been counted <note>referring to an object that is strictly enumerated</note>. And if you should ask: "How then were the people of Israel numbered?" Rather, a ransom was taken from them, and the counting was established through that ransom; the counting did not actually occur until all that ransom was gathered and the total sum rose. First, they would bless the people of Israel, then they would count the ransom, and afterward, they would return and bless Israel again. Thus, Israel was found to be blessed at the beginning and at the end, and no death <note>original: *motana*, meaning plague</note> befell them. Why does death arise during a counting? Because a blessing does not rest upon a number. Once the blessing is removed, the "Other Side" <note>original: *Sitra Achra*, the realm of impurity/evil</note> rests upon it and is able to cause damage. For this reason, they take a ransom and an atonement to remove the strike from upon them, and so it was established and stated.

## The Faithful Shepherd

**The commandment** to give the half-shekel in the shekel of the Sanctuary. The Faithful Shepherd <note>Moses</note> asked: "What is the half-shekel?" It is like the half of the Name <note>the Tetragrammaton, Y-H-V-H</note>, and this is the letter *Yod* [י] which is the median between the two *Hehs* [ה]. Blessed is he who goes to weigh the silver *Yod* which is circular. He studied the Shekel: "The rich shall not give more and the poor shall not give less." One should not increase beyond ten <note>the numerical value of the letter Yod</note>. And so it was explicitly stated: **Ten Sefirot** <note>Divine emanations</note> of nothingness—ten and not eleven. And likewise, one should not decrease. This is the "Righteous One" <note>the Sefirah of Yesod</note> who does not decrease from the ten; all is ten and not nine. The half-shekel is the letter *Yod*. The Faithful Shepherd said: "From the *Aleph* I will fatten you. The secret of Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note> fills your mouth." There is no movement in all those precious things that come out of your mouth, for if this were not by the secret of the King, there would be no movement for their feet to come out with their interpretations—words like harps, pure words—except that "to say" is the movement. He said: "Blessed are you, Faithful Shepherd." From then on, speak your wisdom of service... to hear from you... wheat... to say more, speak your wisdom until another time. The Faithful Shepherd opened the next commandment: To sanctify the Basin, because the Basin is holy, it is the base that is sanctified...

## Main Text (Zohar)

Every arm is spread out <note>referring to a ritual gesture of spreading the hands</note> so that it appears as if the Divine Presence rests upon them, as it is written: *And you shall sanctify the Levites.* And after the New Moon is seen, one recites the blessing over it: "Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the Universe, who by His word created the heavens, and by the breath of His mouth all their host." <note>original: "Baruch Atah... asher be-ma'amaro bara shechakim..."</note> And then she <note>the Moon/Shekhinah</note> is sanctified and blessed through **Beauty** <term>Tiferet: the central Sefirah representing harmony and the sun</term>, because she is a "crown of beauty" for the **Righteous One** <term>Tzadik: the Sefirah Yesod, the foundation and channel of blessing</term>. Thus far.

**Rabbi** Yose and Rabbi Hiyya were walking on the road until evening fell. They sat in silence, wondering what to do. They said: "Let us rise and speak words of Torah as we go on our way." One began and said: "How joyful are the masters of our way! For now, all those 'children of faith' from the Mountains of Light are gathering toward this light and worshipping it until the sun comes out. For as soon as the sun emerges, all those who worship the sun depart. Those who worship the light call to this light that shines in the crown of the sun until it emerges and passes by like a shining pearl. And they place their trust in these 'gods' of the shining pearl."

"And if you say that this worship was directed toward an appointee <note>an angel or celestial governor</note> from among the Ancient Holy Ones—they knew the wisdom of the time when the sun is bright, until that appointee who is in charge of the sun emerges. The holy ones of the sun are appointed over it, marked upon the 'head' of the sun. And by the power of those letters <note>mystical Hebrew letters engraved on the sun's orb</note>, he opens the gates for all the children of heaven and flies through them and passes. And there is a great appointee over that river of light that shines around the sun, and he is found there until the sun goes out and spreads through the world. That appointee is in charge of gold and fine pearls. And they worship that image that is there, according to the commands prepared by the ancients. These are the ones who know the 'commands of the sun' to find the places of gold and pearls."

Rabbi Yose said: "How many such false worships are there in the world! For falsehood has no standing to endure." He opened his discourse and said:
> *The lip of truth shall be established forever, but a lying tongue is but for a moment.* (Proverbs 12:19)

Come and see: all the people of the world used to worship this side <note>the side of idolatry</note>, every light that shines. If only it were the truth! The stars of the heights of heaven are indeed truth <note>as creations of God</note>, but through their own folly and corruption, they [the idolaters] speak and call them 'gods.' This is like a light vessel whose works are from ancient times. But for the Altar that is to come, the stars and lights of the world shall not be changed for anyone who worshipped them.

And this verse is as follows: *The lip of truth shall be established forever.* These are the People of Israel who take hold of the 'lip of truth'—*The Lord our God, the Lord is One.* And all of it is the Name and the Master of Truth, and they conclude: *The Lord your God is Truth.* And this is 'the lip of truth shall be established forever.' *But for a moment* <note>Hebrew: 'Aregi'ah'</note>—it should have said 'for a second.' What is *Aregi'ah*? It means: how long will the 'tongue' [of falsehood] endure in the world? Only until the time comes for this difficult worship they perform to pass away. And in a moment, the 'lying tongue' will be changed. The tongue shall be changed from those who call 'god' to that which is not God. But regarding Israel, who are the 'lip of truth,' it is written: *The Lord, I have set His praise and our story.*

Regarding this, I remember a story of what Rabbi Eleazar once did with a certain man. Rabbi Eleazar, the sage of the province of Judea, was traveling. That man said to him: "I know [your Torah]." He said to him: "Do you not say that your faith is truth and your freedom is truth, while our faith is a lie and our freedom is a lie? Yet it is written: *The lip of truth shall be established forever, but a lying tongue is but for a moment.* Behold, the appointees of the world <note>the nations/idolatrous powers</note> endure in their kingdom and have never been removed; thus the 'crown of the generation' is established forever. But you—you had a kingdom for only a short time and it was immediately lost to you. Therefore, this verse is fulfilled in us, for it is written: *but a lying tongue is but for a moment* <note>The skeptic argues that Israel's brief kingdom proves they are the 'lying tongue' that only lasted a moment</note>."

Rabbi Eleazar said to him: "I see in you a wisdom as empty as your 'freedom.' May the spirit of that man be deflated..."

<summary>This page discusses the blessing of the New Moon and the mystical mechanics of the sun's light, leading into a debate between Rabbi Eleazar and a skeptic over the interpretation of Proverbs 12:19 regarding the endurance of Truth versus Falsehood.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

That man went on to explain another verse: *The lip of truth shall be established forever* <note>Proverbs 12:19</note>, as we have said. But it is not written "is established," rather *shall be established* <note>original: תכון (tikon) - future tense</note>. The lip of truth is destined to be repaired in a way that is not currently the case; for now, the lip of falsehood stands firm, and the lip of truth is cast down to the dust. But at that future time, it shall rise to its standing, and out of the sorrows <note>original: וחדן (vadin) - likely referring to the pangs of exile</note> it shall be comforted; then, *the lip of truth shall be established forever.* That man said to him: "Fortunate is your portion, and fortunate is the nation of the Torah who inherit the truth!"

After some days, I heard that he passed away. If only they had reached a certain field and uncovered their heads <note>A gesture of mourning or deep mystical focus</note>. Once they uncovered their heads, they said: "From here on, it is written as a folly..." and it is written in the vertebrae <note>original: בחוליתה (be-chulita) - referring to the spinal column where deeds and sufferings are spiritually recorded</note>.

Rabbi Yose opened and said: *Behold, they shall cry out and all who were incensed against you shall be ashamed...* <note>Isaiah 41:11</note>. The Holy One, Blessed Be He, is destined to settle the account for Israel for all those slaughters that the seventy nations <note>The traditional number of the gentile nations in Jewish thought</note> committed against them, and for all the evils Israel suffered in their exile. If it were not for all those slaughters and blows being recorded in the "vertebrae," they would not be able to stand and endure the exile. But they go to the Houses of Study, open the books, and see all those slaughters that were struck against them—and these blows are written in the vertebrae, for the Holy One, Blessed Be He, accounts them to their credit. Thus they are comforted in their exile, even while the nations taunt and blaspheme them, saying to them: "He has forsaken you! Where are those slaughters you say are destined for us? Will all the nations of the world really be put to shame because of you?"

Listen to the word of the Lord, you who tremble at His word: *Your brothers who hate you... have said, "Let the Lord be glorified"* <note>Isaiah 66:5</note>. These "tremblers" are those who remember and endure many evils, hearing report after report, one after another, and they tremble over them, as it is said: *For we have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace* <note>Jeremiah 30:5</note>. These are the ones who tremble constantly at His word, as we have learned. *Your brothers who hate you*—these are the brothers of Esau <note>The descendants of Edom, often identified with Rome or Christendom in medieval Jewish literature</note>. *Who cast you out*—calling you "unclean" and "happened upon by chance" <note>A play on the word 'Kari' (impurity/chance)</note>. For there is no nation that treats them as such outcasts as the children of Edom and Ishmael <note>original: ארמי (Aramean/Ishmael) - referring to the Islamic world</note>; they all drag them down. And it is not just that they cast you out, but they say: *Let the Lord be glorified through us*, for we are the children of the Living God, whose Name is written upon us. Indeed, the dominion of the world belongs to that "great portion." Esau is called "the great son," and just as the Holy One, Blessed Be He, is called *Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised*, so we are the children of the Great One, and to Him belongs greatness. Certainly, *Let the Lord be glorified through us*. But you [Israel] are the smallest of all; "Isaac's small son" <note>Jacob/Israel</note> is written of you—where is He with you? Where are those slaughters that will cause all the nations to be ashamed because of you? *Let us see your joy*—as you say will happen.

And the verse concludes: *But they shall be ashamed.* The Holy Spirit says: *But they shall be ashamed.* Just as a curse is hung upon another, because they said that by right [Israel] should be ashamed and confounded. But the Holy Spirit says this word: *Behold, all they that were incensed against you shall be ashamed and confounded.* These are all who were incensed to strengthen their holes <note>their fortifications/strongholds</note> in anger against you in exile; at that time, they shall be ashamed and confounded by all the good things they shall see bestowed upon Israel.

Rabbi Hiyya said: "It is certainly so. But we see that the 'Watchers of the World' <note>Angels or great Sages</note> see that the exile is prolonged, and the Son of David <note>The Messiah</note> has not yet come." Joseph bar Abba said to him: "It is so. But what makes Israel endure in this exile? All those 'beatings' that the Holy One, Blessed Be He, has struck them with. This is what is meant by what they do in the Synagogues and Houses of Study: they recount all those strikes and beatings in their hearts to endure whatever comes upon them. If not for this, they could not endure."

Rabbi Hiyya said: "It is certainly so, and the whole verse depends on this. And if you say: 'Let them awaken in repentance all as one now'—they cannot. Why can they not? Because it is written: *And it shall come to pass, when all these things are come upon thee...* <note>Deuteronomy 30:1</note> and then it is written: *And thou shalt return unto the Lord thy God.* And then: *The Lord will turn thy captivity and have compassion upon thee and will return and gather thee.* And it is written: *And thou shalt call them to mind among all the nations, whither the Lord thy God hath driven thee.* Until all those words are fulfilled, they cannot awaken [the redemption]."

It emphasizes that the redemption depends on the fulfillment of the biblical cycle of suffering and repentance.</summary>

# Parashat Ki Tissa

...to find repentance before them. Rabbi Yose said: How many gates of mercy and merit are open to all those in the <term>Exile</term> <note>Hebrew: Galuta</note>, yet they do not have the strength to open their mouths in prayer. If it were so, it would be as it has been in every generation: that they would not suffer the exile, nor be driven from the place of Torah to be mingled among the mountain-dwelling nations. He opened his discourse and said: *“Like a woman with child, that draweth near the time of her delivery, is in pain, and crieth out in her pangs...”* <note>Isaiah 26:17</note>

Come and see: Just as a pregnant woman whose womb is narrowed for her delivery, and nine months have not yet passed over her, and there is no one in the world who has not passed through sickness—yet in one day she lives through two years of thoughts and worries. All the times and pangs for a woman with child are filled with such thoughts. And even if only one day of sickness passes over them, it is considered as if they had passed through all those weighed-out thoughts. So too with Israel: once they have tasted the taste of death in exile, if they return in repentance, it will be accounted to them as if they had passed through all those things written in this Torah; for many are the sufferings that have passed over them from the day the exile began. Everything that is written, *“When it is narrow for you and all these things have found you in the end of days,”* <note>Deuteronomy 4:30</note> shows how much mercy the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>Aramaic: Kudsha Brich Hu</note> has for Israel.

This is comparable to a King who had an only son whom he loved with his very soul. Out of his love for him, he gave him a <term>Matronita</term> <note>The Queen/Shekhinah; the feminine aspect of the Divine</note> to raise him and teach him proper ways. One time, the son sinned against his father. The father came and struck him, and after he had transgressed his father's will, he returned to his old ways and sinned again. His father removed him from his sight and banished him. That son went out from his father's presence.

Later, when the King felt true mercy and saw the son was worthy as is fitting, so that the King his father should hear and have compassion on him—what did the son do? He said, "I am banished from the <term>Palace</term> <note>Aramaic: Heikhala</note> to another place; from now on I will do whatever I desire." What did he do? He went and joined with harlots and defiled himself with their filth, and no sickness was found in their filth to deter him.

The <term>Matronita</term>, who watches over that son every day, knew that he was dwelling among harlots and had joined them, and all his companions were of their kind. She separated herself from her place and exerted herself for her son. One day the King came to her and found her weeping. He asked her, "Why do you weep?" She said, "Should I not weep? For your son has gone out from the King's palace. And not only is he mixed among the commoners, but he sits among harlots! What will all the people of the world say—that the King's son sits among harlots?" She sought to appease and speak wisdom to the King.

The King said, "For your sake, let him return to his place." She said, "Indeed." The King said, "Since it is so, it is not necessary to bring him back by day, for it would be a shame for us that he should return from among harlots. And if he were not like this one who defiled himself so, he would see my glory as he went, and all my hosts would see my son in great honor. With how many a <term>Lamp</term> <note>Aramaic: Butzina; a metaphor for divine illumination</note> he would stand, and how many would wait for his approach at our right hand, a sight for all the people of the world to know and recognize that he is the King's son! Now, since he has defiled himself and diminished my glory, he shall return in secret so they do not know of him." And he returned to the King's presence and looked toward his brothers as in days of old.

What did the King do? He brought him and his mother out as witnesses from the palace. He said to the <term>Matronita</term>: "Prepare yourselves and you shall both suffer the exile and the blows there. Since you both suffer as one, then the time will come for my son to sit as is fitting." So it is with Israel: they are like the King's children. He brought them out from their confinement. And you might say that at that time they did not consider the decree of the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, for after he was seen to be established before his enemies... [text breaks off]

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Ki Tissa** <-
<note>original: "כי תשא" - The name of the Torah portion, meaning "When you take [a census]"</note>

From above. For all until they emerged. He brings them into concealment and they are not seen as is fitting. He opened [the discourse] and said:
> **"As a rose among the thorns, so is my beloved among the daughters."**
<note>Song of Songs 2:2</note>
Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, acts for Israel in concealment above, so too the matter revolves on earth in the supernal likeness. And at the time when the scent rises and is clarified from all the other roses of the world, it is only that one which rises from among the thorns. And this is the proper way. And until the seed of the <term>Siphunim</term> <note>likely referring to the "seventy souls" of Jacob's family</note> who were seventy souls, and He led them among the thistles. And they were hidden immediately, for they were this and that; there the branches and leaves ascended and ruled over the world, and then the rose blossomed among them. Then, just as the Holy One, blessed be He, needs to bring out the rose and pluck it from among them, then the thorns dry up and are cast away. And they are found and yet not found to be anything, like the reason one goes to pluck this rose to bring out the firstborn son <note>original: "ברה בוכרא" - referring to Israel as God's firstborn</note> as in that time. And the King's army came amidst many great hosts, and their rulers with flags spread out, and He brought out His firstborn son with many mighty deeds and armed him for His palace and returned the presence of the King's children. It blossomed as before and He measured with kindness and deposited from His strength. What did they do? And Israel saw that they were scattered among all, mixed among the nations like melting miracles among the creatures, and they gave birth because of their strength. The Holy Mercy <note>original: "רחמי קדישא"</note> acted as a guardian over them. And because the Holy One, blessed be He, did this, He sees the makeup and the shame for them; let the son come from his own place, makeup and flute, and it is not seen that he is here, and the strength is there to bring him out and to perform miracles and wonders for him as before. They shall all be like a cry that appears to them, all worship and miracles, but there they are scattered, all of them there in poverty, and they shall come to the King's palace in shame, and the Holy Mercy prepared for them. They were spared as before. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He brought out this son as before from His palace, and His mercies and kindnesses see their strength, and further mercy and pain, and they shall consume many evils together, kindness and <term>Pitucha</term> <note>a mystical term for "mixture" or "engraving"</note> wisdom ascends. And regarding this it is written in the Prophet: "And from its midst all things are smooth in the End of Days." What is "in the End of Days"? Rather, this is the Holy Mercy which is the End of Days, and the days bore all that they bore in exile. And they shall return in repentance, even one like this or one young woman, and it shall be listened to regarding them; they all bore everything. And the living and hidden one envied the evil, and all the generations with him, as the Holy Lamp <note>original: "בוצינא קדישא" - referring to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> said, as it is written: "to its paths, for the one who acquires it for his generations." And in this matter, it depends on repentance. Rabbi [Shimon] said: Hope and push, thus he hoped. And until the exile is extended, everything is the Holy One, blessed be He; all that He sees for Israel is all for the End of Days, and He performs miracles and vengeances, as it is written:
> **"And it shall come to pass in the End of Days, that the mountain of the Lord's house shall be established at the top of the mountains."**
<note>Isaiah 2:2</note>
What is this Holy Womb? This is the Ancient Matron <note>original: "חברתא סבא" - a reference to a high Sefirah, likely Binah</note> in this chariot, the womb of all. And because it should be a womb, the Cup of Blessing <note>original: "כוס דברכה"</note> is given there in this Holy Womb, this first Ancient Matron, and afterwards the Holy Cup of Blessing. And it is necessary to place the weight <note>original: "מתקלא" - the balance/scale of the Sefirot</note> on the right. And he took the hills <note>original: "מגבעות"</note>. And it is necessary for his finger to be upright so that it may be a secret upright from the table to bless the Holy One, blessed be He, and this is it, and thus the hills. What is it? Rather, it is Understanding <note>original: "Binah"</note>. And because the blessings are to join his will, his error is for them; he took the Cup of Blessing, the hills, and for life. And until here it is precise for this firstborn son in the End of Days. And remember for good, you have said well; a voice called and pushed, thus he hoped. In the Holy Womb. This is the right side, the Ancient Matron, for it is the Holy Womb and for life. And he took the hills from the measure of the hills, for they are his will. And you have said well. And after these, all the nations. What is "hoped"? And his memory is for a blessing, even the elder and the youth. For the one who serves at the table, fresh to the lap, this is dark-eyed, and it is necessary to hear and to say to them: that a man should not hasten here, not the dark-eyed and the blue-eyed, no.

Since we do not need this time, let us hear a word that will gladden us. And their end is within it. This is: *Praise the Lord, all you nations* <note>Psalm 117:1</note>. These are the [nations of] Datis and Kitos <note>Likely referring to historical Roman-era persecutors or symbolic enemies</note> who are exempt from the commandments, for on the day of the universal blessing, they are only obligated to know how to bless. And this is the meaning of *Then all the nations shall praise Him*. Rabbi Yose opened [the discourse] and went out. He said: How beautiful is this word and how powerful in its wisdom. He opened with this precise point: "I have spoken half before You." What is the meaning of *The House of the Lord was visited*? It should have written "the visitation of freedom" before You. It is established that the Lord, may He be blessed, is the Lord in spread-out mercy. What is the meaning of *In the end of days, the House of the Lord shall be established*? <note>Isaiah 2:2</note> Rather, the "End of Days" is the Tree <note>The Sephirotic Tree</note> that extends from the heights to its mouth, which is the Tree of Good and Evil. And the verse comes to clarify: *In the end of days*, and it brings forth *the House of the Lord was visited*. This is Good and that is Evil. "The Mountain of the Lord" is certainly a place where the **Other Side** <note>The realm of impurity/evil</note> has no portion, for the Mountain of the House of the Lord has been clarified. Who is it? It is certainly the Tree of the End of Days, which is the **Cup of Blessing** that is seen, for example, in the mystery of the spread [mercy]. Rabbi Yose and all the companions said: This is to the merit of our King. But we have heard this: One day occurred between us as we walked together, and I was astonished, and I said to Rav Hamnuna the Elder that the verse was expounded, and I called to Rabbi Isaac... and since we heard it from its place, freedom was tied to his wings and his garments so that it would never depart from his vessels. He said: This holy word illuminates the concealment of the holy stars. Blessed is the generation that sustains the world, whose pillars are occupied with it. And if the wisdom of prophecy in this matter is like the scent of myrrh that shall not depart from you, my beloved, this connection of three is further bound in the knees with silver that shall not depart from his vessels forever. Regarding that matter which the Holy One, Blessed Be He, sees below—for example, when He saw that a beloved remnant remained before Him like all the generations—and the generation did not want to protest against the "Saturians" <note>Possibly a reference to forces of judgment or specific adversaries</note>. From where do we know this? From that which is written: *The beginning of the word of the Lord to Joshua* <note>Hosea 1:2, though the text mentions Joshua, the quote is often linked to Hosea</note>. This was established as a word until the number of his kin shall be as the sand of the sea, etc. We are meritorious in this; this is blessed like many blessings to crown them with the rebuke that is below them, regarding their merit in Heaven. And He does not move from there until the Holy One, Blessed Be He, forgives their sins and their life is restored before Him. Elijah—what is written of him? *And he sat under a certain broom tree* <note>1 Kings 19:4</note> etc. He said: The sicknesses of the lower world were arranged for Israel, and he [Elijah] spoke before Him. For it is written: *And she sat under the palm tree of Deborah* <note>Judges 4:5</note>. This one [Elijah] saw a broom tree. And she [Deborah] restored them to the good, as it is written: *Until I, Deborah, arose*. And there was an eternal love between them and a companionship before them, and he could not [succeed], until while he was sitting, the Holy One, Blessed Be He, was revealed to him. He said to him: *What are you doing here, Elijah?* He said: *I have been very zealous* <note>1 Kings 19:10</note> for the former things, for the accuser has risen and they have neglected the **Covenant**. And since I have seen that you were zealous for Me regarding that Covenant, it is covered for you with the desire of sweetness, and it is given to you until you go... He said thus: *I give him My covenant of peace* <note>Numbers 25:12</note>. Now that you have seen this, you shall not be signed to accuse them; you should have sought [mercy] before Me as in the beginning, for what was mine I provided to another hand and did not accuse him. *What are you doing here?* What is "here" (*Poh*)? The Covenant exists; the "Mouth of the Lord" (*Peh*) is He. Since you did not want to open your mouth for them, it shall be broken like the seal of that mouth. We have learned: At that moment, He removed from him that cloak which gave him strength. For we learned: What is the meaning of that which is written: *And he went in the strength of that food... unto Horeb the mount of God*? <note>1 Kings 19:8</note> To seek from there. Did he really need to seek from there? Rather, to seek as in the beginning from that which he inherited at the Mount of God—the Covenant of the Eighth [Day]. Elijah certainly opened in one level. He said: Moses did not have the strength to receive from the power of the sickness, but go to the children of Israel, bring them down... and see, it will be sufficient for you. And so he did. How much goodness does the Holy One, Blessed Be He, do for every single generation. Come and see what is written: *And I sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam* <note>Micah 6:4</note>. Was it by the staff in their hands? They were the staff and the portion...

## Ki Tissa

"And I shall send before you the white and the black staff, and you shall open your eyes and see and gaze upon how much blackness is in its striking, and how it is scattered and separated. And this is a threefold vision." Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "My people, my children, do not remember all the merits I performed for you, and how I arranged to do good for you and to provide sustenance." 

This is like a king of flesh and blood who had a province and decreed to take foreign property for the governors <note>original: *eparchs*, high-ranking officials</note> so that the people would be sustained by them. They looked into them and their ways; whoever needed to show a spark of their purity in matters that the people of the province would need, they did so against their will, and they needed to look into them and take from them and call out. 

"I arranged to do good for you and placed before you and shone light for you and your children and your children's children, to exert effort in your purity and in everything you required. I arranged for your lack, that there should be palaces to delay for you the footsteps of honor, to serve over you among kings. You lacked precious mountains so that you would not approach your neighbors and those above you, and they would be afraid at all times. I arranged for the sustenance of life in the fortress to strengthen you, and you and your cattle were satisfied. Grace was given to you, and from their own you ate and drank, and you sat in their canopy of honor. Yet from your own you did not give to them; and not only that, but they exerted themselves for you and carried your burden on their shoulders, while you were plucking and clipping them."

Rabbi Yose said: "Is it not the end of the matter that He has mercy on His children in holiness?" And the verse is as it is written: *Not one word has failed of all His good promise...* <note>Joshua 21:43 / I Kings 8:56</note>. Come and see His mercy: if it had said "not one word has failed of all His word" and no more, it would have been better for the world not to have been created. But since it says *of all His **good** word*, go out and see the reverse: for He does not wish to perform an evil matter. Even though there is anger, wrath, and rage below, He saw and it was strengthened by His right arm, and the lash stood in its place and did not descend below, and it was not carried out. Because of the anger, both were a vision of wrath and a smile held by His right hand. 

And if you say, from where do we know this? From the matter that was seen as revealed, as it is written: 
> *Go, get down, for your people have dealt corruptly* <note>Exodus 32:7</note> 

For He looked backward, and the staff—which did not know mercy—saw what was unleashed. When the Holy One, Blessed be He, saw this, He embraced him and was angry with him and said: 
> *Now therefore let Me alone* <note>Exodus 32:10</note> 

Immediately he seized the staff and held the arm of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: 
> *Remember Abraham...* <note>Exodus 32:13</note> 

This refers to His right arm. Because of this, the lash did not descend. And if you say he saw that he was a messenger to sound the lash of the King, which left the matter to do good... I do not know the clarity of the matter until I am before the Holy Lamp <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note>. 

When he came before Rabbi Shimon, a redness <note>a blush or divine glow</note> broke out on his face. He said: "Enter, holy children! Enter, beloved of the King! Enter, my beloved ones! Cast love here!" 

For Rabbi Abba said: "All those companions who do not love one another depart from the world before their time has arrived." All the companions in the days of Rabbi Shimon had a love of soul and spirit between them. Because of this, in the generation of Rabbi Shimon, everything was revealed. For in the end, Rabbi Shimon said: "All the companions who do not love one another cause a situation where 'the end does not discipline the beginning.' Furthermore, they cause a defect <term>peguim: a spiritual blemish or flaw</term> in that Torah; for love, distance, and quarreling are within it." 

Abraham loved Isaac, and Isaac loved Abraham; they were embraced one with the other. Jacob held both of them in love and brotherhood, and their spirits merited one another. The companions must follow that example so as not to create a defect. When he saw the redness in his face and he spoke to them thus, they said to him: "Surely a gathered spirit labors over the Holy Lamp, and thus we need to know." 

Rabbi Shimon wept and said: "One word! These matters are precious to see from the Head of the Academy of the Garden of Eden, which they did not say openly. This is the Secret of Faith for you: now love, now love like a pomegranate bud! What shall I do? They told me in a whisper, and here I see it all revealed, and for the rest, the wise are covered in a covering of all..."

Rather, "Mixed Multitude" (*Erev Rav*) refers to a specific group.

They would climb the levels to the Mountains of Darkness, and their spirit would be defiled by all those sorceries. They performed all these things that were seen until their will was achieved. They are called *Erev Rav* because there is "Evening" (*Erev*), and "Watchers" (*Irin*), and "Deception" (*Ta'atu'a*).

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Ki Tissa**<-
<note>Exodus 30:11–34:35</note>

And this "lower wisdom" <note>original: *chokhmata d’letata*</note> belonged to the "mixed multitude" <note>the *Erev Rav*, non-Israelites who joined the Exodus</note>, and there are two types of "mixed" groups. Their wisdom was great, and they observed the hours of the day and gazed upon the level of Moses. They saw that from every side, Moses seemed to have vanished <note>a play on the word *boshesh* (delayed) and *ba shesh* (the sixth hour had come)</note> at the first hour of the day when they looked for him. The higher levels that he held onto were covered and hidden from them. From every side, he was concealed. Because of this, they saw he was delayed in descending from the mountain, as it is written:

> **"When the people saw that Moses delayed coming down from the mountain..."** (Exodus 32:1)

Immediately, **"the people gathered against Aaron."** For we have learned that at that moment, Moses was weakened <note>or "hidden"</note> as he was receiving the Torah alone. All of Israel and the pious ones receive the Torah in the world—even the Scroll of Esther, as it is written, "and the Jews accepted" <note>Esther 9:27</note>. It should have said "the Jews *will* accept" <note>plural</note>, but why does it say "accepted" <note>singular</note>? This refers to Moses, who is equal to all the Jews while he lives. **"The people gathered against Aaron."** Why against Aaron? Because they wanted to be included in the "Right Side" <note>the side of Mercy/Chesed</note>, even though they themselves sought the "Left Side" <note>the side of Judgment/Gevurah</note>. Because Aaron was the inclusion of the Right below, they came against him and said, **"Come, make us gods."** "Gods" <note>Elohim</note> certainly refers to their desire for the Left Side. **"Who shall go before us."** It should have said "who shall go" <note>singular</note>; why **"who shall go"** <note>plural</note>? Because these "gods" are six levels, all on the Left Side. If you say there are seven, the Supernal God <note>Elohim</note> is not included in that count.

Come and see: any species that comes from the side of impurity does not mention the Name of God <note>Elohim</note> as a blessing. This is why it was said to Pharaoh, "I have given..." and further on the Name of the Lord <note>the Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note> <note>original: יהוה</note> so that the "Other Side" <note>the realm of evil</note> would not have strength or prevail in the world. Now, that "king" <note>the impulse of the Erev Rav</note> desired this, saying **"Come, make us gods."** They specifically said **"go"** <note>plural</note> because "we need this matter to strengthen our side, which has been pushed away until now." **"Who shall go before us."** What did they mean? They said: "We see that for these Israelites, all the good and precious things of the world go before them, while we are like those who are cast out." **"And the Lord went before them by day"** <note>Exodus 13:21</note>; likewise, they asked for **"those who shall go before us,"** just as the Lord went before the Israelites.

Come and see: all those precious clouds did not cover anyone except the Children of Israel alone. That Cloud of Glory, of which it is written **"And the Lord went before them by day,"** traveled before them. But these "Mixed Multitude," and all their cattle and oxen, traveled outside the camp of the Shekhinah <note>the Divine Presence</note>. Come and see: all those forty years that Israel traveled in the wilderness, no heat, filth, or waste was found within the clouds. Therefore, the cattle and oxen traveled outside, along with all those on their side. Rabbi Eleazar said: Thus, the Mixed Multitude did not travel from the strength of the Cloud. Rather, they were like a servant given a seal; they traveled from the leftovers of the "Crown" <note>Keter</note>, the refuse and the "scraps" of the camp. When they ate the Manna for forty years, it was not the same. "And the Children of Israel saw and said, **'What is it?'** <note>Man Hu</note>" for they did not know what it was that went to the cattle that were among them. Until now, the Mixed Multitude had been suppressed, but now they rose up and sought an action to strengthen the "Other Side." They said to Aaron: "We have been taken as a holy people and included with you; give us a portion that will go before us, just as your portion goes before you." Aaron thought: "It is better for these to be nullified within the holy people so that all becomes one, and they do not mix with the holy people in a bad way. It is better to separate them from the holy people until Moses arrives." Aaron intended it for good, but there were those from Israel who joined them in their sin. Because of this, every tribe had to be clarified and the holy people had to weep for that sin, and they were given that "drink" <note>the water mixed with the gold dust</note> until they were all clarified.

What is written? *And he took it from their hand and fashioned it with a engraving tool* etc. <note>Exodus 32:4</note>. But these people cast off the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven from upon themselves and sold themselves to another. May those coiled snakes be uprooted, those who sought a source for their corruption! They did not want silence or shame, but rather their sin; they "took off" the yoke of Heaven. Moses commanded them and gave them purity, so they would have no portion in the soft-hearted people. What did they do? The two of them divided that gold, one part like two, and one part escaped. They stood facing the sun with twenty-eight "errors" <note>mystical degrees of impurity</note>. They worked their engraving tools and whispered with their tongues the magic of the mouth. When the beginning of the seven wisdoms arrived, both of them placed their hands upon the hands of Aaron. From here we learn that he took from the hands of both of them and no more, as it is written: *And he took from their hand*—the two of them were there and no more. Since they showed [the gold], he received it from their hand—two, and not "their hands." ... It is written: *For it is in evil* <note>Exodus 32:22</note>—he brought evil upon the world. The secret of the matter is that those wicked ones, the guilty magicians, were the sons of Balaam the sorcerer, the grandsons of Laban the coiled one. They saw that the Cup of Blessing is on the right, a living thing, and from the right it is always strengthened. Life! He said to them: "Set it down as before, and we shall strike it to take it." They were not able to... in the heart of the sand from their hand at all. And the verse is interpreted: *And he took from their hand.* Arise and see what Aaron did: he acted with all of it, he recognized the cup and did not know that it was hidden, like dew from the magic. All the magicians of the world were not able to prevail. But as they finished this deed, it was because it was pressed from the earth.

**And he fashioned** it with an engraving tool. Not as people think, that he made a drawing with a compass or another vessel. Rather, the verse comes to prove the matter of Aaron—that he did not know how to guard himself. If, when he took it from their hands, he had thrown it to the ground and mocked it, and not chosen it, the profanation would not have occurred.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->When You Take Up<- <note>Hebrew: *Ki Tissa* - the opening words of Exodus 30:12, naming the Torah portion.</note>

If not for this evil deed, there would not have been a collective assistance for the evil that took hold here, hidden from the "Evil Eye" in the "Evil Crown" <note>The shadow side of the Sefirot, or divine emanations</note>. The Serpent strikes and decrees—the Serpent—which is everything present here in the vessel of destruction <note>original: *kisa cheres*</note>, and it was preserved. Then everything rose up into action. In the **Book of Enoch** we find that he said as follows: when a spirit is exchanged, it is born from filth, and when they come from the "Other Side" <note>The realm of impurity or evil</note>, they mislead him with that which enters. The children of this place, all their knowledge and their form, are like a candle [engraved] with a **stylus** <note>Hebrew: *cheret*</note>.

With a wise **stylus**—this is the pen of sinful wisdom that misleads human beings. It pushes away the clarity of what is rejected and forced. When the world was misled by the pen, there was a recording of a whisper of all forms and divisions, all of them recorded by that pen with a whisper. And because of this, it says **"with a stylus"** <note>Exodus 32:4</note>, which is to make it known how to act in this way; and this is the clarification. Everything was like dregs in the cup of destruction here, and it was covered from the eye, just as we have said regarding those sorcerers. "And he struck with your staff" <note>referring to the magic of the Egyptians</note> in the manner of these sorcerers. And this is the work done with these styluses; the matter was needed to be revealed and to shine.

Afterward, it required hiding and covering. First, they are hidden from the eye, and afterward, it comes out in its time and its craft. The matter that was hidden in weeping was afterward hidden in the grasp of the beginning. Now, the children of his beloved, the beloved of hunger, even to act and to push, it was necessary to engrave a connection and a hiding of words.

On the side of Holiness, that True God <note>original: *Elohim de-Kashut*</note> who reigns over the world, participated in three matters:
1. In **Creation** <note>Beriah</note>
2. In **Formation** <note>Yetzirah</note>
3. In **Action** <note>Asiyah</note>

And regarding this, it is said that the spirit of everything is here.
Corresponding to **Creation**: <note>Exodus 32:4</note> **"And he took it from their hand"**—a matter that had nothing in it until now.
Corresponding to **Formation**: <note>Exodus 32:4</note> **"And he fashioned it with a stylus"**.
Corresponding to **Action**: <note>Exodus 32:4</note> **"And he made it a molten calf"**.

The seers saw sorcerers throughout the whole world. Now it must be asked: is it not written, <note>Psalms 106:20</note> **"And they exchanged their glory"** and no more? And then, "and he fashioned this calf." But now you say, "and he made it a molten calf." Rather, see that Aaron acted and called out to Wisdom, as it is written, <note>Exodus 32:20</note> **"And he took the calf which they had made."** But from what is written, "And he took from their hand" and "And he fashioned it with a stylus," it implies that if these two "nothings" <note>referring to the mystical elements or the sorcerers' contributions</note> had not been done, it would be as if he [Aaron] had made it. If those two "nothings" were not there, it would not have been made and would not have emerged into its craft. For whoever is made through those two, it is as if "he made it" for him, yet it says "they made."

While the life-force was drawing out the matter for laughter, the sorcerers were performing their craft and whispering with their mouths, pouring a small amount of spirit from below, from the "Other Side." They poured two spirits as one: one male and one female. On the outside, it struggled in the form of an **ox**; at the point, it was in the form of a **donkey**. Both were included as one. Why these two? Rather, the ox is mentioned, and the donkey is its companion. Because of these styluses that are mentioned, it is written of them: <note>Ezekiel 23:20</note> **"Whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys."** And because of this, all those of Israel who died were buried together in their shame. And because there were two forms, it is written: <note>Exodus 32:4</note> **"These are your gods, O Israel,"** and it does not say "This is." Rather, "These" refers to the two that were as one. The calf was lacking from the hole... the calf and not the calf.

**"And he made it a molten calf, and they said"**—it is written "and they said," not "and he [Aaron] said," for Aaron said nothing. The onlookers saw, and there were twenty talents [of gold] in it. How then is it written, "And he took from their hand"? Did they all have all those talents? Rather, from the totality of those talents, all were matters of the [mystical] form. And that small amount rose above them all as if it were all of them in their hands. Come and see, it is written: <note>Exodus 32:5</note> **"And Aaron saw, and he built an altar before it."** Oh, holy pious one! How much your will was for the good, yet you did not know how to be on guard. Since they banned him on the mountain to strengthen the matter of the "Other Side," the firstborn was there, and the form emerged.

## Main Text (Zohar)

The male image, as we have said, follows two paths toward the **Other Side** <note>original: *sitra achra*, the realm of evil or impurity in Kabbalah</note>. Immediately, "And Aaron saw" (Exodus 32:5). What did Aaron see? He saw that the **Other Side** was gaining strength and moving toward the powers of judgment, and he recognized that this world was about to be destroyed. It is like a bandit who was bent on plundering and killing. What did he do? To prevent the king's property from being stolen, the bandit <note>referring here to the personified evil force</note> bowed down as if he were powerful, attempting to go his own way with the king. When he saw the "Image of the King" <note>the Divine presence or a holy representative</note> standing before him, he immediately knelt and prostrated himself backward. So too, "And Aaron saw" that the **Other Side** had grown strong. It began to lodge itself and strengthen within the side of **Holiness**, and Aaron trembled before it. Once the Evil Side saw the Image of the King standing before it, it immediately turned backward and its strength was weakened. Regarding this, it says: "And he built an altar before it" (Exodus 32:5). This proves that the **Other Side** was removed and weakened. Come and see what is written:

---

# **And He Called**
"Aaron [called out] and said: A feast to the Lord tomorrow." A feast to the Lord, and not to the "tail" <note>the lower, impure forces</note>. He acted for the side of **Holiness** and drew near to the side of **Holiness**. This is the "Art of Holiness," for without this, the world would not remain on its foundations. Yet, despite all this, the Divine anger was not removed from Aaron, even though he did not intend any evil. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: "Aaron, two other things will happen to you because of what they desired. By your life, your two sons shall fall." This decree was cut because of that incident. "Tomorrow" was meant to destroy them. These were the sons of Belial <note>wicked men</note>, and their fruit was destroyed from above. For "fruit" refers to his sons. Just as Aaron trembled before that proof and the Calf was pushed backward, his sons trembled before the **Other Side** and the side of **Holiness** was pushed backward, as it is written: "And they offered before the Lord" (Leviticus 10:1).

> And they offered before the Lord. (Leviticus 10:1)

They trembled "before the Lord." They were seized by this sin. Aaron had said, "Let it be tomorrow," meaning he delayed the altar until the next day. If it had been as they [the sinners] wanted, it would have happened immediately. But he hurried to set up a staff <note>a symbol of authority or a barrier</note> for that altar to guard it, just as the children of Iddo stood over the altar at Bethel. But here, another "king" was visible. And it is written: "And he burned the calf which they had made," but it does not say he destroyed the altar. Come and see:

"And Aaron called." Aaron himself called out and said. It is written here "And he called and said," and it is written regarding Hanukkah <note>or a dedication context</note> "And he called to the Lord." Just as there it refers to a male principle, here too it refers to the male. "A feast to the Lord tomorrow." At that time, the altar was prepared to trouble them. "A feast to the Lord" was meant to act with strength. Then the judgment came and the Lord struck the people. One strike was through the Levites, and one was the plague upon the Children of Israel. This was the "feast" of the Levites—the Levites through whom the Lord struck. "Tomorrow" he set them up. They stayed that night, and in the morning they were found bound and dead. They were like guests in death all night, and by morning they were found dead. Thus, "A feast to the Lord tomorrow." All the strength that Aaron exerted was because it is written, "And he built an altar before him." Come and see, it is written "And he saw the calf and the molten image," but it does not say he saw the altar, for Aaron was sanctifying his hands. Aaron intended it for his own soul, and his will was entirely for good, as he did not intend evil.

Rabbi Eleazar said: Is it really so? Did Jeroboam not also make calves? The Israelites made them. He said to him: My friend and my teacher, he [Jeroboam] reached out and killed, and he was punished because he certainly did evil. Rabbi Y.B.A. said: Behold, it is known that the side of **Holiness** does not trouble itself even for the heart of the world, and the "thief" could not steal from that side in this way. What did he do? Immediately "The King gave and he looked," etc. When the Evil one took it, he said, "Take it."
