Because it was shown that the profane was found in every place. And so, in this way of restoration, it was distanced because of it, for in all of this, she <note>referring to the Divine Presence or the community of Israel</note> could be delayed even in the representation of the mountain. Two stone tablets were living engravings, as it is written: *Engraved upon the tablets* <note>Exodus 32:16; the Sages play on the word "charut" (engraved) and "cherut" (freedom)</note>. Thus were those two evil spirits who destroyed as was fitting for them; they are male and female. The female was in the form of which it is written:
> For the lips of a strange woman drip honey
<note>Proverbs 5:3</note>
And beneath them there is more to her crowns, as it is written: *And the man went before the one as far as Dan.* And because of two wheels they were guarding them, and he rode in the holy way, and there was laughter over him and over Israel. And he withheld blessings from the world, and they shall flow down; it is written: *golden earrings* and so forth. And because of this they were acting, for behold, the first garment that was worn because of it, which showed the mountain of the bosom <note>a mystical reference to the site of the revelation</note> as has been said. And if you say they saw the mountain of the bosom as a calf—it was certainly seen as such, and so in all sides is the beginning of evil, and this is the "bosom" that we have established. And because of this, the children of mercy, once they had sinned, sought and covered so as to belittle the wisdom of their deeds; the first destruction is hot to see this always, like the arm of the King, and the ascent of this will was there. And it was necessary for Moses to see there in this, since the Holy One, Blessed be He, looked at him, he looked. Three times He doubled it for him; he saw the staff of the <term>Faithful Shepherd</term> <note>Aramaic: Ra'aya Meheimna; a title for Moses</note>, how great is the mighty strength, how great is Your power. Three times He doubled it for him, as it is written:
> And now, let Me be, that My anger may blaze against them and I may consume them
<note>Exodus 32:10</note>
This makes two.
> And I will make of you a great nation
<note>Exodus 32:10</note>
This makes three. The wisdom of Moses proceeded in three strikes. He desired with the right arm corresponding to *let Me be*. He grew weak in the left arm corresponding to *that My anger may blaze against them and I may consume them*. He embraced the body of the King corresponding to *and I will make of you a great nation*. And when he is embraced in the body, the two arms from this side and from that side do not delay the side between them; this was the wisdom of Moses, for just as the King's officials know in each one of them in which place to strengthen, so he acted with wisdom. Rabbi Eleazar said, and the companions assisted his hands. Rabbi Abba was there and said: If we were only brought into this world to hear this, it would be enough for us! He wept and rejoiced, saying: Woe, Rabbi, when you depart from the world, who will shine and reveal the lights of the Torah? For this matter is like darkness that will be awakened until now, which went out from us and shines to the height of the firmament, and in the throne of the King it trembles, saying what is there at this time. Behold the strength! Behold the addition called by the Holy King; who will awaken words of wisdom in prayer like you?

Come and see: before they sinned, Adam would ascend and stand in supernal wisdom in the higher light, and he was not separated from the force of life. Once they sinned, he was distanced from the wisdom of knowing, and to take below he was drawn after them until he was separated from the <term>Tree of Life</term> <note>Hebrew: Etz ha-Chayim</note> and knew evil and abandoned good. And about this it is written:
> For You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You
<note>Psalms 5:5</note>
Whoever is drawn after evil has no dwelling with the Tree of Life. And because of this sin, they would hear a voice from above and knew supernal wisdom and did not fear. Once they sinned, the voice went out from below and they were not able to stand in it. In this same manner, because of this, Israel sinned. At the hour when Israel stood at Mount Sinai, that which was dark was removed from them, like a fetus that is shaved <note>purified</note>, and they were made like it, and then they were attached to the Tree of Life and ascended above and did not descend below. Then they knew and saw through the <term>shining mirror</term> <note>Aramaic: Aspaklaria; a prophetic vision</note>, and their eyes were enlightened to stand and to know. And then the Holy One, Blessed be He, girded them with <term>crowns of armor</term> <note>Aramaic: Kitrin de-Zaynin</note> of the <term>Holy Name</term> <note>Aramaic: Shema Kadisha</note>, so that the <term>evil serpent</term> <note>Aramaic: Chiva Bisha</note> could not rule over them and would not defile them as before. Once they sinned with the Calf, all those levels and supernal lights were removed from them, and the shield of the shield—the crowns of the Holy Name—was removed from them, and the evil serpent drew near to them as at first and caused death for the whole world. And later, what is written?
> And the children of Israel saw the face of Moses, that it shone
<note>Exodus 34:35</note>

# Ki Tissa

Because the skin of Moses' face shone, and they were afraid to come near him. Come and see what was written previously: "And Israel saw the great hand," and they all saw the supernal lights and were illuminated by the **shining mirror** <note>original: "aspaklaria de-nahara," referring to a clear prophetic vision</note>, as it is written: "And all the people saw the voices." Because of this, they saw and did not fear.

-> But once they sinned, what is written? "And they were afraid to come near him." Come and see what is written concerning them: <-

**And the children of Israel stripped themselves** of their ornaments from Mount Horeb. These were the crowns <note>original: "zivunin," radiant spiritual garments or crowns</note> with which they were crowned at Mount Sinai so that the **evil serpent** <note>original: "hivya bisha," representing the inclination toward evil and death</note> would not have power over them. Once these were removed from them, what is written? "And Moses took the tent and pitched it outside the camp, far from the camp." Rabbi Elazar asked: What does this verse have to do with that one? Rather, once Moses knew that those supernal crowns had been removed from them, he said: "Surely from now on the evil serpent will come to dwell among them, and if the Sanctuary remains here among them, it will be defiled." Immediately:

**And Moses** took the tent and pitched it outside the camp, far from the camp. This was because Moses saw that the evil serpent would now have power, which was not the case before. And he called it the **Tent of Meeting** <note>original: "Ohel Moed"</note>. Was it not called the Tent of Meeting before? Previously it was just called "the Tent," but now it is "the Tent of Meeting." What is the meaning of "Meeting" <note>original: "Moed," which can mean an appointed time, a festival, or a boundary</note>? Rabbi Elazar said it is for good. Rabbi Abba said it is for ill.

Rabbi Elazar said it is for good: Just as a "Moed" <note>festival</note> is a day of joy for the Moon <note>the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> in which holiness is increased and the inner realm rules, so too here he called it by this name for joy, for it was only distanced from the congregation for their benefit. Therefore, it is written: "And he called it the Tent of Meeting."

But Rabbi Abba said it is for ill: Until now it was simply "the Tent"—the "Bride" <note>original: "Kallah," a wordplay on "Kalah" meaning finished/complete</note>—a tent for all times, every hour and every moment. But now it is a "Tent of Meeting" <note>an appointed time</note>. Previously, they were destined for eternal life, so that death would never rule over them. From this point forward, it is a "Tent of Meeting," as it says:
> "And the house of meeting for all living" (Job 30:23) <note>A biblical euphemism for the grave</note>.

Now a fixed time <note>a lifespan</note> was placed within it, and it invited "cutting off" <note>mortality</note> into the world. Previously there was no defect, but now there is a defect. Previously there was the union and joining of the Moon with the Sun <note>the Divine masculine and feminine</note> that would never cease. Now it is a "Tent of Meeting"—limited to a specific time. And because of this, "he called it the Tent of Meeting," which was not its name before.

Rabbi Shimon was sitting one night toiling in the Torah, and Rabbi Judah, Rabbi Isaac, and Rabbi Yose were sitting before him. Rabbi Judah said: It is written, "And the children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb." We have said that they brought death upon themselves, and from that time on the evil serpent ruled over them, which had previously been removed from them. This makes sense for the Israelites. But Joshua, who did not sin—why was that radiance removed from him? Did he receive that counsel of Mount Sinai or not? If you say it was not removed from him, then why did he die like all other men? And if you say it was removed from him, why? He did not sin, for he was with Moses at the time Israel sinned! And if you say he did not receive that crown at Mount Sinai as the rest of Israel did—come and see. He opened and said:
> "For the Lord is righteous, He loves righteousness; the upright shall behold His face" (Psalms 11:7).

The companions have said what they have said about this verse. But "For the Lord is righteous"—He is righteous and His name is Righteous, and therefore He loves acts of righteousness. "Upright"—this refers to the one who is entirely righteous and upright, and because of this "they shall behold His face"—all the people of the world—and their paths shall be mended to walk in the upright path as is fitting. And come and see: when the Holy One, blessed be He, created this world, it was to grant merit to the sides of human beings. And come and see: everything the Holy One, blessed be He, spared from destruction... [the sin] caused that species of the side of death to rule over the whole world... a defect in the Moon, until Israel stood at Mount Sinai. Once Israel stood at the mountain...

<meta>This page concludes the commentary on the Torah portion Ki Tissa and begins the portion Vayakhel. It continues the discussion of the spiritual damage caused by the Golden Calf, specifically focusing on the "blemishing" of the Moon (the Shekhinah) and the role of Joshua bin Nun.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

### [End of the Portion of Ki Tissa]

...who helped to impregnate that inner aspect of the Moon <note>original: *Siahra*; a reference to the Sefirah of Malkhut, the feminine Divine presence</note> so that it stood to shine constantly. However, once Israel sinned with the Calf, the Moon returned to its former state of being blemished. That Evil Snake <note>original: *Chuvya Bisha*; representing the primordial force of impurity</note> gained dominion, took hold of her, and pulled her toward him, and she was blemished. When Moses knew that Israel had sinned and were stripped of those holy armors <note>original: *zaynin kaddishin*; the spiritual crowns or protections granted at Sinai</note>, he knew for certain that the Moon had returned to its previous state, finding itself in a state of blemish. He then took it <note>the Tabernacle/Presence</note> outside. 

Even though the Moon stood in a state of blemish, Joshua remained protected by its "armor." Since the inner aspect was troubled and joined with that fear <note>the impure side</note> as it was blemished, no human could endure, and death originated from the "Other Side" <note>original: *Sitra Achra*; the realm of evil</note>, except for Moses who had dominion over it. Because of this, he constantly urged Joshua to remain [in the tent] and not to depart from it, for it was troubled, and who could approach it? 

Therefore, there is a Spirit of Life on the right above, and a living creature prepared below. There is a holy living creature above, and an impure living creature below. There is a living creature of the right above in supreme holiness, and a living creature of the right below in the "Other Side." There is a living creature of the left above in supreme holiness to awaken love, so the Moon may be bound in a holy knot above to be illuminated. But there is a living creature of the left below that separates the love above and prevents it from shining, causing a withdrawal and an approach to the "waste" <note>impurity</note>; this is the side of the Evil Snake. 

When this "left" below is awakened, it pulls the Moon and separates her from above; her light is darkened and she clings to the Snake. Then the darkness of death descends below to all, for all are attached to death and distanced from the portion of life. This caused death for the entire world, and the sanctuary was not spared until a set time when the Moon is repaired and returns to shine—this is the **Field of Appointed Time** <note>original: *Chakal Moed*; a mystical name for the Shekhinah/Moon when restored</note>. 

Because of this, Joshua died only due to the "counsel of the Snake" <note>a Talmudic concept that some righteous people died only because death was decreed on humanity by the original serpent, not for their own sins</note> which approached and darkened the face as before. This is the secret of what is written: *And Joshua the son of Nun, a youth...* <note>Exodus 33:11</note>. Even though he is called a "youth" below, corresponding to the Moon, *he did not depart from the tent*. Just as the one was blemished, so too was this one blemished, even though he possessed holy merit. Since it was blemished, he certainly was not saved from that actual Snake alone, as has been stated. 

Happy are the righteous who know the secrets of the Torah and cling to the Torah, fulfilling the verse: *And you shall meditate on it day and night...* <note>Joshua 1:8</note>. Because of it, they will merit the life of the World to Come, as it is written: *For it is your life and the length of your days...* <note>Deuteronomy 30:20</note>.

-># The Portion of Vayakhel<-

**And Moses assembled all the congregation of the children of Israel, etc.** <note>Exodus 35:1</note>. Rabbi Hiyya opened: *“If it had not been the Lord who was for us,” let Israel now say...* <note>Psalms 124:2</note>. Come and see: regarding the Calf, it is written, *And the people assembled against Aaron* <note>Exodus 32:1</note>—this refers to the Mixed Multitude <note>original: *Erev Rav*; the non-Israelites who left Egypt and instigated the Golden Calf</note> from the "Other Side." They gathered all the forces to wage war against Israel, which they should not have done before Him in that battle that Amalek waged against them. Indeed, the battle of Amalek was on all sides, above and below, for it was on the side of the Snake, to strengthen the Evil Snake above and to strengthen it below. Just as the Evil Snake lies in wait at the crossroads to confuse all, so Amalek was the Evil Snake toward Israel, lying in wait for them at the crossroads...

# Main Text (Zohar)

The dew of the blessing of Hermon, as it is written <note>Psalm 133:3</note>: *As the dew of Hermon, that descends upon the mountains of Zion.* This is like one who was above to connect the Sanctuary, and like one who was below to connect Israel. From where do we know this? As it is written <note>Deuteronomy 25:18</note>: *How he met you [karcha] on the way.* It is written here "met you" [*karcha*], and it is written there <note>Deuteronomy 23:11</note>: *If there be among you any man, that is not clean by reason of a chance [mikreh] that happens him by night.* And concerning Balaam it is written <note>Numbers 23:4</note>: *And God met [vayikar] Balaam.* Rather, the "husk" <note>term: Kelipah; the spiritual shell or outer layer of impurity that conceals the inner holiness</note> prepared that place to be found in impurity, according to the level he was attached to for his defilement. What did Balaam do? He increased his efforts in the preparation of sacrifices to ascend on high; immediately, the Holy One, blessed be He, prepared that place for him. But I am amazed at your confusion, as it was told to you regarding *And God met Balaam.* Because of this, it says *How he met you on the way...*—he [Amalek] invited that evil serpent above to destroy you on all sides. And were it not for the joining of the Name which is *Ziv"t* <note>A mystical permutation of a Divine Name</note> below, Israel would not have been able to withstand him. Therefore, the Holy One, blessed be He, bound that one who delayed for generations upon generations. From the children of [Cain] who improved to be uprooted, you stand behind. And because of this, *I have remembered* <note>1 Samuel 15:2</note> as a visitation, for there was hinted the secret that the holy standing did not remain.

Come and see what is written: *And he said to the Kenite* <note>1 Samuel 15:6</note>. See, this Kenite is Jethro. Did King Saul act on account of Jethro, to save those who dwelt among Amalek? But where did the Kenites dwell? For it is written <note>Judges 1:16</note>: *And the children of the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law, went up out of the city of palm trees with the children of Judah into the wilderness of Judah.* And from there they turned in their integrity toward Amalek until the time that King Saul came, as it is written <note>1 Samuel 15:6</note>: *And Saul said... depart, get you down from among the Amalekites.* Because when a judgment stands, those pious and righteous ones found among them are seized for their sins, as they have established. For this reason, were it not for that "mixture" <note>the Mixed Multitude</note> that was mingled among Israel, Israel would not have been delayed by the incident of the [Golden] Calf.

And come and see what was written at first: *under all the heavens* <note>note: original "h-s" likely abbreviation for HaShamayim</note> *which He gave to you*, to include everyone. For the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to perform a work that would be found on all sides, like the "brain" and the "husk" <note>term: Moach and Kelipah; the inner essence and the outer shell</note>. And because those Mixed Multitude were among them, it was said *under all the heavens which He gave to you* to include them among Israel, who are the "brain" [the essence]. And they were all commanded. Afterward, they strayed and committed harlotry after those Mixed Multitude and worshipped the Calf; they strayed, and after them those who died caused death and slaughter for Israel.

Afterward, the Holy One, blessed be He, desired from that point forward that the work to be found should only be from the side of Israel alone. Immediately <note>Exodus 35:1</note>: *And Moses gathered [Vayakhel] all the congregation of the children of Israel...* and it is written after it: *Take from among you an offering to the Lord*—"from among you" specifically, and not as before when it was written *under all the heavens which He gave to you.* *And Moses gathered...* why did he gather them? Because those Mixed Multitude were among them, Moses needed to gather them [Israel] to separate them from their midst.

->**Vayakhel (And He Gathered)**<-
---

*And Moses [gathered].* Rabbi Abba opened: *And he gathered the people* like a gathering and a collection and a flooding. Just as there they were all Israel, so here they were all Israel. And who are they? As the Mishnah taught. Rabbi Eleazar opened the verse regarding Israel when Moses descended from Mount Sinai, as it is written <note>Exodus 32:17-18</note>: *And when Joshua heard the noise of the people as they shouted [be-re'oh], he said unto Moses: There is a noise of war in the camp.* *And Joshua heard.* Did Joshua hear and Moses not hear? Rather, to the "other side" <note>term: Sitra Achra; the side of spiritual impurity</note> Joshua was not aware, but Moses was aware. If so, what is *be-re'oh* [as they shouted]? Rather, *be-re'oh* is written because it was a voice from the "Other Side" <note>a play on the word 'ra' meaning evil</note>. And Joshua, who merited to be the "face of the moon" <note>a metaphor for Joshua's relationship to Moses, who is the "face of the sun"</note>, looked into that voice which was from the side of evil; immediately, *he said to Moses: There is a noise of war in the camp.* At that moment, the two stone tablets that were at first were broken. And we have established that they became heavy in his hands and fell.

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Vayakhel (And He Assembled)** <-

...and they were decreed and clarified like wheat that is separated and thinned out from the chaff <note>original: "chiti" (wheat) and "mago lomi" (from the husks/chaff). This refers to the process of spiritual refinement where good is separated from evil.</note>. Come and see: in all sides of the world, during the four seasonal turning points, a sound is awakened. And within that sound, an awakening of the **Other Side** <note>The *Sitra Achra*, representing the forces of impurity or evil</note> is stirred. Through that awakening, the Other Side enters between one sound and another and is found within that lower sound. 
And because that upper sound did not reach the lower sound, that awakening preceded it. Regarding this, it is written that this sound is a "sound of war," a "bad sound" <note>original: "kol ra." A play on Exodus 32:17 where Joshua hears the noise of the people</note>. One should not be caught in the "bad." Joshua heard it and did not fail because he took that "bad" [ra] into the voice of Moses, who was shown in the secret of Joshua. And it ascended alone to that side. Joshua heard, and all of Israel were silenced by those shouts of that evil found among them. Once the **Holy One, Blessed Be He**, arrived among them, then **"Moses assembled all the congregation of the children of Israel and said to them: These are the things..."** <note>Exodus 35:1</note>. For that "Mixed Multitude" <note>The *Erev Rav* who joined Israel leaving Egypt</note> had become mixed into the commandment.

Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Yose were sitting one night and were occupied with the study of Torah until the night was divided at midnight. When the rooster crowed, a man began the blessings. Rabbi Eleazar said to him: "Now is the time when the **Holy One, Blessed Be He**, enters the **Garden of Eden** to delight with the righteous." Rabbi Yose said to him: "I hear a sound." Rabbi Eleazar bowed and said: "Come and see, until now the **Holy One, Blessed Be He**, has shaken three hundred and ninety firmaments and flown through them, and wept over the destruction of the Holy Temple, and shed two tears into the Great Sea. And all of them are counted before Him, because the night is divided into three sides across the twelve hours that are hinted at within it."

And if you say that the hours of the day are different, they are indeed distinct, but the night is carved into its own twelve. And those twelve are divided into three sides, and three watches of holy camps are divided among those three sides. 

The **first camp** is appointed over the first four hours of the night's beginning to praise their Master. They begin by saying: ***"The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof... For He has founded it upon the seas... Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord? ... He who has clean hands and a pure heart"*** <note>Psalm 24:1-4</note>. What is the reason? Because when night spreads its wings over the world, all the inhabitants of the world taste the taste of death <note>Sleep is considered 1/60th of death in Jewish mysticism</note>, and their souls depart to ascend above. And those angels stand and say: **"Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord?"** 

The "Mountain of the Lord" refers to the Temple Mount. "His Holy Place" refers to the **Court of Israel**. Just as it is above, so it is below. For in every firmament, there are many appointees and many officers standing there. And when the souls depart and seek to ascend, if they are not worthy, those officers push them outside. They seize them and strike them in the world, and nullify them with many confusing visions, telling them false things, and occasionally true things about what will happen in the near future, as has been established. 

But those souls of the righteous go and ascend above, and they open gates for them. They bring them into that place called the "Mountain of the Lord," corresponding to the spirit of the Temple Mount below. From there, they enter the place called "His Holy Place," where all the souls are seen before their Master, corresponding to the place where Israel prostrates before the **Holy One, Blessed Be He**, the place called the **Court of Israel**. When the souls stand there, then there is the joy of their Master to be adorned by them in the place called the **Holy of Holies**. There, all their deeds are hinted at and prepared for them.

The **second camp** is appointed over the next four hours. They do not say song except for two hours until the night is divided and the **Holy One, Blessed Be He**, enters the **Garden of Eden**. These are the ones who dwell in rest and those who weep over the destruction of the Holy Temple. At the beginning of the [next] four hours, they open and say: ***"By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept..."*** <note>Psalm 137:1</note>. These are the ones who wept by the rivers of Babylon along with Israel.

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Vayakhel (And He Assembled)** <-

It is implied that it is also written as a nickname. And from all of them, they wept there, as it is written: *Behold, you have been anxious with all this anxiety* <note>original: "hen charadtem"; referencing 2 Kings 4:13</note>. What is meant by "anxiety" <note>literally "strength" or "harshness"</note>? This refers to all the structures, for all their boldness reaches everywhere, and there they wept for my people. And because of this, they begin with this and conclude with: *Remember, O Lord, against the children of Edom...* <note>Psalms 137:7</note>. Then a voice is awakened in its levels and strikes the heavens, and twelve thousand worlds tremble. It cries out and weeps, as it is written: *The Lord shall roar from on high, and utter His voice from His holy habitation; He shall mightily roar upon His dwelling place* <note>Jeremiah 25:30</note>. He remembers Israel and lets fall two tears into the Great Sea.

And then a single flame <term>shalehovita - a spiritual spark or flame</term> is awakened from the North side, and a wind from the South side strikes that flame. It goes and wanders through the world, circling around until midnight. Then the flame goes and strikes the wings of the rooster <term>tarnegola - the rooster, whose crowing marks spiritual shifts</term>, and it crows. But the voice has no power until it rises above to the Garden of Eden <term>Ginneta d'Eden</term> to mingle with the souls of the righteous <term>tzaddikaya</term>.

And the secret of this is: *For as we wept for you and my people...* and *The king said, "Who is in the court?"* <note>Esther 6:4</note>. And *The king arose in his wrath from the banquet of wine and went into the palace garden...* <note>Esther 7:7</note>. At the moment the Holy One, Blessed be He <term>Kudsha Brich Hu</term>, enters the Garden of Eden, then all the hosts and the masters of the daughters and all those souls of the righteous open their mouths and say: *Open the gates, that the righteous nation may enter...* <note>Isaiah 26:2</note> and *Who is this King of Glory?* <note>Psalms 24:8</note>. Open the gates of mercy!

And at the time when the souls of the righteous who are on earth return to their bodies, then all those angels strengthen them and say: "Give a blessing to the living," and "All you servants of the Lord," and this is their portion. The third camp arises and they say this in the morning watch, the final watch, until the morning star rises. And then all those stars and constellations praise their Master, and all those high angels whose dominion is by day, they all praise their Master and sing a song: *When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy* <note>Job 38:7</note>.

At the hour when the sun <term>shimsha</term> comes out during the day, Israel ceases their song below and the sun sings above. And at the hour when the sun sets in its orbit, it opens a voice of pleasantness and sings a song. And what is the song they say? *Give thanks to the Lord, call upon His name... Sing to Him, sing praises to Him...* <note>Psalms 105:1-2</note>. And Israel praises the Holy One, Blessed be He, during the day along with the sun. For "he shall be feared as long as the sun endures," as we have established regarding this verse.

Rabbi Eleazar said: The dreams of the people of the world are blocked; they are closed-eyed and cannot stand the pleasant voice of the sun's orbit when it sets.

The pious ones who occupied themselves with the Torah during the day arose and went before Rabbi Shimon. When he saw them, Rabbi Shimon said: "Eleazar my son, you are wise and blessed. Keep yourselves hidden these three days and do not go outside, because the Angel of Death <term>Malakh ha-Mavet</term> is found in the city, and he has permission to destroy." For once permission is given to the destroyer, he can destroy. When a person stands before him, he rises and accuses him, and does not mention his merits <term>zakhvatan</term>. He demands judgment before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and does not move from there until that person is judged and permission is given to kill him.

Rabbi Shimon said: If not for the majority of the world, people would not die until their time arrived, except that they do not know how to guard themselves. For at the hour when a dead person is taken from his house to the graveyard, the Angel of Death is found among them. Why among them? Because he is the "prepared destruction" who is open to death, and because of him, death was caused for the whole world. And when he kills a person and strangers are found with the dead, he enters among them like a sword. He has no permission to kill openly, but from the moment they take the body from the house to the graveyard until they return to their houses, he causes death for many strangers in the world before their time has arrived. And regarding this it is written: *But there is that which is swept away without judgment* <note>Proverbs 13:23</note>. Because he rises and accuses and mentions merits—he mentions this before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and they are judged for those sins and taken away before their time. What is the remedy? At the hour they carry the dead to the graveyard, every man should turn to cover...

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Vayakhel (And He Assembled)**<-

To subdue [the evil side], one must turn their back to it. And see, those who go before it should put their hands behind them so that they are not seen face-to-face with it. And after they return from the cemetery, one should arrange themselves in that path which is written, standing still, and should not look at those [spirits] at all, nor stray to another path. Because people do not know and do not observe that the spirit of the world <note>The Angel of Death</note> returns in judgment and snatches them away before their time has arrived.

Rabbi Eleazar said: "By the Living God! Is it better for a person not to come to death at all?" He said to him: "No. For a person who guards himself as is proper, rest will be seen for the path that is prepared, and all the more so for the World to Come."

Come and see: it was not for nothing that the early scribes established the practice of observing the dead from a window <note>or "crevice"</note> toward the cemetery. If you say it was for the sake of the dead—no! Rather, it was to lead the living so that the Angel of Death <note>original: Malach ha-Mavet</note> should not rule over them to lead them astray above, and they be destroyed by him.

He opened his discourse and said:
> "When you go to war in your land against the adversary who oppresses you..." (Numbers 10:9)

And we have scrutinized this: "Against the adversary"—this is the Angel of Death. "Who oppresses you"—constantly, killing human beings and distressing them unto death, seeking to kill others. What is the remedy and the meeting with him? In the great way of the sound of the time <note>The Shofar</note>, for those who are above. The Angel of Death stands below in order to be found in the gathering, to ascend above and prosecute <note>term: Katigor - a spiritual prosecutor or accuser</note> them. And Israel, who know that the Angel of Death is present at that time below to place an accusation against them, they precede him with the Shofar to subdue him so that he cannot prevail over them or be found against them.

And all the time of the hour when he performs judgment and kills among everyone, he is found below. And all the time of the hour when they go to the cemetery and return from the cemetery, for that is the hour of which it is written:
> "Her feet go down to death..." (Proverbs 5:5)

In death, he is found before them, as it is written: "Her feet go down to death." They go down to where? To that place called "Death." And because of this, death was caused for the whole world. May the Merciful One save us!

Come and see, it is written:
> "Such is the way of an adulterous woman..." (Proverbs 30:20)

And we have established this. But "Such is the way of an adulterous woman"—this is the Angel of Death, who watches and blows <note>or "entices"</note>, and thus is called "She eats and wipes her mouth," destroying the whole world and killing among everyone before their time has arrived, and she says, "I have done no wrong," for the spirit sought them out, and they were found with sins, and they died by harsh judgment.

At the time when Israel made the Calf and all those multitudes died, the Angel of Death was found among the assembly, within the camps of Israel. As soon as Moses saw that the Angel of Death was found among the assembly and the camps of Israel were between them, he immediately gathered all the strangers <note>or "multitudes"</note> to be armed. This is what is written:
> "And Moses assembled all the congregation of the children of Israel" (Exodus 35:1).

These are the strangers of whom it is written they were "digging" <note>unclear: possibly referring to the mixed multitude</note> to be armed, and the Angel of Death did not depart from among the children until the Tabernacle <note>term: Mishkan - the portable earthly dwelling place of God</note> was established, as it is written:
> "And Moses reared up the Tabernacle" (Exodus 40:18).

And even at the time when the children were coming purely to be found, he did not depart from their midst until Moses showed and gathered the men with counsel, that they should not come as a single group with them, and should not be seen face-to-face, but rather behind their backs he would testify and they would stay in the lodging <note>original: achsanya</note> upon the assembly. "And they were able" is not written, but "And they finished" <note>wordplay on the Hebrew root</note>. On the path they did not ascend except behind their backs, because the Angel of Death did not depart from their midst until the Tabernacle was established.

Come and see: he is not found among them in less than a covering, nor less than ten. And on the path, as it is revealed openly, he is found and seeks judgment in the place of secrecy to kill. And because he was found among them in a revealed way, it is written they stayed in the lodging upon the assembly. All the companions guarded themselves that whole day and labored in the Torah <note>original: Oraita</note>.

Rabbi Shimon opened and said:
> "And they said to him, 'Where is Sarah your wife?'" (Genesis 18:9)

He said: "And all your house do not... <note>text breaks off</note>" The verse stands and we have established it, but come—could the Holy One, Blessed be He, not cancel for a person...

## Main Text (Zohar)

...from the midst of the whole world, and he does not take when he undermines, as it is written: *the wings of a dove covered with silver* <note>Psalm 68:14</note> and so on. And because of this, he saw that the male is fit to guard him according to the way of Israel, as it is written: *for [it is] not a soul as on a day of wrath* that does not: in their death... <unclear>illegible</unclear> ...rather, since the Destroyer <note>The Angel of Death</note> is common to the world, they saw that he does not close himself off, and he is found before him like a beast that is seen in its soul, for he kills himself. From here we learn what is written: *Escape for your life; look not behind you* <note>Genesis 19:17</note>. What is the reason <note>original: "mai ta'ama"</note> for *look not behind you*? Because the Destroyer walks behind one's shoulders, and if he turns his head and looks at him, and they are face to face, he is able to harm him. And regarding this it is written: *And the Lord shut him in* <note>Genesis 7:16</note>, so that the Angel of Death <term>Malakha de-Muta: The personification of death in Jewish mysticism</term> would not have power over him. And while they were hidden, there were thirteen foreigners... in their deaths... Rabbi Shimon said: Blessed be the Merciful One that he did not look upon the splendor of the form of the Angel of Death.

# **Vayakhel**
*And Moses gathered...* <note>Exodus 35:1</note> and so on. He returned them to the original matter of the work of the Tabernacle <term>Mishkan: The portable earthly dwelling place of God's presence</term>. Rabbi Hiyya said: All of them are as they have been stated. And the work of the Tabernacle was not performed except by Israel alone, and not those of the Mixed Multitude <term>Erev Rav: The group of non-Israelites who joined the Exodus from Egypt, often blamed in the Zohar for spiritual setbacks</term>, because those of the Mixed Multitude drew the Angel of Death into the world. Once Moses looked at this, he dismissed those of the Mixed Multitude and gathered Israel alone; this is what is written: *And Moses gathered...* Rabbi Shimon opened [with the verse]: *Who has ascended into heaven and descended? Who has gathered the wind in his fists? Who has bound the waters in a garment? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son’s name, if you know?* <note>Proverbs 30:4</note>. This verse, we have already established it, and how many pillars are in it, and all of it is said regarding the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>, for He is all, and it is said: *What is his name and what is his son's name, if you know?* This is the Holy One, Blessed be He. *What is his name?* [The name] *I Am*. *And what is his son's name?* Israel. As it is written: *Israel is my son, my firstborn* <note>Exodus 4:22</note>, and we have already established this. *Who has ascended into heaven?* We established that this is Moses, as it is written: *And to Moses He said, "Come up to the Lord"* <note>Exodus 24:1</note>. But *Who has ascended into heaven?*—this is Elijah, as it is written of him: *And Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven* <note>2 Kings 2:11</note>. And how could Elijah ascend to heaven? For all the heavens are not able to endure even a thought like a sifted mustard seed of this world! And yet you say, *And Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven*? Rather, it is in this manner: *And the Lord descended upon Mount Sinai* <note>Exodus 19:20</note>, and it is written: *And Moses entered into the midst of the cloud and went up into the mountain* <note>Exodus 24:18</note>. And did he ride a horse on Mount Sinai? And it is written: *And the appearance of the glory of the Lord was like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain* <note>Exodus 24:17</note>—how could Moses ascend to it? Rather, as it is written: *And Moses entered into the midst of the cloud and went up into the mountain*. Just as one enters a cloud as if he were clothed in a garment, so too he was clothed in the cloud and entered into it. And within the cloud, he approached the fire and was able to draw near. It is he of whom it is written: *And Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven*—for he entered into the whirlwind and was clothed in it like that whirlwind above. And we find [the concept of] Spirit <note>original: "Ruach"</note> in the Book of Adam, which says regarding those generations of the world: the spirit inherits a form for the world like the earth and is clothed in a body, and Elijah [ascended to] heaven. And in that body he shall ascend, and his body shall be perfected and transformed in the whirlwind, and a body of light shall be prepared for him to be among the angels. And when he merits, he is clothed in that body to be transformed in that whirlwind, and in that body he is stationed below. And in his place, he is above. And this is the spirit of *Who has ascended into heaven and descended?* There was no man whose spirit ascended to heaven and afterwards descended below except for Elijah, who ascends above and descends below. Another interpretation: *Who has ascended into heaven?* This is Elijah. *And descended?* This is Jonah, as it is written of him: *Jonah [went down] into the depths of the sea*. Jonah is compared [to Elijah] for he comes from him. Elijah ascended, Jonah descended. This one went in a ship to death, and that one went in a ship to death <note>A mystical comparison between Elijah's "chariot" and Jonah's "ship"</note>. And because of this, he is called "the son of Amittai" <note>Jonah 1:1</note>, and it is written: *and the word of the Lord in your mouth is truth* <note>1 Kings 17:24, "truth" is "Emet," the root of Amittai</note>. *Who has bound the waters?* This is Elijah, who bound the spirit of the waters in the world, and the rain of heaven did not descend upon it...

<meta>This page begins the mystical commentary on Parashat Vayakhel (Exodus 35). The text transitions from the general laws of the Tabernacle to a deep esoteric explanation of how the physical assembly of Israel mirrors the gathering of celestial forces. It focuses on the relationship between the "Matronita" (the Divine Presence/Shekhinah) and her "Husband" (the Holy One, blessed be He), mediated by the prophet Elijah and the archangels.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And He Assembled**<-

He spread his cloak to make coverings. **"Who has gathered the wind in his fists?"** <note>Proverbs 30:4</note> This refers to Elijah, who binds the spirit of a person within their inward parts <note>original: *me'oi*</note>; it is lacking, just as it is said regarding the silver of the Menorah. **"Who has established all the ends of the earth?"** <note>Proverbs 30:4</note> This is he who, after he **"wrapped the waters in a garment,"** <note>Proverbs 30:4</note> wrapped the kindness <note>original: *chesed*</note> in his exile and established the whole world, and his power is the rain, and his life-force is proven to all. **"What is his name, and what is his son’s name?"** <note>Proverbs 30:4</note> This is he. "And what is his son’s name?" This is Elijah. "What is his name?"—everything that ascends above is He. "And what is his son’s name?"—everything that descends below and becomes a messenger to make coverings, that is his name. 
The male aspect is "Who" <note>original: *Mi*</note>, the hidden one who is close; this is the Holy One, blessed be He, as we have established. And the "spirit below" is also "Who," as we have established. And here is the union of the **Supernal Chariot** <term>Merkavah: the divine "throne-chariot" representing the structure of the spiritual realms</term> as four sides, which are the primary foundations of all, and they all hang in that supernal place called "Who," as has been stated. 

Furthermore, see that when the hour of favor stands before the Holy One, blessed be He, to move the Supernal Chariot so that they all become purified, a voice goes out from that holy supernal place called "Heaven" and gathers all those holy ones below, and all those holy princes and supernal hosts, so that they are all ready as one. This is what is written: **"And Moses assembled all the congregation of the children of Israel"** <note>Exodus 35:1</note>. These are the twelve holy supernal sides. "And he said to them"—and he strengthens [the matter] and says: **"This is the thing... Take from among you an offering to the Lord"** <note>Exodus 35:4-5</note>. Prepare yourselves, for it is upon you to be united, and he called to the **Holy Throne** <note>the Shekhinah</note> to ascend above. Separate from among you those precious ones, those supernal princes, to raise up that "offering" <note>original: *Terumah*</note>, the mystery of the Holy Throne which is found as one. For the **Matronita** <term>The Divine Matron or Queen; a title for the Shekhinah</term> does not appear to come to her Husband except through those maiden-damsels who adorn themselves with her and accompany her until she reaches her Husband, as it is said: **"The virgins in her train, her companions..."** <note>Psalms 45:14</note>. And why all this? To come and be found with her Husband.

**Every** "willing-hearted" <note>original: *Nediv Lev*</note> person—these are the four supernal sides in which all the other hosts are included. And these are the ones who emerge from the **Supernal Wisdom** <note>original: *Chokhmah Ila'ah*</note>, who are called "willing ones" <note>original: *Nedivim*</note>, as we have established, for it is written: **"The well which the princes digged, the nobles of the people delved it"** <note>Numbers 21:18</note>. These are the priests. "Let him bring it" <note>original: *Yevi'ah*</note>—it does not say "let him bring her" <note>original: *Yevi'enah*</note>, but "let him bring it," to unite them all as one. And likewise, "let him bring" is not written, but "let him bring it" <note>ending in the letter He</note> to raise her up to her Husband as is required. **"The offering of the Lord"** <note>Exodus 35:5</note>—the word "Eth" <note>a grammatical marker</note> comes to include all those other supernal hosts that are found all as one, and they are twelve in total. **"Gold, and silver, and brass; and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats' hair; and rams' skins dyed red, and tachash skins, and acacia wood; and oil for the light, and spices for the anointing oil, and for the sweet incense"** <note>Exodus 35:5-8</note>. These are the twelve supernal hosts that are included all as one within the four sides of the **Holy Living Creatures** <term>Chayot HaKodesh: the highest order of angels supporting the Divine Throne</term>, as has been stated. And all these ascend to the Holy Throne to delight her above, to be found with her Husband so that they all become one. Because the Supernal Root is found with her, then the King sits upon the Holy Throne and is found below with her Husband so that they all become one. And then there is joy for all. 

Come and see: here the order counts gold first and silver after, because this is the lower dwelling. But when one comes to see the strength of the Chariot above, the order counts from the right first and afterwards from the left. From this it is written: **"The silver is Mine, and the gold is Mine"** <note>Haggai 2:8</note>—silver first and afterwards gold. But in the lower Chariot, the order is from the left and afterwards from the right, as it is written: "Gold, and silver, and brass"—gold first and afterwards silver. And all those who are called "willing-hearted"—all of them are the side of the Chariots. "Heart" <note>original: *Lev*</note>—what is "Heart"? It is the mystery of that which is written: **"A cheerful heart has a continual feast"** <note>Proverbs 15:15</note>. And this is the Heart of all, and this is the Holy Throne. And because of this, they are called "Heart."

<meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Vayakhel, specifically focusing on the construction of the Tabernacle and the spiritual requirements for those who contribute to it. ## Main Text (The Zohar)

The heart of every **willing heart** <note>Hebrew: *Nediv Lev*</note> is the wisdom of the foundation of the fortress where these [lights] are all guarded and called by one spirit. It is written: *The offering of the Lord* <note>Exodus 35:5</note>, which is in the likeness of the holy [supernal realm]. Because they lift it up on high and raise it to the highest levels, it is called "the Lord’s offering." Therefore, when the spirit of the likeness is seen and weighed, those who ascend are not seen, for she [the Shekhinah/Divine Presence] ascends to the Supernal King in concealment, in secret, and in supernal glory. And **every wise-hearted person** among you—these are the sources of the springs that sustain the world, and from them, they are established to strike and to heal. They strike only so that they may come to oversee the wings of life, and afterward, they provide the counsel that the Holy One, Blessed be He, commanded them to find for the world.

---

->**Take from among you an offering for the Lord**<- <note>Exodus 35:5</note> Rabbi Yehuda opened the discussion: ***Is it not to share your bread with the hungry...*** <note>Isaiah 58:7</note> Come and see: the portion of a man, when a poor person visits his house, that poor person is a gift sent to him by the Holy One, Blessed be He. He who supports and sustains him, receiving that gift with a shining countenance, [receives] his full portion. Come and see: one who gives to the poor and restores his soul, the Holy One, Blessed be He, considers it as if he had created that soul himself. Regarding this, the wisdom that stood for all the people of the world was credited by the Holy One, Blessed be He, as if He had created them, as it is written: ***And they turned over that which they had made*** <note>original: *v’tithapech asher asu* - a mystical reading of the "action" of righteousness</note>. 

And even though we have established this, look at the word "share" <note>Hebrew: *paros*</note>. Does "share" mean merely to spread a tablecloth for him with bread and food to eat? No, "share" means to break off pieces, like breaking bread <note>original: *perisin*</note> that is set before him so that he should not feel ashamed. And it says *your bread*—it does not just say "bread," but *your* bread. This means it must be from your own property and money, and not from what was stolen, or oppressed, or taken by theft. For if it is such, it is not a merit; rather, woe to that person whose sins are remembered because of it. This is why it says **Take from among you an offering**—it must be from what is *yours*, and not from oppression, robbery, or theft. This is true wisdom.

Rabbi Hiyya, Rabbi Yitzchak, and Rabbi Yose were walking on the road. As they were walking, Rabbi Abba met them. He said, "Surely the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> is with us!" When he reached them, Rabbi Abba said: It is written, ***Since the day that I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel to build a house, that my name might be therein... but I chose David...*** <note>I Kings 8:16</note>. This verse—its beginning does not match its end, and its end does not match its beginning! For it says "I chose no city" and then "I chose David." What does one have to do with the other? It should have said "I chose Jerusalem." 

However, when the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires to establish a people, He first looks at the head [the leader] to prepare the people for the city, and afterward He prepares the city and sees the people within it. Thus, "I chose no city" until I looked upon David to appoint him as a shepherd over Israel. For a city and all the children of the city all stand upon the merit of the shepherd. As it is written: *As the shepherd is, so is the flock.* If the shepherd is good, it is good for the city and good for the people. But if the shepherd is bad, woe to him, woe to the city, and woe to the people. And now that the Holy One, Blessed be He, has looked upon the world and it has risen in His will to establish it, He has strengthened it through the merit of the generation of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, to stand before Him. 

He opened and said: ***Happy is he whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the Lord his God*** <note>Psalm 146:5</note>. Why does it say "the God of Jacob" and not the God of Abraham or the God of Isaac? It is because Jacob did not rely on his wealth or his father-in-law when he fled from his father-in-law; he went alone, hoping for help, as it is said: ***For with my staff I passed over this Jordan*** <note>Genesis 32:11</note>. He relied only on the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: ***If God will be with me and keep me...*** <note>Genesis 28:20</note>. They all feared before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and He gave them "hope in the Lord his God," for in Him they saw their restoration and their trust. Do not read it as "his hope" <note>Hebrew: *Sivro*</note> but as "his looking" <note>Hebrew: *Sivro* - implying a prophetic vision or intense gaze</note>, for they gazed upon the Lord their God. ***For Your sake we are killed all the day long*** <note>Psalm 44:23</note>.

<summary>This page discusses the spiritual requirements for the Tabernacle offerings, emphasizing that charity must come from honest earnings. It also explains that the quality of a community depends on its leader (shepherd), highlighting King David and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai as exemplary figures.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Vayakhel, specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of the Tabernacle offerings and the concept of "Conditions of Creation" (Tnai Ma'aseh Bereshit).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The meaning is that "upon You we have trusted for healing." This is like Jacob, of whom it is written, *And Jacob came* <note>Genesis 33:18</note>, for he then thought in Egypt that he saw the breaking of the exile that would happen to him in Egypt, and the Holy One, Blessed Be He, strengthened his power. And because Jacob suffered the breaking of the exile, there was not found in them the spirit of faith from their wisdom, and the brain of truth was like a pleasant thing in their mouths. And regarding this it is written, *and my wine is a healing medicine* <note>original: "v'chamri li mas saman"</note> because they knew Him but did not merit Him for eternity, and they finished this breaking of theirs upon the nest. And because of this, etc., for redemptions and for longing and for many holy, supreme joys, those who suffer the breaking of the body search and search for the Holy One, Blessed Be He. How much more so are the righteous worthy there to perform for you miracles and redemptions, and you shall merit the life of the World to Come. See them all as one. He opened and said:

---

-> **128** <-

**Take from among you an offering to the Lord; whoever is of a willing heart, let him bring it, etc.** <note>Exodus 35:5</note> Come and see: at the moment a person places his **will** <note>Aramaic: *re'uta*; focused spiritual intention</note> toward the service of his Master, that will first ascends upon the heart, which is the sustenance and foundation of the whole body. Afterward, that good will ascends over all the limbs of the body, and the will of all the limbs and the will of the heart join together as one. They then draw upon themselves the radiance of the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence</note> to dwell with them, and that person becomes a portion of the Holy One, Blessed Be He.

**Take from among you an offering.** "From among you" was said to show that they should take it upon themselves for this offering to become a portion for the Lord. And if you should say that this matter is not within a person's own power, come and see: **whoever is of a willing heart, let him bring the Lord’s offering.** Truly, whoever's heart is willing for Her <note>the Shekhinah</note> to merit to dwell with him—the testimony of the produce of fire for their rejection as it ascends above—he shall bring it from the highest hidden place to cause Her to dwell with him. And when She comes to dwell with him, how many blessings and how much wealth come with Her! This is the meaning of **gold, silver, and copper**; for him, no wealth in the world is lacking. This is hidden in every world. All you holy supreme ones, "Take from among you an offering to the Lord."

One opened—the one who was weary from the road—and cited the verse regarding Jonah. He opened and said: *And Jonah called to the Lord...* <note>Jonah 2:2</note> and so on. Is this the place to speak of the sea? Rather, at the time the Holy One, Blessed Be He, created the world through the **Work of Creation**, on the middle day <note>the fourth day</note> He created the stars and constellations. At that time, He commanded and made a **condition** <note>Aramaic: *tna*; a cosmic stipulation</note> that a certain fish should be ready to swallow Jonah, and he would be in its belly for three days and three nights, and afterward it would cast him out.

And not only this, but everything the Holy One, Blessed Be He, made during the Work of Creation, He made a condition with it. On the first day, He created the heavens and made a condition with them that they should lift Elijah to heaven in a whirlwind, as it is written: > And Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven < <note>II Kings 2:11</note>. On the [second] day, He made a condition with it that it should darken for the Copper [Serpent] in its belly for three days, as it is written: > and there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days < <note>Exodus 10:22</note>. On the second day, He created the firmament which separates between water and water, as it is written: > And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters < <note>Genesis 1:6</note>. And the Holy One, Blessed Be He, made a condition with them that the waters should separate for Israel between purity and purity to be cleansed in them, and so it was.

On the third day, He brought the earth out from the midst of the waters and gathered the waters, and He made the gathering of the impurity of the gathering to become one sea. And He made a condition on that day to act for Israel as if on dry land, and to act against the Egyptians. And so it was, as it is written: > and the sea returned to its strength when the morning appeared < <note>Exodus 14:27</note>. Do not read "to its strength" <note>Hebrew: *le-eitano*</note> but rather "to its **condition**" <note>Hebrew: *le-tna'o*</note>—for the Holy One, Blessed Be He, had made a condition with it during the Work of Creation. Furthermore, He made a condition with the earth that it should open its mouth during the dispute of Korah and swallow Korah and all his assembly, and so it was, as it is written: > And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and Korah < <note>Numbers 16:32</note>. On the fourth day, He created the sun and the moon, as it is written: > Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven < <note>Genesis 1:14</note>. And He made a condition with the sun to stand still in the middle of the sky in the days of Joshua, as it is written—

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the soul's journey. While the previous section may have dealt with the construction of the Tabernacle (Vayakhel), the Zohar here pivots to an allegorical interpretation of the Book of Jonah to explain the soul's descent into the physical world and its eventual return to the Creator.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Vayakhel** <-

As it is written: *Then stood up Phinehas, and executed judgment: and so the plague was stayed* <note>Psalm 106:30</note>. A woman <note>The Shekhinah or the soul is often personified as feminine in mystical texts</note> among the stars to wage war like the moon, as it is written: **The stars in their courses fought against Sisera** <note>Judges 5:20</note>. On the day when the frost strengthens, all the stars of the sea and the clear waters come in flight to feed their ravens at the time He decreed for the children, as it is written: **And I have commanded the ravens** <note>The text notes a correction to 1 Kings 17:4</note> **to feed thee there.** The word "commanded" is precise. A woman among the stars of the sea is prepared, all as one, to swallow Jonah and to be found as a male <note>A reference to the fish in Jonah changing gender in Midrashic tradition</note>. On the day the frost strengthens for the month, and they come with him to go out from the house below to the sparks of the moon, as it is written here: *I have commanded there*—lacking the vowel *cholam*—*to sustain you.* Here, "I commanded" refers to the creation of the world. And so, in every single deed used in the world, the Holy One, blessed be He, ordained that deed from the day the world was created. Also here, *they became warm* <note>original: "vayeichamu"</note>... the days of Creation are mentioned here to show how much providence we have in the world over the deeds of human beings in this world.

**Jonah** who descended into the ship—this is the **soul** <term>Neshamah: the highest level of the human soul</term> of a person that descends into this world to be within the body of a human being. Why is it called a "woman"? <margin>Another version: "A woman"</margin> Because once it is joined with the body, it is then like a "dove" <note>The Hebrew word "Yonah" means "Dove"</note> in this world. As it is said: *Ye shall not therefore oppress one another* <note>Leviticus 25:17; the word for "oppress," "tonu," shares a root with "Yonah"</note>. And then a person travels through this world like a ship in the great sea that is destined to be broken, as it is said: **And the ship was like to be broken** <note>Jonah 1:4</note>. And when a person is in this world, he sins and imagines he is fleeing from before his Master, and he is not found in this world. And then the Holy One, blessed be He, brings a mighty tempest—this is the **decree of judgment** <term>Gezirat Dina: the heavenly verdict</term> that stands constantly before the Holy One, blessed be He, demanding judgment for every soul before Him. And this is what tosses the ship and the limbs of the person to break him. When a person is seized by that storm in his illness, what is written? **And they were afraid... and he went down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep** <note>Jonah 1:5</note>. Even though the person is in his illness, the soul does not awaken to return before its Master to redeem its sins. What is written? **So the shipmaster came to him.** Who is the "shipmaster"? This is the **good inclination** <term>Yetzer Tov: the internal moral guide</term> which leads everything. And he said to him: **What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God** etc. <note>Jonah 1:6</note>. This is not the time to sleep, for they are taking you to judgment for all that you have done in this world; repent of your sins! Look at from where you came and return to your Master. What is your "work" <note>The Hebrew "melachtekha" can mean work or craft</note> that you occupied yourself with in this world, for it comes up before your Master? And those "arrivals"—look at from where you came, from a putrid drop, and do not be arrogant before Him. What is your "wisdom"—for it is for labor and to the earth you shall return. And "what is your people"—look to see if you have the **merit** <term>Zechu: spiritual credit</term> of your fathers to protect you. When they bring the soul to judgment to quiet that storm—which is the decree of judgment that storms over a person—it demands from the King all those who are "prisoners" of the King, and they all come one by one before Him like a stormy sea approaching for judgment. There are those among them who open with merits, and those who open with sins. And the decree of judgment demands justice. And if that person is not worthy, what is written? **Nevertheless the men rowed hard to bring it to the land; but they could not** <note>Jonah 1:13</note>. These are those who seek his merits to return him to this world, but they cannot. Why? *For the sea wrought, and was tempestuous against them.* The decree of judgment goes and storms with the person's sins and overpowers them. Then three appointed messengers descend upon him: one who writes all the merits and all the sins a person did in this world, one who makes an accounting of his days, and one who was with him while he was in his mother's womb. And it is seen and found that the decree of judgment will not turn back until the time of which it is written: **So they took up Jonah** <note>Jonah 1:15</note>. They "took him up" when his fathers <note>ancestors or burial society</note> lower him to the place of the graves; then they make a proclamation over him. If he is righteous, they proclaim over him and say: "Thus shall be done for the **likeness of the King**" <term>Dyokan de-Malka: the divine image in man</term>. **He shall enter into peace: they shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness** <note>Isaiah 57:2</note>. From where do we know this? As it is written: **And thy righteousness shall go before thee; the glory...** <note>Isaiah 58:8</note>

-> **The Glory** <-

<summary>This page presents a mystical allegory where the story of Jonah represents the soul's journey: the ship is the body, the storm is the divine decree of judgment, and the "shipmaster" is the good inclination urging the soul to repent before death.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Vayakhel, specifically focusing on the eschatological journey of the soul and the resurrection of the dead as mirrored in the Book of Jonah.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Vayakhel**<-
<note>Exodus 35:1–38:20</note>

The glory of the Lord shall cover you. And if they are not worthy, they proclaim about him and the masters of judgment say of such a person: "It would have been better for him had he not been created." Then what is written? *So they took up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea: and the sea ceased from its raging* <note>Jonah 1:15</note>. When they place him in the grave, which is after the judgment, then the decree of judgment that was stormy subsides from its rage. And the resting place for all of this is the grave. What is written? *And Jonah was in the belly of the fish* <note>Jonah 2:1</note>. The "belly of the fish" refers to the <term>smallness of the spleen</term> <note>A kabbalistic anatomical reference linking the spleen to melancholy and the gravity of the grave</note>. For it is written: "his storm is like the smallness of the spleen." And Job was in the belly of a similar thing, and they called it the smallness of the spleen... <unclear>illegible</unclear>. For three days a man is in the grave and his entrails burst. After three days, the filth of the stomach is cast upon his face and says: "Take what you gave me! For you ate and drank all your days and gave nothing to the poor; all your days were like feasts and delicacies, while the poor were hungry and did not eat of your meal. Take what you gave me!" This is what is written: *I will spread dung upon your faces* <note>Malachi 2:3</note>. And come and see, we have established this.

After these three days and onward, a person is judged for his eyes, his hands, and his feet, and we have established this continues until thirty days. All those thirty days, the soul and the body are judged together. Therefore, the soul remains below on the earth and does not ascend to its place, like a woman who sits outside during the days of her impurity. Afterward, the soul ascends and the body decays in the earth until the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, shall awaken to bring the dead back to life. And a voice will be destined to awaken those who dwell in the graves, saying: *Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead* <note>Isaiah 26:19</note>. And this time will be when the Angel of Death is removed from the world, as it is written: *He will swallow up death forever...* <note>Isaiah 25:8</note>. Once He swallows up death forever, *the Lord God will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of His people shall He take away from off all the earth.* Then it is written: *And the Lord spoke unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land* <note>Jonah 2:11</note>. Once that crystalline voice is awakened, then all the graves will vomit out the dead that are in them, and *the earth shall cast out the dead*. What is "cast out"? That it will eject them outside.

**The Rephaim** <note>original: רפאים - a biblical term for the departed or giants</note>
What are the *Rephaim*? Those who received loving-kindness <note>original: חסידות - chasidut</note> as in the beginning, and were healed <note>a wordplay on the root R-P-A, meaning to heal</note> by the light of life in their bones; these are called *Rephaim*. And if you say it is written of others, *The Rephaim shall not rise* <note>Isaiah 26:14</note>, surely the whole world will have their bones healed in the graves, but those who are worthy will rise, and those who are not will not rise; and regarding this it is written: *The Rephaim shall not rise*. Blessed is the portion of Israel, of whom it is written: *My dead body shall arise* <note>Isaiah 26:19</note>. And at that time, words of healing will be found for the whole world. Come and see: when the fish swallowed Jonah, he was considered as dead. And Jonah was in it for three days. Afterward, he was sustained as before and the fish vomited Jonah out. And we have established that it is written: *Then Jonah prayed unto the Lord his God out of the fish's belly* <note>Jonah 2:2</note>.

In this same manner, the Land of Israel is destined to be awakened first, and afterward *the earth shall cast out the dead*. And we have established that **seven judgments** pass over a person when he departs from this world:
1. The first is the **Supernal Judgment**, when the spirit departs from the body.
2. The second is when his deeds and his words appear before him and they proclaim about him.
3. The third is when he enters the grave.
4. The fourth is the **Judgment of the Grave** <note>original: Chibbut HaKever - the "beating" of the grave</note>.
5. The fifth is the **Judgment of the Worm**.
6. The sixth is the **Judgment of Gehenna** <note>Purgatory/Hell</note>.
7. The seventh is the judgment of the spirit that wanders and roams through the world and finds no resting place until its deeds are rectified.

Therefore, a person must always look into his deeds and return before his Master. And when King David looked upon these judgments, he remembered them and said: *Bless the Lord, O my soul* <note>Psalm 103:1</note>—before you depart from the world, while you are still with the body. *And all that is within me, bless His holy name*—these are the limbs of the body that are joined together with the spirit; strive that they be found with you to bless His holy name before the time arrives when you will not be able to bless or praise. As it is written, he said: *Bless the Lord, O my soul. Hallelujah.* Those beings came and lifted their heads...

<summary>This page uses the story of Jonah and the fish as an allegory for the soul's journey through death, the decomposition of the body, and the eventual resurrection. It details the seven stages of judgment a person undergoes after death and emphasizes the importance of repentance during one's lifetime.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of Parashat Vayakhel, focusing on the opening verse of the portion regarding the 'Terumah' (offering). It establishes the metaphysical link between the creation of the world and the study of Torah, specifically distinguishing between the Written and Oral Torah as manifestations of different spiritual realms.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

**Take** <note>original: "K'chu" - Exodus 35:5</note> the thought of an offering <note>original: "Terumah"</note> unto the Lord. Come and see: The Holy One, Blessed be He, when He created the world, did not create it except for the sake of Israel, so they would come and receive the Torah. The world was created through it, and upon the Torah it stands. This is as it is written:

> If My covenant be not **day and night, I have not set the statutes of heaven and earth.** 
<note>Reference to Jeremiah 33:25; the "covenant" is interpreted as the Torah.</note>

And the Torah is the path of life in this world and the path of life in the World to Come. Anyone who exerts themselves in the Torah is as if they exerted themselves in the Palace of the Holy One, Blessed be He, for the Supreme Palace of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is the Torah itself. Therefore, when a person occupies themselves with the Torah, the Holy One, Blessed be He, stands there and listens to their voice, as it is written:

> **And the Lord hearkened, and heard, etc.**
<note>Malachi 3:16</note>

And such a person is saved from all those who judge, the masters of this world, and from the judgment of the Angel of Death—who cannot gain dominion over them—and from the judgment of Gehenna <note>The place of spiritual purification/purgatory</note>. **A book of remembrance** <note>original: "Sefer Zikaron"</note> is written of them. There is a "Book" above and there is a "Book" below. "Remembrance" <note>original: "Zikaron"</note> is the place of the Holy Covenant, as it is written: "And a remembrance for your children all the days of their lives above." "Book of Remembrance" refers to two levels that are one, and the secret of this is that "Book" and "Remembrance" are one. And it is one secret. And the whole matter is one because there is a <term>Name</term> <note>A divine manifestation</note> and there is a <term>Name</term>. There is a Name above and there is a Name below (here a name is missing) from that which is not known and is not grasped by knowledge at all. And this is called the **Supreme Point** <note>original: "Nekudah Ila'ah"</note>. The Name below is called "the Name from the end of heaven unto the end of heaven," because the "end of heaven" is called "Remembrance." And she is a "Name," she is a "Point below," which is a "Name" from the conclusion of "Remembrance," which is the "end of heaven," as it is written: "all the days of life above," and this is the "end of heaven below." And its secret is the "Point below." This Point is the "Book" that stands in this manner, and sometimes it is called the "Book" we mentioned, and the secret is one; from it, in all directions, is this Point. Because it stands in warmth, it is supreme over all that is below. These are the six sides <note>The six directions/Sefirot of Zeir Anpin</note> below in the Supreme Book, and it is over them. The six sides below are in the Lower Book, and it is over them. The Supreme Book and the Lower Book are both called "Torah." What is the difference between this one and that one?

Rather, the Supreme Book is the **Written Torah** <note>original: "Torah she-bi-Khtav"</note> because it is hidden and does not stand except in "Writing," for there is the place that is revealed below. And what is it? The World to Come <note>Binah</note>. The Lower Book is the Torah called the **Oral Torah** <note>original: "Torah she-be-al Peh"</note>. And what is "Upon the Mouth" <note>Literal translation of "Oral"</note>? These are the Chariots <note>original: "Ratichin"</note> below, for life stands upon them. And because they are included in what is written above, they are called "Upon the Mouth," and this Torah stands "Upon the Mouth" because it is written: "And the spirit of life was in the wheels" and the Chariot. And the Supreme Torah, even though it stands above the "Writing," is only called "that which stands in Writing." And from that "Writing," a Palace was made for the Prophet, and she stands within that Palace and is not hidden there; therefore, it is called "Torah in Writing" and not "Upon Writing." But the Torah of below stands upon its Chariots and is called "Upon the Mouth" <note>Oral</note> because she stands upon them. And because she is not settled from within the inclusion of "Writing," they did not become a Palace like this Point, which is the Supreme Point. And because she stands upon them, she is called **Terumah** <note>Offering/Heave-offering</note>. Furthermore, I have heard from the power of all that is holy:

"Terumah"—what is "Terumah"? As we have established: "Two out of a hundred" <note>original: "Trei mi-Me'ah" - a wordplay on the word Terumah (Trei-Me'ah)</note>. Come and see: all those holy levels in the Spirit of Faith of the Holy One, Blessed be He, that are revealed from Him, are ten levels, and they are the Ten Utterances as we have established. And these ten rise to a hundred. And when we need this Lower Point to raise her up, we lack [the means] and need her study, only for her and for her sake, and not like the "two out of them" of the matter we spoke of, because it is not necessary to separate at all, but to unify her and raise her. And for this reason, she is called "Terumah" in a single manner. And come and see: every day in the spirit, all the inhabitants of the world call out in the line of the secret of this word.

<summary>This page explains that the Torah is the blueprint of creation and the ultimate protection for those who study it. It distinguishes between the Written Torah (associated with the hidden realm of Binah) and the Oral Torah (associated with Malchut and the Divine Chariots), interpreting the word 'Terumah' as a mystical unification of divine levels.</summary>
