## Main Text (Zohar)

The arrangement of the praise is for the splendor and life of the world. One might say this matter is upon you. All of this, the heart is able to contain; from here is our portion of the spirit for the exile of man <note>The "exile of man" refers to the soul's descent into the physical world or the state of spiritual distance</note>. A man who fears his Master and prepares the supernal arrangement as it was established of old in the mountains and the praises that the high angels say above. And in this order that you arrange, which is said below, she <note>The Shekhinah/Matronita</note> prepares her limbs and is adorned in her finery, just as the lower assembly is prepared for the upper. And according to the order of the exile, in that preparation of the exile, the Maiden <note>The Shekhinah</note> and all her attendants are adorned, and they are all bound together in order. After they are all prepared and arranged, when they reach "Life" <note>Likely referring to the blessing of "Grant Peace" or the conclusion of the Amidah</note>, then they are all prepared—the Life and the Maiden—until they reach the hidden and the secret. Then it is necessary for all of them to stand on their foundations. For when a man reaches the point of bowing and sitting, and all are prepared, the worlds are all seen as preparing themselves before the **Higher King** <note>original: *Malka Ila'ah* — the masculine aspect of the Divine, Tiferet</note>. When they reach the hidden and the secret, then the **Holy King** above takes His steps and bends to receive her, to be nourished before the Higher King, standing on His foundation in warmth and trembling. Then He extends His right hand to her, and afterwards His left, which He places under her head. Afterwards, both are prepared as one in longing. These are the first three <note>The first three blessings of the Amidah</note>, and a man must direct his heart and his will, and intend in all these preparations and arrangements of the exile, his mouth and his heart and his will as one. Now that the Higher King and the **Matron** <note>original: *Matronita* — the feminine aspect of the Divine, the Shekhinah</note> are as one in one dwelling, in those longings, it is necessary to pray and to wait. Then is the hour of Will <note>Ratzon</note>. When a man has finished and comes before the King and the Matron, then he should prepare himself in his will and heart for the other three <note>The final three blessings</note> to awaken the hidden joy. The three are blessed in a single attachment, and a man should prepare himself to depart from before them, and include them as a hidden treasure of three words, and make it his will that the lower ones shall be blessed from those blessings together in secret. And then it is necessary to fall upon his face and to surrender his soul at the hour of the "binding of the knot" <note>A mystical term for the union of Divine forces</note> of spirits and souls. Then is seen the hour when he unifies his soul in those wings of the "binding of the knot," for then the light of his strength is as it should be. This matter is hidden in the holy secrets and was not given permission to be revealed except to the high pious ones. And at that hour of the "binding of the knot" of spirits and souls, in the will of a single attachment, he is the life and splendor of his heart and will. And he gives his soul in attachment, just as his will is for everything to be in that attachment; it is accepted at that hour, in that will of those souls and spirits. And at times, in the "binding of the knot," a man is drawn into the fire of life in this world and in the world to come. Furthermore, he needs to be included from all sides—the King and the Matron, from above and from below—and to be crowned with her beauty on all sides; to be crowned with her beauty from above and to be crowned with her beauty from below. And a man should direct his heart and his will to all this, and hand over his soul from below in attachment and will as has been said. Then the **Holy One, Blessed Be He** <note>original: *Kadosh Barukh Hu*</note> rejoices in him and calls him "Peace" below, in the likeness of that Peace above. He blesses the Matron and includes her and crowns her on all sides. Just so, this man is called "Peace" below, then *“And he called him, ‘The Lord is Peace’”* <note>Judges 6:24</note>. And they see that thus they call him above, "Peace," because he included and crowned the Matron below in the likeness of that Peace above. And when that man departs from this world, his soul ascends and breaks through all those firmaments, and there is no one to protest against him. And the Holy One, Blessed Be He, calls to her and says: *“He shall enter into peace; they shall rest in their beds...”* <note>Isaiah 57:2</note> and they shall open for her the

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the Tabernacle's construction from Parashat Vayakhel. It transitions from the physical materials of the sanctuary to the spiritual qualities of the builders and the internal nature of divine service.</meta>

# Vayakhel

The mountains of pure balsam <note>original: *Afarsemona*; a metaphor for the highest spiritual emanations</note> are always fragrant, and these scents of day and night rest and rejoice. Therefore, blessed are those who set their prophecy and their will toward Him. Regarding this, it is written:
> *Whoever is of a willing heart, let him bring it as an offering to the Lord* <note>Exodus 35:5</note>
This refers to the Supernal King, as has been explained. Rabbi Abba raised his voice and said: "Woe, Rabbi Shimeon! You are among the living, yet I weep for you. I do not weep for you, but I weep for the companions and I weep for the world. Rabbi Shimeon is like a star of light that kindles above and kindles below. Like the moon that shines below, all the inhabitants of the world are illuminated. Woe to the world when the light below is removed like the moon above. Who then will illuminate the light of the Torah for the world?" Rabbi Abba stood and kissed his arms and smiled. He said to him: "These matters were within your power, and for this reason I have stood by you until now, for these things were spoken with you. Blessed is my portion!" Rabbi Yose opened the scripture and said:

**"And** *every wise-hearted person among you shall come and make..."* <note>Exodus 35:10</note>. This verse has been established. But come and see: at the time when the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses, *"Get you wise men, and understanding <note>Hebrew: 'Navon'</note>, and known to your tribes,"* <note>Deuteronomy 1:13</note> wise men were found among all Israel, but "understanding" ones were not found. This is as it is written: *“So I took the heads of your tribes, wise men and known...”* <note>Deuteronomy 1:15</note> but "understanding" <note>Navon</note> is not written. And if you say that they are of a higher degree than all, they are certainly hidden. What is the difference between this one and that one? A "Wise Man" <note>Chakham</note> is one of Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>; even a student who makes his teacher wise is called "wise." A wise man is one who knows for himself all that is necessary. An "Understanding Man" <note>Navon</note> has many levels within him, for he gazes at everything and knows through his speech and his ways. Your sign for this is:
> *A righteous man knows the soul of his beast* <note>Proverbs 12:10</note>.
"Righteous" is the Foundation of the World <note>The Sefirah of Yesod</note>. And here, "wise-hearted" is precisely stated. It is all Wisdom, and not another assembly, because everything stands upon it. And they, above and below, gaze at his speech and his ways. He opened and said:
> *“And He said to me, ‘You are My servant...’”* <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>
Here in exile, every person needs to reveal before the Holy One, blessed be He, that his service <note>Pulchana</note> is one great and precious service among those other services. There is a service of the Holy One, blessed be He, that stands in the body through the action of the body, and that is service. And there is a service of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is a more internal service, which is the essence of all that exists—that internal service which is the essence of everything. In the body, there are twelve limbs <note>Shayfin</note> that stand in the action of the body, as we have established. And these are the limbs of the body, and the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, through action stands within them. For the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, is on two sides: in the external limbs of the body, and there are twelve other internal limbs within the body, and they are supernal and internal and are not known; he proclaims, "Blessed is their portion!" These are the internal arrangements within the body, and within them is found the arrangement of the Spirit <note>Ruach</note>, which is the precious, internal service of the Holy One, blessed be He, as we have established within the internal mysteries that Rabbi Shimeon spoke. The exile of a person is the service of the Spirit, which stands in supernal mysteries. Because of this, whoever exerts himself with his spirit pierces seventy firmaments, opens gates, and ascends on high. At the time when the light shines and the light is separated from the darkness, then a herald goes out through all the firmaments: "Prepare, masters of the gates of the palaces!" Each one to his watch, because those whose governance is by day are not those whose governance is by night. And when night enters, the governors of the day pass away, and the governors who rule at night are found, and these are exchanged for those. This is as it is written:
> *“The greater light to rule the day...”* <note>Genesis 1:16</note>.
And the governance of the day and the governance of the night are governors who are appointed, and there are governors who are appointed at night. And these are called "Governance of the Day," and these are called "Governance of the Night." When night enters, a herald goes out: "Prepare, governors of the night, every..."

## Vayakhel

->**And He Assembled**<-

When the day shines and the light of day breaks, a herald goes forth and the governors of the day are established, each one in his place. Then the governors of the night pass away and the governors of the day are appointed. When the herald makes the proclamation, then each and every one is appointed over that place which is fitting for him. Then the *Shekhinah* <note>The Divine Presence, often personified as the feminine aspect of God</note> arrives early, and many types of "eyes" <note>Angelic watchers or observers</note> look toward the synagogue to find their Master. Openings, songs, and praises are required of a person once he has prepared himself with the requirements of the commandment and holiness, to unify his heart in the proper arrangement of the service of his Master. He must extend his heart and his will in that service with words of truth. For behold, the word ascends, and there are appointees <term>Mammanin: angelic officials or overseers</term> who stand on the side of the perfect ones.

On the **Eastern side** of the worlds, one appointee is designated with many other appointees and officers <term>Sarchin: high-ranking angelic princes</term> with him. They stand in a vision of colors, red and black. These officers and appointees are the "long ones" who wait for that word of prayer. When it ascends in their vision, this appointee takes it. If it is a word spoken as is fitting and proper, all those officers open a path for that word and ascend with it until that white firmament above. There, other appointees and officers dwell. When the word is proper, they open and surround it, and all of them descend with their will to crown their Master with holy crowns. Blessed is the portion of the mouth that crowns Him! Then, from his mouth go forth divisions and repetitions <note>or "second-rank angels"</note> who stand in the holy silver-white light.

On the **South side**, there is another appointee who rules over the white light of the radiance. Many other appointees and officers are with him—afflicted ones, red and scarred—who hold the keys that surround that side. All those officers who are distressed by the prayers of their hearts to their Master, who have known distress and recognized the Living One—that word, when it is proper, ascends to the white light. This appointee takes it and covers it <note>or "longs for it"</note> as it ascends on that side. As it is written of him, he opens, and his slight heat <note>or "wrath"</note> shows pity to receive it. Concerning this, it is said that mercies ascend with it, along with all those holy appointees and all those officers of that side. The divisions and repetitions of the holy name, who are the thirty grooms, are crowned and planted on that side in the white light, and they ascend on that side of the white light until the firmament.

On the **North side**, there is another appointee who supports many officers and appointees who rule in the white light. The name of that appointee is *Patika*. He is appointed over the white light of that side and all those who season <note>or "salt"</note> their prayers concerning their enemies who distress them. When the word of that prayer ascends into the white light of that side, the Living One—blessed is the mouth—this appointee takes it and longs for it. Then a certain spirit is awakened that goes out from the depths on the North side. That spirit is as swift as all those "swine" <note>likely a reference to destructive forces or specific angelic types</note> and it takes all those words and raises them to the firmament. Angels gather to meet them, and they break through the firmaments until they ascend with it.

To the **First Firmament**, the prayer ascends from below toward a single appointee who is designated for the **Western side**. There, nine gates stand, and in them stand many officers and many appointees. Over them is one appointee who hides the dwelling <note>Zevul</note> and does not spare those who wish to see in this firmament by day. Permission is not given to him until the light of the moon ascends. Then all those hosts and all those appointees go forth. When the day shines, they all enter one of the keys of those nine gates, and he sees a gate above all of them when the prayer ascends with him.

## Main Text (Zohar)

Now at that portal, all the chariots and all the appointed overseers emerge from that gate. Over all of them is one great overseer; they all go forth, longing for the <term>Prayer (Tzaluta)</term> <note>The Zohar personifies prayer as a feminine entity ascending to her Groom, the Holy One</note> and traveling with her until the second firmament. When the prayer ascends to that second firmament, twelve gates are opened in that firmament. At each of these twelve gates stands an overseer through whom the prayer enters. One overseer bathes over many hosts and many <term>guardians (metronin)</term>. When the prayer ascends, this overseer stands and proclaims at all those portals—and which portals are they? The gates of the Garden of Eden. All the gates are opened, and she passes through all those portals. Then, a certain overseer who stands on the South side is awakened; his name is <term>Azriel</term> <note>Azriel is often associated with the South, the side of Mercy (Chesed)</note>. He opens the gates, and sometimes he is called "the Camps" because he oversees sixty myriads of guardians. All of them are masters of wings, masters of guardians, and masters of eyes. Before them stand those watchers, the masters of rejoicings, and they are called "rejoicers" because they are the joy of all those who are included in the prayer alone, by the permission of the Master, so that the prayer is not used for another <note>Meaning the prayer is directed purely to God without ulterior motives or "foreign" thoughts</note>. This prayer ascends, and all those called the masters of rejoicings have joy in her. But if that prayer is used for mundane things by a <term>human being (bar nash)</term>, there is no one who rejoices in her above, nor do her companions have joy in her, except for the one who first heard it. A <term>human being</term> must be careful that they do not let that prayer be swallowed up in a "house of the chair" <note>original: "bi kisse" - a euphemism for a latrine or bathroom</note>. Furthermore, the word of prayer is joined in the world upon the redness of the upper world; it must not be defiled. This is like those who read from the Scroll of the Torah: one reads and one is silent. If two read from the Torah together, they diminish the faith above, because one voice and one speech are all one. Therefore, two voices and two speeches cause a deficiency in faith—rather, specifically one voice and one speech, as is necessary, for that voice and that speech are one. It is the five <note>referring to the five phonetic points of articulation</note> that speak, surrounded by red and white. When that prayer ascends alone, all those sixty myriads of guardians and all those masters of smiles and all those of joy, the masters of rejoicings, all go out and long for that word of prayer that ascends. They stand smiling, and seven times seventy righteous and meritorious ones in prayer smile... for there are masters of smiles above, and they are the prayer of those who are masters of rejoicings.

In the third firmament, that prayer ascends and reaches that firmament. There is an overseer there called Gadriya, and with him are many chariots and many overseers. They offer praise three times a day toward a single <term>Scepter of Radiance</term> that emerges and is hidden, which examines and descends and does not remain after one. This one beholds the <term>Scepter of Dew</term>. When the prayer ascends, it strikes that scepter and flows before that prayer. This sweetens firmament to firmament by the scepter. And as it ascends now, the overseer is hidden in the name of that scepter, after it flows in a powerful measure of radiance... all the camps of that firmament emerge from that reward, three hundred and seventy-five hosts... they emerge there from the day the Torah descended to earth, because they were reflected to be created entirely beneath the earth... except for that time when the prayer ascends. They open and desire... what is seen is supported in all worlds... the prayer that ascends over all these firmaments. Then they prostrate before her, and the prayer is crowned with supernal crowns and ascends into the fourth firmament. Then the <term>Sun (Shimsha)</term> goes out in its degrees, and a great overseer is placed in charge. Three hundred and sixty-five guardians <note>Corresponding to the solar year</note> ascend with him into that firmament, and they are called the "Days of the Sun." All of them crown that prayer with crowns of the silver of Eden. There the prayer is delayed until all the guardians ascend with her into the fifth firmament. There, the overseer is named <term>Gadriel</term>, and he is the master of wars who surrounds the nations. When the prayer ascends, then he and all his guardians are shaken, and

are broken.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the mystical ascent of prayer from the previous section of Parashat Vayakhel. It focuses on the transition of the prayer from the lower firmaments into the Seven Heavenly Palaces (Heikhalot) and the specific devotional requirements (commandments) of the prayer service.</meta>

# Vayakhel

## Main Text (Zohar)

The angels of the lower realms bow and submit themselves, crowning that prayer and ascending with it until they reach the lowest firmament. Then, many hosts and many camps go forth and receive that prayer, ascending with it until they reach the seventy gates. Standing there is a chief appointee whose name is **Tzagfiel** <note>original: "צגפיאל"; a high-ranking angel in Zoharic lore responsible for guarding the gates of the firmament</note>, a great prince. He and his living beings crown that prayer with seventy crowns. Once the prayer is adorned with all these crowns, all the hosts of all the firmaments join together and raise that prayer—now adorned on all sides—to the seventh firmament. Then the prayer enters, and **Sandalfon** <note>original: "סנדלפון"; a primary archangel in Jewish mysticism, often described as weaving the prayers of Israel into crowns for the Creator</note>, the great, honored, and supreme prince who holds all the keys of his Master in his hand, brings that prayer into the seven palaces.

**Come and see:** These seven palaces are the mysteries of the Kingdom <note>term: "Malchut" (Kingdom) - the final of the ten Sefirot or Divine emanations, associated with the communal soul of Israel and the destination of prayer</note> when the prayer is adorned with all these crowns.

When the prayer comes from below, it is fitting for it to be adorned above, to hand over everything as one in the proper manner. Thus, the Holy Side is adorned on all sides, above and below, to become one. Then it is written: *Blessings are upon the head of the righteous* <note>Proverbs 10:6</note>. Fortunate is the portion of the person who knows how to arrange their prayer properly, for it is a prayer in which the Holy One, blessed be He, takes pride. He waits until all the prayers of Israel are finished, and then they are all included together as is fitting, above and below. From this point forward, there are commandments of the Torah that stand through speech just as they stand through action; these are the six commandments that exist within the prayer service:

1.  **First:** To fear the glorious and awesome Name <note>original: "יראה"; the awe/fear of God</note>, a sense of shame and humility before Him.
2.  **Second:** To bless Him <note>referring to the "Barchu" call to prayer</note>.
3.  **Third:** To have the Priest bless the people.
4.  **Fourth:** To surrender one's soul to Him.

And these six commandments exist in the "exile of speech" <note>note: This refers to the performance of commandments through liturgy when physical Temple service is absent</note>, just as there are commandments that exist in physical action, such as the Fringes (Tzitzit) and Phylacteries (Tefillin). Regarding the fear of the Name: this commandment stands during the songs of praise uttered by King David <note>term: "Pesukei D'Zimrah" - the Verses of Praise in the morning service</note> and like the offerings of the Torah. There, a person must feel awe before his Master, for there are "sentinel birds" standing in that place to honor the fear of the Name; they are the mystery of the fear of the Holy One, blessed be He. A person must direct his will toward these "birds" in fear, to strengthen his connection. After all those songs and praises and mysteries of the "windows," when a person reaches the blessings, he should set his will to bless the Holy One, blessed be He, such as in the blessings: *Who forms light and creates darkness* <note>Isaiah 45:7</note>.

To love Him: this occurs when one reaches the blessing *Eternal Love* and the verse *And you shall love the Lord your God* <note>Deuteronomy 6:5</note>, for this is the spirit of love for the Holy One, blessed be He. And they have established the requirement to unify Him:

> Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is One. <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note>

For here stands the spirit of unification for the Holy One, blessed be He, to unify His Name with the heart's desire as is proper. From there, one proceeds to the redemption and the remembrance of the Exodus, as it is written:

> And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt. <note>Deuteronomy 5:15</note>

Then, the Priest blesses the people in order to include all of Israel as one. At that moment, when the blessings are awakened above, the Congregation of Israel is blessed like dew. The essence of this will is for a person to surrender his life to Him and give Him his soul with the heart's desire, as when we fall upon our faces <note>term: "Tachanun" - the prayer of supplication where one leans on their arm</note> and say:

> To You, O Lord, I lift up my soul. <note>Psalms 25:1</note>

One should direct his heart and will toward Him, to hand over his soul with the heart's desire. These are the six commandments that stand within the prayer, which correspond to the six thousand commandments of the Torah. And if you say there are thirteen gates more, these stand to extend the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy, all of which are included in these six commandments of prayer. Fortunate is the portion of one who knows how to direct his heart and will in awe and love for Him.

Afterward, a second color, white, is poured into its place, and that white is on top. Once this color stands firm, that lower dwelling-place rises in the path and pushes that white color to the outside and brings those others inside. <meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Torah portion Vayakhel. It focuses on the transition between the sacred time of the Sabbath and the mundane week, specifically addressing the spiritual mechanics of the "Clouds of Glory" and the "Chashmal" from Ezekiel’s vision.</meta>

## Vayakhel
-> **And He Assembled** <-

As it is written <note>Exodus 40:38</note> **"For the cloud of the Lord was upon them by day,"** and <note>Numbers 14:14</note> **"and Your cloud stands over them."** These living beings <note>The *Hayyot*, the high-ranking angels of Ezekiel's chariot</note> are a cloud to this light, and all lights are arranged to be guided by this cloud. For every such cloud, there is a dark cloud that does not shine at all, at all times; all lights are unable to be seen before it. It is like a sheath <note>original: *nadna*</note> for the bread of the offering, and the living being does not stir. Rather, the living being, once it rules, does not stir that great Altar, since it covers all lights so they are not seen before it, yet its kindness is great over all the works of the world. And kindness is gathered, for the kindness of small judgment is never removed from it. And regarding the phrase "surrounding it," even though all this stands in the hand of the assembly "surrounding it," from here comes the exchange; for even though there is no other side <note>the side of evil/impurity</note> to His kingdom, it "surrounds it" and they do not guard it outside, except to cleanse it on the outside. This is because it "surrounds it." The guard of holiness and of faith belongs to it, and they do not guard it to treat it with disgrace; therefore, one must give it a portion from the side of holiness and faith.

The Elder, Rav Hamnuna, said this: Does it "surround it" and yet one must testify to its disgrace? It is a gathering for us, a living being; it does not stand outside. And because it stands, that gathering is within the chambers, and it is sweet <term>like the appearance of Chashmal</term> <note>Ezekiel 1:4</note> **"from the midst of the fire."** From its midst, as they saw from the midst of that gathering. Like the appearance of the *Chashmal* <note>A mystical substance or angelic energy seen by the prophet Ezekiel; the word is often split by the Zohar into *Chash* (silence) and *Mal* (speech)</note> they saw, mouth to mouth, the vision of the speaking kindness to every holy dwelling that mixes the spirit of secrets within me. When the "foreskin" <term>Orlah</term> <note>The spiritual shell or *kelipah* that conceals holiness</note> rests upon the holy covenant to wait for the Sanctuary, then the impurity of the Sanctuary is delayed from circulating the spirit that does not stand within the **foreskin**. And when this gathering is over my garden, and it carves between the foreskin and the Sanctuary, then they investigate the <term>Chashmal</term>: **Chash** (Silence) and for the revelation, **Mal** (Speech). What is *Mal*? It is like "circumcision" <note>original: *mal*</note> and truth; a spirit that does not stand, which is not delayed from being revealed from within the foreskin. And another spirit lives, for its light is seen and yet not seen, and when the *Chashmal* is revealed, its light is darkened. But the first spirit is the spirit of the calling, as is proper, and everything is beautiful and living. And cheapness was seen in this gathering, enticing below to cancel the light. And about this it is written <note>Proverbs 5:3</note> **"and her speech is smoother than oil,"** scattering the secret in the book of cutting <note>a bill of divorce</note>. And because of this, it entices it and cancels the light. And it is not living, the opening that entices below, as it is written: "the lips of a strange woman drip honey," etc.

Come and see: on the sixth day, when the time of the "Watcher" arrives, that dwelling-place leaps down and rises up to enter into the colors. Then Israel prepares below and arranges the meals, and they prepare the lamps, each one on his table. Then a flame goes out and flows like that dwelling-place; once it flows, that divinity and that dwelling-place roll and enter into the "female" of the Great Abyss and are hidden there. And that flame is from the Left Side <note>the side of Judgment/Gevurah</note>, and because it goes from the Left Side, it is made for that dwelling-place, and it enters into the female of the Great Abyss and sits there until the Sabbath departs. Once the Sabbath departs, it is necessary for the people to guard and to bless over the fire, and that flame goes out through the blessing below and rules over that dwelling-place all that night, and that dwelling-place is subdued.

Come and see: once the Sabbath enters and is crowned, that dwelling-place and all the forces of small judgment are hidden and subdued, and they cover the fire of Gehenna <note>the purgatorial underworld</note>, and the guilty in Gehenna have rest. And everyone, below and above, has rest. When the Sabbath departs and Israel blesses over the fire, then all those who were hidden go out, each one to his place. And so as not to arouse the "other" below, it is written <note>Exodus 35:3</note> **"You shall kindle no fire throughout your settlements on the Sabbath day,"** as they have established it. The fire of the Altar is what is seen, but when the Sabbath enters with a cold spirit, all the firmaments are prepared, the chariots are prepared, and the Ruler <note>Metatron</note> is in the lands of His kingdom. Then a single spirit goes out from the South side, and that spirit spreads over all...

Over all those colors and they are handed over to the "Left Side" <note>The realm of judgment or the "Other Side"</note> and are found within it. And all those six days of the week, that Point is hidden from them. Once the Sabbath enters, then that Point ascends and is crowned and united above, and all things are hidden within it.

**Sabbath** [שבת]: The letters *Shin* [ש], *Bet* [ב], *Tav* [ת]. The *Shin* is the seal, the mystery of the **Three Patriarchs** <note>Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, representing the three primary emanations</note> who are united as one, unique, and the joy is crowned in them, and they are in the **World to Come**. And all is one joy, and this joy is *Shin-Bat* <note>The letter Shin joined with the word Bat (Daughter)</note> so that all becomes one. And if you say the Sabbath is great and its joy is above, yet its joy is small? The spirit that goes everywhere is like a "Point" whose joy is the root of all goodness, and it is called **Daughter** <note>original: *Bat*</note>. Everything that is seen like the vision of the "apple of the eye" <note>original: *bat ayin*</note> is because its joy is like a Point, the root of all goodness, called "Daughter." The World to Come is the joy that is a sign for that supernal Point. And when its joy stands like dew on the wing of the palate to be crowned above, the whole is called Sabbath. And when the Fifty are crowned above like the supernal Point, it is called Sabbath. Like the lower Point, when it is crowned in the Fifty, it is called Sabbath. That lower Point ascends and is seen and sanctified; then every dwelling is found above and below, and all worlds are in joy.

And all through the night, that Point spreads out like a **Tabernacle** <note>original: *Sukkah*</note> and spreads its wings over the world, and all other "rulers" <note>external spiritual forces</note> pass away, and protection is found over the world. And then an **Additional Soul** <note>original: *ruach nishmata*</note> is added to Israel, to each and every one. And at the hour that the "Extra" descends, all labors and anxieties are covered and pushed away, and nothing is found but joy above and below. That spirit which is added in several worlds, when it descends, it is perfumed with the spices of the **River of Eden**, and it descends and rests upon the holy people. As that spirit descends, there descend with it from the Garden of Eden chariots crowned on six sides. And when it reaches the Garden of Eden, then all those spirits and souls that are in the Garden of Eden are all awakened by that spirit. They open and say: "Fortunate are you, Israel, the holy people, for the will of your Master is to awaken toward you."

Regarding them, there is a spirit of secrets for those who know wisdom; they are meritorious when this spirit is below. This spirit is the spreading forth of that point <note>The "point" often refers to the Sephirah of Yesod or the initial point of creation/wisdom</note>. To establish this—it is written "Shabbat," but it says **"You shall keep My Sabbaths"** <note>plural</note>. This spirit is guided like this one and rests from the side of the palaces, delighting them and giving them pleasure through food and drink three times, corresponding to the three meals which are the three levels of faith <term>levels of faith: the three meals represent the three Patriarchs or three specific Sephirot (divine emanations)</term>, as we have established. And this spirit wanders and delights in those meals of Israel. All of them are sustained by what is prepared for it, and one delights it on this day. It stands with him as male and female, etc. One must guard this spirit, which is the spreading of that point. And this spreading—when holiness and blessings are added from above upon that point—everything is illuminated and becomes a spirit of light on all sides. It divides above and shines; it divides below and shines. And this is what is written:
> **"Between Me and the children of Israel, it is a sign forever"** <note>Exodus 31:17</note>
We do not have them as one. The upper portion is crowned on this day with supernal holy delight and is guided by the supernal vision. The lower portion is crowned on this day with delight below and is guided by these meals. Therefore, one must delight it with food, drink, and the joy of a bride with honorable garments. When this lower portion is crowned and adorned as is necessary, it ascends above and joins with that other portion. And this point receives everything from above and below and is included from all sides. Because it is crowned on Shabbat from above and below, all the other days give strength and life to it, and it has dominion above and below. Because the name of the King is found there, it is established as a holy merit for all who see the portion of Israel. It is written:
> **"And He rested and was refreshed"** <note>Exodus 31:17; the Hebrew "Vayinafash" is interpreted here as "Woe, the soul!"</note>
They explained: "Woe, the soul <note>original: "Vai Nefesh"</note> that is lost!" and the living sapphire. But "living" also means "breathed into," and it must be said that it is lost as the verse says. But the spirit is like a person who lives, as the verse says:
> **"And sweetness to the soul..."** <note>Proverbs 16:24</note>
To this spirit from the eve of Shabbat. And that spirit seizes the hidden treasure of that verse and dwells in it all the day of Shabbat. And they complete that extra soul <term>extra soul: Neshama Yeteira, the additional spiritual dimension granted to Jews on Shabbat</term> with blessings and benefit more than what was before. Therefore, all the Assembly of Israel <note>Knesset Yisrael, often identifying with the Sephirah of Malkhut</note> are crowned on the day of Shabbat, and their crown hovers with this spirit in their beauty. Once Shabbat departs, "Woe, the soul that is lost"—what is lost? That crown and that holy strength that was within it is lost, and that is the departure of Shabbat. Once this Shabbat ascends above to the Crown <note>Keter</note>, "Woe, the soul that is lost." It is good for the wise who know the supernal secrets of the fullness of Shabbat until the night of Shabbat, and they established it. Everything comes from her; she ascends to the holy assembly, for the life of this Crown of Praise takes what it takes during the day, and when it is included, it gives to all from its portion as we have established. As it is written:
> **"She rises while it is yet night, and gives food to her household and a portion to her maidens"** <note>Proverbs 31:15</note>
Like a harvest in the day that is given at night. And another opening of the moon is found in this night, and what is of the moon is found in this night. And why? Because this night searches like treasures for all the life of the wise.

Since they know that He invites, arranges, and prepares for it, it is found that on another day <note>a weekday</note> there is a total mixture of confusion. However, because the souls of the wise are divided among the wise, like the righteous among the pious as is fitting, furthermore, in every single night it is found that there is fear and the "division of the night" <note>midnight</note>, and we have established this. But in all aspects, the wise who know the mysteries seek to arrange the service for this [Divine Presence] on this night. What is the reason? Because every day, there is a space found for the master of sin over the world, but on this night, there is a space found for the High Holy Master below toward the holy ones. And regarding this spirit, it is written of the Holy Ancient One <note>original: *Atika Kadisha*, the highest level of Divinity</note> of all ancient ones, that it descends into the Lower Point <note>original: *Nekuda Tata’ah*, referring to the Shekhinah or the realm of Malkhut</note> to give assistance to all. It is not divided to all sides above and below; as we have said, there is nothing between Him and the Children of Israel. 

And when those wise ones dwell in that holy spirit, the supernal spirit, they desire to taste the bed of this hidden spirit, as it is written below: all those holy souls inherit the holy supernal ones in this spirit—holy supernal souls as is fitting. Since this spirit rests upon the world, all evil spirits and all accusers all depart from the world, and they do not need to keep watch <note>in the mundane sense</note> because Israel is protected by that spirit, and the **Sukkah of Peace** is spread over them, and they are protected from everything. 

And if you say: "Behold, we have learned that a person should not go out alone, neither on the fourth night of the week nor on the night of the Sabbath, and a person needs to guard himself," yet we have said that on the night of the Sabbath, people are protected from all the accusers of the world and do not need to keep watch? Come and see: it is certainly so. On the fourth night of the week, we need to be guarded from them, from L. <note>original: *Tet*, an abbreviation for Lilith</note>, because it is written: "Let there be lights" <note>Genesis 1:14</note>—written deficiently <note>original: *me'orot* is written without the letter 'vav', which can be read as *me'erat*, meaning 'curse'</note>. And we have established that because it is deficient, many types of "shining ones" <note>original: *tehirin*, a class of demons</note> are included in this curse, and they are the will of the moon, and they all rule on this night. 

But on the night of the Sabbath, since they are all hidden above in the "hole of the dust" <note>a spiritual abyss</note> where they cannot rule, should a person still guard himself when alone? Furthermore, even though they cannot rule, they appear at times, and a person alone needs to guard himself from this matter. Thus we have learned: and so it is in the desire of protection. But on the Sabbath, protection is found for the holy people, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, when the Sabbath enters, crowns every single one of Israel, and they need to guard that holy crown with which they are crowned. And even though they are not found in inhabited areas at times, they appear to a person alone to teach or to warn him that a person needs to be crowned with the holy crown and to guard it. Ultimately, protection is found on that night for the holy people, and the **Sukkah of Peace** is spread over the people. For we have learned: in every place where the Sukkah of Peace is found, the "Other Side" <note>original: *Sitra Achra*, the forces of evil</note> is not found there. 

And regarding the protection of the day of the Sabbath, it is found precisely so, and everything is found above and below. And the Lower Point shines to receive from above in the beauty of the crowns, seventy portions more, and it circles all sides below. Then, when the light rises, the holy people go early to the synagogue; as it were, they are crowned with the holy crown above through prayer. The precious ones, the protected ones, and the praises in that spirit that stands below, they raise praises above. Those above and those below are all as one, and they are all crowned as one. The supernal ones open and say: "Happy are the holy people on earth, for their Master is crowned over them, and all the holy hosts are crowned because of them." The day rejoices—the day of souls—and the day of the body lives, because it rises to the light of the souls, and they stand upon it, and those below are all in one likeness.

There is no space between one word and the next for any "other" <note>external/evil force</note>, but rather each word leads to its specific level. And in the supernal world, the vitality of the spirit and the holy sides are between one and the other.

This addition is seen upon the souls that descend upon them on the seventh day; it stands praising and saying to the Supernal King an extra blessing. All of this addition ascends on high, and we have learned that the Chariots are prepared for them, and all of them attend to this addition from the holy time, and they raise it up to be crowned with it. ## Main Text (Zohar)

Within the holy Throne <note>original: *korsaya*</note> and those images <note>original: *dyoknin*</note> of the mission that is written in the Torah, which He bent and through them acted below, to be made from the Male principle. They surrounded and gazed upon the world of holiness as is fitting. Because of this, when one is found within the synagogue—for behold, the Throne is found and adorned there from the spirit of the Torah that was written—and there above are all those images, and the vision is sanctified by it, everyone must be sanctified to be as is proper. Then all are sanctified with a supernal holiness as is fitting for them, and so it is every day.

On this day <note>the Sabbath</note>, one must bring up seven men for the mystery of the Torah, corresponding to the seven voices <note>referring to the seven times "The voice of the Lord" appears in Psalm 29</note>. Similarly, for the appointed times and festivals, five men are called, corresponding to the mystery of the letter *He* <note>the numerical value of the Hebrew letter ה is 5</note>. On the Day of Atonement, six are called, within the supernal mystery of the letter *He*. All of them follow the mystery of five and five, which are the five levels below the level of the "primordial air" <note>a high kabbalistic realm</note> below, and they are the spirit of the Torah. Six corresponds to the six sides <note>the six directions of the physical world</note>, and all are one spirit within those five.

Seven corresponds to the seven voices, and all are one spirit and not divided parts, except that one is added to the three <note>referring to the structure of the sefirot</note> because the Male supports the Moon <note>the *Shekhinah* or Divine Presence</note> at that time, to add light upon the Moon. And those who are the "additional" spirit <note>the *Musaf* service</note>, like the Torah scroll itself, must be heard as one voice. The Male speaks to arrange the holy people on this day.

And in the elevation of the days of the Torah scroll, one must arrange and prepare the setting like a single Throne of established order. That Throne should have six steps to ascend upon and no more, as it is written:
> And there were six steps to the throne.
<note>1 Kings 10:19</note>
And there is one level above to raise the Torah scroll upon and to let it rest for all to see. When the Torah scroll ascends there, then all the people must arrange themselves accordingly, with awe, with trembling, with fear, and with shaking—everyone below—and direct their hearts as if they were standing at Mount Sinai to receive the Torah. They should listen and incline their ears, and no person has permission to open their mouth regarding the Torah, and certainly not for any other matter, but all should be in silence like one who has no mouth. For they have established this, as it is written:
> And when he opened it, all the people stood up.
<note>Nehemiah 8:5</note>
And behold, all the people looked toward the Torah scroll.

Rabbi Shimon said: Whenever the scroll is opened in the congregation to read from it, the gates of heaven's mercy are opened and they awaken the Love above. It is worthy for a person to say the following:

**Blessed be the Name** <note>original: *Brich Shmeh*</note> of the Master of the universe! Blessed be Your crown and Your place. May Your favor be with Your people Israel forever. Show Your people the redemption of Your right hand in Your Holy Temple. Extend to us the bounty of Your light, and accept our prayer with mercy. May it be Your will to prolong our lives in goodness. May I be counted among the righteous, so that You may have compassion on me and protect me and all that belongs to me and to Your people Israel. You are He who feeds and sustains all. You are He who rules over all. You are He who rules over kings, for the kingdom is Yours. I am the servant of the Holy One, blessed be He, whom I prostrate myself before, and before the glory of His Torah at all times. Not in man do I put my trust, nor upon any angel <note>literally "son of gods"</note> do I rely, but only on the God of heaven, who is the God of truth, whose Torah is truth, whose prophets are truth, and who abounds in performing goodness and truth. In Him do I trust, and unto His holy and glorious Name do I utter praises. May it be Your will to open my heart to the Torah, and to fulfill the desires of my heart and the hearts of all Your people Israel for good, for life, and for peace.

And it is proper that only one person reads from the Torah scroll, and all others listen and prepare themselves so that they hear the words from his mouth as if they were receiving them at that moment from Mount Sinai. And we have learned that for those who study the Torah, one should stand over it; and it is answered that there should be only one male found there, not two males. The Holy Tongue <note>Hebrew</note> is one and one, not two. If two are found reading the Torah scroll, it is a diminishment of the spirit of faith and a diminishment of the honor of the Torah. The one who translates <note>the *Targum*</note> is the mystery of the shell <note>original: *klipa*</note> and the brain <note>the kernel</note>. The spirit of this world and the spirit of the World to Come are all prepared, and one reads, as it is written:
> And God spoke all these words, saying...
<note>Exodus 20:1</note>
They shall be above, and all the people below, as it is written: "And they stood at the foot of the mountain."

They assemble in the perfection of the Book. And it is written: *And Moses went up to God* <note>Exodus 19:3</note>. And he who reads from the Torah <term>Orayta; the Law</term> must direct his heart and his will to those words. For just as the living beings below <note>The angelic Chariot creatures</note> stand ready as a dwelling place, so too these words must be heard by all the people, for the holy living being is modeled after the supernal form. Therefore, one who goes up to read from the Torah should first arrange those words in his house <note>Practice the reading privately</note>, and if not, he should not read from the Torah. From here onward, let a person remember that he should not let the holy people hear the Torah until—what is written? <margin>(Job 28)</margin> *Then He saw it and declared it; He prepared it and also searched it out.* And afterward: *And He said to man, "Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom"* etc. <margin>(ibid.)</margin>. It is a deficiency for one who reads the Torah to stop a portion <term>Parashata</term> or to skip a word from the speech; rather, just as Moses divided the portions for the holy people for all eternity, so should he divide them. He must not stop the words of the portion that is worthy to be seen in this Sabbath. This spirit, at the hour when they divide the portions before the Holy One, Blessed Be He, each and every one is crowned and stands before Him.

For the movements of the one who divides the portions for the entire Torah are crowned before the Holy One, Blessed Be He, and He says: "Fortunate is the faithfulness of so-and-so, and fortunate is the faithfulness of such-a-one." Just as the verse bears witness to heal a great sickness and to be seen, so there are three holy chariots <term>Retikin</term> established by His hands. And they were appointed for us in the hidden depths of the Torah. Each and every chariot is appointed over the portion of so-and-so, and the goodness of so-and-so, and such-a-one's chariot is over the portion of the Sabbath of so-and-so. And so each and every one is an appointee of the Torah for his specific Sabbath. We are unable to arrange all of these, but only to learn of the chariot of the chariot that proclaims many days in advance. We do not finish in one haste or skip one by one. Rather, each and every one is as the Holy One, Blessed Be He, divided for us, and as He appointed for us all the portions, each one at its post. And because of this, when this portion is crowned, it ascends with those words of that portion which are sealed in fire. They are taken to that chariot appointed over that portion, and it raises them before the Holy One, Blessed Be He. Those very words literally stand before Him and say: "We are the portion of so-and-so, which was built for me by so-and-so in such-a-way." If they are sealed as is fitting, those words ascend and are crowned upon the Holy Throne <term>Kurseya Kadisha</term>. And that chariot is praised before Him—each and every chariot, the portion of each and every Sabbath. They are all crowned within the Holy Throne, and through them, the Living One ascends to be unified higher and higher, and to make everything a single whole. Therefore, happy is the portion of one who prepares the portion of each and every Sabbath as is proper. And there is merit for one who divides above twice.

On the Sabbath, we read in secret, in wisdom, according to the knowledge of the balance that hangs above. In the evening, they need to be included in the praise of the right side, for the Torah was given from between the sides, as it is written <margin>(Deuteronomy 33)</margin>: *From His right hand went a fiery law for them.* And from the beginning, they move toward the Torah scroll in perfection with its help. There are verses, perhaps more, but they do not diminish the portion, for the perfection <term>Shleimu</term> of the portion is only on the right, and it remains ready until the hour of assembly. And they established it in its time, and in the heavens on the Sabbath, because the levels <term>Dargin</term> descend below to all those of the Torah. And you might say this: they are specified below. Rather, it is so, and for life for all this below, everything is the collective of the Torah, and each and every one is included in each and every one. And the spirit of the word—these are the supernal levels that read the portion first, and afterward nine levels emerge from them below, which are as one. And because of this, there are nine men <note>Referring to the total number of people called to the Torah across the week</note>: three on the Sabbath in wisdom, and three on the second day <note>Monday</note>, and three on the fifth day <note>Thursday</note>—behold, there are nine. And in the book of Rav Yeiva the Elder, it is explained in wisdom according to knowledge: behold, the spirit of the heavens is awakened, and the lower point on that left side receives the spirit of the Torah. At that time, in the dew of the rain of heaven, and from His own we read, for He stands in the mystery <term>Raza</term> of nine...

->**And they made**, every wise-hearted man among those who performed the work...<- <note>Exodus 36:8</note> 
It is written: **The heavens are the Lord’s heavens, but the earth He has given to the children of men** <note>Psalms 115:16</note>. This verse should have simply said: "The heavens are the Lord's and the earth He gave to men." Why does it say "The heavens are the Lord's heavens" <note>repeating the word 'heavens'</note>? Rather, here one must look, because there are heavens, and below them are "heavens of heavens"—heavens below and earth below. And there are heavens above and earth below that gather [all things], and all the levels, upper and lower, are all gathered one into the other. The "heavens below" are the ten curtains <note>of the Tabernacle</note>, as it is said: *“Who stretches out the heavens like a curtain.”* And the Holy One, blessed be He, made them so that the lower earth could be looked upon, and their coverings are according to their colors. Nineteen coverings are below that hide like a knot of bundles. The crown of mercy is the root, and all the guardians are appointed until the seventh. It was found that for that lower living creature <note>original: *chayah*</note>, the measure is from within the Supernal Throne and it circles around. And the crown is called "the mountain" which they hold, and it gives to the lower [realms] and their life to be supported below. This eighth [level] is when the matters of the stars are commanded, and that standing priest embraces them and gives strength to each and every one to be anointed in that place to be guarded, as it is written: **He who brings out their host by number...** <note>Isaiah 40:26</note>. "By the greatness of His might"—this is the Living Creature <note>the *Chayah*</note>, and it says in the language of investigation "greatness of might." And every single firmament is appointed and commanded over the world and over the earth to illuminate, except for the Land of Israel, which no firmament hides and no [angelic] appointee [rules], but the Holy One, blessed be He, alone, and this has already been established. And if you say: how can the firmament dwell over the Land of Israel? Behold, rain and rest descend from the firmament upon it like all the earth! Rather, [the difference is that] over every other firmament there are appointed rulers over the world.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**And He Assembled**<-
<note>original: "Vayakhel" (Exodus 35:1)</note>

And that appointed official who rules over that firmament <note>The Hebrew/Aramaic term *Rakia* refers to a celestial expanse or "heavenly layer."</note> holds onto it, for he has nothing of his own from that firmament except what he takes to bring down below. And that firmament takes from that appointed official and gives it down to the earth. Yet that official only receives from the eight celestial powers above. In every firmament, there are known gates that are under the authority of every appointed official; gate by gate is marked, and beyond that gate, an official does not rule even by a hair’s breadth. One does not enter the domain of his fellow’s gate unless permission is granted for one to overlap with the other; then the kings of the earth rule over one another <note>The Zohar suggests that earthly political shifts are reflections of these celestial boundary changes.</note>. At the awakening of all the firmaments, there is one gate called **Zebulun** <note>The name of one of the twelve tribes, also used in the Talmud to describe the specific heaven containing the Celestial Temple.</note>, and beneath that gate, there are seventy other gates below. Seventy appointed officials guard them from a distance of two thousand cubits so that they do not draw near to it. From that gate, one ascends higher and higher until reaching the midst of the High Throne. They arrange the gates on all sides of the firmament up to the entrance of the gate called Zebulun <note>Reference to Zohar II, 203b</note> (**Page 203b**), for there is the end of the firmament that marks the boundary of the Land of Israel. And all those gates are marked within that gate called Zebulun; they are all marked like the Holy Throne, and we call them all the **Gates of Justice** <note>original: "Sha'arei Tzedek"</note>, for no "other side" <note>evil or impure forces</note> rules over them. It issues commands to the Land of Israel, and in that firmament, from the opening of the gate, it is commanded as is necessary. From the appointment of that command, those seventy officials take and give to all the other officials.

In the lower Garden of Eden, there are high mysteries within the firmament that stands over it. The firmament that stands over it contains high mysteries. When <term>The Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu" (the standard way to refer to God in the Zohar)</note> passes through this firmament of the Living Creatures <note>The *Chayot*, a high order of angels</note> and draws from the midst of the Throne of Glory, they emerge as one and pass from here, leaning downward and spreading out until they reach that place of the Garden of Eden and dwell there. What does the Holy One do? He takes the essence of the holy prayers of the days, which are comforted and not found, to be hidden and not revealed. These are the essences that were prepared from the high essences; He made from them the repairs for the firmament, and it joins within another firmament and stretches out. Over this lower Garden, there are four colors in that stretching of the firmament that is over the Garden: white, red, green, and black. Corresponding to these colors, there are four gates at the four sides of the firmament that is over the Garden. From here, that firmament is opened as four gates; four lights to the right side. In that gate, from the stretching of the right side, two lights shine, included within the openings of the gates. In the gate of the right and in the gate of the vision within, they cover the light that shines to the right side. A single light is sprinkled, shining and swallowed; and because it is included within that light, this is the letter **M** <note>The Hebrew letter Mem (מ)</note>, and it stands in the awakening of that light of the gate. This letter ascends and descends; it does not stay in one place. That light nullifies that letter and embraces it, therefore it does not stay in one place. On the side that shines, on the side of the vision, opposite the coverings, a single light is sprinkled that shines and is included and gathered like a gathering within that light, and this is the letter **R** <note>The Hebrew letter Resh (ר)</note>. Sometimes the R is seen and stands in the awakening of that light of the gate, ascending and descending; sometimes it is revealed and sometimes it is not revealed, and it does not stay in one place. These two letters stand, and when the firmament is stretched over the Garden of Eden, these two letters emerge from within that light and stand upon that which is stretched, ascending and descending. Then the stretching of the two gates precedes, and two chariots descend from above. One high chariot in the likeness of **Michael**, the Great Prince/Official. A second chariot in the likeness of the Holy Chariot, the Great Official of the Inquiry of All (this is a precious hidden secret of the inquiry).

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Vayakhel**<-
<note>original: "ויקהל" - And he assembled. This is the title of the Torah portion.</note>

A person in this world, through the commandments of the Torah—all of them stand as a surrounding shield in the Garden of Eden, to clothe other precious righteous ones. When the soul ascends through that gate of the firmament above, other precious, supernal garments are prepared for it, which come from the will and the <term>intention of the heart</term> <note>original: "כוונה" (Kavanah) - the focused spiritual intent during a ritual act</note> in Torah study and in prayer. For when the soul ascends, it is crowned with that crown by which it is crowned, and its portion remains for this person, and from it is made a **garment of light** to clothe the soul so it may ascend on high. And come and see: it has been established that these garments are like the deeds of human beings that they performed with a <term>willingness of spirit</term> <note>original: "רעותא דרוחא"</note>, as we have said, to establish for us holy angelic spirits—though this is not the full clarification of the matter. And in the holy foundation, I have seen it thus: that these garments below, in the earthly Garden, are like the deeds of human beings, while those above are from the spirit, the will, and the intention of the heart.

**"And a river went out of Eden to water the garden..."** <note>Genesis 2:10</note> and they have explained it. But in this Garden below, a river certainly goes out from Eden, and it is necessary to know where the root and the path of this river that emerges from the soul below is located. In what place in Eden? This "Eden" is a supernal spirit, and the secret of it is not settled so that the eye of understanding can know it. The spirit of the matter is this: this place is spoken of below, yet it shines from the place of the holy Supernal Eden, which was given at the end to be known. Because of the hiddenness of the glory of the holy Supernal Eden, of which it is said, "they shall delight in Eden," the beginning of this river that flows and emerges from it is not permitted to be explained to those souls in the Garden of Eden. Just as this river divides and goes out from the Garden of Eden to be attached to the Garden in two ways: from within that middle gate of the Garden, a single light emerges which divides into four sides toward all the gates we have mentioned. The place where those inscribed letters stand—that light which divides into four lights—all of them emerge and go out from Eden, the place where the river is a point, both below and above.

And from that point which shines and becomes "Eden" to give light, there is no one who is permitted to see or to know this point, except for that light which spreads from it, which the righteous in the Garden of Eden grasp before them, as has been said. And through this point from below, the soul lives toward the Supernal Eden, a place that is not settled for knowing or for gazing upon. Concerning all this, it is written: ->**"No eye has seen, O God, besides You"**<- <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>. That which is not explained as "God besides You" is the holy lower point, which knows the life that stands over us below, which is hidden like the Garden, and there is no searching out the matter to know it. "God besides You"—this is the Supernal Eden above all, the life-spirit of the World to Come, which knows the lower point as a single Righteous One <note>The Sefirah of Yesod</note> from whom a river emerges to water it. And there is none who knows it except for the Life that is within them, and this Life looks upward, upward, unto the **Infinite** <note>original: "אין סוף" (Ein Sof) - the Boundless/Infinite Godhead</note>.

And this river that goes out from Eden below—this spirit is life for the wise in spirit, as it is written: ->**"And He will satisfy your soul in parched places"**<- <note>Isaiah 58:11</note>. And this matter is explained above and below. When it extends and emerges from the source of the World to Come, life is sealed to look upon this person who was given to study His Torah for life. Thus, each and every one is the life of the soul, as you say: "Come and see, come and see the life of those souls in the mountains of the Garden, the firmament, and the palaces of the Garden." And if that garment were cheapened, they would not be able to contemplate. And by that river that goes out from Eden, all those souls sit upon that river like garments of glory. And then they are settled, and the spirit is in their palate, and they are able to contemplate. And in that river is the life-sustenance of the souls, to be settled, to be enlightened, and to be strengthened by those comforts and delights of the river, upon that river where they are settled. That supernal river breaks forth like gifts and blossoms from it into the Garden; it is the river below, like the earthly Garden, prepared like gifts to be established and settled in the palate of...

# Vayakhel

Signs <note>original: "Atoti"</note> exist in this manner, like this world, except for the scent which settles like a soul to be illuminated, for it emerges from the root of the body. And because they are guided like the blind upon that river that flows out of Eden, they then settle as a bride <note>or "essence"</note> and a living creature <note>Chayyah</note> to ascend above. Like that opening of the firmament's essence, there is one pillar that stands as a descending essence; by that same pillar, they ascend above into that opening of the firmament. And within it, there are surrounding layers: thicket, cloud, and branch. And even though they established this verse <note>Ezekiel 1:4</note> regarding "a great cloud," these are from the outside, etc. And this is their "Living Creature" <note>Chayyah</note> that ascends above so they will not be seen by the creatures that dwell below. And this is the "level of the spirit" that arms all the houses of the Holy One, Blessed be He, to be prepared and adorned with crowns and cushions and garments from the side of the four male faces. And the creatures gather there and strike these thirty faces and go inside by that pillar that stands as an essence. And by that same taste, that pillar of the serpent and sin and the prepared one ascends from the musicians. And these two "searches" are the "Foundation of Mount Zion and its Sanctuary." The "Foundation of Mount Zion" is a powerful Living Creature above. When the voice comes, it is established, and the creatures are cooled by that command to be adorned. Once these blind ones ascend to that opening of the firmament, then that firmament circles the circles of the Garden three times. And from the pleasant sound of that firmament's circling, all those blind ones emerge and strike the pleasantness of that firmament, and they strike that pillar that ascends—it and the serpent and the prepared one that burns—and they close them all. Then, when they come and ascend through that opening, they enter the circle that surrounds like a point. Then they strike what they strike. And from the light and the joy of what they strike, they ascend and are gathered, circling and distant, and a third Living Creature is with them and is adorned in light. Then, thousands are jealous of the light of one Supernal Righteous One <note>Tzaddik</note> and look upon the beauty of this point and the preparation. And it is desired when he raises it to him and shines light within light. And he is pious; all the hosts of heaven open with that same taste and say: "How worthy are you, O Righteous ones, who guard the Torah!" And all the creatures who look into the Torah, for the joy of your guard is like this, for the crown of your guard is the Mishnah <note>Oral Law</note> like this. Then, since they shine with light, two lights are joined as one and shine afterward. The creatures see and look to take pleasure in those blind ones for the Righteous, and they are prepared for them as a crown above. And concerning this, it is said:
-> "No eye has seen, O God, besides You, what He acts for him who waits for Him." <- <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>

-> "And over the heads of the Living Creature there was the likeness of a firmament, like the color of the terrible ice, stretched out over their heads from above." <- <note>Ezekiel 1:22</note>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Vayakhel**<-

Regarding this **point** <note>The "point" refers to a specific mystical Sephirah or divine focus</note> that we have discussed: just as it has a portion above, so too it has a portion below on the earth. And in this **Garden** <note>The Garden of Eden</note> below, there is a portion of this point for delighting with the **souls of the righteous** on earth, and to be guided in all directions, above and below. Above, through the **prophet**; below, in that **Palace** of the **Righteous** <note>Tzaddik</note>. No delight is found above or below except through this Righteous one. And in this Garden, it is from that point which is called **Eden**. Those **running living creatures** <note>The Chayyot, angelic beings from Ezekiel's vision</note> are four heads that cover [the chariot]. One is South, as it is written: *and the face of a lion was on the right side* <note>Ezekiel 1:10</note>. And one is North, as it is written: *and the face of an ox on the left side* <note>Ezekiel 1:10</note>. And one is East, as it is written: *and the face of an eagle for the four of them* <note>Ezekiel 1:10</note>. And one is the inclusion of them all, as it is written: *and the likeness of their faces was the face of a man* <note>Ezekiel 1:10</note>.

And these four heads are lights that reach toward the **Holy Throne**, and they are the burden-bearers for it. And from that sweat produced by their burden, that **River of Fire** <note>Nahar di-Nur</note> is created, as it is written: *A river of fire issued and came forth from before Him; thousand thousands ministered to Him* <note>Daniel 7:10</note>. And at times, when they ascend, they immerse themselves in that River of Fire; they ascend as an offering and are not consumed, but rather purified.

Come and see: from the **salamander** <note>A mythical creature believed to be born from fire</note> they make a garment. Because its garment is from fire, that garment can only be cleansed in fire. So too here, these are the **garments of the soul**; for this garment is likewise purified by the fire below. This is the holy fire of the forge, as it is written: *like a sea of glowing coals, screens of fire*. At the time when the portion of that point desires to rise and be transformed like fire, it is purified, and the fire consumes all that **filth** <note>Zuhama: spiritual impurity or residue from the physical world</note> which is in the soul, so that the soul may shine and be clothed.

And you might say: if so, does the soul not suffer punishment in this? Come and see: woe to the soul that consumes fire like fire, even though it is clothed. But when that portion rises, it is certainly the garment of the soul that receives that punishment, because all that filth is the portion in the fire. And from the first power, once it has received punishment in the body, it goes into the river and it is consumed little by little within it. There is one place called **The Throne** <note>Kisse</note>... rather, there is one place between them where souls are kept in light to be clothed before they ascend into the Garden of Eden.

How meritorious are those souls when they enter that place! Two angels stand at the right in the Garden of Eden and stand at the gate, and they give rest to those in that place of **Gehenna** <note>Purgatory/Hell</note> in order to receive that soul. And before that soul is clothed in fire, those appointed ones give them rest and say, "Enter." And at times when she is clothed, they go out with her from that place and guide her toward the opening of the Garden of Eden, where they wait and say to them, "Enter." These are the souls that are clothed; then they go to that soul in the Garden of Eden. And how broken she is from that breaking of being clothed in Gehenna, which is the breaking below, even though it is dark within. But once she reaches that Garden, she is weak and does not lick [the light], but in the gift she is crowned and joined. Then the Holy One, blessed be He, brings out the **Sun of Light**, and those four openings shine in the firmament above the Garden, and it reaches that soul and she is healed. This is what is meant by: *But unto you that fear My name shall the sun of righteousness arise with healing in its wings* <note>Malachi 3:20</note>.

And from the second power, after she dwells in the Garden of Eden below all that time that she dwells there, she is not separated from those radiances that come from the world of all. When they bring her up above, she must be separated from every living thing and every radiance of below, and she passes through that River of Fire. Then the soul is clothed in it entirely and goes out and appears before the **Master of the World** in spirit from all sides. Once she gazes upon that light, she is made pious and illuminated by all of them. And then those souls stand in garments, crowned before their Master. Happy is the portion of the righteous!

## Main Text (Zohar)

Of the righteous in this world, and he strikes below. And those hidden ones who are in the lower Garden of Eden wander about on every New Moon and Sabbath, ascending to that place called the **Walls of Jerusalem**, where they sit many times and return to establish the walls, as it is written <note>Isaiah 62:6</note> **"Upon your walls, O Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen."** They ascend to that place but do not enter within until they gaze and come to prostrate themselves, drawing from that light, and then they return inside. They go out from there and roam the world, seeing in a vision the bodies of the wicked in their punishment, as it is written <note>Isaiah 66:24</note> **"And they shall go out and look upon the corpses of the people who have rebelled against Me; for their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched, and they shall be an abhorrence to all flesh."** He strikes on every side to show the rest of the bodies on their sides, as has been established.

Afterward, they roam and gaze upon those who are stricken with pains and illnesses, and those who suffer for the sake of the unification of their Master, and they return and tell the Messiah. When they tell the Messiah of the sorrow of Israel in their exile, and of the wicked among them who do not look to know their Master, he raises his voice and weeps for those wicked ones among them, for this is what is written <note>Isaiah 53:5</note> **"But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was crushed for our iniquities."** Those hidden ones return and stand in their places.

In the Garden of Eden, there is one palace called the **Palace of the Sons of Sickness**. Then the Messiah enters that palace and calls for all the sicknesses, all the pains, and all the sufferings of Israel to come upon him, and they all come upon him. And were it not that he lightens them from Israel and takes them upon himself, there would be no human being able to endure the sufferings of Israel for the punishments of the Torah; this is what is written: **"Surely he has borne our sicknesses..."** <note>Isaiah 53:4</note>. In this manner, Rabbi Eleazar, when he would enter the booth of the Sukkah <note>referring to his own period of suffering</note>, those sufferings that stood over him—which he remembered every day—would all be silenced from the world at the time he engaged with the Torah.

When Israel was in the Holy Land, through those services and sacrifices they performed, they would remove all those sicknesses and sufferings from the world. Now, the Messiah removes them from the people of the world until a person departs from this world and receives his punishment as has been stated. When those wicked ones are judged deep within Gehenna <note>the realm of purgation or punishment</note> in other dwellings, receiving great punishment from the heat and the filth of the dross, then a great fear ascends to consume that filth. Woe to that soul that endures that punishment! And concerning those angels of destruction in Gehenna who drive them like cattle to burn that filth—woe to the soul that endures that punishment!

Happy are those who keep the commandments of the Holy Torah to live by them, to delight above in the spirits of the righteous, as was said. Everyone seeks to delight below in the spirits of the righteous, like the heat of the sun upon the wings of the heat to cover them. But at midnight, the living creature <note>Chayah - a high level of soul or angelic being</note> descends and delights in this firmament we mentioned. To sustain the life of the creature, it stands upon thirty times, and those are the thirty living creatures we mentioned—the spirit of the thirty creatures. And this firmament stands below, just as the firmament below is like a voice above, standing upon those thirty creatures we mentioned. And that firmament is in the likeness of the living creature to be joined in a holy manner.

In this firmament, four quarters are observed, and all their hosts are below. When this firmament is prepared in this manner, then all the chariots and all the hosts know and travel, for their portion of nourishment is given to them. This firmament is embroidered with all holy colors. In it stand four hidden gates facing four directions. One gate is hidden on the East side, and in that gate below stands the letter *Lamed* <note>original: ל</note>, and this is prepared and ascends and is silenced in the strength of the gate. This gate shines and prepares, gathering light, and sees the letter prepared and enclosed within the living creature below, and it ascends and spreads out in that gate. A second gate is hidden on the North side, and in it stands below the living creature of the letter *Lamed*...

->And to him<-
