<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Heavenly Palaces (Hechalot) within the Zohar's commentary on the portion of Vayakhel. It specifically details the movements of divine letters and angelic forces within a celestial firmament (Raqia), focusing on the southern and eastern directions.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->And He Assembled<-

And this [firmament] stands, and they all ascend and descend, and it is closed like that gate. At times it is in a state of longing, and at times it is crowned with a crown that shines and yet does not shine. Because of this, there is a fear that stands with great permanence, and there is that which is cast down like that gate. The third gate is its bosom, a gate that stands on the **west** side, and in it stands that which is cast down of the cast down; it is illuminated like that gate, but it has no bosoms or paths. Just as in longing, like that fourth gate, it has a bosom—a gate that stands on the **south** side. In it stands the impression of a single lower point, which is needed for the lower ones but not [dependent] on the lower ones, and this is the letter *Yod* <note>The smallest letter, representing a concentrated point of divine energy</note>. And these are four letters for the four sides of that firmament, like those gates. Within this firmament, other letters are inscribed with crowns upon their heads, and these are the twenty-two letters <note>The Hebrew Alphabet</note> adorned with crowns.

This firmament is like a shadow, and a crown is above the Living Creatures <note>The *Chayyot*, a high order of angels</note> in the lower impression. A spirit is drawn to dwell within a spirit to form a single group, and they are the letter combinations: **Ch-T, K-M, G-Z, D-Y** <note>These are mystical permutations of the alphabet used in meditative prayer</note>. These letters encompass that firmament through the spirit of other letters above them, holy and hidden. And those other letters are concealed, the secrets of that firmament. Then these letters appear like engravings, which are the **L-T, K-M** <note>Further mystical letter groupings</note>, and they are inscribed in this firmament.

At the time when this firmament shines, the four holy sides are illuminated within it. They are a group like the groups that hang, and two blades. Then, the power of the *Sela* <note>A weight or coin, here likely a measure of divine light</note> descends from this firmament like those letters of the spirit of the Holy Name, and all those chariots and all those holy hosts and camps are nourished. And they are all as one. At the time when the balance hangs, those letters are transformed and recognized as **L-G, N, D** and they are **T, Ch**.

At the time when they are recognized and hidden, then a voice goes out and is awakened, and they know that the balance is spread over the world. In this firmament, a single color is cast down which includes all colors when this firmament is shaded. From the **east** side, there are four paths that we mentioned, like four wings <margin>Another version: letters</margin>, all of them like coverings, and they ascend in an ascent on high. And when they are shaded and ascend on high, the city is withdrawn, and the letters are transformed and appear like shadows in the first spirit: **Ch-T, K-M, G-Z, D-Y**. That firmament is embroidered, and then it shines like its light. And when this firmament shines as before, all the letters are restored and go to seek prey and sustenance <note>Metaphor for divine emanation/energy</note>. Since they turn and ascend, a voice—that voice is heard high above. Then all the blessings and sanctifications are given, for upon them the hidden letters roll and testify to that firmament. Those letters stand on the **south** side. Once those letters stand on the south side, they ascend and are gathered in longing and they flame.

Then the power of the *Matnita* <note>Likely referring to a specific structural power or "Mishnah" of the firmament</note> of that firmament, a single impression, is cast down. And that impression belongs to the Holy One. When this [letter] *Dalet* is cast down and seen, then three other letters flame in their crowns. These letters were gathered in the middle of this firmament, all of them, and they descend from the flaming, established in the flaming. Then, for the crown of these, thirteen times they flame, descending from the words of the crown. The letters are included and crowned with the letter *Vav*, and it is not known. Then all the hosts and all the camps are as one in joy, and they ascend to the towers and are entwined in this firmament, as they prepared and testified and rolled. And those first letters that we mentioned, which are **Ch-T, K-M**, are all included in those upper letters, the secret of the Holy Name that we mentioned. They testify to that firmament. And those letters that were the power of the *Matnita*, the spirit of the Holy Name, they were all cast down to the **south** side; they were cast down and yet not cast down. There is no one who can look toward that side; they are all covered and they say with a pleasant voice:

> **Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place.** <note>Ezekiel 3:12</note>

They are covered from the side of the smoke, from the wings.

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of Parashat Vayakhel, specifically focusing on the architecture of the celestial realms as mirrored by the construction of the Tabernacle. It transitions from the general description of the firmaments to the specific interplay of Divine Names and the distinction between holy and unholy layers.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

(A portion for the wise) And they say: these are enfolded from all sides and aspects. This is the firmament that surrounds as in the beginning. When it is revealed from the side of the side <note>referring to the emanation of one spiritual level from another</note>, then a pleasant sound of rain-showers <note>metaphor for divine flow or influence</note> branches out on this side, and a pleasant sound of rain-showers branches out on that side, and likewise to the four directions. At that moment, that firmament shines with a light that is visible more than it ever was, and it stands in light because it is a single crown included in all colors.

And those letters that we mentioned ascend upward into that firmament and receive three-in-one <note>a triad of spiritual forces</note>, which is the supernal unity that connects to this matter through these letters. For even though these letters belong to the Holy Name <note>original: *Sama Kadisha*, likely a variant of *Shema* or the "Holy Elixir"</note>, they are a Name that is included below so that this spirit may be included above and included below. 

And when it is included below, these letters ascend to receive the three-in-one, for it receives the sign <note>the letter/mark</note> and the inner essence. These letters are below, and that sign is the Divine Name <note>original: *Chayahu*, a permutation of the Tetragrammaton</note> which descends, and these letters connect to that sign. Then they all shine as a single crown, and a complete Name is formed. 

Below, the Name is complete and yet not complete. It is a complete Name when seen as the Divine permutations <note>original: *Chayahu* and *Yahud*</note>, the spirit of male and female. They resemble a complete Name when these letters are the sweet union of the Name, a Name complete in everything. Another Name is *Chayahu*, *Chayahu*, and *Yihyu* in the vision as we said. For all this, the Name is complete in everything. 

Once these letters are joined, that firmament shines with two and two lights; then everything is the Holy Name, all is holy in a single spirit above and below. All those chariots <note>celestial assemblies</note> and all those showers stand in a spirit of perfection, and all levels are established in their places, each one as is fitting. 

In this firmament stands the side of the North, a flame of fire that is never extinguished. The Name strikes against other letters, and they crown the Names; sometimes they strike the Names, and all of them are unified in this firmament and shine all as one. 

From the power of this firmament, all those lower firmaments on the side of holiness are sustained, until they reach those other firmaments on the "Other Side" <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of impurity or evil</term>. And these are called **curtains of goats' hair**, as it is written: *“And he made curtains of goats' hair for a tent over the Tabernacle”* <note>Exodus 36:14</note>. For there are curtains and there are curtains. The curtains of the Tabernacle are the curtains called the "Firmaments of the Dwelling" which cover the holiness. The curtains of goats' hair are the other firmaments of the Other Side. These firmaments are in a spirit that is not pure—membranes and husks <term>Kelipot: spiritual shells that conceal the divine light</term>. 

These firmaments belong to the "Male" <note>the active force of the Other Side</note> that stands in the inflation of worldly matters; they are the sides of desires and the works of inflation, and the "Great Dragons" are over them. These are the firmaments that are within the husk, covering the "Brain" <note>the inner light/wisdom</note>. The inner firmaments are that husk that stands over the brain, and these are called the Names of the "Other Side" <note>original: *Sami S' Nu'*, likely referring to Samael and Lilith</note> for the side below. 

Other firmaments are above, and they are the inner firmaments called the "Firmaments of the Hardness," which are the secret of the Holy Name in the spirit of the waters that surround them. These are the supernal secrets in the Secret of the Torah, the totality of the twenty-two letters engraved in the sign that emerges from within the supernal firmament—the support of the Divine Name, the firmament that is above the "Living Creatures" <note>the *Chayot*, the highest order of angels</note>. 

Regarding this Name, there is no comparison. It stands hidden and concealed; it has no color. All colors emerge from it, yet it has no color; it is not seen and not revealed. That Name which brings forth all lights within it is not seen—neither light, nor darkness, nor any color at all—except for the souls of the righteous who see from the lower firmament, like through a hole in a wall, the light that emerges and shines from that supernal firmament. That light never ceases, yet there is no one who knows it and no one who can stand within it. 

From this point, all those firmaments are included in one name, which is called **Heaven** <note>Hebrew: *Shamayim*</note>. These are called the "Lower Heavens," while the "Upper Heaven" is called by the Name. These belong to the Holy Name that is crowned as a Priest. And concerning this it is written: *“The heavens are the Lord’s heavens”* <note>Psalms 115:16</note>, referring to that hiddenness of the supernal firmament that is spread over them.

It explains how the Divine Name permeates these levels, providing light to the souls of the righteous while remaining essentially unknowable.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the "Heichalot" (Celestial Palaces) within the portion of Vayakhel. It focuses on the nocturnal ascent of the soul, the mechanics of spiritual attachment (devekut), and the renewal of the soul each morning.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Vayakhel**<-
<note>original: "Vayakhel" - And he assembled</note>

Upon them. Until here, the holy souls are cast down when that field of holy apples <note>A Kabbalistic term for the Shekhinah or the Garden of Eden</note> goes forth and they are joined together. There is no one wise in his craft who can know or attach himself at all, except for one small priest; all of them stand to be settled within it. Happy is the portion of one who enters and exits and knows how to gaze into the secrets of his Master and to attach himself to Him. Through these secrets, a person can attach himself to his Master according to his will, directing his heart to know the dominion of wisdom in the supernal spirit. When he serves his Master with the soul and attaches his will to Him through the soul, it is to unify those firmaments that are below, on the side of holiness, to crown them with a single lower soul. From there onwards, he shall see those supernal, inner firmaments, to show that they are all one in that supernal firmament that stands over them. And all breadths and vessels <note>or "ships"</note> are far from his heart; he shall direct his will and ascend higher and higher to grasp everything in the spirit of secrets, for there is the fixing of all wills and thoughts in the spirit that stands in a vision of the end that is not in any pride. And he completes it with the intention of the body and with strength in this every single day, to dismiss his days; then the supernal days are included in his walking. And they see his will, for behold, he has departed from this world and his soul has gone out from him, and he returns it to the Master of all. For every single night, the spirit of secrets stands to know those wisdoms of the power of this lower firmament in the spirit of that point <note>The "Point" often refers to the foundational Sephirah of Yesod or the start of Malchut</note> which stands in what we have said. That firmament is included from above and from below, and day and night below are like this level that ascends in the secret of wisdom to be unified like its white and red light. It is below like this wick, as a partner; so it is below like that point, for as the day is included from the night, at night it is included from below through those souls of the righteous. And all the matters of the world are behind them all, to uproot and to pave the path and the scratch that comes out from it. And how many varieties and kinds are there to nullify each and every one as is fitting for it; even the nights and the officials like it, the soul goes and flies and reaches that root that is fitting for her. The body lies thin like a husk, and it is possible for that place which is fitting for him to watch over him. Because of this, the body returns to its waste and the soul to its side. The soul spreads over it the spirit of the "Other Side" <note>Sitra Achra - the realm of impurity/evil</note>, and because of this his hands are defiled and he must wash them, as we have established, for the entire inclusion returns to be emptied. And the souls of the righteous ascend and return to their sheath, and she is crowned by them, the Mother who is crowned and included from all sides; then the glory of the Holy One, Blessed be He, ascends and is crowned by all. At night, appointees rule who are charged over those souls of the righteous to bring them up above and to receive them as a pleasing offering to their Master. *Kasot* is the appointee charged over all those watches; *Suria* is the great appointee. Once the soul ascends through all those firmaments, then they bring her close to Him, and He rejoices in her, as it is said:
> "And He shall make him of quick understanding in the fear of the Lord"
<note>Isaiah 11:3</note>
Just as the King Messiah is destined to do in the world, and through him they all pass into the deposit, through him to draw near to God. And all the souls, when they are brought near to that place where they are brought near and are seen there, this is the spirit; all the souls are included in that point, and it takes them and strikes once like one who swallows a mouthful and rests, and she is crowned like a bridegroom who is crowned. This spirit is the Master of Masters. When this point is crowned below, she is conceived from below from that strike in which the soul was included. What is the taste? Pure deeds and like that whiteness that one strives in like the day. And it takes that will of this world, and through it, it is prepared in joy and included from all sides. Afterwards, she brings them out and gives birth to them as at first, and the soul is now new as at first. And this spirit is "new every morning" <note>Lamentations 3:23</note>, truly new, as it has been said. What is the reason? To you...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the construction of the Tabernacle, specifically focusing on the Ark (Aron). It transitions from a discussion on the incense (Ketoret) and the fifty gates of understanding to the specific symbolism of the Ark as a vessel for the Torah and the Holy Spirit. It also introduces a complex linguistic and theological comparison between the "Ark" (Aron) and "Araunah" (Aruna) the Jebusite.</meta>

Those fifty times are the Spirit, as it is written: *And you shall call your walls Salvation and your gates Praise* <note>Isaiah 60:18</note>, to include them and to bring them into concealment and to cover them, for they are dwellings. And for this reason, the galbanum in the incense is mixed in at that time. Blessed are the righteous in the world who know how to see the rising of light and the brain <note>The "brain" or "moach" refers to the hidden, inner wisdom or the source of divine emanation</note>. Rabbi Abba said: On the day the light was turned to favor the world, they stood and returned, and its cycles whirled around. They said to the prophet: "Words that were hidden to be completed, I shall write." Blessed is your portion in this path, in taking and in stars, to praise the Holy One, Blessed be He, because of wisdom. Rabbi Abba opened his discourse and said:

**And Bezalel made the Ark of acacia wood...** <note>Exodus 37:1</note> Here, even though the companions have already established all the secrets of the Tabernacle with holy intention, here one must look closer, for this Spirit is crowned with many secrets and filled with wisdom. This Ark is the Spirit meant to bring in the Written Torah and to be built within it. These are the six directions <note>The six sefirot from Chesed to Yesod, often called the "six extremities" or "six sides"</note> that are hidden, and this is called the Ark (*Aron*). When those six are seen to be as one, then it is one body to bring into it the Spirit of the Torah through nine sides. And those directions are five, and five books <note>The Five Books of Moses</note> enter into it. And those five are six in one upper level, which is in concealment and is called the Spirit of All. It is the "wheat" <note>A mystical metaphor for the essence or sustenance</note> of the Spirit that includes everything. When this enters into those five directions, then Araunah <note>A play on the word "Aron" (Ark) and the name "Aruna" (Araunah)</note> and the Torah stand in the Spirit of nine levels, which are two supports. Afterwards, it stands as one Spirit, an Upper Spirit that hovers over everything. And such is the Holy Spirit that stands in secret and hovers over all, and all of them stand in concealment. Here we must look and know the secrets of Araunah. There is an "Ark" (*Arona*) and there is an "Araunah" (*Aruna*), one corresponding to the other.

He opened and said: *All these, O Araunah the king, does he give to the king...* <note>2 Samuel 24:23</note> Was Araunah then a king? Even though the companions established that this refers to David—for it is written of him: *Whosoever smites the Jebusites, let him get up to the watercourse...* <note>2 Samuel 5:8</note> and he took Jerusalem, and it was his by right of purchase with silver. And if you say that even though Jerusalem was David's, that specific place belonged to Araunah—just as it was with the Vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, where even though Ahab ruled and was king, he needed to seek the right to that vineyard—so too with David. Yet certainly, Araunah was a "king" in that he was the ruler over that specific place where his throne was. And when the time came for him to release his hold, he did not release it except through much blood and slaughter in Israel <note>Referring to the plague in the time of David described in 2 Samuel 24</note>. Therefore, after the slaughter and death, that destroying king <note>The Angel of Destruction</note> stood over that place. And there, while he was killing and standing over that place, he was unable to continue and desired a substitute.

And in that place—the place where Isaac was bound <note>The Binding of Isaac, the Akedah</note>—Abraham had built the altar and bound Isaac his son. When the Holy One, Blessed be He, saw that place, He was filled with mercy. This is what is written: *And the Lord repented...* <note>2 Samuel 24:16</note> He saw the Binding of Isaac in that place and returned and had mercy on them. Immediately, *He said to the destroying angel: It is enough (Rav), now stay your hand.* What is the meaning of "Rav" (Great/Enough)? The companions have established: "Take the Great One" <note>A midrashic interpretation that God saw the merit of a "great" ancestor, like Jacob or Isaac</note>. But it is also written here "Rav" and written elsewhere: *You have stayed long enough (Rav) at this mountain* <note>Deuteronomy 1:6</note>. So too here: "It is enough (Rav) for you to have this place under your hand." From here on, "Rav"—return the place to its Master. For through blood, death, and striking, he released his hold.

Why is he called Araunah? It is written "Araunah" and it is written "Aron" (Ark). While that place was under his hand, it was called Araunah—the "Ark" of the Other Side (*Sitra Achra*). Therefore, extra letters were added to it <note>The name Araunah (ארונה) has more letters than Aron (ארון)</note>. This is because an "Evil Eye"—the spirit of the Other Side—always seeks addition, but that addition is actually a curse and a deficiency. In the same way, regarding the holy incense, letters are subtracted and its holiness is increased. This is the Spirit of which it is written: *Upon twelve oxen...* <note>Referring to the base of the molten sea in the Temple</note>. Subtracting... [text breaks off]

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Tabernacle's construction, specifically focusing on the symbolic number of curtains and the spiritual implications of the "Holy Covenant" (circumcision). It contrasts the structural perfection of holiness with the "surplus" or "excess" associated with the forces of evil.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Vayakhel** <-
<note>Vayakhel: "And he assembled," the name of the Torah portion in Exodus 35:1–38:20</note>

It is not written "around" but rather "many." And to the **Other Side** <note>Sitra Achra: the realm of evil or impurity</note> they give a "surplus" or an addition for a second time, as it is written: *“And you shall make curtains of goats’ hair for a tent over the Tabernacle; eleven curtains shall you make them”* <note>Exodus 26:7</note>. And all of these are visions of wickedness. But in the **Side of Holiness**, there are ten and no more. Thus, here there are eleven. And all of these are visions of the [unholy] domain.

And so it was necessary for that Shepherd <note>likely referring to Moses or a spiritual leader</note> to perfect his eyes and his very self. In this same manner, "Wrath" <note>Hebrew: *Charon*</note> is an addition for a second time. It is not written simply as "Wrath," but rather the **Side of Holiness** is called the "Wrath of the Covenant." And regarding this "Wrath" that was cut <note>referring to the act of circumcision</note>, it was said of the body that the **Image of Man** <note>the divine archetype</note> should enter into it. Because of this, those who were not holy and pious, when they departed from this world, they [the angels] would raise them up by degrees. For the **Other Side** is not established with a body, nor does it live like the entirety of the human body. Therefore, their bodies were not created for that **Other Side**, because they are not like the entirety of the human body.

Regarding Joseph, what is written? *“And he left his garment in her hand”* <note>Genesis 39:12; Joseph fleeing Potiphar's wife to guard his purity</note>. At that time, all those [forces] were broken—the covenant within the covenant. The spirit below is like the spirit above, and until the spirit strikes the "taste" <note>mystical perception</note>, because after the **Holy Covenant** is strengthened within him, he is seen above in his degree, and everything is as it should be.

How soft and how bitter! Woe to the children of the world who do not know that end! Woe to that punishment! For anyone who wishes to enter like a spirit [must be careful]. For it is not permitted to enter like a spirit except for the **Righteous** <note>Tzadik</note> who knows his own soul and recognizes within himself that he has not sinned against that **Covenant** which has been established as holy from the beginning of the world, and he guarded it properly and lived. Woe to him who should not have entered like a spirit and instead damaged the "Wrath."

The spirit must be broken like this holy standing [of the covenant], a pressed spirit that is fitting for him and not for another. For "Wrath" is not broken except according to the secret of what is written regarding this holy standing. And one who damages the **Covenant**, woe to him! For he has damaged it during his life. Woe to him! For they turn him over at his death. Woe to him from that punishment! Woe to him for damaging this holy standing. At the hour when they judge him in that world, they look at his deeds to see if he turned away the spirit of the **Holy Covenant** that is sealed in his flesh. And if the face of the "Wrath of his Covenant" appears like this, then he has no portion among the **Righteous**. They look at him and judge him as being outside the "Category of Man." Once he is removed from the category of Man, he is removed from the category of all others who were made for eternal life. And how can that "Wrath" exist if it is not included in the spirit of the human body? Since he is left to that [Other] Side, woe to him! For they bring him into **Gehenna** <note>Hell/Purgatory</note> and he never leaves it. Concerning this, it is written: *“And they shall go forth and look upon the carcasses of the men who have rebelled against Me...”* <note>Isaiah 66:24</note>. These are those who were initially formed like the "all" of Man.

And these words apply when one has not performed **Complete Repentance**. A "pressed" repentance is required to appear and atone for all his deeds. Therefore, the meritorious one does not enter like a [mere] spirit. For as long as the body exists like a hidden treasure that is purified and does not enter to be mixed—except for those **Supernal Pious Ones** whose portion is earned in this world and the World to Come. For there is no rebuke that stands before **The Holy One, Blessed Be He**, like one who dishonors and damages this holy standing [of the Covenant]. Regarding this rebuke, it is written: *“And Esau was loathsome in the eyes of the Lord.”* What is written here? *“And he rolled the Wrath like a wheel.”* And when He saw that they did not perform [repentance], those beloved ones who passed away found the "Wrath." Rather, all of them are the "pressure of the push" of the **Holy Covenant**, and he guarded it and lived. Holy is the congregation whose portion is the "pressure" of one who exerts himself in the work of Judgment and did not sin.

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the mystical nature of spiritual paths, specifically contrasting the "Orach" (private path) and "Derech" (public way). It transitions into the relationship between Moses (the Sun) and Joshua (the Moon) as a model for the transmission of divine wisdom.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Behold, this **path** <note>Aramaic: *Orach*</note> is the one that all those holy living creatures <note>The *Chayyot*, high-ranking angels</note> must gaze upon. The path of the **image** <note>Aramaic: *Diyukna*, the spiritual template</note>—the path that the image travels upon—is a narrow path. It is the path that the Holy One, blessed be He, desires. The path where the living creatures walk before them, and all those who are prepared to hear the words of the wise, to speak them and utter them with their mouths. It is like a light that grows brighter and brighter and never darkens at all, unlike the wise of the nations whose way is to be constantly darkened in everything.
> **The way of the wicked is like darkness, etc.** <note>Proverbs 4:19</note>

And regarding the path of the image: what is the difference between a **path** <note>*Orach*</note> and a **way** <note>*Derech*</note>? They have already established this: a "path" is that which is opened and drawn forth for the Woman <note>The *Shekhinah* or *Malchut*</note>, becoming like that place—a path where "feet" were not previously mentioned. It is trodden like a winepress <note>Aramaic: *Gat*</note> where feet are mentioned for anyone who wishes. Regarding the "image," it is called a "path" because those [holy forces] were before it to open that place. It travels to every place, and it is a "new path" <note>Aramaic: *Orach Charash*</note> that the inhabitants of the world travel. In this place, the opening of the windows within the image is the "whiteness of the woman." The opening is that place where no one travels except when it is prepared for the worlds, because the "images" create something new for that entire place, just as many high matters of holiness are desired by the Holy One, blessed be He. Furthermore, the "glass" <note>The prophetic lens</note> travels through that place in a way it never did before. Therefore, it is called the "path of the image" because it is renewed through it, and they added holiness upon it.

A **way** <note>*Derech*</note>, however, is open to all, and it is written of it that anyone who wishes may tread it, even the guilty. A "way" is the spirit that returns within it, called a "way" because the "Other Side" <note>The forces of evil/impurity</note> treads upon it where it should not, and prevails to see the poor. Therefore, the righteous alone stand and prevail in that place called a **path**, as we have established. A "way" is for everyone—for this side and for that side. Come and see: for the holy celestial beings, a "path" is prepared for them, and they are seen in it, and high, exalted matters are arranged before the **Ancient of Days** <note>The highest aspect of the Divine</note>, and all of them are their portion. Rabbi Shimon opened and said:
> **And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands upon him.** <note>Deuteronomy 34:9</note>

In many places we have learned that Moses's wings were like the wings of the **Sun**, and Joshua's were like the wings of the **Moon**. For the Moon has no light of its own, only from the light of the Sun. All its power to dwell and to spread forth is filled from within the Sun, and when it is filled, it then stands in **perfection** <note>Aramaic: *Shelimuta*</note>. What is the "gazing of the Moon"? It is the spirit of all, which is called the "likeness" in the spirit of the Sun that is upon it. This power does not stand except at the time it stands in perfection. For behold, there are many times when it is dark and called "covered," according to the hour that stands within it. According to that hour, it lives; so it is called at that very moment. But when it stands in this spirit of perfection and is completed from all sides, then it is called "Vav" <note>The letter representing connection and the Sun/Tiferet</note>, for its perfection is like the perfection above—the daughter inheriting from the mother. This is the meaning of "days," as it is written regarding the staff... the tenth of the month... Sukkot... and it is written:
> **But on the tenth day of this seventh month...** <note>Leviticus 23:27</note>

And all is one spirit. When the World to Come stands in the spirit of every crown, they are stringent regarding this "month." It is called "on the tenth" because the Moon is placed in its perfection, full of stars. It is called "the staff of the crown," for the letter **He** is joined and strengthened between them. This spirit is **Yah** <note>The first two letters of the Divine Name</note>; it is in the spirit of the **He**, just as before they were one, to be strengthened and joined in the spirit above. From this light, merit is drawn below, and then the Moon stands in perfection on all sides, above and below, in the spirit of the Sun. This is to benefit all as one spirit, and we have revealed one thing: Joshua is the spirit of the perfection of the Moon. For we have learned "Son of Nun"—the "Son of Nun" certainly, for in the spirit of the Moon he is full of the spirit of the perfection of the holy Sun. Then he is "full of the spirit of wisdom." It shines because of the point upon it, to add and to spread and to bring forth spirit and light. The spirit makes a **Palace** <note>Aramaic: *Heichala*</note>; that spirit spreads and becomes six sides. That spirit spreads in the spirit of all these, and they go and make a Palace below, and everything is filled, and it becomes the spirit of the Sun.

## Vayakhel
->**And He Assembled**<-

The holy support is like a single perfection. And see, "Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands upon him" <note>Deuteronomy 34:9</note>, and he poured out blessings and they were found within him from him. And you, holy supreme ones, each one is focused and filled with the spirit of wisdom and stands in perfection within the secret of wisdom, because the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired you and laid His hands upon you. Fortunate is my portion that my eyes have seen this, and have seen the completion of the secret of wisdom in you. It is written:
> "You shall not eat anything with the blood; neither shall you practice divination, nor shall you observe times." (Leviticus 19:26)

This verse is established and the secret of the matter stands: whoever eats without prayer, his judgment is weighed upon his blood, and he is like a <term>diviner (menachesh)</term> and a <term>soothsayer (me'onen)</term>. Because the mixture <note>of the physical and spiritual</note> rises and joins to see the supreme precious secret, just as the body is prepared and established when that brain is prepared within the blood to sustain the body, and he passes and tastes the taste of death to receive it. When a person awakens to life, he is pure, but the <term>Other Side (Sitra Achra)</term> <note>The realm of impurity or evil in Kabbalah</note> rules over a place that stands without a soul. Once he has purified himself with water, even though a person exerts himself in the Torah, that soul does not remain in its place and does not rule over him, for a person is then only the sustenance of the blood alone, which is called <term>Nefesh</term> <note>The lowest level of the soul, associated with biological life</note>, which is joined as is fitting, as we have established. 

And when a person prays the prayer of the "partition" <note>the morning prayer that separates the physical from the spiritual</note> of his Master, then the matter of the blood is settled in its place, and the brain of the <term>Neshamah</term> <note>The higher intellectual soul</note> is joined and settled over that place. Then the person becomes complete before his Master as is necessary—the *Nefesh* below and the *Ruach* <note>The middle soul, associated with speech and emotion</note> of the word of wisdom above. Therefore, one who has not prayed his prayer before he eats has not established himself as is necessary, nor deposited the soul in its dwelling place as is required. 

If he eats before he prays to settle the blood in its place, he is like a diviner and a soothsayer, because he is casting sustenance like a diviner to later ascend to the crown and see the side of holiness. To see—and such a person who exerts himself in this side is called a "diviner," who exerts himself in sorcery to gather strength for the matter and to prevail. This is like one who worships idols and is silent; so too he serves that matter of the blood and does not serve the Holy One, Blessed be He, to strengthen the side of the soul with the dew of holiness. A "soothsayer" (*me'onen*) is one who exerts himself in clouds (*anan*) and does not exert himself in merit. And see, wonder at this, for all punishment is thus. 

Behold, they cannot cast a curse from that "Other Side" until they mix in a branch of the side of holiness, like a single thin thread. One who wishes to establish a lie must mix in a word of truth so that the lie will endure. Therefore, the "cloud" is a matter of falsehood, and to make it endure, the one above takes a word of truth and grabs a bit of kindness to establish that falsehood. Thus, one who does not pray before the Holy One, Blessed be He, before he eats, is like a diviner and a soothsayer regarding his blood. 

The prayer of a man, as you have said, you holy supreme ones—fortunate is their portion! For behold, the man himself and his soul are repaired and made complete. Prayer consists of repairs <note>Tikkunim</note> that are prepared together, and they are four:

**The First Repair:** The repair of oneself toward perfection.
**The Second Repair:** The repair of this world.
**The Third Repair:** The repair of the world above among all the heavenly hosts.
**The Fourth Repair:** The repair of the Holy Name in the secret of the holy chariots, and all the worlds, above and below, are in the repair of this Holy Name as is fitting.

The first repair is the repair of oneself, because one must prepare himself as a holy vessel and prepare himself with offerings and elevations that purify. The second repair is the repair of the standing of this world through the Work of Creation, to bless the Holy One, Blessed be He, for all His works and the work of the standing of this world. Therefore, **"Blessed be He who spoke"** <note>The *Baruch She'amar* prayer</note> is a blessing over all of them. The third repair is the repair of the upper world...

To the upper world, to all those hosts and <term>matronin</term> <note>original: "matronin" - high-ranking celestial governors or feminine spiritual powers</note> included therein, these stars pass through the hollows of the "heaven of heavens" etc. <note>Psalm 148:4</note>. The fourth restoration is the restoration of the exile, in the restoration of the spirit of impurity as you have said. Blessed is your portion and blessed is the spirit of the restoration, for my portion is blessed along with yours in this world and in the world to come. The <term>commandments of the Torah</term> <note>original: "pekudei oraitha"</note> which you spoke of regarding the exile—it is certainly so. He opened and said: It is written,
> **You shall fear the Lord your God; Him shall you serve** <note>Deuteronomy 10:20</note>

And it is written, **and you shall fear from your God** <note>Leviticus 19:14</note>. Regarding this verse, one must say: "and you shall fear your God," because it is already written, **the Lord your God you shall fear**. What then is the meaning of **from your God**? Rather, it is a spirit that is certainly cast down from that place which was mentioned; a word to say that it is hidden "from your God," for it does not resemble Him, since the spirit dwells there. And those below... there are three colors in this first <term>hollow</term> <note>original: "chalal" - a void or space within the celestial spheres</note>. It is a hollow that is in the voice, a hollow as we have said, not entirely according to his will.

The second hollow is the hollow of which it is written that he built for himself below a "wing" <note>referring to a spiritual extremity or protection</note>. And this is the hollow that stands within the inner hollow as has been stated.

The third hollow is the hollow that proclaims below the "wing," and in this hollow the fears are stirred to provide sustenance. And over the middle cloud of the four colors of the hollow, these four take hold of one hollow here. In that hollow of which we spoke, which belongs to the spirit, it is written: **and you shall fear from your God**, meaning from that <term>ring</term> <note>original: "izka" - a signet ring or a spiritual seal of authority</note> of His.

And in the place where mercy is required to circumcise his will... to fear on this side and to trample like this rain. And in those colors we mentioned, and in that which is protected, one should fear the "stings." For whoever transgresses the commandments of the Torah is punished by that "male" side that dwells on that side, to bring him low until he is removed from this world and the world to come. And likewise, one must fear this hollow where the "protected one" dwells, to truly spread the "male hollow" we mentioned. And regarding this it is written:
> **You shall not fear the gods of the peoples** <note>Judges 6:10</note>

For one must fear only Him. And this "likeness" of which we spoke is holy and shares in holiness, and it is this that proclaims to incline the mouth. And he is the "male" place that joins with this lowliness, and sometimes it is made from him and does not join with the Holy One... then it is a sin of darkness, and it darkens.

Afterward, as we have established, the spirit hovers and speaks because the moon was carved upon them... when it is not mixed afterward, and here it is the "Right Side" <note>the side of Mercy/Chesed</note>. For whoever worships from this place cleaves to the Supernal place above and cleaves to the holiness of the world to come, because he rises to be mixed and to cleave to the Right Side. And if you say that worship from the side of "bread" <note>referring to physical or lower sustenance</note> is not worship—it is holy, but it does not rise to cleave above. But when one worships out of darkness, he rises to be awakened above and to cleave to the world to come. This is the portion of one who is destined for the world to come; blessed is his portion, for he rules over the place of "bread," as no one rules over that level except from here.

The spirit that is found is the **Spirit of Unity** which is required for one who is worthy of the world to come: to fear the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, and to unify the <term>limbs</term> <note>original: "shayfin" - the various parts or emanations of the Divine Body</note> and the levels above, all as one. It is necessary to tie the knot of faith. And this is the spirit of which it is written:
> **Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is One** <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note>

And in the word "Hear" (*Shema*), the letter *Ayin* is large <note>In Torah scrolls, the Ayin of Shema and Dalet of Echad are enlarged</note>, and this includes "One Israel." This refers to **Israel the Elder** <note>original: "Yisrael Saba" - a high level of the sefirot</note>, because there is also the "Youth," as it is written:
> **When Israel was a youth, I loved him** <note>Hosea 11:1</note>

And this is Israel the Elder, the Holy Spirit as a new general principle. Afterward, they are included one in the other as a single whole. Then it is necessary to unify the

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Vayakhel**<-
<note>original: "ויקהל" (And he assembled). This refers to the Torah portion in Exodus 35:1–38:20.</note>

The limbs <note>term: "sheifin" - the various spiritual emanations or "parts" of the Divine body</note> gather and the two sides connect as one. All these limbs, through the desire of the heart, rise to cling to the Infinite <note>term: "Ein Sof" - the Boundless, God prior to any self-manifestation</note>, so that everything there becomes one single will, above and below. And this spirit shall be the entirety of the Name **Y-H-V-H**, the Lord is One, through the spirit of the Foundation <note>term: "Yesod" - the procreative or connecting emanation</note> of the masculine, to cling together as one. The inner palace below exists because of that supreme point of life; and this is their life, the spirit, for generation after generation. These are the two letters of life <note>note: referring to the letters Yod (י) and He (ה)</note>, and all limbs are included in that place from which life emerges. The inner palace below brings the things from below to the root, the foundation, and their source, up to that place which is the masculine root below. Those two letters are called "of life," **Y-H**, so that the **Y** may be joined and cling to the **H**. The **Y** is the life of the holy masculine spirit, and this **H** is the life of the palace below, which is hidden. For behold, the holy masculine spirit consists of **Y** and **H** upon the life of the second **V**, which contains the mystery of all three <note>note: the letter Vav (ו) often represents the central column or the six directions</note>, to unify the masculine and feminine as one.

The place for unification is from there and above, where everything is as one. The desire rises to bind everything from below to above in a single bond, to raise the desire in awe and love higher and higher, until no desire is found among all those levels and limbs except to be found clinging to them, so that everything becomes one bond without end <note>note: "Ein Sof"</note>. This is the unification of **Rav Hamnuna Saba** <note>note: A prominent, often legendary, sage in the Zohar known for his deep mystical insights</note>, who passed his thought and wisdom through the Chariot <note>term: "Merkavah" - the Divine Throne-Chariot</note> until the entrance of the leap and the sapphire of life and the unification in its proper arrangement.

And even though we have established that this is like many spirits, all those spirits rise into one. But this spirit is found like a sapphire, the sapphire of life and the unification in its arrangement. He proceeds with them in the unification of the spirit; the levels and the words are intermingled, and the life, the sapphire, and the unification are as they should be. Thus, all this is a single unification in its proper arrangement. This was the life and the labor of Rav Hamnuna Saba. Furthermore, he would say words of his desire to include all the spirits of unification, like a vision that is even more beautiful. Therefore, we go together to raise his desire from above to below and from below to above, so that all becomes one unification in this spirit. It shall be a support in the world of life to give us life, as we have learned: the place where the spirit exists above and below, to the four sides of the world. Thus is the life for the unification above and below, as has been stated, and to the four sides of the world. These are the spirits of the supreme Chariot, to include everything as one in one bond, in one unification, unto the Infinite.

As we have established, the spirit of the masculine is unified within it. Afterward, because the **Shekhinah** <note>term: "Shekhinah" - the Divine Presence, personified as feminine</note> was in exile <note>term: "Galut"</note>, and as it were, life was revealed but not as "buried" life to be harnessed as a chariot. Then the lower world was like the upper world, to be seen from the mystery of that exile that occurred in Babylon, like many kinds of deeds the Holy One, blessed be He, performed. That redemption <note>term: "Purkana"</note> must be mentioned and strengthened; for even though life is in exile now, it stands as life and not death. For those bonds within it were damaged, the lower lives and types were made, and it is necessary to show her mystery because she is joined with her husband. In order to "join redemption to prayer" <note>note: a Talmudic concept regarding the flow of the liturgy, here given mystical weight</note> so that all becomes one without separation, and not to show any divorce or diminishment—

> **"And a woman divorced from her husband they shall not take"** <note>Leviticus 21:7</note>

And if you say that while in exile she is "divorced," it is not so! Rather, certainly in exile He is considered to dwell with the people of Israel to rest upon them, but she was not divorced. The Shekhinah was not below like them <note>note: in their state of impurity</note>; she wept greatly until Israel was exiled, and she rose above. Afterward, life went to dwell with them, but she was never "of the earth" <note>note: meaning she did not become mundane</note>. In everything, one must show the redemption of life within her through the four exiles, corresponding to the four exiles, so that He may take His mate and not take a divorcee. At that time, she stands and is redeemed from the four exiles by that merit of the Sanctuary <note>term: "Mikdash"</note>, and by that which was guarded in its proper arrangement to be joined with her husband. It is necessary to show that she is in the Sanctuary of exile, having lived through the four exiles, and because of this, it must be mentioned.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the mystical mechanics of prayer and Torah study. It focuses on how the words spoken by the righteous on earth ascend through the celestial spheres to form crowns for the Creator.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

To be remembered in that place: "Truth, Truth, Truth" regarding the "Help of our fathers." This is the support and pillar that guards them all. From there onward, there are four other times where "Truth, Truth, Truth, Truth" is mentioned to establish the four wheels <note>original: *galgalin*, referring to the wheels of the Divine Chariot</note> in a firm standing, in the perfect strength of the King’s treasuries. These four wheels are doubled in their standing, and all of them are within that "Remembrance of the Males," which is the light of the masculine principle. There are ten wheels in this mystery, and a witness proclaims it at all times. In this cycle, the Holy Name is not found in its full restoration to be unified.

And because of this, one must remember the light that shines constantly upon all the holy ones of the **Holy One, Blessed be He**—blessed be His name forever and for all eternity. The mystery of the holiness of His name is established through them, for through holiness, all things above and below are sanctified. All levels and all supernal and lower chariots <note>original: *ratchin*, the spiritual vehicles of Divine manifestation</note> are all sanctified by the holiness of their Master and by the holiness of the Spirit. We have established these supernal mysteries for the masters of mysteries who gather in the holiness of their Master, and all of them are their portion. It is a mystery to be delivered according to the proper way; let it stand before your words, friends, and all their portions. Happy are those who are like this, who merit in life that holy words are crowned in this world, because they are all written above before the Holy King. He opened and said:

> **"Then those who feared the Lord spoke to one another, and the Lord hearkened and heard, and a book of remembrance was written before Him for those who feared the Lord and for those who thought upon His name."** <note>Malachi 3:16</note>

This verse must be looked into. If it says "they spoke," why does it then say "they remembered"? What is "as they remembered"? Rather, they were remembered above by all those holy chariots and all those holy hosts, because those holy words ascend on high. And how many are there who go before and take them to the Holy King? They are crowned with many crowns like those supernal lights, and all of them are remembered before the King. Who has seen the joys, who has seen the praises that ascend through all those firmaments before the Holy King? And the Holy King looks at them and is crowned by them, and they ascend upon His head and become a crown. Then they descend and rest upon His lap <note>or "bosom"</note> in His strength, and from there they ascend again upon His head. He sees His delights day by day. It is not written "and He saw them," but "and He sees them" at every time and every moment that the supernal words ascend before Him. And here, "those who fear the Lord" is written twice. Why? Rather, "those who fear the Lord" above, and "those who fear the Lord" below. "Those who fear the Lord" stand below, and the words stand written above.

And this Spirit is found according to what is close to all the words of the righteous who are on earth; they are crowned and stand before the King, and the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, delights in them. They are engraved and stand before Him in the very image of that righteous person who spoke them. The **Holy One, Blessed be He**, delights in that image, and afterwards they are "written in the book of remembrance before Him" to be sustained before Him in a permanent standing. "And for those who thought upon His name"—what does "those who thought upon His name" mean? This we have established regarding all those who meditate on the words of Torah to cleave to their Master through the spirit of the Holy Name. It is written:

> **"And above the firmament that was over their heads was the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone."** <note>Ezekiel 1:26</note>

This verse we have already established. But "above the firmament," as you have said, friends—and all are our portion, and happy is their portion—is like that firmament below which is within the firmament above. There is no one who can gaze at it or attain it. From it stands that sapphire stone, for it was made by the spirit of that good and precious pearl, as we have established. It appeared "like the appearance," and it does not say "the likeness of the throne" <note>with the definite article</note> because there is a throne and there is a throne. There is a supernal throne, hidden, which is not revealed, and there is no one who can stand within it or know how to gaze at it; therefore it is written as a "hidden throne." It is not like that which is below, "the likeness as the appearance of a man." Since it says "likeness as the appearance," it would be enough to say "the likeness of a man." Rather, "the likeness of a man" is the mystery of that supernal Glory, the image of Man <note>referring to *Adam Kadmon* or the Divine Human form</note>. But this which was added, "as the appearance of a man," is to include those images of the words of wisdom and those mysteries of wisdom.

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Vayakhel (And He Assembled)**<-

Look at how we have established this: he shall surely be blessed, and it is fitting in the praise contained within it, in its holiness and its radiance, that it should rest as a blessing. Through the celestial constellation <note>Hebrew: *Mazal*, referring to the flow of divine influence</note> that assists the blessing, and in its vitality, He gave His gift to every place that required it—to rest from all sides. In a place that has nothing of its own, a place that should be from all sides and included from all sides—these matters were only handed over to the wise, to know the way of the Torah.

Come and see: how much good is there, and the strength of the balance was not in the world. What is written?
> The breath that comes from your mouth is like the best wine, as it is written: "within a heap of wheat" <note>Song of Songs 7:3</note>.
From "breath" <note>Hebrew: *Hevel*</note> we learn that every word that blesses a blessing is proven right when done with sustenance and the will of the heart. When it rises before the Most High—the place prepared for it within the supernal mysteries in holy wisdom—blessed is the portion of the person who guards the commandments of his Master and knows their praise. For you do not have a single commandment in the Torah upon which supernal mysteries, lights, and supernal radiances do not hang. And those who do not know and do not gaze upon the glory of their Master—blessed is the portion of the righteous, those who labor in the Torah; they are meritorious in this world and in the world to come.

Come and see: all those who are stiff-necked <note>literally "strong of forehead"</note> have no attachment and no portion in this world or the world to come. All those stiff-necked ones who were among Israel—when they would gaze upon the <term>Incense (Ketoret)</term> <note>The blend of eleven spices burned in the Tabernacle/Temple</note>, they would break their hearts and look into their deeds. Because this [the incense] stands against the Holy Woman <note>A reference to the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note>, and anyone who gazes upon it would feel shame for his deeds. Therefore, this [the incense] atones for those who are insolent and stiff-necked.

The smoke of the spirit is a holy medicine, for they were engraved upon its children, the Priests and Levites. Because of this, anyone who looked at the incense—just as the smoke doubled its appearance—his heart would be broken within him. Then, it would find favor and atone for them in this manner, since he established a way to melt his heart and humble himself before his Master. In this same way, regarding the incense: anyone who smelled it as it rose in that pillar from that "smoke-raiser" <note>A specific herb, *Ma'aleh Ashan*, used to make the smoke rise straight</note>, his heart would be broken with the clarity of light and with the joy of serving his Master. The <term>Evil Inclination (Yetzer Hara)</term> <note>The internal drive toward selfishness or sin</note> would be stirred by it, but it would have no power—no power at all—against the Beloved. For it is written that the purpose of the incense is surely the breaking of the Evil Inclination.

In all aspects, just as this was praised above all else, so too with the incense: you have no thing in the world that breaks the <term>Other Side (Sitra Achra)</term> <note>The realm of evil or demonic forces in Kabbalah</note> except for the incense. Come and see what is written:
> "Take the fire-pan and put fire on it from the altar and place incense... for wrath has gone out from the Lord; the plague has begun" <note>Numbers 17:11</note>.
For there is no breaking of that Other Side except through the incense. There is no matter more beloved before the Holy One, Blessed be He, than the incense. It has the power to nullify sorcery and evil things. The scent and the strength of the incense that humans make—for all that work is a strike! This is the incense.

This matter is a standing decree before the Holy One, Blessed be He: that anyone who looks at and reads the section of the Incense every day will be saved from all matters of sorcery in the world, from all evil mishaps, from evil thoughts, and from <term>Plague (Motana)</term> <note>Epidemics or sudden death</note>. He will not be harmed all that day, for the Other Side cannot rule over him, provided he focuses his intention on it. Rabbi Levi said: If human beings knew the portion of the work of the incense before the Holy One, Blessed be He, they would take every single word of it and raise it as a crown upon their heads like a crown of gold.

And whoever labors in it needs to look into the work of the incense and focus his intention on it every day. He will have a portion in this world and the world to come. Plague will be removed from him and from his surroundings, and he will be saved from all the judgments of this world, from the evil sides, from the judgment of Gehenna <note>Purgatory/Hell</note>, and from the judgment of foreign kingdoms. Regarding that incense: when the smoke rose in a pillar, the Priest would see the nourishment of the spirit rising in holiness.

The holy ones separate like white light and ascend above like a pillar. It removes the **impurity** <note>original: *zuhama*, the spiritual filth of the serpent</note> so that it does not cover everything, allowing all to be illuminated, rectified, and bound as one. What is written regarding Moses? "The Lord said to Moses: Take for yourself **spices**..." <note>original: *samim*; Exodus 30:34</note>. ## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Vayakhel**<-
<note>And he assembled</note>

It is established that in this manner, the **calf** <note>original: "egel"</note> is a bull for the horn, and it is said to be an atonement for the sin of the voice of the cloud that accompanied and caused Israel to stray. Regarding this, it is written: **"Take for yourself"** <note>Exodus 30:34</note>—for your own benefit and utility. The **incense** <note>original: "Ketoret"</note> is a bond <note>original: "ketiru"</note> of light upon light, and it causes the filth to pass away. It is for binding the [letter] *S* to *H*, to be joined, etc. The *Y* ascends and is crowned in the *H*; the *Q* to be joined, etc. . . . and the whole will ascends to the **Infinite** <note>original: "Ein Sof"</note> and becomes one single bond. One knot is made in the spirit, so that it may be a supreme bond of all through strength and radiance. The stars and constellations are illuminated and all worlds are blessed, and all is through the spirit of the incense. Therefore, it is for atonement first, to remove the filth and to be purified first, and afterwards the chains and entanglements of our exile are removed, as we have said. Happy are the people of Israel in this world and in the world to come, for they know how to arrange the **rectification** <note>original: "tikkun"</note> of above and below as required. To arrange the rectification from below to above until everything is bound together in one bond, like this supreme incense <margin>(or: knot)</margin>, as we seek to repair through the rectification of the engraved letters by which the Holy One, blessed be He, is called.

Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Eleazar his son were sitting one night and laboring in the Torah. Rabbi Eleazar said to Rabbi Shimon his father: It is written: **"The brook Kishon, that ancient brook"** <note>Judges 5:21</note>. [He continues with a difficult allegorical passage:] Your longing and your tenderness are like a grape hanging in a pouch, and the brook of your desire's smile, etc., and the changes where the spirit did not rest upon it. This is fine for the lower realm, but what can be said of the "smile" in the manner of the upper realm? Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse and said: **"As the deer pants for the water brooks..."** <note>Psalm 42:2</note>

Let us establish this verse. For every living being, there is one **Living Being** <note>original: "Chayah," a high-level angelic or divine force</note> in the world, and this Living Being rules with authority over a thousand keys every day. This Living Being cries out and desires constantly for the water brooks. Here, to look at the Living Being: first it is written "as a deer" <note>masculine form</note> and not "as a hind" <note>feminine form</note>, but then it says "she pants" <note>feminine verb</note> and not "he pants." This is because every spirit is male and female as one, so as not to be separated. They are one, and one does not need to ascend without the other, but both together. And this strength "pants for the water brooks." The Living Being becomes pregnant from the male and stands over her, for she stands upon judgment and gives birth. And the Holy One, blessed be He, prepares for her one great supreme **snake** <note>original: "chivya"</note> who comes and bites at that place, and she gives birth. This is the secret of your longing and your labor, because the Living Being from below [labors] every day like a cloud over the works of the world. "Like a grape hanging in a pouch"—like a grape that does not reveal the secrets seen in the affairs of the world. "The brook of your desire's smile"—all are upon the water brooks. And it will be revealed thus: the spirit of the Living Being rules over it. And why all this? Because the wine is the **moon** <note>original: "sihara"</note>, as we have learned, and the grape receives the light and its small dominion, and they have no secret of their own, for everything is given to it. "Like a grape hanging in a pouch," as we have established. And if you say, why is this snake necessary? Rather, this opens the way for the spirit to descend below so they are not bound, just as it is written: **"Sin crouches at the door"** <note>Genesis 4:7</note>. From the canopy of that door which is below to give birth, to bring forth likenesses to the world, the holy Living Being is at that door and has no permission [to enter] in those likenesses. And were it not for this snake that bites and surrounds that door, it would not be opened to be purified. And the whole Living Being is a supreme spirit, like a grape hanging in a pouch. This spirit of wisdom is deep.

<meta>This page continues the discourse on Parashat Pekudei, specifically focusing on the mystical parallels between the creation of the universe and the construction of the Tabernacle. ## Main Text (Zohar)

131 <note>original: קל"א</note> According to the mouth of the wise, it has been said: the children of the world are silenced, for the visionaries have revealed the preparation of the betrothal that the Perfect One <note>God</note> designated for us. They grasp His feet, like the sapphire-work of His feet, wheels that turn constantly, ascending and descending. Woe to those whose feet resemble the wheels within the depths of the hidden, woe to the wicked of the world! Woe to those who stumble and shall not rise, and shall not shine with the Light that is hidden for the righteous in the World to Come.

The righteous are worthy in the World to Come, for many hidden lights are stored for them; many delights are concealed for them in that hidden world, as it is written: <note>Psalms 31:20</note> **How great is Your goodness, which You have hidden for those who fear You.** "How great is Your goodness"—this refers to Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>, that same Loving-kindness <note>Chesed</note> which is hidden for the righteous in the World to Come. He gave Loving-kindness to those <note>original: לאינון</note> who saw "the light, that it was good." And it is written: <note>Psalms 97:11</note> **Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart.** And regarding this: "How great is Your goodness." It is written here, "How great is Your goodness," and it is written there: <note>Genesis 1:4</note> **And God saw the light, that it was good.** "Which You have hidden"—because the Holy One, Blessed be He, looked to the end of the light and saw those wicked ones who were destined to sin in the world, and because of this, He hid the light to be merited by the righteous in the World to Come, as has been stated. "You have wrought" <note>from Psalms 31:20</note>—at first it went forth, and afterward "You have wrought." Rather, it went forth as we said: "You have wrought," because with that light which He hid within it, the Holy One, Blessed be He, performed the craftsmanship of the world. From where do we know this? As it is written: <note>Genesis 2:4</note> **These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created.** And that light of the beginning, the Holy One, Blessed be He, hid it, and with it He performed the craftsmanship of the world, as it is written: "You have wrought for those who take refuge in You"—for those who placed their hope in the Holy One, Blessed be He. "In the sight of the sons of men"—for all the craftsmanship that was done with this light exists for the sake of that <note>humanity</note> in the world. And their existence remains, even though that light is hidden within it, the people of this world exist. "You have wrought"—the craftsmanship of this world, for through it everything was made.

The craftsmanship of this world is like the craftsmanship of the Tabernacle <note>Mishkan</note>, for that craftsmanship was in the likeness of the world, as we have established. It is written here: **These are the accounts of the Tabernacle**, and it is written there: **These are the generations of the heavens and the earth.** Because all those "generations" that the heavens and the earth produced and brought forth were all made and emerged through the power of that hidden light. "The accounts of the Tabernacle"—they emerged through that same power. From where do we know this? As it is written: <note>Exodus 38:22</note> **And Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah**—this is the power of that light from the side of the Right <note>the attribute of Chesed/Kindness</note>. And we find Oholiab—this is the power from the side of the Left <note>the attribute of Gevurah/Strength</note>. And we find it from the side of the Right, and we find it for strength, and it was made; and from the side that was between them, He established the laws.

Rabbi Eleazar opened and said: <note>Isaiah 16:5</note> **And a throne shall be established in loving-kindness, and He shall sit upon it in truth.** "And a throne shall be established in loving-kindness"—this we have established: when the observation ascends in the will of joy from the depth of all hidden things, which is neither known nor grasped, that joy reaches and is gathered into the Thought <note>the Sephirah of Binah/Understanding</note>. Then the Supernal Crown <note>Keter</note> enters until they are built together as one Supernal Palace, hidden above. And from there, all the lights of the Right are created and drawn forth, which were nullified at first, and afterward all of them were nullified and the side of the Right extended to prepare the Throne below. For the Holy One, Blessed be He, prepared that Throne with Loving-kindness <note>Chesed</note>, "and He shall sit upon it in truth"—for that is the primary preparation of all, and He does not sit upon that Throne except with this seal of Truth. All of these belong to David, for that is the place of the Throne: **A judge who seeks justice and is swift in righteousness.** "A judge"—from the side of the Arm <note>Gevurah</note>; "and seeks justice"—from the side of Mercy <note>Tiferet</note>; "and is swift in righteousness"—so that the Throne shall be for judgment, for that judgment is below. Come and see: in this manner we find it was not prepared except through this side, in the manner of Loving-kindness <note>Chesed</note> as we said above. And because of this, the "generations" were prepared and all were prepared below.

### **These** are the accounts of the Tabernacle, the Tabernacle of the Testimony, as they were counted by the commandment of Moses. Rabbi Shimon opened: <note>Genesis 1:1</note> **In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.** This verse we have established...

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the Tabernacle's construction, focusing on how the physical structure mirrors the divine architecture of the upper worlds.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

They established it and saw it through **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note> on all sides. For every human being, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kadosh Baruch Hu"</note> acts in a manner corresponding to the Above, so that this world exists as a reflection of the Upper World. All those colors and forms from Above were established below to cause the worlds to cling together and be bound as one. When the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> desired to create the world, He gazed into the Torah and created it; He looked upon the Holy Soul, which is the sum of the Torah and the sustenance of the world. On three sides the world is sustained, and they are: <term>Wisdom</term>, <term>Understanding</term>, and <term>Knowledge</term> <note>The Sefirot: Chokhmah, Tevunah/Binah, and Da'at</note>. As it is said and written:
> **The Lord by wisdom founded the earth; by understanding He established the heavens; by His knowledge the depths were broken up.** <note>Proverbs 3:19-20</note>

Behold, these are the foundations of the world. And by these same three, the Tabernacle was built, as it is written:
> **And I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge.** <note>Exodus 31:3</note>

All three are hinted at in the work of Creation, as it is said: "In Wisdom" refers to "In the beginning God created" <note>Genesis 1:1</note>. "By understanding He established the heavens" refers to "the heavens." "By His knowledge" refers to "and the earth." All of these are written regarding the work of the Tabernacle. Because of this, it is written: **These are the accounts of the Tabernacle** <note>Exodus 38:21</note>—this is the spirit of Wisdom. **The Tabernacle of Testimony**—this is the spirit of Understanding. **As they were rendered at the commandment of Moses**—this is the spirit of Knowledge. Each one corresponds to the other. For everything the Holy One, Blessed be He, created in this world, He created its likeness Above. Everything was inscribed in the work of the Tabernacle.

Come and see: at the moment the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> told Moses to make the Tabernacle, Moses stood in wonder, for he did not know what to do until the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> showed him the likeness, as it is written:
> **And see that thou make them after their pattern, which hath been shown thee in the mount.** <note>Exodus 25:40</note>

What is meant by **after their pattern**? Rather, we learn that the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> showed Moses the <term>spiritual form</term> <note>original: "dyukna"</note> of every single thing, according to the form that exists Above. Each part was made as a spiritual form of the Above, according to the vision seen Above. And each one made his own form according to the vision seen below, until they were all completed. 

Moses then spoke further regarding this. It should have said "which Moses accounted." However, we learn this to exclude the idea that it was not like that which he saw in the hidden realm. All those colors and forms made below were exactly like the vision seen in the hidden realm of all those forms. This is the meaning of "which were rendered at the commandment of Moses." It is the place of the Spirit that ascends, unlike that which he saw in the hidden realm of all those forms; he saw them from the side of every single word in its proper arrangement, just as we see a garment, etc., a vision of the Above. When Moses looked at them, they were established before him. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: "Moses, you stand below and see in your days." Then Moses was settled in all the work.

When all the work was done, Moses needed to count everything so that people would not say, "The Merciful One has spread out silver and gold and he has taken it for himself." Because of this, he needed to give an accounting before Israel, as it is written:
> **Then ye shall be guiltless before the Lord, and before Israel.** <note>Numbers 32:22</note>

And because of this, it is written: **These are the accounts of the Tabernacle, the Tabernacle of Testimony**, which contains a holy secret. He showed them the accounting of all the gold and silver, as it is written:
> **And the silver of them that were numbered of the congregation was a hundred talents, etc.** <note>Exodus 38:25</note>
> **All the gold that was used for the work, etc.** <note>Exodus 38:24</note>

For the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> was pleased with those craftsmen and masters of <term>faithfulness</term> <note>original: "meimanuta"</note> who stood before all. **These are the accounts of the Tabernacle.** Come and see: at the time the work of the Tabernacle was done, the <term>Other Side</term> <note>the forces of evil</note> looked on and grew weak; it was unable to incite or find any fault in the faithfulness of the craftsmen. Eventually, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> subdued it before Moses, and it saw the accounting of faithfulness against its will. Their faithfulness rose above all. And this spirit is what is written: **These are the accounts of the Tabernacle**, as we have established. "These" refers to the whole, yet you find it written "which were rendered at the commandment of Moses," for there they were numbered and appointed until the accounting of the accounting was made before Moses and all of Israel.

<summary>This page explains that the Tabernacle was built using the same divine attributes (Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge) used to create the world, and that Moses provided a public accounting of materials to demonstrate the absolute integrity of the work against the "Other Side."</summary>
