<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Tabernacle (Mishkan) construction, focusing on the symbolic significance of colors and the unique role of Moses. It transitions from the general laws of the Tabernacle to the specific spiritual mechanics of its erection.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Accountings (Pekudei)**<-

Come and see: in all the works that were found, the color of **blue** <note>original: "Techelet"</note> was present, because blue is the color that is crowned by the spirit of all colors. As it is written:
> And they made the garments of ministry to serve in the holy place, the blue, and purple, and scarlet <note>Exodus 39:1</note>
In the spirit of that which is written: "And they made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, and wrote upon it a writing, like the engravings of a signet: HOLY TO THE LORD." <note>Exodus 39:30</note>

---

## Addition (Tosefta)

In the higher secrets of the "Accountings" <note>Pekudei</note>, these appointments rise and are hidden, and these stand in their positions: the holy **wheels** <note>original: "galgalin," referring to celestial spheres or angelic ranks</note> stand here and there from the dust of the end. These wheels are called the "Worlds of the Chariot" <note>The *Merkavah*, the divine throne-chariot</note> which are led by the beauty of the spark within them; one wheel exists inside them. This wheel is of the sun <note>Heres</note> and yet not of the sun; it stands as a throne, passing through worlds in their beauty, rising and descending within them. Beneath that wheel stands a **column** <note>original: "amuda"</note> like a support for all that is rolled within it. These upright ones rise and are hidden; that column stands over them, appearing and not appearing, like a cloak from above to below, surrounding the upper ones and crowning the wheels of the chariot of that column. The wheel is supported by the surrounding veils of praise in twelve thousand worlds. They are of the sun, yet found not to be of the sun; the craftsman supports it, standing upon the thrones that pass through the worlds. In it stands the weight of the balance that calls to be hidden, from the wheel to the mass. And a thousand pressures are known to the "Master of the Eyes" in his measurements; he knows and gazes with the **wisdom** <note>original: "chokhmata"</note> of the Master, and he knows those upper leaves of the keys of the levels that stand there, which are hidden until the Holy One is found. And all of these are in this world, and their merit shall be for you in the World to Come. Concerning them it is written:
> Blessed is the man whose strength is in Thee; in whose heart are the highways <note>Psalms 84:6</note>
They say:
> Happy is the man whom Thou choosest, and causest to approach, that he may dwell in Thy courts <note>Psalms 65:5</note>
As it is written: "We shall be satisfied with the goodness of Thy house, Thy holy temple."

---

## Main Text (Continuation)

In the spirit that is found, there stand upper secrets in the spirit of the High Holy Name. And because this is the spirit that is found—a spirit like the upper likeness—it is a spirit that shows itself, as it is written: "Behold, another spirit," which judges all others. And to sustain all others, this is the Holy Spirit of the Name that passes through **ADNY** <note>original: "Dalet Nun Yud," the Name Adonai, associated with the Shekhinah/Kingdom</note>. And this is in the likeness of the spirit of the High Holy Name **YHVH** <note>original: "Yud Vav," referring to the Tetragrammaton</note>. They placed these in the likeness of the "Oak": the *Aleph* is the life, the *Yud* is the spirit. This is in the likeness of that, and the Sages established that the *Dalet* is the spirit of the *Heh*, and this is in the likeness of that, and all is one likeness and one secret. The *Nun* is the life of the spirit of the *Dalet* and the *Vav*; these are the Male and this is the Female, and in all this, one is included in the other. The Sages established this as 7 and 6, because they are one collective. The *Heh* is the spirit of the *Dalet* and *Yud*, because the sum of this is **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note> and the form called the "Wisdom of Solomon." They were included and placed in the flames, and all are one spirit, included one in the other, and all are one. All is one spirit that burns in the holy depths. Therefore, it is found below as a kneeling form; all stands like the spirit found above. And that one is found standing in the spirit of another that is found above all, and each is included in the other to become one. Concerning this it is written:
> And the Tabernacle shall be one <note>Exodus 36:13</note>
It is also written:
> Amalek was the first of the nations; but his latter end shall be that he perish for ever <note>Numbers 24:20</note>
Come and see: on the day the Tabernacle was established, Moses set it up, as it is said:
> And Moses reared up the Tabernacle <note>Exodus 40:18</note>
For it could not be stood up until he set it up for the **Matron** <note>original: "Matronita," the Divine Presence/Shekhinah</note>, for no other man has permission to set her up except for her husband <note>Moses is mystically considered the "husband" of the Shekhinah</note>. So too, all those craftsmen came to show their work, but it could not be stood up by their hands until Moses came and established it, because he is the **Master of the House** <note>original: "Mare d'Beita"</note>. Once Moses established the Tabernacle below, another Tabernacle was established above. As the Sages established: it is written "was reared up" <note>passive voice</note> and it does not specify by whose hand, but rather it was established by the spirit of the upper world, which is hidden and concealed, by the hand of the spirit of Moses, because he was found to be exactly so. What is written above? "And all the wise men, that wrought all the work of the sanctuary, came..."

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the construction of the Tabernacle (Mishkan) from the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei. It explores the metaphysical impact of the Tabernacle's completion on the forces of death and the "Other Side."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> Pekudei <note>The name of the Torah portion, meaning "Accounts"</note> <-

They spread out here before, and so on. These are the "lesser sages" of the right and the left and all the service of their sides. They are meritorious above in the days of the King, and they constructed the Tabernacle <note>original: *matkana* / *mishkan*</note> above. They did not establish it in this manner in the stream <note>likely referring to the flow of emanation</note>, neither for him on the side of the right nor on the side of the left in the stream—not from Judah and not from Dan. Afterwards, with all the strength of every heart, "all the wise men who performed [the work] finished" <note>Exodus 36:4</note>, as we have established, and everything was modeled after the pattern above. On that day when that Tabernacle was established, death was abolished from the world. It was abolished—do not say merely that it departed from the world, but rather that it could no longer rule. As we have established, the "evil leaven" <note>the inclination toward evil</note> will not be fully abolished from the world until the King Messiah comes and the Holy One, blessed be He, is alone in His works, and then:
> **He will swallow up death forever** (Isaiah 25:8) 
When the Tabernacle was established by the hand of Moses, then the power of the Evil Inclination <term>Yetzer Hara: the innate human impulse toward self-gratification or evil</term> was separated and subdued, and it was unable to rule at that hour. The "strong poison" <note>original: *sama takif*</note>, the anger that reaches from the strength of the evil life, was separated and could not rule over the world, nor could it connect with it as it had before. Rabbi Judah said: When Israel made the Golden Calf, what is written? 
> **And Moses took the tent and pitched it outside the camp** (Exodus 33:7) 
What is the reason? Because he saw the Evil Inclination prowling among them. He said: The side of holiness shall not dwell with the side of impurity <term>Sitra Achra: the "Other Side" or the realm of evil/impurity</term>. Rabbi Eleazar said: Whenever the side of holiness rules, the side of impurity cannot rule and is subdued before it. And regarding this, they established: Whenever Jerusalem is full, the "other kingdom" <note>Rome or the forces of exile</note> is destroyed. He opened and said: 
> **And she said to the servant, "Who is this man walking in the field toward us?" and the servant said...** (Genesis 24:65) 
What is written above this? 
> **And Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and she saw Isaac, and she fell from the camel** (Genesis 24:64) 
This verse needs to be written in its context, for she saw the beauty of Isaac. Why then did she ride upon a camel? Rather, it is a mystery of the spirit of the Serpent <note>original: *chiva*</note>. Come and see: "And she saw Isaac"—through the power of knowledge she saw Isaac. But she saw Isaac because at that moment she perceived what she had not known before: that he represented Harsh Judgment <term>Din Kashia: the divine attribute of strict justice/judgment</term>. And because the end of that harsh anger is the "Camel" <note>original: *gemal*</note> below—which is the Serpent of Death—she therefore rode upon it. She lowered herself because she saw the Camel ascending; for when she looked at Isaac, that Camel was strengthened, and because of this, she slipped herself away from it and did not remain there. Come and see: this Camel is the spirit of which it is written, "and his recompense <note>original: *gemulo*, a play on *gamal* (camel)</note> shall be paid to him." This is the retribution of the wicked, as it is written: 
> **Woe to the wicked! It shall be ill with him, for the reward <note>recompense/gemul</note> of his hands shall be done to him** (Isaiah 3:11) 
And this Serpent-Camel stands ready to consume all and to rest upon all. It is always ready to confront the face of Moses. Because of this, those who see death in a dream see a camel—I say to them, it is a death that has been decreed and then diverted from him. Come and see: this side of impurity is called thus because it appears as death to the whole world. It is the one that seduced Adam and his wife. The one who rides upon it is Samael <note>the primary archangel of evil in Jewish mysticism</note>, and they are the woman who misleads the world and brings death to all. Because of this, he comes and rises above all. Adam saw him as a prophet, and once he saw him, he seduced him; then he was drawn after them until he was seduced. Regarding this, Solomon said: 
> **And do not come near the door of her house** (Proverbs 5:8) 
For anyone who approaches her house, she then comes out and attaches herself and he is drawn after her. Therefore, when Rebekah saw that she was to be attached to the side of Harsh Judgment—since she saw Isaac in the spirit of Harsh Judgment—and because from the side of impurity there emerges another powerful force from the "filth of gold" <note>the dross of the attribute of Judgment</note>, when she saw this, immediately "she fell from the camel," because they were separated from the judgment of that filth. And it is written: 
> **The voice of the Lord rendering recompense <note>gemul</note> to His enemies** (Isaiah 66:6) 
From that filth. Come and see...

<summary>This page interprets the construction of the Tabernacle as a cosmic event that subdued the Evil Inclination and death. It also provides a mystical reading of Rebekah falling from her camel, identifying the camel with the Serpent and the demonic forces of Samael that are drawn to the attribute of Harsh Judgment.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the spiritual mechanics of the Golden Calf incident. It explores the linguistic and metaphysical roots of the word "Eleh" (These) as a designation for the forces of impurity, contrasting it with the holiness of "Zot" (This).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Pekudei**<-

When Israel performed that deed <note>the making of the Golden Calf</note> and caused that altar to be built, see the reason why it was a **calf** and not another cow. And if you say they were small inside, it is not so. Rather, they said, "Rise up, make for us gods who shall go before us," and Aaron’s will was to delay them. But certainly, the work had to be done as was fitting. For from the side of gold emerges the <term>female</term> <note>original: nukvita; referring here to the feminine aspect of the "Other Side"</note> for all clarification. And from there, all those sides of the **spleen** <note>original: tahala; in Kabbalistic anatomy, the spleen is the seat of melancholy and the "Other Side"</note> spread out, which are the dross of that refuse of gold, and they divide into many sides. And all those who have a vision of the time when the hidden things of gold stand together, when the spleen is in its strength—because the strength of the spleen sees gold and it is sweet to it in its desire. And that altar, in that strength of the spleen, saw its judgment like a **calf**, and it is called "the destruction that wastes at noonday" <note>Psalms 91:6</note>. And this emerges from within the calf, the dross of the spleen. And all these curses come from that red side, the <term>spirit of impurity</term> <note>original: ruach mesava</note>, for all those who separate from the spirit of impurity spread through the world. And if this spirit of the living king possesses it, there is a matter that rides upon it, and they are male and female, and they are called **"These"** <note>original: Eleh</note>, for they are present in the world in all those sides of theirs.

But the Holy Spirit is called **"This"** <note>original: Zot</note>, which is the male spirit of the drop of holiness that is always found with it, male and female, as in "This is the Lord" and "This is our God." But these others are called **"These"** <note>original: Eleh</note>, and regarding this it is written: >These are your gods, O Israel< <note>Exodus 32:4</note>. And because of this it is written: >Even these may forget< <note>Isaiah 49:15</note>. And therefore the spirit of sin is not found. And it is written: >For these things I weep< <note>Lamentations 1:16</note>, for that altar caused them to weep many weepings. <term>Another explanation</term>: "For these things I weep"—for what reason? Because permission was given to this place to rule over Israel and to destroy the Holy Temple. And because permission was given to them to rule, it is written: "For these things I weep." The spirit of the matter is "for these" <note>Eleh</note>, for this is the side of impurity to which permission was given to rule. "I weep"—this is the Holy Spirit that is called "I."

And if you say, "But it is written: 'These are the words of the covenant,'" it is so, and it pushes back, for all those do not exist except from within "These" <note>Eleh</note> where all colors are found, as we have established that it is "cursed," as it is written: >Cursed are you above all cattle< <note>Genesis 3:14</note>. And because of this, he sanctified and said "These" <note>Eleh</note> which stands for whoever transgresses the words of the covenant. This is the one who... <unclear>textual corruption</unclear> ...because the commandment of the Torah is to be purified when one sins and not to stray to this path, and to be crowned from there and separated from them.

And if you say, "These are the generations of Noah, Noah," it is certainly so, for there emerged from him that which is like a branch, and it says "Cursed be Canaan," and this spirit is called "These" <note>Eleh</note>. And because of this, all these are the dross of the refuse of gold. And Aaron brought the gold near, which is the <term>Other Side</term> <note>original: Sitra Achra</note>, the judgments included in the strength of gold, and they are all one. And this side is gold and sin. And the spirit of impurity is always found, as mentioned, to crown the side at that time to be strengthened by it. And what happened to Israel? Since they sinned and raised the height of the mountain like a calf, they caused death for all. For when they stood at Mount Sinai, it removed from them as before <note>the primordial state</note>, forgiving them and strengthening them, but [the sin] brought death upon them and upon the whole world and for their generations after them. <term>This is what is written</term>: >I said, "You are angels..." but indeed like men you shall die< <note>Psalms 82:6-7</note>. And because of this, they lacked the crown to be purified by the spirit of higher faith during those seven holy days, and to be purified from the calf.

And come and see: Aaron wanted all of them to be purified, for he is life—no, this is not so, the calf emerged. Why? Because it returned and rested, and the life-strength of <term>Samael</term> <note>the archangel of the Other Side</note> and the gold of Samael, the spirit of impurity, descended and was included there. And Israel joined together and the life-force was dragged down until it was purified. Why was it dragged down? Because the calf emerged, which is from the side of the spleen, which is the dwelling and the strike of the calf and the life of the spleen, as it was said, as it is written: "And they turned..."

<summary>This passage provides a Kabbalistic interpretation of the Golden Calf, linking the Hebrew word "Eleh" (These) to the forces of impurity and the "Other Side." It explains that the sin of the calf reintroduced mortality to Israel, which had been briefly suspended at Mount Sinai.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Zohar’s mystical exposition on the Tabernacle and the nature of sin, specifically focusing on the Golden Calf incident from Parashat Pekudei. It links the physical act of the calf-making to the cosmic "Left Side" and the ongoing struggle against the "Impure Spirit."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

"And the face of an ox was on the left side of the four of them" <note>Ezekiel 1:10; the ox represents the attribute of Judgment/Gevurah on the Divine Chariot</note>. They investigated the vision and the appearance of the blue <note>techelet</note>, a cup of impurity that bends by its hands. 
And because of this, a calf was given to him, just as the vision describes. For when this spirit of defilement spreads below, 
it rules over the world as it did before. For at the time when the kingdom of the "crushing one" <note>the Sitra Achra/Other Side</note> rules because they sinned against it, that Evil Serpent 
returns as in the beginning. When Israel was purified, they sought to gaze [at the Divine], but they needed to draw near only a little, for if they had diminished 
the portion of that Evil Inclination, that spirit of defilement would not have spread as we said. It is written: 
> They exchanged their glory for the image of an ox that eats grass. <note>Psalms 106:20</note>

What is the "image of an ox"? For the calf is a mountain-crusher of the fool <note>original: "sachla"</note> 
to Aaron; and the brain of the blue <note>techelet</note> of the fool was in it, and it grew strong through it and bent by its hands. Come and see: 
**"They exchanged their glory"**—this refers to the Shekhinah <note>the Divine Presence</note> who walked before them, and they exchanged Her for a place of defilement and traded Her for another. And because of 
this, that filth <note>zuhama</note> was not removed from the world until that time when the Holy One, blessed be He, shall remove it from the world, 
as it is said: 
> And I will remove the spirit of impurity from the land. <note>Zechariah 13:2</note>

And we have established this. It is written: 
> And they made a molten calf. <note>Exodus 32:4</note>

And it is written: 
> I cast it into the fire, and this calf came out. <note>Exodus 32:24</note>

This implies that he [Aaron] did not "make" it. If so, why does it say **"And they made"**? 
Certainly, as we have established, when they investigated the vessel, the spirit of defilement was strengthened to be included here 
among all the rectifications that a wise man needs to observe. Come and see the "beast of the windows" <note>a reference to sorcery</note> 
who performs sorceries and trembling is in his hands. And the "beast of the windows" who makes them in that exact manner, yet does not consume 
with his hands, for in these deeds the weight that is needed is not recognized. Come and see from Balaam, who strengthened his vision 
through his sorcerous visions to see with his hands, as it is written: 
> The speech of the man whose eye is open <note>Numbers 24:3; the Zohar reads this as "closed eye"</note>.

"Closed eye" <note>original: "stum ha-ayin"</note> 
or "open eye"—it is all one. For one eye was always closed, and the life of his eyes was not in the choice of the vessel, 
but was in it like his eyes. It is written that there was no pity in him... they saw with his eyes that he would not be fit. For every 
Holy Spirit, they look directly. What is written? 
> For any man who has a blemish shall not approach. <note>Leviticus 21:18</note>

Whether an ox 
or a lame one, all of them were prepared for the impure spirit to take its place in the surroundings. Darkness is remembered, 
a narrowness close to all, as it is written: "like a moth, a predator, and a scorpion," etc., for there the vision of his kingdom 
is hidden, for here is the proper sufficiency. Other wise men seek to be strengthened in those days and to be included in it, 
then the places are healed as they should be, and they go out and are completed. And from all of them, the spirit of defilement was present, as it is written: 
> Oh, this people has sinned a great sin. <note>Exodus 32:31</note>

This refers to the spirit of defilement as before, as we have said in several 
places. And at the time when Aaron wanted to look toward the calf from that side to perform 
judgment upon it as before, he made it for the surroundings. And now, in doing so, he intended to subdue it, for when 
the spirit is made on this side, all those who are blinded by its side are subdued. Come and see, regarding the "crushing" 
of that side to be smitten, it is written: **"You shall not eat of it raw..."** <note>Exodus 12:9</note> so that its scent should rise 
when they sinned... to recognize it and subdue it, and then all those who sinned from its side are not completed. 
In this same manner: **"A red heifer, whole..."** <note>Numbers 19:2</note> in order to subdue all those sides of defilement so they shall not rule. 
Rabbi Zakkai said to him: "Is the heifer holy? For it is written 'living' and 'living'!" He said to him: "It is so, and we have established 
that it corresponds to the four kingdoms." The heifer is entirely like: 
> For like a wayward heifer, Israel has gone astray. <note>Hosea 4:16</note>

**"Red"**—this is 
the Kingdom of Babylon, of whom it is written: 
> You are the head of gold. <note>Daniel 2:38; gold is associated with the red/fire of Gevurah</note>

**"Whole"** <note>temimah</note>—this is the Kingdom of Media. **"In which there is 
no blemish"**—this is the Kingdom of Greece, for they are close to the paths of faith. **"Upon which no yoke has come"**—this is 
the Kingdom of Edom <note>Rome/Western Christendom</note>, for no yoke [of Heaven] has ascended upon it. And the spirit of this matter, even though many words were given to be expounded 
in the assemblies, they are all one regarding the hidden thing, as it is written: 
> Who can produce a clean thing from an unclean? Is it not the One? <note>Job 14:4</note>

Who can produce a clean thing 
from an unclean?

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of Parashat Pekudei, specifically focusing on the paradox of the Red Heifer—how a ritual that purifies the impure simultaneously renders the pure handlers impure. It transitions into the cosmic necessity of "appeasing" the Accuser during high holy days.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> Pekudei <-

This spirit of impurity is so great that it cannot become pure until it emerges from that first side which is impure. But now that judgment has been executed upon it, and it has been burned—and it must be burned with the intensity of a fire that blazes until it becomes ash—now it is "pure from the impure," a purity that emerges from impurity. And because of this, all those who occupy themselves with the ritual become impure, for such is the way of it. Once it has become ash, until it is gathered and removed from there, it imparts impurity to them all <note>The text discusses how those involved in the Red Heifer ritual become impure (Num 19)</note> all of them... and the vessel is praised... and impure. Ash is the end of all, and the matter is hidden, for "they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet." And once water is placed upon that ash, then it is "pure from the impure" and the spirit of impurity is broken, as it is written: *Water of purification* <note>original: "Mei Chatat"</note>, for *sin crouches at the door.* And because of this "door of sin," it was written first: *and the heifer shall be a sin offering outside the camp.* Therefore, it is a "sin offering" <note>term: Chatat - usually a sacrifice for unintentional sins, but here applied to the Red Heifer ritual</note> and not for the High Priest, and it is "pure from the impure"—originally impure, but now pure. And every side of the spirit of impurity, once it is impure, does not flee and does not dwell in the ritual bath <note>term: Mikvah - a ritual immersion pool</note>, as it is written *Water of purification*—certainly water that finishes the impurity. In all this, the Holy Spirit rules and the spirit of impurity is subdued so that it does not rule at all; and this is the judgment of the spirit of impurity... because of the spirit of impurity, as it is written: *and her mouth is a smooth trap.* Rabbi Abba opened and struck the ground. Rabbi Shimon said: Even though all these matters are as we have said, the Holy One, Blessed Be He, gave it <note>the impure side</note> dominion, and the spirit of impurity must be subdued on all sides.

Come and see a single mystery <note>original: "raza"</note>, and it is not given for revelation except to those high holy ones. Come and see: to this place which is the spirit of impurity, the Holy One, Blessed Be He, gave dominion to rule in the world in several ways, and it is able to cause damage. But it has no permission to touch the Holy One, Blessed Be He, as it is written: *to be guarded from it,* so that it does not draw near to our holy cloud. And because of this, there is one spirit that we must give a small place to, similar to our own holiness, so that no Accuser <note>term: Mekatreg - the spiritual prosecutor or Satan who points out human failings</note> shall be found within our holiness. For from the midst of holiness its dominion emerges, and we need a spirit of preparation to subdue a single hair of the cloud that goes outside and is seen. For the thread of this hair does not impart impurity except... it joins and takes the hair and becomes like a small goat... at the very least it does not impart impurity. And this "hair" <note>a metaphor for the thin attachment of the "Other Side" to the realm of holiness</note> we must bring into our high holiness and establish a place for it there, so that it does not accuse us within the holiness. When it goes out from that hair to the outside, it is seen that when it sees that throne of high holiness and its portion is associated there, then it will not accuse and will not be able to destroy above or below. For a place was given to it. But if that portion is not given a place in this holiness, it is able to destroy below, and the Accuser ascends above and says: "So-and-so, who is sanctifying himself below, did such-and-such on such-and-such a day," and these are his faults—until judgment is handed over against that man and he is punished by its hand. And so, "pure from purity."

And so Israel used to do, for they knew this mystery: every sin... in high holiness on the Day of Atonement <note>Yom Kippur</note>, they would immediately look to take a portion for this place and give it a portion of shame <note>referring to the Scapegoat sent to Azazel</note> so that no Accuser would be found against them, and it would not come to mention their sins—for there are many destroyers and many sides that are ready to bring a word from it to the world when it comes to accuse. Blessed is the portion of one who can be saved so that his sins are not mentioned above and they do not hand him over to evil. Regarding this, the eyes of Rabbi Elazar were worthy, for he said: "Blessed, blessed... and the luck of the fin is your crown and deposited in your kill," for the secrets of the Torah were given to the righteous, as it is written: *The secret of the Lord is with them that fear Him* <note>Psalms 25:14</note>. Come and see: on the day of Rosh Hashanah, the world is judged, and the Holy Judgment—the Holy One, Blessed Be He—sits and judges the whole world. And he, the Other Side <note>Sitra Achra</note>, stands on this side, and all those who are not purified... to accuse them and to confuse them before Him. And at the time that Israel...

<summary>This page explains the mystical mechanics of the Red Heifer, describing it as a process of extracting purity from impurity. It further details the necessity of "giving a portion" to the Accuser (Satan) during holy times like Yom Kippur and Rosh Hashanah to prevent him from testifying against the people in the Heavenly Court.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Tabernacle's construction, focusing on the spiritual mechanics of how the earthly structure reflects the heavenly Chariot. It transitions from discussing the protection of Israel from the "Old and Foolish King" (the Sitra Achra) to the specific mystery of bringing the Tabernacle to Moses.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

When Israel awakens mercies through the sound of the Shofar, then [the Accuser] becomes entirely confused, for he does not know and cannot look upon the repairs that are being established. Until the crown, all those who are not arranged in the proper order are subject to death, which surely goes out against them from the King and they are delivered to him. Once they are delivered to him, he does not arrange his decrees until judgment is executed. Therefore, all of Israel must be careful from this point on. When a person invites—and all the more so <note>original: וכ"ס - וכל שכן</note> since there is a herald above—we must be careful and give to him every single day. One must give a small portion <note>original: קל טעיר; likely referring to the "scapegoat" or the portion given to the "Other Side" to prevent interference</note> so that he does not prosecute first (some say: so he does not bring shame) and takes his portion as is fitting for him. Then the holy food may be eaten in holiness for the future as is appropriate.

And because he is fed every single day, he is called "Burning" <note>original: בער; a play on the word for a brutish person or one who consumes</note>. Regarding this, we have established that this donkey <note>original: חמרא; a reference to the materialistic or demonic forces</note> who is always present in his camp and does not leave it is called the "Old and Foolish King." Because of this, the holy Israel, who are one nation in holy Unity <term>Yichud: the mystical act of unifying the Divine names and attributes through prayer and ritual</term>, the Holy One, blessed be He, gives them counsel to be saved from him. They are meritorious in this world and in the world to come, as it is written:
> And your people shall all be righteous; they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, that I may be glorified. <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>
---
->**And they brought** the Tabernacle to Moses, etc.<- <note>Exodus 39:33</note>
It is written: "And above the firmament..." This is the firmament that stands over them, the four Living Creatures <term>Chayot: the four-faced angelic beings described in Ezekiel's vision of the Divine Chariot</term>. When they ascend, they build a single atmosphere that strikes them, so they do not lift their heads to look upward, because that humming spirit strikes them all. By that spirit, they all ascend, as it is written:
> And when the Living Creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up beside them. <note>Ezekiel 1:21</note>
And it is written: "For the spirit of the Living Creature was in the wheels." You might see them ascending, but when that atmosphere strikes them, it raises these four "likenesses of the Living Creature," and they do not ascend higher until they reach the "Higher Moses" <note>In the Zohar, Moses often represents the sephirah of Tiferet or the channel through which Divine flow reaches the world</note>. This is the spirit of which it is written, "the virgins her companions follow her," which proves it to you. Because of the four, they are called thus. Rather, this radiance is the Throne for the worlds, and they raise it from below to above to be established as is fitting before Moses. This spirit is the Unity, as it is written: "And you shall ascend, and you shall ascend from the earth." When it becomes silent above and goes and raises them, then it is written: "And they brought the Tabernacle to Moses." "And they brought the Tabernacle"—this is proven to you. And it is written: "And they saw the structure" <note>The text here glosses the verse: "And Moses saw all the work"</note> to Moses, like the likeness of the appearance of a man upon it from above. This is the spirit of Moses, and from here he is called "Man" <term>Adam</term>, as it is written:
> My spirit shall not judge man <note>Adam</note> forever. <note>Genesis 6:3</note>
This refers to Moses. Because of this, upon this Throne stands the image of a Man, and that is Moses. "And they brought the Tabernacle"—these are the four Living Creatures when they ascend as we have said. "And they brought the Tabernacle"—all the ends of the body, all of which are in holy repair. Rabbi Abba said: They all rejoice as one to cleave together, male and female as one.

"And they brought the Tabernacle"—to lead them all to the wedding canopy <term>Chuppah</term> as at first. They must raise her <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence, symbolized by the Tabernacle</note> and bring her to him, and afterward he will always come to her. We have established that "And they brought the Tabernacle" is the secret of all those who tie the knot of Unity and give the "arm of faith." All these kinds, these four Living Creatures, raise this Throne until they bring it to Moses. Once they join her to Moses, then they are the secret of the arms, blessings from the Source of Life upon this spirit, like the incense-binding of Unity that they tie. And this descends when they tie the Unity of all as is appropriate. And regarding this spirit, it is written:
> And Moses saw all the work, etc., and Moses blessed them. <note>Exodus 39:43</note>
The spirit of blessings from below rests in Moses, and this is the "Work of the Sanctuary," because he knew how to arrange the holy service. See, because of this, anyone who prays a prayer and ties the knot of Unity—[the angels] look at him to see if it is a prayer and a binding as is appropriate. Then that prayer lives, and that...

It emphasizes that human prayer and the act of "Unity" (Yichud) facilitate this cosmic marriage between Divine forces.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the construction of the Tabernacle (Mishkan) from the end of the Book of Exodus, transitioning into the laws of the Burnt Offering (Olah) in Leviticus. It focuses on the unique role of Moses as the only one capable of harmonizing the physical structure with its heavenly counterpart.</meta>

# Pekudei (Accounts)

And when the opening was carved out as is fitting, then it was blessed first from the place where all blessings emerge. Then "and you shall screen with it the Ark" <note>Exodus 40:3</note> and immediately "And Moses blessed them" <note>Exodus 39:43</note>. And because of this, they brought the Tabernacle to Moses, for they were the masters of the explanation of the repairs <note>The "repairs" or *tikkunim* refer to the mystical alignment of the physical components with spiritual forces</note> of its existence, and he was required to see its repairs and its secrets, which were not given to any other to gaze upon or to see—those hidden things and explanations of its secrets—except for Moses alone. And regarding this: "And they brought the Tabernacle to Moses, the tent and all its furnishings." And when Moses saw it, all of them were shown to him in their forms and known patterns, each one to be repaired at the edge of the heavenly form, one corresponding to the other. And when they <note>the craftsmen</note> wanted to repair this one corresponding to that, and to raise this one corresponding to that, it did not succeed in their hands. As soon as they showed it to Moses, immediately everything rose up as it should, and every edge and form was elevated and rose, as it is written: "And Moses saw the Tabernacle" and it is written "And the Tabernacle was erected," as we have established.

Come and see: at that hour when Moses began to erect the Tabernacle and to prepare the repairs of the heavenly forms, one corresponding to the other, then all the forms and repairs of the <term>Other Side</term> <note>original: *Sitra Achra*; the realm of impurity or evil</note> were weakened. When this side of the holy vision begins to be strengthened, the impure Other Side is weakened. Regarding this repair, when this one is strengthened, that one is weakened. And we have established that whenever the Other Side is in its strength, these forms are weakened—this one is full and that one is destroyed; this is Jerusalem, and remember that when this is full, that is destroyed. And because of this, when this is strengthened, that is weakened. And for this reason, "Moses erected the Tabernacle" to be strengthened by the spirit from above, so that it would not be strengthened by the spirit from below. And because of this, Moses, who was from the spirit within the <term>shining mirror</term> <note>original: *aspaklaria de-nahara*; a technical term for the highest level of prophetic clarity unique to Moses</note>, was required to guard the Tabernacle from it <note>the impure side</note> and not from another. And for this reason, the calling was required to guard from the impure and not from another. Come and see: the Assembly of Israel <note>The *Shekhinah* or Divine Presence</note> needs to be strengthened above and to cleave without impurity. He opened and said:

> "And this is the law of the burnt offering: it is the burnt offering..." <note>Leviticus 6:2</note>

<term>Rabbi Shimon</term> and <term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> said that which we have stated: it is written "Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains; Your judgments are like the great deep; O Lord, You preserve man and beast." The <term>burnt offering</term> <note>original: *Olah*; literally "that which ascends"</note> ascends as the bond of the Assembly of Israel to the heights, and its cleaving is within the <term>World to Come</term> <note>original: *Alma de-Ate*; the source of divine emanation</note> so that all becomes one; it is called the <term>Holy of Holies</term>. And because of this, it is called *Olah* (Ascending), for it ascends and is crowned to become one, like a single incense. And because it ascends higher and higher, it is written "This is the law of the burnt offering," the secret of the male and female as one. "Law" (*Torah*) is as it is written, "and the law/teaching of..." the ring of the burnt offering that ascends into the World to Come to be bound within it, which is certainly called the Holy of Holies. And because of this, its dwelling is in its hiddenness on the North side, which is the side of the generations of this "Law-Ring" that is forged; she ascends in her love when the North side is crowned, as it is written: "His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me." And then she ascends in love to be crowned by the Right and to be joined in desire, and to be covered entirely by the spirit of the Holy of Holies. And this is from the spirit of the blood of the legs of the Throne, like a hewn stone and like a spark. And we have established how the burnt offering is the Holy of Holies through the spirit of the Supernal Spirit, because three spirits are bound as one: the lower spirit which is called the <term>Holy Spirit</term> <note>original: *Ruach HaKodesh*</note>, the spirit that is within the innermost desire called the spirit of wisdom and understanding, and so the lower spirit is called for all these—the spirit that emerges from the Shofar, included as one. And how much more so the Supernal Spirit, which is hidden in silence, in which all holy spirits and all shining faces exist. And because of this, the burnt offering returns to be actual spirit, and from the spirit of the Throne they are satisfied, and their descent is to bind the "other spirit" which is within the waste of the food... as it was said. Therefore, the burnt offering is the Holy of Holies, the secret of the sacrifices that make peace in the world, all of them from several sides; and the masters of judgment are removed and sweetened from within the will of the one who offers the sacrifice, so that it may be crowned higher and higher.

<summary>This text explains that Moses alone could properly assemble the Tabernacle because his unique prophetic level allowed him to align the physical structure with its spiritual archetype, thereby weakening the forces of the "Other Side." It also provides a mystical interpretation of the Burnt Offering (Olah) as a mechanism for unifying the divine realms and transforming physical matter into spiritual energy.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Tabernacle service from Parashat Pekudei. It focuses on the spiritual mechanics of the sacrifices and incense, explaining how physical offerings trigger a chain of ascent through the angelic realms (Michael and Gabriel) toward the Infinite (Ein Sof).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

...above in the Holy of Holies, and because of this, there are "Offerings of Lesser Sanctity" <note>Hebrew: *Kodashim Kalim*; these are sacrifices with a lower level of holiness compared to the Most Holy offerings</note> and their longing is included [in the higher realm] as we have established. For all those spirits of the Holy of Holies, the service is not through [animal] sacrifices, for everything there is the "Work of the Holy." Come and see what is written: *And to the sons of Kohath he gave none* <note>Numbers 7:9</note>; when these [priests] enter covered and armed for holiness, so it is fitting to approach the Holiness. And it is written that they are "opposite the Holy," and the secret of the matter is like the spices of the incense, for this is the meaning of "Holy." Rather, the Spirit of the King, as we have said, is the Holy of Holies which elevates everything and is crowned in the Holy of Holies like the incense of myrrh and frankincense. From before it, a sobering spirit passes and guides everything so that nothing [unclean] is found; this shall approach within the Sanctuary and be removed from all sides of holiness, and everything remains holy, most holy, and unified.

And Rabbi Shimon said: It has already been stated, as it is written, *Man and beast You deliver, O Lord* <note>Psalm 36:7; original: *Adam u-vehemah toshia Hashem*</note>. And thus the spirit of "Man" ascends from the side of Man, and the spirit of "Beast" from the side of the Beast. For this reason it is written: *When a man [Adam] among you brings an offering* <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>—"Man" certainly, for his offering above is called "Incense." And afterwards, *from the cattle*—and the whole is called "Man and Beast." And it is the spirit that is required to bring "Man" closer, as we have said.

Come and see: when the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world, He made it thus—Man and Beast. And if you should say, "Behold, it is written: *and let birds fly above the earth* <note>Genesis 1:20</note>, for from them too they bring sacrifices, and they are burnt offerings, as it is written: *And if his offering... be a burnt sacrifice of birds* <note>Leviticus 1:14</note>." Come and see: of those birds, they only offer turtledoves and young pigeons. But this spirit that is found in this [offering]—if it is disqualified, the whole is disqualified; this one is prepared and this one ascends, and all is one.

"He shall fly" [*Ye'ofef*] and "Bird" [*Oaf*]—we have already established that these are the spirits of the Chariot <note>The *Merkavah* or Divine Chariot</note>, and through them the Holy Spirit ascends for the man above. For they are two: one to the right and one to the left. "Bird" [*Oaf*] is to the right, and this is the angel **Michael**. "And shall fly" [*Ye'ofef*] is to the left, and this is the angel **Gabriel**. This is right and this is left. Because of this, these two are brought near to elevate the Holy Spirit, etc., which crowns and arms [the Divine Presence] below to that side which is right-to-right, and the lower is bound to her Husband to become one. Then everything ascends and is bound together, both above and below, even down to the flickering of the flame. In the ancient books, it is discussed that this gives a portion below within the above to be bound; but everything above and below is bound, each one to its side as is fitting, and this we have established.

Rabbi Eleazar asked Rabbi Shimon, saying: "Behold, the incense is for everything to be bound in the Holy of Holies, to illuminate the attachment of the Will [*Re'uta*] of the Priest, the Levite, and the Israelite toward the heights. How far does it ascend?"

He said to him: "Come and see: from here until the **Infinite** [*Ein Sof*] <note>The ultimate, unknowable Godhead beyond all emanations</note>. For everything is a path, a brain, and a conclusion to know that Spring which is not opened and not known, for the Will of all wills is within it. The Infinite [*Ein Sof*] does not stand to be known, nor to make an 'End' [*Sof*], nor to create a 'Male' <note>A reference to the beginning of manifestation</note>. Just as the 'Primordial Nothing' [*Ayin*] brought forth a secret and an end from within the secret—this is the **Supreme Point** <note>The Sephirah of *Chokhmah* or Wisdom</note> which is the head of all, hidden, standing within Thought—and it made an 'End' which is called 'The end of the matter, all has been heard.' <note>Ecclesiastes 12:13</note>

There, at the Infinite [*Ein Sof*], there are no wills, no lights, and no lamps on the side of the Infinite. All these stars and lights depend on it to be sustained, but they do not stand to be grasped through knowledge. It is nothing but the Supreme Will, the most hidden of all hidden things. And concerning the Supreme Point and the World to Come <note>The Sephirah of *Binah* or Understanding</note>, to be attached [to the Infinite], they do not know anything except the 'Scent,' like one who smells and is drawn in, and this is hidden within it. And this is what is written: *I will not smell the savor of your sweet odors* <note>Leviticus 26:31</note>. For this 'Scent' is the Will of all wills toward Him. And the will of the body and the will of the Priest—when they are all one spirit, then they all become one Will. And that is called *Nichoach* [Sweet Savor]—a 'Will,' as the Aramaic translation renders it. Then everything is bound and illuminated as is fitting, as has been said. And because of this, this side was given over into the hand of the Priest, as it is written of him: *to satisfy the soul...*

It concludes by describing the ultimate ascent of the human 'Will' toward the Infinite (Ein Sof), which can only be perceived as a 'scent' rather than through direct knowledge.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Tabernacle and the sacrificial service from the Zohar, specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of the Burnt Offering (Olah) and the elevation of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Pekudei**<-
<note>The title of the Torah portion, meaning "Accounts."</note>

This is because another spirit endures, for we have established that it contains nothing but wood, and it comes to be added to it to burn that **evil thought** and to remove it from the holy place through this desire that ascends above. All the smoke and vapors are meant to be burned so that it is removed from the holy place. Their shame and their will stand to separate it from the holy place from within the refuse of the **sacrifice** <term>Korban: an offering brought to "draw near" to the Divine</term>. And if you say, "Are the merits of Israel like this?" Indeed, it is so, for in their will they stand whenever they perform the will of others <note>referring to idolatry or sin</note>, and it cannot ascend over them. In this verse, everything comes to be strict: the spirit of the matter is to crown that **Holy Spirit** higher and higher, and to separate the impure spirit to subdue it lower and lower. This is done through will and through everything as we have said, and not like the action of everything before Him. In this verse, it is proven regarding them, as it is written: "You are lacking and there is nothing in you for wine" <note>The translator notes this is a mystical interpretation of a phrase regarding spiritual lack</note>. This refers to the **impure secret** <note>original: "Raza Messaba"</note> regarding the wine below which is called the "moon."
The Name of God is written here regarding wine, and it is written there: 
> "If a man sends away his wife, and she goes from him and becomes another man's, shall he return to her again? Would not that land be greatly polluted?..." (Jeremiah 3:1)
And we have established it. Because of this, everything was said, and here it stands to be repaired entirely through the spirit of **Kindness** <term>Chesed: the Sephirah of expansive love</term> and through mercy. Blessed is the portion of the righteous in this world and in the world to come, for they know the paths of the Torah and walk in it on the **path of truth**. Regarding them it is written: 
> "O Lord, by these things men live, and in all these things is the life of my spirit..." (Isaiah 38:16)
See the paths of the Torah: "they shall live"—they shall be sustained in this world and in the world to come. Come and see, it is written: 
> "This is the law of the burnt offering: it is the burnt offering on the flame upon the altar all night..." (Leviticus 6:2)
Rabbi Hiyya said: "The Burnt Offering" <note>Olah: literally "that which ascends"</note>—we have established this in relation to this: "This is the law"—this is the **Assembly of Israel** <term>Knesset Yisrael: a title for the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</term>. "The Burnt Offering"—for she ascends and is crowned higher and higher to be bound as is fitting, until the place called the **Holy of Holies**.
Another explanation <note>Original: ד"א</note>: "This is the law"—this is the Assembly of Israel. "The Burnt Offering"—this is the **evil thought** that ascends upon the will of a man <note>Original: כג'</note> to turn him away from the path of truth. "It is the burnt offering"—it is she who ascends and turns him outward <note>Original: כג'</note> to burn him in fire so that he does not approach the Palace of God.
And because of this: "on the flame upon the altar all night." What is burning? This is the Assembly of Israel that comes to purify him outwardly <note>Original: כג'</note> from that evil, "on the flame," because the "River of Fire" is the place that burns all those who do not stand in their persistence. For they enter them into that burning fire and remove their filth from the world. Because of this, it is crowned "on the flame upon the altar all night," and it is subdued. This one ascends, and because of this, the refuse is subdued and ascends. The Assembly of Israel—which is the **Holy Spirit**—ascends and is crowned above, for the ascent is complete when that **Other Side** <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of evil or impurity</term> is subdued and separated from her.
Therefore, we require the spirit of the sacrifice to separate this side from the **holy secret** and to give it its portion, so that the Holy Spirit may ascend above. And come and see: at the time the Tabernacle was prepared and made, the Other Side was subdued and departed from the world. And when it departed from the world and the Tabernacle was strengthened by the hand of Moses, then it was established above and below. It returns: 
> "And Moses raised the Tabernacle, and laid its sockets..." (Exodus 40:18)
What is "and he raised"? Rather, he caused her to ascend higher and higher. And regarding this, "Moses raised"—he who was worthy to raise her as one who raises one who has fallen. Similarly, regarding the time to come, it is written: 
> "In that day I will raise up the fallen Tabernacle of David..." (Amos 9:11)
It is written: 
> "The virgin of Israel is fallen, she shall no more rise..." (Amos 5:2)
What is "she shall no more rise"? This is a difficult statement, for she has risen at other times! Rather, at other times she rose on her own, and **the Holy One, Blessed Be He** <note>Original: קדשא בריך הוא</note> did not raise her. For in the exile of Egypt, the Holy One, Blessed Be He <note>Original: קב"ה</note> raised her and performed many miracles to raise her. But in the exile of Babylon, He did not raise her; rather, she rose herself, and the children of the exile went up as they could, but there was no redemption and no response from the Holy One, Blessed Be He <note>Original: קב"ה</note> upon them, because of that sin that they...

## Main Text (Zohar)

For they are the planting of creation, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, shall raise up the Assembly of Israel <note>The *Shekhinah*, the Divine Presence</note> and act for her with might and power. At that time, as it is said: "She shall fall and rise no more" (Amos 5:2)—specifically, she shall not rise *on her own*. Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, shall raise her up, as it is written: "In that day I will raise up the falling booth of David" (Amos 9:11), and it is written: "And David their king, whom I will raise up for them" (Jeremiah 30:9). And just as it is written: "And Moses raised the Tabernacle" (Exodus 40:18).

Come and see: whenever Moses raised it, the new Tabernacle was established from the ancient one, and the Supernal Tabernacle <note>The spiritual archetype of the earthly Tabernacle</note> was investigated and testified to everything. For the Supernal Tabernacle is covered and hidden high above, and the other Tabernacle below rests upon the Tabernacle below, standing upon it just as that Supernal Tabernacle stands over all. And when the Tabernacle below was raised by the hand of Moses, it was raised above. From this, it is written: "And Moses raised the Tabernacle." Come and examine closely: two Tabernacles were established through the spirit of Moses.

Rabbi Yose said: "And Moses raised..."—everything was prepared to be established, yet it did not stand as a living thing until everything below was completed and he took from the limbs <note>The components of the structure</note> that which was not yet raised.

Rabbi Isaac said: With three knots <note>Or "connections/bonds"</note> Moses raised the Tabernacle. What is written? "And Moses raised the Tabernacle, and laid its sockets, and set up its boards" (Exodus 40:18). With these three knots Moses raised the Tabernacle, and through these three knots the Tabernacle ascended and the "Other Side" <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of evil or impurity</term> was subdued. For this reason, Moses raised it—to subdue the Other Side; therefore, Moses had to raise it and no one else.

Come and see: it is written, "And he laid its sockets." At that moment, the *Chuldarga* <note>original: חולדרגא; a cryptic Zoharic term likely referring to a subterranean power of the Other Side</note> was struck down from the two hundred and forty chariots that were with him, and he fled four hundred parasangs into the purity of the "female of the dust." Moses went and strengthened this side, and then the powers of the Other Side were surrendered and subdued.

He opened and said: "'In that day I will raise up the falling booth of David' (Amos 9:11). What is 'In that day'? On the day that the Holy One, Blessed be He, shall execute judgment in the world and the guilty of the world shall go out in their shame. For there is no rising for the Assembly of Israel from her dust as long as the guilty of Israel remain in the world. What is written above? 'All the sinners of My people shall die by the sword, who say: The evil shall not overtake nor confront us' (Amos 9:10). What is written immediately after? 'In that day I will raise up the falling booth of David...'"

One must look into this: there are broken parts and there are breaches that cause anger. But "I will wall up their breaches"—this refers to the destruction of the guilty, as it is written, "All the sinners of My people shall die by the sword," for then the redemption of Israel is made. And regarding this: "I will wall up their breaches and raise up its ruins." This is from David, because when a kingdom strengthens itself in the world, then the [holy] kingdom will be raised and strengthened, and He will restore, as it were, His own. Therefore: "And I will raise up its ruins." For we have learned: as long as one side is strengthened, the other side does not serve or grow. Therefore, until that time, the [worldly] kingdom strengthens itself. On that day, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will strengthen and establish the holy kingdom, and regarding this: "And I will raise up its ruins and build it as in the days of old." "And I will build it as in the days of old"—this is what is written: "And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun" (Isaiah 30:26).

"And Moses raised the Tabernacle"—he raised it by giving it sockets, as it is written: "And he laid its sockets." He gave them supports beneath to stand upon and to be strengthened by. These are the lamps that open, for those supports beneath are the endurance of the surrounding area. He gave and established them in their strength. At that moment, those supports were superior to the chariots of the Other Side. And concerning this it is written: "Remember, O Lord, against the children of Edom the day of Jerusalem, who said: Raze it, raze it, even to its foundation" (Psalms 137:7). Therefore, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to build Jerusalem from foundations that rule over all. And who are they? The Sapphires <note>The Sefirot of Netzach and Hod</note>, as it is written: "And I will lay your foundations with sapphires" (Isaiah 54:11), which are not weak, but are strong and victorious supports that have no prior loosening. This is the reason they are called "ancient stones."

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Pekudei**<-
<note>original: "Pekudei" (Accounts) — the name of the final Torah portion in Exodus, dealing with the accounting of the Tabernacle's materials.</note>

The first ones were darkened and bowed down, and all the surrounding nations ruled over them. Their taste was bitter <note>original: "mar" (bitter)</note> because there was no radiance that shone as is fitting. In all these things, they are lacking from the supernal radiance and are sunk within the depths, so that they cannot cast a shadow over them. These are the "sapphires" <note>referring to the Sefirot or divine emanations</note> that were broken above and below. And if you say: because at that time the radiance that shines above and below will be increased, those first foundations were nullified? Behold, it is written here: "The wise bow down, the bent are humbled." He bows them down to repair the breakage. What is "bent"? It is the Bride <note>Knesset Yisrael/the Shekhinah</note>. And beneath the "bent," the eyes of the wise are not called to go out. Why? Because he says: "Behold, our vision is the spirit of his bosom," and the spirit is not given to be received, it is given to know.

Come and see: those wise ones of the foundations, once they dwell in the world, the Life <note>Chai</note> that ruled over them hid the Right Hand, so they could not stand or be repaired. They were all diminished, and the Holy One, blessed be He, gathered them. All those foundations of the Holy House were diminished and not seen, even their voice was lowered. But when the Holy One, blessed be He, returns and establishes Jerusalem in its place, those first wise ones will return to their places, and no "other eye" <note>the Evil Eye or the Sitra Achra</note> shall rule over them. As it is written: "As a man paints his eyes with that mouth." And what are his eyes? They are lowered. And then he sees all the wise ones and all the foundations of Jerusalem established in their place, such that the other nations do not rule over them. All those wise ones shall be called "others," and all those lowered wise ones shall all stand in their permanence. And then: "For eye to eye they shall see when the Lord returns to Zion" (Isaiah 52:8). What is "the Lord returns"? Rather, when the other nations ruled over her, the Holy One, blessed be He, took her up on high; the Priest and the Sacrifice shall return to their place, as it is written: "When the Lord returns the captivity of Zion" (Psalm 126:1).

And come and see: anyone who is assisted by merit and does not strengthen the mystery to cast an eye upon it, the [Evil] Eye cannot rule over him, except for the Priest of the kind of known matters. And because of this, here "the wise bow down, the bent are humbled." And come and see: all these wise ones will be established in their places. And these first foundations and the foundations of the other sapphires will be established in another place, like a mark for opening and lengthening. It says: "I will lay your foundations with sapphires" (Isaiah 54:11). At the time when the Holy One, blessed be He, establishes His House in that manner, what is written of it? "A vision for the children." As we have said: "The Lord has swallowed up and not pitied" (Lamentations 2:2). In that cup of staggering, take the sea. And if you say: that "swallowing" is for a known time, and it is written that He chastised them? It is written "forever" <note>Lanzach</note>. What is "forever"? For generations upon generations, and not just a chastisement. And it is like that time when the time arrived to erect the Tabernacle. The Holy One, blessed be He, went out and established the Assembly of Israel <note>Knesset Yisrael</note>, and established the pillars and the sockets, and all that is called the "House" in its repair, in strength forever and ever. And it is written: "Enlarge the place of your tent" (Isaiah 54:2), because the **Other Side** <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of evil or "the other side" in Kabbalah</term> will be swallowed up and will not rise forever, for then "the reproach of His people He will take away from all the earth, for the Lord has spoken" (Isaiah 25:8).

**And Moses erected** the Tabernacle (Exodus 40:18). At that time, he struck those pillars to repair them and to place them in their positions. They stood, and those that were weak were removed from their places—the pillars from the side of the **Other Side**. And regarding this: "And he placed its sockets" <note>Adanav</note>. What is "and he placed"? Rather, this is a teaching: he took them from the place of the "hollow" <note>the void/impurity</note>. The Accuser <note>the Sitra Achra</note> went to prosecute him, and then he overpowered him and bound him before him, and erected it and gave it to its supports. And it is written: "And he placed its sockets"—he placed them with such strength that no other man could cast an eye upon it or place supports in their place. For with great strength Moses erected it.

At that time, to repair the Tabernacle, when the time arrived to make it wise, it was like a single gathering. And at that time, there was strength for the **Other Side** in the world, for in the time of Nisan <note>the month of Passover</note>, the "Head of the Ox" <note>Taurus</note> is in the second image. And when Nisan arrived, he saw the "hollow" and went around to burn it, but the time passed over him. And then "he placed its sockets"—he went around and gave below, and those who went around gave above.

That which is above corresponds to that which is below. At the time when this [earthly structure] was established, another holy [structure] was established above. Through it, the Divine Names were purified, and it flowed and supplied lights to every side, and the worlds were adorned. <note>Zohar II, 221a</note> Rabbi Yose asked, and Rabbi Shimon went on: We have learned that there are three Tabernacles, as it is written: *And on the day that the Tabernacle was reared up...* at the end of the verse we find: *the Tabernacle of the Tent of the Testimony; and at even there was upon the Tabernacle as it were the appearance of fire, until morning.* Behold, three Tabernacles are mentioned here. For it was made wise when the Holy Temple was established in the days of King Solomon; for then there was "rest" above and below, a building where the form <term>Yokna - the spiritual blueprint</term> was strengthened, and the "thief" <note>Referring to external spiritual forces or "husks"</note> could not break in below.

What is the reason? Because it is written: *and My soul shall not abhor you.* We learn the depths of this: a Tabernacle is like a king who comes to visit his beloved and does not bring all his legions with him, so as not to burden his friend; he comes to him with only a few beautiful portions. But a "House" is where he brings all his matters and all his legions with him to dwell properly as befits a house. This is the difference between a Tabernacle and a House. The Holy Temple is a dwelling for the day, for eternity, with all those Divine Chariots <term>Rethichin</term>, with all those forms, with all those works, in the likeness of that which is above, for the works below were fashioned in the likeness of those above. The Tabernacle is like the mountains of forms in small works above and not below, and all is according to the secret of the upper realm.

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> Pekudei <note>The name of the Torah portion, meaning "Accounts"</note> <-

Blessed is He, for He has called me by name in general and we are fit to go. And it is written: *And Bezalel and the wise-hearted and every wise-hearted person worked...* <note>Exodus 36:1</note>. We see that all of this is "below," meaning that man performs the action and it is established through him. And regarding all this, since He commanded and it was done through His command, He showed mercy to all. We have learned: no work is established except through the assistance of action, and therefore **Moses raised the Tabernacle.** All those wise-hearted men wanted to raise it, but it would not stand because of the honor of Moses, until Moses came and raised it, as they have established.

### He Raised
**Moses the Tabernacle.** **Rabbi Yehuda** opened his discourse: <quote>Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy; though I am fallen, I shall arise...</quote> <note>Micah 7:8</note>. This verse is said by the Assembly of Israel <note>original: "Knesset Yisrael," a mystical term for the collective soul of Israel and the Divine Presence</note> to her enemy: "Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy; though I am fallen, I shall arise." This is unlike the other nations, for once they fall, they shall never rise again. But the Assembly of Israel, even though she has fallen, she shall rise—and she has risen many times. For it is written, *though I am fallen, I shall arise,* because many times the Assembly of Israel has fallen into exile <note>original: "galuta"</note> and sat among those masters of enmity <note>the hostile nations</note>. The other nations rose against Israel to destroy them from the world, but they could not succeed at all. <quote>They take crafty counsel against Your people</quote> and it is written <quote>For they have consulted together with one heart...</quote> <note>Psalms 83:4; 83:6</note>. <quote>They have said: 'Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation.'</quote> And despite all this, even though the other nations rose against them, the Holy One, Blessed Be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>, did not leave them in their hands. And they rose again and again, as it is written: *though I am fallen, I shall arise,* for the Holy One, Blessed Be He, raises her up constantly. And the Assembly of Israel is destined to say at that time when the Holy One, Blessed Be He, will raise her from the dust of exile and she shall ascend from it: "Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy; though I am fallen, I shall arise." Though I fell into exile and they enslaved me, I have arisen at this time. And because of this, at that time when Moses brought forth the Tabernacle, when the Holy One, Blessed Be He, made them wise, pious, and mighty to perform the work, then **Moses raised the Tabernacle** is written, for it was raised by the hand of Moses as in every age.

**Rabbi Shimon** <note>Bar Yochai</note> opened and said: <quote>When those went, these went... when those stood, these stood</quote> <note>Ezekiel 1:21</note>. This verse must be looked into. *When those went, these went*—do we not know that when they go, they go, and when they stand, they stand? Rather, *when those went* refers to the movement of the Living Creatures <note>original: "Hayot," a high rank of angels</note>; when they go, the Wheels <note>original: "Ofanim," another rank of angels</note> go as we have said: *And when the Living Creatures went, the Wheels went beside them.* Therefore, *when those went, these went and when those stood, these stood,* because all the movements of those Wheels are not like the movements of the Living Creatures; their existence does not stand on its own, but everything depends on the Living Creatures. And so it is written: *And when the Living Creatures were lifted up from the earth, the Wheels were lifted up beside them,* because the Living Creatures and the Wheels move as one.

And come and see: there are twenty-four <unclear>metakofin</unclear> that beat upon them, standing within one <unclear>mastakofa</unclear> on the eastern side, open to the living. There are four hundred and forty-four hidden and concealed ones, the strength of the crown and the word within that <unclear>mastakofa</unclear> from that eastern side. And four hundred and forty-four supports are beneath them, and upon these supports stand the twenty-four <unclear>metakofin</unclear>. These stand constantly and do not fly through the air like the others; these are the "standing ones" for investigation, as it is said: <quote>I will give you a place to walk among these who stand by</quote> <note>Zechariah 3:7</note>. And these "standing ones" remain on those supports, and in them are secrets to be established in their places. All these pillars stand on their foundations; they are all rulers who stand over them, hovering and encompassing the whole world. They are "eyes" and they are those who grasp the voices that ascend above, as it is said: <quote>For a bird of the air shall carry the voice</quote> <note>Ecclesiastes 10:20</note>. Because of this, those supports stand in permanent establishment. Come and see: *when those went, these went* as we have said, *and when they were lifted up from the earth, the Wheels were lifted up beside them.*

## Main Text (Zohar)

"Opposite them." Just as those living creatures <note>original: *Chayot*, the angelic beings from Ezekiel's vision</note> strike and ascend, so too are these. What is the reason? Because "the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels" <note>original: *Ofanim*</note>. The spirit of the living creature is the Holy Spirit, as it is written <note>Ezekiel 1:20</note> > "and when they went, they turned, and the wheels followed them." It is found that whoever is in a higher degree <term>Darga: a spiritual level or rank</term> strikes that which strikes him. Come and see: those living creatures at the end strike that which strikes them; so too, the living creatures strike the wheels. 

And if you say, "the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels" is written here because it is the mouth of the living creatures—first to the right, then to the left, then forward, and then backward—this is the "Living Creature" <note>singular</note>, and these are the "Living Creatures" <note>plural</note>. It is written <note>Ezekiel 10:20</note> > "This is the living creature that I saw under the God of Israel." When I saw this, it was the living creature of the Chariot <term>Merkavah: the Divine Chariot-Throne</term> for the four sides of the world. And this is what sustains the Throne of the likeness of Man, as it is written <note>Ezekiel 1:26</note> > "and upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man upon it from above." And all of them belong to that high, holy, and hidden degree called the "God of Israel." 

And this is the lower living creature that stands beneath all the holy upper living creatures. For there are upper living creatures, one above the other. The Throne that is beneath the "God of Israel" is the image <term>Dyukna: spiritual form or likeness</term> of Jacob, and the lower Throne is the image of David, which is the Chariot for the four sides of the world. Because of this, the spirit emerges from above, gathers, and is drawn from degree to degree until it strikes all the lower letters. That spirit is found in everything, to establish the rectification <note>original: *tikkun*, the process of spiritual repair or ordering</note> of all things.

In this exact manner, it was established below. What is written above? "For the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels." And it is written, "Whithersoever the spirit was to go, they went." Below, what is written? <note>Exodus 40:18</note> > "And Moses erected the Tabernacle." Just as the spirit of that degree exists below in the image of that upper spirit—it stands "under," as in "I saw under the God of Israel"—and the living creature, the soul, and the spirit are seen to rectify everything; so too Moses stands and gives spirit below to rectify everything, because it is written: "and he erected," "and he gave," "and he placed." All of these were the spirit to rectify everything. 

Come and see: at first, when Moses made the Tabernacle <term>Mishkan: the portable sanctuary in the desert</term>, they rectified it through the spirit of the living creatures of the upper degree in which he stood. At first, when Solomon made [the Temple], he rectified it through the spirit of that Crown <note>Keter</note> that emerges from Eden, which is the "Peace of the House" <note>a play on Solomon's name, *Shlomo*, meaning peace</note> and the living creatures in the "Day of the House." Therefore, like the spirit that finds the living creatures—the sacrifice of belovedness in the degree of the body—that degree in which Moses stood is surely the sacrifice of belovedness in Unity. When Solomon came and established the Sanctuary, that Sanctuary was established in the spirit of belovedness in Unity. 

Because of this, it is written regarding Solomon: "Give, and he shall add a line of measurement." <note>referring to the architectural precision of the Temple</note> Therefore, this was established in one degree and that was established in one degree; the image of this is like that, and the spirit of this is like that. <note>Genesis 37:2</note> > "These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph." The beginning of the return of Moses to rectify this place of the living creatures on the side of holiness—the statutes <note>Chukim</note> stand at the Point <term>Nekudah: the primal point of creation or a specific Sefirah</term> that stands in the whisper of the voice; it went and sank behind it and was not seen and did not shine at all. The beginning of all the statutes is for this Point that was sunk behind it, and afterwards for all the other living creatures in the building of this Point. If this Point is not rectified first, all that spreads from it cannot be rectified. But once this Point is rectified and shines, then the entire order of rectification is established and shines as is fitting. 

Therefore: "And Moses erected the Tabernacle." The word "the" <note>the Hebrew particle *et*</note> refers to this Point that was hidden and sunk behind it. And afterwards: "and he gave its sockets" <note>Adanim</note>—these are the supports of the living creatures from here and from there. For there are sockets and there are living sockets, and all of them were from the four to be found, and all were gathered into the two, as it is written: "under the sockets... a talent for a socket." And these sockets...
