It concludes with a transition to a discourse by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai regarding the fall of Adam.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And if they <note>The heavenly forces of holiness.</note> do not rejoice over them to subdue the Accuser <note>original: *Mekatreg*; the spiritual prosecutor or Satan.</note> and finish him... and furthermore, surely for all his sins—especially those of sexual immorality <note>original: *zenuvta*</note> that disrupt the unity—he ties a knot [of impurity]. But to be blessed, the lower realms must deal with that portion of the Other Side <note>original: *Sitra Achra*; the realm of evil or impurity.</note>. All those sins are taken and placed upon it; they all become its portion. This is the secret of the goat <note>The "Scapegoat" sent to Azazel on Yom Kippur.</note> of which it is written: <note>Leviticus 16:21</note> "And he shall lay both his hands [upon the head of the live goat] and confess over it all the iniquities..." This is its portion, its designated prey, and its gathering place.

But if that man returns to his Master [in repentance] for his sins, woe to him <note>The Accuser.</note>! For they are all taken from that side against the will of the "Side of the Serpent" <note>The primary source of temptation.</note>. And who is it that takes them from before that side against its will? Then [the Accuser] is weakened, and the Accuser turns back and accuses him <note>The Serpent or the evil impulse itself.</note>. And when they rejoice over him, they take them from that Other Side, its life, its prey, and its portion. The secret of this is like the sacrifice <note>original: *korban*</note> which requires one to confess all his sins and thoughts over that sacrifice, to give a portion to the one who needs it <note>The Zohar teaches that a small "bribe" or portion of the sacrifice is given to the forces of impurity to distract them from accusing the person.</note>.

The sacrifice is entirely for this side: the portion of holiness and the will of holiness. And for the other side, that portion of the sins which were committed on the path of that side of the sacrifice. As it is written: <unclear>is not the evil your good</unclear> <note>The OCR here contains fragmented biblical references regarding the inheritance of the wicked.</note>. Blessed is he who knows how to offer mercy to all [even] the accusers. And anyone who does not know how to serve his Master well, it would have been better for him not to have been created.

For one needs to cry out in distress and level the path above, because one needs the "provision" of the mixture and the will to purify. The Voice <note>original: *Kala*</note> and the Word <note>original: *Milla*</note> of the lips are needed to create perfection, a bond, and a unity above, in the same way that it is above. Just as perfection is hidden from above to below, so too is a bond required from below to above, as is fitting. This is the secret of the speech where they give <unclear>wine and a staff</unclear>.

**Thought**, **Will**, **Voice**, and **Word**—these four are the knots that bind. Afterwards, there are four pillars to be crowned with, and the danger is removed from them through all those bonds upon him. **Thought** brings forth **Will**. **Will** brings forth **Voice**. The **Will** that bends from within **Thought** brings forth **Voice**. The **Voice** that is heard ascends to tie the knots from below to above.

The lower Palaces have their masters. The **Voice** is what ties the knots and draws blessings from above to below. All of these are supported by these four: Thought, Will, Voice, and Word. They are the support at the conclusion of the binding, after everything is tied together as one. Blessed is the person who binds the knots of his Master and supports the supports as is fitting, and intends all these words we have said... in this world and the world to come. Until here, the Palaces on the side of Holiness are perfected.

**Rabbi** Shimon opened his discourse and said: <note>Hosea 6:7</note> "But they like Adam have transgressed the covenant; there they dealt treacherously with Me." Who will brush the dust from your eyes, Adam the First? For the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: *HaKadosh Baruch Hu*</note>, gave you a single command, and you could not fulfill it. Because you were seduced by the evil words that the Evil Serpent dug for you, as it is written: <note>Genesis 3:1</note> "Now the serpent was more cunning..." and thus you were seduced after him and brought death upon yourself and all the generations that come from you.

Come and see: anyone who is seduced after him and denies [God] even for a single moment is joined to him. Come and see, David stood like a fountain of water... and when a woman joins another... and according to the youth that was opened from the Holy Land, even though he descended level by level to the lowest, he remained in his standing and did not enter the Other Side, and was protected from it. What is written? "And the soul lived..." <note>original: *Vechai Nafshecha*</note>.

...Blessed is the one who is protected from that evil side and from all the levels of that side that are found in the world. For many sides and levels does the Evil One have: many "crooked ones," the Satan, and the Angel of Death.

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the "Other Side" (the forces of impurity) from the previous page, shifting focus from the specific ritual of the scapegoat to a systematic description of the structure of the realm of impurity. It establishes a parallel between the Palaces of Holiness and the Palaces of Defilement, specifically naming the divisions of Gehenna and the aspects of the Evil Inclination.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

"Death shall be their shepherd" <note>This refers to Psalm 49:15, discussing the fate of the wicked.</note> and this has been established. For although they are called by seven names—the Evil Inclination is called: **Impure, Enemy, Stumbling Block, Uncircumcised, Contemptible, Foolish, and Hidden** <note>original: *Tamei, Soneh, Even Mikhshol, Arel, Navzi, Nevuni, Palin*. These represent various psychological and spiritual aspects of temptation and moral failure.</note>—these seven names correspond to the seven degrees of degradation, all of which come from the Side of Impurity <note>original: *Sitra Mas'ava*</note> as we have said. Corresponding to these seven names are the levels of Gehenna <note>The realm of spiritual purification or punishment after death.</note>, the place where the guilty of the world are judged. And these are they: **Pit, Destruction, Silence, Miry Clay, Sheol, Shadow of Death, and the Lower Land.** <note>original: *Bor, Shachat, Dumah, Tit HaYaven, Sheol, Tzalmavet, Eretz Tachtit*.</note>

All these seven dwellings of Gehenna correspond to these seven names belonging to the Evil Inclination. And we have already established that just as there are levels and Palaces for the side of Holiness, so too are there in the Side of Impurity; they all exist and rule in the world from the side of defilement. There are seven Palaces for those seven names by which Gehenna is called (and not just the Evil Inclination). All of them stand ready for judgment, to close the gates against the guilty of the world who cling to them and do not guard their paths from [sin] while they are in this world.

For anyone who comes to be purified from the side of purity, they purify him in that place called the "Spirit of Faith." There, many levels and many appointees exist to bring him close to the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, and to purify him. But he who comes to be defiled, they defile him from this "Other Side" <note>original: *Sitra Achra*</note> which is the source of impurity. For there are many levels and many appointees standing there to bring them close to the Other Side so that he might be found on that side, as it is written:

-> "What man can live and not see death? Can he deliver his soul [from the power of the grave]?" <-
<note>Psalm 89:49</note>

Heaven forbid that a person should be created in the world and not see death, that world which is preserved for the merit [of the soul]. For at the time when a person is about to depart from his Master's presence, before he leaves this world, he sees [death], as we have established. And these seven Palaces, which are the seven dwellings of Gehenna, are called "Twelve Months." <note>This refers to the traditional Jewish belief that the judgment of the wicked in Gehenna lasts for twelve months.</note> For just as the Side of Faith has twelve months of holy degrees, so too the Other Side has these twelve months in which the guilty are judged, and they are found there to be purified by fire. In this is the portion of the righteous, who are found among the children of [the Master's] house and do not approach those gates, so as not to be found among them in that world.

---

**The First Palace** is the beginning of the side of the Evil Inclination. This first palace is called the **Empty Pit** <note>original: *Bor Rika*</note>. To anyone who comes to enter it, there is no one who shows mercy or who takes hold of him to [protect] him... in this palace stands a certain appointee named **Dumah** <note>The angel in charge of the souls of the dead.</note>, and he stands in authority and strength. A person is pushed away from the Holy Palace by the hand of that appointee... and he stands at the gate of that side. Because of this, Dumah stands ready to seize the soul... and beneath this appointee stands another appointee who follows and rides beneath him, and this appointee is called **Patut** <note>original: *Patut*, meaning "The Enticer" or "The Seducer."</note>. He stands to entice human beings, following them and leading them astray.

He watches to see what is not necessary for [the person]—looking at various types [of forbidden things] and various improprieties. All those who [look] deeply into these are standing before him, and they join him to lead his eyes astray to look at what is not necessary. These are the "evil intermediaries" <note>original: *Sarsora Bisha*</note> for all those evil things. This [spirit] stands over the grave at the time when that body is judged, and he breaks the eyes because they showed the spirit all the sights of this world. He crushes them in this place of judgment until [the soul] enters the place called the Pit, where there are many serpents and scorpions that sting that soul.

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> Pekudei <-

In this assembly, they seek to falsify it <note>Meaning the spiritual record of a person's deeds or their prayers.</note>. Because of this, a specific path is found at the gate for their prayers to ascend over all of them. This spirit stands over this entire Palace, and all the others are struck by him and then stand firm. They are called the **Law-Guards** <note>original: *Nemimusa/Nimosin*, likely referring to the "guards of the law" or "customs" of the dark palace.</note> of the palace; he is red as a rose and stands ready to constantly suppress. For whenever a prayer descends, he pushes it away unless it is found worthy through testimony. When this spirit stands and is silenced, it is as if a praise-filled response rises above all else, and the person’s merit is remembered before the Holy One, Blessed be He. 

Your sign for this is the verse: "And the Satan also came among them" <note>Job 1:6.</note>. It does not simply say, "And the Satan came," but "also" (*gam*). What does this "also" signify? It refers to what a person has entrusted to his own mouth. When a person utters holy words after having uttered impure words, woe to them! Woe to their lives! These people cause those other "guards" to become defiled and to damage the place of holiness. Woe to them in this world, and woe to them in the World to Come! 

Because these impure spirits take that impure word, and when the person later speaks a holy word, those impure spirits rush forward and seize that impure word and use it to defile the holy word. Thus, the person gains no merit from it, and—as it were—the holy power is diminished <note>The text warns that mixing holy words with impure speech causes the Other Side to seize the holiness.</note>. 

Then the hanging ones of this palace enter, and a ruler named **Psifurita** <note>An entity whose name is associated with "judgment" or "calculation" in this dark context.</note> is his name. Under his authority are a hundred judicial guards, all of whom are "deaf" to everything except evil words. They lie in wait for everything a person throws out in falsehood when anger rests upon him. At that moment, this ruler, **Psifurita**, records that word which the person threw out in anger. He ascends and proclaims: "This is the sacrifice of So-and-so, which he has offered to our side!" 

For everything on the side of holiness comes from the "Right Side" and the side of Faith, but the side of anger comes from the "Other Side," the side of impurity. Therefore, those who cast words from their hands <margin>from their memory</margin>, all these guards strike that word which was cast out and carry it upward, offering it to that "Other Side," saying: "This is the sacrifice of So-and-so." A herald then calls out through all those firmaments, saying: "Woe to So-and-so who has sinned before a foreign god and has blemished the holy by following another god!" 

And the herald cries: "Fortunate is the strong one!" <note>Reference to one who overcomes his impulses.</note> ... Fortunate is the person who does not speak a word that swerves to the right or the left and does not become spiritually defiled, for a deep blemish is created that he might not be able to remove.

---

-> **The Palace** <-

The second palace: This palace is darker than the first palace. These are called by the name **Impure** <term>Tamei: spiritually defiled or unholy</term>. Because the first palace was called **Pit** <note>original: *Bor*</note> corresponding to the name **Satan**, this one is called **Destruction** <note>original: *Shachat*</note> corresponding to the name **Impure**. 

In this palace, there are three gates facing three sides. At the first gate stands a ruler named **Afturita** <note>A demonic entity whose name suggests "dismissal" or "exemption" from holiness.</note>. Under him are many thousands and myriads of officers. They all stand over those who "look backward" in their calculations and those who are stingy or have an evil eye <note>Meaning those who are begrudging in charity or calculations of merit.</note>, whose will is not united [with the divine]. This also applies to all those who do not care to achieve any merit at all. 

This ruler from the side of impurity, whom they call upon, comes out at that time with his thousands and myriads; they all gather upon that person and defile him in this world. When his body leaves this world, this ruler and all those with him defile his soul. They seize it, it becomes defiled by them, and it is handed over to be punished by them. These spirits are called the "entangling net," for they are all impure angers standing over this. They all stand and wait for a person at the time he descends... and they snatch away his repentance <note>original: *teshuvah*</note>. Then they strike that repentance, and that "seed" <note>Metaphor for the potential of the soul or the act of repentance.</note> is lost in the waste. They overpower it, seize it, and carry it upward, causing the **Covenant** <note>original: *Brit*, referring to the sacred sign of the soul's connection to God.</note> to not be enslaved after impurity.

<meta>This page continues the description of the "Seven Palaces of Impurity" (the dark counterparts to the heavenly halls). ## The Second Opening

**The Second Opening** contains a certain appointed official <note>original: *memana*</note> who is hidden and revealed. He is appointed over all those who corrupt their ways without mercy, acting wickedly toward one another, behaving like beasts—like horses and mules—in their lustful desires. This official takes many thousands and tens of thousands of agents who all stand ready to corrupt and destroy, as has been explained. 

Come and see: all those who were executed by the court, or those who were righteous and suffered, all of them are honored [in the higher realms], but the "impure sides" have no portion in them. This official is called the **Cup of Reeling** <note>original: *kos ha-tarelah*; a biblical term from Isaiah 51:17 referring to a cup of divine wrath or poison.</note>, prepared for all those who did not fear that cup. When such a soul departs from this world, this official and all his hosts seize it on that bitter day. They saturate that soul with many harsh and terrifying judgments. 

In this palace stands a certain spirit, and an appointed official is under him, though he is not like the official *Kichuliel* <note>A holy angel mentioned in other Zohar passages.</note>. From this powerful spirit emerge three bitter drops that correspond to this "cup of bitterness": one is called *Chanz*, one is called **Bitter Death** <note>original: *mar ha-mavet*</note>, and one is called **Dregs** <note>original: *kuba'at*</note>. These three drops fall from this cup onto the sword that kills with it, as the sages have established.

---

## The Third Opening

**The Third Opening** contains an official named **Sagnadiel**, who is hidden and concealed. He is appointed over all those whose eyes damage the **Holy Covenant** <note>original: *berit kodesha*; in the Zohar, this specifically refers to sexual immorality or "guarding the sign" of circumcision.</note> through forbidden sights, and over all those who corrupt their ways and are called "breachers of the Holy Covenant." This official and all the other officials with him are appointed with great fury, for they are like the lower impurities that defile that holy covenant. All of them are marked before him when a person departs from this world, and they subsequently corrupt him.

In this palace hang all the secrets of the poisons used to kill human beings; because of this, they [the demons] descend and strike them. All these poisons are meant to guard those humans who use their own "poisons" <note>Metaphorical for harmful actions or words.</note> to set themselves up as a sharp sword in opposition to the light. This spirit of mercy is like a beast, and because of this, it comes with three types of rot and a spirit of darkness. 

Because of this, this palace is called the **Opening of the Serpent** <note>original: *Petach Nachash*</note>. In this palace, there is another spirit that is appointed under that spirit of *Sagnadiel*, and he is called **Sartiya**. Many thousands and tens of thousands are under him, and they all stand ready for the word that emerges from a human's mouth. If a word comes from the "impure side," this impure spirit and all the "executioners" <note>original: *gardinei*; agents of punishment.</note> with him emerge and attach themselves to that word. They carry it and mix it with a bit of truth—just as leaven is mixed into dough—to make it believable. 

They then inform the person of things they are lacking, or lying words, or a word of gossip. For if it were not for that small word of truth, the lie would not be able to stand or be established. Therefore, since these spirits mix in words of gossip and weaken them, they inform the person of a word of truth just to sustain the lie. Afterward, they spread out into the lower realms where they have no permanence and will not endure; yet they inform people of these things through many "sides" and many types. 

From this palace emerge two spirits that transform into males and females at different times. These spirits wander and stray through the world in white garments, and they feed people in the midst of a dream. They show themselves as beautiful vessels in the vision of the dream to lead the person's thoughts astray. These are called "lower spirits" that emerge from the flash of the flame. When those higher spirits within this palace take flight, two flashes of fire emerge and fly through the world, becoming these two spirits as we have said. All of this is from the **Impure Side** <note>original: *Sitra Mas'aba*</note>. 

Happy are the righteous who are [instead] punished by these sides in this world to be protected from their punishments [in the next], and because of this...

## Main Text (Zohar)

**The Second Palace** of this series is the Palace of Darkness and gloom; there is no light in it at all. Those who stand beneath it from the beginning are under an official called *Duma* <note>The angel of silence or the graveyard</note>, and because of his name, he is also called "the Blind One" <note>original: *suma*; a wordplay on Duma</note>. In this palace stand judges who judge those who wavered, standing neither here nor there.

One official stands over these first gates, appointed with the power of the world’s wrath and every kind of hidden evil. He sits at this gate, armed and ready to strike at the gates of the synagogues. He is called *Kastartaya* <note>Likely derived from the Latin *castigator*, meaning a punisher or guard</note>, and he is the "thorn of the world." Concerning this it is written:
> The way of the wicked is like deep darkness; they do not know what makes them stumble. <note>Proverbs 4:19</note>

This official stands at the crossroads to observe those who travel. When he gains dominion, he dwells in the world to observe and lie in wait for those individuals who are alone. He has the power to harm them and cause them to see frightening visions in the evening.

**The Second Opening:** Within it stands a spirit appointed over scorching. He stands to nullify the "judgment slips" <note>original: *pitkin de-dina*; decrees of the heavenly court</note>. He is called *Handika*, and beneath him are many, many officers of law who hold authority to receive those judgment slips. He stands at this gate, and when he takes a judgment slip, he descends to the dark openings below—one to the place called *Tophet* <note>A place of fire and sacrifice</note> and one called the **Pit** <note>original: *Bor*</note>. Many thousands and tens of thousands of officials are ready there, who rule the world to execute judgment until the judgment is completed at that opening.

**The Third Opening:** At this opening, there is an official named *Changerin the Blind*. He stands over all those illnesses, pains, and tremors that cause the bones to suffer. From him emerge many thousands and tens of thousands of officials who accompany him over all those illnesses and pains, as has been stated.

**The Fourth Opening:** Here is a certain spirit that conducts itself in the likeness of the moon, and it is called *Chasakhta* <note>original: "Darkness" or "Dimness"</note>. It stands over those who kill on the roads. It strikes them and laughs at them until it drags them down to the paths of pain and hopelessness.

In the likeness of this palace, there stands a spirit called *Lenirumin*. He is appointed over all those who waste their money on many vanities until they reach great crowns <note>perhaps meaning high status or pride</note>, and he is their killer, as we have established. This is under the responsibility of the **Snake** <term>original: *Nachash*; the primordial serpent representing the source of all impurity and temptation</term>, as we have said. He stands in mockery and treats what follows with contempt. Regarding this, he is called "Death, Death, Death," as it is written:
> And behold, it was very good <note>Genesis 1:31</note>
Our sages have established that from here, two types of destruction spread out and emerge: **Anger and Wrath** <term>original: *Af ve-Chemah*; personified demonic forces of divine indignation</term>. These strike all those who hear a group laboring in the Torah and supporting it, yet do not take it upon themselves. Likewise, they strike all those who mock the words of the Torah or the words of the Sages. For from "Anger and Wrath" emerge many thousands and tens of thousands of spirits; they all go out and surround those people who look into the Torah or into words of repentance, making them look at [forbidden] things instead, so they will be delayed and not gaze upon the Truth. Because of these two forces, the "end of all their fatness" shall rot, and they will die from the burden, as it is written:
> For I was afraid of the Anger and the Wrath <note>Deuteronomy 9:19</note>

Beneath these is a single spirit that stands over all those who announce "evil times." Anyone who is stirred at the threshold by this spirit—that person is stirred by an evil garment. Then this spirit of "Evil Times," called **Discord** <note>original: *Sikhsukha*</note>, is awakened in him. They circle around him and the stirrings of the evil garment that people wore, and they ascend on high. Through that awakening, he causes "evil times"—death, the sword, and killing—to come upon the world...

<meta>This page transitions from the description of the Second Palace of Impurity (the "Other Side") to the profound spiritual consequences of human speech, ultimately leading into a description of the Fourth Palace of Holiness, known as the Palace of Merit.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Woe to those who stir up this <term>evil speech</term> <note>original: *lishna bisha*; commonly known as *Lashon Hara*, referring to gossip or slander</note> and do not guard their mouths and tongues. Such actions reveal sins and they do not seek to repent. When things are stirred up below, they cause an equivalent stirring above, whether for good or for evil. 

Come and see: when people stir up evil speech below, the <term>twisting serpent</term> <note>original: *nachash akalton*; a primordial symbol of chaos and evil</note> and the <term>fleeing serpent</term> <note>original: *nachash bariach*</note> raise their scales and hold them high. Eventually, the serpent is aroused from its head to its feet. When its scales are raised and stirred, the entire body is aroused; these scales are all the <term>prosecuting angels</term> <note>original: *gardinei nimusin*; derived from the Greek *nomos* for law, these are the celestial guards who enforce strict justice</note> who exist on the outside. They are all aroused and take pleasure in that evil talk, stirring themselves toward that sin. Through the "fleeing serpent," the entire body of evil is aroused from head to foot, including all those palaces of the "husks" <note>original: *klipot*; the outer shells that conceal the light of holiness</note>. 

All those scales act like a barber's blade <note>original: *galach*</note> below, and that blade spreads from here and there below, while the body rises and is stirred to become a slanderer <note>original: *delatora*; from the Latin *delator*, an informant or accuser</note> above. 

Come and see: although a fixed time is set for all the beasts of the world to shed their skin <note>original: *lekhasel chaspa*</note>, they do not spread except at the time when people stir up evil speech below. Then, that evil spirit is stirred above and spreads its wings and its scales. This one rises and that one descends until that spreading of scales reaches everywhere. Why? Because the separation from the "nourishment of bread" <note>the spiritual essence of the meal</note> is like a single connection; the worlds cannot endure them, and all this is because of the arousal of evil speech below. 

When the lower nourishment is spread from that screen, then each and every one gives voice and is stirred into many kinds of spirits that stand in that place called the "Crucible" <note>original: *kur*</note>, where many sins exist. All of them are informers who stir this evil spirit to blow upon the world, and all because of this stirring of evil speech when it stands aroused below. 

In a similar manner, the side of holiness has many kinds of spirits called the <term>Holy Tongue</term> <note>original: *Lashon HaKodesh*</note> that join together and stir an arousal toward that place called "Holy Tongue"—a tongue originating from that supreme Holiness above. Many sanctities and holy beings are stirred from all sides. Happy is the portion of the righteous who cause these holy stirrings above and below, both the supreme holiness and the lower holiness. Concerning this, it is written:
> And you shall sanctify yourselves, and you shall be holy. <note>Leviticus 11:44</note>

"And you shall sanctify yourselves" refers to the <term>first waters</term> <note>original: *mayim rishonim*; the ritual washing of hands before eating bread</note> which correspond to those supreme waters. "And you shall be holy" refers to the <term>last waters</term> <note>original: *mayim acharonim*; the ritual washing of hands after a meal</note>, and they are indeed called "Last Waters." The nourishment of the bread occurs between the first waters and the last waters. For this reason, the nourishment is not like the last waters, but rather like the first waters; for the first waters come from above, and the nourishment depends upon them, unlike the last waters. Through this, the spirit of holiness ascends to its proper arrangement. Happy is the portion of those who pray for these things in this world and in the World to Come.

->**The Fourth Palace**<-
This palace is called "The Merit-Giver" <note>original: *Mazka*</note>. It is a place of radiance and goodness, standing opposite another opening called "Debt and Obstacle." Yet it is all one "Merit-Giver," for there stand all those who advocate for the world, finding merit. For when human beings are found worthy, all those prosecuting angels ascend, and these merits strike them down through this palace called "Merit." 

All the merits of the world are holy angels appointed over the world’s virtues; they all ascend to show their strength and wisdom in this **Fourth Palace**, which is called "Justice/Merit." There stand the merits of human beings. Merits also stand in another palace called "The Merit-Giver," and they are weighed together on the Day of Judgment <note>Rosh Hashanah</note>:
> For God has made the one as well as the other. <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14; referring to the balance of good and evil</note>

After the merits or debts are weighed to this side or that side, the judgment is built. Therefore, on the day of Rosh Hashanah, when these two sides—Merit and Debt, Life and Death—are joined, if the merits outweigh to this side called "Merit," the person is inscribed in that side called "Life," because...

Because of this, two sides exist at the time when these two emerge, this one and that one, on each side. But if he is like one who sells himself to this "Other Side," the impure side, which seeks only the hour of death, and he desires what belongs to it—claiming "this is mine"—then he is written for his own evil. This is what we have learned: that at this time, a person's path is written, whether for life or for death, <term>heaven forbid</term> <note>original: *chas veshalom*</note>. If he is written on the side of holiness, he is written for life and established there. But if he is written on the Other Side, he is established on the side of impurity and clings to it; this is the meaning of "destined for life or destined for death." Every living righteous person stands on this side of holiness. All sanctifications and purities cling to him. The glory of the <term>Holy One, blessed be He</term> <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note>, dwells upon him and hears him. Concerning him it is written:

It is better for you to go to your shop," or similar vanities regarding loss and profit, until the person is enticed by it. Then all those who stray follow and are drawn after it, along with many other "beasts" that stand beneath it. They all surround him in this world and remove him from the next world. They are called the "lower inheritance," as it is written: "it shall be a wasteland for him." These are the levels that stand to cause constant loss in that place.

In the depths of this palace, there is another spirit that seeks out <term>affliction</term> <note>original: *nega*</note> and strikes. It opens the gate to the guilty who seek the <term>plague of leprosy</term> <note>original: *nega tsara'at*</note>. ## Main Text (Zohar)

-> Pekudei <-

The foreskin <note>original: *Orlah*; in Kabbalah, this refers to the spiritual "husks" or barriers that block holiness</note>. The branches of the foreskin. And above them is one appointee called the "Crown of Rest" <note>original: *Nezar de-Nicha*</note>. He stands over all those who are burdened by the many knots of the foreskin that we have discussed, and over all those types of things that hinder the covenant <note>the ritual of circumcision, *Brit Milah*</note> for their sons. Because of this, the serpent sought to bite the son of Moses until Zipporah descended to him, as it is written:
> "Then Zipporah took a sharp stone and cut off the foreskin of her son, etc." <note>Exodus 4:25</note>
And this spirit is appointed over the sons of men who corrupt their ways and do not bring the foreskin of others to guard the holy covenant. She <note>the spirit of impurity</note> drags them into Gehenna <note>the spiritual realm of purgatory/punishment</note> to that place called **Sheol** and **Abaddon** <note>traditional names for the lowest depths of the underworld</note>, and there they remain, as we have established here. Within this palace are hidden many punishments for neglecting the words of the Torah, in order to prevent them from clinging from below to above. For this entire palace is a mockery; it is a "husk" <note>original: *Klipah*; the outer shell that conceals the inner spark of holiness</note>, and all those surrounding it stand to mislead the clear-sighted ones <note>original: *hakfin behirin*; the righteous or scholars</note> to mock them and entice them so that they deviate from the path of truth, misleading them to their lower realms. Afterward, these forces kill and destroy them across the worlds, as it is written:
> "But her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a two-edged sword." <note>Proverbs 5:4</note>
In this spirit, she is called *Afrach Afrach Afrach* <note>a term suggesting "flying" or "dust," implying something without substance or fruit</note> of the holy side that does not produce offspring and mocks the worlds forever. For this force creates ash and hovers over that which is called "dust." This is not the holy dust that produces fruit, which is called "gold dust," but rather it is entirely like the "ashes from the burning of the sin offering" <note>Numbers 19:9; referring to the Red Heifer used for purification, here contrasted with its dark counterpart</note>. This is the dust of the burnt sin offering, and this support exists on two sides: one because it is included in this surrounding spirit of that powerful serpent, and one because every person who commits a killing strengthens this dust and causes hatred in the world. This is included in the "bitter, curse-bearing waters" <note>Numbers 5:18; referring to the *Sotah* ritual, the ordeal of the suspected adulteress</note>. Therefore, she <note>the woman</note> must be cleared of the misleading influence under the wing [of the serpent]. If she has performed an action below, she must be purified to remove her from being included in this dust, which is the "dust from the floor of the Tabernacle" <note>Numbers 5:17</note>. This dust misleads the place called the "ground," and that is called the "floor of the Tabernacle." This dust misleads the ground, and for this reason, marble was required <note>referring to the Temple floor</note> so that this assembly would not emerge below. All of this is an exalted hint. And the portion of Israel is that the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> [HaKadosh Baruch Hu] purifies them with pure waters poured upon them, as it is written:
> "And I will sprinkle pure water upon you, and you shall be clean." <note>Ezekiel 36:25</note>
Regarding "pure water," these are between the "Waters of Mercy" and the "Other Waters." Even though we have established that the "Waters of Mercy" are clear, they are called such; and the "Other Waters," which are a mockery, are also called such. We have established this regarding these two sides: this side of holiness is called "Living Water," and that powerful serpent is called "Water." Because of this, the dew revives the dead, and regarding this, it is written: "And I will sprinkle pure water upon you, and you shall be clean."

-> **The Palace** <-

The Third. This palace stands above all those other lower palaces. It has 212 gates <note>212 is the numerical value of *Yirah*, meaning "Fear"</note>. To all of them, these are the portions of the "Eighteen Deaths." A stream is called "Evil," one is called "Darkness," and one is called "Shadow." These four gates stand constantly to deny. These are the general forces, just as there are in the side of holiness, in the "Spirit of Faith," four sides that are knotted one to another and are all holy. So too below, they are deceptive. When they join one with another in this palace, it becomes a "house of harlotry" <note>original: *beit hachur*</note>, all of them being the machinations of the lords of ruin. This palace stands to deny constantly. Regarding this palace, it is written:
> "But the kisses of an enemy are deceitful." <note>Proverbs 27:6</note>
Because the nest of the "Serpent" <note>original: *Kina*, also hinting at Cain</note> surrounds all those evil kisses and evil curses. And all the pleasures of this world appear to the humble below as a cup of dregs for my people, and they strike my people. Regarding this palace, it is written:
> "For the lips of a strange woman drip honey." <note>Proverbs 5:3</note>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> Pekudei <-

"Her lips drip honey..." <note>original: *noft titfuna*; a reference to Proverbs 5:3</note>. In this palace stands a certain spirit who is appointed over all those below, and all other spirits are gathered under him. This palace is adorned with decorations of sapphire <note>a false imitation of the Divine Throne</note> above all those other palaces. It is about this palace, in which they clothe and crown themselves, that it is written:
> **"Do not lust after her beauty in your heart, and do not let her captivate you with her eyelids."** (Proverbs 6:25)

In this palace hang all the worldly desires and all those pleasures of the foolish who lack a heart and lack knowledge, as it says: **"For the waywardness of the simple shall slay them, and the complacency of fools shall destroy them"** (Proverbs 1:32). He is one who lacks a heart—**"He who troubles his own house shall inherit the wind"** and **"As a dog returns to his vomit..."** At that time, his feet draw near to their palace, and they all accompany him. Then he goes after the "voice" <note>the call of temptation</note> of the harlot and the filth of the heart. This is this palace, which is an opening to all the other palaces. In it stands the "harlot" to open the way for fools. She stands at the opening and the threshold, rising and going astray, as it is said:
> **"Her feet do not stay at home; now she is in the street, now in the squares."** (Proverbs 7:11-12)

When she rises to preen herself <note>literally "to crawl like a reptile," implying a predatory grace</note>, every corner is filled with sweetness, as it is written: **"Her lips drip honey..."** She gathers for him sins upon sins to entice and to cut down the children of men. Here is the attachment to all bad, sinful debts and all foreign adulteries and all foreign "species" <note>referring to forbidden spiritual forces or idolatry</note>. These things are sweet to the taste, but woe to their end! As we have established: **"And her speech is smoother than oil, but in the end she is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a double-edged sword."** (Proverbs 5:3-4).

When a person is enticed by her in this world and reaches the time of death, she stands over the person, appearing to him like a beautiful garment to look upon. She holds a sword in her hand, and upon it is a single drop of gall. This drop of life-taking bitterness <note>original: *tifa de-chaya*; ironically "drop of life," but referring to the venom of death</note> is placed into the person's mouth. It enters his innards, and then the person dies <note>literally "is consumed"</note>. He opens his eyes and sees his body being uprooted, and the soul is uprooted from within him. She does not leave the soul a way to return. Life becomes **bitter as wormwood**, and the person tastes that bitterness in exchange for the sweetness they pursued in this world when they were drawn after her.

Afterward, she returns to that drop of gall, and the person’s life departs and he dies. Then she returns again... <note>The text describes the spiritual decomposition and the "greenish" pallor associated with the judgment of the grave</note>. Because she is like a cold, bald entity, she rules over him. This is the one who watches and flees from before him, and no life is found. Because of this, as much as one attached himself to those evil sins in this world, so too is he drawn after this bitter taste. He leaves the Holy Side <note>the *Sitra Kadisha*</note>, and just as he was drawn after her in this world, so too does that soul fall under her dominion. It exits in pain and darkness. All of this is because of those sins he committed in this world which were sweet at first but later became bitter to him. Concerning this, "he vomits it up," as we have established.

In this palace stand all the accusers <note>original: *katigorin*</note> and all the evil messengers who look toward a person and cause him to fixate on his own finery, to curl his hair and be seized by vanity. Here stands a spirit of mockery and contempt, who is appointed over all the grooming and vanity of men. Inside this palace stands one appointee who incites the person after he has groomed himself and curled his hair. He takes in his hand a mirror <note>original: *mercha*; a looking glass</note> to look into. He holds it in his hand and looks into it, seeing his own image in that mirror. This awakens that spirit to pursue transgression. From here emerge all those visions that appear like bears <note>distorted or frightening images</note> to people in their dreams, and all those visions of things that will not be fulfilled...

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> Pekudei <-

And afterwards, all those people who are found in that vision of coldness <note>Original: *de-lakiru*. All of this is caused by that vision of the spirit of the beast that he gazed upon. For just as one causes a disgrace <note>Original: *gnuta*</note> in his heart, so too does he cause an evil secret to come upon him. All of this stands over the one who awakens below.

"O righteous ones, I have **peace offerings** <note>Original: *shelamim*</note> upon me." Come and see: a peace offering does not come for a liability or for a sin, but for prayer <note>Or "supplication"</note>. What is the meaning of "peace offerings"? It means "peace" from two sides, so that no accuser is found against it, neither above nor below. What is this "beast of accusation"? For that side of the arm <note>The Left Side, Gevurah/Judgment</note> knows that it is found in the peace of the Right. Therefore, "I have peace offerings upon me"—this is the purification in her heart toward you, to see you... and because of this, there are peace offerings, so as to always open these worlds.

"Therefore I came out to meet you..." <note>Reference to Proverbs 7:15</note> for I know that there is kindness <note>Hebrew: *Chesed*</note> for the pure son—a great kindness that said "your face" is to be found with you in all the matters of the world. It will appear to you to consume you and to lead you astray after your desires. And now the world is certainly full for him, and a cup is covered for the wicked to lead them with a tongue of foolishness and the burden of "your face." And I was diligent when I found you, to see you with an open eye. "Come, let us take our fill of love until morning..." <note>Proverbs 7:18</note>. Everyone says "money of blood," for then is the time of the beast's curse. "Let us take our fill of love"—just as it pushes, the power is with you, for now you ride with power like a living king. You have opened, you shall not delight in your high places... a vision and resting place... for the life that sews in this house is the **Good Inclination** <term>Yetzer Tov: the inner drive toward morality and divine connection</term>, who does not trouble himself like a sober man. And this beast rests.

"The man is not at home; **he has gone on a long journey**" <note>Reference to Proverbs 7:19</note>. He [the Good Inclination] does not trouble a person until he is twelve years old and onward. Until then, he rests in every person, and the [evil] power stands with you from the day you were born—this is "at the opening, sin crouches" <note>Genesis 4:7</note>. You shall be for the desire of the youth... and it rests for you, you shall not delight in your high places. "**He took a bag of money with him and will come home at the full moon**" <note>Proverbs 7:20</note>. When will he come toward him? "On the day of the throne" <note>A pun on *Keseh* (throne/full moon) and *Kassa* (covered/hidden)</note> of the beast, on the day of judgment, as it is written: "**at the full moon on our feast day**" <term>Original: *Bakiseh l’yom chageinu* (Psalm 81:4)</term>. At the time when a person needs to enjoy the world and be established in it, they are found away from him; like a burden that troubles all the children of this world in this judgment, to perform judgment upon him. And regarding this: "**With her much fair speech she caused him to yield**" <note>Proverbs 7:21</note> until an arrow pierces his liver. All those who are wise know the holy paths to walk in, and they shall not stray to the right or the left, both in this world and the world to come.

---

### **The Palace**

The **Seventh Palace**: This is the palace they say belongs to the "Master of Expansion" <note>Original: *le-itravacha*, implying a false sense of relief or spreading out</note>. In it, one is found to be "of the wine," as in "**he drank of the wine and became drunk and was uncovered within his tent**" <note>Genesis 9:21, referring to Noah</note>. For all those who perform evil deeds, here the beast is their destroyer <note>Or "their death"</note>. It is not the "living wine" <note>Holy wine</note>, but the wine of the dregs, for there is no one who drinks of it who does not bring death to his soul. This wine was tasted by the "End of Days" <note>Referring to the primordial Serpent or the Harlot</note> for her husband; she entered with him into this palace to establish the side of the [forbidden] grapes. She forced it upon him and caused death for him and for the whole world.

In this palace stand all the **impure sides** <term>Sitra Achra: forces of spiritual pollution</term> that exert power over all those on this side who cling to her. And by that spirit, power is exerted over all those from this side. This palace functions in this manner for those who strayed from their paths in this world and engaged in **immorality** <term>Zonuta: refers both to physical lust and spiritual unfaithfulness to God</term> where it was not permitted, just as it is found in that [palace].

---

<summary>This page describes the psychological and spiritual traps of the Seventh Palace of Impurity, using the "Strange Woman" of Proverbs to illustrate how the Evil Inclination leads people astray. It specifically notes that the Good Inclination only takes an active role in a person after age twelve, leaving the youth vulnerable to the "wine" of spiritual intoxication.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the description of the "Seven Palaces" (Heichalot) of the Side of Impurity (Sitra Achra). The previous page discussed the deceptive nature of temptation and the spiritual "coldness" that can overtake a person. Here, the text concludes the description of the Seventh and lowest palace, detailing the various spirits that emerge from it, the fate of those who follow them, and surprisingly, a place of relative honor for those from other nations who treated Israel with kindness.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> Pekudei <- -> 268 <-

In this manner, when an evil spirit emerges from the flesh, it is found there for him and for all who are hungry <note>Original: *de-khaphin*. This refers to spiritual hunger or craving for the impure</note>. And this spirit is called **Impure-Born** <note>Original: *Mamzer*. In Jewish law, a mamzer is a child of a forbidden union; here, it refers to a spirit born from the "Other Side"</note> who comes from this "Stranger" side <note>Original: *Sitra Za'ar*. Referring to the "Strange Woman" or the foreign/impure side</note>, who is taken to cling to that arrangement of the evil spirit. So too, he draws toward himself that other spirit from the one that ascends, and all those who bow down to it are consumed by the **Impure-Born**; and so are all his deeds and outcomes in that very same way. It is found that there is one bowed spirit appointed over those spirits that search the soul and return the soul there. And this spirit is appointed over this, and this is the seventh palace, corresponding to that opening that faces it in the teaching <note>Original: *matnita*. Refers to a traditional study or a specific section of the Zohar's internal teachings</note>. And regarding this it is written: **"And you shall remove the altar from upon you"** <note>This is a Kabbalistic adaptation of a biblical theme, suggesting the removal of the "altar" of impurity or the false sacrifices of the ego</note>. This spirit is a single command that stands before us, and from here emerge all those other spirits that wander in the world and rule over all those matters that were handed over from the **Left Side** <note>The side of Gevurah/Judgment which, when unbalanced, becomes the source of evil</note>. From here emerge all those hidden sparks that cling to a place of debris and are extinguished; and from the hollows emerge other spirits that stray in the world, for they are the **Great Abyss** <note>Original: *Tehoma Raba*. A primordial state of chaos and depth</note>, and for them, this palace is as one from the side of the Great Abyss. And those spirits that were not permitted to wander in the worlds appear and do not appear to those below, as has been said. And afterwards, those spirits that stray in the world stand at a distance, like a kind of throne, because these do not stand in a pattern that is as unified as the others. And one spirit is appointed over them, and they search the "Saw" <note>Original: *Nesira*. A Kabbalistic term for the separation of the masculine and feminine or the carving out of entities</note> which is meant to be scattered from those sides that are more unified. And these fly in the air and deny their own side in order to act like those who are from the **Side of Holiness**. And from this spirit, it is announced that they search the dwelling of the poor. From it emerge several other sides, branching out into their various kinds, and all of them stand ruling in the world, each one as is fitting for it, until kings and officers are appointed below. But they have no permanent existence like those on the sides above. In this palace is the clinging of the **Impure Side** <note>Original: *Sitra Mas'ava*</note>, and all the impure arrangements that defile the world. And this is ready to emerge every day—a spirit of sin—and there is no one who is holy before it. From here emerges the sin of a strong spirit below, in which the world's guilty are found. And from here emerges a spirit from the flame of him who is sin, and it shaves/erases what is sought by the tongue, just as there is "dread" <note>Original: *chatatnu*. Wordplay on sin and fear/dread</note> at all times. In this palace stand four openings that branch out to the four sides, for every corner is sharp and they do not resemble the **Side of Holiness**, which is not grasped by the lower power. In those openings is a light that shines and a lap <note>Original: *cheiku*. A place of refuge</note>, a place prepared for those acts of kindness that went with them—those who did not deny Israel and dealt with them in truth. These all stand at the openings. And since... at the opening of this palace, all the leaven <note>Original: *chamieuta*. Symbolic of the ego or the "Evil Inclination"</note> is outside the six openings that cling to this palace, and all of them covet it. The Priest... there are windows open to the side of the **Holy Masculine**, and those platforms are prepared for the kings of the other nations, those who did not distress Israel and protected them constantly. If they have honor in their possessions... and to be established in this hollow where they dwell, like that of the Holy Masculine. "All the kings of the nations, all of them, lie in glory" <note>Isaiah 14:18</note>, for they acted kindly toward Israel. They are distanced from those who covet them below. And they are judged three times a day, with several balanced judgments. If any of those kings reached out to harm Israel in this world, they face many judgments. And every single day they bear witness regarding Israel and their faithfulness. And when they die below and are purified there, they see the power of Israel in this world and in the World to Come. Thus far are the **Seven Palaces** of the dwellings of the Impure Side, as it is written: "For in the sin of her sacrifice, her portion is from the midst of her sister." He brings it down from his house and removes it so that it will not be scattered from his house and will not cast into it a shard of death. From all...

--- Page 538 ---
<meta>This page continues the discussion of spiritual dangers from the previous page, moving from the specific "palaces" of impurity to the overarching figure of the primordial Serpent. It transitions from the mechanics of sin to the mechanics of purification through sacrifice and the ultimate ascent of the human soul toward the Infinite.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Pekudei**<-

From all sides, one must guard oneself against it <note>original: "minneih" — referring to the Serpent or the Evil Inclination</note>, from above and below. Whoever occupies themselves with this secret will be saved from the snare. For like a dog, it strikes the head and barks, strikes and kills; and despite all this, wisdom is never exhausted without a whispered spell <note>original: "lachash" — a mystical or protective incantation</note>, just as we have learned concerning the secret that emerges in the cycle of reincarnation. Because of this, a person must be careful not to return before the Holy One, Blessed be He, lest they be snatched up by that serpent who drags one down and kills. **“And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground”** <note>Genesis 2:7</note>; it says "dust of creatures" <note>original: "afar chayon"</note> and does not say "dust of a living being" <note>original: "afar chaya"</note>. It refers to the dust of all things, for **“dust you are, and to dust you shall return”** <note>Genesis 3:19</note> after having sinned. And because of this, it is written of the serpent: **“And dust you shall eat all the days of your life”** <note>Genesis 3:14</note>. This "dust" refers to Man, of whom it is written, **“For dust you are...”** And because of this, it is written "dust" <note>Hebrew: *afar*</note> and not "earth" <note>Hebrew: *adamah*</note> or "clay" <note>Hebrew: *chomer*</note>, and it is written, **“and the serpent's food shall be dust”** <note>Isaiah 65:25</note>.

This continues until the Holy One, Blessed be He, awakens and shakes that spirit of impurity <note>original: *rucha mesava* — the source of spiritual defilement</note> from the world, as it is written: **“He will swallow up death forever...”** <note>Isaiah 25:8</note> and He will raise that dust and awaken it to rejoice in the world, as it is written: **“Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust...”** <note>Isaiah 26:19</note>. It is written, **“Now the serpent was more cunning”** <note>Genesis 3:1</note>; this is the spirit of impurity that exists on every side to oppose humanity. It is given the power to rule, to entice, and to lead astray. This is the "male" spirit, for the male rules over the female and imparts within her an impure and defiled strength; they are joined together and are never separated. They are darkness, a darkening gloom, a total end, and an added darkness of gloom; darkness and a thick cloud. For there is "darkness" and then there is the "living creature of darkness." We have learned: whoever sins before Him, death is decreed upon them. To be saved—because the impure serpent is an impure path—it is called "the living creature, the nest of every bird." <note>This refers to a specific cryptic teaching regarding the source of impure spirits</note>

One day, Rabbi Eleazar was sitting before Rabbi Shimeon. Rabbi Eleazar said: This "nest of every bird" refers to the sweetening of the sacrifices that Israel used to offer upon the altar. Rabbi Shimeon said to him: They were not satisfied all at once, above and below. Come and see: the Priests, the Levites, and the Israelites established the "Human" <note>original: *Adam* — the spiritual archetype of humanity</note> in the dwelling place for the holy desires that ascend from them. That lamb, or sheep, or whatever the sacrifice happened to be, was required—before it was offered on the altar—to have all their sins, transgressions, and all the evil thoughts they had committed declared over it. Then that sacrifice was called "the carrier of all sins," covering over the transgressions and the thoughts, much like the burnt offering, as it is written: **“And he shall confess over it all the iniquities of the children of Israel...”** <note>Leviticus 16:21</note>. So too it is here. 

And when the sacrifice ascends upon the altar, it reaches its place in a twofold manner. Because of this, one part ascends to its place and the other ascends to its place; one is included in the "Human" and the other is included in the "Beast," as you say: **“Man and beast You save, O Lord”** <note>Psalms 36:7</note>. The grain offerings and all other meal offerings are the "bread of the damaging raven" <note>A metaphor for the forces that seek to prosecute man</note> which they bring forth through the will of the Priest, the prayer of the Levite, and the assembly of Israel. Through that smoke, the support, and the incense that ascends, all the other "prosecutors of judgment" <note>original: *chamrei de-dinin* — the forces of strict justice/judgment</note> are satisfied and satiated so that they cannot bring accusations against that spirit which comes to be purified; and they all become as one. 

Come and see: everything is done through the spirit of faith, to be satisfied and to ascend above. One must see that it is necessary to reach as far as the <term>Ein Sof</term> <note>The Infinite/Without End — the highest, most unknowable level of the Divine</note>. Rabbi Shimeon said: I lift my hands in prayer to the heights! For when the Supreme Will ascends higher and higher, it stands upon that Will which is neither known nor grasped—the Head that is most concealed of all. And that Head brings forth what it brings forth, though it is not known; and it illuminates what it illuminates, yet all is in concealment. The desire of the "Higher Thought" <note>original: *Machshavah Ila'ah* — the first glimmer of divine intellect</note> is to pursue it and to be illuminated by it. When the curtains are spread, they are spread; and from within that curtain, in the pursuit of that Higher Thought, it reaches and yet does not reach <note>original: *mati velo mati* — a classic Kabbalistic paradox of touching the untouchable</note>, until that curtain is illuminated by what it is illuminated. Then that Thought illuminates with a hidden illumination that is not known. Thus the Thought stands unknown, and then it illuminates and stands within the concealment of the "Sanctuary" <note>original: *Mikdasha*</note> that is not known, through the illumination of the curtain that stands and shines from that which is not...

<summary>This page discusses the spiritual battle against the "Serpent" (the Evil Inclination), the relationship between human mortality and the dust, and the restorative power of sacrifices to satisfy judgmental forces while the worshiper's "Higher Thought" ascends toward the Infinite (Ein Sof).</summary>
<keywords>Serpent, Evil Inclination, Dust, Resurrection, Sacrifice, Altar, Higher Thought, Ein Sof, Impurity, Rabbi Shimeon bar Yochai</keywords>

--- Page 539 ---
<meta>This page continues the exploration of the spiritual realms, shifting from the cautionary warnings about the primordial serpent to the sublime mechanics of the Divine Mind and the sanctification of the Tabernacle. It bridges the gap between the "Other Side" (the realm of impurity) and the "Infinite" (the source of all light).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

That which is not known, nor can it be known, nor is it revealed. And then, this light of Divine Thought <note>original: "Machshava" — the primordial spark of the Divine mind</note>, which is not known, strikes against the light of the expanse. All of them are unified as nine palaces <note>original: "Heichalin" — spiritual chambers or levels of emanation</note> that are not spirits and are not souls, and there is no one who can grasp them. The will of all nine lights exists within the Thought, which is one of them in the count. All of them pursue them <note>the higher lights</note> at the time they stand within the Thought, yet they cannot be grasped or known. These do not stand in will or in thought; though they <note>the lower levels</note> grasp at it, they do not truly grasp it. All of them stand as the secrets of faith, and all those lights from the spirit of the Supernal Thought downward are all called <term>Ein Sof</term> <note>original: "The Infinite" — referring here to the unified flow of light from the hidden source</note>. Until this point, the sides reach yet do not reach, and they are not known. Here, there is neither will nor thought. When Thought shines, though it is not known, it is sealed within Understanding <note>original: "Binah" — the third Sefirah or Divine attribute</note>. In this, for the one who shines and enters, one enters into the other until they are all included as one. Just like the smoke of the sacrifice, when everything ascends and is bound one to another, and one shines within the other—then they all stand, and Thought is crowned with the <term>Ein Sof</term>. That light from which Thought emerges, which is not known and has no substance at all, is called <term>Ayin</term> <note>original: "Nothingness" — the highest, most hidden state of the Divine</note>; from it, the light of longing is found and established. And upon this, everything depends. Happy is the portion of the righteous in this world and in the world to come.

Come and see: the <term>Sitra Achra</term> <note>original: "The Other Side" — the realm of evil or impurity</note> is called "the end of all flesh," just as we have said above. Just as there is joy on the side of holiness, so too there is a simulation below. But joy and will are not found at all [on the Other Side] above or below, and the Spirit stands over Israel as is proper. Come and see: in every New Moon, when the moon is renewed, this "end of all flesh" is given a portion from the sacrifices which are poured out for him, and he is enticed by his portion. This side is given to Israel for their portion because they are measured in their kingdom, so that there should be no "hairy one" <note>original: "sa'ir" — a reference to the goat-demon or Esau</note>, because he is the portion of Esau, as it is written, **"Esau was a hairy man"** <note>Genesis 27:11</note>. We are the portion of the "thread of the city" <note>likely referring to the lineage of Jerusalem/Holiness</note>, and because of this, he is enticed by his portion, and Israel is spared from his portion. Because of this, it is written:
> **For the Lord has chosen Jacob for Himself, Israel for His own possession.** • <note>Psalms 135:4</note>

And come and see: there is no crown whose will is not on the side of the male. Because of this, it is the rectification of the male. And concerning this, there is the law of "the end of all flesh." And when he rules over the body but not over the soul, the soul ascends to the wealth <note>spiritual reward</note>, and the crown is given to this place through the law of the sacrifice. For the will ascends to one place and the crown to another place. And when he is subdued and everything is restored, the sacrifice strikes for atonement, and below there are no children with a blemish, as it is written, **"for it shall not be accepted for you"** <note>Leviticus 22:20</note>. And because of this, the Righteous One <note>original: "Tzaddik"</note> is an atonement in the world and is a literal sacrifice. The portion of the righteous is in this world and in the world to come.

**"And the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting"** <note>Exodus 40:34</note>. For then, the Tabernacle was expanded <note>or "the Serpent was puffed up," a play on words regarding the protective surrounding of the Divine Presence</note>, and the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> surrounded it like a serpent <note>meaning a protective circle</note>, and the spirit of impurity—which is the "end of all flesh"—was removed from the world. It departed and entered the opening of the Great Abyss. Then the Holy Spirit hovered over the world, as it is written, **"And the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting."** And it is written, **"And Moses was not able to enter the Tent of Meeting because the cloud settled upon it"** <note>Exodus 40:35</note>, because the Holy Spirit was hovering over the world and the spirit of impurity had departed. When those wicked ones darken it <note>the world</note>, just as they did at first, the living creatures push it away and it is darkened for the world and is not found. But in the time to come, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to remove it from the world, as it is written:
> **He will swallow up death forever; and the Lord God will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the reproach of His people shall He take away from off all the earth; for the Lord has spoken it.** • <note>Isaiah 25:8</note>
Blessed be the Lord forever, Amen and Amen. May the Lord reign forever, Amen and Amen.

<meta>This page serves as the colophon, or concluding statement, for this printed edition of the Zohar. It transitions from the profound mystical teachings of the previous pages to the practical and pious reflections of the printers and proofreaders who brought this monumental work to the press in 16th-century Italy.</meta>

## Closing Statement of the Zohar Edition

->**The proofreaders** <note>original: *magihim* — the scholars responsible for correcting the text before printing</note> **said:**<- 
These "schoolchildren" <note>a humble idiom used by scholars to describe themselves</note> declare that the "Torches" <note>likely referring to specific illuminated passages or a cross-reference title</note> were printed according to the version found in the reference on page 179: 
"That which is not common to him, what is common to him is the sealed mystery hidden in the treasure of the most Ancient of Ancients, and the end of this, etc." <note>This Aramaic phrase reflects the cryptic, mystical style of the Zohar itself, discussing the hidden nature of Divine emanations.</note>

---

->**Blessed**<- be the Lord who has shown His wondrous kindness to us—those standing here and those afar—to sustain them in this land, by the merit of the gathering of this book and its words, sweeter than honey, which were spoken by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>the traditional author of the Zohar</note> and all the holy company <note>original: *chavurata kadisha*</note> with him. Therefore, may the Lord be with us and grant us favor in the eyes of the nations, for His remembrance and for our support. <note>The printers here add a poetic prayer for the successful distribution of the book and for the well-being of the Jewish community in exile.</note>
May He gather the books, and the book of books of old, in joy and gladness.
May He also return our exiles as a crown, establishing us
and granting us life before Him.

---

->**Finished and completed; praise be to God, Creator of the world.**<-

Today, Tuesday, the 19th day of the month of Elul, in the year [5]320 <note>September 1560. The original uses the "Minor Era" (*lifrat katan*) which omits the millennium</note>, by the partners:
The humble Samuel, son of Meir of blessed memory, son of Ephraim and all his company, 
and Jacob, son of the honored Naftali HaKohen <note>the Priest</note> of blessed memory, from Gazzuolo <note>a town in Lombardy, Italy, known for its Hebrew press</note>.
May it be His will that His mercy merits him to produce books
without end, and that he may magnify the Torah 
and make it glorious. Amen.
->**Blessed be the Lord forever, Amen and Amen.**<-
